@@@ kernel/arch/aarch64/boot/header.S @@@
1:// Header multiboot2 per GRUB
2:.section .multiboot2_header
3:.align 8
4:
5:multiboot2_start:
6:    // Magic number
7:    .long 0xe85250d6              // magic
8:    .long 0                       // architecture (0 = i386, but GRUB handles AArch64)
9:    .long multiboot2_end - multiboot2_start  // header_length
10:    // checksum
11:    .long -(0xe85250d6 + 0 + (multiboot2_end - multiboot2_start))
12:
13:    // Entry address tag
14:    .short 5                      // type = entry_address
15:    .short 0                      // flags
16:    .long 16                      // size (type + flags + size + entry_addr = 2+2+4+8)
17:    .quad _start                  // entry point (64-bit)
18:
19:    // Framebuffer tag
20:    .short 8                      // type = framebuffer
21:    .short 0                      // flags
22:    .long 20                      // size
23:    .long 0                       // width
24:    .long 0                       // height
25:    .long 0                       // depth
26:
27:    // End tag
28:    .short 0                      // type = end
29:    .short 0                      // flags
30:    .long 8                       // size
31:
32:multiboot2_end:
33:

@@@ kernel/arch/aarch64/boot/stage1.S @@@
1:.section .text
2:
3:// Entry point dal GRUB multiboot2
4:.global _start
5:.type _start, @function
6:
7:_start:
8:    // Salva il multiboot info pointer e magic
9:    mov x19, x0    // multiboot2 info pointer
10:    mov x20, x1    // multiboot2 magic
11:    
12:    // Verifica magic number
13:    ldr x0, =0x36d76289
14:    cmp x20, x0
15:    bne halt
16:    
17:    // Disabilita interrupts
18:    msr daifset, #0xf
19:    
20:    // Setup stack primario
21:    adrp x0, __stack_top
22:    add x0, x0, :lo12:__stack_top
23:    mov sp, x0
24:    
25:    // Salva core ID
26:    mrs x21, mpidr_el1
27:    and x21, x21, #0xff
28:    
29:    // Solo core primario procede
30:    cbz x21, primary_core_init
31:    
32:    // Core secondari attendono
33:    b secondary_core_wait
34:
35:primary_core_init:
36:    // Parse multiboot2 info
37:    bl parse_multiboot2_info
38:    
39:    // Setup paginazione
40:    bl setup_paging
41:    
42:    // Setup MMU
43:    bl enable_mmu
44:    
45:    // Inizializza core secondari
46:    bl init_secondary_cores
47:    
48:    // Salta a stage2
49:    ldr x0, =stage2_entry
50:    br x0
51:
52:halt:
53:    wfe
54:    b halt
55:
56:// Parse multiboot2 information structure
57:parse_multiboot2_info:
58:    mov x0, x19    // multiboot2 info pointer
59:    
60:    // Verifica versione (deve essere 0)
61:    ldr w1, [x0, #4]
62:    cbz w1, parse_continue
63:    b halt
64:    
65:parse_continue:
66:    // Calcola lunghezza totale
67:    ldr w2, [x0]    // total_size
68:    // Estendi w2 a x2 per l'aritmetica a 64-bit
69:    uxtw x2, w2
70:    add x3, x0, x2  // end pointer
71:    
72:    // Inizio tags
73:    add x4, x0, #16
74:    
75:parse_loop:
76:    cmp x4, x3
77:    bge parse_done
78:    
79:    // Leggi tag type e size
80:    ldr w5, [x4]     // type
81:    ldr w6, [x4, #4] // size
82:    
83:    // Allinea size a 8 byte
84:    add w6, w6, #7
85:    and w6, w6, #0xfffffff8
86:    
87:    // Switch su type
88:    cmp w5, #6    // MEMORY_MAP
89:    beq parse_memory_map
90:    
91:    cmp w5, #9    // ENTRY_ADDRESS
92:    beq parse_entry_address
93:    
94:    // Prossimo tag
95:    uxtw x6, w6
96:    add x4, x4, x6
97:    b parse_loop
98:
99:parse_memory_map:
100:    // Processa memory map - usa adrp/add per indirizzamento
101:    adrp x7, multiboot_mmap_tag
102:    add x7, x7, :lo12:multiboot_mmap_tag
103:    str x4, [x7]
104:    uxtw x6, w6
105:    add x4, x4, x6
106:    b parse_loop
107:
108:parse_entry_address:
109:    // Processa entry address
110:    ldr x5, [x4, #8]
111:    adrp x7, kernel_entry_point
112:    add x7, x7, :lo12:kernel_entry_point
113:    str x5, [x7]
114:    uxtw x6, w6
115:    add x4, x4, x6
116:    b parse_loop
117:
118:parse_done:
119:    ret
120:
121:// Setup paginazione 4-level
122:setup_paging:
123:    // Azzera le tabelle di paginazione
124:    adrp x0, page_table_l0
125:    add x0, x0, :lo12:page_table_l0
126:    mov x1, #0
127:    mov x2, #4096 * 4  // 4 pagine per tabelle
128:clear_tables:
129:    str xzr, [x0], #8
130:    subs x2, x2, #8
131:    bne clear_tables
132:    
133:    // Crea identity mapping per i primi 4GB
134:    adrp x0, page_table_l0
135:    add x0, x0, :lo12:page_table_l0
136:    adrp x1, page_table_l1
137:    add x1, x1, :lo12:page_table_l1
138:    orr x1, x1, #0x3  // valid + page table
139:    str x1, [x0]
140:    
141:    // Setup L1 table (1GB block entries)
142:    // Per blocchi da 1GB usiamo descriptor di tipo block (bits [1:0] = 01)
143:    adrp x0, page_table_l1
144:    add x0, x0, :lo12:page_table_l1
145:    mov x1, #0        // start address 0x0
146:    mov x2, #4        // 4 entries (4GB)
147:    
148:    // Attributi per block descriptor: AF=1, nG=0, AP=00, SH=10 (outer shareable)
149:    // Lower attrs: 0x401 (valid block) + 0x400 (AF bit)
150:    movz x8, #0x0401
151:    
152:setup_l1_loop:
153:    orr x3, x1, x8    // address + attributes
154:    str x3, [x0], #8
155:    // Incrementa di 1GB (0x40000000)
156:    mov x9, #0x4000
157:    lsl x9, x9, #16   // x9 = 0x40000000
158:    add x1, x1, x9
159:    subs x2, x2, #1
160:    bne setup_l1_loop
161:    
162:    ret
163:
164:// Abilita MMU
165:enable_mmu:
166:    // Setup MAIR_EL1 (Memory Attribute Indirection Register)
167:    // Attr0: Device-nGnRnE, Attr1: Normal Write-Back
168:    movz x0, #0x0044
169:    movk x0, #0xff00, lsl #16
170:    msr mair_el1, x0
171:    
172:    // Setup TCR_EL1 (Translation Control Register)
173:    // T0SZ=25 (39-bit VA), IRGN0=1, ORGN0=1, SH0=3, TG0=0 (4KB)
174:    movz x0, #0x0019
175:    movk x0, #0x8080, lsl #16
176:    movk x0, #0x0035, lsl #32
177:    msr tcr_el1, x0
178:    
179:    // Setup TTBR0_EL1 (Translation Table Base Register)
180:    adrp x0, page_table_l0
181:    add x0, x0, :lo12:page_table_l0
182:    msr ttbr0_el1, x0
183:    
184:    // Invalida TLB
185:    tlbi vmalle1
186:    dsb sy
187:    isb
188:    
189:    // Setup SCTLR_EL1 (System Control Register)
190:    mrs x0, sctlr_el1
191:    orr x0, x0, #0x1    // M bit (MMU enable)
192:    orr x0, x0, #0x4    // C bit (cache enable)
193:    orr x0, x0, #0x1000 // I bit (instruction cache)
194:    msr sctlr_el1, x0
195:    isb
196:    
197:    ret
198:
199:// Inizializza core secondari
200:init_secondary_cores:
201:    mov x0, #1  // start from core 1
202:    
203:init_core_loop:
204:    cmp x0, #8  // max 8 cores
205:    bge init_cores_done
206:    
207:    // Scrivi entry point per core secondario
208:    adrp x1, secondary_core_entry
209:    add x1, x1, :lo12:secondary_core_entry
210:    adrp x2, cpu_entry_addrs
211:    add x2, x2, :lo12:cpu_entry_addrs
212:    str x1, [x2, x0, lsl #3]
213:    
214:    // Scrivi stack per core secondario
215:    adrp x1, __stack_base
216:    add x1, x1, :lo12:__stack_base
217:    add x1, x1, x0, lsl #16  // 64KB per core
218:    add x1, x1, #0x4000      // stack pointer a fine area
219:    adrp x2, cpu_stacks
220:    add x2, x2, :lo12:cpu_stacks
221:    str x1, [x2, x0, lsl #3]
222:    
223:    add x0, x0, #1
224:    b init_core_loop
225:    
226:init_cores_done:
227:    ret
228:
229:// Core secondari attendono
230:secondary_core_wait:
231:    // Setup stack per core secondario
232:    mrs x0, mpidr_el1
233:    and x0, x0, #0xff
234:    
235:    adrp x1, cpu_stacks
236:    add x1, x1, :lo12:cpu_stacks
237:    ldr x2, [x1, x0, lsl #3]
238:    mov sp, x2
239:    
240:    // Abilita MMU
241:    mrs x1, sctlr_el1
242:    orr x1, x1, #0x1
243:    msr sctlr_el1, x1
244:    isb
245:    
246:    // Attendi entry point
247:secondary_wait_loop:
248:    wfe
249:    adrp x1, cpu_entry_addrs
250:    add x1, x1, :lo12:cpu_entry_addrs
251:    ldr x2, [x1, x0, lsl #3]
252:    cbz x2, secondary_wait_loop
253:    br x2
254:
255:secondary_core_entry:
256:    // Core secondario entry point
257:    b secondary_core_main
258:
259:secondary_core_main:
260:    // Qui arrivano i core secondari
261:    // In un sistema reale, qui si integrerebbe con il kernel
262:    wfe
263:    b secondary_core_main
264:
265:.section .data
266:.align 8
267:
268:.global multiboot_mmap_tag
269:multiboot_mmap_tag:
270:    .quad 0
271:
272:.global kernel_entry_point
273:kernel_entry_point:
274:    .quad 0
275:
276:.section .bss
277:.align 16
278:
279:// Tabelle di paginazione
280:.balign 4096
281:page_table_l0:
282:    .skip 4096
283:
284:.balign 4096
285:page_table_l1:
286:    .skip 4096
287:
288:.balign 4096
289:page_table_l2:
290:    .skip 4096
291:
292:.balign 4096
293:page_table_l3:
294:    .skip 4096
295:
296:// Stack per i core
297:.balign 16
298:__stack_base:
299:    .skip 8 * 131072  // 8 core * 128KB ciascuno
300:__stack_top:
301:
302:// Entry points e stack per core secondari
303:.balign 8
304:cpu_entry_addrs:
305:    .skip 8 * 8  // 8 entry points
306:
307:.balign 8
308:cpu_stacks:
309:    .skip 8 * 8  // 8 stack pointers
310:

@@@ kernel/arch/aarch64/boot/stage2.S @@@
1:.section .text
2:
3:.global stage2_entry
4:.type stage2_entry, @function
5:
6:stage2_entry:
7:    // Setup ambiente kernel
8:    bl setup_kernel_environment
9:    
10:    // Inizializza dispositivi base
11:    bl init_basic_devices
12:    
13:    // Salta al kernel entry point
14:    adrp x0, kernel_multiboot_info
15:    add x0, x0, :lo12:kernel_multiboot_info
16:    ldr x0, [x0]
17:    adrp x1, kernel_entry_address
18:    add x1, x1, :lo12:kernel_entry_address
19:    ldr x1, [x1]
20:    cbz x1, stage2_halt  // Se non c'è entry point, halt
21:    br x1
22:
23:stage2_halt:
24:    wfe
25:    b stage2_halt
26:
27:// Setup ambiente kernel
28:setup_kernel_environment:
29:    // Setup stack kernel
30:    adrp x0, __kernel_stack_top
31:    add x0, x0, :lo12:__kernel_stack_top
32:    mov sp, x0
33:    
34:    // Prepara multiboot info strutturata per kernel
35:    bl prepare_kernel_multiboot_info
36:    
37:    ret
38:
39:// Prepara info multiboot per kernel
40:prepare_kernel_multiboot_info:
41:    // Crea struttura multiboot info semplificata per kernel
42:    adrp x0, kernel_multiboot_info_struct
43:    add x0, x0, :lo12:kernel_multiboot_info_struct
44:    
45:    // Copia info rilevanti dal multiboot originale
46:    adrp x1, multiboot_mmap_tag
47:    add x1, x1, :lo12:multiboot_mmap_tag
48:    ldr x1, [x1]
49:    str x1, [x0, #8]  // memory map
50:    
51:    // Setup flags
52:    mov x1, #0x1      // basic memory info
53:    str x1, [x0]
54:    
55:    ret
56:
57:// Inizializzazione dispositivi base
58:init_basic_devices:
59:    // Qui si inizializzerebbero dispositivi essenziali
60:    // UART, timer, ecc.
61:    ret
62:
63:.section .data
64:.align 8
65:
66:kernel_multiboot_info:
67:    .quad 0
68:
69:kernel_entry_address:
70:    .quad 0
71:
72:kernel_multiboot_info_struct:
73:    .quad 0    // flags
74:    .quad 0    // memory map pointer
75:    .quad 0    // boot device
76:    .quad 0    // cmdline
77:    .quad 0    // mods count
78:    .quad 0    // mods addr
79:    .quad 0    // elf sections
80:    .quad 0    // memory map length
81:    .quad 0    // boot loader name
82:    .quad 0    // apm table
83:    .quad 0    // vbe info
84:
85:.section .bss
86:.align 16
87:
88:// Stack kernel
89:.balign 16
90:__kernel_stack:
91:    .skip 131072  // 128KB stack kernel
92:__kernel_stack_top:

@@@ kernel/arch/aarch64/cpu/cpu.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/aarch64/cpu/cpu.c
3: * AArch64 CPU initialisation, synchronous exception dispatch, and SMP support.
4: *
5: * Role:
6: *   This file owns three distinct concerns for the AArch64 port:
7: *   1. Per-CPU hardware initialisation (CPACR, NEON, VBAR installation).
8: *   2. The C-level synchronous exception handler (sync_handler), which is the
9: *      top of the dispatch chain entered from exception.S's vector_stub macro.
10: *      It decodes ESR_EL1.EC and routes to the syscall handler, the memory-probe
11: *      recovery path, or a per-EL fault printer / panic / process terminator.
12: *   3. SMP helper routines: per-CPU kernel stack management, secondary-CPU PGD
13: *      propagation, and the early MMU-enable sequence (arch_vmm_init_hw).
14: *
15: * Invariants:
16: *   - sync_handler is called with IRQs already masked (DAIF.I/F set by hardware
17: *     on exception entry); it may only re-enable IRQs under specific recovery
18: *     paths (see is_kernel_user_access_fault branch).
19: *   - arch_vmm_init_hw must be called exactly once on the primary CPU before any
20: *     secondary CPU is woken; secondaries read secondary_ttbr0 after this point.
21: *   - CPACR_EL1.FPEN is set to 0b11 on every CPU so that the full NEON register
22: *     set can be saved/restored by exception.S (q0–q31, FPSR, FPCR).
23: *
24: * Known issues:
25: *   ARCH-04 (W2 BAD-IMPL·BUG)  FDT memory parse often fails; the manual probe
26: *            fallback in arch_platform_get_mem_regions (platform.c:62–96) then
27: *            sets arch_mem_regions[0] twice — once at lines 83–86 and again at
28: *            91–94 — the second write silently overrides the first. See
29: *            platform.c comments for detail.
30: *   ARCH-05 (W2 REFINE) The probe relies on sync_handler's probe_in_progress
31: *            shortcut; a fault during probing of device memory windows may
32: *            trigger undesirable side-effects before the handler fires.
33: *   AMMU-08 (W2 BUG) arch_vmm_init_hw issues TLB flush only on the current CPU;
34: *            no SMP TLB shootdown is performed when secondary CPUs arrive.
35: *   CPU-AARCH64-01 (W2 REFINE) sync_handler: a wild kernel pointer that
36: *            happens to fall in the user VA range is misclassified as a
37: *            kernel-uaccess fault, leading to silent process termination instead
38: *            of a kernel panic. [static]
39: *   SYS-AARCH64-02 (W2 BAD-IMPL) The is_kernel_user_access_fault recovery
40: *            path unconditionally releases current_process->mm_lock and calls
41: *            local_irq_enable(), assuming exact lock discipline that is not
42: *            documented or enforced. A future refactor of uaccess critical
43: *            sections could silently violate this coupling.
44: */
45:#include <kernel/printk.h>
46:#include <kernel/string.h>
47:#include <kernel/types.h>
48:
49:/* Exception frame structure */
50:#include <kernel/cpu.h>
51:#include <kernel/fault.h>
52:#include <kernel/sched.h>
53:
54:#include <kernel/arch.h>
55:#include <kernel/vmm.h>
56:
57:/* External definitions from core */
58:extern struct cpu_info cpu_data[MAX_CPUS];
59:extern uint32_t nr_cpus;
60:
61:/*
62: * Per-CPU EL1 fault (abort) stacks — Phase A step 4.
63: *
64: * aarch64 has no IST: an EL1-from-EL1 sync abort or SError re-uses SP_EL1,
65: * so a kernel-stack overflow or a fault with a wild SP recursed until silent
66: * death.  handle_el1_spx_sync/serror (exception.S) switch onto
67: * arch_fault_stack_top[cpu] before building the 816-byte frame; the original
68: * SP is parked in the 16-byte slot directly above the frame so the C handler
69: * can both report it and copy the frame back for resuming paths (probe fixup).
70: *
71: * 16KB per CPU sized for: sync_handler + classification + fault_printf dump +
72: * the backtrace walk, with margin.  In .bss → identity-mapped in kernel_pgd.
73: */
74:#define FAULT_STACK_SIZE 16384
75:static uint8_t fault_stacks[MAX_CPUS][FAULT_STACK_SIZE] __attribute__((aligned(16)));
76:uint64_t arch_fault_stack_top[MAX_CPUS]; /* read by exception.S vectors */
77:
78:/*
79: * arch_frame_on_fault_stack - is this exception frame on a per-CPU fault stack?
80: * Used by sync_handler to know whether the parked-SP slot at frame+816 exists
81: * and whether a resuming path must copy the frame back to the original stack.
82: */
83:int arch_frame_on_fault_stack(const void *frame) {
84:  uintptr_t p = (uintptr_t)frame;
85:  uintptr_t base = (uintptr_t)fault_stacks;
86:  return p >= base && p < base + sizeof(fault_stacks);
87:}
88:
89:/*
90: * arch_cpu_info_fault_safe - per-CPU info with no faultable dependencies
91: * (kernel/fault.h, Phase A step 5).
92: *
93: * On aarch64 the CPU id comes from MPIDR_EL1 — a system-register read that
94: * cannot fault — so this is simply the bounds-checked cpu_data[] lookup.
95: */
96:struct cpu_info *arch_cpu_info_fault_safe(void) {
97:  uint32_t id = arch_impl_get_cpu_id();
98:  if (id >= MAX_CPUS)
99:    return NULL;
100:  return &cpu_data[id];
101:}
102:
103:/* External functions from assembly */
104:extern void exception_vectors_install(void);
105:
106:/*
107: * arch_cpu_init - per-CPU hardware initialisation (called on every core).
108: *
109: * Actions performed on each CPU:
110: *   1. Records cpu_id and marks the CPU online in cpu_data[].
111: *   2. Increments nr_cpus atomically for secondaries (primary sets nr_cpus=1).
112: *   3. Enables the FPU/SIMD (NEON) unit by setting CPACR_EL1.FPEN[21:20]=0b11,
113: *      which allows EL0 and EL1 to execute floating-point and NEON instructions
114: *      without trapping to a higher EL.  An ISB is issued to ensure the CPACR
115: *      write takes effect before any subsequent NEON instruction.
116: *   4. Installs the exception vector table (VBAR_EL1) via exception_vectors_install.
117: *
118: * Side effects: modifies CPACR_EL1, VBAR_EL1; prints boot diagnostics.
119: * EL context: called at EL1 (MMU may or may not be active; called both pre- and
120: *             post-MMU during primary and secondary CPU bring-up).
121: */
122:void arch_cpu_init(void) {
123:  uint32_t id = arch_get_cpu_id();
124:
125:  cpu_data[id].cpu_id = id;
126:  cpu_data[id].online = 1;
127:
128:  /* Publish this CPU's EL1 fault-stack top BEFORE installing the vectors:
129:   * from the first VBAR exception onward, handle_el1_spx_sync/serror switch
130:   * onto it (a zero entry makes the vector stay on the current stack). */
131:  arch_fault_stack_top[id] = (uint64_t)&fault_stacks[id][FAULT_STACK_SIZE];
132:
133:  if (id == 0) {
134:    nr_cpus = 1;
135:    pr_info("CPU: Primary core %u initialized\n", id);
136:  } else {
137:    /* Avoid pr_info here as it might cause lock contention with primary core
138:     * boot logs */
139:    __sync_fetch_and_add(&nr_cpus, 1);
140:  }
141:
142:  /* Enable FPU/SIMD (NEON) - set CPACR_EL1.FPEN = 0b11.
143:   * FPEN[21:20] == 0b00 traps FP/NEON from EL0+EL1 to EL1.
144:   * FPEN[21:20] == 0b11 disables the trap entirely; needed so that
145:   * exception.S can save/restore q0-q31 without faulting. */
146:  uint64_t cpacr = arch_impl_get_cpacr();
147:  cpacr |= (3 << 20); /* FPEN bits [21:20] = 0b11 */
148:  arch_impl_set_cpacr(cpacr);
149:  arch_impl_mb();
150:  arch_impl_isb(); /* ensure CPACR change is visible before NEON use */
151:
152:  /* Install exception vector table */
153:  exception_vectors_install();
154:
155:  pr_info("CPU: Vector Table set to 0x%lx\n", arch_impl_get_vbar());
156:}
157:
158:/*
159: * probe_in_progress / probe_failed - volatile flags for safe memory probing.
160: *
161: * Set by the manual RAM discovery loop in platform.c (arch_platform_get_mem_regions)
162: * when the FDT memory parse fails.  When probe_in_progress is true and a Data Abort
163: * or Instruction Abort fires, sync_handler advances ELR_EL1 by 4 to skip the faulting
164: * load and sets probe_failed so the caller knows the address is unmapped.
165: *
166: * Both flags must be volatile: they are written by C code and tested in the
167: * exception handler on the same CPU; without volatile the compiler could optimise
168: * away the test or hoist the write out of the loop.
169: *
170: * NOTE(ARCH-05): This mechanism works only because QEMU's virt machine delivers
171: * aborts synchronously on an invalid load.  On real hardware with speculative
172: * prefetch or device windows that do not abort cleanly, the probe may have
173: * undesirable side-effects (e.g., triggering a device register read).
174: */
175:volatile bool probe_in_progress = false;
176:volatile bool probe_failed = false;
177:
178:/*
179: * sync_handler - C-level synchronous exception handler called from exception.S.
180: *
181: * Parameters:
182: *   frame  Pointer to the 816-byte exception frame pushed on the kernel stack by
183: *          the vector_stub macro in exception.S.  The handler may modify frame->elr
184: *          to change the return address (e.g., probe recovery), or swap in a
185: *          different frame pointer entirely (e.g., schedule() returning a new task).
186: *
187: * Returns: pointer to the exception frame that should be restored on eret.
188: *          Normally the same frame; after schedule() it is the new task's frame.
189: *
190: * EL context: entered at EL1 with IRQs masked (DAIF.I set by hardware).
191: *
192: * EC decoding (ESR_EL1[31:26]):
193: *   0x00  Unknown / uncategorized — print and fall through to fault handler.
194: *   0x15  SVC instruction from AArch64 EL0 — dispatch to syscall_handler().
195: *   0x20  Instruction Abort from lower EL (EL0 code page fault).
196: *   0x21  Instruction Abort from same EL (EL1 code fault — kernel bug).
197: *   0x24  Data Abort from lower EL (EL0 load/store fault).
198: *   0x25  Data Abort from same EL (EL1 load/store fault — kernel bug or probe).
199: *   0x26  SP alignment fault.
200: *   other  Unhandled — print and panic (kernel) or terminate (user).
201: *
202: * Probe recovery path (probe_in_progress == true):
203: *   If a Data or Instruction Abort occurs while probe_in_progress is set,
204: *   probe_failed is marked and ELR_EL1 is advanced by 4 to skip the faulting
205: *   single instruction.  This is the only case where the handler returns early
206: *   without the full fault-classification logic.
207: *   NOTE(ARCH-05): See probe_in_progress declaration for caveats on real hardware.
208: *
209: * Fault classification (for all non-SVC ECs):
210: *   is_user_fault       — SPSR.M[3:0] == 0b0000 (EL0t, i.e. exception came from EL0).
211: *   is_kernel_user_access_fault — kernel was executing but FAR_EL1 points into user
212: *                         VA range; implies an arch_copy_from/to_user access faulted.
213: *
214: *   NOTE(CPU-AARCH64-01): A wild kernel pointer coincidentally in user VA range is
215: *   misclassified as is_kernel_user_access_fault and leads to process termination
216: *   instead of a kernel panic.  [static]
217: *
218: * User / uaccess fault handling:
219: *   The current process is terminated and schedule() is called to pick a new task.
220: *   NOTE(SYS-AARCH64-02): If is_kernel_user_access_fault is true, this code assumes
221: *   the faulting code held mm_lock and had IRQs disabled, and unconditionally calls
222: *   spin_unlock + local_irq_enable before process_terminate.  This is fragile; any
223: *   future change to the uaccess critical section discipline must update this path.
224: *
225: * Kernel fault handling: dumps all registers and calls panic().
226: */
227:struct pt_regs *sync_handler(struct pt_regs *frame) {
228:  uint64_t esr, far, elr;
229:  uint32_t ec;
230:
231:  if (!frame)
232:    return NULL;
233:
234:  /* Read exception syndrome */
235:  esr = arch_get_fault_status(); /* ESR_EL1: exception syndrome register */
236:  far = arch_get_fault_address(); /* FAR_EL1: fault address register (valid for aborts) */
237:  elr = frame->elr; /* ELR_EL1 saved in frame by vector_stub */
238:
239:  /* ESR_EL1[31:26]: Exception Class — identifies the exception type */
240:  ec = (esr >> 26) & 0x3F;
241:
242:  /* SVC from EL0 is a syscall, not a fault: bypass the recursion guard and
243:   * every fault-path primitive entirely. */
244:  if (ec == 0x15)
245:    return syscall_handler(frame);
246:
247:  /* Fault recursion guard (Phase A step 7): an abort inside this handler used
248:   * to recurse on the kernel stack until silent death.  Detect nesting FIRST
249:   * — before anything that could itself abort — and stop with one raw line.
250:   * fault_exit() runs on every resuming path below; the panic path keeps the
251:   * depth elevated so panic() selects its fault-safe output mode. */
252:  if (fault_enter() > 1) {
253:    fault_printf("\n[FATAL] NESTED EL1 EXCEPTION EC=0x%x ELR=%016lx FAR=%016lx — halting\n",
254:                 ec, elr, far);
255:    arch_cpu_halt();
256:  }
257:
258:  /* Probe recovery: if a Data Abort (EC=0x24/0x25) or Instruction Abort
259:   * (EC=0x20/0x21) fires while a RAM probe is in progress, set probe_failed
260:   * and skip the faulting instruction by advancing ELR_EL1 by 4.
261:   * The probe load is always a single 4-byte instruction (ldr/ldur), so +4 is safe.
262:   * NOTE(ARCH-05): On real hardware with speculative loads this may not be
263:   * sufficient; a proper exception-table fixup (like Linux's extable) is safer. */
264:  if (probe_in_progress && (ec == 0x24 || ec == 0x25 || ec == 0x20 || ec == 0x21)) {
265:    probe_failed = true;
266:    /* Skip the faulting instruction (increment ELR by 4) */
267:    frame->elr += 4;
268:    fault_exit();
269:    /* If the vector switched us onto the per-CPU fault stack, the eret
270:     * epilogue computes the final SP as frame+816 — which would resume the
271:     * probe loop ON the fault stack.  Rebuild the frame just below the
272:     * original SP (free space: stacks grow down) and return that instead,
273:     * so execution resumes with SP exactly as it was at the abort. */
274:    if (arch_frame_on_fault_stack(frame)) {
275:      uint64_t old_sp = *(uint64_t *)((char *)frame + 816) + 16; /* +16: scratch push */
276:      struct pt_regs *orig = (struct pt_regs *)(old_sp - 816);
277:      memcpy(orig, frame, sizeof(*frame));
278:      return orig;
279:    }
280:    return frame;
281:  }
282:
283:  /* One-line classification banner.  fault_printf (not printk): the address
284:   * space and lock state are unknown at this point for EL1-origin faults. */
285:  switch (ec) {
286:  case 0x00: /* Unknown exception — ESR does not encode a specific cause */
287:    fault_printf("Unknown exception at 0x%016lx\n", elr);
288:    break;
289:
290:  case 0x20: /* Instruction abort from lower EL (EL0 code page not mapped) */
291:  case 0x21: /* Instruction abort from same EL (EL1 instruction fault — kernel bug) */
292:    fault_printf("Instruction abort at 0x%016lx, FAR=0x%016lx\n", elr, far);
293:    break;
294:
295:  case 0x24: /* Data abort from lower EL (EL0 load/store to unmapped/protected addr) */
296:  case 0x25: /* Data abort from same EL (EL1 load/store fault — kernel bug or probe) */
297:    fault_printf("Data abort at 0x%016lx, FAR=0x%016lx\n", elr, far);
298:    break;
299:
300:  case 0x26: /* SP alignment fault — SP not 16-byte aligned on exception entry */
301:    fault_printf("SP alignment fault at 0x%016lx\n", elr);
302:    break;
303:
304:  default:
305:    fault_printf("Unhandled exception EC=0x%x at 0x%016lx\n", ec, elr);
306:    break;
307:  }
308:
309:  {
310:    /* User-vs-kernel decision (Phase A steps 8/10): delegated to the generic
311:     * helper.  is_user_fault = SPSR.M[3:0] == 0b0000 (EL0t).  The old
312:     * "FAR in user VA implies a uaccess fault" heuristic (CPU-AARCH64-01) is
313:     * gone: the helper recovers ONLY when the per-CPU uaccess_active flag —
314:     * set exclusively inside arch_copy_{from,to,string_from}_user — marks the
315:     * dereference window; the mm_lock/IRQ unwind (SYS-AARCH64-02) lives in
316:     * arch_uaccess_fault_fixup next to the code that takes those locks.
317:     * A wild kernel pointer that merely lands in user VA now panics below. */
318:    struct pt_regs *next = fault_handle_user_or_panic(
319:        frame, (frame->spsr & 0xF) == 0, far, elr, "SYNC EXCEPTION", esr);
320:    if (next)
321:      return next;
322:
323:
324:    /* Kernel fault: the address space may be compromised — every line below
325:     * goes through fault_printf (lock-free, no per-CPU buffer).  panic() at
326:     * the end sees fault_depth() > 0 and uses its fault-safe output mode. */
327:    fault_printf("%s", "--- Kernel Exception Context Dump ---\n");
328:    fault_printf("Process: PID %d\n",
329:                 current_process ? (int)current_process->pid : -1);
330:    fault_printf("SPSR_EL1: 0x%016lx\n", frame->spsr);
331:    fault_printf("ELR_EL1:  0x%016lx\n", frame->elr);
332:    fault_printf("FAR_EL1:  0x%016lx\n", far);
333:    fault_printf("ESR_EL1:  0x%016lx\n", esr);
334:    fault_printf("EC: 0x%x, ISS: 0x%x\n", ec, (uint32_t)(esr & 0xFFFFFF));
335:    if (arch_frame_on_fault_stack(frame)) {
336:      /* The vector switched us onto the per-CPU fault stack; the SP at the
337:       * moment of the abort was parked just above the frame. */
338:      fault_printf("Frame: %p (per-CPU fault stack), faulting SP: 0x%016lx\n",
339:                   (void *)frame, *(uint64_t *)((char *)frame + 816) + 16);
340:    } else {
341:      fault_printf("Frame: %p (faulting kernel stack)\n", (void *)frame);
342:    }
343:
344:    if (elr == 0) {
345:        fault_printf("%s", "CRITICAL: Kernel jumped to NULL! Check exception vector table and function pointers.\n");
346:        fault_printf("Stack at 0x%lx:\n", (uint64_t)frame);
347:        for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
348:            fault_printf("  [%p] 0x%016lx\n", (void*)&((uint64_t*)frame)[i*2], ((uint64_t*)frame)[i*2]);
349:        }
350:    }
351:
352:    for (int i = 0; i < 31; i += 2) {
353:      if (i + 1 < 31) {
354:        fault_printf("X%02d: 0x%016lx  X%02d: 0x%016lx\n", i, frame->regs[i], i + 1,
355:                     frame->regs[i + 1]);
356:      } else {
357:        fault_printf("X%02d: 0x%016lx\n", i, frame->regs[i]);
358:      }
359:    }
360:    fault_printf("SP_EL0:  0x%016lx\n", frame->sp_el0);
361:    fault_printf("%s", "-----------------------------\n");
362:    backtrace_regs(frame->elr, frame->regs[29]);
363:    backtrace_scan((uint64_t)frame);
364:    panic("Unrecoverable kernel exception");
365:  }
366:
367:  /* Unreachable today (the block above either schedules or panics); kept so
368:   * any future early-return path unwinds the recursion guard correctly. */
369:  fault_exit();
370:  return frame;
371:}
372:
373:/*
374: * fiq_handler - unexpected FIQ (Phase A step 13).
375: *
376: * This kernel never configures FIQ sources; the vectors used to be `b .`
377: * silent hangs.  An EL0-origin FIQ terminates the task (something user-
378: * triggerable raised it); an EL1-origin FIQ means misconfigured hardware or
379: * vector corruption — panic with the full diagnostic.
380: */
381:struct pt_regs *fiq_handler(struct pt_regs *frame) {
382:  if (fault_enter() > 1) {
383:    fault_printf("\n[FATAL] NESTED FIQ ELR=%016lx — halting\n", frame->elr);
384:    arch_cpu_halt();
385:  }
386:  fault_printf("\n[FIQ] Unexpected FIQ: ELR=%016lx SPSR=%016lx (FIQ is never enabled)\n",
387:               frame->elr, frame->spsr);
388:  struct pt_regs *next = fault_handle_user_or_panic(
389:      frame, (frame->spsr & 0xF) == 0, 0, frame->elr, "UNEXPECTED FIQ", 0);
390:  if (next)
391:    return next;
392:  backtrace_regs(frame->elr, frame->regs[29]);
393:  backtrace_scan((uint64_t)frame);
394:  panic("Unexpected FIQ at EL1 (ELR 0x%lx)", frame->elr);
395:}
396:
397:/*
398: * aarch32_handler - exception from AArch32 EL0 (Phase A step 13).
399: *
400: * The kernel only loads AArch64 ELFs, so this means a process switched to
401: * AArch32 state (or SPSR corruption).  Terminate it; if the frame claims EL1
402: * origin the vector table itself is suspect — panic.
403: */
404:struct pt_regs *aarch32_handler(struct pt_regs *frame) {
405:  if (fault_enter() > 1) {
406:    fault_printf("\n[FATAL] NESTED AArch32 exception ELR=%016lx — halting\n", frame->elr);
407:    arch_cpu_halt();
408:  }
409:  fault_printf("\n[EL0-32] AArch32 EL0 exception: ELR=%016lx SPSR=%016lx (unsupported)\n",
410:               frame->elr, frame->spsr);
411:  struct pt_regs *next = fault_handle_user_or_panic(
412:      frame, 1, 0, frame->elr, "AARCH32 EL0 EXCEPTION", 0);
413:  if (next)
414:    return next;
415:  backtrace_regs(frame->elr, frame->regs[29]);
416:  backtrace_scan((uint64_t)frame);
417:  panic("AArch32 exception with no current task (ELR 0x%lx)", frame->elr);
418:}
419:
420:/*
421: * arch_secondary_stacks[] - per-CPU kernel stack top pointers for CPUs 0..MAX_CPUS-1.
422: * Index i holds the TOP (highest address) of the 128KB kernel stack for CPU i,
423: * because AArch64 stacks grow downward.
424: * Populated by arch_smp_setup_stacks() before any secondary CPU is woken.
425: */
426:void *arch_secondary_stacks[MAX_CPUS] = {0};
427:extern char __kernel_stack[]; /* BSS symbol; MAX_CPUS * 128KB array, see start.S */
428:
429:/*
430: * arch_smp_setup_stacks - allocate and record kernel stack tops for all CPUs.
431: *
432: * Parameters:
433: *   cpu_count  Number of CPUs to prepare stacks for (clamped to MAX_CPUS).
434: *
435: * Strategy:
436: *   CPUs 0..7 (indices 0-based) use a static BSS region (__kernel_stack) that is
437: *   pre-allocated in the linker script as MAX_CPUS * 128KB.  The top of CPU i's
438: *   slice is at &__kernel_stack[(i+1) * 131072] (131072 == 128 KB).
439: *
440: *   CPUs 8 and above receive a dynamically allocated 128KB region from the PMM.
441: *   The pointer stored is the HIGH end (top) because stacks grow downward.
442: *
443: * Side effects: writes arch_secondary_stacks[]; allocates PMM pages for CPUs >= 8.
444: * Called by: arch_smp_init() in platform.c before arch_cpu_wake_secondary().
445: */
446:void arch_smp_setup_stacks(uint32_t cpu_count) {
447:    if (cpu_count > MAX_CPUS) cpu_count = MAX_CPUS;
448:
449:    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < cpu_count; i++) {
450:        if (i < 8) {
451:            /* First 8 cores use the static BSS stack area (512KB reserved).
452:             * Each 128KB slice: CPU i occupies [i*128KB .. (i+1)*128KB).
453:             * The stack pointer is set to the TOP of the slice (+1 past end). */
454:            arch_secondary_stacks[i] = (void *)&__kernel_stack[(uint64_t)(i + 1) * 131072];
455:        } else {
456:            /* Core 9+ needs dynamic allocation from PMM */
457:            void *ptr = pmm_alloc_pages(131072 / 4096);
458:            if (!ptr) {
459:                pr_err("CPU: OOM! Cannot allocate stack for core %u\n", i);
460:                break;
461:            }
462:            /* Stack grows down, return the TOP */
463:            arch_secondary_stacks[i] = (void *)((uintptr_t)ptr + 131072);
464:            pr_info("CPU: Core %u using dynamic stack at %p\n", i, arch_secondary_stacks[i]);
465:        }
466:    }
467:}
468:
469:/*
470: * arch_get_kernel_stack - return the kernel stack top for a given CPU.
471: *
472: * Parameters:
473: *   cpu_id  Zero-based CPU index.
474: * Returns: pointer to the top (highest address) of the kernel stack, or NULL
475: *          if cpu_id >= MAX_CPUS.
476: *
477: * Prefers the arch_secondary_stacks[] entry if it has been set up (non-NULL).
478: * Falls back to the BSS array formula for CPUs not yet set up (bootstrap path).
479: */
480:void *arch_get_kernel_stack(uint32_t cpu_id) {
481:    if (cpu_id >= MAX_CPUS) return NULL;
482:
483:    /* If dynamic stacks are set up, use them */
484:    if (arch_secondary_stacks[cpu_id]) return arch_secondary_stacks[cpu_id];
485:
486:    /* Bootstrap fallback: same formula as arch_smp_setup_stacks for CPUs < 8 */
487:    return (void *)&__kernel_stack[(uint64_t)(cpu_id + 1) * 131072];
488:}
489:
490:/*
491: * arch_vmm_set_secondary_pgd - publish the KERNEL PGD to secondary CPUs.
492: *
493: * Parameters:
494: *   pgd  Physical address of the kernel L0 page table (the TTBR1 root).
495: *
496: * secondary_ttbr1 (defined in start.S .data) is read by secondary_startup
497: * in start.S before the secondary CPU has its own MMU enabled and loaded
498: * into TTBR1_EL1 (the kernel half; TTBR0 gets the boot identity tables).
499: * Writing the value and then cache-cleaning it ensures the physical cache
500: * line is written back to DRAM so that the secondary CPU's pre-MMU
501: * (uncached) read sees the correct value.
502: */
503:extern uint64_t secondary_ttbr1;
504:void arch_vmm_set_secondary_pgd(uint64_t pgd) {
505:    secondary_ttbr1 = pgd;
506:    arch_cache_clean_range(&secondary_ttbr1, sizeof(secondary_ttbr1));
507:    arch_mb();
508:}
509:
510:/*
511: * arch_vmm_init_hw - install the kernel PGD in TTBR1_EL1.
512: *
513: * Parameters:
514: *   kernel_pgd  Physical address of the kernel L0 page table (higher-half
515: *               direct map + image, built by vmm_init via vmm_map_ram_wx).
516: *
517: * Higher-half model (see memlayout.h / boot/start.S): the MMU, caches,
518: * MAIR and TCR (48/48 TTBR0/TTBR1 split, 4KB granules, IPS=40-bit) are
519: * already configured by start.S before any C runs — the kernel executes
520: * at its link address through TTBR1 boot tables.  This function only
521: * swaps the boot TTBR1 tables for the real kernel PGD.
522: *
523: * TTBR0 is the USER half: it keeps the boot identity tables until the
524: * scheduler loads the first process PGD (or the idle user PGD allocated
525: * here, which contains no mappings at all).
526: */
527:static uint64_t *aarch64_idle_user_pgd;
528:
529:void arch_vmm_init_hw(uint64_t kernel_pgd) {
530:  pr_info("AArch64 VMM: Installing kernel PGD 0x%lx in TTBR1\n", kernel_pgd);
531:
532:  /* Idle/kernel-thread TTBR0: an empty L0 table, so a CPU parked on a
533:   * kernel thread maps NO user half at all (instead of a stale process
534:   * PGD — SCHED-UAF-01 — or the kernel PGD aliased into the low half). */
535:  if (!aarch64_idle_user_pgd) {
536:    aarch64_idle_user_pgd = pmm_alloc_page();
537:    if (aarch64_idle_user_pgd) {
538:      memset(aarch64_idle_user_pgd, 0, 4096);
539:      arch_cache_clean_range(aarch64_idle_user_pgd, 4096);
540:    }
541:  }
542:
543:  /* Ensure the new tables are visible to the walker, then switch TTBR1. */
544:  arch_impl_mb();
545:  arch_impl_tlb_flush_local();
546:  arch_vmm_set_kernel_pgd(kernel_pgd);
547:  arch_impl_mb();
548:  arch_impl_tlb_flush_local();
549:  arch_impl_isb();
550:
551:  pr_info("%s", "AArch64 VMM: Kernel PGD active (TTBR1).\n");
552:}
553:
554:/* idle_user_pgd_phys - PA of the empty TTBR0 table for kernel threads;
555: * 0 if not yet allocated (pre-VMM). */
556:static uint64_t idle_user_pgd_phys(void) {
557:  return aarch64_idle_user_pgd ? virt_to_phys(aarch64_idle_user_pgd) : 0;
558:}
559:
560:/*
561: * arch_vmm_map_mmio - identity-map the QEMU virt MMIO window into a PGD.
562: *
563: * Parameters:
564: *   pgd  Pointer to the L0 page table (physical address assumed == virtual for
565: *        identity-mapped kernel bootstrap context).
566: *
567: * Maps [0x08000000 .. 0x0A800000) (40 MB) with PAGE_DEVICE attributes
568: * (Device nGnRE via MAIR index 1, non-cacheable, strongly ordered).
569: * This window covers the standard QEMU virt board device layout:
570: *   0x08000000 GIC distributor / redistributor
571: *   0x09000000 PL011 UART
572: *   0x0A000000 VirtIO MMIO devices (VIRTIO_MMIO_BASE, 32 slots * 0x200)
573: *
574: * Called from kernel_main during early MMU setup for both the primary kernel
575: * PGD and each process PGD (via arch_vmm_create_process_pgd -> arch_vmm_map_mmio).
576: */
577:void arch_vmm_map_mmio(uint64_t *pgd) {
578:  /* Map MMIO (UART, GIC, VirtIO) at its direct-map VA (phys_to_virt;
579:   * identity while KERNEL_VIRT_BASE == 0).
580:   * 0x08000000 to 0x0A800000 covers typical QEMU virt devices. */
581:  /* This one range carries the GIC, the PL011 UART and all 32 VirtIO-MMIO
582:   * slots.  If it is not mapped there is no interrupt controller, no console
583:   * and no device of any kind -- and the failure would appear as a system that
584:   * boots into silence, which is indistinguishable from a hang.  The amd64
585:   * counterpart in arch/amd64/mm/mmu.c makes the same call fatal for the same
586:   * reason; keeping the two arches identical HERE is what stops one platform
587:   * from silently tolerating what the other refuses. */
588:  if (arch_vmm_map_range(virt_to_phys(pgd),
589:                         (uint64_t)phys_to_virt(0x08000000UL), 0x08000000UL,
590:                         0x02800000UL, PAGE_DEVICE) != 0)
591:    panic("arch_vmm_map_mmio: cannot map the 0x08000000..0x0A800000 MMIO "
592:          "window — GIC, UART and VirtIO are all unreachable");
593:}
594:
595:/*
596: * arch_cpu_switch_context - perform the architecture-specific address-space switch.
597: *
598: * Parameters:
599: *   next  Process descriptor for the task being scheduled in.
600: *
601: * Writes TTBR0_EL1 with the physical address of next->page_table (the process's
602: * L0 PGD).  The caller (schedule / ctx_switch) is responsible for saving and
603: * restoring the general-purpose register context (via ctx_switch in context.S).
604: *
605: * A kernel thread (e.g. idle) has no private address space (page_table == NULL):
606: * switch it onto the shared kernel_pgd instead of leaving the PREVIOUS process's
607: * PGD active in TTBR0_EL1.
608: *
609: * SCHED-UAF-01 (interactive-close residual, aarch64 HAL): the whole aarch64
610: * kernel runs from TTBR0 only (EPD1=1, no TTBR1 higher-half — see
611: * arch_vmm_init_hw).  If a CPU keeps a terminated process's PGD in TTBR0 —
612: * because it switched prev->idle and we skipped the reload — then when that
613: * process is reaped and its PGD pages are freed, the CPU is left executing on a
614: * freed PGD.  Its identity map (including printk) vanishes and the next fetch
615: * faults, mirroring the amd64 triple-fault-on-window-close failure.  Load the
616: * shared kernel_pgd for NULL page_table to keep the kernel mapping live.
617: *
618: * This is now the SINGLE source of truth for the scheduler address-space switch
619: * (the redundant hal_vmm_set_pgd block in schedule() was removed), so the TLB
620: * maintenance the scheduler block used to issue is performed here:
621: * arch_vmm_set_pgd is a bare "msr ttbr0_el1" (arch.h) with no implicit
622: * barriers, and arch_tlb_flush_all already ends with DSB ISH + ISB (arch.h),
623: * which completes the switch — no further barrier is needed after it.
624: */
625:void arch_cpu_switch_context(struct process *next) {
626:    /* TTBR0 is the USER half only (the kernel lives in TTBR1).  A process
627:     * gets its own PGD; a kernel thread (idle) gets the EMPTY idle user
628:     * PGD — never a stale process PGD (SCHED-UAF-01) and never the kernel
629:     * PGD (which would alias all RAM into the user VA range).
630:     *
631:     * ASID-TAGGED SWITCH (perf §3, DIR-06): TTBR0_EL1[63:48] carries the
632:     * address-space ASID (next->asid, assigned in process_create; 16-bit since
633:     * TCR_EL1.AS=1).  Because every TLB entry is tagged with its ASID, the
634:     * switch needs NO TLB flush: entries for other ASIDs stay valid, and this
635:     * ASID's entries were cleared at the previous owner's teardown
636:     * (arch_tlb_shootdown_all on PGD destroy) before the pool slot — hence the
637:     * ASID — was recycled.  Kernel threads use the idle user PGD with ASID 0.
638:     * An ISB after the TTBR0 write makes the new regime effective for the kernel
639:     * epilogue; the ERET back to user is itself context-synchronizing. */
640:    uint64_t pgd = next->page_table ? virt_to_phys(next->page_table)
641:                                    : idle_user_pgd_phys();
642:    if (pgd) {
643:        uint64_t asid = next->page_table ? (uint64_t)next->asid : 0;
644:        arch_vmm_set_pgd(pgd | (asid << 48));
645:        arch_isb();
646:    }
647:}

1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/aarch64/cpu/exception.S
3: * Exception vector table for AArch64
4: *
5: * Exception frame layout (816 bytes):
6: *   0-240:  x0-x30
7: *   256:    elr_el1
8: *   264:    spsr_el1
9: *   272:    sp_el0
10: *   288-800: q0-q31 (FPU/SIMD)
11: *   800:    fpsr
12: *   804:    fpcr
13: */
14:
15:.section .text
16:
17:/*
18: * arch_cpu_yield - cooperative reschedule from KERNEL (task) context.
19: *
20: * The HAL primitive that lets a kernel thread voluntarily enter the scheduler
21: * without a hardware trap: it builds a pt_regs frame on its own kernel stack
22: * exactly as irq_stub would, calls schedule() (same signature as irq_handler:
23: * pt_regs* in/out), then restores the NEXT task's frame and erets into it.
24: *
25: * When THIS thread is later rescheduled, whichever context performs the switch
26: * restores this saved frame; because we set elr = our return address, the eret
27: * lands back in the C caller (kthread_block) with the callee-saved registers
28: * intact.  Thus arch_cpu_yield() "returns" only once this thread runs again.
29: *
30: * Caller contract: IRQs must be masked on entry (kthread_block does this) so
31: * the frame build is atomic; the frame's SPSR (EL1h, DAIF clear) re-enables
32: * IRQs on resume.  Reuses the proven SLEEPING->schedule->wake_up path (the
33: * same one sys_read blocks on), so the SMP wake race is already handled.
34: */
35:.global arch_cpu_yield
36:arch_cpu_yield:
37:    msr daifset, #3          /* mask IRQ/FIQ for the frame build */
38:    sub sp, sp, #816
39:    stp x0, x1,   [sp, #0]
40:    stp x2, x3,   [sp, #16]
41:    stp x4, x5,   [sp, #32]
42:    stp x6, x7,   [sp, #48]
43:    stp x8, x9,   [sp, #64]
44:    stp x10, x11, [sp, #80]
45:    stp x12, x13, [sp, #96]
46:    stp x14, x15, [sp, #112]
47:    stp x16, x17, [sp, #128]
48:    stp x18, x19, [sp, #144]
49:    stp x20, x21, [sp, #160]
50:    stp x22, x23, [sp, #176]
51:    stp x24, x25, [sp, #192]
52:    stp x26, x27, [sp, #208]
53:    stp x28, x29, [sp, #224]
54:    str x30,      [sp, #240]
55:
56:    /* elr = return address (x30 on entry); spsr = EL1h, IRQs enabled;
57:     * sp_el0 = 0 (kernel thread has no user stack). */
58:    str x30,      [sp, #256]     /* elr = caller return address */
59:    mov x0, #0x05
60:    str x0,       [sp, #264]     /* spsr = EL1h */
61:    str xzr,      [sp, #272]     /* sp_el0 */
62:
63:    stp q0, q1,   [sp, #288]
64:    stp q2, q3,   [sp, #320]
65:    stp q4, q5,   [sp, #352]
66:    stp q6, q7,   [sp, #384]
67:    stp q8, q9,   [sp, #416]
68:    stp q10, q11, [sp, #448]
69:    stp q12, q13, [sp, #480]
70:    stp q14, q15, [sp, #512]
71:    stp q16, q17, [sp, #544]
72:    stp q18, q19, [sp, #576]
73:    stp q20, q21, [sp, #608]
74:    stp q22, q23, [sp, #640]
75:    stp q24, q25, [sp, #672]
76:    stp q26, q27, [sp, #704]
77:    stp q28, q29, [sp, #736]
78:    stp q30, q31, [sp, #768]
79:    mrs x0, fpsr
80:    mrs x1, fpcr
81:    str w0,       [sp, #800]
82:    str w1,       [sp, #804]
83:
84:    /* schedule(frame) -> next task's frame in x0.  Restore it via the ONE
85:     * shared epilogue (below), the exact path the trap stubs use — no
86:     * hand-rolled second restore (DIR-06 / roadmap Phase 1.A). */
87:    mov x0, sp
88:    bl schedule
89:    b restore_context
90:
91:/*
92: * restore_context - the single pt_regs restore + exception-return epilogue.
93: *
94: * Entered with x0 = pointer to the pt_regs frame to load (the return value of
95: * schedule() or an *_handler()).  Switches SP onto that frame, masks IRQ/FIQ,
96: * restores ELR/SPSR/SP_EL0, the full FPU/SIMD file and x0-x30, then ERETs.
97: *
98: * This is the ONLY copy of the restore sequence in the kernel: the sync-
99: * exception stub (vector_stub), the IRQ stub (irq_stub) and the cooperative
100: * yield (arch_cpu_yield) all reach it by branch, so the 816-byte frame layout
101: * lives in exactly one place.  The ERET is context-synchronizing, so a TTBR0
102: * switch performed by schedule()/arch_cpu_switch_context before we get here is
103: * in effect for the returned context.
104: */
105:.global restore_context

108:    msr daifset, #3
109:    ldr x0, [sp, #256]
110:    ldr x1, [sp, #264]
111:    ldr x2, [sp, #272]
112:    msr elr_el1, x0
113:    msr spsr_el1, x1
114:    msr sp_el0, x2
115:    ldp q0, q1,   [sp, #288]
116:    ldp q2, q3,   [sp, #320]
117:    ldp q4, q5,   [sp, #352]
118:    ldp q6, q7,   [sp, #384]
119:    ldp q8, q9,   [sp, #416]
120:    ldp q10, q11, [sp, #448]
121:    ldp q12, q13, [sp, #480]
122:    ldp q14, q15, [sp, #512]
123:    ldp q16, q17, [sp, #544]
124:    ldp q18, q19, [sp, #576]
125:    ldp q20, q21, [sp, #608]
126:    ldp q22, q23, [sp, #640]
127:    ldp q24, q25, [sp, #672]
128:    ldp q26, q27, [sp, #704]
129:    ldp q28, q29, [sp, #736]
130:    ldp q30, q31, [sp, #768]
131:    ldr w0, [sp, #800]
132:    ldr w1, [sp, #804]
133:    msr fpsr, x0
134:    msr fpcr, x1
135:    ldp x0, x1,   [sp, #0]
136:    ldp x2, x3,   [sp, #16]
137:    ldp x4, x5,   [sp, #32]
138:    ldp x6, x7,   [sp, #48]

361:handle_el1_sp0_sync:
362:    stp x0, x1, [sp, #-16]!
363:    mov x0, #0x09000000
364:    mov w1, #75
365:    /* str w1, [x0] */

375:/*
376: * EL1-from-EL1 synchronous abort (Phase A step 4): run the handler on the
377: * per-CPU fault stack so a kernel-stack overflow or wild SP cannot recurse.
378: *
379: * The original SP is parked in the 16-byte slot directly above the 816-byte
380: * frame (i.e. at frame+816): sync_handler reads it for diagnostics and, on
381: * the only resuming path (probe fixup), copies the frame back below the
382: * original SP so the eret epilogue (mov sp, x0 ... add sp, #816) leaves SP
383: * exactly where the faulting code expects it.
384: *
385: * The 16-byte scratch push on the old SP is the unavoidable minimum — if even
386: * that aborts, the CPU was unrecoverable before this code ran.  A nested
387: * abort while already on the fault stack re-parks at the top and clobbers the
388: * outer frame; that is caught immediately by the fault_enter() depth guard.
389: */
390:handle_el1_spx_sync:
391:    stp x0, x1, [sp, #-16]!
392:    mrs x0, mpidr_el1
393:    and x0, x0, #0xFF
394:    adrp x1, arch_fault_stack_top
395:    add  x1, x1, :lo12:arch_fault_stack_top
396:    ldr  x1, [x1, x0, lsl #3]
397:    cbz  x1, 1f                  /* fault stack not published yet: stay */
398:    mov  x0, sp                  /* x0 = old SP (after the 16-byte push)  */
399:    str  x0, [x1, #-16]!         /* park it; x1 -> top-16                 */
400:    mov  sp, x1                  /* switch to the fault stack             */
401:    ldp  x0, x1, [x0]            /* restore scratch from the old stack    */
402:    b    2f
403:1:
404:    ldp x0, x1, [sp], #16
405:2:
406:    vector_stub sync
407:
408:handle_el1_spx_irq:
409:    stp x0, x1, [sp, #-16]!
410:    mov x0, #0x09000000
411:    mov w1, #105
412:    /* str w1, [x0] */
413:    ldp x0, x1, [sp], #16
414:    irq_stub
415:
416:/* EL1-from-EL1 SError: same fault-stack switch as el1_spx_sync.  The SError
417: * handler never resumes (panic), so no copy-back path is needed here. */
418:handle_el1_spx_serror:
419:    stp x0, x1, [sp, #-16]!
420:    mrs x0, mpidr_el1
421:    and x0, x0, #0xFF
422:    adrp x1, arch_fault_stack_top
423:    add  x1, x1, :lo12:arch_fault_stack_top
424:    ldr  x1, [x1, x0, lsl #3]
425:    cbz  x1, 1f
426:    mov  x0, sp
427:    str  x0, [x1, #-16]!
428:    mov  sp, x1
429:    ldp  x0, x1, [x0]
430:    b    2f
431:1:
432:    ldp x0, x1, [sp], #16
433:2:
434:    vector_stub serror

478: * Enter User Mode
479: * void enter_user_mode(uint64_t entry, uint64_t sp);

481:.global arch_enter_user_mode
482:arch_enter_user_mode:
483:    /* x0 = entry point (ELR_EL1) */
484:    /* x1 = stack pointer (SP_EL0) */
485:    /* x2 = kernel stack pointer (SP_EL1) */

35:/* Secure memory access helpers with Page Table Switching */
36:int arch_copy_from_user(void *dest, const void *src, size_t n) {
37:  uint64_t src_addr = (uint64_t)src;
38:  if (src_addr + n < src_addr)
39:    return -1; /* Wrap around */
40:
41:  /* UACC-05 (HAL-0): validate the LAST BYTE TOUCHED, not one-past-the-end.
42:   * src+n is the first address the copy does NOT read, so a region ending
43:   * exactly at the user boundary was refused although it is entirely legal,
44:   * and n == 0 checked a byte that is never accessed. */
45:  if (n == 0)
46:    return 0;
47:  if (!vmm_is_user_addr(src_addr) || !vmm_is_user_addr(src_addr + n - 1))
48:    return -1;
49:
50:  if (!current_process || !current_process->page_table)
51:    return -1;
52:
53:  /* Check if range is valid and mapped in user page table */
54:  if (vmm_check_range(current_process->page_table, src_addr, n, PTE_VALID) != 0)
55:    return -1;
56:
57:  /* Save and disable interrupts to prevent scheduler preemption */
58:  uint64_t flagsptr = local_irq_save();
59:
60:  /* Lock the address space for this process */
61:  spin_lock(&current_process->mm_lock);
62:
63:  /* Save kernel TTBR0 (usually 0 or points to identity map initially) */
64:  uint64_t old_pgd = arch_vmm_get_pgd();
65:
66:  /* Switch to user's page table (must use physical address) */
67:  arch_vmm_set_pgd(virt_to_phys(current_process->page_table));
68:  arch_tlb_flush_all();
69:  arch_isb();
70:
71:  /* Perform copy while user space is mapped at TTBR0.  uaccess_active flags
72:   * the dereference window for the fault classifier (kernel/core/fault.c):
73:   * an abort here is recoverable (terminate the process via
74:   * arch_uaccess_fault_fixup), anywhere else it is a kernel bug. */
75:  get_cpu_info()->uaccess_active = 1;
76:  memcpy(dest, src, n);
77:  get_cpu_info()->uaccess_active = 0;
78:
79:  /* Restore kernel/previous TTBR0 */
80:  arch_vmm_set_pgd(old_pgd);
81:  arch_tlb_flush_all();
82:  arch_isb();
83:
84:  spin_unlock(&current_process->mm_lock);
85:  local_irq_restore(flagsptr);
86:
87:  return 0;
88:}
89:
90:int arch_copy_to_user(void *dest, const void *src, size_t n) {
91:  uint64_t dest_addr = (uint64_t)dest;
92:  if (dest_addr + n < dest_addr)
93:    return -1; /* Wrap around */
94:
95:  /* UACC-05 (HAL-0): last byte touched, not one-past-the-end. */
96:  if (n == 0)
97:    return 0;
98:  if (!vmm_is_user_addr(dest_addr) || !vmm_is_user_addr(dest_addr + n - 1))
99:    return -1;
100:
101:  /* UACC-AARCH64-01: guard current_process before dereferencing its
102:   * page_table, matching arch_copy_from_user above. */
103:  if (!current_process || !current_process->page_table)
104:    return -1;
105:
106:  if (vmm_check_range(current_process->page_table, dest_addr, n, PTE_VALID) != 0)
107:    return -1;
108:
109:  uint64_t flagsptr = local_irq_save();
110:  spin_lock(&current_process->mm_lock);
111:
112:  uint64_t old_pgd = arch_vmm_get_pgd();
113:  arch_vmm_set_pgd(virt_to_phys(current_process->page_table));
114:  arch_tlb_flush_all();
115:  arch_isb();
116:
117:  /* uaccess window — see arch_copy_from_user */
118:  get_cpu_info()->uaccess_active = 1;
119:  memcpy(dest, src, n);
120:  get_cpu_info()->uaccess_active = 0;
121:
122:  arch_vmm_set_pgd(old_pgd);
123:  arch_tlb_flush_all();
124:  arch_isb();
125:
126:  spin_unlock(&current_process->mm_lock);
127:  local_irq_restore(flagsptr);
128:
129:  return 0;
130:}
131:
132:/*
133: * arch_uaccess_fault_fixup - release the uaccess critical section after an
134: * abort inside one of the copy windows above (kernel/core/fault.c).
135: *
136: * The copies hold: IRQs masked (local_irq_save), current_process->mm_lock,
137: * TTBR0 = the user PGD, and uaccess_active = 1.  The faulting context is
138: * being discarded (process terminated), so: clear the flag, drop mm_lock,
139: * re-enable IRQs (SYS-AARCH64-02 made explicit in ONE place).  TTBR0 is NOT
140: * restored here — the scheduler loads the next task's PGD unconditionally on
141: * the switch (SCHED-UAF-01 fix).
142: */
143:void arch_uaccess_fault_fixup(void) {
144:  struct cpu_info *ci = arch_cpu_info_fault_safe();
145:  if (ci) {
146:    ci->uaccess_active = 0;
147:    if (ci->current_task)
148:      spin_unlock(&ci->current_task->mm_lock);
149:  }
150:  local_irq_enable();
151:}
152:
153:/* Copy null-terminated string from user space safely with Page Table Switching
154: */
155:/*
156: * arch_copy_string_from_user_n - HAL uaccess provider (kernel/hal_uaccess.h).
157: *
158: * Reports what the copy loop already knows and used to discard: how much was
159: * copied, and whether the source was LONGER than the destination.  Without
160: * that, a truncated string is indistinguishable from a complete one and every
161: * caller proceeds with a value the process never passed.
162: */
163:int arch_copy_string_from_user_n(char *dest, const char *src, size_t max_len,
164:                                 size_t *out_len, int *out_truncated) {
165:  if (out_len)
166:    *out_len = 0;
167:  if (out_truncated)
168:    *out_truncated = 0;
169:  if (!vmm_is_user_addr((uint64_t)src))
170:    return -1;
171:
172:  if (!current_process || !current_process->page_table)
173:    return -1;
174:  /* max_len 0 would underflow `max_len - 1` below and run away; a zero-sized
175:   * destination cannot hold even the terminator, so refuse it outright. */
176:  if (max_len == 0)
177:    return -1;
178:
179:  uint64_t flagsptr = local_irq_save();
180:  spin_lock(&current_process->mm_lock);
181:
182:  uint64_t old_pgd = arch_vmm_get_pgd();
183:  arch_vmm_set_pgd(virt_to_phys(current_process->page_table));
184:  arch_tlb_flush_all();
185:  arch_isb();
186:
187:  /* uaccess window — see arch_copy_from_user */
188:  get_cpu_info()->uaccess_active = 1;
189:
190:  int ret = 0;
191:  size_t i = 0;
192:
193:  for (i = 0; i < max_len - 1; i++) {
194:    /* One page-table walk per page touched, never two.
195:     *
196:     * UACC-04 (FIXED 2026-07-23, HAL-0): the `i == 0` term is the fix — the
197:     * alignment test alone validates each NEW page at its first byte, but the
198:     * page containing src is only aligned when src is, so for any unaligned src
199:     * the starting page was never checked.  Documented on the amd64 side as
200:     * UACC-AMD64-04; equally present here and recorded nowhere.  Folded into
201:     * the loop rather than added as a separate pre-walk: a standalone pre-check
202:     * repeats the i == 0 walk whenever src IS aligned, on the hottest string
203:     * path in the kernel. */
204:    if (i == 0 || ((uint64_t)&src[i] & 0xFFF) == 0) {
205:       if (vmm_check_range(current_process->page_table, (uint64_t)&src[i], 1, PTE_VALID) != 0) {
206:         /* HAL-0: a failed validation is a FAILURE.  This used to `goto out`
207:          * with ret still 0, so a string that ran into an unmapped page was
208:          * reported as a successful (silently truncated) copy — the caller then
209:          * acted on a partial path/key.  amd64 already returned -1 here. */
210:         ret = -1;
211:         goto out;
212:       }
213:    }
214:
215:    dest[i] = src[i];
216:    if (src[i] == '\0')
217:      goto out;
218:  }
219:  /* Ran out of destination before the terminator: the source is longer. */
220:  if (out_truncated)
221:    *out_truncated = 1;
222:
223:out:
224:  /* HAL-0: terminate on EVERY path.  The early exits used to leave dest
225:   * unterminated (only the fall-through wrote the NUL), handing the caller a
226:   * string with no end — the classic overrun-in-the-consumer. */
227:  dest[max_len - 1] = '\0';
228:  if (out_len)
229:    *out_len = i;
230:  get_cpu_info()->uaccess_active = 0;
231:  arch_vmm_set_pgd(old_pgd);
232:  arch_tlb_flush_all();
233:  arch_isb();
234:  spin_unlock(&current_process->mm_lock);
235:  local_irq_restore(flagsptr);
236:  return ret;
237:}
238:
239:struct pt_regs *syscall_handler(struct pt_regs *frame) {
240:  /* Check Exception Syndrome to distinguish SVC from Aborts */
241:  uint64_t esr = arch_get_fault_status();
242:  uint64_t ec = (esr >> 26) & 0x3F;
243:
244:  /* EC 0x15 = SVC from AArch64 */
245:  if (ec != 0x15) {
246:    uint64_t far = arch_get_fault_address();
247:    uint64_t iss = esr & 0x1FFFFFF;
248:
249:    /* Recursion guard (Phase A step 7): a fault while handling this EL0
250:     * fault arrives as an EL1 sync abort, but guard this path too so e.g. a
251:     * fault inside process_terminate stops cleanly. */
252:    if (fault_enter() > 1) {
253:      fault_printf("\n[FATAL] NESTED EXCEPTION in EL0-fault path EC=0x%lx ELR=%016lx — halting\n",
254:                   ec, frame->elr);
255:      arch_cpu_halt();
256:    }
257:
258:    /* Decode the abort class → the human-readable desc passed to the common
259:     * fault handler (which logs the ONE unified "[FAULT] <class>: PID … pc …
260:     * addr … cause=0x<ESR>" line — the user-fault debug, now IDENTICAL across
261:     * arches; the ESR/EC/ISS detail rides in cause=0x<ESR>, FAR in addr, ELR in
262:     * pc).  The raw register dump is reserved for the kernel/corruption path
263:     * below, mirroring amd64 (DIR-06 HAL conformance: one reporting path). */
264:    const char *ec_name = "Unknown";
265:    switch (ec) {
266:    case 0x00:
267:      ec_name = "Unknown/Uncategorized";
268:      break;
269:    case 0x01:
270:      ec_name = "WFI/WFE";
271:      break;
272:    case 0x20:
273:      ec_name = "Instruction Abort (Lower EL)";
274:      break;
275:    case 0x21:
276:      ec_name = "Instruction Abort (Same EL)";
277:      break;
278:    case 0x24:
279:      ec_name = "Data Abort (Lower EL)";
280:      break;
281:    case 0x25:
282:      ec_name = "Data Abort (Same EL)";
283:      break;
284:    default:
285:      break;
286:    }
287:
288:    /* This vector (el0_64_sync) only fires for EL0-origin exceptions: always
289:     * user-attributable.  A NULL return = no current task on this vector =
290:     * scheduler-state corruption: dump the raw syndrome and panic. */
291:    {
292:      struct pt_regs *next =
293:          fault_handle_user_or_panic(frame, 1, far, frame->elr, ec_name, esr);
294:      if (next)
295:        return next;
296:      pr_err(
297:          "PID %d EXCEPTION: EC=0x%lx ESR=0x%lx FAR=0x%lx ELR=0x%lx ISS=0x%lx\n",
298:          current_process ? (int)current_process->pid : -1, ec, esr, far,
299:          frame->elr, iss);
300:      panic("Fatal EL0 exception with no current task (EC=0x%lx)", ec);
301:    }
302:  }
303:
304:  /* Dispatch via agnostic core */
305:  extern struct pt_regs *kernel_syscall_dispatcher(struct pt_regs *regs);
306:  return kernel_syscall_dispatcher(frame);
307:}
308:
309:/* Legacy tolerant spelling — truncation is success.  See kernel/hal_uaccess.h
310: * for why both exist and which call sites must use the strict form instead. */
311:int arch_copy_string_from_user(char *dest, const char *src, size_t max_len) {
312:  return arch_copy_string_from_user_n(dest, src, max_len, (size_t *)0,
313:                                      (int *)0);
314:}

56: * watchdog.  Used by the HAL arch_reboot() wrapper. */

120: * *IS (inner-shareable) TLBI variants, which the hardware DVM broadcasts to
121: * every PE in the inner-shareable domain; the DSB ISH then waits for
122: * completion on ALL PEs, not just the local one.  The cross-CPU shootdown
123: * contract is therefore already satisfied without IPIs — these are aliases,

134:  uint64_t s = (uint64_t)start;
135:  uint64_t e = s + size;
136:  s &= ~63UL;
137:  for (; s < e; s += 64) {
138:    __asm__ __volatile__("dc cvac, %0" ::"r"(s) : "memory");
139:  }

143:  uint64_t s = (uint64_t)start;
144:  uint64_t e = s + size;
145:  s &= ~63UL;
146:  for (; s < e; s += 64) {
147:    __asm__ __volatile__("dc cvau, %0\n"
148:                         "ic ivau, %0" ::"r"(s)
149:                         : "memory");
150:  }
151:  __asm__ __volatile__("dsb ish\n isb" ::: "memory");
152:}

211:static inline uint64_t arch_impl_timer_get_count(void) {
212:  uint64_t val;
213:  __asm__ __volatile__("mrs %0, cntvct_el0" : "=r"(val));
214:  return val;
215:}
216:
217:static inline void arch_impl_timer_set_compare(uint64_t val) {
218:  __asm__ __volatile__("msr cntv_cval_el0, %0" ::"r"(val));
219:}
220:
221:static inline void arch_impl_timer_control(uint32_t val) {
222:  __asm__ __volatile__("msr cntv_ctl_el0, %0" ::"r"((uint64_t)val));
223:}
224:
225:/* --- Entropy (ISA primitive) --- */
226:/* arch_impl_hw_random: one attempt at the architected RNG (FEAT_RNG / RNDR).
227: * Returns 1 and writes *out on success; 0 if FEAT_RNG is absent (e.g. the
228: * QEMU virt cortex-a57 default, which is ARMv8.0) or the read transiently
229: * failed.  Pure ISA wrapper: the retry/mix policy lives in the generic
230: * entropy layer (kernel/lib/entropy.c). */
231:static inline int arch_impl_hw_random(uint64_t *out) {
232:  uint64_t isar0;
233:  __asm__ __volatile__("mrs %0, id_aa64isar0_el1" : "=r"(isar0));
234:  if (((isar0 >> 60) & 0xf) == 0)
235:    return 0; /* no FEAT_RNG */
236:  uint64_t r, nzcv;
237:  __asm__ __volatile__("mrs %0, s3_3_c2_c4_0\n\t" /* RNDR */
238:                       "mrs %1, nzcv\n\t"
239:                       : "=r"(r), "=r"(nzcv));
240:  if (nzcv & (1ULL << 30))
241:    return 0; /* PSTATE.Z set => transient failure */
242:  *out = r;
243:  return 1;
244:}
245:
246:/* --- Spinlocks --- */
247:static inline void arch_impl_spin_lock(volatile uint32_t *lock) {
248:  while (__sync_lock_test_and_set(lock, 1)) {
249:    while (*lock)
250:      __asm__ __volatile__("wfe");
251:  }
252:}
253:
254:static inline void arch_impl_spin_unlock(volatile uint32_t *lock) {
255:  __sync_lock_release(lock);
256:}
257:
258:static inline int arch_impl_spin_trylock(volatile uint32_t *lock) {
259:  return __sync_lock_test_and_set(lock, 1) == 0;
260:}
261:
262:/* --- Constants --- */
263:#define HAL_RAM_START 0x40000000UL
264:#define HAL_RAM_SIZE 0x80000000UL /* 2GB */
265:#define HAL_ALIAS_OFFSET 0x40000000UL
266:
267:#endif /* _ARCH_AARCH64_H */
268:
