@@@ kernel/arch/aarch64/include/arch/pt_regs.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/aarch64/include/arch/pt_regs.h
3: * AArch64 register frame layout (816 bytes)
4: *
5: * Must match the stack layout in exception.S exactly.
6: */
7:#ifndef _ARCH_AARCH64_PT_REGS_H
8:#define _ARCH_AARCH64_PT_REGS_H
9:
10:#include <kernel/nx_contract.h>
11:#include <stdint.h>
12:
13:/* Full Register State (matching stack layout in exception.S) */
14:struct pt_regs {
15:  uint64_t regs[31]; /* x0-x30 */
16:  uint64_t unused;   /* Padding to align to 16 bytes (32 * 8 = 256) */
17:  uint64_t elr;      /* 256 */
18:  uint64_t spsr;     /* 264 */
19:  uint64_t sp_el0;   /* 272 */
20:  uint64_t padding;  /* 280 */
21:
22:  /* FPU/SIMD State (NEON q0-q31 = 32 * 16 bytes = 512 bytes) */
23:  __uint128_t qregs[32]; /* 288 - 800 */
24:  uint32_t fpsr;         /* 800 */
25:  uint32_t fpcr;         /* 804 */
26:  uint64_t fpu_padding;  /* 808-816 */
27:};
28:
29:/*
30: * Same contract as amd64: this layout is written BY HAND in the exception
31: * vectors, and the offsets in the comments above were maintained by eye.  The
32: * FPU block makes it worse than amd64's — inserting anything before qregs[]
33: * shifts 512 bytes of NEON state that the save/restore stubs address by
34: * constant, and the failure would appear as corrupted floating-point results
35: * in userland, not as a fault at the edit.  Pinned so a reorder breaks the
36: * build here instead.
37: */
38:NX_ASSERT_OFFSET(struct pt_regs, elr, 256);
39:NX_ASSERT_OFFSET(struct pt_regs, spsr, 264);
40:NX_ASSERT_OFFSET(struct pt_regs, sp_el0, 272);
41:NX_ASSERT_OFFSET(struct pt_regs, qregs, 288);
42:NX_ASSERT_OFFSET(struct pt_regs, fpsr, 800);
43:NX_ASSERT_OFFSET(struct pt_regs, fpcr, 804);
44:
45:/* ─── Architecture-Agnostic Accessors ─── */
46:
47:/* Syscall number: x8 on AArch64 */
48:static inline uint64_t pt_regs_syscall_num(struct pt_regs *r) {
49:  return r->regs[8];
50:}
51:
52:/* Syscall arguments: x0-x5 on AArch64 */
53:static inline uint64_t pt_regs_arg(struct pt_regs *r, int n) {
54:  return r->regs[n]; /* x0..x5 maps directly */
55:}
56:
57:/* Set syscall return value: x0 on AArch64 */
58:static inline void pt_regs_set_return(struct pt_regs *r, uint64_t v) {
59:  r->regs[0] = v;
60:}
61:
62:/* Get program counter (ELR_EL1) */
63:static inline uint64_t pt_regs_pc(struct pt_regs *r) { return r->elr; }
64:
65:/* Set program counter */
66:static inline void pt_regs_set_pc(struct pt_regs *r, uint64_t v) {
67:  r->elr = v;
68:}
69:
70:/* Get user stack pointer (SP_EL0) */
71:static inline uint64_t pt_regs_user_sp(struct pt_regs *r) {
72:  return r->sp_el0;
73:}
74:
75:/* Set user stack pointer */
76:static inline void pt_regs_set_user_sp(struct pt_regs *r, uint64_t v) {
77:  r->sp_el0 = v;
78:}
79:
80:/* Retry syscall: rewind PC by 4 bytes (ARM instruction size) */
81:static inline void pt_regs_retry_syscall(struct pt_regs *r) { r->elr -= 4; }
82:
83:/* Initialize context for a user-mode process (ELF entry) */
84:static inline void pt_regs_init_user_task(struct pt_regs *r, uint64_t entry,
85:                                           uint64_t usp) {
86:  r->elr    = entry;
87:  r->sp_el0 = usp;
88:  r->spsr   = 0; /* EL0t, IRQs unmasked */
89:}
90:
91:/* Pass main()'s argc/argv to a fresh user task (AArch64 AAPCS: x0, x1).
92: * Call after pt_regs_init_user_task(); argv is a user virtual address. */
93:static inline void pt_regs_set_user_args(struct pt_regs *r, uint64_t argc,
94:                                         uint64_t argv) {
95:  r->regs[0] = argc;
96:  r->regs[1] = argv;
97:}
98:
99:/* Initialize context for a kernel-mode thread (ksp unused on AArch64) */
100:static inline void pt_regs_init_kernel_task(struct pt_regs *r, uint64_t entry,
101:                                             uint64_t ksp) {
102:  (void)ksp;
103:  r->elr  = entry;
104:  r->spsr = 0x05; /* EL1h, IRQs unmasked */
105:  r->sp_el0 = 0;
106:}
107:
108:#endif /* _ARCH_AARCH64_PT_REGS_H */
109:

@@@ kernel/arch/aarch64/kinit/start.S @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/aarch64/boot/start.S
3: * Kernel entry point — higher-half bring-up.
4: *
5: * The kernel is LINKED at 0xFFFF000040080000 (KERNEL_VIRT_BASE + load PA,
6: * see memlayout.h / kernel.ld) but LOADED and ENTERED at physical
7: * 0x40080000 with the MMU off.  Everything in this file up to the "br"
8: * into the higher half is position-independent (adrp/PC-relative), so it
9: * runs correctly at the load address: adrp resolves link-relative, which
10: * equals the PHYSICAL address while PC is low and the VIRTUAL address
11: * once PC is high.
12: *
13: * Boot page tables (built here, in BSS, before the MMU is enabled):
14: *   boot_pt_l1      one shared L1 table:
15: *                     [0]      1GB Device block  (PA 0: UART/GIC/VirtIO)
16: *                     [1..127] 1GB Normal blocks (PA 1GB..128GB: covers all
17: *                              possible RAM; the platform RAM probe relies
18: *                              on mapped-but-unbacked PAs still faulting)
19: *   boot_pgd_ttbr0  L0 with [0] -> boot_pt_l1   (identity, for this file)
20: *   boot_pgd_ttbr1  L0 with [0] -> boot_pt_l1   (higher half: VA-base+PA)
21: *
22: * After SCTLR.M is set the code jumps (absolute literal) to the link
23: * address, moves SP to the linked stack and calls kernel_main.  C code
24: * never runs identity-mapped.  vmm_init/vmm_dynamic_remap later replace
25: * TTBR1 with the real kernel PGD (W^X, precise regions); TTBR0 keeps the
26: * boot identity tables until the first process switch loads a user PGD.
27: */
28:
29:#include <kernel/cpu.h>
30:
31:/* Keep in sync with KERNEL_VIRT_BASE in kernel/include/kernel/memlayout.h */
32:#define KVB 0xFFFF000000000000
33:
34:/* TCR_EL1: T0SZ=16, T1SZ=16 (48-bit both halves), 4KB granules
35: * (TG0=0, TG1=2), inner WB/WA + inner-shareable walks on both halves,
36: * IPS=2 (40-bit PA — RAM tops out below 1TB on QEMU virt).
37: * AS=1 (bit 36): 16-bit ASID — TTBR0_EL1[63:48] tags each address space for
38: *   flush-free context switches (perf §3).  A1=0 (TTBR0 defines the ASID). */
39:#define BOOT_TCR 0x12B5103510
40:
41:/* Block descriptors: VALID | AF | attrs (level-1 1GB blocks, bit1 = 0). */
42:#define BLK_DEVICE 0x405       /* AttrIndx=1 (Device nGnRE), AF */
43:#define BLK_NORMAL 0x701       /* AttrIndx=0 (Normal WB), SH=inner, AF */
44:
45:.section .text.boot
46:.global _start
47:
48:/*
49: * Kernel entry point
50: * Called from bootloader/QEMU with:
51: *   x0 = DTB pointer (PHYSICAL)
52: *   x1 = 0 (reserved)
53: *
54: * QEMU virt machine starts kernel at EL1 directly
55: */
56:_start:
57:    /* Save boot info (DTB physical address) immediately */
58:    mov x20, x0
59:    adrp x1, boot_info
60:    str x0, [x1, :lo12:boot_info]
61:
62:    /* Disable interrupts */
63:    msr daifset, #0xf
64:
65:    /* Get CPU ID */
66:    mrs x1, mpidr_el1
67:    and x1, x1, #0xff
68:
69:    /* CPU 0 does primary init */
70:    cbz x1, primary_init
71:
72:    /* Secondary CPUs wait (PSCI handles this, but if we get here, hang) */
73:    b halt
74:
75:/*
76: * Primary CPU initialization
77: */
78:primary_init:
79:    adrp x0, __kernel_stack
80:    add x0, x0, :lo12:__kernel_stack
81:    add x0, x0, #131072    /* Use first 128KB slice for CPU 0 */
82:    mov sp, x0
83:
84:    /* Switch to SP_EL1 */
85:    msr spsel, #1
86:    /* Re-set SP for EL1 just in case */
87:    mov sp, x0
88:
89:    /* Check current exception level */
90:    mrs x0, CurrentEL
91:    lsr x0, x0, #2      /* Extract EL bits */
92:
93:    cmp x0, #3
94:    beq el3_setup
95:    cmp x0, #2
96:    beq el2_setup
97:    /* Already at EL1, continue */
98:    b el1_setup
99:
100:/*
101: * EL3 setup (if started by firmware at EL3)
102: */
103:el3_setup:
104:    /* Configure EL3 to drop to EL1 */
105:    mov x0, #0x531          /* SCR_EL3: RW=1, NS=1 (EL1 AArch64, non-secure) */
106:    msr scr_el3, x0
107:
108:    mov x0, #0x3c5          /* SPSR: EL1h, all interrupts masked */
109:    msr spsr_el3, x0
110:
111:    adrp x0, el1_setup
112:    add x0, x0, :lo12:el1_setup
113:    msr elr_el3, x0
114:    eret
115:
116:/*
117: * EL2 setup (if started by hypervisor at EL2)
118: */
119:el2_setup:
120:    /* Enable EL1 access to timers */
121:    mrs x0, cnthctl_el2
122:    orr x0, x0, #3          /* EL1PCEN, EL1PCTEN */
123:    msr cnthctl_el2, x0
124:    msr cntvoff_el2, xzr    /* Virtual timer offset = 0 */
125:
126:    /* Configure HCR_EL2 */
127:    mov x0, #(1 << 31)      /* RW bit: EL1 uses AArch64 */
128:    msr hcr_el2, x0
129:
130:    /* SPSR_EL2: Return to EL1h with interrupts masked */
131:    mov x0, #0x3c5
132:    msr spsr_el2, x0
133:
134:    adrp x0, el1_setup
135:    add x0, x0, :lo12:el1_setup
136:    msr elr_el2, x0
137:    eret
138:
139:/*
140: * EL1 setup: FPU, BSS, boot page tables, MMU on, jump to the higher half.
141: */
142:el1_setup:
143:    /* Temporary physical SP (nothing is pushed before the MMU jump) */
144:    adrp x0, __kernel_stack_top
145:    add x0, x0, :lo12:__kernel_stack_top
146:    mov sp, x0
147:
148:    /* Enable FPU/SIMD (NEON) before anything else */
149:    /* Set CPACR_EL1.FPEN = 0b11 to enable FP/SIMD at EL0 and EL1 */
150:    mov x0, #(3 << 20)
151:    msr cpacr_el1, x0
152:    isb
153:
154:    /* Clear BSS (adrp yields physical addresses while PC is low) */
155:    adrp x0, __bss_start
156:    add x0, x0, :lo12:__bss_start
157:    adrp x1, __bss_end
158:    add x1, x1, :lo12:__bss_end
159:clear_bss:
160:    cmp x0, x1
161:    bge bss_done
162:    str xzr, [x0], #8
163:    b clear_bss
164:bss_done:
165:
166:    /*
167:     * Build the boot page tables (they live in BSS, just cleared).
168:     * x1 = PA(boot_pt_l1)
169:     */
170:    adrp x1, boot_pt_l1
171:    add x1, x1, :lo12:boot_pt_l1
172:
173:    /* L1[0]: 1GB Device block at PA 0 (UART/GIC/VirtIO window) */
174:    mov x2, #BLK_DEVICE
175:    str x2, [x1]
176:
177:    /* L1[1..127]: 1GB Normal blocks covering PA 1GB..128GB */
178:    mov x3, #1
179:    ldr x4, =BLK_NORMAL
180:1:  lsl x2, x3, #30
181:    orr x2, x2, x4
182:    str x2, [x1, x3, lsl #3]
183:    add x3, x3, #1
184:    cmp x3, #128
185:    b.lt 1b
186:
187:    /* boot_pgd_ttbr0[0] = boot_pgd_ttbr1[0] = L1 | TABLE | VALID */
188:    orr x2, x1, #0x3
189:    adrp x0, boot_pgd_ttbr0
190:    add x0, x0, :lo12:boot_pgd_ttbr0
191:    str x2, [x0]
192:    adrp x5, boot_pgd_ttbr1
193:    add x5, x5, :lo12:boot_pgd_ttbr1
194:    str x2, [x5]
195:
196:    /* MAIR: Attr0 = Normal WB/WA (0xFF), Attr1 = Device nGnRE (0x04) */
197:    mov x2, #0xff
198:    orr x2, x2, #(0x04 << 8)
199:    msr mair_el1, x2
200:
201:    /* TCR: 48-bit VA on both halves, 4KB granules, IPS=40-bit */
202:    ldr x2, =BOOT_TCR
203:    msr tcr_el1, x2
204:
205:    /* TTBR0 = identity L0, TTBR1 = higher-half L0 (same L1 underneath) */
206:    msr ttbr0_el1, x0
207:    msr ttbr1_el1, x5
208:
209:    tlbi vmalle1
210:    dsb ish
211:    isb
212:
213:    /* Enable MMU + D/I caches.  RES1 bits per ARM DDI 0487 D5.2.88;
214:     * A/SA (alignment checks) stay off, matching the previous C bring-up. */
215:    mrs x2, sctlr_el1
216:    orr x2, x2, #(1 << 29)
217:    orr x2, x2, #(1 << 28)
218:    orr x2, x2, #(1 << 23)
219:    orr x2, x2, #(1 << 22)
220:    orr x2, x2, #(1 << 20)
221:    orr x2, x2, #(1 << 11)
222:    orr x2, x2, #(1 << 0)   /* M */
223:    orr x2, x2, #(1 << 2)   /* C */
224:    orr x2, x2, #(1 << 12)  /* I */
225:    bic x2, x2, #(1 << 1)   /* A */
226:    bic x2, x2, #(1 << 3)   /* SA */
227:    dsb ish
228:    msr sctlr_el1, x2
229:    isb
230:
231:    /* Jump to the link address (literal = virtual/high) */
232:    ldr x9, =boot_high_entry
233:    br x9
234:
235:boot_high_entry:
236:    /* PC is now in the higher half; adrp yields virtual addresses */
237:    adrp x0, __kernel_stack_top
238:    add x0, x0, :lo12:__kernel_stack_top
239:    mov sp, x0
240:
241:    /* Call kernel main with the DTB physical address */
242:    mov x0, x20
243:    bl kernel_main
244:
245:    /* Should never return */
246:halt:
247:    wfe
248:    b halt
249:
250:/*
251: * Secondary CPU startup (PSCI Entry Point) — entered at PA, MMU off.
252: * x0 = context_id = kernel stack top (VIRTUAL, used only after MMU on)
253: */
254:secondary_startup:
255:    mov sp, x0              /* high VA; untouched until the MMU is on */
256:
257:    /* 1. TTBR1 = kernel PGD (physical, published by the primary CPU) */
258:    adrp x4, secondary_ttbr1
259:    add x4, x4, :lo12:secondary_ttbr1
260:    ldr x4, [x4]
261:    msr ttbr1_el1, x4
262:
263:    /* TTBR0 = boot identity tables (defined state until a process loads) */
264:    adrp x5, boot_pgd_ttbr0
265:    add x5, x5, :lo12:boot_pgd_ttbr0
266:    msr ttbr0_el1, x5
267:
268:    /* 2. MAIR (Attr0=Normal, Attr1=Device) — must match the primary CPU */
269:    mov x4, #0xff
270:    orr x4, x4, #(0x04 << 8)
271:    msr mair_el1, x4
272:
273:    /* 3. TCR — same 48/48 split as the primary CPU */
274:    ldr x4, =BOOT_TCR
275:    msr tcr_el1, x4
276:    isb
277:
278:    /* 4. SCTLR_EL1 (Enable M, C, I) */
279:    mrs x4, sctlr_el1
280:    orr x4, x4, #(1 << 0)  /* M */
281:    orr x4, x4, #(1 << 2)  /* C */
282:    orr x4, x4, #(1 << 12) /* I */
283:    dsb ish
284:    msr sctlr_el1, x4
285:    isb
286:
287:    /* Jump to C code (absolute virtual address via TTBR1) */
288:    ldr x3, =kernel_secondary_main
289:    br x3
290:    b halt
291:
292:/*
293: * Wake secondary CPU
294: */
295:.global cpu_wake_secondary
296:/*
297: * Wake secondary CPU via PSCI
298: * x0 = cpu id
299: * x1 = entry point (user C function) - ignored, we use secondary_startup
300: * x2 = stack pointer - passed as context_id
301: */
302:.global arch_cpu_wake_secondary
303:arch_cpu_wake_secondary:
304:    mov x3, x2          /* x3 = context_id (stack, virtual) */
305:
306:    /* PSCI needs the PHYSICAL entry point.  adrp at a high PC yields the
307:     * link (virtual) address — subtract KERNEL_VIRT_BASE. */
308:    adrp x2, secondary_startup
309:    add x2, x2, :lo12:secondary_startup
310:    ldr x4, =KVB
311:    sub x2, x2, x4
312:
313:    mov x1, x0          /* x1 = target_cpu (MPIDR) */
314:
315:    /* Load PSCI_CPU_ON_64 (0xC4000003) */
316:    mov x0, #0x0003
317:    movk x0, #0xC400, lsl #16
318:
319:    hvc #0              /* Call PSCI via HVC */
320:    ret
321:
322:/*
323: * Get boot info pointer (the stored value is the DTB's PHYSICAL address)
324: */
325:.global arch_get_boot_info
326:arch_get_boot_info:
327:    adrp x0, boot_info
328:    add x0, x0, :lo12:boot_info
329:    ldr x0, [x0]
330:    ret
331:
332:/*
333: * Data section
334: */
335:.section .data
336:.balign 8
337:
338:.global boot_info
339:boot_info:
340:    .quad 0
341:
342:cpu_spin_table:
343:    .skip MAX_CPUS * 16     /* MAX_CPUS entries */
344:
345:cpu_stacks:
346:    .skip MAX_CPUS * 16     /* MAX_CPUS stack pointers */
347:
348:/*
349: * BSS section
350: */
351:.section .bss
352:.balign 16
353:
354:/* Per-CPU stacks (128KB each) */
355:.global __kernel_stack
356:__kernel_stack:
357:    .skip 131072 * MAX_CPUS     /* MAX_CPUS * 128KB */
358:.global __kernel_stack_top
359:__kernel_stack_top:
360:
361:/* Boot page tables (cleared with BSS, then built by el1_setup) */
362:.balign 4096
363:boot_pgd_ttbr0:
364:    .skip 4096
365:.global boot_pgd_ttbr1
366:boot_pgd_ttbr1:
367:    .skip 4096
368:boot_pt_l1:
369:    .skip 4096
370:
371:.section .data
372:.align 3
373:.global secondary_ttbr1
374:secondary_ttbr1: .quad 0
375:

@@@ kernel/arch/aarch64/mm/mmu.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/aarch64/mm/mmu.c
3: * AArch64 4-level (48-bit VA, 4KB granule) page table management.
4: *
5: * Role:
6: *   Provides the arch_vmm_* interface required by the generic VMM layer
7: *   (kernel/mm/vmm.c) and by the kernel boot path (cpu.c:arch_vmm_init_hw).
8: *   PGD arguments are PHYSICAL addresses; table memory is dereferenced
9: *   through phys_to_virt() (higher-half direct map, kernel/memlayout.h).
10: *   The kernel half lives in TTBR1_EL1; per-process user tables in TTBR0.
11: *
12: * Page table layout (ARMv8-A 48-bit VA, 4KB granule, TCR.T0SZ=16):
13: *   Level 0 (PGD) — 9 bits [47:39] — table descriptor only (512 entries × 8B).
14: *   Level 1 (PUD) — 9 bits [38:30] — table OR 1GB block descriptors.
15: *   Level 2 (PMD) — 9 bits [29:21] — table OR 2MB block descriptors.
16: *   Level 3 (PT)  — 9 bits [20:12] — 4KB page descriptors.
17: *
18: * AArch64 descriptor bit format (simplified):
19: *   [1:0]  = 0b11 for a table/page entry (PTE_TABLE | PTE_VALID).
20: *   [1:0]  = 0b01 for a block entry (PTE_VALID but bit 1 clear).
21: *   [47:12] = output physical address (OA).
22: *   Upper/lower attribute bits encode MAIR index, AP, SH, UXN, PXN, AF, nG, etc.
23: *
24: * Block splitting (get_next_table with alloc=1 on a block entry):
25: *   When a 1GB (L1) or 2MB (L2) block entry exists at a level and a finer
26: *   granularity is needed (e.g. to map a single 4KB page inside a 2MB block),
27: *   the block is split into a new sub-table whose entries reproduce the same
28: *   physical mapping at the next level.
29: *
30: * Known issues:
31: *   AMMU-01 RESOLVED (Phase B2, b745a74): PAGE_KERNEL is RW+UXN+PXN; kernel
32: *            text is mapped PAGE_KERNEL_RX and rodata PAGE_KERNEL_RO by
33: *            vmm_map_ram_wx() — W^X holds for all RAM.
34: *   AMMU-08 RESOLVED (Phase B2): not by new code but by the ISA — the TLB
35: *            flush primitives in arch/arch.h use the inner-shareable TLBI
36: *            variants (vaae1is/vmalle1is), which the hardware DVM broadcasts
37: *            to every PE; DSB ISH waits for global completion.  The older
38: *            "local-only" notes in this file were factually wrong.
39: */
40:#include <kernel/arch.h>
41:#include <kernel/pmm.h>
42:#include <kernel/vmm.h>
43:#include <kernel/string.h>
44:
45:/*
46: * VA-to-table-index macros (4KB granule, 48-bit VA, TCR.T0SZ=16).
47: * Each level uses 9 bits of the virtual address:
48: *   PGD_INDEX: bits [47:39]
49: *   PUD_INDEX: bits [38:30]
50: *   PMD_INDEX: bits [29:21]
51: *   PT_INDEX:  bits [20:12]
52: * Result is 0..511 (the index into a 512-entry page table).
53: */
54:#define PGD_INDEX(x) (((x) >> 39) & 0x1FF)
55:#define PUD_INDEX(x) (((x) >> 30) & 0x1FF)
56:#define PMD_INDEX(x) (((x) >> 21) & 0x1FF)
57:#define PT_INDEX(x)  (((x) >> 12) & 0x1FF)
58:
59:/*
60: * PTE_ADDR_MASK - bits that hold the output physical address in a PTE.
61: * Bits [47:12] are the OA for 4KB granule.  Bits [11:0] are attribute/control
62: * bits; bits [63:48] are reserved (or IGNORED/UXN/PXN in upper attributes).
63: */
64:#define PTE_ADDR_MASK 0x0000FFFFFFFFF000UL
65:
66:/*
67: * get_next_table - walk or allocate the next-level page table at a given index.
68: *
69: * Parameters:
70: *   table  Pointer to the current-level page table (512 × uint64_t).
71: *   index  Index into table (0..511).
72: *   alloc  If non-zero, allocate a new sub-table (or split a block) when the
73: *          entry is absent or is a block entry.  If zero, return NULL for absent
74: *          or block entries without allocation.
75: *   level  Current table level: 1 = PGD→PUD walk (L0→L1), 2 = PUD→PMD (L1→L2),
76: *          3 = PMD→PT (L2→L3).  Used only during block-split to determine which
77: *          block size is being split.
78: *
79: * Returns: pointer to the next-level table, or NULL on failure / absent entry
80: *          when alloc==0.
81: *
82: * Fast path (table entry already a table descriptor):
83: *   entry & PTE_VALID && entry & 0x2 → return (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(entry & PTE_ADDR_MASK).
84: *
85: * Block-split path (entry valid but bit 1 == 0, i.e. a block descriptor):
86: *   Called when arch_vmm_map needs to place a 4KB page inside an existing
87: *   1GB (L1) or 2MB (L2) block mapping.
88: *   Steps:
89: *     1. Allocate a new 4KB sub-table (pmm_alloc_page, zeroed).
90: *     2. Populate each sub-table entry to reproduce the same physical mapping
91: *        at the finer granularity:
92: *          L1 block (1GB, level==1): 512 × 2MB L2 block entries, each offset by
93: *            i × 2MB from the original block base PA.
94: *          L2 block (2MB, level==2): 512 × 4KB L3 page entries, each offset by
95: *            i × 4KB from the original block base PA.
96: *     3. Cache-clean the new sub-table and the parent entry; DSB via arch_mb().
97: *     4. Write the parent entry as a table descriptor pointing to the new sub-table.
98: *
99: *   NOTE: No TLB flush is issued here; the caller (arch_vmm_map) handles the
100: *   TLB invalidation for the specific VA being modified (broadcast IS TLBI,
101: *   so siblings are covered — AMMU-08 resolved).
102: *
103: * Fresh-allocation path (entry == 0, alloc == 1):
104: *   Allocate and zero a new 4KB page; write as a table descriptor; cache-clean.
105: *
106: * Attribute notes for block-split:
107: *   block_flags = entry & ~PTE_ADDR_MASK preserves upper/lower attribute bits.
108: *   sub_flags   = block_flags | 0x2: sets bit 1 (the "table/page" discriminator)
109: *                 for L3 page entries.
110: *   L2 block entries use (block_flags & ~0x2) | 0x1: bit 1 = 0 (block), bit 0 = 1.
111: */
112:static uint64_t *get_next_table(uint64_t *table, uint64_t index, int alloc, int level) {
113:  uint64_t entry = table[index];
114:
115:  if (entry & PTE_VALID) {
116:    /* AArch64 descriptor bit 1: 0 = block descriptor, 1 = table/page descriptor.
117:     * At L3 all valid entries are page descriptors (bit 1 must be 1).
118:     * At L0 all valid entries must be table descriptors (no block at L0). */
119:    if (!(entry & 0x2)) {
120:      /* Block mapping at L1 (1GB) or L2 (2MB) — must split to allow finer map. */
121:      if (!alloc) return NULL; /* caller did not request allocation; fail cleanly */
122:
123:      /* SPLIT BLOCK: Convert Block to Table */
124:      void *new_table = pmm_alloc_page();
125:      if (!new_table) return NULL;
126:      memset(new_table, 0, 4096);
127:
128:      uint64_t block_pa    = entry & PTE_ADDR_MASK;  /* physical base of block */
129:      uint64_t block_flags = entry & ~PTE_ADDR_MASK; /* all attribute bits */
130:      /* sub_flags: page-level version of the same attributes (bit 1 set). */
131:      uint64_t sub_flags = block_flags | 0x2;
132:
133:      uint64_t *sub_table = (uint64_t *)new_table;
134:      /* 'level' is the level of the table being RETURNED (call sites pass
135:       * 1/2/3 for the L0→L1, L1→L2, L2→L3 steps).  A block found at the
136:       * L1→L2 step (level==2) is a 1GB L1 block; one found at the L2→L3
137:       * step (level==3) is a 2MB L2 block.  FIX: the branches previously
138:       * tested level==1/level==2, so a 2MB block was "split" into an EMPTY
139:       * L3 table — silently unmapping the other 511 pages of the block (the
140:       * ELF header-page map at 0x7ffff000 hit exactly this; benign only
141:       * because no PMM frame from that physical range was ever handed out). */
142:      if (level == 2) {
143:          /* L1 Block (1GB) -> L2 Table (512 x 2MB blocks).
144:           * Each child is a 2MB block, so bit 1 stays 0 (block); bit 0 stays 1. */
145:          for (int i = 0; i < 512; i++) {
146:            sub_table[i] = (block_pa + (uint64_t)i * 0x200000) | (block_flags & ~0x2) | 0x1;
147:          }
148:      } else if (level == 3) {
149:          /* L2 Block (2MB) -> L3 Table (512 x 4KB pages).
150:           * Each child is an L3 page descriptor (bit 1 = 1). */
151:          for (int i = 0; i < 512; i++) {
152:            sub_table[i] = (block_pa + (uint64_t)i * 4096) | sub_flags;
153:          }
154:      } else {
155:          /* L0 entries are architecturally always table descriptors; a
156:           * "block" here means corruption — refuse instead of fabricating
157:           * an empty table. */
158:          pmm_free_page(new_table);
159:          return NULL;
160:      }
161:
162:      arch_cache_clean_range(sub_table, 4096); /* write back new sub-table to DRAM */
163:      arch_mb(); /* DSB: ensure sub-table is visible before parent entry update */
164:
165:      /* Update the parent table to point to the new sub-table (table descriptor). */
166:      table[index] = virt_to_phys(new_table) | PTE_TABLE | PTE_VALID;
167:      arch_cache_clean_range(&table[index], 8); /* write back parent entry */
168:      arch_mb();
169:
170:      /* The caller's TLBI for the VA being mapped is the broadcast (IS)
171:       * variant; the block-split itself preserves the old translations
172:       * (same PA, same attributes at finer grain), so no extra flush is
173:       * required here. */
174:
175:      return new_table;
176:    }
177:    /* Existing table descriptor: extract next-level table pointer from OA field. */
178:    return (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(entry & PTE_ADDR_MASK);
179:  }
180:
181:  /* Entry is absent (not valid); allocate a new table page if permitted. */
182:  if (!alloc) return NULL;
183:
184:  void *page = pmm_alloc_page();
185:  if (!page) return NULL;
186:
187:  memset(page, 0, 4096);
188:  arch_cache_clean_range(page, 4096);
189:  arch_mb();
190:
191:  /* Install the new table as a table descriptor (PTE_TABLE | PTE_VALID). */
192:  table[index] = virt_to_phys(page) | PTE_TABLE | PTE_VALID;
193:
194:  arch_cache_clean_range(&table[index], 8);
195:  arch_mb();
196:
197:  return (uint64_t *)page;
198:}
199:
200:/*
201: * arch_vmm_map - create a single 4KB page mapping (VA → PA) in the given PGD.
202: *
203: * Parameters:
204: *   pgd_addr  Physical address of the L0 page table.
205: *   va        Virtual address to map (must be 4KB aligned; low 12 bits ignored
206: *             in the PTE but should be 0 for correctness).
207: *   pa        Physical address of the target page (4KB aligned).
208: *   flags     PTE attribute bits (PTE_VALID | PTE_TABLE | MAIR index | AP | SH |
209: *             UXN | PXN | AF | nG ...).  Combined with pa via bitwise OR.
210: * Returns: 0 on success, -1 on PMM exhaustion.
211: *
212: * Walks three levels (PGD → PUD → PMD → PT) via get_next_table() with alloc=1,
213: * allocating new sub-tables or splitting existing block mappings as needed.
214: * Then writes the L3 page descriptor pa|flags into PT[PT_INDEX(va)].
215: *
216: * Cache coherency: pt_entry is cleaned to PoC (arch_cache_clean_range) so the
217: * hardware page-table walker (which may cache-bypass to main memory) sees the
218: * new entry.  arch_mb() (DSB ISH) ensures the write is globally visible before
219: * the TLB invalidation.
220: *
221: * TLB maintenance:
222: *   A local TLB flush for the specific VA is issued only when pgd_addr matches
223: *   the currently loaded TTBR0_EL1 (i.e., this is the active address space).
224: *   Mappings in inactive PGDs do not require a TLB flush at map time because
225: *   they are not cached in any CPU's TLB yet.
226: *   arch_tlb_flush_va is TLBI VAAE1IS: broadcast to every PE in the
227: *   inner-shareable domain by hardware (AMMU-08 resolved — no IPI needed).
228: */
229:int arch_vmm_map(uint64_t pgd_addr, uint64_t va, uint64_t pa, uint64_t flags) {
230:  uint64_t *pgd = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pgd_addr);
231:  uint64_t *pud, *pmd, *pt;
232:
233:  pud = get_next_table(pgd, PGD_INDEX(va), 1, 1); /* L0 → L1 */
234:  if (!pud) return -1;
235:
236:  pmd = get_next_table(pud, PUD_INDEX(va), 1, 2); /* L1 → L2 */
237:  if (!pmd) return -1;
238:
239:  pt = get_next_table(pmd, PMD_INDEX(va), 1, 3);  /* L2 → L3 */
240:  if (!pt) return -1;
241:
242:  /* Write the L3 page descriptor.  flags must include PTE_VALID (bit 0) and
243:   * PTE_TABLE (bit 1) for a page entry; pa provides the OA at bits [47:12]. */
244:  uint64_t *pt_entry = &pt[PT_INDEX(va)];
245:  *pt_entry = pa | flags;
246:
247:  arch_cache_clean_range(pt_entry, 8); /* flush PT entry to PoC for page walker */
248:  arch_mb(); /* DSB ISH: ensure entry visible to all observers before TLB op */
249:
250:  /* Flush TLB for this VA only if this PGD is currently live — in TTBR0
251:   * (a process half) or TTBR1 (the kernel half).  The TLBI is the
252:   * broadcast (IS) variant: siblings are covered too. */
253:  if (pgd_addr == arch_impl_get_pgd() ||
254:      pgd_addr == arch_impl_get_kernel_pgd()) {
255:    arch_tlb_flush_va(va);
256:    arch_mb();
257:    arch_isb();
258:  }
259:
260:  return 0;
261:}
262:
263:/*
264: * arch_vmm_unmap - remove the 4KB page mapping for va from the given PGD.
265: *
266: * Parameters:
267: *   pgd_addr  Physical address of the L0 page table.
268: *   va        Virtual address of the page to unmap.
269: * Returns: 0 always (idempotent if the mapping did not exist).
270: *
271: * Walks without allocating (alloc=0): if any level is absent, returns 0
272: * immediately (mapping was never created; nothing to do).
273: *
274: * Clears the PT entry to 0 (invalid), cleans it to PoC, then issues a full
275: * DSB + TLBI VAE1 (via arch_tlb_flush_va) + ISB sequence.
276: *
277: * NOTE: The page table sub-levels (PT, PMD, PUD) are NOT freed even when they
278: * become entirely empty after the unmap.  This means unmapping many individual
279: * pages from a large process VA space accumulates empty page-table pages.
280: *
281: * arch_tlb_flush_va is TLBI VAAE1IS + DSB ISH: the invalidation is broadcast
282: * to all PEs and awaited globally (AMMU-08 resolved) — when this returns no
283: * sibling CPU still translates 'va' through the cleared entry.
284: */
285:int arch_vmm_unmap(uint64_t pgd_addr, uint64_t va) {
286:  uint64_t *pgd = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pgd_addr);
287:  uint64_t *pud, *pmd, *pt;
288:
289:  pud = get_next_table(pgd, PGD_INDEX(va), 0, 1); /* no alloc */
290:  if (!pud) return 0; /* not mapped at this level; nothing to do */
291:
292:  pmd = get_next_table(pud, PUD_INDEX(va), 0, 2);
293:  if (!pmd) return 0;
294:
295:  pt = get_next_table(pmd, PMD_INDEX(va), 0, 3);
296:  if (!pt) return 0;
297:
298:  uint64_t *pt_entry = &pt[PT_INDEX(va)];
299:  *pt_entry = 0; /* clear: PTE_VALID bit 0 = 0 → entry is invalid */
300:
301:  arch_cache_clean_range(pt_entry, 8); /* writeback cleared entry for page walker */
302:  arch_mb();                            /* DSB ISH before TLBI */
303:  arch_tlb_flush_va(va);               /* TLBI VAE1 for this VA on local CPU */
304:  arch_mb();
305:  arch_isb();                           /* pipeline flush after TLBI */
306:
307:  return 0;
308:}
309:
310:/*
311: * arch_vmm_protect - rewrite the attributes of existing 4KB mappings (AMMU-02).
312: *
313: * Parameters:
314: *   pgd_addr  Physical address of the L0 page table.
315: *   va, size  Range to change; rounded outward to page boundaries.
316: *   flags     FULL aarch64 page profile (PAGE_KERNEL / PAGE_KERNEL_RO /
317: *             PAGE_USER_DATA ... — the same vocabulary arch_vmm_map takes):
318: *             every attribute bit of each leaf PTE is replaced; only the
319: *             output address is preserved.
320: *
321: * A 1GB/2MB block covering part of the range is first split into the next
322: * finer granularity (get_next_table with alloc=1) so the change applies with
323: * 4KB precision; translations outside the requested range are preserved
324: * bit-identically by the split.
325: *
326: * Returns 0 on success; -1 if any page in the range is unmapped or a split
327: * allocation fails (pages BEFORE the failure keep the new attributes — the
328: * TLB flush below runs on both paths so the PTEs already rewritten are
329: * never left visible only in stale TLB copies).
330: *
331: * TLB: one broadcast invalidate-all (TLBI VMALLE1IS via arch_tlb_flush_all)
332: * after the loop — cross-CPU by hardware, no IPI needed.
333: */
334:int arch_vmm_protect(uint64_t pgd_addr, uint64_t va, uint64_t size, uint64_t flags) {
335:  uint64_t *pgd = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pgd_addr);
336:  uint64_t v = va & ~0xFFFUL;
337:  uint64_t end = (va + size + 0xFFFUL) & ~0xFFFUL;
338:  int rc = 0;
339:
340:  for (; v < end; v += 4096) {
341:    uint64_t pgde = pgd[PGD_INDEX(v)];
342:    if (!(pgde & PTE_VALID)) { rc = -1; break; }
343:    uint64_t *pud = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pgde & PTE_ADDR_MASK); /* L0: always a table */
344:
345:    uint64_t pude = pud[PUD_INDEX(v)];
346:    if (!(pude & PTE_VALID)) { rc = -1; break; }
347:    uint64_t *pmd;
348:    if (!(pude & 0x2)) {
349:      pmd = get_next_table(pud, PUD_INDEX(v), 1, 2); /* split 1GB block */
350:      if (!pmd) { rc = -1; break; }
351:    } else {
352:      pmd = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pude & PTE_ADDR_MASK);
353:    }
354:
355:    uint64_t pmde = pmd[PMD_INDEX(v)];
356:    if (!(pmde & PTE_VALID)) { rc = -1; break; }
357:    uint64_t *pt;
358:    if (!(pmde & 0x2)) {
359:      pt = get_next_table(pmd, PMD_INDEX(v), 1, 3); /* split 2MB block */
360:      if (!pt) { rc = -1; break; }
361:    } else {
362:      pt = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pmde & PTE_ADDR_MASK);
363:    }
364:
365:    uint64_t *pte = &pt[PT_INDEX(v)];
366:    if (!(*pte & PTE_VALID)) { rc = -1; break; }
367:    *pte = (*pte & PTE_ADDR_MASK) | flags;
368:    arch_cache_clean_range(pte, 8); /* visible to the hardware walker */
369:  }
370:
371:  arch_mb();            /* DSB ISH: PTE writes complete before TLBI */
372:  arch_tlb_flush_all(); /* TLBI VMALLE1IS: broadcast to all PEs */
373:  arch_isb();
374:  return rc;
375:}
376:
377:/*
378: * arch_vmm_get_physical - translate a virtual address to its physical address.
379: *
380: * Parameters:
381: *   pgd_addr  Physical address of the L0 page table.
382: *   va        Virtual address to translate.
383: * Returns: physical address with page offset, or 0 if not mapped / not valid.
384: *
385: * Walks all four levels without allocating (alloc=0 at each level).  If any
386: * level table is absent, or the final L3 entry has PTE_VALID clear, returns 0.
387: *
388: * The physical address is reconstructed as:
389: *   (entry & PTE_ADDR_MASK) | (va & 0xFFF)
390: * where PTE_ADDR_MASK extracts the OA [47:12] and (va & 0xFFF) restores the
391: * 12-bit page offset from the original virtual address.
392: *
393: * Handles 1GB (L1) and 2MB (L2) block descriptors by combining the block
394: * base OA with the in-block offset of 'va' — previously a block anywhere on
395: * the walk made the function return 0 (get_next_table with alloc=0 refuses
396: * blocks), so lookups inside the 2MB-block RAM identity map always failed.
397: */
398:uint64_t arch_vmm_get_physical(uint64_t pgd_addr, uint64_t va) {
399:  uint64_t *pgd = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pgd_addr);
400:
401:  uint64_t pgde = pgd[PGD_INDEX(va)];
402:  if (!(pgde & PTE_VALID)) return 0;
403:  uint64_t *pud = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pgde & PTE_ADDR_MASK); /* L0: always a table */
404:
405:  uint64_t pude = pud[PUD_INDEX(va)];
406:  if (!(pude & PTE_VALID)) return 0;
407:  if (!(pude & 0x2)) /* 1GB L1 block */
408:    return ((pude & PTE_ADDR_MASK) & ~0x3FFFFFFFUL) | (va & 0x3FFFFFFFUL);
409:  uint64_t *pmd = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pude & PTE_ADDR_MASK);
410:
411:  uint64_t pmde = pmd[PMD_INDEX(va)];
412:  if (!(pmde & PTE_VALID)) return 0;
413:  if (!(pmde & 0x2)) /* 2MB L2 block */
414:    return ((pmde & PTE_ADDR_MASK) & ~0x1FFFFFUL) | (va & 0x1FFFFFUL);
415:  uint64_t *pt = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pmde & PTE_ADDR_MASK);
416:
417:  uint64_t entry = pt[PT_INDEX(va)];
418:  if (!(entry & PTE_VALID)) return 0;
419:
420:  /* Reconstruct PA: OA from PTE [47:12] | page offset from VA [11:0]. */
421:  return (entry & PTE_ADDR_MASK) | (va & 0xFFF);
422:}
423:
424:/*
425: * arch_vmm_map_range - map a contiguous VA range to a contiguous PA range.
426: *
427: * Parameters:
428: *   pgd    Physical address of the L0 page table.
429: *   va     Start virtual address (must be page-aligned).
430: *   pa     Start physical address (must be page-aligned).
431: *   size   Length of the mapping in bytes (must be a multiple of PAGE_SIZE).
432: *   flags  PTE attribute bits, interpreted as for arch_vmm_map.
433: * Returns: 0 on success, -1 on PMM exhaustion or table walk failure.
434: *
435: * Performance optimisation: uses 2MB block descriptors (L2 blocks) when both
436: * v and p are 2MB-aligned AND at least 2MB remains to be mapped.  This reduces
437: * the number of page-table allocations and TLB entries significantly for large
438: * contiguous regions (e.g., kernel .text/.data, RAM identity map).
439: *
440: * 2MB block descriptor format:
441: *   bits[1:0] = 0b01 (block, not table/page): PTE_VALID but bit 1 clear.
442: *   (flags & ~0x2): clear bit 1 from the flags, which are otherwise page-level
443: *     flags (0b11); for a block the hardware requires bit 1 = 0.
444: *   Result: p | (flags & ~0x2) | 0x1.
445: *
446: * 4KB page fallback (arch_vmm_map):
447: *   Used when alignment or remaining size prevents a 2MB block.  This path also
448: *   handles the final sub-2MB tail of a region.
449: *
450: * NOTE: arch_mb / TLB flush after 2MB block writes are omitted; the function
451: * relies on the caller to issue a global TLB flush (e.g., arch_vmm_init_hw)
452: * after the full table is built.  Inserting per-entry TLBIs here would be
453: * correct but very slow for large ranges.
454: */
455:int arch_vmm_map_range(uint64_t pgd, uint64_t va, uint64_t pa, uint64_t size, uint64_t flags) {
456:  uint64_t v = va;
457:  uint64_t p = pa;
458:  uint64_t end = va + size;
459:
460:  while (v < end) {
461:    uint64_t remaining = end - v;
462:
463:    /* 2MB block optimisation: use an L2 block descriptor when both VA and PA
464:     * are 2MB-aligned and at least 2MB remains unmapped. */
465:    if ((v & 0x1FFFFF) == 0 && (p & 0x1FFFFF) == 0 && remaining >= 0x200000) {
466:      uint64_t *pgd_ptr = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pgd);
467:      uint64_t *pud = get_next_table(pgd_ptr, PGD_INDEX(v), 1, 1);
468:      if (!pud) return -1;
469:
470:      uint64_t *pmd = get_next_table(pud, PUD_INDEX(v), 1, 2);
471:      if (!pmd) return -1;
472:
473:      /* Write a 2MB L2 block descriptor:
474:       *   AArch64 block entry: [1:0] = 0b01 (PTE_VALID=1, table-bit=0).
475:       *   (flags & ~0x2): strip the page-level table-bit from flags so the
476:       *   hardware interprets this as a block, not a table pointer.
477:       *   | 0x1: set PTE_VALID.
478:       * Result: hardware-correct 2MB block OA=p with flags' attributes. */
479:      pmd[PMD_INDEX(v)] = p | (flags & ~0x2) | 0x1;
480:
481:      arch_cache_clean_range(&pmd[PMD_INDEX(v)], 8); /* flush entry to PoC */
482:      v += 0x200000;
483:      p += 0x200000;
484:    } else {
485:      /* Fallback to 4KB page via the full 4-level walk. */
486:      if (arch_vmm_map(pgd, v, p, flags) != 0) return -1;
487:      v += 4096;
488:      p += 4096;
489:    }
490:  }
491:  return 0;
492:}
493:
494:/*
495: * arch_vmm_map_device - map a device MMIO region [base, base+size) into the
496: * kernel's higher-half direct map as Device-nGnRnE memory (PAGE_DEVICE).
497: *
498: * Mirrors the amd64 contract used by the PCI scan / USB-xHCI BAR mapping. On
499: * aarch64 the MMIO direct map lives at KERNEL_VIRT_BASE + PA, so the mapping
500: * is VA = phys_to_virt(PA) -> PA, exactly what drivers dereference after
501: * phys_to_virt(bar). Needed for the PCIe-ECAM bring-up and any PCI BAR above
502: * the boot-time MMIO window.
503: */
504:int arch_vmm_map_device(uint64_t base, uint64_t size);
505:int arch_vmm_map_device(uint64_t base, uint64_t size) {
506:  if (!base || !size)
507:    return -1;
508:  uint64_t pgd = arch_impl_get_kernel_pgd();
509:  uint64_t start = base & ~0xFFFUL;
510:  uint64_t end = (base + size + 0xFFFUL) & ~0xFFFUL;
511:  for (uint64_t a = start; a < end; a += 4096) {
512:    /* Recoverable and runtime: a BAR that cannot be mapped is a device the
513:     * driver must be told about, not a dead kernel.  The loop returned 0
514:     * whatever happened, so a caller mapped nothing and believed it had --
515:     * the SAME defect as the amd64 twin in arch/amd64/mm/mmu.c, which is
516:     * exactly why the two are fixed identically. */
517:    if (arch_vmm_map(pgd, (uint64_t)phys_to_virt(a), a, PAGE_DEVICE) != 0) {
518:      arch_tlb_flush_all();
519:      return -ENOMEM;
520:    }
521:  }
522:  arch_tlb_flush_all();
523:  return 0;
524:}
525:
526:/*
527: * arch_vmm_create_process_pgd - allocate a new per-process (TTBR0) PGD.
528: *
529: * Returns: physical address of the new L0 page table, or 0 on PMM exhaustion.
530: *
531: * Higher-half model: the kernel lives entirely in TTBR1 (image, direct map
532: * and MMIO at KERNEL_VIRT_BASE + PA — see memlayout.h), which the hardware
533: * uses for every VA whose top bits are set.  A process PGD therefore
534: * contains ONLY user mappings: it starts out completely empty and the ELF
535: * loader / sbrk fill it via arch_vmm_map().  Nothing is shared with
536: * kernel_pgd, which makes vmm_destroy_pgd's ownership rules trivial — every
537: * table page reachable from this PGD belongs to the process.
538: */
539:uint64_t arch_vmm_create_process_pgd(void) {
540:  uint64_t *pgd = (uint64_t *)pmm_alloc_page();
541:  if (!pgd) return 0;
542:  memset(pgd, 0, 4096);
543:
544:  arch_cache_clean_range(pgd, 4096);
545:  arch_mb();
546:  /* Contract: the arch layer returns the PGD's PHYSICAL address;
547:   * vmm_create_pgd() converts back to a pointer. */
548:  return virt_to_phys(pgd);
549:}
550:

@@@ kernel/arch/aarch64/hal.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/aarch64/hal.c
3: * AArch64 Hardware Abstraction Layer — platform bus scan, IRQ, and timer init.
4: *
5: * Role:
6: *   Implements the three arch_* hooks that the generic kernel calls during
7: *   device discovery:
8: *   - arch_bus_scan(): probes VirtIO MMIO slots and registers found devices
9: *     in the HAL device registry (hal_bus.c).
10: *   - arch_irq_init(): delegates to gic_register() to install the GIC driver
11: *     into the kernel IRQ controller abstraction.
12: *   - arch_timer_init(): delegates to timer_init() to program the ARM Generic
13: *     Timer (sys_timer.c) for the kernel tick.
14: *
15: * HAL over-abstraction note (HAL-01):
16: *   hal_read32(base) expands to a compound-literal hal_device_t construction +
17: *   heuristic bus-type detection + indirect call through hal_dev_read32.
18: *   For a hot MMIO read this is significantly more expensive than a single
19: *   memory-mapped load.  arch_bus_scan() calls hal_read32 only twice per slot
20: *   (magic + device_id) during boot, so the overhead here is acceptable.
21: *   Drivers that call hal_read32 in interrupt handlers should be aware of
22: *   the overhead (see HAL-01 in docs/review/analysis/02-boot-arch-hal.md).
23: */
24:#include <kernel/hal.h>
25:#include <kernel/string.h>
26:#include <kernel/printk.h>
27:#include <kernel/platform.h>
28:#include <arch/platform.h>
29:#include <drivers/virtio.h>
30:#include <drivers/pci.h>
31:
32:/* QEMU virt PCIe ECAM (compatible "pci-host-ecam-generic"). Base taken from the
33: * board DTB pcie node: reg = <0x40 0x10000000 ...> -> 0x4010000000, 256 MB,
34: * bus-range 0..255. Standard ECAM addressing: base + (bus<<20|dev<<15|fn<<12).
35: *
36: * NOTE(ASTRA-VIOLATION): base is hardcoded for the QEMU virt board; derive it
37: * from the FDT pcie node once an FDT parser exists. Only the first buses are
38: * populated on virt, so we map and bound the scan to a 16 MB window. */
39:#define VIRT_ECAM_BASE  0x4010000000UL
40:#define VIRT_ECAM_BUSES 16
41:
42:static uint32_t ecam_off(uint8_t bus, uint8_t dev, uint8_t fn, uint8_t off) {
43:  return ((uint32_t)bus << 20) | ((uint32_t)dev << 15) |
44:         ((uint32_t)fn << 12) | (off & 0xFFC);
45:}
46:static uint32_t ecam_read32(uint8_t bus, uint8_t dev, uint8_t fn, uint8_t off) {
47:  if (bus >= VIRT_ECAM_BUSES) return 0xFFFFFFFF;
48:  return *(volatile uint32_t *)phys_to_virt(VIRT_ECAM_BASE + ecam_off(bus, dev, fn, off));
49:}
50:static void ecam_write32(uint8_t bus, uint8_t dev, uint8_t fn, uint8_t off, uint32_t v) {
51:  if (bus >= VIRT_ECAM_BUSES) return;
52:  *(volatile uint32_t *)phys_to_virt(VIRT_ECAM_BASE + ecam_off(bus, dev, fn, off)) = v;
53:}
54:static struct pci_config_ops ecam_ops = { ecam_read32, ecam_write32 };
55:
56:/* arch_platform_get_boot_module (HAL contract, platform.h): aarch64 boots a
57: * raw kernel + a virtio-blk disk, with no GRUB/initrd module today.  Returns
58: * 0; a future DTB /chosen initrd would slot in here, keeping the ramdisk
59: * block backend identical to amd64. */
60:int arch_platform_get_boot_module(uint64_t *base, uint64_t *size) {
61:  (void)base;
62:  (void)size;
63:  return 0;
64:}
65:
66:/*
67: * arch_bus_scan - probe VirtIO MMIO slots and register discovered devices.
68: *
69: * VirtIO MMIO layout on QEMU virt (aarch64):
70: *   Base address: VIRTIO_MMIO_BASE (platform.h, typically 0x0A000000).
71: *   Each device slot occupies VIRTIO_MMIO_STRIDE bytes (typically 0x200 = 512B).
72: *   Number of slots: VIRTIO_COUNT (typically 32).
73: *
74: * Discovery sequence per slot:
75: *   1. Read VIRTIO_MMIO_MAGIC_VALUE at offset 0x000.
76: *      Valid VirtIO devices respond with 0x74726976 ("virt" in little-endian).
77: *   2. If magic matches, read VIRTIO_MMIO_DEVICE_ID at offset 0x008.
78: *      Device ID 0 means the slot is empty; skip it.
79: *   3. Populate a hal_device descriptor and call hal_register_device().
80: *
81: * IRQ assignment: the QEMU virt board maps VirtIO MMIO IRQs starting at 48
82: * (SPI 16 in GIC terms); device i uses IRQ 48 + i.
83: * Vendor ID 0x1AF4 is the standard VirtIO PCI/MMIO vendor.
84: */
85:void arch_bus_scan(void) {
86:    pr_info("%s", "HAL: Scanning Platform Bus (MMIO)...\n");
87:
88:    for (int i = 0; i < VIRTIO_COUNT; i++) {
89:        uintptr_t base = VIRTIO_MMIO_BASE + i * VIRTIO_MMIO_STRIDE;
90:        /* Read the VirtIO magic value; valid devices return "virt" (0x74726976). */
91:        uint32_t magic = hal_read32(base + VIRTIO_MMIO_MAGIC_VALUE);
92:
93:        if (magic == 0x74726976) { /* "virt" in little-endian ASCII */
94:            uint32_t dev_id = hal_read32(base + VIRTIO_MMIO_DEVICE_ID);
95:            if (dev_id != 0) { /* device_id == 0 means slot is empty */
96:                struct hal_device dev;
97:                memset(&dev, 0, sizeof(dev));
98:
99:                dev.bus_type  = HAL_BUS_TYPE_VIRTIO_MMIO;
100:                dev.vendor_id = 0x1AF4;           /* VirtIO standard vendor */
101:                dev.device_id = (uint16_t)dev_id; /* e.g. 1=net, 2=blk, 9=gpu */
102:                dev.base      = base;
103:                dev.irq       = 48 + i;           /* QEMU virt IRQ allocation */
104:
105:                snprintf(dev.name, sizeof(dev.name), "VirtIO-%d", dev_id);
106:
107:                hal_register_device(&dev);
108:            }
109:        }
110:    }
111:
112:    /* Unify with amd64: bring up the PCIe ECAM bus so the same PCI providers
113:     * (xHCI/VGA/...) enumerate here too. virtio stays on MMIO above; this adds
114:     * the PCI side (e.g. -device qemu-xhci) behind the same HAL registry. */
115:    extern int arch_vmm_map_device(uint64_t base, uint64_t size);
116:    arch_vmm_map_device(VIRT_ECAM_BASE, (uint64_t)VIRT_ECAM_BUSES << 20);
117:    pci_set_config_ops(&ecam_ops);
118:    /* PCI MMIO windows from the virt DTB pcie ranges (32-bit @ 0x10000000,
119:     * 64-bit @ 0x80_00000000), used to assign BARs the (absent) firmware did
120:     * not program. */
121:    pci_set_mmio_windows(0x10000000UL, 0x2eff0000UL,
122:                         0x8000000000UL, 0x8000000000UL);
123:    pci_scan_and_register();
124:}
125:
126:/*
127: * arch_irq_init - install the platform interrupt controller driver.
128: *
129: * Calls gic_register() to register the GIC (Generic Interrupt Controller)
130: * irq_ctrl_ops with the kernel IRQ subsystem.  The actual GIC hardware
131: * initialisation (GICD enable, per-CPU GICC/GICR setup) happens inside
132: * gic_register() or the GIC driver's init path.
133: *
134: * Must be called before any IRQ is enabled or any driver calls request_irq().
135: */
136:void arch_irq_init(void) {
137:    extern void gic_register(void);
138:    gic_register();
139:}
140:
141:/*
142: * arch_timer_init - initialise the system tick timer.
143: *
144: * Delegates to timer_init() (kernel/drivers/sys_timer.c), which programs the
145: * ARM Generic Timer (CNTP_CTL_EL0 / CNTP_TVAL_EL0 or equivalent) to fire
146: * periodic interrupts for the kernel scheduler tick.
147: */
148:void arch_timer_init(void) {
149:    extern void timer_init(void);
150:    timer_init();
151:}
152:

@@@ kernel/arch/aarch64/kernel.ld @@@
1:/*
2: * Kernel linker script for AArch64
3: * Loaded at PHYSICAL 0x40080000 (QEMU -kernel raw binary), linked in the
4: * higher half at KERNEL_VIRT_BASE (0xFFFF000000000000) + load PA, so the
5: * single direct-map offset converts every kernel VA (memlayout.h).
6: * start.S runs PC-relative at the load PA until it enables the MMU
7: * (TTBR0 identity + TTBR1 higher half) and jumps to the link address.
8: */
9:ENTRY(_start)
10:
11:SECTIONS
12:{
13:    . = 0xFFFF000040080000;
14:    
15:    /* Code section */
16:    .text : {
17:        __text_start = .;       /* W^X RX window start (vmm_map_ram_wx) */
18:        KEEP(*(.text.boot))     /* Boot code first */
19:        *(.text)
20:        *(.text.*)
21:    }
22:    _etext = .;
23:    
24:    . = ALIGN(4096);
25:    
26:    /* Read-only data */
27:    .rodata : {
28:        *(.rodata)
29:        *(.rodata.*)
30:
31:        . = ALIGN(16); /* GCC DATA_ALIGNMENT ups >=16-byte aggregates to 16 on
32:         * x86-64: with ALIGN(8) the linker could pad AFTER __ktests_start,
33:         * making the first walked descriptor garbage (S-ALIGN F9 fix). */
34:        __ktests_start = .;
35:        KEEP(*(.ktests))
36:        __ktests_end = .;
37:
38:        /* In-kernel symbol table (tools/gen_ksyms.sh, two-pass link).
39:         * MUST be an allocated section inside .rodata: kernel.bin is produced
40:         * with objcopy -O binary, which keeps only allocated sections — this
41:         * is the only way the running aarch64 image gets live symbolization. */
42:        . = ALIGN(8);
43:        __ksyms_start = .;
44:        KEEP(*(.ksyms))
45:        __ksyms_end = .;
46:    }
47:    __erodata = .;
48:
49:    . = ALIGN(4096);
50:
51:    /* Read-write data */
52:    .data : {
53:        *(.data)
54:        *(.data.*)
55:    }
56:    
57:    . = ALIGN(4096);
58:    
59:    /* BSS (uninitialized data) */
60:    __bss_start = .;
61:    .bss : {
62:        *(.bss)
63:        *(.bss.*)
64:        *(COMMON)
65:    }
66:    __bss_end = .;
67:    
68:    . = ALIGN(4096);
69:    
70:    /* End of kernel */
71:    __kernel_end = .;
72:    
73:    /* Discard unwanted sections */
74:    /DISCARD/ : {
75:        *(.comment)
76:        *(.gnu*)
77:        *(.note*)
78:        *(.eh_frame*)
79:    }
80:}
81:
82:/* Provide symbols for runtime (link/virtual addresses) */
83:PROVIDE(__kernel_start = 0xFFFF000040080000);
84:PROVIDE(__kernel_size = __kernel_end - __kernel_start);
