@@@ kernel/arch/aarch64/platform.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/aarch64/platform.c
3: * Platform hardware discovery and SMP bring-up for AArch64 (QEMU virt machine).
4: *
5: * Role:
6: *   This file implements the arch_platform_* interface declared in
7: *   kernel/include/kernel/platform.h for the AArch64 target.  It is responsible
8: *   for three tasks:
9: *   1. Early init (arch_platform_early_init): register the GIC interrupt
10: *      controller and initialise the FDT/DTB parser.
11: *   2. Memory discovery (arch_platform_get_mem_regions): obtain a list of usable
12: *      RAM regions for the PMM.  Primary path: FDT "memory" node parse.  Fallback:
13: *      manual physical-page probe using the probe_in_progress / probe_failed flags
14: *      and the EL1 Data Abort recovery path in sync_handler (cpu.c).
15: *   3. SMP bring-up (arch_smp_init): wake secondary CPUs via PSCI CPU_ON
16: *      (arch_cpu_wake_secondary, start.S), wait for each to acknowledge, and
17: *      create an idle task for each newly-online CPU.
18: *
19: * Known issues:
20: *   ARCH-04 (W2 BAD-IMPL·BUG) The manual probe fallback writes arch_mem_regions[0]
21: *            TWICE: once at lines 83–86 (after finding found_end), and again at
22: *            91–94 (the "safety" adjustment).  The second write silently overwrites
23: *            the first, making the lines 83–86 dead.  The size computed in the second
24: *            write also subtracts PAGE_SIZE regardless of whether found_end > probe_base,
25: *            which can produce size == 0 when found_end == probe_base. [static]
26: *   ARCH-05 (W2 REFINE) The probe reads at 128MB intervals (0x08000000) from the
27: *            QEMU virt base.  On real hardware some physical addresses in the probe
28: *            range map to device registers that do not cleanly abort; a read could
29: *            trigger an unintended device side-effect before the sync exception fires.
30: */
31:#include <kernel/fdt.h>
32:#include <kernel/arch.h>
33:#include <kernel/cpu.h>
34:#include <kernel/memlayout.h>
35:#include <kernel/pmm.h>
36:#include <kernel/platform.h>
37:#include <kernel/printk.h>
38:#include <drivers/gic.h>
39:#include <drivers/uart.h>
40:
41:/*
42: * arch_mem_regions[] - static array of usable RAM descriptors filled by
43: * arch_platform_get_mem_regions() from FDT or the manual probe.
44: * Sized to MAX_CPUS * 2 which is larger than the typical 1–2 QEMU virt
45: * memory regions; this avoids dynamic allocation during early boot.
46: */
47:static struct mem_region arch_mem_regions[MAX_CPUS * 2]; /* Enough slots */
48:static size_t arch_region_count = 0;
49:
50:/*
51: * arch_platform_early_init - very early platform setup before PMM is available.
52: *
53: * Called by kernel_main() before memory discovery; must not call kmalloc.
54: *
55: * Actions:
56: *   1. Register the GIC (Generic Interrupt Controller) driver via gic_register().
57: *      This installs the GIC's irq_ctrl_ops into the kernel IRQ subsystem;
58: *      the GIC is not yet initialised for per-CPU distributor/redistributor
59: *      setup (that happens later in arch_irq_init / hal.c).
60: *   2. Parse the Device Tree Blob (DTB) passed by the firmware/QEMU in x0 at
61: *      kernel entry.  The DTB pointer is saved as boot_fdt_ptr in start.S.
62: *      fdt_init() makes the FDT available for subsequent fdt_get_mem_regions()
63: *      and fdt_count_cpus() calls.
64: *
65: * If boot_fdt_ptr is NULL (no DTB from firmware), hardware discovery falls back
66: * to the manual probe path in arch_platform_get_mem_regions (ARCH-04/05).
67: */
68:void arch_platform_early_init(void) {
69:    uart_puts("PLATFORM: arch_platform_early_init starting\n");
70:    /*
71:     * Register the Interrupt Controller.
72:     * gic_register() installs the GIC irq_ctrl_ops; the physical GIC init
73:     * (GICD/GICR programming) happens later in arch_irq_init().
74:     */
75:    gic_register();
76:
77:    /* Initialize FDT parser from the DTB pointer saved by start.S at _start. */
78:    if (boot_fdt_ptr) {
79:        if (fdt_init(boot_fdt_ptr) == 0) {
80:            pr_info("AArch64: IDTF/FDT initialized from 0x%lx\n", boot_fdt_ptr);
81:        } else {
82:            pr_warn("AArch64: [IDTF] Failed to initialize FDT from 0x%lx! Hardware discovery compromised.\n", boot_fdt_ptr);
83:        }
84:    } else {
85:        pr_warn("%s", "AArch64: [IDTF] No Hardware Description Tree (DTB) found! System will attempt manual discovery.\n");
86:    }
87:}
88:
89:/*
90: * arch_platform_get_mem_regions - discover and return usable RAM regions.
91: *
92: * Parameters:
93: *   count  Output: number of valid entries in the returned array.
94: * Returns: pointer to the static arch_mem_regions[] array.
95: *
96: * Idempotent: if arch_region_count > 0 the cached result is returned immediately.
97: *
98: * Primary path — FDT memory parse:
99: *   fdt_get_mem_regions() walks the FDT "/memory" nodes and fills arch_mem_regions[].
100: *   On QEMU virt with a DTB, this correctly discovers all RAM (e.g., 3967 MB at
101: *   0x40000000 for "-m 4G").
102: *
103: * Fallback path — manual physical probe (NOTE(ARCH-04), NOTE(ARCH-05)):
104: *   When FDT parse fails or returns 0 regions, the code performs a bus-abort probe:
105: *   - Start at 0x40000000 + 1GB (skip the kernel's own 1GB).
106: *   - Advance in 128MB (0x08000000) steps up to a 128GB ceiling.
107: *   - For each candidate address: set probe_in_progress, attempt a volatile read,
108: *     then check probe_failed (set by sync_handler if a Data Abort fires).
109: *   - Stop when probe_failed is true; found_end is the last successfully read addr.
110: *
111: *   NOTE(ARCH-04): The probe result is written to arch_mem_regions[0] TWICE:
112: *     First write (lines 83–86): base=probe_base, size=found_end-probe_base.
113: *       This is immediately followed by arch_region_count=1 and a pr_info.
114: *     Second write (lines 91–94): base=probe_base, size=(found_end-probe_base-PAGE_SIZE)
115: *       or 0.  This is the effective write; lines 83–86 are dead code.
116: *     The second write also sets arch_region_count=1 redundantly.
117: *     If found_end == probe_base (nothing found), size is set to 0.
118: *
119: *   NOTE(ARCH-05): The probe reads at 128MB intervals from 0x40000000+1GB.
120: *   On QEMU virt this is safe because physical RAM is at 0x40000000 and the
121: *   machine model aborts reads above the configured RAM ceiling.  On real
122: *   hardware some addresses in the range may be device registers; a read can
123: *   cause an unintended side-effect before the abort arrives.
124: */
125:struct mem_region *arch_platform_get_mem_regions(size_t *count) {
126:    if (arch_region_count > 0) {
127:        /* Cached from a previous call; return immediately. */
128:        if (count) *count = arch_region_count;
129:        return arch_mem_regions;
130:    }
131:
132:    if (fdt_get_mem_regions(arch_mem_regions, MAX_CPUS * 2, &arch_region_count) == 0 && arch_region_count > 0) {
133:        /* FDT parse succeeded; log each discovered region. */
134:        for (size_t i = 0; i < arch_region_count; i++) {
135:            pr_info("AArch64: IDTF RAM Region [%zu]: 0x%lx - 0x%lx\n",
136:                    i, arch_mem_regions[i].base, arch_mem_regions[i].base + arch_mem_regions[i].size);
137:        }
138:    } else {
139:        extern volatile bool probe_in_progress;
140:        extern volatile bool probe_failed;
141:
142:        pr_warn("%s", "AArch64: [IDTF] Memory discovery failed! Attempting manual page-by-page probe...\n");
143:
144:        /* Manual Probe Fallback: scan physical RAM in 128MB steps.
145:         * QEMU virt places RAM at 0x40000000; probe_base skips the kernel's 1GB. */
146:        uint64_t probe_base  = 0x40000000UL;
147:        uint64_t probe_limit = 0x40000000UL + (128UL << 30); /* cap at 128GB total */
148:        uint64_t found_end   = probe_base;
149:
150:        for (uint64_t addr = probe_base + (1UL << 30); addr < probe_limit; addr += 0x08000000UL) {
151:            /* Signal sync_handler to recover from an abort at this address. */
152:            probe_in_progress = true;
153:            probe_failed = false;
154:            arch_mb(); /* DSB: ensure flags visible before the load */
155:
156:            /* Issue the probe load; if addr is unmapped, a Data Abort fires.
157:             * sync_handler sets probe_failed=true and increments ELR_EL1 by 4
158:             * to skip this instruction, then returns to the instruction below. */
159:            /* 'addr' is a PHYSICAL address; probe through its direct-map
160:             * VA (identity while KERNEL_VIRT_BASE == 0). */
161:            volatile uint64_t *ptr = (volatile uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(addr);
162:            (void)*ptr;
163:
164:            arch_mb(); /* DSB: ensure probe_failed is current after handler runs */
165:            if (probe_failed) {
166:                probe_in_progress = false;
167:                break; /* addr is unmapped; stop probing */
168:            }
169:
170:            probe_in_progress = false;
171:            found_end = addr; /* addr is mapped; extend found_end */
172:        }
173:
174:        /* NOTE(ARCH-04): Dead write — immediately overwritten by lines 91–94 below.
175:         * The intent was to save the result before applying the PAGE_SIZE safety trim.
176:         * In practice the second write clobbers this unconditionally. */
177:        if (found_end > probe_base) {
178:            arch_mem_regions[0].base = probe_base;
179:            arch_mem_regions[0].size = found_end - probe_base;
180:            arch_mem_regions[0].type = MEM_REGION_USABLE;
181:            arch_region_count = 1;
182:            pr_info("AArch64: Manual discovery found %lu MB RAM\n", arch_mem_regions[0].size / 1024 / 1024);
183:        }
184:
185:        /* Effective write (NOTE(ARCH-04)): subtract PAGE_SIZE to avoid mapping the
186:         * last probed page which may not be fully present.  If found_end == probe_base
187:         * (probe found nothing), size is set to 0. */
188:        arch_mem_regions[0].base = probe_base;
189:        arch_mem_regions[0].size = (found_end > probe_base) ? (found_end - probe_base - PAGE_SIZE) : 0;
190:        arch_mem_regions[0].type = MEM_REGION_USABLE;
191:        arch_region_count = 1;
192:
193:        pr_info("AArch64: Manual probe discovered %lu MB RAM\n", arch_mem_regions[0].size / (1024 * 1024));
194:    }
195:
196:    if (count) *count = arch_region_count;
197:    return arch_mem_regions;
198:}
199:extern void *arch_secondary_stacks[MAX_CPUS];
200:extern void kernel_secondary_main(void);
201:
202:/*
203: * arch_smp_init - wake and synchronise all secondary CPUs.
204: *
205: * Called by kernel_main() after the primary CPU's scheduler is ready.
206: *
207: * Sequence:
208: *   1. Publish the current TTBR0_EL1 (kernel PGD) to secondary_ttbr0 via
209: *      arch_vmm_set_secondary_pgd().  Secondaries read this in secondary_startup
210: *      (start.S:159-161) before enabling their MMU.  The cache clean in
211: *      arch_vmm_set_secondary_pgd ensures secondaries see the correct value.
212: *   2. Query FDT for CPU count (fdt_count_cpus).  Falls back to a small cap if
213: *      FDT reports 0 (e.g., no FDT or FDT without cpu nodes).
214: *   3. Pre-allocate kernel stacks for all CPUs via arch_smp_setup_stacks().
215: *      This must be done before any CPU is woken to avoid races on the stack
216: *      array.
217: *   4. For each secondary CPU i (1 .. cpu_count-1): obtain/allocate its stack
218: *      top, then hand off to smp_bringup_secondary() (kernel/core/smp.c) —
219: *      the shared arch-neutral primitive that owns the idle-task-first
220: *      invariant (#169/#170), the PSCI wake via arch_cpu_wake_secondary, and
221: *      the acquire/release ack handshake with a wall-time timeout.  Only the
222: *      per-arch failure POLICY lives here (PSCI failure = remaining CPUs
223: *      absent -> break; ack timeout = skip this CPU, free its dynamic stack).
224: */
225:void arch_smp_init(void) {
226:    /* Publish the KERNEL PGD (TTBR1 root) before waking any secondary CPU.
227:     * secondary_startup (start.S) reads secondary_ttbr1 and loads it into
228:     * TTBR1_EL1; TTBR0 (user half) gets the boot identity tables. */
229:    uint64_t current_pgd = arch_vmm_get_kernel_pgd();
230:    arch_vmm_set_secondary_pgd(current_pgd);
231:
232:    /* Discover CPU count from FDT; fall back to a small sane cap if unavailable.
233:     * Using MAX_CPUS (64) as a fallback would allocate 56 wasted dynamic stacks
234:     * and attempt PSCI CPU_ON for 60 non-existent cores.  Instead, cap at 8 CPUs
235:     * (the maximum supported by the pre-allocated BSS stacks in start.S), which
236:     * avoids any dynamic stack allocation for the fallback path.  If FDT is
237:     * working correctly (x0 set by QEMU -dtb), this branch is never taken. */
238:#define AARCH64_FALLBACK_CPU_CAP 8
239:    uint32_t cpu_count = fdt_count_cpus();
240:    if (cpu_count == 0) {
241:        pr_warn("AArch64: FDT CPU discovery failed, capping at %d cores (fallback)\n",
242:                AARCH64_FALLBACK_CPU_CAP);
243:        cpu_count = AARCH64_FALLBACK_CPU_CAP;
244:    }
245:    if (cpu_count > MAX_CPUS) cpu_count = MAX_CPUS;
246:
247:    pr_info("AArch64: Starting SMP initialization for %u potential cores\n", cpu_count);
248:
249:    /* Pre-allocate kernel stacks for all CPUs before waking any secondary.
250:     * This prevents race conditions on arch_secondary_stacks[] between CPUs. */
251:    arch_smp_setup_stacks(cpu_count);
252:
253:    for (uint32_t i = 1; i < cpu_count; i++) {
254:        void *stack = NULL;
255:        bool allocated = false;
256:
257:        if (i < 8) {
258:            /* CPUs 0..7: use pre-allocated BSS stack slices. */
259:            stack = arch_get_kernel_stack(i);
260:        } else {
261:            /* CPUs 8+: allocate a dynamic 128KB stack from PMM. */
262:            void *ptr = pmm_alloc_pages(131072 / 4096);
263:            if (!ptr) {
264:                pr_err("AArch64: Failed to allocate stack for CPU %d\n", i);
265:                break;
266:            }
267:            /* Stack grows downward; pass the TOP (highest address). */
268:            stack = (void *)((uintptr_t)ptr + 131072);
269:            arch_secondary_stacks[i] = stack;
270:            allocated = true;
271:        }
272:
273:        /* Shared bring-up primitive (S-ALIGN F8, B6 slice): idle-task-first
274:         * (#169/#170) + PSCI CPU_ON + bounded acquire-wait for the ack all
275:         * live in kernel/core/smp.c.  Only the failure POLICY stays here:
276:         * a PSCI failure means the remaining CPUs are absent too (break),
277:         * an ack timeout skips just this CPU. */
278:        int ret = smp_bringup_secondary(
279:            i, (void (*)(void))kernel_secondary_main, stack);
280:
281:        if (ret == 0) {
282:            pr_info("AArch64: CPU %d online\n", i);
283:        } else if (ret == -2) {
284:            pr_warn("AArch64: CPU %d failed to acknowledge boot (timeout)\n", i);
285:            if (allocated) {
286:                /* Reclaim the dynamic stack; ptr = top - 131072. */
287:                pmm_free_pages((void *)((uintptr_t)stack - 131072), 32);
288:                arch_secondary_stacks[i] = 0;
289:            }
290:        } else {
291:            /* PSCI CPU_ON failed (e.g., CPU not present or firmware error). */
292:            if (allocated) {
293:                pmm_free_pages((void *)((uintptr_t)stack - 131072), 32);
294:                arch_secondary_stacks[i] = 0;
295:            }
296:            break; /* assume remaining CPUs are also absent */
297:        }
298:    }
299:}
300:

@@@ kernel/arch/aarch64/virtio.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/aarch64/virtio.c
3: * AArch64 VirtIO MMIO transport layer.
4: *
5: * Role:
6: *   Implements the arch_virtio_* interface for the VirtIO MMIO transport used
7: *   on the QEMU virt AArch64 machine.  Provides:
8: *   - arch_virtio_scan(): enumerates all VirtIO MMIO device slots and populates
9: *     the internal virtio_devices[] table.
10: *   - arch_virtio_get_count() / arch_virtio_get_device(): query the table by
11: *     device type ID (e.g. 2 = block, 1 = net, 9 = GPU).
12: *   - virtio_setup_queue(): programs the MMIO registers to configure a virtqueue
13: *     (VirtIO legacy MMIO spec, version 1).
14: *
15: * Transport ops:
16: *   mmio_ops is a static virtio_transport_ops struct providing read32/write32/notify
17: *   over hal_read32/hal_write32.  Every virtio_device installed by arch_virtio_scan
18: *   points to this single shared ops table.
19: *
20: * MMIO register layout (VirtIO 1.0 MMIO, offsets from device base):
21: *   0x000  MagicValue   (R)  — must be 0x74726976 ("virt").
22: *   0x004  Version      (R)  — 1 = legacy, 2 = modern.
23: *   0x008  DeviceID     (R)  — device type (0 = empty slot).
24: *   0x00C  VendorID     (R)  — 0x554D4551 (QEMU) or 0x1AF4.
25: *   0x020  QueueSel     (W)  — select active queue.
26: *   0x024  QueueNumMax  (R)  — max queue size for selected queue.
27: *   0x028  GuestPageSize(W)  — page size (legacy only; must be 4096 for 4KB).
28: *   0x030  QueuePFN     (W)  — page-frame number of virtqueue (legacy).
29: *   0x050  QueueNotify  (W)  — kick selected queue.
30: *
31: * NOTE: virtio_setup_queue() uses the VirtIO legacy MMIO interface (QueuePFN /
32: * GuestPageSize) rather than the split-queue modern interface.  The avail_addr
33: * and used_addr parameters are silently ignored — they are relevant only for
34: * the modern interface.  This works on QEMU virt because QEMU defaults to
35: * supporting the legacy interface when QueuePFN is used.
36: */
37:#include <arch/arch.h>
38:#include <arch/platform.h>
39:#include <drivers/virtio.h>
40:#include <kernel/hal.h>
41:
42:/*
43: * virtio_devices[] - table of discovered VirtIO MMIO devices.
44: * Populated by arch_virtio_scan(); indexed by discovery order.
45: * Supports up to MAX_VIRTIO_DEVS non-empty device slots.
46: */
47:#define MAX_VIRTIO_DEVS 16
48:static struct virtio_device virtio_devices[MAX_VIRTIO_DEVS];
49:static int virtio_dev_count = 0;
50:
51:/* MMIO Implementation of Transport Ops.
52: * These three functions form the virtio_transport_ops for every MMIO device.
53: * They delegate to hal_read32/hal_write32 which perform a 32-bit MMIO access
54: * at the device's base address + the given register offset. */
55:
56:/* mmio_read32 - read a 32-bit MMIO register from a VirtIO device. */
57:static uint32_t mmio_read32(struct virtio_device *dev, uint32_t offset) {
58:    return hal_read32(dev->base + offset);
59:}
60:
61:/* mmio_write32 - write a 32-bit value to a VirtIO device MMIO register. */
62:static void mmio_write32(struct virtio_device *dev, uint32_t offset, uint32_t val) {
63:    hal_write32(dev->base + offset, val);
64:}
65:
66:/* mmio_notify - kick a virtqueue by writing its index to QUEUE_NOTIFY.
67: * This signals the device that new descriptor chains are available in the
68: * queue's available ring. */
69:static void mmio_notify(struct virtio_device *dev, uint32_t queue_idx) {
70:    mmio_write32(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_NOTIFY, queue_idx);
71:}
72:
73:/* Shared transport ops table; all MMIO devices point here. */
74:static const struct virtio_transport_ops mmio_ops = {
75:    .read32  = mmio_read32,
76:    .write32 = mmio_write32,
77:    .notify  = mmio_notify
78:};
79:
80:/*
81: * arch_virtio_scan - enumerate VirtIO MMIO device slots and fill virtio_devices[].
82: *
83: * Probes VIRTIO_COUNT slots starting at VIRTIO_MMIO_BASE, stepping by
84: * VIRTIO_MMIO_STRIDE bytes per slot.  For each slot:
85: *   - Reads MAGIC_VALUE (offset 0x000); non-matching value → skip.
86: *   - Reads DEVICE_ID  (offset 0x008); 0 → empty slot, skip.
87: *   - Records base, IRQ (48+i), device_id, and mmio_ops into virtio_devices[].
88: *
89: * IRQ: QEMU virt assigns SPI 0..31 to VirtIO MMIO slots 0..31.  GIC SPI 0
90: * corresponds to IRQ 32 in the CPU interrupt numbering; however, QEMU's
91: * virtio-mmio device uses IRQs 48..79 in the kernel's flat IRQ space
92: * (GIC base 32 + platform-specific offset 16).
93: *
94: * Called once from the kernel device initialisation path; not thread-safe.
95: * virtio_dev_count is reset to 0 at the start to support re-scan if needed.
96: */
97:void arch_virtio_scan(void) {
98:    virtio_dev_count = 0;
99:    for (int i = 0; i < VIRTIO_COUNT; i++) {
100:        uintptr_t base = VIRTIO_MMIO_BASE + i * VIRTIO_MMIO_STRIDE;
101:        uint32_t magic = hal_read32(base + VIRTIO_MMIO_MAGIC_VALUE);
102:
103:        if (magic == 0x74726976) { /* "virt" little-endian: slot is a VirtIO device */
104:            uint32_t dev_id = hal_read32(base + VIRTIO_MMIO_DEVICE_ID);
105:            if (dev_id != 0 && virtio_dev_count < MAX_VIRTIO_DEVS) {
106:                virtio_devices[virtio_dev_count].base      = base;
107:                virtio_devices[virtio_dev_count].irq       = 48 + i;
108:                virtio_devices[virtio_dev_count].device_id = dev_id;
109:                virtio_devices[virtio_dev_count].ops       = &mmio_ops;
110:                virtio_dev_count++;
111:            }
112:        }
113:    }
114:}
115:
116:/*
117: * virtio_setup_queue - configure a legacy MMIO virtqueue for the given device.
118: *
119: * Parameters:
120: *   dev        Handle to the VirtIO MMIO device (from arch_virtio_get_device).
121: *   queue_idx  Index of the virtqueue to configure (0 = request queue for blk).
122: *   desc_addr  Physical address of the virtqueue descriptor table.
123: *              The legacy interface combines desc, avail, and used rings in a
124: *              single contiguous buffer at this address; avail_addr and used_addr
125: *              are not used and are silently discarded.
126: *   avail_addr Ignored (legacy MMIO; rings are at fixed offsets from desc_addr).
127: *   used_addr  Ignored (same reason).
128: *
129: * Register sequence (VirtIO 1.0, Section 4.2.3 — legacy MMIO):
130: *   1. Write QueueSel (0x020) = queue_idx: select the target queue.
131: *   2. Write GuestPageSize (0x028) = 4096: inform the device of our page size.
132: *      This is a legacy-only register absent from the modern spec.
133: *   3. Write QueuePFN (0x030) = desc_addr >> 12: the page frame number of the
134: *      virtqueue buffer.  The device uses GuestPageSize to compute ring offsets.
135: *
136: * NOTE: The avail and used ring addresses are derived by the device from
137: * QueuePFN and the queue size, per the legacy spec.  Any mismatch between
138: * what the driver places at desc_addr and what the device computes leads to
139: * silent descriptor corruption.  Callers must lay out the virtqueue exactly
140: * as specified in VirtIO 1.0 Section 2.4 (legacy MMIO layout).
141: */
142:void virtio_setup_queue(virtio_handle_t dev, uint32_t queue_idx, uint64_t desc_addr, uint64_t avail_addr, uint64_t used_addr) {
143:    (void)avail_addr; /* unused: legacy MMIO derives ring offsets from QueuePFN */
144:    (void)used_addr;  /* unused: same reason */
145:    virtio_write_reg(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_SEL, queue_idx);
146:    /* VIRTIO_MMIO_GUEST_PAGE_SIZE is 0x028: tell device page size = 4096. */
147:    hal_write32(dev->base + 0x028, 4096);
148:    /* QueuePFN = physical frame number of the virtqueue buffer.
149:     * desc_addr >> 12 converts from byte address to 4KB page frame number. */
150:    virtio_write_reg(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_PFN, desc_addr >> 12);
151:}
152:
153:/*
154: * arch_virtio_get_count - count devices of a given VirtIO device type ID.
155: *
156: * Parameters:
157: *   device_id  VirtIO device type (e.g. 1=net, 2=block, 9=GPU, 16=input).
158: * Returns: number of devices of that type found by arch_virtio_scan().
159: */
160:int arch_virtio_get_count(uint32_t device_id) {
161:    int count = 0;
162:    for (int i = 0; i < virtio_dev_count; i++) {
163:        if (virtio_devices[i].device_id == device_id) count++;
164:    }
165:    return count;
166:}
167:
168:/*
169: * arch_virtio_get_device - retrieve a specific VirtIO device by type and index.
170: *
171: * Parameters:
172: *   device_id  VirtIO device type ID to search for.
173: *   index      Zero-based index among devices of that type (0 = first found).
174: *   out_dev    Output: pointer to the virtio_device handle, or unchanged if -1.
175: *   out_irq    Output: IRQ number for the device, or unchanged if -1.
176: * Returns: 0 if found, -1 if no device of that type at that index.
177: */
178:/* Device-config access on VirtIO-MMIO: config space is at base+VIRTIO_MMIO_CONFIG
179: * (0x100).  (GFX-DYN-01 F7) */
180:uint32_t virtio_config_read32(virtio_handle_t dev, uint32_t offset) {
181:    return hal_read32(dev->base + VIRTIO_MMIO_CONFIG + offset);
182:}
183:
184:void virtio_config_write32(virtio_handle_t dev, uint32_t offset, uint32_t val) {
185:    hal_write32(dev->base + VIRTIO_MMIO_CONFIG + offset, val);
186:}
187:
188:int arch_virtio_get_device(uint32_t device_id, int index, virtio_handle_t *out_dev, uint32_t *out_irq) {
189:    int current = 0;
190:    for (int i = 0; i < virtio_dev_count; i++) {
191:        if (virtio_devices[i].device_id == device_id) {
192:            if (current == index) {
193:                if (out_dev) *out_dev = &virtio_devices[i];
194:                if (out_irq) *out_irq = virtio_devices[i].irq;
195:                return 0;
196:            }
197:            current++;
198:        }
199:    }
200:    return -1;
201:}
202:

@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/boot/boot.S @@@
1:/*
2: * boot/amd64/boot.S
3: * x86-64 Multiboot2 Boot Entry (GRUB-compatible)
4: *
5: * Enters in 32-bit protected mode (Multiboot2 spec).
6: * - Detects CPU capabilities
7: * - Sets up paging for Long Mode
8: * - Loads complete GDT with user/kernel segments and TSS
9: * - Jumps to 64-bit kernel_main
10: */
11:
12:/* Multiboot2 header constants */
13:.set MB2_MAGIC,        0xE85250D6
14:.set MB2_ARCH_I386,    0
15:.set MB2_HEADER_LEN,   (mb2_header_end - mb2_header)
16:.set MB2_CHECKSUM,     -(MB2_MAGIC + MB2_ARCH_I386 + MB2_HEADER_LEN)
17:
18:/* Paging constants */
19:.set PAGE_PRESENT,  0x01
20:.set PAGE_WRITE,    0x02
21:.set PAGE_SIZE_BIT, 0x80   /* 2MB pages */
22:
23:/* Control Register bits */
24:.set CR0_PE,  (1 << 0)
25:.set CR0_PG,  (1 << 31)
26:.set CR4_PAE, (1 << 5)
27:.set CR4_PGE, (1 << 7)
28:.set EFER_MSR, 0xC0000080
29:.set EFER_LME, (1 << 8)    /* Long Mode Enable */
30:.set EFER_SCE, (1 << 0)    /* System Call Enable */
31:
32:/* CPUID flags for long mode */
33:.set CPUID_LONG_MODE_BIT, (1 << 29)
34:
35:/* GDT selector indices */
36:.set KERNEL_CODE_SEL, 0x08
37:.set KERNEL_DATA_SEL, 0x10
38:.set USER_DATA_SEL,   0x18
39:.set USER_CODE_SEL,   0x20
40:.set TSS_SEL,         0x28
41:
42:/* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
43:   MULTIBOOT2 HEADER (must be in first 32KB of the binary)
44:   ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
45:
46:.section .multiboot2, "a"
47:.align 8
48:mb2_header:
49:    .long MB2_MAGIC
50:    .long MB2_ARCH_I386
51:    .long MB2_HEADER_LEN
52:    .long MB2_CHECKSUM
53:    /* End tag */
54:    .word 0    /* type */
55:    .word 0    /* flags */
56:    .long 8    /* size */
57:mb2_header_end:
58:
59:/* ─── MULTIBOOT1 HEADER (for QEMU -kernel) ─── */
60:.set MB1_MAGIC,    0x1BADB002
61:.set MB1_FLAGS,    (1 << 0) | (1 << 1) /* ALIGN + MEMINFO */
62:.set MB1_CHECKSUM, -(MB1_MAGIC + MB1_FLAGS)
63:
64:.section .multiboot, "a"
65:.align 4
66:    .long MB1_MAGIC
67:    .long MB1_FLAGS
68:    .long MB1_CHECKSUM
69:
70:/* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
71:   32-BIT ENTRY POINT
72:   ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
73:
74:.section .text.boot
75:.code32
76:.global _start
77:_start:
78:    /* Disable interrupts */
79:    cli
80:
81:    /* Save multiboot info pointer (EBX) and magic (EAX) */
82:    movl %ebx, (mb_info_ptr)
83:    movl %eax, (mb_magic)
84:
85:    /* Set up temporary 32-bit stack */
86:    movl $_stack_top, %esp
87:
88:    /* Clear BSS */
89:    movl $_bss_start, %edi
90:    movl $_bss_end, %ecx
91:    subl %edi, %ecx
92:    shrl $2, %ecx
93:    xorl %eax, %eax
94:    rep stosl
95:
96:    /* ─── CPU Detection: Check for Long Mode support ─── */
97:    movl $0x80000001, %eax
98:    cpuid
99:    testl $CPUID_LONG_MODE_BIT, %edx
100:    jz .cpu_error
101:
102:    /* ─── Setup Identity-Mapped Paging for Long Mode ─── */
103:
104:    /* PML4[0] -> PDPT */
105:    movl $boot_pml4, %eax
106:    orl  $(PAGE_PRESENT | PAGE_WRITE), %eax
107:    movl %eax, (boot_pml4 + 0)
108:
109:    /* PDPT[0] -> PD */
110:    movl $boot_pd, %eax
111:    orl  $(PAGE_PRESENT | PAGE_WRITE), %eax
112:    movl %eax, (boot_pdpt + 0)
113:
114:    /* PD: Identity map first 1GB with 2MB pages (512 entries) */
115:    movl $boot_pd, %edi
116:    movl $(PAGE_PRESENT | PAGE_WRITE | PAGE_SIZE_BIT), %eax
117:    movl $512, %ecx
118:.fill_pd:
119:    movl %eax, (%edi)
120:    movl $0, 4(%edi)
121:    addl $0x200000, %eax    /* Next 2MB page */
122:    addl $8, %edi
123:    decl %ecx
124:    jnz .fill_pd
125:
126:    /* ─── Enable PAE ─── */
127:    movl %cr4, %eax
128:    orl  $(CR4_PAE | CR4_PGE), %eax
129:    movl %eax, %cr4
130:
131:    /* ─── Load PML4 into CR3 ─── */
132:    movl $boot_pml4, %eax
133:    movl %eax, %cr3
134:
135:    /* ─── Enable Long Mode via IA32_EFER MSR ─── */
136:    movl $EFER_MSR, %ecx
137:    rdmsr
138:    orl  $(EFER_LME | EFER_SCE), %eax
139:    wrmsr
140:
141:    /* ─── Enable Paging (CR0.PG) ─── */
142:    movl %cr0, %eax
143:    orl  $(CR0_PG | CR0_PE), %eax
144:    movl %eax, %cr0
145:
146:    /* ─── Load 64-bit GDT and far jump to Long Mode ─── */
147:    lgdt (boot_gdtr)
148:    ljmp $KERNEL_CODE_SEL, $long_mode_entry
149:
150:/* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
151:   ERROR HANDLING
152:   ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
153:
154:.cpu_error:
155:    /* CPU doesn't support long mode - halt */
156:    cli
157:.cpu_error_loop:
158:    hlt
159:    jmp .cpu_error_loop
160:
161:/* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
162:   64-BIT ENTRY
163:   ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
164:
165:.code64
166:long_mode_entry:
167:    /* Reload data segments */
168:    movw $KERNEL_DATA_SEL, %ax
169:    movw %ax, %ds
170:    movw %ax, %es
171:    movw %ax, %fs
172:    movw %ax, %gs
173:    movw %ax, %ss
174:
175:    /* Set up 64-bit stack */
176:    movabs $_stack_top, %rsp
177:
178:    /* Load multiboot info pointer as first argument (RDI) to kernel_main */
179:    movl (mb_info_ptr), %edi
180:
181:    /* Clear direction flag */
182:    cld
183:
184:    /* Call kernel_main(uint32_t mb_info_ptr) */
185:    call kernel_main
186:
187:    /* If kernel_main returns, halt */
188:    cli
189:.halt_loop:
190:    hlt
191:    jmp .halt_loop
192:
193:/* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
194:   BOOT DATA
195:   ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
196:
197:.section .data
198:
199:/* Saved multiboot pointers */
200:.global mb_info_ptr
201:.global mb_magic
202:mb_info_ptr: .long 0
203:mb_magic:    .long 0
204:
205:/* ─── 64-bit GDT with kernel/user segments and TSS ─── */
206:.align 16
207:boot_gdt:
208:    .quad 0x0000000000000000   /* 0x00: Null */
209:    .quad 0x00AF9A000000FFFF   /* 0x08: Kernel Code (64-bit, DPL=0) */
210:    .quad 0x00CF92000000FFFF   /* 0x10: Kernel Data (DPL=0) */
211:    .quad 0x00CFF2000000FFFF   /* 0x18: User Data (DPL=3) */
212:    .quad 0x00AFFA000000FFFF   /* 0x20: User Code (DPL=3) */
213:    /* 0x28: TSS (16 bytes in 64-bit mode - will be filled by kernel) */
214:    .quad 0x0000000000000000
215:    .quad 0x0000000000000000
216:boot_gdt_end:
217:
218:boot_gdtr:
219:    .word boot_gdt_end - boot_gdt - 1
220:    .quad boot_gdt
221:
222:/* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
223:   PAGE TABLES (BSS — zeroed)
224:   ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
225:
226:.section .bss
227:.align 4096
228:
229:.global boot_pml4
230:boot_pml4:   .skip 4096
231:boot_pdpt:   .skip 4096
232:boot_pd:     .skip 4096
233:
234:/* Kernel stack (128 KB) */
235:.align 4096
236:.global _stack_bottom
237:_stack_bottom:
238:    .skip 0x20000   /* 128 KB */
239:.global _stack_top
240:_stack_top:
241:

@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/boot/stage1.S @@@
1:/*
2: * boot/amd64/stage1.S
3: * AMD64 Bootloader - Stage 1 (32-bit)
4: * Parity with aarch64 implementation
5: */
6:
7:.code32
8:.section .text
9:
10:.global _start
11:_start:
12:    /* Disable interrupts */
13:    cli
14:
15:    /* Save multiboot info */
16:    movl %ebx, (multiboot_info_ptr)
17:    movl %eax, (multiboot_magic)
18:
19:    /* Setup 32-bit stack */
20:    movl $__boot_stack_top, %esp
21:
22:    /* 1. Parse Multiboot2 Info */
23:    call parse_multiboot2_info
24:
25:    /* 2. CPU Check: Long Mode Support */
26:    movl $0x80000001, %eax
27:    cpuid
28:    testl $(1 << 29), %edx
29:    jz .no_long_mode
30:
31:    /* 3. Setup Paging (Identity Map 1GB) */
32:    movl $page_table_l4, %edi
33:    xorl %eax, %eax
34:    movl $4096, %ecx
35:    rep stosl
36:
37:    /* PML4[0] -> PDP */
38:    movl $page_table_l4, %edi
39:    movl $page_table_l3, %eax
40:    orl  $0x3, %eax
41:    movl %eax, (%edi)
42:
43:    /* PDP[0] -> PD */
44:    movl $page_table_l3, %edi
45:    movl $page_table_l2, %eax
46:    orl  $0x3, %eax
47:    movl %eax, (%edi)
48:
49:    /* PD -> 2MB Pages */
50:    movl $page_table_l2, %edi
51:    movl $0x83, %eax
52:    movl $512, %ecx
53:.fill_pd:
54:    movl %eax, (%edi)
55:    addl $0x200000, %eax
56:    addl $8, %edi
57:    loop .fill_pd
58:
59:    /* 4. Enable PAE */
60:    movl %cr4, %eax
61:    orl  $(1 << 5), %eax
62:    movl %eax, %cr4
63:
64:    /* 5. Load PML4 */
65:    movl $page_table_l4, %eax
66:    movl %eax, %cr3
67:
68:    /* 6. Enable Long Mode */
69:    movl $0xC0000080, %ecx
70:    rdmsr
71:    orl  $(1 << 8), %eax
72:    wrmsr
73:
74:    /* 7. Enable Paging */
75:    movl %cr0, %eax
76:    orl  $(1 << 31), %eax
77:    movl %eax, %cr0
78:
79:    /* 8. Jump to stage2 (64-bit) */
80:    lgdt (boot_gdtr)
81:    ljmp $0x08, $stage2_entry_trampoline
82:
83:.no_long_mode:
84:    hlt
85:    jmp .no_long_mode
86:
87:/* Multiboot2 Parser */
88:parse_multiboot2_info:
89:    movl (multiboot_info_ptr), %ebx
90:    testl %ebx, %ebx
91:    jz .parse_done
92:
93:    /* Skip total size and reserved */
94:    addl $8, %ebx
95:    
96:.parse_loop:
97:    movl (%ebx), %eax        /* type */
98:    movl 4(%ebx), %ecx       /* size */
99:    
100:    testl %eax, %eax         /* end tag? */
101:    jz .parse_done
102:    
103:    cmpl $9, %eax            /* ENTRY_ADDRESS tag? */
104:    jne .next_tag
105:    
106:    /* Found Entry Address */
107:    movl 8(%ebx), %eax
108:    movl %eax, (kernel_entry_point)
109:    
110:.next_tag:
111:    addl $7, %ecx            /* align to 8 bytes */
112:    andl $0xfffffff8, %ecx
113:    addl %ecx, %ebx
114:    jmp .parse_loop
115:
116:.parse_done:
117:    ret
118:
119:.section .data
120:.align 4
121:.global multiboot_info_ptr
122:.global multiboot_magic
123:.global kernel_entry_point
124:multiboot_info_ptr:  .long 0
125:multiboot_magic:     .long 0
126:kernel_entry_point: .quad 0
127:
128:.section .bss
129:.align 4096
130:page_table_l4: .skip 4096
131:page_table_l3: .skip 4096
132:page_table_l2: .skip 4096
133:__boot_stack:  .skip 16384
134:__boot_stack_top:
135:
136:.section .rodata
137:.align 16
138:boot_gdt:
139:    .quad 0x0000000000000000
140:    .quad 0x00AF9A000000FFFF
141:    .quad 0x00CF92000000FFFF
142:boot_gdt_end:
143:
144:boot_gdtr:
145:    .word boot_gdt_end - boot_gdt - 1
146:    .quad boot_gdt
147:

@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/boot/stage2.S @@@
1:/*
2: * boot/amd64/stage2.S
3: * AMD64 Bootloader - Stage 2 (64-bit)
4: * Parity with aarch64 implementation
5: */
6:
7:.code64
8:.section .text
9:
10:.global stage2_entry_trampoline
11:stage2_entry_trampoline:
12:    /* Reload segments */
13:    movw $0x10, %ax
14:    movw %ax, %ds
15:    movw %ax, %es
16:    movw %ax, %fs
17:    movw %ax, %gs
18:    movw %ax, %ss
19:

22:
23:    /* Setup kernel environment */
24:    call setup_kernel_environment

42:    /* Minimal for now, parity with aarch64 */

@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/cpu/apic.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/amd64/cpu/apic.c
3: * Local APIC (LAPIC) Initialization, EOI, IPI, and Timer Calibration
4: *
5: * Responsibilities:
6: *   - Enable the LAPIC via IA32_APIC_BASE MSR (bit 11 = APIC global enable).
7: *   - Set the Spurious Interrupt Vector Register (SVR) to enable the LAPIC
8: *     and assign vector 0xFF as the spurious vector.
9: *   - Configure LINT0 as ExtINT to forward legacy 8259 PIC interrupts when no
10: *     I/O APIC is present.
11: *   - Provide lapic_eoi() for hardware interrupt acknowledgement.
12: *   - Provide lapic_send_ipi() for inter-processor interrupts (SMP startup,
13: *     future TLB shootdown, etc.).
14: *   - Calibrate the LAPIC timer against the 8254 PIT to determine
15: *     ticks_per_ms, then set up a periodic timer at a given HZ rate.
16: *
17: * Invariants:
18: *   - LAPIC registers are accessed via lapic_read/lapic_write (defined in
19: *     arch/amd64/apic.h) using the memory-mapped register window at
20: *     LAPIC_DEFAULT_BASE (0xFEE00000), which must be identity-mapped before
21: *     this file's functions are called.
22: *   - ticks_per_ms is set once by lapic_timer_calibrate() and never cleared;
23: *     the guard 'if (ticks_per_ms != 0) return' makes calibration idempotent.
24: *
25: * Known issues:
26: *   EXC-AMD64-03 RESOLVED (Phase A step 14): the double-tick hazard came
27: *     from the PIT being left free-running (mode 2) after calibration while
28: *     LINT0 ExtINT can deliver PIC IRQ 0 on vector 32 — the same vector as
29: *     the LAPIC periodic timer.  lapic_timer_calibrate() now halts the PIT
30: *     (mode-0 control word, no count) before the LAPIC timer starts; PIC
31: *     IRQ 0 additionally stays masked (pic_init).  LINT0 remains ExtINT on
32: *     purpose: it is the only delivery path for legacy PIC lines (PCI INTx).
33: */
34:#include <arch/amd64/apic.h>
35:#include <kernel/printk.h>
36:#include <kernel/arch.h>
37:#include <kernel/cpu.h>
38:#include <drivers/timer.h>
39:#include <arch/amd64_internal.h>
40:
41:/* ticks_per_ms: LAPIC timer decrements per millisecond at LAPIC_TIMER_DIV16.
42: * Set by lapic_timer_calibrate(); used by lapic_timer_setup() and udelay(). */
43:uint32_t ticks_per_ms = 0;
44:
45:/* tsc_hz: measured TSC frequency in counts/second (docs/TIMER-MODEL.md §1).
46: * This is the real-time reference the whole 3-tier clock is built on:
47: * arch_impl_timer_get_freq() (arch/arch.h) returns it, and the arch-neutral
48: * mono_ns() in kernel/core/timer.c divides the free-running RDTSC by it.
49: *
50: * Set ONCE on the BSP by tsc_calibrate() (called from lapic_timer_calibrate())
51: * against the same 8254 PIT window the LAPIC timer is calibrated with.  Until
52: * that runs, arch_impl_timer_get_freq() returns a safe 1 GHz fallback so early
53: * callers never divide by zero; tsc_calibrate() then publishes the real value.
54: * The 0 sentinel makes calibration idempotent (APs reuse the BSP value; the
55: * invariant/constant TSC of the QEMU targets makes that correct). */
56:uint64_t tsc_hz = 0;
57:
58:/*
59: * lapic_init - enable and configure the LAPIC for the calling CPU.
60: *
61: * Steps:
62: *   1. Read IA32_APIC_BASE (MSR 0x1B); set bit 11 (AEN) if not already set.
63: *   2. Write SVR: set Enable bit (bit 8) and spurious vector 0xFF.
64: *   3. Configure LINT0 as ExtINT (delivery mode 0x700, not masked) so the
65: *      legacy 8259 PIC can deliver its IRQs via the LAPIC when no I/O APIC
66: *      is present.
67: *
68: * NOTE(EXC-AMD64-03, resolved): the PIT is halted after calibration and PIC
69: * IRQ 0 stays masked, so vector 32 only ever comes from the LAPIC timer.
70: *
71: * The 'outb L' at the start is a debug breadcrumb on COM1 serial port
72: * (0x3F8 = COM1 data register).
73: */
74:void lapic_init(void) {
75:    /* Debug: Print 'L' using %dx for 16-bit port */
76:    __asm__ __volatile__("movw $0x3f8, %%dx; movb $'L', %%al; outb %%al, %%dx" ::: "ax", "dx");
77:
78:    /* Ensure APIC is enabled in MSR (bit 11 = APIC global enable) */
79:    uint64_t apic_msr = rdmsr(0x1B); /* IA32_APIC_BASE */
80:    if (!(apic_msr & 0x800)) {
81:        wrmsr(0x1B, apic_msr | 0x800);
82:    }
83:
84:    /* Set Spurious Interrupt Vector (0xFF) and enable LAPIC (SVR bit 8) */
85:    lapic_write(LAPIC_SVR, lapic_read(LAPIC_SVR) | 0xFF | LAPIC_SVR_ENABLE);
86:
87:    /* Configure LINT0 for ExtINT (Legacy PIC) — necessary if no IOAPIC is used.
88:     * Delivery mode 0x700 = ExtINT; not masked (bit 16 = 0).
89:     * NOTE(EXC-AMD64-03, resolved): PIC IRQ 0 could reach vector 32 through
90:     * here, but the PIT is halted after calibration and IRQ 0 stays masked. */
91:    lapic_write(LAPIC_LVT_LINT0, 0x00000700); /* ExtINT, not masked */
92:
93:    pr_info("AMD64: LAPIC %u initialized at 0x%lx\n", lapic_get_id(), LAPIC_DEFAULT_BASE);
94:}
95:
96:/*
97: * lapic_eoi - signal end-of-interrupt to the local APIC.
98: *
99: * Must be called after every hardware IRQ vector (32-255) is serviced.  The
100: * LAPIC will not deliver further interrupts at the same or lower priority until
101: * the EOI write completes.  Writing any value (here 0) to LAPIC_EOI suffices.
102: *
103: * Called from amd64_isr_dispatch after each hardware interrupt handler.
104: * Does NOT satisfy the 8259 PIC EOI for legacy vectors 32-47; idt.c calls
105: * pic_send_eoi() separately for those.
106: */
107:void lapic_eoi(void) {
108:    lapic_write(LAPIC_EOI, 0);
109:}
110:
111:/*
112: * lapic_get_id - return the LAPIC ID of the calling CPU.
113: *
114: * The LAPIC ID register bits [31:24] hold the 8-bit APIC ID.  Used to index
115: * cpu_data[] and to address IPIs.
116: */
117:uint32_t lapic_get_id(void) {
118:    return lapic_read(LAPIC_ID) >> 24;
119:}
120:
121:/*
122: * lapic_send_ipi - send an inter-processor interrupt.
123: *
124: * Params:
125: *   lapic_id - destination APIC ID (placed in ICR_HIGH bits [31:24]).
126: *   flags    - ICR_LOW encoding (vector, delivery mode, level, trigger, dest).
127: *
128: * Spins on ICR_LOW.ICR_SEND_PENDING (bit 12) before writing to ensure any
129: * previous IPI has been accepted by the interconnect.  The write to ICR_HIGH
130: * must precede the write to ICR_LOW because the latter triggers the IPI.
131: *
132: * Used by arch_cpu_wake_secondary in platform.c for INIT-SIPI sequence.
133: * NOTE(BOOT-03): platform.c sends only a single STARTUP IPI; the SDM
134: * recommends INIT + two SIPIs for reliability.
135: */
136:void lapic_send_ipi(uint32_t lapic_id, uint32_t flags) {
137:    /* Wait for previous IPI to complete (ICR_SEND_PENDING bit must be clear) */
138:    while (lapic_read(LAPIC_ICR_LOW) & ICR_SEND_PENDING) {
139:        arch_yield();
140:    }
141:
142:    lapic_write(LAPIC_ICR_HIGH, lapic_id << 24); /* destination APIC ID */
143:    lapic_write(LAPIC_ICR_LOW, flags);            /* triggers IPI delivery */
144:}
145:
146:/* PIT Constants for calibration */
147:#ifndef PIT_CH0
148:#define PIT_CH0 0x40 /* I/O port: 8254 PIT Channel 0 counter */
149:#endif /* PIT_CH0 */
150:#ifndef PIT_CMD
151:#define PIT_CMD 0x43 /* I/O port: 8254 PIT command/mode register */
152:#endif /* PIT_CMD */
153:
154:/*
155: * rdtsc64 - read the 64-bit Time Stamp Counter.
156: *
157: * Returns the current TSC value (EDX:EAX).  This is the same free-running
158: * counter arch_impl_timer_get_count() exposes; sampled here across a known
159: * PIT window to derive its frequency.
160: *
161: * IRQ context: safe (plain register read, no side effects).
162: */
163:static inline uint64_t rdtsc64(void) {
164:    uint32_t lo, hi;
165:    __asm__ __volatile__("rdtsc" : "=a"(lo), "=d"(hi));
166:    return ((uint64_t)hi << 32) | lo;
167:}
168:
169:/*
170: * tsc_calibrate - measure the TSC frequency against the 8254 PIT.
171: *
172: * Critical for docs/TIMER-MODEL.md §1: until this runs,
173: * arch_impl_timer_get_freq() returns a hardcoded 1 GHz fallback and every
174: * derived clock (mono_ns, jiffies reconciliation, nanosleep deadlines) is
175: * wrong.  This publishes the *measured* TSC rate into the global tsc_hz.
176: *
177: * Algorithm (mirrors lapic_timer_calibrate's PIT-window technique):
178: *   1. Program PIT Channel 0 in Rate Generator mode (mode 2), count 0xFFFF.
179: *   2. Sample RDTSC, then busy-poll the PIT until it has counted down by
180: *      11932 ticks (11932 / 1193.18 kHz ≈ 10 ms), then sample RDTSC again.
181: *   3. tsc_hz = (tsc_end - tsc_start) * 100  (the 10 ms window is 1/100 s).
182: *   4. Halt the PIT (mode-0 control word, no count) so its IRQ0 line stays
183: *      quiet — same EXC-AMD64-03 hazard lapic_timer_calibrate() guards.
184: *
185: * Idempotent: returns immediately if tsc_hz is already non-zero.  Called once
186: * on the BSP from lapic_timer_calibrate() (before the LAPIC timer starts);
187: * APs reuse the published value (constant/invariant TSC assumed on the QEMU
188: * targets — CPUID 0x80000007 EDX[8] is checked and a warning logged when the
189: * TSC is *not* advertised invariant, but calibration proceeds regardless).
190: *
191: * All math is native 64-bit: the multiply by 100 cannot overflow for any sane
192: * host TSC (a 184-EHz TSC would be needed to wrap), and there is no 128-bit
193: * division — the toolchain links with no libgcc, so __udivti3 is unavailable.
194: *
195: * Locking: none; BSP-only, before SMP.  IRQ context: NO (busy-polls ~10 ms
196: * with the PIT; must run with the timer IRQ not yet started).
197: */
198:void tsc_calibrate(void) {
199:    if (tsc_hz != 0) return;
200:
201:    /* Invariant-TSC advisory (CPUID 0x80000007 EDX bit 8).  When clear, the
202:     * TSC may change rate with P-states / deep C-states and the single BSP
203:     * calibration shared by all APs is theoretically unsafe.  QEMU advertises
204:     * invariant TSC; we still proceed if it does not, but warn loudly. */
205:    {
206:        uint32_t eax, ebx, ecx, edx;
207:        __asm__ __volatile__("cpuid"
208:                             : "=a"(eax), "=b"(ebx), "=c"(ecx), "=d"(edx)
209:                             : "a"(0x80000000U));
210:        if (eax >= 0x80000007U) {
211:            __asm__ __volatile__("cpuid"
212:                                 : "=a"(eax), "=b"(ebx), "=c"(ecx), "=d"(edx)
213:                                 : "a"(0x80000007U));
214:            if (!(edx & (1U << 8))) {
215:                pr_info("TSC: WARNING — invariant TSC not advertised "
216:                        "(CPUID 80000007 EDX[8]=0); using shared BSP "
217:                        "calibration anyway\n");
218:            }
219:        }
220:    }
221:
222:    pr_info("TSC: Calibrating against PIT...\n");
223:
224:    /* Program PIT Channel 0: lobyte/hibyte access, Rate Generator (mode 2). */
225:    outb(PIT_CMD, 0x34);
226:    outb(PIT_CH0, 0xFF); /* low byte of initial count  */
227:    outb(PIT_CH0, 0xFF); /* high byte of initial count */
228:
229:    uint16_t start_tick = 0xFFFF;
230:
231:    uint64_t tsc_start = rdtsc64();
232:
233:    /* Busy-poll PIT until it has ticked down by 11932 counts (~10 ms). */
234:    uint16_t current_tick;
235:    do {
236:        outb(PIT_CMD, 0x00); /* latch Channel 0 count */
237:        current_tick = inb(PIT_CH0);
238:        current_tick |= (inb(PIT_CH0) << 8);
239:    } while ((uint16_t)(start_tick - current_tick) < 11932);
240:
241:    uint64_t tsc_end = rdtsc64();
242:
243:    /* 10 ms window → multiply the delta by 100 to get counts per second. */
244:    tsc_hz = (tsc_end - tsc_start) * 100UL;
245:
246:    /* Halt the PIT (mode 0, no count loaded) so its IRQ0 line stays quiet —
247:     * same EXC-AMD64-03 double-tick hazard lapic_timer_calibrate() guards. */
248:    outb(PIT_CMD, 0x30);
249:
250:    pr_info("TSC: Calibrated: %lu Hz (%lu MHz)\n", tsc_hz, tsc_hz / 1000000UL);
251:}
252:
253:/*
254: * lapic_timer_calibrate - determine LAPIC timer frequency using the PIT.
255: *
256: * Algorithm:
257: *   1. Program the PIT Channel 0 in Rate Generator mode (mode 2) with
258: *      count 0xFFFF (the maximum, ~54.9 ms at 1.19318 MHz PIT clock).
259: *   2. Set LAPIC timer divisor to /16 and initial count to 0xFFFFFFFF.
260: *   3. Busy-poll the PIT current count until it has decreased by 11932 ticks
261: *      (11932 / 1193.18 kHz ≈ 10 ms).
262: *   4. The LAPIC ticks elapsed = 0xFFFFFFFF - LAPIC_TCC.
263: *   5. ticks_per_ms = elapsed / 10.
264: *
265: * The calibration is idempotent: if ticks_per_ms is already non-zero the
266: * function returns immediately.  BSP calls this once in arch_timer_init();
267: * APs do not re-calibrate (ticks_per_ms is a shared global — no race since
268: * APs start after BSP calibration completes).
269: *
270: * NOTE(ARCH-03): timer_get_us() (platform.c) uses jiffies*1000 rather than
271: * the calibrated LAPIC TCC, so the microsecond timestamp is inaccurate.
272: */
273:void lapic_timer_calibrate(void) {
274:    if (ticks_per_ms != 0) return;
275:
276:    /* Measure the TSC frequency first (docs/TIMER-MODEL.md §1): this must be
277:     * published into tsc_hz before the LAPIC timer starts, because the
278:     * arch-neutral mono_ns()/jiffies reconciliation begins on the first tick.
279:     * Idempotent and BSP-only — its own ~10 ms PIT window runs before the one
280:     * below, both with the timer IRQ still off. */
281:    tsc_calibrate();
282:
283:    pr_info("LAPIC: Calibrating timer against PIT...\n");
284:
285:    /* Program PIT Channel 0: lobyte/hibyte access, Rate Generator (mode 2) */
286:    outb(PIT_CMD, 0x34); /* Channel 0, lobyte/hibyte, rate generator (Mode 2) */
287:    outb(PIT_CH0, 0xFF); /* low byte of initial count */
288:    outb(PIT_CH0, 0xFF); /* high byte of initial count */
289:
290:    /* Set LAPIC Timer to Divide by 16 */
291:    lapic_write(LAPIC_TDCR, LAPIC_TIMER_DIV16);
292:
293:    /* Record PIT start count (conceptually 0xFFFF; actual read not stored) */
294:    uint16_t start_tick = 0xFFFF;
295:
296:    /* Start LAPIC Timer with maximum initial count */
297:    lapic_write(LAPIC_TIC, 0xFFFFFFFF);
298:
299:    /* Busy-poll PIT until it has ticked down by 11932 counts (~10 ms).
300:     * PIT latch command (0x00 to PIT_CMD) freezes the counter for reading;
301:     * two reads from PIT_CH0 give the 16-bit current count (lo then hi). */
302:    uint16_t current_tick;
303:    do {
304:        outb(PIT_CMD, 0x00); /* Latch Channel 0 count */
305:        current_tick = inb(PIT_CH0);
306:        current_tick |= (inb(PIT_CH0) << 8);
307:    } while ((start_tick - current_tick) < 11932);
308:
309:    /* Read LAPIC Timer current count; elapsed = initial - current */
310:    uint32_t ticks = 0xFFFFFFFF - lapic_read(LAPIC_TCC);
311:    ticks_per_ms = ticks / 10; /* elapsed in 10 ms → convert to per-ms */
312:
313:    /* FIX(EXC-AMD64-03): silence the PIT now that calibration is done.
314:     * Mode 2 left the counter free-running, pulsing the IRQ0 line forever;
315:     * vector 32 must come from the LAPIC periodic timer ONLY.  Writing the
316:     * mode-0 control word without loading a count halts the counter (the
317:     * 8254 waits for a count after a control-word write), so the line stays
318:     * quiet even if PIC IRQ0 were ever unmasked.  LINT0 stays ExtINT — it is
319:     * the delivery path for every legacy PIC line (PCI INTx included) and
320:     * must NOT be masked. */
321:    outb(PIT_CMD, 0x30); /* channel 0, lobyte/hibyte, mode 0, no count loaded */
322:
323:    pr_info("LAPIC: Timer calibrated: %u ticks per ms\n", ticks_per_ms);
324:}
325:
326:/*
327: * lapic_timer_setup - start the LAPIC periodic timer at hz interrupts/second.
328: *
329: * Ensures calibration has run (calls lapic_timer_calibrate if needed).
330: * Programs LVT timer register with vector 32, periodic mode, divisor /16.
331: * Sets the initial count to ticks_per_ms * (1000/hz).
332: *
333: * NOTE(EXC-AMD64-03, resolved): by the time this runs the PIT has been
334: * halted by lapic_timer_calibrate(), so vector 32 has a single source.
335: *
336: * Params:
337: *   hz - desired interrupt frequency (e.g. HZ = 1000 for 1 kHz timer).
338: */
339:void lapic_timer_setup(uint32_t hz) {
340:    if (ticks_per_ms == 0) {
341:        lapic_timer_calibrate();
342:    }
343:
344:    /* Stop current timer before reconfiguring */
345:    lapic_timer_stop();
346:
347:    /* Set up LAPIC Timer for periodic interrupts.
348:     * Vector 32 (IRQ 0 equivalent), periodic mode (LAPIC_LVT_PERIODIC).
349:     * NOTE(EXC-AMD64-03): same vector 32 as LAPIC LINT0 ExtINT path. */
350:    lapic_write(LAPIC_LVT_TIMER, 32 | LAPIC_LVT_PERIODIC);
351:    lapic_write(LAPIC_TDCR, LAPIC_TIMER_DIV16);
352:
353:    /* Calculate ticks per interrupt: at hz=1000, interval_ms=1 */
354:    uint32_t interval_ms = 1000 / hz;
355:    lapic_write(LAPIC_TIC, ticks_per_ms * interval_ms);
356:
357:    /* Seed the Tier-2 per-CPU software schedule via the arch-neutral, HAL-driven
358:     * timer_percpu_arm() (kernel/core/timer.c), exactly as aarch64's
359:     * timer_init_percpu() does. The vector-32 ISR then calls timer_percpu_tick()
360:     * to advance it against the free-running TSC so a starved core recovers lost
361:     * time. arch_timer_set_compare() inside is a no-op (LAPIC is periodic). */
362:    timer_percpu_arm(get_cpu_info());
363:
364:    pr_info("LAPIC: CPU %u timer started at %u Hz (%u ticks/interval)\n",
365:            lapic_get_id(), hz, ticks_per_ms * interval_ms);
366:}
367:
368:/*
369: * lapic_timer_stop - mask and zero the LAPIC timer.
370: *
371: * Sets LAPIC_LVT_MASKED in the LVT timer entry (bit 16 = mask) and writes 0
372: * to LAPIC_TIC (initial count register) to halt the countdown.  Called by
373: * lapic_timer_setup() before reconfiguring the timer.
374: */
375:void lapic_timer_stop(void) {
376:    lapic_write(LAPIC_LVT_TIMER, LAPIC_LVT_MASKED); /* mask timer LVT entry */
377:    lapic_write(LAPIC_TIC, 0);                       /* stop countdown */
378:}
379:

@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/cpu/context.S @@@
1:/* ============================================================
2: * kernel/arch/amd64/cpu/context.S — x86-64 Context Switch & User Mode
3: * ============================================================ */
4:
5:.section .text
6:
7:/*
8: * void ctx_switch(void *from_ctx, void *to_ctx)
9: * Ctx_amd64 layout: rbx, rbp, r12-r15, rsp, rip
10: */
11:.global ctx_switch
12:ctx_switch:
13:    /* Save callee-saved registers of current process */
14:    movq  %rbx,  0(%rdi)
15:    movq  %rbp,  8(%rdi)
16:    movq  %r12, 16(%rdi)
17:    movq  %r13, 24(%rdi)
18:    movq  %r14, 32(%rdi)
19:    movq  %r15, 40(%rdi)
20:    /* Save RSP */
21:    movq  %rsp, 48(%rdi)
22:    /* Save RIP */
23:    movq  (%rsp), %rax
24:    movq  %rax, 56(%rdi)
25:
26:    /* Restore callee-saved registers of next process */
27:    movq  0(%rsi),  %rbx
28:    movq  8(%rsi),  %rbp
29:    movq  16(%rsi), %r12
30:    movq  24(%rsi), %r13
31:    movq  32(%rsi), %r14
32:    movq  40(%rsi), %r15
33:    movq  48(%rsi), %rsp
34:    /* Jump to saved RIP */
35:    movq  56(%rsi), %rax
36:    jmpq  *%rax
37:
38:/*
39: * void arch_enter_user_mode(uint64_t entry_point, uint64_t user_sp, uint64_t kernel_sp)
40: * rdi = entry_point
41: * rsi = user_sp
42: * rdx = kernel_sp
43: */
44:.global arch_enter_user_mode
45:arch_enter_user_mode:
46:    /* We don't strictly need to switch to kernel_sp here if we're going to iretq
47:     * and the scheduler handles the main stack. But for safety, we set it.
48:     * Wait, if we change RSP now, we lose the return address. But we don't return.
49:     */
50:    movq %rdx, %rsp
51:
52:    /* Construct iretq frame for Ring 3 */
53:    /* Push SS (GDT_USER_DATA | 3) */
54:    pushq $0x1B
55:    
56:    /* Push RSP */
57:    pushq %rsi
58:
59:    /* Push RFLAGS (Enable Interrupts IF=1) */
60:    pushfq
61:    movq (%rsp), %rax
62:    orq $0x200, %rax
63:    movq %rax, (%rsp)
64:
65:    /* Push CS (GDT_USER_CODE | 3) */
66:    pushq $0x23
67:
68:    /* Push RIP */
69:    pushq %rdi
70:
71:    /* Clear registers to prevent leaking kernel data to user space */
72:    xorq %rax, %rax
73:    xorq %rbx, %rbx
74:    xorq %rcx, %rcx
75:    xorq %rdx, %rdx
76:    xorq %r8, %r8
77:    xorq %r9, %r9
78:    xorq %r10, %r10
79:    xorq %r11, %r11
80:    xorq %r12, %r12
81:    xorq %r13, %r13
82:    xorq %r14, %r14
83:    xorq %r15, %r15
84:    xorq %rbp, %rbp
85:    xorq %rdi, %rdi
86:    xorq %rsi, %rsi
87:
88:    /* swapgs not needed here if we haven't loaded kernel GS base yet,
89:     * but standard x86-64 uses it. For our single-core, we'll skip it or 
90:     * configure it later. */
91:    
92:    iretq
93:

@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/cpu/cpu.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/amd64/cpu/cpu.c
3: * AMD64 Per-CPU Initialization and Context-Switch Support
4: *
5: * Responsibilities:
6: *   - Enable SSE/FXSAVE in CR0/CR4 (required early; GCC may auto-vectorise
7: *     even kernel code with XMM registers).
8: *   - Populate cpu_data[id] (struct cpu_info) and write both IA32_GS_BASE
9: *     and IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE so that swapgs gives the kernel per-CPU pointer.
10: *   - Sequence per-CPU GDT, IDT, SYSCALL MSR, and LAPIC init calls.
11: *   - Implement arch_cpu_switch_context: update per-CPU bookkeeping, switch
12: *     CR3 to the next process's PML4, and update TSS RSP0 so interrupt delivery
13: *     uses the new task's kernel stack.
14: *
15: * Invariants:
16: *   - Identity-map: PA == VA throughout the kernel.  All pointer casts from
17: *     physical addresses are safe.
18: *   - GS base: after arch_cpu_init returns, %gs points at cpu_data[id]; all
19: *     assembly stubs (isr_stubs.S, syscall.S) rely on %gs:16 = stack_top and
20: *     %gs:24 = user_stack_tmp matching struct cpu_info field offsets exactly.
21: *     (Verified static: cpu.h:13-19 gives self=0, cpu_id=8, online=12,
22: *     stack_top=16, user_stack_tmp=24 — matching syscall.S lines 41-43.)
23: *
24: * Known issues:
25: *   CPU-AMD64-01 (W3 MISSING) isr_stubs.S common_isr_entry saves only the 15
26: *     GP registers.  No FXSAVE/XSAVE of XMM/AVX state is performed.  This
27: *     file enables SSE (CR4.OSFXSR, :36-39), so the compiler may use XMM regs
28: *     in kernel code.  A preemptive context switch on a timer IRQ between two
29: *     kernel tasks can silently corrupt their XMM state.  Cross-ref:
30: *     isr_stubs.S:95-109, context.S:12-36.
31: *   UACC-AMD64-01 (W2 DOC/MISSING) CR4.SMAP is NOT set here (:36-39); only
32: *     OSFXSR and OSXMMEXCPT are enabled.  uaccess.c's header claims SMAP is
33: *     active — that is wrong.  See uaccess.c Known issues.
34: */
35:#include <kernel/cpu.h>
36:#include <kernel/fault.h>
37:#include <kernel/printk.h>
38:#include <kernel/sched.h>
39:#include <kernel/string.h>
40:#include <kernel/vmm.h>
41:#include <arch/amd64_internal.h>
42:#include <arch/amd64/apic.h>
43:
44:#include <cpuid.h>
45:
46:extern struct cpu_info cpu_data[MAX_CPUS];
47:extern uint32_t nr_cpus;
48:
49:/* PCID-tagged TLB support (perf §3, DIR-06): 1 once CPUID has confirmed PCID +
50: * INVPCID and CR4.PCIDE has been enabled.  Read by the arch.h flush primitives
51: * and arch_cpu_switch_context; 0 (default) keeps the legacy flush-on-switch
52: * behaviour so the build stays portable on CPUs without PCID. */
53:int amd64_pcid_enabled = 0;
54:
55:extern void gdt_init(void);
56:extern void idt_init(void);
57:extern void amd64_syscall_init(void);
58:
59:
60:/*
61: * arch_cpu_init - per-CPU initialization entry point.
62: *
63: * Called by the BSP on the boot path (via kernel_main) and by each APs
64: * secondary_cpu_entry in start.S.  Sequence must match:
65: *   SSE → GDT → GS base → IDT → SYSCALL MSRs → LAPIC
66: *
67: * SSE is enabled FIRST because C code called after this point (including
68: * the GDT/IDT helpers) may be compiled with -msse or auto-vectorised.
69: * NOTE(CPU-AMD64-01): FXSAVE/XSAVE is not used in ctx_switch or
70: * common_isr_entry; enabling SSE here creates the hazard without the
71: * save/restore infrastructure.
72: *
73: * GS base is written AFTER gdt_init() because lgdt wipes all segment
74: * selectors including GS; writing IA32_GS_BASE before lgdt would be lost.
75: * Both IA32_GS_BASE (0xC0000101) and IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE (0xC0000102) are
76: * set to cpu_info_ptr so that swapgs in isr/syscall stubs switches from
77: * user GS to the correct kernel per-CPU pointer.
78: *
79: * nr_cpus: BSP sets unconditionally to 1 (no RMW needed); APs use
80: * __sync_fetch_and_add to safely increment the shared counter.
81: */
82:void arch_cpu_init(void) {
83:  uint32_t id = arch_get_cpu_id();
84:
85:  if (id >= MAX_CPUS) {
86:    /* Fallback for early printk if LAPIC ID is weird */
87:    id = 0;
88:  }
89:
90:  cpu_data[id].cpu_id = id;
91:
92:  /* Enable SSE EARLY (Functions like memset might use XMM registers) */
93:  uint64_t cr0, cr4;
94:  __asm__ __volatile__("mov %%cr0, %0" : "=r"(cr0));
95:  cr0 &= ~(1 << 2); /* Clear EM (Emulation) */
96:  cr0 |= (1 << 1);  /* Set MP (Monitor co-processor) */
97:  __asm__ __volatile__("mov %0, %%cr0" :: "r"(cr0));
98:
99:  /* NOTE(CPU-AMD64-01): OSFXSR+OSXMMEXCPT enable fxsave/fxrstor and unmasked
100:   * SIMD FP exceptions, but no FXSAVE is inserted in ctx_switch or the ISR
101:   * entry path.  CR4.SMAP is intentionally NOT set here — uaccess.c's claim
102:   * of SMAP protection is therefore inaccurate (UACC-AMD64-01). */
103:  __asm__ __volatile__("mov %%cr4, %0" : "=r"(cr4));
104:  cr4 |= (1 << 9);  /* OSFXSR (OS support for fxsave/fxrstor) */
105:  cr4 |= (1 << 10); /* OSXMMEXCPT (OS support for unmasked simd fp exceptions) */
106:  __asm__ __volatile__("mov %0, %%cr4" :: "r"(cr4));
107:
108:  /* PCID-tagged TLB (perf §3, DIR-06): enable CR4.PCIDE per-CPU iff the CPU
109:   * supports PCID (CPUID.01h:ECX[17]).  INVPCID is NOT required — the teardown
110:   * all-PCID flush uses a CR4.PGE toggle instead (see amd64_flush_all_pcids in
111:   * arch.h), so PCID activates on the common CPUs/hypervisors that expose PCID
112:   * but not INVPCID (e.g. HVF here).  CR4.PCIDE may only be set while
113:   * CR3[11:0]==0, which holds here (boot CR3 is page-aligned).  Portable: a CPU
114:   * without PCID keeps flush-on-switch.  Runs on every CPU (BSP + APs), so each
115:   * enables its own CR4.PCIDE before it ever runs the scheduler; the global flag
116:   * is published for the fast paths. */
117:  {
118:    unsigned int eax, ebx, ecx, edx;
119:    int has_pcid = 0, has_invpcid = 0;
120:    if (__get_cpuid(1, &eax, &ebx, &ecx, &edx))
121:      has_pcid = (ecx >> 17) & 1;
122:    if (__get_cpuid_count(7, 0, &eax, &ebx, &ecx, &edx))
123:      has_invpcid = (ebx >> 10) & 1; /* informational only (diagnostic below) */
124:    if (has_pcid) {
125:      uint64_t cr4now;
126:      __asm__ __volatile__("mov %%cr4, %0" : "=r"(cr4now));
127:      cr4now |= (1UL << 17); /* CR4.PCIDE */
128:      __asm__ __volatile__("mov %0, %%cr4" ::"r"(cr4now));
129:      amd64_pcid_enabled = 1;
130:    }
131:    if (id == 0) /* one-shot boot diagnostic (not a hot path) */
132:      pr_info("CPU: PCID-tagged TLB %s (pcid=%d invpcid=%d)\n",
133:              amd64_pcid_enabled ? "ENABLED" : "disabled (flush-on-switch)",
134:              has_pcid, has_invpcid);
135:  }
136:
137:  struct cpu_info *cpu = &cpu_data[id];
138:  cpu->self = cpu;
139:  cpu->online = 1;
140:  spin_lock_init(&cpu->sched_lock);
141:
142:  pr_info("CPU: Initializing GDT...\n");
143:  gdt_init();
144:
145:  /* Set up GS base for per-CPU data access (AFTER GDT to avoid wipeout) */
146:  uint64_t cpu_info_ptr = (uint64_t)cpu;
147:  wrmsr(0xC0000101, cpu_info_ptr); /* IA32_GS_BASE */
148:  wrmsr(0xC0000102, cpu_info_ptr); /* IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE */
149:
150:  pr_info("CPU: Initializing IDT...\n");
151:  idt_init();
152:
153:  pr_info("CPU: Initializing Syscall...\n");
154:  amd64_syscall_init();
155:
156:  pr_info("CPU: Initializing LAPIC...\n");
157:  lapic_init();
158:
159:  if (id == 0) {
160:      nr_cpus = 1;
161:  } else {
162:      __sync_fetch_and_add(&nr_cpus, 1);
163:  }
164:
165:  pr_info("AMD64 CPU %u initialized (GDT, IDT, Syscall, SSE, GS enabled)\n", id);
166:
167:  /* ARCH-AMD64-APPGD-01 (amd64 HAL only): the AP trampoline brings each AP up on
168:   * the stale boot_pml4 (32-bit CR3), which lacks the >4GB device MMIO at
169:   * PML4[1] (e.g. the virtio-input ISR window at 0xc000005000).  Once the live
170:   * kernel_pgd exists (built by vmm_dynamic_remap + arch_vmm_map_device before
171:   * SMP bringup), adopt it here so a device IRQ taken on this CPU cannot
172:   * page-fault on the high MMIO and halt the core.  On the BSP's early
173:   * cpu_init() call kernel_pgd is still NULL (VMM not up yet) -> no-op; the BSP
174:   * already runs on kernel_pgd via vmm_dynamic_remap().  Confined to the amd64
175:   * HAL; platform.c is untouched. */
176:  {
177:    extern uint64_t *kernel_pgd;
178:    if (kernel_pgd)
179:      arch_vmm_set_pgd(virt_to_phys(kernel_pgd)); /* CR3 takes the PA */
180:  }
181:}
182:
183:/*
184: * get_cpu_info - return the per-CPU struct for the calling CPU.
185: *
186: * Reads the LAPIC ID (arch_get_cpu_id) and indexes cpu_data[].  Falls back to
187: * cpu_data[0] if the ID is out of range (paranoia guard for early boot).
188: *
189: * Side effects: none.  May be called from interrupt context.
190: * NOTE: arch_get_cpu_id reads LAPIC MMIO — NOT safe from a fault handler on a
191: * compromised address space; fault paths use arch_cpu_info_fault_safe below.
192: */
193:struct cpu_info *get_cpu_info(void) {
194:  uint32_t id = arch_get_cpu_id();
195:  if (id >= MAX_CPUS) return &cpu_data[0];
196:  return &cpu_data[id];
197:}
198:
199:/*
200: * arch_cpu_info_fault_safe - per-CPU info with no faultable dependencies
201: * (kernel/fault.h, Phase A step 5).
202: *
203: * The LAPIC-MMIO read in arch_get_cpu_id needs a live page-table mapping —
204: * exactly what a freed-PGD fault destroys.  Instead read the IA32_GS_BASE MSR
205: * (rdmsr: register-only, cannot fault) and validate it against the cpu_data[]
206: * bounds BEFORE any dereference.  This also covers the two GS hazards:
207: *   - user GS base (fault inside the syscall-entry window before swapgs):
208: *     fails the bounds check -> NULL, no wild dereference;
209: *   - pre-cpu_init MSR garbage: same.
210: */
211:struct cpu_info *arch_cpu_info_fault_safe(void) {
212:  uint32_t lo, hi;
213:  __asm__ __volatile__("rdmsr" : "=a"(lo), "=d"(hi) : "c"(0xC0000101u));
214:  uintptr_t p = ((uintptr_t)hi << 32) | lo;
215:  uintptr_t base = (uintptr_t)&cpu_data[0];
216:  if (p < base || p >= base + sizeof(cpu_data))
217:    return NULL;
218:  if ((p - base) % sizeof(struct cpu_info) != 0)
219:    return NULL;
220:  return (struct cpu_info *)p;
221:}
222:
223:/*
224: * arch_cpu_switch_context - switch the hardware context to run 'next'.
225: *
226: * Called by the scheduler before invoking ctx_switch (context.S) with the
227: * two ctx_amd64 save-area pointers.  This function updates the per-CPU
228: * bookkeeping that the assembly stubs depend on:
229: *
230: *   cpu->stack_top:    read by syscall_entry (%gs:16) to load the kernel RSP
231: *                      on the SYSCALL fast path.
232: *   cpu->current_task: used by the generic scheduler and kernel_syscall_dispatcher
233: *                      to find current_process.
234: *   CR3:               loaded with next->page_table (physical PA of PML4), or
235: *                      with the shared kernel_pgd when page_table is NULL
236: *                      (kernel thread — SCHED-UAF-01: never leave the previous
237: *                      process's possibly-freed PGD active).
238: *   TSS RSP0:          updated via gdt_set_rsp0 so that hardware interrupt
239: *                      delivery from Ring 3 uses the correct kernel stack.
240: *
241: * Params:
242: *   next - the process to switch to; must not be NULL.
243: *
244: * NOTE(CPU-AMD64-01): No FPU/XMM state save/restore is done here.  This is the
245: * cooperative switch path; the Intel ABI treats XMM regs as caller-saved, so
246: * a cooperative switch is safe.  The hazard is preemptive switches via the
247: * timer ISR in common_isr_entry, which does not save/restore XMM state.
248: */
249:void arch_cpu_switch_context(struct process *next) {
250:  struct cpu_info *cpu = get_cpu_info();
251:
252:  /* Update per-CPU data for assembly stubs (syscall.S / isr_stubs.S) */
253:  cpu->stack_top = next->kernel_stack;
254:  cpu->current_task = next;
255:
256:  /* Switch address space.  A kernel thread (e.g. idle) has no private address
257:   * space (page_table == NULL): switch it onto the shared kernel_pgd instead of
258:   * leaving the PREVIOUS process's PGD active in CR3.
259:   *
260:   * SCHED-UAF-01 (interactive-close residual): if a CPU keeps a terminated
261:   * process's PGD as CR3 — because it switched prev->idle and we skipped the
262:   * reload — then when that process is reaped and its PGD pages are freed, the
263:   * CPU is left executing on a freed PGD.  Its kernel low-half identity map
264:   * (which includes printk) vanishes, so the next kernel fetch #PFs; the amd64
265:   * #PF handler then calls printk, which #PFs again -> recursive fault ->
266:   * stack overflow -> #DF -> triple fault.  That is the "Terminating process
267:   * ... PID" -> instant reboot seen on window close.  Confined to the amd64 HAL. */
268:  {
269:    extern uint64_t *kernel_pgd;
270:    /* page_table / kernel_pgd are kernel virtual pointers; CR3 takes the
271:     * PHYSICAL PML4 base — translate with virt_to_phys. */
272:    uint64_t pgd = next->page_table ? virt_to_phys(next->page_table)
273:                                    : (kernel_pgd ? virt_to_phys(kernel_pgd) : 0);
274:    if (pgd) {
275:      if (amd64_pcid_enabled) {
276:        /* PCID-tagged, flush-free switch (perf §3, DIR-06): CR3[11:0] = PCID
277:         * (next->asid; 0 for kernel/idle), bit 63 set = PRESERVE this PCID's
278:         * cached TLB entries (no flush) — the entries are this address space's
279:         * own and were cleared at the previous owner's teardown before the tag
280:         * was recycled.  Mirrors the aarch64 ASID-tagged TTBR0 switch. */
281:        uint64_t pcid = next->page_table ? (uint64_t)next->asid : 0;
282:        arch_vmm_set_pgd(pgd | pcid | (1ULL << 63));
283:      } else {
284:        arch_vmm_set_pgd(pgd); /* legacy: CR3 reload implicitly flushes */
285:      }
286:    }
287:  }
288:
289:  /* Update TSS RSP0 for interrupt stack switching */
290:  gdt_set_rsp0(next->kernel_stack);
291:}
292:
