@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/cpu/gdt.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/amd64/cpu/gdt.c
3: * Global Descriptor Table (GDT) and Task State Segment (TSS) for x86-64
4: *
5: * Responsibilities:
6: *   - Maintain per-CPU GDT (gdt_raw[MAX_CPUS][GDT_ENTRIES]) and TSS
7: *     (tss_data[MAX_CPUS]) so each CPU has its own descriptor tables.
8: *   - Install 5 usable segments (indices 1-4) and a 64-bit TSS descriptor
9: *     at index 5-6 (TSS occupies two consecutive 8-byte slots).
10: *   - Load the new GDT via a far-return sequence that atomically switches CS.
11: *   - Load the TSS via 'ltr' so that hardware interrupt delivery uses the
12: *     correct RSP0 from tss.rsp0.
13: *   - Provide gdt_set_rsp0() so the scheduler can update RSP0 on each
14: *     context switch without reloading the entire GDT.
15: *
16: * GDT layout (index → selector):
17: *   0 → 0x00  Null descriptor (required)
18: *   1 → 0x08  Kernel Code 64-bit (DPL=0, L=1, access=0x9A, gran=0xAF)
19: *   2 → 0x10  Kernel Data 64-bit (DPL=0, access=0x92, gran=0xCF)
20: *   3 → 0x18  User Data   32/64  (DPL=3, access=0xF2, gran=0xCF)
21: *   4 → 0x20  User Code   64-bit (DPL=3, L=1, access=0xFA, gran=0xAF)
22: *   5 → 0x28  TSS low word  (16-byte system descriptor, occupies slots 5+6)
23: *   6 → 0x30  TSS high word
24: *
25: * Invariants:
26: *   - gdt_raw and tss_data are statically allocated; no dynamic memory is used.
27: *   - Each CPU calls gdt_init() independently; GDTR points at cpu-specific array.
28: *   - tss.rsp0 is the only TSS field written at runtime (by gdt_set_rsp0).
29: *
30: * Known issues:
31: *   GDT-AMD64-01 (W2 REFINE) User data (0x18) appears before user code (0x20).
32: *     Conventional x86-64 ABI order is kern-code, kern-data, user-code,
33: *     user-data.  The STAR MSR and pt_regs.h are both consistent with this
34: *     reversed order, so the system functions correctly, but the ordering
35: *     differs from Linux and is a source of confusion.
36: */
37:#include <kernel/types.h>
38:#include <kernel/string.h>
39:#include <kernel/cpu.h>
40:#include <arch/arch.h>
41:#include <arch/amd64_internal.h>
42:#include <kernel/printk.h>
43:#include "gdt_defs.h"
44:
45:/* ─── GDT Segment Selectors ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
46: * These byte offsets into the GDT are the segment selectors loaded into CS,
47: * DS, SS, etc.  RPL bits [1:0] are 0 for kernel selectors; user selectors
48: * have RPL=3 but GDT index determines the descriptor, not the RPL in the
49: * selector itself (the CPU checks DPL ≥ RPL for privilege).
50: * ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────*/
51:#define GDT_NULL      0x00
52:#ifndef GDT_KERN_CODE
53:#endif /* GDT_KERN_CODE */
54:#ifndef GDT_KERN_DATA
55:#endif /* GDT_KERN_DATA */
56:#ifndef GDT_USER_DATA
57:#endif /* GDT_USER_DATA */
58:#ifndef GDT_USER_CODE
59:#endif /* GDT_USER_CODE */
60:#define GDT_TSS       0x28
61:#define GDT_ENTRIES   7
62:
63:/*
64: * struct tss64 - x86-64 Task State Segment (Intel SDM Vol.3 Section 7.7).
65: *
66: * Only rsp0 and iopb_offset are used at runtime:
67: *   rsp0:        kernel stack loaded on interrupt from Ring 3 (updated by
68: *                gdt_set_rsp0 on every context switch).
69: *   iopb_offset: set to sizeof(tss64) so the I/O permission bitmap is empty —
70: *                all port I/O from Ring 3 generates a #GP.
71: *
72: * rsp1, rsp2 and ist[] would be used for more-privileged stacks and IST
73: * entries (e.g. a dedicated #DF/NMI stack).  They remain zero here.
74: */
75:struct tss64 {
76:  uint32_t reserved0;
77:  uint64_t rsp0;
78:  uint64_t rsp1;
79:  uint64_t rsp2;
80:  uint64_t reserved1;
81:  uint64_t ist[7];
82:  uint64_t reserved2;
83:  uint16_t reserved3;
84:  uint16_t iopb_offset;
85:} __packed;
86:
87:/*
88: * struct gdt_entry - 8-byte segment descriptor (code/data segments).
89: *
90: * Fields per Intel SDM Vol.3 Table 3-1:
91: *   limit_lo [15:0], gran[3:0] : 20-bit segment limit (0xFFFFF here → 4GB)
92: *   base_lo/mid/hi             : 32-bit base address (0 for flat model)
93: *   access                     : type, DPL, P, S flags
94: *   granularity                : G, D/B, L, AVL, limit_hi nibble
95: *
96: * In 64-bit long mode most data/code segment fields are ignored except:
97: *   L bit (granularity[5]) = 1 → 64-bit code segment
98: *   D/B bit = 0 when L = 1 (must be 0 per SDM)
99: *   DPL (access[6:5]) = privilege level
100: */
101:struct gdt_entry {
102:  uint16_t limit_lo;
103:  uint16_t base_lo;
104:  uint8_t  base_mid;
105:  uint8_t  access;
106:  uint8_t  granularity;
107:  uint8_t  base_hi;
108:} __packed;
109:
110:/*
111: * struct gdt_system_entry - 16-byte system descriptor used for the TSS.
112: *
113: * The TSS descriptor occupies two consecutive 8-byte GDT slots (indices 5+6).
114: * base_upper holds bits 63:32 of the TSS linear address (needed in 64-bit
115: * mode since the TSS can be anywhere in the 64-bit address space).
116: */
117:struct gdt_system_entry {
118:  uint16_t limit_lo;
119:  uint16_t base_lo;
120:  uint8_t  base_mid;
121:  uint8_t  access;
122:  uint8_t  granularity;
123:  uint8_t  base_hi;
124:  uint32_t base_upper;
125:  uint32_t reserved;
126:} __packed;
127:
128:/*
129: * struct gdtr - GDTR pseudo-descriptor for 'lgdt'.
130: *   limit: byte size of GDT - 1  (GDT_ENTRIES*8 - 1)
131: *   base:  linear address of the GDT array
132: */
133:struct gdtr {
134:  uint16_t limit;
135:  uint64_t base;
136:} __packed;
137:
138:/* Per-CPU GDT and TSS arrays, 16-byte aligned for GDTR requirements. */
139:static struct tss64 tss_data[MAX_CPUS] __aligned(16);
140:static uint64_t gdt_raw[MAX_CPUS][GDT_ENTRIES] __aligned(16);
141:
142:/*
143: * gdt_set_entry - fill a standard 8-byte code/data segment descriptor.
144: *
145: * base is always 0 (flat 64-bit model); limit is 0xFFFFF (max, with G=1 →
146: * granularity in 4KB units → 4GB limit, ignored in 64-bit mode for data segs).
147: * access and gran encode the descriptor type, privilege level, and 64-bit flags.
148: *
149: * Examples used in gdt_init:
150: *   access=0x9A gran=0xAF : Kernel 64-bit code (DPL=0, L=1, D=0, G=1)
151: *   access=0x92 gran=0xCF : Kernel 64-bit data (DPL=0, D=1, G=1)
152: *   access=0xF2 gran=0xCF : User   32/64 data  (DPL=3, D=1, G=1)
153: *   access=0xFA gran=0xAF : User   64-bit code  (DPL=3, L=1, D=0, G=1)
154: */
155:static void gdt_set_entry(uint64_t *gdt, int index, uint8_t access, uint8_t gran) {
156:  struct gdt_entry *e = (struct gdt_entry *)&gdt[index];
157:  e->limit_lo    = 0xFFFF;
158:  e->base_lo     = 0;
159:  e->base_mid    = 0;
160:  e->access      = access;
161:  e->granularity = gran;
162:  e->base_hi     = 0;
163:}
164:
165:/*
166: * gdt_set_tss - fill the 16-byte TSS system descriptor at gdt[index..index+1].
167: *
168: * The TSS descriptor spans two 8-byte slots (the high slot holds base_upper
169: * which is the bits 63:32 of the TSS physical address).  access=0x89 encodes
170: * type=9 (64-bit Available TSS), DPL=0, Present=1.
171: *
172: * After gdt_init calls this, 'ltr' loads the TSS selector (0x28) which marks
173: * the TSS as Busy (type changes from 9 to 11 in the descriptor).
174: */
175:static void gdt_set_tss(uint64_t *gdt, int index, uint64_t base, uint32_t limit) {
176:  struct gdt_system_entry *e = (struct gdt_system_entry *)&gdt[index];
177:  e->limit_lo    = (uint16_t)(limit & 0xFFFF);
178:  e->base_lo     = (uint16_t)(base & 0xFFFF);
179:  e->base_mid    = (uint8_t)((base >> 16) & 0xFF);
180:  e->access      = 0x89; /* Present, DPL=0, 64-bit Available TSS */
181:  e->granularity = (uint8_t)((limit >> 16) & 0x0F);
182:  e->base_hi     = (uint8_t)((base >> 24) & 0xFF);
183:  e->base_upper  = (uint32_t)(base >> 32);
184:  e->reserved    = 0;
185:}
186:
187:/*
188: * gdt_init - build and load the GDT and TSS for the calling CPU.
189: *
190: * Each CPU calls this independently; gdt_raw[cpu_id] and tss_data[cpu_id]
191: * are separate per-CPU arrays.  The GDTR loaded by lgdt points at the CPU's
192: * private gdt_raw[] slice.
193: *
194: * GDT build order (NOTE GDT-AMD64-01: unconventional user-data before user-code):
195: *   idx 0 : null (cleared by memset)
196: *   idx 1 : 0x08 kernel code 64-bit  (access=0x9A L=1)
197: *   idx 2 : 0x10 kernel data 64-bit  (access=0x92)
198: *   idx 3 : 0x18 user data   (DPL=3) (access=0xF2) — before user code
199: *   idx 4 : 0x20 user code   (DPL=3) (access=0xFA L=1)
200: *   idx 5 : 0x28 TSS low  (16-byte descriptor spans indices 5+6)
201: *
202: * The far-return trick to reload CS (0x08):
203: *   'lgdt' updates the GDTR but the CS shadow register still holds the old
204: *   descriptor.  To atomically load the new CS the code pushes 0x08 (kernel
205: *   code selector) + RIP of label 1f, then executes 'lretq' (far return),
206: *   which pops CS:RIP and resumes at label 1.  DS/ES/FS/SS are then set to
207: *   0x10 (kernel data) with movw.
208: *
209: * TSS: iopb_offset = sizeof(tss64) places the IOPB past the end of the TSS,
210: * effectively denying all port I/O to Ring 3 (any access generates #GP).
211: *
212: * 'ltr' loads the TSS register (selector 0x28 = GDT_TSS) and marks the TSS
213: * as Busy.  RSP0 in the TSS is initially 0; it is set by the first call to
214: * gdt_set_rsp0 before the first Ring-3 entry.
215: */
216:/*
217: * Per-CPU IST fault stacks — Phase A step 3.
218: *
219: * Without IST every exception reuses the current RSP (kernel fault) or
220: * TSS.RSP0 = the current task's kernel stack (user fault): a recursive #PF
221: * overflowed that stack into #DF (also IST=0) and triple-faulted — the
222: * SCHED-UAF-01 failure signature.  idt_init points #PF/#GP at IST1 and #DF at
223: * IST2 (separate, so a #PF storm cannot clobber the #DF stack).
224: *
225: * 16KB per stack, sized for handler + fault_printf dump + backtrace walk.
226: * In .bss → always mapped in kernel_pgd.  A nested fault on the same IST
227: * index re-enters at the top and clobbers the outer frame; that is caught
228: * immediately by the fault_enter() depth guard before any state is trusted.
229: */
230:#define IST_STACK_SIZE 16384
231:static uint8_t ist1_fault_stacks[MAX_CPUS][IST_STACK_SIZE] __aligned(16);
232:static uint8_t ist2_df_stacks[MAX_CPUS][IST_STACK_SIZE] __aligned(16);
233:
234:void gdt_init(void) {
235:  uint32_t cpu_id = arch_get_cpu_id();
236:  if (cpu_id >= MAX_CPUS) return;
237:
238:  uint64_t *my_gdt = gdt_raw[cpu_id];
239:  struct tss64 *my_tss = &tss_data[cpu_id];
240:
241:  memset(my_gdt, 0, GDT_ENTRIES * 8);
242:  memset(my_tss, 0, sizeof(struct tss64));
243:
244:  /* IST entries are 1-based in the IDT gate; ist[0] here is IST1.
245:   * IST1 = #PF/#GP fault stack, IST2 = #DF stack (see idt_init). */
246:  my_tss->ist[0] = (uint64_t)&ist1_fault_stacks[cpu_id][IST_STACK_SIZE];
247:  my_tss->ist[1] = (uint64_t)&ist2_df_stacks[cpu_id][IST_STACK_SIZE];
248:
249:  /* NOTE(GDT-AMD64-01): user-data (idx 3, sel 0x18) is before user-code
250:   * (idx 4, sel 0x20).  This is internally consistent with msr.c STAR and
251:   * pt_regs.h but reverses the conventional ordering. */
252:  gdt_set_entry(my_gdt, 1, 0x9A, 0xAF); /* kernel code 64-bit */
253:  gdt_set_entry(my_gdt, 2, 0x92, 0xCF); /* kernel data 64-bit */
254:  gdt_set_entry(my_gdt, 3, 0xF2, 0xCF); /* user data DPL=3 */
255:  gdt_set_entry(my_gdt, 4, 0xFA, 0xAF); /* user code 64-bit DPL=3 */
256:
257:  my_tss->iopb_offset = sizeof(struct tss64);
258:  gdt_set_tss(my_gdt, 5, (uint64_t)my_tss, sizeof(struct tss64) - 1);
259:
260:  struct gdtr gdtr = {
261:    .limit = (GDT_ENTRIES * 8) - 1,
262:    .base  = (uint64_t)my_gdt
263:  };
264:
265:  pr_info("GDT: Loading GDTR...\n");
266:  __asm__ __volatile__(
267:    "lgdt %0\n\t"
268:    /* Far-return to atomically reload CS with the new GDT's kernel code sel */
269:    "pushq $0x08\n\t"          /* new CS = 0x08 (kernel code) */
270:    "leaq 1f(%%rip), %%rax\n\t"/* new RIP = label 1 */
271:    "pushq %%rax\n\t"
272:    "lretq\n\t"                 /* pop CS:RIP → now running with new GDT CS */
273:    "1:\n\t"
274:    "movw $0x10, %%ax\n\t"     /* 0x10 = kernel data selector */
275:    "movw %%ax, %%ds\n\t"
276:    "movw %%ax, %%es\n\t"
277:    "movw %%ax, %%fs\n\t"
278:    "movw %%ax, %%ss\n\t"
279:    :
280:    : "m"(gdtr)
281:    : "rax", "memory"
282:  );
283:
284:  pr_info("GDT: Loading TSS...\n");
285:  __asm__ __volatile__("ltr %0" :: "r"((uint16_t)GDT_TSS));
286:  pr_info("GDT: Done\n");
287:}
288:
289:/*
290: * gdt_set_rsp0 - update TSS.RSP0 for the calling CPU.
291: *
292: * Called by arch_cpu_switch_context on every scheduler switch.  RSP0 is the
293: * kernel stack pointer the CPU loads on a Ring-3→Ring-0 privilege transition
294: * (interrupt or exception delivery).  If this is not updated, a Ring-3 fault
295: * would push the interrupt frame onto the PREVIOUS task's kernel stack.
296: *
297: * Params:
298: *   rsp0 - top of the next task's kernel stack (high address, stack descends).
299: */
300:void gdt_set_rsp0(uint64_t rsp0) {
301:  uint32_t cpu_id = arch_get_cpu_id();
302:  if (cpu_id < MAX_CPUS) {
303:    tss_data[cpu_id].rsp0 = rsp0;
304:  }
305:}
306:

@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/cpu/idt.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/amd64/cpu/idt.c
3: * Interrupt Descriptor Table (IDT) and Exception Dispatcher for x86-64
4: *
5: * Responsibilities:
6: *   - Define the 256-entry 64-bit IDT (struct idt_entry, 16 bytes each).
7: *   - Install all 256 ISR stubs (from isr_stub_table[] in isr_stubs.S) as
8: *     kernel-only interrupt gates (DPL=0, type=0x8E).  There is no user-callable
9: *     gate: the only syscall entry is syscall/sysret via LSTAR (SYS-AMD64-03).
10: *   - Dispatch CPU exceptions (vectors 0-31) and hardware IRQs (32-255) from the
11: *     single C entry point amd64_isr_dispatch.
12: *   - Acknowledge the LAPIC and legacy 8259 PIC after hardware IRQs.
13: *
14: * Invariants:
15: *   - The IDT is a single shared array; all CPUs load the same base address.
16: *     Only CPU 0 fills the table (guarded by idt_initialized).  APs spin-wait.
17: *   - Every hardware IRQ (vec 32-255) ends through irq_chip_end(): the chip
18: *     (pic_chip_end) owns the full LAPIC + 8259 EOI sequence.  Spurious
19: *     IRQ7/IRQ15 (vec 39/47) and the LAPIC spurious vector (0xFF) are
20: *     filtered before dispatch and follow their own EOI rules.
21: *
22: * Known issues:
23: *   EXC-AMD64-01 RESOLVED (Phase A step 14): the dead probe-recovery block
24: *     and the amd64-local probe_in_progress/probe_failed flags were removed.
25: *     Memory probing is an aarch64-only fallback (FDT parse failure); its
26: *     flags and the working ELR_EL1 fixup live in aarch64/cpu/cpu.c.  amd64
27: *     gets its memory map from PVH/multiboot and never probes.
28: *   EXC-AMD64-02 RESOLVED (Phase A): every vector 0-31 routes through
29: *     fault_handle_user_or_panic (kernel/core/fault.c) — user faults
30: *     terminate the process and schedule a successor; kernel faults dump,
31: *     print a symbolized backtrace and panic on the IST fault stacks.
32: *   EXC-AMD64-04 (W2 BUG) idt_initialized is a plain static int with no
33: *     volatile qualifier and no memory barrier.  APs spinning on
34: *     while (!idt_initialized) may cache a stale zero indefinitely; a release
35: *     barrier on the write side and a load-acquire on the read side are needed.
36: *   SYS-AMD64-03 RESOLVED (#168): the legacy int 0x80 gate (DPL=3) was removed.
37: *     Vector 0x80 is now a kernel-only gate like every other; syscall/sysret via
38: *     LSTAR is the sole syscall surface.  A userland int 0x80 raises #GP and is
39: *     handled as a user fault.
40: *   CPU-AMD64-01 RESOLVED (#38): FPU/SSE state is saved/restored per task in
41: *     arch_cpu_switch_context (cpu.c).  common_isr_entry still saves only GP
42: *     regs; the residual kernel-clobber window is tracked in #167.
43: */
44:#include <kernel/types.h>
45:#include <kernel/string.h>
46:#include <kernel/printk.h>
47:#include <kernel/cpu.h>
48:#include <kernel/fault.h>
49:#include <kernel/irq.h>
50:#include <drivers/timer.h> /* HZ, for Tier-2 per-CPU tick accounting */
51:#include <arch/pt_regs.h>
52:#include <arch/arch.h>
53:#include <arch/amd64_internal.h>
54:#include <kernel/arch.h>
55:
56:#define IDT_ENTRIES 256
57:
58:/*
59: * struct idt_entry - x86-64 64-bit interrupt/trap gate descriptor (16 bytes).
60: *
61: * Fields per Intel SDM Vol.3 Table 3-2:
62: *   offset_lo  [15:0]  : bits 0-15 of handler RIP
63: *   selector   [15:0]  : code segment selector (0x08 = kernel CS)
64: *   ist        [2:0]   : Interrupt Stack Table index (0 = none)
65: *   type_attr  [7:0]   : gate type (0x8E=interrupt, 0xEE=trap DPL3) + present
66: *   offset_mid [15:0]  : bits 16-31 of handler RIP
67: *   offset_hi  [31:0]  : bits 32-63 of handler RIP
68: *   zero       [31:0]  : reserved, must be 0
69: *
70: * type_attr encoding:
71: *   0x8E = P=1 DPL=00 S=0 Type=1110 (64-bit interrupt gate, Ring 0 only)
72: *   0xEE = P=1 DPL=11 S=0 Type=1110 (64-bit interrupt gate, callable from Ring 3)
73: */
74:struct idt_entry {
75:  uint16_t offset_lo;
76:  uint16_t selector;
77:  uint8_t  ist;       /* Interrupt Stack Table offset */
78:  uint8_t  type_attr; /* Type and Attributes */
79:  uint16_t offset_mid;
80:  uint32_t offset_hi;
81:  uint32_t zero;
82:} __packed;
83:
84:/*
85: * struct idtr - IDTR pseudo-descriptor loaded with 'lidt'.
86: *   limit: byte length of IDT - 1  (256*16 - 1 = 0xFFF)
87: *   base:  linear address of idt[]
88: */
89:struct idtr {
90:  uint16_t limit;
91:  uint64_t base;
92:} __packed;
93:
94:/* idt[]: the 256-entry Interrupt Descriptor Table, 16-byte aligned for lidt.
95: * All CPUs share this single table; it is filled only by CPU 0. */
96:static struct idt_entry idt[IDT_ENTRIES] __aligned(16);
97:/* static struct idtr idtr; - Removed, using local idtr in idt_init */
98:
99:/* Defined in isr_stubs.S — 256-entry array of isr_stub_N addresses. */
100:extern uint64_t isr_stub_table[];
101:
102:/*
103: * idt_set_gate - write one IDT descriptor.
104: *
105: * num:   vector index 0-255
106: * base:  64-bit handler address (isr_stub_N from isr_stub_table[])
107: * sel:   code segment selector (0x08 = GDT_KERN_CODE)
108: * flags: type_attr byte (0x8E = kernel interrupt gate; 0xEE = user trap gate)
109: * ist:   IST stack index (0 = use the current RSP/TSS RSP0)
110: *
111: * The 64-bit offset is split across offset_lo/mid/hi as required by the
112: * x86-64 descriptor format.
113: */
114:static void idt_set_gate(uint8_t num, uint64_t base, uint16_t sel, uint8_t flags, uint8_t ist) {
115:  idt[num].offset_lo  = (uint16_t)(base & 0xFFFF);
116:  idt[num].selector   = sel;
117:  idt[num].ist        = ist;
118:  idt[num].type_attr  = flags;
119:  idt[num].offset_mid = (uint16_t)((base >> 16) & 0xFFFF);
120:  idt[num].offset_hi  = (uint32_t)(base >> 32);
121:  idt[num].zero       = 0;
122:}
123:
124:/* idt_initialized: flag set by CPU 0 after filling the IDT; APs spin on it.
125: * NOTE(EXC-AMD64-04): This is a plain int with no volatile or memory barrier.
126: * On SMP the compiler and CPU are free to cache the zero in a register; the
127: * spin loop on APs may never observe the write.  A proper release/acquire pair
128: * (e.g. __atomic_store_n + __atomic_load_n) is needed for correctness. */
129:static int idt_initialized = 0;
130:
131:/*
132: * idt_init - initialise and load the IDT for the calling CPU.
133: *
134: * CPU 0 path: fills all 256 entries with DPL-0 interrupt gates and sets
135: * idt_initialized = 1 when done.  SYS-AMD64-03 (#168): no DPL-3 gate is
136: * installed — the legacy int 0x80 syscall surface was removed; syscall/sysret
137: * via LSTAR is the sole syscall entry.
138: *
139: * AP path: spins on idt_initialized (NOTE EXC-AMD64-04: no memory barrier),
140: * then executes lidt with a CPU-local idtr pointing at the shared idt[].
141: * Each CPU must execute lidt itself; the IDTR is per-CPU.
142: */
143:void idt_init(void) {
144:  if (arch_get_cpu_id() == 0) {
145:      memset(&idt, 0, sizeof(struct idt_entry) * IDT_ENTRIES);
146:
147:      /* Set up IDT gates: all 256 as kernel-only interrupt gates (0x8E) */
148:      for (int i = 0; i < IDT_ENTRIES; i++) {
149:        idt_set_gate(i, isr_stub_table[i], 0x08, 0x8E, 0);
150:      }
151:
152:      /* SYS-AMD64-03 (#168): vector 0x80 intentionally stays a kernel-only gate
153:       * (DPL=0, set by the loop above).  The legacy int 0x80 syscall surface is
154:       * removed; the only syscall entry is syscall/sysret via LSTAR.  A userland
155:       * int 0x80 now raises #GP and is handled as a user fault. */
156:
157:      /* Dedicated IST fault stacks (Phase A step 3; stacks live in gdt.c):
158:       *   IST1 -> #GP (13) and #PF (14): the handler always runs on a fresh,
159:       *           always-mapped stack even if the faulting RSP is wild or the
160:       *           task kernel stack has overflowed.
161:       *   IST2 -> #DF (8): separate index so that even a #PF/#GP storm that
162:       *           clobbers IST1 cannot take down double-fault reporting.
163:       * NMI (2) deliberately stays IST=0: an IST NMI needs the paranoid
164:       * swapgs-entry pattern, out of scope here (see Phase A plan, Risks). */
165:      idt_set_gate(8,  isr_stub_table[8],  0x08, 0x8E, 2);
166:      idt_set_gate(13, isr_stub_table[13], 0x08, 0x8E, 1);
167:      idt_set_gate(14, isr_stub_table[14], 0x08, 0x8E, 1);
168:
169:      idt_initialized = 1;
170:  }
171:
172:  /* Wait for CPU 0 to finish if needed (not strictly necessary with sequential boot) */
173:  while (!idt_initialized) arch_nop(); /* NOTE(EXC-AMD64-04): missing barrier */
174:
175:  struct idtr local_idtr;
176:  local_idtr.limit = sizeof(struct idt_entry) * IDT_ENTRIES - 1;
177:  local_idtr.base  = (uint64_t)&idt;
178:
179:  __asm__ __volatile__("lidt %0" : : "m"(local_idtr));
180:}
181:
182:/*
183: * fault_cpu_id - CPU id for fault banners, via the MSR-based safe path.
184: * Returns -1 when the per-CPU structure cannot be located (early boot or
185: * corrupted GS); never touches LAPIC MMIO (kernel/fault.h, step 5).
186: */
187:static int fault_cpu_id(void) {
188:  struct cpu_info *ci = arch_cpu_info_fault_safe();
189:  return ci ? (int)ci->cpu_id : -1;
190:}
191:
192:/*
193: * amd64_dump_regs - print all saved registers from the exception frame.
194: *
195: * Params:
196: *   regs - pointer to the pt_regs struct built by common_isr_entry.
197: * Called unconditionally before halting on any unhandled exception.
198: *
199: * Uses fault_printf (lock-free, no per-CPU buffer, no LAPIC reads): by the
200: * time this runs the address space and lock state may be arbitrary, and a
201: * printk here is exactly the recursive-fault chain that used to end in a
202: * triple fault (SCHED-UAF-01 post-mortem).
203: */
204:static void amd64_dump_regs(struct pt_regs *regs) {
205:  fault_printf("RIP: %016lx CS: %02lx RFLAGS: %016lx\n", regs->rip, regs->cs, regs->rflags);
206:  fault_printf("RAX: %016lx RBX: %016lx RCX: %016lx RDX: %016lx\n", regs->rax, regs->rbx, regs->rcx, regs->rdx);
207:  fault_printf("RSI: %016lx RDI: %016lx RBP: %016lx RSP: %016lx\n", regs->rsi, regs->rdi, regs->rbp, regs->rsp);
208:  fault_printf("R8:  %016lx R9:  %016lx R10: %016lx R11: %016lx\n", regs->r8, regs->r9, regs->r10, regs->r11);
209:  fault_printf("R12: %016lx R13: %016lx R14: %016lx R15: %016lx\n", regs->r12, regs->r13, regs->r14, regs->r15);
210:  fault_printf("Vector: %ld, Error Code: %lx\n", regs->vec, regs->err);
211:}
212:
213:/*
214: * amd64_page_fault_handler - handle vector 14 (#PF).
215: *
216: * CR2 holds the faulting linear address.  Error code bits (Intel SDM Vol.3
217: * Section 6.15):
218: *   bit 0  P   : 0 = not-present, 1 = protection violation
219: *   bit 1  W/R : 0 = read, 1 = write
220: *   bit 2  U/S : 0 = kernel, 1 = user
221: *   bit 3  RSVD: reserved-bit violation
222: *   bit 4  I/D : instruction fetch (NX violation)
223: *
224: * NOTE(EXC-AMD64-02): The U/S bit (err & 4) is printed but never branched on.
225: * A user-space page fault causes the kernel to halt rather than delivering a
226: * signal to the user process.  Fix: if (regs->cs & 3) == 3, call
227: * process_terminate(current_process) + schedule() instead of halting.
228: */
229:static struct pt_regs *amd64_page_fault_handler(struct pt_regs *regs) {
230:  uint64_t cr2;
231:  __asm__ __volatile__("mov %%cr2, %0" : "=r"(cr2));
232:
233:  uint64_t error_code = regs->err;
234:
235:  /* EXC-AMD64-02 resolved: user #PF (or a fault inside the explicit
236:   * user-copy window) terminates the process and schedules a successor —
237:   * it no longer halts the kernel. */
238:  struct pt_regs *next =
239:      fault_handle_user_or_panic(regs, (regs->cs & 3) == 3, cr2, regs->rip,
240:                                 "PAGE FAULT", regs->err);
241:  if (next)
242:    return next;
243:
244:  fault_printf("\n[C%d] KERNEL PAGE FAULT: Access to 0x%lx\n", fault_cpu_id(), cr2);
245:  fault_printf("Frame: %p (IST1 fault stack)\n", (void *)regs);
246:  fault_printf("Error Code: 0x%lx (P:%d, W:%d, U:%d, R:%d, I:%d)\n",
247:               error_code,
248:               (error_code & 1) ? 1 : 0,
249:               (error_code & 2) ? 1 : 0,
250:               (error_code & 4) ? 1 : 0,
251:               (error_code & 8) ? 1 : 0,
252:               (error_code & 16) ? 1 : 0);
253:
254:  amd64_dump_regs(regs);
255:  backtrace_regs(regs->rip, regs->rbp);
256:  backtrace_scan(regs->rsp);
257:  panic("Unrecoverable kernel #PF at RIP 0x%lx (CR2 0x%lx)", regs->rip, cr2);
258:}
259:
260:/*
261: * amd64_gpf_handler - handle vector 13 (#GP).
262: *
263: * General Protection Fault: can be caused by descriptor/segment violations,
264: * invalid IOPL instructions, or non-canonical addresses.
265: * NOTE(EXC-AMD64-02): No user-vs-kernel discrimination; both halt the kernel.
266: */
267:static struct pt_regs *amd64_gpf_handler(struct pt_regs *regs) {
268:  struct pt_regs *next =
269:      fault_handle_user_or_panic(regs, (regs->cs & 3) == 3, 0, regs->rip,
270:                                 "GENERAL PROTECTION FAULT", regs->err);
271:  if (next)
272:    return next;
273:
274:  fault_printf("\n[C%d] KERNEL GENERAL PROTECTION FAULT\n", fault_cpu_id());
275:  amd64_dump_regs(regs);
276:  backtrace_regs(regs->rip, regs->rbp);
277:  backtrace_scan(regs->rsp);
278:  panic("Unrecoverable kernel #GP at RIP 0x%lx (err 0x%lx)", regs->rip, regs->err);
279:}
280:
281:/*
282: * amd64_double_fault_handler - handle vector 8 (#DF).
283: *
284: * Double fault occurs when an exception fires while handling another exception.
285: * The CPU pushes a zero error code.  Recovery is impossible in the general case;
286: * a dedicated IST stack entry should be used for #DF to avoid stack-overflow
287: * recursion (IST=0 here, so it shares the TSS RSP0 stack — risky).
288: */
289:static void amd64_double_fault_handler(struct pt_regs *regs) {
290:  fault_printf("\n[C%d] DOUBLE FAULT\n", fault_cpu_id());
291:  amd64_dump_regs(regs);
292:  backtrace_regs(regs->rip, regs->rbp);
293:  backtrace_scan(regs->rsp);
294:  arch_cpu_halt();
295:}
296:
297:/* kernel_syscall_dispatcher: reached only via syscall/sysret (syscall.S) since
298: * the legacy int 0x80 gate was removed (SYS-AMD64-03 #168). */
299:extern struct pt_regs *kernel_timer_tick(struct pt_regs *regs);
300:
301:/*
302: * amd64_isr_dispatch - central exception and interrupt dispatcher.
303: *
304: * Called from common_isr_entry (isr_stubs.S) with RSP pointing at struct
305: * pt_regs.  Returns a (possibly different) pt_regs* — the common entry writes
306: * the return value to RSP before restoring registers, allowing a context
307: * switch by returning a different task's frame.
308: *
309: * Dispatch logic:
310: *   vec < 32  : CPU exceptions.  Recursion guard (fault_enter), then switch
311: *               on vec 8/13/14; every vector routes through
312: *               fault_handle_user_or_panic (user → terminate, kernel → panic).
313: *   (vector 0x80 is a kernel-only gate now — the legacy int 0x80 syscall
314: *    surface was removed, SYS-AMD64-03 #168; syscalls use syscall/sysret.)
315: *   vec 32-255: Hardware IRQs.  Spurious 39/47/0xFF filtered first; vec==32
316: *               (timer) → kernel_timer_tick; others → irq_dispatch.  All end
317: *               through irq_chip_end() (chip-owned LAPIC + PIC EOI).
318: *               NOTE(EXC-AMD64-03, resolved): the PIT is halted after LAPIC
319: *               calibration, so vec 32 has a single source (LAPIC timer).
320: *
321: * Calling convention: called from assembly with a C ABI call; RDI = &pt_regs.
322: * Returns RAX = new RSP (next task's pt_regs or the same regs on no-switch).
323: *
324: * NOTE(CPU-AMD64-01): No FXSAVE in common_isr_entry; XMM state is not
325: * preserved across a preemptive switch triggered by the timer IRQ (vec==32).
326: */
327:struct pt_regs *amd64_isr_dispatch(struct pt_regs *regs) {
328:  uint64_t vec = regs->vec;
329:
330:  if (vec < 32) {
331:    /* Fault recursion guard (Phase A step 7): a fault inside a fault handler
332:     * used to recurse on the same stack until #DF -> triple fault.  Detect
333:     * the nesting FIRST — before any code that could itself fault — and stop
334:     * with one raw line.  fault_exit() runs on every path below that resumes
335:     * execution; the halting paths deliberately keep the depth elevated. */
336:    if (fault_enter() > 1) {
337:      fault_printf("\n[C%d] NESTED CPU EXCEPTION vec=%lu err=0x%lx rip=%016lx — halting\n",
338:                   fault_cpu_id(), vec, regs->err, regs->rip);
339:      arch_cpu_halt();
340:    }
341:
342:    /* Handle exceptions (EXC-AMD64-02 resolved): user-attributable faults —
343:     * any vector 0-31 from CS RPL 3, e.g. #DE, #UD, #PF, #GP — terminate the
344:     * process via fault_handle_user_or_panic and return the next task's
345:     * frame.  Kernel faults dump and panic.  #DF never attempts recovery:
346:     * machine state is not trustworthy by definition. */
347:    switch (vec) {
348:      case 8: /* Double Fault (#DF) */
349:        amd64_double_fault_handler(regs);
350:        break;
351:      case 13: /* General Protection Fault (#GP) */
352:        return amd64_gpf_handler(regs);
353:      case 14: /* Page Fault (#PF) — CR2 holds faulting address */
354:        return amd64_page_fault_handler(regs);
355:      default: {
356:        struct pt_regs *next =
357:            fault_handle_user_or_panic(regs, (regs->cs & 3) == 3, 0, regs->rip,
358:                                       "CPU EXCEPTION", regs->err);
359:        if (next)
360:          return next;
361:        fault_printf("\n[C%d] Unhandled kernel CPU Exception: %ld\n",
362:                     fault_cpu_id(), vec);
363:        amd64_dump_regs(regs);
364:        backtrace_regs(regs->rip, regs->rbp);
365:        backtrace_scan(regs->rsp);
366:        panic("Unrecoverable kernel exception (vec %lu) at RIP 0x%lx", vec, regs->rip);
367:      }
368:    }
369:  } else {
370:    /* Hardware interrupts (32-255).  SYS-AMD64-03 (#168): the legacy int 0x80
371:     * syscall surface was removed — vector 0x80 is now a kernel-only gate, so a
372:     * userland int 0x80 raises #GP (handled as a user fault) and the only
373:     * syscall entry is syscall/sysret via LSTAR. */
374:    struct pt_regs *ret_regs = regs;
375:
376:    /* 8259 spurious IRQ7/IRQ15 (vectors 39/47): not real interrupts — a
377:     * level pulse deasserted before INTA.  Filtered BEFORE dispatch because
378:     * their EOI rules differ (none / master-only); pic_handle_spurious()
379:     * performs what is needed.  Likewise the LAPIC spurious vector (0xFF,
380:     * set in SVR) requires no EOI and no dispatch. */
381:    if ((vec == 39 || vec == 47) && pic_handle_spurious((uint32_t)vec)) {
382:        return ret_regs;
383:    }
384:    if (vec == 0xFF) {
385:        return ret_regs;
386:    }
387:
388:    if (vec == 32) {
389:        /* Timer Interrupt (LAPIC periodic, vector 32; the PIT is halted
390:         * after calibration — EXC-AMD64-03 resolved).
391:         * NOTE(CPU-AMD64-01): No FPU save; ctx_switch on this path risks XMM
392:         * corruption between concurrently running kernel tasks. */
393:
394:        /* Tier-2 per-CPU drift accounting (docs/TIMER-MODEL.md §3): the
395:         * arch-neutral, HAL-driven timer_percpu_tick() advances the software
396:         * per-CPU schedule against the free-running TSC so lost ticks are
397:         * recovered per core. arch_timer_set_compare() is a no-op here (the
398:         * LAPIC stays periodic). Done BEFORE the tick so it reflects this IRQ. */
399:        timer_percpu_tick(get_cpu_info());
400:
401:        ret_regs = kernel_timer_tick(regs);
402:    } else {
403:        /* All other Hardware interrupts - route via generic system */
404:        pr_debug("AMD64: Hardware Interrupt Vector %lu triggered!\n", vec);
405:        extern struct pt_regs *irq_dispatch(uint32_t irq, struct pt_regs * regs);
406:        ret_regs = irq_dispatch(vec, regs);
407:    }
408:
409:    /* End-of-interrupt through the chip (IRQ-01 fix): pic_chip_end() owns
410:     * the complete LAPIC + 8259 sequence; nothing here EOIs by hand. */
411:    irq_chip_end((uint32_t)vec);
412:
413:    return ret_regs;
414:  }
415:
416:  return regs;
417:}
418:

@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/cpu/isr_stubs.S @@@
1:/* ============================================================
2: * hal/amd64/isr_stubs.S — 256 ISR entry stubs for x86-64
3: * ============================================================
4: * Each stub:
5: *   1. Pushes a dummy error code (0) if the CPU doesn't push one
6: *   2. Pushes the vector number
7: *   3. Jumps to common_isr_entry
8: *
9: * common_isr_entry saves all GP registers and calls nexs_isr_dispatch(IsrFrame*).
10: * ============================================================ */
11:
12:.extern amd64_isr_dispatch
13:
14:/* (The old HAS_ERR(v) macro was defined but never referenced — the ERR vs
15: * NOERR split is done by the explicit ISR_ERR/ISR_NOERR emission below, so it
16: * was dead. Removed.) */
17:
18:/* Generate a stub for vector V */
19:.altmacro
20:
21:.macro ISR_NOERR v
22:.global isr_stub_\v
23:isr_stub_\v:
24:    pushq $0
25:    pushq $\v
26:    jmp   common_isr_entry
27:.endm
28:
29:.macro MAKE_ISR_NOERR v
30:    ISR_NOERR %v
31:.endm
32:
33:.macro ISR_ERR v
34:.global isr_stub_\v
35:isr_stub_\v:
36:    pushq $\v
37:    jmp   common_isr_entry
38:.endm
39:
40:.macro MAKE_ISR_ERR v
41:    ISR_ERR %v
42:.endm
43:
44:.section .text
45:
46:/* Exceptions 0-31 */
47:ISR_NOERR 0
48:ISR_NOERR 1
49:ISR_NOERR 2
50:ISR_NOERR 3
51:ISR_NOERR 4
52:ISR_NOERR 5
53:ISR_NOERR 6
54:ISR_NOERR 7
55:ISR_ERR   8
56:ISR_NOERR 9
57:ISR_ERR   10
58:ISR_ERR   11
59:ISR_ERR   12
60:ISR_ERR   13
61:ISR_ERR   14
62:ISR_NOERR 15
63:ISR_NOERR 16
64:ISR_ERR   17
65:ISR_NOERR 18
66:ISR_NOERR 19
67:ISR_NOERR 20
68:ISR_ERR   21
69:ISR_NOERR 22
70:ISR_NOERR 23
71:ISR_NOERR 24
72:ISR_NOERR 25
73:ISR_NOERR 26
74:ISR_NOERR 27
75:ISR_NOERR 28
76:ISR_ERR   29
77:ISR_ERR   30
78:ISR_NOERR 31
79:
80:/* IRQs / Software interrupts 32-255 */
81:.set V, 32
82:.rept 224
83:MAKE_ISR_NOERR V
84:.set V, V+1
85:.endr
86:
87:/* ── Common handler ───────────────────────────────────────── */
88:common_isr_entry:
89:    cld                        /* SysV: C runs with DF=0 (rep movsb/stosb) */
90:    /* Check if we came from user mode (CS & 3 != 0)
91:     * Stack layout: vec (0), err (8), rip (16), cs (24) */
92:    testb $3, 24(%rsp)
93:    jz 1f
94:    swapgs
95:1:
96:    /* Save GP registers */
97:    pushq %rax
98:    pushq %rbx
99:    pushq %rcx
100:    pushq %rdx
101:    pushq %rsi
102:    pushq %rdi
103:    pushq %rbp
104:    pushq %r8
105:    pushq %r9
106:    pushq %r10
107:    pushq %r11
108:    pushq %r12
109:    pushq %r13
110:    pushq %r14
111:    pushq %r15
112:
113:    /* Pass pointer to pt_regs as first argument */
114:    movq  %rsp, %rdi
115:    call  amd64_isr_dispatch
116:    /* amd64_isr_dispatch returned the next context in rax; restore it via the
117:     * ONE shared epilogue (restore_context) the cooperative yield also uses.
118:     * The whole GP restore + swapgs-if-ring3 + iretq lives in one place now. */
119:    jmp   restore_context
120:
121:/*
122: * arch_cpu_yield - cooperative reschedule from KERNEL (task) context.
123: *
124: * Builds a pt_regs frame on the current kernel stack identical to what
125: * common_isr_entry would produce (synthetic iretq frame + vec/err + GP regs),
126: * calls schedule() (same signature/return as amd64_isr_dispatch: pt_regs* ->
127: * next pt_regs*), then restores the returned task's frame and iretq's into it.
128: *
129: * The saved frame's RIP is this function's return address and CS is the kernel
130: * selector, so when this thread is next scheduled the restoring context iretq's
131: * straight back into the C caller (kthread_block) with callee-saved registers
132: * intact and IRQs re-enabled (RFLAGS.IF set in the saved frame).  The restore
133: * tail mirrors common_isr_entry exactly, including the swapgs-if-returning-to-
134: * ring3 case (schedule may hand us a USER task's frame).
135: *
136: * Caller contract: IRQs masked on entry (kthread_block does cli); the frame
137: * build is then atomic.  Reuses the proven SLEEPING->schedule->wake_up path.
138: */
139:.global arch_cpu_yield
140:arch_cpu_yield:
141:    cli
142:    cld                        /* SysV: schedule()/C runs with DF=0 */
143:    popq  %r11                 /* r11 = return address; rsp -> caller frame */
144:    movq  %rsp, %r10           /* r10 = resume RSP (caller stack) */
145:    /* Synthetic iretq frame (high->low: ss, rsp, rflags, cs, rip). */
146:    pushq $0x10                /* ss  = kernel data */
147:    pushq %r10                 /* rsp = resume stack */
148:    pushq $0x202               /* rflags: IF set (IRQs on at resume) */
149:    pushq $0x08                /* cs  = kernel code */
150:    pushq %r11                 /* rip = caller return address */
151:    pushq $0                   /* err */
152:    pushq $0                   /* vec */
153:    /* GP regs in pt_regs order (rax first ... r15 last), as common_isr_entry. */
154:    pushq %rax
155:    pushq %rbx
156:    pushq %rcx
157:    pushq %rdx
158:    pushq %rsi
159:    pushq %rdi
160:    pushq %rbp
161:    pushq %r8
162:    pushq %r9
163:    pushq %r10
164:    pushq %r11
165:    pushq %r12
166:    pushq %r13
167:    pushq %r14
168:    pushq %r15
169:    movq  %rsp, %rdi
170:    call  schedule
171:    /* schedule() returned the next context in rax; restore it via the ONE
172:     * shared epilogue below (restore_context) — the same path the ISR entry
173:     * uses, so there is no second hand-rolled restore (DIR-06 / Phase 1.A). */
174:    jmp   restore_context
175:
176:/*
177: * restore_context - the single GP-register restore + iretq epilogue (amd64).
178: *
179: * Entered with rax = pointer to the pt_regs frame to load (the return value of
180: * amd64_isr_dispatch() or schedule()).  Points rsp at that frame, pops the GP
181: * file in pt_regs order, swaps GS back iff returning to ring 3, skips the
182: * vec+err slots and iretq's into the frame.  This is the ONLY copy of the
183: * restore sequence: common_isr_entry and arch_cpu_yield both reach it by jmp,
184: * so the frame layout lives in exactly one place (DIR-06).
185: */
186:.global restore_context
187:restore_context:
188:    movq  %rax, %rsp
189:    popq  %r15
190:    popq  %r14
191:    popq  %r13
192:    popq  %r12
193:    popq  %r11
194:    popq  %r10
195:    popq  %r9
196:    popq  %r8
197:    popq  %rbp
198:    popq  %rdi
199:    popq  %rsi
200:    popq  %rdx
201:    popq  %rcx
202:    popq  %rbx
203:    popq  %rax
204:    testb $3, 24(%rsp)         /* returning to ring3? (cs & 3) */
205:    jz    1f
206:    swapgs
207:1:
208:    addq  $16, %rsp            /* skip vec + err */
209:    iretq
210:
211:.macro QUAD_GEN v
212:    .quad isr_stub_\v
213:.endm
214:
215:.macro DO_QUAD v
216:    QUAD_GEN %v
217:.endm
218:
219:/* ── Table of stub addresses (used by idt_init) ─────────── */
220:.section .rodata
221:.global isr_stub_table
222:isr_stub_table:
223:.set V, 0
224:.rept 256
225:    DO_QUAD V
226:    .set V, V+1
227:.endr
228:

@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/cpu/msr.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/amd64/cpu/msr.c
3: * Model-Specific Register (MSR) Configuration for the SYSCALL Fast Path (x86-64)
4: *
5: * Responsibilities:
6: *   Configure the four MSRs that enable and control the SYSCALL/SYSRET
7: *   instruction pair on x86-64:
8: *     IA32_EFER  (0xC0000080) — enable SCE (System Call Enable) bit
9: *     IA32_STAR  (0xC0000081) — segment selectors for SYSCALL/SYSRET
10: *     IA32_LSTAR (0xC0000082) — kernel entry RIP for SYSCALL
11: *     IA32_FMASK (0xC0000084) — RFLAGS bits cleared on SYSCALL entry
12: *
13: * STAR encoding [verified static against gdt.c and pt_regs.h]:
14: *   STAR[47:32] = GDT_KERN_CODE (0x08) → SYSCALL loads CS=0x08 (kernel code),
15: *                                         SS=0x08+8=0x10 (kernel data).
16: *   STAR[63:48] = GDT_KERN_DATA (0x10) → SYSRET would load CS=0x10+16=0x20
17: *                                         (user code), SS=0x10+8=0x18 (user data).
18: *   These selectors match the GDT layout in gdt.c:100-103 and the segment
19: *   constants in pt_regs.h:99-107.  The STAR value is correct [static].
20: *
21: * FMASK: 0x600 clears IF (bit 9, interrupt enable) and DF (bit 10, direction
22: *   flag) on SYSCALL entry, preventing user RFLAGS from enabling interrupts or
23: *   setting DF in kernel context before the kernel stack is set up.
24: *
25: * Known issues:
26: *   SYS-AMD64-01 (W2 PERF/REFINE) The fast path is correctly configured via
27: *     LSTAR (syscall_entry in syscall.S), but the return path uses 'iretq'
28: *     instead of 'sysretq' (syscall.S:105-107).  This is intentional ("more
29: *     robust") but 20-50 cycles slower.  Prerequisites for sysretq are met
30: *     (RCX holds return RIP, R11 holds return RFLAGS), so the switch is
31: *     straightforward when the performance regression is deemed unacceptable.
32: */
33:#include <kernel/types.h>
34:#include <arch/arch.h>
35:#include <arch/amd64_internal.h>
36:#include <kernel/printk.h>
37:#include "gdt_defs.h"
38:
39:#define IA32_EFER       0xC0000080
40:#define IA32_STAR       0xC0000081
41:#define IA32_LSTAR      0xC0000082
42:#define IA32_FMASK      0xC0000084
43:
44:#define EFER_SCE        0x01       /* System Call Enable */
45:
46:/* GDT Selectors (Must match gdt.c) */
47:#ifndef GDT_KERN_CODE
48:#endif /* GDT_KERN_CODE */
49:#ifndef GDT_KERN_DATA
50:#endif /* GDT_KERN_DATA */
51:#ifndef GDT_USER_DATA
52:#endif /* GDT_USER_DATA */
53:#ifndef GDT_USER_CODE
54:#endif /* GDT_USER_CODE */
55:
56:extern void syscall_entry(void);
57:
58:/*
59: * amd64_syscall_init - program the SYSCALL MSRs for this CPU.
60: *
61: * Must be called after gdt_init() (so the GDT selectors are valid) and after
62: * the GS base is set (so syscall_entry can access cpu_info via %gs).
63: * Called from arch_cpu_init() for both BSP and APs (each CPU needs its own
64: * LSTAR/STAR/FMASK settings, though the values are identical across CPUs).
65: *
66: * Side effects:
67: *   - IA32_EFER.SCE = 1  : SYSCALL/SYSRET instructions enabled.
68: *   - IA32_STAR programmed: see file header for selector encoding.
69: *   - IA32_LSTAR = &syscall_entry : CPU will jump here on SYSCALL.
70: *   - IA32_FMASK = 0x600 : IF and DF cleared on SYSCALL entry.
71: *
72: * NOTE(SYS-AMD64-01): syscall_entry (syscall.S) currently returns via iretq,
73: * not sysretq.  The LSTAR/FMASK setup is correct for both; only the exit path
74: * in syscall.S needs to change to use sysretq.
75: */
76:void amd64_syscall_init(void) {
77:  uint64_t star;
78:
79:  /* IA32_EFER.SCE = 1: enable SYSCALL/SYSRET instructions */
80:  uint64_t efer = rdmsr(IA32_EFER);
81:  wrmsr(IA32_EFER, efer | EFER_SCE);
82:
83:  /* IA32_STAR (Bits 63:48 user CS/SS, Bits 47:32 kernel CS/SS)
84:   * Sysret computes User CS from Bits 63:48 + 16, and User SS from + 8.
85:   * Thus we put GDT_USER_DATA (0x18) there, so it yields User CS = 0x28, SS = 0x20??
86:   * Wait, Linux convention is:
87:   * SYSRET loads CS from STAR[63:48] + 16.
88:   * We want CS = 0x20 (GDT_USER_CODE). So STAR[63:48] must be 0x10 (GDT_KERN_DATA)? No.
89:   * If STAR[63:48] = 0x10.
90:   * CS = 0x10 + 16 = 0x20. (matches GDT_USER_CODE)
91:   * SS = 0x10 + 8 = 0x18.  (matches GDT_USER_DATA)
92:   *
93:   * SYSCALL loads CS from STAR[47:32].
94:   * We want CS = 0x08 (GDT_KERN_CODE).
95:   * SS = 0x08 + 8 = 0x10 (GDT_KERN_DATA).
96:   *
97:   * So STAR = (0x10ULL << 48) | (0x08ULL << 32)
98:   */
99:  star = ((uint64_t)GDT_KERN_DATA << 48) | ((uint64_t)GDT_KERN_CODE << 32);
100:  wrmsr(IA32_STAR, star);
101:
102:  /* IA32_LSTAR contains the RIP to jump to on syscall */
103:  wrmsr(IA32_LSTAR, (uint64_t)syscall_entry);
104:
105:  /* IA32_FMASK: RFLAGS to clear on syscall.
106:   * Mask interrupts (IF=0x200), Direction flag (DF=0x400)
107:   */
108:  wrmsr(IA32_FMASK, 0x200 | 0x400);
109:
110:  pr_info("AMD64 MSR SYSCALL configured\n");
111:}
112:

@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/cpu/syscall_hal.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/amd64/cpu/syscall_hal.c
3: * Thin AMD64 Syscall HAL — forwards to the arch-neutral dispatcher.
4: *
5: * This file is a minimal shim.  The actual syscall dispatch logic lives in
6: * kernel/core/syscall_dispatch.c (kernel_syscall_dispatcher).  amd64_syscall_handler
7: * was likely intended as a hook for any future amd64-specific pre/post processing
8: * (e.g. saving/restoring additional state) but currently does nothing beyond
9: * forwarding the frame pointer.
10: *
11: * Calling convention:
12: *   amd64_syscall_handler is currently not called from any assembly path;
13: *   both the SYSCALL fast path (syscall.S) and the int 0x80 slow path
14: *   (idt.c:amd64_isr_dispatch) invoke kernel_syscall_dispatcher directly.
15: *   This function is retained as a named hook for future use.
16: *
17: * No known defects specific to this file.
18: */
19:#include <kernel/types.h>
20:#include <arch/pt_regs.h>
21:#include <kernel/sched.h>
22:#include <kernel/printk.h>
23:
24:/* The generic syscall dispatcher is in kernel/core/syscall.c (if we created it)
25: * or currently in aarch64/cpu/syscall.c for now. Wait, I should make sure
26: * I extract the dispatcher.
27: */
28:
29:/* For now, just forward it. */
30:extern struct pt_regs *kernel_syscall_dispatcher(struct pt_regs *regs);
31:
32:struct pt_regs *amd64_syscall_handler(struct pt_regs *frame);
33:
34:/*
35: * amd64_syscall_handler - AMD64-specific syscall entry hook.
36: *
37: * Params:
38: *   frame - pointer to the pt_regs saved frame built by the entry stub.
39: *           On the SYSCALL fast path (syscall.S), this is the kernel stack
40: *           frame with rax = syscall number and rdi/rsi/rdx/r10/r8/r9 = args.
41: *           On the int 0x80 slow path (common_isr_entry), same layout.
42: *
43: * Returns the (possibly modified) pt_regs* that the entry stub will write to
44: * RSP before restoring GP registers.  A different return value performs an
45: * in-place context switch.
46: *
47: * Currently a direct forward; no amd64-specific pre/post logic is applied.
48: */
49:struct pt_regs *amd64_syscall_handler(struct pt_regs *frame) {
50:  return kernel_syscall_dispatcher(frame);
51:}

@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/cpu/syscall.S @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/amd64/cpu/syscall.S
3: * Fast Path Syscall Entry (MSR LSTAR)
4: */
5:
6:.section .text
7:.global syscall_entry
8:.extern kernel_syscall_dispatcher
9:
10:/*
11: * On entry:
12: *   RCX = Return RIP
13: *   R11 = Return RFLAGS
14: *   RSP = User Stack Pointer (NOT kernel stack!)
15: *
16: * We must:
17: *   1. SwapGS to get kernel per-CPU data (which contains kernel RSP)
18: *   2. Switch RSP to kernel stack
19: *   3. Push `struct pt_regs`
20: *   4. Call C handler
21: *   5. Restore registers
22: *   6. sysretq
23: */
24:
25:/* Minimal GS offsets for now.
26: * GS:0x00 will be Kernel RSP.
27: * GS:0x08 will be User RSP temp storage.
28: * Actually, to avoid SwapGS complexity initially, we can use the TSS rsp0
29: * directly if we are single-core, or just a global kernel_rsp.
30: * Wait, SYSCALL doesn't switch stacks automatically like interrupts do.
31: * If we don't have per-CPU GS set up yet, we can use a global variable
32: * to store the user RSP and load the kernel RSP, but that's not thread-safe.
33: * Let's assume SwapGS works and we set GS base to a `struct cpu_info` later.
34: */
35:
36:syscall_entry:
37:    /* Swap GS to kernel per-CPU data */
38:    swapgs
39:
40:    /* Store user RSP in cpu_info->user_stack_tmp (offset 24) */
41:    movq %rsp, %gs:24
42:    /* Load kernel RSP from cpu_info->stack_top (offset 16) */
43:    movq %gs:16, %rsp
44:
45:    /* Now we are on kernel stack. Construct pt_regs.
46:     * Match layout in pt_regs.h:
47:     * CPU pushes (conceptually): SS, RSP, RFLAGS, CS, RIP
48:     * We simulate the iret frame for compatibility with ISR dispatch
49:     */
50:    /* Build pt_regs frame manually (to match isr_stubs.S) 
51:     * Correct Order (High to Low): SS, RSP, RFLAGS, CS, RIP */
52:    pushq $0x1B         /* SS */
53:    pushq %gs:24        /* User RSP */
54:    pushq %r11          /* RFLAGS (saved in r11 by syscall) */
55:    pushq $0x23         /* CS */
56:    pushq %rcx          /* RIP (saved in rcx by syscall) */
57:
58:    /* "Error Code" and "Vector" */
59:    pushq $0            /* Error code */
60:    pushq $0x80         /* Vector (dummy for syscall) */
61:
62:    /* GP Registers */
63:    pushq %rax          /* System call number */
64:    pushq %rbx
65:    pushq %rcx          /* User RIP (saved by syscall) */
66:    pushq %rdx          /* Arg 2 */
67:    pushq %rsi          /* Arg 1 */
68:    pushq %rdi          /* Arg 0 */
69:    pushq %rbp
70:    pushq %r8           /* Arg 4 */
71:    pushq %r9           /* Arg 5 */
72:    pushq %r10          /* Arg 3 */
73:    pushq %r11          /* User RFLAGS (saved by syscall) */
74:    pushq %r12
75:    pushq %r13
76:    pushq %r14
77:    pushq %r15
78:
79:    /* Call C handler */
80:    movq %rsp, %rdi
81:    call kernel_syscall_dispatcher
82:    movq %rax, %rsp
83:
84:    /* Restore registers */
85:    /* Restore GP registers (Reverse order of pushes!) */
86:    popq  %r15
87:    popq  %r14
88:    popq  %r13
89:    popq  %r12
90:    popq  %r11
91:    popq  %r10
92:    popq  %r9
93:    popq  %r8
94:    popq  %rbp
95:    popq  %rdi
96:    popq  %rsi
97:    popq  %rdx
98:    popq  %rcx
99:    popq  %rbx
100:    popq  %rax
101:
102:    /* Skip error code and vector */
103:    addq $16, %rsp
104:
105:    /* Return via iretq (more robust than sysretq for now) */
106:    swapgs
107:    iretq
108:

1:#ifndef _ARCH_AMD64_H
2:#define _ARCH_AMD64_H
3:
4:#include <stdint.h>

12:/* --- Interrupt Control --- */
13:static inline void arch_impl_irq_enable(void) {
14:  __asm__ __volatile__("sti" ::: "memory");
15:}
16:
17:static inline void arch_impl_irq_disable(void) {
18:  __asm__ __volatile__("cli" ::: "memory");
19:}
20:
21:static inline void arch_impl_irq_save(uint64_t *flags) {
22:  __asm__ __volatile__("pushfq\n\t"
23:                       "popq %0\n\t"
24:                       "cli"
25:                       : "=r"(*flags)
26:                       :
27:                       : "memory");
28:}
29:
30:static inline void arch_impl_irq_restore(uint64_t flags) {
31:  __asm__ __volatile__("pushq %0\n\t"
32:                       "popfq"
33:                       :
34:                       : "r"(flags)
35:                       : "memory", "cc");
36:}
37:
38:static inline void arch_impl_irq_save_all(uint64_t *flags) {
39:  arch_impl_irq_save(flags);
40:}
41:
42:static inline void arch_impl_irq_restore_all(uint64_t flags) {
43:  arch_impl_irq_restore(flags);
44:}

46:static inline void arch_impl_irq_disable_all(void) {
47:  arch_impl_irq_disable();
48:}

51:static inline void arch_impl_nop(void) { __asm__ __volatile__("nop"); }
52:static inline void arch_impl_idle(void) { __asm__ __volatile__("hlt"); }
53:static inline void arch_impl_yield(void) { __asm__ __volatile__("pause"); }
54:static inline void arch_impl_cpu_notify(void) { /* NOP on x86 for now */ }

57:static inline void arch_impl_isb(void) { __asm__ __volatile__("mfence" ::: "memory"); }
58:static inline void arch_impl_mb(void)  { __asm__ __volatile__("mfence" ::: "memory"); }
59:static inline void arch_impl_rmb(void) { __asm__ __volatile__("lfence" ::: "memory"); }
60:static inline void arch_impl_wmb(void) { __asm__ __volatile__("sfence" ::: "memory"); }

62:static inline uint32_t arch_impl_get_cpu_id(void) {
63:  /* Use the actual LAPIC ID register for more accuracy than CPUID leaf 1.
64:   * 0xFEE00020 is the LAPIC-ID PHYSICAL address; access it through the
65:   * direct map (KERNEL_VIRT_BASE offset — identity while it is 0).  The
66:   * constant is open-coded instead of using phys_to_virt() to keep this
67:   * header free of include cycles with memlayout.h users. */
68:  return (*(volatile uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)(0xFEE00020UL + KERNEL_VIRT_BASE)) >> 24;
69:}

71:/* --- VMM / TLB --- */
72:static inline void arch_impl_set_pgd(uint64_t pgd) {
73:  __asm__ __volatile__("mov %0, %%cr3" ::"r"(pgd) : "memory");
74:}
75:
76:static inline uint64_t arch_impl_get_pgd(void) {
77:  uint64_t pgd;
78:  __asm__ __volatile__("mov %%cr3, %0" : "=r"(pgd));
79:  return pgd;
80:}
81:
82:/* On amd64 the kernel half lives in the same PML4 (indices 256..511), so
83: * the "kernel root" accessors are simple aliases of the CR3 ones.  They
84: * exist so shared code can address the kernel address-space root without
85: * caring that aarch64 keeps it in a separate register (TTBR1). */
86:static inline void arch_impl_set_kernel_pgd(uint64_t pgd) {
87:  arch_impl_set_pgd(pgd);
88:}
89:
90:static inline uint64_t arch_impl_get_kernel_pgd(void) {
91:  return arch_impl_get_pgd();
92:}
93:
94:/* PCID-tagged TLB (perf §3, DIR-06): set in cpu.c arch_cpu_init when CPUID
95: * reports PCID.  When PCID is enabled, a CR3 reload only flushes the CURRENT
96: * PCID's entries, so the full-flush primitive — which the SMP teardown shootdown
97: * (arch_tlb_shootdown_all in vmm_destroy_pgd) relies on to clear a dying address
98: * space before its tag is recycled — must drop EVERY tag. */
99:extern int amd64_pcid_enabled;
100:
101:/* Flush ALL TLB entries — every PCID plus globals — WITHOUT needing INVPCID
102: * (PCID-capable CPUs/hypervisors do not always expose INVPCID; e.g. HVF here
103: * reports pcid=1 invpcid=0).  Any MOV-to-CR4 that CHANGES CR4.PGE flushes the
104: * whole TLB including globals, so flip PGE then restore it: two full flushes
105: * that leave CR4 (and PCIDE) unchanged.  A transient interrupt during the flip
106: * only sees PGE momentarily toggled, which is harmless (it affects nothing in
107: * the two-instruction window). */
108:static inline void amd64_flush_all_pcids(void) {
109:  uint64_t cr4;
110:  __asm__ __volatile__("mov %%cr4, %0" : "=r"(cr4));
111:  __asm__ __volatile__("mov %0, %%cr4" ::"r"(cr4 ^ (1UL << 7)) : "memory");
112:  __asm__ __volatile__("mov %0, %%cr4" ::"r"(cr4) : "memory");
113:}
114:
115:static inline void arch_impl_tlb_flush_local(void) {
116:  if (amd64_pcid_enabled) {
117:    amd64_flush_all_pcids();
118:    return;
119:  }
120:  uint64_t cr3;
121:  __asm__ __volatile__("mov %%cr3, %0\n\t"
122:                       "mov %0, %%cr3"
123:                       : "=r"(cr3)::"memory");
124:}
125:
126:static inline void arch_impl_tlb_flush_all(void) {
127:  arch_impl_tlb_flush_local();
128:}
129:
130:static inline void arch_impl_tlb_flush_va(uintptr_t va) {
131:  __asm__ __volatile__("invlpg (%0)" ::"r"(va) : "memory");
132:}
133:
134:/* SMP TLB shootdown (MM-VMM-05/AMMU-08): invlpg and CR3 reloads are strictly
135: * LOCAL on x86 — there is no hardware broadcast like AArch64's TLBI *IS.
136: * Implemented in kernel/arch/amd64/mm/tlb.c with a fixed-vector LAPIC IPI
137: * (vector 0xFD) and bounded acknowledgement wait. */
138:void amd64_tlb_shootdown_va(uintptr_t va);
139:void amd64_tlb_shootdown_all(void);
140:void amd64_tlb_ipi_init(void);
141:static inline void arch_impl_tlb_shootdown_va(uintptr_t va) {
142:  amd64_tlb_shootdown_va(va);
143:}
144:static inline void arch_impl_tlb_shootdown_all(void) {
145:  amd64_tlb_shootdown_all();
146:}

148:/* Cache Control */
149:static inline void arch_impl_cache_clean_range(void *start, size_t size) {
150:  uint64_t s = (uint64_t)start;
151:  uint64_t e = s + size;
152:  s &= ~63UL;
153:  for (; s < e; s += 64) {
154:    __asm__ __volatile__("clflush (%0)" ::"r"(s) : "memory");
155:  }
156:}

158:static inline void arch_impl_cache_sync_icache(void *start, size_t size) {
159:  (void)start;
160:  (void)size;
161:  __asm__ __volatile__("mfence" ::: "memory");
162:}

164:/* --- Timer --- */
165:/* tsc_hz: measured TSC frequency, published by tsc_calibrate() in
166: * kernel/arch/amd64/cpu/apic.c (declared there and in arch/amd64/apic.h;
167: * re-declared here so this header has no include dependency on apic.h).
168: * Zero until calibration runs on the BSP. */
169:extern uint64_t tsc_hz;
170:
171:/* arch_impl_timer_get_freq - the HAL real-time-reference frequency (Hz).
172: *
173: * Returns the calibrated TSC frequency (tsc_hz).  Before tsc_calibrate() runs
174: * on the BSP, tsc_hz is 0; this returns a SAFE 1 GHz fallback so early callers
175: * of the arch-neutral mono_ns() (kernel/core/timer.c) never divide by zero.
176: * After calibration the real measured value is returned. */
177:static inline uint64_t arch_impl_timer_get_freq(void) {
178:  return tsc_hz ? tsc_hz : 1000000000ULL; /* fallback until BSP calibration */
179:}
180:
181:static inline uint64_t arch_impl_timer_get_count(void) {
182:  uint32_t lo, hi;
183:  __asm__ __volatile__("rdtsc" : "=a"(lo), "=d"(hi));
184:  return ((uint64_t)hi << 32) | lo;
185:}
186:
187:static inline void arch_impl_timer_set_compare(uint64_t val) { (void)val; }
188:static inline void arch_impl_timer_control(uint32_t val) { (void)val; }
189:
190:/* --- Entropy (ISA primitive) --- */
191:/* arch_impl_hw_random: one attempt at RDRAND (the on-chip DRBG).  Returns 1 and
192: * writes *out on success; 0 if CPUID.01h:ECX[30] does not advertise RDRAND (the
193: * default QEMU CPU model) or the read transiently failed.  Pure ISA wrapper:
194: * the retry/mix policy lives in the generic entropy layer (kernel/lib/entropy.c). */
195:static inline int arch_impl_hw_random(uint64_t *out) {
196:    uint32_t a, b, c, d;
197:    __asm__ __volatile__("cpuid"
198:                         : "=a"(a), "=b"(b), "=c"(c), "=d"(d)
199:                         : "0"(1u), "2"(0u));
200:    if (!(c & (1u << 30)))
201:        return 0; /* no RDRAND */
202:    uint64_t r;
203:    unsigned char ok;
204:    __asm__ __volatile__("rdrand %0; setc %1" : "=r"(r), "=qm"(ok));
205:    if (!ok)
206:        return 0; /* transient failure */
207:    *out = r;
208:    return 1;
209:}
210:
211:/* --- Spinlocks --- */
212:static inline void arch_impl_spin_lock(volatile uint32_t *lock) {
213:    while (__sync_lock_test_and_set(lock, 1)) {
214:        while (*lock) __asm__ __volatile__("pause");
215:    }
216:}
217:
218:static inline void arch_impl_spin_unlock(volatile uint32_t *lock) {
219:    __sync_lock_release(lock);
220:}
221:
222:static inline int arch_impl_spin_trylock(volatile uint32_t *lock) {
223:    return __sync_lock_test_and_set(lock, 1) == 0;
224:}
225:
226:/* --- System Registers --- */
227:static inline uint64_t arch_impl_get_fault_address(void) {
228:  uint64_t cr2;
229:  __asm__ __volatile__("mov %%cr2, %0" : "=r"(cr2));
230:  return cr2;
231:}
232:
233:static inline uint64_t rdmsr(uint32_t msr) {
234:  uint32_t low, high;
235:  __asm__ __volatile__("rdmsr" : "=a"(low), "=d"(high) : "c"(msr));
236:  return ((uint64_t)high << 32) | low;
237:}
238:
239:static inline void wrmsr(uint32_t msr, uint64_t val) {
240:  uint32_t low = (uint32_t)val;
241:  uint32_t high = (uint32_t)(val >> 32);
242:  __asm__ __volatile__("wrmsr" : : "a"(low), "d"(high), "c"(msr));
243:}
244:
245:static inline void outb(uint16_t port, uint8_t val) {
246:  __asm__ __volatile__("outb %0, %1" : : "a"(val), "Nd"(port));
247:}
248:
249:/* arch_impl_reboot - reset the machine: the 0xCF9 reset-control register first,
250: * then the 8042 keyboard-controller reset line as a fallback (DIR-05 #139
251: * watchdog).  Used by the HAL arch_reboot() wrapper. */
252:static inline void arch_impl_reboot(void) {
253:  outb(0xCF9, 0x02); /* RST_CPU prepare */
254:  outb(0xCF9, 0x0E); /* FULL_RST | RST_CPU | SYS_RST -> hard reset */
255:  outb(0x64, 0xFE);  /* 8042 pulse the CPU reset line (fallback) */
256:}
257:
258:static inline uint8_t inb(uint16_t port) {
259:  uint8_t val;
260:  __asm__ __volatile__("inb %1, %0" : "=a"(val) : "Nd"(port));
261:  return val;
262:}
263:
264:static inline void outw(uint16_t port, uint16_t val) {
265:  __asm__ __volatile__("outw %0, %1" : : "a"(val), "Nd"(port));
266:}
267:
268:static inline uint16_t inw(uint16_t port) {
269:  uint16_t val;
270:  __asm__ __volatile__("inw %1, %0" : "=a"(val) : "Nd"(port));
271:  return val;
272:}
273:
274:static inline void outl(uint16_t port, uint32_t val) {
275:  __asm__ __volatile__("outl %0, %1" : : "a"(val), "Nd"(port));
276:}
277:
278:static inline uint32_t inl(uint16_t port) {
279:  uint32_t val;
280:  __asm__ __volatile__("inl %1, %0" : "=a"(val) : "Nd"(port));
281:  return val;
282:}
283:
284:static inline uint64_t arch_impl_get_fault_status(void) {
285:  return 0; /* x86 uses error code on stack */
286:}
287:
288:/* --- Constants --- */
289:#define HAL_RAM_START 0x0UL
290:#define HAL_RAM_SIZE  0x40000000UL
291:#define HAL_ALIAS_OFFSET 0x0UL
292:
293:#endif /* _ARCH_AMD64_H */
294:
