@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/include/arch/pt_regs.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/amd64/include/arch/pt_regs.h
3: * x86-64 register frame layout
4: *
5: * Must match the stack layout in isr_stubs.S and syscall.S exactly.
6: * Layout: GP regs pushed by stub, then CPU-pushed interrupt frame.
7: */
8:#ifndef _ARCH_AMD64_PT_REGS_H
9:#define _ARCH_AMD64_PT_REGS_H
10:
11:#include <kernel/nx_contract.h>
12:#include <stdint.h>
13:
14:/*
15: * Full Register State for x86-64 exceptions/syscalls.
16: * Pushed by isr_stubs.S (GP regs) + CPU (iret frame).
17: */
18:struct pt_regs {
19:  /* Pushed by software (isr_stubs.S common_isr_entry) */
20:  uint64_t r15;
21:  uint64_t r14;
22:  uint64_t r13;
23:  uint64_t r12;
24:  uint64_t r11;
25:  uint64_t r10;
26:  uint64_t r9;
27:  uint64_t r8;
28:  uint64_t rbp;
29:  uint64_t rdi;
30:  uint64_t rsi;
31:  uint64_t rdx;
32:  uint64_t rcx;
33:  uint64_t rbx;
34:  uint64_t rax;
35:
36:  /* Pushed by ISR stub */
37:  uint64_t vec; /* interrupt/exception vector number */
38:  uint64_t err; /* error code (0 if none) */
39:
40:  /* CPU-pushed interrupt/iretq frame */
41:  uint64_t rip;
42:  uint64_t cs;
43:  uint64_t rflags;
44:  uint64_t rsp; /* user RSP (only valid from Ring 3) */
45:  uint64_t ss;  /* user SS  (only valid from Ring 3) */
46:};
47:
48:/*
49: * The layout above is built BY HAND in assembly — syscall_entry in
50: * kernel/arch/amd64/cpu/syscall.S pushes these fields one at a time, and
51: * common_isr_entry in isr_stubs.S does the same for the interrupt path.  The C
52: * struct and those push sequences are two statements of one layout with
53: * nothing connecting them, so inserting a field here would silently shift
54: * every offset the assembly writes and the dispatcher reads.
55: *
56: * `rip` at 0x88 is not a decorative number: it is the offset the compiler
57: * emits for pt_regs_retry_syscall's `r->rip -= 2`, and a kernel #PF writing to
58: * frame+0x88 is what made that visible.  Pinning these three makes a reorder a
59: * BUILD failure at the edit instead of a page fault at runtime.
60: */
61:NX_ASSERT_OFFSET(struct pt_regs, rbx, 0x68);
62:NX_ASSERT_OFFSET(struct pt_regs, rax, 0x70);
63:NX_ASSERT_OFFSET(struct pt_regs, vec, 0x78);
64:NX_ASSERT_OFFSET(struct pt_regs, err, 0x80);
65:NX_ASSERT_OFFSET(struct pt_regs, rip, 0x88);
66:NX_ASSERT_SIZE(struct pt_regs, 0xB0);
67:
68:/* ─── Architecture-Agnostic Accessors ─── */
69:
70:/* Syscall number: RAX on x86-64 (Linux convention) */
71:static inline uint64_t pt_regs_syscall_num(struct pt_regs *r) {
72:  return r->rax;
73:}
74:
75:/* Syscall arguments: RDI, RSI, RDX, R10, R8, R9 (Linux x86-64 ABI) */
76:static inline uint64_t pt_regs_arg(struct pt_regs *r, int n) {
77:  switch (n) {
78:  case 0:
79:    return r->rdi;
80:  case 1:
81:    return r->rsi;
82:  case 2:
83:    return r->rdx;
84:  case 3:
85:    return r->r10; /* R10 replaces RCX (clobbered by syscall) */
86:  case 4:
87:    return r->r8;
88:  case 5:
89:    return r->r9;
90:  default:
91:    return 0;
92:  }
93:}
94:
95:/* Set syscall return value: RAX on x86-64 */
96:static inline void pt_regs_set_return(struct pt_regs *r, uint64_t v) {
97:  r->rax = v;
98:}
99:
100:/* Get program counter (RIP) */
101:static inline uint64_t pt_regs_pc(struct pt_regs *r) { return r->rip; }
102:
103:/* Set program counter */
104:static inline void pt_regs_set_pc(struct pt_regs *r, uint64_t v) {
105:  r->rip = v;
106:}
107:
108:/* Get user stack pointer (RSP from iret frame) */
109:static inline uint64_t pt_regs_user_sp(struct pt_regs *r) { return r->rsp; }
110:
111:/* Set user stack pointer */
112:static inline void pt_regs_set_user_sp(struct pt_regs *r, uint64_t v) {
113:  r->rsp = v;
114:}
115:
116:/* Retry syscall: rewind PC by 2 bytes (syscall instruction is 0F 05) */
117:static inline void pt_regs_retry_syscall(struct pt_regs *r) { r->rip -= 2; }
118:
119:/* Initialize context for a user-mode process (ELF entry)
120: * GDT_USER_CODE=0x20 → selector 0x23 (ring3), GDT_USER_DATA=0x18 → 0x1B */
121:static inline void pt_regs_init_user_task(struct pt_regs *r, uint64_t entry,
122:                                           uint64_t usp) {
123:  r->rip    = entry;
124:  r->rsp    = usp;
125:  r->rflags = 0x202;  /* IF + reserved */
126:  r->cs     = 0x23;   /* user code segment, ring 3 */
127:  r->ss     = 0x1B;   /* user data segment, ring 3 */
128:  
129:  /* For AMD64, SYSRET uses RCX for RIP and R11 for RFLAGS. 
130:   * If we return via sysretq path (context switch during syscall),
131:   * these must be correctly initialized. */
132:  r->rcx = entry;
133:  r->r11 = 0x202;
134:}
135:
136:/* Pass main()'s argc/argv to a fresh user task (System V AMD64: rdi, rsi).
137: * Call after pt_regs_init_user_task(); argv is a user virtual address. */
138:static inline void pt_regs_set_user_args(struct pt_regs *r, uint64_t argc,
139:                                         uint64_t argv) {
140:  r->rdi = argc;
141:  r->rsi = argv;
142:}
143:
144:/* Initialize context for a kernel-mode thread */
145:static inline void pt_regs_init_kernel_task(struct pt_regs *r, uint64_t entry,
146:                                             uint64_t ksp) {
147:  r->rip    = entry;
148:  r->cs     = 0x08;   /* kernel code segment */
149:  r->rflags = 0x202;  /* IF + reserved */
150:  r->rsp    = ksp;
151:  r->ss     = 0x10;   /* kernel data segment */
152:}
153:
154:#endif /* _ARCH_AMD64_PT_REGS_H */
155:

@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/kinit/start.S @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/amd64/boot/start.S — higher-half bring-up.
3: *
4: * The .text.boot code below is linked at VA == PA (1MB, see kernel.ld)
5: * because it runs in 32-bit protected mode and during the paging switch.
6: * The kernel proper is linked at KERNEL_VIRT_BASE + 2MB (memlayout.h).
7: *
8: * Boot page tables (in .boot_bss, low):
9: *   boot_pml4[0]   -> boot_pdpt   identity:    VA 0..1GB  -> PA 0..1GB
10: *   boot_pml4[256] -> boot_pdpt   higher half: KVB+0..1GB -> PA 0..1GB
11: *   boot_pdpt[0]   -> boot_pd       (2MB pages, PA 0..1GB)
12: *   boot_pdpt[3]   -> boot_pd_high  (2MB pages, PA 3..4GB: LAPIC/MMIO,
13: *                                    visible both identity and at KVB+3GB)
14: * Sharing boot_pdpt between PML4[0] and PML4[256] gives the direct map
15: * and the identity map for free with one set of tables.  APs boot on the
16: * same boot_pml4 (kernel_pgd_phys is patched into the trampoline), so
17: * they can reach the high secondary_cpu_entry before adopting the real
18: * kernel PGD in arch_cpu_init.
19: */
20:#include <kernel/cpu.h>
21:
22:.section .multiboot, "a"
23:.align 8
24:multiboot2_header:
25:    .long 0xe85250d6        /* Multiboot 2 Magic */
26:    .long 0                 /* Architecture: i386 */
27:    .long multiboot2_header_end - multiboot2_header
28:    .long -(0xe85250d6 + 0 + (multiboot2_header_end - multiboot2_header))
29:
30:    .align 8
31:    .short 3
32:    .short 0
33:    .long 12
34:    .long _start_32
35:
36:    .align 8
37:    .short 0
38:    .short 0
39:    .long 8
40:multiboot2_header_end:
41:
42:/* PVH Header */
43:.section .note.PVH, "a"
44:.align 4
45:    .long 4             /* Namesz */
46:    .long 4             /* Descsz */
47:    .long 18            /* Type (XEN_ELFNOTE_PHYS32_ENTRY) */
48:    .ascii "Xen\0"      /* Name */
49:    .long _start_32     /* Desc (Entry point) */
50:
51:.section .text.boot, "ax"
52:.code32
53:.global _start_32
54:_start_32:
55:    cli
56:    cld
57:
58:    /* 2. Setup temporary stack */
59:    movl $boot_stack_top, %esp
60:
61:    /* Save magic and info on stack */
62:    pushl %eax
63:    pushl %ebx
64:
65:    /* 1. Setup minimal GDT for 32-bit mode */
66:    lgdt (boot_gdtr_32)
67:    movw $0x10, %ax
68:    movw %ax, %ds
69:    movw %ax, %es
70:    movw %ax, %ss
71:    movw %ax, %fs
72:    movw %ax, %gs
73:
74:    /* GDT already loaded, segments set */
75:
76:    /* 3. Clear Page Tables */
77:    movl $boot_pml4, %edi
78:    xorl %eax, %eax
79:    movl $4096, %ecx /* 4 pages * 1024 dwords each */
80:    rep stosl
81:
82:    /* 4. Enable PAE */
83:    movl %cr4, %eax
84:    orl $(1 << 5), %eax
85:    movl %eax, %cr4
86:
87:    /* 5. Setup Page Tables (identity 1GB + higher-half alias) */
88:    movl $boot_pdpt, %eax
89:    orl $3, %eax
90:    movl %eax, (boot_pml4)          /* PML4[0]:   identity low */
91:    movl $0, (boot_pml4 + 4)
92:    movl %eax, (boot_pml4 + 2048)   /* PML4[256]: KERNEL_VIRT_BASE alias */
93:    movl $0, (boot_pml4 + 2052)
94:
95:    movl $boot_pd, %eax
96:    orl $3, %eax
97:    movl %eax, (boot_pdpt)
98:    movl $0, (boot_pdpt + 4)
99:
100:    /* PDPT[3] = boot_pd_high (for 3GB-4GB: LAPIC and friends) */
101:    movl $boot_pd_high, %eax
102:    orl $3, %eax
103:    movl %eax, (boot_pdpt + 24)
104:    movl $0, (boot_pdpt + 28)
105:
106:    /* PD[0..511] = 0, 2MB, 4MB, ... 1GB */
107:    movl $boot_pd, %edi
108:    movl $0x83, %eax
109:    movl $512, %ecx
110:.fill_pd:
111:    movl %eax, (%edi)
112:    movl $0, 4(%edi)
113:    addl $0x200000, %eax
114:    addl $8, %edi
115:    loop .fill_pd
116:
117:    /* PD_HIGH (3GB-4GB) */
118:    movl $boot_pd_high, %edi
119:    movl $0xC0000083, %eax
120:    movl $512, %ecx
121:.fill_pd_high:
122:    movl %eax, (%edi)
123:    movl $0, 4(%edi)
124:    addl $0x200000, %eax
125:    addl $8, %edi
126:    loop .fill_pd_high
127:
128:    /* 6. Load PML4 */
129:    movl $boot_pml4, %eax
130:    movl %eax, %cr3
131:
132:    /* 7. Enable Long Mode + NXE (PTE bit 63 — W^X needs it; without NXE a
133:     * set NX bit is a reserved-bit #PF) */
134:    movl $0xC0000080, %ecx
135:    rdmsr
136:    orl $(1 << 8 | 1 << 11), %eax
137:    wrmsr
138:
139:    /* 8. Enable Paging */
140:    movl %cr0, %eax
141:    orl $(1 << 31 | 1 << 16), %eax
142:    movl %eax, %cr0
143:
144:    /* Restore magic and info from stack */
145:    popl %esi    /* Info */
146:    popl %ebp    /* Magic */
147:
148:    /* 9. Jump to 64-bit (still in the low boot section) */
149:    /* Debug: Print 'C' */
150:    movb $'C', %al
151:    movw $0x3f8, %dx
152:    outb %al, %dx
153:
154:    pushl $0x08
155:    pushl $_start_64_low
156:    lret
157:
158:.code64
159:_start_64_low:
160:    /* Reload GDTR with the 64-bit descriptor (same boot GDT) */
161:    lgdt (boot_gdtr_64)
162:
163:    /* Segment registers to NULL */
164:    xorl %eax, %eax
165:    movw %ax, %ds
166:    movw %ax, %es
167:    movw %ax, %fs
168:    movw %ax, %gs
169:    movw %ax, %ss
170:
171:    /* Save magic and info to the (high) kernel .data while both the
172:     * identity and the higher-half mappings are live */
173:    movl %ebp, %eax
174:    movabsq $mb_magic, %rcx
175:    movq %rax, (%rcx)
176:    movl %esi, %eax
177:    movabsq $mb_info_ptr, %rcx
178:    movq %rax, (%rcx)
179:
180:    /* Debug: Print 'E' */
181:    movb $'E', %al
182:    movw $0x3f8, %dx
183:    outb %al, %dx
184:
185:    /* Jump to the link address (higher half) */
186:    movabsq $_start_64_high, %rax
187:    jmp *%rax
188:
189:/* ── Higher half from here on ──────────────────────────────────────── */
190:.section .text
191:.code64
192:_start_64_high:
193:    /* Debug: Print 'F' */
194:    movb $'F', %al
195:    movw $0x3f8, %dx
196:    outb %al, %dx
197:
198:    /* Clear BSS */
199:    movabsq $__bss_start, %rdi
200:    movabsq $__bss_end, %rcx
201:    subq %rdi, %rcx
202:    jz .bss_done
203:    xorq %rax, %rax
204:    rep stosb
205:.bss_done:
206:
207:    /* Debug: Print 'G' */
208:    movb $'G', %al
209:    movw $0x3f8, %dx
210:    outb %al, %dx
211:
212:    movabsq $__kernel_stack, %rsp
213:    addq $131072, %rsp
214:    movq %rsp, %rbp
215:
216:    movq mb_magic(%rip), %rdi
217:    movq mb_info_ptr(%rip), %rsi
218:    call kernel_main
219:
220:.halt:
221:    hlt
222:    jmp .halt
223:
224:.global secondary_cpu_entry
225:secondary_cpu_entry:
226:    /* Debug: Print 'S' */
227:    movb $'S', %al
228:    movw $0x3f8, %dx
229:    outb %al, %dx
230:    cli
231:    xorl %eax, %eax
232:    movw %ax, %ds
233:    movw %ax, %es
234:    movw %ax, %fs
235:    movw %ax, %gs
236:    movw %ax, %ss
237:    call arch_cpu_init
238:    call kernel_secondary_main
239:
240:.global arch_yield
241:arch_yield:
242:    pause
243:    ret
244:
245:.global arch_impl_idle
246:arch_impl_idle:
247:    hlt
248:    ret
249:
250:/* Boot GDT must stay in the low region: the 32-bit lgdt runs pre-paging
251: * and the descriptor bases are physical addresses. */
252:.section .boot_bss, "aw", @nobits
253:.align 4096
254:boot_stack:
255:    .skip 4096
256:boot_stack_top:
257:
258:.align 4096
259:.global boot_pml4
260:boot_pml4: .skip 4096
261:.global boot_pdpt
262:boot_pdpt: .skip 4096
263:.global boot_pd
264:boot_pd:   .skip 4096
265:.global boot_pd_high
266:boot_pd_high: .skip 4096
267:
268:.section .text.boot, "ax"
269:.align 16
270:boot_gdt:
271:    .quad 0x0000000000000000 /* Null */
272:    .quad 0x00af9a000000ffff /* Kernel Code 64 */
273:    .quad 0x00cf92000000ffff /* Kernel Data 64 (Usable in 32-bit too) */
274:boot_gdt_end:
275:
276:boot_gdtr_32:
277:    .word boot_gdt_end - boot_gdt - 1
278:    .long boot_gdt
279:
280:boot_gdtr_64:
281:    .word boot_gdt_end - boot_gdt - 1
282:    .quad boot_gdt
283:
284:/* Kernel proper data (higher half) */
285:.section .data
286:.global mb_magic, mb_info_ptr
287:mb_magic:    .quad 0
288:mb_info_ptr: .quad 0
289:
290:.global kernel_pgd_phys
291:kernel_pgd_phys: .quad boot_pml4
292:
293:.section .bss
294:.align 4096
295:.global __kernel_stack
296:__kernel_stack:
297:    .skip 131072 * MAX_CPUS
298:.global __kernel_stack_top
299:__kernel_stack_top:
300:

@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/kinit/trampoline.S @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/amd64/boot/trampoline.S
3: * Secondary CPU Trampoline (16-bit -> 64-bit)
4: */
5:.section .trampoline, "ax"
6:.code16
7:
8:.global trampoline_start
9:.global trampoline_end
10:
11:trampoline_start:
12:    cli
13:    cld
14:
15:    /* Set up segments */
16:    xor %ax, %ax
17:    mov %ax, %ds
18:    mov %ax, %es
19:    mov %ax, %ss
20:
21:    /* Load temporary GDT */
22:    lgdtl (trampoline_gdt_ptr - trampoline_start + 0x1000)
23:
24:    /* Enable Protected Mode */
25:    mov %cr0, %eax
26:    or $1, %eax
27:    mov %eax, %cr0
28:
29:    /* Long jump to protected mode */
30:    ljmp $0x08, $(trampoline_pm - trampoline_start + 0x1000)
31:
32:.code32
33:trampoline_pm:
34:    mov $0x10, %ax
35:    mov %ax, %ds
36:    mov %ax, %es
37:    mov %ax, %ss
38:
39:    /* Enable PAE */
40:    mov %cr4, %eax
41:    or $(1 << 5), %eax
42:    mov %eax, %cr4
43:
44:    /* Load PML4 */
45:    mov (trampoline_pml4 - trampoline_start + 0x1000), %eax
46:    mov %eax, %cr3
47:
48:    /* Enable Long Mode + NXE in EFER (APs must match the BSP: kernel_pgd
49:     * PTEs carry the NX bit) */
50:    mov $0xC0000080, %ecx
51:    rdmsr
52:    or $(1 << 8 | 1 << 11), %eax
53:    wrmsr
54:
55:    /* Enable Paging and Write Protect */
56:    mov %cr0, %eax
57:    or $(1 << 31 | 1 << 16), %eax
58:    mov %eax, %cr0
59:
60:    /* Long jump to 64-bit mode */
61:    ljmp $0x18, $(trampoline_lm - trampoline_start + 0x1000)
62:
63:.code64
64:trampoline_lm:
65:    /* Load stack pointer */
66:    mov (trampoline_stack - trampoline_start + 0x1000), %rsp
67:    
68:    /* Call C entry point */
69:    mov (trampoline_entry - trampoline_start + 0x1000), %rax
70:    call *%rax
71:
72:    /* Should not return */
73:1:  hlt
74:    jmp 1b
75:
76:.align 16
77:trampoline_gdt:
78:    .quad 0x0000000000000000 /* Null */
79:    .quad 0x00cf9a000000ffff /* 32-bit Code */
80:    .quad 0x00cf92000000ffff /* 32-bit Data */
81:    .quad 0x00af9a000000ffff /* 64-bit Code */
82:trampoline_gdt_end:
83:
84:trampoline_gdt_ptr:
85:    .word (trampoline_gdt_end - trampoline_gdt - 1)
86:    .long (trampoline_gdt - trampoline_start + 0x1000)
87:
88:.align 8
89:.global trampoline_pml4
90:.global trampoline_stack
91:.global trampoline_entry
92:trampoline_pml4:  .long 0
93:trampoline_stack: .quad 0
94:trampoline_entry: .quad 0
95:
96:trampoline_end:
97:

@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/mm/mmu.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/amd64/mm/mmu.c
3: * x86-64 Four-Level Paging (PML4 / PDPT / PD / PT) Implementation
4: *
5: * Responsibilities:
6: *   - arch_vmm_init_hw: switch to the kernel PML4, direct-map all usable
7: *     RAM regions reported by the platform, and map the MMIO window.
8: *   - arch_vmm_map / arch_vmm_unmap / arch_vmm_get_physical: single-page
9: *     4KB operations that walk/allocate/free PML4→PDPT→PD→PT chains.
10: *   - arch_vmm_map_range: bulk mapping using 2MB large pages where alignment
11: *     and size permit, falling back to 4KB pages.
12: *   - arch_vmm_create_process_pgd: process address-space creation (PML4
13: *     clone; teardown is the generic vmm_destroy_pgd in kernel/mm/vmm.c).
14: *   - arch_vmm_protect: 4KB-precise attribute rewrite of existing mappings
15: *     (splits large pages as needed; ends with an SMP TLB shootdown).
16: *   - arch_vmm_map_mmio: maps the PCI/LAPIC/MMIO window 0xFE000000–
17: *     0xFFFFFFFF at its direct-map VA + the low-2MB identity window for
18: *     the SMP trampoline and the low-linked boot sections.
19: *
20: * Invariants (higher-half model, see kernel/memlayout.h):
21: *   - Kernel VA = PA + KERNEL_VIRT_BASE (0xFFFF800000000000) for the image,
22: *     all RAM and MMIO; PA<->pointer crossings go through
23: *     phys_to_virt()/virt_to_phys().  The kernel half lives in PML4
24: *     entries 256..511, shared with processes by value-copy at creation.
25: *   - Boot PML4 (boot_pml4, identity + higher-half alias of PA 0..1GB):
26: *     established by start.S; the kernel switches to the dynamic PML4 in
27: *     arch_vmm_init_hw; APs still boot on boot_pml4 and adopt kernel_pgd
28: *     in arch_cpu_init.
29: *   - Intermediate page-table pages are allocated from pmm_alloc_page() and
30: *     are never freed; the page-table tree only grows.
31: *
32: * Known issues:
33: *   AMMU-01 RESOLVED (Phase B2, b745a74): x86_leaf_flags() translates the
34: *     vmm.h profiles explicitly (opt-in RW, native PTE_NX honoured);
35: *     vmm_map_ram_wx() maps text RX, rodata RO+NX, other RAM RW+NX.
36: *   AMMU-02 RESOLVED (Phase B2): arch_vmm_protect is real — 4KB-precise
37: *     attribute rewrite with large-page splitting and SMP TLB shootdown.
38: *   AMMU-03 (FIXED) the divergent arch teardown was removed; the single
39: *     path is vmm_destroy_pgd() in kernel/mm/vmm.c, which frees private
40: *     table pages and PTE_USER frames (see its ownership rules).
41: *   AMMU-04 (W2 BUG) get_next_table's large-page split code never runs in
42: *     arch_vmm_map (which passes level=0 for the PML4→PDPT step, skipping the
43: *     block-split branch); the vmm.c generic walker does not understand 2MB/1GB
44: *     blocks at all — walking a region mapped by arch_vmm_map_range (2MB pages)
45: *     via vmm.c's get_next_table dereferences the block entry as a table pointer.
46: *   AMMU-05 (W2 SECURITY) All intermediate page-table entries (PDPT/PD/PT)
47: *     are tagged X86_PTE_US (user-accessible), making them more permissive than
48: *     necessary; only leaf PTEs for user pages need X86_PTE_US.
49: *   AMMU-06 (W2 PERF) arch_vmm_map_mmio maps 0xFE000000–0xFFFFFFFF one 4KB
50: *     page at a time (~8192 iterations) at every PGD setup.  A single 2MB page
51: *     or a pre-computed PDPT entry would suffice.
52: *   AMMU-07 (W2 PERF/REFINE) MMIO identity-mapped only for 0xFE000000–
53: *     0xFFFFFFFF.  Devices with BAR addresses outside this window are unmapped.
54: *   AMMU-08 RESOLVED (Phase B2): arch_vmm_unmap performs an IPI-based SMP
55: *     shootdown (amd64_tlb_shootdown_va, kernel/arch/amd64/mm/tlb.c) so peer
56: *     CPUs cannot keep using a cleared mapping.  arch_vmm_map keeps its local
57: *     invlpg only: x86 TLBs do not cache not-present entries, so mapping a
58: *     previously-absent VA needs no remote flush, and today's callers never
59: *     live-remap a VA that another CPU is concurrently using.
60: */
61:#include <arch/amd64_internal.h>
62:#include <arch/arch.h>
63:#include <kernel/pmm.h>
64:#include <kernel/platform.h>
65:#include <kernel/printk.h>
66:#include <kernel/string.h>
67:#include <kernel/types.h>
68:#include <kernel/vmm.h>
69:#include "../../../include/kernel/pmm.h"
70:
71:#ifndef PAGE_MASK
72:#endif /* PAGE_MASK */
73:/* ── Page Table Entry Flag Bits (Intel SDM Vol.3, Table 4-20) ──────────────
74: * These apply to all four levels (PML4E, PDPTE, PDE, PTE) where relevant.
75: * ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────*/
76:#define X86_PTE_P   0x001         /* Present: entry is valid */
77:#define X86_PTE_RW  0x002         /* Read/Write: 0=read-only, 1=writable */
78:#define X86_PTE_US  0x004         /* User/Supervisor: 1=user-accessible */
79:#define X86_PTE_PWT 0x008         /* Page-level write-through cache policy */
80:#define X86_PTE_PCD 0x010         /* Page-level cache disable */
81:#define X86_PTE_A   0x020         /* Accessed: set by CPU on any access */
82:#define X86_PTE_D   0x040         /* Dirty: set by CPU on write */
83:#define X86_PTE_PAT 0x080         /* Page Attribute Table index bit */
84:#define X86_PTE_G   0x100         /* Global: don't flush from TLB on CR3 write */
85:#define X86_PTE_NX  (1ULL << 63)  /* No-Execute (requires IA32_EFER.NXE=1) */
86:
87:/* PTE_ADDR_MASK: extract the 40-bit physical page-frame address from a PTE.
88: * Bits [11:0] are flags; bits [63:52] are reserved/NX; bits [51:12] are PA. */
89:#define PTE_ADDR_MASK 0x000FFFFFFFFFF000ULL
90:
91:/* Virtual address index extractors for each paging level.
92: * PML4: VA[47:39] (9 bits) → one of 512 PML4 entries → covers 512 GB each.
93: * PDPT: VA[38:30] (9 bits) → one of 512 PDPT entries → covers 1 GB each.
94: * PD:   VA[29:21] (9 bits) → one of 512 PD entries  → covers 2 MB each.
95: * PT:   VA[20:12] (9 bits) → one of 512 PT entries  → covers 4 KB each. */
96:#define PML4_INDEX(a) (((a) >> 39) & 0x1FF)
97:#define PDPT_INDEX(a) (((a) >> 30) & 0x1FF)
98:#define PD_INDEX(a)   (((a) >> 21) & 0x1FF)
99:#define PT_INDEX(a)   (((a) >> 12) & 0x1FF)
100:
101:int arch_vmm_map(uint64_t pgd, uint64_t va, uint64_t pa, uint64_t flags);
102:int arch_vmm_unmap(uint64_t pgd, uint64_t va);
103:uint64_t arch_vmm_get_physical(uint64_t pgd, uint64_t va);
104:
105:extern uint64_t boot_pml4[];
106:
107:/*
108: * arch_vmm_init_hw - switch to and fully populate the kernel PML4.
109: *
110: * Called once by the BSP after pmm_init() has populated the memory map.
111: * Steps:
112: *   1. Load kernel_pgd into CR3 (arch_vmm_set_pgd), replacing the minimal
113: *      boot_pml4 set up by start.S.
114: *   2. Identity-map the low 1 MB [0, 0x100000) for the SMP trampoline
115: *      (TRAMPOLINE_BASE = 0x1000) and legacy BIOS data areas.
116: *   3. Identity-map all usable RAM regions reported by arch_platform_get_mem_regions.
117: *      arch_vmm_map_range uses 2MB large pages where VA/PA are 2MB-aligned
118: *      for efficiency, then 4KB pages for the remainder.
119: *   4. Identity-map the MMIO window via arch_vmm_map_mmio.
120: *
121: * NOTE(AMMU-01): Kernel RAM is mapped PTE_RW without PTE_NX because the NX
122: * condition in arch_vmm_map only sets X86_PTE_NX when BOTH PTE_UXN and
123: * PTE_PXN are set.  Neither flag is passed here, so kernel code pages are
124: * mapped W+X.
125: * NOTE(AMMU-08): After this switch all other CPUs (not yet started) will
126: * have stale TLBs for the old boot_pml4; no SMP shootdown is needed at this
127: * point since APs have not enabled paging yet.
128: */
129:void arch_vmm_init_hw(uint64_t kernel_pgd) {
130:  /* Switch to the new kernel PML4 */
131:  arch_vmm_set_pgd(kernel_pgd);
132:  pr_info("AMD64 VMM: Switched to kernel PGD at %p\n", (void *)kernel_pgd);
133:
134:  /* Register the TLB shootdown IPI (MM-VMM-05/AMMU-08).  Before this point
135:   * only the BSP runs, so local flushes were sufficient. */
136:  amd64_tlb_ipi_init();
137:
138:  /* Pre-populate the kernel half's top-level slots (PML4 256..259, i.e.
139:   * direct-map VAs for PA 0..2TB) with empty PDPTs.  Process PML4s share
140:   * the kernel half by COPYING entries 256..511 at creation time; a
141:   * top-level entry created later (e.g. arch_vmm_map_device for a >512GB
142:   * BAR) would be invisible to already-created processes.  Pre-allocating
143:   * the PDPTs makes those slots shared pointers from day one. */
144:  uint64_t *pml4_va = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(kernel_pgd);
145:  for (int i = 256; i < 260; i++) {
146:    if (!(pml4_va[i] & X86_PTE_P)) {
147:      void *pdpt = pmm_alloc_page();
148:      if (!pdpt)
149:        break;
150:      memset(pdpt, 0, PAGE_SIZE);
151:      pml4_va[i] = virt_to_phys(pdpt) | X86_PTE_P | X86_PTE_RW;
152:    }
153:  }
154:
155:  /* Map all detected RAM regions (the low-2MB identity window for the
156:   * SMP trampoline is part of arch_vmm_map_mmio, so EVERY kernel PGD —
157:   * this one and vmm_dynamic_remap's — gets it). */
158:  size_t count = 0;
159:  struct mem_region *regions = arch_platform_get_mem_regions(&count);
160:
161:  for (size_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
162:    if (regions[i].type == MEM_REGION_USABLE) {
163:      pr_info("AMD64 VMM: Mapping RAM 0x%lx - 0x%lx\n",
164:              regions[i].base, regions[i].base + regions[i].size);
165:      /* W^X section split (AMMU-01 resolved): text RX, rodata RO+NX,
166:       * the rest RW+NX.  kernel_pgd is a PA here; vmm_map_ram_wx takes
167:       * the pointer form. */
168:      vmm_map_ram_wx((uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(kernel_pgd), regions[i].base,
169:                     regions[i].size);
170:    }
171:  }
172:
173:  /* Map MMIO regions (LAPIC, VirtIO, PCI) */
174:  arch_vmm_map_mmio((uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(kernel_pgd));
175:}
176:
177:/*
178: * arch_vmm_map_mmio - identity-map the 32-bit MMIO window into pgd.
179: *
180: * Maps 0xFE000000–0xFFFFFFFF (not including 0xFFFFFFFF itself) as uncached,
181: * write-through, present, R/W pages.  This range covers:
182: *   0xFEE00000 : LAPIC base (LAPIC_DEFAULT_BASE)
183: *   0xFEC00000 : I/O APIC base (if present)
184: *   0xFE000000+ : PCI MMIO BARs that QEMU places in the 3–4 GB hole
185: *
186: * NOTE(AMMU-06): ~8192 individual 4KB arch_vmm_map calls are issued per PGD
187: * setup.  This is inefficient; a single 2MB large page per 2MB-aligned chunk
188: * (or pre-populating the PDPT entry for 0xFE000000–0xFFFFFFF) would be faster.
189: * NOTE(AMMU-07): Devices with BAR addresses outside 0xFE000000–0xFFFFFFFF
190: * are not mapped here and will fault on access.  Notably, at '-m 4G' QEMU
191: * places virtio-blk BARs above 4 GB — those are outside this window and also
192: * above 32-bit PA so pci_get_bar can't address them (DRV-VIRTIO-01/DRV-PCI-02).
193: *
194: * PTE flags: P|RW|PCD|PWT — cache-disabled, write-through for MMIO registers.
195: */
196:void arch_vmm_map_mmio(uint64_t *pgd) {
197:  /* Map PCI MMIO and System MMIO (0xFE000000 to 0xFFFFFFFF) at their
198:   * direct-map VAs (phys_to_virt).
199:   * Covers PCI devices, LAPIC, IOAPIC, and upper BIOS ranges.
200:   * NOTE(AMMU-06): ~8192 individual 4KB map calls per PGD — inefficient. */
201:  for (uint64_t addr = 0xFE000000UL; addr < 0xFFFFFFFFUL; addr += 4096) {
202:    /* A failure here means the page-table allocator is exhausted during boot.
203:     * This used to be dropped: the window came out partially mapped and the
204:     * first driver to touch the missing page faulted somewhere unrelated, with
205:     * nothing pointing back here.  It is unrecoverable and boot-critical, so it
206:     * says so at the point it happens. */
207:    if (arch_vmm_map(virt_to_phys(pgd), (uint64_t)phys_to_virt(addr), addr,
208:                     PAGE_DEVICE) != 0)
209:      panic("arch_vmm_map_mmio: cannot map MMIO page 0x%lx", addr);
210:  }
211:
212:  /* Identity-map the low 2MB into every KERNEL PGD (this function is
213:   * called for the phase-1 PGD and for vmm_dynamic_remap's, never for
214:   * process PGDs):
215:   *  - [0, 1MB): SMP trampoline target (TRAMPOLINE_BASE 0x1000 must be
216:   *    writable: arch_cpu_wake_secondary copies and patches it there) and
217:   *    legacy BIOS data areas.
218:   *  - [1MB, 2MB): the low-linked boot sections (kernel.ld) — platform.c
219:   *    reads the trampoline blob via its low link address.
220:   * NX is safe: APs execute the trampoline in real mode (paging off) and
221:   * then on boot_pml4, never through these kernel_pgd entries. */
222:  /* The SMP trampoline lives in this window.  Dropping the result meant a
223:   * failure surfaced later as secondary CPUs that never came online, which
224:   * looks like an SMP bug rather than a mapping one. */
225:  if (arch_vmm_map_range(virt_to_phys(pgd), 0, 0, 0x200000, PAGE_KERNEL) != 0)
226:    panic("arch_vmm_map_mmio: cannot identity-map the low 2MB (SMP trampoline)");
227:}
228:
229:/*
230: * arch_vmm_map_device - identity-map a device MMIO region [base, base+size)
231: * into the active kernel page tables as uncached device memory (PCD|PWT).
232: *
233: * FIX(DRV-VIRTIO-01 / AMMU-07): called by the amd64 PCI scan for a device's
234: * BAR so the region is reachable even when QEMU places a 64-bit BAR ABOVE 4 GB
235: * (e.g. with '-m 4G'), which the fixed 0xFE000000-0xFFFFFFFF window misses.
236: * Identity (VA==PA), consistent with the rest of the amd64 MMU model.
237: */
238:int arch_vmm_map_device(uint64_t base, uint64_t size);
239:int arch_vmm_map_device(uint64_t base, uint64_t size) {
240:  extern uint64_t *kernel_pgd;
241:  if (!base || !size)
242:    return -1;
243:  uint64_t start = base & ~0xFFFUL;
244:  uint64_t end = (base + size + 0xFFFUL) & ~0xFFFUL;
245:  for (uint64_t a = start; a < end; a += 4096) {
246:    /* Runtime, and recoverable: a BAR that cannot be mapped is a device the
247:     * driver must be told about, not a dead kernel.  Previously the loop
248:     * returned 0 whatever happened, so the caller mapped nothing and believed
249:     * it had. */
250:    if (arch_vmm_map(virt_to_phys(kernel_pgd), (uint64_t)phys_to_virt(a), a,
251:                     PAGE_DEVICE) != 0) {
252:      arch_tlb_flush_all();
253:      return -ENOMEM;
254:    }
255:  }
256:  arch_tlb_flush_all();
257:  return 0;
258:}
259:
260:/*
261: * arch_vmm_init - early VMM initialisation (boot path).
262: *
263: * Called before arch_vmm_init_hw.  At this point boot_pml4 (set up by start.S)
264: * is already loaded in CR3 with a 1 GB identity map.  This function only logs
265: * the boot PML4 address; the full map is built in arch_vmm_init_hw.
266: */
267:void arch_vmm_init(void) {
268:  /* Boot PML4 is already set up with identity map by boot.S */
269:  pr_info("AMD64 VMM initialized (PML4 @ %p)\n", (void *)boot_pml4);
270:}
271:
272:/*
273: * get_next_table - walk or allocate the next-level page table.
274: *
275: * Params:
276: *   table  - current-level page table (PML4, PDPT, or PD)
277: *   index  - entry index within 'table' (0-511)
278: *   alloc  - 1 = allocate a new page if the entry is absent
279: *   level  - 0=PML4→PDPT, 1=PDPT→PD (1GB blocks), 2=PD→PT (2MB blocks)
280: *
281: * Returns pointer to the next-level table page, or NULL on absent/OOM.
282: *
283: * Large-page / block-entry handling:
284: *   If the entry has the PS bit (bit 7, 0x080) set and alloc==1, the block
285: *   is split: a new page table is allocated and filled with 512 entries that
286: *   each cover one sub-region.
287: *     level==1: 1GB block → 512×2MB entries (each with PS bit preserved)
288: *     level==2: 2MB block → 512×4KB entries (PS bit cleared for leaf PTEs)
289: *
290: * NOTE(AMMU-05): New intermediate table entries always include X86_PTE_US
291: * (user-accessible), which is more permissive than necessary for kernel-only
292: * intermediate nodes.
293: *
294: * NOTE(AMMU-04): arch_vmm_map calls get_next_table with level=0, 1, 2 for
295: * the PML4→PDPT, PDPT→PD, and PD→PT steps respectively.  The block-split
296: * code for level==1/2 is only exercised when walking a range that was
297: * previously mapped as a large page — which requires the caller to know that
298: * situation exists.  vmm.c's generic get_next_table does not understand large
299: * pages at all: it will dereference a 2MB-block PDE as a table pointer and
300: * corrupt memory.  [inferred; cross-ref AMMU-04]
301: */
302:static uint64_t *get_next_table(uint64_t *table, uint64_t index, int alloc, int level) {
303:  uint64_t entry = table[index];
304:
305:  if (entry & X86_PTE_P) {
306:    /* Check for 2MB/1GB block (PS bit = bit 7) */
307:    if (entry & 0x080) {
308:      if (!alloc) return NULL;
309:
310:      /* SPLIT BLOCK: allocate a new sub-table and fill it with fine-grained entries */
311:      void *new_table = pmm_alloc_page();
312:      if (!new_table) return NULL;
313:      memset(new_table, 0, PAGE_SIZE);
314:
315:      uint64_t block_pa = entry & PTE_ADDR_MASK;
316:      uint64_t block_flags = entry & ~PTE_ADDR_MASK;
317:      /* Remove PS bit and ensure table bits are correct */
318:      uint64_t *sub_table = (uint64_t *)new_table;
319:      if (level == 1) {
320:        /* 1GB Block → 512 × 2MB blocks (preserve PS bit in sub-entries) */
321:        for (int i = 0; i < 512; i++) {
322:          sub_table[i] = (block_pa + (uint64_t)i * 0x200000) | block_flags;
323:        }
324:      } else if (level == 2) {
325:        /* 2MB Block → 512 × 4KB pages (clear PS bit: leaf PTEs have no PS) */
326:        for (int i = 0; i < 512; i++) {
327:          sub_table[i] = (block_pa + (uint64_t)i * 4096) | (block_flags & ~0x080);
328:        }
329:      }
330:
331:      /* Replace the block entry with a pointer to the new sub-table.
332:       * NOTE(AMMU-05): X86_PTE_US on an intermediate entry; kernel-only
333:       * intermediate tables do not need to be user-accessible. */
334:      table[index] = virt_to_phys(new_table) | X86_PTE_P | X86_PTE_RW | X86_PTE_US;
335:      return (uint64_t *)new_table;
336:    }
337:    /* Entry is present and not a large page: return the next-level table PA.
338:     * Identity-map invariant: PA == VA, so the cast is safe. */
339:    return (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(entry & PTE_ADDR_MASK);
340:  }
341:
342:  if (!alloc) return NULL;
343:
344:  /* Entry is absent: allocate a new page table page */
345:  void *page = pmm_alloc_page();
346:  if (!page) return NULL;
347:  memset(page, 0, PAGE_SIZE);
348:
349:  /* NOTE(AMMU-05): X86_PTE_US on intermediate table entry */
350:  table[index] = virt_to_phys(page) | X86_PTE_P | X86_PTE_RW | X86_PTE_US;
351:  return (uint64_t *)page;
352:}
353:
354:/*
355: * arch_vmm_map - map a single 4KB virtual page to a physical page.
356: *
357: * Params:
358: *   pgd   - physical address of the PML4 (== virtual due to identity map)
359: *   va    - virtual address to map (4KB-aligned)
360: *   pa    - physical address to map to (4KB-aligned)
361: *   flags - arch-neutral PTE_* flags (PTE_USER, PTE_RO, PTE_UXN, PTE_PXN,
362: *           PTE_ATTR_DEVICE) converted to x86 PTE bits here
363: *
364: * Flag translation:
365: *   PTE_USER  → X86_PTE_US (user-accessible leaf PTE)
366: *   !PTE_RO   → X86_PTE_RW (writable; read-only if PTE_RO set)
367: *   PTE_UXN && PTE_PXN → X86_PTE_NX (no-execute)
368: *     NOTE(AMMU-01): NX requires BOTH PTE_UXN and PTE_PXN to be set.
369: *     Kernel mappings pass PTE_RW only → NX is never set → W+X pages.
370: *   PTE_ATTR_DEVICE → X86_PTE_PCD | X86_PTE_PWT (uncached MMIO)
371: *
372: * TLB invalidation: if the pgd being modified is the active CR3 for this CPU,
373: * invlpg flushes the single VA's TLB entry.  If modifying a different PGD
374: * (e.g. a new process), no flush is issued for this CPU — correct, since the
375: * modified PGD is not loaded.
376: * No IPI is sent on map: x86 TLBs do not cache not-present entries, so a
377: * fresh mapping cannot be stale anywhere; live remaps do not exist in
378: * today's callers (see AMMU-08 note in the file header).
379: *
380: * Returns 0 on success, -1 if any page-table page allocation fails.
381: */
382:/*
383: * x86_leaf_flags - translate arch-neutral PTE/PAGE profile bits to x86 PTE bits.
384: *
385: * Flag translation (AMMU-01 resolved): callers pass the amd64 PTE/PAGE
386: * profiles from vmm.h, which carry the final x86 bits — translate them
387: * explicitly.  Writability is OPT-IN (PTE_RW present), so read-only user
388: * segments and kernel text are actually read-only (CR0.WP is set).  NX is
389: * honoured both natively (PTE_NX) and from the arch-neutral UXN+PXN
390: * encoding used by shared code.  Shared by arch_vmm_map, the 2MB path of
391: * arch_vmm_map_range, and arch_vmm_protect.
392: */
393:static uint64_t x86_leaf_flags(uint64_t flags) {
394:  uint64_t x86_flags = X86_PTE_P;
395:  if (flags & PTE_USER)
396:    x86_flags |= X86_PTE_US;
397:  if (flags & PTE_RW)
398:    x86_flags |= X86_PTE_RW;
399:  if (flags & PTE_PWT)
400:    x86_flags |= X86_PTE_PWT;
401:  if (flags & PTE_PCD)
402:    x86_flags |= X86_PTE_PCD;
403:  if ((flags & PTE_NX) || ((flags & PTE_UXN) && (flags & PTE_PXN)))
404:    x86_flags |= X86_PTE_NX;
405:  return x86_flags;
406:}
407:
408:int arch_vmm_map(uint64_t pgd, uint64_t va, uint64_t pa, uint64_t flags) {
409:  uint64_t *pml4 = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pgd);
410:  uint64_t x86_flags = x86_leaf_flags(flags);
411:
412:  /* Walk (and allocate if absent) PML4 → PDPT → PD → PT */
413:  uint64_t *pdpt = get_next_table(pml4, PML4_INDEX(va), 1, 0);
414:  if (!pdpt) return -1;
415:
416:  uint64_t *pd = get_next_table(pdpt, PDPT_INDEX(va), 1, 1);
417:  if (!pd) return -1;
418:
419:  uint64_t *pt = get_next_table(pd, PD_INDEX(va), 1, 2);
420:  if (!pt) return -1;
421:
422:  /* Write the leaf PTE: physical address + flags */
423:  pt[PT_INDEX(va)] = (pa & PTE_ADDR_MASK) | x86_flags;
424:
425:  /* Optimized TLB flush: only if we are modifying the ACTIVE address space.
426:   * Local-only by design — fresh mappings are never cached remotely. */
427:  uint64_t current_cr3;
428:  __asm__ volatile("mov %%cr3, %0" : "=r"(current_cr3));
429:  if ((pgd & PTE_ADDR_MASK) == (current_cr3 & PTE_ADDR_MASK)) {
430:    __asm__ volatile("invlpg (%0)" ::"r"(va) : "memory");
431:  }
432:
433:  return 0;
434:}
435:
436:/*
437: * arch_vmm_unmap - clear the leaf PTE for a single 4KB virtual page.
438: *
439: * Walks PML4→PDPT→PD→PT without allocating; if any level is absent (not
440: * present), returns 0 silently (idempotent).  On success, zeroes the leaf
441: * PTE and performs an SMP TLB shootdown for the VA (AMMU-08 resolved): when
442: * this returns, no online CPU still translates 'va' through the old entry,
443: * so the caller may safely recycle the backing frame.
444: *
445: * NOTE(AMMU-03): Does not free the physical frame that was backing 'va'.
446: *   Frame lifecycle is tracked in process.c; this function only clears the
447: *   page-table entry.
448: *
449: * Returns 0 always (no failure path for missing entries).
450: */
451:int arch_vmm_unmap(uint64_t pgd, uint64_t va) {
452:  uint64_t *pml4 = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pgd);
453:
454:  if (!(pml4[PML4_INDEX(va)] & X86_PTE_P))
455:    return 0;
456:  uint64_t *pdpt = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pml4[PML4_INDEX(va)] & PTE_ADDR_MASK);
457:
458:  if (!(pdpt[PDPT_INDEX(va)] & X86_PTE_P))
459:    return 0;
460:  uint64_t *pd = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pdpt[PDPT_INDEX(va)] & PTE_ADDR_MASK);
461:
462:  if (!(pd[PD_INDEX(va)] & X86_PTE_P))
463:    return 0;
464:  uint64_t *pt = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pd[PD_INDEX(va)] & PTE_ADDR_MASK);
465:
466:  pt[PT_INDEX(va)] = 0;
467:  amd64_tlb_shootdown_va(va); /* local invlpg + IPI to online peers */
468:  return 0;
469:}
470:
471:/*
472: * arch_vmm_get_physical - translate a virtual address to its physical address.
473: *
474: * Walks PML4→PDPT→PD→PT without allocation; returns 0 if any level is not
475: * present.  On success returns (leaf_PTE & PTE_ADDR_MASK) | (va & 0xFFF),
476: * which is the physical byte address corresponding to 'va'.
477: *
478: * Handles 1GB (PDPTE.PS) and 2MB (PDE.PS) large pages by combining the
479: * block base with the in-block offset of 'va' — previously these were
480: * misread as table pointers and the lookup returned 0/garbage for any
481: * address inside the 2MB-mapped RAM identity window.
482: */
483:uint64_t arch_vmm_get_physical(uint64_t pgd, uint64_t va) {
484:  uint64_t *pml4 = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pgd);
485:
486:  if (!(pml4[PML4_INDEX(va)] & X86_PTE_P))
487:    return 0;
488:  uint64_t *pdpt = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pml4[PML4_INDEX(va)] & PTE_ADDR_MASK);
489:
490:  uint64_t pdpte = pdpt[PDPT_INDEX(va)];
491:  if (!(pdpte & X86_PTE_P))
492:    return 0;
493:  if (pdpte & 0x080) /* 1GB page */
494:    return ((pdpte & PTE_ADDR_MASK) & ~0x3FFFFFFFULL) | (va & 0x3FFFFFFFULL);
495:  uint64_t *pd = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pdpte & PTE_ADDR_MASK);
496:
497:  uint64_t pde = pd[PD_INDEX(va)];
498:  if (!(pde & X86_PTE_P))
499:    return 0;
500:  if (pde & 0x080) /* 2MB page */
501:    return ((pde & PTE_ADDR_MASK) & ~0x1FFFFFULL) | (va & 0x1FFFFFULL);
502:  uint64_t *pt = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pde & PTE_ADDR_MASK);
503:
504:  if (!(pt[PT_INDEX(va)] & X86_PTE_P))
505:    return 0;
506:
507:  return (pt[PT_INDEX(va)] & PTE_ADDR_MASK) | (va & 0xFFF);
508:}
509:
510:uint64_t arch_vmm_create_process_pgd(void);
511:
512:/*
513: * arch_vmm_create_process_pgd - allocate a PML4 for a new user process.
514: *
515: * Strategy (higher-half model):
516: *   1. Allocate a fresh PML4 page, zeroed.
517: *   2. Copy the kernel-half entries (PML4 indices 256-511) from kernel_pgd
518: *      by value.  arch_vmm_init_hw pre-populates every slot the kernel can
519: *      ever need (256..259), so the copies always point at SHARED PDPTs and
520: *      later kernel mappings are visible to all processes automatically.
521: *   3. The user half (indices 0..255) starts EMPTY; the ELF loader and
522: *      sbrk populate it on demand via arch_vmm_map().
523: *
524: * Teardown: the generic vmm_destroy_pgd() (kernel/mm/vmm.c) walks the
525: * private index-0 subtree built on demand and reclaims table pages + user
526: * frames; the copied kernel-half entries are never descended.
527: *
528: * Returns the physical address of the new PML4, or 0 on allocation failure.
529: */
530:uint64_t arch_vmm_create_process_pgd(void) {
531:  uint64_t *new_pml4 = (uint64_t *)pmm_alloc_page();
532:  if (!new_pml4)
533:    return 0;
534:
535:  memset(new_pml4, 0, PAGE_SIZE);
536:
537:  /*
538:   * Higher-half model (memlayout.h):
539:   *   PML4 index 0..255   user half — starts EMPTY; the ELF loader / sbrk
540:   *                       populate it via arch_vmm_map().
541:   *   PML4 index 256..511 kernel half — shared by copying the kernel_pgd
542:   *                       entries by value.  Every kernel top-level slot
543:   *                       that can ever be needed (direct map of RAM and
544:   *                       device BARs: 256..259, pre-populated by
545:   *                       arch_vmm_init_hw) already exists, so later
546:   *                       kernel mappings land in SHARED PDPTs and are
547:   *                       visible to every process automatically.
548:   * Nothing else is cloned: no low identity, no per-process MMIO map.
549:   */
550:  extern uint64_t *kernel_pgd;
551:  for (int i = 256; i < 512; i++) {
552:    new_pml4[i] = kernel_pgd[i];
553:  }
554:
555:  /* Contract: return the PGD's PHYSICAL address (vmm_create_pgd converts). */
556:  return virt_to_phys(new_pml4);
557:}
558:
559:/* AMMU-03 resolved: the divergent arch teardown (which freed only the PML4
560: * page and leaked the private PDPT + all PD/PT pages and user frames) has
561: * been removed — it had no callers.  The single teardown path is the generic
562: * vmm_destroy_pgd() (kernel/mm/vmm.c), which walks the private index-0
563: * subtree, frees process-private table pages and PTE_USER leaf frames, and
564: * skips entries shared by value with kernel_pgd. */
565:
566:/*
567: * arch_vmm_protect - rewrite the attributes of existing 4KB mappings (AMMU-02
568: * resolved).
569: *
570: * Params:
571: *   pgd       physical address of the PML4.
572: *   va, size  range to change; rounded outward to page boundaries.
573: *   flags     arch-neutral PTE/PAGE profile (same vocabulary as
574: *             arch_vmm_map); every attribute bit of each leaf PTE is
575: *             replaced via x86_leaf_flags(), only the frame address is kept.
576: *
577: * A 1GB/2MB large page covering part of the range is first split into the
578: * next finer granularity (get_next_table with alloc=1, which preserves the
579: * translations bit-identically) so the change applies with 4KB precision.
580: *
581: * Returns 0 on success; -1 if any page in the range is unmapped or a split
582: * allocation fails (pages BEFORE the failure keep the new attributes).
583: *
584: * TLB: one SMP shootdown round (full flush, all online CPUs) after the
585: * loop — runs on both success and failure paths so rewritten PTEs are never
586: * masked by stale TLB copies anywhere.
587: */
588:int arch_vmm_protect(uint64_t pgd, uint64_t va, uint64_t size, uint64_t flags);
589:int arch_vmm_protect(uint64_t pgd, uint64_t va, uint64_t size, uint64_t flags) {
590:  uint64_t *pml4 = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pgd);
591:  uint64_t x86_flags = x86_leaf_flags(flags);
592:  uint64_t v = va & ~0xFFFUL;
593:  uint64_t end = (va + size + 0xFFFUL) & ~0xFFFUL;
594:  int rc = 0;
595:
596:  for (; v < end; v += 4096) {
597:    uint64_t pml4e = pml4[PML4_INDEX(v)];
598:    if (!(pml4e & X86_PTE_P)) { rc = -1; break; }
599:    uint64_t *pdpt = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pml4e & PTE_ADDR_MASK);
600:
601:    uint64_t pdpte = pdpt[PDPT_INDEX(v)];
602:    if (!(pdpte & X86_PTE_P)) { rc = -1; break; }
603:    uint64_t *pd;
604:    if (pdpte & 0x080) {
605:      pd = get_next_table(pdpt, PDPT_INDEX(v), 1, 1); /* split 1GB page */
606:      if (!pd) { rc = -1; break; }
607:    } else {
608:      pd = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pdpte & PTE_ADDR_MASK);
609:    }
610:
611:    uint64_t pde = pd[PD_INDEX(v)];
612:    if (!(pde & X86_PTE_P)) { rc = -1; break; }
613:    uint64_t *pt;
614:    if (pde & 0x080) {
615:      pt = get_next_table(pd, PD_INDEX(v), 1, 2); /* split 2MB page */
616:      if (!pt) { rc = -1; break; }
617:    } else {
618:      pt = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pde & PTE_ADDR_MASK);
619:    }
620:
621:    uint64_t pte = pt[PT_INDEX(v)];
622:    if (!(pte & X86_PTE_P)) { rc = -1; break; }
623:    pt[PT_INDEX(v)] = (pte & PTE_ADDR_MASK) | x86_flags;
624:  }
625:
626:  amd64_tlb_shootdown_all();
627:  return rc;
628:}
629:
630:/*
631: * arch_vmm_map_range - map a contiguous VA→PA range, using 2MB pages where possible.
632: *
633: * Iterates [va, va+size) and maps each chunk:
634: *   - If both VA and PA are 2MB-aligned AND remaining size >= 2MB: map a single
635: *     2MB large page in the PD (PS bit = 0x080, level 2 in PD) without a PT.
636: *   - Otherwise: falls through to arch_vmm_map for 4KB granularity.
637: *
638: * After the loop, arch_tlb_flush_all() (write to CR3) flushes the entire
639: * local TLB.  Local-only is correct here: map_range is used at boot (before
640: * SMP) and for fresh ranges, never to live-remap pages another CPU uses.
641: *
642: * The 2MB path builds the PD entry with PS|P|RW (and optionally US) but does
643: * NOT set NX, because PTE_UXN/PTE_PXN flags are not in the arch_vmm_map_range
644: * callers' flag set.  NOTE(AMMU-01): same W+X issue as arch_vmm_map.
645: *
646: * Returns 0 on success, -1 if any allocation fails.
647: */
648:int arch_vmm_map_range(uint64_t pgd, uint64_t va, uint64_t pa, uint64_t size, uint64_t flags) {
649:  uint64_t v = va;
650:  uint64_t p = pa;
651:  uint64_t end = va + size;
652:
653:  while (v < end) {
654:    uint64_t remaining = end - v;
655:    
656:    if ((v & 0x1FFFFF) == 0 && (p & 0x1FFFFF) == 0 && remaining >= 0x200000) {
657:      uint64_t *pml4 = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pgd);
658:      uint64_t *pdpt = get_next_table(pml4, PML4_INDEX(v), 1, 0);
659:      if (!pdpt) return -1;
660:
661:      uint64_t *pd = get_next_table(pdpt, PDPT_INDEX(v), 1, 1);
662:      if (!pd) return -1;
663:
664:      /* Level 2 2MB Page Mapping — same explicit translation as
665:       * arch_vmm_map (opt-in RW, NX from PTE_NX or UXN+PXN). */
666:      uint64_t x86_flags = x86_leaf_flags(flags) | 0x080; /* PS bit for 2MB */
667:
668:      pd[PD_INDEX(v)] = (p & PTE_ADDR_MASK) | x86_flags;
669:      v += 0x200000;
670:      p += 0x200000;
671:    } else {
672:      if (arch_vmm_map(pgd, v, p, flags) != 0) return -1;
673:      v += 4096;
674:      p += 4096;
675:    }
676:  }
677:  arch_tlb_flush_all();
678:  return 0;
679:}

@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/mm/tlb.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/amd64/mm/tlb.c
3: * SMP TLB shootdown via fixed-vector LAPIC IPI — amd64
4: *
5: * Resolves MM-VMM-05 / AMMU-08 on this arch.  x86 has no hardware TLB
6: * broadcast (unlike AArch64's inner-shareable TLBI, which the DVM carries to
7: * every PE): invlpg and CR3 reloads only affect the executing CPU, so after
8: * an unmap/permission change every peer CPU may keep using a stale
9: * translation — a correctness and isolation hole once the backing frame is
10: * recycled.
11: *
12: * Protocol (one round at a time, serialised by tlb_shoot_lock):
13: *   1. The initiator flushes locally, then publishes the set of online peer
14: *      CPUs in tlb_shoot_waiting (one bit per cpu_id) and broadcasts the
15: *      fixed IPI vector TLB_IPI_VECTOR (0xFD, all-excluding-self shorthand).
16: *   2. Each peer's IPI handler performs a FULL local flush (CR3 reload) and
17: *      clears its bit.  The handler flushes unconditionally — even when its
18: *      bit was already force-cleared by an initiator timeout — so a late IPI
19: *      can never be a missed flush.  A full flush (rather than a per-VA
20: *      invlpg) sidesteps the race where a late handler reads the address of
21: *      a NEWER round and leaves the old VA stale; on a 4-CPU QEMU guest the
22: *      precision loss is noise.
23: *   3. The initiator spins (bounded) until all bits clear.  A peer running
24: *      with IRQs masked acknowledges late: the IPI stays pending in its
25: *      LAPIC IRR and the flush happens the moment it unmasks, so a timeout
26: *      here only means the ack was not OBSERVED in time, not that the peer
27: *      will skip the flush.
28: *
29: * Deadlock safety: a CPU that wants to start its own round while another is
30: * in flight spins on tlb_shoot_lock with IRQs possibly disabled (callers may
31: * hold mm_lock irqsave); the spin loop services the in-flight round inline
32: * (tlb_ipi_service), so the current initiator never waits forever on a CPU
33: * that is itself waiting for the lock.
34: *
35: * Perf note: callers that unmap N pages in a loop currently trigger N
36: * rounds (N×(ncpu-1) IPIs + full flushes).  Acceptable for today's rare
37: * unmap paths (sbrk shrink, teardown does ONE _all round); if profiling ever
38: * flags it, add a range/batch API on the same protocol.
39: */
40:#include <arch/amd64/apic.h>
41:#include <kernel/arch.h>
42:#include <kernel/cpu.h>
43:#include <kernel/irq.h>
44:#include <kernel/printk.h>
45:#include <kernel/spinlock.h>
46:#include <kernel/types.h>
47:
48:#define TLB_IPI_VECTOR 0xFD
49:
50:/* TLB_ACK_TIMEOUT_SPINS: pause-loop iterations before the initiator stops
51: * waiting for stragglers.  Generous on purpose: under QEMU TCG a vCPU can be
52: * de-scheduled by the host for milliseconds. */
53:#define TLB_ACK_TIMEOUT_SPINS 50000000UL
54:
55:/* tlb_shoot_waiting: bitmask (1 << cpu_id) of peers that still owe an ack
56: * for the in-flight round.  Written by the initiator under tlb_shoot_lock;
57: * bits cleared by peers with an atomic AND. */
58:static volatile uint64_t tlb_shoot_waiting;
59:static DEFINE_SPINLOCK(tlb_shoot_lock);
60:
61:/* tlb_ipi_ready: set once the handler is registered; before that (early
62: * boot, single CPU running) shootdowns degrade to the local flush. */
63:static int tlb_ipi_ready;
64:
65:/*
66: * tlb_ipi_service - service the in-flight round if it targets this CPU.
67: *
68: * Called from the lock-acquisition spin in tlb_shootdown(): a CPU waiting to
69: * start its own round may have IRQs disabled (caller holds mm_lock irqsave),
70: * so the IPI could not be delivered — without this inline service the
71: * current initiator would wait for our ack until timeout.
72: */
73:static void tlb_ipi_service(void) {
74:  uint64_t bit = 1UL << hal_cpu_id();
75:  if (tlb_shoot_waiting & bit) {
76:    arch_impl_tlb_flush_local();
77:    __sync_fetch_and_and(&tlb_shoot_waiting, ~bit);
78:  }
79:}
80:
81:/*
82: * tlb_ipi_handler - IPI entry (vector 0xFD) on a peer CPU.
83: *
84: * Flushes unconditionally (see header: a late IPI after an initiator
85: * timeout must still flush), then clears this CPU's ack bit.
86: * EOI is chip-owned: idt.c calls irq_chip_end(vec) → lapic_eoi().
87: */
88:static void tlb_ipi_handler(uint32_t irq, void *data) {
89:  (void)irq;
90:  (void)data;
91:  arch_impl_tlb_flush_local();
92:  __sync_fetch_and_and(&tlb_shoot_waiting, ~(1UL << hal_cpu_id()));
93:}
94:
95:/*
96: * amd64_tlb_ipi_init - register the shootdown IPI handler.
97: *
98: * Called once by the BSP from arch_vmm_init_hw(); before this, shootdowns
99: * are local-only, which is correct because no AP is online yet.
100: * pic_chip_enable() ignores vectors >= 48, so registering does not touch the
101: * 8259; delivery is pure LAPIC fixed-vector.
102: */
103:void amd64_tlb_ipi_init(void) {
104:  if (irq_register(TLB_IPI_VECTOR, tlb_ipi_handler, NULL) == 0) {
105:    tlb_ipi_ready = 1;
106:    pr_info("AMD64 TLB: shootdown IPI registered on vector 0x%x\n",
107:            TLB_IPI_VECTOR);
108:  } else {
109:    pr_err("%s", "AMD64 TLB: failed to register shootdown IPI vector\n");
110:  }
111:}
112:
113:/*
114: * tlb_shootdown - run one shootdown round.
115: *
116: * @va: target virtual address, or 0 for a full address-space flush.
117: *      (VA 0 is never a mapped page — the NULL page is deliberately
118: *      unmapped — so the overload is unambiguous.)
119: *
120: * The local flush always happens, even before SMP is up.
121: */
122:static void tlb_shootdown(uintptr_t va) {
123:  /* Local CPU first. */
124:  if (va)
125:    arch_impl_tlb_flush_va(va);
126:  else
127:    arch_impl_tlb_flush_local();
128:
129:  if (!tlb_ipi_ready)
130:    return;
131:
132:  /* Snapshot the online peers.  cpu_id is the LAPIC ID (< MAX_CPUS = 64,
133:   * matching the width of tlb_shoot_waiting). */
134:  uint64_t mask = 0;
135:  uint32_t me = hal_cpu_id();
136:  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < MAX_CPUS && i < 64; i++) {
137:    if (i != me && cpu_data[i].online)
138:      mask |= 1UL << i;
139:  }
140:  if (!mask)
141:    return;
142:
143:  /* Serialise rounds; service the in-flight one while waiting (deadlock
144:   * safety — see file header). */
145:  uint64_t flags;
146:  while (!spin_trylock_irqsave(&tlb_shoot_lock, &flags)) {
147:    tlb_ipi_service();
148:    __asm__ __volatile__("pause");
149:  }
150:
151:  tlb_shoot_waiting = mask;
152:  arch_wmb();
153:  lapic_send_ipi(0, ICR_FIXED | ICR_ASSERT | ICR_ALL_EXCL_SELF |
154:                        TLB_IPI_VECTOR);
155:
156:  uint64_t spins = 0;
157:  while (tlb_shoot_waiting != 0) {
158:    __asm__ __volatile__("pause");
159:    if (++spins == TLB_ACK_TIMEOUT_SPINS) {
160:      pr_warn("AMD64 TLB: shootdown ack timeout (waiting=0x%lx); peers will "
161:              "flush on IRQ unmask\n",
162:              tlb_shoot_waiting);
163:      tlb_shoot_waiting = 0;
164:      break;
165:    }
166:  }
167:
168:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&tlb_shoot_lock, flags);
169:}
170:
171:/* amd64_tlb_shootdown_va - make a single VA's translation globally invisible. */
172:void amd64_tlb_shootdown_va(uintptr_t va) { tlb_shootdown(va); }
173:
174:/* amd64_tlb_shootdown_all - flush the whole TLB on every online CPU. */
175:void amd64_tlb_shootdown_all(void) { tlb_shootdown(0); }

@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/mm/uaccess.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/amd64/mm/uaccess.c
3: * Kernel-to-User and User-to-Kernel Memory Copy Primitives (AMD64)
4: *
5: * Purpose:
6: *   Provide arch_copy_from_user, arch_copy_to_user, and
7: *   arch_copy_string_from_user.  These are called by syscall handlers that
8: *   need to read or write user-space buffers.  On AMD64, the user PML4 is
9: *   already loaded in CR3 (unified address space), so no TTBR switch is needed
10: *   (unlike aarch64 which must swap TTBR0_EL1).  Validation is done via
11: *   vmm_is_user_addr (range check) and vmm_check_range (page-table walk).
12: *
13: * Invariants:
14: *   - current_process != NULL and current_process->page_table != NULL before
15: *     any copy function is called (each function checks and returns -1).
16: *   - Source/destination addresses must satisfy vmm_is_user_addr for every
17: *     byte in the range.
18: *
19: * Known issues:
20: *   UACC-AMD64-01 (W2 DOC/MISSING) The file header and the module-level
21: *     comment below claim "stac/clac" SMAP protection.  No stac/clac
22: *     instructions are emitted.  CR4.SMAP is NOT enabled in cpu.c:36-39 (only
23: *     OSFXSR/OSXMMEXCPT are set).  Currently harmless because SMAP is off, but
24: *     the comment creates a false security guarantee.  If SMAP is enabled in
25: *     the future without adding stac/clac, every uaccess call traps.
26: *   UACC-AMD64-02 (W3 SECURITY/TOCTOU) arch_copy_from_user: vmm_check_range
27: *     runs at :23, memcpy runs at :26 — no lock between them.  On SMP, a
28: *     concurrent munmap between the check and the copy allows the copy to read
29: *     a freed or remapped page.  Fix: hold mm_lock + disable IRQs around both.
30: *   UACC-AMD64-03 (W3 SECURITY/TOCTOU) arch_copy_to_user: same TOCTOU window
31: *     at :37-41.
32: *   UACC-AMD64-04 (W3 SECURITY) arch_copy_string_from_user: the first byte
33: *     of 'src' is not validated via vmm_check_range before reading if it is
34: *     not at a page boundary (the per-page check fires only at 0-mod-0x1000).
35: *     A user can place src at the last byte of a valid page so the initial
36: *     vmm_is_user_addr passes, then the string extends unmapped into the next
37: *     page.  Also shares the TOCTOU window of UACC-AMD64-02.
38: *   UACC-AMD64-05 (W2 BUG) Overflow check at :19 'src_addr + n < src_addr'
39: *     does not catch src_addr + n == 0 (the exact canonical boundary); the
40: *     vmm_is_user_addr(0) check catches the 0 case, but a range whose end
41: *     equals exactly the top of user VA (0xFFFF000000000000) passes the
42: *     overflow test and is only caught by the second vmm_is_user_addr call.
43: *     Edge case; not immediately exploitable.
44: */
45:#include <kernel/types.h>
46:#include <kernel/vmm.h>
47:#include <kernel/string.h>
48:#include <kernel/sched.h>
49:#include <kernel/fault.h>
50:#include <arch/arch.h>
51:
52:/*
53: * arch_uaccess_fault_fixup - release the uaccess critical section after a
54: * #PF inside one of the copy windows below (kernel/core/fault.c).
55: *
56: * The copies hold IRQs-masked + uaccess_active + current_process->mm_lock.
57: * The faulting context is being discarded (process terminated), so the flag is
58: * cleared and the lock dropped; schedule() returns a frame whose saved RFLAGS
59: * govern the next task, so IRQ state needs no explicit restore here.
60: *
61: * HAL-0 (2026-07-23): mm_lock is NEW on this side.  Dropping it here is not
62: * optional bookkeeping — a #PF inside a copy window would otherwise leave
63: * mm_lock held by a process that is being torn down, and the next acquirer of
64: * that lock would wait forever.  This mirrors aarch64's
65: * arch_uaccess_fault_fixup exactly; the two providers now differ only where a
66: * written contract says they may (aarch64 additionally restores TTBR0 — it
67: * swaps address spaces, amd64 does not).
68: */
69:void arch_uaccess_fault_fixup(void) {
70:  struct cpu_info *ci = arch_cpu_info_fault_safe();
71:  if (ci) {
72:    ci->uaccess_active = 0;
73:    if (ci->current_task)
74:      spin_unlock(&ci->current_task->mm_lock);
75:  }
76:}
77:
78:/*
79: * AMD64 uses a unified address space: the user PML4 is already in CR3 when
80: * a syscall handler runs.  No TTBR switch (unlike aarch64) is needed.
81: *
82: * UACC-AMD64-01 (CLOSED 2026-07-23, HAL-0): the note recorded that a comment
83: * claimed stac/clac SMAP bracketing that is not emitted.  Verified: no
84: * stac/clac anywhere in this file and CR4.SMAP is not enabled, so there is no
85: * SMAP protection to bracket — the claim was the defect, and the misleading
86: * comment is gone.  Stated positively so nobody re-derives it: user memory is
87: * reachable from kernel mode here because SMAP is OFF; the protection that
88: * actually holds is the explicit vmm_is_user_addr + vmm_check_range validation
89: * under mm_lock below.  Enabling CR4.SMAP (and then genuinely bracketing these
90: * copies with stac/clac) is a hardening step in its own right, tracked with the
91: * other amd64 CPU-feature work rather than pretended here.
92: */
93:
94:/*
95: * arch_copy_from_user - copy 'n' bytes from user-space 'src' to kernel 'dest'.
96: *
97: * Validation steps (in order):
98: *   1. Wrap-around check: src+n < src would indicate integer overflow.
99: *   2. Range check: both src and src+n must be in the canonical user VA range
100: *      (vmm_is_user_addr, typically [0x1000, 0xFFFF000000000000)).
101: *      NOTE(UACC-AMD64-05): src+n == canonical boundary is an edge case.
102: *   3. Null process/page_table guard.
103: *   4. vmm_check_range: walks the page table to confirm all pages are present.
104: *   5. memcpy: the actual copy.
105: *
106: * UACC-AMD64-02 (FIXED 2026-07-23, HAL-0): the check and the copy now run
107: * under current_process->mm_lock, closing the window in which a concurrent
108: * unmap on another CPU could free a page between vmm_check_range() and the
109: * memcpy.  aarch64 has always held mm_lock here; amd64 answering the same
110: * concurrency question differently, in a security-sensitive primitive, was the
111: * divergence HAL-0 exists to remove.  What legitimately still differs is the
112: * TTBR0 swap (aarch64 splits address spaces, amd64 does not) — that is written
113: * down in kernel/hal_uaccess.h rather than left implicit.
114: *
115: * Returns 0 on success, -1 on any validation failure.
116: */
117:int arch_copy_from_user(void *dest, const void *src, size_t n) {
118:  uint64_t src_addr = (uint64_t)src;
119:  /* UACC-AMD64-05 (CLOSED 2026-07-23, HAL-0): the wrap check rejects an
120:   * overflowing src+n, and the range check below is applied to the LAST BYTE
121:   * ACTUALLY TOUCHED (src+n-1), not to the one-past-the-end address.  Checking
122:   * src+n was the recorded edge case: for a region ending exactly at the user
123:   * boundary the one-past address is the first non-user byte, so a perfectly
124:   * legal copy was refused; and n == 0 made src+n == src, checking a byte the
125:   * copy never reads.  n == 0 is now short-circuited (nothing to validate). */
126:  if (src_addr + n < src_addr) return -1;
127:  if (n == 0) return 0;
128:  if (!vmm_is_user_addr(src_addr) || !vmm_is_user_addr(src_addr + n - 1))
129:    return -1;
130:  if (!current_process || !current_process->page_table) return -1;
131:
132:  /* uaccess window (Phase A step 9/10): flag the copy so the fault classifier
133:   * treats a #PF on a user VA here as recoverable (terminate the process)
134:   * rather than a kernel bug.  IRQs are masked so the flag cannot leak to a
135:   * different task via preemption; aarch64 already masks for its TTBR swap.
136:   *
137:   * mm_lock is taken BEFORE the range check so validation and use are one
138:   * critical section — checking first and locking after would leave exactly the
139:   * TOCTOU this fixes.  arch_uaccess_fault_fixup() drops it if the copy faults.
140:   */
141:  uint64_t uflags = local_irq_save();
142:  spin_lock(&current_process->mm_lock);
143:
144:  if (vmm_check_range(current_process->page_table, src_addr, n, PTE_VALID) !=
145:      0) {
146:    spin_unlock(&current_process->mm_lock);
147:    local_irq_restore(uflags);
148:    return -1;
149:  }
150:
151:  get_cpu_info()->uaccess_active = 1;
152:
153:  memcpy(dest, src, n); /* NOTE(UACC-AMD64-01): no stac/clac bracketing */
154:
155:  get_cpu_info()->uaccess_active = 0;
156:  spin_unlock(&current_process->mm_lock);
157:  local_irq_restore(uflags);
158:
159:  return 0;
160:}
161:
162:/*
163: * arch_copy_to_user - copy 'n' bytes from kernel 'src' to user-space 'dest'.
164: *
165: * Same validation sequence as arch_copy_from_user with dest as the address.
166: * UACC-AMD64-03 (FIXED 2026-07-23, HAL-0): the write-side mirror of
167: * UACC-AMD64-02 — check and copy now share one mm_lock critical section, so a
168: * concurrent unmap can no longer land this write in a newly-allocated kernel
169: * page.
170: *
171: * Returns 0 on success, -1 on any validation failure.
172: */
173:int arch_copy_to_user(void *dest, const void *src, size_t n) {
174:  uint64_t dest_addr = (uint64_t)dest;
175:  /* UACC-AMD64-05: last byte touched, not one-past-the-end.  See
176:   * arch_copy_from_user. */
177:  if (dest_addr + n < dest_addr) return -1;
178:  if (n == 0) return 0;
179:  if (!vmm_is_user_addr(dest_addr) || !vmm_is_user_addr(dest_addr + n - 1))
180:    return -1;
181:  if (!current_process || !current_process->page_table) return -1;
182:
183:  /* uaccess window — see arch_copy_from_user */
184:  uint64_t uflags = local_irq_save();
185:  spin_lock(&current_process->mm_lock);
186:
187:  if (vmm_check_range(current_process->page_table, dest_addr, n, PTE_VALID) !=
188:      0) {
189:    spin_unlock(&current_process->mm_lock);
190:    local_irq_restore(uflags);
191:    return -1;
192:  }
193:
194:  get_cpu_info()->uaccess_active = 1;
195:
196:  memcpy(dest, src, n); /* NOTE(UACC-AMD64-01): no stac/clac bracketing */
197:
198:  get_cpu_info()->uaccess_active = 0;
199:  spin_unlock(&current_process->mm_lock);
200:  local_irq_restore(uflags);
201:
202:  return 0;
203:}
204:
205:/*
206: * arch_copy_string_from_user - copy a NUL-terminated string from user space.
207: *
208: * Copies up to max_len-1 characters from 'src' to 'dest', always NUL-terminates.
209: * Per-page validation: vmm_check_range is called only when '&src[i]' crosses a
210: * 4KB page boundary ((uint64_t)&src[i] & 0xFFF == 0).
211: *
212: * NOTE(UACC-AMD64-04): The very first byte is NOT individually validated by
213: * vmm_check_range — only vmm_is_user_addr guards the starting address.  A user
214: * can set src to the last byte of a valid page; the initial check passes, but
215: * the next page (potentially unmapped) is read without a boundary check.  The
216: * boundary check fires at page-aligned offsets i, not at the crossing point
217: * (i.e., at i = 0, 4096, 8192, …) — so the crossing from page N to page N+1
218: * is caught at the first i that is 0-mod-0x1000, which is the START of page
219: * N+1, not the boundary.  For src at offset 1 of a page: i=4095 crosses the
220: * boundary but is not 0-mod-0x1000 (4096 mod 4096 == 0 is the check for i=4095
221: * pointing to &src[4095] = src+4095 ... actually at i=4095 addr=src+4095 mod
222: * 0xFFF is != 0 if src is not page-aligned — so the check may not fire at the
223: * crossing point).  Also has the same TOCTOU window as UACC-AMD64-02.
224: *
225: * Returns 0 on success, -1 if a page boundary check fails (string truncated).
226: */
227:/*
228: * arch_copy_string_from_user_n - HAL uaccess provider (kernel/hal_uaccess.h).
229: * Mirror of the aarch64 provider; kept deliberately symmetric so the two
230: * architectures cannot drift on semantics the way they did while this had no
231: * written contract at all.
232: */
233:int arch_copy_string_from_user_n(char *dest, const char *src, size_t max_len,
234:                                 size_t *out_len, int *out_truncated) {
235:  if (out_len) *out_len = 0;
236:  if (out_truncated) *out_truncated = 0;
237:  if (!vmm_is_user_addr((uint64_t)src)) return -1;
238:  if (!current_process || !current_process->page_table) return -1;
239:  /* max_len 0 would underflow `max_len - 1` below and run away; a zero-sized
240:   * destination cannot hold even the terminator, so refuse it outright. */
241:  if (max_len == 0)
242:    return -1;
243:
244:  /* uaccess window — see arch_copy_from_user.  mm_lock spans the whole walk:
245:   * the string is validated page by page AS IT IS READ, so the lock must cover
246:   * every check/read pair, not just one (UACC-AMD64-02 for the string path). */
247:  uint64_t uflags = local_irq_save();
248:  spin_lock(&current_process->mm_lock);
249:  get_cpu_info()->uaccess_active = 1;
250:
251:  size_t i;
252:  int ret = 0;
253:
254:  for (i = 0; i < max_len - 1; i++) {
255:    /* Per-page validation, one walk per page touched and no more.
256:     *
257:     * UACC-AMD64-04 (FIXED 2026-07-23, HAL-0): the `i == 0` term is the fix.
258:     * The alignment test alone validates each NEW page at its first byte, but
259:     * the page containing src is only page-aligned when src is — so for any
260:     * unaligned src the STARTING page went entirely unchecked (vmm_is_user_addr
261:     * had merely confirmed it was a user address).  A user could point src at
262:     * an unmapped page and the first read would fault inside the kernel.
263:     *
264:     * Folded into the loop rather than done as a separate pre-check before it:
265:     * a standalone pre-walk repeats the same page-table walk the i == 0
266:     * iteration already performs whenever src IS aligned, and this is the
267:     * hottest string path in the kernel (every path, every registry key and
268:     * value).  One walk per page, never two. */
269:    if (i == 0 || ((uint64_t)&src[i] & 0xFFF) == 0) {
270:       if (vmm_check_range(current_process->page_table, (uint64_t)&src[i], 1, PTE_VALID) != 0) {
271:         ret = -1;
272:         break;
273:       }
274:    }
275:    dest[i] = src[i];
276:    if (src[i] == '\0') break;
277:  }
278:  /* Ran the destination out before the terminator: the source is longer.
279:   * i == max_len - 1 only when the loop exhausted its bound rather than
280:   * breaking on the NUL. */
281:  if (ret == 0 && i == max_len - 1 && out_truncated)
282:    *out_truncated = 1;
283:  if (out_len) *out_len = i;
284:
285:  /* Terminate on EVERY path, including the mid-loop validation failure — an
286:   * unterminated dest hands the caller a string with no end. */
287:  dest[max_len - 1] = '\0';
288:  get_cpu_info()->uaccess_active = 0;
289:  spin_unlock(&current_process->mm_lock);
290:  local_irq_restore(uflags);
291:
292:  return ret;
293:}
294:
295:/* Legacy tolerant spelling — truncation is success.  See kernel/hal_uaccess.h. */
296:int arch_copy_string_from_user(char *dest, const char *src, size_t max_len) {
297:  return arch_copy_string_from_user_n(dest, src, max_len, (size_t *)0,
298:                                      (int *)0);
299:}

1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/amd64/platform/platform.c
3: * AMD64 Platform Initialization: Boot Protocol Parsing, Memory Discovery,
4: * SMP Bringup, Timer Stubs, and PCI Init
5: *
6: * Responsibilities:
7: *   - arch_platform_early_init: detect the boot protocol (Multiboot1,
8: *     Multiboot2, PVH, or unknown fallback), parse the memory map, populate
9: *     arch_mem_regions[] for the PMM, and initialise the legacy PIC.
10: *   - arch_smp_init: detect CPU count via CPUID, copy the AP trampoline to
11: *     TRAMPOLINE_BASE, send INIT-SIPI sequences, and wait for AP ACKs.
12: *   - arch_pci_init / arch_get_boot_info / arch_get_kernel_stack /
13: *     arch_vmm_set_secondary_pgd: supporting stubs and utilities.
14: *   - timer_get_us / udelay: timer utilities (stub and LAPIC-based delay).
15: *
16: * Boot protocol support matrix:
17: *   MB1_MAGIC (0x2BADB002): Multiboot v1 — parses MMAP flag (bit 6).
18: *   MB2_MAGIC (0x36D76289): Multiboot v2 — walks tag chain for MMAP tag.
19: *   PVH_MAGIC             : Parses hvm_start_info.memmap_paddr entries.
20: *   Unknown               : Fallback to hardcoded 1 GB map.
21: *
22: * Known issues:
23: *   BOOT-01 (W4 BUG/WRONG-DESIGN) On 'make run ARCH=amd64' QEMU boots via PVH
24: *     but delivers the hvm_start_info pointer in %ebx with magic inside the
25: *     struct's first field, not in a "magic register" value.  The code checks
26: *     'mb_magic == PVH_MAGIC' expecting a saved register, but QEMU's PVH ABI
27: *     sets mb_magic = the raw %eax (which is 0 or another value, not PVH_MAGIC).
28: *     Result: the else branch fires and the 1 GB fallback is used.  [verified:
29: *     serial shows "Magic: 0x0"]
30: *   BOOT-02 (W4 BUG) Consequence of BOOT-01: hardcoded 1 GB RAM map at
31: *     arch_platform_early_init:173-185.  The real RAM amount is ignored; '-m 4G'
32: *     causes a crash downstream via DRV-VIRTIO-01.
33: *   BOOT-03 (W2 REFINE) arch_cpu_wake_secondary sends INIT + one STARTUP IPI
34: *     at :272-279.  Intel SDM recommends INIT + two SIPIs for reliability on
35: *     real hardware.  QEMU accepts a single SIPI so no observed failure.
36: *   BOOT-04 (W1 DOC/BAD-IMPL) 'secondary_ttbr0' and 'arch_vmm_set_secondary_pgd'
37: *     at :224-228 use the AArch64 register name "ttbr0" for an x86 CR3 value —
38: *     cross-architecture naming leak.
39: *   ARCH-01 (W3 WRONG-DESIGN) amd64_count_cpus uses CPUID.01h EBX[23:16] which
40: *     returns the max addressable APIC IDs (not online CPUs); on single-socket
41: *     systems it may match, but on NUMA or hyperthreaded systems it over-counts.
42: *     Should parse ACPI MADT for accurate online CPU discovery.
43: *   ARCH-02 (W3 STUB) arch_pci_init is an empty stub at :222; amd64 has no
44: *     ACPI table parsing; PCI enumeration relies solely on pci_enumerate/HAL.
45: *   ARCH-03 (W2 STUB) timer_get_us returns jiffies*1000; 'jiffies' is a dummy
46: *     counter incremented by the timer ISR and not a real microsecond source.
47: */
