142:/*
143: * arch_platform_early_init - detect boot protocol and build the memory map.
144: *
145: * Called very early (before PMM, VMM, or SMP); only UART and PIC are
146: * initialised here for output and IRQ masking.
147: *
148: * Protocol detection via mb_magic (saved from %eax in start.S _start_64):
149: *   MB1_MAGIC (0x2BADB002): Multiboot 1 — parse mmap if flag bit 6 set,
150: *     otherwise use mem_upper for two regions.
151: *   MB2_MAGIC (0x36D76289): Multiboot 2 — walk tag chain, collect MMAP tags.
152: *   PVH_MAGIC            : Parse hvm_start_info.memmap_paddr.
153: *     NOTE(BOOT-01): PVH magic is in the struct, not in %eax; this branch is
154: *     never reached on 'make run ARCH=amd64' (mb_magic == 0 from QEMU PVH).
155: *   else (unknown/0)     : Fallback to hardcoded 640KB + (1GB - 1MB) regions.
156: *     NOTE(BOOT-02): The 1 GB fallback is the path taken on 'make run' because
157: *     BOOT-01 prevents PVH detection.  Real memory size is ignored.
158: *
159: * Side effects:
160: *   - uart_init(), pic_init() called.
161: *   - arch_mem_regions[] and arch_region_count populated.
162: */
163:void arch_platform_early_init(void) {
164:  uart_init();
165:  pr_info("AMD64 Platform Initialization (Magic: 0x%lx, Info: 0x%lx)\n",
166:          mb_magic, mb_info_ptr);
167:
168:  pic_init();
169:
170:  if (mb_info_ptr == 0) {
171:    pr_warn(
172:        "Boot information missing! Attempting to continue with fallback.\n");
173:  }
174:
175:  arch_region_count = 0;
176:
177:  if (mb_magic == MB1_MAGIC) {
178:    /* Multiboot v1: %eax == 0x2BADB002 set by the MB1-compliant bootloader */
179:    struct mb1_info *mb1 = (struct mb1_info *)mb_info_ptr;
180:    pr_info("Multiboot v1: Upper memory %u KB\n", mb1->mem_upper);
181:
182:    if (mb1->flags & (1 << 6)) { /* MMAP available (Multiboot1 flags bit 6) */
183:      uint32_t mmap_ptr = mb1->mmap_addr;
184:      uint32_t mmap_len = mb1->mmap_len;
185:      uint32_t processed = 0;
186:
187:      while (processed < mmap_len && arch_region_count < 32) {
188:        uint32_t size = *(uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)mmap_ptr;
189:        struct mb2_mmap_entry *entry =
190:            (struct mb2_mmap_entry *)(uintptr_t)(mmap_ptr + 4);
191:
192:        arch_mem_regions[arch_region_count].base = entry->addr;
193:        arch_mem_regions[arch_region_count].size = entry->len;
194:        arch_mem_regions[arch_region_count].type =
195:            (entry->type == 1) ? MEM_REGION_USABLE : MEM_REGION_RESERVED;
196:        arch_region_count++;
197:
198:        mmap_ptr += size + 4;
199:        processed += size + 4;
200:      }
201:    } else {
202:      /* Fallback if no mmap */
203:      arch_mem_regions[0].base = 0;
204:      arch_mem_regions[0].size = 640 * 1024;
205:      arch_mem_regions[0].type = MEM_REGION_USABLE;
206:      arch_mem_regions[1].base = 0x100000;
207:      arch_mem_regions[1].size = (uint64_t)mb1->mem_upper * 1024;
208:      arch_mem_regions[1].type = MEM_REGION_USABLE;
209:      arch_region_count = 2;
210:    }
211:  } else if (mb_magic == MB2_MAGIC) {
212:    /* Multiboot v2: walk the tag list starting 8 bytes past the header.
213:     * Tags are 8-byte aligned; the loop advances by (tag->size + 7) & ~7. */
214:    uint8_t *mb_data = (uint8_t *)mb_info_ptr;
215:    struct mb2_tag *tag = (struct mb2_tag *)(mb_data + 8);
216:    while (tag->type != MB2_TAG_TYPE_END && arch_region_count < 32) {
217:      if (tag->type == MB2_TAG_TYPE_MMAP) {
218:        struct mb2_tag_mmap *mmap = (struct mb2_tag_mmap *)tag;
219:        uint32_t entry_size = mmap->entry_size;
220:        uint32_t num_entries =
221:            (mmap->size - sizeof(struct mb2_tag_mmap)) / entry_size;
222:        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < num_entries && arch_region_count < 32; i++) {
223:          struct mb2_mmap_entry *entry =
224:              (struct mb2_mmap_entry *)((uint8_t *)mmap->entries +
225:                                        i * entry_size);
226:          arch_mem_regions[arch_region_count].base = entry->addr;
227:          arch_mem_regions[arch_region_count].size = entry->len;
228:          arch_mem_regions[arch_region_count].type =
229:              (entry->type == 1) ? MEM_REGION_USABLE : MEM_REGION_RESERVED;
230:          arch_region_count++;
231:        }
232:      }
233:      tag = (struct mb2_tag *)((uint8_t *)tag + ((tag->size + 7) & ~7));
234:    }
235:  } else if (mb_magic == PVH_MAGIC ||
236:             (mb_info_ptr &&
237:              ((struct hvm_start_info *)mb_info_ptr)->magic == PVH_MAGIC)) {
238:    /* FIX(BOOT-01/02): QEMU's PVH boot ('make run ARCH=amd64' via -kernel) sets
239:     * %eax (mb_magic) to 0 and passes the hvm_start_info pointer in %ebx
240:     * (mb_info_ptr); the identifying magic lives INSIDE the struct, not in a
241:     * register. Detect PVH by the struct magic so the REAL memory map (up to
242:     * 4GB) is parsed instead of the hardcoded 1GB fallback. */
243:    /* PVH boot: hvm_start_info at mb_info_ptr contains the E820/memmap.
244:     * NOTE(BOOT-01): On QEMU PVH boot mb_magic is 0, not PVH_MAGIC; this
245:     * branch is never reached.  mb_info_ptr would be the hvm_start_info PA
246:     * but only if start.S correctly saved %ebx — which it does via %esi.
247:     * The root cause of BOOT-01 is the magic check, not the pointer save. */
248:    struct hvm_start_info *pvh = (struct hvm_start_info *)mb_info_ptr;
249:    pr_info("PVH: Memmap at 0x%lx, entries: %u\n", pvh->memmap_paddr,
250:            pvh->memmap_entries);
251:
252:    struct hvm_memmap_table_entry *entries =
253:        (struct hvm_memmap_table_entry *)pvh->memmap_paddr;
254:    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < pvh->memmap_entries && arch_region_count < 32;
255:         i++) {
256:      arch_mem_regions[arch_region_count].base = entries[i].addr;
257:      arch_mem_regions[arch_region_count].size = entries[i].len;
258:      arch_mem_regions[arch_region_count].type =
259:          (entries[i].type == 1) ? MEM_REGION_USABLE : MEM_REGION_RESERVED;
260:      arch_region_count++;
261:    }
262:  } else {
263:    /* NOTE(BOOT-02): This branch fires on 'make run ARCH=amd64' because
264:     * BOOT-01 prevents PVH detection.  mb_magic == 0 on that path. */
265:    pr_warn("AMD64: [IDTF] Unknown boot protocol (Magic: 0x%lx). Using safe "
266:            "1GB default.\n",
267:            mb_magic);
268:
269:    /* Safe default for QEMU/Basic systems.
270:     * NOTE(BOOT-02): Hardcoded 1 GB ignores actual RAM size; '-m 4G' results
271:     * in a crash via DRV-VIRTIO-01 (PCI BAR above 4GB). */
272:    arch_mem_regions[0].base = 0;
273:    arch_mem_regions[0].size = 640 * 1024;
274:    arch_mem_regions[0].type = MEM_REGION_USABLE;
275:    arch_mem_regions[1].base = 0x100000;
276:    arch_mem_regions[1].size = (1024UL * 1024 * 1024) - 0x100000;
277:    arch_mem_regions[1].type = MEM_REGION_USABLE;
278:    arch_region_count = 2;
279:  }
280:}
281:
282:/*
283: * timer_get_us - return a pseudo-microsecond timestamp.
284: *
285: * NOTE(ARCH-03): This is a stub.  'jiffies' is a tick counter incremented by
286: * kernel_timer_tick at HZ rate.  Multiplying by 1000 converts ticks to rough
287: * millisecond values, not microseconds.  A real implementation would read the
288: * TSC (with a calibrated ns/tick ratio) or the HPET.
289: *
290: * Returns: jiffies * 1000 (milliseconds, labelled as "microseconds").
291: */
292:uint64_t timer_get_us(void) {
293:  /* NOTE(ARCH-03): jiffies*1000 is millisecond granularity, not microseconds */
294:  return jiffies * 1000;
295:}
296:
297:/*
298: * udelay - spin for approximately 'us' microseconds.
299: *
300: * If the LAPIC timer has been calibrated (ticks_per_ms != 0), reads LAPIC_TCC
301: * (Timer Current Count, MMIO offset 0x390) to measure elapsed LAPIC ticks.
302: * The elapsed calculation handles counter wrap-around (LAPIC counts down from
303: * TIC to 0 and reloads for periodic mode).
304: *
305: * If ticks_per_ms == 0 (calibration not yet run), falls back to a busy-loop
306: * writing to port 0x80 (a conventional POST-code delay port).
307: *
308: * Caution: assumes the LAPIC timer is in periodic mode and running.  Before
309: * lapic_timer_calibrate() has been called (e.g. in early boot), only the port
310: * 0x80 fallback is accurate.
311: *
312: * NOTE(ARCH-03): Microsecond accuracy depends on ticks_per_ms calibration;
313: * accuracy is typically ±1 ms due to the PIT 10ms measurement window in
314: * lapic_timer_calibrate.
315: */
316:extern uint32_t ticks_per_ms;
317:void udelay(uint32_t us) {
318:  if (ticks_per_ms == 0) {
319:    /* Fallback: rough delay via port 0x80 writes (~1µs each on legacy systems) */
320:    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < us * 10; i++) {
321:      outb(0x80, 0);
322:    }
323:    return;
324:  }
325:
326:  uint32_t ticks_to_wait = (ticks_per_ms * us) / 1000;
327:  if (ticks_to_wait == 0)
328:    ticks_to_wait = 1;
329:
330:  /* Use LAPIC Timer Current Count (LAPIC_TCC, register offset 0x390) for delay.
331:   * LAPIC counts down; handles wrap-around when the timer reloads at zero. */
332:  uint32_t start = lapic_read(0x0390); /* LAPIC_TCC: current countdown value */
333:  while (1) {
334:    uint32_t current = lapic_read(0x0390);
335:    uint32_t elapsed =
336:        (start > current) ? (start - current) : (0xFFFFFFFF - current + start);
337:    if (elapsed >= ticks_to_wait)
338:      break;
339:    arch_nop();
340:  }
341:}
342:
343:/*
344: * arch_pci_init - AMD64 PCI controller initialization.
345: *
346: * NOTE(ARCH-02): Empty stub.  amd64 has no ACPI table parsing.  PCI
347: * enumeration is performed later by arch_bus_scan (hal.c) via pci_enumerate,
348: * which uses the legacy CF8/CFC configuration mechanism.  A complete
349: * implementation would parse ACPI MCFG for PCIe MMCFG base addresses.
350: */
351:void arch_pci_init(void) { /* Minimal stub — NOTE(ARCH-02): no ACPI parsing */ }
352:
353:extern char __kernel_stack[];
354:/* secondary_ttbr0: the kernel PML4 physical address written for AP trampoline use.
355: * NOTE(BOOT-04): Named 'ttbr0' (an AArch64 register) for an x86 CR3 value —
356: * cross-arch naming leak; should be 'secondary_cr3' or 'secondary_pgd_phys'. */
357:uint64_t secondary_ttbr0 = 0;
358:
359:/*
360: * arch_vmm_set_secondary_pgd - record the PML4 PA for AP trampoline use.
361: *
362: * The trampoline reads trampoline_pml4 (patched in arch_cpu_wake_secondary)
363: * directly; secondary_ttbr0 is a separate copy for callers that query the
364: * current secondary PGD before waking the AP.
365: *
366: * NOTE(BOOT-04): Cross-arch naming; 'secondary_ttbr0' is confusingly AArch64.
367: */
368:void arch_vmm_set_secondary_pgd(uint64_t pgd) { secondary_ttbr0 = pgd; }
369:
370:/*
371: * arch_get_kernel_stack - return the top of the kernel stack for cpu_id.
372: *
373: * __kernel_stack is a statically allocated BSS region of size 128KB * MAX_CPUS
374: * (start.S: .skip 131072 * MAX_CPUS).  Each CPU gets 131072 bytes.
375: * The stack grows downward, so the top of CPU N's slice is at:
376: *   &__kernel_stack[(N+1) * 131072]
377: *
378: * This address is passed to trampoline_stack in arch_cpu_wake_secondary and
379: * will become the AP's RSP when it starts executing C code after the trampoline.
380: *
381: * Returns NULL if cpu_id >= MAX_CPUS.
382: */
383:extern char __kernel_stack[];
384:void *arch_get_kernel_stack(uint32_t cpu_id) {
385:  if (cpu_id >= MAX_CPUS)
386:    return NULL;
387:  /* Each CPU gets 128KB stack. We return the TOP of the stack (descending). */
388:  return (void *)&__kernel_stack[(uint64_t)(cpu_id + 1) * 131072];
389:}
390:
391:/* External symbols for the AP trampoline code (trampoline.S) */
392:extern char trampoline_start[], trampoline_end[];
393:extern uint32_t trampoline_pml4;
394:extern uint64_t trampoline_stack, trampoline_entry;
395:extern uint64_t kernel_pgd_phys;
396:extern void secondary_cpu_entry(void);
397:
398:/*
399: * arch_cpu_wake_secondary - boot an AP from real mode via INIT-SIPI sequence.
400: *
401: * The AP starts executing in real mode at the 4KB-aligned physical address
402: * given by the STARTUP IPI vector field (vector << 12 = 0x01 << 12 = 0x1000).
403: * TRAMPOLINE_BASE must match this address.
404: *
405: * Steps:
406: *   1. Copy the trampoline blob (trampoline.S) to TRAMPOLINE_BASE (0x1000).
407: *      The trampoline is position-independent; it references its own data
408: *      using base-relative addressing (e.g. trampoline_pml4 - trampoline_start + 0x1000).
409: *   2. Patch the trampoline's PML4, stack, and entry-point fields at their
410: *      relocated addresses inside the trampoline copy.
411: *      - trampoline_pml4 (uint32_t): CR3 value for 64-bit mode.
412: *      - trampoline_stack (uint64_t): RSP to load before calling C code.
413: *      - trampoline_entry (uint64_t): the C entry point (secondary_cpu_entry).
414: *   3. Send INIT IPI (edge-triggered, assert, physical destination).
415: *   4. Wait 10 ms (Intel SDM requirement between INIT and first STARTUP).
416: *   5. Send STARTUP IPI with vector 0x01 (page 0x1000).
417: *      NOTE(BOOT-03): SDM recommends two SIPIs (the second after 200µs) for
418: *      robust bringup on real hardware.  Only one SIPI is sent here; QEMU
419: *      accepts a single SIPI so no observed failure in emulation.
420: *
421: * Params:
422: *   cpu_id - destination LAPIC ID.
423: *   entry  - ignored (entry point is hard-coded to secondary_cpu_entry).
424: *   stack  - top of the AP kernel stack (as returned by arch_get_kernel_stack).
425: *
426: * NOTE(CPU-TRAMP-01): The trampoline GDT (trampoline.S:76-81) has only 4
427: *   entries: null, 32-bit code, 32-bit data, 64-bit code.  After the far jump
428: *   to 64-bit mode (ljmp $0x18), DS/ES/SS still hold 0x10 (the 32-bit data
429: *   descriptor); no 64-bit data segment is present.  Some CPUs may enforce the
430: *   D-bit on SS in 64-bit mode.  [inferred; not observed to crash on QEMU]
431: *
432: * Returns 0 on success, -1 if cpu_id is out of range.
433: */
434:int arch_cpu_wake_secondary(uint64_t cpu_id, void (*entry)(void), void *stack) {
435:  (void)entry; /* hard-coded to secondary_cpu_entry in trampoline patch below */
436:
437:  if (cpu_id >= MAX_CPUS)
438:    return -1;
439:
440:  /* 1. Copy trampoline to TRAMPOLINE_BASE (physical address 0x1000).
441:   * The low 1 MB is identity-mapped (RW) by arch_vmm_init_hw. */
442:  uint8_t *dest = (uint8_t *)TRAMPOLINE_BASE;
443:  size_t size = trampoline_end - trampoline_start;
444:  memcpy(dest, trampoline_start, size);
445:
446:  /* 2. Patch trampoline parameters at their relocated addresses.
447:   * Each parameter's address is (TRAMPOLINE_BASE + (symbol - trampoline_start))
448:   * because the copied code was originally linked at trampoline_start. */
449:  uint32_t *p_pml4 =
450:      (uint32_t *)(TRAMPOLINE_BASE +
451:                   ((uintptr_t)&trampoline_pml4 - (uintptr_t)trampoline_start));
452:  uint64_t *p_stack =
453:      (uint64_t *)(TRAMPOLINE_BASE + ((uintptr_t)&trampoline_stack -
454:                                      (uintptr_t)trampoline_start));
455:  uint64_t *p_entry =
456:      (uint64_t *)(TRAMPOLINE_BASE + ((uintptr_t)&trampoline_entry -
457:                                      (uintptr_t)trampoline_start));
458:
459:  *p_pml4 = (uint32_t)kernel_pgd_phys;  /* CR3: kernel PML4 physical address */
460:  *p_stack = (uint64_t)stack;            /* RSP: top of AP kernel stack */
461:  *p_entry = (uint64_t)secondary_cpu_entry; /* call target after long mode */
462:
463:  /* 3. Send INIT IPI: reset AP to 'wait-for-SIPI' state */
464:  lapic_send_ipi(cpu_id, ICR_INIT | ICR_ASSERT | ICR_LEVEL | ICR_PHYSICAL);
465:
466:  /* 4. Wait 10 ms (Intel SDM: 10ms between INIT and SIPI for spec compliance) */
467:  udelay(10000);
468:
469:  /* 5. Send STARTUP IPI: vector 0x01 → AP starts at physical 0x1000.
470:   * NOTE(BOOT-03): SDM recommends a second SIPI after 200µs; omitted here. */
471:  lapic_send_ipi(cpu_id, ICR_STARTUP | 0x01 | ICR_PHYSICAL);
472:
473:  pr_info("AMD64: Sent INIT-SIPI to CPU %lu\n", cpu_id);
474:  return 0;
475:}
476:
477:/* arch_get_boot_info - return the physical address of the boot info structure. */
478:uint64_t arch_get_boot_info(void) { return (uint64_t)mb_info_ptr; }
479:
480:/*
481: * amd64_count_cpus - estimate the number of logical CPUs via CPUID.
482: *
483: * Executes CPUID with EAX=01h and extracts EBX[23:16], which the Intel SDM
484: * defines as "Maximum number of addressable IDs for logical processors in this
485: * physical package."  On simple single-socket systems this equals the number
486: * of logical cores.
487: *
488: * NOTE(ARCH-01): EBX[23:16] is the MAX APIC ID count, not necessarily the
489: * number of *online* cores.  On hyperthreaded or NUMA systems this field can
490: * be a power-of-two larger than the actual core count.  The correct approach
491: * is to parse the ACPI MADT (Multiple APIC Description Table) which enumerates
492: * exactly the enabled/online LAPIC entries.  This function may over-count.
493: *
494: * Returns: number of logical CPUs in range [1, MAX_CPUS].
495: */
496:static uint32_t amd64_count_cpus(void) {
497:  uint32_t ebx;
498:  uint32_t cpu_count = 1; /* At least the BSP */
499:
500:  /* CPUID EAX=01h: EBX[23:16] = maximum addressable APIC IDs in package.
501:   * NOTE(ARCH-01): Over-counts on HT/NUMA; should use ACPI MADT instead. */
502:  __asm__ volatile(
503:      "movl $1, %%eax\n\t"
504:      "cpuid\n\t"
505:      : "=b"(ebx)
506:      :
507:      : "eax", "ecx", "edx"
508:  );
509:
510:  cpu_count = (ebx >> 16) & 0xFF;
511:  if (cpu_count == 0) cpu_count = 1;
512:  if (cpu_count > MAX_CPUS) cpu_count = MAX_CPUS;
513:
514:  pr_info("AMD64: CPUID reports %u logical processors\n", cpu_count);
515:  return cpu_count;
516:}
517:
518:extern void secondary_cpu_entry(void);
519:
520:/*
521: * arch_smp_init - bring application processors online one at a time.
522: *
523: * Called by the BSP after all per-CPU BSP init (GDT/IDT/LAPIC) is complete.
524: * Iterates logical CPU IDs 1..(cpu_count-1) (skipping the BSP ID).
525: *
526: * For each AP: compute its kernel stack slice (arch_get_kernel_stack returns
527: * the bottom; stack_top = bottom + 131072 for 128 KB per CPU), then hand off
528: * to smp_bringup_secondary() (kernel/core/smp.c) — the shared arch-neutral
529: * primitive owning the idle-task-first invariant (#169/#170), the INIT-SIPI
530: * wake via arch_cpu_wake_secondary, and the acquire/release ack handshake
531: * with a ~10 s wall-time timeout.  A timeout just skips the CPU (absent AP
532: * or very slow hypervisor — its idle task already exists, so a late-arriving
533: * AP still schedules safely).
534: *
535: * NOTE(ARCH-01): cpu_count from amd64_count_cpus may over-count; APs that
536: * don't exist simply time out and emit a warning.
537: * NOTE(BOOT-03): arch_cpu_wake_secondary sends only one SIPI; see BOOT-03.
538: */
539:void arch_smp_init(void) {
540:  uint32_t bsp_id = (uint32_t)hal_cpu_id();
541:  pr_info("AMD64: Initializing SMP (BSP ID: %u)\n", bsp_id);
542:
543:  /* Determine the number of CPUs to probe (like fdt_count_cpus() on aarch64).
544:   * NOTE(ARCH-01): CPUID-based; may over-count on HT/NUMA systems. */
545:  uint32_t cpu_count = amd64_count_cpus();
546:  if (cpu_count > MAX_CPUS) cpu_count = MAX_CPUS;
547:
548:  pr_info("AMD64: Starting SMP initialization for %u potential cores\n", cpu_count);
549:
550:  /* Iterate only up to detected CPU count */
551:  for (uint32_t i = 1; i < cpu_count; i++) {
552:    if (i == bsp_id)
553:      continue;
554:
555:    /* Stack slice: 128KB per CPU (131072 bytes).  arch_get_kernel_stack returns
556:     * the bottom of the slice; add 131072 for the top (stack descends). */
557:    void *stack_bottom = arch_get_kernel_stack(i);
558:    void *stack_top = (void *)((uintptr_t)stack_bottom + 131072);
559:
560:    /* Shared bring-up primitive (S-ALIGN F8, B6 slice): idle-task-first
561:     * (#169/#170), the INIT-SIPI wake and the ack handshake all live in
562:     * kernel/core/smp.c — the ordering fix is reasoned about ONCE, not once
563:     * per arch.  NOTE(BOOT-03): single SIPI only. */
564:    if (smp_bringup_secondary(i, secondary_cpu_entry, stack_top) == 0) {
565:      pr_info("AMD64: CPU %u is online\n", i);
566:    } else {
567:      /* Wake failed, or the AP did not respond in time (absent, or a very
568:       * slow hypervisor).  Its idle task already exists, so if it comes up
569:       * late it schedules safely. */
570:      pr_warn("AMD64: CPU %u failed to ACK boot\n", i);
571:    }
572:  }
573:}

@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/hal.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/amd64/hal.c
3: * AMD64 Hardware Abstraction Layer — PCI Bus Scan and Timer Init
4: *
5: * Responsibilities:
6: *   - amd64_pci_callback: called by pci_enumerate for each discovered PCI
7: *     function; enables Bus Master + I/O + Memory access, reads BAR0 and BAR4,
8: *     translates VirtIO device IDs, assigns the IRQ, and registers the device
9: *     with the HAL device table via hal_register_device.
10: *   - arch_bus_scan: invokes pci_enumerate(amd64_pci_callback) to build the
11: *     HAL device list.
12: *   - arch_irq_init: initialises the legacy 8259 PIC.
13: *   - arch_timer_init: runs LAPIC calibration once on the BSP.
14: *   - timer_init_percpu: starts the per-CPU LAPIC periodic timer at HZ.
15: *
16: * Known issues:
17: *   DRV-VIRTIO-01 (W5 BUG) pci_get_bar (pci.c:106) returns uint32_t.  For
18: *     64-bit BAR entries (type bits [2:1] = 0b10), the high 32 bits of the
19: *     MMIO base address are in the NEXT BAR register and are not read.  When
20: *     QEMU places the virtio-blk BAR above 4 GB ('-m 4G'), the low 32 bits
21: *     returned by pci_get_bar(bdf, 4) are 0 or an alias, so dev->base is
22: *     wrong.  The virtio driver reads QUEUE_NUM_MAX from the wrong address and
23: *     gets 0 → "Invalid queue size (0)!" → downstream divide-by-zero crash.
24: *     Cross-ref: DRV-PCI-02 (pci.c:106-111).
25: *     Fix: in amd64_pci_callback, after reading b4, check bits [2:1]; if 10b,
26: *     read BAR5 and compose a uint64_t base address.
27: */
28:#include <kernel/hal.h>
29:#include <drivers/pci.h>
30:#include <kernel/string.h>
31:#include <kernel/printk.h>
32:#include <kernel/platform.h>
33:#include <kernel/multiboot2.h>
34:#include <drivers/timer.h>
35:#include <arch/amd64/apic.h>

37:/* arch_platform_get_boot_module (HAL contract, platform.h): walk the GRUB
38: * multiboot2 tag chain for a MODULE (the release rootfs disk.img loaded into
39: * RAM).  Cached on first call (invoked early, before the identity map is torn
40: * down) so later callers — the ramdisk backend after vmm_init — still get it.
41: * mb_magic / arch_get_boot_info() come from this arch's boot stub. */
42:extern uint64_t mb_magic;
43:uint64_t arch_get_boot_info(void);
44:
45:int arch_platform_get_boot_module(uint64_t *base, uint64_t *size) {
46:  static int probed = 0;
47:  static uint64_t mod_base, mod_size;
48:  if (!probed) {
49:    probed = 1;
50:    if (mb_magic == MB2_MAGIC) {
51:      uint8_t *d = (uint8_t *)arch_get_boot_info();
52:      if (d) {
53:        struct mb2_tag *tag = (struct mb2_tag *)(d + 8);
54:        while (tag->type != MB2_TAG_TYPE_END) {
55:          if (tag->type == MB2_TAG_TYPE_MODULE) {
56:            struct mb2_tag_module *m = (struct mb2_tag_module *)tag;
57:            mod_base = m->mod_start;
58:            mod_size = (uint64_t)m->mod_end - m->mod_start;
59:            break;
60:          }
61:          tag = (struct mb2_tag *)((uint8_t *)tag + ((tag->size + 7) & ~7u));
62:        }
63:      }
64:    }
65:  }
66:  if (mod_base) {
67:    if (base) *base = mod_base;
68:    if (size) *size = mod_size;
69:    return 1;
70:  }
71:  return 0;
72:}
73:
74:static void amd64_pci_callback(int bdf, uint16_t vendor, uint16_t device_id) {
75:    struct hal_device dev;
76:    memset(&dev, 0, sizeof(dev));
77:    
78:    dev.bus_type = HAL_BUS_TYPE_PCI;
79:    dev.vendor_id = vendor;
80:    dev.device_id = device_id;
81:    dev.pci_bdf = (uint32_t)bdf;
82:
83:    /* Class triplet (offset 0x08): lets the driver-binding layer match generic
84:     * controllers (xHCI/AHCI/VGA/NVMe) by function instead of vendor:device. */
85:    uint32_t cls = pci_get_class(bdf);
86:    dev.class_code  = (cls >> 24) & 0xFF;
87:    dev.subclass    = (cls >> 16) & 0xFF;
88:    dev.prog_if     = (cls >> 8)  & 0xFF;
89:    dev.header_type = pci_get_header_type(bdf);
90:
91:    /* Enable PCI Bus Master and IO/Mem space */
92:    uint32_t cmd = pci_config_read((bdf >> 16) & 0xFF, (bdf >> 8) & 0xFF, bdf & 0x7, 0x04);
93:    pci_config_write((bdf >> 16) & 0xFF, (bdf >> 8) & 0xFF, bdf & 0x7, 0x04, cmd | 0x7);
94:
95:    /* Get BAR address. Modern devices use BAR4 for MMIO usually. Legacy uses BAR0 for Port I/O. */
96:    uint32_t b0 = pci_get_bar(bdf, 0);
97:    uint32_t b4 = pci_get_bar(bdf, 4);
98:
99:    bool is_modern = (vendor == 0x1AF4 && device_id >= 0x1041);
100:    
101:    if (is_modern && b4 != 0 && !(b4 & 1)) {
102:        /* FIX(DRV-VIRTIO-01): read the FULL 64-bit BAR. For a 64-bit memory BAR
103:         * (type bits [2:1] == 0b10) the high 32 bits live in BAR5; reading only
104:         * BAR4 truncates the base when QEMU places it above 4GB ('-m 4G'),
105:         * yielding a wrong dev.base -> virtio reads QUEUE_NUM_MAX as 0 -> crash. */
106:        dev.base = (uintptr_t)(b4 & ~0xFU);
107:        if ((b4 & 0x6) == 0x4) { /* 64-bit memory BAR */
108:            uint32_t b5 = pci_get_bar(bdf, 5);
109:            dev.base |= ((uintptr_t)b5 << 32);
110:        }
111:        /* FIX(AMMU-07): map the BAR MMIO so it is reachable even above 4GB
112:         * (the fixed 0xFE000000-0xFFFFFFFF identity window does not cover it). */
113:        extern int arch_vmm_map_device(uint64_t base, uint64_t size);
114:        arch_vmm_map_device(dev.base, 0x10000);
115:    } else {
116:        dev.base = b0;
117:        if (dev.base & 1) dev.base &= ~3;
118:        else dev.base &= ~0xF;
119:    }
120:    
121:    /* Handle VirtIO ID translation */
122:    if (vendor == 0x1AF4) {
123:        if (is_modern) {
124:            dev.device_id = device_id - 0x1040;
125:        } else {
126:            /* Legacy device: Use Subsystem Device ID for type */
127:            uint32_t sub_id = pci_config_read((bdf >> 16) & 0xFF, (bdf >> 8) & 0xFF, bdf & 0x7, 0x2C);
128:            dev.device_id = sub_id >> 16;
129:        }
130:    }
131:    
132:    dev.irq = 32 + pci_get_interrupt(bdf);
133:    
134:    /* Basic naming */
135:    if (vendor == 0x1AF4) {
136:        snprintf(dev.name, sizeof(dev.name), "VirtIO-%d", device_id);
137:    } else {
138:        snprintf(dev.name, sizeof(dev.name), "PCI-%04x:%04x", vendor, device_id);
139:    }
140:    
141:    hal_register_device(&dev);
142:}
143:
144:void arch_bus_scan(void) {
145:    pr_info("%s", "HAL: Scanning PCI Bus...\n");
146:    pci_enumerate(amd64_pci_callback);
147:}
148:
149:void arch_irq_init(void) {
150:    extern void pic_init(void);
151:    pic_init();
152:}
153:
154:void arch_timer_init(void) {
155:    /* BSP Global Timer initialization.
156:     * We perform LAPIC calibration here once using the legacy PIT. */
157:    pr_info("HAL: Initializing global timer state (LAPIC calibration)\n");
158:    lapic_timer_calibrate();
159:}
160:
161:void timer_init_percpu(void) {
162:    /* Initialize local APIC timer for the current CPU at configured HZ.
163:     * This is called by every CPU during its local initialization. */
164:    lapic_timer_setup(HZ);
165:}

@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/kernel.ld @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/amd64/kernel.ld — x86-64 Linker Script (higher half)
3: *
4: * Physical layout (what GRUB / QEMU's PVH loader places in RAM, by p_paddr):
5: *   1MB..2MB  boot region, linked VA == PA: multiboot/PVH headers, the
6: *             32-bit entry + long-mode stub (.text.boot), the boot GDT and
7: *             the boot page tables (.boot_bss).  This code runs before/
8: *             during paging enable, so it must execute at its link address.
9: *   2MB..     kernel proper, linked at KERNEL_VIRT_BASE + PA
10: *             (0xFFFF800000000000 + 2MB — see kernel/memlayout.h) and
11: *             loaded at the AT() physical address.  start.S jumps here
12: *             after enabling paging with both the identity and the
13: *             higher-half mappings.
14: */
15:
16:OUTPUT_FORMAT("elf64-x86-64")
17:OUTPUT_ARCH(i386:x86-64)
18:ENTRY(_start_32)
19:
20:KVB = 0xFFFF800000000000;
21:
22:/*
23: * One segment per permission set.  The boot region used to be a single
24: * FLAGS(7) R+W+X PT_LOAD holding both the pre-paging code and the boot page
25: * tables, which is why the link emitted "LOAD segment with RWX permissions":
26: * the image itself contradicted the charter's W^X claim before a single page
27: * table was ever built.  The input sections were already correctly marked
28: * ("ax" for .text.boot, "aw",@nobits for .boot_bss) — only the script fused
29: * them, so splitting the segment costs nothing and makes the ELF say what the
30: * sections already said.
31: *
32: * NOTE: this fixes the IMAGE half of HAL-0b.  The RUNTIME half — amd64 still
33: * identity-maps all RAM in the low half alongside the higher-half map, and
34: * kernel pages are mapped without NX (AMMU-01) — is untouched and remains
35: * open in the plan.  Do not read the absence of this warning as W^X being
36: * enforced at runtime.
37: */
38:PHDRS
39:{
40:    boot      PT_LOAD FLAGS(5); /* R+X: pre-paging code + boot headers */
41:    note      PT_NOTE FLAGS(4); /* R:   PVH note, for the QEMU PVH loader */
42:    boot_data PT_LOAD FLAGS(6); /* R+W: boot GDT + boot page tables       */
43:    text      PT_LOAD FLAGS(5); /* R+X */
44:    data      PT_LOAD FLAGS(6); /* R+W */
45:}
46:
47:SECTIONS {
48:    /* ── Low boot region (VA == PA) ─────────────────────────────────── */
49:    . = 1M;
50:
51:    .boot.text : ALIGN(8) {
52:        KEEP(*(.multiboot))
53:        KEEP(*(.text.boot))
54:    } :boot
55:
56:    /* In BOTH segments on purpose.  PT_NOTE is how QEMU's PVH loader finds the
57:     * entry point, but PT_NOTE is not loadable — an SHF_ALLOC section that
58:     * belongs to no PT_LOAD is what produced "allocated section `.note.PVH'
59:     * not in segment".  Naming :boot as well places the bytes in a loadable
60:     * segment; :note still describes them to the loader. */
61:    .note.PVH : ALIGN(4) {
62:        KEEP(*(.note.PVH))
63:    } :boot :note
64:
65:    .boot_bss : ALIGN(4096) {
66:        *(.boot_bss*)
67:    } :boot_data
68:
69:    . = ALIGN(4096);
70:    __boot_phys_end = .;
71:    ASSERT(__boot_phys_end <= 2M, "boot region overflows the 1MB..2MB window")
72:
73:    /* ── Kernel proper (higher half, loaded at PA = VA - KVB) ───────── */
74:    . = KVB + 2M;
75:
76:    .text : AT(ADDR(.text) - KVB) ALIGN(4096) {
77:        __text_start = .;
78:        *(.text*)
79:        /* AP trampoline blob: copied to 0x1000 at SMP bring-up; fully
80:         * position-independent, never executed in place. */
81:        . = ALIGN(8);
82:        KEEP(*(.trampoline))
83:    } :text
84:    _etext = .;
85:
86:    .rodata : AT(ADDR(.rodata) - KVB) ALIGN(4096) {
87:        *(.rodata*)
88:        . = ALIGN(16); /* GCC DATA_ALIGNMENT ups >=16-byte aggregates to 16 on
89:         * x86-64: with ALIGN(8) the linker could pad AFTER __ktests_start,
90:         * making the first walked descriptor garbage (S-ALIGN F9 fix). */
91:        __ktests_start = .;
92:        KEEP(*(.ktests))
93:        __ktests_end = .;
94:        /* In-kernel symbol table (tools/gen_ksyms.sh, two-pass link).
95:         * Placed after .text so a populated table never shifts text
96:         * addresses between the two link passes. */
97:        . = ALIGN(8);
98:        __ksyms_start = .;
99:        KEEP(*(.ksyms))
100:        __ksyms_end = .;
101:    } :text
102:    __erodata = .;
103:
104:    .data : AT(ADDR(.data) - KVB) ALIGN(4096) {
105:        *(.data*)
106:    } :data
107:
108:    .bss : AT(ADDR(.bss) - KVB) ALIGN(4096) {
109:        __bss_start = .;
110:        *(.bss*)
111:        *(.lbss*)
112:        *(COMMON)
113:        __bss_end = .;
114:    } :data
115:    __kernel_end = .;
116:
117:    /DISCARD/ : {
118:        *(.comment)
119:        *(.note*)
120:        *(.eh_frame*)
121:    }
122:}
123:
124:/* __kernel_start is the VIRTUAL address of everything the loader placed in
125: * RAM (boot region included): virt_to_phys(__kernel_start) == 1MB, so the
126: * PMM reserves the whole image, boot sections and all. */
127:PROVIDE(__kernel_start = KVB + 1M);
128:PROVIDE(__kernel_size = __kernel_end - __kernel_start);
129:

@@@ kernel/arch/amd64/virtio.c @@@
1:#include <drivers/pci.h>
2:#include <drivers/virtio.h>
3:#include <arch/arch.h>
4:#include <arch/platform.h>
5:#include <kernel/hal.h>
6:#include <kernel/printk.h>
7:#include <kernel/string.h>
8:#include <kernel/vmm.h>
9:
10:#define MAX_VIRTIO_DEVS 8
11:
12:static struct virtio_device virtio_devices[MAX_VIRTIO_DEVS];
13:static int virtio_dev_count = 0;
14:
15:/* Translation helpers (reuse logic from original) */
16:static uint32_t translate_legacy(uint32_t offset) {
17:  switch (offset) {
18:  case VIRTIO_MMIO_DEVICE_FEATURES:
19:    return 0x00;
20:  case VIRTIO_MMIO_DRIVER_FEATURES:
21:    return 0x04;
22:  case VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_PFN:
23:    return 0x08;
24:  case VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_NUM_MAX:
25:    return 0x0C;
26:  case VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_NUM:
27:    return 0x0C;
28:  case VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_SEL:
29:    return 0x0E;
30:  case VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_NOTIFY:
31:    return 0x10;
32:  case VIRTIO_MMIO_STATUS:
33:    return 0x12;
34:  case VIRTIO_MMIO_INTERRUPT_STATUS:
35:  case VIRTIO_MMIO_INTERRUPT_ACK:
36:    return 0x13;
37:  default:
38:    return 0xFFFFFFFF;
39:  }
40:}
41:
42:static uint32_t translate_modern(uint32_t offset) {
43:  switch (offset) {
44:  case VIRTIO_MMIO_DEVICE_FEATURES:
45:    return 0x04;
46:  case VIRTIO_MMIO_DRIVER_FEATURES:
47:    return 0x0C;
48:  case VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_SEL:
49:    return 0x16;
50:  case VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_NUM_MAX:
51:    return 0x18;
52:  case VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_NUM:
53:    return 0x18;
54:  case VIRTIO_MMIO_STATUS:
55:    return 0x14;
56:  case VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_PFN:
57:    return 0x20; /* queue_desc_lo */
58:  case VIRTIO_MMIO_INTERRUPT_STATUS:
59:    return 0x60; /* Standard MMIO offset, might need adjustment for PCI */
60:  case VIRTIO_MMIO_INTERRUPT_ACK:
61:    return 0x64;
62:  default:
63:    return 0xFFFFFFFF;
64:  }
65:}
66:
67:/* Modern (MMIO) Implementation */
68:static uint32_t modern_read32(struct virtio_device *dev, uint32_t offset) {
69:  if (offset == VIRTIO_MMIO_MAGIC_VALUE)
70:    return 0x74726976;
71:  if (offset == VIRTIO_MMIO_VERSION)
72:    return 2;
73:  
74:  if (offset == VIRTIO_MMIO_INTERRUPT_STATUS || offset == VIRTIO_MMIO_INTERRUPT_ACK) {
75:    if (dev->isr_base) {
76:      return hal_read8(dev->isr_base);
77:    }
78:    /* Fallback: try both 32-bit and 8-bit reads from standard MMIO offset */
79:    uint32_t val32 = hal_read32(dev->base + 0x60);
80:    if (val32 != 0)
81:      return val32;
82:    /* Try 8-bit read in case device uses narrow reads */
83:    return hal_read8(dev->base + 0x60);
84:  }
85:
86:  uint32_t mod_off = translate_modern(offset);
87:  if (mod_off == 0xFFFFFFFF)
88:    return 0;
89:  return hal_read32(dev->base + mod_off);
90:}
91:
92:static void modern_write32(struct virtio_device *dev, uint32_t offset,
93:                           uint32_t val) {
94:  if (offset == VIRTIO_MMIO_INTERRUPT_ACK) {
95:    if (dev->isr_base) {
96:      hal_read8(dev->isr_base); /* Reading ISR status acknowledges on PCI */
97:    } else {
98:      /* Fallback: write to standard MMIO offset 0x64 if isr_base not set */
99:      hal_write32(dev->base + 0x64, val);
100:    }
101:    return;
102:  }
103:
104:  uint32_t mod_off = translate_modern(offset);
105:  if (mod_off != 0xFFFFFFFF) {
106:    hal_write32(dev->base + mod_off, val);
107:  }
108:}
109:
110:static void modern_notify(struct virtio_device *dev, uint32_t queue_idx) {
111:  if (dev->notify_base) {
112:    hal_write16(dev->notify_base, (uint16_t)queue_idx);
113:  } else {
114:    /* Fallback if no notify capability found */
115:    hal_write16(dev->base + 0x3000, (uint16_t)queue_idx);
116:  }
117:}
118:
119:/* Legacy (Port I/O) Implementation */
120:static uint32_t legacy_read32(struct virtio_device *dev, uint32_t offset) {
121:  if (offset == VIRTIO_MMIO_MAGIC_VALUE)
122:    return 0x74726976;
123:  if (offset == VIRTIO_MMIO_VERSION)
124:    return 1;
125:  uint32_t pci_off = translate_legacy(offset);
126:  if (pci_off == 0xFFFFFFFF)
127:    return 0;
128:  uint16_t port = (uint16_t)dev->base + pci_off;
129:  if (pci_off == 0x12 || pci_off == 0x13)
130:    return hal_read8(port);
131:  if (pci_off == 0x0C || pci_off == 0x0E || pci_off == 0x10)
132:    return hal_read16(port);
133:  return hal_read32(port);
134:}
135:
136:static void legacy_write32(struct virtio_device *dev, uint32_t offset,
137:                           uint32_t val) {
138:  uint32_t pci_off = translate_legacy(offset);
139:  if (pci_off == 0xFFFFFFFF)
140:    return;
141:  uint16_t port = (uint16_t)dev->base + pci_off;
142:  if (pci_off == 0x12 || pci_off == 0x13)
143:    hal_write8(port, (uint8_t)val);
144:  else if (pci_off == 0x0C || pci_off == 0x0E || pci_off == 0x10)
145:    hal_write16(port, (uint16_t)val);
146:  else
147:    hal_write32(port, val);
148:}
149:
150:static void legacy_notify(struct virtio_device *dev, uint32_t queue_idx) {
151:  hal_write16((uint16_t)dev->base + 0x10, (uint16_t)queue_idx);
152:}
153:
154:static const struct virtio_transport_ops modern_ops = {
155:    modern_read32, modern_write32, modern_notify};
156:static const struct virtio_transport_ops legacy_ops = {
157:    legacy_read32, legacy_write32, legacy_notify};
158:
159:/* PCI Discovery Callback */
160:static void virtio_pci_init_device(struct hal_device *hdev) {
161:  if (virtio_dev_count >= MAX_VIRTIO_DEVS)
162:    return;
163:
164:  struct virtio_device *vdev = &virtio_devices[virtio_dev_count];
165:  memset(vdev, 0, sizeof(struct virtio_device));
166:
167:  /* Store HAL handle and basic info */
168:  vdev->hal_dev.base = hdev->base;
169:  vdev->hal_dev.irq = hdev->irq;
170:  vdev->hal_dev.bus_type = hdev->bus_type;
171:  vdev->hal_dev.io_type = (hdev->base < 0x10000) ? HAL_RES_PORT : HAL_RES_MMIO;
172:
173:  vdev->base = hdev->base;
174:  vdev->irq = hdev->irq;
175:  vdev->device_id = hdev->device_id;
176:  vdev->is_legacy = (hdev->vendor_id == 0x1AF4 && hdev->device_id < 0x1000);
177:
178:  int bdf = hdev->pci_bdf;
179:  uint8_t bus = (bdf >> 16) & 0xFF;
180:  uint8_t dev_idx = (bdf >> 8) & 0xFF;
181:  uint8_t func = bdf & 0x7;
182:
183:  /* Scans Capabilities for Modern Device */
184:  bool is_modern = (hdev->vendor_id == 0x1AF4 && hdev->device_id >= 0x1); // Simplified check since IDs are already translated
185:
186:  if (is_modern && vdev->hal_dev.io_type == HAL_RES_MMIO) {
187:    uint8_t cap_ptr = pci_config_read(bus, dev_idx, func, 0x34) & 0xFF;
188:    while (cap_ptr != 0 && cap_ptr != 0xFF) {
189:      uint32_t cap_header = pci_config_read(bus, dev_idx, func, cap_ptr);
190:      uint8_t cap_id = cap_header & 0xFF;
191:      uint8_t next_cap = (cap_header >> 8) & 0xFF;
192:
193:      if (cap_id == 0x09) { /* Vendor Specific (VirtIO) */
194:        uint8_t type = (cap_header >> 24) & 0xFF;
195:        uint8_t bar = pci_config_read(bus, dev_idx, func, cap_ptr + 4) & 0xFF;
196:        uint32_t offset = pci_config_read(bus, dev_idx, func, cap_ptr + 8);
197:
198:        /* FIX(DRV-VIRTIO-01): read the FULL 64-bit BAR. pci_get_bar() returns
199:         * only the low 32 bits; a 64-bit memory BAR (type bits [2:1]==0b10) has
200:         * its high dword in the next BAR slot. Truncating it yields a wrong
201:         * config base when QEMU places the BAR above 4GB ('-m 4G') -> virtio
202:         * reads QUEUE_NUM_MAX from the wrong address as 0 -> divide-by-zero. */
203:        uint32_t bar_lo = pci_get_bar(bdf, bar);
204:        uintptr_t bar_addr = (uintptr_t)(bar_lo & ~0xFU);
205:        if ((bar_lo & 0x6) == 0x4)
206:          bar_addr |= ((uintptr_t)pci_get_bar(bdf, bar + 1) << 32);
207:        /* FIX(AMMU-07): map the BAR MMIO so the config structs are reachable
208:         * even above 4GB (the fixed 0xFE000000-0xFFFFFFFF window misses it). */
209:        extern int arch_vmm_map_device(uint64_t base, uint64_t size);
210:        arch_vmm_map_device(bar_addr, 0x10000);
211:
212:        if (type == 1) { /* Common Config */
213:          vdev->base = bar_addr + offset;
214:          vdev->hal_dev.base = vdev->base;
215:        } else if (type == 2) { /* Notifications */
216:          vdev->notify_base = bar_addr + offset;
217:        } else if (type == 3) { /* ISR Status */
218:          vdev->isr_base = bar_addr + offset;
219:        } else if (type == 4) { /* Device Specific */
220:          vdev->priv = (void *)(bar_addr + offset);
221:        }
222:      }
223:      cap_ptr = next_cap;
224:    }
225:    vdev->ops = &modern_ops;
226:    pr_info("VirtIO: Found Modern device (PCI) at Common=0x%lx, ISR=0x%lx, ID %d\n",
227:            vdev->base, vdev->isr_base, vdev->device_id);
228:  } else {
229:    vdev->ops = &legacy_ops;
230:    vdev->is_legacy = true;
231:    pr_info("VirtIO: Found Legacy device (PCI) at 0x%lx, ID %d\n", vdev->base,
232:            vdev->device_id);
233:  }
234:
235:  virtio_dev_count++;
236:}
237:
238:void arch_virtio_scan(void) {
239:  virtio_dev_count = 0;
240:  
241:  /* Scan PCI-based VirtIO devices */
242:  int count = hal_device_get_count();
243:  for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
244:    struct hal_device *hdev = hal_device_get(i);
245:    if (hdev && hdev->vendor_id == 0x1AF4) {
246:      virtio_pci_init_device(hdev);
247:    }
248:  }
249:  
250:  /* Also scan fixed MMIO addresses (QEMU virt machine type) */
251:  for (int i = 0; i < VIRTIO_COUNT && virtio_dev_count < MAX_VIRTIO_DEVS; i++) {
252:    uintptr_t base = VIRTIO_MMIO_BASE + i * VIRTIO_MMIO_STRIDE;
253:    uint32_t magic = hal_read32(base + VIRTIO_MMIO_MAGIC_VALUE);
254:    
255:    if (magic == 0x74726976) {  /* Magic: "virt" */
256:      uint32_t dev_id = hal_read32(base + VIRTIO_MMIO_DEVICE_ID);
257:      if (dev_id != 0) {
258:        struct virtio_device *vdev = &virtio_devices[virtio_dev_count];
259:        memset(vdev, 0, sizeof(struct virtio_device));
260:        vdev->base = base;
261:        vdev->irq = 48 + i;  /* VirtIO IRQs start at 48 */
262:        vdev->device_id = dev_id;
263:        vdev->ops = &modern_ops;  /* MMIO is always modern */
264:        vdev->hal_dev.base = base;
265:        vdev->hal_dev.irq = 48 + i;
266:        vdev->hal_dev.bus_type = HAL_BUS_TYPE_VIRTIO_MMIO;
267:        vdev->hal_dev.io_type = HAL_RES_MMIO;
268:        vdev->is_legacy = 0;
269:        virtio_dev_count++;
270:      }
271:    }
272:  }
273:}
274:
275:/* Device-config access (GFX-DYN-01 F7).  On a modern PCI device the device-
276: * specific config region was captured into dev->priv (cap type 4) during probe;
277: * read it directly.  Otherwise (MMIO-on-amd64 fallback) config is at
278: * base+VIRTIO_MMIO_CONFIG. */
279:uint32_t virtio_config_read32(virtio_handle_t dev, uint32_t offset) {
280:  if (dev->priv)
281:    return hal_read32((uintptr_t)dev->priv + offset);
282:  return hal_read32(dev->base + VIRTIO_MMIO_CONFIG + offset);
283:}
284:
285:void virtio_config_write32(virtio_handle_t dev, uint32_t offset, uint32_t val) {
286:  if (dev->priv)
287:    hal_write32((uintptr_t)dev->priv + offset, val);
288:  else
289:    hal_write32(dev->base + VIRTIO_MMIO_CONFIG + offset, val);
290:}
291:
292:int arch_virtio_get_count(uint32_t device_id) {
293:  int count = 0;
294:  for (int i = 0; i < virtio_dev_count; i++) {
295:    if (virtio_devices[i].device_id == device_id)
296:      count++;
297:  }
298:  return count;
299:}
300:
301:int arch_virtio_get_device(uint32_t device_id, int index,
302:                           virtio_handle_t *out_dev, uint32_t *out_irq) {
303:  int current = 0;
304:  for (int i = 0; i < virtio_dev_count; i++) {
305:    if (virtio_devices[i].device_id == device_id) {
306:      if (current == index) {
307:        if (out_dev)
308:          *out_dev = &virtio_devices[i];
309:        if (out_irq)
310:          *out_irq = virtio_devices[i].irq;
311:        return 0;
312:      }
313:      current++;
314:    }
315:  }
316:  return -1;
317:}
318:
319:void virtio_setup_queue(virtio_handle_t dev, uint32_t queue_idx,
320:                        uint64_t desc_addr, uint64_t avail_addr,
321:                        uint64_t used_addr) {
322:  if (dev->ops == &modern_ops) {
323:    modern_write32(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_SEL, queue_idx);
324:    /* Modern registers: desc(0x20), avail(0x28), used(0x30) */
325:    hal_write32(dev->base + 0x20, (uint32_t)desc_addr);
326:    hal_write32(dev->base + 0x24, (uint32_t)(desc_addr >> 32));
327:    hal_write32(dev->base + 0x28, (uint32_t)avail_addr);
328:    hal_write32(dev->base + 0x2C, (uint32_t)(avail_addr >> 32));
329:    hal_write32(dev->base + 0x30, (uint32_t)used_addr);
330:    hal_write32(dev->base + 0x34, (uint32_t)(used_addr >> 32));
331:    /* Queue enable (0x1C) */
332:    hal_write32(dev->base + 0x1C, 1);
333:  } else {
334:    uint32_t pfn = (uint32_t)(desc_addr >> 12);
335:    pr_info("VirtIO: Setting Legacy PFN 0x%x for queue %u at 0x%lx\n", pfn,
336:            queue_idx, dev->base);
337:    hal_write16((uint16_t)dev->base + 0x0E, (uint16_t)queue_idx);
338:    hal_write32((uint16_t)dev->base + 0x08, pfn);
339:  }
340:}

@@@ kernel/core/fault.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/core/fault.c
3: * Generic user-vs-kernel fault decision (Phase A step 8).
4: *
5: * Both HAL exception dispatchers route recoverable-fault classification
6: * through fault_handle_user_or_panic():
7: *
8: *   - fault from user mode (CS RPL==3 on amd64, SPSR.M==EL0t on aarch64), or
9: *   - fault from kernel mode while arch_copy_{from,to}_user was dereferencing
10: *     user memory (per-CPU uaccess_active set, fault address in user VA)
11: *
12: *   -> log, terminate the process, return schedule()'s next frame.
13: *
14: * Everything else is a kernel bug: the function returns NULL and the caller
15: * performs its arch-specific register dump and panics (panic() is fault-safe
16: * here because the dispatcher's fault_enter() depth is still held).
17: *
18: * The uaccess_active gate is the CPU-AARCH64-01 fix: a wild kernel pointer
19: * that merely happens to land in user VA range is NOT recoverable and must
20: * panic; only a fault raised by the explicit user-copy window may terminate
21: * the process and continue.
22: */
23:#include <kernel/nx_contract.h>
24:#include <kernel/cpu.h>
25:#include <kernel/fault.h>
26:#include <kernel/printk.h>
27:#include <kernel/registry.h>
28:#include <kernel/sched.h>
29:#include <kernel/string.h>
30:#include <kernel/types.h>
31:#include <kernel/vmm.h>
32:
33:extern struct pt_regs *schedule(struct pt_regs *regs);
34:extern int process_terminate(int pid);
35:
36:/* fault_notify_user - post a RED notification (severity 2) about a crashing user
37: * process to the notification server (nxntfy_srv), so a userland crash is visible
38: * ON SCREEN, not only on the UART.  Best-effort: skipped if the server is not up
39: * (registry key srv.notify_pid absent).  Safe in this path: a user fault leaves
40: * the kernel healthy, so registry_get + kernel_ipc_send are ordinary calls. */
41:static void fault_notify_user(struct process *task, const char *desc) {
42:  char pidbuf[16];
43:  if (registry_get("srv.notify_pid", pidbuf, sizeof(pidbuf)) != 0)
44:    return;
45:  int npid = atoi(pidbuf);
46:  if (npid <= 0)
47:    return;
48:  struct ipc_message m;
49:  m.from = task->pid; /* group the crash notification under the crashing process */
50:  m.type = IPC_TYPE_NOTIFY;
51:  m.data1 = 2; /* severity: error -> red popup (1 = warning/yellow, 0 = info) */
52:  m.data2 = (uint64_t)task->pid;
53:  snprintf(m.payload, sizeof(m.payload), "%s crashed: %s", task->name, desc);
54:  /* DIR-05's contract is that a userland crash is VISIBLE, not that an IPC was
55:   * attempted.  Discarding the result satisfied the letter and lost the point:
56:   * when the notification server is wedged or its queue is full -- exactly the
57:   * moment a crash matters most -- the popup silently never appears and the
58:   * only trace is gone.  So the failure falls back to the channel that cannot
59:   * itself be full. */
60:  if (kernel_ipc_send(npid, &m) != 0)
61:    fault_printf("[FAULT] crash popup NOT delivered to the notify server "
62:                 "(pid %d): %s\n",
63:                 npid, m.payload);
64:}
65:
66:struct pt_regs *fault_handle_user_or_panic(struct pt_regs *regs, int user_mode,
67:                                           uint64_t fault_addr, uint64_t fault_pc,
68:                                           const char *desc, uint64_t syndrome) {
69:  /* Fault context: locate per-CPU state via the MSR/MPIDR path, never via
70:   * the LAPIC-MMIO read (kernel/fault.h). */
71:  struct cpu_info *ci = arch_cpu_info_fault_safe();
72:  struct process *task = ci ? ci->current_task : NULL;
73:
74:  int uaccess = (!user_mode && ci && ci->uaccess_active &&
75:                 vmm_is_user_addr(fault_addr));
76:
77:  if ((user_mode || uaccess) && task) {
78:    /* User-attributable fault: the kernel itself is healthy.  fault_printf
79:     * is still used (not printk) because on the uaccess path we may hold
80:     * arch-side locks until the fixup below. */
81:    fault_printf("\n[FAULT] %s%s: PID %d (%s) pc=0x%016lx addr=0x%016lx cause=0x%016lx — terminating\n",
82:                 desc, uaccess ? " (uaccess)" : "", task->pid, task->name,
83:                 fault_pc, fault_addr, syndrome);
84:
85:    if (uaccess) {
86:      /* Release the arch uaccess critical section (locks/IRQ state/flag);
87:       * the address-space switch is reconciled by the scheduler below. */
88:      arch_uaccess_fault_fixup();
89:    }
90:
91:    fault_notify_user(task, desc); /* DIR-05 #139: red crash popup, best-effort */
92:    /* We are already in the fault handler for this task; there is no caller
93:     * left to propagate to.  Reported so a teardown that fails does not leave a
94:     * faulted process silently alive and schedulable. */
95:    if (process_terminate(task->pid) != 0)
96:      fault_printf("[FAULT] process_terminate(%d) FAILED after a user fault\n",
97:                   task->pid);
98:    fault_exit(); /* fault handled — unwind the recursion guard */
99:    return schedule(regs);
100:  }
101:
102:  /* A USER-attributable fault with no current task is not a kernel fault: it
103:   * means this CPU took an exception from user mode while its current_task was
104:   * NULL, i.e. the scheduler state is corrupt.  Naming it here, in the shared
105:   * decision, is what makes the two architectures agree: aarch64's EL0 vector
106:   * already panicked with that diagnosis while amd64 fell through and printed
107:   * "KERNEL PAGE FAULT", classifying the same condition as something else
108:   * entirely.  Each caller still dumps its own register set — those genuinely
109:   * differ — but the diagnosis no longer depends on which arch you are on. */
110:  if ((user_mode || uaccess) && !task)
111:    fault_printf("\n[FAULT] %s from user mode with NO CURRENT TASK on cpu %d — "
112:                 "scheduler-state corruption (pc=0x%016lx addr=0x%016lx "
113:                 "cause=0x%016lx)\n",
114:                 desc, ci ? (int)ci->cpu_id : -1, fault_pc, fault_addr,
115:                 syndrome);
116:
117:  return NULL; /* kernel fault: caller dumps registers and panics */
118:}
119:

@@@ kernel/core/hal_bus.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/core/hal_bus.c
3: * Hardware Abstraction Layer — Device Registry
4: *
5: * This file is the *thin* device registry half of the HAL: it maintains a
6: * fixed-size array of hal_device descriptors that arch-specific bus-scan code
7: * populates at boot.  The upper half of the HAL (register-accessor macros and
8: * their heuristic dispatch) lives in kernel/include/kernel/hal.h and is
9: * deliberately kept separate.
10: *
11: * Role / layering:
12: *   boot -> arch_bus_scan() (pci.c / platform MMIO) -> hal_register_device()
13: *        -> arch_virtio_scan() (virtio.c, queries registry)           -> drivers
14: *   Generic kernel code calls hal_device_find() / hal_device_get() to look up
15: *   devices by vendor:device pair; it never accesses hal_devices[] directly.
16: *
17: * Key invariants:
18: *   - hal_devices[] is a flat array; devices are never removed after registration.
19: *   - hal_device_count is only modified during boot, before SMP secondaries start;
20: *     no lock is taken here.  Do not call hal_register_device() after SMP init.
21: *   - MAX_HAL_DEVICES (64) is a hard limit; registration beyond it is silently
22: *     dropped with a pr_warn (see hal_register_device).
23: *
24: * Known issues:
25: *   HAL-02  (W2 BAD-IMPL) The broader HAL is spread over four headers
26: *           (hal.h, hal_unified.h, hal_device.h, hal_platform.h); this file
27: *           is the one piece the review explicitly calls "genuinely thin and
28: *           fine."  The defect is in the header layer, not here.
29: *   HAL-01  (W3 WRONG-DESIGN/PERF) hal_read32() in hal.h synthesises a
30: *           compound-literal hal_device_t and runs address-heuristic dispatch
31: *           on every MMIO access; not a defect in this file.
32: */
33:#include <kernel/hal.h>
34:#include <kernel/driver.h>
35:#include <kernel/string.h>
36:#include <kernel/printk.h>
37:#include <drivers/virtio.h>
38:
39:#define MAX_HAL_DEVICES 64
40:
41:/* hal_devices[]: flat boot-time registry of discovered hardware devices.
42: * Populated by arch_bus_scan() (PCI) and arch_virtio_scan(); immutable after
43: * SMP init.  Access without a lock is safe only during the single-threaded
44: * boot phase. */
45:static struct hal_device hal_devices[MAX_HAL_DEVICES];
46:/* hal_device_count: number of valid entries in hal_devices[].
47: * Monotonically increasing; never decremented. */
48:static int hal_device_count = 0;
49:
50:/*
51: * hal_bus_init - initialise the device registry and trigger bus discovery.
52: *
53: * Called once from the boot path (CPU 0, single-threaded) before any driver
54: * or SMP secondary starts.  Resets hal_device_count, then calls
55: * arch_bus_scan() to enumerate PCI/platform devices (each device calls
56: * hal_register_device()), followed by arch_virtio_scan() to probe VirtIO
57: * devices found on the bus.
58: *
59: * Locking: none — must be called before SMP is active.
60: * IRQ context: no — called from boot path with IRQs disabled.
61: */
62:void hal_bus_init(void) {
63:    hal_device_count = 0;
64:    pr_info("%s", "HAL: Initializing Bus Manager...\n");
65:    
66:    /* Architecture-specific bus discovery (PCI, Platform MMIO, etc) */
67:    arch_bus_scan();
68:
69:    /* Discover VirtIO devices based on found bus devices */
70:    arch_virtio_scan();
71:}
72:
73:/*
74: * hal_device_get_count - return the number of registered devices.
75: *
76: * Returns hal_device_count.  Safe to call after boot; no lock needed because
77: * hal_device_count is not modified after SMP init.
78: */
79:int hal_device_get_count(void) {
80:    return hal_device_count;
81:}
82:
83:/*
84: * hal_device_get - return a pointer to the device at position 'index'.
85: *
86: * Returns NULL if index is out of range [0, hal_device_count).
87: * The returned pointer is into the static hal_devices[] array; it is stable
88: * for the lifetime of the kernel.
89: */
90:struct hal_device *hal_device_get(int index) {
91:    if (index < 0 || index >= hal_device_count) return NULL;
92:    return &hal_devices[index];
93:}
94:
95:/*
96: * hal_device_find - find the Nth device matching a vendor:device pair.
97: *
98: * Scans hal_devices[] linearly and returns a pointer to the 'index'th
99: * (zero-based) entry whose vendor_id==vendor and device_id==device.
100: * Returns NULL if fewer than (index+1) matching devices exist.
101: *
102: * Used by driver probes (e.g. virtio_blk) to locate their PCI/MMIO device
103: * descriptor without knowing the slot number.
104: */
105:struct hal_device *hal_device_find(uint16_t vendor, uint16_t device, int index) {
106:    int found = 0;
107:    for (int i = 0; i < hal_device_count; i++) {
108:        if (hal_devices[i].vendor_id == vendor && hal_devices[i].device_id == device) {
109:            if (found == index) return &hal_devices[i];
110:            found++;
111:        }
112:    }
113:    return NULL;
114:}
115:
116:/*
117: * hal_device_find_class - find the Nth device matching a PCI class triplet.
118: *
119: * Each of class_code/subclass/prog_if may be DRV_ANY_CLASS (0xFF) to act as a
120: * wildcard on that field. Used by class-based driver probes (xHCI, AHCI, VGA)
121: * to locate their controller without a vendor:device list.
122: */
123:struct hal_device *hal_device_find_class(uint8_t class_code, uint8_t subclass,
124:                                         uint8_t prog_if, int index) {
125:    int found = 0;
126:    for (int i = 0; i < hal_device_count; i++) {
127:        struct hal_device *d = &hal_devices[i];
128:        if (class_code != DRV_ANY_CLASS && d->class_code != class_code) continue;
129:        if (subclass   != DRV_ANY_CLASS && d->subclass   != subclass)   continue;
130:        if (prog_if    != DRV_ANY_CLASS && d->prog_if    != prog_if)    continue;
131:        if (found == index) return d;
132:        found++;
133:    }
134:    return NULL;
135:}
136:
137:/* --- Driver-binding layer (kernel/driver.h) --- */
138:
139:/* driver_list: head of the registered-driver chain. Mutated only during
140: * single-threaded boot, like hal_devices[]; no lock taken. */
141:static struct device_driver *driver_list = NULL;
142:
143:static int driver_matches(const struct device_driver *drv,
144:                          const struct hal_device *dev) {
145:    /* ID match takes priority when the driver specifies a concrete vendor. */
146:    if (drv->vendor != DRV_ANY_ID) {
147:        if (dev->vendor_id != drv->vendor) return 0;
148:        if (drv->device != DRV_ANY_ID && dev->device_id != drv->device) return 0;
149:        return 1;
150:    }
151:    /* Otherwise fall back to class match (any field may be wildcard). */
152:    if (drv->class_code != DRV_ANY_CLASS && dev->class_code != drv->class_code) return 0;
153:    if (drv->subclass   != DRV_ANY_CLASS && dev->subclass   != drv->subclass)   return 0;
154:    if (drv->prog_if    != DRV_ANY_CLASS && dev->prog_if    != drv->prog_if)    return 0;
155:    /* A driver that wildcards everything would match all devices; require it to
156:     * pin at least one of class_code or vendor to avoid accidental capture. */
157:    if (drv->class_code == DRV_ANY_CLASS) return 0;
158:    return 1;
159:}
160:
161:void driver_register(struct device_driver *drv) {
162:    if (!drv) return;
163:    drv->next = driver_list;
164:    driver_list = drv;
165:}
166:
167:void driver_match_all(void) {
168:    for (int i = 0; i < hal_device_count; i++) {
169:        struct hal_device *dev = &hal_devices[i];
170:        if (dev->driver) continue; /* already bound */
171:        for (struct device_driver *drv = driver_list; drv; drv = drv->next) {
172:            if (!driver_matches(drv, dev)) continue;
173:            if (drv->probe && drv->probe(dev) == 0) {
174:                dev->driver = drv;
175:                pr_info("HAL: bound driver '%s' to device '%s'\n",
176:                        drv->name, dev->name);
177:                break; /* device claimed */
178:            }
179:        }
180:    }
181:}
182:
183:/*
184: * hal_register_device - add a device descriptor to the global registry.
185: *
186: * Called by arch_bus_scan() / arch_virtio_scan() for each discovered device.
187: * Copies *dev into hal_devices[hal_device_count] and increments the count.
188: * If the registry is full (>= MAX_HAL_DEVICES), emits pr_warn and returns
189: * without registering the device — the caller receives no error indication.
190: *
191: * Locking: none — must be called during single-threaded boot only.
192: * IRQ context: no.
193: *
194: * Side effects: updates hal_device_count; logs device details via pr_info.
195: */
196:/* API for architecture-specific code to register devices found during scan */
197:void hal_register_device(struct hal_device *dev) {
198:    if (hal_device_count >= MAX_HAL_DEVICES) {
199:        pr_warn("HAL: Maximum device count reached, skipping %s\n", dev->name);
200:        return;
201:    }
202:    
203:    hal_devices[hal_device_count] = *dev;
204:    pr_info("HAL: Registered device '%s' (Bus=%d, ID=%04x:%04x, Class=%02x:%02x:%02x, Base=0x%lx, IRQ=%u)\n",
205:            dev->name, dev->bus_type, dev->vendor_id, dev->device_id,
206:            dev->class_code, dev->subclass, dev->prog_if, dev->base, dev->irq);
207:    hal_device_count++;
208:}

@@@ kernel/core/object.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/core/object.c
3: * Kernel object manager + capability handle table — the REAL capability layer
4: * (ASTRA §6.1/6.2/6.5).  See kernel/include/kernel/object.h and
5: * include/api/object.h for the model.
6: *
7: * Invariants enforced here:
8: *   - Unforgeability: a handle is an index into the caller's PRIVATE table; a
9: *     value with no installed slot returns -EBADF.  A process can only act on
10: *     objects it was handed.
11: *   - Attenuation only: duplicate()/grant() compute new_rights &
12: * current_rights, so rights can never grow (no escalation), mirroring the
13: * caps.h spawn cut.
14: *   - Acquisition is ambient-gated: getting a write FILE capability still needs
15: *     CAP_FS_WRITE + the /bin,/sys ACL; getting a PROCESS capability needs the
16: *     same authority as kill (self/descendant/privileged).  Once held, the
17: *     handle is the only thing that matters.
18: *
19: * Locking: one global object_lock guards refcounts and slot install/close/grant
20: * (short, allocation-free critical sections).  Blocking VFS I/O runs OUTSIDE
21: * the lock via a pin (refcount++) / use / unpin pattern, so a concurrent
22: * close() cannot free an object mid-I/O.  Lock order object_lock ->
23: * kmalloc_lock is consistent (kmalloc/kfree never take object_lock), so kfree()
24: * under the lock cannot deadlock.
25: */
26:#include <kernel/cpu.h>
27:#include <kernel/graphics.h> /* OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW backends: compositor_* (§6.7) */
28:#include <kernel/kmalloc.h>
29:#include <kernel/nx_contract.h>
30:#include <kernel/object.h>
31:#include <kernel/printk.h>
32:#include <kernel/registry.h>
33:#include <kernel/sched.h>
34:#include <kernel/spinlock.h>
35:#include <kernel/string.h>
36:#include <kernel/types.h>
37:#include <kernel/vfs.h>
38:
39:/* Upper bound for a single object read/write bounce buffer (mirrors the
40: * dispatcher's SYSCALL_MAX_IO_BYTES so a user size argument cannot ask the
41: * kernel for an absurd allocation). */
42:#define OBJ_MAX_IO_BYTES (16u * 1024u * 1024u)
43:
44:extern int arch_copy_from_user(void *dest, const void *src, size_t n);
45:extern int arch_copy_to_user(void *dest, const void *src, size_t n);
46:extern int arch_copy_string_from_user(char *dest, const char *src,
47:                                      size_t max_len);
48:
49:/* Serialises refcount changes and handle-table slot mutations. */
50:static DEFINE_SPINLOCK(object_lock);
51:
52:/* Live-object instrumentation (perf brief §1/§2.6; surfaced via OS1_sys_stats).
53: * The capability layer is the newest, least-tested subsystem and the highest-
54: * leverage leak suspect: a missed decref on process teardown leaks the kobject
55: * even after the handle table is freed.  Every kobject is born in kobj_alloc()
56: * and dies in kobj_free(); routing all frees through one wrapper keeps the
57: * per-type live count exactly symmetric regardless of which free path runs
58: * (never-installed cleanup, handle_close, or process_handles_destroy).
59: * Relaxed atomics — independent of object_lock. */
60:static uint64_t obj_live_count[OBJ_TYPE_COUNT];
61:
62:/*
63: * struct kpipe - the payload of an OBJ_TYPE_PIPE kobject (ASTRA §6.2 anonymous
64: * byte pipe).  Heap-allocated and pointed to by kobject.pipe so the buffer +
65: * wait queue don't bloat every kobject.  `buf` is a ring of PIPE_BUF_SIZE
66: * bytes. `readers`/`writers` are OPEN-handle counts (maintained by
67: * pipe_handle_count at every handle lifecycle edge): a reader on an empty pipe
68: * blocks on `wq` until a writer publishes data (wake_up) or the LAST writer
69: * closes (writers==0 → EOF).
70: */
71:#define PIPE_BUF_SIZE 4096u
72:struct kpipe {
73:  uint8_t *buf;
74:  uint32_t head; /* next byte to read */
75:  uint32_t tail; /* next slot to write */
76:  uint32_t count;
77:  int readers;
78:  int writers;
79:  struct wait_queue_head rq; /* readers waiting for data / EOF */
80:  struct wait_queue_head wq; /* writers waiting for buffer space / EPIPE */
81:};
82:
83:/*
84: * struct kport - the payload of an OBJ_TYPE_PORT kobject: a Mach-style message
85: * MAILBOX that is itself a capability (ASTRA §6.5).  Heap-allocated like kpipe.
86: *
87: * The rights on a handle ARE the port rights: OS1_RIGHT_WRITE is the SEND right
88: * and OS1_RIGHT_READ the RECEIVE right.  A service acquires the port with READ
89: * (becoming its owner) and hands clients attenuated SEND-only handles, so a
90: * client names the SERVICE, never a pid — the seL4 rule ("no PID-by-number
91: * access without a capability") that ambient SYS_SEND violates.
92: *
93: * ASTRA §6.5 says the semantics "ride on the existing B3 IPC layer": we reuse
94: * struct ipc_message verbatim and only relocate the QUEUE (from a pid's mailbox
95: * to the port object) and the AUTHORITY (from process_ipc_allowed to the
96: * handle's rights).  `name` is the published identity clients resolve.
97: */
98:#define PORT_QUEUE_MAX 32
99:#define PORT_NAME_MAX 32
100:struct kport {
101:  struct ipc_message q[PORT_QUEUE_MAX];
102:  uint32_t head, tail, count;
103:  int senders;   /* open handles holding the SEND right    */
104:  int receivers; /* open handles holding the RECEIVE right */
105:  int owner_pid;
106:  char name[PORT_NAME_MAX];
107:  struct wait_queue_head rq; /* receivers waiting for a message  */
108:  struct wait_queue_head wq; /* senders waiting for queue space  */
109:};
110:
111:/* Named-port registry: the name→port map that lets a client acquire a send
112: * capability BY NAME.  Small and fixed: ports are system services, not a
113: * per-application resource.  Guarded by object_lock. */
114:#define PORT_TABLE_MAX 16
115:static struct kobject *port_table[PORT_TABLE_MAX];
116:
117:/* port_find_locked - resolve a published port name.  Caller holds object_lock.
118: */
119:static struct kobject *port_find_locked(const char *name) {
120:  for (int i = 0; i < PORT_TABLE_MAX; i++) {
121:    if (port_table[i] && port_table[i]->port &&
122:        strcmp(port_table[i]->port->name, name) == 0)
123:      return port_table[i];
124:  }
125:  return NULL;
126:}
127:
128:/* endpoint_handle_count - adjust a PIPE's or PORT's open endpoint counts by
129: * 'delta' for a handle carrying 'rights'.  Called (under object_lock) at EVERY
130: * handle lifecycle edge — install (+1), close/destroy/redirect-overwrite (-1) —
131: * so the counts exactly track live handles.  A no-op for other types, so
132: * callers need not special-case.  For a pipe, closing the last writer wakes
133: * blocked readers (EOF) and closing the last reader wakes blocked writers
134: * (EPIPE); a port behaves the same way, so a client blocked on a reply is
135: * released when the service dies instead of hanging forever. */
136:static void pipe_handle_count(struct kobject *o, uint32_t rights, int delta) {
137:  if (o && o->type == OBJ_TYPE_PORT && o->port) {
138:    if (rights & OS1_RIGHT_READ) {
139:      o->port->receivers += delta;
140:      if (delta < 0 && o->port->receivers == 0) {
141:        /* The service released its receive right: UNPUBLISH the name here,
142:         * under object_lock, so no new client can resolve a send capability to
143:         * a dead service.  Doing it at free time instead would race, because
144:         * kobj_free runs both inside and outside the lock. */
145:        for (int i = 0; i < PORT_TABLE_MAX; i++) {
146:          if (port_table[i] == o)
147:            port_table[i] = NULL;
148:        }
149:        wake_up(&o->port->wq); /* service gone → senders stop waiting */
150:      }
151:    }
152:    if (rights & OS1_RIGHT_WRITE) {
153:      o->port->senders += delta;
154:      if (delta < 0 && o->port->senders == 0)
155:        wake_up(&o->port->rq); /* last client gone → receiver wakes */
156:    }
157:    return;
158:  }
159:  if (!o || o->type != OBJ_TYPE_PIPE || !o->pipe)
160:    return;
161:  if (rights & OS1_RIGHT_READ) {
162:    o->pipe->readers += delta;
163:    if (delta < 0 && o->pipe->readers == 0)
164:      wake_up(&o->pipe->wq); /* last reader gone → writers get EPIPE */
165:  }
166:  if (rights & OS1_RIGHT_WRITE) {
167:    o->pipe->writers += delta;
168:    if (delta < 0 && o->pipe->writers == 0)
169:      wake_up(&o->pipe->rq); /* last writer gone → readers see EOF */
170:  }
171:}
172:
173:/* pipe still-block predicates for kthread_block (return 1 = keep sleeping).  A
174: * reader sleeps while the pipe is empty AND a writer still exists; a writer
175: * sleeps while the pipe is full AND a reader still exists.  Evaluated under the
176: * wait queue lock, serialised against the producer/consumer's wake_up(). */
177:static int pipe_readable_block(void *arg) {
178:  struct kpipe *kp = ((struct kobject *)arg)->pipe;
179:  return kp->count == 0 && kp->writers > 0;
180:}
181:static int pipe_writable_block(void *arg) {
182:  struct kpipe *kp = ((struct kobject *)arg)->pipe;
183:  return kp->count == PIPE_BUF_SIZE && kp->readers > 0;
184:}
185:/* Port equivalents: a receiver sleeps while the mailbox is empty AND a sender
186: * still exists; a sender sleeps while it is full AND a receiver still exists.
187: */
188:static int port_readable_block(void *arg) {
189:  struct kport *kp = ((struct kobject *)arg)->port;
190:  return kp->count == 0 && kp->senders > 0;
191:}
192:static int port_writable_block(void *arg) {
193:  struct kport *kp = ((struct kobject *)arg)->port;
194:  return kp->count == PORT_QUEUE_MAX && kp->receivers > 0;
195:}
196:
197:/* kobj_alloc - allocate a zeroed kobject of 'type'.  refcount starts at 0; the
198: * first handle_install_locked() that succeeds takes it to 1. */
199:static struct kobject *kobj_alloc(uint8_t type) {
200:  struct kobject *o = kmalloc(sizeof(struct kobject));
201:  if (!o)
202:    return NULL;
203:  memset(o, 0, sizeof(*o));
204:  o->type = type;
205:  o->refcount = 0;
206:  if (type < OBJ_TYPE_COUNT)
207:    __sync_fetch_and_add(&obj_live_count[type], 1);
208:  return o;
209:}
210:
211:/* kobj_free - the single free path for a kobject; keeps the live-object count
212: * symmetric with kobj_alloc().  Replaces every bare kfree() of a kobject. */
213:static void kobj_free(struct kobject *o) {
214:  if (!o)
215:    return;
216:  if (o->type < OBJ_TYPE_COUNT)
217:    __sync_fetch_and_sub(&obj_live_count[o->type], 1);
218:  if (o->type == OBJ_TYPE_PIPE && o->pipe) {
219:    kfree(o->pipe->buf);
220:    kfree(o->pipe);
221:  }
222:  if (o->type == OBJ_TYPE_PORT && o->port)
223:    kfree(o->port); /* already unpublished when its last receiver closed */
224:  kfree(o);
225:}
226:
227:/* object_get_live_counts - copy the per-type live-kobject counts (perf brief
228: * §1/§2.6).  'out' is filled for indices [0, min(max, OBJ_TYPE_COUNT)). */
229:void object_get_live_counts(uint64_t *out, int max) {
230:  if (!out)
231:    return;
232:  for (int i = 0; i < max && i < OBJ_TYPE_COUNT; i++)
233:    out[i] = obj_live_count[i];
234:}
235:
236:/* handles_ensure - lazily allocate the caller's (or a target's) handle table.
237: * NULL until a process first touches the object ABI, so processes that never
238: * use it pay nothing.  Allocation happens with the lock released; publication
239: * is double-checked under the lock. */
240:static int handles_ensure(struct process *p) {
241:  if (p->handles)
242:    return 0;
243:  struct handle_entry *tbl =
244:      kmalloc(sizeof(struct handle_entry) * NPROC_HANDLES);
245:  if (!tbl)
246:    return -ENOMEM;
247:  memset(tbl, 0, sizeof(struct handle_entry) * NPROC_HANDLES);
248:  uint64_t flags;
249:  spin_lock_irqsave(&object_lock, &flags);
250:  if (p->handles) {
251:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
252:    kfree(tbl);
253:    return 0;
254:  }
255:  p->handles = tbl;
256:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
257:  return 0;
258:}
259:
260:/* handle_install_locked - place a reference to 'o' in p's first free slot and
261: * bump the object refcount.  Caller MUST hold object_lock.  Returns the handle
262: * index, -EBADF if the table vanished (target died), or -EMFILE if full. */
263:static int handle_install_locked(struct process *p, struct kobject *o,
264:                                 uint32_t rights) {
265:  if (!p->handles)
266:    return -EBADF;
267:  for (int i = 0; i < NPROC_HANDLES; i++) {
268:    if (p->handles[i].obj == NULL) {
269:      p->handles[i].obj = o;
270:      p->handles[i].rights = rights;
271:      o->refcount++;
272:      pipe_handle_count(o, rights, +1); /* track a new pipe reader/writer */
273:      return i;
274:    }
275:  }
276:  return -EMFILE;
277:}
278:
279:/* obj_unref - drop one reference taken by a pin; free at zero. */
280:static void obj_unref(struct kobject *o) {
281:  struct kobject *to_free = NULL;
282:  uint64_t flags;
283:  spin_lock_irqsave(&object_lock, &flags);
284:  if (--o->refcount <= 0)
285:    to_free = o;
286:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
287:  if (to_free)
288:    kobj_free(to_free);
289:}
290:
291:/*
292: * sys_handle_create - OS1low_handle_create(ns, path, rights, type).
293: * Acquire a fresh capability (handle) to a named object.
294: */
295:long sys_handle_create(int ns, const char *upath, uint32_t rights, int type) {
296:  struct process *cur = current_process;
297:  if (!cur)
298:    return -EPERM;
299:  /* CREATE is acquisition-only (open(O_CREAT) semantics, FS namespace):
300:   * capture it, then strip it via the OS1_RIGHT_ALL mask so it never lands
301:   * in the installed handle's rights (cannot be duplicated/granted). */
302:  int want_create = (rights & OS1_RIGHT_CREATE) != 0;
303:  rights &= OS1_RIGHT_ALL;
304:
305:  char kpath[OBJ_FILE_PATH_MAX];
306:  if (arch_copy_string_from_user(kpath, upath, OBJ_FILE_PATH_MAX) != 0)
307:    return -EFAULT;
308:
309:  if (handles_ensure(cur) != 0)
310:    return -ENOMEM;
311:
312:  if (ns == OS1_NS_FS) {
313:    /* open() ≡ handle_create(OS1_NS_FS): the PATH'S PROVIDER decides the object
314:     * TYPE (FILE for ext4/regfs, PROCESS for /proc/<pid>, …) — the namespace IS
315:     * the object space.  The 'type' argument is only a hint; the resolution is
316:     * the single source of truth. */
317:    (void)type;
318:    char resolved[OBJ_FILE_PATH_MAX];
319:    vfs_resolve_path(kpath, resolved, OBJ_FILE_PATH_MAX);
320:    struct vfs_objref ref;
321:    memset(&ref, 0, sizeof(ref));
322:    int rr = vfs_resolve_object(resolved, &ref);
323:    if (rr == -2) {
324:      /*
325:       * A DIRECTORY IS A FILE YOU READ (ASTRA §6.3, Programme R1).
326:       *
327:       * vfs_resolve_object reports -2 for a directory but has already filled
328:       * `ref` (OBJ_TYPE_FILE + the dir node), so everything needed is here —
329:       * acquisition simply used to refuse.  A READ-only handle is now allowed,
330:       * which is what makes sys_object_read's VFS_TYPE_DIR branch reachable and
331:       * lets OS1_fs_list() be handle_create + object_read + close instead of a
332:       * private ambient verb.
333:       *
334:       * WRITE stays -EISDIR: writing a directory as a byte stream is not an
335:       * operation the VFS has, and silently accepting the handle would move the
336:       * failure to the first write.  Directory MUTATION (create/remove a node)
337:       * needs its own verb — tracked as R1b, still open.
338:       *
339:       * Found by the maintainer: `ls` broke with "cannot list ." because the
340:       * listing path could not acquire the handle at all.  The dir-read code
341:       * was unreachable until this gate opened.
342:       */
343:      if (rights & (OS1_RIGHT_WRITE | OS1_RIGHT_CREATE))
344:        return -EISDIR;
345:      rr = 0;
346:    }
347:    if (rr != 0) {
348:      /* O_CREAT semantics (ASTRA §6.8: open(O_CREAT) → handle_create): a
349:       * missing path with CREATE+WRITE is created as an empty FILE through
350:       * the provider, behind the SAME vfs_write_allowed seam every other
351:       * write-class modification uses (S-ALIGN F6).  CREATE without WRITE
352:       * is meaningless and stays -ENOENT. */
353:      if (!want_create || !(rights & OS1_RIGHT_WRITE))
354:        return -ENOENT;
355:      long cperm = vfs_write_allowed(resolved);
356:      if (cperm != 0)
357:        return cperm;
358:      if (vfs_create(resolved, VFS_TYPE_FILE) != 0)
359:        return -EIO;
360:      rr = vfs_resolve_object(resolved, &ref);
361:      if (rr != 0)
362:        return -ENOENT;
363:    }
364:
365:    struct kobject *o;
366:    if (ref.obj_type == OBJ_TYPE_FILE) {
367:      /* Ambient gate to ACQUIRE a write capability — the SAME
368:       * vfs_write_allowed() seam used by every write-capability acquisition
369:       * (S-ALIGN F6).
370:       * Use of an already-held handle is rights-only (seL4/Mach delegation). */
371:      if (rights & OS1_RIGHT_WRITE) {
372:        long wperm = vfs_write_allowed(resolved);
373:        if (wperm != 0)
374:          return wperm;
375:      }
376:      /* Namespace mutation is distinct from writing a directory as a byte
377:       * stream. WRITE on a directory remains -EISDIR above; MUTATE is a
378:       * capability to this directory's children, acquired through the same
379:       * VFS ACL and then delegable like every other object right. */
380:      if (rights & OS1_RIGHT_MUTATE) {
381:        if (ref.node.type != VFS_TYPE_DIR)
382:          return -ENOTDIR;
383:        long mperm = vfs_write_allowed(resolved);
384:        if (mperm != 0)
385:          return mperm;
386:      }
387:      o = kobj_alloc(OBJ_TYPE_FILE);
388:      if (!o)
389:        return -ENOMEM;
390:      o->node = ref.node;
391:      o->offset = 0;
392:      strncpy(o->path, resolved, OBJ_FILE_PATH_MAX - 1);
393:      o->path[OBJ_FILE_PATH_MAX - 1] = '\0';
394:    } else if (ref.obj_type == OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS) {
395:      /* Same acquisition gate as OS1_NS_PROC: a destructive handle (kill /
396:       * IPC-send) needs kill authority; a READ/WAIT status handle only needs
397:       * the process to exist (object_at already verified it). */
398:      if ((rights & (OS1_RIGHT_DESTROY | OS1_RIGHT_WRITE)) &&
399:          !process_kill_allowed(cur, ref.pid))
400:        return -EPERM;
401:      o = kobj_alloc(OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS);
402:      if (!o)
403:        return -ENOMEM;
404:      o->pid = ref.pid;
405:    } else {
406:      return -EINVAL; /* namespace path resolved to an unsupported type */
407:    }
408:
409:    uint64_t flags;
410:    spin_lock_irqsave(&object_lock, &flags);
411:    int h = handle_install_locked(cur, o, rights);
412:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
413:    if (h < 0) {
414:      kobj_free(o); /* never installed: refcount stayed 0 */
415:      return h;
416:    }
417:    return h;
418:  }
419:
420:  /*
421:   * OS1_NS_PORT — acquire a capability to a NAMED service port (ASTRA §6.5).
422:   * This is the verb that lets a client address a SERVICE instead of a pid.
423:   *
424:   * Acquisition policy:
