425:   *   - asking for the RECEIVE right (OS1_RIGHT_READ) PUBLISHES the port and
426:   *     makes the caller its owner — that is how a service announces itself.
427:   *     A second receiver for an existing name is refused (-EADDRINUSE-ish
428:   *     -EEXIST): one mailbox, one service, so a rogue process cannot steal a
429:   *     service's identity by racing it.
430:   *   - asking without READ yields a SEND-only capability to an EXISTING port;
431:   *     possession is thereafter the authority (no ambient pid check).
432:   */
433:  if (ns == OS1_NS_PORT) {
434:    (void)type;
435:    if (handles_ensure(cur) != 0)
436:      return -ENOMEM;
437:    int want_recv = (rights & OS1_RIGHT_READ) != 0;
438:
439:    uint64_t pflags;
440:    spin_lock_irqsave(&object_lock, &pflags);
441:    struct kobject *existing = port_find_locked(kpath);
442:    if (!want_recv) {
443:      if (!existing) {
444:        spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, pflags);
445:        return -ENOENT; /* no such service published */
446:      }
447:      int h = handle_install_locked(cur, existing, rights & ~OS1_RIGHT_READ);
448:      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, pflags);
449:      return h;
450:    }
451:    if (existing) {
452:      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, pflags);
453:      return -EEXIST; /* a service already owns this name */
454:    }
455:    int slot = -1;
456:    for (int i = 0; i < PORT_TABLE_MAX; i++) {
457:      if (!port_table[i]) {
458:        slot = i;
459:        break;
460:      }
461:    }
462:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, pflags);
463:    if (slot < 0)
464:      return -ENOSPC; /* port table full */
465:
466:    /* Allocate with the lock released (kmalloc), then publish under it. */
467:    struct kport *kp = kmalloc(sizeof(struct kport));
468:    if (!kp)
469:      return -ENOMEM;
470:    memset(kp, 0, sizeof(*kp));
471:    kp->owner_pid = (int)cur->pid;
472:    snprintf(kp->name, PORT_NAME_MAX, "%s", kpath);
473:    INIT_LIST_HEAD(&kp->rq.task_list);
474:    spin_lock_init(&kp->rq.lock);
475:    INIT_LIST_HEAD(&kp->wq.task_list);
476:    spin_lock_init(&kp->wq.lock);
477:
478:    struct kobject *o = kobj_alloc(OBJ_TYPE_PORT);
479:    if (!o) {
480:      kfree(kp);
481:      return -ENOMEM;
482:    }
483:    o->port = kp;
484:    o->pid = (int)cur->pid;
485:
486:    spin_lock_irqsave(&object_lock, &pflags);
487:    if (port_find_locked(kpath)) { /* lost a publish race */
488:      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, pflags);
489:      kobj_free(o); /* never installed: refcount still 0 */
490:      return -EEXIST;
491:    }
492:    int h = handle_install_locked(cur, o, rights);
493:    if (h >= 0)
494:      port_table[slot] = o;
495:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, pflags);
496:    if (h < 0)
497:      kobj_free(o);
498:    return h;
499:  }
500:
501:  if (ns == OS1_NS_PROC && type == OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS) {
502:    int pid = atoi(kpath); /* libkernel parser (kernel/lib/string.c) */
503:    if (pid <= 0)
504:      return -EINVAL;
505:    /* Acquisition policy (seL4 separable rights, F4 M4.5): a DESTRUCTIVE handle
506:     * — one that can kill (DESTROY) or IPC-send (WRITE) — still needs kill
507:     * authority. A non-destructive WAIT/READ-only handle (status query, the
508:     * OS1_object_wait path behind OS1low_process_wait) only needs the process
509:     * to exist, matching the permissive ambient SYS_WAIT.  This separates
510:     * wait-right from kill-right without widening kill/send acquisition. */
511:    int destructive = (rights & (OS1_RIGHT_DESTROY | OS1_RIGHT_WRITE)) != 0;
512:    if (destructive && !process_kill_allowed(cur, pid))
513:      return -EPERM;
514:    if (!process_find_by_pid(pid))
515:      return -ESRCH;
516:
517:    struct kobject *o = kobj_alloc(OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS);
518:    if (!o)
519:      return -ENOMEM;
520:    o->pid = pid;
521:
522:    uint64_t flags;
523:    spin_lock_irqsave(&object_lock, &flags);
524:    int h = handle_install_locked(cur, o, rights);
525:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
526:    if (h < 0) {
527:      kobj_free(o); /* never installed: refcount stayed 0 */
528:      return h;
529:    }
530:    return h;
531:  }
532:
533:  if (ns == OS1_NS_REG && type == OBJ_TYPE_REGKEY) {
534:    /* A registry key is a capability too (ASTRA §6.6: every node has an
535:     * associated capability).  A WRITE handle needs CAP_REG_WRITE to acquire —
536:     * the SAME registry_write_allowed() seam sys_registry and regfs check, so
537:     * the three entry points cannot drift (S-ALIGN F5); reads are open.  The
538:     * key is stored in the kobject's path field, capped at the registry key
539:     * length so create/get/set all agree on the same string. */
540:    /* R2: a VIRTUAL per-process key (sys.proc.<pid>.env.*) is exempt from
541:     * CAP_REG_WRITE — writing your own environment is ordinary unprivileged
542:     * work, and proc_env_set enforces the real rule (self always, others only
543:     * if privileged).  sys_registry already worked this way; this door demanded
544:     * the machine-reconfiguration capability for a setenv, so the same
545:     * operation succeeded or failed depending on which entry point was used. */
546:    if ((rights & OS1_RIGHT_WRITE) && !registry_key_is_virtual(kpath) &&
547:        !registry_write_allowed())
548:      return -EPERM;
549:    if (kpath[0] == '\0')
550:      return -EINVAL;
551:    struct kobject *o = kobj_alloc(OBJ_TYPE_REGKEY);
552:    if (!o)
553:      return -ENOMEM;
554:    strncpy(o->path, kpath, MAX_KEY_LEN - 1);
555:    o->path[MAX_KEY_LEN - 1] = '\0';
556:
557:    uint64_t flags;
558:    spin_lock_irqsave(&object_lock, &flags);
559:    int h = handle_install_locked(cur, o, rights);
560:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
561:    if (h < 0) {
562:      kobj_free(o); /* never installed: refcount stayed 0 */
563:      return h;
564:    }
565:    return h;
566:  }
567:
568:  if (ns == OS1_NS_WIN && type == OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW) {
569:    /* A compositor window is a capability object (ASTRA §6.7).  Acquisition is
570:     * ambient-gated like the other types: a handle to YOUR OWN window is free;
571:     * a WRITE/DESTROY handle to ANOTHER process's window is window-manager
572:     * authority (machine/root only) — that is how /sys/bin/nxui (the dock) can
573:     * minimize/restore/focus/close any app.  READ stays open (inspect).  Once
574:     * held, the handle's rights are the only authority that matters. */
575:    int wid = atoi(kpath);
576:    if (wid <= 0)
577:      return -EINVAL;
578:    int owner = compositor_window_owner(wid);
579:    if (owner < 0)
580:      return -ESRCH;
581:    if (owner != (int)cur->pid &&
582:        (rights & (OS1_RIGHT_WRITE | OS1_RIGHT_DESTROY)) &&
583:        !proc_is_machine(cur) && cur->level > PLVL_ROOT)
584:      return -EPERM;
585:
586:    struct kobject *o = kobj_alloc(OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW);
587:    if (!o)
588:      return -ENOMEM;
589:    o->window_id = wid;
590:    o->pid = owner;
591:
592:    uint64_t flags;
593:    spin_lock_irqsave(&object_lock, &flags);
594:    int h = handle_install_locked(cur, o, rights);
595:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
596:    if (h < 0) {
597:      kobj_free(o); /* never installed: refcount stayed 0 */
598:      return h;
599:    }
600:    return h;
601:  }
602:
603:  return -EINVAL;
604:}
605:
606:/*
607: * sys_handle_dup - OS1low_handle_duplicate(handle, new_rights).
608: * A second handle to the SAME object, with rights attenuated to a subset of the
609: * source's.  Needs OS1_RIGHT_DUPLICATE on the source.
610: */
611:long sys_handle_dup(int handle, uint32_t new_rights) {
612:  struct process *cur = current_process;
613:  if (!cur || !cur->handles || handle < 0 || handle >= NPROC_HANDLES)
614:    return -EBADF;
615:  new_rights &= OS1_RIGHT_ALL;
616:
617:  uint64_t flags;
618:  spin_lock_irqsave(&object_lock, &flags);
619:  struct handle_entry *src = &cur->handles[handle];
620:  if (!src->obj) {
621:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
622:    return -EBADF;
623:  }
624:  if (!(src->rights & OS1_RIGHT_DUPLICATE)) {
625:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
626:    return -EPERM;
627:  }
628:  uint32_t rights = new_rights & src->rights; /* attenuation only */
629:  int h = handle_install_locked(cur, src->obj, rights);
630:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
631:  return h;
632:}
633:
634:/*
635: * sys_handle_close - OS1low_handle_close(handle).  Drop this handle; free the
636: * object if it was the last reference.
637: */
638:long sys_handle_close(int handle) {
639:  struct process *cur = current_process;
640:  if (!cur || !cur->handles || handle < 0 || handle >= NPROC_HANDLES)
641:    return -EBADF;
642:
643:  struct kobject *to_free = NULL;
644:  uint64_t flags;
645:  spin_lock_irqsave(&object_lock, &flags);
646:  struct handle_entry *e = &cur->handles[handle];
647:  if (!e->obj) {
648:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
649:    return -EBADF;
650:  }
651:  struct kobject *o = e->obj;
652:  pipe_handle_count(o, e->rights, -1); /* untrack this pipe reader/writer */
653:  e->obj = NULL;
654:  e->rights = 0;
655:  if (--o->refcount <= 0)
656:    to_free = o;
657:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
658:  if (to_free)
659:    kobj_free(to_free);
660:  return 0;
661:}
662:
663:/*
664: * sys_cap_query - OS1low_cap_query(handle).  Return (type<<24)|rights for an
665: * installed handle, else -EBADF.  The unforgeability probe in tests.
666: */
667:long sys_cap_query(int handle) {
668:  struct process *cur = current_process;
669:  if (!cur || !cur->handles || handle < 0 || handle >= NPROC_HANDLES)
670:    return -EBADF;
671:  uint64_t flags;
672:  spin_lock_irqsave(&object_lock, &flags);
673:  struct handle_entry *e = &cur->handles[handle];
674:  if (!e->obj) {
675:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
676:    return -EBADF;
677:  }
678:  long packed = OS1_CAPQ_PACK(e->obj->type, e->rights);
679:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
680:  return packed;
681:}
682:
683:/*
684: * sys_cap_grant - OS1low_cap_grant(target_pid, handle, rights).  Delegate a
685: * capability: install an attenuated handle to the SAME object in target_pid's
686: * table (true sharing — seL4 grant).  Needs OS1_RIGHT_TRANSFER on the source
687: * and IPC authority to the target.  Returns the handle index installed in the
688: * TARGET (the grantor relays it to the target, e.g. over IPC).
689: *
690: * OBJ-GRANT-REAP (RESOLVED 2026-07-23, was: "granting to a process being reaped
691: * on another CPU is unsupported"): it is supported now.  The whole grant runs
692: * under sched_lock, which pins the target in the process pool — a concurrent
693: * reap cannot remove and free it mid-install (PROC-REF-01).  Lock order is
694: * sched_lock -> object_lock; the source handle belongs to current_process,
695: * which cannot be reaped underneath its own syscall.
696: */
697:long sys_cap_grant(int target_pid, int handle, uint32_t rights) {
698:  struct process *cur = current_process;
699:  if (!cur || !cur->handles || handle < 0 || handle >= NPROC_HANDLES)
700:    return -EBADF;
701:  rights &= OS1_RIGHT_ALL;
702:
703:  if (!process_ipc_allowed(cur, target_pid))
704:    return -EPERM;
705:
706:  uint64_t sflags;
707:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &sflags);
708:  struct process *tgt = __process_find_by_pid(target_pid);
709:  int h;
710:  if (!tgt) {
711:    h = -ESRCH;
712:  } else if (!tgt->handles) {
713:    /* No table and none can be made here: handles_ensure would kmalloc, which
714:     * must not happen under sched_lock.  Every real IPC target already has one
715:     * (it took a handle to be addressable); a kernel thread that never did is
716:     * simply not a grant target. */
717:    h = -ENOMEM;
718:  } else {
719:    spin_lock(&object_lock);
720:    struct handle_entry *src = &cur->handles[handle];
721:    if (!src->obj)
722:      h = -EBADF;
723:    else if (!(src->rights & OS1_RIGHT_TRANSFER))
724:      h = -EPERM;
725:    else
726:      h = handle_install_locked(tgt, src->obj, rights & src->rights);
727:    spin_unlock(&object_lock);
728:  }
729:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, sflags);
730:  return h;
731:}
732:
733:/*
734: * sys_pipe - OS1low_pipe(int fds[2]).  Create an anonymous byte pipe (ASTRA
735: * §6.2 OBJ_TYPE_PIPE) and install BOTH ends in the caller's handle table:
736: * fds[0] is the READ end, fds[1] the WRITE end (POSIX pipe() order).  One
737: * kobject, two handles (rights = READ / WRITE); reader/writer counts start at
738: * 1/1 via the install path.  Returns 0, or -ENOMEM/-EMFILE/-EFAULT.
739: */
740:long sys_pipe(int *ufds) {
741:  struct process *cur = current_process;
742:  if (!cur)
743:    return -EPERM;
744:  if (handles_ensure(cur) != 0)
745:    return -ENOMEM;
746:
747:  struct kpipe *kp = kmalloc(sizeof(struct kpipe));
748:  if (!kp)
749:    return -ENOMEM;
750:  memset(kp, 0, sizeof(*kp));
751:  kp->buf = kmalloc(PIPE_BUF_SIZE);
752:  if (!kp->buf) {
753:    kfree(kp);
754:    return -ENOMEM;
755:  }
756:  INIT_LIST_HEAD(&kp->rq.task_list);
757:  spin_lock_init(&kp->rq.lock);
758:  INIT_LIST_HEAD(&kp->wq.task_list);
759:  spin_lock_init(&kp->wq.lock);
760:
761:  struct kobject *o = kobj_alloc(OBJ_TYPE_PIPE);
762:  if (!o) {
763:    kfree(kp->buf);
764:    kfree(kp);
765:    return -ENOMEM;
766:  }
767:  o->pipe = kp;
768:
769:  /* Both ends carry TRANSFER and DUPLICATE alongside their direction right.
770:   * Without TRANSFER a pipe end cannot be handed to another process at all
771:   * (sys_cap_grant requires it), which would make a pipe usable only INSIDE the
772:   * creating process — defeating its whole purpose as an IPC channel and, in
773:   * particular, breaking the out-of-line request transfer the execution service
774:   * depends on.  Note this does NOT widen access to the pipe itself: the
775:   * direction right is still what gates read vs write, and a grant can only
776:   * attenuate. */
777:  uint64_t flags;
778:  spin_lock_irqsave(&object_lock, &flags);
779:  int rfd = handle_install_locked(
780:      cur, o, OS1_RIGHT_READ | OS1_RIGHT_TRANSFER | OS1_RIGHT_DUPLICATE);
781:  int wfd = (rfd >= 0)
782:                ? handle_install_locked(cur, o,
783:                                        OS1_RIGHT_WRITE | OS1_RIGHT_TRANSFER |
784:                                            OS1_RIGHT_DUPLICATE)
785:                : rfd;
786:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
787:
788:  if (rfd < 0 || wfd < 0) {
789:    if (rfd >= 0)
790:      NX_DISCARD(
791:          sys_handle_close(rfd),
792:          "error unwind: the pipe creation already failed, and a failing "
793:          "close changes nothing the caller can act on");
794:    else
795:      kobj_free(o); /* never installed: refcount 0, free the whole pipe */
796:    return (rfd < 0) ? rfd : wfd;
797:  }
798:
799:  int fds[2] = {rfd, wfd};
800:  if (arch_copy_to_user(ufds, fds, sizeof(fds)) != 0) {
801:    NX_DISCARD(sys_handle_close(rfd), "unwinding a failed copy_to_user");
802:    NX_DISCARD(sys_handle_close(wfd), "unwinding a failed copy_to_user");
803:    return -EFAULT;
804:  }
805:  return 0;
806:}
807:
808:/* pin_handle - look up a handle, check required rights, and pin the object
809: * (refcount++) so blocking I/O can run with the lock released.  Returns the
810: * pinned object (caller must obj_unref) or NULL with *err set. */
811:static struct kobject *pin_handle(int handle, uint32_t need, long *err) {
812:  struct process *cur = current_process;
813:  if (!cur || !cur->handles || handle < 0 || handle >= NPROC_HANDLES) {
814:    *err = -EBADF;
815:    return NULL;
816:  }
817:  uint64_t flags;
818:  spin_lock_irqsave(&object_lock, &flags);
819:  struct handle_entry *e = &cur->handles[handle];
820:  if (!e->obj) {
821:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
822:    *err = -EBADF;
823:    return NULL;
824:  }
825:  if ((e->rights & need) != need) {
826:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
827:    *err = -EPERM;
828:    return NULL;
829:  }
830:  struct kobject *o = e->obj;
831:  o->refcount++; /* pin */
832:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
833:  return o;
834:}
835:
836:/*
837: * sys_port_send_caps - send a message through a PORT, TRANSFERRING capabilities
838: * with it (ASTRA §6.5, Mach: "ports are first-class objects ... a port is
839: * itself a capability", and a Mach message carries port RIGHTS).
840: *
841: * Why this verb has to exist: a handle index is meaningful only inside ONE
842: * process's table, so a client that merely names its fds in a message is
843: * describing slots the service cannot resolve.  The alternative — cap_grant
844: * first — is addressed BY PID, which would drag pid-addressing straight back
845: * into the one path that exists to remove it (you would need the service's pid
846: * to talk to a service you found by NAME).  Transferring the rights along the
847: * message keeps discovery and delegation both capability-based.
848: *
849: * The kernel installs each handle into the RECEIVER (the port's owner) and
850: * rewrites the leading int slots of the message payload with the indices as the
851: * receiver sees them, so the service reads valid handles with no translation
852: * step of its own.  Attenuation only: the transferred rights are the sender's.
853: */
854:long sys_port_send_caps(int handle, const void *umsg, const int *ufds,
855:                        int nfds) {
856:  if (nfds < 0 || nfds > 4)
857:    return -EINVAL; /* payload space for the rewritten indices */
858:  long err = 0;
859:  struct kobject *o = pin_handle(handle, OS1_RIGHT_WRITE, &err);
860:  if (!o)
861:    return err;
862:
863:  long ret;
864:  struct kport *kp = o->port;
865:  struct ipc_message m;
866:  int fds[4];
867:  if (o->type != OBJ_TYPE_PORT || !kp) {
868:    ret = -EINVAL;
869:  } else if (arch_copy_from_user(&m, umsg, sizeof(m)) != 0 ||
870:             (nfds > 0 && arch_copy_from_user(
871:                              fds, ufds, (size_t)nfds * sizeof(int)) != 0)) {
872:    ret = -EFAULT;
873:  } else {
874:    /* PROC-REF-01: hold sched_lock across the receiver lookup AND the whole
875:     * handle install, so the service cannot be reaped and freed out from under
876:     * us between finding it and writing into its table.  process_find_by_pid()
877:     * would return a pointer valid only for the instant it held the lock.  Lock
878:     * order sched_lock -> object_lock; the receiver's table is NOT allocated
879:     * here (kmalloc under sched_lock is forbidden) — a real port owner always
880:     * has one, having taken a handle to publish the port. */
881:    uint64_t sflags;
882:    spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &sflags);
883:    struct process *rcv = __process_find_by_pid(kp->owner_pid);
884:    if (!rcv) {
885:      ret = -ESRCH;
886:      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, sflags);
887:    } else if (!rcv->handles) {
888:      ret = -ENOMEM;
889:      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, sflags);
890:    } else {
891:      int installed[4];
892:      int n_ok = 0;
893:      struct kobject *to_free = NULL;
894:      ret = 0;
895:      spin_lock(&object_lock); /* nested under sched_lock; IRQs already off */
896:      for (int i = 0; i < nfds; i++) {
897:        if (fds[i] < 0 || fds[i] >= NPROC_HANDLES || !current_process ||
898:            !current_process->handles ||
899:            !current_process->handles[fds[i]].obj) {
900:          ret = -EBADF;
901:          break;
902:        }
903:        struct handle_entry *src = &current_process->handles[fds[i]];
904:        int h = handle_install_locked(rcv, src->obj, src->rights);
905:        if (h < 0) {
906:          ret = h;
907:          break;
908:        }
909:        installed[n_ok++] = h;
910:      }
911:      /* Only try to enqueue if every handle installed.  The enqueue can STILL
912:       * fail (receiver gone, queue full) AFTER the handles are in the
913:       * receiver's table — and those failures must unwind the install too.
914:       *
915:       * PORTCAP-01 (found 2026-07-23, audit programme A): the rollback used to
916:       * cover ONLY the install loop.  On -EPIPE / -EAGAIN the transferred
917:       * handles were left installed, so:
918:       *   - a receiver that died between the install and the enqueue kept
919:       *     capabilities for a message it never got (a leak that also touches
920:       *     PROC-REF-01: rcv may be freeing right now);
921:       *   - worse, -EAGAIN is the RETRYABLE path (PORT_QUEUE_MAX full), and the
922:       *     client retries the whole send — so a peer that merely keeps a
923:       *     service's port queue full makes every retry leak a fresh set of
924:       *     handles into the service's table until it hits NPROC_HANDLES.  A
925:       *     capability-table exhaustion DoS from an unprivileged sender.
926:       * The unwind is now driven by `ret < 0` regardless of WHERE it was set.
927:       */
928:      if (ret == 0) {
929:        /* Publish the receiver-side indices in the payload, then enqueue. */
930:        for (int i = 0; i < nfds; i++)
931:          memcpy(m.payload + (size_t)i * sizeof(int), &installed[i],
932:                 sizeof(int));
933:        m.from = current_process ? (int)current_process->pid : 0;
934:        if (kp->receivers == 0) {
935:          ret = -EPIPE;
936:        } else if (kp->count >= PORT_QUEUE_MAX) {
937:          ret = -EAGAIN; /* caller retries; blocking here would hold the lock */
938:        } else {
939:          kp->q[kp->tail] = m;
940:          kp->tail = (kp->tail + 1) % PORT_QUEUE_MAX;
941:          kp->count++;
942:          ret = (long)sizeof(m);
943:        }
944:      }
945:      if (ret < 0) {
946:        /* Any failure after (or during) install unwinds every handle that made
947:         * it in — leaving half the rights installed hands the service
948:         * capabilities for a request it will never see.
949:         *
950:         * The unwind DROPS the reference but never frees here: kobj_free()
951:         * kfree()s, and we hold sched_lock, which would create the
952:         * sched_lock -> kmalloc_lock order process.c says nothing establishes
953:         * (the same order that deadlocked dispatch_spawn against an idle core).
954:         * A last reference is handed to `to_free` and released after both locks
955:         * are dropped; at most one object can reach zero per unwind, because
956:         * each installed slot holds exactly one reference. */
957:        for (int i = 0; i < n_ok; i++) {
958:          struct handle_entry *e = &rcv->handles[installed[i]];
959:          pipe_handle_count(e->obj, e->rights, -1);
960:          if (--e->obj->refcount <= 0)
961:            to_free = e->obj;
962:          e->obj = NULL;
963:          e->rights = 0;
964:        }
965:      }
966:      spin_unlock(&object_lock);
967:      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, sflags);
968:      if (to_free)
969:        kobj_free(to_free); /* frees (kfree) — never under sched_lock */
970:      if (ret > 0)
971:        wake_up(&kp->rq); /* outside both locks: wake_up touches runqueues */
972:    }
973:  }
974:  obj_unref(o);
975:  return ret;
976:}
977:
978:/*
979: * sys_object_read - OS1_object_read(handle, buf, n).  Needs OS1_RIGHT_READ.
980: * FILE: VFS read at the object's offset (shared across handles to it).
981: */
982:long sys_object_read(int handle, void *ubuf, size_t n) {
983:  if (n > OBJ_MAX_IO_BYTES)
984:    return -EINVAL;
985:  long err = 0;
986:  struct kobject *o = pin_handle(handle, OS1_RIGHT_READ, &err);
987:  if (!o)
988:    return err;
989:
990:  long ret;
991:  if (o->type == OBJ_TYPE_FILE) {
992:    if (n == 0) {
993:      ret = 0;
994:    } else {
995:      uint8_t *kb = kmalloc(n);
996:      if (!kb) {
997:        ret = -ENOMEM;
998:      } else {
999:        /* A2 (capability read/write symmetry): re-sync the cached node from the
1000:         * handle's path before reading, exactly as sys_object_write refreshes
1001:         * it after writing.  Without this a long-lived READ handle keeps the
1002:         * size it saw at handle_create and never sees data a later writer
1003:         * appended.  The path is the handle's stable identity; the node is a
1004:         * cache.  Best-effort: if the path vanished, fall back to the cached
1005:         * node (an open handle to a since-deleted file still reads what it last
1006:         * resolved). */
1007:        NX_DISCARD(vfs_open(o->path, &o->node),
1008:                   "best-effort refresh: on failure the CACHED node is the "
1009:                   "documented fallback, so an open handle to a since-deleted "
1010:                   "file still reads what it last resolved");
1011:        int got;
1012:        if (o->node.type == VFS_TYPE_DIR) {
1013:          /*
1014:           * A DIRECTORY IS A FILE YOU READ (ASTRA §6.3, Programme R1).
1015:           *
1016:           * Reading a directory handle yields its listing, which is the Plan 9
1017:           * rule the whole namespace model rests on — and it is what lets
1018:           * OS1_fs_list() be handle_create + object_read + close instead of a
1019:           * private ambient verb (SYS_LIST_DIR) reaching into the VFS beside
1020:           * the object layer.
1021:           *
1022:           * The listing is produced WHOLE, and the offset is treated as a byte
1023:           * cursor into it: vfs_list_dir has no incremental form, so a partial
1024:           * read cannot be resumed mid-directory without re-listing.  That is
1025:           * why the cursor advances by what was handed out — a second read
1026:           * returns the tail, and a read past the end returns 0 (EOF), which is
1027:           * the behaviour any reader loop already expects from a file.
1028:           */
1029:          /* Scratch is sized from the CALLER's request plus the cursor, not
1030:           * from OBJ_MAX_IO_BYTES.  The first version allocated the 16 MiB
1031:           * ceiling on every single listing — the old ambient verb allocated
1032:           * exactly what the caller asked for, and a per-`ls` 16 MiB kmalloc is
1033:           * a performance defect, not a safety margin.  A listing longer than
1034:           * (offset + n) is simply truncated at the cursor window, which is the
1035:           * same thing a short read does on any file. */
1036:          size_t want = (size_t)o->offset + n;
1037:          if (want > OBJ_MAX_IO_BYTES)
1038:            want = OBJ_MAX_IO_BYTES;
1039:          char *full = kmalloc(want);
1040:          if (!full) {
1041:            got = -1;
1042:          } else {
1043:            int total = vfs_list_dir(o->path, full, (uint32_t)want);
1044:            if (total < 0) {
1045:              got = -1;
1046:            } else if (o->offset >= (uint64_t)total) {
1047:              got = 0; /* cursor past the end: EOF */
1048:            } else {
1049:              size_t avail = (size_t)total - (size_t)o->offset;
1050:              got = (int)(avail < n ? avail : n);
1051:              memcpy(kb, full + o->offset, (size_t)got);
1052:            }
1053:            kfree(full);
1054:          }
1055:        } else {
1056:          got = vfs_read(&o->node, o->offset, kb, (uint32_t)n);
1057:        }
1058:        if (got < 0) {
1059:          ret = -EIO;
1060:        } else if (got > 0 && arch_copy_to_user(ubuf, kb, (size_t)got) != 0) {
1061:          ret = -EFAULT;
1062:        } else {
1063:          o->offset +=
1064:              (uint64_t)got; /* benign shared-offset race, documented */
1065:          ret = got;
1066:        }
1067:        kfree(kb);
1068:      }
1069:    }
1070:  } else if (o->type == OBJ_TYPE_REGKEY) {
1071:    /* read = registry_get the key's value (ASTRA §6.6) */
1072:    char val[MAX_VAL_LEN];
1073:    if (registry_get(o->path, val, sizeof(val)) != 0) {
1074:      ret = -ENOENT;
1075:    } else {
1076:      size_t vlen = strlen(val) + 1; /* include NUL */
1077:      if (vlen > n)
1078:        vlen = n;
1079:      ret = (vlen > 0 && arch_copy_to_user(ubuf, val, vlen) != 0) ? -EFAULT
1080:                                                                  : (long)vlen;
1081:    }
1082:  } else if (o->type == OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW) {
1083:    /* read = this window's info record (ASTRA §6.7).  A short read (n <
1084:     * sizeof) copies a prefix, like the other object reads. */
1085:    struct window_info wi;
1086:    if (compositor_window_info(o->window_id, &wi) != 0) {
1087:      ret = -ESRCH;
1088:    } else {
1089:      size_t cn = sizeof(wi);
1090:      if (cn > n)
1091:        cn = n;
1092:      ret = (cn > 0 && arch_copy_to_user(ubuf, &wi, cn) != 0) ? -EFAULT
1093:                                                              : (long)cn;
1094:    }
1095:  } else if (o->type == OBJ_TYPE_CONSOLE) {
1096:    /* stdin: drain the IPC input queue for one pressed/repeat key (the
1097:     * folded-in FD_KBD path).  Release events and non-input messages are
1098:     * discarded, as before.  When nothing is pending we return -EAGAIN; the
1099:     * SYS_READ dispatcher turns that into a blocking sleep — rescheduling needs
1100:     * the trap frame, which lives in the dispatcher, not here. */
1101:    if (n == 0) {
1102:      ret = 0;
1103:    } else {
1104:      ret = -EAGAIN;
1105:      while (1) {
1106:        struct ipc_node *node = pop_message(current_process, -1); /* from ANY */
1107:        if (!node)
1108:          break; /* queue empty → -EAGAIN, caller blocks */
1109:        if (node->msg.type == IPC_TYPE_INPUT && node->msg.data2 != 0) {
1110:          char c = (char)node->msg.data1;
1111:          ret = (arch_copy_to_user(ubuf, &c, 1) != 0) ? -EFAULT : 1;
1112:          kfree(node);
1113:          break;
1114:        }
1115:        kfree(node); /* release event / non-input: discard */
1116:      }
1117:    }
1118:  } else if (o->type == OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS) {
1119:    /* read = the process's live state as a text status block.  The process
1120:     * object NOTIFIES its state THROUGH the unified object mechanism (parallels
1121:     * OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW returning window_info) — not a side-channel.  Acquiring a
1122:     * READ handle is the ambient "status query" gate (sys_handle_create PROC
1123:     * branch); this is its payload.  A short buffer truncates, like the
1124:     * REGKEY/WINDOW reads. */
1125:    struct ps_info pi;
1126:    /* Lineage is read separately rather than widened into ps_info: that struct
1127:     * is a userland ABI read as an ARRAY by ps/nxproc, so growing it would move
1128:     * every element. */
1129:    int lin_parent = 0, lin_owner = 0;
1130:    NX_DISCARD(proc_get_lineage(o->pid, &lin_parent, &lin_owner),
1131:               "lineage is optional in this status block; the zero-initialised "
1132:               "parent/owner above are the intended fallback");
1133:    if (proc_get_info(o->pid, &pi) != 0) {
1134:      ret = -ESRCH;
1135:    } else {
1136:      char stbuf[256];
1137:      int len = snprintf(
1138:          stbuf, sizeof(stbuf),
1139:          "pid=%d\nname=%s\nstate=%s\nprio=%d\ncpu_ms=%llu\noncpu=%d\n"
1140:          "parent=%d\nowner=%d\n",
1141:          pi.pid, pi.name, proc_state_name(pi.state), pi.priority,
1142:          (unsigned long long)pi.cpu_time, pi.on_cpu, lin_parent, lin_owner);
1143:      size_t cn = (len > 0) ? (size_t)len : 0;
1144:      if (cn > n)
1145:        cn = n;
1146:      ret = (cn > 0 && arch_copy_to_user(ubuf, stbuf, cn) != 0) ? -EFAULT
1147:                                                                : (long)cn;
1148:    }
1149:  } else if (o->type == OBJ_TYPE_PORT) {
1150:    /* Port RECEIVE (needs the receive right, checked by pin_handle above).
1151:     * Dequeues one whole ipc_message — the message is the unit, unlike the
1152:     * pipe's byte stream.  Blocks while empty and a sender still exists;
1153:     * returns 0 when the last sender is gone, so a service loop terminates
1154:     * instead of hanging. */
1155:    struct kport *kp = o->port;
1156:    if (!kp) {
1157:      ret = -EIO;
1158:    } else if (n < sizeof(struct ipc_message)) {
1159:      ret = -EINVAL; /* a partial message would desync the mailbox */
1160:    } else {
1161:      for (;;) {
1162:        uint64_t f2;
1163:        spin_lock_irqsave(&object_lock, &f2);
1164:        if (kp->count > 0) {
1165:          struct ipc_message m = kp->q[kp->head];
1166:          kp->head = (kp->head + 1) % PORT_QUEUE_MAX;
1167:          kp->count--;
1168:          spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, f2);
1169:          wake_up(&kp->wq); /* freed a slot → wake a blocked sender */
1170:          ret = (arch_copy_to_user(ubuf, &m, sizeof(m)) != 0) ? -EFAULT
1171:                                                              : (long)sizeof(m);
1172:          break;
1173:        }
1174:        if (kp->senders == 0) { /* nobody left to send → end of service */
1175:          spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, f2);
1176:          ret = 0;
1177:          break;
1178:        }
1179:        spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, f2);
1180:        kthread_block(&kp->rq, port_readable_block, o);
1181:      }
1182:    }
1183:  } else if (o->type == OBJ_TYPE_PIPE) {
1184:    /* Pipe read: block until data is available or every writer has closed
1185:     * (EOF → 0).  The still-block predicate is re-checked under the reader wait
1186:     * queue lock so a writer's publish-then-wake_up can never be lost. */
1187:    struct kpipe *kp = o->pipe;
1188:    if (n == 0 || !kp) {
1189:      ret = (n == 0) ? 0 : -EIO;
1190:    } else {
1191:      uint8_t *kb = kmalloc(n);
1192:      if (!kb) {
1193:        ret = -ENOMEM;
1194:      } else {
1195:        for (;;) {
1196:          uint64_t f2;
1197:          spin_lock_irqsave(&object_lock, &f2);
1198:          if (kp->count > 0) {
1199:            uint32_t take = (kp->count < n) ? kp->count : (uint32_t)n;
1200:            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < take; i++) {
1201:              kb[i] = kp->buf[kp->head];
1202:              kp->head = (kp->head + 1) % PIPE_BUF_SIZE;
1203:            }
1204:            kp->count -= take;
1205:            spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, f2);
1206:            wake_up(&kp->wq); /* freed space → wake a blocked writer */
1207:            ret =
1208:                (arch_copy_to_user(ubuf, kb, take) != 0) ? -EFAULT : (long)take;
1209:            break;
1210:          }
1211:          if (kp->writers == 0) { /* empty and no writers → EOF */
1212:            spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, f2);
1213:            ret = 0;
1214:            break;
1215:          }
1216:          spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, f2);
1217:          kthread_block(&kp->rq, pipe_readable_block, o);
1218:        }
1219:        kfree(kb);
1220:      }
1221:    }
1222:  } else {
1223:    ret = -EINVAL;
1224:  }
1225:
1226:  obj_unref(o);
1227:  return ret;
1228:}
1229:
1230:/*
1231: * sys_object_write - OS1_object_write(handle, buf, n).  Needs OS1_RIGHT_WRITE.
1232: * FILE: VFS write at the object's offset.
1233: */
1234:long sys_object_write(int handle, const void *ubuf, size_t n) {
1235:  if (n > OBJ_MAX_IO_BYTES)
1236:    return -EINVAL;
1237:  long err = 0;
1238:  struct kobject *o = pin_handle(handle, OS1_RIGHT_WRITE, &err);
1239:  if (!o)
1240:    return err;
1241:
1242:  long ret;
1243:  if (o->type == OBJ_TYPE_FILE) {
1244:    if (n == 0) {
1245:      ret = 0;
1246:    } else {
1247:      uint8_t *kb = kmalloc(n);
1248:      if (!kb) {
1249:        ret = -ENOMEM;
1250:      } else if (arch_copy_from_user(kb, ubuf, n) != 0) {
1251:        kfree(kb);
1252:        ret = -EFAULT;
1253:      } else {
1254:        int wr = vfs_write_file(o->path, kb, (uint32_t)n, (uint32_t)o->offset);
1255:        kfree(kb);
1256:        if (wr < 0) {
1257:          ret = -EIO;
1258:        } else {
1259:          o->offset += (uint64_t)wr;
1260:          NX_DISCARD(vfs_open(o->path, &o->node),
1261:                     "best-effort size refresh after a successful write; the "
1262:                     "write itself already succeeded and is what we report");
1263:          ret = wr;
1264:        }
1265:      }
1266:    }
1267:  } else if (o->type == OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS) {
1268:    /* Capability IPC send (ASTRA §6.2/§6.5, Mach ports-as-objects): writing to
1269:     * a PROCESS object delivers an ipc_message to that process's queue.  The
1270:     * handle's WRITE right IS the authority — there is deliberately NO ambient
1271:     * process_ipc_allowed() check here, because that gates capability
1272:     * ACQUISITION (handle_create/grant), not use.  A process holding a granted
1273:     * WRITE handle can therefore message a target it could not reach by PID —
1274:     * this is the seL4/Mach delegation property. */
1275:    if (n != sizeof(struct ipc_message)) {
1276:      ret = -EINVAL;
1277:    } else {
1278:      struct ipc_message m;
1279:      if (arch_copy_from_user(&m, ubuf, sizeof(m)) != 0) {
1280:        ret = -EFAULT;
1281:      } else {
1282:        m.from = current_process ? (int)current_process->pid : 0;
1283:        ret = (kernel_ipc_send(o->pid, &m) == 0) ? 0 : -ESRCH;
1284:      }
1285:    }
1286:  } else if (o->type == OBJ_TYPE_REGKEY) {
1287:    /* write = registry_set the key's value (ASTRA §6.6).  Ownership stays
1288:     * first-writer-wins (registry_set), so a granted REGKEY cannot hijack
1289:     * another owner's key. */
1290:    if (n == 0 || n > MAX_VAL_LEN) {
1291:      ret = -EINVAL;
1292:    } else {
1293:      size_t cn = (n < MAX_VAL_LEN) ? n : (MAX_VAL_LEN - 1);
1294:      char val[MAX_VAL_LEN];
1295:      if (arch_copy_from_user(val, ubuf, cn) != 0) {
1296:        ret = -EFAULT;
1297:      } else {
1298:        val[cn] = '\0';
1299:        int rc = registry_set(o->path, val, registry_caller_owner());
1300:        ret = (rc == 0) ? (long)n : (rc == -EACCES ? -EACCES : -EINVAL);
1301:      }
1302:    }
1303:  } else if (o->type == OBJ_TYPE_CONSOLE) {
1304:    /* stdout/stderr: resolve the caller's OWN window first (a process with its
1305:     * own window renders there), else its controlling terminal (the launching
1306:     * shell) — the folded-in FD_WIN path.  window_text_write copies the user
1307:     * buffer and mirrors it to the UART.
1308:     *
1309:     * self_rendered (sched.h) processes are excluded from the own-window
1310:     * branch: once a process has blitted its OWN pixel content into a
1311:     * window (SYS_WINDOW_BLIT, syscall_dispatch.c), that window's buffer is
1312:     * its custom UI, not a text console — an implicit stdout write here
1313:     * (printf, an uncaught crash message, ...) must not draw glyphs over
1314:     * it.  Falls through to ctty_win (a self-rendering app's own printf
1315:     * still lands SOMEWHERE sane if it has a controlling terminal) or -1
1316:     * (window_text_write's `win_id > 0` gate then skips the compositor
1317:     * draw entirely; the UART mirror above is unaffected either way).
1318:     * SYS_WINDOW_WRITE (printf_win) is a SEPARATE, explicit call a self-
1319:     * rendering app can still use on purpose — only this implicit fd=1/2
1320:     * path is gated. */
1321:    int win_id = (current_process && !current_process->self_rendered)
1322:                     ? compositor_get_window_by_pid((int)current_process->pid)
1323:                     : -1;
1324:    if (win_id <= 0 && current_process)
1325:      win_id = current_process->ctty_win;
1326:    ret = window_text_write(win_id, (const char *)ubuf, n);
1327:  } else if (o->type == OBJ_TYPE_PORT) {
1328:    /* Port SEND (needs the send right).  The handle's WRITE right IS the
1329:     * authority — deliberately NO process_ipc_allowed() check, exactly as the
1330:     * OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS send path documents: ambient checks gate ACQUISITION,
1331:     * not use.  That is the whole point of a port: the client never names a
1332:     * pid.  `from` is stamped by the kernel so it cannot be forged. */
1333:    struct kport *kp = o->port;
1334:    if (!kp) {
1335:      ret = -EIO;
1336:    } else if (n != sizeof(struct ipc_message)) {
1337:      ret = -EINVAL;
1338:    } else {
1339:      struct ipc_message m;
1340:      if (arch_copy_from_user(&m, ubuf, sizeof(m)) != 0) {
1341:        ret = -EFAULT;
1342:      } else {
1343:        m.from = current_process ? (int)current_process->pid : 0;
1344:        for (;;) {
1345:          uint64_t f2;
1346:          spin_lock_irqsave(&object_lock, &f2);
1347:          if (kp->receivers == 0) { /* service gone → no point queueing */
1348:            spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, f2);
1349:            ret = -EPIPE;
1350:            break;
1351:          }
1352:          if (kp->count < PORT_QUEUE_MAX) {
1353:            kp->q[kp->tail] = m;
1354:            kp->tail = (kp->tail + 1) % PORT_QUEUE_MAX;
1355:            kp->count++;
1356:            spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, f2);
1357:            wake_up(&kp->rq); /* message available → wake the service */
1358:            ret = (long)sizeof(m);
1359:            break;
1360:          }
1361:          spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, f2);
1362:          kthread_block(&kp->wq, port_writable_block, o); /* mailbox full */
1363:        }
1364:      }
1365:    }
1366:  } else if (o->type == OBJ_TYPE_PIPE) {
1367:    /* Pipe write: append to the ring buffer, blocking while it is full and a
1368:     * reader still exists; -EPIPE if every reader has closed (no SIGPIPE here).
1369:     * Wakes a blocked reader after each chunk lands. */
1370:    struct kpipe *kp = o->pipe;
1371:    if (n == 0 || !kp) {
1372:      ret = (n == 0) ? 0 : -EIO;
1373:    } else {
1374:      uint8_t *kb = kmalloc(n);
1375:      if (!kb) {
1376:        ret = -ENOMEM;
1377:      } else if (arch_copy_from_user(kb, ubuf, n) != 0) {
1378:        kfree(kb);
1379:        ret = -EFAULT;
1380:      } else {
1381:        size_t done = 0;
1382:        ret = 0;
1383:        while (done < n) {
1384:          uint64_t f2;
1385:          spin_lock_irqsave(&object_lock, &f2);
1386:          if (kp->readers ==
1387:              0) { /* no reader will ever consume → broken pipe */
1388:            spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, f2);
1389:            ret = (done > 0) ? (long)done : -EPIPE;
1390:            break;
1391:          }
1392:          uint32_t space = PIPE_BUF_SIZE - kp->count;
1393:          if (space == 0) { /* full: wait for a reader to drain */
1394:            spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, f2);
1395:            kthread_block(&kp->wq, pipe_writable_block, o);
1396:            continue;
1397:          }
1398:          uint32_t chunk = (n - done < space) ? (uint32_t)(n - done) : space;
1399:          for (uint32_t i = 0; i < chunk; i++) {
1400:            kp->buf[kp->tail] = kb[done + i];
1401:            kp->tail = (kp->tail + 1) % PIPE_BUF_SIZE;
1402:          }
1403:          kp->count += chunk;
1404:          done += chunk;
1405:          spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, f2);
1406:          wake_up(&kp->rq); /* data available → wake a blocked reader */
1407:        }
1408:        if (ret == 0)
1409:          ret = (long)done;
1410:        kfree(kb);
1411:      }
1412:    }
1413:  } else {
1414:    ret = -EINVAL;
1415:  }
1416:
1417:  obj_unref(o);
1418:  return ret;
1419:}
1420:
1421:/*
1422: * sys_object_wait - OS1_object_wait(handle, arg).  Needs OS1_RIGHT_WAIT.
1423: * PROCESS: non-blocking process_wait() — status if dead, -1 alive, -2 gone.
1424: */
1425:long sys_object_wait(int handle, long arg) {
1426:  long err = 0;
1427:  struct kobject *o = pin_handle(handle, OS1_RIGHT_WAIT, &err);
1428:  if (!o)
1429:    return err;
1430:
1431:  long ret;
1432:  if (o->type == OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS) {
1433:    /* Phase 2: `arg`, if non-NULL, is a user int* that receives the reaped
1434:     * process's exit_code (raw). The libc personality (waitpid) wraps it in
1435:     * the POSIX status encoding. Only meaningful on reap (ret == pid). */
1436:    int code = 0;
1437:    ret = process_wait(o->pid, &code);
1438:    if (arg) {
1439:      extern int arch_copy_to_user(void *dst, const void *src, size_t n);
1440:      /* A bad status pointer is -EFAULT, not a reap that quietly delivered no
1441:       * status.  The (void) cast here suppressed nothing and only made the
1442:       * omission read as intentional. */
1443:      if (arch_copy_to_user((void *)arg, &code, sizeof(code)) != 0)
1444:        ret = -EFAULT;
1445:    }
1446:  } else {
1447:    ret = -EINVAL;
1448:  }
1449:
1450:  obj_unref(o);
1451:  return ret;
1452:}
1453:
1454:/*
1455: * sys_object_ctl - OS1_object_ctl(handle, cmd, arg).
1456: * Type-specific control verbs on an object you hold a capability to.
1457: * PROCESS + OBJ_CTL_KILL needs OS1_RIGHT_DESTROY and terminates the target
1458: * (machine-level processes stay protected inside process_terminate).  Holding a
1459: * DESTROY capability IS the authority — a GRANTED destroy handle lets its
1460: * holder kill a process it could not reach by process_kill_allowed (seL4
1461: * delegation of the kill right; acquisition was gated at handle_create time).
1462: */
1463:long sys_object_ctl(int handle, int cmd, long arg) {
1464:  /* PROCESS: terminate via a DESTROY capability (seL4 delegable kill). */
1465:  if (cmd == OBJ_CTL_KILL) {
1466:    long err = 0;
1467:    struct kobject *o = pin_handle(handle, OS1_RIGHT_DESTROY, &err);
1468:    if (!o)
1469:      return err;
1470:    long ret;
1471:    if (o->type == OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS) {
1472:      /* window-aware kill: the target + its windowless helpers die; its own
1473:       * windowed children are spared (docs/PROCESS-KILL-MODEL.md). */
1474:      process_kill_subtree(o->pid);
1475:      ret = 0;
1476:    } else {
1477:      ret = -EINVAL;
1478:    }
1479:    obj_unref(o);
1480:    return ret;
1481:  }
1482:
1483:  /* PROCESS job control (Phase 2): suspend/resume via the same DESTROY
1484:   * capability as kill — process-control authority. */
1485:  if (cmd == OBJ_CTL_STOP || cmd == OBJ_CTL_CONT) {
1486:    long err = 0;
1487:    struct kobject *o = pin_handle(handle, OS1_RIGHT_DESTROY, &err);
1488:    if (!o)
1489:      return err;
1490:    long ret;
1491:    if (o->type == OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS)
1492:      ret = (cmd == OBJ_CTL_STOP) ? process_stop(o->pid) : process_cont(o->pid);
1493:    else
1494:      ret = -EINVAL;
1495:    obj_unref(o);
1496:    return ret;
1497:  }
1498:
1499:  /* WINDOW control (ASTRA §6.7): minimize/restore/focus need OS1_RIGHT_WRITE,
1500:   * close needs OS1_RIGHT_DESTROY.  The right IS the authority — a granted
1501:   * window capability lets its holder (e.g. the dock /sys/bin/nxui) drive a
1502:   * window it does not own; acquisition was gated at handle_create. */
1503:  if (cmd == OBJ_CTL_MINIMIZE || cmd == OBJ_CTL_RESTORE ||
1504:      cmd == OBJ_CTL_FOCUS || cmd == OBJ_CTL_CLOSE) {
1505:    /* NOTE(OBJ-WIN-FOCUS): FOCUS needs only READ, so a READ-only window handle
1506:     * — which handle_create hands out for ANY window, ungated — can redirect
1507:     * keyboard focus.  This deliberately mirrors the compositor's unprivileged
1508:     * click-to-focus (any user may focus any window with the mouse) so the
1509:     * keyboard `focus` path is as open as the mouse.  minimize/restore/close
1510:     * stay window-manager authority (WRITE/DESTROY, gated at handle_create).
1511:     * Unifying this with SYS_SET_FOCUS's stricter cross-pid rule is a
1512:     * security-phase item. */
1513:    uint32_t need = (cmd == OBJ_CTL_CLOSE)   ? OS1_RIGHT_DESTROY
1514:                    : (cmd == OBJ_CTL_FOCUS) ? OS1_RIGHT_READ
1515:                                             : OS1_RIGHT_WRITE;
1516:    long err = 0;
1517:    struct kobject *o = pin_handle(handle, need, &err);
1518:    if (!o)
1519:      return err;
1520:    long ret;
1521:    if (o->type != OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW) {
1522:      ret = -EINVAL;
1523:    } else if (cmd == OBJ_CTL_MINIMIZE) {
1524:      ret = compositor_minimize_window(o->window_id);
1525:    } else if (cmd == OBJ_CTL_RESTORE) {
1526:      ret = compositor_restore_window(o->window_id);
1527:    } else if (cmd == OBJ_CTL_FOCUS) {
1528:      ret = compositor_focus_window(o->window_id);
1529:    } else { /* OBJ_CTL_CLOSE */
1530:      /* Close TERMINATES the owning process (window-aware, docs/PROCESS-KILL-
1531:       * MODEL.md): the target app and its windowless helpers die, while its own
1532:       * windowed children are SPARED (the user closes those via their red
1533:       * button).  Consistent with the titlebar red button
1534:       * (window_request_close). Previously a plain process_terminate; before
1535:       * THAT it only destroyed the WINDOW, leaving the app headless ("close
1536:       * does not kill").  Machine-level owners stay protected inside
1537:       * process_terminate. */
1538:      process_kill_subtree(o->pid);
1539:      ret = 0;
1540:    }
1541:    obj_unref(o);
1542:    return ret;
1543:  }
1544:
1545:  /* FILE: seek the object's shared byte offset (F4 M4.5).  Positioning needs
1546:   * only the handle itself (any FILE capability), so write-at-offset works on a
1547:   * WRITE-only handle too.  arg = absolute offset; returns the new offset. */
1548:  if (cmd == OBJ_CTL_SEEK) {
1549:    long err = 0;
1550:    struct kobject *o = pin_handle(handle, 0, &err);
1551:    if (!o)
1552:      return err;
1553:    long ret;
1554:    if (o->type != OBJ_TYPE_FILE || arg < 0) {
1555:      ret = -EINVAL;
1556:    } else {
1557:      o->offset = (uint64_t)arg;
1558:      ret = (long)o->offset;
1559:    }
1560:    obj_unref(o);
1561:    return ret;
1562:  }
1563:
1564:  /*
1565:   * PROCESS: hand a spawned job to its LOGICAL owner (Q3, ASTRA §6.5).
1566:   *
1567:   * Authority is deliberately doubled: DESTROY on the target (you must already
1568:   * control the process) AND a privileged caller — because this DELEGATES
1569:   * kill/stop/cont authority over that process to `arg`.  Without the
1570:   * privilege gate any process could hand its child to a third party, or
1571:   * re-home itself under a victim to borrow their authority chain.
1572:   */
1573:  if (cmd == OBJ_CTL_SETOWNER) {
1574:    long err = 0;
1575:    struct kobject *o = pin_handle(handle, OS1_RIGHT_DESTROY, &err);
1576:    if (!o)
1577:      return err;
1578:    long ret;
1579:    if (o->type != OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS || arg <= 0) {
1580:      ret = -EINVAL;
1581:    } else if (!current_process || !proc_is_privileged(current_process)) {
1582:      ret = -EPERM;
1583:    } else {
1584:      ret = process_set_owner(o->pid, (int)arg);
1585:    }
1586:    obj_unref(o);
1587:    return ret;
1588:  }
1589:
1590:  /* FILE: truncate to empty through an open descriptor (Phase 1 leftover:
1591:   * ftruncate).  Needs OS1_RIGHT_WRITE — this destroys data, unlike SEEK.  The
1592:   * provider's primitive is whole-file-replace, so an offset-0 zero-length
1593:   * vfs_write_file() empties the file; this is the one truncation a POSIX
1594:   * write(fd,...,0) cannot express (that is defined as a no-op).  Non-empty
1595:   * lengths are composed in libc's ftruncate() and never arrive here. */
1596:  if (cmd == OBJ_CTL_TRUNCATE) {
1597:    long err = 0;
1598:    struct kobject *o = pin_handle(handle, OS1_RIGHT_WRITE, &err);
1599:    if (!o)
1600:      return err;
1601:    long ret;
1602:    if (o->type != OBJ_TYPE_FILE || arg != 0) {
1603:      ret = -EINVAL;
1604:    } else if (vfs_write_file(o->path, "", 0, 0) < 0) {
1605:      ret = -EIO;
1606:    } else {
1607:      o->offset = 0;
1608:      NX_DISCARD(
1609:          vfs_open(o->path, &o->node),
1610:          "best-effort refresh after a successful truncate; the truncate "
1611:          "is what we report, and the cached node is the fallback");
1612:      ret = 0;
1613:    }
1614:    obj_unref(o);
1615:    return ret;
1616:  }
1617:
1618:  /* Namespace mutation (Programme R1b): the parent directory capability,
1619:   * rather than an ambient path syscall, names the namespace being changed.
1620:   * `arg` is deliberately only ONE child name: accepting slash-separated text
1621:   * would let a caller escape the directory it holds through `..` or a nested
1622:   * path. Recursive work stays in userland composition. */
1623:  if (cmd == OBJ_CTL_MKDIR || cmd == OBJ_CTL_UNLINK) {
1624:    long err = 0;
1625:    struct kobject *o = pin_handle(handle, OS1_RIGHT_MUTATE, &err);
1626:    if (!o)
1627:      return err;
1628:
1629:    long ret;
1630:    if (o->type != OBJ_TYPE_FILE || o->node.type != VFS_TYPE_DIR) {
1631:      ret = -ENOTDIR;
1632:    } else if (arg == 0) {
1633:      ret = -EFAULT;
1634:    } else {
1635:      char name[OBJ_FILE_PATH_MAX];
1636:      if (arch_copy_string_from_user(name, (const char *)arg, sizeof(name)) != 0) {
1637:        ret = -EFAULT;
1638:      } else {
1639:        size_t nlen = strlen(name);
1640:        int invalid = nlen == 0 || strcmp(name, ".") == 0 ||
1641:                      strcmp(name, "..") == 0;
1642:        for (size_t i = 0; i < nlen; i++)
1643:          if (name[i] == '/')
1644:            invalid = 1;
1645:        if (invalid) {
1646:          ret = -EINVAL;
1647:        } else {
1648:          size_t plen = strlen(o->path);
1649:          size_t sep = (plen == 1 && o->path[0] == '/') ? 0 : 1;
1650:          if (plen + sep + nlen >= OBJ_FILE_PATH_MAX) {
1651:            ret = -EINVAL;
1652:          } else {
1653:            char child[OBJ_FILE_PATH_MAX];
1654:            memcpy(child, o->path, plen);
1655:            if (sep)
1656:              child[plen++] = '/';
1657:            memcpy(child + plen, name, nlen + 1);
1658:            ret = (cmd == OBJ_CTL_MKDIR)
1659:                      ? vfs_create(child, VFS_TYPE_DIR)
1660:                      : vfs_unlink(child);
1661:          }
1662:        }
1663:      }
1664:    }
1665:    obj_unref(o);
1666:    return ret;
1667:  }
1668:
1669:  /* FILE: report the CURRENT size in bytes (Stage 4: lseek SEEK_END / stat via
1670:   * the object, so a FILE handle can fully back open()/read()/write()/lseek()).
1671:   * Reads the live size (another handle may have grown the file), falling back
1672:   * to the cached open-time size. */
1673:  if (cmd == OBJ_CTL_STAT) {
1674:    long err = 0;
1675:    struct kobject *o = pin_handle(handle, 0, &err);
1676:    if (!o)
1677:      return err;
1678:    long ret;
1679:    if (o->type != OBJ_TYPE_FILE) {
1680:      ret = -EINVAL;
1681:    } else {
1682:      /* Re-sync the cached node, do NOT run a second full path resolution.
1683:       *
1684:       * This used to call vfs_stat(o->path), which resolves the path from the
1685:       * mount table all over again — while handle_create had just resolved the
1686:       * very same path into o->node microseconds earlier.  For the size-probe
1687:       * idiom (handle_create -> STAT -> close, which is what every fopen does)
1688:       * that doubled the VFS work for no new information.  vfs_open refreshes
1689:       * the node in place, the same way sys_object_read does before a read, so
1690:       * a long-lived handle still sees a writer's appended size. */
1691:      NX_DISCARD(vfs_open(o->path, &o->node),
1692:                 "best-effort: on failure the cached node's size is returned, "
1693:                 "which is the last value this handle actually resolved");
1694:      ret = (long)o->node.size;
1695:    }
1696:    obj_unref(o);
1697:    return ret;
1698:  }
1699:
1700:  return -EINVAL;
1701:}
1702:
1703:/*
1704: * sys_object_lseek - POSIX lseek(2) on a FILE handle: reposition the shared
1705: * byte offset per 'whence' and return the new absolute position.  SEEK_END
1706: * reads the live size (vfs_stat) so it tracks growth by another handle.  A
1707: * non-seekable object (CONSOLE stdin/stdout/stderr, …) returns -ESPIPE.
1708: * Positioning needs only the handle itself (no rights), matching OBJ_CTL_SEEK.
1709: */
1710:long sys_object_lseek(int handle, long off, int whence) {
1711:  long err = 0;
1712:  struct kobject *o = pin_handle(handle, 0, &err);
1713:  if (!o)
1714:    return err;
1715:  long ret;
1716:  if (o->type != OBJ_TYPE_FILE) {
1717:    ret = -ESPIPE; /* streams cannot seek */
1718:  } else {
1719:    long base;
1720:    if (whence == SEEK_SET) {
1721:      base = 0;
1722:    } else if (whence == SEEK_CUR) {
1723:      base = (long)o->offset;
1724:    } else if (whence == SEEK_END) {
1725:      struct vfs_stat st;
1726:      base = (vfs_stat(o->path, &st) == 0) ? (long)st.size : (long)o->node.size;
1727:    } else {
1728:      base = -1; /* invalid whence */
1729:    }
1730:    if (base < 0) {
1731:      ret = -EINVAL;
1732:    } else {
1733:      long npos = base + off;
1734:      if (npos < 0) {
1735:        ret = -EINVAL;
1736:      } else {
1737:        o->offset = (uint64_t)npos;
1738:        ret = npos;
1739:      }
1740:    }
1741:  }
1742:  obj_unref(o);
1743:  return ret;
1744:}
1745:
1746:/*
1747: * process_install_stdio - give a freshly created process its
1748: * stdin/stdout/stderr as capability handles (ASTRA §6.2: the fd table folds
1749: * into the object table). Handles 0/1/2 share ONE refcounted CONSOLE object — a
1750: * process has a single controlling terminal: handle 0 holds READ (stdin
1751: * keyboard drain), handles 1/2 hold WRITE (stdout/stderr → the process's own
1752: * window, else its ctty).  The table is allocated eagerly so every process is
1753: * born with the trio, replacing the old fd-table pre-open.  Returns 0, or
1754: * -ENOMEM.
1755: */
1756:int process_install_stdio(struct process *p, struct process *parent) {
1757:  (void)
1758:      parent; /* currently unused; reserved for future ctty/stdio inheritance */
1759:  if (!p)
1760:    return -EINVAL;
1761:  if (handles_ensure(p) != 0)
1762:    return -ENOMEM;
1763:  struct kobject *con = kobj_alloc(OBJ_TYPE_CONSOLE);
1764:  if (!con)
1765:    return -ENOMEM;
1766:  uint64_t flags;
1767:  spin_lock_irqsave(&object_lock, &flags);
1768:  /* Slots 0/1/2 of a just-allocated table are free; install the shared console
1769:   * directly (not via the find-free path, which is for handles >= 3). */
1770:  p->handles[0].obj = con;
1771:  p->handles[0].rights = OS1_RIGHT_READ;
1772:  p->handles[1].obj = con;
1773:  p->handles[1].rights = OS1_RIGHT_WRITE;
1774:  p->handles[2].obj = con;
1775:  p->handles[2].rights = OS1_RIGHT_WRITE;
1776:  con->refcount = 3; /* three handles reference it */
1777:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
1778:  return 0;
1779:}
1780:
1781:/*
1782: * process_redirect_child_fd - install the SPAWNER's open handle 'parent_fd'
1783: * into the freshly-created child's slot 'child_slot', OVERWRITING the
1784: * pre-installed console there (Phase 4 shell redirection: `<`/`>`/`>>`/`2>`).
1785: * This is the fork+dup2 primitive expressed as a capability dup — the child
1786: * gets a SECOND handle to the SAME kobject (shared FILE offset, ASTRA §6.2), so
1787: * its read(0)/write(1) flow to the file instead of the terminal.  Called from
1788: * dispatch_spawn BEFORE the child is enqueued, with the spawner as
1789: * current_process; the spawner closes its own copies after the spawn returns.
1790: * Returns 0, or -EINVAL/-EBADF/-ENOMEM.
1791: */
1792:int process_redirect_child_fd_from(struct process *owner, struct process *child,
1793:                                   int child_slot, int parent_fd) {
1794:  struct process *parent =
1795:      owner; /* the fd's owner; not necessarily the spawner */
1796:  if (!child || !parent)
1797:    return -EINVAL;
1798:  if (child_slot < 0 || child_slot >= NPROC_HANDLES || parent_fd < 0 ||
1799:      parent_fd >= NPROC_HANDLES)
1800:    return -EBADF;
1801:  if (!parent->handles)
1802:    return -EBADF;
1803:  if (handles_ensure(child) != 0) /* normally already done by install_stdio */
1804:    return -ENOMEM;
1805:
1806:  struct kobject *to_free = NULL;
1807:  uint64_t flags;
1808:  spin_lock_irqsave(&object_lock, &flags);
1809:  struct handle_entry *src = &parent->handles[parent_fd];
1810:  if (!src->obj) {
1811:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
1812:    return -EBADF;
1813:  }
1814:  /* Drop whatever the child already held there (its shared console handle) and
1815:   * point the slot at the spawner's object with the SAME rights. */
1816:  struct handle_entry *dst = &child->handles[child_slot];
1817:  struct kobject *old = dst->obj;
1818:  uint32_t old_rights = dst->rights;
1819:  dst->obj = src->obj;
1820:  dst->rights = src->rights;
1821:  src->obj->refcount++;
1822:  pipe_handle_count(src->obj, src->rights, +1); /* child gains a pipe end */
1823:  if (old) {
1824:    pipe_handle_count(old, old_rights, -1); /* child loses the old handle */
1825:    if (--old->refcount <= 0)
1826:      to_free = old; /* last ref to the console → free outside the lock */
1827:  }
1828:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
1829:  if (to_free)
1830:    kobj_free(to_free);
1831:  return 0;
1832:}
1833:
1834:/* process_redirect_child_fd - the spawner-is-the-source form (today's callers:
1835: * the SYS_SPAWN redirection list, where the fds belong to the process calling
1836: * spawn).  Kept as a thin wrapper so the source stays parameterised: an
1837: * execution SERVICE spawning on a client's behalf needs the source to be the
1838: * CLIENT, not itself (Q2 hybrid).  Splitting the source out now means that path
1839: * is a caller change rather than a rewrite. */
1840:int process_redirect_child_fd(struct process *child, int child_slot,
1841:                              int parent_fd) {
1842:  return process_redirect_child_fd_from(current_process, child, child_slot,
1843:                                        parent_fd);
1844:}
1845:
1846:/*
1847: * process_handles_destroy - close every handle a dying process holds and free
1848: * its table.  Called from BOTH process free sites (immediate teardown and the
1849: * deferred reaper) before the struct process page is freed.  NULL-safe.
1850: */
1851:void process_handles_destroy(struct process *p) {
1852:  if (!p)
1853:    return;
1854:  uint64_t flags;
1855:  spin_lock_irqsave(&object_lock, &flags);
1856:  struct handle_entry *tbl = p->handles;
1857:  p->handles = NULL; /* blocks a concurrent grant-into-dead under this lock */
1858:  if (!tbl) {
1859:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
1860:    return;
1861:  }
1862:  for (int i = 0; i < NPROC_HANDLES; i++) {
1863:    struct kobject *o = tbl[i].obj;
1864:    if (!o)
1865:      continue;
1866:    pipe_handle_count(o, tbl[i].rights, -1); /* untrack pipe reader/writer */
1867:    tbl[i].obj = NULL;
1868:    if (--o->refcount <= 0)
1869:      kobj_free(o); /* object_lock -> kmalloc_lock order is consistent */
1870:  }
1871:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&object_lock, flags);
1872:  kfree(tbl);
1873:}

@@@ kernel/core/smp.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/core/smp.c
3: * Arch-neutral secondary-CPU bring-up (S-ALIGN F8 — first slice of B6 #96).
4: *
5: * Both arch_smp_init() loops (PSCI on aarch64, INIT-SIPI on amd64) used to
6: * implement the same logical step independently: "publish the CPU's idle task,
7: * wake it through the arch contract, wait for its boot ack".  The SMP-IDLE-RACE
8: * fix (#169/#170, commit 74fc5cc) had to be applied twice — once per arch —
9: * because no shared primitive existed.  This module IS that primitive: the
10: * ordering invariant and the ack handshake live here, once.
11: *
12: * The ack wait is bounded by wall time through the HAL timer contract
13: * (arch_timer_get_count/_get_freq — the DIR-06 reference seam, same pattern as
14: * the panic watchdog in printk.c), replacing the per-arch nop-count/udelay
15: * divergence.  The handshake variable is acquire/release-paired with
16: * smp_ack_boot() so the secondary's per-CPU initialization writes are visible
17: * to the BSP before the ack is (S-ALIGN F3).
18: */
19:#include <kernel/arch.h>
20:#include <kernel/cpu.h>
21:#include <kernel/printk.h>
22:#include <kernel/types.h>
23:
24:/* The boot-ack handshake cell.  Written ONLY through smp_ack_boot() by the
25: * secondary, read ONLY by smp_bringup_secondary() on the BSP. */
26:static volatile uint32_t cpu_boot_ack;
27:
28:/* smp_ack_boot - the secondary CPU announces itself online (called from
29: * kernel_secondary_main after its per-CPU init).  Release store: everything
30: * the secondary initialized must be visible before the BSP sees the ack. */
31:void smp_ack_boot(uint32_t cpu) {
32:  __atomic_store_n(&cpu_boot_ack, cpu, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
33:}
34:
35:/*
36: * smp_bringup_secondary - bring one secondary CPU online.
37: *
38: * The one place that encodes the bring-up invariant (SMP-IDLE-RACE #169/#170):
39: * the CPU's idle task is published BEFORE the wake, because the secondary
40: * enables IRQs in kernel_secondary_main and can be preempted into schedule()
41: * — which picks cpu_data[cpu].idle_task — before the BSP would otherwise
42: * create it (NULL idle task -> context switch into NULL).
43: *
44: * cpu:       logical CPU id to start.
45: * entry:     arch entry point handed to arch_cpu_wake_secondary (PSCI target /
46: *            SIPI trampoline).
47: * stack_top: top of the CPU's kernel stack (stacks descend), passed through
48: *            the arch wake contract.
49: *
50: * Returns 0 when the CPU acked, -1 if the arch wake call itself failed
51: * (firmware error / CPU absent), -2 on ack timeout (absent CPU or a very
52: * slow hypervisor — its idle task already exists, so a late-arriving CPU
53: * still schedules safely).  Failure POLICY (skip vs. abort the loop) stays
54: * with the arch caller: only the mechanism is shared.
55: */
56:int smp_bringup_secondary(uint32_t cpu, void (*entry)(void), void *stack_top) {
57:  /* Fresh handshake for this CPU (uniform: amd64 always reset, aarch64
58:   * relied on ids never repeating — resetting is correct for both). */
59:  __atomic_store_n(&cpu_boot_ack, 0u, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
60:
61:  /* 1. Idle task BEFORE the wake — the single-sourced #169/#170 invariant. */
62:  smp_create_idle_task(cpu);
63:
64:  /* 2. Wake through the arch contract. */
65:  if (arch_cpu_wake_secondary(cpu, entry, stack_top) != 0)
66:    return -1;
67:
68:  /* 3. Bounded acquire-wait for the ack (~10 s wall time, generous for a
69:   * slow hypervisor; the watchdog in printk.c uses the same timer seam). */
70:  uint64_t freq = arch_timer_get_freq();
71:  uint64_t deadline = arch_timer_get_count() + freq * 10ULL;
72:  while (__atomic_load_n(&cpu_boot_ack, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) != cpu) {
73:    if ((int64_t)(deadline - arch_timer_get_count()) <= 0)
74:      return -2;
75:    arch_nop();
76:  }
77:  return 0;
78:}

@@@ kernel/core/syscall_dispatch.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/core/syscall_dispatch.c
3: * Architecture-Agnostic Syscall Dispatcher
4: *
5: * This file is the central syscall switch for OS1/NEXS.  The arch-specific
6: * syscall entry stub (aarch64: svc_handler / amd64: syscall entry in cpu.c)
7: * calls kernel_syscall_dispatcher() with the saved register frame.  This
8: * function reads the syscall number and arguments from the frame via the
9: * pt_regs_* accessor macros (arch-agnostic) and dispatches to the appropriate
10: * implementation.
11: *
12: * Role / layering:
13: *   userland svc/syscall -> arch entry (context.S / cpu.c)
14: *                        -> kernel_syscall_dispatcher()  [this file]
15: *                        -> sys_* / process_* / compositor_* / vfs_*
16: *   Returns a pt_regs* to restore; may differ from the input frame when
17: *   schedule() performs a context switch (IPC block, exit, yield).
18: *
19: * Key invariants:
20: *   - All user pointers (arg0..arg5) must be validated via
21: * arch_copy_*_from_user or arch_copy_string_from_user before being dereferenced
22: * in the kernel.
23: *   - Syscall implementations must not return directly; they write the return
24: *     value via pt_regs_set_return() and fall through to "return frame", OR
25: *     they call schedule() and return its result (a different task's frame).
26: *   - cpu->syscall_buf (a per-CPU scratch buffer) is used for path/title
27: * copies; only one such copy is in flight per CPU at any time.
28: *
29: * ABI (Phase B3):
30: *   Numbering (ABI-01/ABI-SYS-01 RESOLVED): the switch uses the SYS_*
31: *   macros from include/api/syscall_nums.h — the same header the userland
32: *   stubs assemble against, so the two sides cannot drift.  The legacy
33: *   duplicate IPC numbers (30/31/32) are gone (SEND/RECV/TRY_RECV =
34: *   230/231/233).
35: *   Error model (ABI-02 RESOLVED): failures return negative errno values
36: *   from posix_types.h (-EFAULT for bad user pointers, -ENOMEM, -EINVAL,
37: *   -ENOSYS for unknown numbers...); >= 0 means success.  VFS-layer calls
38: *   still return their own negatives (mapped to -EIO/-ENOENT where the
39: *   cause is unambiguous).
40: *
41: * Capability checks (ABI-04 batch 2 + USR-SEC-03 #79 batch 6):
42: *   Privilege levels: machine (bypasses all checks, unkillable) > root >
43: *   user > guest.  Fine-grained caps (CAP_*) gate each surface; the cut at
44: *   spawn is monotonic (a child is never more privileged than its creator).
45: *   SYS_SPAWN / SYS_SPAWN_CAPS  need CAP_SPAWN — else -EPERM.
46: *   SYS_KILL         caller must be privileged, the target itself, or an
47: *                    ancestor of it (process_kill_allowed) — else -EPERM.
48: *   SYS_CREATE_WINDOW / SYS_SET_FOCUS  need CAP_WINDOW — else -EPERM;
49: *                    cross-PID focus still needs machine level.
50: *   SYS_DESTROY_WINDOW  owner or machine only — else -EPERM.
51: *   SYS_OPEN(write) / SYS_FILE_WRITE  need CAP_FS_WRITE; the /bin and /sys
52: *                    trees stay machine-only (EXT4-02) — else -EPERM/-EACCES.
53: *   SYS_SEND         need CAP_IPC_ANY for non-relatives (process_ipc_allowed);
54: *                    parent/descendants always allowed — else -EPERM.
55: *   SYS_REGISTRY     write needs CAP_REG_WRITE; ownership enforced in
56: *                    registry_set (LIB-REG-02/USR-SEC-01) — else
57: * -EPERM/-EACCES. Kernel-internal paths (compositor close button, init
58: * supervision, process teardown) call the underlying functions directly and
59: * bypass these checks by design.
60: *
61: * Descriptor model (ASTRA §6.2 — the fd table folded into the object table):
62: *   a POSIX descriptor IS a capability handle (fd N == handle N).  Every
63: *   process is born with handles 0/1/2 as one shared OBJ_TYPE_CONSOLE object
64: *   (0 = stdin keyboard, 1/2 = stdout+stderr window); open() ≡
65: *   handle_create(FILE) and hands out handles >= 3; read/write/lseek/close
66: *   (63/64/62/57) route through the object layer (sys_object_read/_write/
67: *   _lseek + sys_handle_close).  There is no separate fd array.
68: *
69: * Known issues:
70: *   ABI-07  (W2 BUG) SYS_SPAWN disables IRQs across process_create +
71: *           process_load_elf, which may trigger blocking virtio/ext4 disk I/O.
72: *   GFX-FONT-01  (W4 SECURITY/BUG) SYS_SET_FONT: stores a raw user
73: *           pointer into kernel globals; dereferenced in IRQ-context rendering
74: *           (sys_set_font in graphics/font.c) → UAF / info-leak.
75: */
76:#include <arch/pt_regs.h>
77:#include <kernel/cpu.h>
78:#include <kernel/kmalloc.h>
79:#include <kernel/object.h>
80:#include <kernel/printk.h>
81:#include <kernel/registry.h>
82:#include <kernel/sched.h>
83:#include <kernel/string.h>
84:#include <kernel/types.h>
85:#include <kernel/vfs.h>
86:#include <style_names.h>
87:#include <syscall_nums.h>
88:
89:/* Defined below (after sys_get_time); used by the SYS_NANOSLEEP dispatch case.
90: */
91:static struct pt_regs *sys_nanosleep(struct pt_regs *regs, uint64_t ns);
92:/* Yield with per-process anti-spin throttle; used by the SYS_YIELD case. */
93:static struct pt_regs *sys_yield(struct pt_regs *regs);
94:
95:/*
96: * FIX(EXT4-07): upper bound for kmalloc'd bounce buffers whose size comes
97: * straight from a user syscall argument (arg2) in FILE_WRITE/FILE_READ/LIST_DIR
98: * (cases 251/252/254).  Without a cap a process can pass size=4 GB and make the
99: * kernel attempt an enormous pmm_alloc_pages() — at best a slow contiguous scan
100: * that fails (NULL), at worst draining kernel RAM (there is no per-process
101: * quota) → OOM/DoS.
102: *
103: * 16 MiB sits above every legitimate single-syscall transfer: the largest
104: * routine read is a ~98 KB font (read whole-file at boot), DOOM reads WAD lumps
105: * individually (each well under 1 MB), and the ext4 driver's own
106: * single-indirect read ceiling is ~4 MB (double-indirect is unimplemented) — so
107: * this cap never truncates a read the driver could actually satisfy, while
108: * rejecting absurd allocations.  size==0 (the FILE_READ size-probe) is never >
109: * the cap, so it is unaffected.
110: */
111:#define SYSCALL_MAX_IO_BYTES (16u * 1024u * 1024u) /* 16 MiB */
