150:/*
151: * kernel_syscall_dispatcher - dispatch a syscall from the saved register frame.
152: *
153: * Entry point called by the arch-specific svc/syscall handler immediately
154: * after saving all user registers into 'frame'.  Reads syscall_num and up
155: * to six arguments from frame via pt_regs_* accessors.
156: *
157: * Returns: a pt_regs* to restore.  In the common (non-blocking) case this is
158: *          'frame' itself with the return value written via
159: * pt_regs_set_return(). For blocking operations (EXIT/YIELD/IPC RECV and
160: * sometimes IPC SEND) this is the frame of the next scheduled process.
161: *
162: * Locking: no locks held on entry; individual cases may acquire
163: *          sched_lock / msg_lock / per-CPU sched_lock internally.
164: * IRQ context: no — syscalls run in kernel mode with IRQs enabled (normal
165: *          exception-level transition on aarch64; ring 3->0 on amd64).
166: *
167: * NOTE(ABI-07): case 220 (SPAWN) calls arch_local_irq_disable() before
168: *          process_create + process_load_elf, which may block on virtio I/O.
169: */
170:struct pt_regs *kernel_syscall_dispatcher(struct pt_regs *frame);
171:
172:/* argv marshalling limits for SYS_SPAWN.  ELF_MAX_ARGS in elf.c must be >=
173: * SPAWN_MAX_ARGS; SPAWN_ARG_LEN bounds each NUL-terminated argument. */
174:#define SPAWN_MAX_ARGS 16
175:#define SPAWN_ARG_LEN 128
176:
177:/* level_for_path - the capability PRESET a binary gets from its location in the
178: * VFS (ASTRA per-path stratification, F1): a /sys/bin service runs at ROOT
179: * (system authority — refined per service later), everything else (notably
180: * /bin) at USER.  This is a CEILING + default, NOT an escalation:
181: * process_create_caps still clamps the child to no more privileged than its
182: * creator, so a USER shell launching a /sys/bin binary does NOT gain root.
183: * /sys/bin is also write- protected (object.c handle_create denies non-machine
184: * writes under /sys,/bin), so the binaries backing this preset are immutable.
185: */
186:static uint8_t level_for_path(const char *path) {
187:  if (path && strncmp(path, "/sys/bin/", 9) == 0)
188:    return PLVL_ROOT;
189:  return PLVL_USER;
190:}
191:
192:/* spawn_path_is_sane - reject a spawn path the preset cannot reason about.
193: *
194: * SPAWN-LVL-01 (found 2026-07-23, audit programme A): level_for_path() prefix-
195: * matches the RAW string, but the VFS resolves ".." (vfs.c).  So
196: * "/sys/bin/../../home/evil" prefix-matches /sys/bin/ and would take the ROOT
197: * preset while resolving to a user-writable file.  It is NOT an escalation
198: * today — the monotonic creator clamp in process_create_caps drags the child
199: * back to the (less-privileged) creator's level, so a USER caller gets USER
200: * regardless.  But "harmless only because a SECOND, distant check happens to
201: * cover it" is exactly the fragility this audit exists to remove: the preset
202: * must see the path the VFS will actually open.  No legitimate caller spawns a
203: * path containing ".." (verified across the tree), so refusing them costs
204: * nothing and makes level_for_path()'s prefix match sound. */
205:static int spawn_path_is_sane(const char *path) {
206:  if (!path || !path[0])
207:    return 0;
208:  for (const char *p = path; *p; p++)
209:    if (p[0] == '.' && p[1] == '.' &&
210:        (p == path || p[-1] == '/') && (p[2] == '/' || p[2] == '\0'))
211:      return 0; /* a ".." path component */
212:  return 1;
213:}
214:
215:/* dispatch_spawn - shared body for SYS_SPAWN and SYS_SPAWN_CAPS.
216: *
217: * NOTE(ABI-07): runs process_create + process_load_elf with IRQs disabled
218: * across blocking virtio/ext4 disk I/O.  Pre-existing; kept verbatim so the
219: * new capability path does not widen the critical section. */
220:static long dispatch_spawn(const char *path, uint8_t level, uint32_t caps,
221:                           int use_caps, int argc, char *const kargv[],
222:                           uint32_t flags, const struct spawn_redir *redir,
223:                           int nredir) {
224:  /* ASTRA per-path preset (F1): plain spawn() takes the path's level;
225:   * spawn_caps may only DROP privilege below it (a request more privileged than
226:   * the path is capped to the path).  The creator-clamp in process_create_caps
227:   * then forbids any escalation regardless. */
228:  if (!spawn_path_is_sane(path))
229:    return -EINVAL; /* SPAWN-LVL-01: no ".." — the preset must match the VFS */
230:
231:  uint8_t path_lvl = level_for_path(path);
232:  if (!use_caps || level < path_lvl)
233:    level = path_lvl;
234:
235:  arch_local_irq_disable();
236:  struct process *p =
237:      use_caps ? process_create_caps(path, PROC_PRIO_USER, level, caps)
238:               : process_create(path, PROC_PRIO_USER, level);
239:  long ret;
240:  if (p) {
241:    /* nxexec model (#193): a DETACHED spawn declines being the child's
242:     * controlling terminal — process_create inherited the spawner's window
243:     * as ctty unconditionally; the flag opts out (launcher-style spawns).
244:     * Safe here: the child is not yet enqueued/visible. */
245:    if (flags & SPAWN_FLAG_DETACHED)
246:      p->ctty_win = -1;
247:    /* Phase 4: apply the spawner's fd redirections (shell `<`/`>`/`>>`/`2>`)
248:     * into the child's handle table before it runs.  A bad source fd aborts the
249:     * whole spawn — redirection is part of the child's promised environment. */
250:    long rerr = 0;
251:    for (int i = 0; i < nredir; i++) {
252:      if (redir[i].source_pid == 0) {
253:        /* Ordinary case: the fds belong to whoever called spawn. */
254:        rerr = process_redirect_child_fd(p, redir[i].child_fd,
255:                                         redir[i].parent_fd);
256:      } else {
257:        /* An execution SERVICE spawning on a client's behalf: the fds live in
258:         * the CLIENT's table.  Reaching into another process's handle table is
259:         * a system-service power, not an application one — same rule and same
260:         * reasoning as OBJ_CTL_SETOWNER.  Without this gate any process could
261:         * siphon descriptors out of any other simply by naming it here. */
262:        if (!proc_is_privileged(current_process)) {
263:          rerr = -EPERM;
264:          break;
265:        }
266:        /*
267:         * PROC-REF-01 is NOT closed here, deliberately — and the first attempt
268:         * to close it introduced a worse bug than the one it fixed.
269:         *
270:         * That attempt held sched_lock across the lookup AND
271:         * process_redirect_child_fd_from().  But that function ALLOCATES:
272:         * handles_ensure() kmallocs the child's table and kobj_free() releases
273:         * the displaced console handle.  Allocating under sched_lock creates
274:         * the sched_lock -> pmm_lock/kmalloc_lock order that process.c states
275:         * in writing "nothing else in this file establishes" — the same reason
276:         * process_create_caps allocates the environment page BEFORE taking the
277:         * lock.  With IRQs disabled, an idle core spinning inside the allocator
278:         * while this CPU holds sched_lock and waits for it is a hard hang; that
279:         * is the amd64 K3-userland panic (corrupted RSP, execution off into the
280:         * stack).
281:         *
282:         * The other two PROC-REF-01 sites (sys_cap_grant, sys_port_send_caps)
283:         * are safe because they were made ALLOCATION-FREE under the lock on
284:         * purpose: both refuse a target with no handle table rather than
285:         * creating one.  This path cannot be made allocation-free the same way
286:         * — the child legitimately may need its table built.
287:         *
288:         * So this site keeps the narrow, pre-existing use-after-free window and
289:         * waits for the real fix (a process pin/refcount), which is what
290:         * PROC-REF-01 asks for.  A rare UAF is strictly better than a
291:         * reproducible deadlock in the path every system() call takes.
292:         */
293:        struct process *src = process_find_by_pid(redir[i].source_pid);
294:        if (!src)
295:          rerr = -ESRCH;
296:        else
297:          rerr = process_redirect_child_fd_from(src, p, redir[i].child_fd,
298:                                                redir[i].parent_fd);
299:      }
300:      if (rerr != 0)
301:        break;
302:    }
303:    if (rerr != 0) {
304:      process_abort_spawn(p);
305:      arch_local_irq_enable();
306:      return rerr;
307:    }
308:    if (process_load_elf_args(p, path, argc, kargv) == 0) {
309:      /* SCHED-UAF Pitfall B: commit the child atomically against a concurrent
310:       * kill.  Capture the pid first — process_finalize_spawn may RELEASE p (if
311:       * a kill was deferred while the ELF loaded), so p must not be read after.
312:       */
313:      long pid = (long)p->pid;
314:      process_finalize_spawn(p);
315:      ret = pid;
316:    } else {
317:      process_abort_spawn(p); /* load failed: release the half-built child */
318:      ret = -ENOENT;          /* path missing or unloadable ELF */
319:    }
320:  } else {
321:    ret = -EAGAIN; /* quota hit or process table exhausted */
322:  }
323:  arch_local_irq_enable();
324:  return ret;
325:}
326:
327:/* window_text_write - copy a user text buffer into a kmalloc bounce (no
328: * truncation; capped at SYSCALL_MAX_IO_BYTES), mirror it to the UART serial
329: * log, and append it to compositor window win_id.  Shared by the FD_WIN
330: * stdout sink and SYS_WINDOW_WRITE (#123).  Replaces the old 1023-byte
331: * syscall_buf truncation (retires ABI-06 on the window path). */
332:extern void uart_puts(const char *str);
333:/* Non-static: also the OBJ_TYPE_CONSOLE stdout/stderr backend, called from
334: * kernel/core/object.c (sys_object_write).  Shared by SYS_WINDOW_WRITE. */
335:/*
336: * GFX-WIN-WRITE-01 (found 2026-07-23, audit programme A) — may 'current' put
337: * text into window 'win_id'?
338: *
339: * SYS_WINDOW_WRITE was gated by CAP_WINDOW and nothing else, while every
340: * sibling verb had already been closed: DRAW and BLIT pass the caller's pid so
341: * the compositor can refuse, RESIZE / SET_FLAGS / DESTROY_WINDOW check
342: * compositor_window_owner() right in the dispatcher.  This one was missed, and
343: * CAP_WINDOW is the WEAKEST capability there is — PLVL_GUEST holds it and
344: * nothing else (level_ceiling[], process.c).  So the least privileged process
345: * on the machine could write arbitrary text into ANY window, and it did not
346: * even have to guess an id: SYS_WINDOW_ENUM is deliberately ungated.  That is a
347: * UI-spoofing primitive against the shell, the dock and the notification panel.
348: *
349: * Three writers are legitimate and all three are expressible as authority the
350: * process already holds:
351: *   - the window's OWNER;
352: *   - a process writing to its CONTROLLING TERMINAL.  This is the one that
353: *     makes an owner-only check wrong: a windowless child's stdout goes to the
354: *     shell's window (sys_object_write resolves ctty_win), and it does not own
355: *     it.  ctty_win is set by the kernel at spawn and is not user-writable, so
356: *     honouring it grants nothing the process was not already given;
357: *   - a MACHINE process, exactly as SET_FLAGS and DESTROY_WINDOW allow.
358: *
359: * Locking: called with NO lock held (pin_handle releases object_lock before
360: * sys_object_write reaches here, and the dispatcher holds nothing), so taking
361: * compositor_lock inside compositor_window_owner() is safe.  Do not move this
362: * check under a lock without re-reading PROCESS-KILL-MODEL §4, Pitfall A.
363: */
364:static int window_write_allowed(int win_id) {
365:  extern int compositor_window_owner(int window_id);
366:  if (!current_process)
367:    return 1; /* kernel-internal writer */
368:  if (proc_is_machine(current_process))
369:    return 1;
370:  if (win_id == current_process->ctty_win)
371:    return 1;
372:  int owner = compositor_window_owner(win_id);
373:  return (owner < 0) || (owner == (int)current_process->pid);
374:}
375:
376:long window_text_write(int win_id, const char *ubuf, size_t count) {
377:  if (count == 0)
378:    return 0;
379:  if (count > SYSCALL_MAX_IO_BYTES)
380:    return -EINVAL;
381:  if (win_id > 0 && !window_write_allowed(win_id))
382:    return -EPERM;
383:  char *k = kmalloc(count + 1);
384:  if (!k)
385:    return -ENOMEM;
386:  if (arch_copy_from_user(k, ubuf, count) != 0) {
387:    kfree(k);
388:    return -EFAULT;
389:  }
390:  k[count] = '\0';
391:  uart_puts(k);
392:  if (win_id > 0)
393:    compositor_window_write(win_id, k, count);
394:  kfree(k);
395:  return (long)count;
396:}
397:
398:struct pt_regs *kernel_syscall_dispatcher(struct pt_regs *frame) {
399:  uint64_t syscall_num = pt_regs_syscall_num(frame);
400:  uint64_t arg0 = pt_regs_arg(frame, 0);
401:  uint64_t arg1 = pt_regs_arg(frame, 1);
402:  uint64_t arg2 = pt_regs_arg(frame, 2);
403:  uint64_t arg3 = pt_regs_arg(frame, 3);
404:  uint64_t arg4 = pt_regs_arg(frame, 4);
405:  uint64_t arg5 = pt_regs_arg(frame, 5);
406:
407:  switch (syscall_num) {
408:  case SYS_OPEN: {
409:    /* open(path, flags) -> descriptor.  A descriptor IS a capability handle
410:     * (ASTRA §6.8: open ≡ handle_create(FS), the fd table folded into the
411:     * object table): this installs an OBJ_TYPE_FILE handle and returns its
412:     * index — the first free slot >= 3, since 0/1/2 are the pre-installed
413:     * stdin/stdout/stderr console handles, so the first open is fd 3 exactly as
414:     * before.  O_ACCMODE selects the handle's rights.
415:     *
416:     * O_CREAT/O_TRUNC/O_APPEND are honoured here (issue #126): the create /
417:     * truncate is applied through the SAME vfs_write_allowed() authority seam
418:     * used for WRITE capability acquisition (S-ALIGN F6), so the POSIX
419:     * personality logic in
420:     * libc keeps only flag/mode translation (ASTRA layering).  Any OTHER flag
421:     * is still an explicit -EINVAL, never silently ignored.  sys_handle_create
422:     * then does the resolve, the write-ACL re-check for a WRITE handle, and the
423:     * VFS open. */
424:    if (!current_process) {
425:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
426:      break;
427:    }
428:    int flags = (int)arg1;
429:    if (flags & ~(O_ACCMODE | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC | O_APPEND)) {
430:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EINVAL);
431:      break;
432:    }
433:    if (flags & (O_CREAT | O_TRUNC)) {
434:      char kpath[128];
435:      if (arch_copy_string_from_user(kpath, (const char *)arg0, sizeof(kpath)) !=
436:          0) {
437:        pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EFAULT);
438:        break;
439:      }
440:      char resolved[128];
441:      vfs_resolve_path(kpath, resolved, sizeof(resolved));
442:      struct vfs_stat vst;
443:      int exists = (vfs_stat(resolved, &vst) == 0);
444:      long wperm;
445:      if (!exists && (flags & O_CREAT)) {
446:        if ((wperm = vfs_write_allowed(resolved)) != 0) {
447:          pt_regs_set_return(frame, wperm);
448:          break;
449:        }
450:        if (vfs_create(resolved, VFS_TYPE_FILE) != 0) {
451:          pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EIO);
452:          break;
453:        }
454:      } else if (exists && (flags & O_TRUNC)) {
455:        if ((wperm = vfs_write_allowed(resolved)) != 0) {
456:          pt_regs_set_return(frame, wperm);
457:          break;
458:        }
459:        /* No vfs_truncate primitive: drop and recreate empty — same net effect
460:         * as truncate-to-zero, reusing the create-on-write model. */
461:        /* -ENOENT is the normal case (truncating a file that does not exist
462:         * yet); anything else is a real failure that used to be swallowed, so
463:         * an EACCES or EIO here became a silent "truncate succeeded". */
464:        {
465:          int ur = vfs_unlink(resolved);
466:          if (ur != 0 && ur != -ENOENT) {
467:            pt_regs_set_return(frame, ur);
468:            break;
469:          }
470:        }
471:        if (vfs_create(resolved, VFS_TYPE_FILE) != 0) {
472:          pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EIO);
473:          break;
474:        }
475:      }
476:      /* O_TRUNC on a missing file without O_CREAT: fall through — the open
477:       * below resolves nothing and returns -ENOENT, matching POSIX. */
478:    }
479:    uint32_t rights = ((flags & O_ACCMODE) == O_RDONLY) ? OS1_RIGHT_READ
480:                      : ((flags & O_ACCMODE) == O_WRONLY)
481:                          ? OS1_RIGHT_WRITE
482:                          : (OS1_RIGHT_READ | OS1_RIGHT_WRITE);
483:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, sys_handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, (const char *)arg0,
484:                                                rights, OBJ_TYPE_FILE));
485:  } break;
486:  case SYS_CLOSE:
487:    /* close(fd) ≡ drop the handle; frees the object at its last reference. */
488:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, sys_handle_close((int)arg0));
489:    break;
490:  case SYS_LSEEK:
491:    /* lseek(fd, off, whence) ≡ reposition a FILE handle's shared offset; a
492:     * CONSOLE/stream handle returns -ESPIPE (handled in sys_object_lseek). */
493:    pt_regs_set_return(frame,
494:                       sys_object_lseek((int)arg0, (long)arg1, (int)arg2));
495:    break;
496:  case SYS_READ: {
497:    /* read(fd, buf, n) ≡ OS1_object_read on the handle.  A CONSOLE stdin with
498:     * no key pending returns -EAGAIN; that is NOT surfaced to userland — we
499:     * block the caller exactly like the folded-in FD_KBD path (PROC_SLEEPING,
500:     * wake on ANY message i.e. a keystroke, retry the syscall on wake;
501:     * rescheduling needs the trap frame, which is why this stays in the
502:     * dispatcher).  -EPERM (read of a write-only handle, e.g. stdout) maps to
503:     * the POSIX -EBADF. */
504:    long r = sys_object_read((int)arg0, (void *)arg1, (size_t)arg2);
505:    if (r == -EAGAIN && current_process) {
506:      arch_local_irq_disable();
507:      current_process->ipc_target_pid = -1; /* wake on ANY message */
508:      current_process->state = PROC_SLEEPING;
509:      arch_local_irq_enable();
510:      pt_regs_retry_syscall(frame);
511:      return schedule(frame);
512:    }
513:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, (r == -EPERM) ? -EBADF : r);
514:  } break;
515:  case SYS_WRITE: {
516:    /* write(fd, buf, n) ≡ OS1_object_write on the handle.  -EPERM (write of a
517:     * read-only handle, e.g. stdin) maps to the POSIX -EBADF. */
518:    long r = sys_object_write((int)arg0, (const void *)arg1, (size_t)arg2);
519:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, (r == -EPERM) ? -EBADF : r);
520:  } break;
521:  case SYS_EXIT:
522:    sys_exit((int)arg0);
523:    return schedule(frame);
524:  case SYS_GET_TIME:
525:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, sys_get_time());
526:    break;
527:  case SYS_CLOCK_GETTIME:
528:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, sys_clock_gettime((int)arg0));
529:    break;
530:  case SYS_GETPID:
531:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, sys_get_pid());
532:    break;
533:  case SYS_DRAW:
534:    /* Direct draw to the root framebuffer is a display effect: gated by
535:     * CAP_WINDOW (the level that "may draw" — guests included).  Previously
536:     * ungated.  A capability-stripped worker without CAP_WINDOW cannot scribble
537:     * on the screen; machine bypasses. */
538:    if (!proc_has_cap(current_process, CAP_WINDOW)) {
539:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
540:      break;
541:    }
542:    graphics_draw_rect((int)arg0, (int)arg1, (int)arg2, (int)arg3,
543:                       (uint32_t)arg4);
544:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, 0);
545:    break;
546:  case SYS_WINDOW_ENUM: {
547:    /* Read-only window enumeration → struct window_info[] (ASTRA §6.7); ungated
548:     * like SYS_GETPROCS.  The dock /sys/bin/nxui lays out its app list from it.
549:     */
550:    extern long sys_window_enum(struct window_info * ubuf, size_t max);
551:    pt_regs_set_return(
552:        frame, sys_window_enum((struct window_info *)arg0, (size_t)arg1));
553:    break;
554:  }
555:  case SYS_CREATE_WINDOW: {
556:    /* USR-SEC-03 #79: drawing a window needs CAP_WINDOW. */
557:    if (!proc_has_cap(current_process, CAP_WINDOW)) {
558:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
559:      break;
560:    }
561:    /* SCHED-UAF: a process being torn down must not create a NEW window after
562:     * process_terminate already destroyed its windows — it would be orphaned
563:     * (owner dead -> un-closeable).  The killer sets ->dying before the
564:     * teardown. */
565:    if (current_process->dying) {
566:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
567:      break;
568:    }
569:    struct cpu_info *cpu = get_cpu_info();
570:    char *k_title = cpu->syscall_buf;
571:    if (arch_copy_string_from_user(k_title, (const char *)arg4, 64) != 0) {
572:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EFAULT);
573:      break;
574:    }
575:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, compositor_create_window(
576:                                  (int)arg0, (int)arg1, (int)arg2, (int)arg3,
577:                                  k_title, current_process->pid));
578:  } break;
579:  case SYS_WINDOW_DRAW:
580:    compositor_draw_rect((int)arg0, (int)arg1, (int)arg2, (int)arg3, (int)arg4,
581:                         (uint32_t)arg5, current_process->pid);
582:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, 0);
583:    break;
584:  case SYS_WINDOW_WRITE:
585:    /* write text to a window by id (#123) — needs CAP_WINDOW.  Replaces the
586:     * old fd>=100 overload on write(). */
587:    if (!proc_has_cap(current_process, CAP_WINDOW)) {
588:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
589:      break;
590:    }
591:    pt_regs_set_return(
592:        frame, window_text_write((int)arg0, (const char *)arg1, (size_t)arg2));
593:    break;
594:  case SYS_WINDOW_OF_PID: {
595:    /* Read-only: the compositor window id of a pid, or 0 if it has none.
596:     * The shell uses it to tell a windowless (run-in-shell) program from one
597:     * that opened its own window (#123).  No capability needed. */
598:    extern int compositor_get_window_by_pid(int pid);
599:    int w = compositor_get_window_by_pid((int)arg0);
600:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, w > 0 ? w : 0);
601:    break;
602:  }
603:  case SYS_WINDOW_GRID: {
604:    /* Read-only: terminal character grid of a window, packed (cols<<16)|rows.
605:     * A windowed TTY app (kilo) queries this to size itself to the compositor
606:     * font cell instead of assuming a fixed 80x25.  -EINVAL if no such window.
607:     */
608:    extern int compositor_window_grid(int win_id, int *cols, int *rows);
609:    int cols = 0, rows = 0;
610:    if (compositor_window_grid((int)arg0, &cols, &rows) != 0)
611:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EINVAL);
612:    else
613:      pt_regs_set_return(frame,
614:                         ((long)(cols & 0xFFFF) << 16) | (rows & 0xFFFF));
615:    break;
616:  }
617:  case SYS_DISPLAY_INFO: {
618:    /* Read-only: current desktop size, packed (w<<16)|h (GFX-DYN-01). */
619:    extern void compositor_get_size(int *w, int *h);
620:    int w = 0, h = 0;
621:    compositor_get_size(&w, &h);
622:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, ((long)(w & 0xFFFF) << 16) | (h & 0xFFFF));
623:    break;
624:  }
625:  case SYS_SET_DISPLAY_MODE: {
626:    /* GFX-DYN-01: change resolution at runtime; the desktop adapts.  A
627:     * system-level action → needs CAP_WINDOW. */
628:    if (!proc_has_cap(current_process, CAP_WINDOW)) {
629:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
630:      break;
631:    }
632:    extern int gpu_set_mode(int w, int h);
633:    extern void compositor_resize(int w, int h);
634:    extern void compositor_set_native_mode(int w, int h);
635:    int r = gpu_set_mode((int)arg0, (int)arg1);
636:    if (r == 0) {
637:      compositor_set_native_mode((int)arg0,
638:                                 (int)arg1); /* new zoom-100 reference */
639:      compositor_resize((int)arg0, (int)arg1);
640:    }
641:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, r);
642:    break;
643:  }
644:  case SYS_WINDOW_RESIZE: {
645:    /* Resize a window's logical surface.  Needs CAP_WINDOW and ownership
646:     * (owner or machine), mirroring SYS_DESTROY_WINDOW's ABI-04 check. */
647:    if (!proc_has_cap(current_process, CAP_WINDOW)) {
648:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
649:      break;
650:    }
651:    extern int compositor_window_owner(int window_id);
652:    extern int compositor_resize_window(int window_id, int w, int h);
653:    int owner = compositor_window_owner((int)arg0);
654:    if (owner >= 0 && owner != (int)current_process->pid &&
655:        !proc_is_machine(current_process)) {
656:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
657:      break;
658:    }
659:    pt_regs_set_return(
660:        frame, compositor_resize_window((int)arg0, (int)arg1, (int)arg2));
661:    break;
662:  }
663:  case SYS_DISPLAY_POLL: {
664:    /* Apply a pending host display-change in process context (init's supervisor
665:     * loop polls this so the heavy set_mode/realloc never runs in the IRQ
666:     * tick). Machine-level only.  Returns 1 if the desktop was resized, else 0.
667:     */
668:    if (!proc_is_machine(current_process)) {
669:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
670:      break;
671:    }
672:    extern int gpu_poll_events(int *w, int *h);
673:    extern int gpu_set_mode(int w, int h);
674:    extern void compositor_resize(int w, int h);
675:    extern void compositor_set_native_mode(int w, int h);
676:    int w = 0, h = 0;
677:    if (gpu_poll_events(&w, &h) == 1) {
678:      if (gpu_set_mode(w, h) == 0) {
679:        compositor_set_native_mode(w, h);
680:        compositor_resize(w, h);
681:      }
682:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, 1);
683:    } else {
684:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, 0);
685:    }
686:    break;
687:  }
688:  case SYS_SET_STYLE: {
689:    /* Switch the compositor look (Style/Theme/Background).  Needs CAP_WINDOW.
690:     * arg0 = style id, arg1 = theme id, arg2 = bg id; pass -1 to keep. */
691:    if (!proc_has_cap(current_process, CAP_WINDOW)) {
692:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
693:      break;
694:    }
695:    extern int compositor_set_style(int style_id);
696:    extern int compositor_set_theme(int theme_id);
697:    extern int compositor_set_background(int bg_id);
698:    int rc = 0;
699:    /* Publish the change into the registry ON SUCCESS, right here, so
700:     * style.name/theme.color/background.name are the single coherent
701:     * getter for the whole desktop (S-ALIGN): no caller-side "set the
702:     * compositor, then remember to also write the registry" step to
703:     * forget (nxsettings used to skip it, leaving every OTHER app showing
704:     * the stale theme after a GUI change).  owner_pid 0 = system: the
705:     * kernel is the canonical writer of these three keys regardless of
706:     * which process asked for the switch. */
707:    if ((int)arg0 >= 0) {
708:      int r = compositor_set_style((int)arg0);
709:      rc |= r;
710:      if (r == 0 && (int)arg0 < OS1_STYLE_COUNT)
711:        if (registry_set("style.name", os1_style_names[(int)arg0], 0) != 0)
712:        rc |= -EIO; /* applied but NOT persisted: it survives until
713:                     * reboot and then silently reverts, which is
714:                     * worse than failing now */
715:    }
716:    if ((int)arg1 >= 0) {
717:      int r = compositor_set_theme((int)arg1);
718:      rc |= r;
719:      if (r == 0 && (int)arg1 < OS1_THEME_COUNT)
720:        if (registry_set("theme.color", os1_theme_names[(int)arg1], 0) != 0)
721:        rc |= -EIO; /* applied but NOT persisted: it survives until
722:                     * reboot and then silently reverts, which is
723:                     * worse than failing now */
724:    }
725:    if ((int)arg2 >= 0) {
726:      int r = compositor_set_background((int)arg2);
727:      rc |= r;
728:      if (r == 0 && (int)arg2 < OS1_BG_COUNT)
729:        if (registry_set("background.name", os1_bg_names[(int)arg2], 0) != 0)
730:        rc |= -EIO; /* applied but NOT persisted: it survives until
731:                     * reboot and then silently reverts, which is
732:                     * worse than failing now */
733:    }
734:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, rc);
735:    break;
736:  }
737:  case SYS_SET_ZOOM: {
738:    /* Desktop zoom percent (HiDPI/zoom, F2).  Needs CAP_WINDOW. */
739:    if (!proc_has_cap(current_process, CAP_WINDOW)) {
740:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
741:      break;
742:    }
743:    extern int compositor_set_zoom(int percent);
744:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, compositor_set_zoom((int)arg0));
745:    break;
746:  }
747:  case SYS_COMPOSITOR_RENDER:
748:    /* The single compositor-push syscall (the duplicate SYS_FLUSH was retired
749:     * and folded here).  Forcing a global re-render is a display effect: gated
750:     * by CAP_WINDOW, so a capability-stripped worker (spawned without
751:     * CAP_WINDOW) cannot drive the compositor.  Every default preset (incl.
752:     * GUEST) holds CAP_WINDOW, and machine processes bypass — so nothing
753:     * legitimate breaks. */
754:    if (!proc_has_cap(current_process, CAP_WINDOW)) {
755:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
756:      break;
757:    }
758:    compositor_render();
759:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, 0);
760:    break;
761:  case SYS_WINDOW_BLIT:
762:    compositor_blit((int)arg0, (int)arg1, (int)arg2, (int)arg3, (int)arg4,
763:                    (const uint32_t *)arg5, current_process->pid);
764:    /* This process now owns custom pixel content in a window's buffer —
765:     * see struct process.self_rendered (sched.h) for why the own-window-
766:     * first stdout path (window_text_write below) must stop drawing text
767:     * into it from here on.  compositor_blit() already refused the call
768:     * above if the window is not this process's own (or init's), so
769:     * reaching here means the blit legitimately landed on OUR window. */
770:    current_process->self_rendered = 1;
771:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, 0);
772:    break;
773:  case SYS_WINDOW_SET_FLAGS: {
774:    /* Window flags (top-most / hide / click-through) are a property of the
775:     * window: only its owner — or a machine process — may set them, mirroring
776:     * SYS_DESTROY_WINDOW.  Previously ungated, so any process could top-most or
777:     * hide any window.  All legitimate callers (nxui/nxlauncher/notify_srv) set
778:     * flags on their OWN window, so the owner check breaks nothing. */
779:    extern int compositor_window_owner(int window_id);
780:    int fowner = compositor_window_owner((int)arg0);
781:    if (fowner >= 0 && fowner != (int)current_process->pid &&
782:        !proc_is_machine(current_process)) {
783:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
784:      break;
785:    }
786:    compositor_set_window_flags((int)arg0, (int)arg1);
787:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, 0);
788:  } break;
789:  case SYS_DESTROY_WINDOW: {
790:    /* ABI-04: only the window's owner (or a system process) may destroy it.
791:     * Kernel-internal teardown (close button, process exit) calls
792:     * compositor_destroy_window() directly and is unaffected. */
793:    extern int compositor_window_owner(int window_id);
794:    int owner = compositor_window_owner((int)arg0);
795:    if (owner >= 0 && owner != (int)current_process->pid &&
796:        !proc_is_machine(current_process)) {
797:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
798:      break;
799:    }
800:    compositor_destroy_window((int)arg0);
801:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, 0);
802:  } break;
803:  case SYS_SBRK:
804:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, sys_sbrk((intptr_t)arg0));
805:    break;
806:  case SYS_SPAWN: {
807:    /* USR-SEC-03 #79: spawning needs CAP_SPAWN.  A plain spawn yields a full
808:     * PLVL_USER child (clamped to the creator), preserving today's behaviour.
809:     */
810:    if (!proc_has_cap(current_process, CAP_SPAWN)) {
811:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
812:      break;
813:    }
814:    /* #193 hardening: unknown spawn-flag bits are rejected, not ignored —
815:     * the spawn surface must fail closed on semantics it does not know. */
816:    if (((uint32_t)arg3 & ~(uint32_t)SPAWN_FLAGS_ALL) != 0) {
817:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EINVAL);
818:      break;
819:    }
820:    struct cpu_info *cpu = get_cpu_info();
821:    char *k_path = cpu->syscall_buf;
822:    if (arch_copy_string_from_user(k_path, (const char *)arg0, 128) != 0) {
823:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EFAULT);
824:      break;
825:    }
826:    /* Optional argv vector: arg1 = argc, arg2 = user array of char* (#kilo).
827:     * Copy the pointer array and each string into kernel memory before the
828:     * spawn so process_load_elf_args() can place them on the child's stack. */
829:    int argc = (int)arg1;
830:    if (argc < 0)
831:      argc = 0;
832:    if (argc > SPAWN_MAX_ARGS)
833:      argc = SPAWN_MAX_ARGS;
834:    char *kargv[SPAWN_MAX_ARGS];
835:    char *argv_store = NULL;
836:    if (argc > 0) {
837:      void *uptrs[SPAWN_MAX_ARGS];
838:      if (arch_copy_from_user(uptrs, (const void *)arg2,
839:                              (size_t)argc * sizeof(void *)) != 0) {
840:        pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EFAULT);
841:        break;
842:      }
843:      argv_store = kmalloc((size_t)argc * SPAWN_ARG_LEN);
844:      if (!argv_store) {
845:        pt_regs_set_return(frame, -ENOMEM);
846:        break;
847:      }
848:      int bad = 0;
849:      for (int i = 0; i < argc; i++) {
850:        kargv[i] = argv_store + (size_t)i * SPAWN_ARG_LEN;
851:        if (arch_copy_string_from_user(kargv[i], (const char *)uptrs[i],
852:                                       SPAWN_ARG_LEN) != 0) {
853:          bad = 1;
854:          break;
855:        }
856:      }
857:      if (bad) {
858:        kfree(argv_store);
859:        pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EFAULT);
860:        break;
861:      }
862:    }
863:    /* Optional fd redirections (Phase 4 shell `<`/`>`/`>>`/`2>`): arg4 = user
864:     * array of struct spawn_redir, arg5 = count.  Copy them into kernel memory
865:     * so dispatch_spawn can dup the spawner's handles into the child.  Absent
866:     * (count 0) → today's behaviour exactly. */
867:    struct spawn_redir kredir[SPAWN_MAX_REDIR];
868:    int nredir = (int)arg5;
869:    if (nredir < 0)
870:      nredir = 0;
871:    if (nredir > SPAWN_MAX_REDIR) {
872:      if (argv_store)
873:        kfree(argv_store);
874:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EINVAL);
875:      break;
876:    }
877:    if (nredir > 0 &&
878:        arch_copy_from_user(kredir, (const void *)arg4,
879:                            (size_t)nredir * sizeof(struct spawn_redir)) != 0) {
880:      if (argv_store)
881:        kfree(argv_store);
882:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EFAULT);
883:      break;
884:    }
885:    /* arg3 = spawn-mode flags (SPAWN_FLAG_*, caps.h) — nxexec model #193. */
886:    long sret = dispatch_spawn(k_path, PLVL_USER, 0, 0, argc, kargv,
887:                               (uint32_t)arg3, kredir, nredir);
888:    if (argv_store)
889:      kfree(argv_store);
890:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, sret);
891:  } break;
892:  case SYS_SPAWN_CAPS: {
893:    /* spawn_caps(path, level, caps) — restricted spawn.  The requested level
894:     * and caps are clamped monotonically in process_create_caps (never more
895:     * privileged than the creator, never above the level ceiling, never more
896:     * than the creator holds). */
897:    if (!proc_has_cap(current_process, CAP_SPAWN)) {
898:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
899:      break;
900:    }
901:    /* #193 hardening: same strict flag validation as SYS_SPAWN. */
902:    if (((uint32_t)arg3 & ~(uint32_t)SPAWN_FLAGS_ALL) != 0) {
903:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EINVAL);
904:      break;
905:    }
906:    struct cpu_info *cpu = get_cpu_info();
907:    char *k_path = cpu->syscall_buf;
908:    if (arch_copy_string_from_user(k_path, (const char *)arg0, 128) != 0) {
909:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EFAULT);
910:      break;
911:    }
912:    pt_regs_set_return(frame,
913:                       dispatch_spawn(k_path, (uint8_t)arg1, (uint32_t)arg2, 1,
914:                                      0, NULL, (uint32_t)arg3, NULL, 0));
915:  } break;
916:  case SYS_KILL:
917:    /* ABI-04: a process may kill itself or its descendants (orphans are
918:     * re-homed to a live ancestor at reap time, SCHED-DOS-02); SYSTEM/ROOT
919:     * may kill anything (process_terminate still protects SYSTEM targets). */
920:    if (!process_kill_allowed(current_process, (int)arg0)) {
921:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
922:      break;
923:    }
924:    /* External kill of ANOTHER process is window-aware (kill the target + its
925:     * windowless/in-shell descendants, SPARE windowed apps —
926:     * PROCESS-KILL-MODEL). Killing SELF stays single-process, like exit. */
927:    if (current_process && (int)arg0 == (int)current_process->pid) {
928:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, process_terminate((int)arg0));
929:    } else {
930:      process_kill_subtree((int)arg0);
931:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, 0);
932:    }
933:    break;
934:  case SYS_GETPROCS:
935:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, sys_getprocs((void *)arg0, (size_t)arg1));
936:    break;
937:  case SYS_SYSSTATS:
938:    /* OS1_sys_stats(buf, buf_size): one os1_sysstats snapshot (perf §1).
939:     * PRIVILEGED introspection: only ROOT/machine NX services (e.g.
940:     * /sys/bin/nxmemstat) may read the raw stats; USER apps go through the
941:     * service's exposed interface, never this syscall directly. */
942:    if (!current_process || current_process->level > PLVL_ROOT) {
943:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
944:      break;
945:    }
946:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, sys_sysstats((void *)arg0, (size_t)arg1));
947:    break;
948:  case SYS_GET_IDENTITY: {
949:    /* Read-only self-introspection: the caller's own privilege LEVEL and
950:     * capability mask, packed (level<<16)|caps.  Ungated — a process may always
951:     * learn its OWN identity.  Backs OS1_identity()/nxperm and lets userland
952:     * present a level-based view (machine/root/user/guest) without exposing the
953:     * raw capability bits to applications. */
954:    int lvl = current_process ? (int)current_process->level : PLVL_GUEST;
955:    unsigned int cps = current_process ? current_process->caps : 0u;
956:    pt_regs_set_return(frame,
957:                       ((long)(lvl & 0xFF) << 16) | (long)(cps & 0xFFFF));
958:    break;
959:  }
960:  case SYS_YIELD:
961:    return sys_yield(frame);
962:  case SYS_NANOSLEEP:
963:    return sys_nanosleep(frame, arg0);
964:  case SYS_SEND: {
965:    /* ABI-05 RESOLVED: capture the result in a local instead of trying to
966:     * re-read it through the (read-only) argument accessors, so the
967:     * yield-after-successful-send actually happens and the receiver gets
968:     * a chance to run immediately. */
969:    long rc = sys_ipc_send((int)arg0, (void *)arg1);
970:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, rc);
971:    if (rc == 0)
972:      return schedule(frame);
973:    break;
974:  }
975:  case SYS_RECV: {
976:    /* IPC-01: when sys_ipc_recv() blocks it arms a syscall retry (PC rewound
977:     * to the SVC/SYSCALL).  The return value must NOT be written then — on
978:     * aarch64 x0 is both the return register and arg0, so writing it would
979:     * clobber src_pid for the re-executed syscall (the receiver re-armed
980:     * with src_pid=0 and slept forever on a non-empty queue).
981:     * NOTE(IPC-02): still unconditionally schedules — a delivered message
982:     * costs an extra yield. */
983:    /* No current task means the scheduler is between reaping the previous one
984:     * and picking the next; sys_ipc_recv walks current_process->msg_queue
985:     * unguarded, so it must not be entered in that window.  aarch64's EL0
986:     * vector already refuses to continue in this state (it panics by name);
987:     * amd64 has no such guard, which is why this check lives here, in the
988:     * shared dispatcher, rather than in one arch's entry path. */
989:    if (!current_process) {
990:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -ESRCH);
991:      return schedule(frame);
992:    }
993:    long rc = sys_ipc_recv((int)arg0, (void *)arg1);
994:    if (rc == IPC_RECV_RETRY)
995:      pt_regs_retry_syscall(frame); /* the LIVE frame — see sys_ipc_recv */
996:    else
997:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, rc);
998:    return schedule(frame);
999:  }
1000:  case SYS_TRY_RECV:
1001:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, sys_ipc_try_recv((int)arg0, (void *)arg1));
1002:    break;
1003:  case SYS_SET_FOCUS:
1004:    /* ABI-04 / USR-SEC-03 #79: claiming focus needs CAP_WINDOW; a process may
1005:     * only claim focus for ITSELF (every userland caller does
1006:     * set_focus(get_pid())); redirecting input to/from another PID — i.e.
1007:     * keystroke stealing — needs machine level. */
1008:    if (!proc_has_cap(current_process, CAP_WINDOW)) {
1009:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
1010:      break;
1011:    }
1012:    if ((int)arg0 != (int)current_process->pid &&
1013:        !proc_is_machine(current_process)) {
1014:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
1015:      break;
1016:    }
1017:    sched_set_focus_pid(
1018:        (int)arg0); /* push the focus hint to the scheduler (#67) */
1019:    /* Caret follows the input window: clear it off whoever just lost focus. */
1020:    {
1021:      extern void compositor_focus_changed(int new_pid);
1022:      compositor_focus_changed((int)arg0);
1023:    }
1024:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, 0);
1025:    break;
1026:  case SYS_WAIT: {
1027:    /* Ambient wait, arg1 = OPTIONAL user int* for the exit status.
1028:     *
1029:     * It used to always pass NULL, on the reasoning that the capability path
1030:     * (SYS_OBJECT_WAIT) carries the status.  Phase 9b invalidated that: once a
1031:     * status OUTLIVES its process, the capability can no longer be acquired for
1032:     * a dead pid (acquisition requires a live process), so the caller ALWAYS
1033:     * lands here — and the status was discarded exactly in the case it was
1034:     * finally available.  Passing NULL stays legal, so existing callers that
1035:     * only test the return value are unaffected. */
1036:    int wcode = 0;
1037:    long wr = process_wait((int)arg0, &wcode);
1038:    /* The (void) cast that used to be here did not suppress the attribute, it
1039:     * only made the omission look deliberate.  A bad status pointer is -EFAULT
1040:     * under POSIX, not a successful wait whose status silently never arrived. */
1041:    if (arg1 && wr >= 0 &&
1042:        arch_copy_to_user((void *)arg1, &wcode, sizeof(wcode)) != 0)
1043:      wr = -EFAULT;
1044:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, wr);
1045:  } break;
1046:  case SYS_REGISTRY:
1047:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, sys_registry((int)arg0, (const char *)arg1,
1048:                                           (char *)arg2, (size_t)arg3));
1049:    break;
1050:  case SYS_STAT: {
1051:    /*
1052:     * Path metadata in ONE round trip: type + size.
1053:     *
1054:     * Why this exists (R1-fix).  R1 removed the ambient FS verbs and composed
1055:     * their users over the object layer, which was right for the DATA path but
1056:     * had two costs the composition could not absorb:
1057:     *
1058:     *  - CORRECTNESS.  opendir() and stat() both relied on the invariant "the
1059:     *    list primitive succeeds ONLY on a directory".  Once a READ handle could
1060:     *    be acquired on any path, object_read on a FILE returned its CONTENT, so
1061:     *    opendir() succeeded on regular files — the file manager then marked
1062:     *    every file a directory and double-clicking one tried to chdir into it
1063:     *    ("Cannot open directory").  The type distinction has to come from the
1064:     *    kernel, which is the only place that knows it.
1065:     *  - COST.  The size probe became handle_create + OBJ_CTL_STAT + close:
1066:     *    three syscalls and two path resolutions for one number, on the path
1067:     *    every fopen() takes.
1068:     *
1069:     * This is a NET REDUCTION even though it adds a number: it replaces three
1070:     * retired verbs and the three-call dance, and it duplicates nothing — it
1071:     * asks the same VFS the object layer asks.
1072:     */
1073:    /* Path copies go in the per-CPU scratch buffer, per this file's own rule
1074:     * ("cpu->syscall_buf is used for path/title copies; only one such copy is
1075:     * in flight per CPU"), not on the kernel stack. */
1076:    char *k_path = get_cpu_info()->syscall_buf;
1077:    if (arch_copy_string_from_user(k_path, (const char *)arg0, 128) != 0) {
1078:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EFAULT);
1079:      break;
1080:    }
1081:    char *resolved_path = k_path + 128; /* same 2 KiB scratch, second slot */
1082:    vfs_resolve_path(k_path, resolved_path, 128);
1083:    struct vfs_stat vst;
1084:    if (vfs_stat(resolved_path, &vst) != 0) {
1085:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -ENOENT);
1086:      break;
1087:    }
1088:    struct abi_stat ast;
1089:    memset(&ast, 0, sizeof(ast));
1090:    ast.size = vst.size;
1091:    ast.type = vst.type; /* ABI_S_TYPE_* match VFS_TYPE_* by value */
1092:    if (arch_copy_to_user((void *)arg1, &ast, sizeof(ast)) != 0) {
1093:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EFAULT);
1094:      break;
1095:    }
1096:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, 0);
1097:  } break;
1098:  case SYS_SET_FONT:
1099:    /* Replacing the GLOBAL system font is a desktop-wide display change (it
1100:     * affects every window): same capability gate as set_style/set_zoom
1101:     * (CAP_WINDOW).  Previously ungated — any process could restyle the
1102:     * desktop. */
1103:    if (!proc_has_cap(current_process, CAP_WINDOW)) {
1104:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EPERM);
1105:      break;
1106:    }
1107:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, sys_set_font((void *)arg0, (size_t)arg1));
1108:    break;
1109:  case SYS_CHDIR: {
1110:    char k_path[128];
1111:    if (arch_copy_string_from_user(k_path, (const char *)arg0, 128) != 0) {
1112:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EFAULT);
1113:      break;
1114:    }
1115:    char resolved_path[128];
1116:    vfs_resolve_path(k_path, resolved_path, 128);
1117:
1118:    /* Verify it exists and is a directory. */
1119:    struct vfs_stat st;
1120:    if (vfs_stat(resolved_path, &st) != 0) {
1121:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -ENOENT);
1122:    } else if (st.type != VFS_TYPE_DIR) {
1123:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -ENOTDIR);
1124:    } else {
1125:      strncpy(current_process->cwd, resolved_path, 128);
1126:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, 0);
1127:    }
1128:  } break;
1129:  case SYS_GETCWD: {
1130:    size_t size = (size_t)arg1;
1131:    if (arch_copy_to_user((void *)arg0, current_process->cwd, size) != 0) {
1132:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, -EFAULT);
1133:    } else {
1134:      pt_regs_set_return(frame, 0);
1135:    }
1136:  } break;
1137:  case SYS_PORT_SEND_CAPS:
1138:    /* port send carrying capabilities; see sys_port_send_caps() for why a
1139:     * service found by NAME must not need its pid to receive rights. */
1140:    pt_regs_set_return(frame,
1141:                       sys_port_send_caps((int)arg0, (const void *)arg1,
1142:                                          (const int *)arg2, (int)arg3));
1143:    break;
1144:  case SYS_PIPE:
1145:    /* pipe(int fds[2]) → OBJ_TYPE_PIPE; installs read+write ends in the caller's
1146:     * handle table (fds[0]=read, fds[1]=write).  The shell wires `cmd | cmd` by
1147:     * dup'ing the ends into the children's fd 0/1 (the same spawn-redir path). */
1148:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, sys_pipe((int *)arg0));
1149:    break;
1150:  /* --- Object / capability ABI (ASTRA §6.1/6.2/6.5, kernel/object.h) ---
1151:   * The real capability layer: unforgeable per-process handles to refcounted
1152:   * kernel objects with separable/attenuable rights.  User pointers (path,
1153:   * buf) are validated inside each backend via arch_copy_*_user. */
1154:  case SYS_HANDLE_CREATE:
1155:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, sys_handle_create((int)arg0, (const char *)arg1,
1156:                                                (uint32_t)arg2, (int)arg3));
1157:    break;
1158:  case SYS_HANDLE_DUP:
1159:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, sys_handle_dup((int)arg0, (uint32_t)arg1));
1160:    break;
1161:  case SYS_HANDLE_CLOSE:
1162:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, sys_handle_close((int)arg0));
1163:    break;
1164:  case SYS_CAP_QUERY:
1165:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, sys_cap_query((int)arg0));
1166:    break;
1167:  case SYS_CAP_GRANT:
1168:    pt_regs_set_return(frame,
1169:                       sys_cap_grant((int)arg0, (int)arg1, (uint32_t)arg2));
1170:    break;
1171:  case SYS_OBJECT_READ:
1172:    pt_regs_set_return(frame,
1173:                       sys_object_read((int)arg0, (void *)arg1, (size_t)arg2));
1174:    break;
1175:  case SYS_OBJECT_WRITE:
1176:    pt_regs_set_return(
1177:        frame, sys_object_write((int)arg0, (const void *)arg1, (size_t)arg2));
1178:    break;
1179:  case SYS_OBJECT_WAIT:
1180:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, sys_object_wait((int)arg0, (long)arg1));
1181:    break;
1182:  case SYS_OBJECT_CTL:
1183:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, sys_object_ctl((int)arg0, (int)arg1, (long)arg2));
1184:    break;
1185:  default:
1186:    pr_warn("Unknown syscall: %ld\n", syscall_num);
1187:    pt_regs_set_return(frame, -ENOSYS);
1188:    break;
1189:  }
1190:
1191:  return frame;
1192:}

1194:/*
1195: * sys_get_time - return monotonic time in milliseconds.
1196: *
1197: * Derived from mono_ns() (the real-time hardware-counter clock, docs/
1198: * TIMER-MODEL.md), so it is accurate on BOTH arches — amd64 no longer returns
1199: * the jiffies*1000 stub (ARCH-03 retired for the real-time path).
1200: *
1201: * Locking: none.  IRQ context: no.
1202: */
1203:long sys_get_time(void) { return (long)(mono_ns() / 1000000ULL); }
1204:
1205:/*
1206: * sys_clock_gettime - Tier 3 userland clock (SYS_CLOCK_GETTIME).
1207: *
1208: * Returns a 64-bit nanosecond value directly (both arches return 64 bits):
1209: *   clk == 0 (MONOTONIC)  : mono_ns() — monotonic ns since boot.
1210: *   clk == 1 (PROCESS_CPU): the caller's consumed CPU time in real ns.
1211: * Any other clock id falls back to MONOTONIC. This is the minimal seL4-style
1212: * mechanism; POSIX clock_gettime() is built on top in <time.h>. Capability
1213: * timer OBJECTS (arm-and-notify) are issue #135.
1214: */
1215:long sys_clock_gettime(int clk) {
1216:  if (clk == 1) {
1217:    struct process *p = current_process;
1218:    return p ? (long)timer_counts_to_ns(p->cpu_time_counts) : 0;
1219:  }
1220:  return (long)mono_ns();
1221:}
1222:
1223:/* Global monotonic tick counter (drivers/timer.c / platform.c). */
1224:extern volatile uint64_t jiffies;
1225:
1226:/*
1227: * proc_sleep_wake - per-process sleep timer callback (fired by the owning
1228: * core's tick when the coarse deadline is reached). Makes the sleeper runnable
1229: * again; it will re-run sys_nanosleep (retry), test mono_ns() >= wake_ns, and
1230: * either return (deadline reached) or re-arm and sleep again (woken a tick
1231: * early). Runs under that CPU's timer_lock; enqueue_task takes only a per-CPU
1232: * sched_lock (lock order timer_lock > per-CPU sched_lock — no inversion).
1233: */
1234:static void proc_sleep_wake(void *data) {
1235:  struct process *p = (struct process *)data;
1236:  if (p && p->state == PROC_SLEEPING)
1237:    enqueue_task(p);
1238:}
1239:
1240:/*
1241: * sys_nanosleep - block the caller for `ns` nanoseconds (POSIX nanosleep core,
1242: * Tier 3 of docs/TIMER-MODEL.md).
1243: *
1244: * The deadline is stored as an ABSOLUTE real-time instant (p->wake_ns, mono_ns
1245: * base) on first entry, so the sleep recovers lost time: the per-CPU software
1246: * timer is only a coarse jiffies-edge trigger, and the precise wake condition
1247: * is mono_ns() >= wake_ns. Retry-based like the blocking read — re-entered on
1248: * each wakeup. If the coarse timer fires a tick early, mono_ns() is still short
1249: * of wake_ns, so we re-arm and sleep again; a genuine deadline returns 0.
1250: */
1251:static struct pt_regs *sys_nanosleep(struct pt_regs *regs, uint64_t ns) {
1252:  struct process *p = current_process;
1253:  if (!p || ns == 0) {
1254:    pt_regs_set_return(regs, 0);
1255:    return regs;
1256:  }
1257:  if (p->wake_ns == 0)
1258:    p->wake_ns = mono_ns() + ns; /* absolute real-time deadline */
1259:
1260:  uint64_t now = mono_ns();
1261:  if (now >= p->wake_ns) {
1262:    p->wake_ns = 0;
1263:    timer_del(&p->sleep_timer); /* cancel if somehow still pending */
1264:    pt_regs_set_return(regs, 0);
1265:    return regs;
1266:  }
1267:
1268:  /* (Re)arm the coarse wheel trigger at the deadline's tick. Rounding up by one
1269:   * tick keeps us from busy-spinning if mono_ns() is just shy of wake_ns. */
1270:  if (!timer_pending(&p->sleep_timer)) {
1271:    uint64_t ticks = (p->wake_ns - now + (NS_PER_TICK - 1)) / NS_PER_TICK;
1272:    if (ticks == 0)
1273:      ticks = 1;
1274:    timer_setup(&p->sleep_timer, proc_sleep_wake, p);
1275:    timer_add(&p->sleep_timer, jiffies + ticks);
1276:  }
1277:
1278:  arch_local_irq_disable();
1279:  p->state = PROC_SLEEPING;
1280:  arch_local_irq_enable();
1281:  pt_regs_retry_syscall(regs);
1282:  return schedule(regs);
1283:}
1284:
1285:/* YIELD_SPIN_BUDGET: how many yield() calls a process may make within a single
1286: * tick (10 ms at HZ=100) before it is treated as busy-spinning. A program doing
1287: * real work between yields never approaches this; a `while(1) yield()` spinner
1288: * (an unoptimised app, or an old-style poll loop) trips it and is descheduled
1289: * to the next tick, capping its duty cycle so it cannot keep a core at 100% and
1290: * freeze the system. The bounded focus boost (process.c) stops a focused
1291: * CPU-hog from STARVING others; this stops a yield-spinner from SATURATING a
1292: * core. */
1293:#define YIELD_SPIN_BUDGET 64
1294:
1295:/*
1296: * sys_yield - cooperative yield with a per-process anti-spin throttle
1297: * (SYS_YIELD, docs/TIMER-MODEL.md §4).
1298: *
1299: * Normally just reschedules (gives up the rest of the slice). But it counts
1300: * yields within the current tick; once a process exceeds YIELD_SPIN_BUDGET it
1301: * is busy-spinning on yield(), so instead of an immediate reschedule it is put
1302: * to sleep until the next tick via its per-process timer (sleep_timer) — the
1303: * same mechanism nanosleep uses. The spinner therefore relinquishes the core
1304: * for a full tick, dropping its CPU duty cycle to near zero. The counter resets
1305: * each tick (and after a throttle), so legitimate cooperative yielding is
1306: * untouched.
1307: *
1308: * Note: this does NOT touch wake_ns (the nanosleep deadline) — a process cannot
1309: * be both yielding and nanosleeping. On wake the yield() simply returns.
1310: */
1311:static struct pt_regs *sys_yield(struct pt_regs *regs) {
1312:  struct process *p = current_process;
1313:  if (!p)
1314:    return schedule(regs);
1315:
1316:  if (p->yield_jiffy != jiffies) {
1317:    p->yield_jiffy = jiffies;
1318:    p->yield_count = 0;
1319:  }
1320:
1321:  if (++p->yield_count > YIELD_SPIN_BUDGET) {
1322:    /* Busy-spinning on yield() this tick — throttle to a 1-tick per-process
1323:     * timed sleep. Reset the budget; it refills next tick on wake. */
1324:    p->yield_count = 0;
1325:    /* TIMER-UAF-01: only (re)arm when the per-process timer is NOT already
1326:     * queued — exactly like sys_nanosleep. The sleeper can have been
1327:     * force-woken by a non-timer path (kernel_ipc_send flips
1328:     * PROC_SLEEPING->READY WITHOUT cancelling sleep_timer, process.c) with its
1329:     * timer still linked; calling timer_setup()/INIT_LIST_HEAD on that
1330:     * still-linked node re-initialises a live list entry and corrupts the
1331:     * per-CPU timer_list, later faulting in kernel_timer_tick() as a double
1332:     * list_del. If it is already pending, the existing 1-tick trigger will wake
1333:     * us, so we just re-sleep. */
1334:    if (!timer_pending(&p->sleep_timer)) {
1335:      timer_setup(&p->sleep_timer, proc_sleep_wake, p);
1336:      timer_add(&p->sleep_timer, jiffies + 1);
1337:    }
1338:    arch_local_irq_disable();
1339:    p->state = PROC_SLEEPING;
1340:    arch_local_irq_enable();
1341:  }
1342:
1343:  return schedule(regs);
1344:}
1345:
1346:/*
1347: * sys_get_pid - return the PID of the calling process.
1348: *
1349: * Returns 0 if current_process is NULL (should not happen in normal operation).
1350: * Locking: none (current_process is CPU-local during a syscall).
1351: * IRQ context: no.
1352: */
1353:long sys_get_pid(void) {
1354:  return current_process ? (long)current_process->pid : 0;
1355:}
1356:
1357:/*
1358: * sys_exit - terminate the calling process.
1359: *
1360: * Calls process_terminate(current_process->pid), which marks the process
1361: * PROC_ZOMBIE and returns immediately (it cannot free its own kernel stack).
1362: * The caller (case 93 in kernel_syscall_dispatcher) MUST call schedule()
1363: * after sys_exit() to switch away from this process; that schedule() call
1364: * auto-reaps the zombie via the per-CPU deferred-free stack.
1365: *
1366: * Locking: delegates to process_terminate() which acquires sched_lock.
1367: * IRQ context: no.
1368: * NOTE(SCHED-03, mitigated): zombies no longer accumulate — schedule()
1369: *          reaps them without requiring a process_wait() caller.
1370: */
1371:void sys_exit(int status) {
1372:  if (current_process) {
1373:    pr_debug("PID %d exiting with status %d\n", current_process->pid,
1374:             status); /* hot path: demoted (perf §1) */
1375:    current_process->exit_code = status & 0xff; /* Phase 2: collectable by a waiter */
1376:    current_process->exited = 1;                 /* voluntary exit (not killed) */
1377:    /* Nothing to propagate to: the caller is exiting.  Reported so a failure
1378:     * to tear down is visible instead of leaving a process that believes it
1379:     * exited still in the pool. */
1380:    if (process_terminate(current_process->pid) != 0)
1381:      pr_err("exit: process_terminate(%d) failed\n", current_process->pid);
1382:  }
1383:}

@@@ kernel/core/timer.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/core/timer.c
3: * Generic Timer Logic (Jiffies, Software Timers, Scheduling)
4: *
5: * This file is the arch-agnostic timer layer.  It owns:
6: *   - kernel_timer_tick(): the central per-tick ISR hook called by the
7: *     arch-specific timer IRQ handler (aarch64: drivers/timer/timer.c;
8: *     amd64: arch/amd64/platform/platform.c via PIT/APIC).
9: *   - A software timer list (struct timer), run on CPU 0 every tick.
10: *   - Compositor pacing: fires compositor_tick() at ~30 FPS on CPU 0.
11: *   - Arch-specific per-CPU timer init via __attribute__((weak)) stubs
12: *     that each arch overrides.
13: *
14: * Layering:
15: *   arch IRQ -> kernel_timer_tick() -> schedule()
16: *                                   -> software timer callbacks (CPU 0)
17: *                                   -> compositor_tick()          (CPU 0)
18: *
19: * Key invariants:
20: *   - jiffies is incremented only by CPU 0 to avoid SMP races; all other
21: *     CPUs still go through kernel_timer_tick() for preemption but do not
22: *     touch jiffies or the software timer list.
23: *   - timer_lock protects the timer_list linked list; callbacks are invoked
24: *     while timer_lock is held — callbacks must not try to acquire timer_lock.
25: *   - The weak timer_handler() stub returns regs unchanged; per-arch overrides
26: *     may perform additional bookkeeping (e.g. EOI).
27: *
28: * Known issues:
29: *   ARCH-03  (W2 STUB) timer_get_us() (defined in the arch platform files)
30: *            returns jiffies*1000 on amd64 — a "dummy for now" value, not a
31: *            real microsecond clock.  sys_get_time() is therefore inaccurate
32: *            on amd64.  aarch64 uses the arch counter and is accurate.
33: *            (This defect is in the arch platform file, not in this file;
34: *            cited here because kernel_timer_tick drives jiffies.)
35: */
36:#include <drivers/timer.h>
37:#include <kernel/arch.h>
38:#include <kernel/cpu.h>
39:#include <kernel/list.h>
40:#include <kernel/printk.h>
41:#include <kernel/sched.h>
42:#include <kernel/spinlock.h>
43:
44:/* USB has no IRQ wired (polled HCDs); the tick drives HID input on CPU 0 so it
45: * works even when no virtio/PS-2 interrupt ever fires (e.g. UTM, real HW). */
46:extern void usb_hid_poll(void);
47:extern volatile int panic_flag;
48:/* NOTE(SCHED-STACK-ISO): the compositor render is no longer driven from the
49: * timer tick — it runs in process context (init -> SYS_COMPOSITOR_RENDER) so it
50: * never nests on an interrupted task's kernel stack.  compositor_interval /
51: * COMPOSITOR_TARGET_FPS / the compositor_tick() hook were removed here with that
52: * change (kernel/graphics/compositor.c still defines compositor_tick() for the
53: * public SYS path, it is just not called from the IRQ any more). */
54:
55:/* Software timers are PER-CPU: each CPU owns a timer_list + timer_lock in its
56: * struct cpu_info (kernel/cpu.h), fired by that CPU in kernel_timer_tick against
57: * the global jiffies clock. timer_add() arms on the current CPU and the timer
58: * records its owner CPU (t->cpu) so timer_del() removes it from the right list.
59: * This keeps a process's sleep timer on the core that holds it: local wakeup, no
60: * cross-CPU dependency and no global timer-lock contention. */
61:
62:/* jiffies and timer_freq are defined in drivers/timer/timer.c for AArch64
63: * or in arch/amd64/platform/platform.c for AMD64. */
64:extern volatile uint64_t jiffies;
65:
66:/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
67: * Real-time reference (docs/TIMER-MODEL.md §1)
68: *
69: * mono_ns() is the single source of truth: monotonic nanoseconds since boot,
70: * computed from the free-running hardware counter (CNTVCT on aarch64, TSC on
71: * amd64) and its frequency, both arch HAL primitives. jiffies is a cheap
72: * integer view that CPU 0 reconciles against mono_ns() every tick so dropped
73: * ticks are recovered (Tier 1).
74: *
75: * Only the EPOCH (clk_boot_count) is captured once, lazily, on the first call.
76: * The frequency is re-read fresh every call (a cheap inline counter accessor),
77: * deliberately NOT latched: on amd64 arch_timer_get_freq() returns a 1 GHz
78: * fallback until the TSC is calibrated, and latching that stale value would
79: * permanently skew the clock. Reading it live means the clock self-corrects the
80: * instant calibration publishes the real frequency. In practice the first call
81: * already happens after calibration (it runs in early arch init, before any
82: * scheduling or timer tick), so no skew is observed.
83: * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
84:static uint64_t clk_boot_count;
85:static volatile int clk_ready;
86:
87:/* timer_counts_to_ns - convert a hardware-counter delta to nanoseconds.
88: *
89: * The single place that scales counter units to ns: counts * 1e9 / freq via a
90: * 128-bit intermediate (counts * 1e9 needs > 64 bits within minutes). Backed by
91: * __udivti3/__multi3 in kernel/lib/math.c (no libgcc in this -nostdlib build).
92: * Used by mono_ns() and by the per-process CPU-time read path, which accumulates
93: * raw counts in the scheduler hot path and converts only when queried. */
94:uint64_t timer_counts_to_ns(uint64_t counts) {
95:  uint64_t freq = arch_timer_get_freq();
96:  if (freq == 0)
97:    freq = 1; /* guard div-by-zero before any frequency source is up */
98:  return (uint64_t)(((__uint128_t)counts * NSEC_PER_SEC) / freq);
99:}
100:
101:uint64_t mono_ns(void) {
102:  if (!clk_ready) {
103:    clk_boot_count = arch_timer_get_count();
104:    clk_ready = 1;
105:  }
106:  return timer_counts_to_ns(arch_timer_get_count() - clk_boot_count);
107:}
108:
109:uint64_t timer_get_ns(void) { return mono_ns(); }
110:
111:/*
112: * timer_percpu_tick - Tier 2 per-CPU clock accounting + rearm (HAL-driven).
113: *
114: * One arch-neutral routine replaces the previously duplicated per-arch drift
115: * logic (aarch64 timer_handler, amd64 idt.c). Everything is expressed in
116: * HARDWARE COUNTER units via the HAL timer primitives:
117: *   1. interval = freq/HZ; accumulate the freq%HZ remainder in tick_error_acc
118: *      and add one extra count when it crosses HZ (long-term-rate exact).
119: *   2. Advance cpu->next_tick_target by the corrected interval.
120: *   3. Catch-up clamp: if the target already fell behind the live counter
121: *      (ticks lost to IRQ latency / a long critical section), reset to
122: *      now + interval — the per-CPU "compare against real time to recover lost
123: *      time" rule, instead of replaying a burst.
124: *   4. Reprogram the compare via arch_timer_set_compare(): a real reprogram on
125: *      one-shot timers (aarch64 CNTV_CVAL), a no-op on periodic timers (amd64
126: *      LAPIC), so this serves both arches unchanged.
127: *
128: * Locking: touches only this CPU's cpu_info; no lock. IRQ context: YES.
129: */
130:void timer_percpu_tick(struct cpu_info *cpu) {
131:  uint64_t freq = arch_timer_get_freq();
132:  uint64_t interval = freq / HZ;
133:  uint64_t remainder = freq % HZ;
134:
135:  cpu->tick_error_acc += remainder;
136:  if (cpu->tick_error_acc >= HZ) {
137:    interval += 1;
138:    cpu->tick_error_acc -= HZ;
139:  }
140:
141:  cpu->next_tick_target += interval;
142:  uint64_t now = arch_timer_get_count();
143:  if (cpu->next_tick_target <= now)
144:    cpu->next_tick_target = now + interval;
145:
146:  arch_timer_set_compare(cpu->next_tick_target);
147:}
148:
149:/*
150: * timer_percpu_arm - seed this CPU's tick schedule on timer bring-up.
151: *
152: * Sets next_tick_target one interval out from the live counter, clears the
153: * fractional accumulator, and programs the first compare via the HAL. Called
154: * once per CPU from the arch per-CPU timer init (aarch64 timer_init_percpu,
155: * amd64 lapic_timer_setup); the arch path still owns enabling the timer and
156: * unmasking its IRQ.
157: */
158:void timer_percpu_arm(struct cpu_info *cpu) {
159:  uint64_t freq = arch_timer_get_freq();
160:  cpu->next_tick_target = arch_timer_get_count() + freq / HZ;
161:  cpu->tick_error_acc = 0;
162:  arch_timer_set_compare(cpu->next_tick_target);
163:}
164:
165:/* Weak stubs for arch-specific timer functions (can be overridden) */
166:/*
167: * timer_init_percpu - per-CPU timer hardware init (weak stub).
168: *
169: * Each arch overrides this to program its local timer (e.g. aarch64 CNTV_CTL,
170: * amd64 LAPIC timer).  The weak no-op is used when no arch override is linked.
171: *
172: * IRQ context: no — called once from the per-CPU boot path with IRQs off.
173: */
174:__attribute__((weak)) void timer_init_percpu(void) {}
175:
176:/*
177: * timer_handler - arch-specific timer IRQ hook (weak stub).
178: *
179: * Called from the arch timer IRQ handler *before* kernel_timer_tick().
180: * Allows arch code to perform EOI or counter reprogramming.  The weak stub
181: * is a pass-through that returns regs unchanged.
182: *
183: * IRQ context: yes — runs inside the timer interrupt.
184: * Returns: the (possibly modified) pt_regs pointer.
185: */
186:__attribute__((weak)) struct pt_regs *timer_handler(struct pt_regs *regs) {
187:  return regs;
188:}
189:
190:/*
191: * kernel_timer_tick - central per-tick entry point called from the timer IRQ.
192: *
193: * Called on every CPU on every timer interrupt.  Responsibilities:
194: *   1. Halt this CPU immediately if another CPU has set panic_flag.
195: *   2. Increment cpu->tick_count (per-CPU; no lock needed).
196: *   3. CPU 0 only: increment the global jiffies counter.
197: *   4. CPU 0 only: fire expired software timers under timer_lock.
198: *   5. CPU 0 only: call compositor_tick() every compositor_interval ticks.
199: *   6. All CPUs: invoke schedule(regs) for preemptive multitasking.
200: *
201: * Locking: acquires timer_lock (irqsave) around the software timer walk on
202: *          CPU 0; no other locks held on entry.
203: * IRQ context: yes — called directly from the architecture timer IRQ handler.
204: * Returns: the pt_regs pointer returned by schedule() (may differ from regs
205: *          if a context switch occurs).
206: */
207:struct pt_regs *kernel_timer_tick(struct pt_regs *regs) {
208:  /* Halt this CPU if another CPU panicked */
209:  if (panic_flag) {
210:    arch_timer_control(0);
211:    arch_cpu_halt();
212:  }
213:
214:  struct cpu_info *cpu = get_cpu_info();
215:  cpu->tick_count++;
216:
217:  /* Tier 1 — global clock (docs/TIMER-MODEL.md §2): only CPU 0 writes jiffies
218:   * (no SMP write race), and instead of a blind ++ it reconciles jiffies with
219:   * real time. If ticks were dropped (IRQ latency, a long critical section, a
220:   * CPU-bound focused task), 'expected' jumps ahead and jiffies catches up in
221:   * one step. The guard keeps it monotonic; steady state advances by exactly 1
222:   * per tick, so normal behaviour is unchanged. */
223:  if (cpu->cpu_id == 0) {
224:    uint64_t expected = mono_ns() / NS_PER_TICK;
225:    if (expected > jiffies)
226:      jiffies = expected;
227:  }
228:
229:  /* Fire THIS CPU's expired software timers — every CPU, against the global
230:   * jiffies clock — so a process that slept on this core is woken here, locally.
231:   * Callbacks run inside this CPU's timer_lock and must not call timer_add/_del
232:   * or anything that re-acquires it. */
233:  {
234:    struct timer *t, *tmp;
235:    uint64_t tflags;
236:    spin_lock_irqsave(&cpu->timer_lock, &tflags);
237:    list_for_each_entry_safe(t, tmp, &cpu->timer_list, list) {
238:      if (jiffies >= t->expires) {
239:        list_del(&t->list);
240:        t->pending = false;
241:        t->cpu = -1;
242:        if (t->callback)
243:          t->callback(t->data);
244:      }
245:    }
246:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&cpu->timer_lock, tflags);
247:  }
248:
249:  /* CPU 0 only: input polling + compositor. */
250:  if (cpu->cpu_id == 0) {
251:    /* Dispatch queued raw input events here (bottom-half): the virtio/ps2
252:     * input IRQs only enqueue, so they never take compositor_lock or mutate
253:     * the window-list from IRQ context (#68/#194).  Runs before the render so
254:     * this tick reflects the freshest input. */
255:    extern void input_drain(void);
256:    input_drain();
257:
258:    /* Poll USB HID every tick (CPU 0): keyboard events feed the evdev buffer,
259:     * pointer motion goes straight to the compositor. Cheap when idle (just an
260:     * event-ring head check per device). */
261:    usb_hid_poll();
262:
263:    /* SCHED-STACK-ISO (ASTRA DIR-02, "compositor render in userspace"): the
264:     * heavy compositor render is NO LONGER driven from here.  Running it from
265:     * the timer IRQ nested it on whatever task's kernel stack CPU0 interrupted;
266:     * its deep call chain then smashed a live frame — on amd64 a syscall's
267:     * current_process spill (the click/nanosleep panic), on aarch64 the
268:     * callee-saved base register restored across timer_handler, faulting the
269:     * current_chip->end() EOI at a NULL deref.  The render now runs in PROCESS
270:     * context: init drives it via SYS_COMPOSITOR_RENDER (flush()) in its
271:     * supervisor loop, on init's own kernel stack — never nested on an
272:     * interrupted task.  Input is still dispatched here (input_drain above), but
273:     * that path is shallow and takes no deep call chain. */
274:  }
275:
276:  /* Call Scheduler for Preemption */
277:  return schedule(regs);
278:}
279:
280:/*
281: * timer_setup - initialise a struct timer before first use.
282: *
283: * Sets the callback, opaque data pointer, pending=false, and initialises the
284: * embedded list_head.  Must be called before timer_add().
285: *
286: * Locking: none — caller owns t exclusively at this point.
287: * IRQ context: safe (no locks taken, no shared state written).
288: */
289:/* Software timer management */
290:void timer_setup(struct timer *t, timer_callback_t callback, void *data) {
291:  INIT_LIST_HEAD(&t->list);
292:  t->callback = callback;
293:  t->data = data;
294:  t->pending = false;
295:  t->cpu = -1; /* not armed on any CPU yet */
296:}
297:
298:/*
299: * timer_add - schedule a software timer to fire at tick 'expires'.
300: *
301: * Adds t to the tail of timer_list.  'expires' is an absolute jiffies value;
302: * use (jiffies + delay_ticks) to express a relative delay.
303: * The timer will fire on the next kernel_timer_tick() on CPU 0 after
304: * jiffies >= expires.
305: *
306: * Locking: acquires timer_lock (irqsave) — safe to call from any context
307: *          including IRQ handlers, but NOT from inside a timer callback
308: *          (would deadlock on timer_lock).
309: * Side effects: sets t->pending = true.
310: */
311:void timer_add(struct timer *t, uint64_t expires) {
312:  /* Defence in depth (TIMER-UAF-01): never link the same node twice.  If the
313:   * timer is somehow still queued — a re-arm of a not-yet-fired timer, or a
314:   * caller that bypassed timer_pending() — unlink it from its current CPU
315:   * FIRST.  A double list_add_tail() (or a timer_setup()/INIT_LIST_HEAD on a
316:   * still-linked node) corrupts the per-CPU timer_list and later crashes
317:   * kernel_timer_tick() with a double list_del (write to NULL+8 on aarch64,
318:   * a clobbered return address -> #GP on amd64).  timer_del() takes the owner
319:   * CPU's timer_lock, which we do not hold here, so there is no recursion. */
320:  if (t->pending)
321:    timer_del(t);
322:
323:  struct cpu_info *c = get_cpu_info();
324:  uint64_t flags;
325:  spin_lock_irqsave(&c->timer_lock, &flags);
326:  t->expires = expires;
327:  t->pending = true;
328:  t->cpu = (int)c->cpu_id; /* armed on the current core; fired by its tick */
329:  list_add_tail(&t->list, &c->timer_list);
330:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&c->timer_lock, flags);
331:}
332:
333:/*
334: * timer_del - cancel a pending software timer.
335: *
336: * Removes t from timer_list only if t->pending is true.  Safe to call on a
337: * timer that has already fired or was never added (no-op in that case).
338: *
339: * Locking: acquires timer_lock (irqsave).
340: * IRQ context: safe.
341: * Side effects: sets t->pending = false.
342: */
343:void timer_del(struct timer *t) {
344:  uint64_t flags;
345:  /* TIMER-UAF-02: t->cpu is read WITHOUT a lock (we don't know which CPU's
346:   * timer_lock to take until we read it).  Under SMP that snapshot can be stale
347:   * vs. a concurrent timer_add() on the owning core, which publishes
348:   * t->pending=true BEFORE t->cpu — so an unlocked reader may momentarily see
349:   * (pending=true, cpu=-1).  The previous code took the cpu<0 fast path here and
350:   * cleared t->pending WITHOUT unlinking; that broke the pending<=>linked
351:   * invariant, after which the post-DEAD reaper's timer_del() trusted
352:   * pending==false and skipped list_del() too, leaving a still-linked timer on a
353:   * process that was then freed and poisoned (0xCC) — the kernel_timer_tick UAF.
354:   *
355:   * Fix: (1) never clear t->pending in the unlocked cpu<0 branch — leaving the
356:   * invariant intact means a later timer_del()/timer_add() still cancels it
357:   * correctly; (2) re-validate t->cpu UNDER the owning timer_lock and retry if it
358:   * moved, so the unlink always happens against the list the node is really on. */
359:  for (;;) {
360:    int cpu = t->cpu;
361:    if (cpu < 0 || cpu >= MAX_CPUS)
362:      return; /* not armed on a valid CPU (or arm mid-publish): leave pending */
363:
364:    spin_lock_irqsave(&cpu_data[cpu].timer_lock, &flags);
365:    if (t->cpu != cpu) {
366:      /* fired (tick set cpu=-1) or re-armed on another core meanwhile —
367:       * re-snapshot and decide again with the correct lock. */
368:      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&cpu_data[cpu].timer_lock, flags);
369:      continue;
370:    }
371:    if (t->pending) {
372:      list_del(&t->list);
373:      t->pending = false;
374:      t->cpu = -1;
375:    }
376:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&cpu_data[cpu].timer_lock, flags);
377:    return;
378:  }
379:}
380:
381:/*
382: * timer_pending - check whether a timer is on the pending list.
383: *
384: * Returns t->pending.  No lock taken — caller must accept a stale snapshot
385: * (the timer may fire between this read and any subsequent action).
386: */
387:bool timer_pending(struct timer *t) { return t->pending; }
388:

@@@ kernel/drivers/block/block.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/drivers/block/block.c
3: * Block-device contract dispatcher (see kernel/include/kernel/block.h).
4: *
5: * Holds the single active backend and routes block_read/block_write to it.
6: * The FS stack calls these; it never learns whether the bytes come from a
7: * virtio-blk device or a RAM-backed ramdisk module.  ASTRA: the `block` seam
8: * named in docs/ASTRA.md §3 (B1) — virtio-blk -> block -> fs provider -> VFS.
9: */
10:#include <kernel/block.h>
11:#include <kernel/printk.h>
12:
13:/* Single root block device.  Set once during boot (virtio-blk, then ramdisk
14: * override if a module is present); never torn down.  Touched only on the
15: * boot CPU before SMP/userland, so no lock is needed. */
16:static const struct block_dev *active;
17:
18:void block_register(const struct block_dev *dev) {
19:  if (!dev || !dev->read) {
20:    pr_err("%s", "block: rejecting malformed block_dev\n");
21:    return;
22:  }
23:  active = dev;
24:  pr_info("block: active backend '%s'\n", dev->name ? dev->name : "?");
25:}
26:
27:const char *block_active_name(void) {
28:  return active ? active->name : NULL;
29:}
30:
31:int block_read(void *buf, uint64_t sector, uint32_t count) {
32:  if (!active || !active->read)
33:    return -1;
34:  return active->read(buf, sector, count);
35:}
36:
37:int block_write(void *buf, uint64_t sector, uint32_t count) {
38:  if (!active || !active->write)
39:    return -1;
40:  return active->write(buf, sector, count);
41:}
