@@@ kernel/drivers/block/ramdisk.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/drivers/block/ramdisk.c
3: * RAM-backed block backend over a firmware boot module (the release rootfs).
4: *
5: * ASTRA: a provider behind the `block` contract (kernel/block.h), fully
6: * arch-neutral.  The arch-specific "is there a boot module, and where" lives
7: * behind the HAL contract arch_platform_get_boot_module() (platform.h),
8: * implemented equivalently per arch — so this driver carries no #ifdef.  On
9: * aarch64 the HAL reports no module and this provider stays inert.
10: */
11:#include <kernel/block.h>
12:#include <kernel/bootmodule.h>
13:#include <kernel/memlayout.h>
14:#include <kernel/platform.h>
15:#include <kernel/printk.h>
16:#include <kernel/string.h>
17:
18:/* Module extent (physical), 0 = none. */
19:static uint64_t mod_base;
20:static uint64_t mod_size;
21:
22:/* The module bytes are reachable through the kernel direct map (phys_to_virt);
23: * the region is reserved before the PMM (main.c) so it is never reused. */
24:static int ramdisk_io(void *buf, uint64_t sector, uint32_t count, int write) {
25:  uint64_t off = sector * 512ULL;
26:  uint64_t len = (uint64_t)count * 512ULL;
27:  if (!mod_base || off + len > mod_size)
28:    return -1; /* outside the module's bounds */
29:  uint8_t *disk = (uint8_t *)phys_to_virt(mod_base) + off;
30:  if (write)
31:    memcpy(disk, buf, len); /* RAM-backed: writes are volatile (lost on reboot) */
32:  else
33:    memcpy(buf, disk, len);
34:  return 0;
35:}
36:
37:static int ramdisk_read(void *buf, uint64_t sector, uint32_t count) {
38:  return ramdisk_io(buf, sector, count, 0);
39:}
40:
41:static int ramdisk_write(void *buf, uint64_t sector, uint32_t count) {
42:  return ramdisk_io(buf, sector, count, 1);
43:}
44:
45:void ramdisk_init(void) {
46:  if (!arch_platform_get_boot_module(&mod_base, &mod_size))
47:    return;
48:  static const struct block_dev ramdisk_bdev = {"ramdisk", ramdisk_read,
49:                                                ramdisk_write};
50:  block_register(&ramdisk_bdev);
51:  pr_info("ramdisk: rootfs module at phys 0x%lx, %lu KB\n", mod_base,
52:          mod_size / 1024);
53:}
54:

2: * kernel/drivers/gic/gic_regs.h

19:#define GICD_ISENABLER(n) (0x100 + ((n) * 4))  /* Set Enable */

34:#define GICC_IAR 0x0C   /* Interrupt Acknowledge */
35:#define GICC_EOIR 0x10  /* End of Interrupt */
36:#define GICC_RPR 0x14   /* Running Priority */
37:#define GICC_HPPIR 0x18 /* Highest Priority Pending */
38:

@@@ kernel/drivers/gic/gic.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/drivers/gic/gic.c
3: * ARM GICv2 Interrupt Controller Driver — QEMU virt (aarch64)
4: *
5: * Implements the struct irq_chip interface for the ARM Generic Interrupt
6: * Controller version 2 (GICv2) as found on the QEMU 'virt' board.
7: *
8: * GICv2 overview (relevant to this driver):
9: *   Distributor (GICD, at GICD_BASE): global; manages SPI routing, priority,
10: *   enable/disable, and pending state for all interrupts.
11: *   CPU Interface (GICC, at GICC_BASE): per-CPU; controls priority masking,
12: *   acknowledges (IAR read) and EOI (EOIR write) for this CPU.
13: *
14: * Interrupt categories:
15: *   SGI (IDs  0-15): Software-Generated Interrupts; per-CPU, used for IPIs.
16: *   PPI (IDs 16-31): Private Peripheral Interrupts; per-CPU (timer at 27).
17: *   SPI (IDs 32+):   Shared Peripheral Interrupts; routed to CPUs via ITARGETSR.
18: *
19: * Invariants:
20: *   - gic_init_dist() is called once on the boot CPU (via irq_init()).
21: *   - gic_init_cpu() is called on every CPU (via irq_init_percpu()).
22: *   - GICC_PMR = 0xFF: all interrupt priorities are accepted.
23: *   - All SPIs are hard-routed to CPU 0 (GICD_ITARGETSR = 0x01010101).
24: *
25: * Known issues:
26: *   DRV-GIC-01  (W3 WRONG-DESIGN) All SPIs permanently targeted to CPU 0
27: *               via GICD_ITARGETSR = 0x01010101 in gic_init_dist().  No
28: *               affinity hints, no round-robin — all device interrupts
29: *               serialise on core 0; blocks SMP load distribution.
30: *   DRV-GIC-02  (W2 BUG) gic_eoi() writes only the IRQ number to GICC_EOIR.
31: *               For SGIs (irq < 16), GICv2 requires bits [12:10] to hold the
32: *               source CPU ID; writing an IRQ number without those bits may
33: *               leave the SGI active on the distributor.
34: */
35:#include <drivers/gic.h>
36:#include "gic_regs.h"
37:#include <kernel/irq.h>
38:#include <kernel/memlayout.h>
39:#include <kernel/printk.h>
40:#include <kernel/sched.h>
41:#include <kernel/types.h>
42:
43:/* GICD_REG(off): dereference GICD MMIO register at GICD_BASE + off (32-bit).
44: * GICC_REG(off): dereference GICC MMIO register at GICC_BASE + off (32-bit).
45: * Both bases come from gic_regs.h (physical addresses); the access happens
46: * at their direct-map kernel VA via phys_to_virt (identity while
47: * KERNEL_VIRT_BASE == 0). */
48:/* MMIO access */
49:#define GICD_REG(off) (*(volatile uint32_t *)phys_to_virt(GICD_BASE + (off)))
50:#define GICC_REG(off) (*(volatile uint32_t *)phys_to_virt(GICC_BASE + (off)))
51:
52:/* gic_num_irqs: total interrupt lines reported by GICD_TYPER, clamped to
53: * GIC_MAX_IRQS.  Set once in gic_init_dist(); read-only thereafter. */
54:/* Number of interrupt lines */
55:static uint32_t gic_num_irqs;
56:
57:/*
58: * gic_init_dist - initialise the GIC distributor (boot CPU only).
59: *
60: * Called once via irq_init() → chip->init().  Programs the distributor:
61: *   1. Disable distributor (GICD_CTLR = 0) before programming.
62: *   2. Read GICD_TYPER bits[4:0] to determine number of interrupt lines
63: *      (ITLinesNumber): gic_num_irqs = (ITLinesNumber + 1) * 32, capped at
64: *      GIC_MAX_IRQS.
65: *   3. Write 0xFFFFFFFF to every GICD_ICENABLER register to disable all IRQs.
66: *   4. Write 0xFFFFFFFF to every GICD_ICPENDR register to clear pending state.
67: *   5. Set priority 0xA0 for all SPIs (IDs >= GIC_SPI_START = 32) via
68: *      GICD_IPRIORITYR; 4 priorities per 32-bit register.
69: *   6. Target all SPIs to CPU 0 via GICD_ITARGETSR = 0x01010101.
70: *      NOTE(DRV-GIC-01): hard-codes all SPIs to CPU 0; no SMP distribution.
71: *   7. Configure all SPIs as level-triggered (GICD_ICFGR = 0 for word i>=2).
72: *   8. Enable distributor (GICD_CTLR = 1).
73: *
74: * MMIO registers written: GICD_CTLR, GICD_ICENABLER[], GICD_ICPENDR[],
75: *   GICD_IPRIORITYR[], GICD_ITARGETSR[], GICD_ICFGR[].
76: * MMIO registers read: GICD_TYPER.
77: *
78: * Locking: called before SMP; no concurrent access.
79: * IRQ context: NO.
80: */
81:/*
82: * Initialize GIC distributor (called once on boot CPU)
83: */
84:static void gic_init_dist(void) {
85:  uint32_t typer;
86:  uint32_t i;
87:
88:  /* Disable distributor */
89:  GICD_REG(GICD_CTLR) = 0;
90:
91:  /* Get number of interrupt lines */
92:  typer = GICD_REG(GICD_TYPER);
93:  gic_num_irqs = ((typer & 0x1F) + 1) * 32;
94:  if (gic_num_irqs > GIC_MAX_IRQS)
95:    gic_num_irqs = GIC_MAX_IRQS;
96:
97:  pr_info("GIC: %u interrupt lines\n", gic_num_irqs);
98:
99:  /* Disable all interrupts */
100:  for (i = 0; i < gic_num_irqs / 32; i++)
101:    GICD_REG(GICD_ICENABLER(i)) = 0xFFFFFFFF;
102:
103:  /* Clear all pending interrupts */
104:  for (i = 0; i < gic_num_irqs / 32; i++)
105:    GICD_REG(GICD_ICPENDR(i)) = 0xFFFFFFFF;
106:
107:  /* Set all SPIs to lowest priority */
108:  for (i = GIC_SPI_START / 4; i < gic_num_irqs / 4; i++)
109:    GICD_REG(GICD_IPRIORITYR(i)) = 0xA0A0A0A0;
110:
111:  /* Target all SPIs to CPU 0 */
112:  /* NOTE(DRV-GIC-01): 0x01010101 packs four CPU-target bytes each = 0x01
113:   * (CPU 0 only).  All SPIs arrive exclusively on core 0; no SMP balancing. */
114:  for (i = GIC_SPI_START / 4; i < gic_num_irqs / 4; i++)
115:    GICD_REG(GICD_ITARGETSR(i)) = 0x01010101;
116:
117:  /* Configure all SPIs as level-triggered */
118:  for (i = 2; i < gic_num_irqs / 16; i++)
119:    GICD_REG(GICD_ICFGR(i)) = 0;
120:
121:  /* Enable distributor */
122:  GICD_REG(GICD_CTLR) = 1;
123:
124:  pr_info("%s", "GIC: Distributor initialized\n");
125:}
126:
127:/*
128: * gic_init_cpu - initialise the GIC CPU interface (called on each CPU).
129: *
130: * Called via irq_init_percpu() → chip->init_percpu() on every CPU at SMP
131: * bring-up.  Programs this CPU's GICC interface:
132: *   1. Write 0xFFFFFFFF to GICD_ICENABLER(0) to disable all SGIs and PPIs
133: *      for this CPU (distributor register 0 covers IDs 0-31, which are
134: *      per-CPU and therefore banked).
135: *   2. Write priority 0xA0 for all SGIs/PPIs via GICD_IPRIORITYR (banked
136: *      registers for IDs 0-31; GIC_SPI_START = 32).
137: *   3. GICC_PMR = 0xFF: priority mask allows all interrupts through.
138: *   4. GICC_BPR = 0: no priority grouping / preemption splitting.
139: *   5. GICC_CTLR = 1: enable this CPU's interface.
140: *
141: * MMIO registers written: GICD_ICENABLER(0), GICD_IPRIORITYR(0..7),
142: *   GICC_PMR, GICC_BPR, GICC_CTLR.
143: *
144: * Locking: operates on per-CPU (banked) GICC registers; no shared-state lock.
145: * IRQ context: NO — called from CPU bring-up code.
146: */
147:/*
148: * Initialize GIC CPU interface (called on each CPU)
149: */
150:static void gic_init_cpu(void) {
151:  uint32_t i;
152:
153:  /* Disable all SGIs and PPIs */
154:  GICD_REG(GICD_ICENABLER(0)) = 0xFFFFFFFF;
155:
156:  /* Set priority for SGIs and PPIs */
157:  for (i = 0; i < GIC_SPI_START / 4; i++)
158:    GICD_REG(GICD_IPRIORITYR(i)) = 0xA0A0A0A0;
159:
160:  /* Set priority mask - accept all priorities */
161:  GICC_REG(GICC_PMR) = 0xFF;
162:
163:  /* No priority grouping */
164:  GICC_REG(GICC_BPR) = 0;
165:
166:  /* Enable CPU interface */
167:  GICC_REG(GICC_CTLR) = 1;
168:}
169:
170:/*
171: * gic_enable - unmask a single interrupt line at the distributor.
172: *
173: * @irq: interrupt ID to enable (0..gic_num_irqs-1).
174: *
175: * Writes a single bit to the appropriate GICD_ISENABLER register.  Each
176: * GICD_ISENABLER word controls 32 interrupts; bit position = irq % 32.
177: * Writing 0 bits has no effect (set-enable register).
178: *
179: * MMIO register written: GICD_ISENABLER(irq / 32).
180: *
181: * Locking: none; single 32-bit write; atomic at hardware level for same-word
182: *          enable operations (GICv2 spec §4.3.6).
183: * IRQ context: safe.
184: */
185:/*
186: * Enable an interrupt
187: */
188:static void gic_enable(uint32_t irq) {
189:  if (irq >= gic_num_irqs)
190:    return;
191:
192:  uint32_t reg = irq / 32;
193:  uint32_t bit = irq % 32;
194:
195:  GICD_REG(GICD_ISENABLER(reg)) = (1U << bit);
196:}
197:
198:/*
199: * gic_disable - mask a single interrupt line at the distributor.
200: *
201: * @irq: interrupt ID to disable.
202: *
203: * Writes a single bit to GICD_ICENABLER (clear-enable register; writing 0
204: * has no effect).  Called by irq_unregister() and irq_disable() from irq.c
205: * to prevent interrupt storms for unhandled IRQs.
206: *
207: * MMIO register written: GICD_ICENABLER(irq / 32).
208: *
209: * Locking: none (same atomicity argument as gic_enable).
210: * IRQ context: safe.
211: */
212:/*
213: * Disable an interrupt
214: */
215:static void gic_disable(uint32_t irq) {
216:  if (irq >= gic_num_irqs)
217:    return;
218:
219:  uint32_t reg = irq / 32;
220:  uint32_t bit = irq % 32;
221:
222:  GICD_REG(GICD_ICENABLER(reg)) = (1U << bit);
223:}
224:
225:/*
226: * gic_set_prio - set the priority of a single interrupt.
227: *
228: * @irq:      interrupt ID to modify.
229: * @priority: 8-bit priority value (lower = higher priority in GICv2).
230: *
231: * Each GICD_IPRIORITYR register holds 4 priority bytes (one per interrupt).
232: * The byte position within the word is (irq % 4) * 8.  Performs a
233: * read-modify-write to update only the target byte.
234: *
235: * MMIO registers touched: GICD_IPRIORITYR(irq / 4) read then write.
236: *
237: * Locking: read-modify-write is not atomic with respect to concurrent
238: *          priority changes for the same register word.  Safe at boot.
239: * IRQ context: safe for isolated calls, but see atomicity caveat above.
240: */
241:static void gic_set_prio(uint32_t irq, uint8_t priority) {
242:  if (irq >= gic_num_irqs)
243:    return;
244:
245:  uint32_t reg = irq / 4;
246:  uint32_t shift = (irq % 4) * 8;
247:  uint32_t val = GICD_REG(GICD_IPRIORITYR(reg));
248:
249:  val &= ~(0xFFU << shift);
250:  val |= ((uint32_t)priority << shift);
251:
252:  GICD_REG(GICD_IPRIORITYR(reg)) = val;
253:}
254:
255:/*
256: * gic_send_ipi - broadcast SGI0 to all CPUs except the sender.
257: *
258: * Writes GICD_SGIR with TargetListFilter = 0b01 (bits [25:24]) which means
259: * "all PEs except the requesting PE" (GICv2 spec §4.3.15), and SGI ID = 0
260: * (bits [3:0]).  irq_handler() in irq.c treats SGI0 as a panic-halt IPI.
261: *
262: * MMIO register written: GICD_SGIR (write-only in GICv2).
263: *
264: * Locking: none; GICD_SGIR write is self-contained.
265: * IRQ context: safe.
266: */
267:static void gic_send_ipi(void) {
268:  /* TargetListFilter bits[25:24] = 0b01 means "all CPUs except requestor" */
269:  GICD_REG(GICD_SGIR) = (1U << 24) | 0; /* filter=broadcast-except-self, SGI0 */
270:}
271:
272:/*
273: * gic_ack - acknowledge the current interrupt and return its ID.
274: *
275: * Reads GICC_IAR (Interrupt Acknowledge Register, CPU interface offset
276: * GICC_IAR).  This read both signals the acknowledgement to the GIC and
277: * returns a 10-bit interrupt ID in bits [9:0].  Value 1023 = spurious.
278: *
279: * Must be called at the start of interrupt processing; the GIC transitions
280: * the interrupt to the Active state upon IAR read.
281: *
282: * MMIO register read: GICC_IAR.
283: * Returns: interrupt ID (0..1022) or 1023 (spurious/no interrupt).
284: *
285: * Locking: per-CPU GICC register; no cross-CPU contention.
286: * IRQ context: YES — must be called from IRQ handler.
287: */
288:static uint32_t gic_ack(void) { return GICC_REG(GICC_IAR) & 0x3FF; }
289:
290:/*
291: * gic_eoi - signal End-Of-Interrupt to the GIC CPU interface.
292: *
293: * @irq: interrupt ID returned by gic_ack() for this interrupt.
294: *
295: * Writes @irq to GICC_EOIR (End Of Interrupt Register) to transition the
296: * interrupt from Active to Inactive, allowing lower-priority interrupts to
297: * be signalled.  Must be called after the handler finishes processing.
298: *
299: * MMIO register written: GICC_EOIR.
300: *
301: * NOTE(DRV-GIC-02): For SGIs (irq < 16) the GICv2 spec requires bits [12:10]
302: * of GICC_EOIR to contain the source CPU ID (from GICC_IAR bits [12:10]).
303: * Writing only the IRQ number (bits[9:0]) with bits[12:10]=0 may leave the
304: * SGI active on the distributor for the wrong source CPU.
305: *
306: * Locking: per-CPU GICC register; no lock needed.
307: * IRQ context: YES — must be called from the IRQ dispatch path.
308: */
309:static void gic_eoi(uint32_t irq) {
310:  volatile uint32_t *eoir_reg =
311:      (volatile uint32_t *)phys_to_virt(GICC_BASE + GICC_EOIR);
312:  *eoir_reg = irq;
313:}
314:
315:/* gic_chip: irq_chip vtable for the ARM GICv2 on aarch64.
316: * Registered via gic_register() → irq_register_chip(); becomes current_chip
317: * in irq.c.  All ops are filled; the chip is fully used on aarch64. */
318:/* irq_chip implementation */
319:static struct irq_chip gic_chip = {
320:  .name = "ARM GICv2",
321:  .init = gic_init_dist,
322:  .init_percpu = gic_init_cpu,
323:  .enable = gic_enable,
324:  .disable = gic_disable,
325:  .set_priority = gic_set_prio,
326:  .send_ipi_all = gic_send_ipi,
327:  .acknowledge = gic_ack,
328:  .end = gic_eoi,
329:};
330:
331:/*
332: * gic_register - make the GICv2 the active irq_chip.
333: *
334: * Calls irq_register_chip(&gic_chip) to store gic_chip as current_chip in
335: * irq.c.  Must be called before irq_init().  Typically invoked from the
336: * aarch64 HAL's arch_irq_init() during early boot.
337: *
338: * Locking: none; called before SMP.
339: */
340:void gic_register(void) {
341:  irq_register_chip(&gic_chip);
342:}
343:

@@@ kernel/drivers/gpu/gpu_core.c @@@
1:#include <drivers/gpu/gpu.h>
2:#include <kernel/gfx_surface.h>
3:#include <kernel/printk.h>
4:#include <kernel/spinlock.h>
5:#include <kernel/string.h>
6:
7:static struct gpu_device *gpu_list = NULL;
8:static struct gpu_device *primary_gpu = NULL;
9:static DEFINE_SPINLOCK(gpu_list_lock);
10:
11:int gpu_register(struct gpu_device *dev) {
12:  if (!dev)
13:    return -1;
14:
15:  uint64_t flags;
16:  spin_lock_irqsave(&gpu_list_lock, &flags);
17:
18:  dev->next = gpu_list;
19:  gpu_list = dev;
20:
21:  if (!primary_gpu) {
22:    primary_gpu = dev;
23:    pr_info("GPU: Primary device set to %s\n", dev->name);
24:  }
25:
26:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&gpu_list_lock, flags);
27:  pr_info("GPU: Registered %s\n", dev->name);
28:  return 0;
29:}
30:
31:void gpu_unregister(struct gpu_device *dev) {
32:  if (!dev)
33:    return;
34:
35:  uint64_t flags;
36:  spin_lock_irqsave(&gpu_list_lock, &flags);
37:
38:  struct gpu_device **pp = &gpu_list;
39:  while (*pp) {
40:    if (*pp == dev) {
41:      *pp = dev->next;
42:      break;
43:    }
44:    pp = &(*pp)->next;
45:  }
46:
47:  if (primary_gpu == dev) {
48:    primary_gpu = gpu_list; /* Failover to head of list */
49:    pr_info("GPU: Primary device removed. Switched to %s\n",
50:            primary_gpu ? primary_gpu->name : "None");
51:  }
52:
53:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&gpu_list_lock, flags);
54:}
55:
56:struct gpu_device *gpu_get_primary(void) { return primary_gpu; }
57:
58:/* Contract wrappers over the primary GPU (GFX-DYN-01).  Each is a no-op
59: * returning -1 if there is no primary device or the driver does not implement
60: * the op, so the compositor can call them unconditionally. */
61:int gpu_set_mode(int width, int height) {
62:  struct gpu_device *dev = primary_gpu;
63:  if (!dev || !dev->ops || !dev->ops->set_mode)
64:    return -1;
65:  return dev->ops->set_mode(dev, width, height);
66:}
67:
68:int gpu_get_display_info(int *width, int *height) {
69:  struct gpu_device *dev = primary_gpu;
70:  if (!dev || !dev->ops || !dev->ops->get_display_info)
71:    return -1;
72:  return dev->ops->get_display_info(dev, width, height);
73:}
74:
75:int gpu_poll_events(int *new_w, int *new_h) {
76:  struct gpu_device *dev = primary_gpu;
77:  if (!dev || !dev->ops || !dev->ops->poll_events)
78:    return -1;
79:  return dev->ops->poll_events(dev, new_w, new_h);
80:}
81:
82:int gpu_present_surface(const struct gl_surface *src,
83:                        const struct gfx_rect *damage) {
84:  struct gpu_device *dev = primary_gpu;
85:  if (!dev || !dev->ops || !dev->ops->present || !src || !damage)
86:    return -1;
87:  /* S-STAB invariant gate at the contract seam: a surface whose geometry
88:   * outruns its backing must fail loud here, never as an OOB copy below. */
89:  gfx_surface_verify(src, "gpu_present_surface");
90:  if (src->stride != src->width)
91:    return -1; /* the provider transfers tightly packed rows only */
92:  if (damage->width <= 0 || damage->height <= 0)
93:    return 0; /* empty damage: consumed, nothing to upload */
94:  return dev->ops->present(dev, src->buffer, src->width, src->height,
95:                           damage->x, damage->y, damage->width,
96:                           damage->height);
97:}

@@@ kernel/drivers/gpu/virtio_gpu.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/drivers/gpu/virtio_gpu.c
3: * VirtIO GPU Driver — single arch-neutral service over the HAL virtio
4: * transport.
5: *
6: * The same driver drives virtio-gpu on both transports: VirtIO-MMIO on the
7: * AArch64 QEMU virt machine and VirtIO-over-PCI on amd64.  It never touches the
8: * ISA — it speaks only the transport contract (virtio_read_reg /
9: * virtio_write_reg / virtio_notify / virtio_setup_queue) and the GPU contract
10: * (struct gpu_ops).
11: *
12: * GFX-DYN-01:
13: *  - #54: resolution is queried from the host with GET_DISPLAY_INFO, not the
14: *    old hard-coded 720x1280.
15: *  - #49: vgpu_set_mode() really reconfigures the scanout to a new size.
16: *  - #53: the virtqueue rings (desc/avail/used) and command/response buffers
17: *    are per-device (in struct virtio_gpu_state), not module globals; all ring
18: *    access is serialised by gpu_lock, and init runs to completion before
19: *    gpu_register() publishes the device (so flush/set_mode cannot race init).
20: */
21:#include <drivers/gpu/gpu.h>
22:#include <drivers/virtio.h>
23:#include <drivers/virtio_gpu.h>
24:#include <kernel/arch.h>
25:#include <kernel/fault.h>
26:#include <kernel/kmalloc.h>
27:#include <kernel/pmm.h>
28:#include <kernel/printk.h>
29:#include <kernel/spinlock.h>
30:#include <kernel/string.h>
31:#include <kernel/vmm.h>
32:
33:/* Default fallback when the host advertises no usable mode (landscape, not the
34: * old portrait 720x1280 that forced sideways rendering — #54). */
35:#define VGPU_DEFAULT_W 1024
36:#define VGPU_DEFAULT_H 768
37:
38:/* virtio-gpu device-config field offsets (struct virtio_gpu_config), read via
39: * the transport-agnostic virtio_config_read32/write32 (works on MMIO + PCI). */
40:#define VGPU_CFG_EVENTS_READ 0
41:#define VGPU_CFG_EVENTS_CLEAR 4

43:struct virtio_gpu_state {
44:  virtio_handle_t handle;
45:  uint32_t qsize;
46:  void *backing_store;  /* guest framebuffer (DMA backing of the resource) */
47:  uint32_t resource_id; /* current scanout resource id */
48:  uint32_t next_resource_id;
49:  struct gpu_device *dev;
50:
51:  /* Per-device control virtqueue (queue 0) — was module-global (#53). */
52:  struct vring_desc *desc;
53:  struct vring_avail *avail;
54:  struct vring_used *used;
55:  void *cmd_buf;  /* DMA page for outgoing control commands */
56:  void *resp_buf; /* DMA page for responses */
57:};

59:static DEFINE_SPINLOCK(gpu_lock);

61:static int virtio_gpu_send(struct virtio_gpu_state *priv, void *cmd,
62:                           uint32_t cmd_len, void *resp, uint32_t resp_len);

64:/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
65:/* Control-queue command helpers (caller serialises via gpu_lock or runs at */
66:/* init before the device is published). */
67:/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

69:static int vgpu_create_2d(struct virtio_gpu_state *priv, uint32_t res_id, int w,
70:                          int h) {
71:  memset(priv->cmd_buf, 0, 4096);
72:  struct virtio_gpu_resource_create_2d *c = priv->cmd_buf;
73:  c->hdr.type = VIRTIO_GPU_CMD_RESOURCE_CREATE_2D;
74:  c->resource_id = res_id;
75:  c->format = VIRTIO_GPU_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM;
76:  c->width = w;
77:  c->height = h;
78:  return virtio_gpu_send(priv, c, sizeof(*c), priv->resp_buf,
79:                         sizeof(struct virtio_gpu_ctrl_hdr));
80:}
81:
82:static int vgpu_attach_backing(struct virtio_gpu_state *priv, uint32_t res_id,
83:                               void *backing, uint32_t len) {
84:  memset(priv->cmd_buf, 0, 4096);
85:  struct virtio_gpu_resource_attach_backing *a = priv->cmd_buf;
86:  struct virtio_gpu_mem_entry *ent =
87:      (struct virtio_gpu_mem_entry *)((uint8_t *)priv->cmd_buf + sizeof(*a));
88:  a->hdr.type = VIRTIO_GPU_CMD_RESOURCE_ATTACH_BACKING;
89:  a->resource_id = res_id;
90:  a->nr_entries = 1;
91:  ent->addr = virt_to_phys(backing); /* device DMA: physical address */
92:  ent->length = len;
93:  return virtio_gpu_send(priv, a, sizeof(*a) + sizeof(*ent), priv->resp_buf,
94:                         sizeof(struct virtio_gpu_ctrl_hdr));
95:}

97:static int vgpu_set_scanout(struct virtio_gpu_state *priv, uint32_t res_id,
98:                            int w, int h) {
99:  memset(priv->cmd_buf, 0, 4096);
100:  struct virtio_gpu_set_scanout *s = priv->cmd_buf;
101:  s->hdr.type = VIRTIO_GPU_CMD_SET_SCANOUT;
102:  s->scanout_id = 0;
103:  s->resource_id = res_id;
104:  s->r.x = 0;
105:  s->r.y = 0;
106:  s->r.width = w;
107:  s->r.height = h;
108:  return virtio_gpu_send(priv, s, sizeof(*s), priv->resp_buf,
109:                         sizeof(struct virtio_gpu_ctrl_hdr));
110:}

112:static int vgpu_unref(struct virtio_gpu_state *priv, uint32_t res_id) {
113:  memset(priv->cmd_buf, 0, 4096);
114:  struct virtio_gpu_resource_unref *u = priv->cmd_buf;
115:  u->hdr.type = VIRTIO_GPU_CMD_RESOURCE_UNREF;
116:  u->resource_id = res_id;
117:  return virtio_gpu_send(priv, u, sizeof(*u), priv->resp_buf,
118:                         sizeof(struct virtio_gpu_ctrl_hdr));
119:}

121:/* Query the host's preferred display size via GET_DISPLAY_INFO (#54).  Returns
122: * 0 and fills w/h with the first enabled scanout's size, -1 on failure or if no
123: * scanout reports a usable size. */
124:static int vgpu_query_display_info(struct virtio_gpu_state *priv, int *w,
125:                                   int *h) {
126:  memset(priv->cmd_buf, 0, 4096);
127:  memset(priv->resp_buf, 0, 4096);
128:  struct virtio_gpu_ctrl_hdr *cmd = priv->cmd_buf;
129:  cmd->type = VIRTIO_GPU_CMD_GET_DISPLAY_INFO;
130:
131:  struct virtio_gpu_resp_display_info *resp = priv->resp_buf;
132:  if (virtio_gpu_send(priv, cmd, sizeof(*cmd), resp, sizeof(*resp)) != 0)
133:    return -1;
134:  if (resp->hdr.type != VIRTIO_GPU_RESP_OK_DISPLAY_INFO)
135:    return -1;
136:
137:  for (int i = 0; i < VIRTIO_GPU_MAX_SCANOUTS; i++) {
138:    if (resp->pmodes[i].enabled && resp->pmodes[i].r.width > 0 &&
139:        resp->pmodes[i].r.height > 0) {
140:      if (w)
141:        *w = (int)resp->pmodes[i].r.width;
142:      if (h)
143:        *h = (int)resp->pmodes[i].r.height;
144:      return 0;
145:    }
146:  }
147:  return -1;
148:}

151:/* gpu_ops */
152:/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

154:/* vgpu_xfer_flush_locked - issue TRANSFER_TO_HOST_2D + RESOURCE_FLUSH for the
155: * region (x,y,w,h) against the CURRENT scanout resource.  Caller MUST hold
156: * gpu_lock (or be in single-threaded fault context): it touches priv->cmd_buf
157: * and priv->resource_id, which set_mode also mutates. */
158:static void vgpu_xfer_flush_locked(struct virtio_gpu_state *priv,
159:                                   struct gpu_device *dev, int x, int y, int w,
160:                                   int h) {
161:  /* 1. Transfer guest memory to the host resource. */
162:  memset(priv->cmd_buf, 0, 4096);
163:  struct virtio_gpu_transfer_to_host_2d *xfer = priv->cmd_buf;
164:  xfer->hdr.type = VIRTIO_GPU_CMD_TRANSFER_TO_HOST_2D;
165:  xfer->r.x = x;
166:  xfer->r.y = y;
167:  xfer->r.width = w;
168:  xfer->r.height = h;
169:  xfer->offset = (uint64_t)y * dev->width * 4 + (x * 4);
170:  xfer->resource_id = priv->resource_id;
171:  virtio_gpu_send(priv, xfer, sizeof(*xfer), priv->resp_buf,
172:                  sizeof(struct virtio_gpu_ctrl_hdr));
173:
174:  /* 2. Flush the host resource to the display. */
175:  memset(priv->cmd_buf, 0, 4096);
176:  struct virtio_gpu_resource_flush *fl = priv->cmd_buf;
177:  fl->hdr.type = VIRTIO_GPU_CMD_RESOURCE_FLUSH;
178:  fl->r.x = x;
179:  fl->r.y = y;
180:  fl->r.width = w;
181:  fl->r.height = h;
182:  fl->resource_id = priv->resource_id;
183:  virtio_gpu_send(priv, fl, sizeof(*fl), priv->resp_buf,
184:                  sizeof(struct virtio_gpu_ctrl_hdr));
185:}
186:
187:static int vgpu_flush(struct gpu_device *dev, int x, int y, int w, int h) {
188:  if (!dev || !dev->priv)
189:    return -1;
190:  struct virtio_gpu_state *priv = (struct virtio_gpu_state *)dev->priv;
191:
192:  /* In a panic/fault context the gpu_lock holder may be a now-halted CPU; the
193:   * system is single-threaded by then (panic quiesced the others), so skip the
194:   * lock to present the on-screen panic without deadlocking (DIR-05 #139). */
195:  int faulting = (fault_depth() > 0);
196:  uint64_t flags = 0;
197:  if (!faulting)
198:    spin_lock_irqsave(&gpu_lock, &flags);
199:
200:  vgpu_xfer_flush_locked(priv, dev, x, y, w, h);
201:
202:  if (!faulting)
203:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&gpu_lock, flags);
204:  return 0;
205:}
206:
207:/* vgpu_present - RC2 fix: copy the backbuffer region into the scanout backing
208: * AND transfer+flush it, atomically under gpu_lock.  This is what makes the
209: * compositor↔GPU seam safe against a concurrent set_mode: the same lock that
210: * vgpu_set_mode() takes to swap priv->backing_store and free the old buffer is
211: * held for the entire copy, so the scanout can never be freed mid-memcpy (the
212: * use-after-free behind the resize/zoom panics).  Geometry is validated against
213: * the LIVE scanout under the lock; a mismatch (a mode change landed first) skips
214: * the frame instead of copying past the new, smaller backing. */
215:static int vgpu_present(struct gpu_device *dev, const uint32_t *src, int src_w,
216:                        int src_h, int x, int y, int w, int h) {
217:  if (!dev || !dev->priv || !src)
218:    return -1;
219:  struct virtio_gpu_state *priv = (struct virtio_gpu_state *)dev->priv;
220:
221:  uint64_t flags;
222:  spin_lock_irqsave(&gpu_lock, &flags);
223:
224:  /* The source (compositor backbuffer) must match the CURRENT scanout exactly:
225:   * both are resized together, but through different locks, so re-check here.
226:   * If a set_mode already changed dev->{width,height}, skip — the compositor
227:   * will present again next frame at the new size. */
228:  uint32_t *fb = (uint32_t *)priv->backing_store;
229:  if (!fb || src_w != dev->width || src_h != dev->height) {
230:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&gpu_lock, flags);
231:    return -1;
232:  }
233:
234:  /* Clamp the region to the scanout (defensive; the compositor already clips) */
235:  if (x < 0) {
236:    w += x;
237:    x = 0;
238:  }
239:  if (y < 0) {
240:    h += y;
241:    y = 0;
242:  }
243:  if (x + w > dev->width)
244:    w = dev->width - x;
245:  if (y + h > dev->height)
246:    h = dev->height - y;
247:  if (w <= 0 || h <= 0) {
248:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&gpu_lock, flags);
249:    return 0;
250:  }
251:
252:  /* Row-by-row copy backbuffer -> scanout backing (both stride == dev->width). */
253:  for (int row = y; row < y + h; row++) {
254:    memcpy((uint8_t *)fb + ((size_t)row * dev->width + x) * 4,
255:           (const uint8_t *)src + ((size_t)row * src_w + x) * 4, (size_t)w * 4);
256:  }
257:
258:  vgpu_xfer_flush_locked(priv, dev, x, y, w, h);
259:
260:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&gpu_lock, flags);
261:  return 0;
262:}
263:
264:static void *vgpu_get_framebuffer(struct gpu_device *dev, size_t *size) {
265:  if (!dev || !dev->priv)
266:    return NULL;
267:  struct virtio_gpu_state *priv = (struct virtio_gpu_state *)dev->priv;
268:  if (size)
269:    *size = dev->framebuffer_size;
270:  return priv->backing_store;
271:}
272:
273:/* Reconfigure the scanout to width x height at runtime (#49).
274: *
275: * Sequence under gpu_lock: create a fresh resource at the new size, allocate &
276: * attach a new backing store, point the scanout at it, then release the old
277: * resource and backing.  dev->{width,height,framebuffer_size} and
278: * priv->backing_store are updated so the compositor's next get_framebuffer()
279: * + flush() target the new surface.
280: */
281:static int vgpu_set_mode(struct gpu_device *dev, int width, int height) {
282:  if (!dev || !dev->priv)
283:    return -1;
284:  if (width <= 0 || height <= 0 || width > 8192 || height > 8192)
285:    return -1;
286:  struct virtio_gpu_state *priv = (struct virtio_gpu_state *)dev->priv;
287:
288:  if (width == dev->width && height == dev->height)
289:    return 0; /* nothing to do */
290:
291:  size_t new_size = (size_t)width * height * 4;
292:  int new_pages = (new_size + 4095) / 4096;
293:  void *new_backing = pmm_alloc_pages_dma(new_pages);
294:  if (!new_backing) {
295:    pr_err("VirtIO-GPU: set_mode %dx%d: out of memory\n", width, height);
296:    return -1;
297:  }
298:  memset(new_backing, 0, new_size);
299:
300:  uint64_t flags;
301:  spin_lock_irqsave(&gpu_lock, &flags);
302:
303:  uint32_t old_res = priv->resource_id;
304:  void *old_backing = priv->backing_store;
305:  size_t old_size = dev->framebuffer_size;
306:  uint32_t new_res = priv->next_resource_id++;
307:
308:  if (vgpu_create_2d(priv, new_res, width, height) != 0 ||
309:      vgpu_attach_backing(priv, new_res, new_backing, (uint32_t)new_size) !=
310:          0 ||
311:      vgpu_set_scanout(priv, new_res, width, height) != 0) {
312:    /* Roll back: keep the old resource/backing as the live scanout. */
313:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&gpu_lock, flags);
314:    pmm_free_pages(new_backing, new_pages);
315:    pr_err("VirtIO-GPU: set_mode %dx%d failed; keeping %dx%d\n", width, height,
316:           dev->width, dev->height);
317:    return -1;
318:  }
319:
320:  /* New scanout is live: publish it and release the old resource. */
321:  priv->resource_id = new_res;
322:  priv->backing_store = new_backing;
323:  dev->width = width;
324:  dev->height = height;
325:  dev->framebuffer_size = new_size;
326:
327:  vgpu_unref(priv, old_res);
328:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&gpu_lock, flags);
329:
330:  if (old_backing)
331:    pmm_free_pages(old_backing, (old_size + 4095) / 4096);
332:
333:  pr_info("VirtIO-GPU: mode set to %dx%d (resource %u)\n", width, height,
334:          new_res);
335:  return 0;
336:}
337:
338:static int vgpu_get_display_info(struct gpu_device *dev, int *width,
339:                                 int *height) {
340:  if (!dev || !dev->priv)
341:    return -1;
342:  struct virtio_gpu_state *priv = (struct virtio_gpu_state *)dev->priv;
343:  uint64_t flags;
344:  spin_lock_irqsave(&gpu_lock, &flags);
345:  int r = vgpu_query_display_info(priv, width, height);
346:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&gpu_lock, flags);
347:  return r;
348:}
349:
350:/* Poll the device-config events register for a host-initiated display change.
351: * Returns 1 (and the new size) if the host resized the output to a different
352: * resolution, 0 if nothing changed.  Reads device config via the
353: * transport-agnostic virtio_config_read32/write32 (F7), so host-driven
354: * auto-resize works on both VirtIO-MMIO (aarch64) and VirtIO-PCI (amd64). */
355:static int vgpu_poll_events(struct gpu_device *dev, int *new_w, int *new_h) {
356:  if (!dev || !dev->priv)
357:    return -1;
358:  struct virtio_gpu_state *priv = (struct virtio_gpu_state *)dev->priv;
359:
360:  uint32_t events = virtio_config_read32(priv->handle, VGPU_CFG_EVENTS_READ);
361:  if (!(events & VIRTIO_GPU_EVENT_DISPLAY))
362:    return 0;
363:
364:  /* Acknowledge the event. */
365:  virtio_config_write32(priv->handle, VGPU_CFG_EVENTS_CLEAR,
366:                        VIRTIO_GPU_EVENT_DISPLAY);
367:
368:  int w = 0, h = 0;
369:  uint64_t flags;
370:  spin_lock_irqsave(&gpu_lock, &flags);
371:  int r = vgpu_query_display_info(priv, &w, &h);
372:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&gpu_lock, flags);
373:  if (r != 0)
374:    return 0;
375:
376:  if (w == dev->width && h == dev->height)
377:    return 0; /* event but same size */
378:
379:  if (new_w)
380:    *new_w = w;
381:  if (new_h)
382:    *new_h = h;
383:  return 1;
384:}
385:
386:static void vgpu_destroy(struct gpu_device *dev) {
387:  kfree(dev->priv);
388:  kfree(dev);
389:}
390:
391:static struct gpu_ops vgpu_ops = {
392:    .flush = vgpu_flush,
393:    .get_framebuffer = vgpu_get_framebuffer,
394:    .present = vgpu_present,
395:    .set_mode = vgpu_set_mode,
396:    .destroy = vgpu_destroy,
397:    .get_display_info = vgpu_get_display_info,
398:    .poll_events = vgpu_poll_events,
399:};
400:
401:/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
402:/* Raw control-queue transport */
403:/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
404:
405:static int virtio_gpu_send(struct virtio_gpu_state *priv, void *cmd,
406:                           uint32_t cmd_len, void *resp, uint32_t resp_len) {
407:  if (!priv->handle)
408:    return -1;
409:
410:  struct vring_desc *desc = priv->desc;
411:  struct vring_avail *avail = priv->avail;
412:  struct vring_used *used = priv->used;
413:
414:  /* Descriptor addresses are PHYSICAL (DMA). */
415:  desc[0].addr = virt_to_phys(cmd);
416:  desc[0].len = cmd_len;
417:  desc[0].flags = VRING_DESC_F_NEXT;
418:  desc[0].next = 1;
419:
420:  volatile uint16_t *idx_ptr = &used->idx;
421:  uint16_t old_idx = *idx_ptr;
422:
423:  desc[1].addr = virt_to_phys(resp);
424:  desc[1].len = resp_len;
425:  desc[1].flags = VRING_DESC_F_WRITE;
426:  desc[1].next = 0;
427:
428:  uint16_t ava_slot = avail->idx % priv->qsize;
429:  avail->ring[ava_slot] = 0;
430:
431:  arch_mb();
432:  avail->idx++;
433:  arch_mb();
434:
435:  virtio_notify(priv->handle, 0);
436:
437:  uint64_t timeout = 200000000;
438:  while (*idx_ptr == old_idx && timeout > 0) {
439:    timeout--;
440:  }
441:  virtio_read_reg(priv->handle, VIRTIO_MMIO_INTERRUPT_ACK);
442:
443:  if (timeout == 0) {
444:    pr_err("%s", "VirtIO-GPU: Timeout!\n");
445:    return -1;
446:  }
447:  return 0;
448:}
449:
450:void virtio_gpu_init(void) {
451:  pr_info("%s", "VirtIO-GPU: Probing...\n");
452:
453:  virtio_handle_t dev_handle = NULL;
454:  uint32_t irq = 0;
455:
456:  if (arch_virtio_get_device(VIRTIO_DEV_GPU, 0, &dev_handle, &irq) != 0) {
457:    pr_info("%s", "VirtIO-GPU: Not found\n");
458:    return;
459:  }
460:  pr_info("VirtIO-GPU: Found device (IRQ %u)\n", irq);
461:
462:  struct gpu_device *dev = kmalloc(sizeof(struct gpu_device));
463:  struct virtio_gpu_state *priv = kmalloc(sizeof(struct virtio_gpu_state));
464:  if (!dev || !priv) {
465:    if (dev)
466:      kfree(dev);
467:    if (priv)
468:      kfree(priv);
469:    return;
470:  }
471:  memset(dev, 0, sizeof(*dev));
472:  memset(priv, 0, sizeof(*priv));
473:
474:  priv->handle = dev_handle;
475:  priv->dev = dev;
476:  dev->priv = priv;
477:  dev->ops = &vgpu_ops;
478:  strlcpy(dev->name, "VirtIO-GPU", sizeof(dev->name));
479:
480:  /* Reset + Acknowledge + Driver. */
481:  virtio_write_reg(dev_handle, VIRTIO_MMIO_STATUS, 0);
482:  uint32_t status = VIRTIO_STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGE | VIRTIO_STATUS_DRIVER;
483:  virtio_write_reg(dev_handle, VIRTIO_MMIO_STATUS, status);
484:
485:  /* Feature negotiation. */
486:  uint32_t features = virtio_read_reg(dev_handle, VIRTIO_MMIO_DEVICE_FEATURES);
487:  virtio_write_reg(dev_handle, VIRTIO_MMIO_DRIVER_FEATURES, features);
488:  status |= VIRTIO_STATUS_FEATURES_OK;
489:  virtio_write_reg(dev_handle, VIRTIO_MMIO_STATUS, status);
490:  if (!(virtio_read_reg(dev_handle, VIRTIO_MMIO_STATUS) &
491:        VIRTIO_STATUS_FEATURES_OK)) {
492:    pr_err("%s", "VirtIO-GPU: Negotiation failed\n");
493:    kfree(dev);
494:    kfree(priv);
495:    return;
496:  }
497:
498:  /* Control queue (queue 0) setup — per-device rings (#53). */
499:  virtio_write_reg(dev_handle, VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_SEL, 0);
500:  uint32_t qmax = virtio_read_reg(dev_handle, VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_NUM_MAX);
501:  priv->qsize = (qmax > 16) ? 16 : qmax;
502:  virtio_write_reg(dev_handle, VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_NUM, priv->qsize);
503:
504:  void *qmem = pmm_alloc_pages_dma(2);
505:  memset(qmem, 0, 8192);
506:  priv->desc = (struct vring_desc *)qmem;
507:  priv->avail = (struct vring_avail *)((uint8_t *)qmem + priv->qsize * 16);
508:  priv->used = (struct vring_used *)((uint8_t *)qmem + 4096);
509:
510:  virtio_setup_queue(dev_handle, 0, virt_to_phys(priv->desc),
511:                     virt_to_phys(priv->avail), virt_to_phys(priv->used));
512:
513:  priv->cmd_buf = pmm_alloc_page_dma();
514:  priv->resp_buf = pmm_alloc_page_dma();
515:
516:  /* Driver OK. */
517:  virtio_write_reg(dev_handle, VIRTIO_MMIO_STATUS,
518:                   VIRTIO_STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGE | VIRTIO_STATUS_DRIVER |
519:                       VIRTIO_STATUS_DRIVER_OK);
520:
521:  /* Resolution: ask the host (#54) instead of hard-coding 720x1280. */
522:  int qw = 0, qh = 0;
523:  if (vgpu_query_display_info(priv, &qw, &qh) != 0 || qw <= 0 || qh <= 0) {
524:    qw = VGPU_DEFAULT_W;
525:    qh = VGPU_DEFAULT_H;
526:    pr_info("VirtIO-GPU: no host mode reported, defaulting to %dx%d\n", qw, qh);
527:  } else {
528:    pr_info("VirtIO-GPU: host display %dx%d\n", qw, qh);
529:  }
530:
531:  dev->width = qw;
532:  dev->height = qh;
533:  dev->bpp = 32;
534:  dev->framebuffer_size = (size_t)qw * qh * 4;
535:
536:  int pages = (dev->framebuffer_size + 4095) / 4096;
537:  priv->backing_store = pmm_alloc_pages_dma(pages);
538:  memset(priv->backing_store, 0, dev->framebuffer_size);
539:  /* panic_screen/graphics and the compositor all reach this backing store
540:   * through the ops->get_framebuffer contract (S-ALIGN F7) — there is no
541:   * second field-level path any more (the old dev->framebuffer_virt started
542:   * life unassigned and silently no-op'd the red panic screen, DIR-05 #139). */
543:  priv->resource_id = 1;
544:  priv->next_resource_id = 2;
545:
546:  /* Create the scanout resource at the queried size. */
547:  vgpu_create_2d(priv, priv->resource_id, dev->width, dev->height);
548:  vgpu_attach_backing(priv, priv->resource_id, priv->backing_store,
549:                      (uint32_t)dev->framebuffer_size);
550:  vgpu_set_scanout(priv, priv->resource_id, dev->width, dev->height);
551:
552:  gpu_register(dev); /* publish last: flush/set_mode cannot race init (#53) */
553:}

107:/*
108: * Initialize keyboard subsystem
109: */
110:void keyboard_init(void) {
111:  shift_pressed = 0;
112:  ctrl_pressed = 0;
113:  caps_lock = 0;
114:
115:  pr_info("%s", "Input: Initializing input subsystem...\n");
116:
117:  /* Device-manager-driven bring-up: probe every input provider; each one
118:   * detects its own hardware and feeds the unified input_report() core. No
119:   * hardcoded per-arch "virtio or PS/2" selection anymore — whatever is
120:   * actually present (virtio-input, USB HID, legacy PS/2) becomes active, on
121:   * both architectures. Absent providers no-op (e.g. PS/2 on aarch64). */
122:  virtio_input_init(); /* virtio-input: MMIO on aarch64, PCI on amd64 */
123:  usb_init();          /* xHCI/EHCI/UHCI via the PCI driver manager + USB HID */
124:  ps2_init();          /* legacy 8042 (amd64 only; no-op elsewhere) */
125:
126:  current_layout = &layout_it;
127:
128:  INIT_LIST_HEAD(&keyboard_wait_queue.task_list);
129:  spin_lock_init(&keyboard_wait_queue.lock);
130:
131:  pr_info("Keyboard: Initialized (Layout: %s)\n", current_layout->name);
132:}
133:
134:/* Wait Queue for blocking reads */
135:struct wait_queue_head keyboard_wait_queue;
136:
137:/*
138: * Notification from low-level driver
139: * Called from Interrupt Context (VirtIO Handler)
140: */
141:void keyboard_notify_input(void) {
142:  /* Poll hardware to transfer from VirtIO buffer to Keyboard buffer */
143:  keyboard_poll();
144:
145:  /* Wake up waiting processes */
146:  wake_up(&keyboard_wait_queue);
147:}
148:
149:/*
150: * Process a key event
151: */
152:static void keyboard_process_key(uint16_t code, int32_t value) {
153:  /* value: 0 = released, 1 = pressed, 2 = repeat */
154:
155:  /* Handle modifier keys */
156:  if (code == KEY_LEFTSHIFT || code == KEY_RIGHTSHIFT) {
157:    shift_pressed = (value != 0);
158:    return;
159:  }
160:
161:  if (code == KEY_LEFTCTRL) {
162:    ctrl_pressed = (value != 0);
163:    return;
164:  }
165:
166:  if (code == KEY_CAPSLOCK && value == 1) {
167:    caps_lock = !caps_lock;
168:    return;
169:  }
170:
171:  /* Convert scancode to ASCII */
172:  if (code >= 128)
173:    return;
174:
175:  char c;
176:  int use_shift = shift_pressed;
177:
178:  /* Apply caps lock to letters */
179:  if (code >= KEY_Q && code <= KEY_P)
180:    use_shift ^= caps_lock;
181:  if (code >= KEY_A && code <= KEY_L)
182:    use_shift ^= caps_lock;
183:  if (code >= KEY_Z && code <= KEY_M)
184:    use_shift ^= caps_lock;
185:
186:  /* Read the ASCII from the active layout's maps (KBD-LAYOUT-01), falling back
187:   * to the built-in US tables if a layout omits them. */
188:  const char *amap =
189:      (current_layout && current_layout->ascii_map) ? current_layout->ascii_map
190:                                                     : scancode_to_ascii;
191:  const char *smap = (current_layout && current_layout->shifted_map)
192:                         ? current_layout->shifted_map
193:                         : scancode_to_ascii_shift;
194:  if (use_shift)
195:    c = smap[code];
196:  else
197:    c = amap[code];
198:
199:  /* Ctrl + key -> control code (TTY semantics): Ctrl-A..Ctrl-Z => 0x01..0x1A,
200:   * Ctrl-@..Ctrl-_ => 0x00..0x1F.  Generalises the old Ctrl-C-only path so
201:   * full-screen apps (kilo: Ctrl-S/Q/F) and the shell's Ctrl-C all work
202:   * uniformly.  When folding to a control code we skip the UTF-8 override
203:   * pass below (a control char is never an accented glyph). */
204:  int is_ctrl_combo = 0;
205:  if (ctrl_pressed && c) {
206:    unsigned char uc = (unsigned char)c;
207:    if (uc >= 'a' && uc <= 'z') {
208:      c = (char)(uc - 'a' + 1);
209:      is_ctrl_combo = 1;
210:    } else if (uc >= 'A' && uc <= 'Z') {
211:      c = (char)(uc - 'A' + 1);
212:      is_ctrl_combo = 1;
213:    } else if (uc >= '@' && uc <= '_') {
214:      c = (char)(uc - '@');
215:      is_ctrl_combo = 1;
216:    }
217:  }
218:
219:  /* Per-keystroke logging is debug-only: at pr_info level every press AND
220:   * release printed a line from IRQ context, flooding the serial log and
221:   * serialising all CPUs on the printk path while typing. */
222:  /* Snapshot the focus hint ONCE (#67): route this keystroke to a single,
223:   * consistent target instead of re-reading the shared global between the test
224:   * and the send (where the compositor could change it). */
225:  int focus_pid = sched_get_focus_pid();
226:
227:  if (c != 0) {
228:    pr_debug("Keyboard: Char='%c' (val=%d) -> PID %d\n", c, value, focus_pid);
229:  }
230:
231:  /* Send IPC message if we have a focus PID */
232:  if (focus_pid > 0) {
233:    struct ipc_message msg;
234:    memset(&msg, 0, sizeof(msg));
235:    msg.from = 0; /* Kernel/Driver */
236:    msg.type = IPC_TYPE_INPUT;
237:    msg.data1 = ((uint64_t)code << 16) | (uint8_t)c;
238:    msg.data2 = (uint64_t)value; /* 0=release, 1=press, 2=repeat */
239:
240:    /* UTF-8 Handling */
241:    if (c != 0) {
242:      msg.payload[0] = c;
243:      msg.payload[1] = '\0';
244:    }
245:
246:    /* Apply Layout Overrides (skipped for Ctrl-folded control codes) */
247:    if (value != 0 && current_layout && !is_ctrl_combo) {
248:      for (int i = 0; i < 16 && current_layout->utf8_overrides[i].utf8 != NULL;
249:           i++) {
250:        if (current_layout->utf8_overrides[i].code == code &&
251:            current_layout->utf8_overrides[i].shifted == shift_pressed) {
252:          strlcpy(msg.payload, current_layout->utf8_overrides[i].utf8,
253:                  sizeof(msg.payload));
254:          break;
255:        }
256:      }
257:    }
258:
259:    /* A failed send here IS a lost keystroke: the focused process is gone or
260:     * its queue is full.  Discarding it made "the shell sometimes misses keys"
261:     * unattributable, which is the worst possible property for an input path.
262:     *
263:     * IRQ context, so there is no caller to return to and no room to log per
264:     * event -- a full queue would become an interrupt storm of its own.  The
265:     * loss is therefore COUNTED, and only the transition into a lossy state is
266:     * announced.  A counter that can be read after the fact turns an anecdote
267:     * into a number. */
268:    if (kernel_ipc_send(focus_pid, &msg) != 0) {
269:      if (kbd_dropped_events++ == 0)
270:        pr_err("keyboard: input to pid %d is being DROPPED (receiver gone or "
271:               "queue full); further drops are counted, not logged\n",
272:               focus_pid);
273:    }
274:  }
275:}
276:
277:/* Compositor sinks for pointer events (graphics layer). These update window
278: * state + damage; the repaint is the compositor's own 30 Hz tick. */
279:extern void compositor_update_mouse(int dx, int dy, int absolute);
280:extern void compositor_handle_click(int button, int state);
281:
282:/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *
283: * INPUT DECOUPLING (DIR-02/DIR-03, #68/#131/#194).
284: *
285: * The hardware input IRQs (virtio-input, PS/2) no longer touch the compositor.
286: * They ONLY enqueue a raw evdev event into the ring below (input_report); the
287: * dispatch — key->layout+IPC, pointer->compositor — runs in input_drain(),
288: * called from the compositor tick (timer IRQ, CPU0).  So the input IRQs never
289: * take compositor_lock and never mutate the window-list, killing the
290: * cross-core input-IRQ-vs-render stall (#194) and the IRQ-context window
291: * mutation from those paths (#68).  Dispatch is now a single serialized
292: * bottom-half in one context (the tick), reflected in the same tick's render.
293: *
294: * DO NOT MIGRATE to the kthread path (input_thread_entry / input_server_start):
295: * that kthread infra is UNSTABLE and DISABLED — see docs/report/KTHREAD-STATUS.md
296: * and the banner on input_server_start() below.  kthread_block/arch_cpu_yield
297: * stall CPU0 on the yield-to-USER leg, and a kthread created that way lives
298: * outside the per-CPU idle-task ordering the SMP scheduler relies on.  The
299: * correct end state for IRQ-decoupled input is a SUPERVISED USERLAND PROCESS
300: * (the notification-service model), not a kernel thread.  Until then, dispatch
301: * stays in this tick bottom-half.
302: * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
303:
304:struct input_evt {
305:  uint16_t type;
306:  uint16_t code;
307:  int32_t value;
308:};
309:
310:#define INPUT_RING_SZ 256 /* power of two; ~256 evdev events of backlog */
311:static struct input_evt input_ring[INPUT_RING_SZ];
312:static volatile uint32_t input_ring_head; /* producer index (IRQ) */
313:static volatile uint32_t input_ring_tail; /* consumer index (thread) */
314:static DEFINE_SPINLOCK(input_ring_lock);
315:static uint64_t input_ring_dropped;
316:static struct wait_queue_head input_wait_queue;
317:static int input_ring_pop(struct input_evt *out);
318:
319:/* input_dispatch - the actual event handling (key->layout+IPC, pointer->
320: * compositor).  Currently invoked SYNCHRONOUSLY from input_report; becomes
321: * the input server thread's body once the yield-to-user path is fixed. */
322:static void input_dispatch(uint16_t type, uint16_t code, int32_t value) {
323:  switch (type) {
324:  case EV_KEY:
325:    if (code == BTN_LEFT || code == BTN_RIGHT || code == BTN_MIDDLE) {
326:      /* All pointer buttons reach the compositor; it drives WM actions
327:       * (drag/resize/titlebar) from BTN_LEFT only and forwards every
328:       * button to the focused app (right/middle were silently dropped
329:       * before, so apps could never see them). */
330:      compositor_handle_click((int)code, value);
331:    } else {
332:      keyboard_process_key(code, value);
333:      wake_up(&keyboard_wait_queue);
334:    }
335:    break;
336:  case EV_REL:
337:    if (code == REL_X) compositor_update_mouse(value, 0, 0);
338:    else if (code == REL_Y) compositor_update_mouse(0, value, 0);
339:    break;
340:  case EV_ABS:
341:    if (code == ABS_X) compositor_update_mouse(value, -1, 1);
342:    else if (code == ABS_Y) compositor_update_mouse(-1, value, 1);
343:    break;
344:  default: /* EV_SYN and others */
345:    break;
346:  }
347:}
348:
349:/*
350: * input_report - the single entry point for every input provider (IRQ / poll
351: * context).  DIAGNOSTIC/bottom-half mode: enqueue the raw event; the actual
352: * dispatch runs in input_drain() from the compositor tick (timer IRQ, CPU0) —
353: * proven context — so the virtio/ps2 INPUT IRQs no longer take compositor_lock
354: * (kills the cross-core input-IRQ-vs-render stall, #194/#68).
355: */
356:void input_report(uint16_t type, uint16_t code, int32_t value) {
357:  uint64_t flags;
358:  spin_lock_irqsave(&input_ring_lock, &flags);
359:  uint32_t next = (input_ring_head + 1) & (INPUT_RING_SZ - 1);
360:  if (next == input_ring_tail) {
361:    input_ring_dropped++;
362:  } else {
363:    input_ring[input_ring_head].type = type;
364:    input_ring[input_ring_head].code = code;
365:    input_ring[input_ring_head].value = value;
366:    input_ring_head = next;
367:  }
368:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&input_ring_lock, flags);
369:}
370:
371:/* input_drain - dispatch all queued raw events.  Called from the compositor
372: * tick (timer IRQ, CPU0), so input dispatch is serialized with the render in
373: * one context and never spins cross-core on compositor_lock from an input IRQ. */
374:void input_drain(void) {
375:  struct input_evt e;
376:  while (input_ring_pop(&e))
377:    input_dispatch(e.type, e.code, e.value);
378:}
379:
380:/* input_ring_pop - consumer side (input thread): pull one event, or 0 if empty.
381: * Part of the staged decoupling plumbing (unused until the thread is on). */
382:static int input_ring_pop(struct input_evt *out) {
383:  uint64_t flags;
384:  int got = 0;
385:  spin_lock_irqsave(&input_ring_lock, &flags);
386:  if (input_ring_tail != input_ring_head) {
387:    *out = input_ring[input_ring_tail];
388:    input_ring_tail = (input_ring_tail + 1) & (INPUT_RING_SZ - 1);
389:    got = 1;
390:  }
391:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&input_ring_lock, flags);
392:  return got;
393:}
394:
395:/* input_ring_nonempty - lost-wakeup guard: evaluated under the wq lock,
396: * serialized against a producer's wake_up() (see kthread_block).
397: * __attribute__((unused)): referenced only by the DISABLED kthread input server
398: * (input_server_start's body is compiled out — see KTHREAD-STATUS.md), kept as
399: * reference skeleton without tripping -Werror=unused-function. */
400:static int __attribute__((unused)) input_ring_nonempty(void *arg) {
401:  (void)arg;
402:  return input_ring_head != input_ring_tail;
403:}
404:
405:/* input_thread_entry - the input server kernel thread body (staged): drains
406: * the ring and dispatches in TASK context, blocking when idle.  DISABLED —
407: * input_server_start (its only user) is compiled out (KTHREAD-STATUS.md); kept
408: * as the reference skeleton for the future USERLAND input service.  unused so
409: * -Werror=unused-function does not fire. */
410:static void __attribute__((unused)) input_thread_entry(void) {
411:  for (;;) {
412:    struct input_evt e;
413:    while (input_ring_pop(&e))
414:      input_dispatch(e.type, e.code, e.value);
415:    kthread_block(&input_wait_queue, input_ring_nonempty, NULL);
416:  }
417:}
418:
419:/* input_server_start - create the input server kernel thread.
420: *
421: * !!! DISABLED — DO NOT ENABLE (KTHREAD-STATUS, docs/report/KTHREAD-STATUS.md).
422: * The kthread-based input server is UNSTABLE and UNTESTED.  Two problems, both
423: * unfixed:
424: *   1. kthread_block()/arch_cpu_yield() cooperatively switch TO a freshly-woken
425: *      task; the yield-to-USER leg stalls CPU0 (a cross-CPU EL0-return quirk in
426: *      the hand-rolled epilogue).
427: *   2. A kthread created here lives OUTSIDE the per-CPU idle-task ordering the
428: *      SMP scheduler relies on for process sandboxing, so it can perturb the
429: *      idle/pick invariants (#169/#170 family).
430: * Input is dispatched safely instead from the timer-tick bottom-half
431: * (input_drain, kernel/core/timer.c).  The correct end state is input as a
432: * SUPERVISED USERLAND PROCESS (the notification-service model), NOT a kthread.
433: *
434: * The body is compiled out unless NEXS_ENABLE_UNSTABLE_KTHREAD_INPUT is defined,
435: * so this can never be wired up by accident (an unguarded call is a no-op that
436: * warns).  See also kthread_create()/kthread_block() (kernel/sched/process.c)
437: * and arch_cpu_yield() (kernel/include/kernel/arch.h): same status. */
438:void input_server_start(void) {
439:#ifdef NEXS_ENABLE_UNSTABLE_KTHREAD_INPUT
440:  INIT_LIST_HEAD(&input_wait_queue.task_list);
441:  spin_lock_init(&input_wait_queue.lock);
442:  (void)input_ring_dropped;
443:  kthread_create("input", input_thread_entry);
444:  pr_info("%s", "Input: server thread started (IRQ-decoupled dispatch)\n");
445:#else
446:  (void)input_ring_dropped;
447:  pr_warn("%s", "input_server_start: DISABLED (unstable kthread infra — see "
448:                "docs/report/KTHREAD-STATUS.md); using tick bottom-half\n");
449:#endif
450:}
451:
452:/*
453: * Poll keyboard for new input
454: */
455:void keyboard_poll(void) {
456:  struct virtio_input_event event;
457:
458:  while (virtio_input_poll(&event)) {
459:    input_report(event.type, event.code, event.value);
460:  }
461:}

463:/*
464: * Check if keyboard has buffered input
465: */
466:/*
467: * Read one character from keyboard buffer (non-blocking) - DEPRECATED
468: * Standard input should now be handled via IPC messages.
469: */
470:int keyboard_read_char_nonblock(void) { return -1; }
471:
472:/*
473: * Read one character from keyboard buffer (blocking) - DEPRECATED
474: */
475:char keyboard_read_char(void) { return 0; }
476:
477:/*
478: * Read a line of input (blocking, with echo)
479: */
480:int keyboard_read_line(char *buf, int max_len) {
481:  int i = 0;
482:
483:  while (i < max_len - 1) {
484:    char c = keyboard_read_char();
485:
486:    if (c == '\n' || c == '\r') {
487:      buf[i] = '\0';
488:      return i;
489:    }
490:
491:    if (c == '\b' || c == 127) {
492:      if (i > 0) {
493:        i--;
494:        /* Echo backspace */
495:        printk("\b \b");
496:      }
497:      continue;
498:    }
499:
500:    if (c >= 32 && c < 127) {
501:      buf[i++] = c;
502:      /* Echo character */
503:      printk("%c", c);
504:    }
505:  }
506:
507:  buf[i] = '\0';
508:  return i;
509:}
