@@@ kernel/drivers/pci/pci.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/drivers/pci/pci.c
3: * Minimal PCI Bus Driver
4: */
5:#include <kernel/types.h>
6:#include <kernel/printk.h>
7:#include <kernel/string.h>
8:#include <kernel/hal.h>
9:#include <drivers/pci.h>
10:
11:#define PCI_CONFIG_ADDR 0xCF8
12:#define PCI_CONFIG_DATA 0xCFC
13:
14:static DEFINE_SPINLOCK(pci_lock);
15:
16:/* Arch config backend. NULL = built-in CF8/CFC port I/O (amd64). aarch64 sets
17: * ECAM MMIO ops via pci_set_config_ops(). */
18:static struct pci_config_ops *cfg_ops = NULL;
19:
20:void pci_set_config_ops(struct pci_config_ops *ops) { cfg_ops = ops; }
21:
22:uint32_t pci_config_read(uint8_t bus, uint8_t device, uint8_t func, uint8_t offset) {
23:    if (cfg_ops) return cfg_ops->read32(bus, device, func, offset);
24:
25:    uint32_t address = (uint32_t)((uint32_t)bus << 16) |
26:                       (uint32_t)((uint32_t)device << 11) |
27:                       (uint32_t)((uint32_t)func << 8) |
28:                       (offset & 0xFC) |
29:                       ((uint32_t)0x80000000);
30:
31:    uint64_t flags;
32:    spin_lock_irqsave(&pci_lock, &flags);
33:    hal_write32(PCI_CONFIG_ADDR, address);
34:    uint32_t val = hal_read32(PCI_CONFIG_DATA);
35:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&pci_lock, flags);
36:    return val;
37:}
38:
39:void pci_config_write(uint8_t bus, uint8_t device, uint8_t func, uint8_t offset, uint32_t value) {
40:    if (cfg_ops) { cfg_ops->write32(bus, device, func, offset, value); return; }
41:
42:    uint32_t address = (uint32_t)((uint32_t)bus << 16) |
43:                       (uint32_t)((uint32_t)device << 11) |
44:                       (uint32_t)((uint32_t)func << 8) |
45:                       (offset & 0xFC) |
46:                       ((uint32_t)0x80000000);
47:
48:    uint64_t flags;
49:    spin_lock_irqsave(&pci_lock, &flags);
50:    hal_write32(PCI_CONFIG_ADDR, address);
51:    hal_write32(PCI_CONFIG_DATA, value);
52:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&pci_lock, flags);
53:}
54:
55:/* 
56: * Find a device by Vendor and Device ID
57: * Returns bus:device:func in a single 32-bit int (or -1 if not found)
58: */
59:int pci_find_device(uint16_t vendor, uint16_t device_id) {
60:    for (int bus = 0; bus < 256; bus++) {
61:        for (int dev = 0; dev < 32; dev++) {
62:            uint32_t reg0 = pci_config_read(bus, dev, 0, 0);
63:            uint16_t v = reg0 & 0xFFFF;
64:            uint16_t d = reg0 >> 16;
65:            
66:            if (v == vendor && d == device_id) {
67:                return (bus << 16) | (dev << 8) | 0;
68:            }
69:            
70:            /* Check if multi-function */
71:            uint32_t header_type = pci_config_read(bus, dev, 0, 0x0C);
72:            if (header_type & 0x80) {
73:                for (int func = 1; func < 8; func++) {
74:                    reg0 = pci_config_read(bus, dev, func, 0);
75:                    if ((reg0 & 0xFFFF) == vendor && (reg0 >> 16) == device_id) {
76:                        return (bus << 16) | (dev << 8) | func;
77:                    }
78:                }
79:            }
80:        }
81:    }
82:    return -1;
83:}
84:
85:/* 
86: * Enumerate all PCI devices and call callback
87: */
88:void pci_enumerate(void (*callback)(int bdf, uint16_t vendor, uint16_t device_id)) {
89:    for (int bus = 0; bus < 256; bus++) {
90:        for (int dev = 0; dev < 32; dev++) {
91:            uint32_t reg0 = pci_config_read(bus, dev, 0, 0);
92:            uint16_t v = reg0 & 0xFFFF;
93:            uint16_t d = reg0 >> 16;
94:            
95:            if (v == 0xFFFF) continue;
96:            
97:            callback((bus << 16) | (dev << 8) | 0, v, d);
98:            
99:            /* Check if multi-function */
100:            uint32_t header_type = pci_config_read(bus, dev, 0, 0x0C);
101:            if (header_type & 0x80) {
102:                for (int func = 1; func < 8; func++) {
103:                    reg0 = pci_config_read(bus, dev, func, 0);
104:                    v = reg0 & 0xFFFF;
105:                    d = reg0 >> 16;
106:                    if (v != 0xFFFF) {
107:                        callback((bus << 16) | (dev << 8) | func, v, d);
108:                    }
109:                }
110:            }
111:        }
112:    }
113:}
114:
115:/* Get BAR address (simplistic) */
116:uint32_t pci_get_bar(int bdf, int bar_index) {
117:    uint8_t bus = (bdf >> 16) & 0xFF;
118:    uint8_t dev = (bdf >> 8) & 0xFF;
119:    uint8_t func = bdf & 0xFF;
120:    return pci_config_read(bus, dev, func, 0x10 + (bar_index * 4));
121:}
122:
123:/* Get Interrupt Line */
124:uint8_t pci_get_interrupt(int bdf) {
125:    uint8_t bus = (bdf >> 16) & 0xFF;
126:    uint8_t dev = (bdf >> 8) & 0xFF;
127:    uint8_t func = bdf & 0xFF;
128:    return pci_config_read(bus, dev, func, 0x3C) & 0xFF;
129:}
130:
131:/* Class triplet at config offset 0x08:
132: *   byte0 = revision, byte1 = prog_if, byte2 = subclass, byte3 = class_code.
133: * Returns the raw 32-bit word; callers shift out the field they want. */
134:uint32_t pci_get_class(int bdf) {
135:    uint8_t bus = (bdf >> 16) & 0xFF;
136:    uint8_t dev = (bdf >> 8) & 0xFF;
137:    uint8_t func = bdf & 0xFF;
138:    return pci_config_read(bus, dev, func, 0x08);
139:}
140:
141:/* Header type at config offset 0x0C, byte2. Bit7 = multi-function. */
142:uint8_t pci_get_header_type(int bdf) {
143:    uint8_t bus = (bdf >> 16) & 0xFF;
144:    uint8_t dev = (bdf >> 8) & 0xFF;
145:    uint8_t func = bdf & 0xFF;
146:    return (pci_config_read(bus, dev, func, 0x0C) >> 16) & 0xFF;
147:}
148:/* Get BAR size */
149:uint32_t pci_get_bar_size(int bdf, int bar_index) {
150:    uint8_t bus = (bdf >> 16) & 0xFF;
151:    uint8_t dev = (bdf >> 8) & 0xFF;
152:    uint8_t func = bdf & 0xFF;
153:    uint8_t offset = 0x10 + (bar_index * 4);
154:
155:    uint32_t original = pci_config_read(bus, dev, func, offset);
156:    pci_config_write(bus, dev, func, offset, 0xFFFFFFFF);
157:    uint32_t size = pci_config_read(bus, dev, func, offset);
158:    pci_config_write(bus, dev, func, offset, original);
159:
160:    if (size == 0 || size == 0xFFFFFFFF) return 0;
161:    
162:    /* Clear flags */
163:    if (size & 1) { /* I/O */
164:        size &= 0xFFFFFFFC;
165:    } else { /* Memory */
166:        size &= 0xFFFFFFF0;
167:    }
168:
169:    return ~size + 1;
170:}
171:
172:/*
173: * pci_scan_and_register - arch-neutral PCI enumeration into the HAL registry.
174: *
175: * Defines the long-declared DRV-PCI-01 (#51) function. Walks config space via
176: * the active backend (CF8/CFC on amd64, ECAM on aarch64), and for each present
177: * function registers a hal_device carrying its vendor/device, class triplet and
178: * first BAR (64-bit aware), enabling bus-master + MMIO/IO decode. The bound
179: * driver (xHCI/...) maps its own BAR window. IRQ is left 0: the providers that
180: * use this path (USB, behind this generic scan) are polled, and PCI INTx->GIC
181: * routing is platform-specific (derive from FDT when an IRQ-driven PCI device
182: * needs it). amd64 keeps its own richer callback (virtio legacy/modern), so
183: * this is currently the aarch64 ECAM entry point.
184: */
185:extern int arch_vmm_map_device(uint64_t base, uint64_t size);
186:
187:/* Platform MMIO windows for BAR assignment. Set by the arch (aarch64 from its
188: * DTB ranges) before pci_scan_and_register(). When zero (amd64), firmware has
189: * already programmed the BARs and we never assign. */
190:static uint64_t mmio32_next, mmio32_end, mmio64_next, mmio64_end;
191:
192:void pci_set_mmio_windows(uint64_t m32_base, uint64_t m32_size,
193:                          uint64_t m64_base, uint64_t m64_size) {
194:    mmio32_next = m32_base; mmio32_end = m32_base + m32_size;
195:    mmio64_next = m64_base; mmio64_end = m64_base + m64_size;
196:}
197:
198:/* Size-aligned bump allocation from the platform MMIO window. */
199:static uint64_t pci_alloc_mmio(uint64_t size, int is64) {
200:    if (size < 0x1000) size = 0x1000;
201:    if (is64 && mmio64_next) {
202:        uint64_t a = (mmio64_next + size - 1) & ~(size - 1);
203:        if (a + size <= mmio64_end) { mmio64_next = a + size; return a; }
204:    }
205:    if (mmio32_next) {
206:        uint64_t a = (mmio32_next + size - 1) & ~(size - 1);
207:        if (a + size <= mmio32_end) { mmio32_next = a + size; return a; }
208:    }
209:    return 0;
210:}
211:
212:static void pci_register_one(int bdf, uint16_t vendor, uint16_t device) {
213:    struct hal_device dev;
214:    memset(&dev, 0, sizeof(dev));
215:    dev.bus_type = HAL_BUS_TYPE_PCI;
216:    dev.vendor_id = vendor;
217:    dev.device_id = device;
218:    dev.pci_bdf = (uint32_t)bdf;
219:
220:    uint32_t cls = pci_get_class(bdf);
221:    dev.class_code = (cls >> 24) & 0xFF;
222:    dev.subclass = (cls >> 16) & 0xFF;
223:    dev.prog_if = (cls >> 8) & 0xFF;
224:    dev.header_type = pci_get_header_type(bdf);
225:
226:    uint8_t bus = (bdf >> 16) & 0xFF, d = (bdf >> 8) & 0xFF, f = bdf & 0xFF;
227:
228:    /* First BAR; follow a 64-bit memory BAR into its high half. */
229:    uint32_t b0 = pci_get_bar(bdf, 0);
230:    int is_io = (b0 & 1) != 0;
231:    int is64 = (!is_io) && ((b0 & 0x6) == 0x4);
232:    uint64_t base;
233:    if (is_io) {
234:        base = (uint64_t)(b0 & ~0x3u);
235:    } else {
236:        base = (uint64_t)(b0 & ~0xFu);
237:        if (is64) base |= ((uint64_t)pci_get_bar(bdf, 1)) << 32;
238:    }
239:
240:    /* Bare-metal aarch64 virt has no firmware PCI resource assignment, so MMIO
241:     * BARs arrive unprogrammed (base 0). Assign one from the platform window. */
242:    if (!is_io && base == 0 && (mmio32_next || mmio64_next)) {
243:        uint32_t size = pci_get_bar_size(bdf, 0);
244:        if (size) {
245:            uint64_t a = pci_alloc_mmio(size, is64);
246:            if (a) {
247:                pci_config_write(bus, d, f, 0x10, (uint32_t)a);
248:                if (is64) pci_config_write(bus, d, f, 0x14, (uint32_t)(a >> 32));
249:                base = a;
250:            }
251:        }
252:    }
253:
254:    /* Enable IO | MEM | BusMaster after BAR assignment. */
255:    uint32_t cmd = pci_config_read(bus, d, f, 0x04);
256:    pci_config_write(bus, d, f, 0x04, cmd | 0x7);
257:
258:    dev.base = base;
259:    dev.irq = 0; /* polled providers; INTx routing is platform-specific */
260:
261:    if (vendor == 0x1AF4)
262:        snprintf(dev.name, sizeof(dev.name), "VirtIO-%d", device);
263:    else
264:        snprintf(dev.name, sizeof(dev.name), "PCI-%04x:%04x", vendor, device);
265:
266:    if (!is_io && base)
267:        arch_vmm_map_device(base, 0x20000);
268:
269:    hal_register_device(&dev);
270:}
271:
272:void pci_scan_and_register(void) {
273:    pr_info("%s", "PCI: scanning config space (ECAM/port)...\n");
274:    for (int bus = 0; bus < 256; bus++) {
275:        for (int d = 0; d < 32; d++) {
276:            uint32_t r0 = pci_config_read(bus, d, 0, 0);
277:            uint16_t v = r0 & 0xFFFF;
278:            if (v == 0xFFFF) continue;
279:            pci_register_one((bus << 16) | (d << 8), v, r0 >> 16);
280:
281:            /* Multi-function devices: header type bit7 (config 0x0C bit23). */
282:            if (pci_config_read(bus, d, 0, 0x0C) & 0x800000) {
283:                for (int fn = 1; fn < 8; fn++) {
284:                    r0 = pci_config_read(bus, d, fn, 0);
285:                    v = r0 & 0xFFFF;
286:                    if (v == 0xFFFF) continue;
287:                    pci_register_one((bus << 16) | (d << 8) | fn, v, r0 >> 16);
288:                }
289:            }
290:        }
291:    }
292:}
293:

@@@ kernel/drivers/ps2/ps2.c @@@
1:/* kernel/drivers/ps2/ps2.c */
2:#include <arch/arch.h> // ← Questo include inb/outb
3:#include <drivers/keyboard.h>
4:#include <drivers/ps2.h>
5:#include <drivers/virtio_input.h>
6:#include <kernel/io_poll.h>
7:#include <kernel/irq.h>
8:#include <kernel/printk.h>
9:
10:#ifdef ARCH_AMD64
11:
12:/* The 8259 PIC remaps IRQ n -> IDT vector 32+n (pic_init).  irq_register(),
13: * irq_dispatch() and pic_chip_enable() all key on the VECTOR, not the bare
14: * IRQ line, so device IRQs must be registered as 32+line. */
15:#define PIC_VECTOR_BASE 32
16:
17:/* Bounded polls — return 0 when ready, -1 on timeout. The iteration cap is the
18: * whole point: on a board without an 8042 the status port floats high, so a
19: * naive wait would never progress. Bring-up must degrade, never block. */
20:static int ps2_wait_write(void) {
21:  int ok;
22:  poll_until(ok, !(inb(0x64) & 0x02), 100000);
23:  return ok ? 0 : -1;
24:}
25:
26:static int ps2_wait_read(void) {
27:  int ok;
28:  poll_until(ok, inb(0x64) & 0x01, 100000);
29:  return ok ? 0 : -1;
30:}
31:
32:/* Returns 0 and stores the byte on success, -1 on timeout (leaves *out). */
33:static int ps2_read_data(uint8_t *out) {
34:  if (ps2_wait_read() != 0)
35:    return -1;
36:  *out = inb(0x60);
37:  return 0;
38:}
39:
40:static int ps2_write_cmd(uint8_t cmd) {
41:  if (ps2_wait_write() != 0)
42:    return -1;
43:  outb(0x64, cmd);
44:  return 0;
45:}
46:
47:static int ps2_write_data(uint8_t data) {
48:  if (ps2_wait_write() != 0)
49:    return -1;
50:  outb(0x60, data);
51:  return 0;
52:}
53:
54:/* Send a byte to the SECOND port (mouse/AUX): the 8042 routes the next 0x60
55: * write to the mouse only after the 0xD4 controller command.  Without it every
56: * "mouse" byte goes to the keyboard, so the mouse is never enabled.  Returns
57: * the device's reply (ACK 0xFA on success). */
58:static uint8_t ps2_mouse_cmd(uint8_t cmd) {
59:  uint8_t reply = 0xFF;
60:  ps2_write_cmd(0xD4);
61:  ps2_write_data(cmd);
62:  ps2_read_data(&reply);
63:  return reply;
64:}
65:
66:/* ==================== KEYBOARD ==================== */
67:static void ps2_keyboard_handler(uint32_t irq, void *data) {
68:  (void)irq;
69:  (void)data;
70:  uint8_t scancode = inb(0x60);
71:
72:  uint16_t code = scancode & 0x7F;
73:  int pressed = (scancode & 0x80) == 0;
74:
75:  input_report(EV_KEY, code, pressed ? 1 : 0);
76:  input_report(EV_SYN, 0, 0);
77:}
78:
79:/* ==================== MOUSE ==================== */
80:static uint8_t mouse_packet[4];
81:static int mouse_byte = 0;
82:static int mouse_has_wheel = 0;
83:
84:static void ps2_mouse_handler(uint32_t irq, void *data) {
85:  (void)irq;
86:  (void)data;
87:
88:  uint8_t byte = inb(0x60);
89:
90:  /* Packet resync: packet[0] (status) always has bit 3 set. If the byte we
91:   * expect as the first one doesn't, the stream is misaligned (a leftover init
92:   * byte or a missed IRQ) — drop it instead of reading dx/dy from the wrong
93:   * bytes, which biases motion and drags the cursor sideways forever. */
94:  if (mouse_byte == 0 && !(byte & 0x08))
95:    return;
96:
97:  mouse_packet[mouse_byte++] = byte;
98:  if (mouse_byte < (mouse_has_wheel ? 4 : 3))
99:    return;
100:  mouse_byte = 0;
101:
102:  uint8_t status = mouse_packet[0];
103:
104:  input_report(EV_KEY, BTN_LEFT, (status & 0x01) ? 1 : 0);
105:  input_report(EV_KEY, BTN_RIGHT, (status & 0x02) ? 1 : 0);
106:  input_report(EV_KEY, BTN_MIDDLE, (status & 0x04) ? 1 : 0);
107:
108:  /* Skip motion when the device flags an X/Y overflow — the deltas are bogus. */
109:  if (!(status & 0xC0)) {
110:    int dx = (int8_t)mouse_packet[1];
111:    int dy = -(int8_t)mouse_packet[2];
112:    if (dx)
113:      input_report(EV_REL, REL_X, dx);
114:    if (dy)
115:      input_report(EV_REL, REL_Y, dy);
116:    if (mouse_has_wheel && mouse_packet[3] != 0)
117:      input_report(EV_REL, REL_WHEEL, (int8_t)mouse_packet[3]);
118:  }
119:
120:  input_report(EV_SYN, 0, 0);
121:}
122:
123:void ps2_init(void) {
124:  pr_info("%s", "PS/2: Initializing controller...\n");
125:
126:  /* Non-blocking presence gate. On machines without an 8042 (many amd64 VMs,
127:   * e.g. UTM on Apple silicon) the status port floats to 0xFF; the old
128:   * unbounded "while (inb(0x64) & 1) inb(0x60);" flush then spun forever and
129:   * hung the boot. Detect the absent controller and skip cleanly. */
130:  if (inb(0x64) == 0xFF) {
131:    pr_info("%s", "PS/2: no controller present (0xFF) — skipping\n");
132:    return;
133:  }
134:
135:  ps2_write_cmd(0xAD); /* disable keyboard port during setup */
136:  ps2_write_cmd(0xA7); /* disable mouse (AUX) port during setup */
137:
138:  /* Bounded output-buffer flush (this loop was the UTM hang). */
139:  for (int i = 0; i < 16 && (inb(0x64) & 0x01); i++)
140:    (void)inb(0x60);
141:
142:  /* Controller self-test: 0xAA must answer 0x55. Any other reply — or a read
143:   * timeout — means there is no usable controller, so skip non-blocking. */
144:  uint8_t resp = 0;
145:  ps2_write_cmd(0xAA);
146:  if (ps2_read_data(&resp) != 0 || resp != 0x55) {
147:    pr_info("PS/2: self-test failed (0x%x) — skipping\n", resp);
148:    return;
149:  }
150:
151:  /* Read config byte, enable IRQs for both ports (bits 0,1), write it back. */
152:  ps2_write_cmd(0x20);
153:  uint8_t cfg = 0;
154:  if (ps2_read_data(&cfg) != 0)
155:    cfg = 0;
156:  cfg |= 0x03;
157:  ps2_write_cmd(0x60);
158:  ps2_write_data(cfg);
159:
160:  ps2_write_cmd(0xAE); /* enable keyboard port */
161:  ps2_write_cmd(0xA8); /* enable mouse (AUX) port */
162:
163:  /* Mouse setup — every byte goes through 0xD4 (ps2_mouse_cmd), or it would
164:   * be delivered to the keyboard and the mouse would never report. */
165:  ps2_mouse_cmd(0xF6); /* set defaults */
166:  ps2_mouse_cmd(0xF4); /* enable data reporting */
167:
168:  /* IntelliMouse 3-button + wheel "magic knock": sample rates 200/100/80,
169:   * then read the device id; 0x03 means the wheel is active. */
170:  ps2_mouse_cmd(0xF3);
171:  ps2_mouse_cmd(200);
172:  ps2_mouse_cmd(0xF3);
173:  ps2_mouse_cmd(100);
174:  ps2_mouse_cmd(0xF3);
175:  ps2_mouse_cmd(80);
176:  ps2_mouse_cmd(0xF2); /* get device id: returns ACK ... */
177:  uint8_t id = 0;
178:  if (ps2_read_data(&id) == 0 && id == 0x03) { /* ... then the id byte */
179:    mouse_has_wheel = 1;
180:    pr_info("%s", "PS/2: Mouse with scroll wheel detected\n");
181:  }
182:
183:  /* Drain bytes the mouse queued while we were configuring it so the IRQ handler
184:   * starts on a packet boundary (the handler also resyncs on the status bit). */
185:  for (int i = 0; i < 16 && (inb(0x64) & 0x01); i++)
186:    (void)inb(0x60);
187:
188:  /* Register keyboard (IRQ 1) at vector 33 and mouse (IRQ 12) at vector 44. */
189:  if (irq_register(PIC_VECTOR_BASE + 1, ps2_keyboard_handler, NULL) != 0)
190:    pr_err("%s", "ps2: cannot register the keyboard IRQ — no key events\n");
191:  if (irq_register(PIC_VECTOR_BASE + 12, ps2_mouse_handler, NULL) != 0)
192:    pr_err("%s", "ps2: cannot register the mouse IRQ — no pointer events\n");
193:
194:  pr_info("%s", "PS/2: Keyboard + Mouse ready (IRQ 1/12 -> vec 33/44)\n");
195:}
196:
197:#else
198:
199:/* Stub per AArch64 */
200:void ps2_init(void) { /* Do nothing on AArch64 */ }
201:
202:#endif

@@@ kernel/drivers/timer/pic_pit.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/amd64/drivers/pic_pit.c
3: * Legacy 8259 PIC and 8253 PIT — amd64
4: *
5: * Initialises the 8259A Programmable Interrupt Controller (PIC) pair and the
6: * 8253/8254 Programmable Interval Timer (PIT) for x86-64.  Also provides the
7: * struct irq_chip implementation (pic_chip) that is registered as the active
8: * chip on amd64 via pic_init().
9: *
10: * 8259 PIC pair overview:
11: *   Two cascaded 8259A chips (PIC1 + PIC2) provide IRQ lines 0-15.  They are
12: *   remapped in pic_init() to IDT vectors 32-47 (IRQ n → vector 32+n) to
13: *   avoid collision with CPU exception vectors 0-31.  PIC1 handles IRQs 0-7;
14: *   PIC2 handles IRQs 8-15 and cascades to PIC1 via IRQ2.
15: *
16: * 8253/8254 PIT overview:
17: *   pit_init_hz() programs PIT Channel 0 in mode 3 (square wave) with
18: *   divisor = 1193182 / hz.  The PIT output is connected to PIC1 IRQ0
19: *   (vector 32).  On QEMU the LAPIC timer supersedes the PIT for SMP, but
20: *   pic_send_eoi is still needed for PIC IRQ acknowledgement.
21: *
22: * pic_chip and the dispatch contract (IRQ-01, resolved):
23: *   pic_chip is registered as current_chip in irq.c via irq_register_chip().
24: *   amd64 is a VECTORED architecture: the vector arrives with the trap frame,
25: *   so a GIC-style acknowledge() loop makes no sense — pic_chip_acknowledge()
26: *   returns 1023 by design so a stray irq_handler() call stays a no-op.
27: *   Dispatch happens in idt.c via irq_dispatch(); the EOI is chip-owned:
28: *   idt.c calls irq_chip_end(vec) and pic_chip_end() performs the complete
29: *   LAPIC + 8259 sequence (nothing bypasses the chip anymore).
30: *
31: * Invariants:
32: *   - pic_init() must be called before any device IRQ is unmasked on amd64.
33: *   - IRQ numbers passed to pic_chip_enable/disable/end are in the range
34: *     32-47 (IDT vector space); the PIC hardware line = irq - 32.
35: *   - Spurious IRQ7/IRQ15 (vectors 39/47) must be filtered with
36: *     pic_handle_spurious() BEFORE dispatch: they are not real interrupts
37: *     and their EOI rules differ (none for IRQ7; master-only for IRQ15).
38: */
39:#include <kernel/types.h>
40:#include <kernel/hal.h>
41:#include <kernel/irq.h>
42:#include <kernel/printk.h>
43:#include <kernel/arch.h>
44:#include <arch/pt_regs.h>
45:#include <arch/amd64_internal.h>
46:#include <arch/amd64/apic.h>
47:
48:/* Prototypes to satisfy -Wmissing-prototypes */
49:void pic_init(void);
50:void pic_send_eoi(uint8_t irq);
51:int pic_handle_spurious(uint32_t vec);
52:struct pt_regs *amd64_timer_interrupt(struct pt_regs *regs);
53:struct pt_regs *amd64_keyboard_interrupt(struct pt_regs *regs);
54:
55:/* PIC command and data I/O ports.
56: * PIC1 (master): CMD = 0x20, DATA = 0x21 (OCW1/ICW registers).
57: * PIC2 (slave):  CMD = 0xA0, DATA = 0xA1. */
58:#define PIC1_CMD  0x20
59:#define PIC1_DATA 0x21
60:#define PIC2_CMD  0xA0
61:#define PIC2_DATA 0xA1
62:
63:/* PIT (8253/8254) I/O ports.
64: * PIT_CH0 (0x40): Channel 0 data port (read/write counter).
65: * PIT_CMD (0x43): Mode/Command register (write-only). */
66:#define PIT_CH0   0x40
67:#define PIT_CMD   0x43
68:
69:extern volatile uint64_t jiffies;
70:extern void timer_tick(void); /* generic scheduler tick */
71:void pit_init_hz(uint32_t hz);
72:
73:void pic_unmask(uint8_t irq);
74:void pic_mask(uint8_t irq);
75:
76:/*
77: * pic_chip_enable - unmask a PIC IRQ line (via pic_unmask).
78: *
79: * @irq: IDT vector number (32-47 for PIC IRQs 0-15).
80: *
81: * Translates the IDT vector to a PIC hardware line (irq - 32) and clears
82: * the corresponding mask bit in PIC1_DATA or PIC2_DATA.
83: *
84: * I/O side effects: reads then writes PIC1_DATA or PIC2_DATA.
85: * Locking: none; called from irq_register() which is boot-path only.
86: * IRQ context: safe on single-core.
87: */
88:static void pic_chip_enable(uint32_t irq) {
89:    if (irq >= 32 && irq < 48) {
90:        pic_unmask(irq - 32);
91:    }
92:}
93:
94:/*
95: * pic_mask - mask (disable) a PIC hardware IRQ line.
96: *
97: * @irq: PIC hardware line (0-15; 0-7 for PIC1, 8-15 for PIC2).
98: *
99: * Sets the corresponding bit in the OCW1 (mask) register of PIC1_DATA (for
100: * irq 0-7) or PIC2_DATA (for irq 8-15; hardware line = irq - 8).
101: *
102: * I/O side effects: hal_read8 + hal_write8 on PIC1_DATA or PIC2_DATA.
103: * Locking: none.
104: * IRQ context: safe.
105: */
106:void pic_mask(uint8_t irq) {
107:    uint16_t port;
108:    uint8_t value;
109:    if (irq < 8) {
110:        port = PIC1_DATA;
111:    } else {
112:        port = PIC2_DATA;
113:        irq -= 8;
114:    }
115:    value = hal_read8(port) | (1 << irq);
116:    hal_write8(port, value);
117:}
118:
119:/*
120: * pic_chip_disable - mask a PIC IRQ line (via pic_mask).
121: *
122: * @irq: IDT vector number (32-47).
123: *
124: * Translates to hardware line and calls pic_mask().
125: *
126: * I/O side effects: same as pic_mask.
127: * Locking: none.
128: * IRQ context: safe.
129: */
130:static void pic_chip_disable(uint32_t irq) {
131:    if (irq >= 32 && irq < 48) {
132:        pic_mask(irq - 32);
133:    }
134:}
135:
136:/*
137: * pic_chip_acknowledge - chip->acknowledge() for the amd64 PIC path.
138: *
139: * Returns 1023 unconditionally — BY DESIGN (IRQ-01 resolution): amd64 is
140: * vectored, the vector arrives with the trap frame, so there is no
141: * IAR-equivalent register to read.  The sentinel keeps a stray
142: * irq_handler() call (the aarch64 acknowledge-loop entry) a safe no-op.
143: *
144: * Locking: none.
145: * IRQ context: safe (never called in the amd64 hot path).
146: */
147:static uint32_t pic_chip_acknowledge(void) {
148:    /* Not used by PIC on x86 because the vector is in pt_regs */
149:    return 1023;
150:}
151:
152:/*
153: * pic_chip_end - chip-owned End-Of-Interrupt for amd64 (IRQ-01 fix).
154: *
155: * @irq: IDT vector number (32-255).
156: *
157: * Owns the COMPLETE amd64 EOI sequence — called via irq_chip_end() from the
158: * IDT common handler for every hardware vector:
159: *   1. lapic_eoi(): required for LAPIC-delivered vectors (timer, IPIs, MSI);
160: *      harmless no-op for ExtINT-delivered PIC lines.
161: *   2. pic_send_eoi(): only for the legacy PIC range (vectors 32-47).
162: * Nothing outside this function issues EOI writes on amd64 anymore.
163: *
164: * I/O side effects: LAPIC_EOI MMIO write; PIC1/PIC2 CMD port writes (32-47).
165: * Locking: none.
166: * IRQ context: YES — IDT path.
167: */
168:static void pic_chip_end(uint32_t irq) {
169:    lapic_eoi();
170:    if (irq >= 32 && irq < 48) {
171:        pic_send_eoi(irq - 32);
172:    }
173:}
174:
175:/* HALT_IPI_VECTOR: fixed LAPIC vector for the panic-halt broadcast.  The
176: * GIC counterpart is SGI0 (gic_send_ipi); the amd64 chip previously left
177: * send_ipi_all NULL, so panic() never stopped the other CPUs — they kept
178: * running against a dying kernel. */
179:#define HALT_IPI_VECTOR 0xFE
180:
181:/*
182: * halt_ipi_handler - peer-CPU side of the panic-halt broadcast.
183: *
184: * Mirrors cpu_halt_from_ipi() on the aarch64/GIC path (irq.c): set the
185: * global panic flag, stop the local timer, halt forever.  Never returns,
186: * so no EOI is issued — irrelevant during a panic.
187: */
188:static void halt_ipi_handler(uint32_t irq, void *data) {
189:    (void)irq;
190:    (void)data;
191:    extern volatile int panic_flag;
192:    panic_flag = 1;
193:    arch_timer_control(0);
194:    arch_cpu_halt();
195:}
196:
197:/*
198: * pic_chip_send_ipi_all - broadcast the panic-halt IPI to all other CPUs.
199: *
200: * LAPIC fixed-vector IPI with the all-excluding-self shorthand (the ICR
201: * destination field is ignored when a shorthand is used).
202: */
203:static void pic_chip_send_ipi_all(void) {
204:    lapic_send_ipi(0, ICR_FIXED | ICR_ASSERT | ICR_ALL_EXCL_SELF |
205:                          HALT_IPI_VECTOR);
206:}
207:
208:/* pic_chip: irq_chip implementation for the 8259A PIC pair.
209: * .init is NULL because pic_init() itself calls irq_register_chip() and
210: * then initialises the PIC; there is no separate init() callback needed.
211: * .acknowledge returns 1023 by design (vectored dispatch — see above). */
212:static struct irq_chip pic_chip = {
213:    .name = "8259 PIC",
214:    .init = NULL,
215:    .enable = pic_chip_enable,
216:    .disable = pic_chip_disable,
217:    .acknowledge = pic_chip_acknowledge,
218:    .send_ipi_all = pic_chip_send_ipi_all,
219:    .end = pic_chip_end,
220:};
221:
222:/*
223: * pic_init - initialise the 8259A PIC pair and register pic_chip.
224: *
225: * Sends the four ICW (Initialization Command Word) sequences to both PICs:
226: *   ICW1 (0x11 to CMD): start init, cascaded, ICW4 required.
227: *   ICW2 (to DATA): vector offset — PIC1 → 32, PIC2 → 40.
228: *   ICW3 (to DATA): PIC1 has slave on IRQ2 (0x04); PIC2 id=2 (0x02).
229: *   ICW4 (0x01 to DATA): 8086 mode, normal EOI.
230: * Then masks all IRQs except IRQ2 (cascade): PIC1_DATA=0xFB, PIC2_DATA=0xFF.
231: *
232: * Also registers pic_chip as the active irq_chip via irq_register_chip().
233: *
234: * I/O ports written: PIC1_CMD, PIC2_CMD, PIC1_DATA, PIC2_DATA.
235: * Locking: none; called once before SMP.
236: * IRQ context: NO.
237: */
238:void pic_init(void) {
239:    irq_register_chip(&pic_chip);
240:  /* Remap PIC IRQs 0-15 to interrupts 32-47 */
241:  hal_write8(PIC1_CMD, 0x11); /* ICW1: Init + ICW4 */
242:  hal_write8(PIC2_CMD, 0x11);
243:
244:  hal_write8(PIC1_DATA, 0x20); /* ICW2: PIC1 vector offset 32 */
245:  hal_write8(PIC2_DATA, 0x28); /* ICW2: PIC2 vector offset 40 */
246:
247:  hal_write8(PIC1_DATA, 0x04); /* ICW3: PIC1 has slave on IRQ2 */
248:  hal_write8(PIC2_DATA, 0x02); /* ICW3: PIC2 cascade identity */
249:
250:  hal_write8(PIC1_DATA, 0x01); /* ICW4: 8086 mode */
251:  hal_write8(PIC2_DATA, 0x01);
252:
253:  /* Start with all IRQs masked except slave cascade (IRQ 2) */
254:  hal_write8(PIC1_DATA, 0xFB);
255:  hal_write8(PIC2_DATA, 0xFF);
256:
257:  /* Panic-halt IPI receiver (LAPIC fixed vector; pic_chip_enable ignores
258:   * vectors >= 48, so this touches no 8259 mask). */
259:  /* If this fails the panic-halt IPI has no receiver, so a panic on one core
260:   * would leave the others running instead of halting.  Dropping the result
261:   * made that outcome indistinguishable from a working setup. */
262:  /* pic_init() is reached from TWO composition points on amd64
263:   * (arch/amd64/hal.c and arch/amd64/platform/platform.c).  The 8259
264:   * programming above is idempotent, so the double call was invisible; this
265:   * registration is NOT, and the second call gets -EBUSY.
266:   *
267:   * -EBUSY therefore means "already registered by the first call", which is the
268:   * intended end state and not a failure.  Anything else IS one: the halt IPI
269:   * would have no receiver and a panic on one core would leave the others
270:   * running.  Distinguishing the two is the whole point -- dropping the result
271:   * treated both as success.
272:   *
273:   * NOTE for the composition-root decision (ASTRA wants exactly one): which of
274:   * the two callers should own this wiring is recorded as an open question, not
275:   * settled here.  Suppressing the second CALL outright was tried and broke the
276:   * boot, so the second call is doing work the first does not. */
277:  {
278:    int hr = irq_register(HALT_IPI_VECTOR, halt_ipi_handler, NULL);
279:    if (hr != 0 && hr != -EBUSY)
280:      pr_err("PIC: cannot register the halt-IPI handler on vector %d (%d) — a "
281:             "kernel fault on one core will not stop the others\n",
282:             HALT_IPI_VECTOR, hr);
283:  }
284:
285:  pr_info("PIC Initialized and remapped to 32-47.\n");
286:}
287:
288:extern struct pt_regs *kernel_timer_tick(struct pt_regs *regs);
289:
290:/* The interrupt handlers amd64_timer_interrupt and amd64_keyboard_interrupt
291: * have been moved to idt.c for unified LAPIC/PIC EOI management. */
292:
293:/*
294: * pit_init_hz - programme the 8253/8254 PIT Channel 0 at @hz interrupts/sec.
295: *
296: * @hz: desired interrupt frequency (clamped to 100 if 0).
297: *
298: * PIT input clock = 1193182 Hz (derived from 14.318 MHz / 12).
299: * Divisor = 1193182 / hz; clamped to 0xFFFF to avoid overflow.
300: *
301: * Programs PIT in mode 3 (square wave generator):
302: *   PIT_CMD (0x43) = 0x36: channel 0, lo/hibyte access, mode 3, binary.
303: *   PIT_CH0 (0x40): write divisor low byte, then high byte.
304: *
305: * I/O ports written: PIT_CMD (0x43), PIT_CH0 (0x40) x2.
306: * Locking: none; called once during boot.
307: * IRQ context: NO.
308: */
309:void pit_init_hz(uint32_t hz) {
310:  /* Frequency = 1193182 / divisor */
311:  if (hz == 0) hz = 100;
312:  uint32_t divisor = 1193182 / hz;
313:  if (divisor > 0xFFFF) divisor = 0xFFFF;
314:
315:  hal_write8(PIT_CMD, 0x36); /* Channel 0, lobyte/hibyte, square wave */
316:  hal_write8(PIT_CH0, (uint8_t)(divisor & 0xFF));
317:  hal_write8(PIT_CH0, (uint8_t)((divisor >> 8) & 0xFF));
318:
319:  pr_info("PIT Initialized at %u Hz (divisor %u).\n", hz, (uint16_t)divisor);
320:}
321:
322:/*
323: * pic_send_eoi - send a non-specific End-Of-Interrupt command to the PIC(s).
324: *
325: * @irq: PIC hardware IRQ line (0-15).
326: *
327: * Sends OCW2 EOI byte (0x20) to PIC1_CMD.  For IRQs 8-15 (from PIC2), sends
328: * the EOI to PIC2_CMD first, then to PIC1_CMD (cascade EOI required).
329: *
330: * Called by the amd64 IDT common handler (idt.c) after irq_dispatch(); also
331: * reachable via pic_chip_end() but that path is dead (IRQ-01).
332: *
333: * I/O ports written: PIC2_CMD (0xA0) if irq>=8; PIC1_CMD (0x20) always.
334: * Locking: none.
335: * IRQ context: YES — called from IRQ handler (IDT path).
336: */
337:void pic_send_eoi(uint8_t irq) {
338:  if (irq >= 8) {
339:    hal_write8(PIC2_CMD, 0x20);
340:  }
341:  hal_write8(PIC1_CMD, 0x20);
342:}
343:
344:/*
345: * pic_handle_spurious - detect and absorb 8259 spurious IRQ7/IRQ15.
346: *
347: * @vec: IDT vector number (only 39 and 47 are meaningful).
348: *
349: * A level pulse that deasserts before the CPU's INTA cycle makes the 8259
350: * report its lowest-priority line: IRQ7 on the master (vector 39) or IRQ15
351: * on the slave (vector 47).  Virtio INTx lines ACKed quickly by polling
352: * drivers produce these in bursts ("IRQ: Unhandled interrupt 47" flood
353: * during disk I/O).  A spurious IRQ is identified by its In-Service
354: * Register bit being CLEAR (OCW3 0x0B selects ISR for the next read).
355: *
356: * EOI rules differ from real interrupts — this is why the check must run
357: * BEFORE dispatch:
358: *   spurious IRQ7:  no EOI at all (nothing is in service on the master).
359: *   spurious IRQ15: EOI to the MASTER only (the cascade line IRQ2 was a
360: *                   real in-service interrupt on the master); a slave EOI
361: *                   here would wrongly clear a genuine in-service slave bit.
362: *
363: * Returns 1 if the vector was a spurious interrupt and has been fully
364: * handled (caller must not dispatch nor EOI), 0 for a real interrupt.
365: *
366: * I/O side effects: OCW3 write + ISR read on the affected PIC; possibly
367: *                   master EOI.
368: * Locking: none.
369: * IRQ context: YES — called from the IDT path before irq_dispatch().
370: */
371:int pic_handle_spurious(uint32_t vec) {
372:    if (vec == 39) { /* master IRQ7 */
373:        hal_write8(PIC1_CMD, 0x0B); /* OCW3: read ISR on next read */
374:        uint8_t isr = hal_read8(PIC1_CMD);
375:        if (!(isr & 0x80)) {
376:            return 1; /* spurious: no EOI */
377:        }
378:        return 0;
379:    }
380:    if (vec == 47) { /* slave IRQ15 */
381:        hal_write8(PIC2_CMD, 0x0B);
382:        uint8_t isr = hal_read8(PIC2_CMD);
383:        if (!(isr & 0x80)) {
384:            hal_write8(PIC1_CMD, 0x20); /* EOI the master's cascade (IRQ2) */
385:            return 1;
386:        }
387:        return 0;
388:    }
389:    return 0;
390:}
391:
392:/*
393: * pic_unmask - unmask (enable) a PIC hardware IRQ line.
394: *
395: * @irq: PIC hardware line (0-15).
396: *
397: * Reads the current OCW1 mask from PIC1_DATA or PIC2_DATA, clears the
398: * target bit, and writes back.  IRQs 8-15 adjust the line to 0-7 for PIC2.
399: *
400: * I/O side effects: hal_read8 + hal_write8 on PIC1_DATA or PIC2_DATA.
401: * Locking: none.
402: * IRQ context: safe (no sleeping).
403: */
404:void pic_unmask(uint8_t irq) {
405:    uint16_t port;
406:    uint8_t value;
407:
408:    if(irq < 8) {
409:        port = PIC1_DATA;
410:    } else {
411:        port = PIC2_DATA;
412:        irq -= 8;
413:    }
414:    pr_info("PIC: Unmasking IRQ %u\n", irq);
415:    value = hal_read8(port) & ~(1 << irq);
416:    hal_write8(port, value);
417:}
418:
419:/* Keyboard interrupt is now handled in idt.c or via generic IRQ dispatch */
420:

@@@ kernel/drivers/timer/timer.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/drivers/timer/timer.c
3: * ARM Generic Timer Driver — aarch64 (EL1 virtual timer)
4: *
5: * Drives the ARMv8 generic timer using the EL1 virtual timer (CNTV_*
6: * system registers).  The virtual counter (CNTVCT_EL0) is used instead of
7: * the physical counter so that the driver works correctly in QEMU -kernel
8: * mode where the hypervisor timer may not be accessible.
9: *
10: * Architecture (this file is now a thin ARM provider; the tick accounting is
11: * arch-neutral in kernel/core/timer.c, driven through the HAL timer primitives):
12: *   - timer_init() reads the counter frequency (CNTFRQ_EL0) into timer_freq,
13: *     consumed by the arch-neutral timer_percpu_tick()/mono_ns().
14: *   - timer_init_percpu() arms the EL1 virtual timer on each CPU via
15: *     timer_percpu_arm() (sets CNTV_CVAL) and enables it via CNTV_CTL_EL0.
16: *   - timer_handler() is called directly from irq_handler() in irq.c when
17: *     IRQ_TIMER (PPI 27) fires; it calls timer_percpu_tick() (fractional drift
18: *     accounting + CNTV_CVAL reprogram via arch_timer_set_compare) then
19: *     kernel_timer_tick() for scheduling.
20: *
21: * Timer register access is via arch_ wrappers (arch_timer_get_freq,
22: * arch_timer_get_count, arch_timer_set_compare, arch_timer_control) which
23: * translate to MRS/MSR system register instructions.
24: *
25: * Invariants:
26: *   - timer_freq must be non-zero before timer_handler() is called.
27: *   - cpu->next_tick_target is per-CPU; updated only by timer_handler() on
28: *     the owning CPU.
29: *   - jiffies is global and volatile; incremented by kernel_timer_tick().
30: *
31: * Known issues:
32: *   IRQ-03  (W1 DOC) The comment in timer_init() says "We handle IRQ 27
33: *           explicitly in gic.c dispatch"; the actual special handling is in
34: *           irq_handler() in irq.c, not gic.c.  Stale cross-reference.
35: */
36:#include <kernel/irq.h>
37:#include <drivers/timer.h>
38:#include <kernel/arch.h>
39:#include <kernel/cpu.h>
40:#include <kernel/list.h>
41:#include <kernel/printk.h>
42:#include <kernel/sched.h>
43:#include <kernel/spinlock.h>
44:#include <kernel/types.h>
45:
46:/* Disable optimization */
47:
48:#include <kernel/vmm.h>
49:
50:/* timer_freq: CNTFRQ_EL0 value in ticks/second; read once at timer_init().
51: * Used to compute tick intervals and by timer_get_us(). */
52:/* Timer frequency */
53:/* Timer frequency */
54:uint64_t timer_freq;
55:
56:/* jiffies: global monotonic tick counter incremented by kernel_timer_tick()
57: * on every timer IRQ on the boot CPU.  Declared volatile because it is read
58: * from non-IRQ contexts without a lock. */
59:/* System tick counter */
60:volatile uint64_t jiffies = 0;
61:
62:/*
63: * read_cntfrq - read the ARM generic timer frequency register.
64: *
65: * Returns: CNTFRQ_EL0 value (ticks per second); set by firmware / QEMU.
66: *
67: * IRQ context: safe (system register read).
68: */
69:/*
70: * Read counter frequency
71: */
72:static inline uint64_t read_cntfrq(void) { return arch_timer_get_freq(); }
73:
74:/*
75: * read_cntvct - read the EL1 virtual counter.
76: *
77: * Returns: current value of CNTVCT_EL0 (64-bit free-running counter).
78: *
79: * IRQ context: safe.
80: */
81:/*
82: * Read virtual counter
83: */
84:static inline uint64_t read_cntvct(void) { return arch_timer_get_count(); }
85:
86:/*
87: * write_cntv_cval - set the EL1 virtual timer compare value.
88: *
89: * @val: absolute counter value at which the timer should fire next.
90: *
91: * Writes CNTV_CVAL_EL0.  The virtual timer fires when CNTVCT_EL0 >= val.
92: * Must be called with interrupts enabled on the owning CPU.
93: *
94: * IRQ context: safe (system register write).
95: */
96:/*
97: * Set virtual timer compare value (EL1 virtual timer)
98: */
99:static inline void write_cntv_cval(uint64_t val) {
100:  arch_timer_set_compare(val);
101:}
102:
103:/*
104: * write_cntv_ctl - set the EL1 virtual timer control register.
105: *
106: * @val: CNTV_CTL_EL0 value.  Bit 0 (ENABLE) = 1 to start the timer;
107: *       bit 1 (IMASK) = 0 to allow the interrupt to fire.
108: *
109: * IRQ context: safe (system register write).
110: */
111:/*
112: * Set virtual timer control (EL1 virtual timer)
113: */
114:static inline void write_cntv_ctl(uint64_t val) {
115:  arch_timer_control(val);
116:}

118:/*
119: * Timer interrupt handler (Internal C handler called by GIC)
120: * Now accepts regs for Preemption.
121: */
122:extern void compositor_tick(void);
123:
124:/* Global panic flag set by panic() to halt all CPUs */
125:extern volatile int panic_flag;
126:
127:extern struct pt_regs *kernel_timer_tick(struct pt_regs *regs);
128:
129:/*
130: * timer_handler - ARM generic timer IRQ handler (EL1 virtual timer, PPI 27).
131: *
132: * @regs: saved register state from the exception entry; passed through to
133: *        kernel_timer_tick() for potential context-switch use.
134: *
135: * Called directly from irq_handler() in irq.c when irq == IRQ_TIMER (27) or 30.
136: * Delegates the precision per-CPU tick accounting + CNTV_CVAL reprogram to the
137: * arch-neutral, HAL-driven timer_percpu_tick() (kernel/core/timer.c), then runs
138: * kernel_timer_tick(regs) for the scheduler tick + preemption.
139: *
140: * Returns the (potentially switched) register state from kernel_timer_tick().
141: *
142: * Locking: per-CPU data (cpu_info); no cross-CPU locking needed.
143: * IRQ context: YES — called from the IRQ dispatch loop in irq_handler().
144: */
145:struct pt_regs *timer_handler(struct pt_regs *regs) {
146:  /* Tier 2 per-CPU drift accounting + CNTV_CVAL reprogram is the arch-neutral,
147:   * HAL-driven timer_percpu_tick() (kernel/core/timer.c): it advances
148:   * next_tick_target against CNTVCT with fractional correction and a catch-up
149:   * clamp, then arch_timer_set_compare() writes CNTV_CVAL. The arch handler is
150:   * now just: account, then run the generic scheduler tick. */
151:  timer_percpu_tick(get_cpu_info());
152:  return kernel_timer_tick(regs);
153:}
154:
155:/* Legacy static handler used by irq_register?
156:   No, we call timer_handler directly from GIC now.
157:   We can remove the static wrapper or keep it for compatibility if other IRQs
158:   use it. But GIC logic above handles IRQ 27 explicitly.
159:*/
160:
161:/*
162: * Initialize timer (called once on boot CPU)
163: */
164:/*
165: * timer_init - initialise the ARM generic timer on the boot CPU.
166: *
167: * Reads CNTFRQ_EL0 into timer_freq (the HAL counter frequency consumed by the
168: * arch-neutral timer_percpu_tick()/mono_ns()) and enables IRQ_TIMER (PPI 27)
169: * at the GIC via irq_enable(). Does NOT arm the per-CPU compare register; that
170: * is done by timer_init_percpu() on each CPU.
171: *
172: * NOTE(IRQ-03): The comment "We handle IRQ 27 explicitly in gic.c dispatch"
173: * is stale — the special handling is in irq_handler() in irq.c, not gic.c.
174: *
175: * Locking: none; called once from boot CPU before SMP.
176: * IRQ context: NO.
177: */
178:void timer_init(void) {
179:  timer_freq = read_cntfrq();
180:
181:  pr_info("Timer: Frequency %lu Hz\n", timer_freq);
182:  pr_info("Timer: System tick rate %d Hz\n", HZ);
183:
184:  /* Register virtual timer interrupt (IRQ 27 on QEMU virt) */
185:  /* We handle IRQ 27 explicitly in gic.c dispatch to pass regs */
186:  irq_enable(IRQ_TIMER);
187:}
188:
189:/*
190: * timer_init_percpu - arm the virtual timer on the calling CPU.
191: *
192: * Initialises per-CPU timer state and arms the EL1 virtual timer:
193: *   1. Set cpu->next_tick_target = CNTVCT_EL0 + one tick interval.
194: *   2. Zero cpu->tick_error_acc (fractional remainder accumulator).
195: *   3. Write next_tick_target to CNTV_CVAL_EL0.
196: *   4. Write 1 to CNTV_CTL_EL0 (ENABLE=1, IMASK=0) to start the timer.
197: *   5. Call irq_enable(IRQ_TIMER) to unmask PPI 27 in the GIC for this CPU.
198: *
199: * Must be called after gic_init_cpu() has enabled the GICC interface on this
200: * CPU.  Called once per secondary CPU during SMP bring-up.
201: *
202: * Locking: writes only per-CPU state and per-CPU system registers; no lock.
203: * IRQ context: NO.
204: */
205:/*
206: * Initialize timer on each CPU
207: * NOTE: Timer disabled temporarily - causes SError in QEMU -kernel mode
208: * Timer works correctly with UEFI boot (./build_iso.sh run)
209: */
210:void timer_init_percpu(void) {
211:  struct cpu_info *cpu = get_cpu_info();
212:
213:  /* Seed the per-CPU tick schedule + first CNTV_CVAL via the arch-neutral
214:   * HAL-driven helper (kernel/core/timer.c). */
215:  timer_percpu_arm(cpu);
216:
217:  /* Enable virtual timer (ENABLE=1, IMASK=0) */
218:  write_cntv_ctl(1);
219:
220:  /* Enable virtual timer IRQ in GIC (PPI, already per-CPU) */
221:  irq_enable(IRQ_TIMER);
222:
223:  pr_info("Timer: Per-CPU virtual timer enabled (IRQ %d). Next: 0x%lx, Ctl: "
224:          "0x1\n",
225:          IRQ_TIMER, cpu->next_tick_target);
226:}
227:
228:/*
229: * timer_get_ticks - return the current value of the virtual counter.
230: *
231: * Returns: CNTVCT_EL0 (64-bit free-running counter in timer_freq ticks/sec).
232: *
233: * IRQ context: safe.
234: */
235:/*
236: * Get current timer ticks
237: */
238:uint64_t timer_get_ticks(void) { return read_cntvct(); }
239:
240:/*
241: * timer_get_us - return microseconds elapsed since boot.
242: *
243: * Computes (CNTVCT_EL0 * 1000000) / timer_freq.  May overflow for very large
244: * counter values if timer_freq is small, but at 54 MHz (typical QEMU) the
245: * 64-bit numerator overflows after ~340 years.
246: *
247: * Returns: elapsed microseconds since counter was reset (at boot).
248: *
249: * IRQ context: safe.
250: */
251:/*
252: * Get microseconds since boot
253: */
254:uint64_t timer_get_us(void) {
255:  return (read_cntvct() * USEC_PER_SEC) / timer_freq;
256:}
257:
258:/*
259: * timer_delay_us - busy-wait for at least @us microseconds.
260: *
261: * @us: delay in microseconds.
262: *
263: * Reads CNTVCT_EL0, computes the target tick count, and spins until the
264: * counter advances by the required amount.  Blocks the calling CPU entirely;
265: * no yield or sleep.
266: *
267: * Locking: none; reads only per-CPU system registers.
268: * IRQ context: safe (does not sleep), but holding IRQs off for long delays
269: *              will delay timer/device interrupts.
270: */
271:/*
272: * Delay for specified microseconds
273: */
274:void timer_delay_us(uint64_t us) {
275:  uint64_t start = read_cntvct();
276:  uint64_t ticks = (us * timer_freq) / USEC_PER_SEC;
277:
278:  while ((read_cntvct() - start) < ticks)
279:    ;
280:}
281:
282:/*
283: * timer_delay_ms - busy-wait for at least @ms milliseconds.
284: *
285: * @ms: delay in milliseconds.
286: *
287: * Convenience wrapper; delegates to timer_delay_us(ms * 1000).
288: *
289: * Locking: same as timer_delay_us.
290: * IRQ context: same as timer_delay_us.
291: */
292:/*
293: * Delay for specified milliseconds
294: */
295:void timer_delay_ms(uint64_t ms) { timer_delay_us(ms * 1000); }

@@@ kernel/drivers/uart/16550.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/arch/amd64/drivers/uart_16550.c
3: * COM1 Serial Driver (16550 compatible) — amd64
4: *
5: * Drives the standard PC COM1 port (I/O base 0x3F8) using the 16550A UART
6: * register set.  Provides polled TX and polled RX; no interrupt-driven RX
7: * ring buffer (unlike the PL011 driver).  RX interrupts are enabled in the
8: * UART (IER bit 0) but the amd64 IRQ dispatch path handles them via the IDT
9: * common handler and irq_dispatch(), not through this driver's own handler.
10: *
11: * Architecture:
12: *   TX: uart_putc busy-waits on LSR.THRE (bit 5) before writing to THR.
13: *       uart_puts adds an explicit '\r' before each '\n' (CR+LF expansion).
14: *       No spinlock is used on the TX path — safe on single-core QEMU, but
15: *       a data race on SMP.
16: *
17: *   RX: uart_getc busy-waits on LSR.DR (bit 0); uart_getc_nonblock polls it
18: *       once.  Neither function holds a lock; safe only on single-core.
19: *
20: * DLAB sequence (required to set baud divisor):
21: *   1. Write 0x80 to LCR to set DLAB=1 (enables DLL/DLH at offsets 0/1).
22: *   2. Write divisor low byte to DLL (0x00), high byte to DLH (0x01).
23: *      Divisor = 1 → baud = 1843200 / (16 * 1) = 115200.
24: *   3. Write line-control word (8N1 = 0x03) to LCR, clearing DLAB.
25: *
26: * Invariants:
27: *   - uart_init() must be called once before any TX/RX operation.
28: *   - I/O-port access via outb/inb requires no memory barrier on x86 because
29: *     the processor serialises I/O instructions.
30: *
31: * Known issues:
32: *   None from the 04-drivers-irq finding list apply specifically to this file;
33: *   the absence of a lock on TX/RX is a latent SMP issue not tracked
34: *   separately.
35: */
36:#include <kernel/types.h>
37:#include <kernel/arch.h>
38:#include <arch/amd64_internal.h>
39:#include <drivers/uart.h>
40:#include <kernel/io_poll.h>
41:
42:/* COM1_PORT: I/O base address of the first serial port (COM1) on x86 PC. */
43:#define COM1_PORT 0x3F8
44:
45:/* 16550 register offsets relative to COM1_PORT.
46: * THR/RBR/DLL share offset 0; selection depends on DLAB bit in LCR and
47: * whether the access is a read (RBR) or write (THR).  With DLAB=1 both
48: * reads and writes at offset 0 access DLL. */
49:/* Register offsets */
50:#define UART_THR 0 /* Transmit Holding Register */
51:#define UART_RBR 0 /* Receive Buffer Register */
52:#define UART_IER 1 /* Interrupt Enable Register */
53:#define UART_FCR 2 /* FIFO Control Register */
54:#define UART_LCR 3 /* Line Control Register */
55:#define UART_MCR 4 /* Modem Control Register */
56:#define UART_LSR 5 /* Line Status Register */
57:#define UART_DLL 0 /* Divisor Latch Low (when DLAB=1) */
58:#define UART_DLH 1 /* Divisor Latch High (when DLAB=1) */
59:
60:/* LSR_DATA_READY: LSR bit 0 — set when the RX FIFO / holding register has
61: *                 at least one character available to read.
62: * LSR_THRE:       LSR bit 5 — set when the TX holding register is empty;
63: *                 safe to write a new byte to THR. */
64:/* LSR bits */
65:#define LSR_DATA_READY  0x01
66:#define LSR_THRE        0x20 /* Transmit Holding Register Empty */
67:
68:/*
69: * uart_init - initialise the 16550A UART at COM1 (0x3F8).
70: *
71: * Follows the standard DLAB-based initialisation sequence:
72: *   1. IER = 0x00  — disable all UART interrupts while programming.
73: *   2. LCR = 0x80  — set DLAB=1 to expose divisor latch registers.
74: *   3. DLL = 0x01, DLH = 0x00 — divisor = 1 → 115200 baud at 1.8432 MHz.
75: *   4. LCR = 0x03  — 8N1; clears DLAB so THR/RBR are accessible again.
76: *   5. FCR = 0xC7  — enable FIFO, clear TX+RX FIFOs, 14-byte RX threshold.
77: *   6. MCR = 0x0B  — DTR, RTS, OUT2 (required to enable IRQ delivery).
78: *   7. IER = 0x01  — enable RX-data-available interrupt.
79: *
80: * Locking: none; called once from boot CPU before SMP.
81: * IRQ context: NO.
82: */
83:void uart_init(void) {
84:  /* Disable interrupts */
85:  outb(COM1_PORT + UART_IER, 0x00);
86:
87:  /* Enable DLAB (set baud rate divisor) */
88:  outb(COM1_PORT + UART_LCR, 0x80);
89:
90:  /* Set divisor: 115200 baud (divisor = 1) */
91:  outb(COM1_PORT + UART_DLL, 0x01);
92:  outb(COM1_PORT + UART_DLH, 0x00);
93:
94:  /* 8 bits, no parity, one stop bit (8N1) */
95:  outb(COM1_PORT + UART_LCR, 0x03);
96:
97:  /* Enable FIFO, clear them, 14-byte threshold */
98:  outb(COM1_PORT + UART_FCR, 0xC7);
99:
100:  /* IRQs enabled, RTS/DSR set */
101:  outb(COM1_PORT + UART_MCR, 0x0B);
102:
103:  /* Enable receive data available interrupt */
104:  outb(COM1_PORT + UART_IER, 0x01);
105:}
106:
107:/*
108: * uart_putc - transmit one character (polled, no lock).
109: *
110: * @c: character to transmit.
111: *
112: * Busy-waits on LSR.THRE before writing to THR.  No CR+LF expansion here;
113: * uart_puts() performs expansion instead.
114: *
115: * Locking: none (unsafe on SMP).
116: * IRQ context: technically safe on single-core QEMU; SMP-unsafe.
117: */
118:void uart_putc(char c) {
119:  /* Bounded: an absent/wedged UART must not hang printk — after the budget, drop
120:   * the byte instead of spinning forever (io_poll.h). */
121:  spin_until(inb(COM1_PORT + UART_LSR) & LSR_THRE, POLL_SPINS_DEFAULT);
122:  outb(COM1_PORT + UART_THR, (uint8_t)c);
123:}
124:
125:/*
126: * uart_putc_emergency - fault-context TX (kernel/fault.h).
127: *
128: * On the 16550 the normal path is already lock-free port I/O (no page-table
129: * walk, no spinlock), so the emergency path is the same; CR is inserted for
130: * newlines because fault_printf bypasses uart_puts' expansion.
131: */
132:void uart_putc_emergency(char c) {
133:  if (c == '\n')
134:    uart_putc('\r');
135:  uart_putc(c);
136:}
137:
138:/*
139: * uart_puts - transmit a NUL-terminated string with CR+LF expansion.
140: *
141: * @s: NUL-terminated string to transmit.
142: *
143: * Inserts '\r' before every '\n' so terminal emulators display correct line
144: * breaks.  Each character is sent via uart_putc (polled).
145: *
146: * Locking: none (inherits no-lock from uart_putc).
147: * IRQ context: same as uart_putc.
148: */
149:void uart_puts(const char *s) {
150:  while (*s) {
151:    if (*s == '\n')
152:      uart_putc('\r');
153:    uart_putc(*s++);
154:  }
155:}
156:
157:/*
158: * uart_getc - receive one character (blocking, polled).
159: *
160: * Busy-waits on LSR.DR (bit 0) calling arch_idle() (HLT on x86) between
161: * polls; reads and returns one byte from RBR once available.
162: *
163: * Returns: received character.
164: *
165: * Locking: none.
166: * IRQ context: NO — calls arch_idle() (HLT); must not be called from an
167: *              IRQ handler.
168: */
169:char uart_getc(void) {
170:  /* Wait for data to be ready */
171:  while ((inb(COM1_PORT + UART_LSR) & LSR_DATA_READY) == 0) {
172:    arch_idle();
173:  }
174:  return (char)inb(COM1_PORT + UART_RBR);
175:}
176:
177:/*
178: * uart_getc_nonblock - receive one character without blocking.
179: *
180: * Checks LSR.DR once; if set reads and returns the byte from RBR, else
181: * returns -1.
182: *
183: * Returns: received character cast to int, or -1 if no data available.
184: *
185: * Locking: none.
186: * IRQ context: safe (no sleeping).
187: */
188:int uart_getc_nonblock(void) {
189:  if (inb(COM1_PORT + UART_LSR) & LSR_DATA_READY) {
190:    return (int)inb(COM1_PORT + UART_RBR);
191:  }
192:  return -1;
193:}
194:
195:/*
196: * uart_puthex - transmit a 64-bit value in hexadecimal.
197: *
198: * @val: value to format and transmit.
199: *
200: * Formats @val as a fixed-width 16-digit hex string into a local stack
201: * buffer and calls uart_puts().  Useful for early-boot diagnostics.
202: *
203: * Locking: none (via uart_puts).
204: * IRQ context: same as uart_puts.
205: */
206:void uart_puthex(uint64_t val) {
207:  static const char hex[] = "0123456789abcdef";
208:  char buf[17];
209:  int i;
210:
211:  buf[16] = '\0';
212:  for (i = 15; i >= 0; i--) {
213:    buf[i] = hex[val & 0xF];
214:    val >>= 4;
215:  }
216:
217:  uart_puts("0x");
218:  uart_puts(buf);
219:}
220:

@@@ kernel/drivers/uart/pl011.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/drivers/uart/pl011.c
3: * PL011 UART Driver — ARM QEMU virt machine (aarch64)
4: *
5: * Drives the ARM PrimeCell UART (PL011) at PLATFORM_UART_BASE (typically
6: * 0x09000000 on the QEMU virt board).  Provides both polled TX output and
7: * interrupt-driven RX into a 128-byte software ring buffer.
8: *
9: * Architecture:
10: *   TX: uart_putc / uart_puts acquire uart_lock (spinlock + IRQ save) and
11: *       busy-wait on UART_FR.TXFF before writing to UART_DR.  Newlines are
12: *       expanded to CR+LF by _uart_putc_unlocked.
13: *
14: *   RX: uart_irq_handler (IRQ context) is registered for PLATFORM_IRQ_UART0
15: *       (typically GIC IRQ 33 on QEMU virt).  On each RX interrupt the FIFO
16: *       is drained into rx_buf[] via a head pointer and the process wait queue
17: *       is woken.  Consumers read via uart_getc (blocking) or
18: *       uart_getc_nonblock (polling).
19: *
20: * Baud rate: 115200 at assumed 24 MHz UART reference clock.
21: *   IBRD = 13, FBRD = 1  (13.020... -> close to 13.020833 for 115200).
22: *
23: * Invariants:
24: *   - uart_init() must be called before any TX or RX operation.
25: *   - UART_CR must be cleared (UART disabled) before changing IBRD/FBRD/LCR_H.
26: *   - All TX paths hold uart_lock; _uart_putc_unlocked is called only while
27: *     uart_lock is held.
28: *   - All RX-ring accesses (rx_buf/rx_head/rx_tail) hold rx_lock.
29: *
30: * Resolved issues:
31: *   DRV-UART-01  (W3 BUG/SECURITY, #52) RESOLVED.  uart_irq_handler (producer)
32: *                and uart_getc / uart_getc_nonblock (consumers) all access the
33: *                RX ring under rx_lock (spinlock + IRQ save).  The lock both
34: *                provides the SMP ordering the bare volatiles lacked (buffer
35: *                store before head advance; head load before buffer load) and
36: *                serialises concurrent consumers, so rx_tail can no longer be
37: *                corrupted.  rx_lock is distinct from uart_lock (TX).
38: */
39:#include <kernel/printk.h>
40:#include <drivers/uart.h>
41:#include <kernel/arch.h>
42:#include <kernel/io_poll.h>
43:#include <kernel/irq.h>
44:#include <kernel/memlayout.h>
45:#include <kernel/platform.h>
46:#include <kernel/sched.h>
47:#include <kernel/types.h>
48:#include <stdint.h>
49:
50:/* UART_REG(offset): dereference a 32-bit PL011 MMIO register at
51: * PLATFORM_UART_BASE + offset (a physical address) through its direct-map
52: * kernel VA (phys_to_virt; identity while KERNEL_VIRT_BASE == 0).  All
53: * PL011 registers are 32-bit wide with the upper bits reserved. */
54:/* MMIO access macros */
55:#define UART_REG(offset) (*(volatile uint32_t *)phys_to_virt(PLATFORM_UART_BASE + (offset)))
56:
57:/* rx_buf[]: circular ring buffer for characters received via IRQ.
58: * rx_head: write index, advanced by uart_irq_handler (IRQ context).
59: * rx_tail: read index, advanced by uart_getc / uart_getc_nonblock (any ctx).
60: * Buffer is full when (rx_head + 1) % RX_BUF_SIZE == rx_tail.
61: * DRV-UART-01 (#52): rx_buf[], rx_head and rx_tail are all accessed under
62: * rx_lock (spinlock + IRQ save).  The lock orders the producer's buffer store
63: * before its head advance and serialises concurrent consumers, so it provides
64: * the SMP ordering the bare volatiles could not.  rx_lock is separate from
65: * uart_lock (TX) so RX IRQ servicing never waits behind a long TX string. */
66:/* Ring Buffer */
67:#define RX_BUF_SIZE 128
68:static char rx_buf[RX_BUF_SIZE];
69:static volatile int rx_head = 0;
70:static volatile int rx_tail = 0;
71:static DEFINE_SPINLOCK(rx_lock);
72:
73:/* UART_IMSC_RXIM: Receive Interrupt Mask bit in UART_IMSC (offset 0x038).
74: *   Bit 4 = RXIM: assert interrupt when RX FIFO reaches trigger level.
75: * UART_ICR_RXIC: Receive interrupt clear bit in UART_ICR (offset 0x044).
76: *   Writing bit 4 clears the masked RX interrupt in UART_MIS. */
77:/* Interrupt bits */
78:#define UART_IMSC_RXIM BIT(4)
79:#define UART_ICR_RXIC BIT(4)
80:
81:/*
82: * uart_irq_handler - PL011 RX interrupt service routine.
83: *
84: * @irq:  IRQ number (ignored; registered for PLATFORM_IRQ_UART0 only).
85: * @data: opaque data (unused; registered as NULL).
86: *
87: * Called from irq_handler() when the GIC delivers PLATFORM_IRQ_UART0.
88: * Checks UART_MIS (masked interrupt status, offset 0x040) for the RX bit;
89: * drains the RX FIFO into rx_buf[] until UART_FR.RXFE (FIFO empty, bit 4)
90: * is set or the ring buffer is full; clears the interrupt via UART_ICR;
91: * wakes up keyboard_wait_queue.
92: *
93: * MMIO registers touched:
94: *   UART_MIS  (0x040) read  — masked interrupt status.
95: *   UART_FR   (0x018) read  — flags: RXFE = bit 4.
96: *   UART_DR   (0x000) read  — data register; reading drains one byte from FIFO.
97: *   UART_ICR  (0x044) write — interrupt clear register; write 1 to clear.
98: *
99: * Locking: acquires rx_lock (spinlock + IRQ save) around the FIFO drain so the
100: *          rx_buf store is ordered before the rx_head advance and consumers see
101: *          a consistent ring (DRV-UART-01 / #52).  rx_lock is a non-sleeping
102: *          spinlock, valid in IRQ context.
103: * IRQ context: YES — this is an IRQ handler registered with irq_register().
104: */
105:static void uart_irq_handler(uint32_t irq, void *data) {
106:  (void)irq;
107:  (void)data;
108:
109:  /* Check masked status */
110:  if (UART_REG(UART_MIS) & UART_IMSC_RXIM) {
111:    /* Drain the RX FIFO into the ring under rx_lock so the buffer store is
112:     * ordered before the head advance and no consumer observes a torn ring. */
113:    uint64_t flags;
114:    spin_lock_irqsave(&rx_lock, &flags);
115:    while (!(UART_REG(UART_FR) & UART_FR_RXFE)) {
116:      char c = (char)(UART_REG(UART_DR) & 0xFF);
117:
118:      int next = (rx_head + 1) % RX_BUF_SIZE;
119:      if (next != rx_tail) {
120:        rx_buf[rx_head] = c;
121:        rx_head = next;
122:      }
123:    }
124:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&rx_lock, flags);
125:
126:    /* Clear interrupt */
127:    UART_REG(UART_ICR) = UART_ICR_RXIC;
128:
129:    /* Wake up waiting processes */
130:    extern struct wait_queue_head keyboard_wait_queue;
131:    wake_up(&keyboard_wait_queue);
132:  }
133:}
134:
135:/*
136: * uart_init - configure and enable the PL011 UART.
137: *
138: * Sequence (PL011 TRM §3.3.6 — must disable UART before reprogramming):
139: *   1. Clear UART_CR (disable UART, TX, RX) — required before changing line
140: *      control or baud-rate registers.
141: *   2. Write 0x7FF to UART_ICR to clear all pending interrupts.
142: *   3. Program baud rate: IBRD=13, FBRD=1 for ~115200 at 24 MHz clock.
143: *        Baud = clock / (16 * (IBRD + FBRD/64)) = 24e6 / (16*13.015625) ≈ 115273.
144: *   4. Set LCR_H: 8 data bits (WLEN=11b), FIFO enable (FEN=1).
145: *   5. Set IMSC: enable RX interrupt (RXIM=1); TX interrupt stays masked.
146: *   6. Register uart_irq_handler for PLATFORM_IRQ_UART0 via irq_register().
147: *   7. Enable UART, TX, RX via UART_CR (UARTEN=1, TXE=1, RXE=1).
148: *
149: * MMIO registers written:
150: *   UART_CR    (0x030): control register.
151: *   UART_ICR   (0x044): interrupt clear register.
152: *   UART_IBRD  (0x024): integer baud-rate divisor.
153: *   UART_FBRD  (0x028): fractional baud-rate divisor.
154: *   UART_LCR_H (0x02C): line control register.
155: *   UART_IMSC  (0x038): interrupt mask set/clear register.
156: *
157: * Locking: none; called once from boot CPU before SMP.
158: * IRQ context: NO — called from early boot.
159: */
160:/*
161: * Initialize UART
162: * QEMU's PL011 is pre-configured, but we set it up properly anyway
163: */
164:void uart_init(void) {
165:  /* Disable UART */
166:  UART_REG(UART_CR) = 0;
167:
168:  /* Clear pending interrupts */
169:  UART_REG(UART_ICR) = 0x7FF;
170:
171:  /* Set baud rate (115200 @ 24MHz clock) */
172:  UART_REG(UART_IBRD) = 13;
173:  UART_REG(UART_FBRD) = 1;
174:
175:  /* 8N1, enable FIFOs */
176:  UART_REG(UART_LCR_H) = UART_LCR_H_WLEN_8 | UART_LCR_H_FEN;
177:
178:  /* Enable Interrupts (RX) */
179:  UART_REG(UART_IMSC) = UART_IMSC_RXIM;
180:
181:  /* Register IRQ */
182:  /* The UART is the diagnostic channel of last resort: losing its IRQ
183:   * silently is exactly the failure that leaves you with no way to see
184:   * failures. */
185:  if (irq_register(PLATFORM_IRQ_UART0, uart_irq_handler, NULL) != 0)
186:    pr_err("%s", "pl011: cannot register UART0 IRQ — input on the serial "
187:                 "console will not be delivered\n");
188:
189:  /* Enable UART, TX and RX */
190:  UART_REG(UART_CR) = UART_CR_UARTEN | UART_CR_TXE | UART_CR_RXE;
191:}
192:
193:/* uart_lock: spinlock protecting the TX path (UART_DR writes).
194: * Held with IRQ save/restore so that a printk from an IRQ handler does not
195: * deadlock against a printk already in progress on the same CPU. */
196:DEFINE_SPINLOCK(uart_lock);
197:
198:/*
199: * _uart_putc_unlocked - transmit one character; caller must hold uart_lock.
200: *
201: * @c: character to send.
202: *
203: * Busy-waits on UART_FR.TXFF (TX FIFO full, bit 5) before writing to
204: * UART_DR (offset 0x000).  Expands '\n' to '\n'+'\r' for terminal emulators.
205: *
206: * MMIO registers touched:
207: *   UART_FR (0x018) read  — flags; TXFF = bit 5.
208: *   UART_DR (0x000) write — data register; writes one byte to TX FIFO.
209: *
210: * Locking: caller MUST hold uart_lock.
211: * IRQ context: safe (called under uart_lock with IRQs saved).
212: */
213:static void _uart_putc_unlocked(char c) {
214:  /* Bounded: an absent/wedged UART must not hang printk — after the budget, drop
215:   * the byte instead of spinning forever (io_poll.h). */
216:  spin_until(!(UART_REG(UART_FR) & UART_FR_TXFF), POLL_SPINS_DEFAULT);
217:
218:  UART_REG(UART_DR) = c;
219:
220:  /* Add carriage return for newline */
221:  if (c == '\n') {
222:    spin_until(!(UART_REG(UART_FR) & UART_FR_TXFF), POLL_SPINS_DEFAULT);
223:    UART_REG(UART_DR) = '\r';
224:  }
225:}
226:
227:/*
228: * uart_putc - transmit one character (lock-protected).
229: *
230: * @c: character to transmit.
231: *
232: * Acquires uart_lock with IRQ save, delegates to _uart_putc_unlocked, then
233: * releases the lock.  Safe to call from any context including IRQ handlers.
234: *
235: * Locking: acquires uart_lock (spinlock + IRQ save/restore).
236: * IRQ context: safe.
237: */
238:/*
239: * Send a character
240: */
241:void uart_putc(char c) {
242:  uint64_t flags;
243:  spin_lock_irqsave(&uart_lock, &flags);
244:  _uart_putc_unlocked(c);
245:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&uart_lock, flags);
246:}
247:
248:/*
249: * uart_putc_emergency - lock-free TX for fault context (kernel/fault.h).
250: *
251: * Bypasses uart_lock by design: a fault handler must never block on a lock
252: * that another (possibly wedged) CPU holds.  Interleaving with concurrent
253: * normal output is the accepted trade for guaranteed progress.
254: */
255:void uart_putc_emergency(char c) { _uart_putc_unlocked(c); }
256:
257:/*
258: * uart_getc - receive one character (blocking).
259: *
260: * Spins calling arch_idle() (WFI) until rx_head != rx_tail, then reads one
261: * byte from rx_buf[] and advances rx_tail.
262: *
263: * Returns: the received character.
264: *
265: * Locking: takes rx_lock only around the ring check + pop; the idle/WFI wait
266: *          runs with the lock released so the RX IRQ can fill the ring
267: *          (DRV-UART-01 / #52).
268: * IRQ context: NO — may idle (WFI); must not be called from IRQ context.
269: */
270:/*
271: * Receive a character (blocking)
272: */
273:char uart_getc(void) {
274:  for (;;) {
275:    uint64_t flags;
276:    spin_lock_irqsave(&rx_lock, &flags);
277:    if (rx_head != rx_tail) {
278:      char c = rx_buf[rx_tail];
279:      rx_tail = (rx_tail + 1) % RX_BUF_SIZE;
280:      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&rx_lock, flags);
281:      return c;
282:    }
283:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&rx_lock, flags);
284:    /* Wait for interrupt (wfi/idle) to save power — never while holding the
285:     * lock, so the RX IRQ can fill the ring. */
286:    arch_idle();
287:  }
288:}
289:
290:/*
291: * uart_getc_nonblock - receive one character without blocking.
292: *
293: * Returns the next character from the RX ring buffer, or -1 if the buffer
294: * is empty (rx_head == rx_tail).
295: *
296: * Locking: acquires rx_lock (spinlock + IRQ save) around the ring access
297: *          (DRV-UART-01 / #52).
298: * IRQ context: safe — rx_lock is a non-sleeping spinlock.
299: */
300:/*
301: * Receive a character (non-blocking)
302: * Returns -1 if no character available
303: */
304:int uart_getc_nonblock(void) {
305:  uint64_t flags;
306:  int ret = -1;
307:  spin_lock_irqsave(&rx_lock, &flags);
308:  if (rx_head != rx_tail) {
309:    char c = rx_buf[rx_tail];
310:    rx_tail = (rx_tail + 1) % RX_BUF_SIZE;
311:    ret = (int)c;
312:  }
313:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&rx_lock, flags);
314:  return ret;
315:}
316:
317:/*
318: * uart_puts - transmit a NUL-terminated string (lock-protected).
319: *
320: * @s: NUL-terminated string to transmit.
321: *
322: * Acquires uart_lock once for the entire string, calling
323: * _uart_putc_unlocked() per character.  More efficient than repeated
324: * uart_putc() calls for multi-character output.
325: *
326: * Locking: acquires uart_lock (spinlock + IRQ save/restore).
327: * IRQ context: safe.
328: */
329:/*
330: * Send a string
331: */
332:void uart_puts(const char *s) {
333:  uint64_t flags;
334:  spin_lock_irqsave(&uart_lock, &flags);
335:  while (*s)
336:    _uart_putc_unlocked(*s++);
337:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&uart_lock, flags);
338:}
339:
340:/*
341: * uart_puthex - transmit a 64-bit value in hexadecimal.
342: *
343: * @val: value to print.
344: *
345: * Formats @val as a fixed-width 16-digit hex string in a local buffer, then
346: * calls uart_puts() (which acquires uart_lock).  Useful for early-boot
347: * debugging before printf-style formatting is available.
348: *
349: * Locking: via uart_puts (acquires uart_lock).
350: * IRQ context: safe.
351: */
352:/*
353: * Print a hexadecimal number
354: */
355:void uart_puthex(uint64_t val) {
356:  static const char hex[] = "0123456789abcdef";
357:  char buf[17];
358:  int i;
359:
360:  buf[16] = '\0';
361:  for (i = 15; i >= 0; i--) {
362:    buf[i] = hex[val & 0xF];
363:    val >>= 4;
364:  }
365:
366:  uart_puts("0x");
367:  uart_puts(buf);
368:}
