@@@ kernel/drivers/usb/ehci.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/drivers/usb/ehci.c
3: * EHCI (USB 2.0) host controller driver — polled.
4: *
5: * EHCI only drives high-speed devices directly; low/full-speed devices (USB
6: * boot keyboards/mice) are handed to a companion UHCI/OHCI by setting the port
7: * owner. So this driver's two jobs are: (1) claim the ports, reset each one and
8: * route non-high-speed devices to the companion (which our UHCI driver then
9: * enumerates), and (2) run an async (control) + periodic (interrupt) schedule
10: * for any genuine high-speed device. Polled, like xHCI/UHCI.
11: */
12:
13:#include <drivers/usb/usb.h>
14:#include <drivers/pci.h>
15:#include <kernel/driver.h>
16:#include <kernel/hal.h>
17:#include <kernel/pmm.h>
18:#include <kernel/printk.h>
19:#include <kernel/string.h>
20:
21:extern int arch_vmm_map_device(uint64_t base, uint64_t size);
22:
23:/* Capability registers (from MMIO base). */
24:#define EHCI_CAPLENGTH 0x00 /* u8 */
25:#define EHCI_HCSPARAMS 0x04
26:
27:/* Operational registers (from base + CAPLENGTH). */
28:#define EHCI_USBCMD    0x00
29:#define EHCI_USBSTS    0x04
30:#define EHCI_USBINTR   0x08
31:#define EHCI_FRINDEX   0x0C
32:#define EHCI_CTRLDSSEG 0x10
33:#define EHCI_PERIODICLB 0x14
34:#define EHCI_ASYNCLB   0x18
35:#define EHCI_CONFIGFLAG 0x40
36:#define EHCI_PORTSC(n) (0x44 + 4 * (n))
37:
38:#define CMD_RUN     (1u << 0)
39:#define CMD_HCRESET (1u << 1)
40:#define CMD_PSE     (1u << 4)
41:#define CMD_ASE     (1u << 5)
42:#define STS_HALTED  (1u << 12)
43:
44:#define PORT_CCS   (1u << 0)
45:#define PORT_CSC   (1u << 1)
46:#define PORT_PED   (1u << 2)
47:#define PORT_PEDC  (1u << 3)
48:#define PORT_RESET (1u << 8)
49:#define PORT_POWER (1u << 12)
50:#define PORT_OWNER (1u << 13)
51:#define PORT_LS_KSTATE (1u << 10) /* line status bit: low-speed (K-state) */
52:
53:/* qTD token. */
54:#define QTD_ACTIVE (1u << 7)
55:#define QTD_HALTED (1u << 6)
56:#define QTD_PID_OUT   0
57:#define QTD_PID_IN    1
58:#define QTD_PID_SETUP 2
59:#define QTD_IOC    (1u << 15)
60:#define QTD_T      1u /* terminate */
61:
62:/* Link pointer type. */
63:#define LP_QH (1u << 1)
64:#define LP_T  1u
65:
66:/* Exactly 32 bytes: qTDs are packed in a pool and the hardware requires each to
67: * be 32-byte aligned, so the struct size must stay a multiple of 32. */
68:struct ehci_qtd {
69:    volatile uint32_t next;
70:    volatile uint32_t alt_next;
71:    volatile uint32_t token;
72:    volatile uint32_t buf[5];
73:} __attribute__((packed));
74:
75:struct ehci_qh {
76:    volatile uint32_t horiz;
77:    volatile uint32_t ep_char;   /* addr, ep, EPS, max packet, H, DTC */
78:    volatile uint32_t ep_cap;    /* mult, hub addr/port, s/c-mask */
79:    volatile uint32_t cur_qtd;
80:    /* qTD overlay */
81:    volatile uint32_t ov_next;
82:    volatile uint32_t ov_alt;
83:    volatile uint32_t ov_token;
84:    volatile uint32_t ov_buf[5];
85:    uint32_t pad[4]; /* pad to 64B (48B used) */
86:} __attribute__((packed));
87:
88:struct ehci_ep {
89:    struct ehci_qh *qh;
90:    uint64_t qh_phys;
91:    struct ehci_qtd *qtd;
92:    uint64_t qtd_phys;
93:    void *buf;
94:    uint64_t buf_phys;
95:    int toggle;
96:    int maxlen;
97:    int active;
98:};
99:
100:struct ehci {
101:    volatile uint8_t *base;
102:    volatile uint8_t *op;
103:    int nports;
104:    uint32_t *framelist;
105:    uint64_t framelist_phys;
106:    struct ehci_qh *async; /* async head QH (H=1) */
107:    uint64_t async_phys;
108:
109:    struct ehci_qh *ctrl_qh;     /* reused per control transfer */
110:    uint64_t ctrl_qh_phys;
111:    struct ehci_qtd *ctrl_qtd;   /* pool */
112:    uint64_t ctrl_qtd_phys;
113:    void *ctrl_buf;
114:    uint64_t ctrl_buf_phys;
115:
116:    struct ehci_ep eps[4];
117:    int ep_count;
118:    uint8_t next_addr;
119:    struct usb_hcd hcd;
120:};
121:
122:static struct ehci ehci_ctrls[2];
123:static int ehci_count;
124:
125:static inline uint32_t rd32(volatile uint8_t *p, uint32_t o) { return *(volatile uint32_t *)(p + o); }
126:static inline void wr32(volatile uint8_t *p, uint32_t o, uint32_t v) { *(volatile uint32_t *)(p + o) = v; }
127:
128:static void *page_va(uint64_t *phys_out) {
129:    if (phys_out) *phys_out = 0;
130:    void *p = pmm_alloc_page_dma();
131:    if (!p) return NULL;
132:    memset(p, 0, PAGE_SIZE);
133:    if (phys_out) *phys_out = virt_to_phys(p);
134:    return p;
135:}
136:
137:static int ehci_address(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *dev);
138:
139:/* Fill a qTD: pid, data toggle, length, buffer phys, IOC. */
140:static void qtd_fill(struct ehci_qtd *t, uint32_t next, int pid, int toggle,
141:                     int len, uint64_t buf, int ioc) {
142:    t->next = next;
143:    t->alt_next = LP_T;
144:    uint32_t tok = QTD_ACTIVE | ((uint32_t)pid << 8) | (3u << 10) /* CERR */ |
145:                   ((uint32_t)len << 16) | ((uint32_t)(toggle & 1) << 31);
146:    if (ioc) tok |= QTD_IOC;
147:    t->token = tok;
148:    for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) t->buf[i] = 0;
149:    if (len) {
150:        t->buf[0] = (uint32_t)buf;
151:        t->buf[1] = (uint32_t)((buf + 0x1000) & ~0xFFFUL);
152:    }
153:}
154:
155:/* Run a qTD chain (starting at ctrl_qtd[0]) through the control QH and wait for
156: * the STATUS qTD to retire. We must poll the qTD itself, not the QH overlay:
157: * the overlay starts inactive (so the controller fetches the first qTD), so
158: * polling it would report "done" immediately. Returns 0 on success. */
159:static int ehci_run_ctrl(struct ehci *e, struct usb_device *dev, struct ehci_qtd *last) {
160:    struct ehci_qh *qh = e->ctrl_qh;
161:    int eps = (dev->speed == USB_SPEED_HIGH) ? 2 : (dev->speed == USB_SPEED_LOW) ? 1 : 0;
162:    int mp = dev->max_packet0 ? dev->max_packet0 : 8;
163:    qh->ep_char = (uint32_t)dev->addr | ((uint32_t)0 << 8) | ((uint32_t)eps << 12) |
164:                  (1u << 14) /* DTC: toggle from qTD */ | ((uint32_t)mp << 16) |
165:                  ((eps != 2) ? (1u << 27) : 0) /* control ep on non-HS */;
166:    qh->ep_cap = (1u << 30); /* mult = 1 */
167:    qh->cur_qtd = 0;
168:    qh->ov_next = (uint32_t)e->ctrl_qtd_phys; /* first qTD */
169:    qh->ov_alt = LP_T;
170:    qh->ov_token = 0; /* inactive -> controller loads the first qTD */
171:
172:    for (long s = 0; s < 60000000L; s++) {
173:        if (!(last->token & QTD_ACTIVE)) break;
174:    }
175:    if (last->token & (QTD_ACTIVE | QTD_HALTED)) return -1;
176:    return 0;
177:}
178:
179:static int ehci_control(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *dev,
180:                        const struct usb_setup *setup, void *data, int len) {
181:    struct ehci *e = hcd->priv;
182:    struct ehci_qtd *td = e->ctrl_qtd;
183:    int dir_in = (setup->bmRequestType & USB_DIR_IN) != 0;
184:    int n = 0;
185:
186:    /* SETUP (DATA0). */
187:    memcpy(e->ctrl_buf, setup, 8);
188:    int last = (len > 0) ? 2 : 1; /* index of STATUS stage */
189:    qtd_fill(&td[0], e->ctrl_qtd_phys + 1 * sizeof(struct ehci_qtd),
190:             QTD_PID_SETUP, 0, 8, e->ctrl_buf_phys, 0);
191:    n = 1;
192:
193:    if (len > 0) {
194:        if (!dir_in) memcpy((uint8_t *)e->ctrl_buf + 64, data, len);
195:        qtd_fill(&td[1], e->ctrl_qtd_phys + 2 * sizeof(struct ehci_qtd),
196:                 dir_in ? QTD_PID_IN : QTD_PID_OUT, 1, len, e->ctrl_buf_phys + 64, 0);
197:        n = 2;
198:    }
199:
200:    /* STATUS (DATA1, opposite dir, IOC). */
201:    qtd_fill(&td[last], LP_T, dir_in ? QTD_PID_OUT : QTD_PID_IN, 1, 0, 0, 1);
202:    n = last + 1;
203:    (void)n;
204:
205:    if (ehci_run_ctrl(e, dev, &td[last]) < 0) return -1;
206:
207:    int transferred = len;
208:    if (dir_in && len > 0) {
209:        int rem = (td[1].token >> 16) & 0x7FFF; /* bytes NOT transferred */
210:        transferred = len - rem;
211:        if (transferred < 0) transferred = 0;
212:        if (data && transferred > 0) memcpy(data, (uint8_t *)e->ctrl_buf + 64, transferred);
213:    }
214:    return transferred;
215:}
216:
217:/* --- ports --- */
218:static int ehci_num_ports(struct usb_hcd *hcd) {
219:    struct ehci *e = hcd->priv;
220:    return e->nports;
221:}
222:static int ehci_port_connected(struct usb_hcd *hcd, int port) {
223:    struct ehci *e = hcd->priv;
224:    return (rd32(e->op, EHCI_PORTSC(port)) & PORT_CCS) ? 1 : 0;
225:}
226:
227:static int ehci_enumerate_port(struct usb_hcd *hcd, int port, struct usb_device *dev) {
228:    struct ehci *e = hcd->priv;
229:    uint32_t sc = rd32(e->op, EHCI_PORTSC(port));
230:    if (!(sc & PORT_CCS)) return -1;
231:
232:    /* Reset to determine speed. A genuine high-speed device ends up enabled
233:     * (PED) and is driven here; anything else (full/low-speed boot keyboard or
234:     * mouse) is released to the companion UHCI/OHCI via the port-owner bit. */
235:    wr32(e->op, EHCI_PORTSC(port), (sc & ~0x2Au) | PORT_RESET);
236:    for (long s = 0; s < 8000000L; s++) { }
237:    wr32(e->op, EHCI_PORTSC(port), rd32(e->op, EHCI_PORTSC(port)) & ~PORT_RESET);
238:    for (long s = 0; s < 4000000L; s++) {
239:        if (!(rd32(e->op, EHCI_PORTSC(port)) & PORT_RESET)) break;
240:    }
241:    sc = rd32(e->op, EHCI_PORTSC(port));
242:
243:    if (!(sc & PORT_PED)) {
244:        /* Not enabled after reset = full/low-speed: hand to the companion. */
245:        wr32(e->op, EHCI_PORTSC(port), (sc & ~0x2Au) | PORT_OWNER);
246:        return -1;
247:    }
248:
249:    dev->speed = USB_SPEED_HIGH;
250:    dev->max_packet0 = 64;
251:    return ehci_address(hcd, dev);
252:}
253:
254:/* Address a device on the default pipe (addr 0). */
255:static int ehci_address(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *dev) {
256:    dev->addr = 0;
257:    struct usb_device_descriptor dd;
258:    memset(&dd, 0, sizeof(dd));
259:    struct usb_setup s8 = { USB_DIR_IN, USB_REQ_GET_DESCRIPTOR, (USB_DT_DEVICE << 8), 0, 8 };
260:    if (ehci_control(hcd, dev, &s8, &dd, 8) < 8) return -1;
261:    if (dd.bMaxPacketSize0) dev->max_packet0 = dd.bMaxPacketSize0;
262:
263:    struct ehci *e = hcd->priv;
264:    uint8_t new_addr = ++e->next_addr;
265:    struct usb_setup sa = { USB_DIR_OUT, USB_REQ_SET_ADDRESS, new_addr, 0, 0 };
266:    if (ehci_control(hcd, dev, &sa, NULL, 0) < 0) return -1;
267:    dev->addr = new_addr;
268:    for (long s = 0; s < 2000000L; s++) { }
269:    return 0;
270:}
271:
272:static int ehci_address_dev(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *dev) {
273:    return ehci_address(hcd, dev);
274:}
275:
276:/* --- interrupt IN endpoint (periodic schedule) --- */
277:static int ehci_intr_open(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *dev,
278:                          uint8_t ep_addr, int max_packet, int interval) {
279:    (void)interval;
280:    struct ehci *e = hcd->priv;
281:    if (e->ep_count >= (int)(sizeof(e->eps) / sizeof(e->eps[0]))) return -1;
282:    struct ehci_ep *ep = &e->eps[e->ep_count];
283:    memset(ep, 0, sizeof(*ep));
284:    ep->qh = (struct ehci_qh *)page_va(&ep->qh_phys);
285:    ep->qtd = (struct ehci_qtd *)page_va(&ep->qtd_phys);
286:    ep->buf = page_va(&ep->buf_phys);
287:    if (!ep->qh || !ep->qtd || !ep->buf) return -1;
288:    ep->maxlen = max_packet;
289:    ep->toggle = 0;
290:    ep->active = 1;
291:    dev->hcd_priv = ep;
292:
293:    int epn = ep_addr & 0x0F;
294:    ep->qh->ep_char = (uint32_t)dev->addr | ((uint32_t)epn << 8) | (2u << 12) /*HS*/ |
295:                      (1u << 14) | ((uint32_t)max_packet << 16);
296:    ep->qh->ep_cap = (1u << 30) | (0x01u << 0) /* S-mask: microframe 0 */;
297:    ep->qh->horiz = LP_T;
298:    qtd_fill(ep->qtd, LP_T, QTD_PID_IN, ep->toggle, max_packet, ep->buf_phys, 1);
299:    ep->qh->ov_next = (uint32_t)ep->qtd_phys;
300:    ep->qh->ov_alt = LP_T;
301:    ep->qh->ov_token = 0;
302:
303:    /* Link the interrupt QH into every periodic frame-list entry. */
304:    uint32_t link = (uint32_t)ep->qh_phys | LP_QH;
305:    for (int i = 0; i < 1024; i++) e->framelist[i] = link;
306:    e->ep_count++;
307:    return 0;
308:}
309:
310:static int ehci_intr_poll(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *dev,
311:                          uint8_t ep_addr, void *buf, int len) {
312:    (void)hcd; (void)ep_addr;
313:    struct ehci_ep *ep = dev->hcd_priv;
314:    if (!ep || !ep->active) return 0;
315:    if (ep->qh->ov_token & QTD_ACTIVE) return 0;
316:
317:    int rem = (ep->qh->ov_token >> 16) & 0x7FFF;
318:    int halted = (ep->qh->ov_token & QTD_HALTED) != 0;
319:    int got = 0;
320:    if (!halted) {
321:        got = ep->maxlen - rem;
322:        if (got > len) got = len;
323:        if (got > 0) memcpy(buf, ep->buf, got);
324:        ep->toggle ^= 1;
325:    }
326:    /* Re-arm. */
327:    qtd_fill(ep->qtd, LP_T, QTD_PID_IN, ep->toggle, ep->maxlen, ep->buf_phys, 1);
328:    ep->qh->ov_next = (uint32_t)ep->qtd_phys;
329:    ep->qh->ov_alt = LP_T;
330:    ep->qh->ov_token = 0;
331:    return got;
332:}
333:
334:static struct usb_hcd_ops ehci_ops = {
335:    .num_ports = ehci_num_ports,
336:    .port_connected = ehci_port_connected,
337:    .enumerate_port = ehci_enumerate_port,
338:    .address_dev = ehci_address_dev,
339:    .control = ehci_control,
340:    .intr_open = ehci_intr_open,
341:    .intr_poll = ehci_intr_poll,
342:};
343:
344:static int ehci_probe(struct hal_device *dev) {
345:    if (ehci_count >= (int)(sizeof(ehci_ctrls) / sizeof(ehci_ctrls[0]))) return -1;
346:    struct ehci *e = &ehci_ctrls[ehci_count];
347:    memset(e, 0, sizeof(*e));
348:
349:    uint64_t base = dev->base;
350:    if (!base) return -1;
351:    arch_vmm_map_device(base, 0x1000);
352:    e->base = (volatile uint8_t *)phys_to_virt(base);
353:    uint8_t caplen = *(volatile uint8_t *)(e->base + EHCI_CAPLENGTH);
354:    e->op = e->base + caplen;
355:    e->nports = rd32(e->base, EHCI_HCSPARAMS) & 0x0F;
356:
357:    pr_info("EHCI: %s base=0x%lx ports=%d\n", dev->name, base, e->nports);
358:
359:    /* Reset. */
360:    wr32(e->op, EHCI_USBCMD, rd32(e->op, EHCI_USBCMD) & ~CMD_RUN);
361:    for (long s = 0; s < 4000000L; s++)
362:        if (rd32(e->op, EHCI_USBSTS) & STS_HALTED) break;
363:    wr32(e->op, EHCI_USBCMD, CMD_HCRESET);
364:    for (long s = 0; s < 8000000L; s++)
365:        if (!(rd32(e->op, EHCI_USBCMD) & CMD_HCRESET)) break;
366:
367:    /* Async head QH (H=1, points to itself). */
368:    e->async = (struct ehci_qh *)page_va(&e->async_phys);
369:    e->ctrl_qh = (struct ehci_qh *)page_va(&e->ctrl_qh_phys);
370:    e->ctrl_qtd = (struct ehci_qtd *)page_va(&e->ctrl_qtd_phys);
371:    e->ctrl_buf = page_va(&e->ctrl_buf_phys);
372:    e->framelist = (uint32_t *)page_va(&e->framelist_phys);
373:    if (!e->async || !e->ctrl_qh || !e->ctrl_qtd || !e->ctrl_buf || !e->framelist) return -1;
374:
375:    /* async ring: head -> ctrl_qh -> head */
376:    e->async->ep_char = (1u << 15); /* H = 1 (head of reclamation) */
377:    e->async->ep_cap = (1u << 30);
378:    e->async->horiz = (uint32_t)e->ctrl_qh_phys | LP_QH;
379:    e->async->ov_next = LP_T;
380:    e->async->ov_token = QTD_HALTED;
381:    e->ctrl_qh->horiz = (uint32_t)e->async_phys | LP_QH;
382:    e->ctrl_qh->ov_next = LP_T;
383:    e->ctrl_qh->ov_token = QTD_HALTED;
384:
385:    for (int i = 0; i < 1024; i++) e->framelist[i] = LP_T;
386:
387:    wr32(e->op, EHCI_CTRLDSSEG, 0);
388:    wr32(e->op, EHCI_PERIODICLB, (uint32_t)e->framelist_phys);
389:    wr32(e->op, EHCI_ASYNCLB, (uint32_t)e->async_phys);
390:    wr32(e->op, EHCI_USBINTR, 0);
391:    wr32(e->op, EHCI_USBCMD, CMD_RUN | CMD_ASE | CMD_PSE | (8u << 16));
392:    wr32(e->op, EHCI_CONFIGFLAG, 1); /* route all ports to EHCI */
393:    for (long s = 0; s < 2000000L; s++) { }
394:
395:    /* Power ports. */
396:    for (int p = 0; p < e->nports; p++) {
397:        uint32_t sc = rd32(e->op, EHCI_PORTSC(p));
398:        if (!(sc & PORT_POWER))
399:            wr32(e->op, EHCI_PORTSC(p), sc | PORT_POWER);
400:    }
401:    for (long s = 0; s < 3000000L; s++) { }
402:
403:    e->hcd.name = "EHCI";
404:    e->hcd.ops = &ehci_ops;
405:    e->hcd.priv = e;
406:    ehci_count++;
407:
408:    usb_register_hcd(&e->hcd);
409:    return 0;
410:}
411:
412:static struct device_driver ehci_driver = {
413:    .name = "ehci",
414:    .vendor = DRV_ANY_ID,
415:    .device = DRV_ANY_ID,
416:    .class_code = 0x0C,
417:    .subclass = 0x03,
418:    .prog_if = 0x20, /* EHCI */
419:    .probe = ehci_probe,
420:};
421:
422:void ehci_register(void) {
423:    driver_register(&ehci_driver);
424:}

@@@ kernel/drivers/usb/uhci.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/drivers/usb/uhci.c
3: * UHCI (USB 1.1) host controller driver — polled.
4: *
5: * UHCI is the companion controller that carries full/low-speed devices on
6: * i440fx and on UTM "USB 2.0" (the EHCI routes 1.1 devices to it), so a USB
7: * boot keyboard/mouse/tablet ends up here. Port-I/O based; schedule is a 1024-
8: * entry frame list pointing at a skeleton of QHs (interrupt then control).
9: * Control transfers run synchronously; interrupt IN endpoints are re-armed and
10: * polled from usb_hid_poll() via the same timer tick as xHCI.
11: */
12:
13:#include <drivers/usb/usb.h>
14:#include <drivers/pci.h>
15:#include <kernel/driver.h>
16:#include <kernel/hal.h>
17:#include <kernel/pmm.h>
18:#include <kernel/printk.h>
19:#include <kernel/string.h>
20:
21:/* --- I/O registers (offset from BAR0 I/O base) --- */
22:#define UHCI_USBCMD    0x00
23:#define UHCI_USBSTS    0x02
24:#define UHCI_USBINTR   0x04
25:#define UHCI_FRNUM     0x06
26:#define UHCI_FRBASEADD 0x08
27:#define UHCI_SOFMOD    0x0C
28:#define UHCI_PORTSC1   0x10
29:
30:#define CMD_RUN     0x0001
31:#define CMD_HCRESET 0x0002
32:#define CMD_GRESET  0x0004
33:#define CMD_MAXP    0x0080
34:
35:#define PORT_CCS  0x0001
36:#define PORT_CSC  0x0002
37:#define PORT_PED  0x0004
38:#define PORT_PEDC 0x0008
39:#define PORT_LS   0x0100  /* low-speed device attached */
40:#define PORT_PR   0x0200  /* port reset */
41:
42:/* Link pointer flags */
43:#define LP_TERMINATE 0x1
44:#define LP_QH        0x2
45:#define LP_VF        0x4  /* depth-first (TD only) */
46:
47:/* TD ctrl_status */
48:#define TD_ACTIVE  (1u << 23)
49:#define TD_IOC     (1u << 24)
50:#define TD_LS      (1u << 26)
51:#define TD_CERR3   (3u << 27)
52:#define TD_SPD     (1u << 29)
53:#define TD_ACTLEN_MASK 0x7FF
54:
55:/* PIDs */
56:#define PID_SETUP 0x2D
57:#define PID_IN    0x69
58:#define PID_OUT   0xE1
59:
60:struct uhci_td {
61:    volatile uint32_t link;
62:    volatile uint32_t ctrl_status;
63:    volatile uint32_t token;
64:    volatile uint32_t buffer;
65:    uint32_t pad[4]; /* pad to 32B; alignment + software use */
66:} __attribute__((packed));
67:
68:struct uhci_qh {
69:    volatile uint32_t head; /* next QH */
70:    volatile uint32_t elem; /* first TD */
71:    uint32_t pad[2];
72:} __attribute__((packed));
73:
74:/* Per-interrupt-endpoint state. */
75:struct uhci_ep {
76:    struct uhci_qh *qh;      /* VA */
77:    uint64_t qh_phys;
78:    struct uhci_td *td;      /* VA */
79:    uint64_t td_phys;
80:    void *buf;               /* VA */
81:    uint64_t buf_phys;
82:    int toggle;
83:    int maxlen;
84:    int low_speed;
85:    uint8_t addr;
86:    uint8_t ep;
87:    int active;
88:};
89:
90:struct uhci {
91:    uint16_t io;
92:    uint32_t *frame;         /* VA of frame list */
93:    uint64_t frame_phys;
94:    struct uhci_qh *qh_ctrl; /* VA */
95:    uint64_t qh_ctrl_phys;
96:    struct uhci_td *ctrl_td; /* VA: pool of control TDs */
97:    uint64_t ctrl_td_phys;
98:    void *ctrl_buf;          /* VA: control data bounce */
99:    uint64_t ctrl_buf_phys;
100:
101:    struct uhci_ep eps[4];
102:    int ep_count;
103:    uint8_t next_addr;
104:    struct usb_hcd hcd;
105:};
106:
107:static struct uhci uhci_ctrls[2];
108:static int uhci_count;
109:
110:static inline void *page_va(uint64_t *phys_out) {
111:    if (phys_out) *phys_out = 0;
112:    void *p = pmm_alloc_page_dma();
113:    if (!p) return NULL;
114:    memset(p, 0, PAGE_SIZE);
115:    if (phys_out) *phys_out = virt_to_phys(p);
116:    return p;
117:}
118:
119:/* --- TD/control helpers --- */
120:static uint32_t mk_token(uint8_t pid, uint8_t addr, uint8_t ep, int toggle, int len) {
121:    uint32_t maxlen = (len == 0) ? 0x7FF : (uint32_t)(len - 1);
122:    return (uint32_t)pid | ((uint32_t)addr << 8) | ((uint32_t)ep << 15) |
123:           ((uint32_t)(toggle & 1) << 19) | (maxlen << 21);
124:}
125:
126:/* Run a TD chain through the control QH and wait for completion.
127: * Returns 0 on success, -1 on error/timeout. */
128:static int uhci_run_ctrl(struct uhci *u, uint64_t first_td_phys) {
129:    u->qh_ctrl->elem = (uint32_t)first_td_phys; /* not terminated, not QH */
130:    /* Wait until the QH element terminates (chain consumed) or a TD errors. */
131:    for (long s = 0; s < 50000000L; s++) {
132:        if (u->qh_ctrl->elem & LP_TERMINATE) break;
133:        /* error: scan control TD pool for a non-active stalled TD */
134:    }
135:    int rc = 0;
136:    if (!(u->qh_ctrl->elem & LP_TERMINATE)) rc = -1;
137:    u->qh_ctrl->elem = LP_TERMINATE;
138:    return rc;
139:}
140:
141:static int uhci_control(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *dev,
142:                        const struct usb_setup *setup, void *data, int len) {
143:    struct uhci *u = hcd->priv;
144:    int ls = (dev->speed == USB_SPEED_LOW) ? TD_LS : 0;
145:    uint8_t addr = dev->addr;
146:    int mp = dev->max_packet0 ? dev->max_packet0 : 8;
147:    int dir_in = (setup->bmRequestType & USB_DIR_IN) != 0;
148:
149:    struct uhci_td *td = u->ctrl_td;
150:    int n = 0;
151:
152:    /* SETUP (DATA0). */
153:    memcpy(u->ctrl_buf, setup, 8);
154:    td[n].ctrl_status = TD_ACTIVE | TD_CERR3 | ls;
155:    td[n].token = mk_token(PID_SETUP, addr, 0, 0, 8);
156:    td[n].buffer = (uint32_t)u->ctrl_buf_phys;
157:    n++;
158:
159:    /* DATA stage (toggle starts at 1), split into max-packet chunks. */
160:    int toggle = 1;
161:    int remaining = len;
162:    uint32_t off = 64; /* keep data after the 8-byte setup in the bounce page */
163:    if (!dir_in && len > 0) memcpy((uint8_t *)u->ctrl_buf + off, data, len);
164:    while (remaining > 0) {
165:        int chunk = remaining > mp ? mp : remaining;
166:        td[n].ctrl_status = TD_ACTIVE | TD_CERR3 | ls | TD_SPD;
167:        td[n].token = mk_token(dir_in ? PID_IN : PID_OUT, addr, 0, toggle, chunk);
168:        td[n].buffer = (uint32_t)(u->ctrl_buf_phys + off);
169:        off += chunk;
170:        remaining -= chunk;
171:        toggle ^= 1;
172:        n++;
173:        if (n >= 30) break;
174:    }
175:
176:    /* STATUS (opposite direction, DATA1, IOC). */
177:    td[n].ctrl_status = TD_ACTIVE | TD_CERR3 | ls | TD_IOC;
178:    td[n].token = mk_token(dir_in ? PID_OUT : PID_IN, addr, 0, 1, 0);
179:    td[n].buffer = 0;
180:    n++;
181:
182:    /* Link the chain depth-first. */
183:    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
184:        if (i == n - 1)
185:            td[i].link = LP_TERMINATE;
186:        else
187:            td[i].link = (uint32_t)(u->ctrl_td_phys + (i + 1) * sizeof(struct uhci_td)) | LP_VF;
188:    }
189:
190:    if (uhci_run_ctrl(u, u->ctrl_td_phys) < 0)
191:        return -1;
192:
193:    /* Compute bytes transferred for IN: sum ActLen of data TDs. */
194:    int transferred = 0;
195:    if (dir_in) {
196:        int idx = 1; /* data TDs start after SETUP */
197:        int rem = len;
198:        while (rem > 0 && idx < n - 1) {
199:            int act = (td[idx].ctrl_status & TD_ACTLEN_MASK);
200:            act = (act == 0x7FF) ? 0 : act + 1; /* ActLen encoding */
201:            int chunk = rem > mp ? mp : rem;
202:            if (act > chunk) act = chunk;
203:            transferred += act;
204:            rem -= chunk;
205:            idx++;
206:        }
207:        if (data && transferred > 0)
208:            memcpy(data, (uint8_t *)u->ctrl_buf + 64, transferred);
209:    }
210:    return dir_in ? transferred : len;
211:}
212:
213:/* --- ports / enumeration --- */
214:static int uhci_address(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *dev);
215:
216:static int uhci_num_ports(struct usb_hcd *hcd) { (void)hcd; return 2; }
217:
218:static int uhci_port_connected(struct usb_hcd *hcd, int port) {
219:    struct uhci *u = hcd->priv;
220:    uint16_t sc = hal_inw(u->io + UHCI_PORTSC1 + port * 2);
221:    return (sc & PORT_CCS) ? 1 : 0;
222:}
223:
224:static int uhci_enumerate_port(struct usb_hcd *hcd, int port, struct usb_device *dev) {
225:    struct uhci *u = hcd->priv;
226:    uint16_t p = u->io + UHCI_PORTSC1 + port * 2;
227:    uint16_t sc = hal_inw(p);
228:    if (!(sc & PORT_CCS)) return -1;
229:
230:    int low_speed = (sc & PORT_LS) ? 1 : 0;
231:
232:    /* Reset sequence: assert PR, hold, deassert, then enable. */
233:    hal_outw(p, sc | PORT_PR);
234:    for (long s = 0; s < 5000000L; s++) { /* ~hold */ }
235:    sc = hal_inw(p);
236:    hal_outw(p, sc & ~PORT_PR);
237:    for (long s = 0; s < 2000000L; s++) { }
238:    /* enable port, clear change bits */
239:    hal_outw(p, (hal_inw(p) | PORT_PED) );
240:    for (long s = 0; s < 2000000L; s++) { }
241:    /* clear CSC/PEDC (write 1 to clear) */
242:    hal_outw(p, hal_inw(p) | PORT_CSC | PORT_PEDC);
243:    if (!(hal_inw(p) & PORT_PED)) return -1;
244:
245:    dev->speed = low_speed ? USB_SPEED_LOW : USB_SPEED_FULL;
246:    dev->max_packet0 = 8;
247:    return uhci_address(hcd, dev);
248:}
249:
250:/*
251: * Assign an address on the default pipe (addr 0). Used both for root-port
252: * devices and hub children — for the latter the hub already reset/enabled the
253: * port, so this is the only step the controller owns. Only one device may sit
254: * at address 0 at a time, which the sequential enumeration guarantees.
255: */
256:static int uhci_address(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *dev) {
257:    struct uhci *u = hcd->priv;
258:    dev->addr = 0;
259:
260:    struct usb_device_descriptor dd;
261:    memset(&dd, 0, sizeof(dd));
262:    struct usb_setup s8 = { USB_DIR_IN, USB_REQ_GET_DESCRIPTOR, (USB_DT_DEVICE << 8), 0, 8 };
263:    if (uhci_control(hcd, dev, &s8, &dd, 8) < 8) return -1;
264:    if (dd.bMaxPacketSize0) dev->max_packet0 = dd.bMaxPacketSize0;
265:
266:    uint8_t new_addr = ++u->next_addr;
267:    struct usb_setup sa = { USB_DIR_OUT, USB_REQ_SET_ADDRESS, new_addr, 0, 0 };
268:    if (uhci_control(hcd, dev, &sa, NULL, 0) < 0) return -1;
269:    dev->addr = new_addr;
270:    for (long s = 0; s < 2000000L; s++) { } /* SET_ADDRESS recovery */
271:    return 0;
272:}
273:
274:static int uhci_address_dev(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *dev) {
275:    return uhci_address(hcd, dev);
276:}
277:
278:/* --- interrupt IN endpoint --- */
279:static int uhci_intr_open(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *dev,
280:                          uint8_t ep_addr, int max_packet, int interval) {
281:    (void)interval;
282:    struct uhci *u = hcd->priv;
283:    if (u->ep_count >= (int)(sizeof(u->eps) / sizeof(u->eps[0]))) return -1;
284:    struct uhci_ep *e = &u->eps[u->ep_count];
285:    memset(e, 0, sizeof(*e));
286:
287:    e->qh = (struct uhci_qh *)page_va(&e->qh_phys);
288:    e->td = (struct uhci_td *)page_va(&e->td_phys);
289:    e->buf = page_va(&e->buf_phys);
290:    if (!e->qh || !e->td || !e->buf) return -1;
291:    e->maxlen = max_packet;
292:    e->low_speed = (dev->speed == USB_SPEED_LOW);
293:    e->addr = dev->addr;
294:    e->ep = ep_addr & 0x0F;
295:    e->toggle = 0;
296:    e->active = 1;
297:    dev->hcd_priv = e;
298:
299:    /* Arm the first IN TD. */
300:    e->td->ctrl_status = TD_ACTIVE | TD_CERR3 | TD_IOC | (e->low_speed ? TD_LS : 0);
301:    e->td->token = mk_token(PID_IN, e->addr, e->ep, e->toggle, e->maxlen);
302:    e->td->buffer = (uint32_t)e->buf_phys;
303:    e->td->link = LP_TERMINATE;
304:    e->qh->elem = (uint32_t)e->td_phys;
305:
306:    /* Chain this QH at the head of the schedule, before the control QH. */
307:    e->qh->head = (uint32_t)u->qh_ctrl_phys | LP_QH;
308:    if (u->ep_count > 0)
309:        u->eps[u->ep_count - 1].qh->head = (uint32_t)e->qh_phys | LP_QH;
310:    uint32_t first = (uint32_t)e->qh_phys | LP_QH;
311:    /* If this is the first interrupt EP, point the frame list at it. */
312:    if (u->ep_count == 0) {
313:        for (int i = 0; i < 1024; i++) u->frame[i] = first;
314:    }
315:    u->ep_count++;
316:    return 0;
317:}
318:
319:static int uhci_intr_poll(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *dev,
320:                          uint8_t ep_addr, void *buf, int len) {
321:    (void)hcd; (void)ep_addr;
322:    struct uhci_ep *e = dev->hcd_priv;
323:    if (!e || !e->active) return 0;
324:    if (e->td->ctrl_status & TD_ACTIVE) return 0; /* still pending */
325:
326:    int act = e->td->ctrl_status & TD_ACTLEN_MASK;
327:    act = (act == 0x7FF) ? 0 : act + 1;
328:    int stalled = (e->td->ctrl_status & (1u << 22)) != 0;
329:    int got = 0;
330:    if (!stalled && act > 0) {
331:        got = act > len ? len : act;
332:        memcpy(buf, e->buf, got);
333:        e->toggle ^= 1;
334:    }
335:    /* Re-arm. */
336:    e->td->ctrl_status = TD_ACTIVE | TD_CERR3 | TD_IOC | (e->low_speed ? TD_LS : 0);
337:    e->td->token = mk_token(PID_IN, e->addr, e->ep, e->toggle, e->maxlen);
338:    e->td->buffer = (uint32_t)e->buf_phys;
339:    e->td->link = LP_TERMINATE;
340:    e->qh->elem = (uint32_t)e->td_phys;
341:    return got;
342:}
343:
344:static struct usb_hcd_ops uhci_ops = {
345:    .num_ports = uhci_num_ports,
346:    .port_connected = uhci_port_connected,
347:    .enumerate_port = uhci_enumerate_port,
348:    .address_dev = uhci_address_dev,
349:    .control = uhci_control,
350:    .intr_open = uhci_intr_open,
351:    .intr_poll = uhci_intr_poll,
352:};
353:
354:static int uhci_probe(struct hal_device *dev) {
355:    if (uhci_count >= (int)(sizeof(uhci_ctrls) / sizeof(uhci_ctrls[0]))) return -1;
356:    struct uhci *u = &uhci_ctrls[uhci_count];
357:    memset(u, 0, sizeof(*u));
358:
359:    /* BAR4 is the UHCI I/O BAR on PIIX/ICH; fall back to dev->base. */
360:    uint32_t bar4 = pci_get_bar(dev->pci_bdf, 4);
361:    uint16_t io = (uint16_t)((bar4 & 1) ? (bar4 & ~0x3u) : (dev->base & 0xFFFF));
362:    if (!io) return -1;
363:    u->io = io;
364:
365:    pr_info("UHCI: %s io=0x%04x\n", dev->name, io);
366:
367:    /* Global + host reset. */
368:    hal_outw(u->io + UHCI_USBCMD, CMD_GRESET);
369:    for (long s = 0; s < 2000000L; s++) { }
370:    hal_outw(u->io + UHCI_USBCMD, 0);
371:    hal_outw(u->io + UHCI_USBCMD, CMD_HCRESET);
372:    for (long s = 0; s < 5000000L; s++)
373:        if (!(hal_inw(u->io + UHCI_USBCMD) & CMD_HCRESET)) break;
374:
375:    /* Frame list + skeleton control QH + control TD pool + bounce. */
376:    u->frame = (uint32_t *)page_va(&u->frame_phys);
377:    u->qh_ctrl = (struct uhci_qh *)page_va(&u->qh_ctrl_phys);
378:    u->ctrl_td = (struct uhci_td *)page_va(&u->ctrl_td_phys);
379:    u->ctrl_buf = page_va(&u->ctrl_buf_phys);
380:    if (!u->frame || !u->qh_ctrl || !u->ctrl_td || !u->ctrl_buf) return -1;
381:
382:    u->qh_ctrl->head = LP_TERMINATE;
383:    u->qh_ctrl->elem = LP_TERMINATE;
384:    for (int i = 0; i < 1024; i++)
385:        u->frame[i] = (uint32_t)u->qh_ctrl_phys | LP_QH;
386:
387:    hal_outl(u->io + UHCI_FRBASEADD, (uint32_t)u->frame_phys);
388:    hal_outw(u->io + UHCI_FRNUM, 0);
389:    hal_outb(u->io + UHCI_SOFMOD, 64);
390:    hal_outw(u->io + UHCI_USBINTR, 0); /* polled, no IRQ */
391:    hal_outw(u->io + UHCI_USBCMD, CMD_RUN | CMD_MAXP);
392:
393:    u->hcd.name = "UHCI";
394:    u->hcd.ops = &uhci_ops;
395:    u->hcd.priv = u;
396:    uhci_count++;
397:
398:    usb_register_hcd(&u->hcd);
399:    return 0;
400:}
401:
402:static struct device_driver uhci_driver = {
403:    .name = "uhci",
404:    .vendor = DRV_ANY_ID,
405:    .device = DRV_ANY_ID,
406:    .class_code = 0x0C,
407:    .subclass = 0x03,
408:    .prog_if = 0x00, /* UHCI */
409:    .probe = uhci_probe,
410:};
411:
412:void uhci_register(void) {
413:    driver_register(&uhci_driver);
414:}

@@@ kernel/drivers/usb/usb_core.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/drivers/usb/usb_core.c
3: * USB core: port enumeration, standard descriptor reads, HID hand-off.
4: *
5: * Controller-agnostic. Each HCD (xHCI/EHCI/UHCI) registers via
6: * usb_register_hcd() after resetting its controller; the core then walks the
7: * root-hub ports, addresses each device through the HCD (enumerate_port),
8: * reads its descriptors over the control pipe, and registers any HID boot
9: * interface for periodic polling (usb_hid.c).
10: */
11:
12:#include <drivers/usb/usb.h>
13:#include <kernel/driver.h>
14:#include <kernel/printk.h>
15:#include <kernel/string.h>
16:
17:#define MAX_USB_DEVICES 16
18:
19:static struct usb_device usb_devices[MAX_USB_DEVICES];
20:
21:static struct usb_device *usb_alloc_device(void) {
22:    for (int i = 0; i < MAX_USB_DEVICES; i++) {
23:        if (!usb_devices[i].in_use) {
24:            memset(&usb_devices[i], 0, sizeof(usb_devices[i]));
25:            usb_devices[i].in_use = 1;
26:            usb_devices[i].hid_iface = -1;
27:            return &usb_devices[i];
28:        }
29:    }
30:    return NULL;
31:}
32:
33:static void usb_setup_device(struct usb_device *dev);
34:static void usb_hub_init(struct usb_device *hub);
35:
36:int usb_control(struct usb_device *dev, uint8_t bmRequestType, uint8_t bRequest,
37:                uint16_t wValue, uint16_t wIndex, void *data, uint16_t wLength) {
38:    struct usb_setup s = {
39:        .bmRequestType = bmRequestType,
40:        .bRequest = bRequest,
41:        .wValue = wValue,
42:        .wIndex = wIndex,
43:        .wLength = wLength,
44:    };
45:    if (!dev->hcd || !dev->hcd->ops->control) return -1;
46:    return dev->hcd->ops->control(dev->hcd, dev, &s, data, wLength);
47:}
48:
49:/*
50: * Parse the configuration descriptor block, locate a HID interface (boot
51: * keyboard/mouse, or a generic report-protocol HID such as a tablet) and its
52: * interrupt-IN endpoint, and record them on the device. Returns 1 if found.
53: */
54:static int usb_parse_hid(struct usb_device *dev, const uint8_t *cfg, int len) {
55:    int i = 0;
56:    int cur_iface = -1;
57:    int cur_is_hid = 0;   /* current interface is HID class */
58:    int cur_is_boot = 0;  /* ... with the boot subclass + kbd/mouse protocol */
59:    uint8_t cur_proto = 0;
60:    while (i + 2 <= len) {
61:        uint8_t blen = cfg[i];
62:        uint8_t btype = cfg[i + 1];
63:        if (blen < 2 || i + blen > len) break;
64:
65:        if (btype == USB_DT_INTERFACE && blen >= sizeof(struct usb_interface_descriptor)) {
66:            const struct usb_interface_descriptor *id =
67:                (const struct usb_interface_descriptor *)(cfg + i);
68:            cur_iface = id->bInterfaceNumber;
69:            cur_is_hid = (id->bInterfaceClass == USB_CLASS_HID);
70:            cur_is_boot = (cur_is_hid &&
71:                           id->bInterfaceSubClass == HID_SUBCLASS_BOOT &&
72:                           (id->bInterfaceProtocol == HID_PROTOCOL_KEYBOARD ||
73:                            id->bInterfaceProtocol == HID_PROTOCOL_MOUSE));
74:            cur_proto = id->bInterfaceProtocol;
75:        } else if (btype == USB_DT_HID && cur_is_hid && blen >= 9) {
76:            /* HID descriptor: capture the report-descriptor length so we request
77:             * exactly that many bytes — UHCI's control path can't tolerate an
78:             * over-sized IN request that the device ends with a short packet. */
79:            dev->hid_report_len = cfg[i + 7] | (cfg[i + 8] << 8);
80:        } else if (btype == USB_DT_ENDPOINT && cur_is_hid && dev->hid_iface < 0 &&
81:                   blen >= sizeof(struct usb_endpoint_descriptor)) {
82:            const struct usb_endpoint_descriptor *ed =
83:                (const struct usb_endpoint_descriptor *)(cfg + i);
84:            int is_in = (ed->bEndpointAddress & 0x80) != 0;
85:            int is_intr = (ed->bmAttributes & 0x03) == 0x03;
86:            if (is_in && is_intr) {
87:                dev->hid_iface = cur_iface;
88:                dev->hid_ep_in = ed->bEndpointAddress;
89:                dev->hid_ep_max = ed->wMaxPacketSize & 0x7FF;
90:                dev->hid_interval = ed->bInterval;
91:                if (cur_is_boot)
92:                    dev->hid_protocol = cur_proto;  /* boot kbd/mouse */
93:                else
94:                    dev->hid_use_report = 1;        /* needs report-descriptor parse */
95:                return 1;
96:            }
97:        }
98:        i += blen;
99:    }
100:    return 0;
101:}
102:
103:/*
104: * Minimal HID report-descriptor parser: walks the item stream tracking the
105: * running bit offset of the input report, recording the absolute X/Y fields
106: * (Generic Desktop usages 0x30/0x31) and the first button block. Enough to
107: * decode a standard USB tablet; sets dev->hid_is_abs on success. (Report IDs
108: * are not handled — QEMU's usb-tablet and typical tablets omit them.)
109: */
110:static void usb_hid_parse_report_desc(struct usb_device *dev, const uint8_t *d, int len) {
111:    uint32_t bit = 0, usage_page = 0, logical_max = 0;
112:    uint32_t report_size = 0, report_count = 0;
113:    uint16_t usages[8];
114:    int nusage = 0;
115:    dev->hid_btn_off = -1;
116:
117:    int i = 0;
118:    while (i < len) {
119:        uint8_t b = d[i++];
120:        if (b == 0xFE) { /* long item: skip its payload */
121:            if (i < len) { int dl = d[i]; i += 2 + dl; }
122:            continue;
123:        }
124:        int isize = b & 0x03;
125:        if (isize == 3) isize = 4;
126:        uint8_t tag = b & 0xFC;
127:        uint32_t val = 0;
128:        for (int k = 0; k < isize && i < len; k++)
129:            val |= (uint32_t)d[i++] << (8 * k);
130:
131:        switch (tag) {
132:        case 0x04: usage_page = val; break;   /* Usage Page (global) */
133:        case 0x24: logical_max = val; break;  /* Logical Maximum (global) */
134:        case 0x74: report_size = val; break;  /* Report Size (global) */
135:        case 0x94: report_count = val; break; /* Report Count (global) */
136:        case 0x08:                            /* Usage (local) */
137:            if (nusage < 8) usages[nusage++] = (uint16_t)val;
138:            break;
139:        case 0x80:                            /* Input (main) */
140:            if (!(val & 0x01)) {              /* skip constant padding */
141:                if (usage_page == 0x09 && dev->hid_btn_off < 0) {
142:                    dev->hid_btn_off = (int16_t)bit;          /* first button bit */
143:                } else if (usage_page == 0x01 && !(val & 0x04)) { /* absolute GD */
144:                    for (uint32_t f = 0; f < report_count; f++) {
145:                        uint16_t u = (f < (uint32_t)nusage) ? usages[f] : 0;
146:                        uint32_t off = bit + f * report_size;
147:                        if (u == 0x30) {                       /* X */
148:                            dev->hid_abs_x_off = (uint16_t)off;
149:                            dev->hid_abs_bits = (uint8_t)report_size;
150:                            dev->hid_abs_max = logical_max;
151:                            dev->hid_is_abs = 1;
152:                        } else if (u == 0x31) {                /* Y */
153:                            dev->hid_abs_y_off = (uint16_t)off;
154:                        }
155:                    }
156:                }
157:            }
158:            bit += report_size * report_count;
159:            nusage = 0;
160:            break;
161:        case 0x90: case 0xB0:                 /* Output/Feature: clear locals */
162:        case 0xA0: case 0xC0:                 /* (End) Collection: clear locals */
163:            nusage = 0;
164:            break;
165:        default: break;
166:        }
167:    }
168:}
169:
170:static void usb_setup_device(struct usb_device *dev) {
171:    struct usb_device_descriptor dd;
172:    memset(&dd, 0, sizeof(dd));
173:
174:    /* Full device descriptor. */
175:    int r = usb_control(dev, USB_DIR_IN | USB_TYPE_STANDARD | USB_RECIP_DEVICE,
176:                        USB_REQ_GET_DESCRIPTOR, (USB_DT_DEVICE << 8), 0,
177:                        &dd, sizeof(dd));
178:    if (r < (int)sizeof(dd)) {
179:        pr_warn("USB: device descriptor read failed on port %d (r=%d)\n", dev->port, r);
180:        return;
181:    }
182:    dev->vendor = dd.idVendor;
183:    dev->product = dd.idProduct;
184:    dev->dev_class = dd.bDeviceClass;
185:    dev->dev_subclass = dd.bDeviceSubClass;
186:    dev->dev_protocol = dd.bDeviceProtocol;
187:    if (dd.bMaxPacketSize0) dev->max_packet0 = dd.bMaxPacketSize0;
188:
189:    pr_info("USB: device %04x:%04x class %02x on port %d (addr %d, speed %d)\n",
190:            dev->vendor, dev->product, dev->dev_class, dev->port, dev->addr, dev->speed);
191:
192:    /* Configuration descriptor: first 9 bytes for wTotalLength, then the whole
193:     * block (interfaces + endpoints). */
194:    uint8_t cfg[256];
195:    memset(cfg, 0, sizeof(cfg));
196:    r = usb_control(dev, USB_DIR_IN | USB_TYPE_STANDARD | USB_RECIP_DEVICE,
197:                    USB_REQ_GET_DESCRIPTOR, (USB_DT_CONFIG << 8), 0, cfg, 9);
198:    if (r < 9) {
199:        pr_warn("USB: config descriptor header read failed (r=%d)\n", r);
200:        return;
201:    }
202:    const struct usb_config_descriptor *cd = (const struct usb_config_descriptor *)cfg;
203:    int total = cd->wTotalLength;
204:    if (total > (int)sizeof(cfg)) total = sizeof(cfg);
205:    if (total > 9) {
206:        r = usb_control(dev, USB_DIR_IN | USB_TYPE_STANDARD | USB_RECIP_DEVICE,
207:                        USB_REQ_GET_DESCRIPTOR, (USB_DT_CONFIG << 8), 0, cfg, total);
208:        if (r < total) total = (r > 0) ? r : 9;
209:    }
210:    uint8_t cfg_value = cd->bConfigurationValue;
211:
212:    /* Select the configuration. */
213:    usb_control(dev, USB_DIR_OUT | USB_TYPE_STANDARD | USB_RECIP_DEVICE,
214:                USB_REQ_SET_CONFIG, cfg_value, 0, NULL, 0);
215:
216:    /* A hub: bring up its downstream ports and recurse. */
217:    if (dev->dev_class == USB_CLASS_HUB) {
218:        dev->is_hub = 1;
219:        usb_hub_init(dev);
220:        return;
221:    }
222:
223:    if (!usb_parse_hid(dev, cfg, total)) {
224:        return; /* not a HID interrupt device; ignored */
225:    }
226:
227:    if (dev->hid_use_report) {
228:        /* Report-protocol HID (e.g. a USB tablet): fetch + parse its report
229:         * descriptor to locate absolute X/Y, then run it in report protocol. */
230:        uint8_t rd[256];
231:        memset(rd, 0, sizeof(rd));
232:        int want = dev->hid_report_len;
233:        if (want <= 0 || want > (int)sizeof(rd)) want = sizeof(rd);
234:        int rl = usb_control(dev, USB_DIR_IN | USB_TYPE_STANDARD | USB_RECIP_INTERFACE,
235:                             USB_REQ_GET_DESCRIPTOR, (USB_DT_HID_REPORT << 8),
236:                             dev->hid_iface, rd, want);
237:        if (rl > 0)
238:            usb_hid_parse_report_desc(dev, rd, rl);
239:        usb_control(dev, USB_DIR_OUT | USB_TYPE_CLASS | USB_RECIP_INTERFACE,
240:                    HID_REQ_SET_PROTOCOL, HID_PROTO_REPORT, dev->hid_iface, NULL, 0);
241:        usb_control(dev, USB_DIR_OUT | USB_TYPE_CLASS | USB_RECIP_INTERFACE,
242:                    HID_REQ_SET_IDLE, 0, dev->hid_iface, NULL, 0);
243:        if (!dev->hid_is_abs) {
244:            pr_info("USB: HID report iface %d is not an absolute pointer; ignored\n",
245:                    dev->hid_iface);
246:            return;
247:        }
248:        pr_info("USB: HID tablet on iface %d ep 0x%02x (X@%u Y@%u %ubit max %u)\n",
249:                dev->hid_iface, dev->hid_ep_in, (unsigned)dev->hid_abs_x_off,
250:                (unsigned)dev->hid_abs_y_off, (unsigned)dev->hid_abs_bits,
251:                (unsigned)dev->hid_abs_max);
252:    } else {
253:        /* Boot protocol kbd/mouse: zero idle so reports only arrive on change. */
254:        usb_control(dev, USB_DIR_OUT | USB_TYPE_CLASS | USB_RECIP_INTERFACE,
255:                    HID_REQ_SET_PROTOCOL, HID_PROTO_BOOT, dev->hid_iface, NULL, 0);
256:        usb_control(dev, USB_DIR_OUT | USB_TYPE_CLASS | USB_RECIP_INTERFACE,
257:                    HID_REQ_SET_IDLE, 0, dev->hid_iface, NULL, 0);
258:        pr_info("USB: HID %s on iface %d ep 0x%02x (max %d)\n",
259:                dev->hid_protocol == HID_PROTOCOL_KEYBOARD ? "keyboard" : "mouse",
260:                dev->hid_iface, dev->hid_ep_in, dev->hid_ep_max);
261:    }
262:
263:    if (dev->hcd->ops->intr_open)
264:        dev->hcd->ops->intr_open(dev->hcd, dev, dev->hid_ep_in,
265:                                 dev->hid_ep_max, dev->hid_interval);
266:
267:    usb_hid_probe_device(dev);
268:}
269:
270:/* Hub class request helpers (USB 2.0 ch.11). */
271:static int hub_port_feature(struct usb_device *hub, uint8_t req, uint16_t feat, uint16_t port) {
272:    return usb_control(hub, USB_DIR_OUT | USB_TYPE_CLASS | USB_RECIP_OTHER,
273:                       req, feat, port, NULL, 0);
274:}
275:static uint16_t hub_port_status(struct usb_device *hub, uint16_t port) {
276:    uint8_t st[4];
277:    memset(st, 0, sizeof(st));
278:    if (usb_control(hub, USB_DIR_IN | USB_TYPE_CLASS | USB_RECIP_OTHER,
279:                    USB_REQ_GET_STATUS, 0, port, st, 4) < 2)
280:        return 0;
281:    return (uint16_t)(st[0] | (st[1] << 8));
282:}
283:
284:/*
285: * usb_hub_init - enumerate an external hub's downstream ports.
286: *
287: * Controller-agnostic: powers and resets each port via hub class requests, then
288: * asks the HCD to address the device through ops->address_dev (the HCD builds
289: * the xHCI route string / assigns the UHCI address). Recurses for nested hubs.
290: */
291:static void usb_hub_init(struct usb_device *hub) {
292:    if (hub->tier >= 5) return; /* USB max topology depth */
293:    if (!hub->hcd->ops->address_dev) return; /* controller without hub support */
294:
295:    uint8_t hd[16];
296:    memset(hd, 0, sizeof(hd));
297:    int r = usb_control(hub, USB_DIR_IN | USB_TYPE_CLASS | USB_RECIP_DEVICE,
298:                        USB_REQ_GET_DESCRIPTOR, (USB_DT_HUB << 8), 0, hd, 9);
299:    if (r < 3) return;
300:    int nports = hd[2];
301:    pr_info("USB: hub on root port %d: %d downstream ports (tier %d)\n",
302:            hub->root_port, nports, hub->tier);
303:
304:    for (int p = 1; p <= nports; p++)
305:        hub_port_feature(hub, USB_REQ_SET_FEATURE, HUB_FEAT_PORT_POWER, p);
306:    for (volatile long s = 0; s < 4000000L; s++) { /* power-on settle */ }
307:
308:    for (int p = 1; p <= nports; p++) {
309:        uint16_t status = hub_port_status(hub, p);
310:        if (!(status & HUB_PORT_CONNECTION)) continue;
311:        hub_port_feature(hub, USB_REQ_CLEAR_FEATURE, HUB_FEAT_C_PORT_CONNECTION, p);
312:
313:        hub_port_feature(hub, USB_REQ_SET_FEATURE, HUB_FEAT_PORT_RESET, p);
314:        for (int t = 0; t < 20; t++) {
315:            for (volatile long s = 0; s < 1000000L; s++) { }
316:            status = hub_port_status(hub, p);
317:            if (status & HUB_PORT_ENABLE) break;
318:        }
319:        hub_port_feature(hub, USB_REQ_CLEAR_FEATURE, HUB_FEAT_C_PORT_RESET, p);
320:        if (!(status & HUB_PORT_ENABLE)) continue;
321:
322:        int speed = (status & HUB_PORT_LOWSPEED)  ? USB_SPEED_LOW
323:                  : (status & HUB_PORT_HIGHSPEED) ? USB_SPEED_HIGH
324:                                                  : USB_SPEED_FULL;
325:
326:        struct usb_device *child = usb_alloc_device();
327:        if (!child) return;
328:        child->hcd = hub->hcd;
329:        child->parent = hub;
330:        child->hub_port = p;
331:        child->root_port = hub->root_port;
332:        child->tier = hub->tier + 1;
333:        child->route = hub->route | ((uint32_t)(p & 0xF) << (4 * hub->tier));
334:        child->speed = speed;
335:        child->max_packet0 = (speed == USB_SPEED_LOW) ? 8
336:                           : (speed == USB_SPEED_SUPER) ? 512 : 64;
337:
338:        if (hub->hcd->ops->address_dev(hub->hcd, child) < 0) {
339:            child->in_use = 0;
340:            continue;
341:        }
342:        usb_setup_device(child);
343:    }
344:}
345:
346:void usb_register_hcd(struct usb_hcd *hcd) {
347:    if (!hcd || !hcd->ops) return;
348:    int nports = hcd->ops->num_ports ? hcd->ops->num_ports(hcd) : 0;
349:    pr_info("USB: %s registered, %d root ports\n", hcd->name, nports);
350:
351:    /* Let the root ports settle before this one-shot scan: some emulated
352:     * controllers (notably under UTM/HVF) raise the connect bit a little after
353:     * the controller is started, so an immediate scan misses a present device.
354:     * Runtime hotplug / re-scan is Fase 2. */
355:    for (volatile long s = 0; s < 3000000L; s++) { }
356:
357:    for (int port = 0; port < nports; port++) {
358:        /* Poll the connect bit a few times (bounded) before giving up. */
359:        int conn = !hcd->ops->port_connected;
360:        for (int t = 0; t < 8 && !conn; t++) {
361:            conn = hcd->ops->port_connected(hcd, port);
362:            if (!conn)
363:                for (volatile long s = 0; s < 500000L; s++) { }
364:        }
365:        pr_info("USB: %s port %d connected=%d\n", hcd->name, port, conn);
366:        if (!conn)
367:            continue;
368:        struct usb_device *dev = usb_alloc_device();
369:        if (!dev) {
370:            pr_warn("%s", "USB: device table full\n");
371:            return;
372:        }
373:        dev->hcd = hcd;
374:        dev->port = port;
375:        dev->root_port = port + 1; /* 1-based for the xHCI slot context */
376:        dev->route = 0;            /* root device: empty route string */
377:        dev->tier = 0;
378:        dev->max_packet0 = 8; /* default until descriptor read */
379:        if (hcd->ops->enumerate_port(hcd, port, dev) < 0) {
380:            dev->in_use = 0;
381:            continue;
382:        }
383:        usb_setup_device(dev);
384:    }
385:}
386:
387:void usb_init(void) {
388:    pr_info("%s", "USB: Initializing host controllers...\n");
389:    xhci_register();
390:    ehci_register();
391:    uhci_register();
392:    driver_match_all();
393:}

2: * kernel/drivers/usb/usb_hid.c
3: * USB HID boot-protocol class driver.
4: *
5: * Translates boot keyboard (8-byte) and boot mouse (3-4 byte) reports into the
6: * existing evdev input core (virtio_input_add_event), exactly as the PS/2 and
7: * virtio-input drivers do. usb_hid_poll() is called from the same place that
8: * services keyboard_poll().

17:/* HID reports are translated to evdev events and pushed through the unified
18: * input_report() sink (keyboard.c), exactly like virtio-input and PS/2. */

20:#define MAX_HID_DEVICES 8

22:struct hid_dev {
23:    struct usb_device *dev;
24:    uint8_t prev[8];   /* last report (for press/release diffing) */
25:    int     in_use;
26:};

28:static struct hid_dev hid_devs[MAX_HID_DEVICES];

30:/*
31: * HID usage -> evdev keycode (Linux drivers/hid/usbhid/usbkbd.c hid_keyboard[]).
32: * Output keycodes match the KEY_* numbering in virtio_input.h (evdev), so the
33: * existing keyboard.c layout logic handles them unchanged.

35:static const uint8_t hid_to_evdev[256] = {

38:    4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 28, 1, 14, 15, 57, 12, 13, 26,
39:    27, 43, 43, 39, 40, 41, 51, 52, 53, 58, 59, 60, 61, 62, 63, 64,
40:    65, 66, 67, 68, 87, 88, 99, 70, 119, 110, 102, 104, 111, 107, 109, 106,

54:/* Modifier byte bit -> evdev keycode (LCtrl..RGui). */
55:static const uint8_t mod_to_evdev[8] = { 29, 42, 56, 125, 97, 54, 100, 126 };

57:void usb_hid_probe_device(struct usb_device *dev) {
58:    for (int i = 0; i < MAX_HID_DEVICES; i++) {
59:        if (!hid_devs[i].in_use) {
60:            hid_devs[i].in_use = 1;
61:            hid_devs[i].dev = dev;
62:            memset(hid_devs[i].prev, 0, sizeof(hid_devs[i].prev));
63:            return;
64:        }
65:    }
66:    pr_warn("%s", "USB-HID: device table full\n");
67:}
68:
69:static void hid_handle_keyboard(struct hid_dev *h, const uint8_t *r, int len) {
70:    if (len < 8) return;
71:    const uint8_t *prev = h->prev;
72:
73:    /* Modifiers: press/release on bit change. */
74:    uint8_t changed = r[0] ^ prev[0];
75:    for (int b = 0; b < 8; b++) {
76:        if (changed & (1 << b))
77:            input_report(EV_KEY, mod_to_evdev[b], (r[0] >> b) & 1);
78:    }
79:
80:    /* Released keys: present in prev[2..7], absent in new. */
81:    for (int i = 2; i < 8; i++) {
82:        uint8_t k = prev[i];
83:        if (k <= 3) continue;
84:        int still = 0;
85:        for (int j = 2; j < 8; j++) if (r[j] == k) { still = 1; break; }
86:        if (!still) input_report(EV_KEY, hid_to_evdev[k], 0);
87:    }
88:    /* Pressed keys: present in new, absent in prev. */
89:    for (int i = 2; i < 8; i++) {
90:        uint8_t k = r[i];
91:        if (k <= 3) continue;
92:        int was = 0;
93:        for (int j = 2; j < 8; j++) if (prev[j] == k) { was = 1; break; }
94:        if (!was) input_report(EV_KEY, hid_to_evdev[k], 1);
95:    }
96:    memcpy(h->prev, r, 8);
97:    input_report(EV_SYN, 0, 0);
98:}
99:
100:static void hid_handle_mouse(struct hid_dev *h, const uint8_t *r, int len) {
101:    if (len < 3) return;
102:    uint8_t buttons = r[0];
103:    int8_t dx = (int8_t)r[1];
104:    int8_t dy = (int8_t)r[2];   /* HID Y grows downward; compositor uses the same */
105:
106:    /* Buttons: report on change; motion as relative deltas; EV_SYN repaints. */
107:    uint8_t changed = buttons ^ h->prev[0];
108:    if (changed & 0x01) input_report(EV_KEY, BTN_LEFT, buttons & 0x01);
109:    if (changed & 0x02) input_report(EV_KEY, BTN_RIGHT, (buttons >> 1) & 1);
110:    if (changed & 0x04) input_report(EV_KEY, BTN_MIDDLE, (buttons >> 2) & 1);
111:
112:    if (dx) input_report(EV_REL, REL_X, dx);
113:    if (dy) input_report(EV_REL, REL_Y, dy);
114:
115:    h->prev[0] = buttons;
116:    input_report(EV_SYN, 0, 0);
117:}
118:
119:/* Extract `bits` (<=32) at bit offset `off` from a little-endian HID report. */
120:static uint32_t hid_get_bits(const uint8_t *r, int len, uint32_t off, uint32_t bits) {
121:    uint32_t v = 0;
122:    for (uint32_t k = 0; k < bits && k < 32; k++) {
123:        uint32_t bo = off + k;
124:        if ((int)(bo >> 3) >= len) break;
125:        if (r[bo >> 3] & (1u << (bo & 7)))
126:            v |= (1u << k);
127:    }
128:    return v;
129:}
130:
131:/*
132: * Absolute pointer (USB tablet): decode X/Y per the parsed report layout, scale
133: * to [0, INPUT_ABS_MAX] (the compositor maps that to framebuffer pixels) and emit
134: * EV_ABS — the same absolute path the compositor already handles. This is what
135: * makes a USB tablet track 1:1 instead of a relative mouse drifting to an edge.
136: */
137:static void hid_handle_tablet(struct hid_dev *h, const uint8_t *r, int len) {
138:    struct usb_device *dev = h->dev;
139:    uint32_t bits = dev->hid_abs_bits ? dev->hid_abs_bits : 16;
140:    uint32_t max = dev->hid_abs_max ? dev->hid_abs_max : ((1u << bits) - 1);
141:    uint32_t x = hid_get_bits(r, len, dev->hid_abs_x_off, bits);
142:    uint32_t y = hid_get_bits(r, len, dev->hid_abs_y_off, bits);
143:    int32_t nx = (int32_t)((uint64_t)x * INPUT_ABS_MAX / max);
144:    int32_t ny = (int32_t)((uint64_t)y * INPUT_ABS_MAX / max);
145:
146:    if (dev->hid_btn_off >= 0) {
147:        uint8_t btn = (uint8_t)hid_get_bits(r, len, (uint32_t)dev->hid_btn_off, 3);
148:        uint8_t changed = btn ^ h->prev[0];
149:        if (changed & 0x01) input_report(EV_KEY, BTN_LEFT, btn & 0x01);
150:        if (changed & 0x02) input_report(EV_KEY, BTN_RIGHT, (btn >> 1) & 1);
151:        if (changed & 0x04) input_report(EV_KEY, BTN_MIDDLE, (btn >> 2) & 1);
152:        h->prev[0] = btn;
153:    }
154:    input_report(EV_ABS, ABS_X, nx);
155:    input_report(EV_ABS, ABS_Y, ny);
156:    input_report(EV_SYN, 0, 0);
157:}
158:
159:void usb_hid_poll(void) {
160:    uint8_t report[64];
161:    for (int i = 0; i < MAX_HID_DEVICES; i++) {
162:        struct hid_dev *h = &hid_devs[i];
163:        if (!h->in_use) continue;
164:        struct usb_device *dev = h->dev;
165:        if (!dev->hcd->ops->intr_poll) continue;
166:
167:        int n = dev->hcd->ops->intr_poll(dev->hcd, dev, dev->hid_ep_in,
168:                                         report, sizeof(report));
169:        while (n > 0) {
170:            if (dev->hid_is_abs)
171:                hid_handle_tablet(h, report, n);
172:            else if (dev->hid_protocol == HID_PROTOCOL_KEYBOARD)
173:                hid_handle_keyboard(h, report, n);
174:            else
175:                hid_handle_mouse(h, report, n);
176:            n = dev->hcd->ops->intr_poll(dev->hcd, dev, dev->hid_ep_in,
177:                                         report, sizeof(report));
178:        }
179:    }
180:}

@@@ kernel/drivers/usb/xhci.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/drivers/usb/xhci.c
3: * xHCI (USB 3.x) host controller driver — polled, boot-input oriented.
4: *
5: * Covers USB low/full/high/super-speed devices directly (no companion
6: * controllers), which is why it is the primary target: it is what UTM "USB
7: * 3.0" and `-device qemu-xhci` expose. Implements usb_hcd_ops for the USB core.
8: *
9: * Model: all rings are polled. The event ring is consumed synchronously after
10: * each command/transfer; no MSI/IRQ is wired (input is serviced from
11: * usb_hid_poll()). Memory for rings/contexts is page-allocated (pmm_alloc_page
12: * returns a kernel VA; the controller is programmed with virt_to_phys()).
13: *
14: * NOTE(ASTRA-VIOLATION): calls arch_vmm_map_device() directly (amd64). The
15: * aarch64 ECAM phase adds the per-arch implementation behind the platform
16: * contract; tracked with the PCI-ECAM work.
17: */
18:
19:#include <drivers/usb/usb.h>
20:#include <drivers/pci.h>
21:#include <kernel/driver.h>
22:#include <kernel/hal.h>
23:#include <kernel/pmm.h>
24:#include <kernel/printk.h>
25:#include <kernel/string.h>
26:
27:extern int arch_vmm_map_device(uint64_t base, uint64_t size);
28:
29:/* --- Capability registers (offset from MMIO base) --- */
30:#define XHCI_CAPLENGTH   0x00 /* u8 */
31:#define XHCI_HCSPARAMS1  0x04
32:#define XHCI_HCSPARAMS2  0x08
33:#define XHCI_HCCPARAMS1  0x10
34:#define XHCI_DBOFF       0x14
35:#define XHCI_RTSOFF      0x18
36:
37:/* --- Operational registers (offset from op base = base + CAPLENGTH) --- */
38:#define XHCI_USBCMD   0x00
39:#define XHCI_USBSTS   0x04
40:#define XHCI_CRCR     0x18 /* 64-bit */
41:#define XHCI_DCBAAP   0x30 /* 64-bit */
42:#define XHCI_CONFIG   0x38
43:#define XHCI_PORTSC(p) (0x400 + 0x10 * (p))
44:
45:#define USBCMD_RUN   (1u << 0)
46:#define USBCMD_HCRST (1u << 1)
47:#define USBSTS_HCH   (1u << 0)
48:#define USBSTS_CNR   (1u << 11)
49:
50:#define PORTSC_CCS (1u << 0)  /* current connect status */
51:#define PORTSC_PED (1u << 1)  /* port enabled */
52:#define PORTSC_PR  (1u << 4)  /* port reset */
53:#define PORTSC_PRC (1u << 21) /* port reset change */
54:#define PORTSC_SPEED_SHIFT 10
55:#define PORTSC_SPEED_MASK 0xF
56:
57:/* --- Runtime interrupter 0 (offset from rt base = base + RTSOFF) --- */
58:#define XHCI_IR0       0x20
59:#define IR_IMAN        0x00
60:#define IR_ERSTSZ      0x08
61:#define IR_ERSTBA      0x10 /* 64-bit */
62:#define IR_ERDP        0x18 /* 64-bit */
63:
64:/* --- TRB types --- */
65:#define TRB_NORMAL     1
66:#define TRB_SETUP      2
67:#define TRB_DATA       3
68:#define TRB_STATUS     4
69:#define TRB_LINK       6
70:#define TRB_ENABLE_SLOT 9
71:#define TRB_ADDRESS_DEV 11
72:#define TRB_CONFIG_EP  12
73:#define TRB_EV_TRANSFER 32
74:#define TRB_EV_CMD_COMP 33
75:#define TRB_EV_PORTSC   34
76:
77:#define TRB_CYCLE   (1u << 0)
78:#define TRB_TC      (1u << 1)  /* toggle cycle (link) */
79:#define TRB_IOC     (1u << 5)
80:#define TRB_IDT     (1u << 6)  /* immediate data (setup) */
81:
82:#define CC_SUCCESS 1
83:
84:#define RING_TRBS 256
85:
86:struct xhci_trb {
87:    uint64_t param;
88:    uint32_t status;
89:    uint32_t control;
90:} __attribute__((packed));
91:
92:struct xhci_ring {
93:    struct xhci_trb *trbs; /* VA */
94:    uint64_t phys;
95:    int enqueue;
96:    uint8_t cycle;
97:};
98:
99:struct xhci_dev {
100:    int slot_id;
101:    void *devctx;   /* VA */
102:    void *inputctx; /* VA */
103:    struct xhci_ring ep0;
104:    struct xhci_ring ep_in; /* interrupt IN */
105:    uint8_t ep_in_dci;
106:    void *bounce;   /* one page bounce buffer (VA) */
107:    int pending;    /* an interrupt TRB is queued and awaiting completion */
108:};
109:
110:struct xhci {
111:    volatile uint8_t *base; /* VA == phys (identity) */
112:    volatile uint8_t *op;
113:    volatile uint8_t *rt;
114:    volatile uint32_t *db;
115:    int max_slots;
116:    int max_ports;
117:    int ctxsz; /* 32 or 64 */
118:
119:    struct xhci_ring cmd;
120:    struct xhci_trb *evt; /* event ring segment VA */
121:    uint64_t evt_phys;
122:    int evt_deq;
123:    uint8_t evt_cycle;
124:    void *dcbaa; /* VA */
125:    void *ctrl_bounce; /* control-transfer data bounce page (VA) */
126:
127:    struct xhci_dev devs[8];
128:    int dev_count;
129:    struct usb_hcd hcd;
130:};
