132:static struct xhci xhci_ctrls[2];
133:static int xhci_count;
134:
135:/* --- MMIO accessors --- */
136:static inline uint32_t rd32(volatile uint8_t *p, uint32_t off) {
137:    return *(volatile uint32_t *)(p + off);
138:}
139:static inline void wr32(volatile uint8_t *p, uint32_t off, uint32_t v) {
140:    *(volatile uint32_t *)(p + off) = v;
141:}
142:static inline void wr64(volatile uint8_t *p, uint32_t off, uint64_t v) {
143:    *(volatile uint32_t *)(p + off) = (uint32_t)v;
144:    *(volatile uint32_t *)(p + off + 4) = (uint32_t)(v >> 32);
145:}
146:
147:static void *alloc_zeroed_page(uint64_t *phys_out) {
148:    if (phys_out) *phys_out = 0;
149:    void *p = pmm_alloc_page_dma();
150:    if (!p) return NULL;
151:    memset(p, 0, PAGE_SIZE);
152:    if (phys_out) *phys_out = virt_to_phys(p);
153:    return p;
154:}
155:
156:static void ring_init(struct xhci_ring *r) {
157:    uint64_t phys;
158:    r->trbs = (struct xhci_trb *)alloc_zeroed_page(&phys);
159:    r->phys = phys;
160:    r->enqueue = 0;
161:    r->cycle = 1;
162:    /* Link TRB at the last slot, back to the start, toggling cycle. */
163:    struct xhci_trb *link = &r->trbs[RING_TRBS - 1];
164:    link->param = phys;
165:    link->status = 0;
166:    link->control = (TRB_LINK << 10) | TRB_TC | r->cycle;
167:}
168:
169:/* Push a TRB (param/status/control without cycle) onto a ring; returns the
170: * physical address of the slot used (for matching the completion event). */
171:static uint64_t ring_push(struct xhci_ring *r, uint64_t param, uint32_t status,
172:                          uint32_t control) {
173:    struct xhci_trb *t = &r->trbs[r->enqueue];
174:    uint64_t slot_phys = r->phys + r->enqueue * sizeof(struct xhci_trb);
175:    t->param = param;
176:    t->status = status;
177:    t->control = control | r->cycle;
178:    r->enqueue++;
179:    if (r->enqueue == RING_TRBS - 1) {
180:        /* hit the Link TRB: update its cycle and wrap. */
181:        struct xhci_trb *link = &r->trbs[RING_TRBS - 1];
182:        link->control = (TRB_LINK << 10) | TRB_TC | r->cycle;
183:        r->enqueue = 0;
184:        r->cycle ^= 1;
185:    }
186:    return slot_phys;
187:}
188:
189:/* Poll the event ring for the next event. Returns 1 and fills *evt on success,
190: * 0 on timeout. Advances ERDP. */
191:static int evt_wait(struct xhci *x, struct xhci_trb *out) {
192:    for (long spin = 0; spin < 20000000L; spin++) {
193:        struct xhci_trb *e = &x->evt[x->evt_deq];
194:        if ((e->control & TRB_CYCLE) == x->evt_cycle) {
195:            *out = *e;
196:            x->evt_deq++;
197:            if (x->evt_deq == RING_TRBS) {
198:                x->evt_deq = 0;
199:                x->evt_cycle ^= 1;
200:            }
201:            uint64_t erdp = x->evt_phys + x->evt_deq * sizeof(struct xhci_trb);
202:            wr64(x->rt, XHCI_IR0 + IR_ERDP, erdp | (1u << 3)); /* clear EHB */
203:            return 1;
204:        }
205:    }
206:    return 0;
207:}
208:
209:/* Issue a command TRB and wait for its Command Completion Event.
210: * Returns completion code; *slot_out gets the event's slot id. */
211:static int cmd_exec(struct xhci *x, uint64_t param, uint32_t control, int *slot_out) {
212:    ring_push(&x->cmd, param, 0, control);
213:    x->db[0] = 0; /* ring command doorbell */
214:    struct xhci_trb ev;
215:    /* Port-status-change and stray transfer events can interleave on the single
216:     * event ring; only a Command Completion Event answers a command. */
217:    for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++) {
218:        if (!evt_wait(x, &ev)) return -1;
219:        if (((ev.control >> 10) & 0x3F) != TRB_EV_CMD_COMP) continue;
220:        if (slot_out) *slot_out = (ev.control >> 24) & 0xFF;
221:        return (ev.status >> 24) & 0xFF;
222:    }
223:    return -1;
224:}
225:
226:/* --- Context helpers --- */
227:static inline uint8_t *ctx_at(struct xhci *x, void *base, int index) {
228:    return (uint8_t *)base + index * x->ctxsz;
229:}
230:
231:static int speed_to_maxpkt0(int speed) {
232:    switch (speed) {
233:    case USB_SPEED_LOW:  return 8;
234:    case USB_SPEED_SUPER: return 512;
235:    default: return 64; /* full / high */
236:    }
237:}
238:
239:/* --- usb_hcd_ops --- */
240:
241:static int xhci_num_ports(struct usb_hcd *hcd) {
242:    struct xhci *x = hcd->priv;
243:    return x->max_ports;
244:}
245:
246:static int xhci_port_connected(struct usb_hcd *hcd, int port) {
247:    struct xhci *x = hcd->priv;
248:    uint32_t sc = rd32(x->op, XHCI_PORTSC(port));
249:    return (sc & PORTSC_CCS) ? 1 : 0;
250:}
251:
252:static int xhci_port_speed(struct xhci *x, int port) {
253:    uint32_t sc = rd32(x->op, XHCI_PORTSC(port));
254:    int psv = (sc >> PORTSC_SPEED_SHIFT) & PORTSC_SPEED_MASK;
255:    /* QEMU xHCI PSI default: 1=full,2=low,3=high,4=super */
256:    switch (psv) {
257:    case 2: return USB_SPEED_LOW;
258:    case 1: return USB_SPEED_FULL;
259:    case 3: return USB_SPEED_HIGH;
260:    case 4: return USB_SPEED_SUPER;
261:    default: return USB_SPEED_FULL;
262:    }
263:}
264:
265:/*
266: * Enable Slot + Address Device using the device's topology (speed/root_port/
267: * route/tier/parent). Shared by root-port enumeration and hub-child addressing;
268: * the only difference between a root device and one behind a hub is the route
269: * string and the TT fields, both derived from udev here.
270: */
271:static int xhci_setup_slot(struct xhci *x, struct usb_device *udev) {
272:    if (x->dev_count >= (int)(sizeof(x->devs) / sizeof(x->devs[0]))) return -1;
273:
274:    int slot_id = 0;
275:    int cc = cmd_exec(x, 0, (TRB_ENABLE_SLOT << 10), &slot_id);
276:    if (cc != CC_SUCCESS || slot_id == 0) {
277:        pr_warn("xHCI: Enable Slot failed (cc=%d)\n", cc);
278:        return -1;
279:    }
280:
281:    struct xhci_dev *xd = &x->devs[x->dev_count];
282:    memset(xd, 0, sizeof(*xd));
283:    xd->slot_id = slot_id;
284:
285:    uint64_t devctx_phys, inputctx_phys;
286:    xd->devctx = alloc_zeroed_page(&devctx_phys);
287:    xd->inputctx = alloc_zeroed_page(&inputctx_phys);
288:    xd->bounce = alloc_zeroed_page(NULL);
289:    ring_init(&xd->ep0);
290:    if (!xd->devctx || !xd->inputctx || !xd->bounce) return -1;
291:
292:    /* DCBAA[slot] = device context phys. */
293:    ((uint64_t *)x->dcbaa)[slot_id] = devctx_phys;
294:
295:    int mp0 = udev->max_packet0 ? udev->max_packet0 : speed_to_maxpkt0(udev->speed);
296:
297:    /* Input control context: add slot (A0) + EP0 (A1). */
298:    uint32_t *icc = (uint32_t *)ctx_at(x, xd->inputctx, 0);
299:    icc[1] = (1u << 0) | (1u << 1);
300:
301:    /* Slot context: route string + speed; root-hub port; TT for a low/full
302:     * speed device behind a high-speed hub (split transactions). */
303:    uint32_t *slot = (uint32_t *)ctx_at(x, xd->inputctx, 1);
304:    slot[0] = (1u << 27) | ((uint32_t)udev->speed << 20) | (udev->route & 0xFFFFF);
305:    slot[1] = ((uint32_t)udev->root_port) << 16;
306:    if (udev->parent && udev->speed != USB_SPEED_HIGH && udev->speed != USB_SPEED_SUPER) {
307:        struct xhci_dev *pd = udev->parent->hcd_priv;
308:        if (pd) slot[2] = (uint32_t)pd->slot_id | ((uint32_t)udev->hub_port << 8);
309:    }
310:
311:    /* EP0 context. */
312:    uint32_t *ep0 = (uint32_t *)ctx_at(x, xd->inputctx, 2);
313:    ep0[1] = (4u << 3) | (3u << 1) | ((uint32_t)mp0 << 16);
314:    *(uint64_t *)&ep0[2] = xd->ep0.phys | xd->ep0.cycle;
315:
316:    cc = cmd_exec(x, inputctx_phys, (TRB_ADDRESS_DEV << 10) | (slot_id << 24), NULL);
317:    if (cc != CC_SUCCESS) {
318:        pr_warn("xHCI: Address Device failed (cc=%d)\n", cc);
319:        return -1;
320:    }
321:
322:    udev->addr = slot_id;
323:    udev->max_packet0 = mp0;
324:    udev->hcd_priv = xd;
325:    x->dev_count++;
326:    return 0;
327:}
328:
329:static int xhci_enumerate_port(struct usb_hcd *hcd, int port, struct usb_device *udev) {
330:    struct xhci *x = hcd->priv;
331:
332:    /* Reset the root port (USB2 needs it; USB3 is usually already enabled). */
333:    uint32_t sc = rd32(x->op, XHCI_PORTSC(port));
334:    if (!(sc & PORTSC_PED)) {
335:        wr32(x->op, XHCI_PORTSC(port), (sc & ~0x80FE0000u) | PORTSC_PR);
336:        for (long s = 0; s < 20000000L; s++) {
337:            sc = rd32(x->op, XHCI_PORTSC(port));
338:            if (sc & (PORTSC_PRC | PORTSC_PED)) break;
339:        }
340:        wr32(x->op, XHCI_PORTSC(port), (rd32(x->op, XHCI_PORTSC(port)) & ~0x80FE0000u) | PORTSC_PRC);
341:        for (long s = 0; s < 2000000L; s++) { /* settle */ }
342:    }
343:    sc = rd32(x->op, XHCI_PORTSC(port));
344:    pr_debug("xHCI: port %d after reset PORTSC=0x%08x\n", port, sc);
345:    if (!(sc & PORTSC_PED)) return -1;
346:
347:    udev->speed = xhci_port_speed(x, port);
348:    return xhci_setup_slot(x, udev);
349:}
350:
351:/* Address a device reached through an external hub (topology already filled). */
352:static int xhci_address_dev(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *udev) {
353:    return xhci_setup_slot(hcd->priv, udev);
354:}
355:
356:/* Control transfer on EP0. */
357:static int xhci_control(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *udev,
358:                        const struct usb_setup *setup, void *data, int len) {
359:    struct xhci *x = hcd->priv;
360:    struct xhci_dev *xd = udev->hcd_priv;
361:    if (!xd) return -1;
362:
363:    int dir_in = (setup->bmRequestType & USB_DIR_IN) != 0;
364:
365:    /* Setup Stage: immediate data = the 8 setup bytes. */
366:    uint64_t setup_param;
367:    memcpy(&setup_param, setup, 8);
368:    uint32_t trt = (len == 0) ? 0 : (dir_in ? 3 : 2);
369:    ring_push(&xd->ep0, setup_param, 8, (TRB_SETUP << 10) | TRB_IDT | (trt << 16));
370:
371:    /* Data Stage. */
372:    if (len > 0) {
373:        if (dir_in) memset(xd->bounce, 0, len);
374:        else memcpy(xd->bounce, data, len);
375:        uint32_t ctl = (TRB_DATA << 10) | (dir_in ? (1u << 16) : 0);
376:        ring_push(&xd->ep0, virt_to_phys(xd->bounce), len, ctl);
377:    }
378:
379:    /* Status Stage (IOC so we get a transfer event). */
380:    uint32_t sdir = (len > 0 && dir_in) ? 0 : (1u << 16);
381:    ring_push(&xd->ep0, 0, 0, (TRB_STATUS << 10) | sdir | TRB_IOC);
382:
383:    x->db[xd->slot_id] = 1; /* DB target = EP0 (DCI 1) */
384:
385:    struct xhci_trb ev;
386:    int got = 0, residual = 0;
387:    /* Wait for the transfer event from the Status Stage. */
388:    for (int tries = 0; tries < 4; tries++) {
389:        if (!evt_wait(x, &ev)) break;
390:        if (((ev.control >> 10) & 0x3F) == TRB_EV_TRANSFER) {
391:            residual = ev.status & 0xFFFFFF;
392:            int cc = (ev.status >> 24) & 0xFF;
393:            if (cc != CC_SUCCESS && cc != 13 /* short packet */) {
394:                /* keep going; report failure */
395:            }
396:            got = 1;
397:            break;
398:        }
399:    }
400:    if (!got) return -1;
401:
402:    int transferred = len - residual;
403:    if (dir_in && data && transferred > 0)
404:        memcpy(data, xd->bounce, transferred);
405:    return transferred;
406:}
407:
408:/* Configure an interrupt IN endpoint and queue the first transfer. */
409:static int xhci_intr_open(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *udev,
410:                          uint8_t ep_addr, int max_packet, int interval) {
411:    struct xhci *x = hcd->priv;
412:    struct xhci_dev *xd = udev->hcd_priv;
413:    int ep_num = ep_addr & 0x0F;
414:    int dci = ep_num * 2 + 1; /* IN endpoint */
415:    xd->ep_in_dci = dci;
416:    ring_init(&xd->ep_in);
417:
418:    /* Input context: A0 (slot) + A(dci). */
419:    memset(xd->inputctx, 0, PAGE_SIZE);
420:    uint32_t *icc = (uint32_t *)ctx_at(x, xd->inputctx, 0);
421:    icc[1] = (1u << 0) | (1u << dci);
422:
423:    uint32_t *slot = (uint32_t *)ctx_at(x, xd->inputctx, 1);
424:    slot[0] = ((uint32_t)dci << 27) | ((uint32_t)udev->speed << 20);
425:    slot[1] = ((uint32_t)(udev->port + 1)) << 16;
426:
427:    uint32_t *ep = (uint32_t *)ctx_at(x, xd->inputctx, dci + 1);
428:    int ival = interval ? interval : 8;
429:    ep[0] = ((uint32_t)ival << 16);
430:    ep[1] = (7u << 3) /* interrupt IN */ | (3u << 1) | ((uint32_t)max_packet << 16);
431:    *(uint64_t *)&ep[2] = xd->ep_in.phys | xd->ep_in.cycle;
432:    ep[4] = max_packet; /* avg TRB length */
433:
434:    int cc = cmd_exec(x, virt_to_phys(xd->inputctx),
435:                      (TRB_CONFIG_EP << 10) | (xd->slot_id << 24), NULL);
436:    if (cc != CC_SUCCESS) {
437:        pr_warn("xHCI: Configure Endpoint failed (cc=%d)\n", cc);
438:        return -1;
439:    }
440:
441:    /* Queue the first interrupt IN transfer. */
442:    memset(xd->bounce, 0, max_packet);
443:    ring_push(&xd->ep_in, virt_to_phys(xd->bounce), max_packet, (TRB_NORMAL << 10) | TRB_IOC);
444:    x->db[xd->slot_id] = dci;
445:    xd->pending = 1;
446:    return 0;
447:}
448:
449:static int xhci_intr_poll(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *udev,
450:                          uint8_t ep_addr, void *buf, int len) {
451:    struct xhci *x = hcd->priv;
452:    struct xhci_dev *xd = udev->hcd_priv;
453:    (void)ep_addr;
454:    if (!xd->pending) return 0;
455:
456:    /* Non-blocking: is there an event at the ring head? The event ring is shared
457:     * by every endpoint, so only consume it if it is a Transfer Event for THIS
458:     * device's slot and interrupt EP; otherwise leave it for the owner. */
459:    struct xhci_trb *e = &x->evt[x->evt_deq];
460:    if ((e->control & TRB_CYCLE) != x->evt_cycle) return 0;
461:    int type = (e->control >> 10) & 0x3F;
462:    if (type != TRB_EV_TRANSFER) {
463:        struct xhci_trb junk;
464:        evt_wait(x, &junk); /* drain port-status/other events */
465:        return 0;
466:    }
467:    int ev_slot = (e->control >> 24) & 0xFF;
468:    int ev_dci = (e->control >> 16) & 0x1F;
469:    if (ev_slot != xd->slot_id || ev_dci != xd->ep_in_dci)
470:        return 0; /* belongs to another device; its own poll will take it */
471:
472:    struct xhci_trb ev;
473:    evt_wait(x, &ev);
474:    int residual = ev.status & 0xFFFFFF;
475:    int got = udev->hid_ep_max - residual;
476:    if (got > len) got = len;
477:    if (got > 0) memcpy(buf, xd->bounce, got);
478:
479:    /* Re-queue another interrupt transfer. */
480:    memset(xd->bounce, 0, udev->hid_ep_max);
481:    ring_push(&xd->ep_in, virt_to_phys(xd->bounce), udev->hid_ep_max,
482:              (TRB_NORMAL << 10) | TRB_IOC);
483:    x->db[xd->slot_id] = xd->ep_in_dci;
484:    return got;
485:}
486:
487:static struct usb_hcd_ops xhci_ops = {
488:    .num_ports = xhci_num_ports,
489:    .port_connected = xhci_port_connected,
490:    .enumerate_port = xhci_enumerate_port,
491:    .address_dev = xhci_address_dev,
492:    .control = xhci_control,
493:    .intr_open = xhci_intr_open,
494:    .intr_poll = xhci_intr_poll,
495:};
496:
497:static int xhci_reset_and_start(struct xhci *x) {
498:    /* Halt. */
499:    uint32_t cmd = rd32(x->op, XHCI_USBCMD);
500:    wr32(x->op, XHCI_USBCMD, cmd & ~USBCMD_RUN);
501:    for (long s = 0; s < 5000000L; s++)
502:        if (rd32(x->op, XHCI_USBSTS) & USBSTS_HCH) break;
503:
504:    /* Reset. */
505:    wr32(x->op, XHCI_USBCMD, USBCMD_HCRST);
506:    for (long s = 0; s < 5000000L; s++)
507:        if (!(rd32(x->op, XHCI_USBCMD) & USBCMD_HCRST)) break;
508:    for (long s = 0; s < 5000000L; s++)
509:        if (!(rd32(x->op, XHCI_USBSTS) & USBSTS_CNR)) break;
510:
511:    /* Max device slots enabled. */
512:    wr32(x->op, XHCI_CONFIG, x->max_slots);
513:
514:    /* DCBAA. */
515:    uint64_t dcbaa_phys;
516:    x->dcbaa = alloc_zeroed_page(&dcbaa_phys);
517:    if (!x->dcbaa) return -1;
518:    wr64(x->op, XHCI_DCBAAP, dcbaa_phys);
519:
520:    /* Command ring. */
521:    ring_init(&x->cmd);
522:    wr64(x->op, XHCI_CRCR, x->cmd.phys | 1 /* RCS */);
523:
524:    /* Event ring + ERST (single segment). */
525:    x->evt = (struct xhci_trb *)alloc_zeroed_page(&x->evt_phys);
526:    x->evt_deq = 0;
527:    x->evt_cycle = 1;
528:    uint64_t erst_phys;
529:    uint32_t *erst = (uint32_t *)alloc_zeroed_page(&erst_phys);
530:    if (!x->evt || !erst) return -1;
531:    erst[0] = (uint32_t)x->evt_phys;
532:    erst[1] = (uint32_t)(x->evt_phys >> 32);
533:    erst[2] = RING_TRBS; /* segment size */
534:    wr32(x->rt, XHCI_IR0 + IR_ERSTSZ, 1);
535:    wr64(x->rt, XHCI_IR0 + IR_ERDP, x->evt_phys);
536:    wr64(x->rt, XHCI_IR0 + IR_ERSTBA, erst_phys);
537:
538:    x->ctrl_bounce = alloc_zeroed_page(NULL);
539:
540:    /* Run. */
541:    wr32(x->op, XHCI_USBCMD, USBCMD_RUN);
542:    for (long s = 0; s < 5000000L; s++)
543:        if (!(rd32(x->op, XHCI_USBSTS) & USBSTS_HCH)) break;
544:
545:    /* Power all root ports (PP, bit 9) so connect status (CCS) becomes valid,
546:     * then let it settle before enumeration reads PORTSC. */
547:    for (int p = 0; p < x->max_ports; p++) {
548:        uint32_t sc = rd32(x->op, XHCI_PORTSC(p));
549:        if (!(sc & (1u << 9)))
550:            wr32(x->op, XHCI_PORTSC(p), (sc & ~0x80FE0000u) | (1u << 9));
551:    }
552:    for (long s = 0; s < 3000000L; s++) { /* settle */ }
553:    return 0;
554:}
555:
556:static int xhci_probe(struct hal_device *dev) {
557:    if (xhci_count >= (int)(sizeof(xhci_ctrls) / sizeof(xhci_ctrls[0]))) return -1;
558:    struct xhci *x = &xhci_ctrls[xhci_count];
559:    memset(x, 0, sizeof(*x));
560:
561:    uint64_t base = dev->base;
562:    arch_vmm_map_device(base, 0x20000);
563:    x->base = (volatile uint8_t *)phys_to_virt(base);
564:
565:    uint8_t caplen = *(volatile uint8_t *)(x->base + XHCI_CAPLENGTH);
566:    uint32_t hcs1 = rd32(x->base, XHCI_HCSPARAMS1);
567:    uint32_t hcc1 = rd32(x->base, XHCI_HCCPARAMS1);
568:    x->max_slots = hcs1 & 0xFF;
569:    x->max_ports = (hcs1 >> 24) & 0xFF;
570:    x->ctxsz = (hcc1 & (1u << 2)) ? 64 : 32;
571:
572:    x->op = x->base + caplen;
573:    x->rt = x->base + (rd32(x->base, XHCI_RTSOFF) & ~0x1Fu);
574:    x->db = (volatile uint32_t *)(x->base + (rd32(x->base, XHCI_DBOFF) & ~0x3u));
575:
576:    pr_info("xHCI: %s base=0x%lx slots=%d ports=%d ctxsz=%d\n",
577:            dev->name, base, x->max_slots, x->max_ports, x->ctxsz);
578:
579:    if (xhci_reset_and_start(x) < 0) {
580:        pr_warn("%s", "xHCI: controller init failed\n");
581:        return -1;
582:    }
583:
584:    x->hcd.name = "xHCI";
585:    x->hcd.ops = &xhci_ops;
586:    x->hcd.priv = x;
587:    xhci_count++;
588:
589:    usb_register_hcd(&x->hcd);
590:    return 0;
591:}
592:
593:static struct device_driver xhci_driver = {
594:    .name = "xhci",
595:    .vendor = DRV_ANY_ID,
596:    .device = DRV_ANY_ID,
597:    .class_code = 0x0C,  /* Serial bus controller */
598:    .subclass = 0x03,    /* USB */
599:    .prog_if = 0x30,     /* xHCI */
600:    .probe = xhci_probe,
601:};
602:
603:void xhci_register(void) {
604:    driver_register(&xhci_driver);
605:}
606:

@@@ kernel/drivers/virtio/virtio_blk.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/drivers/virtio/virtio_blk.c
3: * VirtIO Block Device Driver
4: */
5:#include <drivers/virtio.h>
6:#include <drivers/virtio_blk.h>
7:#include <kernel/arch.h>
8:#include <kernel/block.h>
9:#include <kernel/irq.h>
10:#include <kernel/pmm.h>
11:#include <kernel/printk.h>
12:#include <kernel/spinlock.h>
13:#include <kernel/string.h>
14:#include <kernel/vmm.h>
15:
16:static virtio_handle_t virtio_blk_dev = NULL;
17:static uint32_t virtio_blk_qsize = 0;
18:
19:/* Vring structures */
20:static struct vring_desc *desc;
21:static struct vring_avail *avail;
22:static struct vring_used *used;
23:
24:/* virtio_blk_lock serialises the whole request lifecycle (descriptor setup,
25: * publish, poll, status read).  The driver keeps ONE set of ring descriptors
26: * (desc[0..2]) and one request header: before this lock existed, two CPUs
27: * issuing I/O concurrently (doom loading WAD lumps while another process hit
28: * the FS) clobbered each other's descriptors mid-flight — the device then
29: * read a torn request header and returned VIRTIO_BLK_S_IOERR ("VirtIO: Read
30: * failed status=1" / "W_ReadLump: only read 0 of N" in the boot traces).
31: * irqsave also keeps a timer-tick preemption from interleaving a second
32: * request from the SAME CPU into a half-built ring. */
33:static DEFINE_SPINLOCK(virtio_blk_lock);
34:
35:/* DMA targets for the request header and status byte (DRV-VIRTIO-03): these
36: * used to live on the caller's STACK while the device DMA-wrote into them.
37: * Static copies are safe now that virtio_blk_lock guarantees one request in
38: * flight at a time. */
39:static struct virtio_blk_req blk_req;
40:static volatile uint8_t blk_status;
41:
42:/*
43: * Initialize VirtIO Block Device
44: */
45:void virtio_blk_init(void) {
46:  pr_info("%s", "VirtIO: Probing for block device...\n");
47:
48:  virtio_handle_t dev = NULL;
49:  uint32_t irq = 0;
50:
51:  if (arch_virtio_get_device(VIRTIO_DEV_BLOCK, 0, &dev, &irq) == 0) {
52:    pr_info("VirtIO: Found Block Device (IRQ %u)\n", irq);
53:    virtio_blk_dev = dev;
54:  } else {
55:    pr_info("%s", "VirtIO: No block device found\n");
56:    return;
57:  }
58:
59:  /* === Common initialization (Legacy) === */
60:  uint32_t version = virtio_read_reg(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_VERSION);
61:  pr_info("VirtIO: Version %d\n", version);
62:
63:  /* Reset device */
64:  virtio_write_reg(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_STATUS, 0);
65:
66:  /* Acknowledge + Driver */
67:  uint32_t status = VIRTIO_STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGE | VIRTIO_STATUS_DRIVER;
68:  virtio_write_reg(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_STATUS, status);
69:
70:  /* Feature negotiation */
71:  uint32_t features = virtio_read_reg(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_DEVICE_FEATURES);
72:  virtio_write_reg(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_DRIVER_FEATURES, features);
73:
74:  if (version >= 2) {
75:    status |= VIRTIO_STATUS_FEATURES_OK;
76:    virtio_write_reg(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_STATUS, status);
77:  }
78:
79:  /* Queue 0 setup */
80:  virtio_write_reg(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_SEL, 0);
81:  uint32_t qmax = virtio_read_reg(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_NUM_MAX);
82:  uint32_t qsize = (qmax > 16) ? 16 : qmax;
83:  virtio_blk_qsize = qsize;
84:  if (virtio_blk_qsize == 0) {
85:    pr_err("%s", "VirtIO-Blk: Invalid queue size (0)!\n");
86:    return;
87:  }
88:  virtio_write_reg(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_NUM, qsize);
89:
90:  void *qmem = pmm_alloc_pages_dma(2);
91:  if (!qmem) {
92:    pr_err("%s", "VirtIO: Failed to allocate queue memory\n");
93:    return;
94:  }
95:  memset(qmem, 0, 8192);
96:
97:  desc = (struct vring_desc *)qmem;
98:  avail = (struct vring_avail *)((uint8_t *)qmem + qsize * 16);
99:  used = (struct vring_used *)((uint8_t *)qmem + 4096);
100:
101:  /* Unified HAL API handles Legacy/Modern address registration.
102:   * The device needs PHYSICAL ring addresses (virt_to_phys). */
103:  virtio_setup_queue(dev, 0, virt_to_phys(desc), virt_to_phys(avail),
104:                     virt_to_phys(used));
105:
106:  /* Driver OK */
107:  status |= VIRTIO_STATUS_DRIVER_OK;
108:  virtio_write_reg(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_STATUS, status);
109:
110:  pr_info("%s", "VirtIO: Block Device Initialized successfully\n");
111:
112:  /* Register as the active block backend (ASTRA block contract).  A boot
113:   * module, if present, overrides this later in main.c. */
114:  static const struct block_dev virtio_blk_bdev = {
115:      "virtio-blk", virtio_blk_read, virtio_blk_write};
116:  block_register(&virtio_blk_bdev);
117:}
118:
119:/*
120: * virtio_blk_xfer: issue one synchronous block request (busy-wait).
121: *
122: * @write: 0 = VIRTIO_BLK_T_IN (device writes @buf), 1 = VIRTIO_BLK_T_OUT.
123: *
124: * Caller context: process/boot only (the poll loop with IRQs masked makes it
125: * unsuitable for IRQ context).  Serialised by virtio_blk_lock — see the lock
126: * comment for the SMP corruption this prevents.
127: */
128:static int virtio_blk_xfer(int write, void *buf, uint64_t sector,
129:                           uint32_t count) {
130:  if (!virtio_blk_dev || !desc || !avail || !used)
131:    return -1;
132:
133:  uint64_t flags;
134:  spin_lock_irqsave(&virtio_blk_lock, &flags);
135:
136:  blk_req.type = write ? VIRTIO_BLK_T_OUT : VIRTIO_BLK_T_IN;
137:  blk_req.reserved = 0;
138:  blk_req.sector = sector;
139:  blk_status = 0xFF; /* poisoned: device must overwrite it on completion */
140:
141:  /* Descriptor addresses are PHYSICAL (DMA): virt_to_phys on kernel ptrs. */
142:  /* Header (read-only for the device) */
143:  desc[0].addr = virt_to_phys(&blk_req);
144:  desc[0].len = sizeof(struct virtio_blk_req);
145:  desc[0].flags = VRING_DESC_F_NEXT;
146:  desc[0].next = 1;
147:
148:  /* Data buffer (device writes it on reads, reads it on writes) */
149:  desc[1].addr = virt_to_phys(buf);
150:  desc[1].len = count * 512;
151:  desc[1].flags = (write ? 0 : VRING_DESC_F_WRITE) | VRING_DESC_F_NEXT;
152:  desc[1].next = 2;
153:
154:  /* Status byte (write-only for the device) */
155:  desc[2].addr = virt_to_phys((void *)&blk_status);
156:  desc[2].len = 1;
157:  desc[2].flags = VRING_DESC_F_WRITE;
158:  desc[2].next = 0;
159:
160:  /* Snapshot the used index BEFORE publishing the request (DRV-VIRTIO-04):
161:   * snapshotting after avail->idx++ could miss a completion that lands
162:   * between publish and snapshot, and then poll for one that never comes. */
163:  volatile uint16_t *used_idx_ptr = &used->idx;
164:  uint16_t old_idx = *used_idx_ptr;
165:
166:  /* Publish in the Available Ring */
167:  uint16_t idx = avail->idx % virtio_blk_qsize;
168:  avail->ring[idx] = 0;
169:
170:  hal_mb();
171:  avail->idx++;
172:  hal_mb();
173:
174:  /* Notify */
175:  virtio_notify(virtio_blk_dev, 0);
176:
177:  /* Poll Used Ring (busy wait) */
178:  uint64_t timeout = 1000000000;
179:  while (*used_idx_ptr == old_idx && timeout > 0) {
180:    hal_cpu_yield();
181:    timeout--;
182:  }
183:
184:  /* Clear interrupt status (Legacy VirtIO requirement) */
185:  virtio_read_reg(virtio_blk_dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_INTERRUPT_ACK);
186:
187:  if (timeout == 0) {
188:    uint32_t isr = virtio_read_reg(virtio_blk_dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_INTERRUPT_ACK);
189:    pr_err("VirtIO-Blk: Timeout waiting for device response! (used->idx=%d "
190:           "old_idx=%d, ISR=%02x)\n",
191:           *used_idx_ptr, old_idx, isr);
192:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&virtio_blk_lock, flags);
193:    return -1;
194:  }
195:
196:  /* Order the status read after the used-ring update we just observed. */
197:  hal_mb();
198:  uint8_t status = blk_status;
199:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&virtio_blk_lock, flags);
200:
201:  if (status != VIRTIO_BLK_S_OK) {
202:    pr_info("VirtIO: %s failed status=%d\n", write ? "Write" : "Read", status);
203:    return -1;
204:  }
205:
206:  return 0;
207:}
208:
209:/*
210: * virtio_blk_read: Read sectors from disk
211: * Synchronous implementation (busy-wait), serialised by virtio_blk_lock.
212: */
213:int virtio_blk_read(void *buf, uint64_t sector, uint32_t count) {
214:  return virtio_blk_xfer(0, buf, sector, count);
215:}
216:
217:int virtio_blk_write(void *buf, uint64_t sector, uint32_t count) {
218:  return virtio_blk_xfer(1, buf, sector, count);
219:}
220:

@@@ kernel/drivers/virtio/virtio_input.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/drivers/virtio/virtio_input.c
3: * VirtIO Input Device Driver (Keyboard/Mouse)
4: * Full Virtqueue and Interrupt Implementation
5: */
6:#include <drivers/virtio.h>
7:#include <drivers/virtio_input.h>
8:#include <drivers/keyboard.h>
9:#include <kernel/arch.h>
10:#include <kernel/graphics.h>
11:#include <kernel/irq.h>
12:#include <kernel/pmm.h>
13:#include <kernel/printk.h>
14:#include <kernel/string.h>
15:#include <kernel/types.h>
16:#include <kernel/vmm.h>
17:
18:#ifdef ARCH_AMD64
19:#include <drivers/pci.h>
20:#endif
21:
22:extern void compositor_update_mouse(int dx, int dy, int absolute);
23:
24:#define MAX_INPUT_DEVS 2
25:#define INPUT_QSIZE 16
26:
27:void virtio_input_add_event(uint16_t type, uint16_t code, int32_t value);
28:
29:struct virtio_input_dev {
30:  virtio_handle_t handle;
31:  uint32_t irq;
32:  int active;
33:  int is_pci;
34:  struct vring_desc *desc;
35:  struct vring_avail *avail;
36:  struct vring_used *used;
37:  uint16_t last_used_idx;
38:  struct virtio_input_event *events;
39:};
40:
41:static struct virtio_input_dev input_devs[MAX_INPUT_DEVS];
42:static int input_dev_count = 0;
43:
44:/* Global Input Buffer (Shared by all devices) */
45:#define INPUT_BUFFER_SIZE 256
46:static struct virtio_input_event input_buffer[INPUT_BUFFER_SIZE];
47:static volatile uint32_t input_head = 0;
48:static volatile uint32_t input_tail = 0;
49:
50:/* Forward declarations */
51:static void virtio_input_handler(uint32_t irq, void *data);
52:
53:/* Helper macros / functions for transport abstraction */
54:#define v_read32(dev, off) virtio_read_reg((dev)->handle, (off))
55:#define v_write32(dev, off, val) virtio_write_reg((dev)->handle, (off), (val))
56:#define v_notify(dev, q) virtio_notify((dev)->handle, (q))
57:
58:void virtio_input_add_event(uint16_t type, uint16_t code, int32_t value) {
59:  uint32_t next = (input_head + 1) % INPUT_BUFFER_SIZE;
60:  if (next == input_tail) {
61:    input_tail = (input_tail + 1) % INPUT_BUFFER_SIZE;
62:  }
63:  input_buffer[input_head].type = type;
64:  input_buffer[input_head].code = code;
65:  input_buffer[input_head].value = value;
66:  input_head = next;
67:}
68:
69:static void init_device(virtio_handle_t handle, uint32_t irq, int is_pci) {
70:  (void)is_pci;
71:  if (input_dev_count >= MAX_INPUT_DEVS)
72:    return;
73:
74:  struct virtio_input_dev *dev = &input_devs[input_dev_count++];
75:  dev->handle = handle;
76:  dev->irq = irq;
77:  dev->active = 0;
78:
79:  /* Reset */
80:  v_write32(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_STATUS, 0);
81:  v_write32(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_STATUS,
82:            VIRTIO_STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGE | VIRTIO_STATUS_DRIVER);
83:
84:  /* Features */
85:  v_write32(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_DRIVER_FEATURES, 0);
86:  v_write32(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_STATUS,
87:            v_read32(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_STATUS) | VIRTIO_STATUS_FEATURES_OK);
88:
89:  /* Setup Queue 0 (eventq) */
90:  v_write32(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_SEL, 0);
91:  v_write32(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_QUEUE_NUM, INPUT_QSIZE);
92:
93:  void *qmem = pmm_alloc_pages_dma(2);
94:  if (!qmem) {
95:    /* DRV-VIRTIO-07: bail out gracefully instead of NULL-dereferencing. */
96:    pr_err("%s", "VirtIO-Input: failed to allocate virtqueue memory\n");
97:    input_dev_count--;
98:    return;
99:  }
100:  memset(qmem, 0, 8192);
101:  dev->desc = (struct vring_desc *)qmem;
102:  dev->avail = (struct vring_avail *)((uint8_t *)qmem + INPUT_QSIZE * 16);
103:  dev->used = (struct vring_used *)((uint8_t *)qmem + 4096);
104:
105:  /* Use unified HAL API; the device needs PHYSICAL ring addresses. */
106:  virtio_setup_queue(handle, 0, virt_to_phys(dev->desc),
107:                     virt_to_phys(dev->avail), virt_to_phys(dev->used));
108:
109:  dev->events = (struct virtio_input_event *)pmm_alloc_page_dma();
110:  if (!dev->events) {
111:    /* DRV-VIRTIO-07: free the virtqueue memory and bail out gracefully. */
112:    pr_err("%s", "VirtIO-Input: failed to allocate events buffer\n");
113:    pmm_free_pages(qmem, 2);
114:    input_dev_count--;
115:    return;
116:  }
117:  memset(dev->events, 0, sizeof(struct virtio_input_event) * INPUT_QSIZE);
118:
119:  for (int i = 0; i < INPUT_QSIZE; i++) {
120:    /* Descriptor addresses are PHYSICAL (DMA). */
121:    dev->desc[i].addr = virt_to_phys(&dev->events[i]);
122:    dev->desc[i].len = sizeof(struct virtio_input_event);
123:    dev->desc[i].flags = VRING_DESC_F_WRITE;
124:    dev->avail->ring[i] = i;
125:  }
126:  dev->avail->idx = INPUT_QSIZE;
127:  dev->last_used_idx = 0;
128:
129:  /* Driver OK */
130:  v_write32(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_STATUS,
131:            v_read32(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_STATUS) | VIRTIO_STATUS_DRIVER_OK);
132:
133:  /* Register and Enable Interrupt */
134:  /* A device whose IRQ line is not wired delivers nothing: no keystrokes, no
135:   * mouse.  Dropping this made that look like a dead device rather than a
136:   * failed registration. */
137:  if (irq_register(irq, virtio_input_handler, dev) != 0)
138:    pr_err("virtio-input: cannot register IRQ %u — this device will deliver no "
139:           "events\n", irq);
140:
141:  /* Notify device */
142:  v_notify(dev, 0);
143:
144:  dev->active = 1;
145:}
146:
147:static void virtio_input_handler(uint32_t irq, void *data) {
148:  (void)data; /* Parametro ignorato a favore del polling vettoriale */
149:
150:  for (int i = 0; i < input_dev_count; i++) {
151:    struct virtio_input_dev *dev = &input_devs[i];
152:
153:    /* Filtra i dispositivi disattivi o non pertinenti all'IRQ sollevato */
154:    if (!dev->active || dev->irq != irq) {
155:      continue;
156:    }
157:
158:    uint32_t status = v_read32(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_INTERRUPT_STATUS);
159:    uint16_t processed_count = 0;
160:
161:    while (dev->last_used_idx != dev->used->idx) {
162:      struct vring_used_elem *e =
163:          &dev->used->ring[dev->last_used_idx % INPUT_QSIZE];
164:      uint32_t id = e->id;
165:      struct virtio_input_event *evt = &dev->events[id];
166:
167:      /* Single dispatch point: keys -> keyboard/IPC, pointer -> compositor,
168:       * EV_SYN -> repaint. Same path PS/2 and USB HID use now. */
169:      input_report(evt->type, evt->code, evt->value);
170:
171:      dev->avail->ring[dev->avail->idx % INPUT_QSIZE] = id;
172:      arch_mb();
173:      dev->avail->idx++;
174:      dev->last_used_idx++;
175:      processed_count++;
176:    }
177:
178:    if (status != 0) {
179:      v_write32(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_INTERRUPT_ACK, status);
180:    } else if (processed_count == 0) {
181:      v_read32(dev, VIRTIO_MMIO_INTERRUPT_ACK);
182:    }
183:
184:    if (processed_count > 0) {
185:      v_notify(dev, 0);
186:    }
187:  }
188:}
189:
190:void virtio_input_init(void) {
191:  pr_info("%s", "VirtIO-Input: Probing devices...\n");
192:  input_dev_count = 0; // reset
193:
194:  int count = arch_virtio_get_count(VIRTIO_DEV_INPUT);
195:  for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
196:    virtio_handle_t dev = NULL;
197:    uint32_t irq = 0;
198:    if (arch_virtio_get_device(VIRTIO_DEV_INPUT, i, &dev, &irq) == 0) {
199:      init_device(dev, irq, 0);
200:    }
201:  }
202:
203:  if (input_dev_count > 0) {
204:    pr_info("VirtIO-Input: %d input device(s) initialized\n", input_dev_count);
205:  }
206:}
207:int virtio_input_get_dev_count(void) { return input_dev_count; }
208:
209:int virtio_input_poll(struct virtio_input_event *event) {
210:  if (input_head == input_tail)
211:    return 0;
212:  *event = input_buffer[input_tail];
213:  input_tail = (input_tail + 1) % INPUT_BUFFER_SIZE;
214:  return 1;
215:}
216:
217:int virtio_input_has_event(void) { return input_head != input_tail; }
218:

@@@ kernel/fs/ext4.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/fs/ext4.c
3: * Simplified Ext4 Driver — VFS provider (read + limited write)
4: *
5: * Role in the stack (ASTRA, docs/ASTRA.md):
6: *   This driver is a filesystem PROVIDER behind the <kernel/vfs.h> contract.
7: *   The only kernel-facing symbol is ext4_fs_ops; nothing outside kernel/fs/
8: *   calls ext4_* anymore (VFS-01 resolved).  Per-mount state lives in a
9: *   kmalloc'd struct ext4_fs hung off vfs_mount.fs_private (EXT4-12: multiple
10: *   mounts are now structurally possible, though vfs_init mounts one root).
11: *
12: * On-disk layout accessed (4096-byte blocks, 8 sectors each):
13: *   partition LBA 0        (LBA part+0)  : partition boot record (unused)
14: *   superblock offset 1024 (LBA part+2)  : struct ext4_superblock
15: *   GDT block 1            (LBA part+8)  : struct ext4_group_desc[0] at byte 0
16: *   Block bitmap           (LBA part + bg_block_bitmap_lo × 8) : 4096-byte map
17: *   Inode table            (LBA part + bg_inode_table_lo × 8)  : inode array
18: *   Data blocks            (LBA part + phys_block × 8) : 4096-byte data
19: *
20: * Sector arithmetic common pattern:
21: *   block N → sector = part_start_lba + (N × 8)   [8 = 4096 / 512]
22: *   inode K → byte offset in table = (K-1) × inode_size (from superblock)
23: *
24: * Block mapping (EXT4-01 resolved):
25: *   ext4_bmap() dispatches on i_flags & EXT4_EXTENTS_FL:
26: *     - extent inodes: walk the extent tree rooted in i_block[] (any depth;
27: *       unwritten extents and gaps read as zeros);
28: *     - legacy inodes: direct (0-11), single-indirect (12), double-indirect
29: *       (13) pointer blocks, as before.
30: *
31: * Mount-time enforcement (EXT4-06 resolved):
32: *   - quiet probe failure when s_magic doesn't match (the VFS probes every
33: *     partition; not-ext4 is normal);
34: *   - LOUD rejection of: block size ≠ 4096, unsupported INCOMPAT features
35: *     (64bit, dirty journal, anything unknown), multi-group images
36: *     (EXT4-12/13 made explicit instead of silently misreading);
37: *   - unknown RO_COMPAT features (e.g. metadata_csum, gdt_csum) force a
38: *     read-only mount: our writer maintains no checksums, so writing would
39: *     corrupt the image's self-consistency;
40: *   - a GDT that points its block bitmap / inode bitmap / inode table
41: *     outside the partition is refused outright (EXT4-STRUCT-01): there is
42: *     no bitmap to self-heal against in that case (see
43: *     ext4_repair_structural_sanity below);
44: *   - once the GDT itself checks out, the block bitmap and inode bitmap are
45: *     SELF-HEALED rather than rejected: any of the fixed metadata blocks
46: *     (superblock/GDT/bitmaps/inode table) or reserved inodes (1..10, root
47: *     = 2) found marked FREE are corrected in place and persisted
48: *     (EXT4-STRUCT-01) — this is what lets a save corrupted by an unclean
49: *     shutdown mount cleanly again instead of needing a reformat;
50: *   - the free-block/free-inode COUNTERS are separately reconciled against
51: *     the (now-repaired) bitmaps (ext4_verify_free_count, Fase 1) so a
52: *     stale counter can't later trip ext4_alloc_block's own consistency
53: *     check.
54: *
55: * Key invariants:
56: *   - fs->lock serialises block allocation (alloc block bitmap r-m-w, GDT
57: *     update, superblock update) and inode write-back (ext4_update_inode).
58: *   - fs->sb/fs->bg/fs->part_start_lba are immutable after mount except for
59: *     the allocation counters mutated under fs->lock.
60: *   - The buffer cache (kernel/mm/buffer.c) is NOT used; all block I/O goes
61: *     directly through virtio_blk_{read,write} (EXT4-15).
62: *
63: * Known issues (still open):
64: *   EXT4-05  (W3 MISSING, partially lifted) Write supports: overwrite of any
65: *            mapped block; growth on depth-0 extent roots with a free slot;
66: *            growth through the legacy single-indirect range (~4.2 MB).
67: *            Still rejected loudly: extent-tree growth (depth>0, full root,
68: *            mid-hole insert), double-indirect allocation, file creation.
69: *   EXT4-09  (W2 MISSING) ext4_list returns -2 without syscall-layer errno
70: *            translation.
71: *   EXT4-15  (W1 MISSING) Buffer cache bypassed; all I/O direct to virtio.
72: *            (EXT4-11 resolved: per-loop interior-block cache, see
73: *            struct ext4_icache.)
74: *   EXT4-STRUCT-02 (still open) Structural self-heal (below) recovers the
75: *            FIXED metadata region and the RESERVED inode range only. It
76: *            cannot detect or repair corruption inside a file's own data
77: *            blocks or extent/indirect metadata (no checksums exist in this
78: *            format to tell "wrong content" from "right content") — that
79: *            would need per-block checksums or the Merkle root mkdisk.c
80: *            already computes at image-build time (§4bis) to be threaded
81: *            through to a runtime verifier, which does not exist yet.
82: *   EXT4-GROW-01 (explicitly out of scope) This driver and tools/mkdisk.c
83: *            are both single-block-group by design (one 4 KiB block bitmap
84: *            = 32768 blocks = 128 MiB ceiling, see MKDISK-BITMAP-01 in
85: *            mkdisk.c). Runtime partition resize and multi-group support
86: *            are a different, much larger change (new on-disk layout, GDT
87: *            with N descriptors, cross-group allocation) and are not
88: *            attempted here.
89: */
90:#include <kernel/block.h>
91:#include <kernel/buffer.h>
92:#include <kernel/ext4.h>
93:#include <kernel/gpt.h>
94:#include <kernel/kmalloc.h>
95:#include <kernel/printk.h>
96:#include <kernel/spinlock.h>
97:#include <kernel/string.h>
98:#include <kernel/vfs.h>
99:
100:/* Per-mount driver state (vfs_mount.fs_private). */
101:struct ext4_fs {
102:  uint64_t part_start_lba; /* absolute LBA of the partition's first sector */
103:  uint32_t inode_size;     /* on-disk inode record size (sb.s_inode_size) */
104:  int read_only;           /* set at mount for unknown RO_COMPAT features */
105:  uint32_t n_groups;       /* number of block groups (MKDISK-MULTIGROUP-01) */
106:  uint32_t blocks_per_group; /* s_blocks_per_group from superblock */
107:  struct ext4_superblock sb;
108:  struct ext4_group_desc *bgs; /* [n_groups] kmalloc'd array; NULL until mount */
109:  spinlock_t lock;
110:};
111:
112:/* Mirrors tools/mkdisk.c INODE_TABLE_BLOCKS — the fixed metadata region this
113: * driver's own writer lays out, and what ext4_repair_structural_sanity below
114: * uses to know which blocks must always read as "used" in a sane image. */
115:#define EXT4_INODE_TABLE_BLOCKS 64
116:
117:/* Forward declaration: ext4_sync_bg_sb is DEFINED later in this file
118: * (alongside the create/remove helpers, NOTE(M4.5-FS-WRITE)) but is needed
119: * earlier by ext4_verify_free_count and ext4_repair_structural_sanity
120: * (mount-time recovery, Fase 1 / Fase 1b) and by ext4_alloc_inode/
121: * ext4_free_block/ext4_free_inode.  Without this prototype the compiler
122: * synthesises an implicit int-returning declaration at first use, which then
123: * conflicts with the real "static void(struct ext4_fs *)" definition and
124: * fails the build under -Werror. */
125:static void ext4_sync_bg_sb(struct ext4_fs *fs);
126:
127:/*
128: * Helper: Read/Write Sectors (absolute LBA; thin virtio wrappers).
129: * NOTE(EXT4-15): bypasses the buffer cache (kernel/mm/buffer.c).
130: */
131:static int ext4_bread(uint64_t sector, uint32_t count, void *buf) {
132:  return block_read(buf, sector, count);
133:}
134:
135:static int ext4_bwrite(uint64_t sector, uint32_t count, void *buf) {
136:  return block_write(buf, sector, count);
137:}
138:
139:/*
140: * ext4_alloc_block - allocate one free block from any block group.
141: *
142: * Multi-group (MKDISK-MULTIGROUP-01): scans groups in order, picks the first
143: * group with bg_free_blocks_count_lo > 0, scans its bitmap, sets the bit,
144: * writes the bitmap back, decrements the per-group and superblock counters,
145: * syncs the GDT, and returns the ABSOLUTE block number (group * blocks_per_group
146: * + bit_in_group). Returns 0 on full-partition failure.
147: */
148:static uint32_t ext4_alloc_block(struct ext4_fs *fs) {
149:  for (uint32_t g = 0; g < fs->n_groups; g++) {
150:    if (fs->bgs[g].bg_free_blocks_count_lo == 0)
151:      continue;
152:
153:    uint64_t bitmap_blk = fs->bgs[g].bg_block_bitmap_lo;
154:    uint8_t *bitmap = kmalloc(4096);
155:    if (!bitmap)
156:      return 0;
157:
158:    uint64_t lock_flags;
159:    spin_lock_irqsave(&fs->lock, &lock_flags);
160:
161:    if (ext4_bread(fs->part_start_lba + (bitmap_blk * 8), 8, bitmap) != 0) {
162:      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&fs->lock, lock_flags);
163:      kfree(bitmap);
164:      continue; /* I/O error on this group; try next */
165:    }
166:
167:    /* Scan 32768 bits, LSB-first within each byte. */
168:    uint32_t bit_in_group = 0;
169:    int found = 0;
170:    for (int i = 0; i < 4096 && !found; i++) {
171:      if (bitmap[i] == 0xFF)
172:        continue;
173:      for (int bit = 0; bit < 8; bit++) {
174:        if (!((bitmap[i] >> bit) & 1)) {
175:          bitmap[i] |= (uint8_t)(1 << bit);
176:          bit_in_group = (uint32_t)(i * 8 + bit);
177:          found = 1;
178:          break;
179:        }
180:      }
181:    }
182:
183:    if (!found) {
184:      /* Descriptor said free > 0 but bitmap is full: mismatch.
185:       * ext4_verify_free_count corrects at mount; if it still happens at
186:       * runtime, log it and skip this group rather than returning 0. */
187:      pr_err("Ext4: group %u bitmap/free_count mismatch at alloc\n", g);
188:      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&fs->lock, lock_flags);
189:      kfree(bitmap);
190:      continue;
191:    }
192:
193:    if (ext4_bwrite(fs->part_start_lba + (bitmap_blk * 8), 8, bitmap) != 0) {
194:      pr_err("Ext4: group %u block bitmap write failed\n", g);
195:      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&fs->lock, lock_flags);
196:      kfree(bitmap);
197:      return 0;
198:    }
199:    kfree(bitmap);
200:
201:    fs->bgs[g].bg_free_blocks_count_lo--;
202:    fs->sb.s_free_blocks_count_lo--;
203:
204:    ext4_sync_bg_sb(fs); /* write GDT + superblock */
205:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&fs->lock, lock_flags);
206:
207:    uint32_t abs_block = g * fs->blocks_per_group + bit_in_group;
208:
209:    /* Zero the new block outside the lock (ownership established). */
210:    uint8_t *zero_buf = kmalloc(4096);
211:    if (zero_buf) {
212:      memset(zero_buf, 0, 4096);
213:      ext4_bwrite(fs->part_start_lba + ((uint64_t)abs_block * 8), 8, zero_buf);
214:      kfree(zero_buf);
215:    }
216:
217:    return abs_block;
218:  }
219:
220:  pr_err("%s", "Ext4: No free blocks in any group!\n");
221:  return 0;
222:}
223:
224:/*
225: * ext4_verify_free_count - per-group mount-time inline fsck.
226: * Corrects bg_free_blocks_count_lo if it disagrees with the bitmap.
227: * Must run AFTER ext4_repair_structural_sanity (see that function's comment).
228: * Runs for every group.
229: */
230:static void ext4_verify_free_count(struct ext4_fs *fs) {
231:  for (uint32_t g = 0; g < fs->n_groups; g++) {
232:    uint64_t bitmap_blk = fs->bgs[g].bg_block_bitmap_lo;
233:    uint8_t *bitmap = kmalloc(4096);
234:    if (!bitmap)
235:      continue;
236:    if (ext4_bread(fs->part_start_lba + (bitmap_blk * 8), 8, bitmap) != 0) {
237:      kfree(bitmap);
238:      continue;
239:    }
240:
241:    uint32_t free_in_bitmap = 0;
242:    for (int i = 0; i < 4096; i++) {
243:      uint8_t b = (uint8_t)~bitmap[i];
244:      while (b) {
245:        free_in_bitmap++;
246:        b &= (uint8_t)(b - 1);
247:      }
248:    }
249:    kfree(bitmap);
250:
251:    if (free_in_bitmap != (uint32_t)fs->bgs[g].bg_free_blocks_count_lo) {
252:      pr_warn("Ext4: group %u free_count mismatch: descriptor=%u bitmap=%u; "
253:              "correcting (unclean shutdown?)\n",
254:              g, (unsigned)fs->bgs[g].bg_free_blocks_count_lo, free_in_bitmap);
255:      fs->bgs[g].bg_free_blocks_count_lo = (uint16_t)free_in_bitmap;
256:      ext4_sync_bg_sb(fs);
257:    }
258:  }
259:}
260:
261:/*
262: * ext4_repair_structural_sanity - per-group mount-time self-heal.
263: * For group 0: repair block bitmap (metadata region) + inode bitmap (reserved).
264: * For groups 1+: repair only the per-group metadata blocks (bitmap + inode_bitmap
265: * + dummy inode_table = first GN_META_BLOCKS blocks of the group).
266: */
267:#define GN_META_BLOCKS 3  /* groups 1+: block-bmap + inode-bmap + dummy itable */
268:static int ext4_repair_structural_sanity(struct ext4_fs *fs) {
269:  uint32_t total_blocks = fs->sb.s_blocks_count_lo;
270:
271:  for (uint32_t g = 0; g < fs->n_groups; g++) {
272:    struct ext4_group_desc *bg = &fs->bgs[g];
273:
274:    if (bg->bg_block_bitmap_lo == 0 ||
275:        bg->bg_block_bitmap_lo >= total_blocks ||
276:        bg->bg_inode_bitmap_lo == 0 ||
277:        bg->bg_inode_bitmap_lo >= total_blocks ||
278:        bg->bg_inode_table_lo == 0) {
279:      pr_err("Ext4: group %u GDT pointers out of range "
280:             "(bitmap=%u inode_bitmap=%u inode_table=%u) -- skipping repair\n",
281:             g, bg->bg_block_bitmap_lo, bg->bg_inode_bitmap_lo,
282:             bg->bg_inode_table_lo);
283:      if (g == 0)
284:        return -1; /* group 0 is unrecoverable without correct pointers */
285:      continue;
286:    }
287:
288:    /* Determine which blocks must be marked used in this group's bitmap. */
289:    uint64_t bitmap_blk = bg->bg_block_bitmap_lo;
290:    uint8_t *bitmap = kmalloc(4096);
291:    if (!bitmap)
292:      return -1;
293:    if (ext4_bread(fs->part_start_lba + (bitmap_blk * 8), 8, bitmap) != 0) {
294:      kfree(bitmap);
295:      if (g == 0) return -1;
296:      continue;
297:    }
298:
299:    uint32_t meta_end;
300:    if (g == 0) {
301:      /* Group 0: superblock(0), GDT(1), block-bmap(2), inode-bmap(3),
302:       * inode-table(4..67) = BLK_DATA_START blocks of overhead. */
303:      meta_end = bg->bg_inode_table_lo + EXT4_INODE_TABLE_BLOCKS;
304:    } else {
305:      /* Groups 1+: block-bmap(0), inode-bmap(1), dummy-itable(2) = 3 blocks,
306:       * all at the START of this group.  We repair bits 0..GN_META_BLOCKS-1
307:       * within the group's own bitmap. */
308:      meta_end = GN_META_BLOCKS; /* bits within this group's bitmap */
309:    }
310:
311:    uint32_t repaired = 0;
312:    for (uint32_t b = 0; b < meta_end; b++) {
313:      uint32_t byte = b / 8, bit = b % 8;
314:      if (byte >= 4096) break;
315:      if (!((bitmap[byte] >> bit) & 1)) {
316:        bitmap[byte] |= (uint8_t)(1 << bit);
317:        repaired++;
318:      }
319:    }
320:
321:    if (repaired > 0) {
322:      pr_warn("Ext4: group %u: repaired %u metadata block(s) wrongly free\n",
323:              g, repaired);
324:      if (ext4_bwrite(fs->part_start_lba + (bitmap_blk * 8), 8, bitmap) != 0) {
325:        pr_err("Ext4: group %u: failed to write back repaired block bitmap\n", g);
326:        kfree(bitmap);
327:        if (g == 0) return -1;
328:        continue;
329:      }
330:      if (bg->bg_free_blocks_count_lo >= repaired)
331:        bg->bg_free_blocks_count_lo -= (uint16_t)repaired;
332:      else
333:        bg->bg_free_blocks_count_lo = 0;
334:      if (fs->sb.s_free_blocks_count_lo >= repaired)
335:        fs->sb.s_free_blocks_count_lo -= repaired;
336:      else
337:        fs->sb.s_free_blocks_count_lo = 0;
338:    }
339:    kfree(bitmap);
340:
341:    /* Group 0 inode bitmap: reserved inodes 1..10 (root = 2). */
342:    if (g == 0) {
343:      uint64_t ibitmap_blk = bg->bg_inode_bitmap_lo;
344:      uint8_t *ibitmap = kmalloc(4096);
345:      if (!ibitmap) return -1;
346:      if (ext4_bread(fs->part_start_lba + (ibitmap_blk * 8), 8, ibitmap) != 0) {
347:        kfree(ibitmap); return -1;
348:      }
349:      uint32_t repaired_ino = 0;
350:      for (uint32_t ino = 1; ino <= 10; ino++) {
351:        uint32_t bit = ino - 1, byte = bit / 8, b = bit % 8;
352:        if (!((ibitmap[byte] >> b) & 1)) {
353:          ibitmap[byte] |= (uint8_t)(1 << b);
354:          repaired_ino++;
355:        }
356:      }
357:      if (repaired_ino > 0) {
358:        pr_warn("Ext4: repaired %u reserved inode(s) wrongly free\n", repaired_ino);
359:        ext4_bwrite(fs->part_start_lba + (ibitmap_blk * 8), 8, ibitmap);
360:        if (bg->bg_free_inodes_count_lo >= repaired_ino)
361:          bg->bg_free_inodes_count_lo -= (uint16_t)repaired_ino;
362:        else
363:          bg->bg_free_inodes_count_lo = 0;
364:        if (fs->sb.s_free_inodes_count >= repaired_ino)
365:          fs->sb.s_free_inodes_count -= repaired_ino;
366:        else
367:          fs->sb.s_free_inodes_count = 0;
368:      }
369:      kfree(ibitmap);
370:    }
371:  }
372:
373:  ext4_sync_bg_sb(fs);
374:  return 0;
375:}
376:
377:/*
378: * get_inode_struct - read inode 'ino' from the group-0 inode table.
379: * Multi-group: all inodes are in group 0 (bgs[0].bg_inode_table_lo).
380: */
381:static int get_inode_struct(struct ext4_fs *fs, uint32_t ino,
382:                            struct ext4_inode *inode_out) {
383:  uint64_t table_blk = fs->bgs[0].bg_inode_table_lo;
384:  uint64_t table_byte_offset = table_blk * 4096;
385:  uint64_t inode_offset =
386:      table_byte_offset + (uint64_t)(ino - 1) * fs->inode_size;
387:
388:  uint64_t sector = fs->part_start_lba + (inode_offset / 512);
389:  uint32_t sector_off = inode_offset % 512;
390:
391:  uint8_t *k_buf = kmalloc(512);
392:  if (!k_buf)
393:    return -1;
394:  if (block_read(k_buf, sector, 1) != 0) {
395:    kfree(k_buf);
396:    return -1;
397:  }
398:
399:  memcpy(inode_out, k_buf + sector_off, sizeof(struct ext4_inode));
400:  kfree(k_buf);
401:  return 0;
402:}
403:
404:/*
405: * ext4_update_inode - read-modify-write inode 'ino' back to the group-0 table.
406: */
407:static int ext4_update_inode(struct ext4_fs *fs, uint32_t ino,
408:                             struct ext4_inode *inode) {
409:  uint64_t table_blk = fs->bgs[0].bg_inode_table_lo;
410:  uint64_t table_byte_offset = table_blk * 4096;
411:  uint64_t inode_offset =
412:      table_byte_offset + (uint64_t)(ino - 1) * fs->inode_size;
413:
414:  uint64_t sector = fs->part_start_lba + (inode_offset / 512);
415:  uint32_t sector_off = inode_offset % 512;
416:
417:  uint8_t *k_buf = kmalloc(512);
418:  if (!k_buf)
419:    return -1;
420:
421:  uint64_t lock_flags;
422:  spin_lock_irqsave(&fs->lock, &lock_flags);
423:  if (block_read(k_buf, sector, 1) != 0) {
424:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&fs->lock, lock_flags);
425:    kfree(k_buf);
426:    return -1;
427:  }
428:
429:  memcpy(k_buf + sector_off, inode, sizeof(struct ext4_inode));
430:  int ret = block_write(k_buf, sector, 1);
431:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&fs->lock, lock_flags);
432:  kfree(k_buf);
433:  return ret;
434:}
435:
436:/*
437: * Interior-block cache (EXT4-11 resolved).
438: *
439: * A read/write loop calls ext4_bmap once per 4 KB chunk; without caching,
440: * every call re-reads the same interior metadata blocks (indirect pointer
441: * blocks, extent index/leaf nodes) from disk.  An ext4_icache lives on the
442: * caller's frame for the duration of one loop and holds the last interior
443: * block seen per tree level (two levels cover double-indirect and
444: * depth-2 extent trees; deeper levels share slot 1).  Sequential access —
445: * the dominant pattern (ELF load, WAD streaming, dir scans) — then reads
446: * each metadata block once instead of once per chunk.
447: *
448: * Writers that modify mapping metadata on disk must icache_invalidate()
449: * so later lookups in the same loop re-read the updated block.
450: */
451:struct ext4_icache {
452:  uint64_t blk[2]; /* cached block number per level; 0 = empty slot */
453:  uint8_t *buf[2]; /* lazily allocated 4 KB buffers */
454:};
455:
456:static void icache_release(struct ext4_icache *c) {
457:  for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
458:    if (c->buf[i])
459:      kfree(c->buf[i]);
460:    c->buf[i] = NULL;
461:    c->blk[i] = 0;
462:  }
463:}
464:
465:static void icache_invalidate(struct ext4_icache *c) {
466:  c->blk[0] = 0;
467:  c->blk[1] = 0;
468:}
469:
470:/* Return the contents of interior block 'blk' via the level slot, reading
471: * from disk only on a cache miss.  NULL on OOM or I/O error. */
472:static uint8_t *icache_get(struct ext4_fs *fs, struct ext4_icache *c, int level,
473:                           uint64_t blk) {
474:  if (level > 1)
475:    level = 1;
476:  if (c->buf[level] && c->blk[level] == blk)
477:    return c->buf[level];
478:  if (!c->buf[level]) {
479:    c->buf[level] = kmalloc(4096);
480:    if (!c->buf[level])
481:      return NULL;
482:  }
483:  if (ext4_bread(fs->part_start_lba + blk * 8, 8, c->buf[level]) != 0) {
484:    c->blk[level] = 0;
485:    return NULL;
486:  }
487:  c->blk[level] = blk;
488:  return c->buf[level];
489:}
490:
491:/*
492: * ext4_extent_lookup - map logical block → physical block via the extent
493: * tree rooted in i_block[] (EXT4_EXTENTS_FL inodes).
494: *
495: * Walks interior nodes (eh_depth > 0: ext4_extent_idx records, sorted by
496: * ei_block; the child covering 'blk' is the last entry with ei_block <= blk)
497: * down to the leaf (ext4_extent records).  Holes — logical blocks covered by
498: * no extent — and unwritten extents (ee_len > EXT4_EXT_UNWRITTEN_LEN) yield
499: * *phys_out = 0, which the read loop turns into zeros, matching sparse-file
500: * semantics of the legacy path.
501: *
502: * Returns 0 on success (*phys_out set; 0 means "reads as zeros"),
503: * -1 on a structurally invalid tree or I/O error.
504: */
505:static int ext4_extent_lookup(struct ext4_fs *fs,
506:                              const struct ext4_inode *inode, uint32_t blk,
507:                              uint64_t *phys_out, struct ext4_icache *cache) {
508:  const struct ext4_extent_header *eh =
509:      (const struct ext4_extent_header *)inode->i_block;
510:  /* Max records per node: 4 in the 60-byte i_block root, 340 in a 4 KB
511:   * block ((4096-12)/12).  Used to bound eh_entries before scanning. */
512:  uint16_t max_entries = 4;
513:  *phys_out = 0;
514:
515:  /* eh_depth is bounded by 5 in the format; the guard catches cycles. */
516:  for (int level = 0; level < 6; level++) {
517:    if (eh->eh_magic != EXT4_EXT_MAGIC || eh->eh_entries > eh->eh_max ||
518:        eh->eh_entries > max_entries) {
519:      pr_err("Ext4: invalid extent node (magic=0x%x entries=%d max=%d)\n",
520:             eh->eh_magic, eh->eh_entries, eh->eh_max);
521:      return -1;
522:    }
523:
524:    if (eh->eh_depth > 0) {
525:      /* Interior node: descend into the last child with ei_block <= blk. */
526:      const struct ext4_extent_idx *ix =
527:          (const struct ext4_extent_idx *)(eh + 1);
528:      int sel = -1;
529:      for (int i = 0; i < eh->eh_entries; i++) {
530:        if (ix[i].ei_block <= blk)
531:          sel = i;
532:        else
533:          break;
534:      }
535:      if (sel < 0)
536:        return 0; /* blk precedes the first mapped range: hole. */
537:      uint64_t child =
538:          ix[sel].ei_leaf_lo | ((uint64_t)ix[sel].ei_leaf_hi << 32);
539:      const uint8_t *node = icache_get(fs, cache, level, child);
540:      if (!node)
541:        return -1;
542:      eh = (const struct ext4_extent_header *)node;
543:      max_entries = (4096 - sizeof(*eh)) / sizeof(struct ext4_extent);
544:      continue;
545:    }
546:
547:    /* Leaf node: find the extent covering blk. */
548:    const struct ext4_extent *ex = (const struct ext4_extent *)(eh + 1);
549:    for (int i = 0; i < eh->eh_entries; i++) {
550:      uint32_t start = ex[i].ee_block;
551:      int unwritten = ex[i].ee_len > EXT4_EXT_UNWRITTEN_LEN;
552:      uint32_t len =
553:          unwritten ? ex[i].ee_len - EXT4_EXT_UNWRITTEN_LEN : ex[i].ee_len;
554:      if (blk >= start && blk < start + len) {
555:        if (!unwritten)
556:          *phys_out =
557:              (ex[i].ee_start_lo | ((uint64_t)ex[i].ee_start_hi << 32)) +
558:              (blk - start);
559:        break; /* unwritten: leave *phys_out = 0 → reads as zeros */
560:      }
561:    }
562:    return 0; /* no covering extent: hole → zeros */
563:  }
564:
565:  pr_err("%s", "Ext4: extent tree deeper than 5 levels (corrupt?)\n");
566:  return -1;
567:}
568:
569:/*
570: * ext4_bmap - map logical file block → physical block.
571: * Dispatches on EXT4_EXTENTS_FL (EXT4-01); the legacy path supports direct
572: * (0-11), single-indirect (12) and double-indirect (13) pointers.
573: * *phys_out == 0 means "hole: reads as zeros".  Returns 0 / -1.
574: * Interior metadata blocks go through the caller's icache (EXT4-11).
575: */
576:static int ext4_bmap(struct ext4_fs *fs, const struct ext4_inode *inode,
577:                     uint32_t block_idx, uint64_t *phys_out,
578:                     struct ext4_icache *cache) {
579:  if (inode->i_flags & EXT4_EXTENTS_FL)
580:    return ext4_extent_lookup(fs, inode, block_idx, phys_out, cache);
581:
582:  *phys_out = 0;
583:  if (block_idx < 12) {
584:    *phys_out = inode->i_block[block_idx];
585:    return 0;
586:  }
587:
588:  if (block_idx < 12 + 1024) {
589:    uint32_t indirect_blk_num = inode->i_block[12];
590:    if (indirect_blk_num == 0)
591:      return 0; /* unallocated pointer block: hole */
592:    const uint8_t *ind = icache_get(fs, cache, 0, indirect_blk_num);
593:    if (!ind)
594:      return -1;
595:    *phys_out = ((const uint32_t *)ind)[block_idx - 12];
596:    return 0;
597:  }
598:
599:  uint32_t d_idx = block_idx - 12 - 1024;
600:  uint32_t master_idx = d_idx / 1024;
601:  uint32_t sub_idx = d_idx % 1024;
602:  uint32_t double_indir_blk = inode->i_block[13];
603:
604:  if (double_indir_blk == 0 || master_idx >= 1024)
605:    return double_indir_blk == 0 ? 0 : -1;
606:  const uint8_t *master = icache_get(fs, cache, 0, double_indir_blk);
607:  if (!master)
608:    return -1;
609:  uint32_t sub_indir_blk = ((const uint32_t *)master)[master_idx];
610:  if (sub_indir_blk == 0)
611:    return 0; /* hole */
612:  const uint8_t *sub = icache_get(fs, cache, 1, sub_indir_blk);
613:  if (!sub)
614:    return -1;
615:  *phys_out = ((const uint32_t *)sub)[sub_idx];
616:  return 0;
617:}
618:
619:/*
620: * ext4_read_data - random-access read from an already-fetched inode.
621: * 64-bit offset/file-size arithmetic (EXT4-08 resolved).
622: * Returns bytes read (clamped at EOF) or -1.
623: */
624:static int ext4_read_data(struct ext4_fs *fs, const struct ext4_inode *inode,
625:                          uint64_t offset, uint8_t *buf, uint32_t size) {
626:  uint64_t file_size = inode->i_size_lo | ((uint64_t)inode->i_size_high << 32);
627:  if (size == 0 || buf == NULL)
628:    return 0;
629:  if (offset >= file_size)
630:    return 0;
631:  if (offset + size > file_size)
632:    size = (uint32_t)(file_size - offset);
633:
634:  uint32_t bytes_read = 0;
635:  uint64_t current_offset = offset;
636:  struct ext4_icache cache = {{0, 0}, {NULL, NULL}};
637:
638:  uint8_t *block_buf = kmalloc(4096);
639:  if (!block_buf)
640:    return -1;
641:
642:  while (bytes_read < size) {
643:    uint32_t block_idx = (uint32_t)(current_offset / 4096);
644:    uint32_t block_off = current_offset % 4096;
645:    uint32_t to_copy = 4096 - block_off;
646:    if (to_copy > (size - bytes_read))
647:      to_copy = size - bytes_read;
648:
649:    uint64_t phys_block;
650:    if (ext4_bmap(fs, inode, block_idx, &phys_block, &cache) != 0) {
651:      kfree(block_buf);
652:      icache_release(&cache);
653:      return -1;
654:    }
655:
656:    if (phys_block == 0) {
657:      /* Sparse hole / unwritten extent. */
658:      memset(block_buf, 0, 4096);
659:    } else {
660:      uint64_t sector = fs->part_start_lba + (phys_block * 8);
661:      if (block_read(block_buf, sector, 8) != 0) {
662:        kfree(block_buf);
663:        icache_release(&cache);
664:        return -1;
665:      }
666:    }
667:
668:    memcpy(buf + bytes_read, block_buf + block_off, to_copy);
669:    bytes_read += to_copy;
670:    current_offset += to_copy;
671:  }
672:
673:  kfree(block_buf);
674:  icache_release(&cache);
675:  return bytes_read;
676:}
677:
678:/*
679: * read_inode_data - convenience: fetch inode 'ino' then read its data.
680: */
681:static int read_inode_data(struct ext4_fs *fs, uint32_t ino, uint64_t offset,
682:                           uint8_t *buf, uint32_t size) {
683:  struct ext4_inode inode;
684:  if (get_inode_struct(fs, ino, &inode) != 0) {
685:    pr_err("Ext4: Failed to get inode struct for ino %d\n", ino);
686:    return -1;
687:  }
688:  return ext4_read_data(fs, &inode, offset, buf, size);
689:}
690:
691:/*
692: * ext4_lookup_in_dir - find 'name' in directory inode dir_ino.
693: */
694:static int ext4_lookup_in_dir(struct ext4_fs *fs, uint32_t dir_ino,
695:                              const char *name, uint32_t name_len,
696:                              uint32_t *ino_out) {
697:  struct ext4_inode inode;
698:  if (get_inode_struct(fs, dir_ino, &inode) != 0)
699:    return -1;
700:
701:  uint32_t dir_size = inode.i_size_lo;
702:  uint32_t current_blk_off = 0;
703:  uint8_t *dir_buf = kmalloc(4096);
704:  if (!dir_buf)
705:    return -1;
706:
707:  while (current_blk_off < dir_size) {
708:    if (ext4_read_data(fs, &inode, current_blk_off, dir_buf, 4096) <= 0)
709:      break;
710:
711:    struct ext4_dir_entry *de = (struct ext4_dir_entry *)dir_buf;
712:    uint32_t offset = 0;
713:    while (offset < 4096) {
714:      if (de->rec_len < 8 || de->rec_len > (4096 - offset))
715:        break;
716:
717:      /* inode==0 is a FREED slot (ext4_dir_remove), not end-of-block: skip
718:       * it by rec_len like ext4_dir_insert does.  Breaking here made every
719:       * entry after a deleted one unresolvable (the "unlink one file, lose
720:       * the rest of the folder" bug). */
721:      if (de->inode != 0 && de->name_len > 0 && de->name_len == name_len) {
722:        if (memcmp(de->name, name, name_len) == 0) {
723:          *ino_out = de->inode;
724:          kfree(dir_buf);
725:          return 0;
726:        }
727:      }
728:      offset += de->rec_len;
729:      de = (struct ext4_dir_entry *)((uint8_t *)de + de->rec_len);
730:    }
731:    current_blk_off += 4096;
732:  }
733:  kfree(dir_buf);
734:  return -1;
735:}
736:
737:/*
738: * ext4_find_ino - resolve an absolute path to an inode number (walk from
739: * the root inode, component by component).
740: */
741:static int ext4_find_ino(struct ext4_fs *fs, const char *path,
742:                         uint32_t *ino_out) {
743:  uint32_t current_ino = EXT4_ROOT_INO;
744:  const char *p = path;
745:
746:  if (*p == '/')
747:    p++;
748:
749:  while (*p) {
750:    const char *start = p;
751:    while (*p && *p != '/')
752:      p++;
753:    uint32_t len = p - start;
754:
755:    if (len > 0) {
756:      uint32_t next_ino;
757:      if (ext4_lookup_in_dir(fs, current_ino, start, len, &next_ino) != 0)
758:        return -1;
759:      current_ino = next_ino;
760:    }
761:
762:    if (*p == '/')
763:      p++;
764:  }
765:
766:  *ino_out = current_ino;
767:  return 0;
768:}
769:
770:/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
771:/* VFS provider entry points (the fs_ops contract)                    */
772:/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
773:
774:/*
775: * ext4_mount - probe + mount the partition (fs_ops.mount).
776: * Quiet on "not ext4" (the VFS probes every partition); loud on recognised-
777: * but-unsupported images. Self-heals recoverable bitmap/counter corruption.
778: * See the file header for the full enforcement/repair matrix.
779: */
780:static int ext4_mount(struct vfs_mount *mnt, struct partition *p) {
781:  uint8_t *k_buf = kmalloc(4096);
782:  if (!k_buf)
783:    return -1;
784:
785:  /* Superblock lives at byte offset 1024 = sector 2 of the partition. */
786:  if (block_read(k_buf, p->start_lba + 2, 2) != 0) {
787:    kfree(k_buf);
788:    return -1;
789:  }
790:
791:  struct ext4_fs *fs = kmalloc(sizeof(struct ext4_fs));
792:  if (!fs) {
793:    kfree(k_buf);
794:    return -1;
795:  }
796:  memset(fs, 0, sizeof(*fs));
797:  memcpy(&fs->sb, k_buf, sizeof(fs->sb));
798:
799:  if (fs->sb.s_magic != EXT4_MAGIC) {
800:    /* Not an ext4 partition: quiet probe failure. */
801:    kfree(k_buf);
802:    kfree(fs);
803:    return -1;
804:  }
805:
806:  /* From here on the partition IS ext4: unsupported features fail loudly. */
807:  int reject = 0;
808:
809:  if (fs->sb.s_log_block_size != 2) {
810:    pr_err("Ext4: unsupported block size (log=%d, only 4096 supported)\n",
811:           fs->sb.s_log_block_size);
812:    reject = 1;
813:  }
814:
815:  uint32_t bad_incompat = fs->sb.s_feature_incompat & ~EXT4_INCOMPAT_SUPPORTED;
816:  if (!reject && bad_incompat) {
817:    pr_err("Ext4: unsupported INCOMPAT features 0x%x (supported mask 0x%x) - "
818:           "refusing to mount\n",
819:           bad_incompat, EXT4_INCOMPAT_SUPPORTED);
820:    reject = 1;
821:  }
822:
823:  /* Inode record size: rev0 fixes it at 128; rev1+ reads s_inode_size.
824:   * Must be a multiple of 128 ≥ sizeof(struct ext4_inode) so table records
825:   * never straddle a 512-byte sector read (see get_inode_struct). */
826:  fs->inode_size = (fs->sb.s_rev_level == 0) ? 128 : fs->sb.s_inode_size;
827:  if (!reject && (fs->inode_size < 128 || fs->inode_size > 4096 ||
828:                  (fs->inode_size % 128) != 0)) {
829:    pr_err("Ext4: invalid inode size %d\n", fs->inode_size);
830:    reject = 1;
831:  }
832:
833:  if (reject) {
834:    kfree(k_buf);
835:    kfree(fs);
836:    return -1;
837:  }
838:
839:  uint32_t bad_rocompat =
840:      fs->sb.s_feature_ro_compat & ~EXT4_RO_COMPAT_WRITE_SAFE;
841:  if (bad_rocompat) {
842:    pr_warn("Ext4: RO_COMPAT features 0x%x not write-safe - mounting "
843:            "read-only\n",
844:            bad_rocompat);
845:    fs->read_only = 1;
846:  }
847:
848:  kfree(k_buf);
849:
850:  fs->part_start_lba = p->start_lba;
851:  spin_lock_init(&fs->lock);
852:  mnt->fs_private = fs;
853:  /* --- Multi-group setup (MKDISK-MULTIGROUP-01) ---
854:   * s_blocks_per_group tells us how many groups the image has.
855:   * Allocate and populate the bgs[] array from the on-disk GDT (block 1). */
856:  uint32_t bpg = fs->sb.s_blocks_per_group;
857:  if (bpg == 0) bpg = 8 * 4096; /* legacy single-group images had bpg==total_blocks */
858:  fs->blocks_per_group = bpg;
859:
860:  uint32_t total_blks = fs->sb.s_blocks_count_lo;
861:  uint32_t n_grps = (total_blks + bpg - 1) / bpg;
862:  if (n_grps == 0) n_grps = 1;
863:  if (n_grps > 128) n_grps = 128; /* cap at MAX_GROUPS */
864:  fs->n_groups = n_grps;
865:
866:  fs->bgs = kmalloc(n_grps * sizeof(struct ext4_group_desc));
867:  if (!fs->bgs) {
868:    pr_err("%s", "Ext4: OOM allocating group descriptors\n");
869:    mnt->fs_private = NULL;
870:    kfree(fs);
871:    return -1;
872:  }
873:
874:  /* Read the GDT block (block 1 = sectors 8..15). */
875:  uint8_t *gdt_buf = kmalloc(4096);
876:  if (!gdt_buf) {
877:    kfree(fs->bgs);
878:    mnt->fs_private = NULL;
879:    kfree(fs);
880:    return -1;
881:  }
882:  if (ext4_bread(fs->part_start_lba + 8, 8, gdt_buf) != 0) {
883:    pr_err("%s", "Ext4: failed to read GDT\n");
884:    kfree(gdt_buf);
885:    kfree(fs->bgs);
886:    mnt->fs_private = NULL;
887:    kfree(fs);
888:    return -1;
889:  }
890:  memcpy(fs->bgs, gdt_buf, n_grps * sizeof(struct ext4_group_desc));
891:  kfree(gdt_buf);
892:
893:  pr_info("Ext4: %u block group(s), %u blocks/group\n", n_grps, bpg);
894:
895:  /* Mount-time self-heal (order: structural repair THEN free-count correction). */
896:  if (ext4_repair_structural_sanity(fs) != 0) {
897:    pr_err("%s", "Ext4: structural corruption could not be repaired, "
898:                 "refusing to mount\n");
899:    kfree(fs->bgs);
900:    mnt->fs_private = NULL;
901:    kfree(fs);
902:    return -1;
903:  }
904:  ext4_verify_free_count(fs);
905:
906:  pr_info("Ext4: Mounted. Vol=%s, Inodes=%d, features incompat=0x%x%s\n",
907:          fs->sb.s_volume_name, fs->sb.s_inodes_count,
908:          fs->sb.s_feature_incompat, fs->read_only ? " (read-only)" : "");
909:  return 0;
910:}
911:
912:/*
913: * ext4_open - path → vfs_node (fs_ops.open).
914: */
915:static int ext4_open(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path,
916:                     struct vfs_node *out) {
917:  struct ext4_fs *fs = mnt->fs_private;
918:  uint32_t ino;
919:  struct ext4_inode inode;
920:
921:  if (ext4_find_ino(fs, path, &ino) != 0)
922:    return -1;
923:  if (get_inode_struct(fs, ino, &inode) != 0)
924:    return -1;
925:
926:  out->mnt = mnt;
927:  out->id = ino;
928:  out->size = inode.i_size_lo | ((uint64_t)inode.i_size_high << 32);
929:  out->type = ((inode.i_mode >> 12) == 4) ? VFS_TYPE_DIR : VFS_TYPE_FILE;
930:  return 0;
931:}
932:
933:/*
934: * ext4_read - random-access read from an open node (fs_ops.read).
935: */
936:static int ext4_read(struct vfs_node *node, uint64_t offset, void *buf,
937:                     uint32_t size) {
938:  struct ext4_fs *fs = node->mnt->fs_private;
939:  return read_inode_data(fs, (uint32_t)node->id, offset, buf, size);
940:}
941:
942:/*
943: * ext4_extent_can_append - can a new block mapping for 'logical' be added
944: * to the inode's extent tree?  Conservative: only depth-0 roots with a free
945: * record slot and logical positions at/after the current end are accepted
946: * (mid-hole inserts would need record shifting; a full root would need tree
947: * growth — both still EXT4-05 territory).
948: */
949:static int ext4_extent_can_append(const struct ext4_inode *inode,
950:                                  uint32_t logical) {
951:  const struct ext4_extent_header *eh =
952:      (const struct ext4_extent_header *)inode->i_block;
953:  const struct ext4_extent *ex = (const struct ext4_extent *)(eh + 1);
954:
955:  if (eh->eh_magic != EXT4_EXT_MAGIC || eh->eh_depth != 0)
956:    return 0;
957:  if (eh->eh_entries > 0) {
958:    const struct ext4_extent *last = &ex[eh->eh_entries - 1];
959:    uint32_t len = last->ee_len > EXT4_EXT_UNWRITTEN_LEN
960:                       ? last->ee_len - EXT4_EXT_UNWRITTEN_LEN
961:                       : last->ee_len;
962:    if (logical < last->ee_block + len)
963:      return 0; /* would be a mid-hole insert */
964:  }
965:  return eh->eh_entries < eh->eh_max;
966:}
967:
968:/*
969: * ext4_extent_do_append - record the mapping logical→phys in a depth-0 root
970: * previously validated by ext4_extent_can_append.  Extends the last extent
971: * when physically contiguous, else appends a new record (sorted order is
972: * preserved because logical >= last end).
973: */
974:static void ext4_extent_do_append(struct ext4_inode *inode, uint32_t logical,
975:                                  uint32_t phys) {
976:  struct ext4_extent_header *eh = (struct ext4_extent_header *)inode->i_block;
977:  struct ext4_extent *ex = (struct ext4_extent *)(eh + 1);
978:
979:  if (eh->eh_entries > 0) {
980:    struct ext4_extent *last = &ex[eh->eh_entries - 1];
981:    if (last->ee_len < EXT4_EXT_UNWRITTEN_LEN - 1 &&
982:        logical == last->ee_block + last->ee_len &&
983:        phys == last->ee_start_lo + last->ee_len && last->ee_start_hi == 0) {
984:      last->ee_len++;
985:      return;
986:    }
987:  }
988:  ex[eh->eh_entries].ee_block = logical;
989:  ex[eh->eh_entries].ee_len = 1;
990:  ex[eh->eh_entries].ee_start_hi = 0;
991:  ex[eh->eh_entries].ee_start_lo = phys;
992:  eh->eh_entries++;
993:}
994:
995:/*
996: * ext4_write - path-based write (fs_ops.write; overwrite/append).
997: *
998: * Supported (EXT4-05 partially lifted):
999: *   - overwrite of any already-mapped block (extent trees of any depth,
1000: *     legacy direct/indirect/double-indirect) — no metadata change;
1001: *   - growth on extent inodes with a depth-0 root and a free record slot
1002: *     (extend-if-contiguous, else new extent; sparse tail writes OK);
1003: *   - growth on legacy inodes through the single-indirect range
1004: *     (12+1024 blocks ≈ 4.2 MB), allocating the pointer block on demand.
1005: * Still rejected loudly: read-only mounts, extent-tree growth (depth>0 /
1006: * full root / mid-hole insert), double-indirect allocation, file creation.
1007: */
1008:static int ext4_write(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path,
1009:                      uint64_t offset64, const void *vbuf, uint32_t size) {
1010:  struct ext4_fs *fs = mnt->fs_private;
1011:  const uint8_t *buf = vbuf;
1012:
1013:  if (fs->read_only) {
1014:    pr_err("%s", "Ext4: write rejected (read-only mount)\n");
1015:    return -1;
1016:  }
1017:
1018:  uint32_t ino;
1019:  if (ext4_find_ino(fs, path, &ino) != 0) {
1020:    /* A missing file is a NORMAL negative result of a userland open(), not a
1021:     * kernel error — log at debug so a process probing paths (or the stress
1022:     * file lane) cannot spam the console (perf §1; Linux likewise never
1023:     * printk's on ENOENT). */
1024:    pr_debug("Ext4: File not found: %s\n", path);
1025:    return -1;
1026:  }
1027:
1028:  struct ext4_inode inode;
1029:  if (get_inode_struct(fs, ino, &inode) != 0)
1030:    return -1;
1031:
1032:  int is_extent = (inode.i_flags & EXT4_EXTENTS_FL) != 0;
1033:
1034:  /* 32-bit write path; bound offset before narrowing. */
1035:  if (offset64 > 0xFFFFFFFFULL ||
1036:      offset64 > (uint64_t)inode.i_size_lo + 1048576) {
1037:    pr_err("EXT4: Write offset 0x%lx exceeds reasonable bounds "
1038:           "(i_size_lo=0x%x)\n",
1039:           (unsigned long)offset64, inode.i_size_lo);
1040:    return -1;
1041:  }
1042:  uint32_t offset = (uint32_t)offset64;
1043:
1044:  uint32_t bytes_written = 0;
1045:  uint32_t current_offset = offset;
1046:  struct ext4_icache cache = {{0, 0}, {NULL, NULL}};
1047:
1048:  uint8_t *block_buf = kmalloc(4096);
1049:  if (!block_buf)
1050:    return -1;
1051:
1052:  while (bytes_written < size) {
1053:    uint32_t block_idx = current_offset / 4096;
1054:    uint32_t block_off = current_offset % 4096;
1055:    uint32_t to_copy = 4096 - block_off;
1056:    if (to_copy > (size - bytes_written))
1057:      to_copy = size - bytes_written;
1058:
1059:    uint64_t phys_block;
1060:    if (ext4_bmap(fs, &inode, block_idx, &phys_block, &cache) != 0)
1061:      goto fail;
1062:
1063:    if (phys_block == 0) {
1064:      /* Unmapped block: validate the mapping is recordable BEFORE
1065:       * allocating, so a reject never leaks a bitmap bit. */
1066:      if (is_extent && !ext4_extent_can_append(&inode, block_idx)) {
1067:        pr_err("%s", "Ext4: extent-tree growth (depth>0, full root or "
1068:                     "mid-hole insert) not supported yet\n");
1069:        goto fail;
1070:      }
1071:      if (!is_extent && block_idx >= 12 + 1024) {
1072:        pr_err("%s", "Ext4: double-indirect block write not supported yet\n");
1073:        goto fail;
1074:      }
1075:
1076:      uint32_t nb = ext4_alloc_block(fs);
1077:      if (nb == 0) {
1078:        pr_err("%s", "Ext4: Block allocation failed\n");
1079:        goto fail;
1080:      }
1081:
1082:      if (is_extent) {
1083:        ext4_extent_do_append(&inode, block_idx, nb);
1084:      } else if (block_idx < 12) {
1085:        inode.i_block[block_idx] = nb;
1086:      } else {
1087:        /* Single-indirect: allocate the pointer block on demand (it comes
1088:         * back zeroed from ext4_alloc_block = all slots NULL), then install
1089:         * the new pointer with a sector-granular read-modify-write. */
1090:        uint32_t ind = inode.i_block[12];
1091:        if (ind == 0) {
1092:          ind = ext4_alloc_block(fs);
1093:          if (ind == 0) {
1094:            pr_err("%s", "Ext4: Block allocation failed\n");
1095:            goto fail;
1096:          }
1097:          inode.i_block[12] = ind;
1098:          inode.i_blocks_lo += (4096 / 512);
1099:        }
1100:        uint64_t slot_off = (uint64_t)ind * 4096 + (block_idx - 12) * 4;
1101:        uint64_t slot_sector = fs->part_start_lba + slot_off / 512;
1102:        uint8_t *secbuf = kmalloc(512);
1103:        if (!secbuf)
1104:          goto fail;
1105:        if (ext4_bread(slot_sector, 1, secbuf) != 0) {
1106:          kfree(secbuf);
1107:          goto fail;
1108:        }
1109:        *(uint32_t *)(secbuf + (slot_off % 512)) = nb;
1110:        if (ext4_bwrite(slot_sector, 1, secbuf) != 0) {
1111:          kfree(secbuf);
1112:          goto fail;
1113:        }
1114:        kfree(secbuf);
1115:        /* The pointer block changed on disk: drop cached copies. */
1116:        icache_invalidate(&cache);
1117:      }
1118:
1119:      /* i_blocks_lo counts 512-byte sectors. */
1120:      inode.i_blocks_lo += (4096 / 512);
1121:      phys_block = nb;
1122:    }
1123:
1124:    /* Read-modify-write for partial blocks. */
1125:    if (block_off != 0 || to_copy != 4096) {
1126:      if (ext4_bread(fs->part_start_lba + (phys_block * 8), 8, block_buf) != 0)
1127:        goto fail;
1128:    }
1129:
1130:    memcpy(block_buf + block_off, buf + bytes_written, to_copy);
1131:
1132:    if (ext4_bwrite(fs->part_start_lba + (phys_block * 8), 8, block_buf) != 0)
1133:      goto fail;
1134:
