1135:    bytes_written += to_copy;
1136:    current_offset += to_copy;
1137:  }
1138:
1139:  kfree(block_buf);
1140:  icache_release(&cache);
1141:
1142:  /* New file size.  A write that STARTS at offset 0 replaces the file from the
1143:   * beginning (a whole-file write: an editor save, a cp, a config rewrite), so
1144:   * the file must END exactly where this write ends — a SHORTER rewrite then
1145:   * truncates the stale tail instead of leaving old bytes past the new content
1146:   * (the "shortening a file in the editor leaves trailing characters" bug: the
1147:   * old code was extend-only, so i_size never shrank).  A write at a NON-zero
1148:   * offset is positional (append / in-place overlay) and keeps extend-only
1149:   * semantics, so it never shrinks a file it is only patching.
1150:   *
1151:   * Blocks past the new EOF are not freed here (there is no truncate primitive
1152:   * yet): they are stale-but-unreachable (reads stop at i_size, a later write
1153:   * reuses them), so this is correct on read, with only a transient space cost.
1154:   */
1155:  if (offset == 0)
1156:    inode.i_size_lo = current_offset;
1157:  else if (current_offset > inode.i_size_lo)
1158:    inode.i_size_lo = current_offset;
1159:
1160:  if (ext4_update_inode(fs, ino, &inode) != 0) {
1161:    pr_err("%s", "Ext4: Failed to update inode\n");
1162:    return -1;
1163:  }
1164:
1165:  return bytes_written;
1166:
1167:fail:
1168:  kfree(block_buf);
1169:  icache_release(&cache);
1170:  return -1;
1171:}
1172:
1173:/*
1174: * ext4_list - directory listing as a space-separated string (fs_ops.list).
1175: * Returns the formatted length, -1 not found, -2 not a directory (EXT4-09).
1176: */
1177:static int ext4_list(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path, char *buf,
1178:                     uint32_t size) {
1179:  struct ext4_fs *fs = mnt->fs_private;
1180:  uint32_t dir_ino;
1181:  if (ext4_find_ino(fs, path, &dir_ino) != 0)
1182:    return -1;
1183:
1184:  struct ext4_inode inode;
1185:  if (get_inode_struct(fs, dir_ino, &inode) != 0)
1186:    return -1;
1187:
1188:  if (!((inode.i_mode >> 12) == 4))
1189:    return -2;
1190:
1191:  uint32_t dir_size = inode.i_size_lo;
1192:  uint32_t current_blk_off = 0;
1193:  uint8_t *dir_buf = kmalloc(4096);
1194:  if (!dir_buf)
1195:    return -1;
1196:
1197:  uint32_t buf_pos = 0;
1198:  if (size > 0)
1199:    buf[0] = '\0';
1200:
1201:  while (current_blk_off < dir_size) {
1202:    if (ext4_read_data(fs, &inode, current_blk_off, dir_buf, 4096) <= 0)
1203:      break;
1204:
1205:    struct ext4_dir_entry *de = (struct ext4_dir_entry *)dir_buf;
1206:    uint32_t offset = 0;
1207:    while (offset < 4096) {
1208:      /* Two-sided rec_len guard, same as the lookup path: a corrupt rec_len
1209:       * larger than the block remainder stops the walk (defence in depth;
1210:       * the offset re-check below already prevented the OOB dereference). */
1211:      if (de->rec_len < 8 || de->rec_len > (4096 - offset))
1212:        break;
1213:
1214:      /* inode==0 is a FREED slot (ext4_dir_remove), not end-of-block: skip
1215:       * it by rec_len like ext4_dir_insert does.  Breaking here hid every
1216:       * entry after a deleted one from the listing (the "unlink one file,
1217:       * lose the rest of the folder" bug). */
1218:      if (de->inode != 0 && de->name_len > 0) {
1219:        if (buf_pos + de->name_len + 1 < size) {
1220:          memcpy(buf + buf_pos, de->name, de->name_len);
1221:          buf_pos += de->name_len;
1222:          buf[buf_pos++] = ' ';
1223:          buf[buf_pos] = '\0';
1224:        }
1225:      }
1226:
1227:      offset += de->rec_len;
1228:      if (offset >= 4096)
1229:        break;
1230:      de = (struct ext4_dir_entry *)((uint8_t *)de + de->rec_len);
1231:    }
1232:    current_blk_off += 4096;
1233:  }
1234:
1235:  kfree(dir_buf);
1236:  return (int)buf_pos;
1237:}
1238:
1239:/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
1240:/* File/dir creation and removal (issue #126, NOTE(M4.5-FS-WRITE))    */
1241:/*                                                                      */
1242:/* Everything below mirrors the read/write/allocate patterns already   */
1243:/* established above (ext4_alloc_block, ext4_lookup_in_dir, ext4_bmap, */
1244:/* ext4_extent_lookup) instead of inventing new on-disk-format logic.  */
1245:/* Scope: regular files only (VFS_TYPE_DIR creation / rmdir are out of */
1246:/* scope for this pass - creating "." / ".." bootstrap adds directory- */
1247:/* specific complexity nothing here needs yet).                        */
1248:/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
1249:
1250:/*
1251: * ext4_sync_bg_sb - write back all in-memory group descriptors + superblock.
1252: * Multi-group: the full GDT (n_groups * 32 bytes) fits in one 4 KiB block
1253: * (MAX_GROUPS=128 × 32B = 4096B).  We rewrite the whole block to avoid
1254: * RMW on partial sectors.
1255: */
1256:static void ext4_sync_bg_sb(struct ext4_fs *fs) {
1257:  /* GDT block is block 1 = sectors 8..15 (block * 8 sectors). */
1258:  uint8_t *gdt_buf = kmalloc(4096);
1259:  if (gdt_buf) {
1260:    if (ext4_bread(fs->part_start_lba + 8, 8, gdt_buf) == 0) {
1261:      memcpy(gdt_buf, fs->bgs, fs->n_groups * sizeof(struct ext4_group_desc));
1262:      ext4_bwrite(fs->part_start_lba + 8, 8, gdt_buf);
1263:    }
1264:    kfree(gdt_buf);
1265:  }
1266:
1267:  uint8_t *sb_buf = kmalloc(4096);
1268:  if (sb_buf && ext4_bread(fs->part_start_lba + 2, 2, sb_buf) == 0) {
1269:    memcpy(sb_buf, &fs->sb, sizeof(fs->sb));
1270:    ext4_bwrite(fs->part_start_lba + 2, 2, sb_buf);
1271:  }
1272:  if (sb_buf)
1273:    kfree(sb_buf);
1274:}
1275:
1276:/*
1277: * ext4_alloc_inode - allocate one free inode from group 0's inode bitmap.
1278: * Multi-group: all inodes live in group 0 (groups 1+ have free_inodes=0).
1279: */
1280:static uint32_t ext4_alloc_inode(struct ext4_fs *fs) {
1281:  if (fs->bgs[0].bg_free_inodes_count_lo == 0) {
1282:    pr_err("%s", "Ext4: No free inodes in Group 0!\n");
1283:    return 0;
1284:  }
1285:
1286:  uint64_t bitmap_blk = fs->bgs[0].bg_inode_bitmap_lo;
1287:  uint8_t *bitmap = kmalloc(4096);
1288:  if (!bitmap)
1289:    return 0;
1290:
1291:  uint64_t lock_flags;
1292:  spin_lock_irqsave(&fs->lock, &lock_flags);
1293:
1294:  if (ext4_bread(fs->part_start_lba + (bitmap_blk * 8), 8, bitmap) != 0) {
1295:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&fs->lock, lock_flags);
1296:    kfree(bitmap);
1297:    return 0;
1298:  }
1299:
1300:  uint32_t max_bits = fs->sb.s_inodes_count;
1301:  if (max_bits > 32768)
1302:    max_bits = 32768;
1303:
1304:  uint32_t inode_bit = 0;
1305:  int found = 0;
1306:  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 4096 && !found; i++) {
1307:    if (bitmap[i] == 0xFF)
1308:      continue;
1309:    for (int bit = 0; bit < 8; bit++) {
1310:      uint32_t idx = i * 8 + (uint32_t)bit;
1311:      if (idx >= max_bits)
1312:        break;
1313:      if (!((bitmap[i] >> bit) & 1)) {
1314:        bitmap[i] |= (uint8_t)(1 << bit);
1315:        inode_bit = idx;
1316:        found = 1;
1317:        break;
1318:      }
1319:    }
1320:  }
1321:
1322:  if (!found) {
1323:    pr_err("%s", "Ext4: Inode bitmap check failed (inconsistent with "
1324:                 "free_count)\n");
1325:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&fs->lock, lock_flags);
1326:    kfree(bitmap);
1327:    return 0;
1328:  }
1329:
1330:  if (ext4_bwrite(fs->part_start_lba + (bitmap_blk * 8), 8, bitmap) != 0) {
1331:    pr_err("%s", "Ext4: Failed to update Inode Bitmap\n");
1332:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&fs->lock, lock_flags);
1333:    kfree(bitmap);
1334:    return 0;
1335:  }
1336:  kfree(bitmap);
1337:
1338:  fs->bgs[0].bg_free_inodes_count_lo--;
1339:  fs->sb.s_free_inodes_count--;
1340:  ext4_sync_bg_sb(fs);
1341:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&fs->lock, lock_flags);
1342:
1343:  return inode_bit + 1;
1344:}
1345:
1346:/*
1347: * ext4_free_block - release one block back to its group's bitmap.
1348: * Multi-group: group = block_num / blocks_per_group.
1349: */
1350:static void ext4_free_block(struct ext4_fs *fs, uint32_t abs_block) {
1351:  if (abs_block == 0)
1352:    return;
1353:  uint32_t g   = abs_block / fs->blocks_per_group;
1354:  uint32_t off = abs_block % fs->blocks_per_group;
1355:  if (g >= fs->n_groups)
1356:    return;
1357:  uint32_t byte = off / 8, bit = off % 8;
1358:  if (byte >= 4096)
1359:    return;
1360:
1361:  uint64_t bitmap_blk = fs->bgs[g].bg_block_bitmap_lo;
1362:  uint8_t *bitmap = kmalloc(4096);
1363:  if (!bitmap)
1364:    return;
1365:
1366:  uint64_t lock_flags;
1367:  spin_lock_irqsave(&fs->lock, &lock_flags);
1368:  if (ext4_bread(fs->part_start_lba + (bitmap_blk * 8), 8, bitmap) != 0) {
1369:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&fs->lock, lock_flags);
1370:    kfree(bitmap);
1371:    return;
1372:  }
1373:  if (!((bitmap[byte] >> bit) & 1)) {
1374:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&fs->lock, lock_flags); /* already free */
1375:    kfree(bitmap);
1376:    return;
1377:  }
1378:  bitmap[byte] &= (uint8_t)~(1 << bit);
1379:  if (ext4_bwrite(fs->part_start_lba + (bitmap_blk * 8), 8, bitmap) != 0) {
1380:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&fs->lock, lock_flags);
1381:    kfree(bitmap);
1382:    return;
1383:  }
1384:  kfree(bitmap);
1385:
1386:  fs->bgs[g].bg_free_blocks_count_lo++;
1387:  fs->sb.s_free_blocks_count_lo++;
1388:  ext4_sync_bg_sb(fs);
1389:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&fs->lock, lock_flags);
1390:}
1391:
1392:/* ext4_free_inode - release one inode bit (opposite of ext4_alloc_inode).
1393: * Multi-group: all inodes are in group 0. */
1394:static void ext4_free_inode(struct ext4_fs *fs, uint32_t ino) {
1395:  uint32_t bit  = ino - 1;
1396:  uint32_t byte = bit / 8, b = bit % 8;
1397:  if (byte >= 4096)
1398:    return;
1399:
1400:  uint64_t bitmap_blk = fs->bgs[0].bg_inode_bitmap_lo;
1401:  uint8_t *bitmap = kmalloc(4096);
1402:  if (!bitmap)
1403:    return;
1404:
1405:  uint64_t lock_flags;
1406:  spin_lock_irqsave(&fs->lock, &lock_flags);
1407:  if (ext4_bread(fs->part_start_lba + (bitmap_blk * 8), 8, bitmap) != 0) {
1408:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&fs->lock, lock_flags);
1409:    kfree(bitmap);
1410:    return;
1411:  }
1412:  if (!((bitmap[byte] >> b) & 1)) {
1413:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&fs->lock, lock_flags); /* already free */
1414:    kfree(bitmap);
1415:    return;
1416:  }
1417:  bitmap[byte] &= (uint8_t)~(1 << b);
1418:  if (ext4_bwrite(fs->part_start_lba + (bitmap_blk * 8), 8, bitmap) != 0) {
1419:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&fs->lock, lock_flags);
1420:    kfree(bitmap);
1421:    return;
1422:  }
1423:  kfree(bitmap);
1424:
1425:  fs->bgs[0].bg_free_inodes_count_lo++;
1426:  fs->sb.s_free_inodes_count++;
1427:  ext4_sync_bg_sb(fs);
1428:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&fs->lock, lock_flags);
1429:}
1430:
1431:/*
1432: * ext4_extent_free_tree - recursively free every block an extent (sub)tree
1433: * references, INCLUDING interior index-node blocks themselves.  Mirrors
1434: * ext4_extent_lookup's descent (same depth bound: the format caps eh_depth
1435: * at 5, guarded here against a corrupt tree causing unbounded recursion).
1436: * 'node_buf' is the 60-byte root (i_block[]) at depth 0, or a full 4KB
1437: * interior/leaf block read by the caller for depth > 0.
1438: */
1439:static void ext4_extent_free_tree(struct ext4_fs *fs, const uint8_t *node_buf,
1440:                                  int depth_guard) {
1441:  if (depth_guard > 6)
1442:    return;
1443:  const struct ext4_extent_header *eh =
1444:      (const struct ext4_extent_header *)node_buf;
1445:  if (eh->eh_magic != EXT4_EXT_MAGIC)
1446:    return;
1447:
1448:  if (eh->eh_depth > 0) {
1449:    const struct ext4_extent_idx *ix = (const struct ext4_extent_idx *)(eh + 1);
1450:    for (int i = 0; i < eh->eh_entries; i++) {
1451:      uint64_t child = ix[i].ei_leaf_lo | ((uint64_t)ix[i].ei_leaf_hi << 32);
1452:      uint8_t *cbuf = kmalloc(4096);
1453:      if (cbuf) {
1454:        if (ext4_bread(fs->part_start_lba + child * 8, 8, cbuf) == 0)
1455:          ext4_extent_free_tree(fs, cbuf, depth_guard + 1);
1456:        kfree(cbuf);
1457:      }
1458:      ext4_free_block(fs, (uint32_t)child);
1459:    }
1460:  } else {
1461:    const struct ext4_extent *ex = (const struct ext4_extent *)(eh + 1);
1462:    for (int i = 0; i < eh->eh_entries; i++) {
1463:      int unwritten = ex[i].ee_len > EXT4_EXT_UNWRITTEN_LEN;
1464:      uint32_t len =
1465:          unwritten ? ex[i].ee_len - EXT4_EXT_UNWRITTEN_LEN : ex[i].ee_len;
1466:      uint64_t start = ex[i].ee_start_lo | ((uint64_t)ex[i].ee_start_hi << 32);
1467:      for (uint32_t b = 0; b < len; b++)
1468:        ext4_free_block(fs, (uint32_t)(start + b));
1469:    }
1470:  }
1471:}
1472:
1473:/*
1474: * ext4_free_inode_blocks - free every data/metadata block an inode owns,
1475: * dispatching on EXT4_EXTENTS_FL exactly like ext4_bmap does for reads.
1476: */
1477:static void ext4_free_inode_blocks(struct ext4_fs *fs,
1478:                                   const struct ext4_inode *inode) {
1479:  if (inode->i_flags & EXT4_EXTENTS_FL) {
1480:    ext4_extent_free_tree(fs, (const uint8_t *)inode->i_block, 0);
1481:    return;
1482:  }
1483:
1484:  for (int i = 0; i < 12; i++)
1485:    if (inode->i_block[i])
1486:      ext4_free_block(fs, inode->i_block[i]);
1487:
1488:  if (inode->i_block[12]) {
1489:    uint8_t *ind = kmalloc(4096);
1490:    if (ind) {
1491:      if (ext4_bread(fs->part_start_lba + (uint64_t)inode->i_block[12] * 8, 8,
1492:                     ind) == 0) {
1493:        const uint32_t *ptrs = (const uint32_t *)ind;
1494:        for (int i = 0; i < 1024; i++)
1495:          if (ptrs[i])
1496:            ext4_free_block(fs, ptrs[i]);
1497:      }
1498:      kfree(ind);
1499:    }
1500:    ext4_free_block(fs, inode->i_block[12]);
1501:  }
1502:
1503:  if (inode->i_block[13]) {
1504:    uint8_t *dbl = kmalloc(4096);
1505:    if (dbl) {
1506:      if (ext4_bread(fs->part_start_lba + (uint64_t)inode->i_block[13] * 8, 8,
1507:                     dbl) == 0) {
1508:        const uint32_t *ptrs = (const uint32_t *)dbl;
1509:        for (int i = 0; i < 1024; i++) {
1510:          if (!ptrs[i])
1511:            continue;
1512:          uint8_t *sub = kmalloc(4096);
1513:          if (sub) {
1514:            if (ext4_bread(fs->part_start_lba + (uint64_t)ptrs[i] * 8, 8,
1515:                           sub) == 0) {
1516:              const uint32_t *sptrs = (const uint32_t *)sub;
1517:              for (int j = 0; j < 1024; j++)
1518:                if (sptrs[j])
1519:                  ext4_free_block(fs, sptrs[j]);
1520:            }
1521:            kfree(sub);
1522:          }
1523:          ext4_free_block(fs, ptrs[i]);
1524:        }
1525:      }
1526:      kfree(dbl);
1527:    }
1528:    ext4_free_block(fs, inode->i_block[13]);
1529:  }
1530:}
1531:
1532:/*
1533: * ext4_resolve_parent - split an absolute path into its parent directory's
1534: * inode and the final path component (name/name_len), resolving the parent
1535: * via the existing ext4_find_ino walk.  Used by create and unlink.
1536: */
1537:static int ext4_resolve_parent(struct ext4_fs *fs, const char *path,
1538:                               uint32_t *parent_ino_out, const char **name_out,
1539:                               uint32_t *name_len_out) {
1540:  const char *last_slash = NULL;
1541:  for (const char *p = path; *p; p++)
1542:    if (*p == '/')
1543:      last_slash = p;
1544:
1545:  const char *name = last_slash ? last_slash + 1 : path;
1546:  uint32_t name_len = (uint32_t)strlen(name);
1547:  if (name_len == 0 || name_len > 255)
1548:    return -1;
1549:  if ((name_len == 1 && name[0] == '.') ||
1550:      (name_len == 2 && name[0] == '.' && name[1] == '.'))
1551:    return -1; /* reject creating/removing "." or ".." */
1552:
1553:  uint32_t parent_ino;
1554:  if (!last_slash || last_slash == path) {
1555:    parent_ino = EXT4_ROOT_INO;
1556:  } else {
1557:    char parent_path[256];
1558:    uint32_t plen = (uint32_t)(last_slash - path);
1559:    if (plen >= sizeof(parent_path))
1560:      return -1;
1561:    memcpy(parent_path, path, plen);
1562:    parent_path[plen] = '\0';
1563:    if (ext4_find_ino(fs, parent_path, &parent_ino) != 0)
1564:      return -1;
1565:  }
1566:
1567:  *parent_ino_out = parent_ino;
1568:  *name_out = name;
1569:  *name_len_out = name_len;
1570:  return 0;
1571:}
1572:
1573:/* dirent_ideal_len - minimal 4-byte-aligned rec_len for a name of this
1574: * length (8-byte header + name, rounded up), matching tools/mkdisk.c's
1575: * '(8 + nlen + 3) & ~3' convention exactly. */
1576:static inline uint16_t dirent_ideal_len(uint32_t name_len) {
1577:  return (uint16_t)((8 + name_len + 3) & ~3u);
1578:}
1579:
1580:/* ext4_write_dir_block - write back one already-mapped logical block of a
1581: * directory's data (bmap to physical, then a plain block write). */
1582:static int ext4_write_dir_block(struct ext4_fs *fs,
1583:                                const struct ext4_inode *inode,
1584:                                uint32_t block_idx, const uint8_t *buf) {
1585:  uint64_t phys;
1586:  struct ext4_icache c = {{0, 0}, {NULL, NULL}};
1587:  int rc = ext4_bmap(fs, inode, block_idx, &phys, &c);
1588:  icache_release(&c);
1589:  if (rc != 0 || phys == 0)
1590:    return -1;
1591:  return ext4_bwrite(fs->part_start_lba + (phys * 8), 8, (void *)buf);
1592:}
1593:
1594:/*
1595: * ext4_dir_insert - insert one directory entry (name -> ino) into dir_ino's
1596: * data, following the exact same "split trailing slack, else append a new
1597: * whole-block entry" convention tools/mkdisk.c uses to build the initial
1598: * image (see its rec_len-to-end-of-block handling): the LAST entry in a
1599: * block always carries the block's remaining slack in its rec_len, so a
1600: * subsequent insert either splits that slack or, if none is left anywhere,
1601: * allocates a fresh block and seeds it with one whole-block entry (the new
1602: * "last entry") ready to be split by the next insert.
1603: *
1604: * A dirent with inode==0 is a freed slot (see ext4_dir_remove): its whole
1605: * rec_len is reusable, no split needed.
1606: *
1607: * Only depth-0 extent growth / legacy direct blocks (<12) are supported for
1608: * a NEW directory block, matching ext4_write's own EXT4-05 boundary -
1609: * directories in this driver are expected to stay small.
1610: */
1611:static int ext4_dir_insert(struct ext4_fs *fs, uint32_t dir_ino,
1612:                           const char *name, uint32_t name_len,
1613:                           uint32_t new_ino, uint8_t file_type) {
1614:  uint16_t need = dirent_ideal_len(name_len);
1615:
1616:  struct ext4_inode dir_inode;
1617:  if (get_inode_struct(fs, dir_ino, &dir_inode) != 0)
1618:    return -1;
1619:
1620:  int is_extent = (dir_inode.i_flags & EXT4_EXTENTS_FL) != 0;
1621:  uint32_t dir_size = dir_inode.i_size_lo;
1622:  uint8_t *blk_buf = kmalloc(4096);
1623:  if (!blk_buf)
1624:    return -1;
1625:
1626:  for (uint32_t bidx = 0; bidx * 4096 < dir_size; bidx++) {
1627:    if (ext4_read_data(fs, &dir_inode, (uint64_t)bidx * 4096, blk_buf, 4096) <=
1628:        0)
1629:      break;
1630:
1631:    uint32_t off = 0;
1632:    while (off < 4096) {
1633:      struct ext4_dir_entry *de = (struct ext4_dir_entry *)(blk_buf + off);
1634:      if (de->rec_len < 8 || de->rec_len > (4096 - off))
1635:        break; /* corrupt/end-of-chain: stop scanning this block */
1636:
1637:      uint16_t used = de->inode ? dirent_ideal_len(de->name_len) : 0;
1638:      uint16_t slack = de->rec_len - used;
1639:      if (slack >= need) {
1640:        if (de->inode == 0) {
1641:          de->inode = new_ino;
1642:          de->name_len = (uint8_t)name_len;
1643:          de->file_type = file_type;
1644:          memcpy(de->name, name, name_len);
1645:        } else {
1646:          uint16_t old_rec_len = de->rec_len;
1647:          de->rec_len = used;
1648:          struct ext4_dir_entry *nde =
1649:              (struct ext4_dir_entry *)(blk_buf + off + used);
1650:          nde->inode = new_ino;
1651:          nde->rec_len = old_rec_len - used;
1652:          nde->name_len = (uint8_t)name_len;
1653:          nde->file_type = file_type;
1654:          memcpy(nde->name, name, name_len);
1655:        }
1656:        int rc = ext4_write_dir_block(fs, &dir_inode, bidx, blk_buf);
1657:        kfree(blk_buf);
1658:        return rc;
1659:      }
1660:      off += de->rec_len;
1661:    }
1662:  }
1663:
1664:  /* No slack anywhere: append a new block, seeded with one whole-block
1665:   * entry (the new "last entry", carrying all of the block's slack). */
1666:  uint32_t new_blk_idx = (dir_size > 0) ? (dir_size - 1) / 4096 + 1 : 0;
1667:  uint32_t nb = ext4_alloc_block(fs);
1668:  if (nb == 0) {
1669:    kfree(blk_buf);
1670:    return -1;
1671:  }
1672:
1673:  if (is_extent) {
1674:    if (!ext4_extent_can_append(&dir_inode, new_blk_idx)) {
1675:      pr_err("%s", "Ext4: directory extent growth not supported yet\n");
1676:      kfree(blk_buf);
1677:      return -1;
1678:    }
1679:    ext4_extent_do_append(&dir_inode, new_blk_idx, nb);
1680:  } else if (new_blk_idx < 12) {
1681:    dir_inode.i_block[new_blk_idx] = nb;
1682:  } else {
1683:    pr_err("%s", "Ext4: directory indirect growth not supported yet\n");
1684:    kfree(blk_buf);
1685:    return -1;
1686:  }
1687:  dir_inode.i_blocks_lo += (4096 / 512);
1688:
1689:  memset(blk_buf, 0, 4096);
1690:  struct ext4_dir_entry *nde = (struct ext4_dir_entry *)blk_buf;
1691:  nde->inode = new_ino;
1692:  nde->rec_len = 4096;
1693:  nde->name_len = (uint8_t)name_len;
1694:  nde->file_type = file_type;
1695:  memcpy(nde->name, name, name_len);
1696:
1697:  int rc = ext4_bwrite(fs->part_start_lba + (nb * 8), 8, blk_buf);
1698:  kfree(blk_buf);
1699:  if (rc != 0)
1700:    return -1;
1701:
1702:  dir_inode.i_size_lo = (new_blk_idx + 1) * 4096;
1703:  return ext4_update_inode(fs, dir_ino, &dir_inode);
1704:}
1705:
1706:/*
1707: * ext4_dir_remove - clear the directory entry named 'name' in dir_ino
1708: * (inode = 0, rec_len kept as-is so ext4_dir_insert can reclaim the slot -
1709: * the exact inverse of the "free slot" branch above). Returns 0 found and
1710: * cleared, -1 not found.
1711: */
1712:static int ext4_dir_remove(struct ext4_fs *fs, uint32_t dir_ino,
1713:                           const char *name, uint32_t name_len) {
1714:  struct ext4_inode dir_inode;
1715:  if (get_inode_struct(fs, dir_ino, &dir_inode) != 0)
1716:    return -1;
1717:
1718:  uint32_t dir_size = dir_inode.i_size_lo;
1719:  uint8_t *blk_buf = kmalloc(4096);
1720:  if (!blk_buf)
1721:    return -1;
1722:
1723:  for (uint32_t bidx = 0; bidx * 4096 < dir_size; bidx++) {
1724:    if (ext4_read_data(fs, &dir_inode, (uint64_t)bidx * 4096, blk_buf, 4096) <=
1725:        0)
1726:      break;
1727:
1728:    uint32_t off = 0;
1729:    while (off < 4096) {
1730:      struct ext4_dir_entry *de = (struct ext4_dir_entry *)(blk_buf + off);
1731:      if (de->rec_len < 8 || de->rec_len > (4096 - off))
1732:        break;
1733:
1734:      if (de->inode != 0 && de->name_len == name_len &&
1735:          memcmp(de->name, name, name_len) == 0) {
1736:        de->inode = 0;
1737:        int rc = ext4_write_dir_block(fs, &dir_inode, bidx, blk_buf);
1738:        kfree(blk_buf);
1739:        return rc;
1740:      }
1741:      off += de->rec_len;
1742:    }
1743:  }
1744:
1745:  kfree(blk_buf);
1746:  return -1;
1747:}
1748:
1749:/*
1750: * ext4_create - fs_ops.create.  Handles both VFS_TYPE_FILE and VFS_TYPE_DIR.
1751: * New inodes are legacy-mapped (i_flags=0, no extent header): a file's first
1752: * data block is allocated lazily by ext4_write's direct-block growth path
1753: * (block_idx < 12); a directory is seeded here with a single '.'/'..' block.
1754: * Rejects if the path already exists (caller must not race this, single
1755: * fs->lock-free window between the vfs_stat/ext4_find_ino checks above this
1756: * layer and here - same race class every VFS write already tolerates.)
1757: */
1758:static int ext4_create(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path,
1759:                       uint32_t vfs_type) {
1760:  struct ext4_fs *fs = mnt->fs_private;
1761:  if (fs->read_only)
1762:    return -EROFS;
1763:  if (vfs_type != VFS_TYPE_FILE && vfs_type != VFS_TYPE_DIR)
1764:    return -EINVAL;
1765:
1766:  uint32_t existing;
1767:  if (ext4_find_ino(fs, path, &existing) == 0)
1768:    return -EEXIST; /* already exists */
1769:
1770:  uint32_t parent_ino;
1771:  const char *name;
1772:  uint32_t name_len;
1773:  if (ext4_resolve_parent(fs, path, &parent_ino, &name, &name_len) != 0)
1774:    return -ENOENT;
1775:
1776:  uint32_t new_ino = ext4_alloc_inode(fs);
1777:  if (new_ino == 0)
1778:    return -ENOSPC;
1779:
1780:  struct ext4_inode inode;
1781:  memset(&inode, 0, sizeof(inode));
1782:
1783:  if (vfs_type == VFS_TYPE_DIR) {
1784:    /* A directory must carry its own '.' and '..' before it is linked in, so
1785:     * it needs a seeded data block.  Legacy-map that single block (i_flags=0,
1786:     * i_block[0]) to match ext4_create's file inodes and ext4_dir_insert's
1787:     * <12 direct-block growth path (directories stay small in this driver). */
1788:    uint32_t db = ext4_alloc_block(fs);
1789:    if (db == 0) {
1790:      ext4_free_inode(fs, new_ino);
1791:      return -ENOSPC;
1792:    }
1793:
1794:    uint8_t *blk = kmalloc(4096);
1795:    if (!blk) {
1796:      ext4_free_block(fs, db);
1797:      ext4_free_inode(fs, new_ino);
1798:      return -ENOMEM;
1799:    }
1800:    memset(blk, 0, 4096);
1801:    /* '.' -> self */
1802:    struct ext4_dir_entry *dot = (struct ext4_dir_entry *)blk;
1803:    dot->inode = new_ino;
1804:    dot->rec_len = dirent_ideal_len(1); /* 12 */
1805:    dot->name_len = 1;
1806:    dot->file_type = EXT4_FT_DIR;
1807:    dot->name[0] = '.';
1808:    /* '..' -> parent, carrying the block's remaining slack (the last-entry
1809:     * rule ext4_dir_insert relies on). */
1810:    struct ext4_dir_entry *dotdot =
1811:        (struct ext4_dir_entry *)(blk + dot->rec_len);
1812:    dotdot->inode = parent_ino;
1813:    dotdot->rec_len = (uint16_t)(4096 - dot->rec_len);
1814:    dotdot->name_len = 2;
1815:    dotdot->file_type = EXT4_FT_DIR;
1816:    dotdot->name[0] = '.';
1817:    dotdot->name[1] = '.';
1818:
1819:    int wrc = ext4_bwrite(fs->part_start_lba + ((uint64_t)db * 8), 8, blk);
1820:    kfree(blk);
1821:    if (wrc != 0) {
1822:      ext4_free_block(fs, db);
1823:      ext4_free_inode(fs, new_ino);
1824:      return -EIO;
1825:    }
1826:
1827:    inode.i_mode = 0x4000 | 0755; /* S_IFDIR | rwxr-xr-x */
1828:    inode.i_links_count = 2; /* '.' (self) + the parent dirent added below */
1829:    inode.i_block[0] = db;
1830:    inode.i_size_lo = 4096;
1831:    inode.i_blocks_lo = (4096 / 512);
1832:  } else {
1833:    inode.i_mode = 0x8000 | 0644; /* S_IFREG | rw-r--r-- */
1834:    inode.i_links_count = 1;
1835:  }
1836:
1837:  if (ext4_update_inode(fs, new_ino, &inode) != 0) {
1838:    if (vfs_type == VFS_TYPE_DIR)
1839:      ext4_free_block(fs, inode.i_block[0]);
1840:    ext4_free_inode(fs, new_ino); /* undo: no dirent references it yet */
1841:    return -EIO;
1842:  }
1843:
1844:  uint8_t ft = (vfs_type == VFS_TYPE_DIR) ? EXT4_FT_DIR : EXT4_FT_REG_FILE;
1845:  if (ext4_dir_insert(fs, parent_ino, name, name_len, new_ino, ft) != 0) {
1846:    if (vfs_type == VFS_TYPE_DIR)
1847:      ext4_free_block(fs, inode.i_block[0]);
1848:    ext4_free_inode(fs, new_ino); /* undo: still no dirent, safe to free */
1849:    /* EXT4-ERRNO-01, stated rather than overclaimed: ext4_dir_insert still
1850:     * returns a bare -1 for several causes (allocation, read failure, and a
1851:     * full single-block directory), so this is the ONE bucket that stays
1852:     * undifferentiated.  -EIO is the honest floor; narrowing it means giving
1853:     * ext4_dir_insert its own errnos, which is a separate change. */
1854:    return -EIO;
1855:  }
1856:
1857:  /* A new subdirectory's '..' adds one link to the parent's count. */
1858:  if (vfs_type == VFS_TYPE_DIR) {
1859:    struct ext4_inode pinode;
1860:    if (get_inode_struct(fs, parent_ino, &pinode) == 0) {
1861:      pinode.i_links_count++;
1862:      ext4_update_inode(fs, parent_ino, &pinode);
1863:    }
1864:  }
1865:
1866:  return 0;
1867:}
1868:
1869:/*
1870: * ext4_dir_is_empty - a directory is empty when its only live entries are '.'
1871: * and '..'.  Returns 1 empty, 0 non-empty, -1 on a read/alloc failure (caller
1872: * treats anything but 1 as "do not remove").
1873: */
1874:static int ext4_dir_is_empty(struct ext4_fs *fs, const struct ext4_inode *dir) {
1875:  uint32_t dir_size = dir->i_size_lo;
1876:  uint8_t *blk = kmalloc(4096);
1877:  if (!blk)
1878:    return -1;
1879:
1880:  int empty = 1;
1881:  for (uint32_t bidx = 0; bidx * 4096 < dir_size && empty; bidx++) {
1882:    if (ext4_read_data(fs, dir, (uint64_t)bidx * 4096, blk, 4096) <= 0)
1883:      break;
1884:    uint32_t off = 0;
1885:    while (off < 4096) {
1886:      struct ext4_dir_entry *de = (struct ext4_dir_entry *)(blk + off);
1887:      if (de->rec_len < 8 || de->rec_len > (4096 - off))
1888:        break;
1889:      if (de->inode != 0) {
1890:        int is_dot = (de->name_len == 1 && de->name[0] == '.');
1891:        int is_dotdot =
1892:            (de->name_len == 2 && de->name[0] == '.' && de->name[1] == '.');
1893:        if (!is_dot && !is_dotdot) {
1894:          empty = 0;
1895:          break;
1896:        }
1897:      }
1898:      off += de->rec_len;
1899:    }
1900:  }
1901:  kfree(blk);
1902:  return empty;
1903:}
1904:
1905:/*
1906: * ext4_unlink - fs_ops.unlink.  Removes regular files and EMPTY directories
1907: * (a non-empty directory is refused, matching rmdir/ENOTEMPTY).  Order matters
1908: * for crash safety: remove the dirent FIRST (so a crash after this point leaves
1909: * an orphaned-but-allocated inode+blocks, recoverable, rather than a live
1910: * dirent pointing at freed blocks, which would corrupt a later read).
1911: */
1912:static int ext4_unlink(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path) {
1913:  struct ext4_fs *fs = mnt->fs_private;
1914:  if (fs->read_only)
1915:    return -EROFS;
1916:
1917:  uint32_t ino;
1918:  if (ext4_find_ino(fs, path, &ino) != 0)
1919:    return -ENOENT;
1920:
1921:  struct ext4_inode inode;
1922:  if (get_inode_struct(fs, ino, &inode) != 0)
1923:    return -EIO;
1924:
1925:  int is_dir = ((inode.i_mode >> 12) == 4);
1926:  if (is_dir) {
1927:    /* EXT4-ERRNO-01: "not empty" and "could not be read" were one refusal.
1928:     * ext4_dir_is_empty already distinguishes them (1 / 0 / -1) — only the
1929:     * caller threw the distinction away. */
1930:    int empty = ext4_dir_is_empty(fs, &inode);
1931:    if (empty < 0)
1932:      return -EIO;
1933:    if (empty == 0)
1934:      return -ENOTEMPTY;
1935:  }
1936:
1937:  uint32_t parent_ino;
1938:  const char *name;
1939:  uint32_t name_len;
1940:  if (ext4_resolve_parent(fs, path, &parent_ino, &name, &name_len) != 0)
1941:    return -ENOENT;
1942:
1943:  /* Never unlink the '.'/'..' entries themselves (path canonicalisation should
1944:   * strip them, but a stray one must not corrupt the tree). */
1945:  if ((name_len == 1 && name[0] == '.') ||
1946:      (name_len == 2 && name[0] == '.' && name[1] == '.'))
1947:    return -EINVAL;
1948:
1949:  if (ext4_dir_remove(fs, parent_ino, name, name_len) != 0)
1950:    return -EIO;
1951:
1952:  ext4_free_inode_blocks(fs, &inode);
1953:  ext4_free_inode(fs, ino);
1954:
1955:  /* Removing a subdirectory drops the '..' link it held on its parent. */
1956:  if (is_dir) {
1957:    struct ext4_inode pinode;
1958:    if (get_inode_struct(fs, parent_ino, &pinode) == 0 &&
1959:        pinode.i_links_count > 0) {
1960:      pinode.i_links_count--;
1961:      ext4_update_inode(fs, parent_ino, &pinode);
1962:    }
1963:  }
1964:  return 0;
1965:}
1966:
1967:const struct fs_ops ext4_fs_ops = {
1968:    .name = "ext4",
1969:    .mount = ext4_mount,
1970:    .open = ext4_open,
1971:    .read = ext4_read,
1972:    .write = ext4_write,
1973:    .list = ext4_list,
1974:    .unlink = ext4_unlink,
1975:    .create = ext4_create,
1976:};

@@@ kernel/fs/gpt.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/fs/gpt.c
3: * GPT Partition Table Parser
4: *
5: * Purpose:
6: *   Reads and validates the GUID Partition Table (GPT) from the block device,
7: *   populates the global partitions[] array, and exposes gpt_get_partition() so
8: *   ext4_init() can locate its partition by index.  Falls back to the legacy
9: *   Master Boot Record (MBR) format if the GPT signature or header CRC32 fails.
10: *
11: * On-disk layout accessed:
12: *   LBA 0  (512 bytes) : MBR (fallback; boot code + 4 × mbr_entry + signature)
13: *   LBA 1  (512 bytes) : GPT header (struct gpt_header, 92 bytes used)
14: *   LBA 2+ (variable)  : GPT partition entries at header->partition_entry_lba;
15: *                        typically 128 entries × 128 bytes = 16 384 bytes = 32
16: *                        sectors starting at LBA 2.
17: *
18: * Key invariants:
19: *   - partitions[] is indexed 0-based by GPT path; 1-based by MBR path.
20: *     NOTE(GPT-02): ext4_init() calls gpt_get_partition(2), meaning index 2
21: *     of partitions[].  On GPT that is the third parsed entry (GPT entries are
22: *     0-indexed into partitions[]).  On MBR that is MBR slot 1 (0-indexed MBR
23: *     slot i fills partitions[i+1]).  The asymmetry is undocumented; changing
24: *     the disk image layout will silently mount the wrong partition.
25: *   - CRC32 uses the reflected IEEE-802.3 / PKZIP polynomial (0xEDB88320),
26: *     init 0xFFFFFFFF, final XOR 0xFFFFFFFF — identical to mkdisk.c.
27: *
28: * Known issues:
29: *   GPT-01  (W3 REFINE, FIXED) Partition-entry CRC mismatch now aborts to the
30: *           MBR parser (matching header-CRC behaviour), instead of parsing
31: *           entries[] that may contain corrupt start/end LBAs.
32: *   GPT-02  (W2 BAD-IMPL) MBR path fills partitions[i+1] (1-based); GPT path
33: *           fills partitions[num_partitions] (0-based).  ext4_init(2) gets
34: *           different physical partitions depending on the table type.
35: *   GPT-03  (W1 REFINE) When num_pages > 1 and pmm_alloc_pages() fails, the
36: *           fallback rewrites total_entries_size and sectors_to_read for 32
37: *           entries (32 × entry_size bytes), which fits in the single-page
38: *           buf[] (4096 bytes) only when entry_size ≤ 128.  Standard GPT uses
39: *           entry_size == 128, so 32 × 128 = 4096, which is exactly the page
40: *           boundary.  For non-standard larger entry sizes the fallback would
41: *           read more bytes than buf[] holds.
42: */
43:#include <kernel/block.h>
44:#include <kernel/gpt.h>
45:#include <kernel/pmm.h>
46:#include <kernel/printk.h>
47:#include <kernel/string.h>
48:
49:/* partitions[]: in-memory table populated by gpt_init() or mbr_init().
50: * Indexed 0-based on the GPT path, 1-based on the MBR path (GPT-02). */
51:struct partition partitions[MAX_PARTITIONS];
52:/* num_partitions: count of valid entries written into partitions[]. */
53:int num_partitions = 0;
54:
55:/*
56: * mbr_init - parse a legacy MBR from an already-read 512-byte sector buffer.
57: *
58: * @buf: pointer to a 512-byte buffer containing LBA 0 (the MBR sector).
59: *
60: * Validates the MBR signature (0xAA55 at bytes 510–511), then iterates the
61: * four 16-byte MBR partition entries at offset 446 (bytes 446–509).  Each
62: * non-empty slot (type != 0) is mapped to partitions[i+1], where i is the
63: * 0-based MBR slot index (0..3).  This 1-based mapping leaves partitions[0]
64: * unset when called from the MBR path.
65: *
66: * On-disk MBR layout (struct mbr, gpt.h):
67: *   bytes   0–445: boot code
68: *   bytes 446–461: mbr_entry[0]  (status, chs_start[3], type, chs_end[3],
69: *                                  lba_start u32, sectors u32 = 16 bytes)
70: *   bytes 462–477: mbr_entry[1]
71: *   bytes 478–493: mbr_entry[2]
72: *   bytes 494–509: mbr_entry[3]
73: *   bytes 510–511: signature (0xAA55, little-endian)
74: *
75: * Side effects:
76: *   Writes to partitions[1..4] and num_partitions (global state).
77: *   No disk I/O (buf already contains the sector contents).
78: *
79: * NOTE(GPT-02): MBR fills partitions[i+1] (1-based); GPT fills
80: * partitions[num_partitions] (0-based).  The resulting asymmetry means
81: * gpt_get_partition(2) returns the 2nd MBR partition but the 3rd GPT entry.
82: */
83:static void mbr_init(uint8_t *buf) {
84:  struct mbr *m = (struct mbr *)buf;
85:  if (m->signature != MBR_SIGNATURE) {
86:    pr_err("MBR: Invalid signature: 0x%04x\n", m->signature);
87:    return;
88:  }
89:
90:  pr_info("%s", "MBR: Valid signature found. Scanning partitions...\n");
91:  num_partitions = 0;
92:
93:  for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
94:    struct mbr_entry *e = &m->partitions[i];
95:    if (e->type == 0)
96:      continue;
97:
98:    /* Map MBR partition 1..4 to our internal index 1..4 (or 0..3)
99:     * For compatibility with ext4_init(2), we use the MBR slot index + 1. */
100:    /* NOTE(GPT-02): idx = i+1 means MBR slot 0 → partitions[1], ...,
101:     * slot 3 → partitions[4].  partitions[0] is left zeroed.  The GPT
102:     * path fills from index 0; ext4_init(2) therefore hits a different
103:     * physical partition depending on which table type was found. */
104:    int idx = i + 1;
105:    if (idx >= MAX_PARTITIONS)
106:      continue;
107:
108:    struct partition *p = &partitions[idx];
109:    p->index = idx;
110:    p->start_lba = e->lba_start;
111:    p->size_sectors = e->sectors;
112:    p->end_lba = p->start_lba + p->size_sectors - 1;
113:    memset(p->type_guid, 0, 16);
114:    p->type_guid[0] = e->type;
115:
116:    pr_info("MBR: Partition %d: Type=0x%02x, Start=%ld, Size=%ld sectors\n", idx,
117:            e->type, p->start_lba, p->size_sectors);
118:
119:    if (idx >= num_partitions)
120:      num_partitions = idx + 1;
121:  }
122:}
123:
124:/*
125: * gpt_init - detect and parse the partition table from the block device.
126: *
127: * Reads LBA 1 (512 bytes) via block_read(), attempts to validate the
128: * GPT header signature ("EFI PART", 0x5452415020494645) and its CRC32, then
129: * reads and validates the partition entries.  Falls back to the MBR parser
130: * (mbr_init()) if the GPT signature is absent or the header CRC32 does not
131: * match.
132: *
133: * GPT header CRC32 protocol (verified correct; matches mkdisk.c):
134: *   1. Save header->header_crc32.
135: *   2. Zero header->header_crc32 in the buffer.
136: *   3. Compute crc32(header, header->header_size) — standard IEEE-802.3
137: *      reflected polynomial, init 0xFFFFFFFF, final XOR 0xFFFFFFFF.
138: *   4. Restore header->header_crc32.
139: *   5. Compare computed vs saved; mismatch → MBR fallback.
140: *
141: * Partition-entry CRC32 (GPT-01):
142: *   Computed over total_entries_size bytes at entries_lba.
143: *   Mismatch is logged but parsing continues — entries may contain corrupt
144: *   start/end LBAs.  See NOTE(GPT-01).
145: *
146: * Sector arithmetic:
147: *   total_entries_size = num_entries × entry_size
148: *     (standard: 128 × 128 = 16 384 bytes = 32 sectors at LBA 2)
149: *   sectors_to_read    = (total_entries_size + 511) / 512
150: *   num_pages          = (total_entries_size + PAGE_SIZE - 1) / PAGE_SIZE
151: *
152: * Buffer strategy:
153: *   A single PMM page (4096 bytes) is allocated for the GPT header read.
154: *   If the entries array is also ≤ 4096 bytes (num_pages == 1), the same
155: *   page is reused for entries.  If larger, pmm_alloc_pages(num_pages) is
156: *   called for a dedicated entries buffer; on failure the code falls back to
157: *   the single-page buf[] and caps reads to 32 entries.
158: *   NOTE(GPT-03): The 32-entry fallback limit assumes entry_size ≤ 128 bytes
159: *   (32 × 128 = 4096 = one page); for non-standard larger entry sizes this
160: *   would overrun buf[].
161: *
162: * Side effects:
163: *   Writes partitions[] and num_partitions (global state).
164: *   Two or more block_read() calls; one or more PMM alloc/free cycles.
165: *
166: * Returns: void; callers use gpt_get_partition() to query results.
167: */
168:void gpt_init(void) {
169:  pr_info("%s", "Partition: Initializing...\n");
170:
171:  /* Allocate buffer for reading sectors */
172:  uint8_t *buf = (uint8_t *)pmm_alloc_page();
173:  if (!buf) {
174:    pr_info("%s", "Partition: Failed to allocate buffer\n");
175:    return;
176:  }
177:
178:  /* 1. Try reading GPT Header (LBA 1) */
179:  if (block_read(buf, 1, 1) != 0) {
180:    pr_info("%s", "Partition: Failed to read LBA 1\n");
181:    pmm_free_page(buf);
182:    return;
183:  }
184:
185:  struct gpt_header *header = (struct gpt_header *)buf;
186:
187:  /* 2. Check GPT Signature. If not found, try MBR on LBA 0. */
188:  if (header->signature != GPT_SIGNATURE) {
189:    pr_info("%s", "GPT: Invalid signature. Falling back to MBR...\n");
190:    if (block_read(buf, 0, 1) != 0) {
191:      pr_err("%s", "Partition: Failed to read LBA 0 (MBR)\n");
192:      pmm_free_page(buf);
193:      return;
194:    }
195:    mbr_init(buf);
196:    pmm_free_page(buf);
197:    return;
198:  }
199:
200:  /* 2.1 Verify Header CRC32 */
201:  /* GPT spec: zero the CRC field in the buffer, compute CRC over the first
202:   * header_size bytes (typically 92), then restore the field.  crc32() here
203:   * uses the reflected IEEE-802.3 polynomial (0xEDB88320), init 0xFFFFFFFF,
204:   * final XOR 0xFFFFFFFF — the same implementation as mkdisk.c (verified). */
205:  uint32_t orig_crc = header->header_crc32;
206:  header->header_crc32 = 0;
207:  uint32_t calc_crc = crc32(header, header->header_size);
208:  header->header_crc32 = orig_crc;
209:
210:  if (calc_crc != orig_crc) {
211:    pr_err("GPT: Header CRC mismatch! (calc: 0x%08x, orig: 0x%08x). Falling back to MBR.\n", calc_crc,
212:           orig_crc);
213:
214:           if (block_read(buf, 0, 1) != 0) {
215:      pr_err("%s", "Partition: Failed to read LBA 0 (MBR fallback)\n");
216:      pmm_free_page(buf);
217:      return;
218:    }
219:    mbr_init(buf);
220:    pmm_free_page(buf);
221:    return; 
222:  }  
223:
224:  pr_info("GPT: Valid signature found. Entries: %d @ LBA %ld\n",
225:          header->num_partition_entries, header->partition_entry_lba);
226:
227:  /* 3. Read Partition Entries */
228:  uint64_t entries_lba = header->partition_entry_lba;
229:  /* entry_size: from the GPT header; typically 128 bytes per spec. */
230:  uint32_t entry_size = header->partition_entry_size;
231:  uint32_t num_entries = header->num_partition_entries;
232:  /* entries_crc: CRC32 of the raw entries array as stored in the header. */
233:  uint32_t entries_crc = header->partition_entry_crc32;
234:
235:  /* Calculate total size and pages needed */
236:  /* Standard case: 128 entries × 128 bytes = 16 384 bytes = 32 sectors.
237:   * sectors_to_read = ceil(total_entries_size / 512) using integer arithmetic.
238:   * num_pages       = ceil(total_entries_size / PAGE_SIZE). */
239:  uint32_t total_entries_size = num_entries * entry_size;
240:  uint32_t num_pages = (total_entries_size + PAGE_SIZE - 1) / PAGE_SIZE;
241:  uint32_t sectors_to_read = (total_entries_size + 511) / 512;
242:
243:  /* Allocate buffer for all partition entries if needed */
244:  uint8_t *entries_buf = buf;
245:  if (num_pages > 1) {
246:    /* Allocate additional pages for partition entries */
247:    entries_buf = (uint8_t *)pmm_alloc_pages(num_pages);
248:    if (!entries_buf) {
249:      /* NOTE(GPT-03): fallback: cap to 32 entries and reuse the single-page
250:       * buf[4096].  32 × entry_size must be ≤ 4096, which holds only when
251:       * entry_size ≤ 128.  Standard GPT uses entry_size == 128 exactly
252:       * (32 × 128 = 4096), so the fallback is safe on standard images. */
253:      pr_warn("GPT: Cannot allocate %u pages for entries, limiting to 32\n", num_pages);
254:      total_entries_size = 32 * entry_size;
255:      sectors_to_read = (total_entries_size + 511) / 512;
256:      entries_buf = buf;
257:    }
258:  }
259:
260:  if (block_read(entries_buf, entries_lba, sectors_to_read) != 0) {
261:    pr_info("%s", "GPT: Failed to read partition entries\n");
262:    if (entries_buf != buf) pmm_free_pages(entries_buf, num_pages);
263:    pmm_free_page(buf);
264:    return;
265:  }
266:
267:  /* 3.1 Verify Partition Entries CRC32 */
268:  /* CRC computed over the exact total_entries_size bytes starting at
269:   * entries_buf.  GPT-01 (fixed): a mismatch now aborts to the MBR parser,
270:   * matching the header-CRC behaviour above, instead of parsing entries that
271:   * may carry corrupt start/end LBAs. */
272:  uint32_t calc_entries_crc = crc32(entries_buf, total_entries_size);
273:  if (calc_entries_crc != entries_crc) {
274:    pr_err("GPT: Partition Entries CRC mismatch! (calc: 0x%08x, orig: 0x%08x). Falling back to MBR.\n",
275:           calc_entries_crc, entries_crc);
276:    /* GPT-01: the entries array is untrustworthy — do not parse it.  Abort to
277:     * the MBR parser, mirroring the header-CRC fallback above. */
278:    if (entries_buf != buf) pmm_free_pages(entries_buf, num_pages);
279:    if (block_read(buf, 0, 1) != 0) {
280:      pr_err("%s", "Partition: Failed to read LBA 0 (MBR fallback)\n");
281:      pmm_free_page(buf);
282:      return;
283:    }
284:    mbr_init(buf);
285:    pmm_free_page(buf);
286:    return;
287:  }
288:
289:  /* Parse entries */
290:  /* entries_to_read = actual number of slots in the buffer; may be less than
291:   * num_entries when the fallback capped total_entries_size to 32 × entry_size. */
292:  num_partitions = 0;
293:  uint32_t entries_to_read = total_entries_size / entry_size;
294:
295:  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < entries_to_read; i++) {
296:    struct gpt_partition_entry *entry =
297:        (struct gpt_partition_entry *)(entries_buf + i * entry_size);
298:
299:    /* Check if entry is used (Type GUID != 0) */
300:    /* GPT spec: an all-zero type_guid marks an unused partition slot;
301:     * any non-zero byte in the 16-byte GUID indicates a valid partition. */
302:    int is_unused = 1;
303:    for (int k = 0; k < 16; k++) {
304:      if (entry->type_guid[k] != 0) {
305:        is_unused = 0;
306:        break;
307:      }
308:    }
309:
310:    if (is_unused)
311:      continue;
312:
313:    if (num_partitions >= MAX_PARTITIONS)
314:      break;
315:
316:    /* Populate the in-memory partition descriptor.
317:     * NOTE(GPT-02): GPT path fills partitions[0], [1], [2], … (0-based).
318:     * MBR path fills partitions[1], [2], [3], [4] (1-based).  The caller
319:     * ext4_init() requests index 2: the 3rd GPT entry vs. the 2nd MBR slot. */
320:    struct partition *p = &partitions[num_partitions];
321:    p->index = num_partitions;
322:    p->start_lba = entry->start_lba;
323:    p->end_lba = entry->end_lba;
324:    /* size_sectors: inclusive range; +1 because start_lba..end_lba both belong
325:     * to the partition (e.g. start=34, end=34849 → 34816 sectors). */
326:    p->size_sectors = entry->end_lba - entry->start_lba + 1;
327:    memcpy(p->type_guid, entry->type_guid, 16);
328:
329:    pr_info("GPT: Partition %d: Start=%ld, Size=%ld sectors\n", i, p->start_lba,
330:            p->size_sectors);
331:
332:    num_partitions++;
333:  }
334:
335:  /* Cleanup allocated buffers */
336:  if (entries_buf != buf) pmm_free_pages(entries_buf, num_pages);
337:  pmm_free_page(buf);
338:  pr_info("GPT: Found %d partitions\n", num_partitions);
339:}
340:
341:/*
342: * gpt_get_partition - return a pointer to an in-memory partition descriptor.
343: *
344: * @index: 0-based index into partitions[] (GPT path) or 1-based (MBR path).
345: *         ext4_init() passes 2, which on a GPT disk is the third parsed GPT
346: *         entry and on an MBR disk is the second MBR partition slot.
347: *         NOTE(GPT-02): the index semantics differ between GPT and MBR paths.
348: *
349: * Precondition: gpt_init() must have been called; no locking is performed.
350: *
351: * Returns: pointer into partitions[] on success; NULL if index is out of
352: *          range [0, num_partitions).  Does not distinguish GPT vs. MBR.
353: *
354: * Side effects: none.
355: */
356:struct partition *gpt_get_partition(int index) {
357:  if (index < 0 || index >= num_partitions)
358:    return NULL;
359:  return &partitions[index];
360:}
361:
362:/*
363: * partition_role - decode the NEXS role from a partition's type GUID.
364: *
365: * The GUID is stored little-endian on disk, exactly as GPT specifies for the
366: * first three fields: data1 (4 bytes) and data2 (2 bytes) are LE, data4 is a
367: * byte string.  So "NEXS" (0x4E455853) reads back as 53 58 45 4E, and the role
368: * (data2) as its two bytes low-first.
369: *
370: * Returns the role, or 0 for any partition that is not ours — a foreign
371: * partition, or an image built before roles existed.  0 is not a valid role,
372: * so callers can treat it as "unknown" without a separate flag.
373: */
374:uint16_t partition_role(const struct partition *p) {
375:  if (!p)
376:    return 0;
377:  static const uint8_t nexs_d1[4] = {0x53, 0x58, 0x45, 0x4E}; /* "NEXS" LE */
378:  for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++)
379:    if (p->type_guid[i] != nexs_d1[i])
380:      return 0;
381:  /* data3 + data4 pin the rest of the namespace, so a coincidental match on
382:   * the first four bytes cannot be mistaken for one of our roles. */
383:  if (p->type_guid[6] != 0x58 || p->type_guid[7] != 0x4E)
384:    return 0;
385:  return (uint16_t)((uint16_t)p->type_guid[4] |
386:                    ((uint16_t)p->type_guid[5] << 8));
387:}
388:
389:/*
390: * partition_find_by_role - locate a partition by what it IS.
391: *
392: * This is the seam that retires GPT-02: callers stop passing an index whose
393: * meaning silently differs between the GPT and MBR paths, and stop depending on
394: * the physical ordering of the table.  An installer may lay the disk out in any
395: * order, and re-partitioning cannot move the root out from under the kernel.
396: */
397:struct partition *partition_find_by_role(uint16_t role) {
398:  if (role == 0)
399:    return NULL;
400:  for (int i = 0; i < num_partitions; i++)
401:    if (partition_role(&partitions[i]) == role)
402:      return &partitions[i];
403:  return NULL;
404:}
405:

@@@ kernel/fs/procfs.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/fs/procfs.c
3: * /proc — a synthetic namespace provider: live processes as TYPED capability
4: * objects (the centrality model, ASTRA §6.2/§7; plan Stage 7 "everything in the
5: * namespace").  A path /proc/<pid> resolves (object_at) to an OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS
6: * object; reading it goes THROUGH the object/capability mechanism
7: * (sys_object_read on the PROCESS handle, which reports the live state) — this
8: * is NOT a side-channel that reformats process_pool into a fake file.
9: *
10: * Capability model: acquiring a /proc/<pid> handle is gated exactly like the
11: * OS1_NS_PROC namespace (handle_create) — a destructive (WRITE/DESTROY) handle
12: * needs kill authority; a READ status handle only needs the process to exist;
13: * the read itself needs OS1_RIGHT_READ.  No partition (synthetic), read-only
14: * (write/unlink unsupported).  Mounted at /proc by procfs_init().
15: */
16:#include <kernel/types.h>
17:#include <kernel/vfs.h>
18:#include <kernel/sched.h>
19:#include <kernel/procfs.h>
20:#include <kernel/printk.h>
21:#include <kernel/string.h>
22:#include <object.h> /* OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS */
23:
24:/* Skip leading slashes; return the first path segment start. */
25:static const char *procfs_skip_slashes(const char *p) {
26:  while (*p == '/')
27:    p++;
28:  return p;
29:}
30:
31:/*
32: * procfs_object_at - map a /proc-relative path to the typed object it names.
33: *   "/"        -> the directory (-2)
34: *   "/<pid>"   -> OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS (if the process is live)
35: * One level deep only (a deeper path is -1, not found).
36: */
37:static int procfs_object_at(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path,
38:                            struct vfs_objref *out) {
39:  (void)mnt;
40:  const char *p = procfs_skip_slashes(path);
41:  if (*p == '\0')
42:    return -2; /* /proc itself is a directory */
43:  for (const char *q = p; *q; q++)
44:    if (*q == '/')
45:      return -1; /* only /proc/<pid>, no deeper nodes yet */
46:  int pid = atoi(p);
47:  struct ps_info pi;
48:  if (pid <= 0 || proc_get_info(pid, &pi) != 0)
49:    return -1;
50:  out->obj_type = OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS;
51:  out->pid = pid;
52:  return 0;
53:}
54:
55:/*
56: * procfs_open - the fs_ops contract requires open().  /proc is a directory; a
57: * /<pid> entry is really a PROCESS object (the byte read goes through that
58: * object, not this node), so we expose it as a zero-size FILE node only so a
59: * stat of the path succeeds.
60: */
61:static int procfs_open(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path,
62:                       struct vfs_node *out) {
63:  const char *p = procfs_skip_slashes(path);
64:  if (*p == '\0') {
65:    out->mnt = mnt;
66:    out->id = 0;
67:    out->type = VFS_TYPE_DIR;
68:    out->size = 0;
69:    return 0;
70:  }
71:  int pid = atoi(p);
72:  struct ps_info pi;
73:  if (pid <= 0 || proc_get_info(pid, &pi) != 0)
74:    return -1;
75:  out->mnt = mnt;
76:  out->id = (uint64_t)pid;
77:  out->type = VFS_TYPE_FILE;
78:  out->size = 0;
79:  return 0;
80:}
81:
82:/* procfs_list - the live pids (each is a PROCESS capability object). */
83:static int procfs_list(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path, char *buf,
84:                       uint32_t size) {
85:  (void)mnt;
86:  const char *p = procfs_skip_slashes(path);
87:  if (*p != '\0')
88:    return -2; /* /proc/<pid> is an object, not a directory */
89:  int pids[MAX_PROCESSES];
90:  int n = proc_enum_pids(pids, MAX_PROCESSES);
91:  size_t off = 0;
92:  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
93:    char num[16];
94:    int nl = snprintf(num, sizeof(num), "%d", pids[i]);
95:    if (nl <= 0 || off + (size_t)nl + 2 > size)
96:      break;
97:    if (off)
98:      buf[off++] = ' ';
99:    memcpy(buf + off, num, (size_t)nl);
100:    off += (size_t)nl;
101:  }
102:  buf[off] = '\0';
103:  return (int)off;
104:}
105:
106:static const struct fs_ops procfs_ops = {
107:    .name = "procfs",
108:    .mount = NULL, /* synthetic: mounted via vfs_mount_at, never probed */
109:    .open = procfs_open,
110:    .read = NULL,  /* a /proc/<pid> read goes through the PROCESS object */
111:    .write = NULL, /* read-only namespace */
112:    .list = procfs_list,
113:    .unlink = NULL,
114:    .object_at = procfs_object_at, /* path -> typed PROCESS object */
115:};
116:
117:void procfs_init(void) {
118:  /* A mount that fails leaves /proc simply absent, and every consumer then
119:   * reports "no such file" for a namespace the system believes it published.
120:   * The failure has to be named where it happens. */
121:  if (vfs_mount_at("/proc", &procfs_ops, NULL) != 0)
122:    pr_err("%s", "procfs: /proc could not be mounted — process introspection is "
123:           "unavailable\n");
124:}
125:

@@@ kernel/fs/vfs.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/fs/vfs.c
3: * Virtual Filesystem Switch — provider registry, mount table, dispatch.
4: *
5: * Purpose (VFS-01 resolved):
6: *   The kernel-core side of the filesystem provider contract defined in
7: *   <kernel/vfs.h>.  Holds the registered fs drivers and the mount table,
8: *   probes partitions at vfs_init(), and dispatches the vfs_* API through
9: *   the mounted provider's fs_ops.  Also provides vfs_resolve_path(), the
10: *   path canonicalisation helper used by the syscall layer.
11: *
12: * Role in the stack (ASTRA, docs/ASTRA.md):
13: *   syscall_dispatch.c / elf.c  →  vfs_* (this file)  →  fs_ops provider
14: *   (ext4 today).  No caller outside kernel/fs/ touches ext4_* anymore.
15: *
16: * Resolution model:
17: *   Single root mount ("/"): the first registered provider that successfully
18: *   mounts a partition (probed in partition-table order) becomes the root.
19: *   Multiple mounts/mountpoints are a later step (the table is already
20: *   sized for them).
21: *
22: * Key invariants:
23: *   - vfs_resolve_path output is always NUL-terminated.
24: *   - Normalisation is done entirely in-place on a stack copy; the original
25: *     'in' string is never modified.
26: *   - parts[] stores interior pointers into temp[]; they remain valid for the
27: *     lifetime of the normalisation loop because temp[] is on the same frame.
28: *
29: * Known issues:
30: *   VFS-02  RESOLVED (Phase B2): vfs_resolve_path() guards current_process;
31: *           a relative path resolved from kernel context (no process) is now
32: *           treated as relative to "/".
33: *   VFS-03  (W2 BAD-IMPL) parts[32] limits the resolved path to 32 components;
34: *           deeper paths are silently truncated with no error returned.
35: *   VFS-04  (W1 REFINE) temp[256] and normalized[256] are both stack-allocated.
36: *           A CWD of 127 bytes + in of 128 bytes = 255 chars before the NUL;
37: *           strncat guards the overflow but silently truncates the result.
38: */
39:#include <kernel/types.h>
40:#include <kernel/sched.h>
41:#include <kernel/spinlock.h>
42:#include <kernel/string.h>
43:#include <kernel/vfs.h>
44:#include <kernel/gpt.h>
45:#include <kernel/kmalloc.h>
46:#include <kernel/printk.h>
47:
48:/* Registered filesystem drivers (providers).  Registration happens at boot,
49: * single-threaded, before vfs_init(); no locking needed. */
50:#define VFS_MAX_FS 4
51:static const struct fs_ops *fs_drivers[VFS_MAX_FS];
52:static int fs_driver_count;
53:
54:/* Mount table.  mounts[0] is the root mount (established once at vfs_init()
55: * and never torn down); further slots take vfs_mount_at() mounts, which CAN
56: * be retired by vfs_umount().  mounts_lock guards slot claim/retire and the
57: * resolve+active_ops increment, so a dispatch can never run on a mount being
58: * torn down (see vfs_acquire/vfs_release). */
59:#define VFS_MAX_MOUNTS 4
60:static struct vfs_mount mounts[VFS_MAX_MOUNTS];
61:static DEFINE_SPINLOCK(mounts_lock);
62:
63:/*
64: * vfs_register_fs - register a filesystem provider.
65: * Returns 0, or -1 if the driver table is full or ops is malformed.
66: */
67:int vfs_register_fs(const struct fs_ops *ops) {
68:  if (!ops || !ops->mount || !ops->open || !ops->read) {
69:    pr_err("%s", "VFS: rejecting malformed fs_ops registration\n");
70:    return -1;
71:  }
72:  if (fs_driver_count >= VFS_MAX_FS) {
73:    pr_err("%s", "VFS: fs driver table full\n");
74:    return -1;
75:  }
76:  fs_drivers[fs_driver_count++] = ops;
77:  return 0;
78:}
79:
80:/*
81: * vfs_init - probe partitions and establish the root mount.
82: *
83: * For each partition (table order), each registered provider gets a chance
84: * to mount it.  The first success becomes the root.  Providers must probe
85: * quietly (a partition that is simply not their format is normal) and fail
86: * loudly only on recognised-but-unsupported filesystems.
87: */
88:/* __vfs_try_mount_root - try every FS provider on `p` as the root mount.
89: * Returns 1 if one took it.  `idx` is only for the log line. */
90:static int __vfs_try_mount_root(struct partition *p, int idx) {
91:  if (!p)
92:    return 0;
93:  for (int d = 0; d < fs_driver_count; d++) {
94:    struct vfs_mount *mnt = &mounts[0];
95:    mnt->ops = fs_drivers[d];
96:    mnt->part_index = (uint32_t)idx;
97:    mnt->fs_private = NULL;
98:    mnt->mountpoint = "/"; /* the root mount (Plan 9 namespace fallback) */
99:    if (fs_drivers[d]->mount(mnt, p) == 0) {
100:      mnt->in_use = 1;
101:      pr_info("VFS: mounted %s on partition %d as /\n", fs_drivers[d]->name,
102:              idx);
103:      return 1;
104:    }
105:    mnt->ops = NULL;
106:  }
107:  return 0;
108:}
109:
110:/*
111: * vfs_init - establish the root mount.
112: *
113: * BY ROLE first (F3): the partition whose type GUID says NEXS_ROLE_ROOT becomes
114: * "/", whatever its position in the table.  The old behaviour — mount the first
115: * partition any provider accepts — was safe only while exactly one filesystem
116: * existed on the disk.  It is the mechanism behind GPT-02's warning that
117: * "changing the disk image layout will silently mount the wrong partition", and
118: * it would break the moment the installer adds a second ext4 (MACHINE, USR):
119: * whichever was probed first would silently become the system root.
120: *
121: * The scan is KEPT as a fallback, and that is deliberate rather than defensive:
122: * images that predate roles must still boot, and so must the release ISO, whose
123: * rootfs arrives as a RAM disk built by the same mkdisk.  Falling back is
124: * announced in the log so an unroled disk is visible, not silent.
125: */
126:void vfs_init(void) {
127:  if (fs_driver_count == 0) {
128:    pr_err("%s", "VFS: no filesystem providers registered\n");
129:    return;
130:  }
131:
132:  struct partition *root = partition_find_by_role(NEXS_ROLE_ROOT);
133:  if (root) {
134:    if (__vfs_try_mount_root(root, (int)root->index))
135:      return;
136:    /* A partition that DECLARES it is the root but carries no mountable
137:     * filesystem is a corrupt install, not a reason to go looking elsewhere:
138:     * mounting some other partition as "/" would hide the damage and run the
139:     * system on the wrong tree. */
140:    pr_err("%s", "VFS: NEXS-ROOT partition has no mountable filesystem\n");
141:    return;
142:  }
143:
144:  pr_info("%s", "VFS: no NEXS-ROOT partition; falling back to first mountable "
145:                "(pre-role image)\n");
146:  for (int i = 0; i < num_partitions; i++) {
147:    if (__vfs_try_mount_root(gpt_get_partition(i), i))
148:      return;
149:  }
150:  pr_err("%s", "VFS: no mountable filesystem found on any partition\n");
151:}
152:
153:/*
154: * vfs_mount_at - mount a provider at an absolute path (Plan 9 namespace mount).
155: * mounts[0] is the root; further slots take synthetic/extra mounts.  Stateless
156: * synthetic servers (e.g. regfs) pass fs_private = NULL and need no ops->mount.
157: */
158:int vfs_mount_at(const char *mountpoint, const struct fs_ops *ops,
159:                 void *fs_private) {
160:  if (!mountpoint || !ops || !ops->open) {
161:    pr_err("%s", "VFS: rejecting malformed vfs_mount_at\n");
162:    return -1;
163:  }
164:  uint64_t flags;
165:  spin_lock_irqsave(&mounts_lock, &flags);
166:  for (int i = 1; i < VFS_MAX_MOUNTS; i++) { /* slot 0 is the root */
167:    if (mounts[i].in_use)
168:      continue;
169:    mounts[i].ops = ops;
170:    mounts[i].fs_private = fs_private;
171:    mounts[i].mountpoint = mountpoint;
172:    mounts[i].part_index = 0;
173:    mounts[i].active_ops = 0;
174:    mounts[i].in_use = 1;
175:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&mounts_lock, flags);
176:    pr_info("VFS: mounted %s at %s\n", ops->name, mountpoint);
177:    return 0;
178:  }
179:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&mounts_lock, flags);
180:  pr_err("%s", "VFS: mount table full\n");
181:  return -1;
182:}
183:
184:/*
185: * vfs_umount - retire a NON-root mount by exact mountpoint match.
186: *
187: * Under mounts_lock: refuse while path operations are in flight (-EBUSY —
188: * vfs_acquire holds the same lock to resolve+count, so no new operation can
189: * slip in), then retire the slot.  The provider's optional umount op runs
190: * AFTER the unlock on a stack copy of the retired mount: no new dispatch can
191: * reach it, and provider teardown (kfree etc.) never runs under a spinlock.
192: * Root ("/") teardown is deliberately refused until the ISO-boot rework
193: * (docs/userland-port PLAN phase 4).
194: */
195:int vfs_umount(const char *mountpoint) {
196:  if (!mountpoint || strcmp(mountpoint, "/") == 0)
197:    return -1;
198:  uint64_t flags;
199:  spin_lock_irqsave(&mounts_lock, &flags);
200:  for (int i = 1; i < VFS_MAX_MOUNTS; i++) { /* slot 0 is the root */
201:    if (!mounts[i].in_use || !mounts[i].mountpoint ||
202:        strcmp(mounts[i].mountpoint, mountpoint) != 0)
203:      continue;
204:    if (mounts[i].active_ops != 0) {
205:      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&mounts_lock, flags);
206:      return -EBUSY;
207:    }
208:    struct vfs_mount retired = mounts[i];
209:    mounts[i].in_use = 0;
210:    mounts[i].ops = NULL;
211:    mounts[i].fs_private = NULL;
212:    mounts[i].mountpoint = NULL;
213:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&mounts_lock, flags);
214:    if (retired.ops->umount)
215:      retired.ops->umount(&retired);
216:    pr_info("VFS: unmounted %s from %s\n", retired.ops->name, mountpoint);
217:    return 0;
218:  }
219:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&mounts_lock, flags);
220:  return -1;
221:}
222:
223:/*
224: * vfs_resolve - find the mount responsible for 'path' (LONGEST matching
225: * mountpoint; the root "/" is the fallback) and hand back the path relative to
226: * that mount (always with a leading '/'; the root mount passes the path through
227: * unchanged so existing providers see absolute paths exactly as before).
228: * Matching is component-aware: "/reg" matches "/reg" and "/reg/x", not "/regfoo".
229: */
230:static struct vfs_mount *vfs_resolve(const char *path, const char **rel) {
231:  struct vfs_mount *best = NULL;
232:  size_t best_len = 0;
233:  for (int i = 0; i < VFS_MAX_MOUNTS; i++) {
234:    if (!mounts[i].in_use || !mounts[i].mountpoint)
235:      continue;
236:    const char *mp = mounts[i].mountpoint;
237:    size_t mlen = strlen(mp);
238:    int match;
239:    if (mlen == 1 && mp[0] == '/') {
240:      match = 1; /* root matches everything */
241:    } else {
242:      match = (strncmp(path, mp, mlen) == 0 &&
243:               (path[mlen] == '/' || path[mlen] == '\0'));
244:    }
245:    if (match && (best == NULL || mlen >= best_len)) {
246:      best = &mounts[i];
247:      best_len = mlen;
248:    }
249:  }
250:  if (!best) {
251:    *rel = path;
252:    return NULL;
253:  }
254:  if (best_len <= 1) {
255:    *rel = path; /* root "/": providers keep seeing the full absolute path */
256:  } else {
257:    *rel = path + best_len;   /* "/reg/x" -> "/x"; "/reg" -> "" */
258:    if (**rel == '\0')
259:      *rel = "/";
260:  }
261:  return best;
262:}
263:
264:/*
265: * vfs_acquire / vfs_release - resolve + pin a mount for one path operation.
266: * The resolve and the active_ops increment happen under mounts_lock, so
267: * vfs_umount (same lock) can never observe active_ops == 0 while a dispatch
268: * is between resolve and provider call.  Release is a plain atomic decrement:
269: * umount only needs the count to eventually reach zero, and a torn-down slot
270: * is never handed out again while pinned.
271: */
272:static struct vfs_mount *vfs_acquire(const char *path, const char **rel) {
273:  uint64_t flags;
274:  spin_lock_irqsave(&mounts_lock, &flags);
275:  struct vfs_mount *mnt = vfs_resolve(path, rel);
276:  if (mnt)
277:    __sync_fetch_and_add(&mnt->active_ops, 1);
278:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&mounts_lock, flags);
279:  return mnt;
280:}
281:
282:static void vfs_release(struct vfs_mount *mnt) {
283:  if (mnt)
284:    __sync_fetch_and_sub(&mnt->active_ops, 1);
285:}
286:
287:/*
288: * vfs_open - resolve an absolute normalized path to a vfs_node.
289: * Returns 0 on success, negative on error/not-found.
290: */
291:int vfs_open(const char *path, struct vfs_node *out) {
292:  if (!path || !out)
293:    return -1;
294:  const char *rel;
295:  struct vfs_mount *mnt = vfs_acquire(path, &rel);
296:  if (!mnt)
297:    return -1;
298:  int rc = mnt->ops->open ? mnt->ops->open(mnt, rel, out) : -1;
299:  vfs_release(mnt);
300:  return rc;
301:}
302:
303:/*
304: * vfs_resolve_object - resolve a path to the TYPED object it names.  A provider
305: * with an object_at op maps the path to its native object type (e.g. /proc/<pid>
306: * -> OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS); a provider without one (ext4, regfs) yields a plain FILE
307: * object via open().  This is the namespace→object bridge behind open() ≡
308: * handle_create(OS1_NS_FS): everything resolvable in the namespace is an object.
309: * Returns 0 (out filled), -1 not found, -2 the path is a directory.
310: */
311:int vfs_resolve_object(const char *path, struct vfs_objref *out) {
312:  if (!path || !out)
313:    return -1;
314:  const char *rel;
315:  struct vfs_mount *mnt = vfs_acquire(path, &rel);
316:  if (!mnt || !mnt->ops) {
317:    vfs_release(mnt);
318:    return -1;
319:  }
320:  int rc;
321:  if (mnt->ops->object_at) {
322:    rc = mnt->ops->object_at(mnt, rel, out);
323:  } else if (!mnt->ops->open) {
324:    rc = -1;
325:  } else {
326:    /* Default: the provider's paths are plain FILE objects. */
327:    struct vfs_node node;
328:    if (mnt->ops->open(mnt, rel, &node) != 0) {
329:      rc = -1;
330:    } else {
331:      out->obj_type = OBJ_TYPE_FILE;
332:      out->node = node;
333:      rc = (node.type == VFS_TYPE_DIR) ? -2 : 0;
334:    }
335:  }
336:  vfs_release(mnt);
337:  return rc;
338:}
339:
340:/*
341: * vfs_read - random-access read from an open node.
342: * Returns bytes read (clamped at EOF) or negative on error.
343: */
344:int vfs_read(struct vfs_node *node, uint64_t offset, void *buf,
345:             uint32_t size) {
346:  if (!node || !node->mnt || !node->mnt->ops->read)
347:    return -1;
348:  return node->mnt->ops->read(node, offset, buf, size);
349:}
350:
351:/*
352: * vfs_read_file - path-based convenience read.
353: * buf==NULL or size==0 returns the file size without reading (userland ABI
354: * of SYS_FILE_READ — see user/sys/lib/lib.c file_read).
355: */
356:int vfs_read_file(const char *path, void *buf, uint32_t size,
357:                  uint64_t offset) {
358:  struct vfs_node node;
359:  if (vfs_open(path, &node) != 0)
360:    return -1;
361:  if (buf == NULL || size == 0)
362:    return (int)node.size;
363:  return vfs_read(&node, offset, buf, size);
364:}
365:
366:/*
367: * vfs_write_allowed - THE single write-authority seam for every VFS
368: * write-class entry point (S-ALIGN F6): open-for-write and MUTATE-handle
369: * acquisition (SYS_OPEN → sys_handle_create OS1_NS_FS).
370: * Policy lives only here so the entry points cannot drift:
371: *   - mutating the filesystem needs CAP_FS_WRITE (USR-SEC-03 #79);
372: *   - the binary trees /sys,/bin are immutable for non-machine callers
373: *     (EXT4-02/ABI-04: services + init chain cannot be overwritten).
374: * 'resolved_path' must already be vfs_resolve_path()-canonical.  A NULL
375: * current_process (in-kernel caller) passes: kernel = machine identity.
376: * Use-time writes on an already-held FILE handle are deliberately NOT
377: * re-checked (seL4/Mach delegation: the handle's rights are the authority).
378: * Returns 0, -EPERM (no capability) or -EACCES (protected tree).
379: */
380:int vfs_write_allowed(const char *resolved_path) {
381:  if (!proc_has_cap(current_process, CAP_FS_WRITE))
382:    return -EPERM;
383:  if (proc_is_machine(current_process))
384:    return 0; /* machine identity: full filesystem authority */
385:
386:  /* /tmp, /var/tmp: scratch space POSIX-style, world-writable (sticky-bit
387:   * convention).  coreutils/gnulib assume it's writable by anyone
388:   * (mktemp, mkstemp, sort/cp/mv temp files, etc.) — without this branch
389:   * any command touching /tmp is blocked by the generic ACL further down. */
390:  if (strncmp(resolved_path, "/tmp/", 5) == 0 ||
391:      strcmp(resolved_path, "/tmp") == 0 ||
392:      strncmp(resolved_path, "/var/tmp/", 9) == 0 ||
393:      strcmp(resolved_path, "/var/tmp") == 0) {
394:    return 0;
395:  }
396:
397:  /* Tree ACL (maintainer policy, 2026-07-23 — the LEVEL model's filesystem
398:   * half; the capability mask is the other half):
399:   *   machine           full authority (handled above).
400:   *   /home             every CAP_FS_WRITE holder writes here — except GUEST,
401:   *                     confined to /home/shared.  (Per-user partitions
402:   *                     /mnt/usrN/home are the forward work, B2.3.)
403:   *   /sys/bin,/system  MACHINE only — even ROOT is refused.  /sys/bin is the
404:   *                     supervised boot chain (init/services must not be
405:   *                     swappable out from under init); /system is the machine
406:   *                     configuration tree.  These two are the "root has full
407:   *                     access EXCEPT these" the maintainer named.
408:   *   /sys,/bin,else    ROOT or machine; closed to ordinary users.
409:   * Exact-match guards cover the directory nodes themselves (unlink/create
410:   * of "/bin" etc.), not just children. */
411:  if (strncmp(resolved_path, "/home/", 6) == 0 ||
412:      strcmp(resolved_path, "/home") == 0) {
413:    if (current_process && current_process->level >= PLVL_GUEST &&
414:        !(strncmp(resolved_path, "/home/shared/", 13) == 0 ||
415:          strcmp(resolved_path, "/home/shared") == 0)) {
416:      pr_warn("vfs: guest PID %d denied write outside /home/shared ('%s')\n",
417:              current_process->pid, resolved_path);
418:      return -EACCES;
419:    }
420:    return 0;
421:  }
422:  /* B2.2: /system joins /sys/bin as MACHINE-only — root is refused here, which
423:   * is the "root full access EXCEPT /sys/bin and /system" rule.  Guarding the
424:   * path now (before /system is populated — B2.3 owns its creation/layout) is
425:   * correct and harmless: nothing writes it today, and the ACL must not depend
426:   * on the tree already existing. */
427:  if (strncmp(resolved_path, "/sys/bin/", 9) == 0 ||
428:      strcmp(resolved_path, "/sys/bin") == 0 ||
429:      strncmp(resolved_path, "/system/", 8) == 0 ||
430:      strcmp(resolved_path, "/system") == 0) {
431:    pr_warn("vfs: PID %d denied write to machine-only path '%s'\n",
432:            current_process ? current_process->pid : 0, resolved_path);
433:    return -EACCES;
434:  }
435:  /* Explicit system trees (maintainer-requested branch): /bin and /sys
436:   * (incl. /sys/lib) are the named root-only trees. */
437:  if (strncmp(resolved_path, "/sys/", 5) == 0 ||
438:      strcmp(resolved_path, "/sys") == 0 ||
439:      strncmp(resolved_path, "/bin/", 5) == 0 ||
440:      strcmp(resolved_path, "/bin") == 0) {
441:    if (!proc_is_privileged(current_process)) {
442:      pr_warn("vfs: PID %d denied write to root-only path '%s'\n",
443:              current_process ? current_process->pid : 0, resolved_path);
444:      return -EACCES;
445:    }
446:    return 0;
447:  }
448:  /* Every remaining tree outside /home (/etc, /fonts, /lib, "/", ...) is
449:   * equally closed to ordinary users: only /home has expanded authority. */
450:  if (!proc_is_privileged(current_process)) {
451:    pr_warn("vfs: PID %d denied write outside /home ('%s')\n",
452:            current_process ? current_process->pid : 0, resolved_path);
453:    return -EACCES;
454:  }
455:  return 0;
456:}
457:
458:/*
459: * vfs_write_file - path-based write through the provider.
460: * Returns bytes written or negative; -1 if the provider has no write support.
461: */
462:int vfs_write_file(const char *path, const void *buf, uint32_t size,
463:                   uint64_t offset) {
464:  const char *rel;
465:  struct vfs_mount *mnt = vfs_acquire(path, &rel);
466:  if (!mnt)
467:    return -1;
468:  int rc = mnt->ops->write ? mnt->ops->write(mnt, rel, offset, buf, size) : -1;
469:  vfs_release(mnt);
470:  return rc;
471:}

473:/*
474: * vfs_list_dir - list a directory through the provider.
475: * Returns the formatted length, -1 not found, -2 not a directory.
476: */
477:/* mount_child_of - if mount path 'mp' sits DIRECTLY inside directory 'dir', copy
478: * its leaf name into 'leaf' and return 1; else 0.  Makes a mount visible in its
479: * parent's listing (Plan 9: "ls /" shows "reg" for the /reg mount). */
480:static int mount_child_of(const char *mp, const char *dir, char *leaf,
481:                          size_t leafsize) {
482:  const char *last = mp;
483:  for (const char *p = mp; *p; p++)
484:    if (*p == '/')
485:      last = p;
486:  if (last == mp) { /* mp like "/reg": parent is "/" */
487:    if (strcmp(dir, "/") != 0)
488:      return 0;
489:  } else {
490:    size_t plen = (size_t)(last - mp);
491:    char parent[128];
492:    if (plen >= sizeof(parent))
493:      plen = sizeof(parent) - 1;
494:    memcpy(parent, mp, plen);
495:    parent[plen] = '\0';
496:    if (strcmp(parent, dir) != 0)
497:      return 0;
498:  }
499:  const char *name = last + 1;
500:  if (!*name)
501:    return 0;
502:  strncpy(leaf, name, leafsize - 1);
503:  leaf[leafsize - 1] = '\0';
504:  return 1;
505:}
506:
507:int vfs_list_dir(const char *path, char *buf, uint32_t size) {
508:  const char *rel;
509:  struct vfs_mount *mnt = vfs_acquire(path, &rel);
510:  if (!mnt)
511:    return -1;
512:  if (!mnt->ops->list) {
513:    vfs_release(mnt);
514:    return -1;
515:  }
516:  int res = mnt->ops->list(mnt, rel, buf, size);
517:  vfs_release(mnt);
518:  if (res < 0)
519:    return res;
520:
521:  /* Append any mounts that live directly under 'path' so they show up in the
522:   * listing (a synthetic mount like /reg is not in its parent provider's dir).
523:   * Under mounts_lock: slots can now be retired by vfs_umount, so the
524:   * in_use/mountpoint pair must be read atomically with respect to it. */
525:  size_t off = (size_t)res;
526:  uint64_t lflags;
527:  spin_lock_irqsave(&mounts_lock, &lflags);
528:  for (int i = 0; i < VFS_MAX_MOUNTS; i++) {
529:    if (!mounts[i].in_use || !mounts[i].mountpoint || &mounts[i] == mnt)
530:      continue;
531:    char leaf[64];
532:    if (!mount_child_of(mounts[i].mountpoint, path, leaf, sizeof(leaf)))
533:      continue;
534:    size_t ll = strlen(leaf);
535:    if (off + ll + 2 >= size)
536:      break;
537:    if (off && buf[off - 1] != ' ')
538:      buf[off++] = ' ';
539:    memcpy(buf + off, leaf, ll);
540:    off += ll;
541:    buf[off++] = ' ';
542:    buf[off] = '\0';
543:  }
544:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&mounts_lock, lflags);
545:  return (int)off;
546:}
547:
548:/*
549: * vfs_unlink - remove the file/node at 'path' through the responsible mount.
550: * Returns 0, or negative (provider has no unlink, or its own error).
551: */
552:int vfs_unlink(const char *path) {
553:  const char *rel;
554:  struct vfs_mount *mnt = vfs_acquire(path, &rel);
555:  /* EXT4-ERRNO-01: a bare -1 IS -EPERM (errno 1).  That mattered twice over —
556:   * userland could not tell the causes apart, AND OS1_report_error classifies
557:   * BY errno, so every provider failure was filed as an EPERM policy denial
558:   * (amber warn) whatever it really was.  No mount is -ENOENT; a provider that
559:   * does not implement removal is -ENOSYS.  The provider's own value passes
560:   * through untouched. */
561:  if (!mnt)
562:    return -ENOENT;
563:  int rc = mnt->ops->unlink ? mnt->ops->unlink(mnt, rel) : -ENOSYS;
564:  vfs_release(mnt);
565:  return rc;
566:}
567:
568:/*
569: * vfs_create - create an empty file/dir at 'path' through the responsible
570: * mount's provider (issue #126 / NOTE(M4.5-FS-WRITE)).
571: * Returns 0, or negative (provider has no create support, or its own error).
572: */
573:int vfs_create(const char *path, uint32_t type) {
574:  const char *rel;
575:  struct vfs_mount *mnt = vfs_acquire(path, &rel);
576:  /* EXT4-ERRNO-01, as vfs_unlink above. */
577:  if (!mnt)
578:    return -ENOENT;
579:  int rc = mnt->ops->create ? mnt->ops->create(mnt, rel, type) : -ENOSYS;
580:  vfs_release(mnt);
581:  return rc;
582:}

589:  if (vfs_open(path, &node) != 0)
590:    return -1;
591:  if (st) {
592:    st->size = node.size;
593:    st->type = node.type;
594:  }
595:  return 0;
596:}
