598:/*
599: * vfs_resolve_path - canonicalise a raw user path into an absolute path string.
600: *
601: * @in:   input path (absolute or relative; not modified).
602: * @out:  output buffer; receives the NUL-terminated absolute path.
603: * @size: capacity of out[], including the NUL terminator.
604: *
605: * Preconditions:
606: *   - out != NULL, size >= 1.
607: *   - If in is relative and a current process exists, its cwd must be a
608: *     valid NUL-terminated string.  Without a current process (kernel
609: *     context) relative paths resolve from "/" (FIX VFS-02).
610: *
611: * Algorithm:
612: *   1. Build temp[] = (absolute ? in : cwd + "/" + in), truncated to 255 chars.
613: *   2. Walk temp[] splitting on '/', accumulating component pointers in
614: *      parts[0..31].  ".." decrements part_count; "." is skipped.
615: *      NOTE(VFS-03): parts[] has only 32 slots; the 33rd and later components
616: *      are silently dropped — no error is returned to the caller.
617: *   3. Reassemble parts[] into normalized[] with leading '/'.
618: *   4. strncpy into out[]; force-NUL-terminate at out[size-1].
619: *      NOTE(VFS-04): Both temp[] and normalized[] are 256-byte stack buffers.
620: *      A CWD near 128 bytes joined with 'in' near 128 bytes will be silently
621: *      truncated by strncat before the normalisation loop starts.
622: *
623: * Side effects: none (no disk I/O, no locks).
624: *
625: * Returns: void; result is written to out[].
626: *
627: * Path Resolution:
628: * - If path starts with '/', it's absolute.
629: * - Otherwise, it's relative to current_process->cwd.
630: * - Normalizes . and ..
631: */
632:void vfs_resolve_path(const char *in, char *out, size_t size) {
633:    /* temp[]: working copy of the unsplit path; max 255 chars + NUL.
634:     * NOTE(VFS-04): 256-byte stack buffer; CWD + "/" + in > 255 chars
635:     * will be silently truncated by strncat (the -1 guard below). */
636:    char temp[256];
637:    if (in[0] == '/') {
638:        /* Absolute path: copy verbatim into temp; strncpy NUL-pads. */
639:        strncpy(temp, in, sizeof(temp));
640:    } else {
641:        /* Relative path: prepend current working directory.
642:         * FIX(VFS-02): kernel-context callers (boot, no current process) have
643:         * no cwd — resolve relative to "/" instead of dereferencing NULL. */
644:        if (current_process) {
645:            strncpy(temp, current_process->cwd, sizeof(temp));
646:        } else {
647:            strncpy(temp, "/", sizeof(temp));
648:        }
649:        size_t len = strlen(temp);
650:        /* Ensure exactly one '/' separator between CWD and 'in'. */
651:        if (len > 0 && temp[len-1] != '/') {
652:            strncat(temp, "/", sizeof(temp) - len - 1);
653:        }
654:        strncat(temp, in, sizeof(temp) - strlen(temp) - 1);
655:    }
656:    /* Force NUL-termination in case strncpy filled all 256 bytes. */
657:    temp[sizeof(temp)-1] = '\0';
658:
659:    /* Normalize path: remove redundant /./ and handle /../ */
660:    /* parts[32]: array of interior pointers into temp[], each pointing to
661:     * one decoded path component (NUL-terminated in-place at the '/' char).
662:     * NOTE(VFS-03): capped at 32 slots; the 33rd component is silently
663:     * dropped because the (part_count < 32) guard skips the assignment. */
664:    char *parts[32];
665:    int part_count = 0;
666:
667:    char *s = temp;
668:    /* Skip the leading '/' so strtok-style splitting starts on the first
669:     * component name, not an empty string before the root slash. */
670:    if (*s == '/') s++;
671:
672:    char *token = s;
673:    while (token && *token) {
674:        /* NUL-terminate this component in-place; next points past the '/'. */
675:        char *next = strchr(token, '/');
676:        if (next) *next = '\0';
677:
678:        if (strcmp(token, "..") == 0) {
679:            /* Parent: pop last component (floor at root, never below 0). */
680:            if (part_count > 0) part_count--;
681:        } else if (strcmp(token, ".") != 0 && strlen(token) > 0) {
682:            /* Normal component: store interior pointer into temp[].
683:             * The pointer is valid until the function returns (temp is on
684:             * the same stack frame and is not modified after this loop). */
685:            if (part_count < 32) parts[part_count++] = token;
686:        }
687:
688:        if (next) token = next + 1;
689:        else break;
690:    }
691:
692:    /* Reassemble the canonical path directly into out[] in ONE bounded pass:
693:     * "/" then each component separated by "/".  This replaces the previous
694:     * build-into-a-256B-scratch-then-strncpy approach whose per-component
695:     * strncat + strlen rescanned the whole accumulated string every time —
696:     * O(n^2) in the component count, plus a redundant full-buffer copy.  Now
697:     * each output byte is written exactly once, bounded by 'size'. */
698:    if (size == 0) return;
699:    size_t w = 0;
700:    if (w < size - 1) out[w++] = '/';
701:    for (int i = 0; i < part_count; i++) {
702:        if (i > 0 && w < size - 1) out[w++] = '/';
703:        for (const char *p = parts[i]; *p && w < size - 1; p++)
704:            out[w++] = *p;
705:    }
706:    /* w <= size-1 here, so this NUL is always in bounds. */
707:    out[w] = '\0';
708:}

1:/*

7: * stay data-only in the compositor).  All functions are allocation-free.

12:/* Titlebar button metrics (chrome geometry, not colours). */
13:#define CHROME_BUTTON_SIZE 16
14:#define CHROME_BUTTON_GAP 6 /* px gap between the background and close buttons */

16:/* Integer sqrt by the same incremental search the shadow SDF used inline. */
17:static inline int chrome_isqrt(int v) {
18:  int root = 0;
19:  while ((root + 1) * (root + 1) <= v)
20:    root++;
21:  return root;
22:}
23:
24:int gfx_rrect_contains(int lx, int ly, int w, int h, int r) {
25:  if (r <= 0)
26:    return 1;
27:  if (lx < 0 || ly < 0 || lx >= w || ly >= h)
28:    return 0;
29:  int cx, cy;
30:  if (lx < r && ly < r) {
31:    cx = r - 1 - lx;
32:    cy = r - 1 - ly;
33:  } else if (lx >= w - r && ly < r) {
34:    cx = lx - (w - r);
35:    cy = r - 1 - ly;
36:  } else if (lx < r && ly >= h - r) {
37:    cx = r - 1 - lx;
38:    cy = ly - (h - r);
39:  } else if (lx >= w - r && ly >= h - r) {
40:    cx = lx - (w - r);
41:    cy = ly - (h - r);
42:  } else {
43:    return 1; /* not in a corner square */
44:  }
45:  return (cx * cx + cy * cy) <= (r * r);
46:}

48:void gfx_chrome_shadow_margins(int shadow_type, int shadow_size,
49:                               gfx_chrome_margins_t *out) {
50:  if (!out)
51:    return;
52:  int so = shadow_size > 0 ? shadow_size : 0;
53:  if (shadow_type == 2) {
54:    out->left = so * 2;
55:    out->right = so * 2;
56:    out->top = so * 2;
57:    out->bottom = so * 2 + so;
58:  } else if (shadow_type == 1) {
59:    out->left = so;
60:    out->right = so;
61:    out->top = so;
62:    out->bottom = so;
63:  } else {
64:    out->left = 0;
65:    out->right = so;
66:    out->top = 0;
67:    out->bottom = so;
68:  }
69:}

71:/* Clip a screen pixel against surface bounds and the exclusive clip rect. */
72:static inline int chrome_clipped(const gfx_surface_t *s,
73:                                 const gfx_rect_t *clip, int px, int py) {
74:  if (px < 0 || px >= s->width || py < 0 || py >= s->height)
75:    return 1;
76:  if (px < clip->x || px >= clip->x + clip->width || py < clip->y ||
77:      py >= clip->y + clip->height)
78:    return 1;
79:  return 0;
80:}

82:void gfx_chrome_shadow_solid(gfx_surface_t *surface, const gfx_rect_t *clip,
83:                             const gfx_rect_t *frame, int radius,
84:                             uint32_t argb) {
85:  if (!gfx_surface_valid(surface) || !clip || !frame)
86:    return;
87:  for (int sy = 0; sy < frame->height; sy++) {
88:    int py = frame->y + sy;
89:    for (int sx = 0; sx < frame->width; sx++) {
90:      int px = frame->x + sx;
91:      if (chrome_clipped(surface, clip, px, py))
92:        continue;
93:      if (!gfx_rrect_contains(sx, sy, frame->width, frame->height, radius))
94:        continue;
95:      surface->buffer[py * surface->stride + px] = argb;
96:    }
97:  }
98:}
99:
100:/* Distance from local pixel (lx,ly) to the rounded frame, minus the radius —
101: * the single-pass SDF both gradient shadows are built on. */
102:static inline int chrome_sdf_dist(int lx, int ly, int w, int h, int r) {
103:  int cx = lx;
104:  if (cx < r)
105:    cx = r;
106:  else if (cx > w - 1 - r)
107:    cx = w - 1 - r;
108:  int cy = ly;
109:  if (cy < r)
110:    cy = r;
111:  else if (cy > h - 1 - r)
112:    cy = h - 1 - r;
113:  int dx = lx - cx;
114:  int dy = ly - cy;
115:  return chrome_isqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy) - r;
116:}
117:
118:void gfx_chrome_shadow_fast(gfx_surface_t *surface, const gfx_rect_t *clip,
119:                            const gfx_rect_t *frame, int radius, int spread) {
120:  if (!gfx_surface_valid(surface) || !clip || !frame || spread <= 0)
121:    return;
122:  int dw = frame->width;
123:  int full_h = frame->height;
124:  for (int sy = -spread; sy < full_h + spread; sy++) {
125:    int py = frame->y + sy;
126:    for (int sx = -spread; sx < dw + spread; sx++) {
127:      int px = frame->x + sx;
128:      if (chrome_clipped(surface, clip, px, py))
129:        continue;
130:      if (sx >= 0 && sx < dw && sy >= 0 && sy < full_h &&
131:          gfx_rrect_contains(sx, sy, dw, full_h, radius))
132:        continue;
133:
134:      int dist = chrome_sdf_dist(sx, sy, dw, full_h, radius);
135:      if (dist <= spread) {
136:        int norm = (dist <= 0) ? 64 : ((spread - dist) * 64 / spread);
137:        uint32_t a = (0x30u * (uint32_t)norm * (uint32_t)norm) / (64u * 64u);
138:        if (a > 0)
139:          surface->buffer[py * surface->stride + px] = gl_blend_pixel(
140:              (a << 24) | 0x000000u, surface->buffer[py * surface->stride + px]);
141:      }
142:    }
143:  }
144:}
145:
146:void gfx_chrome_shadow_premium(gfx_surface_t *surface, const gfx_rect_t *clip,
147:                               const gfx_rect_t *frame, int radius,
148:                               int spread) {
149:  if (!gfx_surface_valid(surface) || !clip || !frame || spread <= 0)
150:    return;
151:  int dw = frame->width;
152:  int full_h = frame->height;
153:
154:  /* Two stacked shadows: a small dark contact one (immediate depth) and a
155:   * wide light diffuse one (ambient elevation), both offset downwards. */
156:  int spread_diffuse = spread * 2;
157:  int spread_contact = (spread > 1) ? (spread / 2) : 1;
158:  int y_off_diffuse = spread;
159:  int y_off_contact = spread_contact / 2;
160:
161:  int min_y = -spread_diffuse;
162:  int max_y = full_h + spread_diffuse + y_off_diffuse;
163:  int min_x = -spread_diffuse;
164:  int max_x = dw + spread_diffuse;
165:
166:  for (int sy = min_y; sy < max_y; sy++) {
167:    int py = frame->y + sy;
168:    for (int sx = min_x; sx < max_x; sx++) {
169:      int px = frame->x + sx;
170:      if (chrome_clipped(surface, clip, px, py))
171:        continue;
172:      if (sx >= 0 && sx < dw && sy >= 0 && sy < full_h &&
173:          gfx_rrect_contains(sx, sy, dw, full_h, radius))
174:        continue;
175:
176:      int dist_diffuse =
177:          chrome_sdf_dist(sx, sy - y_off_diffuse, dw, full_h, radius);
178:      int dist_contact =
179:          chrome_sdf_dist(sx, sy - y_off_contact, dw, full_h, radius);
180:
181:      uint32_t a_total = 0;
182:      if (dist_diffuse <= 0) {
183:        a_total += 0x24;
184:      } else if (dist_diffuse <= spread_diffuse) {
185:        int norm = (spread_diffuse - dist_diffuse) * 64 / spread_diffuse;
186:        a_total += (0x24u * (uint32_t)norm * (uint32_t)norm) / (64u * 64u);
187:      }
188:      if (dist_contact <= 0) {
189:        a_total += 0x30;
190:      } else if (dist_contact <= spread_contact) {
191:        int norm = (spread_contact - dist_contact) * 64 / spread_contact;
192:        a_total += (0x30u * (uint32_t)norm * (uint32_t)norm) / (64u * 64u);
193:      }
194:
195:      if (a_total > 0) {
196:        if (a_total > 255)
197:          a_total = 255;
198:        uint32_t shadow_color = (a_total << 24) | 0x050510u;
199:        surface->buffer[py * surface->stride + px] = gl_blend_pixel(
200:            shadow_color, surface->buffer[py * surface->stride + px]);
201:      }
202:    }
203:  }
204:
205:  /* Rim light: one faint bright row just above the frame's top edge. */
206:  {
207:    int py = frame->y - 1;
208:    for (int sx = radius; sx < dw - radius; sx++) {
209:      int px = frame->x + sx;
210:      if (chrome_clipped(surface, clip, px, py))
211:        continue;
212:      surface->buffer[py * surface->stride + px] = gl_blend_pixel(
213:          0x18FFFFFFu, surface->buffer[py * surface->stride + px]);
214:    }
215:  }
216:}
217:
218:uint32_t gfx_chrome_titlebar_tint(int shadow_type, int y, int titlebar_h,
219:                                  uint32_t base) {
220:  if (titlebar_h <= 0)
221:    return base;
222:  if (shadow_type == 1) {
223:    if (y == 0)
224:      base = gl_blend_pixel(0x20FFFFFF, base);
225:  } else if (shadow_type == 2) {
226:    if (y == 0)
227:      base = gl_blend_pixel(0x40FFFFFF, base);
228:    int grad = (y * 24) / titlebar_h;
229:    if (grad > 0)
230:      base = gl_blend_pixel(((uint32_t)grad << 24) | 0x000000, base);
231:  }
232:  return base;
233:}
234:
235:uint32_t gfx_chrome_content_separator(int shadow_type, int y, uint32_t base) {
236:  if (shadow_type == 0) {
237:    if (y == 0)
238:      base = gl_blend_pixel(0x20000000, base);
239:  } else if (shadow_type == 1) {
240:    if (y == 0)
241:      base = gl_blend_pixel(0x30000000, base);
242:    else if (y == 1)
243:      base = gl_blend_pixel(0x10000000, base);
244:  } else if (shadow_type == 2 && y < 4) {
245:    int a = (4 - y) * 16;
246:    base = gl_blend_pixel(((uint32_t)a << 24) | 0x000000, base);
247:  }
248:  return base;
249:}
250:
251:void gfx_chrome_button_geometry(int frame_x, int frame_w, int titlebar_y,
252:                                int titlebar_h, int shape, int side,
253:                                gfx_button_geometry_t *out) {
254:  if (!out)
255:    return;
256:  int btn_size = CHROME_BUTTON_SIZE;
257:  /* Smaller buttons for the square/rounded shapes. */
258:  if (shape == 1 || shape == 2)
259:    btn_size -= 2;
260:
261:  out->size = btn_size;
262:  out->top = titlebar_y + (titlebar_h - btn_size) / 2;
263:
264:  if (side == 0) {
265:    /* Buttons on the left. */
266:    int close_left = frame_x + 4;
267:    out->close_cx = close_left + btn_size / 2;
268:    out->bg_cx = out->close_cx + btn_size + CHROME_BUTTON_GAP;
269:  } else {
270:    /* Buttons on the right. */
271:    int close_right = frame_x + frame_w - 4;
272:    out->close_cx = close_right - btn_size / 2;
273:    out->bg_cx = out->close_cx - btn_size - CHROME_BUTTON_GAP;
274:  }
275:}
276:
277:int gfx_chrome_button_hit(const gfx_button_geometry_t *geometry, int x,
278:                          int y) {
279:  if (!geometry)
280:    return GFX_BUTTON_NONE;
281:  int btn_size = geometry->size;
282:  if (y < geometry->top || y >= geometry->top + btn_size)
283:    return GFX_BUTTON_NONE;
284:  int close_x = geometry->close_cx - btn_size / 2;
285:  int bg_x = geometry->bg_cx - btn_size / 2;
286:  if (x >= close_x && x < close_x + btn_size)
287:    return GFX_BUTTON_CLOSE;
288:  if (x >= bg_x && x < bg_x + btn_size)
289:    return GFX_BUTTON_BACKGROUND;
290:  return GFX_BUTTON_NONE;
291:}
292:
293:uint32_t gfx_chrome_button_pixel(const gfx_button_geometry_t *geometry,
294:                                 int shape, int x, int y, uint32_t close_argb,
295:                                 uint32_t bg_argb, int drop_shadow,
296:                                 uint32_t base) {
297:  if (!geometry)
298:    return base;
299:  int btn_size = geometry->size;
300:  int local_y = y - geometry->top;
301:  int local_x_close = x - geometry->close_cx + (btn_size / 2);
302:  int local_x_bg = x - geometry->bg_cx + (btn_size / 2);
303:
304:  if (shape == 1) {
305:    /* Pure square. */
306:    if (local_x_close >= 0 && local_x_close < btn_size && local_y >= 0 &&
307:        local_y < btn_size)
308:      return close_argb;
309:    if (local_x_bg >= 0 && local_x_bg < btn_size && local_y >= 0 &&
310:        local_y < btn_size)
311:      return bg_argb;
312:    if (drop_shadow) {
313:      if (local_y == btn_size && local_x_close >= 0 && local_x_close < btn_size)
314:        return gl_blend_pixel(0x60000000, base);
315:      if (local_y == btn_size && local_x_bg >= 0 && local_x_bg < btn_size)
316:        return gl_blend_pixel(0x60000000, base);
317:    }
318:    return base;
319:  }
320:
321:  if (shape == 2) {
322:    /* Rounded square (Material). */
323:    int corner_radius = 6;
324:    if (gfx_rrect_contains(local_x_close, local_y, btn_size, btn_size,
325:                           corner_radius))
326:      return close_argb;
327:    if (gfx_rrect_contains(local_x_bg, local_y, btn_size, btn_size,
328:                           corner_radius))
329:      return bg_argb;
330:    if (drop_shadow) {
331:      if (gfx_rrect_contains(local_x_close, local_y - 1, btn_size, btn_size,
332:                             corner_radius))
333:        return gl_blend_pixel(0x50000000, base);
334:      if (gfx_rrect_contains(local_x_bg, local_y - 1, btn_size, btn_size,
335:                             corner_radius))
336:        return gl_blend_pixel(0x50000000, base);
337:    }
338:    return base;
339:  }
340:
341:  /* Classic discs. */
342:  int radius = btn_size / 2 - 1;
343:  int ddy = y - (geometry->top + btn_size / 2);
344:  int dcx = x - geometry->close_cx;
345:  int dbx = x - geometry->bg_cx;
346:
347:  if (dcx * dcx + ddy * ddy <= radius * radius)
348:    return close_argb;
349:  if (dbx * dbx + ddy * ddy <= radius * radius)
350:    return bg_argb;
351:  if (drop_shadow) {
352:    int ddy_s = ddy - 1;
353:    if (dcx * dcx + ddy_s * ddy_s <= radius * radius + 2)
354:      return gl_blend_pixel(0x40000000, base);
355:    if (dbx * dbx + ddy_s * ddy_s <= radius * radius + 2)
356:      return gl_blend_pixel(0x40000000, base);
357:  }
358:  return base;
359:}
360:
361:void gfx_chrome_border(gfx_surface_t *surface, const gfx_rect_t *clip,
362:                       const gfx_rect_t *frame, int radius, uint32_t argb) {
363:  if (!gfx_surface_valid(surface) || !clip || !frame)
364:    return;
365:  int dw = frame->width;
366:  int full_h = frame->height;
367:  for (int ly = 0; ly < full_h; ly++) {
368:    int py = frame->y + ly;
369:    for (int lx = 0; lx < dw; lx++) {
370:      /* perimeter pixels only */
371:      int on_edge = (lx == 0 || ly == 0 || lx == dw - 1 || ly == full_h - 1);
372:      /* for rounded corners, also treat the rounded boundary as edge */
373:      int inside = gfx_rrect_contains(lx, ly, dw, full_h, radius);
374:      int inside_inset =
375:          radius ? gfx_rrect_contains(lx - 1, ly - 1, dw - 2, full_h - 2,
376:                                      radius > 0 ? radius - 1 : 0)
377:                 : (lx > 0 && ly > 0 && lx < dw - 1 && ly < full_h - 1);
378:      if (inside && (on_edge || !inside_inset)) {
379:        int px = frame->x + lx;
380:        if (!chrome_clipped(surface, clip, px, py))
381:          surface->buffer[py * surface->stride + px] = argb;
382:      }
383:    }
384:  }
385:}

1:/*
2: * kernel/graphics/compositor.c
3: * Window Compositor
4: *
5: * Manages windows and composites them to the screen.
6: */
7:#include <drivers/gpu/gpu.h>
8:#include <drivers/timer.h> /* mono_ns: motion-event rate limiting */
9:#include <drivers/virtio_input.h>
10:#include <graphics/gl.h>
11:#include <kernel/arch.h>
12:#include <kernel/compositor_style.h>
13:#include <kernel/cpu.h>

15:#include <kernel/graphics.h>
16:#include <kernel/kmalloc.h>
17:#include <kernel/pmm.h>
18:#include <kernel/printk.h>
19:#include <kernel/sched.h>
20:#include <kernel/spinlock.h>
21:#include <kernel/string.h>
22:#include <kernel/term.h>
23:#include <kernel/types.h>
24:#include <kernel/vmm.h>
25:#include <object.h> /* struct window_info, WININFO_* — windows as objects (§6.7) */
26:#include <stdint.h>
27:
28:#define MAX_WINDOWS 40
29:
30:/*
31: * GFX-COMP-RESERVE-02: MAX_WINDOWS is one flat pool shared by every caller.
32: * A stress test that opens ordinary user windows up to window_count ==
33: * MAX_WINDOWS starves compositor_create_window() for EVERYONE, including a
34: * supervised system service (nxui/dock, nxbar, the launcher) that init just
35: * respawned after a crash — its create_window() call fails exactly like an
36: * unprivileged app's would, and the service exits again (see nxui.c/nxbar.c
37: * main(): `if (g_win < 0) return 1;`).  init's backoff queue (USR-INIT-04)
38: * keeps retrying it, but it can never succeed until user windows close back
39: * below the cap — a stress test can hold the desktop chrome down indefinitely.
40: *
41: * Fix: reserve the last RESERVED_SYSTEM_SLOTS pool entries for PRIVILEGED
42: * callers only (PLVL_ROOT/PLVL_MACHINE — proc_is_privileged(), same check
43: * process.c/object.c already gate other root-only operations on).  Ordinary
44: * PLVL_USER/PLVL_GUEST windows are capped at MAX_WINDOWS -
45: * RESERVED_SYSTEM_SLOTS; a privileged caller may use the full pool.  Sized
46: * for the known supervised /sys/bin singletons (dock, nxbar, launcher) plus
47: * one spare so a destroy+recreate resize (nxui's dock_reinit / nxbar's
48: * set_window_height) never has to land in the exact instant a slot is free
49: * to avoid double-booking itself.
50: */
51:#define RESERVED_SYSTEM_SLOTS 8
52:#define MAX_USER_WINDOWS (MAX_WINDOWS - RESERVED_SYSTEM_SLOTS)

189:struct window {
190:  int id;
191:  int x, y;
192:  int width, height; /* LOGICAL surface size (the app's pixel buffer). */
193:  /* ON-SCREEN size the compositor draws the surface at (GFX-DYN-01 surface
194:   * model).  When draw_w/draw_h differ from width/height the compositor scales
195:   * the logical surface to the draw rect (the app may keep drawing at its old
196:   * size while it reallocates → fluid resize).  0 means "same as logical". */
197:  int draw_w, draw_h;
198:  int z_order;
199:  int visible;
200:  int minimized; /* If true, sent to background by the user/WM (dock-
201:                    restorable).  A minimized window has visible==0 but
202:                    stays in the table so the dock can restore it; this
203:                    distinguishes it from a window an app hid itself. */
204:  int pid;
205:  int protected;     /* If true, cannot be closed */
206:  int top_most;      /* If true, always on top and no decorations */
207:  int passive;       /* If true, click-through: never focused, never hit-tested
208:                        for input (system popups e.g. notifications). */
209:  uint32_t *buffer;  /* Window's pixel buffer */
210:  uint32_t bg_color; /* Default background color */
211:  char title[64];
212:  int radius;
213:  int has_rounded_corners;
214:
215:  /* Terminal State — VT/ANSI emulator extracted to term.c (#123). */
216:  struct terminal term;
217:
218:  /* Compositor flags */
219:  int has_alpha; /* Se 1, contiene trasparenze e non occlude i layer inferiori
220:                  */
221:};
222:
223:/* Global State */
224:static struct window windows[MAX_WINDOWS];
225:static int window_count = 0;
226:static int next_window_id = 100;
227:static volatile int compositor_dirty = 1;
228:static DEFINE_SPINLOCK(compositor_lock);
229:
230:/* Damage rect: tracks the bounding box of pixels that need GPU upload */
231:static int damage_x1 = 0, damage_y1 = 0;
232:static int damage_x2 = 0, damage_y2 = 0;
233:
234:/* Helper to expand damage region */
235:static void expand_damage(int x, int y, int w, int h) {
236:  if (x < damage_x1)
237:    damage_x1 = x;
238:  if (y < damage_y1)
239:    damage_y1 = y;
240:  if (x + w > damage_x2)
241:    damage_x2 = x + w;
242:  if (y + h > damage_y2)
243:    damage_y2 = y + h;
244:  compositor_dirty = 1;
245:}
246:
247:static void expand_window_content_damage(struct window *win, int x, int y,
248:                                         int w, int h) {
249:  if (!win || w <= 0 || h <= 0)
250:    return;
251:
252:  int dw = win->draw_w > 0 ? win->draw_w : win->width;
253:  int dh = win->draw_h > 0 ? win->draw_h : win->height;
254:  if (win->width <= 0 || win->height <= 0 || dw <= 0 || dh <= 0)
255:    return;
256:
257:  int x1 = x;
258:  int y1 = y;
259:  int x2 = x + w;
260:  int y2 = y + h;
261:
262:  if (x1 < 0)
263:    x1 = 0;
264:  if (y1 < 0)
265:    y1 = 0;
266:  if (x2 > win->width)
267:    x2 = win->width;
268:  if (y2 > win->height)
269:    y2 = win->height;
270:  if (x2 <= x1 || y2 <= y1)
271:    return;
272:
273:  int sx1 = win->x + (int)((int64_t)x1 * dw / win->width);
274:  int sy1 = win->y + (int)((int64_t)y1 * dh / win->height);
275:  int sx2 = win->x + (int)(((int64_t)x2 * dw + win->width - 1) / win->width);
276:  int sy2 = win->y + (int)(((int64_t)y2 * dh + win->height - 1) / win->height);
277:  expand_damage(sx1, sy1, sx2 - sx1, sy2 - sy1);
278:}
279:
280:static int window_region_has_alpha(struct window *win, int x, int y, int w,
281:                                   int h) {
282:  if (!win || !win->buffer || w <= 0 || h <= 0)
283:    return 0;
284:
285:  int x1 = x < 0 ? 0 : x;
286:  int y1 = y < 0 ? 0 : y;
287:  int x2 = x + w;
288:  int y2 = y + h;
289:  if (x2 > win->width)
290:    x2 = win->width;
291:  if (y2 > win->height)
292:    y2 = win->height;
293:  if (x2 <= x1 || y2 <= y1)
294:    return 0;
295:
296:  for (int py = y1; py < y2; py++) {
297:    uint32_t *row = win->buffer + (size_t)py * win->width;
298:    for (int px = x1; px < x2; px++) {
299:      if ((row[px] >> 24) != 0xFF)
300:        return 1;
301:    }
302:  }
303:  return 0;
304:}

306:/* Pre-allocated buffers for rendering to avoid stack usage and kmalloc in IRQ
307: */
308:static struct window *sorted_windows[MAX_WINDOWS];
309:static struct region *visible_regions_store[MAX_WINDOWS];
310:/* Backbuffer surface descriptor for the whole render pass — file-static, not
311: * stack-local, so a deep chrome/GL call chain cannot clobber it before
312: * gpu_present_surface() (S-STAB: same rationale as sorted_windows above). */
313:static struct gl_surface compositor_frame_surface;
314:
315:static void compositor_bind_backbuffer_surface(int bb_w, int bb_h, int bb_pg,
316:                                               uint32_t *backbuffer) {
317:  compositor_frame_surface.width = bb_w;
318:  compositor_frame_surface.height = bb_h;
319:  compositor_frame_surface.stride = bb_w;
320:  compositor_frame_surface.buffer = backbuffer;
321:  compositor_frame_surface.alpha_mask = NULL;
322:  compositor_frame_surface.capacity =
323:      (size_t)bb_pg * (4096u / sizeof(uint32_t));
324:}

326:/* Mouse State */
327:static int mouse_x = 400;
328:static int mouse_y = 300;
329:// static uint32_t mouse_color = 0xFFFFFFFF;

331:/* Dragging State */
332:static int dragging_window_id = -1;
333:static int drag_off_x = 0;
334:static int drag_off_y = 0;
335:
336:/* Interactive resize state (edge/corner grip — GFX-DYN-01 F1).  While resizing
337: * we only change the on-screen draw size (draw_w/draw_h): the compositor scales
338: * the logical surface for fluidity (no per-frame realloc in IRQ).  On release
339: * we send the owner an INPUT_TYPE_RESIZE event so it can reallocate a crisp
340: * buffer (apps that ignore it just stay scaled). */
341:#define RESIZE_GRIP 6 /* px hot zone along window edges */
342:#define RESIZE_MIN_W 120
343:#define RESIZE_MIN_H 80
344:#define RESIZE_EDGE_R 1
345:#define RESIZE_EDGE_B 2
346:#define RESIZE_EDGE_L 4
347:static int resizing_window_id = -1;
348:static int resize_edge = 0;
349:static int resize_start_mx = 0, resize_start_my = 0;
350:static int resize_orig_w = 0, resize_orig_h = 0, resize_orig_x = 0;
351:
352:/* Title-bar height now comes from the active style (compositor_titlebar_height,
353: * Phase 5): 20 by default, 0 for the chrome-less Minimal style.  Button
354: * size/gap and their geometry live in gfx_chrome (gfx_chrome_button_geometry),
355: * the single source shared by the render pass and the click hit-test. */
356:
357:/* Compositor backbuffer == the "compositor FB" / desktop-virtual surface
358: * (GFX-DYN-01).  Its size follows the GPU, no longer a hard-coded 720x1280.
359: * It is pre-allocated once to a CAPACITY that covers the current mode plus
360: * reasonable runtime growth, so compositor_resize() never allocates and is
361: * therefore safe to call from the timer-IRQ tick (host display-change path). */
362:#define COMPOSITOR_FALLBACK_W 1024
363:#define COMPOSITOR_FALLBACK_H 768
364:#define COMPOSITOR_MAX_W 1920
365:#define COMPOSITOR_MAX_H 1080
366:
367:static uint32_t *compositor_backbuffer = NULL;
368:static int bb_width = 0; /* render/scanout width (== GPU mode; what apps see) */
369:static int bb_height = 0; /* render/scanout height                            */
370:static int bb_pages = 0;  /* pages backing compositor_backbuffer              */
371:
372:/* Desktop zoom / HiDPI (F2, reworked).  We do NOT scale in software: the GPU
373: * scanout RESOURCE is resized to native*100/zoom and QEMU stretches that to the
374: * host window (which is exactly what the manual set-mode path does).  The
375: * backbuffer == the scanout size; native_w/h is the zoom-100 reference (the
376: * host display size).  zoom>100 ⇒ smaller scanout, QEMU upscales ⇒ HiDPI. */
377:static int native_w = 0, native_h = 0;
378:static int desktop_zoom = 100;
379:
380:/*
381: * Initialize Compositor
382: */
383:void compositor_init(void) {
384:  memset(windows, 0, sizeof(windows));
385:  window_count = 0;
386:  next_window_id = 100;
387:
388:  /* Backbuffer == the GPU scanout size at boot (no hard-coded size). */
389:  struct gpu_device *dev = gpu_get_primary();
390:  int w = dev ? dev->width : COMPOSITOR_FALLBACK_W;
391:  int h = dev ? dev->height : COMPOSITOR_FALLBACK_H;
392:  native_w = w;
393:  native_h = h;
394:  desktop_zoom = 100;
395:
396:  bb_pages = (int)(((size_t)w * h * 4 + 4095) / 4096);
397:  compositor_backbuffer = pmm_alloc_pages_dma(bb_pages);
398:  if (!compositor_backbuffer) {
399:    pr_err("%s", "Compositor: Failed to allocate backbuffer!\n");
400:    bb_pages = 0;
401:    bb_width = 0;
402:    bb_height = 0;
403:    return;
404:  }
405:  bb_width = w;
406:  bb_height = h;
407:
408:  /* First frame is a full upload. */
409:  damage_x1 = 0;
410:  damage_y1 = 0;
411:  damage_x2 = bb_width;
412:  damage_y2 = bb_height;
413:
414:  pr_info("Compositor: Initialized (%dx%d)\n", bb_width, bb_height);
415:}
416:
417:/* Mark the whole desktop dirty (full repaint next tick).  Used by the
418: * Style/Theme switch (compositor_style.c) so a new look shows immediately. */
419:void compositor_full_damage(void) {
420:  uint64_t flags;
421:  spin_lock_irqsave(&compositor_lock, &flags);
422:  damage_x1 = 0;
423:  damage_y1 = 0;
424:  damage_x2 = bb_width;
425:  damage_y2 = bb_height;
426:  compositor_dirty = 1;
427:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&compositor_lock, flags);
428:}
429:
430:/* Report the current desktop (compositor backbuffer) size.  Backs
431: * SYS_DISPLAY_INFO. */
432:void compositor_get_size(int *w, int *h) {
433:  if (w)
434:    *w = bb_width;
435:  if (h)
436:    *h = bb_height;
437:}
438:
439:/*
440: * compositor_reserved_top_locked / compositor_reserved_bottom_locked -
441: * FIX(GFX-COMP-RESERVE-01): infer the screen-edge strip currently claimed by
442: * permanent top_most chrome (nxbar's top bar, nxui's dock) so that ordinary
443: * window placement/resize/drag never slides underneath it.
444: *
445: * Before this fix, compositor_create_window(), compositor_resize(), and
446: * compositor_update_mouse()'s drag clamp only checked compositor_titlebar_
447: * height() at the top (a per-window DECORATION metric — the height of a
448: * window's OWN titlebar — which has nothing to do with nxbar) and the bare
449: * screen edge at the bottom (nothing reserved at all).  Practical effect:
450: *   - a window could be created or dragged with y as low as the titlebar
451: *     height, sliding it underneath nxbar's strip, which the compositor had
452: *     no notion of;
453: *   - any window taller than (screen_h - a few px) got its y clamped to
454: *     "screen_h - h" — flush against the physical bottom edge — with no
455: *     margin for nxui's dock, so it ended up hidden behind the dock instead
456: *     of stopping above it.
457: *
458: * The compositor still does not know "nxbar" or "nxui" by name (kernel/
459: * userland separation, ASTRA §1) — it infers the reservation purely from
460: * geometry: any VISIBLE, TOP_MOST window whose edge sits within
461: * RESERVE_EDGE_SLOP pixels of a screen edge is treated as permanent chrome
462: * anchored to that edge, and its footprint is reserved.  exclude_id lets a
463: * window being placed/dragged skip counting itself (pass 0 if the window has
464: * no id yet, e.g. during creation).  Caller must hold compositor_lock.
465: *
466: * Defined here (ahead of compositor_resize, the first user) rather than
467: * right before compositor_create_window: a static function must be declared
468: * before every call site in the same translation unit, and compositor_resize
469: * appears earlier in this file than compositor_create_window.
470: */
471:#define RESERVE_EDGE_SLOP                                                      \
472:  8 /* nxui's DOCK_MARGIN_BOTTOM (4px) and nxbar's own                         \
473:     * top inset both fall well inside this */
474:
475:static int compositor_reserved_top_locked(int exclude_id) {
476:  /* VECCHIO: partiva da compositor_titlebar_height() → forzava
477:   * anche le finestre senza barra (top_most) a stare sotto un
478:   * margine inesistente.
479:   */
480:  /* NUOVO: la riserva è determinata SOLO dalle finestre top_most
481:   * ancorate al bordo superiore, non dalla decorazione.
482:   */
483:  int top = 0;
484:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_WINDOWS; i++) {
485:    if (windows[i].id == 0 || windows[i].id == exclude_id)
486:      continue;
487:    if (!windows[i].visible || !windows[i].top_most)
488:      continue;
489:    if (windows[i].y <= RESERVE_EDGE_SLOP) {
490:      int reserved = windows[i].y + windows[i].height;
491:      if (reserved > top)
492:        top = reserved;
493:    }
494:  }
495:  return top;
496:}
497:
498:static int compositor_reserved_bottom_locked(int exclude_id) {
499:  int bottom = 0;
500:  int screen_h = bb_height > 0 ? bb_height : 600;
501:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_WINDOWS; i++) {
502:    if (windows[i].id == 0 || windows[i].id == exclude_id)
503:      continue;
504:    if (!windows[i].visible || !windows[i].top_most)
505:      continue;
506:    int gap = screen_h - (windows[i].y + windows[i].height);
507:    if (gap >= 0 && gap <= RESERVE_EDGE_SLOP) {
508:      int reserved = windows[i].height + gap;
509:      if (reserved > bottom)
510:        bottom = reserved;
511:    }
512:  }
513:  return bottom;
514:}
515:
516:/*
517: * compositor_resize - retarget the backbuffer to the scanout's new w x h.
518: *
519: * The caller must have already resized the GPU scanout (gpu_set_mode) to the
520: * SAME size; the backbuffer always matches the scanout, and QEMU stretches the
521: * scanout to the host window (no software scaling here).  Reallocates the
522: * backbuffer to exactly w*h — so it must run in process context (it does:
523: * SYS_SET_DISPLAY_MODE / SYS_SET_ZOOM / SYS_DISPLAY_POLL), never the IRQ tick.
524: * The new buffer is allocated before the lock and the old one freed after, to
525: * keep the compositor_lock hold (shared with the render tick) short.
526: */
527:void compositor_resize(int w, int h) {
528:  if (w <= 0 || h <= 0)
529:    return;
530:  if (w == bb_width && h == bb_height)
531:    return; /* nothing to do */
532:
533:  int npages = (int)(((size_t)w * h * 4 + 4095) / 4096);
534:  uint32_t *nbuf = pmm_alloc_pages_dma(npages);
535:  if (!nbuf) {
536:    pr_err("Compositor: resize %dx%d: out of memory\n", w, h);
537:    return;
538:  }
539:  memset(nbuf, 0, (size_t)npages * 4096);
540:
541:  uint64_t flags;
542:  spin_lock_irqsave(&compositor_lock, &flags);
543:  uint32_t *obuf = compositor_backbuffer;
544:  int opages = bb_pages;
545:  compositor_backbuffer = nbuf;
546:  bb_pages = npages;
547:  bb_width = w;
548:  bb_height = h;
549:
550:  /* Keep every window's title bar / close button on-screen at the new size.
551:   * FIX(GFX-COMP-RESERVE-01): also keep it above nxbar and above nxui's dock
552:   * — previously only compositor_titlebar_height() (top) and a bare 20px
553:   * (bottom) were enforced, with no notion of either chrome strip, so a
554:   * resolution change could resettle a window behind nxbar or behind the
555:   * dock. exclude_id=windows[i].id: a top_most window (nxbar/nxui itself)
556:   * must not count its own footprint against itself.
557:   *
558:   * FIX(GFX-COMP-RESIZE-CLAMP-01): the x clamp used to be a FIXED 40px margin
559:   * ("enough to keep a typical title bar/close button reachable"), which
560:   * only accounts for a NARROW window. A wide window — nxntfy_srv's 280px
561:   * notification popup is the concrete case that surfaced this — positioned
562:   * near the right edge could have its LEFT edge clamped to `bb_width-40`
563:   * while its RIGHT edge (`x + dw`) stayed far past the new, smaller
564:   * bb_width: shrinking the desktop from 1920 to 800 left a 280px-wide popup
565:   * with up to ~240px hanging off-screen, invisible until something
566:   * repositioned it explicitly. Clamp against the window's OWN on-screen
567:   * width/height (draw_w/draw_h, falling back to the logical size — same
568:   * on-screen-size resolution the render/hit-test paths already use) instead
569:   * of a one-size-fits-all constant, so ANY window's full footprint — not
570:   * just its top-left corner — stays reachable after a resize. */
571:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_WINDOWS; i++) {
572:    if (windows[i].id == 0)
573:      continue;
574:    int dw = windows[i].draw_w > 0 ? windows[i].draw_w : windows[i].width;
575:    int dh = windows[i].draw_h > 0 ? windows[i].draw_h : windows[i].height;
576:    /* Keep at least a corner (min 40px) reachable even for a window wider
577:     * than the new screen, instead of pushing x negative. */
578:    int margin_w = dw < 40 ? dw : 40;
579:    int margin_h = dh < 40 ? dh : 40;
580:    if (windows[i].x > bb_width - margin_w)
581:      windows[i].x = bb_width - margin_w;
582:    if (windows[i].x < 0)
583:      windows[i].x = 0;
584:    int reserved_top = compositor_reserved_top_locked(windows[i].id);
585:    int reserved_bottom = compositor_reserved_bottom_locked(windows[i].id);
586:    if (windows[i].y > bb_height - reserved_bottom - margin_h)
587:      windows[i].y = bb_height - reserved_bottom - margin_h;
588:    if (windows[i].y < reserved_top)
589:      windows[i].y = reserved_top;
590:  }
591:
592:  damage_x1 = 0;
593:  damage_y1 = 0;
594:  damage_x2 = bb_width;
595:  damage_y2 = bb_height;
596:  compositor_dirty = 1;
597:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&compositor_lock, flags);
598:
599:  if (obuf)
600:    pmm_free_pages(obuf, opages);
601:  pr_info("Compositor: resized to %dx%d\n", bb_width, bb_height);
602:}
603:
604:/* compositor_set_native_mode - record a real mode change (the user/host set a
605: * concrete resolution): this becomes the zoom-100 reference and resets zoom. */
606:void compositor_set_native_mode(int w, int h) {
607:  if (w > 0 && h > 0) {
608:    native_w = w;
609:    native_h = h;
610:    desktop_zoom = 100;
611:  }
612:}
613:
614:/* compositor_set_zoom - desktop HiDPI/zoom (F2).  Resizes the actual GPU
615: * scanout resource to native*100/zoom and lets QEMU stretch it to the host
616: * window; the backbuffer follows.  Clamped to [100,400] (zoom-in only —
617: * zoom-out would need a scanout larger than the panel).  Backs SYS_SET_ZOOM. */
618:int compositor_set_zoom(int percent) {
619:  if (percent < 100)
620:    percent = 100;
621:  if (percent > 400)
622:    percent = 400;
623:  if (native_w <= 0 || native_h <= 0)
624:    return -1;
625:
626:  int nw = (int)((long)native_w * 100 / percent);
627:  int nh = (int)((long)native_h * 100 / percent);
628:  if (nw < 1 || nh < 1)
629:    return -1;
630:
631:  desktop_zoom = percent;
632:  if (gpu_set_mode(nw, nh) != 0)
633:    return -1;
634:  compositor_resize(nw, nh);
635:  pr_info("Compositor: zoom %d%% -> scanout %dx%d (native %dx%d)\n", percent,
636:          nw, nh, native_w, native_h);
637:  return 0;
638:}
639:
640:/* Forward Declarations */
641:static void compositor_render_internal(void);
642:static void draw_rect_internal(int window_id, int x, int y, int w, int h,
643:                               uint32_t color, int caller_pid);
644:
645:/*
646: * Create Window
647: */
648:/*
649: * Interrupt Locking Helpers
650: * Prevent nested interrupts by saving/restoring PSTATE.DAIF
651: */
652:/* Interrupt Locking Helpers from cpu.h */
653:
654:int compositor_create_window(int x, int y, int w, int h, const char *title,
655:                             int pid) {
656:  /*
657:   * GFX-COMP-RESERVE-02: the caller's privilege is resolved BEFORE
658:   * compositor_lock is taken, and as an int rather than a struct pointer.
659:   *
660:   * Both properties are load-bearing.  process_terminate() holds sched_lock and
661:   * TRYLOCKS compositor_lock (docs/PROCESS-KILL-MODEL.md §4, Pitfall A); a
662:   * blocking compositor_lock -> sched_lock here would close that AB-BA, on the
663:   * hottest path the compositor has.  And a `struct process *` fetched by
664:   * process_find_by_pid() is already stale when the function returns — the
665:   * target can be terminated and its page freed before it is dereferenced.
666:   * proc_pid_is_privileged() answers under sched_lock and lets nothing escape.
667:   *
668:   * An unknown pid (a caller that raced its own exit) reads as UNPRIVILEGED:
669:   * fail closed into the smaller user-window budget rather than hand reserved
670:   * capacity to a caller that can no longer be identified.
671:   */
672:  int privileged = proc_pid_is_privileged(pid);
673:
674:  uint64_t flags;
675:  spin_lock_irqsave(&compositor_lock, &flags);
676:
677:  if (w <= 0 || h <= 0 || w > 4096 || h > 4096) {
678:    pr_err("Compositor: Invalid window dimensions %dx%d\n", w, h);
679:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&compositor_lock, flags);
680:    return -1;
681:  }
682:
683:  /*
684:   * An unprivileged caller (ordinary app) is capped below the full pool so it
685:   * can never crowd out the reserved slots a respawning system service needs.
686:   * A privileged caller (PLVL_ROOT / PLVL_MACHINE — /sys/bin services under
687:   * the ASTRA per-path preset) is checked against the full MAX_WINDOWS:
688:   * privileged windows are a small, fixed, supervised set (dock, nxbar,
689:   * launcher, plus transient destroy+recreate overlap), never something a
690:   * stress test grows without bound, so they don't need — and shouldn't get —
691:   * a *tighter* cap than before.  `privileged` was resolved at entry; see the
692:   * note there for why it cannot be resolved here.
693:   */
694:  int cap = privileged ? MAX_WINDOWS : MAX_USER_WINDOWS;
695:
696:  if (window_count >= cap) {
697:    pr_err(
698:        "%s",
699:        privileged
700:            ? "Compositor: Max windows reached\n"
701:            : "Compositor: Max user windows reached (system slots reserved)\n");
702:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&compositor_lock, flags);
703:    return -1;
704:  }
705:
706:  /* Find free slot */
707:  int slot = -1;
708:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_WINDOWS; i++) {
709:    if (windows[i].id == 0) {
710:      slot = i;
711:      break;
712:    }
713:  }
714:
715:  if (slot < 0) {
716:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&compositor_lock, flags);
717:    return -1;
718:  }
719:
720:  /*
721:   * FIX(GFX-COMP-NEWWIN-01): clamp the initial position so a newly created
722:   * window (including its title bar / close button) lands fully on-screen.
723:   * compositor_update_mouse() already enforces these same bounds while
724:   * dragging a window; without this check here, a window created near a
725:   * screen edge (or larger than the screen) would have its title bar and
726:   * close button off-screen until the user dragged it at least once.
727:   * Mirrors the clamp order used in compositor_update_mouse().
728:   */
729:  {
730:    /* Clamp into the desktop-virtual area (where windows live), not the
731:     * physical scanout — they differ under zoom (F2).  We already hold
732:     * compositor_lock, so read bb_width/bb_height directly (compositor_get_size
733:     * would re-lock). */
734:    int screen_w = bb_width > 0 ? bb_width : 800;
735:    int screen_h = bb_height > 0 ? bb_height : 600;
736:
737:    if (x + w > screen_w)
738:      x = screen_w - w;
739:    if (x < 0)
740:      x = 0;
741:
742:    /* FIX(GFX-COMP-RESERVE-01): clamp against the LIVE top/bottom chrome
743:     * reservation (nxbar/nxui), not just compositor_titlebar_height() at the
744:     * top and the bare screen edge at the bottom — see the helper comment
745:     * above. exclude_id=0: this window has no id yet, nothing to exclude. */
746:    int reserved_top = compositor_reserved_top_locked(0);
747:    int reserved_bottom = compositor_reserved_bottom_locked(0);
748:
749:    if (y + h > screen_h - reserved_bottom)
750:      y = screen_h - reserved_bottom - h;
751:    if (y < reserved_top)
752:      y = reserved_top;
753:  }
754:
755:  /* Allocate window buffer */
756:  size_t buffer_size = w * h * sizeof(uint32_t);
757:  uint32_t *buffer = (uint32_t *)kmalloc(buffer_size);
758:  if (!buffer) {
759:    pr_err("%s", "Compositor: Failed to allocate window buffer\n");
760:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&compositor_lock, flags);
761:    return -1;
762:  }
763:  /* Initialize clear background - use a consistent dark theme */
764:  uint32_t default_bg = compositor_theme_active()->win_bg;
765:  for (int i = 0; i < w * h; i++)
766:    buffer[i] = default_bg;
767:
768:  /* Initialize window */
769:  windows[slot].id = next_window_id++;
770:  windows[slot].x = x;
771:  windows[slot].y = y;
772:  windows[slot].width = w;
773:  windows[slot].height = h;
774:  windows[slot].draw_w = w; /* on-screen == logical until a resize scales it */
775:  windows[slot].draw_h = h;
776:  windows[slot].z_order = window_count;
777:  windows[slot].visible = 1;
778:  windows[slot].minimized = 0;
779:  windows[slot].pid = pid;
780:  windows[slot].buffer = buffer;
781:  windows[slot].bg_color = default_bg;
782:
783:  /* Initialize the embedded terminal emulator (cell grid from font metrics). */
784:  int char_w = graphics_font_max_width();
785:  int char_h = graphics_font_height();
786:  if (term_init(&windows[slot].term, w / char_w, h / char_h, COLOR_FG,
787:                default_bg) != 0) {
788:    pr_err("%s", "Compositor: Failed to allocate terminal grids\n");
789:    kfree(buffer);
790:    windows[slot].id = 0;
791:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&compositor_lock, flags);
792:    return -1;
793:  }
794:
795:  /* Copy title */
796:  int len = 0;
797:  while (title[len] && len < 63) {
798:    windows[slot].title[len] = title[len];
799:    len++;
800:  }
801:  windows[slot].title[len] = '\0';
802:
803:  windows[slot].has_alpha = ((default_bg >> 24) != 0xFF);
804:
805:  /* Clear buffer to background */
806:  for (int i = 0; i < w * h; i++) {
807:    buffer[i] = windows[slot].bg_color;
808:  }
809:
810:  /* Mark main shell (PID 2) as protected */
811:  windows[slot].protected = (pid == 2) ? 1 : 0;
812:  windows[slot].top_most = 0;
813:  windows[slot].passive = 0;
814:
815:  window_count++;
816:
817:  /* ============================================================
818:   * VECCHIO: nessuna chiamata a expand_damage, nessun compositor_dirty
819:   * ============================================================ */
820:
821:  /* ============================================================
822:   * NUOVO: marca l'intera area della finestra (contenuto + barra
823:   * del titolo) come danneggiata così il prossimo compositor_tick
824:   * la ridisegna immediatamente.
825:   * ============================================================ */
826:  int ddw = windows[slot].draw_w > 0 ? windows[slot].draw_w : w;
827:  int ddh = windows[slot].draw_h > 0 ? windows[slot].draw_h : h;
828:  expand_damage(x, y - compositor_titlebar_height(), ddw,
829:                ddh + compositor_titlebar_height());
830:  compositor_dirty = 1;
831:
832:  pr_debug("Compositor: Created window '%s' (%dx%d) at (%d,%d)\n", title, w, h,
833:           x, y); /* hot path under GUI churn: demoted (perf §1) */
834:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&compositor_lock, flags);
835:  return windows[slot].id;
836:}
837:
838:/*
839: * __focus_topmost_locked - re-point keyboard focus after a window goes away.
840: *
841: * Picks the top-most remaining visible window (highest z_order) and gives it
842: * keyboard focus; falls back to the shell default (PID 7) when no window is
843: * left.  Replaces the old hardcoded 'keyboard_focus_pid = 7' reset, which
844: * sent input to a stale/wrong PID whenever the shell was not PID 7 (PID
845: * numbering depends on boot service order) and ignored Z-order entirely.
846: *
847: * Caller MUST hold compositor_lock; destroyed slots are already zeroed and
848: * thus excluded by the id != 0 check.
849: */
850:/* Erase the caret on every window not owned by keep_pid (caller holds
851: * compositor_lock).  Keeps the caret on the input window only. */
852:static void __clear_other_carets_locked(int keep_pid);
853:
854:static void __focus_topmost_locked(void) {
855:  int max_z = -1;
856:  int pid = 7; /* shell default when no window remains */
857:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_WINDOWS; i++) {
858:    if (windows[i].id != 0 && windows[i].visible &&
859:        windows[i].z_order > max_z) {
860:      max_z = windows[i].z_order;
861:      pid = windows[i].pid;
862:    }
863:  }
864:  sched_set_focus_pid(pid); /* push the focus hint down (#67); never write the
865:                               scheduler's global directly */
866:  __clear_other_carets_locked(pid);
867:  pr_debug("Compositor: Focus reset to PID %d\n", pid);
868:}
869:
870:/*
871: * compositor_window_owner - return the owning PID of a window, or -1 if the
872: * window id does not exist.  Used by the syscall layer for the ABI-04
873: * ownership check on SYS_DESTROY_WINDOW (kernel-internal callers like the
874: * close button or process teardown bypass the check by design).
875: */
876:int compositor_window_owner(int window_id) {
877:  uint64_t flags;
878:  int owner = -1;
879:  spin_lock_irqsave(&compositor_lock, &flags);
880:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_WINDOWS; i++) {
881:    if (windows[i].id == window_id) {
882:      owner = windows[i].pid;
883:      break;
884:    }
885:  }
886:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&compositor_lock, flags);
887:  return owner;
888:}
889:
890:/* ========================================================================= */
891:/* Window state control + enumeration (ASTRA §6.7: windows as objects).      */
892:/* These back the OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW capability (kernel/core/object.c) and       */
893:/* SYS_WINDOW_ENUM, used by the dock /sys/bin/nxui and the titlebar           */
894:/* background button below.  The compositor stays the mechanism; policy       */
895:/* (dock layout, what to restore) lives in userland (nxui).                   */
896:/* ========================================================================= */
897:
898:/* __raise_to_front_locked - give a window the highest z-order.  Caller holds
899: * compositor_lock.  Mirrors the click-to-front logic in
900: * compositor_handle_click. */
901:static void __raise_to_front_locked(struct window *w) {
902:  int top_z = 0;
903:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_WINDOWS; i++)
904:    if (windows[i].id != 0 && windows[i].z_order > top_z)
905:      top_z = windows[i].z_order;
906:  w->z_order = top_z + 1;
907:}
908:
909:/* compositor_minimize_window - send a window to the background: hide it but
910: * keep its slot/buffer so the dock can restore it.  If it held focus, focus
911: * falls to the next top-most visible window.  Returns 0, or -ESRCH for an
912: * unknown id. */
913:int compositor_minimize_window(int window_id) {
914:  uint64_t flags;
915:  int ret = -ESRCH;
916:  spin_lock_irqsave(&compositor_lock, &flags);
917:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_WINDOWS; i++) {
918:    if (windows[i].id == window_id) {
919:      windows[i].visible = 0;
920:      windows[i].minimized = 1;
921:      if (keyboard_focus_pid == windows[i].pid)
922:        __focus_topmost_locked(); /* re-point focus off the hidden window */
923:      expand_damage(0, 0, bb_width, bb_height);
924:      compositor_dirty = 1;
925:      ret = 0;
926:      break;
927:    }
928:  }
929:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&compositor_lock, flags);
930:  return ret;
931:}
932:
933:/* compositor_restore_window - bring a backgrounded window back: show it, raise
934: * it to the front and give it keyboard focus.  Returns 0, or -ESRCH for unknown
935: * id. The focus push (sched_set_focus_pid + compositor_focus_changed) runs
936: * AFTER the unlock, matching SYS_SET_FOCUS and keeping compositor_lock off the
937: * focus path. */
938:int compositor_restore_window(int window_id) {
939:  uint64_t flags;
940:  int target_pid = -1;
941:  spin_lock_irqsave(&compositor_lock, &flags);
942:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_WINDOWS; i++) {
943:    if (windows[i].id == window_id) {
944:      windows[i].visible = 1;
945:      windows[i].minimized = 0;
946:      __raise_to_front_locked(&windows[i]);
947:      target_pid = windows[i].pid;
948:      expand_damage(0, 0, bb_width, bb_height);
949:      compositor_dirty = 1;
950:      break;
951:    }
952:  }
953:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&compositor_lock, flags);
954:  if (target_pid < 0)
955:    return -ESRCH;
956:  sched_set_focus_pid(target_pid);
957:  compositor_focus_changed(target_pid);
958:  return 0;
959:}
960:
961:/* compositor_focus_window - raise a window and give it keyboard focus; reveals
962: * it if it was hidden/minimized.  Returns 0, or -ESRCH for an unknown id. */
963:int compositor_focus_window(int window_id) {
964:  uint64_t flags;
965:  int target_pid = -1;
966:  spin_lock_irqsave(&compositor_lock, &flags);
967:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_WINDOWS; i++) {
968:    if (windows[i].id == window_id) {
969:      if (!windows[i].visible) {
970:        windows[i].visible = 1;
971:        windows[i].minimized = 0;
972:      }
973:      __raise_to_front_locked(&windows[i]);
974:      target_pid = windows[i].pid;
975:      expand_damage(0, 0, bb_width, bb_height);
976:      compositor_dirty = 1;
977:      break;
978:    }
979:  }
980:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&compositor_lock, flags);
981:  if (target_pid < 0)
982:    return -ESRCH;
983:  sched_set_focus_pid(target_pid);
984:  compositor_focus_changed(target_pid);
985:  return 0;
986:}
987:
988:/* __fill_window_info_locked - serialise one window slot into the shared ABI
989: * record (include/api/object.h).  Caller holds compositor_lock. */
990:static void __fill_window_info_locked(const struct window *w,
991:                                      struct window_info *wi) {
992:  wi->id = w->id;
993:  wi->pid = w->pid;
994:  wi->x = w->x;
995:  wi->y = w->y;
996:  wi->w = w->draw_w > 0 ? w->draw_w : w->width;
997:  wi->h = w->draw_h > 0 ? w->draw_h : w->height;
998:  unsigned int f = 0;
999:  if (w->visible)
1000:    f |= WININFO_VISIBLE;
1001:  if (w->minimized)
1002:    f |= WININFO_MINIMIZED;
1003:  if (w->top_most)
1004:    f |= WININFO_TOPMOST;
1005:  if (w->passive)
1006:    f |= WININFO_PASSIVE;
1007:  if (w->pid == keyboard_focus_pid)
1008:    f |= WININFO_FOCUSED;
1009:  wi->flags = f;
1010:  int k = 0;
1011:  while (k < 63 && w->title[k]) {
1012:    wi->title[k] = w->title[k];
1013:    k++;
1014:  }
1015:  wi->title[k] = '\0';
1016:}
1017:
1018:/* compositor_window_info - fill one window's info record by id.  Returns 0, or
1019: * -ESRCH for an unknown id.  Backs OS1_object_read() on an OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW. */
1020:int compositor_window_info(int window_id, struct window_info *out) {
1021:  uint64_t flags;
1022:  int ret = -ESRCH;
1023:  spin_lock_irqsave(&compositor_lock, &flags);
1024:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_WINDOWS; i++) {
1025:    if (windows[i].id == window_id) {
1026:      __fill_window_info_locked(&windows[i], out);
1027:      ret = 0;
1028:      break;
1029:    }
1030:  }
1031:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&compositor_lock, flags);
1032:  return ret;
1033:}
1034:
1035:/* sys_window_enum - SYS_WINDOW_ENUM backend: snapshot every live window into
1036: * the caller's struct window_info[] and return the count.  Read-only and
1037: * ungated (enumeration is information, not authority — acting on a window still
1038: * needs an OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW capability).  Mirrors sys_getprocs: snapshot under
1039: * the lock, copy to user after unlocking. */
1040:long sys_window_enum(struct window_info *ubuf, size_t max) {
1041:  if (!ubuf || max == 0)
1042:    return 0;
1043:  if (max > MAX_WINDOWS)
1044:    max = MAX_WINDOWS;
1045:  struct window_info *kbuf =
1046:      (struct window_info *)kmalloc(sizeof(struct window_info) * max);
1047:  if (!kbuf)
1048:    return -ENOMEM;
1049:
1050:  uint64_t flags;
1051:  size_t n = 0;
1052:  spin_lock_irqsave(&compositor_lock, &flags);
1053:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_WINDOWS && n < max; i++) {
1054:    if (windows[i].id != 0)
1055:      __fill_window_info_locked(&windows[i], &kbuf[n++]);
1056:  }
1057:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&compositor_lock, flags);
1058:
1059:  if (n > 0 &&
1060:      vmm_copy_to_user(ubuf, kbuf, sizeof(struct window_info) * n) != 0) {
1061:    kfree(kbuf);
1062:    return -EFAULT;
1063:  }
1064:  kfree(kbuf);
1065:  return (long)n;
1066:}
1067:
1068:/*
1069: * compositor_window_grid - report a window's terminal grid (cols x rows).
1070: *
1071: * The terminal cell size derives from the active font (proportional fonts
1072: * give a cell == max glyph advance), so a windowed TTY app cannot assume a
1073: * fixed 80x25.  Returns 0 and fills cols/rows on success, -1 if the window
1074: * id does not exist.  Backs SYS_WINDOW_GRID.
1075: */
1076:int compositor_window_grid(int window_id, int *cols, int *rows) {
1077:  uint64_t flags;
1078:  int found = -1;
1079:  spin_lock_irqsave(&compositor_lock, &flags);
1080:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_WINDOWS; i++) {
1081:    if (windows[i].id == window_id) {
1082:      if (cols)
1083:        *cols = windows[i].term.cols;
1084:      if (rows)
1085:        *rows = windows[i].term.rows;
1086:      found = 0;
1087:      break;
1088:    }
1089:  }
1090:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&compositor_lock, flags);
1091:  return found;
1092:}
1093:
1094:/*
1095: * Destroy Window
1096: */
1097:void compositor_destroy_window(int window_id) {
1098:  uint64_t flags;
1099:  spin_lock_irqsave(&compositor_lock, &flags);
1100:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_WINDOWS; i++) {
1101:    if (windows[i].id == window_id) {
1102:      int refocus = (windows[i].pid == keyboard_focus_pid);
1103:      /* #118: damage the vacated footprint BEFORE zeroing so the area under the
1104:       * window (and lower windows) is recomposited at the next tick — no ghost.
1105:       */
1106:      int ddw = windows[i].draw_w > 0 ? windows[i].draw_w : windows[i].width;
1107:      int ddh = windows[i].draw_h > 0 ? windows[i].draw_h : windows[i].height;
1108:      expand_damage(windows[i].x, windows[i].y - compositor_titlebar_height(),
1109:                    ddw, ddh + compositor_titlebar_height());
1110:      compositor_dirty = 1;
1111:      if (windows[i].buffer) {
1112:        kfree(windows[i].buffer);
1113:      }
1114:      term_free(&windows[i].term);
1115:      memset(&windows[i], 0, sizeof(struct window));
1116:      window_count--;
1117:      if (refocus) {
1118:        /* The focused window is gone: hand focus to the next in Z-order. */
1119:        __focus_topmost_locked();
1120:      }
1121:      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&compositor_lock, flags);
1122:      return;
1123:    }
1124:  }
1125:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&compositor_lock, flags);
1126:}
1127:
1128:/*
1129: * Destroy all windows owned by a specific PID
1130: */
1131:void compositor_destroy_windows_by_pid(int pid) {
1132:  uint64_t flags;
1133:  int refocus = 0;
1134:  spin_lock_irqsave(&compositor_lock, &flags);
1135:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_WINDOWS; i++) {
1136:    if (windows[i].id != 0 && windows[i].pid == pid) {
1137:      if (windows[i].pid == keyboard_focus_pid) {
1138:        refocus = 1;
1139:      }
1140:      /* #118: damage the vacated footprint before zeroing (no ghost window). */
1141:      int ddw = windows[i].draw_w > 0 ? windows[i].draw_w : windows[i].width;
1142:      int ddh = windows[i].draw_h > 0 ? windows[i].draw_h : windows[i].height;
1143:      expand_damage(windows[i].x, windows[i].y - compositor_titlebar_height(),
1144:                    ddw, ddh + compositor_titlebar_height());
1145:      compositor_dirty = 1;
1146:      if (windows[i].buffer) {
1147:        kfree(windows[i].buffer);
1148:      }
1149:      term_free(&windows[i].term);
1150:      memset(&windows[i], 0, sizeof(struct window));
1151:      window_count--;
1152:    }
1153:  }
1154:  if (refocus) {
1155:    /* All of the dying PID's windows are zeroed by now, so the scan picks
1156:     * the top-most SURVIVING window (or the shell default). */
1157:    __focus_topmost_locked();
1158:  }
1159:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&compositor_lock, flags);
1160:}
1161:
1162:/*
1163: * Get Window Buffer (for direct drawing)
1164: */
1165:uint32_t *compositor_get_buffer(int window_id) {
1166:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_WINDOWS; i++) {
1167:    if (windows[i].id == window_id) {
1168:      return windows[i].buffer;
1169:    }
1170:  }
1171:  return NULL;
1172:}

1174:/*
1175: * Find window by PID
1176: */
1177:int compositor_get_window_by_pid(int pid) {
1178:  uint64_t flags;
1179:  spin_lock_irqsave(&compositor_lock, &flags);
1180:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_WINDOWS; i++) {
1181:    if (windows[i].id != 0 && windows[i].pid == pid) {
1182:      int id = windows[i].id;
1183:      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&compositor_lock, flags);
1184:      return id;
1185:    }
1186:  }
1187:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&compositor_lock, flags);
1188:  return -1;
1189:}

1198:void compositor_move_window(int window_id, int x, int y) {
1199:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_WINDOWS; i++) {
1200:    if (windows[i].id == window_id) {
1201:      windows[i].x = x;
