219:/*
220: * graphics_char_width - return the horizontal advance width for a codepoint.
221: *
222: * Param: codepoint — Unicode scalar value.
223: * Returns advance width in pixels from the active font's glyph_info, or 0 if
224: * the codepoint is outside [first_char, first_char+num_chars).
225: * Used by gl_draw_string and graphics_string_width to advance the cursor.
226: *
227: * Locking: the active font is read under font_lock (GFX-FONT-01).
228: */
229:/*
230: * Get character advance width
231: */
232:int graphics_char_width(uint32_t codepoint) {
233:  uint64_t flags;
234:  spin_lock_irqsave(&font_lock, &flags);
235:  const struct font_state *f = current_font;
236:  int idx = (int)codepoint - f->header.first_char;
237:  int adv = (idx < 0 || idx >= f->header.num_chars) ? 0 : f->glyphs[idx].advance;
238:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&font_lock, flags);
239:  return adv;
240:}
241:
242:/*
243: * gl_draw_string - render a UTF-8 string left-to-right onto surf.
244: *
245: * Params: surf — target surface; x, y — origin of the first glyph cell;
246: *         str — null-terminated UTF-8 string; color — ARGB8888 foreground.
247: *
248: * Decodes each codepoint via utf8_decode, renders it with gl_draw_char at the
249: * current cursor_x, then advances cursor_x by graphics_char_width.  Invalid
250: * UTF-8 sequences (consumed <= 0) consume one byte and continue.
251: *
252: * Locking: none; called under compositor_lock in compositor_render_internal.
253: * Side effects: writes pixels to surf->buffer.
254: */
255:/*
256: * Draw string using GL (UTF-8 supported)
257: */
258:void gl_draw_string(struct gl_surface *surf, int x, int y, const char *str,
259:                    uint32_t color) {
260:  if (!surf || !str)
261:    return;
262:
263:  int cursor_x = x;
264:  uint32_t codepoint;
265:  int consumed;
266:  size_t rem = 0;
267:  const char *p = str;
268:  while (*p) { p++; rem++; }
269:
270:  while (*str) {
271:    consumed = utf8_decode(str, rem, &codepoint);
272:    if (consumed <= 0) {
273:        str++;
274:        rem--;
275:        continue;
276:    }
277:    gl_draw_char(surf, cursor_x, y, codepoint, color);
278:    cursor_x += graphics_char_width(codepoint);
279:    str += consumed;
280:    rem -= consumed;
281:  }
282:}
283:
284:void gl_draw_string_clipped(struct gl_surface *surf, int x, int y,
285:                            const char *str, uint32_t color, int cx1, int cy1,
286:                            int cx2, int cy2) {
287:  if (!surf || !str)
288:    return;
289:
290:  int cursor_x = x;
291:  uint32_t codepoint;
292:  int consumed;
293:  size_t rem = 0;
294:  const char *p = str;
295:  while (*p) { p++; rem++; }
296:
297:  while (*str) {
298:    consumed = utf8_decode(str, rem, &codepoint);
299:    if (consumed <= 0) {
300:        str++;
301:        rem--;
302:        continue;
303:    }
304:    gl_draw_char_clipped(surf, cursor_x, y, codepoint, color, cx1, cy1, cx2, cy2);
305:    cursor_x += graphics_char_width(codepoint);
306:    str += consumed;
307:    rem -= consumed;
308:  }
309:}
310:
311:/*
312: * graphics_string_width - compute pixel width of a UTF-8 string.
313: *
314: * Param: str — null-terminated UTF-8 string (NULL-safe: returns 0).
315: * Sums graphics_char_width for each decoded codepoint.  Mirrors the cursor
316: * advance in gl_draw_string so callers can centre text (e.g. title bar).
317: *
318: * Locking: the active font is read under font_lock (GFX-FONT-01).
319: */
320:/*
321: * Get string width in pixels (UTF-8 supported)
322: */
323:int graphics_string_width(const char *str) {
324:  if (!str)
325:    return 0;
326:
327:  int width = 0;
328:  uint32_t codepoint;
329:  int consumed;
330:  size_t rem = 0;
331:  const char *p = str;
332:  while (*p) { p++; rem++; }
333:
334:  while (*str) {
335:    consumed = utf8_decode(str, rem, &codepoint);
336:    if (consumed <= 0) {
337:        str++;
338:        rem--;
339:        continue;
340:    }
341:    width += graphics_char_width(codepoint);
342:    str += consumed;
343:    rem -= consumed;
344:  }
345:  return width;
346:}
347:
348:/*
349: * graphics_font_height - return the total line height of the active font.
350: *
351: * Returns ascent + descent in pixels.  Used as char_h in compositor for row
352: * count and scroll arithmetic.
353: *
354: * GFX-FONT-02 (fixed): floors to the built-in default height when
355: *   ascent+descent <= 0, so a malformed font (both fields zero, via
356: *   sys_set_font) can no longer cause a divide-by-zero at
357: *   compositor_create_window (h / char_h).
358: *
359: * Locking: reads current_font.header under font_lock (GFX-FONT-01).
360: */
361:/*
362: * Get font height
363: */
364:int graphics_font_height(void) { 
365:    /* GFX-FONT-02: floor to the built-in default height so a malformed font
366:     * (ascent=descent=0 via sys_set_font) cannot make char_h==0 and trigger a
367:     * divide-by-zero in compositor row/scroll arithmetic — mirrors the
368:     * graphics_font_max_width() floor. */
369:    uint64_t flags;
370:    spin_lock_irqsave(&font_lock, &flags);
371:    int h = current_font->header.ascent + current_font->header.descent;
372:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&font_lock, flags);
373:    return h > 0 ? h : (FONT_ASCENT + FONT_DESCENT);
374:}
375:
376:/*
377: * graphics_font_ascent - return the ascent of the active font in pixels.
378: *
379: * Ascent is the distance from the baseline to the top of the tallest glyph.
380: * Used in gl_draw_char to compute start_y = y + ascent + gi->y0.
381: *
382: * Locking: reads current_font under font_lock (GFX-FONT-01).
383: */
384:/*
385: * Get font ascent
386: */
387:int graphics_font_ascent(void) {
388:    uint64_t flags;
389:    spin_lock_irqsave(&font_lock, &flags);
390:    int a = current_font->header.ascent;
391:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&font_lock, flags);
392:    return a;
393:}
394:
395:/*
396: * Get max character width (for grid systems)
397: */
398:int graphics_font_max_width(void) {
399:    uint64_t flags;
400:    spin_lock_irqsave(&font_lock, &flags);
401:    const struct font_state *f = current_font;
402:    int max_w = 0;
403:    for (int i = 0; i < f->header.num_chars; i++) {
404:        if (f->glyphs[i].advance > max_w)
405:            max_w = f->glyphs[i].advance;
406:    }
407:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&font_lock, flags);
408:    return max_w > 0 ? max_w : 8;
409:}
410:
411:/*
412: * System Call: Set Font
413: */
414:int sys_set_font(void *data, size_t size) {
415:    /* GFX-FONT-01: 'data' is a raw userland pointer.  Copy the whole blob into a
416:     * kmalloc'd kernel buffer, validate against the *kernel* copy, then publish an
417:     * immutable descriptor behind font_lock and retire the previous one.  This
418:     * removes the use-after-free (the old code stored interior pointers into user
419:     * memory that dangled after the process exited) and the info-leak (a user
420:     * could point 'data' at kernel VAs and read them back via the framebuffer). */
421:    if (!data || size < sizeof(struct font_header))
422:        return -1;
423:    if (size > FONT_MAX_BLOB)            /* bound before kmalloc (cf. EXT4-07/#62) */
424:        return -1;
425:
426:    /* 1. Copy + validate the header alone first (never deref the user pointer). */
427:    struct font_header h;
428:    if (arch_copy_from_user(&h, data, sizeof(h)) != 0)
429:        return -1;
430:    if (h.magic != FONT_MAGIC)
431:        return -2;
432:    if (h.num_chars == 0 || (uint32_t)h.ascent + (uint32_t)h.descent == 0)
433:        return -3;                        /* reject zero metrics (cf. GFX-FONT-02) */
434:
435:    /* num_chars is uint16 and bitmap_size uint32, so this cannot overflow size_t
436:     * on a 64-bit kernel; FONT_MAX_BLOB bounds the allocation. */
437:    size_t glyphs_bytes = (size_t)h.num_chars * sizeof(struct font_glyph_info);
438:    size_t blob = sizeof(struct font_header) + glyphs_bytes + (size_t)h.bitmap_size;
439:    if (size < blob)
440:        return -3;
441:
442:    /* 2. One kmalloc block holds [font_state | header | glyphs | bitmap]; the
443:     * block base is heap_base so retiring frees everything in one kfree. */
444:    uint8_t *mem = (uint8_t *)kmalloc(sizeof(struct font_state) + blob);
445:    if (!mem)
446:        return -1;
447:    struct font_state *ns = (struct font_state *)mem;
448:    uint8_t *kblob = mem + sizeof(struct font_state);
449:    if (arch_copy_from_user(kblob, data, blob) != 0) {
450:        kfree(mem);
451:        return -1;
452:    }
453:
454:    /* 3. Re-validate against the kernel copy (defend against a TOCTOU header
455:     * change between the two copies) and bound every glyph's bitmap span. */
456:    struct font_header *kh = (struct font_header *)kblob;
457:    if (kh->magic != FONT_MAGIC || kh->num_chars != h.num_chars ||
458:        kh->bitmap_size != h.bitmap_size ||
459:        (uint32_t)kh->ascent + (uint32_t)kh->descent == 0) {
460:        kfree(mem);
461:        return -3;
462:    }
463:    struct font_glyph_info *kglyphs =
464:        (struct font_glyph_info *)(kblob + sizeof(struct font_header));
465:    for (uint16_t i = 0; i < kh->num_chars; i++) {
466:        uint32_t span = (uint32_t)kglyphs[i].width * (uint32_t)kglyphs[i].height;
467:        if (kglyphs[i].data_offset > kh->bitmap_size ||
468:            span > kh->bitmap_size - kglyphs[i].data_offset) {
469:            kfree(mem);                   /* a glyph would read past the bitmap */
470:            return -3;
471:        }
472:    }
473:
474:    /* 4. Build the immutable descriptor (pointers reference the kernel blob). */
475:    ns->header = *kh;
476:    ns->glyphs = kglyphs;
477:    ns->bitmap = kblob + sizeof(struct font_header) + glyphs_bytes;
478:    ns->heap_base = mem;
479:
480:    /* 5. Publish under the lock and retire the previous descriptor.  set_font
481:     * holds font_lock to swap, so no reader is mid-descriptor; after the swap no
482:     * new reader can obtain 'old' (they read the new pointer).  'old' therefore
483:     * has no users once the lock is released, so it is safe to free.  The static
484:     * default is never freed. */
485:    uint64_t flags;
486:    spin_lock_irqsave(&font_lock, &flags);
487:    struct font_state *old = current_font;
488:    current_font = ns;
489:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&font_lock, flags);
490:
491:    if (old != &default_font)
492:        kfree(old->heap_base);            /* heap_base == old (single block) */
493:
494:    return 0;
495:}
496:

@@@ kernel/graphics/gl.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/graphics/gl.c
3: * 2D Software Rasteriser (GL Surface Primitives)
4: *
5: * Role:
6: *   Provides pixel-level drawing primitives that operate on struct gl_surface
7: *   (an in-memory ARGB8888 pixel buffer with explicit width/height/stride).
8: *   This is the 2D software rasteriser — NOT the project's 3D engine, which
9: *   lives in the out-of-scope draw3d.c.
10: *
11: * Primitives:
12: *   gl_clear          — flood-fill entire surface with a solid colour.
13: *   gl_draw_pixel     — write one pixel with bounds check.
14: *   gl_draw_line      — Bresenham integer line (delegates to gl_draw_pixel).
15: *   gl_draw_rect_fill — filled axis-aligned rectangle with clip-to-surface.
16: *   gl_blit           — composite one surface onto another at (dx, dy), with
17: *                       per-pixel Porter-Duff "src over" alpha blending.
18: *
19: * Pixel format:
20: *   All surfaces use ARGB8888 packed as 0xAARRGGBB in a uint32_t.
21: *   Stride may exceed width (pitch-aligned framebuffer); row address =
22: *   buffer + row * stride.
23: *
24: * Alpha blending model:
25: *   blend_over() implements non-pre-multiplied "src over" destination:
26: *     out_channel = (src_channel * a + dst_channel * (255-a)) / 255
27: *   Output alpha is forced to 0xFF (fully opaque destination).
28: *   gl_blit uses a three-way fast path: skip (a=0), copy (a=255), blend.
29: *
30: * Locking & IRQ context:
31: *   None of these functions take any lock.  They are safe to call with
32: *   compositor_lock held (as compositor_render_internal does), but they must
33: *   not be called from hard-IRQ context without that protection.
34: *
35: * Compatibility:
36: *   gl_draw_rect and gl_swizzle_bgr complete the declared internal surface
37: *   contract. They are kernel primitives only; they do not expose OpenGL to
38: *   applications, which remains a userland personality.
39: */
40:#include <graphics/gl.h>
41:#include <kernel/string.h>
42:#include <kernel/types.h>
43:
44:/*
45: * clip - clamp an integer value to [min, max] inclusive.
46: * Used by gl_draw_rect_fill to intersect requested rect with surface bounds.
47: */
48:/* Helper for clipping */
49:static inline int clip(int val, int min, int max) {
50:  if (val < min)
51:    return min;
52:  if (val > max)
53:    return max;
54:  return val;
55:}
56:
57:/*
58: * blend_over - Porter-Duff "src over" composite (non-pre-multiplied ARGB8888).
59: *
60: * Params: src — source pixel (ARGB8888); dst — destination pixel (ARGB8888).
61: * Returns: blended pixel with alpha forced to 0xFF (opaque destination).
62: *
63: * Formula per channel: out = (src_ch * a + dst_ch * (255 - a)) / 255
64: * Division by 255 is exact integer (not approximated by >>8, which would
65: * introduce a systematic -1 error for fully saturated channels).
66: *
67: * Alpha blend: composite src (ARGB8888) over opaque dst.
68: * Standard Porter-Duff "src over" for pre-multiplied-free ARGB:
69: *   out = (src * a + dst * (255 - a)) / 255
70: * Inline so the compiler can hoist it into the blit hot loop.
71: */
72:static inline uint32_t blend_over(uint32_t src, uint32_t dst) {
73:  uint32_t a = (src >> 24) & 0xFF;
74:  uint32_t ia = 255 - a;
75:
76:  uint32_t r = (((src >> 16) & 0xFF) * a + ((dst >> 16) & 0xFF) * ia) / 255;
77:  uint32_t g = (((src >> 8) & 0xFF) * a + ((dst >> 8) & 0xFF) * ia) / 255;
78:  uint32_t b = ((src & 0xFF) * a + (dst & 0xFF) * ia) / 255;
79:
80:  return 0xFF000000 | (r << 16) | (g << 8) | b;
81:}
82:
83:/*
84: * gl_clear - fill an entire gl_surface with a solid colour.
85: *
86: * Params: surf — target surface; color — ARGB8888 fill value.
87: * Writes stride * height pixels, covering the full allocation including any
88: * pitch-padding columns between rows (important for framebuffers where
89: * stride > width; a previous version used width*height and missed padding).
90: *
91: * Side effects: overwrites every word in surf->buffer.
92: * Locking: none.
93: */
94:void gl_clear(struct gl_surface *surf, uint32_t color) {
95:  if (!surf || !surf->buffer)
96:    return;
97:
98:  /*
99:   * BUG FIX (minor): original used width*height, ignoring stride.
100:   * If stride > width (e.g. pitch-aligned framebuffer) the padding columns
101:   * between rows were never cleared, leaving stale data visible.
102:   * Use stride*height to cover the full allocation.
103:   */
104:  int size = surf->stride * surf->height;
105:  for (int i = 0; i < size; i++)
106:    surf->buffer[i] = color;
107:}
108:
109:/*
110: * gl_draw_pixel - write one pixel to a gl_surface with bounds checking.
111: *
112: * Params: surf — target surface; x, y — pixel coordinates; color — ARGB8888.
113: * Silently returns if surf/buffer is NULL or (x, y) is outside [0, width) x
114: * [0, height).  Row addressing uses stride (not width) for pitch-aligned
115: * framebuffers: pixel address = buffer + y * stride + x.
116: *
117: * Side effects: writes one uint32_t to surf->buffer.
118: * Locking: none.
119: */
120:void gl_draw_pixel(struct gl_surface *surf, int x, int y, uint32_t color) {
121:  if (!surf || !surf->buffer)
122:    return;
123:  if (x < 0 || x >= surf->width || y < 0 || y >= surf->height)
124:    return;
125:  surf->buffer[y * surf->stride + x] = color;
126:}
127:
128:/*
129: * gl_draw_line - draw an antialiasing-free line using Bresenham's algorithm.
130: *
131: * Params: surf — target surface; (x0, y0) start, (x1, y1) end; color ARGB8888.
132: * Uses integer error accumulation (classic Bresenham): dx, dy are absolute
133: * deltas; sx, sy are the step signs; err drives the major-axis advance.
134: * Each pixel is written via gl_draw_pixel which bounds-checks individually,
135: * so clipping to surface bounds is handled pixel-by-pixel.
136: *
137: * Side effects: writes pixels to surf->buffer via gl_draw_pixel.
138: * Locking: none.
139: */
140:void gl_draw_line(struct gl_surface *surf, int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1,
141:                  uint32_t color) {
142:  if (!surf)
143:    return;
144:  int dx = (x1 > x0) ? (x1 - x0) : (x0 - x1);
145:  int dy = (y1 > y0) ? (y1 - y0) : (y0 - y1);
146:  int sx = (x0 < x1) ? 1 : -1;
147:  int sy = (y0 < y1) ? 1 : -1;
148:  int err = (dx > dy ? dx : -dy) / 2;
149:  int e2;
150:
151:  for (;;) {
152:    gl_draw_pixel(surf, x0, y0, color);
153:    if (x0 == x1 && y0 == y1)
154:      break;
155:    e2 = err;
156:    if (e2 > -dx) {
157:      err -= dy;
158:      x0 += sx;
159:    }
160:    if (e2 < dy) {
161:      err += dx;
162:      y0 += sy;
163:    }
164:  }
165:}
166:
167:/* Outline rectangle with the same exclusive width/height convention as fill. */
168:void gl_draw_rect(struct gl_surface *surf, int x, int y, int w, int h,
169:                  uint32_t color) {
170:  if (!surf || w <= 0 || h <= 0)
171:    return;
172:  gl_draw_line(surf, x, y, x + w - 1, y, color);
173:  if (h > 1)
174:    gl_draw_line(surf, x, y + h - 1, x + w - 1, y + h - 1, color);
175:  if (w > 1) {
176:    gl_draw_line(surf, x, y + 1, x, y + h - 2, color);
177:    gl_draw_line(surf, x + w - 1, y + 1, x + w - 1, y + h - 2, color);
178:  }
179:}
180:
181:/*
182: * gl_draw_rect_fill - draw a solid axis-aligned rectangle clipped to surface.
183: *
184: * Params: surf — target surface; x, y — top-left; w, h — dimensions;
185: *         color — ARGB8888 fill.
186: *
187: * Clip math: early-reject if entirely off-surface (x >= width, y >= height,
188: * or right/bottom edge <= 0), then clip each corner with clip():
189: *   cx  = clip(x,     0, width-1)   — left edge
190: *   cy  = clip(y,     0, height-1)  — top edge
191: *   x2  = clip(x+w,  0, width)      — right edge (exclusive)
192: *   y2  = clip(y+h,  0, height)     — bottom edge (exclusive)
193: * The inner loops then run j in [cy, y2) and i in [cx, x2) with no further
194: * bounds check — safety is guaranteed by the clip.
195: *
196: * Side effects: writes pixels to surf->buffer.
197: * Locking: none.
198: */
199:void gl_draw_rect_fill(struct gl_surface *surf, int x, int y, int w, int h,
200:                       uint32_t color) {
201:  if (!surf)
202:    return;
203:  if (x >= surf->width || y >= surf->height)
204:    return;
205:  if (x + w < 0 || y + h < 0)
206:    return;
207:
208:  int cx = clip(x, 0, surf->width - 1);
209:  int cy = clip(y, 0, surf->height - 1);
210:  int x2 = clip(x + w, 0, surf->width);
211:  int y2 = clip(y + h, 0, surf->height);
212:
213:  for (int j = cy; j < y2; j++)
214:    for (int i = cx; i < x2; i++)
215:      surf->buffer[j * surf->stride + i] = color;
216:}
217:
218:/* Convert an ABGR8888 buffer to the ARGB8888 contract used by every kernel
219: * surface. This is intentionally in-place: the alpha and green lanes remain
220: * fixed, while red and blue are exchanged. */
221:void gl_swizzle_bgr(struct gl_surface *surf) {
222:  if (!surf || !surf->buffer || surf->width <= 0 || surf->height <= 0 ||
223:      surf->stride < surf->width)
224:    return;
225:  for (int y = 0; y < surf->height; y++) {
226:    for (int x = 0; x < surf->width; x++) {
227:      uint32_t pixel = surf->buffer[y * surf->stride + x];
228:      uint32_t red = pixel & 0x000000ffu;
229:      uint32_t blue = (pixel >> 16) & 0x000000ffu;
230:      surf->buffer[y * surf->stride + x] =
231:          (pixel & 0xff00ff00u) | (red << 16) | blue;
232:    }
233:  }
234:}
235:
236:/*
237: * gl_blit - composite a source gl_surface onto a destination at (dx, dy).
238: *
239: * Params: dst — destination surface; src — source surface; dx, dy — top-left
240: *         offset in dst where src[0,0] is placed.
241: *
242: * Clips src pixels to dst bounds per-pixel (negative dx/dy handled by
243: * continue when dsty<0 or dstx<0; right/bottom handled by >= checks).
244: *
245: * Three-way alpha path (keyed on extracted alpha byte of each source pixel):
246: *   alpha == 0:   skip — fully transparent, no write.
247: *   alpha == 255: fast copy — no blend arithmetic, direct assignment.
248: *   otherwise:    blend_over() — Porter-Duff "src over".
249: *
250: * Side effects: writes pixels to dst->buffer.
251: * Locking: none; called under compositor_lock in compositor_render_internal.
252: *
253: * gl_blit — composite src surface onto dst at (dx, dy).
254: *
255: * BUG FIX (critical): The original implementation performed only an alpha
256: * TEST: any pixel with alpha == 0 was skipped, and every other pixel —
257: * regardless of its actual alpha value — was written at full opacity with
258: * gl_draw_pixel().  Semi-transparent pixels (0 < alpha < 255) were therefore
259: * composited as if they were completely opaque, corrupting the destination
260: * with raw source colours instead of a proper blend.  This is the root cause
261: * of the multicoloured artefact visible in the compositor output.
262: *
263: * Fix: three-way path keyed on the source alpha:
264: *   alpha == 0   → skip (fully transparent, nothing to draw)
265: *   alpha == 255 → fast copy (fully opaque, no arithmetic needed)
266: *   otherwise    → Porter-Duff "src over" blend with the destination pixel
267: */
268:void gl_blit(struct gl_surface *dst, struct gl_surface *src, int dx, int dy) {
269:  if (!dst || !src || !dst->buffer || !src->buffer)
270:    return;
271:
272:  for (int y = 0; y < src->height; y++) {
273:    int dsty = dy + y;
274:    if (dsty < 0 || dsty >= dst->height)
275:      continue;
276:
277:    for (int x = 0; x < src->width; x++) {
278:      int dstx = dx + x;
279:      if (dstx < 0 || dstx >= dst->width)
280:        continue;
281:
282:      uint32_t col = src->buffer[y * src->stride + x];
283:      uint32_t alpha = col >> 24;
284:
285:      if (alpha == 0)
286:        continue; /* fully transparent — nothing to do */
287:
288:      uint32_t *dp = &dst->buffer[dsty * dst->stride + dstx];
289:
290:      if (alpha == 255) {
291:        *dp = col; /* fully opaque — fast path, no blend math */
292:      } else {
293:        *dp = blend_over(col, *dp); /* semi-transparent — proper alpha blend */
294:      }
295:    }
296:  }
297:}

@@@ kernel/graphics/graphics.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/graphics/graphics.c
3: * Graphics Subsystem (Bridging HAL and GL)
4: *
5: * Role:
6: *   Thin HAL bridge between the GPU device driver and the GL rasteriser.
7: *   graphics_screen_surface() is THE single accessor to the scanout buffer
8: *   (S-ALIGN F7): it goes through the gpu_ops.get_framebuffer contract — the
9: *   same method the compositor flush path consumes — so no caller knows which
10: *   provider implementation sits underneath (ASTRA §1 rule 1/2).  The old
11: *   graphics_get_screen_surface() read dev->framebuffer_virt directly (a
12: *   second, field-level path to the same memory) and returned a function-
13: *   static struct (GFX-GFX-01, SMP-unsafe) — both retired.
14: *
15: * Invariants:
16: *   - All draw wrappers silently no-op if no GPU/framebuffer is present.
17: *   - graphics_swap_buffers() is a memory-barrier-only stub; the subsystem
18: *     operates in single-buffered mode (backbuffer lives in compositor.c).
19: */
20:#include <drivers/gpu/gpu.h>
21:#include <graphics/gl.h>
22:#include <kernel/arch.h>
23:#include <kernel/fault.h>
24:#include <kernel/gfx_surface.h>
25:#include <kernel/graphics.h>
26:#include <kernel/printk.h>
27:
28:/*
29: * graphics_init - verify the primary GPU is discoverable through the HAL.
30: *
31: * Pure discovery log: the scanout is always reached per-call through
32: * graphics_screen_surface(), never cached at init (a cached copy went stale
33: * on every runtime resolution change — the retired g_ctx bug).
34: */
35:void graphics_init(void) {
36:  struct gpu_device *dev = gpu_get_primary();
37:  if (dev)
38:    pr_info("Graphics: Initialized via HAL (%dx%d)\n", dev->width, dev->height);
39:  else
40:    pr_err("%s", "Graphics: No GPU device found!\n");
41:}
42:
43:/*
44: * graphics_screen_surface - fill 'out' with a gl_surface over the scanout.
45: *
46: * THE single accessor to the screen buffer (S-ALIGN F7): resolves the primary
47: * GPU per call (picks up runtime mode changes) and reads the buffer through
48: * the gpu_ops.get_framebuffer contract — the same method the compositor's
49: * flush path uses.  The caller owns 'out' (no static: SMP- and fault-safe,
50: * closes GFX-GFX-01).  vgpu_get_framebuffer is lock-free and NULL-safe, so
51: * this path is safe from panic context (panic_screen below).
52: *
53: * Returns 0 on success, -1 if no GPU/framebuffer is present.
54: */
55:int graphics_screen_surface(struct gl_surface *out) {
56:  struct gpu_device *dev = gpu_get_primary();
57:  if (!out || !dev || !dev->ops || !dev->ops->get_framebuffer)
58:    return -1;
59:  uint32_t *fb = (uint32_t *)dev->ops->get_framebuffer(dev, NULL);
60:  if (!fb)
61:    return -1;
62:  out->width = dev->width;
63:  out->height = dev->height;
64:  out->stride = dev->width;
65:  out->buffer = fb;
66:  /* S-STAB: the scanout's true size in pixels.  If a concurrent mode change
67:   * (vgpu_set_mode) left width/height and framebuffer_size momentarily torn —
68:   * the compositor↔GPU seam is unlocked here (S-ALIGN F7) — this makes the
69:   * inconsistency a loud, localized panic instead of an OOB blit into the
70:   * freed/short scanout backing. */
71:  out->capacity = dev->framebuffer_size / sizeof(uint32_t);
72:  gfx_surface_verify(out, "graphics_screen_surface");
73:  return 0;
74:}
75:
76:/*
77: * graphics_draw_pixel - write a single pixel to the screen framebuffer.
78: *
79: * Params: x, y — screen coordinates (clamped/rejected by gl_draw_pixel if
80: *         out of surface bounds).  color — ARGB8888.
81: * Side effects: writes one pixel to the HAL framebuffer via gl_draw_pixel.
82: * Locking: none; wraps gl_draw_pixel which is not IRQ-safe.
83: */
84:void graphics_draw_pixel(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t color) {
85:  struct gl_surface screen;
86:  if (graphics_screen_surface(&screen) == 0) {
87:    struct gl_surface *surf = &screen;
88:    gl_draw_pixel(surf, (int)x, (int)y, color);
89:  }
90:}
91:
92:/*
93: * graphics_draw_rect - fill an axis-aligned rectangle on the screen.
94: *
95: * Params: x, y — top-left corner; w, h — dimensions; color — ARGB8888.
96: * Clips to screen surface bounds via gl_draw_rect_fill.
97: * Side effects: writes pixels to the HAL framebuffer.
98: * Locking: none.
99: */
100:void graphics_draw_rect(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t w, uint32_t h,
101:                        uint32_t color) {
102:  struct gl_surface screen;
103:  if (graphics_screen_surface(&screen) == 0) {
104:    gfx_rect_t rect = {(int)x, (int)y, (int)w, (int)h};
105:    gfx_surface_fill(&screen, &rect, color);
106:  }
107:}
108:
109:/*
110: * graphics_clear - fill the entire screen with a solid colour.
111: *
112: * Param: color — ARGB8888 fill value.
113: * Side effects: overwrites every pixel in the HAL framebuffer (stride*height
114: *               words) via gl_clear.
115: * Locking: none.
116: */
117:void graphics_clear(uint32_t color) {
118:  struct gl_surface screen;
119:  if (graphics_screen_surface(&screen) == 0)
120:    gfx_surface_clear(&screen, color);
121:}
122:
123:/*
124: * graphics_swap_buffers - issue a full memory barrier to commit pending writes.
125: *
126: * The system runs in single-buffered mode: there is no second framebuffer to
127: * swap.  This function exists as an API hook for future double-buffered
128: * support. Currently it only issues arch_mb() to ensure all preceding pixel
129: * writes are visible to the GPU DMA engine before any following flush.
130: *
131: * Side effects: arch_mb() — a full store/load barrier on the current arch.
132: * Locking: none required; barrier is inherently CPU-local.
133: */
134:void graphics_swap_buffers(void) {
135:  /* In single-buffered modes, this is a flush/barrier */
136:  arch_mb();
137:}
138:
139:/*
140: * panic_screen - paint the captured fault transcript on a RED framebuffer.
141: *
142: * DIR-05 / #139: a kernel fault halts everything and is otherwise visible only
143: * on the UART.  This makes it readable on the display too, for machines with no
144: * serial.  Fault-safe by construction: it does NOT touch the compositor (which
145: * may be wedged or mid-render), takes no locks of its own, writes the primary
146: * GPU framebuffer directly, and presents through the device flush op (which
147: * skips its own lock in fault context).  Best-effort: returns quietly if no GPU
148: * / framebuffer is present.  Called from panic() after the other CPUs quiesce.
149: */
150:void panic_screen(const char *text) {
151:  struct gl_surface screen;
152:  if (graphics_screen_surface(&screen) != 0)
153:    return;
154:  struct gl_surface *s = &screen;
155:  if (!s->buffer || s->width <= 0 || s->height <= 0)
156:    return;
157:
158:  const uint32_t RED = 0xFFB91C1C, WHITE = 0xFFFCFCFD;
159:  uint32_t npix = (uint32_t)s->width * (uint32_t)s->height;
160:  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < npix; i++)
161:    s->buffer[i] = RED;
162:
163:  gl_draw_string(s, 12, 8, "*** KERNEL PANIC - system halted ***", WHITE);
164:
165:  /* The fault transcript, line by line, clipped to the screen.  The top lines
166:   * (arch register dump + fault class) are the most diagnostic, so render from
167:   * the top. */
168:  int y = 32;
169:  char line[200];
170:  for (const char *p = text ? text : ""; *p && y < (int)s->height - 16;) {
171:    int k = 0;
172:    while (*p && *p != '\n' && k < (int)sizeof(line) - 1)
173:      line[k++] = *p++;
174:    line[k] = '\0';
175:    if (*p == '\n')
176:      p++;
177:    if (k > 0)
178:      gl_draw_string(s, 12, y, line, WHITE);
179:    y += 16;
180:  }
181:
182:  struct gpu_device *dev = gpu_get_primary();
183:  if (dev && dev->ops && dev->ops->flush)
184:    dev->ops->flush(dev, 0, 0, dev->width, dev->height);
185:}
186:
187:/*
188: * graphics_draw_char - render one Unicode codepoint to the screen framebuffer.
189: *
190: * Params: x, y — baseline-relative top-left; codepoint — Unicode scalar value;
191: *         color — ARGB8888 foreground.
192: * Delegates to gl_draw_char (font.c) which performs per-glyph alpha blending.
193: * Side effects: writes pixels to the HAL framebuffer.
194: * Locking: none; must not be called from IRQ without holding compositor_lock.
195: */
196:void graphics_draw_char(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t codepoint,
197:                        uint32_t color) {
198:  struct gl_surface screen;
199:  if (graphics_screen_surface(&screen) == 0) {
200:    struct gl_surface *surf = &screen;
201:    gl_draw_char(surf, (int)x, (int)y, codepoint, color);
202:  }
203:}
204:
205:/*
206: * graphics_draw_string - render a UTF-8 string to the screen framebuffer.
207: *
208: * Params: x, y — origin; str — null-terminated UTF-8 string; color — ARGB8888.
209: * Delegates to gl_draw_string (font.c) which advances the cursor by each
210: * glyph's advance width after calling gl_draw_char.
211: * Side effects: writes pixels to the HAL framebuffer.
212: * Locking: none; must not be called from IRQ without holding compositor_lock.
213: */
214:void graphics_draw_string(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, const char *str,
215:                          uint32_t color) {
216:  struct gl_surface screen;
217:  if (graphics_screen_surface(&screen) == 0) {
218:    struct gl_surface *surf = &screen;
219:    gl_draw_string(surf, (int)x, (int)y, str, color);
220:  }
221:}

@@@ kernel/graphics/region.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/graphics/region.c
3: * Region Manager — List-of-Rectangles
4: *
5: * Role:
6: *   Implements a dynamic list of non-overlapping (but not guaranteed disjoint
7: *   after region_add_rect absorption) axis-aligned rectangles.  Used by
8: *   compositor.c for occlusion culling (the "occluded" and per-window
9: *   "visible" regions computed in compositor_render_internal).
10: *
11: * API:
12: *   region_create / region_destroy  — allocate / free the list.
13: *   region_add_rect                 — add a rect, absorbing any rects it fully
14: *                                     covers and skipping if fully covered.
15: *   region_subtract                 — boolean difference: removes a rect's
16: *                                     area from all existing rects, splitting
17: *                                     each intersecting rect into up to 4
18: *                                     non-overlapping pieces.
19: *   region_intersect_rect           — clip the region to a bounding rect.
20: *   region_clear                    — reset count to 0 (keeps allocation).
21: *
22: * Invariants:
23: *   - region_destroy(NULL) is a safe no-op.
24: *   - region_add_rect rejects zero/negative-dimension rects at entry.
25: *   - The rectangle list grows up to MAX_RECTS_PER_REGION (256); additions
26: *     beyond that limit are silently dropped.
27: *   - region_subtract and region_intersect_rect build a new_reg, then steal
28: *     its rects array and free the container shell (not the array).
29: *   - region_clear sets count=0 but does NOT null-check reg; caller must not
30: *     pass NULL (unlike region_destroy which guards on NULL).
31: *
32: * Locking: none — all functions are called under compositor_lock in practice.
33: *
34: * Known issues:
35: *   None tracked in docs/review/analysis/06-graphics.md.
36: */
37:#include <kernel/graphics.h>
38:#include <kernel/kmalloc.h>
39:#include <kernel/region.h>
40:#include <kernel/types.h>
41:
42:/* Simple Region Implementation (List of Rectangles) */
43:
44:/*
45: * region_create - allocate a new empty region.
46: *
47: * Allocates a struct region via kcalloc (zeroed) and an initial rect array of
48: * 8 slots via kmalloc.  Returns NULL if either allocation fails; in that case
49: * the partially-allocated struct is freed before returning.
50: *
51: * Locking: inherits kmalloc_lock via kmalloc/kcalloc; safe to call with
52: *          compositor_lock held.
53: * Returns: pointer to new region, or NULL on allocation failure.
54: */
55:struct region *region_create(void) {
56:  struct region *reg = (struct region *)kcalloc(1, sizeof(struct region));
57:  if (!reg)
58:    return NULL;
59:  reg->rects = (struct rect *)kmalloc(sizeof(struct rect) * 8);
60:  if (!reg->rects) {
61:    kfree(reg);
62:    return NULL;
63:  }
64:  reg->count = 0;
65:  reg->capacity = 8;
66:  return reg;
67:}
68:
69:/*
70: * region_destroy - free a region and its rect array.
71: *
72: * NULL-safe: silently returns if reg is NULL.  Frees reg->rects first (if
73: * non-NULL) then frees reg itself.  Callers that have stolen reg->rects
74: * (as region_subtract and region_intersect_rect do) must null the pointer
75: * before calling region_destroy to avoid a double-free.
76: *
77: * Locking: none required beyond what kmalloc_lock provides internally.
78: */
79:void region_destroy(struct region *reg) {
80:  if (reg) {
81:    if (reg->rects)
82:      kfree(reg->rects);
83:    kfree(reg);
84:  }
85:}
86:
87:/* MAX_RECTS_PER_REGION: hard cap on rect count per region.  Additions that
88: * would push count past this limit are silently dropped.  Chosen to limit
89: * worst-case memory and O(n) scan cost per compositor frame. */
90:#define MAX_RECTS_PER_REGION 256
91:
92:/* GFX-PERF-01 (#131 / GFX-COMP-07): region_subtract / region_intersect_rect used
93: * to region_create() a scratch region on EVERY call — i.e. a kmalloc/kfree pair
94: * per occluder per window per frame, all from the timer-IRQ compositor tick.
95: * Instead they now build into a single static scratch (fixed array, never
96: * reallocated — region_add_rect's MAX cap prevents growth) and copy the result
97: * back, so the steady state does no per-frame allocation.  Safe because both run
98: * serially under compositor_lock. */
99:static struct rect g_scratch_rects[MAX_RECTS_PER_REGION];
100:static struct region g_scratch = {.rects = g_scratch_rects,
101:                                  .count = 0,
102:                                  .capacity = MAX_RECTS_PER_REGION};
103:
104:static struct region *region_scratch_reset(void) {
105:  g_scratch.count = 0;
106:  return &g_scratch;
107:}
108:
109:/* Copy src's rects into dst, growing dst->rects once if needed (rare; reaches a
110: * steady capacity after warmup, then never allocates). */
111:static void region_copy_into(struct region *dst, const struct region *src) {
112:  if (dst->capacity < src->count) {
113:    int new_cap = src->count;
114:    struct rect *nr = (struct rect *)kmalloc(sizeof(struct rect) * new_cap);
115:    if (!nr)
116:      return; /* keep dst unchanged on OOM */
117:    if (dst->rects)
118:      kfree(dst->rects);
119:    dst->rects = nr;
120:    dst->capacity = new_cap;
121:  }
122:  for (int i = 0; i < src->count; i++)
123:    dst->rects[i] = src->rects[i];
124:  dst->count = src->count;
125:}
126:
127:/*
128: * region_add_rect - add an axis-aligned rectangle to the region.
129: *
130: * Params: reg — target region (must not be NULL); x, y — top-left corner;
131: *         w, h — dimensions (must be > 0 or the call is ignored).
132: *
133: * Algorithm:
134: *   1. Early exit for zero/negative dimensions.
135: *   2. Containment check: if any existing rect fully covers the new rect,
136: *      skip (the new area is already represented).
137: *   3. Absorption pass: remove any existing rects that are fully covered by
138: *      the new rect (compact the list in-place with a write pointer j).
139: *   4. Capacity guard: drop the addition if count >= MAX_RECTS_PER_REGION.
140: *   5. Grow the rects array by doubling capacity (up to MAX_RECTS_PER_REGION)
141: *      if needed; failure to realloc silently drops the addition.
142: *   6. Append the new rect.
143: *
144: * The region is NOT guaranteed to be disjoint after absorption — two rects
145: * that partially overlap are both retained; subtraction is not performed here.
146: *
147: * Locking: caller must hold compositor_lock if used from compositor context.
148: */
149:void region_add_rect(struct region *reg, int x, int y, int w, int h) {
150:  if (w <= 0 || h <= 0)
151:    return;
152:
153:  int x2 = x + w, y2 = y + h;
154:
155:  /* Skip if already fully covered by an existing rect */
156:  for (int i = 0; i < reg->count; i++) {
157:    struct rect *r = &reg->rects[i];
158:    if (r->x <= x && r->y <= y && r->x + r->w >= x2 && r->y + r->h >= y2)
159:      return;
160:  }
161:
162:  /* Absorb any existing rects fully covered by the new rect */
163:  int j = 0;
164:  for (int i = 0; i < reg->count; i++) {
165:    struct rect *r = &reg->rects[i];
166:    if (!(x <= r->x && y <= r->y && x2 >= r->x + r->w && y2 >= r->y + r->h))
167:      reg->rects[j++] = reg->rects[i];
168:  }
169:  reg->count = j;
170:
171:  if (reg->count >= MAX_RECTS_PER_REGION)
172:    return;
173:
174:  if (reg->count >= reg->capacity) {
175:    int new_cap = reg->capacity * 2;
176:    if (new_cap > MAX_RECTS_PER_REGION)
177:      new_cap = MAX_RECTS_PER_REGION;
178:
179:    struct rect *new_rects =
180:        (struct rect *)kmalloc(sizeof(struct rect) * new_cap);
181:    if (new_rects) {
182:      for (int i = 0; i < reg->count; i++)
183:        new_rects[i] = reg->rects[i];
184:      kfree(reg->rects);
185:      reg->rects = new_rects;
186:      reg->capacity = new_cap;
187:    } else {
188:      return;
189:    }
190:  }
191:  reg->rects[reg->count].x = x;
192:  reg->rects[reg->count].y = y;
193:  reg->rects[reg->count].w = w;
194:  reg->rects[reg->count].h = h;
195:  reg->count++;
196:}
197:
198:/*
199: * region_subtract - remove a rectangle's area from every rect in the region.
200: *
201: * Params: reg — region to modify; x, y, w, h — rectangle to subtract (no-op
202: *         if w <= 0 or h <= 0).
203: *
204: * Algorithm (naive rebuild):
205: *   Allocates a new_reg scratch region.  For each existing rect r:
206: *     - Compute intersection of r and sub (ix, iy, iw, ih).
207: *     - If no intersection: add r verbatim to new_reg.
208: *     - If intersection: split r into up to 4 axis-aligned pieces (top,
209: *       bottom, left, right of the intersection) and add each to new_reg.
210: *   Then steal new_reg->rects into reg (updating count/capacity) and free
211: *   the new_reg container shell (NOT its rects array which is now owned by
212: *   reg).
213: *
214: * The "split into 4" decomposition is the standard rectangle boolean-
215: * difference: top strip (r.y .. iy), bottom strip (iy+ih .. r.y+r.h), left
216: * strip (r.x .. ix, height=ih), right strip (ix+iw .. r.x+r.w, height=ih).
217: * Strips with zero height or width are skipped by region_add_rect's guard.
218: *
219: * Locking: caller must hold compositor_lock if used from compositor context.
220: * NOTE: O(n) per call; called in an inner loop → O(n²) per render frame.
221: */
222:/* Subtract rect (sub) from region (reg) */
223:void region_subtract(struct region *reg, int x, int y, int w, int h) {
224:  /* Boolean difference: For each rect in reg, subtract (x,y,w,h) */
225:  /* This can split 1 rect into up to 4 rects */
226:  /* Since we modify the list in place, we need a temp list or careful iteration
227:   */
228:  /* Naive approach: Create new list */
229:
230:  struct rect sub = {x, y, w, h};
231:  if (w <= 0 || h <= 0)
232:    return;
233:
234:  struct region *new_reg = region_scratch_reset();
235:
236:  for (int i = 0; i < reg->count; i++) {
237:    struct rect r = reg->rects[i];
238:
239:    /* Check intersection */
240:    int ix = (r.x > sub.x) ? r.x : sub.x;
241:    int iy = (r.y > sub.y) ? r.y : sub.y;
242:    int iw = ((r.x + r.w) < (sub.x + sub.w)) ? (r.x + r.w) : (sub.x + sub.w);
243:    int ih = ((r.y + r.h) < (sub.y + sub.h)) ? (r.y + r.h) : (sub.y + sub.h);
244:    iw -= ix;
245:    ih -= iy;
246:
247:    if (iw <= 0 || ih <= 0) {
248:      /* No intersection, keep original */
249:      region_add_rect(new_reg, r.x, r.y, r.w, r.h);
250:      continue;
251:    }
252:
253:    /*
254:     * Split r into up to 4 pieces:
255:     * Top, Bottom, Left, Right relative to intersection
256:     */
257:
258:    /* Top */
259:    if (r.y < iy) {
260:      region_add_rect(new_reg, r.x, r.y, r.w, iy - r.y);
261:    }
262:    /* Bottom */
263:    if (r.y + r.h > iy + ih) {
264:      region_add_rect(new_reg, r.x, iy + ih, r.w, (r.y + r.h) - (iy + ih));
265:    }
266:    /* Left */
267:    if (r.x < ix) {
268:      region_add_rect(new_reg, r.x, iy, ix - r.x, ih);
269:    }
270:    /* Right */
271:    if (r.x + r.w > ix + iw) {
272:      region_add_rect(new_reg, ix + iw, iy, (r.x + r.w) - (ix + iw), ih);
273:    }
274:  }
275:
276:  /* Copy the scratch result back into reg (no per-call allocation). */
277:  region_copy_into(reg, new_reg);
278:}
279:
280:/*
281: * region_intersect_rect - clip the region to a bounding rectangle.
282: *
283: * Params: reg — region to clip in-place; x, y, w, h — clip rectangle.
284: *
285: * For each rect in reg, computes its intersection with the clip rect and
286: * retains only the overlapping portion.  Rects with no intersection are
287: * discarded.  Like region_subtract, builds a scratch new_reg and steals its
288: * rects array into reg.
289: *
290: * Used in compositor_render_internal to clip each window's visible region to
291: * screen bounds after occlusion subtraction.
292: *
293: * Locking: caller must hold compositor_lock if used from compositor context.
294: */
295:void region_intersect_rect(struct region *reg, int x, int y, int w, int h) {
296:  struct rect clip = {x, y, w, h};
297:  struct region *new_reg = region_scratch_reset();
298:
299:  for (int i = 0; i < reg->count; i++) {
300:    struct rect r = reg->rects[i];
301:    int ix = (r.x > clip.x) ? r.x : clip.x;
302:    int iy = (r.y > clip.y) ? r.y : clip.y;
303:    int iw =
304:        ((r.x + r.w) < (clip.x + clip.w)) ? (r.x + r.w) : (clip.x + clip.w);
305:    int ih =
306:        ((r.y + r.h) < (clip.y + clip.h)) ? (r.y + r.h) : (clip.y + clip.h);
307:    iw -= ix;
308:    ih -= iy;
309:
310:    if (iw > 0 && ih > 0) {
311:      region_add_rect(new_reg, ix, iy, iw, ih);
312:    }
313:  }
314:
315:  region_copy_into(reg, new_reg);
316:}
317:
318:/*
319: * region_clear - reset the region's rect count to zero without freeing memory.
320: *
321: * Param: reg — must NOT be NULL (no NULL guard here, unlike region_destroy).
322: * Keeps the allocated rects array for reuse; does not zero the array contents.
323: * The next region_add_rect call will overwrite slots from index 0.
324: *
325: * Locking: caller must hold compositor_lock if used from compositor context.
326: */
327:void region_clear(struct region *reg) { reg->count = 0; }
328:

@@@ kernel/graphics/surface.c @@@
1:/* Kernel-internal surface contract implementation. */
2:#include <kernel/gfx_surface.h>
3:#include <kernel/printk.h>
4:
5:int gfx_surface_valid(const gfx_surface_t *surface) {
6:  return surface && surface->buffer && surface->width > 0 &&
7:         surface->height > 0 && surface->stride >= surface->width;
8:}
9:
10:/* S-STAB invariant gate — see gl.h.  A surface whose geometry outruns its
11: * backing allocation is a memory-corruption bug the instant anything draws to
12: * it; fail loud and precise here rather than let an OOB write corrupt kernel
13: * RAM and surface as an unrelated #PF/#GP later (the UTM panic signature). */
14:void gfx_surface_verify(const gfx_surface_t *surf, const char *where) {
15:  if (!surf)
16:    panic("gfx_surface_verify(%s): NULL surface", where ? where : "?");
17:  if (surf->buffer && surf->stride < surf->width)
18:    panic("gfx_surface_verify(%s): stride %d < width %d (buf=%p)",
19:          where ? where : "?", surf->stride, surf->width, (void *)surf->buffer);
20:  /* capacity==0 means the bind site is not yet instrumented — do not treat the
21:   * absence of a known allocation size as a violation. */
22:  if (surf->capacity == 0)
23:    return;
24:  size_t need = (size_t)(surf->height > 0 ? surf->height : 0) *
25:                (size_t)(surf->stride > 0 ? surf->stride : 0);
26:  if (need > surf->capacity)
27:    panic("gfx_surface_verify(%s): geometry %dx%d stride %d needs %lu px but "
28:          "buffer holds only %lu (buf=%p) — geometry/allocation desync",
29:          where ? where : "?", surf->width, surf->height, surf->stride,
30:          (unsigned long)need, (unsigned long)surf->capacity,
31:          (void *)surf->buffer);
32:}
33:
34:void gfx_surface_clear(gfx_surface_t *surface, uint32_t argb) {
35:  if (gfx_surface_valid(surface))
36:    gl_clear(surface, argb);
37:}
38:
39:void gfx_surface_fill(gfx_surface_t *surface, const gfx_rect_t *rect,
40:                      uint32_t argb) {
41:  if (gfx_surface_valid(surface) && rect && rect->width > 0 &&
42:      rect->height > 0)
43:    gl_draw_rect_fill(surface, rect->x, rect->y, rect->width, rect->height,
44:                      argb);
45:}
46:
47:void gfx_surface_composite_over(gfx_surface_t *destination,
48:                                gfx_surface_t *source, int x, int y) {
49:  if (gfx_surface_valid(destination) && gfx_surface_valid(source))
50:    gl_blit(destination, source, x, y);
51:}

@@@ kernel/graphics/term.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/graphics/term.c
3: * VT/ANSI terminal emulator (extracted from compositor.c — GFX-DYN-01, #123).
4: *
5: * Operates on a struct terminal (cell model) + a struct gl_surface (pixel
6: * target).  No knowledge of windows, PIDs or the compositor: the compositor
7: * owns the terminal and supplies the surface.  Supports the ECMA-48 subset a
8: * full-screen TTY app (kilo) needs: cursor positioning (H/f), erase in line
9: * (K), erase screen (J), SGR colours (m) and DECTCEM caret show/hide (?25 h/l).
10: */
11:#include <kernel/term.h>
12:
13:#include <graphics/gl.h>
14:#include <kernel/graphics.h>
15:#include <kernel/kmalloc.h>
16:#include <kernel/string.h>
17:
18:/* Fill a cell-sized rectangle directly into the surface, clipped to bounds.
19: * Replaces the compositor's draw_rect_internal for terminal-local drawing:
20: * the terminal owns its surface, so no ownership check or window lookup. */
21:static void term_fill_rect(struct gl_surface *surf, int x, int y, int w, int h,
22:                           uint32_t color) {
23:  for (int dy = 0; dy < h; dy++) {
24:    int py = y + dy;
25:    if (py < 0 || py >= surf->height)
26:      continue;
27:    for (int dx = 0; dx < w; dx++) {
28:      int px = x + dx;
29:      if (px < 0 || px >= surf->width)
30:        continue;
31:      surf->buffer[py * surf->stride + px] = color;
32:    }
33:  }
34:}
35:
36:/* xterm 256-colour palette → ARGB (16 base + 6x6x6 cube + 24 grays). */
37:static uint32_t term_xterm256(int n) {
38:  static const uint32_t base16[16] = {
39:      0xFF000000, 0xFFBB0000, 0xFF00BB00, 0xFFBBBB00, 0xFF0000BB, 0xFFBB00BB,
40:      0xFF00BBBB, 0xFFBBBBBB, 0xFF555555, 0xFFFF5555, 0xFF55FF55, 0xFFFFFF55,
41:      0xFF5555FF, 0xFFFF55FF, 0xFF55FFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF};
42:  if (n < 0)
43:    n = 0;
44:  if (n < 16)
45:    return base16[n];
46:  if (n < 232) {
47:    int c = n - 16;
48:    int r = c / 36, g = (c / 6) % 6, b = c % 6;
49:    int R = r ? 55 + r * 40 : 0, G = g ? 55 + g * 40 : 0, B = b ? 55 + b * 40 : 0;
50:    return 0xFF000000u | ((uint32_t)R << 16) | ((uint32_t)G << 8) | (uint32_t)B;
51:  }
52:  if (n > 255)
53:    n = 255;
54:  int v = 8 + (n - 232) * 10;
55:  return 0xFF000000u | ((uint32_t)v << 16) | ((uint32_t)v << 8) | (uint32_t)v;
56:}
57:
58:/* Process an ANSI SGR (Select Graphic Rendition) parameter list. */
59:static void handle_sgr(struct terminal *t) {
60:  int vals[16];
61:  int n = 0, cur = 0, have = 0;
62:  for (int i = 0; i < t->escape_len && n < 16; i++) {
63:    char c = t->escape_buf[i];
64:    if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') {
65:      cur = cur * 10 + (c - '0');
66:      have = 1;
67:    } else if (c == ';') {
68:      vals[n++] = cur;
69:      cur = 0;
70:    }
71:  }
72:  if (n < 16 && (have || t->escape_len == 0))
73:    vals[n++] = cur;
74:  if (n == 0) { /* ESC[m == reset */
75:    t->fg_color = t->default_fg;
76:    t->curr_bg_color = t->bg_color;
77:    t->bold = 0;
78:    return;
79:  }
80:
81:  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
82:    int v = vals[i];
83:    if (v == 0) {
84:      t->fg_color = t->default_fg;
85:      t->curr_bg_color = t->bg_color;
86:      t->bold = 0;
87:    } else if (v == 1) {
88:      t->bold = 1;
89:    } else if (v == 22) {
90:      t->bold = 0;
91:    } else if (v == 39) {
92:      t->fg_color = t->default_fg;
93:    } else if (v == 49) {
94:      t->curr_bg_color = t->bg_color;
95:    } else if (v >= 30 && v <= 37) {
96:      t->fg_color = term_xterm256(v - 30 + (t->bold ? 8 : 0));
97:    } else if (v >= 90 && v <= 97) {
98:      t->fg_color = term_xterm256(v - 90 + 8);
99:    } else if (v >= 40 && v <= 47) {
100:      t->curr_bg_color = term_xterm256(v - 40);
101:    } else if (v >= 100 && v <= 107) {
102:      t->curr_bg_color = term_xterm256(v - 100 + 8);
103:    } else if (v == 38 || v == 48) {
104:      uint32_t *tgt = (v == 38) ? &t->fg_color : &t->curr_bg_color;
105:      if (i + 2 < n && vals[i + 1] == 5) { /* 256-colour: 38;5;N */
106:        *tgt = term_xterm256(vals[i + 2]);
107:        i += 2;
108:      } else if (i + 4 < n && vals[i + 1] == 2) { /* truecolour: 38;2;r;g;b */
109:        *tgt = 0xFF000000u | ((uint32_t)(vals[i + 2] & 0xFF) << 16) |
110:               ((uint32_t)(vals[i + 3] & 0xFF) << 8) | (uint32_t)(vals[i + 4] & 0xFF);
111:        i += 4;
112:      }
113:    }
114:  }
115:}
116:
117:/* Parse up to two decimal CSI parameters separated by ';' from buf[0..len).
118: * Returns how many parameters were present (0, 1 or 2); a and b receive their
119: * values (0 when omitted). */
120:static int csi_params(const char *buf, int len, int *a, int *b) {
121:  int vals[2] = {0, 0};
122:  int which = 0, have = 0;
123:  for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
124:    char c = buf[i];
125:    if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') {
126:      vals[which] = vals[which] * 10 + (c - '0');
127:      have = 1;
128:    } else if (c == ';' && which < 1) {
129:      which++;
130:    }
131:  }
132:  *a = vals[0];
133:  *b = vals[1];
134:  return have ? which + 1 : 0;
135:}
136:
137:/* Clear one terminal cell to the current background (pixels + grids). */
138:static void term_clear_cell(struct terminal *t, struct gl_surface *surf, int cx,
139:                            int cy, int char_w, int char_h) {
140:  if (cx < 0 || cy < 0 || cx >= t->cols || cy >= t->rows)
141:    return;
142:  term_fill_rect(surf, cx * char_w, cy * char_h, char_w, char_h,
143:                 t->curr_bg_color);
144:  if (t->text_grid && t->attr_grid) {
145:    int idx = cy * t->cols + cx;
146:    t->text_grid[idx] = ' ';
147:    t->attr_grid[idx] = t->curr_bg_color;
148:  }
149:}
150:
151:/* Erase a previously painted caret by repainting its cell from the text/attr
152: * grid (background + glyph).  Idempotent; clears caret_shown.  This is what
153: * prevents stray cursor blocks after the cursor moves (newline/scroll). */
154:static void term_erase_caret(struct terminal *t, struct gl_surface *surf,
155:                             int char_w, int char_h) {
156:  if (!t->caret_shown)
157:    return;
158:  int px = t->caret_px, py = t->caret_py;
159:  t->caret_shown = 0;
160:  if (px < 0 || py < 0 || px >= t->cols || py >= t->rows)
161:    return;
162:  term_fill_rect(surf, px * char_w, py * char_h, char_w, char_h, t->bg_color);
163:  if (t->text_grid && t->attr_grid) {
164:    int idx = py * t->cols + px;
165:    char ch = (char)t->text_grid[idx];
166:    if (ch >= 32 && ch < 127)
167:      gl_draw_char(surf, px * char_w, py * char_h, ch, t->attr_grid[idx]);
168:  }
169:}
170:
171:/* Draw the text caret as a translucent block at the cursor cell, blended over
172: * the cell so the glyph stays readable.  Only a focused, caret-visible terminal
173: * shows one.  The previous caret is erased first so movement leaves no trail. */
174:static void term_draw_cursor(struct terminal *t, struct gl_surface *surf,
175:                             int char_w, int char_h) {
176:  term_erase_caret(t, surf, char_w, char_h);
177:
178:  if (!t->focused || !t->cursor_visible)
179:    return;
180:  int cx = t->cursor_x, cy = t->cursor_y;
181:  if (cx < 0 || cy < 0 || cx >= t->cols || cy >= t->rows)
182:    return;
183:
184:  const uint32_t caret = TERM_CARET_COLOR;
185:  int px0 = cx * char_w, py0 = cy * char_h;
186:  for (int y = 0; y < char_h; y++) {
187:    int sy = py0 + y;
188:    if (sy < 0 || sy >= surf->height)
189:      continue;
190:    for (int x = 0; x < char_w; x++) {
191:      int sx = px0 + x;
192:      if (sx < 0 || sx >= surf->width)
193:        continue;
194:      uint32_t *p = &surf->buffer[sy * surf->stride + sx];
195:      *p = gl_blend_pixel(caret, *p);
196:    }
197:  }
198:  t->caret_px = cx;
199:  t->caret_py = cy;
200:  t->caret_shown = 1;
201:}
202:
203:/* Dispatch a complete CSI sequence (ESC [ ... <final>). */
204:static void handle_csi(struct terminal *t, struct gl_surface *surf, char final,
205:                       int char_w, int char_h) {
206:  const char *eb = t->escape_buf;
207:  int len = t->escape_len;
208:
209:  /* Private mode: ESC [ ? Pn h/l — we honour 25 (show/hide caret). */
210:  if (len > 0 && eb[0] == '?') {
211:    int a, b;
212:    csi_params(eb + 1, len - 1, &a, &b);
213:    if (a == 25)
214:      t->cursor_visible = (final == 'h');
215:    return;
216:  }
217:
218:  if (final == 'm') {
219:    handle_sgr(t);
220:    return;
221:  }
222:
223:  int a, b;
224:  int n = csi_params(eb, len, &a, &b);
225:
226:  if (final == 'H' || final == 'f') {
227:    int row = (n >= 1 && a > 0) ? a - 1 : 0;
228:    int col = (n >= 2 && b > 0) ? b - 1 : 0;
229:    if (row >= t->rows)
230:      row = t->rows - 1;
231:    if (col >= t->cols)
232:      col = t->cols - 1;
233:    t->cursor_y = row < 0 ? 0 : row;
234:    t->cursor_x = col < 0 ? 0 : col;
235:  } else if (final == 'K') {
236:    int mode = (n >= 1) ? a : 0;
237:    int x0 = (mode == 1) ? 0 : t->cursor_x;
238:    int x1 = (mode == 0) ? t->cols - 1 : t->cursor_x;
239:    if (mode == 2) {
240:      x0 = 0;
241:      x1 = t->cols - 1;
242:    }
243:    for (int x = x0; x <= x1; x++)
244:      term_clear_cell(t, surf, x, t->cursor_y, char_w, char_h);
245:  } else if (final == 'J') {
246:    term_fill_rect(surf, 0, 0, surf->width, surf->height, t->curr_bg_color);
247:    if (t->text_grid && t->attr_grid) {
248:      memset(t->text_grid, ' ', t->cols * t->rows);
249:      for (int p = 0; p < t->cols * t->rows; p++)
250:        t->attr_grid[p] = t->curr_bg_color;
251:    }
252:    t->cursor_x = 0;
253:    t->cursor_y = 0;
254:  } else if (final == 'A' || final == 'B') {
255:    /* Cursor up/down by N (default 1) — pure vertical movement, clamped to
256:     * the grid. Unlike C/D below, up/down never "wraps" horizontally: that
257:     * would only make sense for something like a wide virtual scrollback,
258:     * which this terminal doesn't have. */
259:    int d = (n >= 1 && a > 0) ? a : 1;
260:    t->cursor_y += (final == 'A') ? -d : d;
261:    if (t->cursor_y < 0)
262:      t->cursor_y = 0;
263:    if (t->cursor_y >= t->rows)
264:      t->cursor_y = t->rows - 1;
265:  } else if (final == 'C' || final == 'D') {
266:    /*
267:     * Cursor forward/back by N cells, WRAPPING across row boundaries.
268:     *
269:     * Plain column clamping used to strand the cursor at column 0 (for 'D')
270:     * or cols-1 (for 'C') the instant a relative move reached the edge of
271:     * the current row, even when more of the move remained and an adjacent
272:     * row held the rest of the same logical line — e.g. a shell command
273:     * long enough to auto-wrap during typing. nxline.h's line editor
274:     * (user/sys/bin/nxline.h) repositions the caret with exactly these
275:     * relative CSI C/D sequences after every insert/delete/history-replace,
276:     * so any input line that wraps during editing would desync the caret
277:     * from the real insertion point without this fix — the visible cursor
278:     * and the byte actually being edited would silently drift apart.
279:     *
280:     * This grid has no per-row "this break was an autowrap, not a real
281:     * newline" flag to consult, so the fix wraps unconditionally across
282:     * every row boundary, not only autowrap ones. That's a deliberate
283:     * simplification: it's harmless for every current caller (nxline.h
284:     * only ever moves the caret within the single line it is actively
285:     * editing, never across an Enter/newline boundary — Enter always
286:     * submits and resets), and matches how most real terminals treat
287:     * relative cursor motion in practice.
288:     */
289:    int d = (n >= 1 && a > 0) ? a : 1;
290:    int pos = t->cursor_y * t->cols + t->cursor_x;
291:    pos += (final == 'C') ? d : -d;
292:    int max_pos = t->rows * t->cols - 1;
293:    if (pos < 0)
294:      pos = 0;
295:    if (pos > max_pos)
296:      pos = max_pos;
297:    t->cursor_y = pos / t->cols;
298:    t->cursor_x = pos % t->cols;
299:  } else if (final == 'G') {
300:    /* Cursor to column N (1-based). */
301:    int col = (n >= 1 && a > 0) ? a - 1 : 0;
302:    t->cursor_x = col < 0 ? 0 : (col >= t->cols ? t->cols - 1 : col);
303:  } else if (final == 'd') {
304:    /* Cursor to row N (1-based). */
305:    int row = (n >= 1 && a > 0) ? a - 1 : 0;
306:    t->cursor_y = row < 0 ? 0 : (row >= t->rows ? t->rows - 1 : row);
307:  } else if (final == 's') {
308:    t->saved_x = t->cursor_x;
309:    t->saved_y = t->cursor_y;
310:  } else if (final == 'u') {
311:    t->cursor_x = t->saved_x;
312:    t->cursor_y = t->saved_y;
313:  }
314:}
315:
316:int term_init(struct terminal *t, int cols, int rows, uint32_t fg,
317:              uint32_t bg) {
318:  if (cols < 1)
319:    cols = 1;
320:  if (rows < 1)
321:    rows = 1;
322:  t->cols = cols;
323:  t->rows = rows;
324:  t->cursor_x = 0;
325:  t->cursor_y = 0;
326:  t->cursor_visible = 1;
327:  t->caret_px = 0;
328:  t->caret_py = 0;
329:  t->caret_shown = 0;
330:  t->focused = 0;
331:  t->fg_color = fg;
332:  t->default_fg = fg;
333:  t->bg_color = bg;
334:  t->curr_bg_color = bg;
335:  t->bold = 0;
336:  t->saved_x = 0;
337:  t->saved_y = 0;
338:  t->escape_state = 0;
339:  t->escape_len = 0;
340:
341:  size_t cells = (size_t)cols * rows;
342:  t->text_grid = (uint8_t *)kmalloc(cells);
343:  t->attr_grid = (uint32_t *)kmalloc(cells * 4);
344:  if (!t->text_grid || !t->attr_grid) {
345:    term_free(t);
346:    return -1;
347:  }
348:  memset(t->text_grid, ' ', cells);
349:  for (size_t i = 0; i < cells; i++)
350:    t->attr_grid[i] = fg;
351:  return 0;
352:}
353:
354:void term_free(struct terminal *t) {
355:  if (t->text_grid) {
356:    kfree(t->text_grid);
357:    t->text_grid = NULL;
358:  }
359:  if (t->attr_grid) {
360:    kfree(t->attr_grid);
361:    t->attr_grid = NULL;
362:  }
363:}
364:
365:int term_resize(struct terminal *t, int cols, int rows) {
366:  if (cols < 1)
367:    cols = 1;
368:  if (rows < 1)
369:    rows = 1;
370:  uint8_t *ntext = (uint8_t *)kmalloc((size_t)cols * rows);
371:  uint32_t *nattr = (uint32_t *)kmalloc((size_t)cols * rows * 4);
372:  if (!ntext || !nattr) {
373:    if (ntext)
374:      kfree(ntext);
375:    if (nattr)
376:      kfree(nattr);
377:    return -1;
378:  }
379:  /* Fresh grids cleared to defaults; pixel reflow is the caller's concern. */
380:  memset(ntext, ' ', (size_t)cols * rows);
381:  for (size_t i = 0; i < (size_t)cols * rows; i++)
382:    nattr[i] = t->default_fg;
383:  term_free(t);
384:  t->text_grid = ntext;
385:  t->attr_grid = nattr;
386:  t->cols = cols;
387:  t->rows = rows;
388:  if (t->cursor_x >= cols)
389:    t->cursor_x = cols - 1;
390:  if (t->cursor_y >= rows)
391:    t->cursor_y = rows - 1;
392:  t->caret_shown = 0;
393:  return 0;
394:}
395:
396:void term_write(struct terminal *t, struct gl_surface *surf, const char *buf,
397:                size_t count) {
398:  if (!surf || !surf->buffer)
399:    return;
400:
401:  int char_w = graphics_font_max_width();
402:  int char_h = graphics_font_height();
403:  int cols = t->cols;
404:  int rows = t->rows;
405:
406:  for (size_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
407:    char c = buf[i];
408:
409:    if (t->escape_state == 0) {
410:      if (c == '\033') {
411:        t->escape_state = 1;
412:        t->escape_len = 0;
413:      } else if (c == '\n') {
414:        t->cursor_x = 0;
415:        t->cursor_y++;
416:      } else if (c == '\r') {
417:        t->cursor_x = 0;
418:      } else if (c == '\b' || c == 127) {
419:        if (t->cursor_x > 0)
420:          t->cursor_x--;
421:      } else if (c >= 32 && c < 127) {
422:        /* Check bounds and wrap BEFORE writing */
423:        if (t->cursor_x < 0)
424:          t->cursor_x = 0;
425:        if (t->cursor_y < 0)
426:          t->cursor_y = 0;
427:        if (t->cursor_x >= cols) {
428:          t->cursor_x = 0;
429:          t->cursor_y++;
430:        }
431:        if (t->cursor_y >= rows) {
432:          /* Scroll pixel buffer up by one text line */
433:          if (surf->height > char_h) {
434:            size_t line_size = (size_t)surf->stride * char_h;
435:            memmove(surf->buffer, surf->buffer + line_size,
436:                    (size_t)surf->stride * (surf->height - char_h) * 4);
437:          }
438:          /* Clear the freed last line */
439:          for (size_t p = (size_t)surf->stride * (surf->height - char_h);
440:               p < (size_t)surf->stride * surf->height; p++) {
441:            surf->buffer[p] = t->bg_color;
442:          }
443:
444:          /* Scroll text grids */
445:          if (t->text_grid && t->attr_grid) {
446:            memmove(t->text_grid, t->text_grid + cols, (size_t)cols * (rows - 1));
447:            memmove(t->attr_grid, t->attr_grid + cols,
448:                    (size_t)cols * (rows - 1) * 4);
449:            int last_row_start = cols * (rows - 1);
450:            memset(t->text_grid + last_row_start, ' ', cols);
451:            for (int p = 0; p < cols; p++)
452:              t->attr_grid[last_row_start + p] = t->default_fg;
453:          }
454:          t->cursor_y = rows - 1;
455:        }
456:
457:        /* Clear the glyph cell to the current background, then draw the glyph. */
458:        term_fill_rect(surf, t->cursor_x * char_w, t->cursor_y * char_h, char_w,
459:                       char_h, t->curr_bg_color);
460:        gl_draw_char(surf, t->cursor_x * char_w, t->cursor_y * char_h, c,
461:                     t->fg_color);
462:
463:        if (t->text_grid && t->attr_grid) {
464:          int idx = t->cursor_y * cols + t->cursor_x;
465:          if (idx < cols * rows) {
466:            t->text_grid[idx] = c;
467:            t->attr_grid[idx] = t->fg_color;
468:          }
469:        }
470:
471:        t->cursor_x++;
472:      }
473:    } else if (t->escape_state == 1) {
474:      if (c == '[')
475:        t->escape_state = 2;
476:      else
477:        t->escape_state = 0;
478:    } else if (t->escape_state == 2) {
479:      if ((c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z')) {
480:        handle_csi(t, surf, c, char_w, char_h);
481:        t->escape_state = 0;
482:      } else if (t->escape_len < 31) {
483:        t->escape_buf[t->escape_len++] = c;
484:      } else {
485:        t->escape_state = 0;
486:      }
487:    }
488:  }
489:
490:  /* Draw the caret at its final position for this batch. */
491:  term_draw_cursor(t, surf, char_w, char_h);
492:}
493:
494:void term_set_focus(struct terminal *t, struct gl_surface *surf, int focused) {
495:  if (focused == t->focused)
496:    return;
497:  if (!focused)
498:    term_clear_caret(t, surf);
499:  t->focused = focused;
500:}
501:
502:void term_clear_caret(struct terminal *t, struct gl_surface *surf) {
503:  if (!surf || !surf->buffer)
504:    return;
505:  int char_w = graphics_font_max_width();
506:  int char_h = graphics_font_height();
507:  term_erase_caret(t, surf, char_w, char_h);
508:}

68:/* LAPIC_DEFAULT_BASE is a physical address; registers are accessed at its
69: * direct-map kernel VA (phys_to_virt — identity while KERNEL_VIRT_BASE==0). */
70:static inline uint32_t lapic_read(uint32_t reg) {
71:    return *(volatile uint32_t *)phys_to_virt(LAPIC_DEFAULT_BASE + reg);
72:}
73:
74:static inline void lapic_write(uint32_t reg, uint32_t val) {
75:    *(volatile uint32_t *)phys_to_virt(LAPIC_DEFAULT_BASE + reg) = val;
76:}
77:
78:void lapic_init(void);
79:void lapic_eoi(void);
80:uint32_t lapic_get_id(void);
81:void lapic_send_ipi(uint32_t lapic_id, uint32_t flags);
82:void lapic_timer_calibrate(void);
83:void lapic_timer_setup(uint32_t hz);
84:void lapic_timer_stop(void);
85:
86:/* tsc_calibrate: measure the TSC frequency against the PIT and publish it into
87: * tsc_hz (docs/TIMER-MODEL.md §1).  Called once on the BSP from
88: * lapic_timer_calibrate(); idempotent.  tsc_hz is read by
89: * arch_impl_timer_get_freq() (arch/arch.h) to feed the arch-neutral mono_ns(). */
90:void tsc_calibrate(void);
91:extern uint64_t tsc_hz;
92:
93:#endif /* ARCH_AMD64_APIC_H */

@@@ kernel/include/drivers/gpu/gpu.h @@@
1:#ifndef _DRIVERS_GPU_H
2:#define _DRIVERS_GPU_H
3:
4:#include <stddef.h>
5:#include <stdint.h>
6:
7:struct gpu_device;
8:
9:struct gpu_ops {
10:  int (*init)(struct gpu_device *dev);
11:  /* Reconfigure the scanout to width x height at runtime.  Recreates the host
12:   * resource + backing and re-points the scanout; updates dev->width/height
13:   * and the framebuffer pointer.  0 on success.  (GFX-DYN-01 #49) */
14:  int (*set_mode)(struct gpu_device *dev, int width, int height);
15:  void *(*get_framebuffer)(struct gpu_device *dev, size_t *size);
16:  int (*flush)(struct gpu_device *dev, int x, int y, int w, int h);
17:  /* Atomically copy a region of a caller-owned ARGB8888 source (src_w x src_h,
18:   * stride == src_w) into the scanout backing AND transfer+flush it to the
19:   * host, all under the driver's own lock (S-STAB / RC2).  The compositor uses
20:   * this instead of get_framebuffer()+memcpy()+flush(): doing the copy under
21:   * the same lock that set_mode() takes to swap+free the backing closes the
22:   * use-after-free where a concurrent resolution/zoom change frees the scanout
23:   * mid-copy.  The driver copies only the intersection with its CURRENT scanout
24:   * and returns <0 (skip this frame) if src geometry no longer matches — never
25:   * an OOB.  0 on success (region presented). */
26:  int (*present)(struct gpu_device *dev, const uint32_t *src, int src_w,
27:                 int src_h, int x, int y, int w, int h);
28:  void (*destroy)(struct gpu_device *dev);
29:  /* Query the host's current preferred display size (what the device
30:   * advertises via GET_DISPLAY_INFO).  0 on success.  (GFX-DYN-01 #54) */
31:  int (*get_display_info)(struct gpu_device *dev, int *width, int *height);
32:  /* Poll for a host-initiated display-change event.  Returns 1 and fills
33:   * new_w/new_h when the host resized the output, 0 if nothing changed,
34:   * <0 on error/unsupported transport. */
35:  int (*poll_events)(struct gpu_device *dev, int *new_w, int *new_h);
36:};
37:
38:struct gpu_device {
39:  char name[32];
40:  int width;
41:  int height;
42:  int bpp;
43:  /* The scanout buffer is reached ONLY through ops->get_framebuffer (S-ALIGN
44:   * F7) — the old raw framebuffer_virt field was a second, field-level path
45:   * to the same memory and is retired. */
46:  size_t framebuffer_size;
47:  struct gpu_ops *ops;
48:  void *priv;              /* Driver private data */
49:  struct gpu_device *next; /* Linked list for multi-gpu */
50:};
51:
52:/* Core GPU Management */
53:int gpu_register(struct gpu_device *dev);
54:void gpu_unregister(struct gpu_device *dev);
55:struct gpu_device *gpu_get_primary(void);
56:
57:/* Contract wrappers over the primary GPU (GFX-DYN-01).  The kernel core
58: * (compositor) calls these instead of reaching into a driver: no driver
59: * internals, no magic numbers in the core. */
60:int gpu_set_mode(int width, int height);
61:int gpu_get_display_info(int *width, int *height);
62:int gpu_poll_events(int *new_w, int *new_h);
63:
64:/* Surface-speaking present (graphics-port): the provider contract talks the
65: * same semantic unit the whole stack does — a validated gfx_surface plus a
66: * damage rect — instead of raw pointer+geometry ints.  The S-STAB
67: * gfx_surface_verify() gate runs HERE, at the core/driver seam, so a
68: * geometry/allocation desync panics loudly at the source instead of becoming
69: * a silent OOB copy in a driver.  Present semantics are unchanged underneath
70: * (atomic copy+flush under the driver lock, <0 = skip this frame). */
71:struct gfx_rect;
72:struct gl_surface;
73:int gpu_present_surface(const struct gl_surface *src,
74:                        const struct gfx_rect *damage);
75:
76:#endif

@@@ kernel/include/drivers/usb/usb.h @@@
1:#ifndef _DRIVERS_USB_USB_H
2:#define _DRIVERS_USB_USB_H
3:
4:/*
5: * kernel/include/drivers/usb/usb.h
6: * USB core — controller-agnostic bus model.
7: *
8: * Layering (ASTRA): a host controller driver (xHCI / EHCI / UHCI) registers a
9: * struct usb_hcd implementing usb_hcd_ops. The core enumerates each port,
10: * reads standard descriptors over the control pipe, and hands HID interfaces
11: * to usb_hid.c, which translates reports into the existing evdev input core
12: * (virtio_input_add_event). The HCD never knows about HID; the HID driver
13: * never knows whether the transport is xHCI/EHCI/UHCI.
14: *
15: * Addressing is delegated to the HCD via enumerate_port(): UHCI/EHCI send a
16: * SET_ADDRESS on the default pipe, xHCI issues an Address Device command — the
17: * core must not assume either.
18: */
19:
20:#include <kernel/types.h>
21:
22:/* --- USB speeds --- */
23:#define USB_SPEED_LOW   1
24:#define USB_SPEED_FULL  2
25:#define USB_SPEED_HIGH  3
26:#define USB_SPEED_SUPER 4
27:
28:/* --- Standard request types (bmRequestType) --- */
29:#define USB_DIR_OUT 0x00
30:#define USB_DIR_IN  0x80
31:#define USB_TYPE_STANDARD 0x00
32:#define USB_TYPE_CLASS    0x20
33:#define USB_RECIP_DEVICE    0x00
34:#define USB_RECIP_INTERFACE 0x01
35:
36:/* --- Standard requests (bRequest) --- */
37:#define USB_REQ_GET_DESCRIPTOR 0x06
38:#define USB_REQ_SET_ADDRESS    0x05
39:#define USB_REQ_SET_CONFIG     0x09
40:
41:/* HID class requests */

52:#define USB_DT_HID       0x21
53:#define USB_DT_HID_REPORT 0x22

59:#define HID_PROTOCOL_KEYBOARD 0x01
60:#define HID_PROTOCOL_MOUSE    0x02

66:#define USB_REQ_SET_FEATURE   0x03

74:#define HUB_PORT_LOWSPEED   0x0200

78:/* 8-byte SETUP packet */
79:struct usb_setup {

81:    uint8_t  bRequest;
82:    uint16_t wValue;
83:    uint16_t wIndex;
84:    uint16_t wLength;

138:/* A USB device the core enumerated and addressed. */
139:struct usb_device {
140:    struct usb_hcd *hcd;
141:    uint8_t  addr;            /* USB address (1..127), HCD-assigned */
142:    uint8_t  speed;
143:    int      port;            /* root-hub port index (for root devices) */
144:    uint8_t  max_packet0;     /* EP0 max packet */
145:    uint16_t vendor, product;
146:    uint8_t  dev_class, dev_subclass, dev_protocol;
147:    void    *hcd_priv;        /* HCD per-device state (xHCI slot, etc.) */
148:
149:    /* Topology (for devices behind external hubs). */
150:    struct usb_device *parent; /* upstream hub, NULL if on the root hub */
151:    uint8_t  hub_port;         /* 1-based port on the parent hub */
152:    uint8_t  root_port;        /* 1-based root-hub port at the top of the path */
153:    uint32_t route;            /* xHCI route string (0 for root devices) */
154:    uint8_t  tier;             /* hub depth from root (0 = root device) */
155:    int      is_hub;
156:
157:    /* HID interface of interest (filled by usb_hid bind) */
158:    int      hid_iface;
159:    uint8_t  hid_ep_in;       /* endpoint address (with 0x80 IN bit) */
160:    int      hid_ep_max;      /* wMaxPacketSize of that endpoint */
161:    uint8_t  hid_interval;
162:    uint8_t  hid_protocol;    /* HID_PROTOCOL_KEYBOARD / _MOUSE (boot) */
163:    int      hid_use_report;  /* 1 = report-protocol HID (non-boot, e.g. tablet) */
164:    int      hid_report_len;  /* report-descriptor length (HID desc wDescriptorLength) */
165:    /* Absolute pointer, parsed from the HID report descriptor (USB tablet). */
166:    int      hid_is_abs;      /* 1 = reports absolute X/Y */
167:    uint16_t hid_abs_x_off;   /* bit offset of X within the input report */
168:    uint16_t hid_abs_y_off;   /* bit offset of Y */
169:    uint8_t  hid_abs_bits;    /* X/Y field size in bits */
170:    uint32_t hid_abs_max;     /* logical max of X/Y (for scaling) */
171:    int16_t  hid_btn_off;     /* bit offset of the first button, -1 if none */
172:    int      in_use;
173:};
174:
175:/* Host controller driver contract. */
176:struct usb_hcd_ops {
177:    int  (*num_ports)(struct usb_hcd *hcd);
178:    int  (*port_connected)(struct usb_hcd *hcd, int port);
179:    /* Reset + address a device on root-hub `port`; fill *out (addr/speed/
180:     * max_packet0/hcd_priv). Returns 0 on success, <0 on failure/no device. */
181:    int  (*enumerate_port)(struct usb_hcd *hcd, int port, struct usb_device *out);
182:    /* Address a device whose topology (parent/route/tier/root_port/speed) the
183:     * core already filled, reached through an external hub. The hub did the
184:     * port reset; this only assigns the address/slot. Optional (NULL = no hub
185:     * support on this controller). Returns 0 on success. */
186:    int  (*address_dev)(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *dev);
187:    /* Control transfer on the device's default pipe. data may be NULL.
188:     * Returns bytes transferred (>=0) or <0 on error. */
189:    int  (*control)(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *dev,
190:                    const struct usb_setup *setup, void *data, int len);
191:    /* Configure an interrupt IN endpoint for periodic polling. */
192:    int  (*intr_open)(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *dev,
193:                      uint8_t ep_addr, int max_packet, int interval);
194:    /* Non-blocking poll of the interrupt IN endpoint: copies up to len bytes
195:     * into buf. Returns bytes (0 if nothing new) or <0. */
196:    int  (*intr_poll)(struct usb_hcd *hcd, struct usb_device *dev,
197:                      uint8_t ep_addr, void *buf, int len);
198:};
199:
200:struct usb_hcd {
201:    const char *name;
202:    struct usb_hcd_ops *ops;
203:    void *priv;
204:};
205:
206:/* --- USB core API --- */
207:
208:/* Called by each HCD after it has reset its controller. The core immediately
209: * enumerates the controller's ports and binds HID devices. */
210:void usb_register_hcd(struct usb_hcd *hcd);
211:
212:/* Control-transfer convenience used by the core and class drivers. */
213:int  usb_control(struct usb_device *dev, uint8_t bmRequestType, uint8_t bRequest,
214:                 uint16_t wValue, uint16_t wIndex, void *data, uint16_t wLength);
215:
216:/* Subsystem entry point: register the HCD drivers and run driver matching so
217: * each present controller is probed. Called from the input init path. */
218:void usb_init(void);
219:
220:/* Periodic poll of all bound HID endpoints; drives the evdev input core.
221: * Called from the same place keyboard_poll() is serviced. */
222:void usb_hid_poll(void);
223:
224:/* Internal: usb_hid.c entry, called by the core for each enumerated device. */
225:void usb_hid_probe_device(struct usb_device *dev);
226:
227:/* HCD driver registration hooks (each calls driver_register on its driver). */
228:void xhci_register(void);
229:void ehci_register(void);
230:void uhci_register(void);
