@@@ kernel/include/drivers/timer.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/drivers/timer.h
3: * ARM Generic Timer
4: */
5:#ifndef _DRIVERS_TIMER_H
6:#define _DRIVERS_TIMER_H
7:
8:#include <kernel/list.h>
9:#include <kernel/types.h>
10:
11:/* Timer frequency (will be read from CNTFRQ_EL0) */
12:extern uint64_t timer_freq;
13:
14:/* System ticks since boot */
15:extern volatile uint64_t jiffies;
16:
17:/* Timer configuration */
18:#define HZ                                                                     \
19:  100 /* Reduced frequency for better performance in non-optimized kernel */
20:
21:/* Time conversion macros */
22:#define MSEC_PER_SEC 1000UL
23:#define USEC_PER_SEC 1000000UL
24:#define NSEC_PER_SEC 1000000000UL
25:
26:#define msecs_to_jiffies(m) ((uint64_t)(m) * HZ / MSEC_PER_SEC)
27:#define jiffies_to_msecs(j) ((uint64_t)(j) * MSEC_PER_SEC / HZ)
28:
29:/* Nanoseconds per scheduler tick (the jiffies granularity). The whole 3-tier
30: * model (docs/TIMER-MODEL.md) reconciles the tick clocks against this real-time
31: * stride derived from the hardware counter. */
32:#define NS_PER_TICK (NSEC_PER_SEC / HZ)
33:
34:/* Functions */
35:void timer_init(void);
36:void timer_init_percpu(void);
37:uint64_t timer_get_ticks(void);
38:uint64_t timer_get_us(void);
39:void timer_delay_us(uint64_t us);
40:void timer_delay_ms(uint64_t ms);
41:
42:/* mono_ns - monotonic nanoseconds since boot, derived from the free-running
43: * hardware counter (arch_timer_get_count / arch_timer_get_freq). This is the
44: * arch-neutral REAL-TIME reference every timer tier compares against to recover
45: * lost ticks; jiffies is a cheap integer view of it. Defined in core/timer.c. */
46:uint64_t mono_ns(void);
47:/* timer_get_ns - alias of mono_ns() (the canonical real-time clock); replaces
48: * the per-arch timer_get_us() path so amd64 stops returning jiffies*1000. */
49:uint64_t timer_get_ns(void);
50:/* timer_counts_to_ns - scale a raw hardware-counter delta to nanoseconds.
51: * The scheduler accumulates per-process CPU time in raw counter units (a cheap
52: * subtraction, no divide in the hot path) and converts via this only on read. */
53:uint64_t timer_counts_to_ns(uint64_t counts);
54:
55:/* Tier 2 per-CPU clock — HAL-driven, arch-neutral (docs/TIMER-MODEL.md §3).
56: * timer_percpu_tick(): per-tick drift accounting + compare reprogram against the
57: *   hardware counter (arch_timer_get_freq/count/set_compare); catch-up clamp
58: *   recovers lost ticks. Called from each arch's timer IRQ before the scheduler
59: *   tick. arch_timer_set_compare() reprograms a one-shot timer (aarch64) and is
60: *   a no-op for a periodic timer (amd64), so the one routine serves both.
61: * timer_percpu_arm(): seed the per-CPU schedule on this core's timer bring-up. */
62:struct cpu_info;
63:void timer_percpu_tick(struct cpu_info *cpu);
64:void timer_percpu_arm(struct cpu_info *cpu);
65:
66:/* Internal Handlers */
67:struct pt_regs;
68:struct pt_regs *timer_handler(struct pt_regs *regs);
69:struct pt_regs *kernel_timer_tick(struct pt_regs *regs);
70:
71:/* Timer callback type */
72:typedef void (*timer_callback_t)(void *data);
73:
74:/* Software timer structure */
75:struct timer {
76:  struct list_head list;
77:  uint64_t expires; /* Expiration time in jiffies (global monotonic base) */

14:/* PL011 Register offsets */
15:#define UART_DR 0x00    /* Data Register */

17:#define UART_FR 0x18    /* Flag Register */
18:#define UART_ILPR 0x20  /* IrDA Low-Power Counter */
19:#define UART_IBRD 0x24  /* Integer Baud Rate */
20:#define UART_FBRD 0x28  /* Fractional Baud Rate */
21:#define UART_LCR_H 0x2C /* Line Control */
22:#define UART_CR 0x30    /* Control Register */
23:#define UART_IFLS 0x34  /* Interrupt FIFO Level Select */
24:#define UART_IMSC 0x38  /* Interrupt Mask Set/Clear */
25:#define UART_RIS 0x3C   /* Raw Interrupt Status */
26:#define UART_MIS 0x40   /* Masked Interrupt Status */
27:#define UART_ICR 0x44   /* Interrupt Clear */
28:#define UART_DMACR 0x48 /* DMA Control */

30:/* Flag Register bits */
31:#define UART_FR_TXFE BIT(7) /* TX FIFO Empty */
32:#define UART_FR_RXFF BIT(6) /* RX FIFO Full */
33:#define UART_FR_TXFF BIT(5) /* TX FIFO Full */
34:#define UART_FR_RXFE BIT(4) /* RX FIFO Empty */
35:#define UART_FR_BUSY BIT(3) /* UART Busy */
36:
37:/* Control Register bits */
38:#define UART_CR_RXE BIT(9)    /* Receive Enable */
39:#define UART_CR_TXE BIT(8)    /* Transmit Enable */
40:#define UART_CR_UARTEN BIT(0) /* UART Enable */
41:
42:/* Line Control bits */
43:#define UART_LCR_H_WLEN_8 (3 << 5) /* 8 bits */
44:#define UART_LCR_H_FEN BIT(4)      /* FIFO Enable */
45:

51:void uart_puts(const char *s);
52:void uart_puthex(uint64_t val);
53:
54:/* uart_putc_emergency - lock-free TX for fault context (see kernel/fault.h).
55: * Identical output path to uart_putc but never takes a spinlock: usable from
56: * an exception handler even when uart_lock is held by a wedged CPU.  May
57: * interleave with concurrent normal output. */

54:#define VIRTIO_STATUS_FAILED 128

56:/* VirtIO Ring Descriptors */
57:#define VRING_DESC_F_NEXT 1
58:#define VRING_DESC_F_WRITE 2
59:#define VRING_DESC_F_INDIRECT 4
60:
61:/* transport ops */
62:struct virtio_device;
63:struct virtio_transport_ops {
64:  uint32_t (*read32)(struct virtio_device *dev, uint32_t offset);
65:  void (*write32)(struct virtio_device *dev, uint32_t offset, uint32_t val);
66:  void (*notify)(struct virtio_device *dev, uint32_t queue_idx);
67:};

70:  hal_device_t hal_dev;
71:  uintptr_t base;
72:  uint32_t irq;
73:  uint32_t device_id;
74:  bool is_legacy;
75:  const struct virtio_transport_ops *ops;
76:  uintptr_t isr_base;
77:  uintptr_t notify_base;
78:  void *priv;
79:  spinlock_t lock;
80:};
81:
82:typedef struct virtio_device *virtio_handle_t;
83:
84:/* VirtIO Ring Descriptors */
85:#define VRING_DESC_F_NEXT 1
86:#define VRING_DESC_F_WRITE 2
87:#define VRING_DESC_F_INDIRECT 4
88:
89:struct vring_desc {
90:  uint64_t addr;
91:  uint32_t len;
92:  uint16_t flags;
93:  uint16_t next;
94:};
95:
96:struct vring_avail {
97:  uint16_t flags;
98:  uint16_t idx;
99:  uint16_t ring[];
100:};
101:
102:struct vring_used_elem {
103:  uint32_t id;
104:  uint32_t len;
105:};
106:
107:struct vring_used {
108:  uint16_t flags;
109:  uint16_t idx;
110:  struct vring_used_elem ring[];
111:};
112:
113:/* API */
114:static inline uint32_t virtio_read_reg(virtio_handle_t dev, uint32_t offset) {
115:  return dev->ops->read32(dev, offset);
116:}
117:
118:static inline void virtio_write_reg(virtio_handle_t dev, uint32_t offset,
119:                                    uint32_t val) {
120:  dev->ops->write32(dev, offset, val);
121:}
122:
123:static inline void virtio_notify(virtio_handle_t dev, uint32_t queue_idx) {
124:  dev->ops->notify(dev, queue_idx);
125:}
126:
127:/* Device-config space access (GFX-DYN-01 F7): reads/writes a device's
128: * device-specific configuration at byte 'offset', transport-agnostically.
129: * On VirtIO-MMIO this is base+VIRTIO_MMIO_CONFIG+offset; on VirtIO-PCI modern it
130: * is the device-specific capability region.  Implemented by the arch transport
131: * so drivers (e.g. virtio-gpu events) need not know the transport. */
132:uint32_t virtio_config_read32(virtio_handle_t dev, uint32_t offset);
133:void virtio_config_write32(virtio_handle_t dev, uint32_t offset, uint32_t val);
134:

139:                           virtio_handle_t *out_dev, uint32_t *out_irq);
140:void virtio_setup_queue(virtio_handle_t dev, uint32_t queue_idx,
141:                        uint64_t desc_addr, uint64_t avail_addr,
142:                        uint64_t used_addr);

1:#ifndef _GRAPHICS_GL_H
2:#define _GRAPHICS_GL_H
3:
4:#include <stddef.h>
5:#include <stdint.h>
6:
7:/*
8: * TinyGL: A simple software rasterization library.
9: * Operates on 32-bit ARGB buffers.
10: */
11:
12:struct gl_surface {
13:  int width;
14:  int height;
15:  int stride; /* in pixels, usually width */
16:  uint32_t *buffer;
17:  uint8_t *alpha_mask;
18:  /* S-STAB: number of valid uint32_t words actually backing 'buffer'.  The
19:   * whole raster path indexes buffer[y*stride+x] and only ever bounds-checks
20:   * against width/height, which is memory-safe ONLY if the geometry matches the
21:   * allocation (stride>=width AND height*stride<=capacity).  Nothing enforced
22:   * that invariant, so any geometry desync (a resize race, a stale scanout, a
23:   * driver reporting a size that outran its buffer) turned into a silent OOB
24:   * write into adjacent kernel RAM — the class of bug behind the UTM panics.
25:   * capacity makes the invariant checkable at the source; 0 = "unknown/legacy"
26:   * (an unconverted construction site), which gfx_surface_verify() treats as
27:   * un-instrumented rather than as a violation. */
28:  size_t capacity;
29:};
30:
31:/* gfx_surface_verify - S-STAB invariant gate.  Panics with the full geometry vs
32: * allocation if a surface is internally inconsistent (stride<width, or
33: * height*stride>capacity), catching a geometry desync at bind time — before the
34: * first OOB write scribbles kernel memory — instead of a mangled fault later.
35: * 'where' names the bind site for the panic message.  No-op when capacity==0
36: * (site not yet instrumented) so partial rollout never false-panics. */
37:void gfx_surface_verify(const struct gl_surface *surf, const char *where);
38:
39:/* Exact round-to-nearest divide-by-255 for x in [0, ~65790] (classic identity,
40: * no integer division).  Replaces the ">>8" (÷256) approximation that dimmed
41: * blended pixels — GFX-DYN-01 #121.4. */
42:static inline uint32_t gl_div255(uint32_t x) {
43:  x += 128;
44:  return (x + (x >> 8)) >> 8;
45:}
46:
47:/* Alpha-blend a source ARGB pixel over a destination ARGB pixel (straight
48: * over operator, opaque result).  Shared by the compositor and the terminal
49: * emulator so both use one definition. */
50:static inline uint32_t gl_blend_pixel(uint32_t fg, uint32_t bg) {
51:  uint32_t alpha = (fg >> 24) & 0xFF;
52:  if (alpha == 255)
53:    return fg;
54:  if (alpha == 0)
55:    return bg;
56:  uint32_t inv_alpha = 255 - alpha;
57:  uint32_t r =
58:      gl_div255(((fg >> 16) & 0xFF) * alpha + ((bg >> 16) & 0xFF) * inv_alpha);
59:  uint32_t g =
60:      gl_div255(((fg >> 8) & 0xFF) * alpha + ((bg >> 8) & 0xFF) * inv_alpha);
61:  uint32_t b = gl_div255((fg & 0xFF) * alpha + (bg & 0xFF) * inv_alpha);
62:  return 0xFF000000 | (r << 16) | (g << 8) | b;
63:}
64:
65:/* Primitives */
66:void gl_clear(struct gl_surface *surf, uint32_t color);
67:void gl_draw_pixel(struct gl_surface *surf, int x, int y, uint32_t color);
68:void gl_draw_line(struct gl_surface *surf, int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1,
69:                  uint32_t color);
70:void gl_draw_rect(struct gl_surface *surf, int x, int y, int w, int h,
71:                  uint32_t color);
72:void gl_draw_rect_fill(struct gl_surface *surf, int x, int y, int w, int h,
73:                       uint32_t color);
74:void gl_blit(struct gl_surface *dst, struct gl_surface *src, int dx, int dy);
75:void gl_draw_char(struct gl_surface *surf, int x, int y, uint32_t codepoint,
76:                  uint32_t color);
77:void gl_draw_string(struct gl_surface *surf, int x, int y, const char *str,
78:                    uint32_t color);
79:/* Clipped variant: identical to gl_draw_string but writes only pixels inside
80: * [cx1,cx2) x [cy1,cy2).  Used by the damage-clipped compositor so title text
81: * never paints outside the per-frame damage box. */
82:void gl_draw_string_clipped(struct gl_surface *surf, int x, int y,
83:                            const char *str, uint32_t color, int cx1, int cy1,
84:                            int cx2, int cy2);
85:void gl_swizzle_bgr(
86:    struct gl_surface *surf); /* Convert ABGR to ARGB if needed */

26: * context.  A kernel thread calls this to enter schedule() without a hardware
27: * trap; it "returns" only when this thread is scheduled again.  Implemented
28: * per-arch (aarch64 exception.S / amd64 isr_stubs.S) by building a pt_regs

35: * leg stalls CPU0; do not build new blocking primitives on this until that is

1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/block.h
3: * Block-device contract (ASTRA seam: virtio-blk -> block -> fs provider -> VFS).
4: *
5: * The FS stack (GPT, ext4, buffer cache) consumes ONLY this contract; it never
6: * names a concrete backend.  Today's backends are virtio-blk (the real device,
7: * `make run` and the dev loop) and the RAM-backed ramdisk (a GRUB multiboot2
8: * module, the self-contained release ISO).  Sectors are 512 bytes.
9: */

20:};

22:/* Make 'dev' the active block backend (last registration wins).  main.c
23: * registers virtio-blk first and lets the ramdisk override it only when a
24: * boot module is present, so the dev loop keeps using the real device. */

1:#ifndef _KERNEL_BOOTPHASE_H
2:#define _KERNEL_BOOTPHASE_H
3:
4:/* Boot-phase tracking (S-ALIGN F9) — the K1/K2/K3 boot model made explicit:
5: *   K1  memory/hardware bring-up (CPU, IRQ, timer, PMM/VMM, SMP)
6: *   K2  kernel subsystem init (bus/block/GPU/VFS/registry/sched/compositor)
7: *   K3  userland bring-up (PID1) — enters ONLY after K1+K2 are confirmed
8: *   RUN steady state
9: * The phase is single-writer (the BSP during kernel_main) and read by
10: * panic() to stamp fault reports and scope failure policy: a K3-only
11: * failure (userland won't load) must not take down a healthy K1+K2 —
12: * the kernel stays alive and diagnosable (kernel-alone mode). */
13:enum boot_phase {
14:  BOOT_PHASE_K1_HW = 0,
15:  BOOT_PHASE_K2_SUBSYS,
16:  BOOT_PHASE_K3_USERLAND,
17:  BOOT_PHASE_RUNNING,
18:};
19:
20:void boot_phase_set(enum boot_phase p);
21:enum boot_phase boot_phase_get(void);
22:const char *boot_phase_name(enum boot_phase p);

24:#endif /* _KERNEL_BOOTPHASE_H */

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/buffer.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/buffer.h
3: * Buffer Cache (Zero-Copy) for Block Devices
4: *
5: * Declares the public API for the buffer cache (kernel/mm/buffer.c).
6: *
7: * The buffer cache sits between the filesystem (ext4) and the VirtIO block
8: * driver.  Each cached block occupies one 4KB PMM page (BLOCK_SIZE ==
9: * PAGE_SIZE).  buf->data points directly into that PMM page (zero-copy).
10: *
11: * Callers must bracket every use of a buffer with buffer_get() / buffer_put()
12: * to maintain the ref_count; buffers with ref_count > 0 are pinned and will
13: * not be evicted.
14: *
15: * Known issues (see docs/review/analysis/01-mm-memory-management.md):
16: *   MM-BUF-01  (W3 BUG)         MAX_BUFFERS not a hard cap.
17: *   MM-BUF-02  (W2 PERF)        Duplicate disk reads on concurrent miss.
18: *   MM-BUF-03  (W2 BUG/SECURITY) No per-buffer content lock; data race.
19: *   MM-BUF-04  (W2 REFINE)      buffer_sync() flushes at most 64 buffers.
20: *   MM-BUF-05  (W1 REFINE)      Weak hash and fixed bucket count.
21: */
22:#ifndef _KERNEL_BUFFER_H
23:#define _KERNEL_BUFFER_H
24:
25:#include <kernel/list.h>
26:#include <kernel/types.h>
27:
28:/* BLOCK_SIZE: filesystem block size; matches PAGE_SIZE (4KB) for zero-copy. */
29:#define BLOCK_SIZE 4096 /* Matches Page Size */
30:#ifndef SECTOR_SIZE
31:#define SECTOR_SIZE 512
32:#endif /* SECTOR_SIZE */
33:/* SECTORS_PER_BLOCK: number of 512-byte disk sectors per cached block (= 8). */
34:#define SECTORS_PER_BLOCK (BLOCK_SIZE / SECTOR_SIZE)
35:
36:/* BUFFER_UPTODATE: buf->data reflects the on-disk content (read has completed). */
37:#define BUFFER_UPTODATE 0x1
38:/* BUFFER_DIRTY: buf->data has been modified and must be written to disk before
39: * the buffer can be evicted.  Set by filesystem code; cleared by buffer_sync(). */
40:#define BUFFER_DIRTY 0x2
41:
42:/*
43: * struct block_buffer - cache entry for one 4KB disk block.
44: *
45: * block:     logical block number (in BLOCK_SIZE units, not sector units).
46: *            Callers multiply by SECTORS_PER_BLOCK to get the sector offset.
47: * data:      pointer to a 4KB PMM page holding the block content.
48: *            NOTE(MM-BUF-03): There is no per-buffer lock protecting data;
49: *            concurrent reads and buffer_sync() writes race.
50: * flags:     OR of BUFFER_UPTODATE / BUFFER_DIRTY; protected by buffer_lock.
51: * ref_count: caller reference count; protected by buffer_lock.
52: *            Buffers with ref_count > 0 cannot be evicted.
53: * list:      entry in the global LRU list; head = most recently used.
54: * hash:      entry in hash_table[bucket] collision list.
55: */
56:struct block_buffer {
57:  uint64_t block; /* Block index (4KB units) */
58:  uint8_t *data;  /* Pointer to 4KB page (Zero-copy) */
59:  uint32_t flags;
60:  uint32_t ref_count;
61:
62:  struct list_head list; /* LRU List */
63:  struct list_head hash; /* Hash Table Collision List */
64:};
65:
66:/* API */
67:void buffer_init(void);
68:
69:/* Get a buffer for a block. Reads from disk if not cached.
70: * Increments ref_count. */
71:struct block_buffer *buffer_get(uint64_t block);
72:
73:/* Release a buffer. Decrements ref_count. */
74:void buffer_put(struct block_buffer *buf);
75:
76:/* Write all dirty buffers to disk */
77:void buffer_sync(void);
78:
79:#endif /* _KERNEL_BUFFER_H */
80:

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/compositor_style.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/compositor_style.h
3: * Compositor appearance model (GFX-DYN-01 / DIR-07).
4: *
5: * Four orthogonal concerns, deliberately separated (the maintainer's model):
6: *
7: *   Policy     = behaviour   (floating / tiled / mobile window management)
8: *   Style      = form        (titlebar? borders? rounded? shadows? sizes)
9: *   Theme      = colours     (window palette: titlebar, text, accent)
10: *   Background = desktop     (base colour + gradient reference colours)
11: *
12: * Style and Theme never touch the scene graph, surfaces, input or buffers —
13: * they only change HOW the existing windows are rendered.  The compositor reads
14: * the active style/theme/background each frame; switching them re-renders with
15: * no other state change.
16: */
17:#ifndef _KERNEL_COMPOSITOR_STYLE_H
18:#define _KERNEL_COMPOSITOR_STYLE_H
19:
20:#include <kernel/nx_contract.h>
21:#include <stdint.h>
22:
23:/* Window-management policy (behaviour).  Tiling/mobile are hooks for the
24: * desktop-vs-mobile transform; floating is the only one wired today. */
25:typedef enum {
26:  WINDOW_POLICY_FLOATING = 0,
27:  WINDOW_POLICY_TILED,
28:  WINDOW_POLICY_MOBILE,
29:} window_policy_t;
30:
31:/* Style = form of the window chrome (no colours here). */
32:typedef struct compositor_style {
33:  int titlebar;        /* draw a title bar + close button                  */
34:  int window_borders;  /* draw a 1px border around windows                 */
35:  int rounded_corners; /* round window corners (border_radius)             */
36:  int shadows;         /* draw drop shadows                                */
37:  int animations;      /* enable open/close/move animations               */
38:  int titlebar_height; /* px; 0 ⇒ no chrome regardless of `titlebar`       */
39:  int border_radius;   /* px corner radius when rounded_corners            */
40:  int shadow_size;     /* px shadow spread when shadows                    */
41:  int shadow_type;     /* 0=solid win_bg (Retro), 1=fast SDF, 2=premium grad.  */
42:  int button_shape;    /* 0 = circle (macOS), 1 = square (Retro/Win95) */
43:  int button_side;     /* 0 = left, 1 = right */
44:} compositor_style_t;
45:
46:/* Theme = colour palette (ARGB8888), windows only. */
47:typedef struct compositor_theme {
48:  uint32_t win_bg;              /* default window background                */
49:  uint32_t title_active;        /* focused title bar                        */
50:  uint32_t title_inactive;      /* unfocused title bar                      */

10:/* Forward declaraton */
11:struct process;

13:/* Per-CPU information structure */
14:struct cpu_info {
15:  struct cpu_info *self; /* Must be at offset 0 for %gs:0 access on x86_64 */
16:  uint32_t cpu_id;
17:  uint32_t online;
18:  uint64_t stack_top;      /* Kernel Stack Top */
19:  uint64_t user_stack_tmp; /* Temp storage for user RSP during syscall/interrupt */
20:  struct process *current_task;
21:  uint64_t next_tick_target;
22:  uint64_t tick_error_acc;
23:  uint64_t tick_count;
24:  /* Raw hardware-counter value at which the current task last started running on
25:   * this CPU; schedule() charges (arch_timer_get_count() - sched_run_count) to
26:   * the outgoing task's cpu_time_counts (Tier 3 per-process CPU time, converted
27:   * to ns only on read — docs/TIMER-MODEL.md §4). */
28:  uint64_t sched_run_count;
29:
30:  /* Scheduler Local Data (Multicore Optimization) */
31:  struct list_head runqueues[32];
32:  uint32_t prio_bitmap;
33:  spinlock_t sched_lock; /* Local runqueue protection */
34:  struct process *idle_task;
35:
36:  /* Per-CPU software timer wheel (kernel/core/timer.c): each CPU fires its OWN
37:   * timers in kernel_timer_tick against the global jiffies clock, so a process
38:   * sleeping on this core is woken locally — no cross-CPU dependency, no global
39:   * timer-lock contention. */
40:  struct list_head timer_list;
41:  spinlock_t timer_lock;
42:
43:  char printk_buf[2048];
44:  char syscall_buf[2048];
45:  uint32_t in_printk;
46:  uint32_t printk_dropped;
47:
48:  /* Fault recursion depth (Phase A, kernel/fault.h).  Incremented by
49:   * fault_enter() at exception-dispatch entry; depth > 1 means a fault
50:   * occurred inside a fault handler — the dispatcher emits one raw line via
51:   * fault_printf and halts instead of recursing to a triple fault. */
52:  uint32_t in_fault;
53:
54:  /* Set while arch_copy_{from,to}_user is dereferencing user memory.  The
55:   * fault classifier treats a kernel-mode fault on a user VA as a recoverable
56:   * uaccess fault ONLY when this is set (CPU-AARCH64-01: a wild kernel
57:   * pointer that merely lands in user VA range must panic, not silently
58:   * terminate the current process). */
59:  uint32_t uaccess_active;
60:
61:  /* Reap stack head (SCHED-UAF-01): processes terminated by process_terminate()
62:   * awaiting deferred destruction, chained via the legacy process.next field;
63:   * drained at the top of the next schedule() on this CPU, after we have
64:   * switched away from them. */
65:  struct process *deferred_free_proc;
66:  /* SCHED-UAF (#169/#170): a task preempted on this CPU is held here for ONE
67:   * schedule before going back on a runqueue.  If it were re-enqueued
68:   * immediately, another CPU could work-steal and run it while THIS CPU is still
69:   * executing on its kernel stack (the IRQ EOI + dispatch epilogue run on prev's
70:   * stack AFTER schedule() returns, before the iretq switches away; the LAPIC EOI
71:   * MMIO write widens that window on UTM).  Two CPUs on one stack smash the
72:   * in-flight return frame.  Drained at the top of the next schedule() here,
73:   * after this CPU has provably iretq'd off that stack — mirrors deferred_free. */
74:  struct process *pending_reenqueue;
75:};
76:#endif

88: * acquire-wait for the ack.  0 = online, -1 = wake failed, -2 = ack timeout.
89: * smp_ack_boot: release-store ack, called by the secondary once initialized. */
90:int smp_bringup_secondary(uint32_t cpu, void (*entry)(void), void *stack_top) NX_MUST_USE;

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/driver.h @@@
1:#ifndef _KERNEL_DRIVER_H
2:#define _KERNEL_DRIVER_H
3:
4:/*
5: * kernel/include/kernel/driver.h
6: * Driver-binding contract (ASTRA wiring layer).
7: *
8: * A device_driver declares what it can drive — either a specific vendor:device
9: * pair (virtio, Bochs VBE, ...) or a generic PCI class triplet
10: * (xHCI = 0x0C/0x03/0x30, AHCI = 0x01/0x06/0x01, VGA = 0x03/0x00/..., ...).
11: * driver_match_all() walks the hal_device registry and calls probe() on every
12: * still-unbound device a driver matches.  This is the seam that lets a "board"
13: * be just a bag of class-identified providers, with no hardcoded model list.
14: */
15:
16:#include <kernel/types.h>
17:#include <kernel/hal.h>
18:
19:#define DRV_ANY_ID    0xFFFF  /* wildcard for vendor/device */
20:#define DRV_ANY_CLASS 0xFF    /* wildcard for class_code/subclass/prog_if */
21:
22:struct device_driver {
23:    const char *name;
24:
25:    /* ID match (either-or with class match): set to DRV_ANY_ID to ignore. */
26:    uint16_t vendor;
27:    uint16_t device;
28:
29:    /* Class match: set any field to DRV_ANY_CLASS to ignore that field. */
30:    uint8_t class_code;
31:    uint8_t subclass;
32:    uint8_t prog_if;
33:
34:    /* Called once per matching, still-unbound device. Return 0 to claim the
35:     * device (it becomes bound), non-zero to decline (stays available). */
36:    int (*probe)(struct hal_device *dev);
37:
38:    struct device_driver *next; /* internal: linked-list link */
39:};
40:
41:/* Register a driver. Safe to call before or after the bus scan; matching is
42: * performed by driver_match_all(), not at registration time. */
43:void driver_register(struct device_driver *drv);
44:
45:/* Probe every registered driver against every unbound device in the hal
46: * registry. Idempotent: already-bound devices are skipped, so it may be called
47: * again after registering more drivers (e.g. once per subsystem init). */
48:void driver_match_all(void);
49:
50:#endif /* _KERNEL_DRIVER_H */

151:/* Extent tree (lives in i_block[] when EXT4_EXTENTS_FL is set).
152: * A node is: one ext4_extent_header followed by eh_entries records —

179:  uint16_t ee_start_hi; /* physical block, high 16 bits */
180:  uint32_t ee_start_lo; /* physical block, low 32 bits */

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/fault.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/fault.h
3: * Fault-safe reporting primitives (Phase A, steps 5-7).
4: *
5: * Everything declared here must be callable from an exception handler whose
6: * address space, stack, or lock state may be compromised:
7: *   - no spinlocks (a stuck CPU holding uart_lock must not deadlock us),
8: *   - no per-CPU printk buffer,
9: *   - no LAPIC-MMIO reads on amd64 (the mapping may be gone — the cpu id is
10: *     recovered from the IA32_GS_BASE MSR instead),
11: *   - bounded stack usage (callable from a 16KB IST/abort stack).
12: */
13:#ifndef _KERNEL_FAULT_H
14:#define _KERNEL_FAULT_H
15:
16:#include <kernel/nx_contract.h>
17:#include <stdarg.h>
18:#include <kernel/types.h>
19:
20:struct cpu_info;
21:struct pt_regs;
22:
23:/*
24: * fault_printf / fault_vprintf - lock-free emergency console output.
25: *
26: * Formats into a stack buffer via the stateless vsnprintf and emits through
27: * uart_putc_emergency (raw MMIO/port write, no locks).  Output may interleave
28: * with a concurrent printk on another CPU; that is the accepted trade for
29: * never deadlocking inside a fault handler.
30: */
31:void fault_printf(const char *fmt, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 1, 2)));
32:/* DIR-05 / #139 — on-screen panic.  fault_text() returns the captured fault
33: * transcript (register dump + class + backtrace); panic_screen() paints it on a
34: * red framebuffer, fault-safe (no compositor, no locks), for when no UART is
35: * attached.  Defined in kernel/graphics/graphics.c. */
36:const char *fault_text(void);
37:void panic_screen(const char *text);
38:void fault_vprintf(const char *fmt, va_list args);
39:
40:/*
41: * Per-CPU fault recursion guard.
42: *
43: * fault_enter() increments the calling CPU's in_fault depth and returns the
44: * new depth (1 = outermost fault).  A dispatcher seeing depth > 1 must emit
45: * one raw fault_printf line and halt — converting any handler-in-handler
46: * recursion into a clean stop instead of a triple fault / silent hang.
47: * fault_exit() decrements on every path that resumes normal execution.
48: *
49: * If the per-CPU structure cannot be located safely (see below) a global
50: * fallback counter is used so the guard still functions during early boot.
51: */
52:unsigned fault_enter(void);
53:void fault_exit(void);
54:unsigned fault_depth(void);
55:
56:/*
57: * arch_cpu_info_fault_safe - per-HAL: locate this CPU's cpu_info via a path
58: * with no faultable dependencies.
59: *
60: *   amd64:   reads the IA32_GS_BASE MSR (rdmsr — no memory access) and
61: *            validates the value against the cpu_data[] bounds BEFORE any
62: *            dereference, so a user GS base (syscall entry window) or an
63: *            uninitialised MSR yields NULL instead of a nested fault.
64: *   aarch64: derives the index from MPIDR_EL1 (register read, always safe).
65: *
66: * Returns NULL when the structure cannot be determined safely.
67: */
68:struct cpu_info *arch_cpu_info_fault_safe(void);
69:
70:/*
71: * arch_frame_on_fault_stack - aarch64 HAL: whether an exception frame lives
72: * on one of the per-CPU EL1 fault stacks (i.e. the vector switched stacks and
73: * parked the original SP at frame+816).  amd64 does not define it — the IST
74: * mechanism is transparent there.
75: */
76:int arch_frame_on_fault_stack(const void *frame) NX_MUST_USE;
77:
78:/*
79: * fault_handle_user_or_panic - generic user-vs-kernel fault decision
80: * (kernel/core/fault.c, Phase A step 8).
81: *
82: * Returns the next frame to restore (the fault was user-attributable: the
83: * process was terminated and schedule() picked a successor), or NULL (kernel
84: * bug: the caller must dump its arch state and panic).  user_mode is the
85: * arch's privilege test at fault time (CS RPL / SPSR.M); fault_addr is
86: * CR2/FAR (0 when the vector has no fault address); syndrome is the arch fault
87: * cause register (aarch64 ESR / amd64 error code, 0 when none) — logged
88: * uniformly so the user-fault debug is identical across arches (DIR-06 HAL
89: * conformance: the reporting lives HERE, not duplicated per arch).
90: */
91:struct pt_regs *fault_handle_user_or_panic(struct pt_regs *regs, int user_mode,
92:                                           uint64_t fault_addr, uint64_t fault_pc,
93:                                           const char *desc, uint64_t syndrome);
94:
95:/*
96: * arch_uaccess_fault_fixup - per-HAL: release the arch_copy_{from,to}_user
97: * critical section after a fault inside the copy window (clear the per-CPU
98: * uaccess_active flag, drop mm_lock / restore IRQ state where the arch holds
99: * them).  Called only by fault_handle_user_or_panic on the uaccess path.
100: */
101:void arch_uaccess_fault_fixup(void);
102:
103:/*
104: * Symbolized frame-pointer backtrace (kernel/lib/backtrace.c, steps 11-12).
105: * backtrace_regs seeds from an exception frame (pc = RIP/ELR, fp = RBP/X29);
106: * backtrace_here walks from the current call site (used by panic()).
107: * ksym_lookup resolves a text address against the .ksyms blob; returns NULL
108: * (and prints raw) when no table is linked.  All output via fault_printf.
109: */
110:void backtrace_regs(uint64_t pc, uint64_t fp);
111:/* backtrace_scan - corruption-robust fallback: walk the raw stack from sp and
112: * symbolize every kernel .text word (used by the fault dumps when the fp chain
113: * is smashed — the stack-corruption crash class #169/#170). */
114:void backtrace_scan(uint64_t sp);
115:void backtrace_here(void);
116:const char *ksym_lookup(uint64_t addr, uint64_t *off);
117:
118:#endif /* _KERNEL_FAULT_H */

1:/*

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/gpt.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/gpt.h
3: * GUID Partition Table (GPT) Definitions
4: */
5:#ifndef _KERNEL_GPT_H
6:#define _KERNEL_GPT_H
7:
8:#include <kernel/types.h>
9:
10:#define GPT_SIGNATURE 0x5452415020494645ULL /* "EFI PART" */
11:#define SECTOR_SIZE 512
12:
13:/* GPT Header (LBA 1) */
14:struct gpt_header {
15:  uint64_t signature;
16:  uint32_t revision;
17:  uint32_t header_size;
18:  uint32_t header_crc32;
19:  uint32_t reserved1;
20:  uint64_t my_lba;
21:  uint64_t alternate_lba;
22:  uint64_t first_usable_lba;
23:  uint64_t last_usable_lba;
24:  uint8_t disk_guid[16];
25:  uint64_t partition_entry_lba;
26:  uint32_t num_partition_entries;
27:  uint32_t partition_entry_size;
28:  uint32_t partition_entry_crc32;
29:} __attribute__((packed));
30:
31:struct gpt_partition_entry {
32:  uint8_t type_guid[16];
33:  uint8_t unique_guid[16];
34:  uint64_t start_lba;
35:  uint64_t end_lba;
36:  uint64_t attributes;
37:  uint16_t partition_name[36]; /* UTF-16LE */
38:} __attribute__((packed));
39:
40:/* Legacy MBR Definitions */
41:struct mbr_entry {
42:  uint8_t status;
43:  uint8_t chs_start[3];
44:  uint8_t type;
45:  uint8_t chs_end[3];
46:  uint32_t lba_start;
47:  uint32_t sectors;
48:} __attribute__((packed));
49:
50:struct mbr {
51:  uint8_t boot_code[446];
52:  struct mbr_entry partitions[4];
53:  uint16_t signature;
54:} __attribute__((packed));
55:
56:#define MBR_SIGNATURE 0xAA55
57:
58:/* In-memory partition info */
59:struct partition {
60:  uint64_t start_lba;
61:  uint64_t end_lba;
62:  uint64_t size_sectors;
63:  uint32_t index;
64:  uint8_t type_guid[16];
65:};
66:
67:/*
68: * NEXS partition ROLES (F1 design doc D1/D10, F3).
69: *
70: * A partition declares what it IS in its type GUID, so the kernel selects
71: * partitions by role and never by table index.  That is what retires GPT-02
72: * ("changing the disk image layout will silently mount the wrong partition")
73: * and what lets an installer re-partition without the kernel guessing.
74: *
75: * The GUID is 4E455853-RRRR-4E58-9C00-4E4558534F53, where data1 is "NEXS" in
76: * ASCII and RRRR is the role below — legible in a hex dump, and impossible to
77: * confuse with the EFI/Linux well-known types.  (The previous constants were
78: * the *Linux filesystem data* GUID, used for two different roles at once.)
79: *
80: * MUST MATCH tools/mkdisk.c, which writes them.  mkdisk is a host tool and
81: * cannot include kernel headers, so it mirrors these the same way it already
82: * mirrors the ext4 on-disk structs; a mismatch means the wrong partition is
83: * mounted, so the two lists are kept adjacent in review.
84: */
85:#define NEXS_ROLE_META 0x0001     /* P0  Merkle roots, install marker, version */
86:#define NEXS_ROLE_KEYSTORE 0x0002 /* PK  secrets; kernel-only, never mounted   */
87:#define NEXS_ROLE_KERNEL_A 0x0003 /* P1a boot chain slot A                     */
88:#define NEXS_ROLE_KERNEL_B 0x0004 /* P1b boot chain slot B                     */
89:#define NEXS_ROLE_ROOT 0x0005     /* P2  "/"                                   */
90:#define NEXS_ROLE_MACHINE 0x0006  /* P3  /system                               */
91:#define NEXS_ROLE_USR 0x0007      /* P4+ per-user                              */
92:
93:/* Global partition table */
94:#define MAX_PARTITIONS 16
95:extern struct partition partitions[MAX_PARTITIONS];
96:extern int num_partitions;
97:
98:/* API */
99:void gpt_init(void);
100:struct partition *gpt_get_partition(int index);
101:/* partition_role - the NEXS role in a partition's type GUID, or 0 if the GUID
102: * is not a NEXS role GUID (a foreign or legacy partition). */
103:uint16_t partition_role(const struct partition *p);
104:/* partition_find_by_role - the first partition carrying `role`, or NULL.
105: * Roles are unique per disk except USR, where the caller iterates by index. */
106:struct partition *partition_find_by_role(uint16_t role);
107:
108:#endif /* _KERNEL_GPT_H */
109:

37:/**
38: * HAL Device Handle
39: */
40:typedef struct {
41:    hal_res_type_t io_type;
42:    hal_bus_type_t bus_type;
43:    uintptr_t base;
44:    uint32_t irq;
45:} hal_device_t;
46:
47:/* --- Register Access Primitives ---
48: *
49: * dev->base carries the device's PHYSICAL MMIO base; the dereference
50: * happens at its direct-map kernel VA (phys_to_virt — identity while
51: * KERNEL_VIRT_BASE == 0).  Port I/O (amd64) is unaffected by paging. */
52:
53:static inline uint8_t hal_dev_read8(hal_device_t *dev, uint32_t reg) {
54:    uintptr_t addr = dev->base + reg;
55:    if (dev->io_type == HAL_RES_MMIO) {
56:        return *(volatile uint8_t *)phys_to_virt(addr);
57:    } else {
58:        return hal_inb((uint16_t)addr);
59:    }
60:}
61:
62:static inline void hal_dev_write8(hal_device_t *dev, uint32_t reg, uint8_t val) {
63:    uintptr_t addr = dev->base + reg;
64:    if (dev->io_type == HAL_RES_MMIO) {
65:        *(volatile uint8_t *)phys_to_virt(addr) = val;
66:    } else {
67:        hal_outb((uint16_t)addr, val);
68:    }
69:}
70:
71:static inline uint16_t hal_dev_read16(hal_device_t *dev, uint32_t reg) {
72:    uintptr_t addr = dev->base + reg;
73:    if (dev->io_type == HAL_RES_MMIO) {
74:        return *(volatile uint16_t *)phys_to_virt(addr);
75:    } else {
76:        return hal_inw((uint16_t)addr);
77:    }
78:}
79:
80:static inline void hal_dev_write16(hal_device_t *dev, uint32_t reg, uint16_t val) {
81:    uintptr_t addr = dev->base + reg;
82:    if (dev->io_type == HAL_RES_MMIO) {
83:        *(volatile uint16_t *)phys_to_virt(addr) = val;
84:    } else {
85:        hal_outw((uint16_t)addr, val);
86:    }
87:}
88:
89:static inline uint32_t hal_dev_read32(hal_device_t *dev, uint32_t reg) {
90:    uintptr_t addr = dev->base + reg;
91:    if (dev->io_type == HAL_RES_MMIO) {
92:        return *(volatile uint32_t *)phys_to_virt(addr);
93:    } else {
94:        return hal_inl((uint16_t)addr);
95:    }
96:}
97:
98:static inline void hal_dev_write32(hal_device_t *dev, uint32_t reg, uint32_t val) {
99:    uintptr_t addr = dev->base + reg;
100:    if (dev->io_type == HAL_RES_MMIO) {
101:        *(volatile uint32_t *)phys_to_virt(addr) = val;
102:    } else {
103:        hal_outl((uint16_t)addr, val);
104:    }
105:}

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/hal_uaccess.h @@@
1:#ifndef _KERNEL_HAL_UACCESS_H
2:#define _KERNEL_HAL_UACCESS_H
3:
4:#include <kernel/nx_contract.h>
5:#include <kernel/types.h>
6:
7:/*
8: * kernel/include/kernel/hal_uaccess.h
9: * HAL contract for USER-MEMORY ACCESS.
10: *
11: * WHY THIS HEADER EXISTS
12: * ----------------------
13: * Copying to and from a user address space is architecture work — it manipulates
14: * the address-space register, the TLB and the fault-fixup window — so under
15: * ASTRA it is a HAL primitive with per-architecture providers, exactly like
16: * `arch_bus_scan` / `arch_irq_init` in <kernel/hal.h>.
17: *
18: * It was not treated as one.  `arch_copy_string_from_user` had no HAL contract
19: * at all: <kernel/vmm.h> macro-aliased it, and kernel/core/syscall_dispatch.c
20: * re-declared it by hand as a local `extern`.  So the two implementations
21: * (kernel/arch/aarch64/cpu/syscall.c, kernel/arch/amd64/mm/uaccess.c) had
22: * nothing binding them to the same semantics, and they drifted apart in
23: * precisely the way an unwritten contract always does.  Naming the contract is
24: * the fix; the truncation problem below is what made the absence visible.
25: *
26: * THE TRUNCATION PROBLEM
27: * ----------------------
28: * Both providers SILENTLY TRUNCATE at max_len and return 0 — success.  Every
29: * caller therefore proceeds with a string that is not the one the process
30: * passed.  For a window title that is harmless.  For a path, a registry key or
31: * an environment value it is a correctness bug that cannot be diagnosed from
32: * the outside: the write "succeeds" and the matching read misses, because the
33: * stored name is not the name that was asked for.
34: *
35: * The fix is NOT a bigger buffer.  Truncation-versus-fit is information the
36: * copy loop already has and throws away; the contract just has to carry it.
37: * So there are two wrappers over ONE provider:
38: *
39: *   hal_copy_string_from_user()         TOLERANT — truncation is success.
40: *                                       For data where a shortened value is
41: *                                       still usable (titles, diagnostics).
42: *
43: *   hal_copy_string_from_user_strict()  STRICT — truncation returns -E2BIG and
44: *                                       the caller refuses the operation.  For
45: *                                       data where a shortened value is a
46: *                                       DIFFERENT value (paths, registry keys
47: *                                       and values, environment variables).
48: *
49: * Which one applies is a property of the DATA, not of the architecture, so the
50: * choice belongs at the call site and the mechanism belongs here.  Raising the
51: * constants instead would be the same defect with a later failure date — see
52: * Phase 18 (unbind the ceilings) in docs/PLAN-2026-07-17-STRATIFICATION.md,
53: * which removes the fixed buffers entirely by moving these transfers
54: * out-of-line, the way the execsvc request body already works.
55: */
56:
57:/* Provider contract — implemented once per architecture.
58: *
59: * arch_copy_string_from_user_n: copy a NUL-terminated string from user space.
60: *   Returns 0 on success, -1 on a bad/unmapped source address.  When out_len is
61: *   non-NULL it receives the number of bytes copied EXCLUDING the terminator,
62: *   and *out_truncated is set to 1 if the source was longer than max_len - 1.
63: *   Reporting both is what lets the two wrappers above share one provider. */
64:int arch_copy_string_from_user_n(char *dest, const char *src, size_t max_len,
65:                                 size_t *out_len, int *out_truncated) NX_MUST_USE;
66:int arch_copy_from_user(void *dest, const void *src, size_t n) NX_MUST_USE;
67:int arch_copy_to_user(void *dest, const void *src, size_t n) NX_MUST_USE;
68:
69:/* Legacy spelling, kept because ~10 call sites use it and truncation is
70: * acceptable for all of them; implemented over the provider above. */
71:int arch_copy_string_from_user(char *dest, const char *src, size_t max_len) NX_MUST_USE;
72:
73:/* E2BIG reaches the kernel today from include/abi/posix_types.h, which the
74: * layering gate counts as a violation (scripts/check-layering.sh).  The
75: * fallback keeps this header self-contained once that include is removed, and
76: * pins the value so the two sides cannot silently disagree in the meantime.
77: * Errno numbering is precisely the "irreducible bootstrap contract" Phase 10a
78: * has to place deliberately rather than inherit by accident. */
79:#ifndef E2BIG
80:#define E2BIG 7
81:#endif
82:
83:/* Tolerant: a truncated result is accepted.  Identical to the historical
84: * behaviour, so existing callers need no change. */
85:static inline int hal_copy_string_from_user(char *dest, const char *src,
86:                                            size_t max_len) {
87:  return arch_copy_string_from_user_n(dest, src, max_len, (size_t *)0,
88:                                      (int *)0);
89:}
90:
91:/* Strict: a source that does not fit is REFUSED with -E2BIG rather than
92: * silently shortened.  Use wherever a shortened string is a different string. */
93:static inline int hal_copy_string_from_user_strict(char *dest, const char *src,
94:                                                   size_t max_len) {
95:  int truncated = 0;
96:  int r = arch_copy_string_from_user_n(dest, src, max_len, (size_t *)0,
97:                                       &truncated);
98:  if (r != 0)
99:    return r;
100:  return truncated ? -E2BIG : 0;
101:}
102:
103:#endif /* _KERNEL_HAL_UACCESS_H */
104:

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/io_poll.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/io_poll.h
3: * Bounded busy-wait contract for driver bring-up and register polling.
4: *
5: * Hardware bring-up must NEVER spin forever. An absent or wedged device leaves a
6: * status bit stuck — a missing 8042 floats its status port to 0xFF, a dead UART
7: * never drains its TX FIFO — so an unbounded `while (!ready) ;` hangs the whole
8: * boot (this is exactly what wedged the PS/2 path on BIOS-less amd64, #124).
9: *
10: * These macros cap the spin so the caller can degrade gracefully (skip the
11: * device, drop the byte) instead of blocking. They are plain do/while macros
12: * (no GNU statement-expression) so they build under -Wpedantic. `cond` is
13: * re-evaluated every iteration — pass a live register read.
14: */
15:#ifndef _KERNEL_IO_POLL_H
16:#define _KERNEL_IO_POLL_H
17:
18:/* Default spin budget: large enough for any real register transition, small
19: * enough to return promptly when the hardware is absent/wedged. */
20:#define POLL_SPINS_DEFAULT 1000000L
21:
22:/*
23: * spin_until(cond, max_spins) - bounded best-effort spin.
24: *
25: * Spins until `cond` becomes true or the budget runs out; the outcome is
26: * discarded. Use where the caller proceeds regardless (e.g. polled console TX:
27: * a wedged UART must not hang printk — drop the byte instead).
28: */
29:#define spin_until(cond, max_spins)                                            \
30:  do {                                                                         \
31:    long _su_n = (max_spins);                                                  \
32:    while (!(cond) && _su_n > 0)                                               \
33:      _su_n--;                                                                 \
34:  } while (0)
35:
36:/*
37: * poll_until(ok, cond, max_spins) - bounded spin with outcome.
38: *
39: * Sets `ok` (int) to 1 if `cond` became true within the budget, 0 on timeout,
40: * so the caller can skip a missing/wedged device.
41: */
42:#define poll_until(ok, cond, max_spins)                                        \
43:  do {                                                                         \
44:    long _pu_n = (max_spins);                                                  \
45:    while (!(cond) && _pu_n > 0)                                               \
46:      _pu_n--;                                                                 \
47:    (ok) = (_pu_n > 0);                                                        \
48:  } while (0)
49:
50:#endif /* _KERNEL_IO_POLL_H */
51:

15: */
16:struct irq_chip {

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/kmalloc.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/kmalloc.h
3: * Kernel Heap Allocator
4: *
5: * Declares the public API of the kernel heap allocator (kernel/lib/kmalloc.c).
6: *
7: * The allocator uses nine power-of-two buckets (16 B - 4 KB) over a fixed
8: * 32 MB bump-pointer pool for small allocations, and passes large requests
9: * (total > 4 KB) directly to pmm_alloc_pages().
10: *
11: * Important constraints:
12: *   - The heap does NOT grow; once exhausted, small allocations fail.
13: *   - Freed small blocks are NOT returned to the PMM (see MM-KM-01).
14: *   - All operations are serialised through a single global spinlock (MM-KM-06).
15: *   - Large allocations return a pointer that is NOT page-aligned (MM-KM-03).
16: *
17: * Known issues (see docs/review/analysis/01-mm-memory-management.md):
18: *   MM-KM-01 through MM-KM-06.
19: */
20:#ifndef _KERNEL_KMALLOC_H
21:#define _KERNEL_KMALLOC_H
22:
23:#include <kernel/types.h>
24:
25:/* kmalloc_init: allocate the 32 MB heap pool from PMM; safe to call multiple
26: * times (idempotent via heap_initialized flag). */
27:void kmalloc_init(void);
28:
29:/* kmalloc: allocate 'size' bytes; returns NULL on size==0 or exhaustion.
30: * NOTE(MM-KM-03): large allocs (size+header > 4096) return a non-page-aligned
31: * pointer even though the underlying PMM page IS page-aligned. */
32:void *kmalloc(size_t size);
33:
34:/* kcalloc: allocate nmemb*size bytes zeroed; overflow-safe. */
35:void *kcalloc(size_t nmemb, size_t size);
36:
37:/* krealloc: resize allocation; always alloc+copy+free (no in-place shrink).
38: * NOTE(MM-KM-04): does not optimise the case where new_size fits the same bucket. */
39:void *krealloc(void *ptr, size_t new_size);
40:
41:/* kfree: return a kmalloc'd pointer.  Small allocations go to the bucket free
42: * list (never returned to PMM).  Large allocations are returned to PMM.
43: * Panics/logs on invalid magic or out-of-range bucket_idx. */
44:void kfree(void *ptr);
45:
46:/* Instrumentation (perf brief §1/§2.2; surfaced via OS1_sys_stats).
47: * Reports cumulative pool size (never shrinks today), current live user bytes,
48: * the high-water mark of live bytes, and the live allocation count.  All
49: * out-params are NULL-skippable. */
50:void kmalloc_get_stats(uint64_t *heap_total_bytes, uint64_t *bytes_in_use,
51:                       uint64_t *high_water_bytes, uint64_t *live_allocs);
52:
53:/* Macros for stb_truetype compatibility */
54:/* Redirect stb heap calls to kmalloc/kfree. */
55:#define STBTT_malloc(x, u) ((void)(u), kmalloc(x))
56:#define STBTT_free(x, u) ((void)(u), kfree(x))
57:
58:#endif /* _KERNEL_KMALLOC_H */
59:

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/list.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/list.h
3: * Doubly-linked list (Linux-style)
4: */
5:#ifndef _KERNEL_LIST_H
6:#define _KERNEL_LIST_H
7:
8:#include <kernel/types.h>
9:
10:struct list_head {
11:  struct list_head *next, *prev;
12:};
13:
14:#define LIST_HEAD_INIT(name) {&(name), &(name)}
15:#define LIST_HEAD(name) struct list_head name = LIST_HEAD_INIT(name)
16:
17:static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) void
18:INIT_LIST_HEAD(struct list_head *list) {
19:  list->next = list;
20:  list->prev = list;
21:}
22:
23:static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) void
24:__list_add(struct list_head *new, struct list_head *prev,
25:           struct list_head *next) {
26:  next->prev = new;
27:  new->next = next;
28:  new->prev = prev;
29:  prev->next = new;
30:}
31:
32:static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) void
33:list_add(struct list_head *new, struct list_head *head) {
34:  __list_add(new, head, head->next);
35:}
36:
37:static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) void
38:list_add_tail(struct list_head *new, struct list_head *head) {
39:  __list_add(new, head->prev, head);
40:}
41:
42:static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) void
43:__list_del(struct list_head *prev, struct list_head *next) {
44:  next->prev = prev;
45:  prev->next = next;
46:}
47:
48:static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) void
49:list_del(struct list_head *entry) {
50:  __list_del(entry->prev, entry->next);
51:  entry->next = NULL;
52:  entry->prev = NULL;
53:}
54:
55:static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) void
56:list_del_init(struct list_head *entry) {
57:  __list_del(entry->prev, entry->next);
58:  INIT_LIST_HEAD(entry);
59:}
60:
61:static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) int
62:list_empty(const struct list_head *head) {
63:  return head->next == head;
64:}
65:
66:static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) void
67:list_move(struct list_head *list, struct list_head *head) {
68:  __list_del(list->prev, list->next);
69:  list_add(list, head);
70:}
71:
72:static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) void
73:list_move_tail(struct list_head *list, struct list_head *head) {
74:  __list_del(list->prev, list->next);
75:  list_add_tail(list, head);
76:}
77:
78:#define list_entry(ptr, type, member) container_of(ptr, type, member)
79:
80:#define list_first_entry(ptr, type, member)                                    \
81:  list_entry((ptr)->next, type, member)
82:
83:#define list_last_entry(ptr, type, member) list_entry((ptr)->prev, type, member)
84:
85:#define list_for_each(pos, head)                                               \
86:  for (pos = (head)->next; pos != (head); pos = pos->next)
87:
88:#define list_for_each_safe(pos, n, head)                                       \
89:  for (pos = (head)->next, n = pos->next; pos != (head); pos = n, n = pos->next)
90:
91:#define list_for_each_entry(pos, head, member)                                 \
92:  for (pos = list_first_entry(head, typeof(*pos), member);                     \
93:       &pos->member != (head);                                                 \
94:       pos = list_entry(pos->member.next, typeof(*pos), member))
95:
96:#define list_for_each_entry_safe(pos, n, head, member)                         \
97:  for (pos = list_first_entry(head, typeof(*pos), member),                     \
98:      n = list_entry(pos->member.next, typeof(*pos), member);                  \
99:       &pos->member != (head);                                                 \
100:       pos = n, n = list_entry(n->member.next, typeof(*pos), member))
101:
102:#define list_for_each_entry_reverse(pos, head, member)                         \
103:  for (pos = list_last_entry(head, typeof(*pos), member);                      \
104:       &pos->member != (head);                                                 \
105:       pos = list_entry(pos->member.prev, typeof(*pos), member))
106:
107:#define list_for_each_entry_safe_reverse(pos, n, head, member) \
108:	for (pos = list_last_entry(head, typeof(*pos), member), \
109:		n = list_entry(pos->member.prev, typeof(*pos), member); \
110:		&pos->member != (head); \
111:		pos = n, n = list_entry(n->member.prev, typeof(*pos), member))
112:
113:#endif /* _KERNEL_LIST_H */

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/memlayout.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/memlayout.h
3: * Kernel physical/virtual address translation (MM-VMM-02 / MM-PMM-07).
4: *
5: * KERNEL_VIRT_BASE is the offset of the kernel's linear ("direct") map:
6: * every byte of physical address space the kernel touches (RAM, MMIO,
7: * page-table pages, DMA buffers) is reachable at
8: *
9: *     VA = PA + KERNEL_VIRT_BASE
10: *
11: * and the kernel image itself is linked inside that window, so the same
12: * single offset converts in both directions for ANY kernel virtual
13: * address (image symbols, PMM allocations, MMIO pointers alike).
14: *
15: * The higher half is LIVE on both arches (aarch64: 0xFFFF000000000000 via
16: * TTBR1; amd64: 0xFFFF800000000000, PML4 slot 256+).  The boot assembly
17: * enables the MMU with boot tables before any C runs, so kernel code only
18: * ever executes at its link address; user space owns the low half
19: * exclusively.
20: *
21: * Contract for the rest of the tree (enforced by the Phase-B2 sweep):
22: *   - uint64_t values named pa/phys/pgd_addr are PHYSICAL addresses;
23: *     pointers are kernel VIRTUAL addresses.
24: *   - pmm_alloc_*() return kernel virtual pointers; what hardware needs
25: *     (PTE output addresses, virtqueue descriptors, DMA registers, CR3/
26: *     TTBR values) must go through virt_to_phys().
27: *   - MMIO register accesses translate their physical base through
28: *     phys_to_virt() (see hal_device.h and the uart/gic/apic accessors).
29: */
30:#ifndef _KERNEL_MEMLAYOUT_H
31:#define _KERNEL_MEMLAYOUT_H
32:
33:#include <kernel/types.h>
34:
35:#ifdef ARCH_AARCH64
36:/* Higher half: TTBR1_EL1 range, T0SZ=T1SZ=16 (48-bit split).  The kernel
37: * image is linked at KERNEL_VIRT_BASE + 0x40080000 (its load PA) and all
38: * RAM/MMIO is direct-mapped at PA + KERNEL_VIRT_BASE via TTBR1; TTBR0 is
39: * user-only (per-process tables). */
40:#define KERNEL_VIRT_BASE 0xFFFF000000000000UL
41:#elif defined(ARCH_AMD64)
42:/* Higher half: PML4 index 256 onward.  The kernel image is linked at
43: * KERNEL_VIRT_BASE + 2MB (loaded at PA 2MB; the low boot sections stay
44: * at PA 1MB) and all RAM/MMIO is direct-mapped at PA + KERNEL_VIRT_BASE.
45: * Process PML4s share the kernel half by copying entries 256..511. */
46:#define KERNEL_VIRT_BASE 0xFFFF800000000000UL
47:#else
48:#error "memlayout.h: unknown architecture"
49:#endif
50:
51:/* phys_to_virt - kernel virtual pointer for a physical address. */
52:static inline void *phys_to_virt(uint64_t phys) {
53:  return (void *)(uintptr_t)(phys + KERNEL_VIRT_BASE);
54:}
55:
56:/* virt_to_phys - physical address behind a kernel virtual pointer.
57: * Valid for every kernel VA (image, PMM pages, MMIO) because the image
58: * is linked inside the direct-map window. */
59:static inline uint64_t virt_to_phys(void *virt) {
60:  return (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)virt - KERNEL_VIRT_BASE;
61:}
62:
63:#endif /* _KERNEL_MEMLAYOUT_H */
64:

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/nx_contract.h @@@
1:#ifndef _KERNEL_NX_CONTRACT_H
2:#define _KERNEL_NX_CONTRACT_H
3:/*
4: * nx_contract.h — the vocabulary for stating, IN THE CODE, the invariants that
5: * C cannot check by itself.
6: *
7: * WHY.  Every defect this kernel has lost days to belonged to a class the
8: * language is blind to: a return value nobody looked at, a struct whose layout
9: * assembly depends on, a lock held across an allocation, a page freed while a
10: * register spilled onto it was still live.  Each was written into a comment
11: * after it was found — and each was then violated again, because a comment
12: * cannot fail a build.
13: *
14: * These macros exist to move an invariant from a comment into something that
15: * DOES fail a build.  Two mechanisms, used for different things:
16: *
17: *   - COMPILER-ENFORCED (this file): warn_unused_result, nonnull, and
18: *     _Static_assert.  Zero cost, no tooling, catches the error at the exact
19: *     line.  Prefer these whenever the invariant is expressible.
20: *   - CHECKER-ENFORCED (scripts/check-contracts.py, `make lockcheck`): the
21: *     interprocedural rules — allocation under a lock, a free of memory the
22: *     running context still needs, a timer outliving its object.  These need a
23: *     call graph, which the C compiler will not give us.
24: *
25: * The annotations below are read by BOTH: the compiler acts on the attribute,
26: * the checker reads the same marker to seed its analysis.  One statement, two
27: * enforcers — the alternative is a second list that drifts from the first,
28: * which is the duplication failure this project already paid for twice.
29: */
30:
31:/*
32: * NX_MUST_USE — the result is not advisory.
33: *
34: * This is `#[must_use]`.  It exists because of EXT4-ERRNO-01: a function
35: * returning -errno whose caller ignores it turns a real failure into silent
36: * success, and the caller that ignores it is invisible in review.  Put it on
37: * EVERY function whose return value carries a failure the caller must act on —
38: * which in this tree is essentially everything returning `int` as -errno.
39: */
40:/* Always on.  It was briefly gated behind NX_STRICT so the backlog could be
41: * measured without breaking the tree, and the predictable result was that
42: * nobody saw a single error: a gate you have to remember to switch on is a gate
43: * that is off.  The diagnosis has to happen during an ordinary build, which is
44: * the only build anyone runs. */
45:#define NX_MUST_USE __attribute__((warn_unused_result))
46:
47:/*
48: * NX_NONNULL(...) — these argument positions may never be NULL.
49: *
50: * 1-based indices, e.g. NX_NONNULL(1, 3).  The compiler both diagnoses a
51: * literal NULL at the call site AND is allowed to assume non-NULL inside, so
52: * do NOT use it on a function that deliberately tolerates NULL — pop_message()
53: * is the counter-example: NULL is a reachable argument there and the guard is
54: * load-bearing, not defensive.
55: */
56:#define NX_NONNULL(...) __attribute__((nonnull(__VA_ARGS__)))
57:
58:/*
59: * NX_DISCARD(expr, why) — deliberately drop a must-use result, with a reason.
60: *
61: * Without an escape hatch a must-use gate does not get satisfied, it gets
62: * DELETED: the first person who meets a legitimately ignorable result and has
63: * no way to say so removes the attribute, and the annotation is gone for every
64: * caller.  So the hatch exists — and it is deliberately more typing than
65: * handling the error, because the common case should be the easy one.
66: *
67: * `why` is a string literal that generates nothing.  Its only job is to make
68: * the author state the justification where the next reader will look, so a
69: * discard can be reviewed instead of merely noticed.  Note that a plain (void)
70: * cast does NOT suppress warn_unused_result under GCC — the tree already had
71: * `(void)arch_copy_to_user(...)` sitting in SYS_WAIT, which looked deliberate
72: * and silenced nothing.
73: *
74: * Legitimate uses are narrow: an error-unwind path where the failure of the
75: * cleanup changes nothing, and a genuinely best-effort refresh whose fallback
76: * is documented.  "I do not know what to do with this" is not one of them.
77: */
78:#define NX_DISCARD(expr, why)                                                  \
79:  do {                                                                         \
80:    __typeof__(expr) _nx_discarded __attribute__((unused)) = (expr);           \
81:    (void)sizeof(why);                                                         \
82:  } while (0)
83:
84:/*
85: * NX_NO_ALLOC / NX_ALLOCATES — the memory contract, for the checker.
86: *
87: * NX_NO_ALLOC declares "nothing on any path from here reaches the allocator",
88: * which is what makes a function safe to call while a sched_lock is held.
89: * NX_ALLOCATES is the opposite claim, stated so a caller cannot be surprised.
90: *
91: * They carry no code generation on purpose: their whole job is to be a claim
92: * the checker can VERIFY against the real call graph, so a wrong annotation is
93: * itself a build failure rather than a comforting lie.
94: */
95:#define NX_NO_ALLOC
96:#define NX_ALLOCATES
97:
98:/*
99: * NX_HOLDS(lock) / NX_ACQUIRES(lock) — the lock a function expects or takes.
100: * Documentation the checker can read, and the seed for the lock-order rules.
101: */
102:#define NX_HOLDS(lock)
103:#define NX_ACQUIRES(lock)
104:
105:/*
106: * The layout-assert macros live in <abi/nx_abi.h>, NOT here.
107: *
108: * They are needed by userland and by the shared ABI headers too, and a second
109: * definition in the kernel tree would be exactly the duplication these asserts
110: * exist to catch: two statements of one contract, drifting.  See that header
111: * for why the boundary is where it is.
112: */
113:#include <nx_abi.h>
114:
115:#endif /* _KERNEL_NX_CONTRACT_H */
116:

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/object.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/object.h
3: * Kernel object manager + per-process capability handle table.
4: *
5: * This is the REAL capability layer (ASTRA §6.1/6.2/6.5): the kernel-side
6: * implementation of the unforgeable-handle model whose ABI lives in
7: * include/api/object.h.  A kernel resource is a refcounted `struct kobject`;
8: * a process names it only through a HANDLE — a small integer index into its
9: * private handle table.  Each handle carries a RIGHTS subset (separable,
10: * attenuable).  There is no way to name a kobject without holding a handle to
11: * it: a handle integer with no installed slot is -EBADF, and a handle's rights
12: * can only shrink across duplicate/grant, so privilege escalation is
13: * impossible by construction (the same invariant as the caps.h spawn cut).
14: *
15: * This ABSORBED the B3 per-process fd table (ASTRA's "seed", §6.2): there is no
16: * separate fd array any more — a POSIX descriptor IS a handle (fd N == handle
17: * N). open() = handle_create(FILE); read/write/lseek/close operate on the
18: * handle table; stdin/stdout/stderr are pre-installed CONSOLE handles 0/1/2.
19: * The object syscalls (235..242) and the POSIX file syscalls are the same
20: * mechanism.
21: *
22: * Concurrency: a single global `object_lock` serialises refcount changes and
23: * handle-table slot install/close/grant (short, no-I/O critical sections).
24: * Object I/O (read/write/wait) uses a pin/use/unpin pattern so blocking VFS
25: * I/O never runs under the lock.
26: */
27:#ifndef _KERNEL_OBJECT_H
28:#define _KERNEL_OBJECT_H
29:
30:#include <kernel/nx_contract.h>
31:#include <kernel/types.h>
32:#include <kernel/vfs.h>
33:#include <object.h> /* shared ABI: OBJ_TYPE_*, OS1_RIGHT_*, OS1_NS_* */
34:
35:#define NPROC_HANDLES 32
36:#define OBJ_FILE_PATH_MAX 128
37:
38:/* A kernel object: a refcounted, typed resource named only through handles.
39: * Payloads for every type are kept inline (a kobject is small and kmalloc'd);
40: * `type` selects which fields are live. */
41:struct kobject {
42:  uint8_t type; /* OBJ_TYPE_* */
43:  int refcount; /* live handles referencing it across ALL processes */
44:
45:  /* OBJ_TYPE_FILE */
46:  struct vfs_node node;
47:  uint64_t offset;              /* shared file position */
48:  char path[OBJ_FILE_PATH_MAX]; /* resolved path (VFS write contract is
49:                                   path-based) */
50:
51:  /* OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS (also the owning pid for OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW) */
52:  int pid;
53:
54:  /* OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW */
55:  int window_id;
56:
57:  /* OBJ_TYPE_PIPE — anonymous kernel byte pipe (ASTRA §6.2).  Heap-allocated
58:   * (struct kpipe, kernel/core/object.c) so the ring buffer + reader wait queue
59:   * don't bloat every kobject; NULL for non-pipe objects. */
60:  struct kpipe *pipe;
61:
62:  /* OBJ_TYPE_PORT — Mach-style message port (ASTRA §6.5): a named mailbox that
63:   * IS a capability.  Heap-allocated (struct kport, kernel/core/object.c) for
64:   * the same reason as the pipe; NULL for non-port objects. */
65:  struct kport *port;
66:};
67:
68:/* A handle-table slot: a capability = (object, held rights). */
69:struct handle_entry {
70:  struct kobject *obj; /* NULL = free slot */
71:  uint32_t rights;     /* OS1_RIGHT_* held via THIS handle */
72:};
73:
74:struct process;
75:
76:/* Close every handle a dying process holds and free its handle table.
77: * NULL-safe (a process that never used a handle has p->handles == NULL).
78: * Called from BOTH process free sites (immediate teardown + deferred reap). */
79:void process_handles_destroy(struct process *p);
80:
81:/* Instrumentation (perf brief §1/§2.6; surfaced via OS1_sys_stats): copy the
82: * per-type live-kobject counts into out[0..min(max,OBJ_TYPE_COUNT)). */
83:void object_get_live_counts(uint64_t *out, int max);
84:
85:/* Syscall backends (dispatched from kernel/core/syscall_dispatch.c).  The
86: * caller is current_process; user pointers are copied with arch_copy_*_user
87: * inside.  Return >= 0 on success, negative errno on failure. */
88:long sys_handle_create(int ns, const char *upath, uint32_t rights,
89:                       int type) NX_MUST_USE;
90:long sys_handle_dup(int handle, uint32_t new_rights) NX_MUST_USE;
91:long sys_handle_close(int handle) NX_MUST_USE;
92:long sys_cap_query(int handle) NX_MUST_USE;
93:long sys_cap_grant(int target_pid, int handle, uint32_t rights) NX_MUST_USE;
94:long sys_object_read(int handle, void *ubuf, size_t n) NX_MUST_USE;
95:long sys_object_write(int handle, const void *ubuf, size_t n) NX_MUST_USE;
96:long sys_object_wait(int handle, long arg) NX_MUST_USE;
97:long sys_object_ctl(int handle, int cmd, long arg) NX_MUST_USE;
98:/* POSIX lseek(2) on a handle: FILE repositions its byte offset per 'whence'
99: * (SEEK_SET/_CUR/_END); a non-seekable object (CONSOLE, …) returns -ESPIPE. */
100:long sys_object_lseek(int handle, long off, int whence) NX_MUST_USE;
101:
102:/* window_text_write - copy a user buffer to window win_id (UART mirror +
103: * compositor append); defined in kernel/core/syscall_dispatch.c.  The shared
104: * backend of SYS_WINDOW_WRITE and the OBJ_TYPE_CONSOLE stdout/stderr handle
105: * (declared here so kernel/core/object.c's console write can reach it). */
106:long window_text_write(int win_id, const char *ubuf, size_t count) NX_MUST_USE;
107:
108:/* process_install_stdio - eagerly allocate p's handle table and pre-install the
109: * standard trio: handles 0/1/2 share one CONSOLE object (0 = read/stdin, 1/2 =
110: * write/stdout+stderr).  Called by process_create() so every process is born
111: * with stdin/stdout/stderr as capability handles.  Returns 0, or -ENOMEM. */
112:int process_install_stdio(struct process *p,
113:                          struct process *parent) NX_MUST_USE;
114:
115:/* process_redirect_child_fd - dup the spawner's open handle 'parent_fd' into a
116: * freshly-created child's 'child_slot', overwriting the console there (Phase 4
117: * shell `<`/`>`/`>>`/`2>`).  Called from dispatch_spawn with the spawner as
118: * current_process, before the child runs.  Returns 0 or -EINVAL/-EBADF/-ENOMEM.
119: */
120:int process_redirect_child_fd(struct process *child, int child_slot,
121:                              int parent_fd) NX_MUST_USE;
122:/* process_redirect_child_fd_from - same, with the SOURCE process explicit.  The
123: * spawner and the fd owner are the same process today, but diverge once an
124: * execution service spawns on a client's behalf (Q2): the fds are the CLIENT's.
125: * Parameterising the source keeps that a caller change, not a rewrite. */
126:int process_redirect_child_fd_from(struct process *owner, struct process *child,
127:                                   int child_slot, int parent_fd) NX_MUST_USE;
128:
129:/* sys_pipe - SYS_PIPE: create an anonymous OBJ_TYPE_PIPE and install its read +
130: * write ends in the caller's table; writes both fds to the user int[2].  0 or
131: * -ENOMEM/-EMFILE/-EFAULT. */
132:long sys_pipe(int *ufds) NX_MUST_USE;
133:/* sys_port_send_caps - SYS_PORT_SEND_CAPS: send through a PORT while
134: * TRANSFERRING handles to the receiver, rewriting the payload with the indices
135: * as the RECEIVER sees them (ASTRA 6.5 Mach rights-in-a-message).  Removes the
136: * need to cap_grant by pid to a service discovered by NAME. */
137:long sys_port_send_caps(int handle, const void *umsg, const int *ufds,
138:                        int nfds) NX_MUST_USE;
139:
140:#endif /* _KERNEL_OBJECT_H */

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/pmm.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/pmm.h
3: * Physical Memory Manager
4: *
5: * Page frame allocator with block-aligned allocation support
6: * for zero-copy I/O and partition management.
7: *
8: * This header defines the public API and key data structures of the PMM.
9: * The PMM is split into two zones:
10: *   ZONE_DMA    (PFN 0 .. dma_end_pfn-1): physical memory below 16 MB,
11: *               reserved for devices requiring sub-16MB DMA addresses.
12: *   ZONE_NORMAL (dma_end_pfn .. total_pages-1): general-purpose allocation.
13: *
14: * PA/VA contract (MM-PMM-07 resolved, see kernel/memlayout.h):
15: *   pmm_alloc_*() return kernel VIRTUAL pointers (direct map,
16: *   phys_to_virt of the frame address); pmm_free_*() take the same
17: *   pointers back.  Callers needing the frame's PHYSICAL address (page
18: *   table entries, DMA descriptors, TTBR/CR3) must use virt_to_phys().
19: *   pmm_phys_to_page()/pmm_page_to_phys() speak physical addresses only.
20: *
21: * Known issues (see docs/review/analysis/01-mm-memory-management.md):
22: *   MM-PMM-01 through MM-PMM-06 (07 resolved).
23: */
24:#ifndef _KERNEL_PMM_H
25:#define _KERNEL_PMM_H
26:
27:#include <kernel/list.h>
28:#include <kernel/spinlock.h>
29:#include <kernel/types.h>
30:
31:/* Page size definitions */
32:/* 4KB granule, matching hardware page tables on both arches. */
33:#define PAGE_SHIFT 12
34:#define PAGE_SIZE (1UL << PAGE_SHIFT) /* 4KB */
35:#define PAGE_MASK (~(PAGE_SIZE - 1))
36:
37:/* Block alignment for I/O */
38:#define BLOCK_SIZE_512 512
39:#define BLOCK_SIZE_4K 4096
40:#define BLOCK_SIZE_64K 65536
41:
42:/* Memory zones */
43:/* NOTE(MM-PMM-04): pmm_alloc_pages() and pmm_alloc_aligned() only search
44: * ZONE_NORMAL; contiguous DMA-zone allocations are not supported. */
45:#define ZONE_DMA 0    /* 0-16MB, for legacy DMA */
46:#define ZONE_NORMAL 1 /* 16MB-end, normal allocations */
47:#define ZONE_COUNT 2
48:
49:/* Page flags */
50:/* Stored in struct page.flags. */
51:#define PG_RESERVED (1 << 0) /* Cannot be allocated */
52:#define PG_KERNEL (1 << 1)   /* Kernel memory */
53:#define PG_USER (1 << 2)     /* User memory */
54:#define PG_DIRTY (1 << 3)    /* Page modified */
55:#define PG_LOCKED (1 << 4)   /* Page locked in memory */
56:
57:/* Physical page descriptor */
58:/*
59: * struct page - per-frame metadata stored in the global page_array.
60: *
61: * One entry exists for every physical page frame between MEMORY_BASE and
62: * MEMORY_BASE + total_pages*PAGE_SIZE.
63: *
64: * refcount: set to 1 on allocation, decremented on pmm_free_page().  If it
65: *           reaches 0 the page is returned to its zone bitmap.  In practice
66: *           it is never incremented above 1 because there is no vmm_map path
67: *           that increments it (frame sharing is not implemented).
68: *           NOTE(MM-VMM-04): vmm_destroy_pgd does not decrement refcount for
69: *           user-mapped frames; those pages therefore never reach refcount 0
70: *           and are never freed on process exit.
71: *
72: * lru, priv: currently unused; reserved for a future page-cache integration.
73: */
74:struct page {
75:  uint32_t flags;
76:  uint32_t refcount;
77:  struct list_head lru; /* For page cache LRU */
78:  void *priv;           /* For slab/buffer use */
79:};
80:
81:/* Memory zone descriptor */
82:/*
83: * struct zone - descriptor for a contiguous range of page frames.
84: *
85: * start_pfn / end_pfn: absolute PFN range [start_pfn, end_pfn).
86: * bitmap:       allocation bitmap; bit i (0-based within the zone) is 1 if
87: *               the corresponding frame is allocated or reserved, 0 if free.
88: * next_free_pfn: next-fit hint; zone-relative PFN where the last single-page
89: *               allocation succeeded.  Wraps to 0 at end_pfn.
90: *               NOTE(MM-PMM-06): ignored by the contiguous-allocation path.
91: * free_pages:   count of free frames in this zone.
92: *               NOTE(MM-PMM-05): updated under zone->lock (non-atomically);
93: *               can transiently disagree with the global atomic free_pages.
94: * lock:         spinlock protecting bitmap and free_pages for this zone.
95: */
96:struct zone {
97:  const char *name;
98:  uint64_t start_pfn;     /* First page frame number */
99:  uint64_t end_pfn;       /* Last page frame number */
100:  uint64_t free_pages;    /* Number of free pages */
101:  uint64_t *bitmap;       /* Allocation bitmap */
102:  uint64_t next_free_pfn; /* Next-Fit optimization: last known free PFN */
103:  spinlock_t lock;        /* Zone lock */
104:};
105:
106:/* Memory region from bootloader/DTB */
107:/*
108: * struct mem_region - a single physical memory extent reported by the boot layer.
109: *
110: * Populated by arch_platform_get_mem_regions() from either the DTB (AArch64)
111: * or the multiboot/PVH memory map (AMD64).  Used by pmm_early_init() and
112: * vmm_dynamic_remap() to discover all of physical RAM.
113: */
114:struct mem_region {
115:  uint64_t base;
116:  uint64_t size;
117:  uint32_t type; /* 1=usable, 2=reserved, etc */
118:};
119:
120:#define MEM_REGION_USABLE 1
121:#define MEM_REGION_RESERVED 2
122:#define MEM_REGION_ACPI 3
123:#define MEM_REGION_MMIO 4
124:
125:/* PMM API */
126:
127:/* Initialize PMM with memory regions */
128:void pmm_early_init(struct mem_region *regions, size_t count);
129:void pmm_init(struct mem_region *regions, size_t count);
130:/* Physical end address of the PMM metadata (page_array + bitmaps), valid after
131: * pmm_early_init(); vmm_init() maps the bootstrap window up to here. */
132:uint64_t pmm_metadata_top(void);
133:/* NOTE(MM-PMM-01): pmm_init_region() is a stub; it only prints and returns. */
134:void pmm_init_region(uint64_t base, uint64_t size);
135:
136:/* Allocate a single page */
137:/* Allocate a single zeroed, CPU-only page (NO cache-clean/fence — perf §3.1).
138: * Returns NULL if all zones are exhausted.  For device-DMA buffers use
139: * pmm_alloc_page_dma(). */
140:void *pmm_alloc_page(void);
141:
142:/* DMA variant: zeroed + cache-cleaned + memory-barrier-fenced so the page is
143: * coherent for a device that may not snoop the CPU caches.  Use ONLY for
144: * buffers a device DMAs to/from (virtqueues, ring/cmd/resp buffers, GPU
145: * backing).  Ordinary kernel allocations must use pmm_alloc_page(). */
146:void *pmm_alloc_page_dma(void);
147:void *pmm_alloc_pages_dma(size_t count);
148:
149:/* Allocate multiple contiguous pages */
150:/* Allocate 'count' physically contiguous pages from ZONE_NORMAL.
151: * NOTE(MM-PMM-02): Does NOT cache-clean or barrier for count>1.
152: * NOTE(MM-PMM-04): Only searches ZONE_NORMAL; no DMA-zone contiguous alloc. */
153:void *pmm_alloc_pages(size_t count);
154:
155:/* Free a single page */
156:/* Free a single page; poisons with 0xCC; panics on double-free. */
157:void pmm_free_page(void *page);
158:
159:/* Free multiple contiguous pages */
160:/* Free 'count' contiguous pages starting at 'page'; calls pmm_free_page()
161: * for each page independently (not an atomic bulk operation). */
162:void pmm_free_pages(void *page, size_t count);
163:
164:/* Allocate with specific alignment (for block I/O) */
165:/* Allocate 'size' bytes with at least 'align'-byte alignment from ZONE_NORMAL.
166: * 'align' must be a power-of-two multiple of PAGE_SIZE.
167: * NOTE(MM-PMM-02): Same cache-clean/barrier omission as pmm_alloc_pages(). */
168:void *pmm_alloc_aligned(size_t size, size_t align);
169:
170:/* Get page descriptor for physical address */
171:/* Return the struct page descriptor for a physical address; NULL if out of range. */
172:struct page *pmm_phys_to_page(uint64_t phys);
173:
174:/* Get physical address for page descriptor */
175:/* Return the physical address for a struct page descriptor. */
176:uint64_t pmm_page_to_phys(struct page *page);
177:
178:/* Convert between physical and page frame number */
179:/* Convert between physical address (relative to MEMORY_BASE) and page frame number.
180: * phys_to_pfn: phys must already have MEMORY_BASE subtracted by the caller.
181: * pfn_to_phys: returns the offset from MEMORY_BASE, NOT an absolute address. */
182:static inline uint64_t phys_to_pfn(uint64_t phys) { return phys >> PAGE_SHIFT; }
183:
184:static inline uint64_t pfn_to_phys(uint64_t pfn) { return pfn << PAGE_SHIFT; }
185:
186:/* Page aligned macros */
187:#define PAGE_ALIGN(addr) (((addr) + PAGE_SIZE - 1) & PAGE_MASK)
188:#define PAGE_ALIGN_DOWN(addr) ((addr) & PAGE_MASK)
189:
190:/* Statistics */
191:uint64_t pmm_get_free_pages(void);
192:/* pmm_get_total_pages: the metadata SPAN (page_array/bitmap bound).  Use it to
193: * validate a PFN, never to report how much memory the machine has — on amd64
194: * the span includes the sub-4GB PCI/MMIO hole. */
195:uint64_t pmm_get_total_pages(void);
196:/* pmm_get_usable_pages: RAM that actually exists (sum of the usable regions).
197: * THIS is "total memory" for any report or budget; see MM-PMM-09 (#94). */
198:uint64_t pmm_get_usable_pages(void);
199:void pmm_dump_stats(void);
200:
201:/* Instrumentation (perf brief §1; surfaced via OS1_sys_stats).
202: * pmm_get_counters: cumulative alloc/free counts and raw bitmap-search ticks
203: *   (convert with timer_counts_to_ns()).  pmm_get_fragmentation: instantaneous
204: *   ZONE_NORMAL largest free run + free-run count.  All out-params NULL-skippable. */
205:void pmm_get_counters(uint64_t *alloc_calls, uint64_t *free_calls,
206:                      uint64_t *search_ticks_total, uint64_t *search_ticks_max);
207:void pmm_get_fragmentation(uint64_t *largest_run, uint64_t *run_count);
208:
209:#endif /* _KERNEL_PMM_H */
210:
