@@@ kernel/include/kernel/registry.h @@@
1:#ifndef _KERNEL_REGISTRY_H
2:#define _KERNEL_REGISTRY_H
3:
4:#include <kernel/nx_contract.h>
5:#include <kernel/types.h>
6:
7:#define MAX_KEY_LEN 64
8:#define MAX_VAL_LEN 128
9:
10:/* Registry Operations */
11:#define REG_OP_READ 0
12:#define REG_OP_WRITE 1
13:#define REG_OP_ENUM 2 /* enumerate keys into 'value' buffer (LIB-REG-04) */
14:#define REG_OP_DEL 3  /* remove a key (frees the node + prunes empty parents) */
15:
16:void registry_init(void);
17:/* registry_set: create or update a key.  'owner_pid' identifies the caller:
18: * 0 for kernel/system (full rights), a PID for user processes.  Updating an
19: * existing key owned by someone else returns -EACCES (first-writer-wins —
20: * a service's routing key cannot be hijacked by another process). */
21:int registry_set(const char *key, const char *value, int owner_pid) NX_MUST_USE;
22:int registry_get(const char *key, char *buffer, size_t size) NX_MUST_USE;
23:/* registry_key_is_virtual - does the key name the COMPUTED per-process view
24: * (sys.proc.<pid>.*) rather than a stored node?  The authority rule belongs to
25: * the key, not to the entry point: a virtual key is exempt from CAP_REG_WRITE
26: * (proc_env_set applies self-or-privileged instead), so every write gate —
27: * sys_registry, the OS1_NS_REG acquisition, regfs_write — consults this and
28: * they cannot disagree about the same key (R2). */
29:int registry_key_is_virtual(const char *key) NX_MUST_USE;
30:/* registry_enum: write the newline-separated list of used keys into 'buf'
31: * (NUL-terminated, bounded by 'size'); returns the number of bytes written
32: * (excluding the NUL), or -1 on bad args (LIB-REG-04).
33: * 'prefix' filters to keys that begin with it — the "list a namespace directory"
34: * primitive (Phase 4.1 A1a); NULL or "" lists ALL keys (backward-compatible). */
35:int registry_enum(const char *prefix, char *buf, size_t size) NX_MUST_USE;
36:/* registry_del: remove 'key', free its node, and prune now-empty parent dirs.
37: * First-writer-wins (owner_pid 0 = kernel/system).  0, -ENOENT, or -EACCES. */
38:int registry_del(const char *key, int owner_pid) NX_MUST_USE;
39:
40:/* Single authority seam (S-ALIGN F5) shared by ALL THREE registry entry
41: * points — sys_registry (syscall 250), the /reg VFS mount (regfs), and the
42: * object manager's OBJ_TYPE_REGKEY acquisition/write path.  Gate decisions and
43: * caller-identity derivation live only here so the entry points cannot drift. */
44:/* registry_write_allowed: mutating the registry needs CAP_REG_WRITE; a NULL
45: * current_process (in-kernel caller) passes (kernel = machine identity). */
46:bool registry_write_allowed(void);
47:/* registry_caller_owner: first-writer-wins identity — 0 for machine/kernel
48: * callers (full rights), the caller's PID otherwise. */
49:int registry_caller_owner(void) NX_MUST_USE;
50:
51:/* Syscall Handler */
52:long sys_registry(int op, const char *key, char *value, size_t size) NX_MUST_USE;
53:
54:/* registry_mount_vfs: mount the registry as the "/reg" file namespace (regfs).
55: * Call from the composition root after vfs_init() + registry_init(). */
56:void registry_mount_vfs(void);

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/registry.h.new @@@
1:#ifndef _KERNEL_REGISTRY_H
2:#define _KERNEL_REGISTRY_H
3:
4:#include <kernel/types.h>
5:
6:#define MAX_KEY_LEN 64
7:#define MAX_VAL_LEN 128
8:
9:/* Registry Operations */
10:#define REG_OP_READ 0
11:#define REG_OP_WRITE 1
12:#define REG_OP_ENUM 2 /* enumerate keys into 'value' buffer (LIB-REG-04) */
13:
14:/*
15: * Registry data model (Phase 4.1 A-tree-1): a hierarchical TREE of dynamically
16: * allocated nodes, NOT a flat array.  Dotted keys ("theme.color") are namespace
17: * PATHS: each segment is a node, leaves carry a value (a "file"), interior nodes
18: * are directories.  Children are kept sorted by name (ordered listing + search).
19: * This is the in-kernel coherent namespace ("/reg") the rest of the system reads;
20: * because it supervises the system it must scale — lookup is O(depth × children),
21: * not the old O(128) flat scan, and the key count is no longer capped.
22: * Each node is reachable as a capability object (OBJ_TYPE_REGKEY); writes are
23: * first-writer-wins by owner_pid (LIB-REG-02) and gated by CAP_REG_WRITE.
24: */
25:
26:void registry_init(void);
27:/* registry_set: create or update a key.  'owner_pid' identifies the caller:
28: * 0 for kernel/system (full rights), a PID for user processes.  Updating an
29: * existing key owned by someone else returns -EACCES (first-writer-wins —
30: * a service's routing key cannot be hijacked by another process). */
31:int registry_set(const char *key, const char *value, int owner_pid);
32:int registry_get(const char *key, char *buffer, size_t size);
33:/* registry_enum: write the newline-separated list of used keys into 'buf'
34: * (NUL-terminated, bounded by 'size'); returns the number of bytes written
35: * (excluding the NUL), or -1 on bad args (LIB-REG-04).  Keys are emitted in
36: * sorted order (the tree keeps children sorted).
37: * 'prefix' filters to keys that begin with it — the "list a namespace directory"
38: * primitive (Phase 4.1 A1a); NULL or "" lists ALL keys. */
39:int registry_enum(const char *prefix, char *buf, size_t size);
40:
41:/* Syscall Handler */
42:long sys_registry(int op, const char *key, char *value, size_t size);
43:
44:#endif

34:/* Scheduler time-slice in ticks (HZ=100 -> 10ms/tick).  Lowered from 10 (100ms)
35: * to 3 (30ms): the old quantum let a CPU-bound task hog a core for 100ms before
36: * an interactive task could preempt it (a real responsiveness tax).  ASID/PCID-
37: * tagged switches (perf §3) made context switches cheap, so the finer quantum's
38: * extra switches are nearly free — better interactivity at negligible
39: * throughput cost. */

50:/* Per-process ENVIRONMENT (Phase 17).
51: *
52: * The environment is per-process state that is INHERITED at spawn and mutable
53: * by its owner — exactly the shape of cwd, which already lives here.  Keeping
54: * it in the kernel is the Phase 5b rule applied consistently: state the kernel
55: * can own authoritatively is not duplicated into a userland-written copy that
56: * then needs a collector.  Userland reads and writes it through the registry
57: * seam (`sys.proc.<pid>.env.<NAME>`), so there is ONE representation.
58: *
59: * Inheritance follows a COPY at spawn, not a live reference to the parent.  A
60: * reference would be cheaper, but it would mean a parent's later `setenv` (or
61: * its death) silently rewrote a running child's environment — POSIX snapshots,
62: * and so do we.
63: *
64: * Sized to fit in a single page, which is also the allocation unit: 24 entries
65: * of 32+128 bytes.  A bound is unavoidable somewhere; making it the page keeps
66: * allocation trivial (pmm_alloc_page returns zeroed memory) and the limit
67: * honest and visible rather than emergent. */
68:#define ENV_KEY_MAX 32
69:#define ENV_VAL_MAX 128
70:#define ENV_MAX 24
71:struct env_entry {
72:  char k[ENV_KEY_MAX]; /* empty k == free slot */
73:  char v[ENV_VAL_MAX];
74:};
75:struct env_block {
76:  struct env_entry e[ENV_MAX];
77:};

79:/* Process Control Block */
80:struct process {
81:  uint32_t pid;
82:  char name[PROCESS_NAME_MAX];
83:
84:  /* Memory */
85:  uint64_t *page_table; /* Physical address of TTBR0_EL1 */
86:  /* Address-space tag for TLB-tagged context switches (perf §3 / DIR-06 HAL).
87:   * Architecture-neutral name: the ISA layer maps it to its native tag — ASID
88:   * on aarch64 (TTBR0_EL1[63:48]), PCID on amd64 (CR3[11:0]).  Assigned in
89:   * process_create() as (pool slot + 1), so it is unique among the <=
90:   * MAX_PROCESSES live address spaces by construction (no generation/rollover
91:   * needed); 0 is reserved for the kernel/idle address space.  The HAL uses it
92:   * to switch address space WITHOUT a full TLB flush; teardown's
93:   * arch_tlb_shootdown_all() clears the tag before its slot is recycled. */
94:  uint16_t asid;
95:  uint64_t kernel_stack; /* Kernel stack top */
96:  uint64_t heap_start;   /* Base address of user heap */
97:  uint64_t heap_end;     /* Current end of user heap */
98:  spinlock_t mm_lock;    /* Protects page table modifications */
99:
100:  /* Context for switching */
101:  struct pt_regs *context;
102:
103:  /* User Context (Initial) */
104:  uint64_t user_entry;
105:  uint64_t user_stack;
106:
107:  /* State, Priority and Permissions */
108:  int state;
109:  uint8_t first_run; /* 1 if never scheduled before (ELF context intact) */
110:  uint8_t
111:      kill_pending;  /* SCHED-UAF (Pitfall B): a kill of this PROC_CREATED
112:                      * child was DEFERRED (it is mid-construction in
113:                      * dispatch_spawn); process_finalize_spawn() releases it
114:                      * instead of enqueuing, so the immediate-free path can
115:                      * never pull the page table out from under the ELF load. */
116:  uint8_t reaping;   /* SCHED-UAF: set once when the process is queued for the
117:                      * deferred reaper (reap_push); a second push (prev==DEAD on
118:                      * one CPU racing a stale runqueue pick on another) is
119:                      * dropped, so its pages are never double-freed. */
120:  uint8_t dying;     /* set by process_terminate BEFORE it tears down this
121:                      * process's windows; SYS_CREATE_WINDOW refuses for a dying
122:                      * process, so it cannot orphan a fresh window created after
123:                      * the teardown (the un-closeable-window leak). */
124:  int exit_code;     /* low byte of status passed to sys_exit() (Phase 2);
125:                      * collected by a waiter via process_wait()'s out-param. */
126:  uint8_t exited;    /* 1 once sys_exit() ran (voluntary exit); stays 0 if the
127:                      * process reached the grave via KILL/fault, so a waiter can
128:                      * tell "Done (N)" from "Killed" (the NEXS stand-in for
129:                      * WIFEXITED vs WIFSIGNALED — there is no signal model). */
130:  int priority;      /* 0 (High) - 31 (Low) */
131:  int time_slice;    /* Ticks remaining */
132:  int quantum_reset; /* Reset value */
133:
134:  uint8_t level; /* privilege level (PLVL_*) — see the capability model below */
135:  uint32_t caps; /* capability mask (CAP_*); machine level bypasses checks */
136:  /* ctty_win: controlling-terminal window (USR-TTY-01 #123).  Inherited from
137:   * the spawner at process_create: the launching shell's window.  A process
138:   * with NO window of its own (a POSIX-like CLI tool) writes stdout here, so
139:   * it runs "in the shell"; a process that opens its own window renders there
140:   * instead (own-window-first in sys_write).  -1 = none. */
141:  int ctty_win;
142:  /* self_rendered: set the first time this process calls SYS_WINDOW_BLIT on
143:   * its OWN window (syscall_dispatch.c) — it owns a custom pixel buffer it
144:   * composites itself (nxbar/nxui/nxlauncher/nxsettings/nxfilem/demo3d/
145:   * doom/any SDL app, ...), as opposed to a plain text console.  Checked by
146:   * the own-window-first stdout resolution (object.c sys_object_write,
147:   * syscall_dispatch.c window_text_write) to skip drawing text into that
148:   * window — text and the app's own blit share the SAME pixel buffer
149:   * (compositor_window_write's term_write and compositor_blit both target
150:   * windows[i].buffer), so a stray printf()/crash message would otherwise
151:   * draw glyphs over the app's own rendering.  UART mirroring is untouched
152:   * (it happens before this flag is even consulted).  Lives on the
153:   * process (scheduler), NOT the compositor: the compositor stays a pure
154:   * rendering/composition engine with no "is this text-safe" policy of its
155:   * own — this is who-owns-what-content, a process/window-ownership
156:   * question. */
157:  int self_rendered;
158:  /* parent_pid: PID of the process that spawned this one (0 = kernel/boot).
159:   * Set by process_create() from current_process; used by the SYS_KILL
160:   * capability check (ABI-04): a process may kill itself or any descendant,
161:   * and a privileged (machine/root) process may kill anything. */
162:  int parent_pid;
163:  /* owner_pid: the LOGICAL parent — who this process belongs to, as opposed to
164:   * parent_pid, which records who mechanically spawned it (ASTRA §6.5 process
165:   * capability; maintainer decision Q3, 2026-07-18).
166:   *
167:   * These diverge as soon as execution moves behind a service: when the nxexec
168:   * daemon spawns a program on a shell's behalf, parent_pid is nxexec but the
169:   * job BELONGS to the shell.  Since kill/stop/cont authority is an ancestry
170:   * walk, without this the shell would silently lose job control over its own
171:   * jobs the moment the daemon lands.
172:   *
173:   * 0 = unset, meaning "same as parent_pid" (every process today).  Only a
174:   * PRIVILEGED process may set it, and setting it DELEGATES authority over the
175:   * child, so it is a capability operation (OBJ_CTL_SETOWNER), not a hint. */
176:  int owner_pid;
177:  /* child_count: live (not yet reaped) children of this process
178:   * (SCHED-DOS-01 #122).  Incremented by process_create() on the creator,
179:   * decremented when a child's pool slot is released (terminate immediate
180:   * free / scheduler reap).  Protected by sched_lock. */
181:  int child_count;

189:  struct wait_queue_head wait_queue;

191:  /* Tier 3 timed sleep (docs/TIMER-MODEL.md §4): a per-process software timer,
192:   * armed on the running core, wakes the process at the ABSOLUTE real-time
193:   * deadline wake_ns (mono_ns base). The wheel fires on a coarse jiffies edge;
194:   * the fine wake condition is mono_ns() >= wake_ns, so the process wakes at
195:   * the right wall-clock instant even if ticks were dropped. 0 = not sleeping.
196:   * cpu_time_counts: CPU time consumed by this process, accumulated in RAW
197:   * hardware-counter units across context switches (a cheap subtraction in the
198:   * scheduler hot path — no divide). Converted to ns only on read via
199:   * timer_counts_to_ns() for os1_cpu_ns()/ps_info. */
200:  uint64_t wake_ns;
201:  uint64_t cpu_time_counts;
202:  struct timer sleep_timer;
203:
204:  /* Yield-throttle anti-spin (per-process, docs/TIMER-MODEL.md §4): yield()
205:   * calls within the current tick are counted in yield_count (for the tick
206:   * yield_jiffy). Beyond YIELD_SPIN_BUDGET the process is busy-spinning on
207:   * yield() rather than doing work and is put to sleep until the next tick via
208:   * sleep_timer, so an unoptimised program cannot keep a core at 100% and
209:   * freeze the system. */

228:   * spawn.  NULL means "no private environment": reads fall through to the
229:   * system defaults under `sys.env.*`.  That is also the graceful degradation
230:   * path if the page allocation fails — a spawn is never failed over the
231:   * environment, the child simply inherits the machine's defaults. */
232:  struct env_block *env;

234:  /* Capability handle table (object/capability ABI, kernel/object.h) — the ONE
235:   * per-process descriptor table (ASTRA §6.2: the fd table folded into it).  A
236:   * POSIX fd IS a handle (fd N == handle N): process_create() pre-installs

239:   * Unforgeable handles to refcounted kernel objects with attenuable rights;
240:   * freed by process_handles_destroy() at teardown. */
241:  struct handle_entry *handles;

263:/* Capability & privilege-level model (B3, USR-SEC-03 #79).  Levels (PLVL_*)
264: * and capability bits (CAP_*) live in the shared api header so the kernel and

268:/* Capability helpers.  A NULL process is the kernel-internal context and is
269: * treated as fully privileged, matching the historical bypass. */
270:static inline int proc_is_machine(const struct process *p) {
271:  return !p || p->level == PLVL_MACHINE;
272:}
273:static inline int proc_is_privileged(const struct process *p) {
274:  return !p || p->level <= PLVL_ROOT;
275:}
276:static inline int proc_has_cap(const struct process *p, uint32_t cap) {
277:  return !p || p->level == PLVL_MACHINE || (p->caps & cap) == cap;
278:}

284: * pool ARRAY bound; the effective limit is derived from usable memory at
285: * process_init() (see proc_limit in process.c) and these gates keep a
286: * single unprivileged process from exhausting it:
287: *   MAX_PROCS_PER_PARENT  live-children quota for non-SYSTEM/ROOT creators;
288: *   RESERVED_PROC_SLOTS   slots only SYSTEM/ROOT creators may dig into, so
289: *                         kill/respawn recovery stays possible at saturation.

309:/* sched_lock — THE global scheduler lock (defined in process.c).  Holding it
310: * pins every entry of process_pool[] in place: every teardown path removes a
311: * process from the pool UNDER this lock and frees its page only afterwards, so
312: * while it is held a `struct process *` obtained from __process_find_by_pid()
313: * cannot become a dangling pointer (PROC-REF-01).  Exposed so a subsystem that
314: * must operate on ANOTHER process's kernel state (installing a handle into it,
315: * reading its handle table) can do lookup+use atomically instead of racing a
316: * concurrent exit.  Lock order is sched_lock -> object_lock -> kmalloc_lock;
317: * nothing takes them in reverse.  Do NOT sleep or allocate a process's handle
318: * table while holding it — refuse instead (see handle_install_into_pid). */
319:extern spinlock_t sched_lock;
320:/* proc_pid_is_privileged - privilege of a pid as a VALUE (0/1).  Use this, not
321: * process_find_by_pid()+proc_is_privileged(), from any subsystem outside the
322: * scheduler: the pointer form both dangles once sched_lock is released and
323: * forces sched_lock underneath whatever lock the caller already holds.  The
324: * compositor is the reason it exists (see the definition, Pitfall A). */
325:int proc_pid_is_privileged(int pid) NX_MUST_USE;
326:/* process_kill_allowed: ABI-04 capability check for SYS_KILL.  Returns
327: * non-zero if 'caller' may terminate 'target_pid': itself, any descendant,
328: * or anything when it is privileged (machine/root).  Kernel-internal
329: * terminate paths (compositor close, init supervision) bypass this and call
330: * process_terminate() directly. */
331:int process_kill_allowed(struct process *caller, int target_pid) NX_MUST_USE;
332:/* process_set_owner - set a process's LOGICAL parent (owner_pid), so a job
333: * spawned BY a service still answers to the client that asked for it.  Only
334: * reachable through OBJ_CTL_SETOWNER, which requires DESTROY on the target and
335: * a privileged caller (it delegates authority).  0, or -ESRCH if either pid is
336: * not live. */
337:int process_set_owner(int pid, int owner_pid) NX_MUST_USE;
338:/* proc_get_lineage - spawning parent + LOGICAL owner of a pid (owner falls back
339: * to parent when unset).  Lets userland follow inheritance across a service
340: * spawn, where the mechanical parent is the service rather than the requester.
341: */
342:int proc_get_lineage(int pid, int *parent, int *owner) NX_MUST_USE;
343:
344:/* Per-process environment (Phase 17).  The AUTHORITY rule is deliberately the
345: * process one, not the registry one: a process may always read and write its
346: * OWN environment (calling setenv is ordinary, unprivileged work), and only a
347: * privileged process may touch another's.  Routing this through CAP_REG_WRITE
348: * because the seam happens to be the registry would have made `setenv` demand
349: * system-configuration authority — the wrong ceiling for the operation.
350: *
351: * proc_env_get   0 on hit, -ENOENT if the process has no such variable.
352: * proc_env_set   0, -ESRCH (no such pid), -EPERM, -ENOMEM (block full/OOM).
353: *                A NULL/empty value UNSETS, which is what the registry DEL op
354: *                and `env -u` both need.
355: * proc_env_enum  newline-separated NAMEs into buf; returns length, or -1.
356: * proc_env_free  release the block at teardown. */
357:int proc_env_get(int pid, const char *key, char *buf, size_t size) NX_MUST_USE;
358:int proc_env_set(struct process *caller, int pid, const char *key,
359:                 const char *value) NX_MUST_USE;
360:int proc_env_enum(int pid, char *buf, size_t size) NX_MUST_USE;
361:void proc_env_free(struct process *p);
362:/* process_ipc_allowed: may 'caller' send IPC to target_pid?  True if the
363: * caller holds CAP_IPC_ANY, or target is the caller's parent or a
364: * descendant.  Acquires sched_lock internally. */
365:int process_ipc_allowed(struct process *caller, int target_pid) NX_MUST_USE;
366:int process_terminate(int pid) NX_MUST_USE;
367:/* dispatch_spawn finalization (SCHED-UAF Pitfall B): the creator calls one of
368: * these AFTER process_load_elf_args (local IRQs off) to commit the new child
369: * atomically against a concurrent kill.  finalize: if a kill was deferred
370: * (kill_pending) release the child, else enqueue it.  abort: the ELF load
371: * failed — release the half-built child. */
372:void process_finalize_spawn(struct process *p);
373:void process_abort_spawn(struct process *p);
374:/* process_kill_subtree - window-aware EXTERNAL kill: terminate root_pid + its
375: * WINDOWLESS descendants, SPARE windowed descendants + their subtrees
376: * (docs/PROCESS-KILL-MODEL.md).  Used by window_request_close, OBJ_CTL_KILL/
377: * CLOSE and SYS_KILL of another process; self-exit/fault stay single-process.
378: */
379:void process_kill_subtree(int root_pid);
380:/* process_wait - reap-poll a process. Returns pid (reaped), -1 (still alive),
381: * or -2 (not found). If out_code != NULL and the process is reaped, *out_code
382: * receives its exit_code (raw). Non-blocking. */
383:int process_wait(int pid, int *out_code) NX_MUST_USE;
384:/* process_stop/process_cont - suspend/resume a process (job control, Phase 2).
385: * stop: RUNNING/READY -> PROC_STOPPED (leaves the runqueue at its next pick).
386: * cont: PROC_STOPPED -> READY + re-enqueued. Return 0, -ESRCH (no such pid),
387: * or -EINVAL (wrong state). */
388:int process_stop(int pid) NX_MUST_USE;
389:int process_cont(int pid) NX_MUST_USE;
390:extern int process_load_elf(struct process *proc, const char *path);
391:/* Like process_load_elf(), but marshals an argv vector onto the new task's
392: * stack and seeds main()'s argc/argv (kargv holds kernel-side string copies;
393: * pass argc=0/kargv=NULL for no arguments). */

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/sha256.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/sha256.h
3: * SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) — the kernel half of the image-integrity primitive.
4: *
5: * THE SAME ALGORITHM AS tools/mkdisk.c.  A digest only means something if both
6: * sides compute it identically, so these must never become two transcriptions
7: * of the spec that drifted; they are kept adjacent in review, and any change to
8: * one is a change to both.
9: *
10: * Used as the leaf primitive of the Merkle tree over a partition (design doc
11: * §4bis, D13): one leaf per 4 KiB block, leaves hashed pairwise up to a root
12: * that lives in the META partition.  Verification then costs a full read at
13: * boot, while a write costs only log2(n) rehashes — which is what lets "verify
14: * ROOT at every boot" survive a writable filesystem.
15: *
16: * ASTRA: a library primitive under kernel/lib, consumed by the block/partition
17: * layer.  Filesystems and drivers do not open-code hashing.
18: */
19:#ifndef _KERNEL_SHA256_H
20:#define _KERNEL_SHA256_H
21:
22:#include <kernel/types.h>
23:
24:#define SHA256_DIGEST_SIZE 32
25:
26:struct sha256_ctx {
27:  uint32_t h[8];
28:  uint64_t len;
29:  uint8_t buf[64];
30:  size_t buflen;
31:};
32:
33:void sha256_init(struct sha256_ctx *c);
34:void sha256_update(struct sha256_ctx *c, const void *data, size_t n);
35:void sha256_final(struct sha256_ctx *c, uint8_t out[SHA256_DIGEST_SIZE]);
36:
37:/* sha256_buf - one-shot convenience over the three calls above. */
38:void sha256_buf(const void *data, size_t n, uint8_t out[SHA256_DIGEST_SIZE]);
39:
40:/*
41: * sha256_merkle_pair - parent = SHA256(left || right).
42: *
43: * A lone node at an odd level is PROMOTED unchanged by the caller, never
44: * paired with a copy of itself: self-pairing is the classic Merkle malleability
45: * bug (CVE-2012-2459), where two different block sequences yield the same root.
46: */
47:void sha256_merkle_pair(const uint8_t left[SHA256_DIGEST_SIZE],
48:                        const uint8_t right[SHA256_DIGEST_SIZE],
49:                        uint8_t out[SHA256_DIGEST_SIZE]);
50:
51:#endif /* _KERNEL_SHA256_H */
52:

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/spinlock.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/spinlock.h
3: * Simple spinlock implementation for AArch64
4: */
5:#ifndef _KERNEL_SPINLOCK_H
6:#define _KERNEL_SPINLOCK_H
7:
8:#include <kernel/arch.h>
9:#include <kernel/types.h>
10:
11:#ifndef __ASSEMBLER__
12:typedef struct {
13:  volatile uint32_t lock;
14:} spinlock_t;
15:
16:#define SPINLOCK_INIT {0}
17:#define DEFINE_SPINLOCK(x) spinlock_t x = SPINLOCK_INIT
18:
19:static inline void spin_lock_init(spinlock_t *lock) { lock->lock = 0; }
20:
21:static inline void spin_lock(spinlock_t *lock) { arch_spin_lock(&lock->lock); }
22:
23:static inline void spin_unlock(spinlock_t *lock) {
24:  arch_spin_unlock(&lock->lock);
25:}
26:
27:static inline int spin_trylock(spinlock_t *lock) {
28:  return arch_spin_trylock(&lock->lock);
29:}
30:
31:/* IRQ-safe spinlock */
32:static inline void spin_lock_irqsave(spinlock_t *lock, uint64_t *flags) {
33:  hal_irq_save(flags);
34:  spin_lock(lock);
35:}
36:
37:static inline int spin_trylock_irqsave(spinlock_t *lock, uint64_t *flags) {
38:  hal_irq_save(flags);
39:  if (spin_trylock(lock)) {
40:    return 1;
41:  }
42:  hal_irq_restore(*flags);
43:  return 0;
44:}
45:
46:static inline void spin_unlock_irqrestore(spinlock_t *lock, uint64_t flags) {
47:  spin_unlock(lock);
48:  hal_irq_restore(flags);
49:}
50:#endif
51:
52:#endif /* _KERNEL_SPINLOCK_H */
53:

4:/*

6: *
7: * stack_guard_init() reseeds the compiler's __stack_chk_guard canary from a
8: * per-arch entropy source (arch_entropy_u64) early in boot, replacing the
9: * compile-time constant.  See kernel/lib/stack_protector.c and issue
10: * LIB-SSP-01 (#71).
11: *
12: * Contract: must be called exactly once, as early as possible in kernel_main
13: * (before any function that runs to completion AFTER the call could have
14: * captured the OLD canary in its prologue).  Because the seeding routine and
15: * kernel_main never return through a canary-checked epilogue with a stale
16: * value, reseeding the global mid-boot is safe.
17: */

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/term.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/term.h
3: * VT/ANSI terminal emulator — extracted from the compositor (GFX-DYN-01, #123).
4: *
5: * The terminal is a self-contained ECMA-48 subset emulator that operates on a
6: * generic pixel target (struct gl_surface) plus its own backing cell grid.  It
7: * has NO dependency on the window/compositor layer: the compositor owns the
8: * struct terminal embedded in each window and hands the terminal the window's
9: * content surface for each operation.  This is the seam on which the modern
10: * terminal protocol (#123 problem 2) and terminal reflow on resize are built.
11: */
12:#ifndef _KERNEL_TERM_H
13:#define _KERNEL_TERM_H
14:
15:#include <kernel/nx_contract.h>
16:#include <kernel/types.h>
17:#include <stddef.h>
18:
19:struct gl_surface;
20:
21:/* Caret colour: 25%-alpha systemBlue block, blended over the cell so the glyph
22: * stays readable.  Phase 5 (Style/Theme) will source this from the theme. */
23:#define TERM_CARET_COLOR 0x40007AFF
24:
25:struct terminal {
26:  int cols, rows;         /* grid size in cells (derived from surface/font)   */
27:  int cursor_x, cursor_y; /* cursor cell position                              */
28:  int cursor_visible;     /* DECTCEM (\x1b[?25h/l); 1 = caret may be drawn     */
29:  int caret_px, caret_py; /* cell where the caret was last painted            */
30:  int caret_shown;        /* 1 = a caret is currently baked at caret_px/py     */
31:  int focused;            /* 1 = this terminal owns input → draw the caret     */
32:  uint8_t *text_grid;     /* cols*rows characters (persistence/repaint)        */
33:  uint32_t *attr_grid;    /* cols*rows per-cell foreground colours             */
34:  uint32_t fg_color;      /* current ANSI foreground                           */
35:  uint32_t default_fg;    /* SGR-reset / default foreground                    */
36:  uint32_t bg_color;      /* default (window) background                       */
37:  uint32_t curr_bg_color; /* current ANSI background                          */
38:  int bold;               /* SGR 1/22: bold ⇒ bright palette for 30-37         */
39:  int saved_x, saved_y;   /* DECSC/DECRC (ESC[s / ESC[u) cursor save/restore   */
40:  int escape_state;       /* 0=normal, 1=saw ESC, 2=in CSI                     */
41:  char escape_buf[32];    /* CSI parameter bytes                               */
42:  int escape_len;
43:};
44:
45:/* Allocate the cell grids and initialise VT state.  Returns 0 on success, -1 if
46: * a grid allocation failed (caller should treat the terminal as unusable). */
47:int term_init(struct terminal *t, int cols, int rows, uint32_t fg, uint32_t bg) NX_MUST_USE;
48:
49:/* Free the cell grids (idempotent; safe on a zeroed terminal). */
50:void term_free(struct terminal *t);
51:
52:/* Reconfigure the grid to new cols/rows: reallocates and clears the grids.
53: * Pixel content is the caller's concern (it owns the surface).  Returns 0/-1. */
54:int term_resize(struct terminal *t, int cols, int rows) NX_MUST_USE;
55:
56:/* Feed bytes to the terminal, rendering glyphs / handling ANSI escapes into
57: * surf, and (re)drawing the caret at the end of the batch. */
58:void term_write(struct terminal *t, struct gl_surface *surf, const char *buf,
59:                size_t count);
60:
61:/* Update focus: on focus loss the caret is erased; the focus flag gates whether
62: * term_write draws a caret. */
63:void term_set_focus(struct terminal *t, struct gl_surface *surf, int focused);
64:
65:/* Erase the caret if currently shown (idempotent). */
66:void term_clear_caret(struct terminal *t, struct gl_surface *surf);
67:
68:#endif /* _KERNEL_TERM_H */

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/test.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/test.h
3: * Lightweight In-Kernel Unit Testing Framework
4: */
5:#ifndef _KERNEL_TEST_H
6:#define _KERNEL_TEST_H
7:
8:#include <kernel/types.h>
9:#include <kernel/printk.h>
10:
11:typedef struct {
12:    const char *name;
13:    void (*func)(void);
14:} ktest_case_t;
15:
16:/* LIB-KTEST-01: set to 1 by KASSERT when an assertion fails, so ktest_run_all()
17: * can tell a real pass from an early return.  Defined in kernel/lib/ktest.c. */
18:extern volatile int ktest_test_failed;
19:
20:/* 
21: * Test Case Declaration Macro 
22: * We use a special section to collect all test cases 
23: */
24:#define KTEST_CASE(test_name) \
25:    void test_name(void); \
26:    __attribute__((used, section(".ktests"))) \
27:    static const ktest_case_t _test_##test_name = { #test_name, test_name }; \
28:    void test_name(void)
29:
30:/* Assertions */
31:/* KASSERT — wrapped in do{}while(0) because the bare `if` it used to be is a
32: * dangling-else trap: `if (c) KASSERT(x); else y;` bound the else to KASSERT's
33: * own if, silently inverting the test.  The compiler cannot warn about a macro
34: * that expands to a syntactically valid wrong thing, which is exactly the class
35: * nx_contract.h exists for. */
36:#define KASSERT(cond) \
37:    do { \
38:        if (!(cond)) { \
39:            printk("[KTEST] FAIL: %s:%d: Assertion failed: %s\n", __FILE__, \
40:                   __LINE__, #cond); \
41:            ktest_test_failed = 1; \
42:            return; \
43:        } \
44:    } while (0)
45:
46:#define KASSERT_EQ(a, b) KASSERT((a) == (b))
47:
48:/* Runner API */
49:void ktest_run_all(void);
50:
51:#endif /* _KERNEL_TEST_H */

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/vfs.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/vfs.h
3: * Virtual Filesystem Switch — the filesystem provider contract.
4: *
5: * ASTRA seam (docs/ASTRA.md): the kernel core (syscall dispatch, ELF loader)
6: * consumes ONLY this interface; the concrete filesystem driver (ext4 today)
7: * is a provider registered behind it at boot.  The composition root is
8: * kernel/main.c: vfs_register_fs(&ext4_fs_ops) then vfs_init().
9: *
10: * Resolution model (deliberately minimal for now):
11: *   - One root mount ("/"), chosen at vfs_init() by probing the GPT/MBR
12: *     partitions with every registered provider, in partition order.
13: *   - Paths handed to providers are absolute, normalized (see
14: *     vfs_resolve_path) and relative to the provider's own root.
15: *   - vfs_node is a plain value type: no refcount, no open-file table; it
16: *     stays valid as long as its mount stays mounted.  The root mount is
17: *     never torn down; non-root mounts can be retired with vfs_umount()
18: *     (in-flight path ops are counted and umount refuses with -EBUSY; a
19: *     node HELD across umount is the caller's responsibility until the
20: *     fd-layer refcount lands — docs/userland-port PLAN phase 4).  The
21: *     per-process fd table is ABI-03 (epic #93) and will layer on top.
22: */
23:#ifndef _KERNEL_VFS_H
24:#define _KERNEL_VFS_H
25:
26:#include <kernel/nx_contract.h>
27:#include <kernel/types.h>
28:#include <object.h> /* OBJ_TYPE_* — a namespace path resolves to a typed object */
29:
30:struct partition; /* kernel/gpt.h */
31:struct vfs_mount;
32:
33:/* Node types (vfs_node.type / vfs_stat.type) */
34:#define VFS_TYPE_FILE 1
35:#define VFS_TYPE_DIR 2
36:
37:/* An open filesystem object. */
38:struct vfs_node {
39:  struct vfs_mount *mnt;
40:  uint64_t id;   /* provider-private identifier (ext4: inode number) */
41:  uint64_t size; /* size in bytes at open time */
42:  uint32_t type; /* VFS_TYPE_* */
43:};
44:
45:struct vfs_stat {
46:  uint64_t size;
47:  uint32_t type; /* VFS_TYPE_* */
48:};
49:
50:/* A typed object a namespace path resolves to (the path→object bridge: in the
51: * unified model a path IS a typed capability object, not merely a file).  Filled
52: * by fs_ops.object_at and consumed by handle_create(OS1_NS_FS), which builds the
53: * matching kobject. */
54:struct vfs_objref {
55:  uint8_t obj_type;     /* OBJ_TYPE_* (include/api/object.h) */
56:  int pid;              /* OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS */
57:  int window_id;        /* OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW */
58:  struct vfs_node node; /* OBJ_TYPE_FILE */
59:};
60:
61:/*
62: * The provider contract.
63: *
64: * mount: probe 'part' and, if the on-disk format is recognised AND
65: *        supported, fill mnt->fs_private and return 0.  A format that is
66: *        simply not this filesystem must fail QUIETLY (probing is normal);
67: *        a recognised-but-unsupported filesystem must fail LOUDLY (pr_err)
68: *        so feature gaps never turn into silent corruption.
69: * open:  resolve path → node.  Returns 0 / negative error.
70: * read:  random-access read; returns bytes read (clamped at EOF) or <0.
71: * write: path-based write (provider may not support it: NULL or -1).
72: * list:  fill buf with space-separated names; returns length, -1 not
73: *        found, -2 not a directory.
74: */
75:struct fs_ops {
76:  const char *name;
77:  int (*mount)(struct vfs_mount *mnt, struct partition *part);
78:  int (*open)(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path, struct vfs_node *out);
79:  int (*read)(struct vfs_node *node, uint64_t offset, void *buf,
80:              uint32_t size);
81:  int (*write)(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path, uint64_t offset,
82:               const void *buf, uint32_t size);
83:  int (*list)(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path, char *buf,
84:              uint32_t size);
85:  /* unlink: remove the file/node at 'path' (provider may not support it:
86:   * NULL pointer or a negative errno such as -ENOSYS). */
87:  int (*unlink)(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path);
88:  /* create: create an empty file/dir at 'path' (type is VFS_TYPE_FILE or
89:   * VFS_TYPE_DIR).  Provider may not support it: NULL pointer or a negative
90:   * errno such as -ENOSYS.  Caller must have already verified 'path' does
91:   * NOT exist (M4.5-FS-WRITE / issue #126). */
92:  int (*create)(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path, uint32_t type);
93:  /* object_at: map 'path' to the TYPED object it names (the namespace→object
94:   * bridge).  Fill *out and return 0; -1 not found; -2 it is a directory.
95:   * Optional — a NULL object_at means the provider's paths are plain FILE
96:   * objects (ext4, regfs); see vfs_resolve_object's default. */
97:  int (*object_at)(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path,
98:                   struct vfs_objref *out);
99:  /* umount: release fs_private and any provider state for this mount.
100:   * Optional — NULL means the provider holds no teardown state.  Called by
101:   * vfs_umount() AFTER the mount slot is retired (no new operations can
102:   * reach the provider), never with operations in flight. */
103:  int (*umount)(struct vfs_mount *mnt);
104:};
105:
106:struct vfs_mount {
107:  const struct fs_ops *ops;
108:  void *fs_private;        /* provider state, owned by ops->mount */
109:  const char *mountpoint;  /* absolute mount path ("/", "/reg", ...) — Plan 9 namespace */
110:  uint32_t part_index;     /* GPT/MBR partition index backing this mount (0 = synthetic) */
111:  int in_use;
112:  /* Path-based operations in flight on this mount (incremented by the
113:   * dispatchers in vfs.c under mounts_lock, decremented on completion).
114:   * vfs_umount refuses with -EBUSY while non-zero, so a provider can never
115:   * be torn down under a running dispatch (the S-STAB lifetime rule the
116:   * "mounts are never torn down" era did not need). */
117:  volatile int active_ops;
118:};
119:
120:/* Provider registration + mounting (called from the composition root) */
121:int vfs_register_fs(const struct fs_ops *ops) NX_MUST_USE;
122:void vfs_init(void);
123:/* vfs_mount_at - mount a provider at an absolute path (Plan 9-style namespace
124: * mount).  'fs_private' is the provider's state (NULL for a stateless synthetic
125: * server like regfs).  Path resolution routes by LONGEST matching mountpoint;
126: * the root "/" mount is the fallback.  Returns 0, or -1 if the table is full /
127: * args are bad.  Called from the composition root, single-threaded. */
128:int vfs_mount_at(const char *mountpoint, const struct fs_ops *ops, void *fs_private) NX_MUST_USE;
129:
130:/* vfs_umount - retire a NON-root mount by exact mountpoint match.  Fails with
131: * -EBUSY while path operations are in flight on it, -1 if not found or root
132: * ("/" teardown arrives with the ISO-boot rework, PLAN phase 4).  The
133: * provider's optional umount op runs after the slot is retired.  NOTE: a
134: * vfs_node held across umount is the caller's responsibility until the
135: * fd-layer refcount lands (documented limitation, docs/userland-port). */
136:int vfs_umount(const char *mountpoint) NX_MUST_USE;
137:
138:/* vfs_resolve_object - resolve a path to the TYPED capability object it names
139: * (delegates to the provider's object_at, else defaults to a FILE).  Returns 0
140: * with *out filled, -1 not found, -2 it is a directory.  Backs open() ≡
141: * handle_create(OS1_NS_FS): everything resolvable in the namespace is an object. */
142:int vfs_resolve_object(const char *path, struct vfs_objref *out) NX_MUST_USE;
143:
144:/* Core-facing API (the only filesystem surface outside kernel/fs/) */
145:int vfs_open(const char *path, struct vfs_node *out) NX_MUST_USE;
146:int vfs_read(struct vfs_node *node, uint64_t offset, void *buf, uint32_t size) NX_MUST_USE;
147:/* vfs_read_file: buf==NULL / size==0 returns the file size (legacy internal
148: * helper; userland metadata probes use OBJ_CTL_STAT). */
149:int vfs_read_file(const char *path, void *buf, uint32_t size, uint64_t offset) NX_MUST_USE;
150:/* vfs_write_allowed: THE single write-authority seam (CAP_FS_WRITE + the
151: * /sys,/bin immutable-tree ACL) shared by WRITE/MUTATE-handle acquisition.
152: * Takes a vfs_resolve_path()-canonical
153: * path; returns 0, -EPERM or -EACCES.  (S-ALIGN F6) */
154:int vfs_write_allowed(const char *resolved_path) NX_MUST_USE;
155:int vfs_write_file(const char *path, const void *buf, uint32_t size,
156:                   uint64_t offset) NX_MUST_USE;
157:int vfs_list_dir(const char *path, char *buf, uint32_t size) NX_MUST_USE;
158:int vfs_unlink(const char *path) NX_MUST_USE; /* remove a file/node by path */
159:/* vfs_create - create an empty file/dir at 'path' (VFS_TYPE_FILE/_DIR)
160: * through the responsible mount's provider.  Returns 0, or negative (the
161: * provider has no create support, or its own error).  Does NOT check
162: * write authority or pre-existence - callers (syscall_dispatch.c) must call
163: * vfs_write_allowed()/vfs_stat() first (issue #126). */
164:int vfs_create(const char *path, uint32_t type) NX_MUST_USE;
165:int vfs_stat(const char *path, struct vfs_stat *st) NX_MUST_USE;
166:
167:void vfs_resolve_path(const char *in, char *out, size_t size);
168:
169:#endif /* _KERNEL_VFS_H */

@@@ kernel/include/kernel/vmm.h @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/include/kernel/vmm.h
3: * Virtual Memory Manager
4: *
5: * Defines the public API of the VMM and all PTE flag constants for both
6: * AArch64 and AMD64.  The constants are mutually exclusive between arches
7: * via the ARCH_AARCH64 / ARCH_AMD64 preprocessor guards.
8: *
9: * Central invariant (DIRECT MAP, see kernel/memlayout.h):
10: *   phys_to_virt()/virt_to_phys() are a single-offset translation
11: *   (KERNEL_VIRT_BASE; 0 == identity while the higher-half flip is staged).
12: *
13: *   MM-VMM-02 + MM-PMM-07 (contract sweep, Phase B2): every PA-to-pointer
14: *   crossing in the tree goes through that pair — page-table walkers,
15: *   PMM returns/frees, process PGD loads (TTBR0/CR3), user-frame maps,
16: *   virtio DMA addresses, MMIO accessors.  Flipping KERNEL_VIRT_BASE plus
17: *   the boot/linker changes is all that remains for the higher half.
18: *
19: * Known issues (see docs/review/analysis/01-mm-memory-management.md):
20: *   MM-VMM-01 through MM-VMM-07.
21: */
22:#ifndef _KERNEL_VMM_H
23:#define _KERNEL_VMM_H
24:
25:#include <kernel/nx_contract.h>
26:#include <kernel/memlayout.h>
27:#include <kernel/pmm.h>
28:#include <kernel/types.h>
29:
30:/* Virtual Memory Map
31: *
32: * 0x0000_0000_0000_0000 - 0x0000_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF : User Space (256 TB)
33: * 0xFFFF_0000_0000_0000 - 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF : Kernel Space (256 TB)
34: *
35: * MM-VMM-02 RESOLVED: this layout is now LIVE on both arches.  The kernel
36: * image and the direct map of all RAM/MMIO live at KERNEL_VIRT_BASE + PA
37: * (memlayout.h); user space owns the low half exclusively (aarch64: TTBR0
38: * per process; amd64: PML4 entries 0..255 private per process).
39: */
40:
41:/* PTE flag constants -- selected by arch at compile time. */
42:#ifdef ARCH_AARCH64
43:/* --- AArch64 Page Table Entry (PTE) Flags --- */
44:/* AArch64 descriptor format and bit details:
45: * AArch64 uses descriptor format: bits [1:0] = 0b11 for page, 0b01 for block.
46: * Attribute index (bits [4:2]) selects the MAIR_EL1 slot (Normal vs Device).
47: * Shareability: bits [9:8]; Inner Shareable = 0b11.
48: * Access flag (AF, bit 10): must be set or a permission fault occurs on first access.
49: * AP bits [7:6]: EL0 read/write access control.
50: * UXN (bit 54): unprivileged execute-never; PXN (bit 53): privileged execute-never. */
51:#define PTE_VALID (1UL << 0)
52:#define PTE_PAGE  (1UL << 1)
53:#define PTE_BLOCK (0UL << 1)
54:
55:#define PTE_AP_EL1_RW (0UL << 6)
56:#define PTE_AP_EL1_RO (2UL << 6)
57:#define PTE_AP_EL0_RW (1UL << 6)
58:#define PTE_AP_EL0_RO (3UL << 6)
59:
60:#define PTE_RW       PTE_AP_EL1_RW
61:#define PTE_USER     PTE_AP_EL0_RW
62:#define PTE_RO       PTE_AP_EL1_RO
63:
64:#define PTE_TABLE    PTE_PAGE
65:
66:/* PTE_IS_TABLE: does this VALID directory entry point to a next-level table?
67: * AArch64: bits[1:0] == 0b11 → table; 0b01 → block. */
68:#define PTE_IS_TABLE(e) (((e) & 0x3UL) == 0x3UL)
69:
70:#define PTE_INNER_SHARE (3UL << 8)
71:#define PTE_AF          (1UL << 10)
72:
73:/* PAGE_KERNEL: kernel RW, not executable (PXN+UXN set).  This is the W^X
74: * default for all RAM (MM-VMM-01 resolved); only the kernel text window is
75: * mapped PAGE_KERNEL_RX by vmm_map_ram_wx(). */
76:#define PAGE_KERNEL \
77:    (PTE_VALID | PTE_PAGE | PTE_ATTR_INDX(PTE_ATTR_NORMAL) | PTE_INNER_SHARE | \
78:     PTE_AF | PTE_AP_EL1_RW | PTE_UXN | PTE_PXN)
79:/* PAGE_KERNEL_EXEC: kernel RW + executable.  W^X-violating by definition;
80: * kept only for exceptional uses — no RAM-wide mapping uses it anymore. */
81:#define PAGE_KERNEL_EXEC \
82:    (PTE_VALID | PTE_PAGE | PTE_ATTR_INDX(PTE_ATTR_NORMAL) | PTE_INNER_SHARE | \
83:     PTE_AF | PTE_AP_EL1_RW | PTE_UXN)
84:/* PAGE_KERNEL_RX: kernel text — read-only at EL1, executable at EL1 only. */
85:#define PAGE_KERNEL_RX \
86:    (PTE_VALID | PTE_PAGE | PTE_ATTR_INDX(PTE_ATTR_NORMAL) | PTE_INNER_SHARE | \
87:     PTE_AF | PTE_AP_EL1_RO | PTE_UXN)
88:/* PAGE_KERNEL_RO: kernel rodata — read-only, never executable. */
89:#define PAGE_KERNEL_RO \
90:    (PTE_VALID | PTE_PAGE | PTE_ATTR_INDX(PTE_ATTR_NORMAL) | PTE_INNER_SHARE | \
91:     PTE_AF | PTE_AP_EL1_RO | PTE_UXN | PTE_PXN)
92:/* PAGE_DEVICE: strongly-ordered Device-nGnRnE memory, not executable. */
93:#define PAGE_DEVICE \
94:    (PTE_VALID | PTE_PAGE | PTE_ATTR_INDX(PTE_ATTR_DEVICE) | PTE_INNER_SHARE | \
95:     PTE_AF | PTE_AP_EL1_RW | PTE_UXN | PTE_PXN)
96:/* PAGE_USER: EL0 (user) RW, not executable at EL1.  EL0-executable: use for
97: * ELF code segments only. */
98:#define PAGE_USER \
99:    (PTE_VALID | PTE_PAGE | PTE_ATTR_INDX(PTE_ATTR_NORMAL) | PTE_INNER_SHARE | \
100:     PTE_AF | PTE_AP_EL0_RW | PTE_PXN)
101:/* PAGE_USER_DATA: user RW data (stack/heap) — never executable (W^X). */
102:#define PAGE_USER_DATA (PAGE_USER | PTE_UXN)
103:/* PAGE_USER_RX: user read-only + EL0-executable (ELF text). PXN keeps it
104: * non-executable at EL1 — the kernel must never execute a user page. */
105:#define PAGE_USER_RX \
106:    (PTE_VALID | PTE_PAGE | PTE_ATTR_INDX(PTE_ATTR_NORMAL) | PTE_INNER_SHARE | \
107:     PTE_AF | PTE_AP_EL0_RO | PTE_PXN)
108:/* PAGE_USER_RO: user read-only data (ELF rodata) — never executable (W^X). */
109:#define PAGE_USER_RO (PAGE_USER_RX | PTE_UXN)
110:
111:#elif defined(ARCH_AMD64)
112:/* --- AMD64 Page Table Entry (PTE) Flags --- */
113:/* AMD64 bit layout details:
114: * AMD64 uses a simpler flat bit layout; no MAIR equivalent.
115: * PTE_NX (bit 63) requires IA32_EFER.NXE=1 (set by arch init).
116: * NOTE(MM-VMM-01): PAGE_KERNEL_EXEC == PAGE_KERNEL on AMD64 (no NX bit set),
117: * so no W^X enforcement exists on this arch either. */
118:#define PTE_VALID (1UL << 0) 
119:#define PTE_RW    (1UL << 1) 
120:#define PTE_USER  (1UL << 2) 
121:#define PTE_PWT   (1UL << 3) 
122:#define PTE_PCD   (1UL << 4) 
123:#define PTE_AF    (1UL << 5) 
124:#define PTE_DIRTY (1UL << 6) 
125:#define PTE_PS    (1UL << 7) 
126:#define PTE_NX    (1ULL << 63)
127:
128:#define PTE_PAGE  (0UL)
129:#define PTE_RO    (0UL)
130:
131:#define PTE_TABLE (PTE_RW | PTE_USER)
132:
133:/* PTE_IS_TABLE: does this VALID directory entry point to a next-level table?
134: * AMD64: PS (bit 7) clear → table; PS set → 2MB/1GB page.  (PTE_TABLE above
135: * is NOT usable for this test — it is an RW|US flag combo for new tables.) */
136:#define PTE_IS_TABLE(e) (!((e) & PTE_PS))
137:
138:/* W^X page profiles (MM-VMM-01/AMMU-01 resolved).  PTE_NX requires
139: * IA32_EFER.NXE=1, set next to LME in start.S (BSP) and trampoline.S (APs);
140: * CR0.WP is set at boot so the kernel honours read-only PTEs. */
141:#define PAGE_KERNEL      (PTE_VALID | PTE_RW | PTE_NX)
142:#define PAGE_KERNEL_EXEC (PTE_VALID | PTE_RW) /* W+X: no RAM-wide user left */
143:#define PAGE_KERNEL_RX   (PTE_VALID)               /* text: RO + executable */
144:#define PAGE_KERNEL_RO   (PTE_VALID | PTE_NX)      /* rodata: RO, no exec */
145:#define PAGE_DEVICE      (PTE_VALID | PTE_RW | PTE_PCD | PTE_PWT | PTE_NX)
146:#define PAGE_USER        (PTE_VALID | PTE_RW | PTE_USER)
147:/* PAGE_USER_DATA: user RW data (stack/heap) — never executable (W^X). */
148:#define PAGE_USER_DATA   (PAGE_USER | PTE_NX)
149:/* PAGE_USER_RX: user read-only + executable (ELF text). */
150:#define PAGE_USER_RX     (PTE_VALID | PTE_USER)
151:/* PAGE_USER_RO: user read-only data (ELF rodata) — never executable (W^X). */
152:#define PAGE_USER_RO     (PTE_VALID | PTE_USER | PTE_NX)
153:
154:#endif
155:
156:/* --- Architecture-Neutral Attribute Definitions --- */
157:/* PTE_ATTR_INDX selects MAIR_EL1 slot on AArch64; unused on AMD64. */
158:#define PTE_ATTR_NORMAL 0UL
159:#define PTE_ATTR_DEVICE 1UL
160:#define PTE_ATTR_INDX(x) ((uint64_t)(x) << 2)
161:
162:/* Execute-Never Bits (Mapped by Arch MMU) */
163:/* AArch64 only; encoded in bits 54/53 of PTE.
164: * On AMD64, PTE_NX plays this role instead. */
165:#define PTE_UXN (1UL << 54)
166:#define PTE_PXN (1UL << 53)
167:
168:/* VMM Types */
169:typedef uint64_t gva_t;
170:typedef uint64_t gpa_t;
171:typedef uint64_t pte_t;
172:/* typedef aliases for documentation clarity:
173: * gva_t = guest/kernel virtual address
174: * gpa_t = guest/kernel physical address
175: * pte_t = raw page table entry value */
176:
177:/* Address Translation: phys_to_virt()/virt_to_phys() live in
178: * kernel/memlayout.h (single KERNEL_VIRT_BASE offset, identity while the
179: * offset is 0).  Included above so all existing users keep compiling. */
180:
181:/* vmm_create_pgd: allocate a new process PGD with kernel half pre-filled. */
182:uint64_t *vmm_create_pgd(void);
183:uint64_t arch_vmm_create_process_pgd(void);
184:/* vmm_destroy_pgd: free the process-private page-table pages AND the user
185: * RAM frames (PTEs carrying PTE_USER) of 'pgd' (MM-VMM-04 resolved).
186: * Entries shared with kernel_pgd (compared by value) are never touched. */
187:void vmm_destroy_pgd(uint64_t *pgd);
188:
189:/* vmm_init: phase-1 MMU bring-up; maps 128 MB bootstrap window; enables MMU. */
190:void vmm_init(void);
191:/* vmm_dynamic_remap: phase-2; maps all detected RAM; switches to new PGD.
192: * NOTE(MM-VMM-03): leaks bootstrap PGD; no IPI to secondary CPUs.
193: * NOTE(MM-VMM-01): maps all RAM PAGE_KERNEL_EXEC; no W^X. */
194:void vmm_dynamic_remap(void);
195:/* vmm_map_page: map one 4KB page; delegates to arch_vmm_map(). */
196:int vmm_map_page(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t virt, uint64_t phys, uint64_t flags) NX_MUST_USE;
197:/* vmm_unmap_page: unmap one page with cross-CPU TLB shootdown (MM-VMM-05
198: * resolved): on return no online CPU translates 'virt' via the old entry. */
199:void vmm_unmap_page(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t virt);
200:/* vmm_protect: rewrite the attributes of existing mappings in [virt,
201: * virt+size) to the given PAGE/PTE profile (AMMU-02 resolved).  Frame
202: * addresses are preserved; large pages are split for 4KB precision; ends
203: * with a cross-CPU TLB shootdown.  Returns 0, or -1 on a hole in range. */
204:int vmm_protect(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t virt, uint64_t size, uint64_t flags) NX_MUST_USE;
205:uint64_t vmm_get_phys(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t virt);
206:
207:struct process;
208:/* vmm_map_page_locked: vmm_map_page wrapped with proc->mm_lock. */
209:int vmm_map_page_locked(struct process *proc, uint64_t virt, uint64_t phys, uint64_t flags) NX_MUST_USE;
210:/* vmm_unmap_page_locked: vmm_unmap_page wrapped with proc->mm_lock. */
211:void vmm_unmap_page_locked(struct process *proc, uint64_t virt);
212:
213:/* vmm_map: map a contiguous range; 4KB pages only; partial on error (no rollback). */
214:int vmm_map(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t virt, uint64_t phys, uint64_t size, uint64_t flags) NX_MUST_USE;
215:/* vmm_map_ram_wx: map a usable RAM range at its direct-map VA with the W^X
216: * split: kernel text RX, rodata RO+NX, everything else RW+NX

218:void vmm_map_ram_wx(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t base, uint64_t size);
219:/* vmm_check_range: verify all pages in range are mapped with required flags. */
220:int vmm_check_range(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t virt, uint64_t size, uint64_t flags_mask) NX_MUST_USE;
221:
222:/*
223: * vmm_is_user_addr - return true if 'addr' falls in the user virtual range.
224: *
225: * Checks that addr >= 0x1000 (excludes NULL page) and that the top 16 bits
226: * are zero (canonical user-space addresses in a 48-bit VA space).
227: * Used by syscall handlers to validate user pointers before access.
228: */
229:static inline bool vmm_is_user_addr(uint64_t addr) {
230:  return (addr >= 0x1000) && ((addr & 0xFFFF000000000000ULL) == 0);
231:}

240:#define vmm_copy_string_from_user(dest, src, max_len) hal_copy_string_from_user(dest, src, max_len)
241:#define vmm_copy_string_from_user_strict(dest, src, max_len) hal_copy_string_from_user_strict(dest, src, max_len)
