@@@ kernel/irq/irq.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/irq/irq.c
3: * Generic IRQ Framework
4: *
5: * Provides a chip-abstraction layer (struct irq_chip) and a 256-entry handler
6: * table that sits between the hardware interrupt controller and device drivers.
7: * Two dispatch entry-points exist for the two supported arches:
8: *
9: *   irq_handler()  -- called from the aarch64 exception vector; drives the
10: *                     acknowledge/dispatch/EOI loop via current_chip ops.
11: *   irq_dispatch() -- called directly from the amd64 IDT common handler
12: *                     (idt.c); bypasses current_chip entirely; EOI is issued
13: *                     by the IDT handler before or after this call.
14: *
15: * Invariants:
16: *   - current_chip must be set via irq_register_chip() before irq_init() is
17: *     called.  All chip ops are guarded by NULL checks.
18: *   - irq_handlers[] entries are written by irq_register/irq_unregister only;
19: *     they are read from IRQ context in irq_handler/irq_dispatch.
20: *   - The timer IRQ (IRQ_TIMER / 30) is handled inline in irq_handler() and
21: *     bypasses the irq_handlers[] table.
22: *
23: * Known issues:
24: *   IRQ-01  RESOLVED (Phase A step 15, by contract redefinition): the two
25: *           dispatch models are now explicit.  aarch64 enters through
26: *           irq_handler() (GIC acknowledge-loop, vector from GICC_IAR);
27: *           amd64 enters through irq_dispatch() (vector already known from
28: *           the IDT stub — an IAR-style acknowledge() makes no sense on x86,
29: *           exactly as in other kernels' vectored dispatch).  What WAS broken
30: *           is fixed: EOI on amd64 no longer bypasses the chip — the IDT
31: *           handler calls irq_chip_end(), and pic_chip->end() owns the full
32: *           LAPIC+PIC EOI sequence.  pic_chip_acknowledge() keeps returning
33: *           1023 so a stray irq_handler() call on amd64 stays a no-op.
34: *   IRQ-02  RESOLVED (Phase A step 15): irq_table_lock protects
35: *           irq_handlers[]; dispatch paths copy the (handler, data) pair
36: *           under the lock and invoke the handler outside it, so a concurrent
37: *           irq_unregister can no longer produce a torn pair or a stale
38: *           pointer dereference.
39: */
40:#include <kernel/irq.h>
41:#include <kernel/printk.h>
42:#include <kernel/sched.h>
43:#include <kernel/spinlock.h>
44:#include <kernel/types.h>
45:
46:#define MAX_IRQS 256
47:
48:/* irq_handlers[]: sparse table mapping IRQ number -> (handler, opaque data).
49: * Entries are set by irq_register() and cleared by irq_unregister().
50: * FIX(IRQ-02): guarded by irq_table_lock; dispatchers copy the pair under
51: * the lock and call the handler after dropping it (a handler may re-register
52: * or disable lines without self-deadlocking). */
53:static struct {
54:  irq_handler_t handler;
55:  void *data;
56:} irq_handlers[MAX_IRQS];
57:
58:/* irq_table_lock: protects irq_handlers[] against concurrent
59: * register/unregister/dispatch across CPUs (IRQ-02). */
60:static DEFINE_SPINLOCK(irq_table_lock);
61:
62:/* current_chip: pointer to the active irq_chip implementation.
63: * Set once at boot via irq_register_chip(); never changed afterwards.
64: * On aarch64: points to gic_chip (gic.c).
65: * On amd64:   points to pic_chip (pic_pit.c) — but see IRQ-01. */
66:static struct irq_chip *current_chip = NULL;
67:
68:/*
69: * irq_register_chip - register the platform interrupt controller.
70: *
71: * Must be called before irq_init().  Stores the chip pointer in current_chip
72: * and logs its name.  Not thread-safe (called once from boot path only).
73: *
74: * Locking: none required; called before SMP is active.
75: */
76:void irq_register_chip(struct irq_chip *chip) {
77:  current_chip = chip;
78:  pr_info("IRQ: Registered chip %s\n", chip->name);
79:}
80:
81:/*
82: * irq_init - call the chip's global (distributor) initialisation hook.
83: *
84: * Delegates to current_chip->init() which, for GICv2, initialises the
85: * GICD distributor, disables all interrupts, clears pending state, and sets
86: * target/priority registers.  For the 8259 PIC chip init is NULL (pic_init()
87: * is called directly from the amd64 HAL).
88: *
89: * Locking: called from boot CPU before SMP; no concurrent access.
90: */
91:void irq_init(void) {
92:  if (current_chip && current_chip->init) {
93:    current_chip->init();
94:  }
95:}
96:
97:/*
98: * irq_init_percpu - call the chip's per-CPU initialisation hook.
99: *
100: * For GICv2, initialises the GICC CPU interface on the calling core:
101: * sets priority mask (GICC_PMR = 0xFF), binary point (GICC_BPR = 0), and
102: * enables the CPU interface (GICC_CTLR = 1).  Called on every CPU at SMP
103: * bring-up via the boot sequence.
104: *
105: * Locking: operates only on per-CPU MMIO registers; no shared state.
106: */
107:void irq_init_percpu(void) {
108:  if (current_chip && current_chip->init_percpu) {
109:    current_chip->init_percpu();
110:  }
111:}
112:
113:/*
114: * irq_register - bind a handler to an IRQ line and enable it.
115: *
116: * @irq:     interrupt number (0..MAX_IRQS-1).
117: * @handler: function called from IRQ context with (irq, data).
118: * @data:    opaque pointer passed to handler; may be NULL.
119: *
120: * Returns 0 on success, -EINVAL if irq >= MAX_IRQS, -EBUSY if already
121: * registered.  After storing the handler, calls chip->enable(irq) to unmask
122: * the line in the interrupt controller.
123: *
124: * Locking: irq_table_lock (irqsave) for the table slot; the chip->enable()
125: *          MMIO write happens after the slot is visible, so the line is
126: *          never unmasked with an empty handler entry.
127: * IRQ context: must NOT be called from an IRQ handler.
128: */
129:int irq_register(uint32_t irq, irq_handler_t handler, void *data) {
130:  if (irq >= MAX_IRQS)
131:    return -EINVAL;
132:
133:  uint64_t flags;
134:  spin_lock_irqsave(&irq_table_lock, &flags);
135:
136:  if (irq_handlers[irq].handler) {
137:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&irq_table_lock, flags);
138:    return -EBUSY;
139:  }
140:
141:  irq_handlers[irq].handler = handler;
142:  irq_handlers[irq].data = data;
143:
144:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&irq_table_lock, flags);
145:
146:  if (current_chip && current_chip->enable) {
147:    current_chip->enable(irq);
148:  }
149:
150:  return 0;
151:}
152:
153:/*
154: * irq_unregister - disable an IRQ line and remove its handler.
155: *
156: * @irq: interrupt number to deregister.
157: *
158: * Calls chip->disable(irq) first to mask the line at the controller, then
159: * clears the handler and data pointers in irq_handlers[].  Silently returns
160: * if irq >= MAX_IRQS.
161: *
162: * Locking: irq_table_lock (irqsave) for the table slot.  A dispatch that
163: *          already copied the pair may still complete one final handler call
164: *          after unregister returns (no synchronize_irq yet); the line is
165: *          masked first, so no NEW interrupts dispatch the stale entry.
166: * IRQ context: must NOT be called from an IRQ handler.
167: */
168:void irq_unregister(uint32_t irq) {
169:  if (irq >= MAX_IRQS)
170:    return;
171:
172:  if (current_chip && current_chip->disable) {
173:    current_chip->disable(irq);
174:  }
175:
176:  uint64_t flags;
177:  spin_lock_irqsave(&irq_table_lock, &flags);
178:  irq_handlers[irq].handler = NULL;
179:  irq_handlers[irq].data = NULL;
180:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&irq_table_lock, flags);
181:}
182:
183:/*
184: * irq_enable - unmask a single IRQ line at the interrupt controller.
185: *
186: * @irq: interrupt number to enable.
187: *
188: * Thin wrapper around chip->enable(); no handler registration side-effect.
189: * Used by timer_init() to enable the ARM timer IRQ independently of
190: * irq_register().
191: *
192: * Locking: chip->enable() on GICv2 writes GICD_ISENABLER; safe to call
193: *          from any context as long as the MMIO window is valid.
194: */
195:void irq_enable(uint32_t irq) {
196:  if (current_chip && current_chip->enable) {
197:    current_chip->enable(irq);
198:  }
199:}
200:
201:/*
202: * irq_disable - mask a single IRQ line at the interrupt controller.
203: *
204: * @irq: interrupt number to disable.
205: *
206: * Thin wrapper around chip->disable().  Called from irq_handler() to silence
207: * an unhandled IRQ and prevent an interrupt storm.
208: *
209: * Locking: same as irq_enable; MMIO write is atomic at the register level.
210: */
211:void irq_disable(uint32_t irq) {
212:  if (current_chip && current_chip->disable) {
213:    current_chip->disable(irq);
214:  }
215:}
216:
217:/*
218: * irq_send_ipi_all - broadcast SGI0 to all other CPUs.
219: *
220: * Delegates to chip->send_ipi_all(); for GICv2, writes GICD_SGIR with
221: * TargetListFilter=0b01 (all CPUs except requestor) and SGI ID 0.
222: * SGI0 is treated by irq_handler() as a panic-halt IPI.
223: *
224: * Locking: no locks; GICD_SGIR write is self-contained.
225: * IRQ context: may be called from any context.
226: */
227:void irq_send_ipi_all(void) {
228:  if (current_chip && current_chip->send_ipi_all) {
229:    current_chip->send_ipi_all();
230:  }
231:}
232:
233:/*
234: * cpu_halt_from_ipi - halt this CPU after receiving a panic IPI (SGI0).
235: *
236: * Sets the global panic_flag, stops the arch timer (prevents further timer
237: * IRQs on this core), and calls arch_cpu_halt() to enter an infinite WFI
238: * loop.  Called only from irq_handler() when irq == 0.
239: *
240: * Locking: panic_flag is a volatile int; no spinlock; intentionally racy
241: *          since all CPUs are being halted simultaneously.
242: * IRQ context: called from IRQ handler after chip->end(0); IRQs are
243: *              effectively disabled by arch_cpu_halt() thereafter.
244: */
245:/* Internal panic halt helper */
246:static void cpu_halt_from_ipi(void) {
247:  extern volatile int panic_flag;
248:  panic_flag = 1;
249:  arch_timer_control(0);
250:  arch_cpu_halt();
251:}
252:
253:/*
254: * irq_handler - main IRQ dispatch loop for aarch64 (GIC path).
255: *
256: * Called from the aarch64 exception vector with the saved register state.
257: * Loops calling chip->acknowledge() (GIC: reads GICC_IAR) until 1023
258: * (spurious / no more) is returned.  For each valid IRQ:
259: *
260: *   irq == 0    (SGI0): EOI, then halt this CPU via cpu_halt_from_ipi().
261: *   irq == IRQ_TIMER or 30: delegate to timer_handler(regs) for scheduling;
262: *                            return immediately with potentially switched regs.
263: *   irq < MAX_IRQS with registered handler: call handler(irq, data), then EOI.
264: *   otherwise: warn and disable the line to prevent storm.
265: *
266: * Returns the (potentially new) register state for the resumed context.
267: *
268: * NOTE(IRQ-01, resolved): this loop is the aarch64 (GIC) entry point only;
269: * amd64 is vectored and enters through irq_dispatch() + irq_chip_end().
270: * FIX(IRQ-02): the (handler, data) pair is copied under irq_table_lock and
271: * invoked after dropping it.
272: *
273: * Locking: runs with IRQs implicitly masked (exception entry).
274: * IRQ context: YES — this IS the IRQ entry point on aarch64.
275: */
276:struct pt_regs *irq_handler(struct pt_regs *regs) {
277:  uint32_t irq;
278:  struct pt_regs *ret_regs = regs;
279:
280:  if (!current_chip)
281:    return regs;
282:
283:  while (1) {
284:    irq = current_chip->acknowledge();
285:
286:    if (irq == 1023) /* Spurious or No more interrupts */
287:      break;
288:
289:#ifdef DEBUG_IRQ
290:    if (irq != IRQ_TIMER && irq != 30) {
291:      pr_info("IRQ: Handling interrupt %u\n", irq);
292:    }
293:#endif
294:
295:    /* SGI0: panic halt IPI */
296:    if (irq == 0) {
297:      current_chip->end(irq);
298:      cpu_halt_from_ipi();
299:    }
300:
301:    /* Handle IRQ */
302:    if (irq == IRQ_TIMER || irq == 30) {
303:      /* Timer Interrupt - Returns new regs if context switch occurred */
304:      extern struct pt_regs *timer_handler(struct pt_regs * regs);
305:
306:      ret_regs = timer_handler(ret_regs);
307:
308:      current_chip->end(irq);
309:      return ret_regs;
310:    }
311:
312:    /* FIX(IRQ-02): snapshot the pair under the lock, call outside it. */
313:    irq_handler_t handler = NULL;
314:    void *data = NULL;
315:    if (irq < MAX_IRQS) {
316:      spin_lock(&irq_table_lock);
317:      handler = irq_handlers[irq].handler;
318:      data = irq_handlers[irq].data;
319:      spin_unlock(&irq_table_lock);
320:    }
321:
322:    if (handler) {
323:      handler(irq, data);
324:    } else {
325:      pr_warn("IRQ: Unhandled interrupt %u\n", irq);
326:      irq_disable(irq); /* Prevent interrupt storm */
327:    }
328:
329:    current_chip->end(irq);
330:  }
331:
332:  return ret_regs;
333:}
334:
335:/*
336: * irq_dispatch - IRQ dispatch entry-point for amd64 (IDT path).
337: *
338: * @irq:  interrupt vector number derived from the IDT stub (0..255).
339: * @regs: saved register state from the IDT common handler.
340: *
341: * Called by the amd64 IDT common handler in idt.c; the IDT handler then
342: * issues the EOI through irq_chip_end() (chip-owned EOI — IRQ-01 fix).
343: * Looks up irq_handlers[irq] and invokes the registered callback if present;
344: * logs a warning otherwise.
345: *
346: * Returns @regs unchanged (no context-switch support on this path; scheduler
347: * preemption on amd64 happens through a separate mechanism).
348: *
349: * NOTE(IRQ-01, resolved): acknowledge() is N/A on a vectored architecture —
350: * the vector arrives with the frame.  EOI goes through the chip now.
351: * FIX(IRQ-02): (handler, data) copied under irq_table_lock, called outside.
352: *
353: * Locking: IRQs are masked by the CPU at IDT entry; irq_table_lock guards
354: *          the table read against concurrent register/unregister.
355: * IRQ context: YES — called from the amd64 IDT handler.
356: */
357:struct pt_regs *irq_dispatch(uint32_t irq, struct pt_regs *regs) {
358:  irq_handler_t handler = NULL;
359:  void *data = NULL;
360:
361:  if (irq < MAX_IRQS) {
362:    spin_lock(&irq_table_lock);
363:    handler = irq_handlers[irq].handler;
364:    data = irq_handlers[irq].data;
365:    spin_unlock(&irq_table_lock);
366:  }
367:
368:  if (handler) {
369:    handler(irq, data);
370:  } else {
371:    pr_warn("IRQ: Unhandled interrupt %u\n", irq);
372:  }
373:  return regs;
374:}
375:
376:/*
377: * irq_chip_end - single EOI mechanism for vectored dispatchers (IRQ-01 fix).
378: *
379: * Routes the end-of-interrupt through the registered chip: on amd64 the
380: * pic_chip->end() implementation owns the complete LAPIC + 8259 sequence,
381: * so idt.c no longer hand-rolls EOI writes behind the chip's back.
382: *
383: * Locking: none; chip->end() is a self-contained MMIO/port write sequence.
384: * IRQ context: YES.
385: */
386:void irq_chip_end(uint32_t irq) {
387:  if (current_chip && current_chip->end) {
388:    current_chip->end(irq);
389:  }
390:}
391:

@@@ kernel/lib/backtrace.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/lib/backtrace.c
3: * Frame-pointer backtrace + in-kernel symbol table lookup (Phase A steps 11-12).
4: *
5: * The walker relies on -fno-omit-frame-pointer (COMMON_FLAGS): every C frame
6: * chains [fp] = caller fp, [fp+8] = return address, identically on amd64
7: * (rbp) and aarch64 (x29).  Assembly boundaries (isr_stubs.S, exception.S,
8: * context.S, syscall.S) do not build frames, so the walk is seeded from the
9: * exception frame's pc/fp — never from the handler's own frame — and stops at
10: * the first frame that leaves the validated ranges.  -O2 tail-calls may merge
11: * a frame; an occasionally skipped entry is accepted.
12: *
13: * Symbolization uses the .ksyms blob generated by tools/gen_ksyms.sh from
14: * `nm -n` of the first-pass link and linked into .rodata on the second pass:
15: *
16: *     u64  count
17: *     u64  addrs[count]       (link addresses, ascending)
18: *     u32  name_offs[count]   (offsets into the names blob)
19: *     char names[]            (NUL-terminated, in table order)
20: *
21: * The section is ALLOC and placed in .rodata so it survives the aarch64
22: * `objcopy -O binary kernel.bin` — that is the only way the running aarch64
23: * image gets live symbolization.  Link address == runtime address on both
24: * arches (identity-mapped kernel), so lookup is a plain binary search.
25: * When the blob is absent (first-pass link), addresses print raw.
26: *
27: * Everything here is fault-context safe: fault_printf output only, every
28: * dereference is bounds-checked first, and a residual bad read is converted
29: * into a clean stop by the fault_enter() depth guard of the dispatcher.
30: */
31:#include <kernel/fault.h>
32:#include <kernel/printk.h>
33:#include <kernel/types.h>
34:
35:/* Linker-script symbols (both kernel.ld files) */
36:extern char __ksyms_start[];
37:extern char __ksyms_end[];
38:extern char __kernel_start[];
39:extern char _etext[];
40:extern char __kernel_end[];
41:
42:#define BACKTRACE_MAX_FRAMES 24
43:
44:/* Plausible-RAM ceiling for frame pointers: kernel stacks (boot stacks in
45: * .bss, per-task stacks from the PMM) all live above the kernel image; 8GB
46: * over __kernel_end covers every supported -m size while filtering wild fps. */
47:#define FP_RANGE_LIMIT (8ULL << 30)
48:
49:static int text_addr_valid(uint64_t pc) {
50:  return pc >= (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)__kernel_start &&
51:         pc < (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)_etext;
52:}
53:
54:static int fp_addr_valid(uint64_t fp) {
55:  if (fp == 0 || (fp & 7) != 0)
56:    return 0;
57:  if (fp + 15 < fp)
58:    return 0;
59:  if (fp < (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)__kernel_start)
60:    return 0;
61:  if (fp + 15 > (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)__kernel_end + FP_RANGE_LIMIT)
62:    return 0;
63:  return 1;
64:}
65:
66:const char *ksym_lookup(uint64_t addr, uint64_t *off) {
67:  const char *blob = __ksyms_start;
68:  uint64_t blob_size = (uint64_t)(__ksyms_end - __ksyms_start);
69:
70:  if (blob_size < 16)
71:    return NULL; /* no table linked (first-pass build) */
72:
73:  uint64_t count = *(const uint64_t *)blob;
74:  const uint64_t *addrs = (const uint64_t *)(blob + 8);
75:  const uint32_t *name_offs = (const uint32_t *)(blob + 8 + count * 8);
76:  const char *names = (const char *)(blob + 8 + count * 8 + count * 4);
77:
78:  /* Sanity: a corrupt header must not send us walking wild memory. */
79:  if (count == 0 || count > blob_size / 12 ||
80:      (const char *)names > __ksyms_end)
81:    return NULL;
82:  if (!text_addr_valid(addr))
83:    return NULL;
84:
85:  /* Binary search: greatest table address <= addr. */
86:  uint64_t lo = 0, hi = count;
87:  while (lo < hi) {
88:    uint64_t mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
89:    if (addrs[mid] <= addr)
90:      lo = mid + 1;
91:    else
92:      hi = mid;
93:  }
94:  if (lo == 0)
95:    return NULL;
96:  lo--;
97:
98:  uint32_t off_val = name_offs[lo];
99:  if ((uint64_t)off_val >= (uint64_t)(__ksyms_end - names))
100:    return NULL;
101:  const char *name = names + off_val;
102:  if (off)
103:    *off = addr - addrs[lo];
104:  return name;
105:}
106:
107:static void backtrace_emit(int idx, uint64_t pc) {
108:  uint64_t off = 0;
109:  const char *name = ksym_lookup(pc, &off);
110:  if (name)
111:    fault_printf("  #%-2d %016lx %s+0x%lx\n", idx, pc, name, off);
112:  else
113:    fault_printf("  #%-2d %016lx\n", idx, pc);
114:}
115:
116:/*
117: * backtrace_regs - walk and print the call chain starting at pc/fp.
118: *
119: * Seed from an exception frame (regs->rip/regs->rbp on amd64,
120: * frame->elr/frame->regs[29] on aarch64) or from the current context via
121: * backtrace_here().  Output goes through fault_printf — callable from any
122: * fault path.
123: */
124:void backtrace_regs(uint64_t pc, uint64_t fp) {
125:  fault_printf("Backtrace (fp chain, max %d):\n", BACKTRACE_MAX_FRAMES);
126:  backtrace_emit(0, pc);
127:
128:  for (int i = 1; i < BACKTRACE_MAX_FRAMES; i++) {
129:    if (!fp_addr_valid(fp))
130:      break;
131:    uint64_t next_fp = *(const uint64_t *)fp;
132:    uint64_t ret = *(const uint64_t *)(fp + 8);
133:    if (!text_addr_valid(ret))
134:      break;
135:    backtrace_emit(i, ret);
136:    if (next_fp <= fp) /* frames must strictly grow toward the stack base */
137:      break;
138:    fp = next_fp;
139:  }
140:}
141:
142:/*
143: * backtrace_scan - corruption-robust backtrace fallback.
144: *
145: * The fp-chain walker (backtrace_regs) is useless precisely when you need it
146: * most: a SMASHED kernel stack has a garbage rbp/x29, so the chain yields one
147: * or two bogus frames and stops (the "#GP on ret with only 2 frames" we keep
148: * seeing).  This instead walks the RAW stack from sp upward and prints every
149: * word that lands in kernel .text.  It includes false positives (stale return
150: * addresses, spilled function pointers), but it RECONSTRUCTS the real call path
151: * the fp walker drops — and, critically, shows the corrupted slots themselves
152: * (a non-canonical / 0xcc… word sitting where a return address belongs is the
153: * smoking gun for the stack-corruption class, #169/#170).
154: *
155: * Bounded: at most ~32 KB of stack and BT_SCAN_MAX hits.  fault_printf-based,
156: * so it is callable from any fault/panic path.
157: */
158:#define BT_SCAN_MAX 32
159:#define BT_RAW_QWORDS 24
160:void backtrace_scan(uint64_t sp) {
161:  if (!fp_addr_valid(sp))
162:    return;
163:  /* RAW window first: the smoking gun of the stack-corruption class (#169/#170)
164:   * is the actual VALUE at the corrupted slot — e.g. the non-canonical / 0xcc…
165:   * word a 'ret'/'iretq' just popped — which a text-only scan hides.  Dump the
166:   * first BT_RAW_QWORDS verbatim from sp, annotating any that resolve to .text.
167:   * sp is the faulting RSP (the CPU was using it), so this small window is
168:   * mapped; we stop at the first hole to avoid a recursive fault. */
169:  fault_printf("Stack raw @%016lx (low->high; +sym = return addr):\n", sp);
170:  uint64_t p = sp;
171:  for (int k = 0; k < BT_RAW_QWORDS; k++, p += 8) {
172:    if (!fp_addr_valid(p)) {
173:      fault_printf("  %016lx  <out-of-range>\n", p);
174:      break;
175:    }
176:    uint64_t v = *(const uint64_t *)p;
177:    uint64_t off = 0;
178:    const char *nm = text_addr_valid(v) ? ksym_lookup(v, &off) : NULL;
179:    if (nm)
180:      fault_printf("  %016lx: %016lx  %s+0x%lx\n", p, v, nm, off);
181:    else
182:      fault_printf("  %016lx: %016lx\n", p, v);
183:  }
184:  /* Then continue text-only up the stack to recover the call path the smashed
185:   * fp-chain dropped. */
186:  fault_printf("Call path (text words up the stack):\n");
187:  int shown = 0;
188:  uint64_t end = sp + 0x8000; /* up to 32 KB */
189:  for (; p < end && shown < BT_SCAN_MAX; p += 8) {
190:    if (!fp_addr_valid(p))
191:      break;
192:    uint64_t v = *(const uint64_t *)p;
193:    if (!text_addr_valid(v))
194:      continue;
195:    uint64_t off = 0;
196:    const char *name = ksym_lookup(v, &off);
197:    if (name)
198:      fault_printf("  @%016lx  %s+0x%lx\n", p, name, off);
199:    else
200:      fault_printf("  @%016lx  %016lx\n", p, v);
201:    shown++;
202:  }
203:}
204:
205:/*
206: * backtrace_here - backtrace of the current call site (e.g. from panic()).
207: */
208:void backtrace_here(void) {
209:  backtrace_regs((uint64_t)(uintptr_t)__builtin_return_address(0),
210:                 (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)__builtin_frame_address(0));
211:}
212:

@@@ kernel/lib/crc32.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/lib/crc32.c
3: * Standard CRC32 Implementation
4: *
5: * Purpose:
6: *   Provides crc32() — an ISO 3309 / ITU-T V.42 CRC-32 checksum function.
7: *   Used by the kernel for data-integrity checks (VirtIO descriptors, GPT
8: *   partition table header, and filesystem metadata).
9: *
10: * Role:
11: *   Called from kernel/fs/gpt.c and any VirtIO driver that validates checksums.
12: *   No callers outside the kernel; not exported to userland.
13: *
14: * Algorithm:
15: *   Sarwate bit-by-bit (no pre-computed table).  Each byte is XOR'd into the
16: *   CRC, then eight one-bit shifts are applied.  On each shift, if the output
17: *   bit is 1 the generator polynomial 0xEDB88320 (bit-reversed form of the
18: *   standard CRC-32 polynomial 0x04C11DB7) is XOR'd in.
19: *
20: *   The `-(crc & 1)` expression produces 0xFFFFFFFF when the low bit is 1
21: *   (all ones mask, so the XOR applies the polynomial) and 0x00000000 when
22: *   the low bit is 0 (no-op XOR).  This is a branchless conditional.
23: *
24: * Invariants:
25: *   - Init value: 0xFFFFFFFF (pre-condition).
26: *   - Final inversion: ~crc (post-condition).
27: *   - Polynomial: 0xEDB88320 (reflected CRC-32).
28: *   - Result is equivalent to standard CRC-32 table lookups.
29: *
30: * Known issues:
31: *   None tracked for this file (see docs/review/analysis/07-lib-headers.md).
32: *   The implementation is correct and produces standard CRC-32 values.
33: *   It is O(8*n) rather than O(n) (table-driven) but adequate for kernel use.
34: */
35:#include <kernel/string.h>
36:#include <kernel/types.h>
37:
38:/*
39: * crc32 - compute the ISO 3309 CRC-32 checksum of a byte buffer.
40: *
41: * Params:
42: *   data    - pointer to input data; must be non-NULL if n_bytes > 0.
43: *   n_bytes - number of bytes to process.
44: * Returns: 32-bit CRC-32 checksum.
45: * Locking: none (stateless).
46: * Side effects: none.
47: */
48:uint32_t crc32(const void *data, size_t n_bytes) {
49:  uint32_t crc = 0xFFFFFFFF;
50:  const uint8_t *p = (const uint8_t *)data;
51:  for (size_t i = 0; i < n_bytes; i++) {
52:    crc ^= p[i];
53:    for (int j = 0; j < 8; j++) {
54:      /* Branchless polynomial step: XOR in 0xEDB88320 iff the output bit is 1.
55:       * -(crc & 1) is 0xFFFFFFFF when low bit is 1, 0x00000000 otherwise. */
56:      crc = (crc >> 1) ^ (0xEDB88320 & -(crc & 1));
57:    }
58:  }
59:  return ~crc;
60:}
61:

@@@ kernel/lib/entropy.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/lib/entropy.c
3: * Unified best-effort entropy source.
4: *
5: * ASTRA (docs/ASTRA.md §1 rule 5: "the HAL is the seam, and divergence is a
6: * bug"): the policy here — prefer the hardware RNG, otherwise mix cycle-counter
7: * jitter — is written once and drives both architectures identically over two
8: * HAL primitives:
9: *   - arch_hw_random()      (ISA: RNDR on AArch64 FEAT_RNG, RDRAND on AMD64)
10: *   - arch_timer_get_count()(ISA: CNTVCT_EL0 / RDTSC, already a HAL contract)
11: * No arch is named below; the only per-arch code is the thin ISA wrapper
12: * arch_impl_hw_random in each kernel/arch/<arch>/include/arch/arch.h.
13: *
14: * Primary consumer: stack_guard_init() reseeds the SSP canary (LIB-SSP-01 / #71).
15: */
16:#include <kernel/arch.h>
17:#include <kernel/entropy.h>
18:#include <stdint.h>
19:
20:/* splitmix64 finalizer/step — a fast, well-distributed bit mixer. */
21:static inline uint64_t splitmix64(uint64_t *state) {
22:  uint64_t z = (*state += 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL);
23:  z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9ULL;
24:  z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94d049bb133111ebULL;
25:  return z ^ (z >> 31);
26:}
27:
28:uint64_t entropy_u64(void) {
29:  /* Prefer the hardware RNG; tolerate a bounded number of transient failures. */
30:  for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
31:    uint64_t hw;
32:    if (arch_hw_random(&hw))
33:      return hw;
34:  }
35:
36:  /* Fallback: fold several cycle-counter samples (boot-time scheduling jitter)
37:   * and a frame address through splitmix64. */
38:  uint64_t state = (uint64_t)__builtin_return_address(0);
39:  for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
40:    state ^= arch_timer_get_count();
41:    (void)splitmix64(&state);
42:  }
43:  return splitmix64(&state);
44:}

@@@ kernel/lib/fault_print.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/lib/fault_print.c
3: * Fault-safe emergency print + per-CPU fault recursion guard (Phase A).
4: *
5: * See kernel/fault.h for the contract.  This file deliberately avoids:
6: *   - spinlocks (uart_lock may be held by a wedged CPU),
7: *   - get_cpu_info() (on amd64 it reads LAPIC MMIO, which may be unmapped
8: *     when the faulting address space is compromised),
9: *   - heap or per-CPU buffers (a 256-byte stack buffer is enough and works
10: *     on the dedicated 16KB fault stacks).
11: *
12: * vsnprintf is stateless and lock-free (see printk.c), so formatting here is
13: * re-entrant by construction.
14: */
15:#include <drivers/uart.h>
16:#include <kernel/cpu.h>
17:#include <kernel/fault.h>
18:#include <kernel/printk.h>
19:#include <kernel/types.h>
20:#include <stdarg.h>
21:
22:/* Fallback depth counter for when arch_cpu_info_fault_safe() returns NULL
23: * (early boot, corrupted GS base).  Global — a false "nested" positive across
24: * two CPUs faulting simultaneously pre-init is acceptable: both halt cleanly. */
25:static volatile uint32_t fault_depth_fallback;
26:
27:/* DIR-05 / #139 — on-screen panic.  Tee every byte of fault output into a plain
28: * buffer so panic() can paint it on the framebuffer when no UART is attached
29: * (the only place a kernel fault is otherwise visible).  Lock-free single-writer
30: * by construction: fault output is serialised by the fault recursion guard +
31: * panic's IPI quiesce. */
32:#define FAULT_TEXT_CAP 8192
33:static char fault_text_buf[FAULT_TEXT_CAP];
34:static volatile uint32_t fault_text_used;
35:
36:static inline void fault_text_putc(char c) {
37:  uint32_t n = fault_text_used;
38:  if (n < FAULT_TEXT_CAP - 1) {
39:    fault_text_buf[n] = c;
40:    fault_text_buf[n + 1] = '\0';
41:    fault_text_used = n + 1;
42:  }
43:}
44:
45:/* The captured fault transcript (NUL-terminated), oldest first.  Returned to
46: * panic_screen(); the leading lines are the arch register dump + fault class,
47: * which is exactly what a maintainer reads off a screen with no serial. */
48:const char *fault_text(void) { return fault_text_buf; }
49:
50:void fault_vprintf(const char *fmt, va_list args) {
51:  char buf[256];
52:  vsnprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), fmt, args);
53:  for (const char *p = buf; *p; p++) {
54:    uart_putc_emergency(*p);
55:    fault_text_putc(*p);
56:  }
57:}
58:
59:void fault_printf(const char *fmt, ...) {
60:  va_list args;
61:  va_start(args, fmt);
62:  fault_vprintf(fmt, args);
63:  va_end(args);
64:}
65:
66:unsigned fault_enter(void) {
67:  struct cpu_info *ci = arch_cpu_info_fault_safe();
68:  if (ci)
69:    return ++ci->in_fault;
70:  return __sync_add_and_fetch(&fault_depth_fallback, 1);
71:}
72:
73:void fault_exit(void) {
74:  struct cpu_info *ci = arch_cpu_info_fault_safe();
75:  if (ci) {
76:    if (ci->in_fault)
77:      ci->in_fault--;
78:  } else {
79:    uint32_t prev = __sync_sub_and_fetch(&fault_depth_fallback, 1);
80:    if (prev == UINT32_MAX) __sync_add_and_fetch(&fault_depth_fallback, 1);
81:  }
82:}
83:
84:unsigned fault_depth(void) {
85:  struct cpu_info *ci = arch_cpu_info_fault_safe();
86:  return ci ? ci->in_fault : fault_depth_fallback;
87:}

@@@ kernel/lib/fdt.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/lib/fdt.c
3: * Flattened Device Tree (FDT / DTB) Parser
4: *
5: * Purpose:
6: *   Parses the Flattened Device Tree blob (DTB) provided by the firmware
7: *   (QEMU) at boot time to discover the system memory map and SMP CPU count.
8: *   All DTB fields are big-endian; this file performs the necessary byte-swap.
9: *
10: * Role:
11: *   On AArch64 this is on the critical boot path:
12: *     kernel_main (x0 = DTB address) → fdt_init() → fdt_get_mem_regions()
13: *                                                  → fdt_count_cpus()
14: *   Results feed directly into pmm_init() (memory regions) and SMP bringup
15: *   (CPU count).  On AMD64 all entry points return -1 / 0 unconditionally;
16: *   memory is discovered via multiboot2 instead.
17: *
18: * Implementation scope:
19: *   Minimal — implements only the two properties the kernel needs:
20: *   1. Memory regions: walks FDT_BEGIN_NODE / FDT_PROP to find `memory@*`
21: *      nodes and read their `reg` properties.
22: *   2. CPU count: counts `cpu@*` child nodes under the `cpus` node.
23: *   The memory reservation map, IRQ topology, `compatible` strings, and all
24: *   other DT properties are not parsed.
25: *
26: * Byte-order:
27: *   The DTB is big-endian on all architectures.  The kernel runs little-endian
28: *   on both amd64 and aarch64.  fdt32_to_cpu() swaps 32-bit DTB values.
29: *   fdt_read32() / fdt_read64() use volatile loads to prevent the compiler
30: *   from emitting an unaligned LDR and then swap.
31: *
32: * Known issues:
33: *   LIB-FDT-01  (W2 REFINE)   No bounds check of off_dt_struct or
34: *               size_dt_struct against totalsize before parsing.  A malformed
35: *               DTB can cause out-of-bounds pointer arithmetic.
36: *   LIB-FDT-02  (W1 MISSING)  Memory reservation map (off_mem_rsvmap) is
37: *               never parsed; firmware-reserved RAM may be overwritten by PMM.
38: *   LIB-FDT-03  (W1 STUB)     AMD64 fdt_init() and fdt_find_in_memory() are
39: *               explicit stubs; expected behaviour, guarded by #ifdef.
40: *   LIB-FDT-04  (W2 SECURITY) fdt_find_in_memory() validates only the magic
41: *               word; does not validate totalsize or structure offsets of the
42: *               candidate DTB.  A crafted RAM layout could produce a false
43: *               positive pointing into arbitrary memory.
44: *   LIB-FDT-05  (W0 DOC)      Stale comment near uart_puts call; printk is
45: *               fully available at the point fdt_init is called.
46: */
47:#include <kernel/fdt.h>
48:#include <kernel/memlayout.h>
49:#include <kernel/string.h>
50:#include <kernel/printk.h>
51:#include <kernel/pmm.h>
52:#include <drivers/uart.h>
53:
54:/* fdt_ptr: pointer to the validated DTB header in memory.
55: * NULL until fdt_init() succeeds.  Set once; never changed after init. */
56:static struct fdt_header *fdt_ptr = NULL;
57:/* boot_fdt_ptr: physical address of the DTB, exported for use by arch code.
58: * Set by fdt_init(); 0 if no DTB was found or on AMD64. */
59:uint64_t boot_fdt_ptr = 0;
60:
61:/*
62: * fdt32_to_cpu - byte-swap a big-endian 32-bit DTB value to host byte order.
63: *
64: * The DTB specification (ePAPR) requires all header and structure fields to be
65: * stored in big-endian byte order.  This kernel runs little-endian on both
66: * aarch64 and amd64, so every 32-bit DTB word must be swapped before use.
67: *
68: * Params: val - raw 32-bit word read from the DTB.
69: * Returns: val in host byte order.
70: */
71:static uint32_t fdt32_to_cpu(uint32_t val) {
72:    return ((val & 0xFF000000) >> 24) |
73:           ((val & 0x00FF0000) >> 8) |
74:           ((val & 0x0000FF00) << 8) |
75:           ((val & 0x000000FF) << 24);
76:}
77:
78:
79:
80:/*
81: * fdt_init - validate and register the Device Tree Blob.
82: *
83: * AArch64 variant (compiled when ARCH_AMD64 is not defined):
84: *   If fdt_addr is 0, attempts to locate the DTB by scanning RAM in the range
85: *   [0x40000000, 0x80000000) via fdt_find_in_memory().
86: *   Validates the FDT_MAGIC (0xd00dfeed) word.  On success, stores fdt_ptr and
87: *   boot_fdt_ptr for use by fdt_get_mem_regions() and fdt_count_cpus().
88: *
89: * NOTE(LIB-FDT-05): The uart_puts("... just manual print ...") comment at the
90: *   address-print site is stale — printk/snprintf are fully available at the
91: *   point this function runs.  The address is never printed.
92: * NOTE(LIB-FDT-01): totalsize and structure offsets are not validated before
93: *   subsequent parsing calls.  A malformed DTB could produce out-of-bounds
94: *   pointer arithmetic in fdt_get_mem_regions().
95: *
96: * AMD64 stub (compiled when ARCH_AMD64 is defined):
97: *   Returns -1 unconditionally.  Memory discovery uses multiboot2.
98: *   NOTE(LIB-FDT-03): This is an explicit, expected stub.
99: *
100: * Params: fdt_addr - physical address of the DTB, or 0 to trigger RAM scan.
101: * Returns: 0 on success; -1 if no valid DTB is found.
102: * Locking: none; called single-threaded during early boot.
103: * Side effects: sets module-static fdt_ptr and boot_fdt_ptr.
104: */
105:#ifndef ARCH_AMD64
106:int fdt_init(uintptr_t fdt_addr) {
107:    if (fdt_addr == 0) {
108:        uart_puts("FDT: No address provided, scanning RAM...\n");
109:        /* Scan up to 1GB of RAM */
110:        fdt_addr = fdt_find_in_memory(0x40000000, 0x80000000);
111:        if (fdt_addr == 0) {
112:            uart_puts("FDT: Scan failed, no DTB found.\n");
113:            return -1;
114:        }
115:        /* Simple hex to string for uart_puts */
116:        uart_puts("FDT: Found magic at 0x");
117:        // ... just manual print for now to avoid dependency on sprintf if not ready
118:        /* NOTE(LIB-FDT-05): above comment is stale; printk is available here. */
119:        uart_puts("... (scanning succeeded)\n");
120:    }
121:
122:    uart_puts("FDT: Probing... \n");
123:    /* fdt_addr is the DTB's PHYSICAL address (x0 from QEMU); parse it
124:     * through the direct map (identity while KERNEL_VIRT_BASE == 0).
125:     * boot_fdt_ptr keeps exporting the physical address. */
126:    struct fdt_header *hdr = (struct fdt_header *)phys_to_virt(fdt_addr);
127:    uint32_t magic = fdt32_to_cpu(hdr->magic);
128:    if (magic != FDT_MAGIC) {
129:        uart_puts("FDT: Invalid magic!\n");
130:        return -1;
131:    }
132:    fdt_ptr = hdr;
133:    boot_fdt_ptr = fdt_addr;
134:    uart_puts("FDT: Successfully initialized\n");
135:    return 0;
136:}
137:#else
138:/* NOTE(LIB-FDT-03): AMD64 stub — DTB not used on AMD64. */
139:int fdt_init(uintptr_t fdt_addr) {
140:    (void)fdt_addr;
141:    return -1;
142:}
143:#endif
144:
145:/*
146: * fdt_find_in_memory - scan a RAM range for a DTB magic signature.
147: *
148: * AArch64 variant:
149: *   Walks aligned 8-byte boundaries from 'start' to 'end', comparing the
150: *   first 4 bytes of each candidate to the little-endian representation of
151: *   the big-endian magic 0xd00dfeed, which is 0xedfe0dd0 in raw memory on a
152: *   little-endian machine.
153: *   Emits a '.' progress dot to UART every 16 MB (addr & 0xFFFFFF == 0).
154: *
155: * NOTE(LIB-FDT-04): Only the magic word is checked.  If a false positive is
156: *   found (a non-DTB region that happens to start with 0xedfe0dd0), subsequent
157: *   calls to fdt_get_mem_regions() will dereference arbitrary memory.  The
158: *   totalsize and structure offsets of the candidate are NOT validated here.
159: *
160: * AMD64 stub: returns 0 unconditionally.
161: * NOTE(LIB-FDT-03): expected stub on AMD64.
162: *
163: * Params:
164: *   start - physical address to begin scanning (inclusive).
165: *   end   - physical address to stop scanning (exclusive).
166: * Returns: physical address of the first candidate DTB, or 0 if not found.
167: * Locking: none; called from fdt_init() during single-threaded early boot.
168: */
169:#ifndef ARCH_AMD64
170:uintptr_t fdt_find_in_memory(uintptr_t start, uintptr_t end) {
171:    /* Scan at 8-byte aligned boundaries */
172:    for (uintptr_t addr = start; addr < end; addr += 8) {
173:        if ((addr & 0xFFFFFF) == 0) {
174:            uart_puts("."); /* Progress indicator */
175:        }
176:        /* 'addr' iterates PHYSICAL addresses; deref via the direct map. */
177:        struct fdt_header *hdr = (struct fdt_header *)phys_to_virt(addr);
178:        /* Check magic without conversion first for speed.
179:         * 0xedfe0dd0 is the big-endian value 0xd00dfeed (FDT_MAGIC) stored in
180:         * little-endian byte order as it appears in raw memory. */
181:        if (hdr->magic == 0xedfe0dd0) { /* BE 0xd00dfeed on LE machine */
182:            uart_puts("\nFDT: Found candidate at 0x");
183:            /* NOTE(LIB-FDT-04): totalsize/structure offsets not validated here. */
184:            /* Success! */
185:            return addr;
186:        }
187:    }
188:    uart_puts("\n");
189:    return 0;
190:}
191:#else
192:/* NOTE(LIB-FDT-03): AMD64 stub — no DTB on AMD64. */
193:uintptr_t fdt_find_in_memory(uintptr_t start, uintptr_t end) {
194:    (void)start; (void)end;
195:    return 0;
196:}
197:#endif
198:
199:/*
200: * fdt_get_string - look up a string in the DTB strings block by offset.
201: *
202: * DTB property names are stored in a separate strings block whose base is
203: * given by fdt_ptr->off_dt_strings (big-endian).  FDT_PROP tags carry an
204: * offset into this block to identify the property name.
205: *
206: * NOTE(LIB-FDT-01): no bounds check against size_dt_strings; an out-of-range
207: *   offset produces a pointer outside the DTB.
208: *
209: * Params: offset - byte offset into the strings block.
210: * Returns: pointer to the NUL-terminated property name string.
211: */
212:static const char *fdt_get_string(uint32_t offset) {
213:    return (const char *)((uintptr_t)fdt_ptr + fdt32_to_cpu(fdt_ptr->off_dt_strings) + offset);
214:}
215:
216:/*
217: * fdt_read32 - read a big-endian 32-bit value from a potentially misaligned
218: *              DTB location, returning it in host byte order.
219: *
220: * Uses a volatile pointer to suppress compiler optimisation that might emit a
221: * wider or differently-aligned load instruction.
222: *
223: * Params: p - pointer to a 32-bit big-endian word in the DTB structure block.
224: * Returns: the value in host (little-endian) byte order.
225: */
226:static uint32_t fdt_read32(uint32_t *p) {
227:    /* Force 32-bit load to avoid alignment issues if compiler tries to optimize */
228:    return fdt32_to_cpu(*(volatile uint32_t *)p);
229:}
230:
231:/*
232: * fdt_read64 - read a big-endian 64-bit value from the DTB as two 32-bit loads.
233: *
234: * AArch64 and AMD64 may generate a single 8-byte LDR for a 64-bit read, which
235: * would be unaligned if the DTB structure is not 8-byte aligned.  Two separate
236: * 32-bit volatile loads are always aligned to 4 bytes and avoid the hazard.
237: * The DTB stores 64-bit values as (high32, low32) in big-endian order.
238: *
239: * Params: p - pointer to the first (high) 32-bit word of the 64-bit DTB value.
240: * Returns: the assembled 64-bit value in host byte order.
241: */
242:static uint64_t fdt_read64(uint32_t *p) {
243:    /* Force two 32-bit loads to avoid unaligned 64-bit load (LDR Xn) */
244:    volatile uint32_t *vp = (volatile uint32_t *)p;
245:    uint64_t high = fdt32_to_cpu(vp[0]);
246:    uint64_t low = fdt32_to_cpu(vp[1]);
247:    return (high << 32) | low;
248:}
249:
250:/*
251: * fdt_get_mem_regions - extract usable RAM regions from the DTB.
252: *
253: * Walks the DTB structure block, identifying `memory@*` (or `memory`) nodes
254: * and reading their `reg` properties to discover physical memory regions.
255: * Also reads `#address-cells` and `#size-cells` from the root node (depth 1)
256: * to determine whether base/size values are 32-bit or 64-bit.
257: *
258: * Walk algorithm:
259: *   - FDT_BEGIN_NODE: enter a node; track depth.  If the node name starts with
260: *     "memory@" or equals "memory", set in_memory_node = current depth.
261: *   - FDT_END_NODE: if leaving the memory node, clear in_memory_node; decrement
262: *     depth.
263: *   - FDT_PROP at depth 1: read #address-cells and #size-cells.
264: *   - FDT_PROP in memory node with name "reg": decode base/size pairs.
265: *     Each pair is (addr_cells × 4) + (size_cells × 4) bytes.
266: *   - FDT_NOP: skip (continue).
267: *   - FDT_END: stop.
268: *
269: * NOTE(LIB-FDT-01): `p` and `end` are computed from off_dt_struct and
270: *   size_dt_struct without validating that those offsets fit within totalsize.
271: *   A malformed DTB can produce `end` outside the DTB allocation.
272: * NOTE(LIB-FDT-02): The memory reservation map (off_mem_rsvmap) is not parsed.
273: *   Firmware-reserved RAM ranges are not communicated to the PMM.
274: *
275: * Params:
276: *   regions   - output array of struct mem_region to fill.
277: *   max_count - capacity of the regions array.
278: *   count     - output; receives the number of regions written (may be NULL).
279: * Returns: 0 on success; -1 if fdt_ptr is NULL (fdt_init not called or failed).
280: * Locking: none; assumes fdt_ptr is stable (set once at boot, read-only after).
281: */
282:int fdt_get_mem_regions(struct mem_region *regions, size_t max_count, size_t *count) {
283:    if (!fdt_ptr) return -1;
284:
285:    /* NOTE(LIB-FDT-01): off_dt_struct / size_dt_struct not validated against totalsize. */
286:    uint32_t *p = (uint32_t *)((uintptr_t)fdt_ptr + fdt32_to_cpu(fdt_ptr->off_dt_struct));
287:    uint32_t *end = (uint32_t *)((uintptr_t)p + fdt32_to_cpu(fdt_ptr->size_dt_struct));
288:
289:    int depth = 0;
290:    int in_memory_node = 0;   /* non-zero = depth at which the memory node began */
291:    size_t found_count = 0;
292:
293:    /* Defaults from ePAPR; overridden by root-node properties at depth == 1 */
294:    uint32_t addr_cells = 2;  /* #address-cells: number of 32-bit words per address */
295:    uint32_t size_cells = 2;  /* #size-cells:    number of 32-bit words per size */
296:
297:    while (p < end && found_count < max_count) {
298:        uint32_t tag = fdt32_to_cpu(*p++);
299:
300:        if (tag == FDT_BEGIN_NODE) {
301:            /* Node name follows the tag as a NUL-terminated string, padded to 4-byte
302:             * boundary.  Advance p past the name. */
303:            const char *name = (const char *)p;
304:            size_t name_len = strlen(name);
305:            p += (name_len + 1 + 3) / 4;
306:
307:            depth++;
308:            /* Detect memory nodes by name prefix or exact match */
309:            if (strncmp(name, "memory@", 7) == 0 || strcmp(name, "memory") == 0) {
310:                in_memory_node = depth;
311:            }
312:        } else if (tag == FDT_END_NODE) {
313:            if (in_memory_node == depth) in_memory_node = 0; /* leaving memory node */
314:            depth--;
315:        } else if (tag == FDT_PROP) {
316:            /* FDT_PROP layout: [len:u32][name_off:u32][data:len bytes, padded to 4] */
317:            uint32_t len = fdt32_to_cpu(*p++);
318:            uint32_t name_off = fdt32_to_cpu(*p++);
319:            const char *name = fdt_get_string(name_off);
320:
321:            /* Root node properties (depth == 1) set the address/size cell widths */
322:            if (depth == 1) {
323:                if (strcmp(name, "#address-cells") == 0) addr_cells = fdt32_to_cpu(*p);
324:                if (strcmp(name, "#size-cells") == 0) size_cells = fdt32_to_cpu(*p);
325:            }
326:
327:            if (in_memory_node && strcmp(name, "reg") == 0) {
328:                /* Parse RAM regions from the `reg` property.
329:                 * Each entry is (addr_cells + size_cells) × 4 bytes.
330:                 * Count of entries: len / ((addr_cells + size_cells) * 4). */
331:                uint32_t *reg_p = p;
332:                for (uint32_t i = 0; i < len / ((addr_cells + size_cells) * 4); i++) {
333:                    uint64_t base, size;
334:                    /* Read base address: 32-bit or 64-bit per addr_cells */
335:                    if (addr_cells == 2) {
336:                        base = fdt_read64(reg_p);
337:                        reg_p += 2;
338:                    } else {
339:                        base = fdt_read32(reg_p++);
340:                    }
341:
342:                    /* Read region size: 32-bit or 64-bit per size_cells */
343:                    if (size_cells == 2) {
344:                        size = fdt_read64(reg_p);
345:                        reg_p += 2;
346:                    } else {
347:                        size = fdt_read32(reg_p++);
348:                    }
349:
350:                    if (found_count < max_count) {
351:                        regions[found_count].base = base;
352:                        regions[found_count].size = size;
353:                        /* NOTE(LIB-FDT-02): all regions marked usable; firmware-
354:                         * reserved ranges from off_mem_rsvmap are not considered. */
355:                        regions[found_count].type = MEM_REGION_USABLE;
356:                        found_count++;
357:                    }
358:                }
359:            }
360:            /* Advance past property data (rounded up to 4-byte boundary) */
361:            p += (len + 3) / 4;
362:        } else if (tag == FDT_NOP) {
363:            continue;
364:        } else if (tag == FDT_END) {
365:            break;
366:        }
367:    }
368:
369:    if (count) *count = found_count;
370:    return 0;
371:}
372:
373:/*
374: * fdt_count_cpus - count CPU entries in the DTB `cpus` node.
375: *
376: * Walks the DTB structure block looking for the `cpus` node, then counts
377: * direct child nodes whose name starts with "cpu@" or equals "cpu".  The
378: * result is used during SMP bringup to determine how many secondary CPUs
379: * to start.
380: *
381: * Walk algorithm mirrors fdt_get_mem_regions():
382: *   - Track depth; note depth at which `cpus` node begins (in_cpus_node).
383: *   - Any direct child (depth == in_cpus_node + 1, i.e., depth - 1 == in_cpus_node)
384: *     whose name matches "cpu@*" or "cpu" is counted as a CPU.
385: *   - FDT_PROP entries are skipped entirely (only node structure matters here).
386: *
387: * NOTE(LIB-FDT-01): same as fdt_get_mem_regions — off_dt_struct/size_dt_struct
388: *   are used without validating against totalsize.
389: *
390: * Params: none.
391: * Returns: number of `cpu@*` / `cpu` nodes found; 0 if fdt_ptr is NULL.
392: * Locking: none; fdt_ptr is read-only after fdt_init().
393: */
394:uint32_t fdt_count_cpus(void) {
395:    if (!fdt_ptr) return 0;
396:
397:    /* NOTE(LIB-FDT-01): structure block bounds not validated against totalsize. */
398:    uint32_t *p = (uint32_t *)((uintptr_t)fdt_ptr + fdt32_to_cpu(fdt_ptr->off_dt_struct));
399:    uint32_t *end = (uint32_t *)((uintptr_t)p + fdt32_to_cpu(fdt_ptr->size_dt_struct));
400:
401:    int depth = 0;
402:    int in_cpus_node = 0;   /* depth at which the `cpus` node began; 0 = not inside */
403:    uint32_t cpu_count = 0;
404:
405:    while (p < end) {
406:        uint32_t tag = fdt32_to_cpu(*p++);
407:
408:        if (tag == FDT_BEGIN_NODE) {
409:            const char *name = (const char *)p;
410:            size_t name_len = strlen(name);
411:            p += (name_len + 1 + 3) / 4;
412:
413:            depth++;
414:            if (strcmp(name, "cpus") == 0) {
415:                in_cpus_node = depth;  /* entered the `cpus` container node */
416:            } else if (in_cpus_node == depth - 1 && (strncmp(name, "cpu@", 4) == 0 || strcmp(name, "cpu") == 0)) {
417:                /* Direct child of `cpus` with a matching name = one CPU */
418:                cpu_count++;
419:            }
420:        } else if (tag == FDT_END_NODE) {
421:            if (in_cpus_node == depth) in_cpus_node = 0; /* left the cpus node */
422:            depth--;
423:        } else if (tag == FDT_PROP) {
424:            uint32_t len = fdt32_to_cpu(*p++);
425:            p++; /* skip name_off — property names not needed for CPU counting */
426:            p += (len + 3) / 4;
427:        } else if (tag == FDT_NOP) {
428:            continue;
429:        } else if (tag == FDT_END) {
430:            break;
431:        }
432:    }
433:
434:    return cpu_count;
435:}
436:

@@@ kernel/lib/kmalloc.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/lib/kmalloc.c
3: * Kernel Heap Allocator (Bucket/Slab-like)
4: *
5: * Uses power-of-two free lists for small allocations (16B to 4KB).
6: * Uses page allocator for large allocations.
7: *
8: * Architecture:
9: *   Small allocations (user-size + header <= 4096 bytes) are served from a
10: *   GROWABLE bump-pointer pool built from 4 MB PMM chunks (FIX MM-KM-01).
11: *   The active chunk is delimited by heap_ptr..heap_end; when it is
12: *   exhausted and the bucket free list is empty, kmalloc() allocates a new
13: *   chunk from the PMM and continues there (at most one bucket slot, < 4 KB,
14: *   is abandoned at each chunk tail).  Nine power-of-two buckets (16, 32,
15: *   64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096 bytes) each maintain a LIFO free
16: *   list of returned blocks.  A freed small block goes onto the head of its
17: *   bucket's list and is reused by the next same-size request; chunks are
18: *   never returned to the PMM (they become the warm pool of the kernel).
19: *
20: *   Large allocations (user-size + header > 4096 bytes) are served directly
21: *   from pmm_alloc_pages(); freed large blocks are returned to the PMM.
22: *
23: *   Every allocation is preceded by a 32-byte struct block_header
24: *   (sizeof = 20 bytes, but __attribute__((aligned(16))) pads to 32 bytes).
25: *
26: * Known issues:
27: *   MM-KM-01  RESOLVED (Phase B2): the pool grows by 4 MB PMM chunks on
28: *             exhaustion; small allocations no longer fail permanently.
29: *             Small-bucket memory still never returns to the PMM (that
30: *             requires per-chunk accounting + coalescing — see MM-KM-02).
31: *   MM-KM-02  (W2 WRONG-DESIGN) No cross-bucket reuse: a freed 512B block
32: *             cannot satisfy a 256B request; structural fragmentation is baked
33: *             into the design.
34: *   MM-KM-03  (W2 BUG) Large allocations return page_start + 32 (not
35: *             page-aligned) -- a footgun for callers expecting page alignment.
36: *   MM-KM-04  (W2 REFINE) krealloc() always alloc+copy+free, even when the
37: *             new size fits in the same bucket.
38: *   MM-KM-05  (W1 PERF) The 32-byte header on a 16-byte minimum bucket means
39: *             kmalloc(1) consumes a 64-byte bucket slot (header 32 + user 1
40: *             rounds up to next bucket: 64B bucket, not 32B).
41: *   MM-KM-06  (W2 PERF) Single global spinlock for all allocations; no per-CPU
42: *             magazines; heavy SMP contention expected at scale.
43: */
44:#include <kernel/kmalloc.h>
45:#include <kernel/pmm.h>
46:#include <kernel/printk.h>
47:#include <kernel/spinlock.h>
48:#include <kernel/string.h>
49:#include <kernel/types.h>
50:
51:/* KMALLOC_CHUNK_SIZE: granule of pool growth (FIX MM-KM-01).  The initial
52: * pool and every later expansion are one contiguous PMM chunk of this size. */
53:#define KMALLOC_CHUNK_SIZE (4 * 1024 * 1024)
54:#define MIN_BUCKET_SIZE 16
55:#define MAX_BUCKET_SIZE 4096
56:#define NUM_BUCKETS 9 /* 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096 */
57:
58:/* BLOCK_MAGIC: sentinel written to block_header.magic for allocated blocks.
59: * kfree() validates this before accepting a pointer.
60: * NOTE(MM-KM-06): The magic check is done under kmalloc_lock to prevent an
61: * SMP double-free race (two CPUs both reading BLOCK_MAGIC and both proceeding). */
62:#define BLOCK_MAGIC 0xDEADBEEF
63:/* BLOCK_FREE: magic value written when a block is on a bucket free list.
64: * Helps catch use-after-free dereferences that read the header region. */
65:#define BLOCK_FREE 0xDEADDEAD
66:
67:/* Block header */
68:/*
69: * struct block_header - per-allocation metadata stored immediately before the
70: *                        user-visible data pointer.
71: *
72: * size:       user-requested size (bytes), not the bucket slot size.
73: * next:       free-list pointer; valid only when magic == BLOCK_FREE.
74: * bucket_idx: index 0..NUM_BUCKETS-1 for small allocations; 0xFFFFFFFF for
75: *             large allocations (served via pmm_alloc_pages).
76: *
77: * NOTE(MM-KM-05): __attribute__((aligned(16))) makes sizeof(block_header)==32,
78: * not 20.  A kmalloc(1) call needs total_req = 1 + 32 = 33 bytes, which falls
79: * in the 64-byte bucket (idx 2), wasting 31 bytes of user payload capacity.
80: *
81: * NOTE(MM-KM-03): For large allocations, (struct block_header *)ptr + 1
82: * evaluates to ptr + 32, which is NOT page-aligned even though ptr came from
83: * pmm_alloc_pages().  Callers that need a page-aligned large allocation will
84: * receive a misaligned pointer.
85: */
86:struct block_header {
87:  uint32_t magic;
88:  uint32_t size;             /* User size */
89:  struct block_header *next; /* In free list */
90:  uint32_t bucket_idx;       /* 0..NUM_BUCKETS-1, or -1 if large */
91:} __attribute__((aligned(16)));
92:
93:/* Global heap state */
94:/* We allocate heap pages from PMM for small objects.
95: * Large objects go directly to PMM.
96: */
97:/* heap_ptr/heap_end: delimit the ACTIVE bump chunk; heap_ptr advances on
98: * every small allocation carved from it.  When exhausted, kmalloc() installs
99: * a fresh KMALLOC_CHUNK_SIZE chunk here (FIX MM-KM-01); old chunks survive
100: * through the blocks already carved from them (headers are self-describing).
101: * heap_total: cumulative pool size across all chunks (statistics/log). */
102:static uint8_t *heap_ptr = NULL;
103:static uint8_t *heap_end = NULL;
104:static size_t heap_total = 0;
105:
106:/* buckets[i]: head of the LIFO free list for bucket index i.
107: * NOTE(MM-KM-02): Blocks freed to bucket[i] can only satisfy future requests
108: * that map to the same bucket index; no cross-bucket reuse occurs. */
109:static struct block_header *buckets[NUM_BUCKETS];
110:static int heap_initialized = 0;
111:/* kmalloc_lock: global spinlock protecting heap_ptr, buckets[], and the magic
112: * field of every block_header for small allocations.
113: * NOTE(MM-KM-06): A single lock serialises all allocators on all CPUs. */
114:static DEFINE_SPINLOCK(kmalloc_lock);
115:
116:/* --- Instrumentation (perf brief §1/§2.2; surfaced via OS1_sys_stats).
117: * Tracks live user bytes, live allocation count, and the high-water mark of
118: * bytes_in_use (never reclaimed today — chunks stay; see MM-KM-01).  Relaxed
119: * atomics so they are correct regardless of whether kmalloc_lock is held (the
120: * large path drops it across the PMM call).  high_water uses a benign racy
121: * compare. */
122:static uint64_t stat_bytes_in_use;
123:static uint64_t stat_high_water;
124:static uint64_t stat_live_allocs;
125:
126:static inline void km_stat_alloc(size_t size) {
127:  uint64_t n = __sync_add_and_fetch(&stat_bytes_in_use, size);
128:  __sync_fetch_and_add(&stat_live_allocs, 1);
129:  if (n > stat_high_water)
130:    stat_high_water = n;
131:}
132:
133:static inline void km_stat_free(size_t size) {
134:  __sync_fetch_and_sub(&stat_bytes_in_use, size);
135:  __sync_fetch_and_sub(&stat_live_allocs, 1);
136:}
137:
138:/* Convert size to bucket index. Returns -1 if too large. */
139:/*
140: * get_bucket_index - map a total allocation size (user + header) to a bucket.
141: *
142: * Returns 0..NUM_BUCKETS-1 for sizes that fit in a small bucket, or -1 for
143: * sizes > 4096 bytes (large path).
144: *
145: * The caller passes (user_size + sizeof(struct block_header)) as 'size', so
146: * the bucket chosen is the smallest power-of-two slot that holds both the
147: * header and user payload.
148: *
149: * NOTE(MM-KM-05): Because sizeof(struct block_header)==32, a user request of
150: * 1 byte requires total_req=33, which lands in the 64-byte bucket (not 32).
151: */
152:static int get_bucket_index(size_t size) {
153:  if (size <= 16)
154:    return 0;
155:  if (size <= 32)
156:    return 1;
157:  if (size <= 64)
158:    return 2;
159:  if (size <= 128)
160:    return 3;
161:  if (size <= 256)
162:    return 4;
163:  if (size <= 512)
164:    return 5;
165:  if (size <= 1024)
166:    return 6;
167:  if (size <= 2048)
168:    return 7;
169:  if (size <= 4096)
170:    return 8;
171:  return -1;
172:}
173:
174:/* get_bucket_size - return the total slot size (header + payload) for bucket idx.
175: * Bucket 0 = 16 bytes, bucket 1 = 32 bytes, ..., bucket 8 = 4096 bytes. */
176:static size_t get_bucket_size(int idx) { return 16 << idx; }
177:
178:/*
179: * Initialize kernel heap
180: *
181: * kmalloc_init - allocate the first small-object heap chunk from the PMM.
182: *
183: * Calls pmm_alloc_pages() to obtain KMALLOC_CHUNK_SIZE/PAGE_SIZE contiguous
184: * pages.  Sets heap_ptr, heap_end, and clears all bucket free-list heads.
185: * Sets heap_initialized = 1 to skip re-init on subsequent calls.
186: *
187: * Later exhaustion is handled inside kmalloc() by installing additional
188: * chunks (FIX MM-KM-01); this function only seeds the first one.
189: *
190: * Locking: acquires kmalloc_lock with IRQ save/restore; safe to call before
191: *          SMP is active or after (idempotent via heap_initialized guard).
192: */
193:void kmalloc_init(void) {
194:  uint64_t flags;
195:  uint32_t pages;
196:  uint8_t *chunk;
197:
198:  spin_lock_irqsave(&kmalloc_lock, &flags);
199:
200:  if (heap_initialized) {
201:    goto out;
202:  }
203:
204:  /* Allocate the first chunk for small allocations */
205:  pages = (KMALLOC_CHUNK_SIZE + 4095) / 4096;
206:  chunk = (uint8_t *)pmm_alloc_pages(pages);
207:
208:  if (!chunk) {
209:    pr_err("%s", "kmalloc: Failed to allocate heap\n");
210:    goto out;
211:  }
212:
213:  heap_ptr = chunk;
214:  heap_end = chunk + KMALLOC_CHUNK_SIZE;
215:  heap_total = KMALLOC_CHUNK_SIZE;
216:
217:  for (int i = 0; i < NUM_BUCKETS; i++) {
218:    buckets[i] = NULL;
219:  }
220:
221:  heap_initialized = 1;
222:
223:  pr_info("kmalloc: Initialized bucket allocator. Chunk: %u MB at %p (growable)\n",
224:          KMALLOC_CHUNK_SIZE / (1024 * 1024), chunk);
225:
226:out:
227:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&kmalloc_lock, flags);
228:}
229:
230:/*
231: * Allocate memory
232: *
233: * kmalloc - allocate 'size' bytes of kernel memory.
234: *
235: * Small path (total_req = size + sizeof(block_header) <= 4096):
236: *   1. Compute bucket index and slot size.
237: *   2. Under kmalloc_lock: pop the bucket free list if non-empty (reuse).
238: *   3. Otherwise: advance heap_ptr by slot size within the active chunk.
239: *   4. If the chunk is exhausted (FIX MM-KM-01): drop the lock, allocate a
240: *      fresh KMALLOC_CHUNK_SIZE chunk from the PMM, re-acquire and re-check
241: *      (another CPU may have grown or freed meanwhile — then donate our
242: *      chunk back), install it as the active chunk, and retry.  Allocation
243: *      fails only when the PMM itself is exhausted.
244: *   5. Initialise block_header (magic=BLOCK_MAGIC, size, bucket_idx).
245: *   6. Return pointer to byte immediately after the header (user payload).
246: *
247: * Large path (total_req > 4096):
248: *   Releases kmalloc_lock before calling pmm_alloc_pages() to avoid holding
249: *   the spinlock across PMM (which takes its own zone lock).
250: *   NOTE(MM-KM-03): Returns (block_header *)ptr + 1 = ptr + 32, which is
251: *   not page-aligned.  Callers expecting page alignment will be misled.
252: *
253: * NOTE(MM-KM-06): kmalloc_lock is a global spinlock; all CPUs serialise here.
254: *
255: * Returns: pointer to user payload, or NULL on size 0, overflow, or PMM
256: *          exhaustion.
257: */
258:void *kmalloc(size_t size) {
259:  void *res = NULL;
260:  uint64_t flags = 0;
261:  int idx;
262:  size_t total_req;
263:
264:  if (!heap_initialized)
265:    kmalloc_init();
266:
267:  if (size == 0)
268:    return NULL;
269:
270:  if (size > (size_t)(-1) - sizeof(struct block_header))
271:    return NULL;
272:
273:  /* Add header overhead */
274:  total_req = size + sizeof(struct block_header);
275:
276:  /* Determine bucket */
277:  idx = get_bucket_index(total_req);
278:
279:  spin_lock_irqsave(&kmalloc_lock, &flags);
280:
281:  if (idx >= 0) {
282:    /* Small allocation from bucket */
283:    size_t bucket_sz = get_bucket_size(idx);
284:
285:    for (;;) {
286:      /* Check free list for this bucket */
287:      if (buckets[idx]) {
288:        struct block_header *blk = buckets[idx];
289:        buckets[idx] = blk->next;
290:        blk->magic = BLOCK_MAGIC;
291:        blk->size = size;
292:        blk->next = NULL;
293:        blk->bucket_idx = idx;
294:
295:        res = (void *)(blk + 1);
296:        goto out;
297:      }
298:
299:      /* No free block, carve from the active chunk */
300:      if (heap_ptr + bucket_sz <= heap_end) {
301:        struct block_header *blk = (struct block_header *)heap_ptr;
302:        heap_ptr += bucket_sz;
303:
304:        blk->magic = BLOCK_MAGIC;
305:        blk->size = size;
306:        blk->next = NULL;
307:        blk->bucket_idx = idx;
308:
309:        res = (void *)(blk + 1);
310:        goto out;
311:      }
312:
313:      /* Active chunk exhausted: grow the pool (FIX MM-KM-01).  The lock is
314:       * dropped across the PMM call (consistent with the large path); after
315:       * re-acquiring, re-check — another CPU may have grown the pool or
316:       * freed a block while we were unlocked. */
317:      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&kmalloc_lock, flags);
318:      uint8_t *chunk = (uint8_t *)pmm_alloc_pages(KMALLOC_CHUNK_SIZE / 4096);
319:      spin_lock_irqsave(&kmalloc_lock, &flags);
320:
321:      if (!chunk) {
322:        if (buckets[idx] || heap_ptr + bucket_sz <= heap_end)
323:          continue; /* progress happened while unlocked; retry without chunk */
324:        pr_err("kmalloc: PMM exhausted growing heap (request %lu)\n", size);
325:        res = NULL;
326:        goto out;
327:      }
328:
329:      if (heap_ptr + bucket_sz <= heap_end) {
330:        /* Lost the grow race: the pool already has room again.  Donate our
331:         * chunk back instead of abandoning the active chunk's free tail. */
332:        spin_unlock_irqrestore(&kmalloc_lock, flags);
333:        pmm_free_pages(chunk, KMALLOC_CHUNK_SIZE / 4096);
334:        spin_lock_irqsave(&kmalloc_lock, &flags);
335:        continue;
336:      }
337:
338:      /* Install the fresh chunk as the active bump area (the old chunk's
339:       * tail, < one bucket slot, is abandoned). */
340:      heap_ptr = chunk;
341:      heap_end = chunk + KMALLOC_CHUNK_SIZE;
342:      heap_total += KMALLOC_CHUNK_SIZE;
343:      pr_info("kmalloc: heap grown to %lu MB (new chunk at %p)\n",
344:              heap_total / (1024 * 1024), chunk);
345:    }
346:
347:  } else {
348:    /* Large allocation: via PMM directly */
349:    /* Unlock before calling PMM to avoid nesting */
350:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&kmalloc_lock, flags);
351:    flags = 0; // Prevent double unlock
352:
353:    size_t pages = (total_req + 4095) / 4096;
354:    void *ptr = pmm_alloc_pages(pages);
355:    if (!ptr)
356:      return NULL;
357:
358:    struct block_header *blk = (struct block_header *)ptr;
359:    blk->magic = BLOCK_MAGIC;
360:    blk->size = size;
361:    blk->next = NULL;
362:    blk->bucket_idx = 0xFFFFFFFF; // Mark as large
363:
364:    km_stat_alloc(size); /* perf brief §1: account live bytes (large path) */
365:    return (void *)(blk + 1);
366:  }
367:
368:out:
369:  if (flags) {
370:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&kmalloc_lock, flags);
371:  }
372:  if (res)
373:    km_stat_alloc(size); /* perf brief §1: account live bytes (small path) */
374:  return res;
375:}
376:
377:/*
378: * Allocate zeroed memory
379: *
380: * kcalloc - allocate nmemb*size bytes, zeroed.
381: *
382: * Overflow-safe: returns NULL if nmemb * size would overflow size_t.
383: * Delegates to kmalloc() and zeros the result with memset().
384: */
385:void *kcalloc(size_t nmemb, size_t size) {
386:  if (nmemb && size > (size_t)(-1) / nmemb)
387:    return NULL;
388:  size_t total = nmemb * size;
389:  void *ptr = kmalloc(total);
390:  if (ptr) {
391:    memset(ptr, 0, total);
392:  }
393:  return ptr;
394:}
395:
396:/*
397: * Free memory
398: *
399: * kfree - return a kmalloc'd allocation.
400: *
401: * Acquires kmalloc_lock BEFORE reading block_header.magic.  This prevents an
402: * SMP double-free race where two CPUs each see magic==BLOCK_MAGIC and both
403: * proceed to "free" the block.  The deliberate, correct ordering is:
404: *   lock -> read magic -> validate -> mutate magic -> act.
405: *
406: * Large allocations (bucket_idx == 0xFFFFFFFF): zero the magic, release the
407: * lock, then call pmm_free_pages().  The lock is NOT held during the PMM call.
408: *
409: * Small allocations: write magic=BLOCK_FREE, push block onto the bucket free
410: * list head (LIFO), release lock.
411: * NOTE(MM-KM-02): The block is returned to its original bucket only; it is
412: * never given back to the PMM and cannot be reused by a request for a
413: * different bucket size (the pool now grows on demand, so this costs RAM
414: * but no longer causes allocation failure — see MM-KM-01 resolution).
415: *
416: * Locking: acquires/releases kmalloc_lock; NOT safe to call from NMI context.
417: */
418:void kfree(void *ptr) {
419:  if (!ptr)
420:    return;
421:
422:  uint64_t flags;
423:  struct block_header *blk = ((struct block_header *)ptr) - 1;
424:
425:  /* Acquire lock BEFORE reading magic to prevent SMP double-free race:
426:   * two CPUs could both see BLOCK_MAGIC and both proceed to free. */
427:  spin_lock_irqsave(&kmalloc_lock, &flags);
428:
429:  if (blk->magic != BLOCK_MAGIC) {
430:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&kmalloc_lock, flags);
431:    pr_err("kfree: Invalid magic %x at %p\n", blk->magic, ptr);
432:    return;
433:  }
434:
435:  if (blk->bucket_idx == 0xFFFFFFFF) {
436:    /* Large allocation - free pages */
437:    size_t total_req = blk->size + sizeof(struct block_header);
438:    size_t pages = (total_req + 4095) / 4096;
439:    km_stat_free(blk->size); /* perf brief §1 */
440:    blk->magic = 0;
441:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&kmalloc_lock, flags);
442:    pmm_free_pages((void *)blk, pages);
443:    return;
444:  }
445:
446:  /* Small allocation - return to bucket free list */
447:  if (blk->bucket_idx >= NUM_BUCKETS) {
448:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&kmalloc_lock, flags);
449:    pr_err("kfree: Invalid bucket index %d\n", blk->bucket_idx);
450:    return;
451:  }
452:
453:  km_stat_free(blk->size); /* perf brief §1 */
454:  blk->magic = BLOCK_FREE;
455:  blk->next = buckets[blk->bucket_idx];
456:  buckets[blk->bucket_idx] = blk;
457:
458:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&kmalloc_lock, flags);
459:}
460:
461:/*
462: * Reallocate memory
463: *
464: * krealloc - resize a kmalloc'd allocation.
465: *
466: * If ptr==NULL, behaves as kmalloc(new_size).
467: * If new_size==0, behaves as kfree(ptr) and returns NULL.
468: * Otherwise: allocates a new buffer, copies min(old_size, new_size) bytes,
469: * and frees the old buffer.
470: *
471: * NOTE(MM-KM-04): Always performs alloc+copy+free regardless of whether
472: * the new_size fits within the same bucket as the original allocation.
473: * A shrink from 200 bytes to 100 bytes (both bucket idx 3: <=128 + header
474: * exceeds 128, so bucket 4: <=256) still allocates a new block, copies, and
475: * frees the old one -- even though the old block could be reused directly.
476: *
477: * Reads old_size from block_header under kmalloc_lock to avoid a race with
478: * a concurrent kfree() on the same pointer.
479: *
480: * Returns: pointer to new allocation, or NULL on failure (old allocation NOT
481: *          freed on NULL return -- standard krealloc contract).
482: */
483:void *krealloc(void *ptr, size_t new_size) {
484:  if (!ptr)
485:    return kmalloc(new_size);
486:  if (new_size == 0) {
487:    kfree(ptr);
488:    return NULL;
489:  }
490:
491:  /* Read size while holding lock to avoid race with concurrent kfree */
492:  uint64_t flags;
493:  spin_lock_irqsave(&kmalloc_lock, &flags);
494:  struct block_header *blk = ((struct block_header *)ptr) - 1;
495:  if (blk->magic != BLOCK_MAGIC) {
496:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&kmalloc_lock, flags);
497:    return NULL;
498:  }
499:  size_t old_size = blk->size;
500:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&kmalloc_lock, flags);
501:
502:  void *new_ptr = kmalloc(new_size);
503:  if (!new_ptr)
504:    return NULL;
505:
506:  size_t copy_size = (old_size < new_size) ? old_size : new_size;
507:  memcpy(new_ptr, ptr, copy_size);
508:  kfree(ptr);
509:
510:  return new_ptr;
511:}
512:
513:/*
514: * kmalloc_get_stats - read the heap instrumentation counters (perf brief §1).
515: *
516: * heap_total_bytes: cumulative pool size (grows by KMALLOC_CHUNK_SIZE, never
517: *   shrinks — see MM-KM-01).  bytes_in_use/live_allocs: current live totals.
518: *   high_water_bytes: peak bytes_in_use since boot.  All out-params NULL-skippable.
519: */
520:void kmalloc_get_stats(uint64_t *heap_total_bytes, uint64_t *bytes_in_use,
521:                       uint64_t *high_water_bytes, uint64_t *live_allocs) {
522:  if (heap_total_bytes) *heap_total_bytes = heap_total;
523:  if (bytes_in_use)     *bytes_in_use = stat_bytes_in_use;
524:  if (high_water_bytes) *high_water_bytes = stat_high_water;
525:  if (live_allocs)      *live_allocs = stat_live_allocs;
526:}

134:/* --- Synthetic RAM provider for the VFS lifecycle test.  One file slot
135: * ("/f"), no allocation, no disk: exercises the vfs.c plumbing (mount_at,
136: * resolve, create, write, read, stat, unlink, umount) end to end. --- */
137:static char tfs_data[64];
138:static uint32_t tfs_size;
139:static int tfs_exists;
140:static int tfs_umount_ran;
141:
142:static int tfs_open(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path,
143:                    struct vfs_node *out) {
144:    if (strcmp(path, "/") == 0) {
145:        out->mnt = mnt; out->id = 0; out->size = 0; out->type = VFS_TYPE_DIR;
146:        return 0;
147:    }
148:    if (tfs_exists && strcmp(path, "/f") == 0) {
149:        out->mnt = mnt; out->id = 1; out->size = tfs_size;
150:        out->type = VFS_TYPE_FILE;
151:        return 0;
152:    }
153:    return -1;
154:}
155:static int tfs_read(struct vfs_node *node, uint64_t offset, void *buf,
156:                    uint32_t size) {
157:    if (node->id != 1 || !tfs_exists || offset >= tfs_size)
158:        return 0;
159:    uint32_t n = tfs_size - (uint32_t)offset;
160:    if (n > size)
161:        n = size;
162:    memcpy(buf, tfs_data + offset, n);
163:    return (int)n;
164:}
165:static int tfs_write(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path, uint64_t offset,
166:                     const void *buf, uint32_t size) {
167:    (void)mnt;
168:    if (!tfs_exists || strcmp(path, "/f") != 0)
169:        return -1;
170:    if (offset + size > sizeof(tfs_data))
171:        return -1;
172:    memcpy(tfs_data + offset, buf, size);
173:    if (offset + size > tfs_size)
174:        tfs_size = (uint32_t)(offset + size);
175:    return (int)size;
176:}
177:static int tfs_create(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path,
178:                      uint32_t type) {
179:    (void)mnt;
180:    if (type != VFS_TYPE_FILE || strcmp(path, "/f") != 0)
181:        return -1;
182:    tfs_exists = 1;
183:    tfs_size = 0;
184:    return 0;
185:}
186:static int tfs_unlink(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path) {
187:    (void)mnt;
188:    if (!tfs_exists || strcmp(path, "/f") != 0)
189:        return -1;
190:    tfs_exists = 0;
191:    tfs_size = 0;
192:    return 0;
193:}
194:static int tfs_umount(struct vfs_mount *mnt) {
195:    (void)mnt;
196:    tfs_umount_ran = 1;
197:    return 0;
198:}
199:static const struct fs_ops tfs_ops = {
200:    .name = "ktestfs",
201:    .open = tfs_open,
202:    .read = tfs_read,
203:    .write = tfs_write,
204:    .create = tfs_create,
205:    .unlink = tfs_unlink,
206:    .umount = tfs_umount,
207:};
208:
209:/* test_vfs_mount_lifecycle - mount → create → write → read → stat → unlink
210: * → umount over a synthetic provider: the full Plan 9-namespace lifecycle
211: * the userland-port programme depends on (docs/userland-port PLAN phase 3).
212: * Also proves umount retires the slot (resolution falls back to root and
213: * fails) and that a second umount is rejected. */
214:KTEST_CASE(test_vfs_mount_lifecycle) {
215:    tfs_exists = 0;
216:    tfs_size = 0;
217:    tfs_umount_ran = 0;
218:
219:    KASSERT_EQ(vfs_mount_at("/ktestfs", &tfs_ops, NULL), 0);
220:    KASSERT_EQ(vfs_create("/ktestfs/f", VFS_TYPE_FILE), 0);
221:    KASSERT_EQ(vfs_write_file("/ktestfs/f", "nexs", 4, 0), 4);
222:
223:    char rb[8] = {0};
224:    KASSERT_EQ(vfs_read_file("/ktestfs/f", rb, sizeof(rb), 0), 4);
225:    KASSERT_EQ(memcmp(rb, "nexs", 4), 0);
226:
227:    struct vfs_stat st;
228:    KASSERT_EQ(vfs_stat("/ktestfs/f", &st), 0);
229:    KASSERT_EQ(st.size, 4);
230:    KASSERT_EQ(st.type, VFS_TYPE_FILE);
231:
232:    KASSERT_EQ(vfs_unlink("/ktestfs/f"), 0);
233:    KASSERT(vfs_stat("/ktestfs/f", &st) != 0);
234:
235:    KASSERT_EQ(vfs_umount("/ktestfs"), 0);
236:    KASSERT_EQ(tfs_umount_ran, 1);
237:    KASSERT(vfs_stat("/ktestfs/f", &st) != 0); /* falls back to root: gone */
238:    KASSERT(vfs_umount("/ktestfs") != 0);      /* double umount rejected */
239:    KASSERT(vfs_umount("/") != 0);             /* root umount refused */
240:}

242:/* test_kmalloc_growth - prove the small-object pool grows past one chunk
243: * (MM-KM-01).  1100 blocks in the 4096-byte bucket exceed a 4 MB chunk
244: * regardless of how full the active chunk already is, so at least one
245: * growth must succeed for every allocation to come back non-NULL.  Each
246: * block is touched (write+readback) and everything is freed to the bucket
247: * lists afterwards, where it stays reusable. */
248:#define KMG_BLOCKS 1100
249:static void *kmg_ptrs[KMG_BLOCKS];
250:KTEST_CASE(test_kmalloc_growth) {
251:    int i;
252:    for (i = 0; i < KMG_BLOCKS; i++) {
253:        kmg_ptrs[i] = kmalloc(4000);
254:        if (!kmg_ptrs[i]) break;
255:        ((uint8_t *)kmg_ptrs[i])[0] = (uint8_t)i;
256:        ((uint8_t *)kmg_ptrs[i])[3999] = (uint8_t)(i ^ 0xFF);
257:    }
258:    int allocated = i;
259:    int corrupt = 0;
260:    for (i = 0; i < allocated; i++) {
261:        if (((uint8_t *)kmg_ptrs[i])[0] != (uint8_t)i ||
262:            ((uint8_t *)kmg_ptrs[i])[3999] != (uint8_t)(i ^ 0xFF))
263:            corrupt++;
264:        kfree(kmg_ptrs[i]);
265:    }
266:    KASSERT_EQ(allocated, KMG_BLOCKS);
267:    KASSERT_EQ(corrupt, 0);
268:}

270:/* test_vmm_protect - prove arch_vmm_protect rewrites live PTEs (AMMU-02).
271: * Takes a fresh PMM page (mapped RW+NX inside a 2MB kernel RAM block),
272: * flips it to PAGE_KERNEL_RO and back, and checks via PTE readback
273: * (vmm_check_range) and PA readback (vmm_get_phys) that only the attribute
274: * bits changed.  Exercises the 2MB→4KB block split on both arches and the
275: * unmapped-hole error path on the NULL page.  Runs on the BSP before SMP,
276: * so splitting the live kernel map here is single-threaded. */
277:KTEST_CASE(test_vmm_protect) {
278:    extern uint64_t *kernel_pgd;
279:    uint8_t *page = (uint8_t *)pmm_alloc_page();
280:    KASSERT(page != NULL);
281:    page[0] = 0xAB; /* RW works while PAGE_KERNEL */
282:    uint64_t pa_before = vmm_get_phys(kernel_pgd, (uint64_t)page);
283:    KASSERT(pa_before != 0);
284:
285:    /* Hole detection: a high user-half VA no map ever touches (the NULL
286:     * page would not do — amd64 identity-maps the low 1MB for the SMP
287:     * trampoline, so VA 0 is mapped there). */
288:    KASSERT(vmm_protect(kernel_pgd, 0x700000000000UL, 4096, PAGE_KERNEL_RO) != 0);
289:
290:    /* RW+NX → RO+NX */
291:    KASSERT_EQ(vmm_protect(kernel_pgd, (uint64_t)page, 4096, PAGE_KERNEL_RO), 0);
292:#ifdef ARCH_AARCH64
293:    /* AP[7:6] = 0b10 (EL1 read-only) must now be set */
294:    KASSERT_EQ(vmm_check_range(kernel_pgd, (uint64_t)page, 4096, PTE_AP_EL1_RO), 0);
295:#else
296:    /* NX must be set, and the RW bit must be GONE */
297:    KASSERT_EQ(vmm_check_range(kernel_pgd, (uint64_t)page, 4096, PTE_NX), 0);
298:    KASSERT(vmm_check_range(kernel_pgd, (uint64_t)page, 4096, PTE_RW) != 0);
299:#endif
300:    /* Frame address preserved; content still readable */
301:    KASSERT_EQ(vmm_get_phys(kernel_pgd, (uint64_t)page), pa_before);
302:    KASSERT_EQ(page[0], 0xAB);
303:
304:    /* back to RW+NX, prove writes work again */
305:    KASSERT_EQ(vmm_protect(kernel_pgd, (uint64_t)page, 4096, PAGE_KERNEL), 0);
306:#ifndef ARCH_AARCH64
307:    KASSERT_EQ(vmm_check_range(kernel_pgd, (uint64_t)page, 4096, PTE_RW), 0);
308:#endif
309:    page[1] = 0xCD;
310:    KASSERT_EQ(page[0], 0xAB);
311:    KASSERT_EQ(page[1], 0xCD);
312:    pmm_free_page(page);
313:}

@@@ kernel/lib/ktest.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/lib/ktest.c
