3: * Kernel Unit Test Runner
4: *
5: * Purpose:
6: *   Provides ktest_run_all(), which iterates over all KTEST_CASE() entries
7: *   registered in the `.ktests` ELF section and runs each test function.
8: *   Called unconditionally from kernel/main.c:87 during boot.
9: *
10: * Role:
11: *   The KTEST_CASE() macro (kernel/include/kernel/test.h) places a ktest_case_t
12: *   descriptor into the `.ktests` ELF section:
13: *     __attribute__((used, section(".ktests"))) static const ktest_case_t ...;
14: *   The linker script collects all such descriptors between the symbols
15: *   __ktests_start and __ktests_end.  ktest_run_all() walks this range.
16: *
17: * KASSERT behaviour:
18: *   KASSERT(cond) in test.h expands to:
19: *     if (!(cond)) { printk(...FAIL...); ktest_test_failed = 1; return; }
20: *   When a KASSERT fires, the test function sets ktest_test_failed and returns
21: *   early.  ktest_run_all() clears the flag before each test and checks it
22: *   after test->func() to record a real PASS or FAIL.
23: *
24: * Fixed issues:
25: *   LIB-KTEST-01  (W3 BUG, FIXED)  ktest_run_all() previously printed "PASS"
26: *                and incremented `passed` after test->func() returned, regardless
27: *                of whether the test exited via KASSERT.  Now KASSERT sets the
28: *                ktest_test_failed flag (test.h); the runner clears it before
29: *                each test and, after test->func(), records a real PASS or FAIL.
30: *                The summary now reports accurate PASSED / FAILED counts.
31: */
32:#include <kernel/test.h>
33:#include <kernel/printk.h>
34:
35:/* __ktests_start / __ktests_end: linker-defined symbols bracketing the
36: * .ktests ELF section that holds all KTEST_CASE() descriptors.
37: * The pointer arithmetic (__ktests_end - __ktests_start) gives the test count. */
38:extern ktest_case_t __ktests_start[];
39:extern ktest_case_t __ktests_end[];
40:
41:/* LIB-KTEST-01: a test sets this (via KASSERT in test.h) when an assertion
42: * fails.  ktest_run_all() clears it before each test and checks it after. */
43:volatile int ktest_test_failed = 0;
44:
45:/*
46: * ktest_run_all - run every KTEST_CASE registered in the .ktests section.
47: *
48: * Iterates from __ktests_start to __ktests_end.  For each entry:
49: *   1. Prints "[KTEST] Running: <name>... ".
50: *   2. Clears ktest_test_failed, then calls test->func().
51: *   3. Prints "PASS" or "FAIL" per the ktest_test_failed flag and counts it.
52: * After all tests, prints the pass/fail summary.
53: *
54: * LIB-KTEST-01 (fixed): step 3 checks the ktest_test_failed flag set by KASSERT,
55: *   so a test that returned early is counted as FAILED and the summary reports
56: *   accurate PASSED / FAILED counts.
57: *
58: * No crash recovery: if a test triggers a kernel panic or fault, the machine
59: * halts.  The comment "setjmp/longjmp" notes the direction for future hardening.
60: *
61: * Locking: none; called single-threaded from kernel/main.c before SMP starts.
62: * Side effects: writes to UART via printk; calls all registered test functions.
63: */
64:void ktest_run_all(void) {
65:    size_t count = __ktests_end - __ktests_start;
66:    size_t passed = 0;
67:    size_t failed = 0;
68:
69:    printk("\n[KTEST] Starting Kernel Unit Tests (%d cases found)...\n", (int)count);
70:
71:    for (ktest_case_t *test = __ktests_start; test < __ktests_end; test++) {
72:        /* Defense against linker padding slots: a descriptor with a NULL
73:         * name/func is not a test — calling it is a jump into rodata (the
74:         * W^X #PF UTM/QEMU caught when .ktests started 8-byte-misaligned).
75:         * The ALIGN(16) in both kernel.ld files prevents this structurally;
76:         * this guard keeps a future layout change from becoming a boot
77:         * crash again. */
78:        if (!test->name || !test->func) {
79:            printk("[KTEST] WARN: skipping padding/garbage slot at %p\n",
80:                   (void *)test);
81:            continue;
82:        }
83:        printk("[KTEST] Running: %s... ", test->name);
84:
85:        /* Note: This is a simplified runner. In a real system, we might want
86:         * to use setjmp/longjmp for crash recovery in tests.
87:         */
88:        ktest_test_failed = 0;
89:        test->func();
90:
91:        /* LIB-KTEST-01: a test that returned early via KASSERT set
92:         * ktest_test_failed; count it as FAILED instead of an unconditional PASS. */
93:        if (ktest_test_failed) {
94:            printk("FAIL\n");
95:            failed++;
96:        } else {
97:            printk("PASS\n");
98:            passed++;
99:        }
100:    }
101:
102:    printk("[KTEST] Completed. Summary: %d PASSED, %d FAILED\n\n",
103:           (int)passed, (int)failed);
104:}
105:

@@@ kernel/lib/math.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/lib/math.c
3: * Fixed-Point Math Functions for Kernel (No FPU)
4: *
5: * Uses 16.16 fixed-point representation where possible.
6: * All operations are integer-only to comply with -mgeneral-regs-only.
7: *
8: * Purpose:
9: *   Provides integer square root, fixed-point arithmetic (multiply, divide,
10: *   convert, abs, floor, ceil), trigonometric approximations (sin, cos), and
11: *   linear interpolation.  All arithmetic avoids the FPU; the kernel is compiled
12: *   with -mgeneral-regs-only (AArch64) or equivalent.
13: *
14: * Role:
15: *   The `k_*` prefixed variants are kernel-only (guarded by `#ifdef KERNEL`).
16: *   The unprefixed `fixmul`, `sin_fp`, `cos_fp`, and `lerp_fp` are shared with
17: *   userland (compiled without KERNEL defined, using os1.h instead of kernel
18: *   headers).  Both sets are exposed via kernel/include/kernel/math.h.
19: *
20: * 16.16 Fixed-Point Convention:
21: *   All fixed-point values use 16 integer bits and 16 fractional bits.
22: *   FP_ONE = 65536 (1.0 in 16.16).  FP_HALF = 32768 (0.5 in 16.16).
23: *   FP_PI  = correct π × 2^16 ≈ 205887 (declared in THIS file's fallback).
24: *
25: * Known issues:
26: *   LIB-MATH-01  (W2 BUG latent)  In kernel builds, <kernel/math.h> defines
27: *                FP_PI = 411775 (≈ 2π × 2^16, mislabeled "π × 131072").
28: *                This shadows the correct fallback `#ifndef FP_PI / 205887`
29: *                below.  As a result, in kernel builds FP_PI == FP_2PI == 411775,
30: *                which makes sin_fp's range-reduction loop `while (x > FP_PI)`
31: *                trigger only for x > 2π, and the reflection `x = FP_PI - x`
32: *                uses the wrong pole.  sin_fp/cos_fp produce wrong results for
33: *                all angles in (π/2, 2π].  LATENT: the only kernel caller,
34: *                kernel/graphics/draw3d.c, is not in the Makefile build; no live
35: *                compiled code calls sin_fp/cos_fp in the kernel today.  Fix:
36: *                change kernel/include/kernel/math.h:16 to `FP_PI 205887`.
37: *   LIB-MATH-03  (W1 REFINE)  sin_fp range-reduces by subtracting FP_2PI in
38: *                a while loop.  For very large inputs this is O(n) rather than
39: *                a single modulo operation.
40: */
41:#ifdef KERNEL
42:#include <kernel/math.h>
43:#include <kernel/types.h>
44:#else
45:#include <os1.h>
46:#endif
47:
48:/* Fixed-point constants (16.16) */
49:/* FP_SHIFT: number of fractional bits; 16.16 → shift = 16. */
50:#ifndef FP_SHIFT
51:#define FP_SHIFT 16
52:#endif /* FP_SHIFT */
53:/* FP_ONE: 1.0 in 16.16 fixed-point (65536). */
54:#ifndef FP_ONE
55:#define FP_ONE (1 << FP_SHIFT)
56:#endif /* FP_ONE */
57:/* FP_HALF: 0.5 in 16.16 fixed-point (32768). */
58:#ifndef FP_HALF
59:#define FP_HALF (1 << (FP_SHIFT - 1))
60:#endif /* FP_HALF */
61:/* FP_PI: π × 2^16 ≈ 205887.  This fallback is correct.
62: * NOTE(LIB-MATH-01): In kernel builds, <kernel/math.h> already defined FP_PI
63: * as 411775 (≈ 2π × 2^16) before this file is compiled, so this #ifndef branch
64: * is never taken.  The compiled kernel has FP_PI == FP_2PI == 411775, breaking
65: * sin_fp for angles in (π/2, 2π].  The fix is in kernel/include/kernel/math.h.
66: * Userland builds (no KERNEL) use os1.h which defines FP_PI 205887 (correct). */
67:#ifndef FP_PI
68:#define FP_PI 205887
69:#endif /* FP_PI */
70:/* FP_2PI: 2π × 2^16 ≈ 411775 (correct in both builds). */
71:#define FP_2PI 411775
72:
73:/*
74: * k_isqrt - integer square root using Newton-Raphson iteration.
75: *
76: * Computes floor(sqrt(n)) using the recurrence y = (x + n/x) / 2, which
77: * converges quadratically.  Terminates when the estimate stops decreasing.
78: *
79: * Params:
80: *   n - unsigned 32-bit input value.
81: * Returns: floor(sqrt(n)); 0 for n == 0.
82: * Locking: none (stateless).
83: * Side effects: none.
84: */
85:#ifdef KERNEL
86:uint32_t k_isqrt(uint32_t n) {
87:  if (n == 0)
88:    return 0;
89:
90:  uint32_t x = n;
91:  uint32_t y = (x + 1) >> 1;
92:
93:  while (y < x) {
94:    x = y;
95:    y = (x + n / x) >> 1;
96:  }
97:  return x;
98:}
99:#endif
100:
101:/*
102: * k_sqrt_fp - fixed-point square root in 16.16 format.
103: *
104: * Approach: to compute sqrt(x) in 16.16, note that x is already scaled by 2^16.
105: *   We want result r such that r × 2^-16 = sqrt(x × 2^-16).
106: *   Shift x left 16 bits (giving x × 2^16 = x << 16 as a 64-bit value).
107: *   The integer sqrt of that 64-bit value is sqrt(x × 2^16) = sqrt(x) × 2^8.
108: *   Shift the result left 8 more bits to get sqrt(x) × 2^16 — the 16.16 result.
109: *
110: * Params:
111: *   x - 16.16 fixed-point input; must be >= 0.
112: * Returns: floor(sqrt(x)) in 16.16 fixed-point; 0 for x <= 0.
113: * Locking: none.
114: */
115:#ifdef KERNEL
116:int32_t k_sqrt_fp(int32_t x) {
117:  if (x <= 0)
118:    return 0;
119:
120:  /* Shift to get more precision before sqrt */
121:  /* sqrt(x * 2^16) = sqrt(x) * 2^8 */
122:  /* We need sqrt(x) * 2^16, so multiply result by 2^8 */
123:  uint64_t n = (uint64_t)x << 16;               /* x * 2^32 */
124:  uint64_t root = k_isqrt((uint32_t)(n >> 16)); /* sqrt of upper 32 bits */
125:
126:  /* Adjust: we computed sqrt(x * 2^16), need sqrt(x) * 2^16 */
127:  return (int32_t)(root << 8);
128:}
129:#endif
130:
131:/*
132: * fixmul - multiply two 16.16 fixed-point values, returning a 16.16 result.
133: *
134: * Computes (a × b) >> 16 using a 64-bit intermediate to avoid overflow.
135: * Both arguments and the result are 16.16 signed fixed-point.
136: *
137: * Params:
138: *   a, b - 16.16 fixed-point operands.
139: * Returns: (a × b) in 16.16 fixed-point (truncated, not rounded).
140: * Locking: none.
141: */
142:int32_t fixmul(int32_t a, int32_t b) {
143:  int64_t result = (int64_t)a * b;
144:  return (int32_t)(result >> FP_SHIFT);
145:}
146:
147:#ifdef KERNEL
148:int32_t k_fixmul(int32_t a, int32_t b) { return fixmul(a, b); }
149:#endif
150:
151:/*
152: * k_fixdiv - divide two 16.16 fixed-point values, returning a 16.16 result.
153: *
154: * Computes (a << 16) / b using a 64-bit intermediate to avoid overflow.
155: * Returns 0 if b == 0 (no trap; silent division-by-zero suppression).
156: *
157: * Params:
158: *   a - dividend in 16.16.
159: *   b - divisor in 16.16; if 0, returns 0.
160: * Returns: (a / b) in 16.16 fixed-point.
161: * Locking: none.
162: */
163:#ifdef KERNEL
164:int32_t k_fixdiv(int32_t a, int32_t b) {
165:  if (b == 0)
166:    return 0;
167:  int64_t result = ((int64_t)a << FP_SHIFT) / b;
168:  return (int32_t)result;
169:}
170:
171:/* k_int_to_fp - convert a signed integer to 16.16 fixed-point (x × 2^16). */
172:int32_t k_int_to_fp(int32_t x) { return x << FP_SHIFT; }
173:
174:/* k_fp_to_int - truncate a 16.16 fixed-point value to integer (floor for +ve). */
175:int32_t k_fp_to_int(int32_t x) { return x >> FP_SHIFT; }
176:
177:/* k_fp_to_int_round - round a 16.16 fixed-point value to the nearest integer.
178: * Adds FP_HALF (0.5) before right-shifting to implement round-half-up. */
179:int32_t k_fp_to_int_round(int32_t x) { return (x + FP_HALF) >> FP_SHIFT; }
180:
181:/* k_fabs_fp - absolute value of a 16.16 fixed-point number. */
182:int32_t k_fabs_fp(int32_t x) { return (x < 0) ? -x : x; }
183:
184:/* k_floor_fp - round a 16.16 fixed-point value down to the nearest whole number.
185: * Clears the 16 fractional bits by ANDing with the integer-part mask. */
186:int32_t k_floor_fp(int32_t x) { return x & ~((1 << FP_SHIFT) - 1); }
187:
188:/*
189: * k_ceil_fp - round a 16.16 fixed-point value up to the nearest whole number.
190: *
191: * If the fractional part is zero, x is already an integer — return unchanged.
192: * For positive values: clear fractional bits and add FP_ONE (round up).
193: * For negative values: clearing the fractional bits already moves toward zero
194: * (which is ceiling direction for negative numbers).
195: */
196:int32_t k_ceil_fp(int32_t x) {
197:  int32_t frac = x & ((1 << FP_SHIFT) - 1);
198:  if (frac == 0)
199:    return x;
200:
201:  if (x >= 0) {
202:    return (x & ~((1 << FP_SHIFT) - 1)) + FP_ONE;
203:  } else {
204:    return x & ~((1 << FP_SHIFT) - 1);
205:  }
206:}
207:#endif
208:
209:/*
210: * sin_fp - sine approximation in 16.16 fixed-point.
211: *
212: * Input: angle in radians, 16.16 fixed-point.
213: * Output: sin(x), 16.16 fixed-point (range approximately [-65536, 65536]).
214: *
215: * Algorithm:
216: *   1. Range-reduce to [-FP_PI, FP_PI] by repeated addition/subtraction of FP_2PI.
217: *      NOTE(LIB-MATH-03): this is an O(n) loop; large inputs are slow.
218: *   2. Reflect into [-π/2, π/2] using sin(x) = sin(π - x) for x > π/2 and
219: *      sin(x) = sin(-π - x) for x < -π/2.
220: *   3. Evaluate the 5th-order Taylor series: sin(x) ≈ x - x³/6 + x⁵/120.
221: *      Coefficients in 16.16: 1/6 ≈ 10923, 1/120 ≈ 546.
222: *
223: * NOTE(LIB-MATH-01): In kernel builds, FP_PI is 411775 (== FP_2PI) due to
224: *   the shadowing in <kernel/math.h>.  The range-reduction loop condition
225: *   `x > FP_PI` is equivalent to `x > FP_2PI`, so inputs in (π/2, 2π] pass
226: *   through unreduced.  The reflection at step 2 then uses the wrong pole
227: *   (FP_PI = 2π instead of π), producing incorrect results for three-quarters
228: *   of the domain.  No live compiled kernel code calls sin_fp today (latent).
229: *
230: * Locking: none (stateless).
231: */
232:int32_t sin_fp(int32_t x) {
233:  /* Reduce to -pi to pi range */
234:  /* NOTE(LIB-MATH-01 + LIB-MATH-03): loop range-reduction; see file header.
235:   * In correct builds (FP_PI=205887), reduces x into (-π, π].
236:   * In kernel builds (FP_PI=411775=FP_2PI), effectively reduces to (-2π, 2π]. */
237:  while (x > FP_PI)
238:    x -= FP_2PI;
239:  while (x < -FP_PI)
240:    x += FP_2PI;
241:
242:  /* Reflect domain to -pi/2 to pi/2 range.
243:   * Taylor series approximation accuracy diminishes rapidly beyond |x| > pi/2.
244:   */
245:  /* half_pi: π/2 in 16.16 fixed-point ≈ 1.5708 × 65536 = 102944.
246:   * NOTE(LIB-MATH-01): with FP_PI=411775 this reflection uses the wrong pole. */
247:  int32_t half_pi = 102944; /* PI / 2 represented in 16.16 fixed point */
248:  if (x > half_pi) {
249:    x = FP_PI - x;
250:  } else if (x < -half_pi) {
251:    x = -FP_PI - x;
252:  }
253:
254:  /* Taylor series: sin(x) ≈ x - x³/6 + x⁵/120 */
255:  int32_t x2 = fixmul(x, x);
256:  int32_t x3 = fixmul(x2, x);
257:  int32_t x5 = fixmul(x3, x2);
258:
259:  /* 1/6 ≈ 10923 in 16.16 */
260:  /* 1/120 ≈ 546 in 16.16 */
261:  /* (65536/6 = 10922.67 rounded; 65536/120 = 546.13 truncated) */
262:  int32_t term1 = x;
263:  int32_t term2 = fixmul(x3, 10923); /* x³/6 */
264:  int32_t term3 = fixmul(x5, 546);   /* x⁵/120 */
265:
266:  return term1 - term2 + term3;
267:}
268:
269:#ifdef KERNEL
270:int32_t k_sin_fp(int32_t x) { return sin_fp(x); }
271:#endif
272:
273:/*
274: * cos_fp - cosine approximation in 16.16 fixed-point.
275: *
276: * Uses the identity cos(x) = sin(x + π/2).  Adds 102944 (≈ π/2 in 16.16) to
277: * the argument and delegates to sin_fp.  Inherits all properties and caveats
278: * of sin_fp, including NOTE(LIB-MATH-01).
279: *
280: * Params:
281: *   x - angle in radians, 16.16 fixed-point.
282: * Returns: cos(x) in 16.16 fixed-point.
283: * Locking: none.
284: */
285:int32_t cos_fp(int32_t x) {
286:  /* PI/2 ≈ 102944 in 16.16 */
287:  return sin_fp(x + 102944);
288:}
289:
290:#ifdef KERNEL
291:int32_t k_cos_fp(int32_t x) { return cos_fp(x); }
292:#endif
293:
294:/*
295: * lerp_fp - linear interpolation between two 16.16 fixed-point values.
296: *
297: * Computes a + t × (b - a), where t is a 16.16 fraction in [0, FP_ONE].
298: * t == 0 returns a; t == FP_ONE returns b.
299: *
300: * Params:
301: *   a, b - 16.16 fixed-point endpoints.
302: *   t    - 16.16 interpolation factor; typically in [0, 65536].
303: * Returns: interpolated 16.16 value.
304: * Locking: none.
305: */
306:int32_t lerp_fp(int32_t a, int32_t b, int32_t t) {
307:  return a + fixmul(t, b - a);
308:}
309:
310:#ifdef KERNEL
311:int32_t k_lerp_fp(int32_t a, int32_t b, int32_t t) { return lerp_fp(a, b, t); }
312:#endif
313:
314:/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
315: * 128-bit integer runtime support (__int128 ABI helpers)
316: *
317: * Both the kernel and userland link -nostdlib with NO libgcc, so the compiler
318: * intrinsics it emits for __int128 division/multiplication (__udivti3,
319: * __umodti3, __multi3) would be undefined symbols at link time. Providing them
320: * here — in the shared math library compiled into both the kernel and lib.o —
321: * makes __uint128_t a first-class type across the codebase (e.g. the real-time
322: * clock mono_ns() in kernel/core/timer.c can use the natural
323: * (__uint128_t)delta * NSEC_PER_SEC / freq form). Add/sub/shift/compare on
324: * __int128 are emitted inline by the compiler and need no helper.
325: *
326: * All three are implemented with only 64-bit operations so they are themselves
327: * self-contained (no recursive intrinsic emission).
328: * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
329:
330:/* Use the GCC predefined 128-bit typedefs (__uint128_t / __int128_t) rather
331: * than the bare `__int128` keyword: the keyword trips -Wpedantic/-Werror in
332: * this ISO-C build, the predefined typedefs do not (the same reason pt_regs.h
333: * and mono_ns() use __uint128_t). The libgcc ABI is identical either way. */
334:
335:/* u128_divmod - unsigned 128-bit division with remainder (binary long division,
336: * O(128)). Returns the quotient; *rem (if non-NULL) receives the remainder.
337: * Division by zero returns all-ones / zero remainder rather than trapping. */
338:static __uint128_t u128_divmod(__uint128_t num, __uint128_t den,
339:                               __uint128_t *rem) {
340:  if (den == 0) { /* mirror hardware-less UB choice: avoid a fault */
341:    if (rem)
342:      *rem = 0;
343:    return ~(__uint128_t)0;
344:  }
345:  __uint128_t q = 0, r = 0;
346:  for (int i = 127; i >= 0; i--) {
347:    r = (r << 1) | ((num >> i) & 1);
348:    if (r >= den) {
349:      r -= den;
350:      q |= ((__uint128_t)1 << i);
351:    }
352:  }
353:  if (rem)
354:    *rem = r;
355:  return q;
356:}
357:
358:/* libgcc-compatible signatures. Declared before definition to satisfy
359: * -Wmissing-prototypes; the compiler emits calls to these by name. */
360:__uint128_t __udivti3(__uint128_t a, __uint128_t b);
361:__uint128_t __umodti3(__uint128_t a, __uint128_t b);
362:__int128_t __multi3(__int128_t a, __int128_t b);
363:
364:__uint128_t __udivti3(__uint128_t a, __uint128_t b) {
365:  return u128_divmod(a, b, 0);
366:}
367:
368:__uint128_t __umodti3(__uint128_t a, __uint128_t b) {
369:  __uint128_t r;
370:  u128_divmod(a, b, &r);
371:  return r;
372:}
373:
374:__int128_t __multi3(__int128_t a, __int128_t b) {
375:  /* Split into 64-bit halves; each partial product is a 64x64→128 widening
376:   * multiply, which the compiler does inline (no __multi3 recursion). Only the
377:   * low 128 bits are defined, which is all the ABI requires. */
378:  __uint128_t ua = (__uint128_t)a, ub = (__uint128_t)b;
379:  uint64_t alo = (uint64_t)ua, ahi = (uint64_t)(ua >> 64);
380:  uint64_t blo = (uint64_t)ub, bhi = (uint64_t)(ub >> 64);
381:  __uint128_t lo = (__uint128_t)alo * blo;
382:  __uint128_t mid = (__uint128_t)alo * bhi + (__uint128_t)ahi * blo;
383:  return (__int128_t)(lo + (mid << 64));
384:}

@@@ kernel/lib/printk.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/lib/printk.c
3: * Kernel printf implementation
4: *
5: * Purpose:
6: *   Provides printk(), vprintk(), snprintf(), and panic() — the formatted output
7: *   and fatal-error reporting interfaces for the entire kernel.  All kernel log
8: *   output eventually flows through this file to the UART.
9: *
10: * Role:
11: *   printk/vprintk are called from every subsystem (drivers, sched, mm, fs,
12: *   irq, graphics).  snprintf is used for string formatting throughout the kernel.
13: *   panic() is the last-resort halt path on unrecoverable errors.
14: *
15: * Architecture:
16: *   - Formatted string production is delegated to vsnprintf() (vsnprintf.c).
17: *   - Each CPU has a per-CPU buffer (cpu->printk_buf, 2048 bytes) to avoid
18: *     sharing a global buffer across CPUs without a lock.
19: *   - A global spinlock (uart_lock) serialises UART writes across all CPUs.
20: *   - A per-CPU recursion guard (cpu->in_printk) detects recursive printk calls
21: *     (e.g. from a fault handler that fires during printk).
22: *   - panic() sets panic_flag atomically so other CPUs can halt via IPI, then
23: *     prints and spins.
24: *
25: * Invariants:
26: *   - uart_lock is always acquired with IRQs saved (spin_lock_irqsave) so that
27: *     a timer IRQ cannot try to printk while uart_lock is already held.
28: *   - in_printk is set AFTER the lock is taken to prevent a false-positive
29: *     recursive-printk detection (see comment in vprintk for the exact race).
30: *
31: * Known issues:
32: *   LIB-PRINTK-01  (W2 REFINE) cpu->printk_buf is 2048 bytes; the prefix
33: *                  consumes 6 bytes.  Long messages are silently truncated by
34: *                  vsnprintf with no dropped-message counter.
35: */
36:#include <drivers/uart.h>
37:#include <kernel/arch.h>
38:#include <kernel/cpu.h>
39:#include <kernel/fault.h>
40:#include <kernel/irq.h>
41:#include <kernel/bootphase.h>
42:#include <kernel/printk.h>
43:#include <kernel/sched.h>
44:#include <kernel/string.h>
45:#include <kernel/types.h>
46:#include <stdarg.h>
47:
48:/* console_loglevel: messages at or below this level are printed.
49: * Initialized to KERN_INFO; may be adjusted at runtime. */
50:int console_loglevel = KERN_INFO;
51:
52:/* Set by panic() to signal all CPUs to halt */
53:volatile int panic_flag = 0;
54:
55:/* vsnprintf is now in vsnprintf.c */
56:
57:/* kputc - write a single character to the UART.
58: * Called only from kputs; not exported. */
59:static void kputc(char c) { uart_putc(c); }
60:
61:/* kputs - write a NUL-terminated string to the UART byte by byte.
62: * Called from vprintk after the formatted buffer is ready.
63: * Not exported; callers outside this file use printk/vprintk. */
64:static void kputs(const char *s) {
65:  while (*s)
66:    kputc(*s++);
67:}
68:
69:/*
70: * snprintf - format a string into a fixed-size buffer (variadic wrapper).
71: *
72: * Delegates directly to vsnprintf().  Provided here so kernel code can call
73: * snprintf() without linking against userland libc.
74: *
75: * Params:
76: *   buf  - destination buffer of 'size' bytes.
77: *   size - total capacity of buf (NUL included in the count).
78: *   fmt  - printf-style format string.
79: *   ...  - format arguments.
80: * Returns: number of characters written (excluding NUL); may be < size - 1
81: *          if the format string is shorter than the buffer.
82: *          NOTE(LIB-VSNPRINTF-02): does NOT return the would-be length on
83: *          truncation; callers cannot detect truncation from the return value.
84: * Locking: none (vsnprintf is stateless).
85: */
86:int snprintf(char *buf, size_t size, const char *fmt, ...) {
87:  va_list args;
88:  int ret;
89:
90:  va_start(args, fmt);
91:  ret = vsnprintf(buf, size, fmt, args);
92:  va_end(args);
93:
94:  return ret;
95:}
96:
97:/*
98: * vprintk - format and emit a log message from a va_list.
99: *
100: * This is the core printk implementation.  It:
101: *   1. Acquires uart_lock with IRQ save BEFORE reading in_printk (see NOTE below).
102: *   2. Checks for recursive printk; if detected, unlocks and emits a bare warning
103: *      directly via uart_puts (which does not go through vprintk).
104: *   3. Sets cpu->in_printk to block re-entry while the buffer is in use.
105: *   4. Formats a "[C<id>] " prefix into cpu->printk_buf (6 bytes).
106: *   5. Formats the message into cpu->printk_buf after the prefix using vsnprintf.
107: *   6. Emits the buffer via kputs.
108: *   7. Clears in_printk and releases uart_lock.
109: *
110: * Params:
111: *   fmt  - printf-style format string.
112: *   args - argument list; caller is responsible for va_start/va_end.
113: * Returns: number of characters written by vsnprintf (message portion only;
114: *          prefix length is not included).
115: * Locking: acquires uart_lock with IRQ save/restore; NOT safe from NMI context.
116: * Side effects: writes to uart; may be called from interrupt context (IRQ disabled
117: *               on entry while lock is held).
118: *
119: * NOTE(LIB-PRINTK-01): cpu->printk_buf is 2048 bytes; the prefix consumes ~6.
120: *   vsnprintf receives (2048 - pfx) bytes.  If the formatted message is longer,
121: *   it is silently truncated at (2048 - pfx - 1) characters with no warning or
122: *   counter increment.
123: *
124: * NOTE on in_printk ordering: uart_lock is acquired BEFORE checking in_printk.
125: *   Without this ordering, the following SMP race can occur:
126: *     CPU A: sets in_printk=1
127: *     Timer IRQ fires, switches to task on CPU A
128: *     CPU A (new task): reads in_printk=1 → false "[RECURSIVE PRINTK DETECTED]"
129: *   By taking the lock first, only one CPU can inspect/modify in_printk at a time.
130: */
131:/* Global UART lock for synchronized serial output */
132:static spinlock_t uart_lock = SPINLOCK_INIT;
133:
134:int vprintk(const char *fmt, va_list args) {
135:  struct cpu_info *cpu = get_cpu_info();
136:  uint64_t flags;
137:  int len;
138:
139:  if (!cpu) {
140:      char buf[512];
141:      len = vsnprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), fmt, args);
142:      spin_lock_irqsave(&uart_lock, &flags);
143:      kputs("[BOOT] ");
144:      kputs(buf);
145:      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&uart_lock, flags);
146:      return len;
147:  }
148:
149:  /* Acquire lock and disable IRQs BEFORE setting in_printk.
150:   * Without this, the timer IRQ can preempt between in_printk=1 and the lock,
151:   * switch to another task, and that task's next printk sees a stale
152:   * in_printk=1 on this CPU → false "[RECURSIVE PRINTK DETECTED]" spam. */
153:  spin_lock_irqsave(&uart_lock, &flags);
154:
155:  if (cpu->in_printk) {
156:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&uart_lock, flags);
157:    uart_puts("\n[RECURSIVE PRINTK DETECTED]\n");
158:    return 0;
159:  }
160:
161:  cpu->in_printk = 1;
162:
163:  /* Prepend "[C%d] " CPU prefix for multi-CPU log disambiguation */
164:  int pfx = snprintf(cpu->printk_buf, 8, "[C%u] ", cpu->cpu_id);
165:  if (pfx < 0)
166:    pfx = 0;
167:
168:  /* Format the actual message after the prefix */
169:  len = vsnprintf(cpu->printk_buf + pfx, sizeof(cpu->printk_buf) - pfx, fmt, args);
170:
171:  if (len >= (int)(sizeof(cpu->printk_buf) - pfx - 1)) {
172:      cpu->printk_dropped++;
173:      int t_len = 11;
174:      if (sizeof(cpu->printk_buf) > (size_t)t_len) {
175:          char *end = cpu->printk_buf + sizeof(cpu->printk_buf) - t_len - 1;
176:          /* strcpy is safe here, but we can just loop or memcpy */
177:          memcpy(end, "...[TRUNC]\n", 12);
178:      }
179:  }
180:
181:  kputs(cpu->printk_buf);
182:
183:  cpu->in_printk = 0;
184:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&uart_lock, flags);
185:
186:  return len;
187:}
188:
189:/*
190: * printk - kernel printf (variadic wrapper around vprintk).
191: *
192: * The primary log-output function for all kernel subsystems.  GCC checks
193: * format/argument types at compile time via the __attribute__((format(printf,...)))
194: * declared in printk.h.
195: *
196: * Params:
197: *   fmt - printf-style format string.
198: *   ... - format arguments.
199: * Returns: characters written (from vsnprintf, message portion only).
200: * Locking: inherits vprintk's uart_lock; NOT safe from NMI context.
201: */
202:int printk(const char *fmt, ...) {
203:  va_list args;
204:  int ret;
205:
206:  va_start(args, fmt);
207:  ret = vprintk(fmt, args);
208:  va_end(args);
209:
210:  return ret;
211:}
212:
213:/*
214: * panic - print a fatal message and halt all CPUs permanently.
215: *
216: * Sequence:
217: *   1. Atomically increments panic_flag so other CPUs' spin loops can detect it.
218: *   2. Sends an IPI (SGI0) to all other CPUs via irq_send_ipi_all(), which causes
219: *      them to enter their halt handler.  This is done BEFORE printing so that no
220: *      other CPU's printk can interleave with the panic message.
221: *   3. Prints "*** KERNEL PANIC ***" banner.
222: *   4. Formats and prints the caller-supplied message via vprintk.
223: *   5. Prints "System halted."
224: *   6. Disables all exceptions (arch_local_irq_save_all) and spins forever.
225: *   7. Marks the spin as unreachable for the compiler.
226: *
227: * Params:
228: *   fmt - printf-style format string describing the panic cause.
229: *   ... - format arguments.
230: * Returns: never.
231: * Locking: calls printk/vprintk (which acquire uart_lock).  The function does
232: *          NOT acquire uart_lock itself; if another CPU holds uart_lock when
233: *          panic() is called, the first printk may spin briefly.
234: * Side effects: sets panic_flag, sends IPI, halts all CPUs.
235: */
236:/* panic_reboot_after_grace - DIR-05 #139 watchdog: after the panic is shown (UART
237: * + red panic_screen), wait a readable grace (~10 s) then HARD-RESET so an
238: * unattended machine self-recovers from a kernel fault.  IRQs stay masked; the
239: * grace spins on the free-running hardware counter (it advances without
240: * interrupts) — NOT arch_idle(), which would wfi/hlt forever with IRQs off.  If
241: * the timer frequency is not up yet (very early boot) the grace is skipped and we
242: * reset immediately.  arch_reboot() is __noreturn (resets, or halts if reset
243: * does not take). */
244:static void panic_reboot_after_grace(void) __noreturn;
245:static void panic_reboot_after_grace(void) {
246:  uint64_t f;
247:  arch_local_irq_save_all(&f);
248:  uint64_t freq = arch_timer_get_freq();
249:  if (freq) {
250:    uint64_t end = arch_timer_get_count() + freq * 10ULL; /* ~10 seconds */
251:    while ((int64_t)(end - arch_timer_get_count()) > 0)
252:      __asm__ __volatile__("" ::: "memory");
253:  }
254:  arch_reboot();
255:}
256:
257:void panic(const char *fmt, ...) {
258:  va_list args;
259:
260:  /* Signal all CPUs to stop BEFORE printing so no interleaving after this */
261:  __sync_fetch_and_add(&panic_flag, 1);
262:
263:  /* Fault context (kernel/fault.h): printk would take uart_lock (possibly
264:   * held by a wedged CPU) and needs get_cpu_info — on amd64 a LAPIC-MMIO read
265:   * that may itself fault.  Use the lock-free emergency path instead; print
266:   * FIRST, then attempt the quiesce IPI (its MMIO write may be the thing
267:   * that is broken). */
268:  if (fault_depth() > 0) {
269:    fault_printf("\n\n*** KERNEL PANIC (fault context) ***\n");
270:    fault_printf("[boot-phase: %s]\n", boot_phase_name(boot_phase_get()));
271:    va_start(args, fmt);
272:    fault_vprintf(fmt, args);
273:    va_end(args);
274:    fault_printf("\n");
275:    backtrace_here();
276:    fault_printf("\nSystem halted.\n");
277:    irq_send_ipi_all();
278:
279:    /* DIR-05 #139: also paint the fault on the framebuffer (no-UART machines).
280:     * fault_text() is the full transcript tee'd through fault_vprintf above. */
281:    panic_screen(fault_text());
282:
283:    panic_reboot_after_grace(); /* DIR-05 #139: ~10 s grace, then hard reset */
284:  }
285:
286:  /* Send IPI (SGI0) to halt all other CPUs */
287:  irq_send_ipi_all();
288:
289:  printk("\n\n*** KERNEL PANIC ***\n");
290:  printk("[boot-phase: %s]\n", boot_phase_name(boot_phase_get()));
291:
292:  va_start(args, fmt);
293:  vprintk(fmt, args);
294:  va_end(args);
295:
296:  printk("\n");
297:  backtrace_here();
298:  printk("\nSystem halted.\n");
299:
300:  /* DIR-05 #139: paint the panic reason on the framebuffer too (no-UART case).
301:   * Non-fault context, so fault_text() is empty — format the reason directly. */
302:  {
303:    char nb[256];
304:    va_start(args, fmt);
305:    vsnprintf(nb, sizeof(nb), fmt, args);
306:    va_end(args);
307:    panic_screen(nb);
308:  }
309:
310:  /* DIR-05 #139 watchdog: ~10 s grace to read the panic, then hard reset. */
311:  panic_reboot_after_grace();
312:
313:  __builtin_unreachable();
314:}
315:

@@@ kernel/lib/registry.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/lib/registry.c
3: * System Registry — hierarchical namespace TREE (Phase 4.1 A-tree-1).
4: *
5: * Purpose:
6: *   The in-kernel COHERENT NAMESPACE: every piece of system state is a path.
7: *   Dotted keys ("theme.color", "srv.notify_pid") are namespace PATHS — each
8: *   segment is a node; a leaf carries a value (a "file"), an interior node is a
9: *   directory.  This is the "tmpvfs"/ground-truth state services read at init,
10: *   and the seam for "/reg" as a VFS file namespace (A1b) and for blocks/
11: *   services/devices to attach as tree nodes (A-tree-3 mount).
12: *
13: * Role:
14: *   Exposed to userland via sys_registry() (REG_OP_READ/WRITE/ENUM) and as
15: *   capability objects (OBJ_TYPE_REGKEY, kernel/core/object.c).  Used by the
16: *   desktop/UI for theme/system settings and by services for routing keys.
17: *
18: * Data model (replaces the old flat 128-slot array, LIB-REG-01):
19: *   A tree of DYNAMICALLY allocated `struct reg_node`.  Children are kept
20: * SORTED by name, so lookup is O(depth × children-scanned-with-early-stop) and
21: * listing is ordered — it scales as the supervisory namespace grows, instead of
22: * the old O(128) scan, and the key count is no longer capped.  kmalloc is
23: * lazily initialised (safe at registry_init: PMM is up first), nodes live for
24: * the kernel lifetime (registry keys are not deleted today).
25: *
26: * Security (LIB-REG-02): writes are first-writer-wins by owner_pid and gated by
27: *   CAP_REG_WRITE (sys_registry) — a service's routing key cannot be hijacked.
28: *
29: * Locking: a reader/writer lock — readers (get/enum/regfs reads) run
30: *   CONCURRENTLY, writers (set/del) are exclusive — so the read-heavy
31: * supervisory namespace is not serialized.  IRQ-safe (sections run IRQs-off);
32: * per-subtree locking is a later refinement.
33: */
34:
35:#include <kernel/kmalloc.h>
36:#include <kernel/nx_contract.h>
37:#include <kernel/printk.h>
38:#include <kernel/registry.h>
39:#include <kernel/sched.h> /* current_process / proc_has_cap / proc_is_machine */
40:#include <kernel/spinlock.h>
41:#include <kernel/string.h>
42:#include <kernel/vfs.h> /* regfs: the registry mounted as a /reg file namespace */
43:#include <kernel/vmm.h>
44:#include <stdbool.h>
45:
46:/* reg_node - one namespace node.  A node is a directory (has children) and/or a
47: * leaf (is_leaf, carries a value).  Children live in a SORTED dynamic array of
48: * pointers (by name) → O(log n) binary-search lookup and ordered listing; the
49: * array grows by doubling (kmalloc, no krealloc in the kernel). */
50:struct reg_node {
51:  char name[MAX_KEY_LEN];     /* this path segment */
52:  char value[MAX_VAL_LEN];    /* leaf value (valid when is_leaf) */
53:  int owner_pid;              /* first-writer-wins owner of the leaf */
54:  int is_leaf;                /* 1 = carries a value */
55:  struct reg_node *parent;    /* owning directory (NULL for the root) */
56:  struct reg_node **children; /* sorted array of child pointers (by name) */
57:  int n_children;             /* number of children */
58:  int cap_children;           /* allocated capacity of children[] */
59:};
60:
61:/* The root is the unnamed anchor; statically allocated (BSS-zeroed), its
62: * children are kmalloc'd.  registry_count = number of leaves (init log). */
63:static struct reg_node reg_root_storage;
64:static struct reg_node *const reg_root = &reg_root_storage;
65:static int registry_count = 0;
66:
67:/* Registry reader/writer lock (Phase 4.1 A-gap3): the supervisory namespace is
68: * read-heavy, so readers run CONCURRENTLY and only writers are exclusive — the
69: * registry is no longer serialized on every access (the old single spinlock).
70: * Critical sections run with IRQs disabled (an IRQ handler never reenters
71: * mid-section); registry writes never originate from IRQ context.
72: *   reg_res_lock — the shared resource: held by a writer, or collectively by
73: * the readers (first reader takes it, last reader releases it). reg_cnt_lock —
74: * guards reg_readers across the reader lock/unlock transitions. */
75:static DEFINE_SPINLOCK(reg_cnt_lock);
76:static DEFINE_SPINLOCK(reg_res_lock);
77:static int reg_readers;
78:
79:static void reg_read_lock(uint64_t *flags) {
80:  spin_lock_irqsave(&reg_cnt_lock, flags);
81:  if (++reg_readers == 1)
82:    spin_lock(&reg_res_lock); /* first reader excludes writers */
83:  spin_unlock(&reg_cnt_lock); /* keep IRQs off until reg_read_unlock */
84:}
85:static void reg_read_unlock(uint64_t flags) {
86:  spin_lock(&reg_cnt_lock); /* IRQs already disabled */
87:  if (--reg_readers == 0)
88:    spin_unlock(&reg_res_lock); /* last reader admits writers */
89:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&reg_cnt_lock, flags);
90:}
91:static void reg_write_lock(uint64_t *flags) {
92:  spin_lock_irqsave(&reg_res_lock,
93:                    flags); /* exclusive: waits out readers/writers */
94:}
95:static void reg_write_unlock(uint64_t flags) {
96:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&reg_res_lock, flags);
97:}
98:
99:/* node_alloc - kmalloc + init a node for segment 'seg'.  NULL on OOM. */
100:static struct reg_node *node_alloc(const char *seg) {
101:  struct reg_node *n = kmalloc(sizeof(*n));
102:  if (!n)
103:    return NULL;
104:  memset(n, 0, sizeof(*n));
105:  strncpy(n->name, seg, MAX_KEY_LEN - 1);
106:  n->name[MAX_KEY_LEN - 1] = '\0';
107:  return n;
108:}
109:
110:/* node_find_child - BINARY SEARCH of immediate child 'seg' in the sorted
111: * children[] array (lock held).  O(log n_children). */
112:static struct reg_node *node_find_child(struct reg_node *p, const char *seg) {
113:  int lo = 0, hi = p->n_children - 1;
114:  while (lo <= hi) {
115:    int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
116:    int cmp = strcmp(p->children[mid]->name, seg);
117:    if (cmp == 0)
118:      return p->children[mid];
119:    if (cmp < 0)
120:      lo = mid + 1;
121:    else
122:      hi = mid - 1;
123:  }
124:  return NULL;
125:}
126:
127:/* node_get_or_add - BINARY SEARCH child 'seg'; return it if present, else
128: * insert it at the sorted position (growing children[] by doubling).  NULL on
129: * OOM (lock held). */
130:static struct reg_node *node_get_or_add(struct reg_node *p, const char *seg) {
131:  /* Binary search for either the match or the insertion point 'lo'. */
132:  int lo = 0, hi = p->n_children - 1;
133:  while (lo <= hi) {
134:    int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
135:    int cmp = strcmp(p->children[mid]->name, seg);
136:    if (cmp == 0)
137:      return p->children[mid];
138:    if (cmp < 0)
139:      lo = mid + 1;
140:    else
141:      hi = mid - 1;
142:  }
143:  /* Grow children[] if full (double, min 4; no krealloc in-kernel). */
144:  if (p->n_children == p->cap_children) {
145:    int newcap = p->cap_children ? p->cap_children * 2 : 4;
146:    struct reg_node **arr = kmalloc(sizeof(struct reg_node *) * (size_t)newcap);
147:    if (!arr)
148:      return NULL;
149:    if (p->children) {
150:      memcpy(arr, p->children,
151:             sizeof(struct reg_node *) * (size_t)p->n_children);
152:      kfree(p->children);
153:    }
154:    p->children = arr;
155:    p->cap_children = newcap;
156:  }
157:  struct reg_node *n = node_alloc(seg);
158:  if (!n)
159:    return NULL;
160:  n->parent = p;
161:  /* Insert at 'lo', shifting the larger names right (keeps the array sorted).
162:   */
163:  for (int i = p->n_children; i > lo; i--)
164:    p->children[i] = p->children[i - 1];
165:  p->children[lo] = n;
166:  p->n_children++;
167:  return n;
168:}
169:
170:/* walk_path - resolve dotted 'key' to its node, creating the path when
171: * 'create'. Returns the final node, or NULL (not found / OOM / empty key). Lock
172: * held. */
173:/* Forward declaration: registry_set/registry_del route virtual per-process keys
174: * (R2) but are defined above the routing helper, which needs reg_proc_split. */
175:static int reg_virtual_proc_write(const char *key, const char *value,
176:                                  long *ret);
177:
178:static struct reg_node *walk_path(const char *key, int create) {
179:  struct reg_node *n = reg_root;
180:  const char *p = key;
181:  int any = 0;
182:  while (*p) {
183:    char seg[MAX_KEY_LEN];
184:    int i = 0;
185:    while (*p && *p != '.' && i < MAX_KEY_LEN - 1)
186:      seg[i++] = *p++;
187:    seg[i] = '\0';
188:    while (*p && *p != '.') /* drop any overflow tail of an over-long segment */
189:      p++;
190:    if (*p == '.')
191:      p++;
192:    if (seg[0] == '\0')
193:      continue; /* skip empty segment (leading/trailing/double dot) */
194:    struct reg_node *c =
195:        create ? node_get_or_add(n, seg) : node_find_child(n, seg);
196:    if (!c)
197:      return NULL;
198:    n = c;
199:    any = 1;
200:  }
201:  return any ? n : NULL;
202:}
203:
204:/*
205: * registry_init - seed the default entries.  reg_root is BSS-zeroed; kmalloc is
206: * lazily initialised on the first node alloc (PMM is already up at this point).
207: *
208: * The base set of keys provides a complete namespace for the userland:
209: *   - theme.color, style.name, background.name → compositor look & feel
210: *   - system.hostname, system.arch, system.version, system.os → system identity
211: *   - system.boot_time                           → uptime sanity (filled later)
212: *   - sys.ntfy.panel_open                        → notification panel state
213: *   - mouse.sensitivity                          → input driver
214: *
215: * Single-threaded before SMP.
216: */
217:/* set_default - install one boot default, reporting the ONE thing that can go
218: * wrong here.  registry_init runs single-threaded on an empty table, so a
219: * failure means the table is full or out of memory -- and the visible symptom
220: * would be a consumer reading a key the system believes it published, which is
221: * indistinguishable from a consumer bug.  Counted centrally so the ten call
222: * sites below do not each carry a copy of the same check. */
223:static int registry_defaults_failed;
224:static void set_default(const char *key, const char *val) {
225:  if (registry_set(key, val, 0) != 0) {
226:    registry_defaults_failed++;
227:    pr_err("registry: default key '%s' could not be installed\n", key);
228:  }
229:}
230:
231:void registry_init(void) {
232:  registry_count = 0;
233:
234:  /* ---- Compositor appearance (read by nxres, nxsettings, nxui, nxlauncher)
235:   * ---- */
236:  set_default("theme.color", "dark");
237:  set_default("style.name", "nexs");
238:  set_default("background.name", "blue");
239:
240:  /* ---- System identity (displayed in "About", network, etc.) ---- */
241:  set_default("system.hostname", "NeXs");
242:  set_default("system.arch", "unknown");  /* will be updated by init/nxinfo */
243:  set_default("system.version", "0.0.0"); /* kernel version placeholder */
244:  set_default("system.os", "NEXS");
245:
246:  /* ---- Boot / runtime markers ---- */
247:  set_default("system.boot_time", "0"); /* filled by init after spawn */
248:
249:  /* ---- Notification infrastructure ---- */
250:  set_default("sys.ntfy.panel_open", "0");
251:
252:  /* ---- Input ---- */
253:  set_default("mouse.sensitivity", "1.0");
254:
255:  pr_info("Registry: Initialized with %d default keys (namespace tree).\n",
256:          registry_count);
257:}
258:
259:/*
260: * registry_set - create or update a key.  Walks/creates the path, then sets the
261: * leaf value.  First-writer-wins: an existing leaf owned by someone else (and
262: * owner_pid != 0) returns -EACCES.  owner_pid 0 = kernel/system (full rights).
263: * Returns 0, -EACCES on ownership violation, -1 on bad args / OOM.
264: */
265:int registry_set(const char *key, const char *value, int owner_pid) {
266:  if (!key || !value)
267:    return -1;
268:
269:  /* R2: route the virtual per-process namespace HERE, at the shared seam, so
270:   * every entry point behaves identically.  It used to be routed only inside
271:   * sys_registry, which meant a setenv arriving through an OBJ_TYPE_REGKEY
272:   * handle or through the /reg mount silently created a STORED node that the
273:   * computed value then shadowed forever — the write appeared to succeed and
274:   * did nothing.  Three doors to one resource must not disagree about what the
275:   * resource IS. */
276:  {
277:    long vret;
278:    if (reg_virtual_proc_write(key, value, &vret))
279:      return (int)vret;
280:  }
281:
282:  uint64_t flags;
283:  reg_write_lock(&flags);
284:
285:  struct reg_node *n = walk_path(key, 1);
286:  if (!n) {
287:    reg_write_unlock(flags);
288:    return -1; /* empty key or OOM */
289:  }
290:  /* Ownership ACL.  owner_pid 0 == the SYSTEM identity (machine/root, see
291:   * registry_caller_owner()); a non-zero owner_pid is an ordinary process
292:   * writing as itself.  A non-system caller may write ONLY a key it already
293:   * owns; everything else is denied.  That single rule covers two cases:
294:   *
295:   *   - another USER's key (n->owner_pid = some other pid) — first-writer-wins,
296:   *     unchanged;
297:   *   - a SYSTEM key (n->owner_pid == 0) — a config/service key first written
298:   *     by init or a root service.
299:   *
300:   * USR-SEC-01 (FIXED 2026-07-23, audit programme A): the deny used to also
301:   * require `n->owner_pid != 0`, which meant a system-owned key was writable by
302:   * ANYONE — an ordinary app could overwrite `srv.notify_pid` (redirecting
303:   * every notification), `theme.*`, `sys.env.*`, etc.  init re-published srv.*
304:   * on each respawn to paper over it (NOTIFY-REG-01), but that only bounded the
305:   * window, it did not close it.  The real separation of root from user here is
306:   * NAMESPACE OWNERSHIP, not the coarse capability mask: a user keeps
307:   * CAP_REG_WRITE (raptor/nxempire persist their own keys), but the keys it
308:   * creates are owned by its pid and it can no longer reach a system key.  A
309:   * system caller (owner_pid == 0) is never denied and may still override any
310:   * key, exactly as before. */
311:  if (n->is_leaf && owner_pid != 0 && n->owner_pid != owner_pid) {
312:    reg_write_unlock(flags);
313:    pr_warn("registry: PID %d denied write to '%s' (owner PID %d)\n", owner_pid,
314:            key, n->owner_pid);
315:    return -EACCES;
316:  }
317:  strncpy(n->value, value, MAX_VAL_LEN - 1);
318:  n->value[MAX_VAL_LEN - 1] = '\0';
319:  if (!n->is_leaf) {
320:    n->is_leaf = 1;
321:    n->owner_pid = owner_pid;
322:    registry_count++;
323:  }
324:  reg_write_unlock(flags);
325:  return 0;
326:}
327:
328:/*
329: * registry_get - resolve a key to its leaf and copy the value.
330: * Returns 0 on success, -1 if not found / not a leaf / bad args.
331: */
332:
333:/*
334: * VIRTUAL per-process keys (Phase 5b) — `sys.proc.<pid>.<field>`.
335: *
336: * These are COMPUTED from the process table on every read, never stored.  They
337: * used to be written by userland (nxexec) after each spawn, which made the
338: * registry a SECOND, best-effort copy of state the kernel already owns
339: * authoritatively.  The proof that copy was a defect rather than a design: its
340: * entries outlived their processes, so a garbage collector
341: * (nxexec_prune_identities) had to be written to sweep them.
342: *
343: * Virtualising deletes the staleness class outright instead of maintaining it:
344: * a dead pid simply has no keys, because there was never a stored node.  It
345: * also avoids a new lock order — reaping stored keys at process death would
346: * have nested sched_lock inside the registry locks, the same AB-BA shape the
347: * roadmap already flags as an open hazard.
348: *
349: * `name` and lineage are FACTS THE KERNEL OWNS.  Program-level policy (an icon)
350: * deliberately does NOT live here: keying a PROGRAM's property by PID is the
351: * modelling error that made it go stale in the first place — it belongs under a
352: * program-keyed namespace, stable across instances.
353: *
354: * Returns 1 if `key` was a virtual key (answer written to buf), 0 otherwise.
355: */
356:/* reg_proc_split - parse "sys.proc.<pid>.<field>".  Returns the field (a
357: * pointer into `key`) and writes the pid, or NULL if `key` is not in the
358: * per-process namespace at all.  Shared by the read and write paths so they
359: * cannot disagree about what counts as a virtual key. */
360:static const char *reg_proc_split(const char *key, int *out_pid) {
361:  const char *p = key;
362:  if (strncmp(p, "sys.proc.", 9) != 0)
363:    return NULL;
364:  p += 9;
365:  int pid = 0;
366:  if (*p < '0' || *p > '9')
367:    return NULL;
368:  while (*p >= '0' && *p <= '9')
369:    pid = pid * 10 + (*p++ - '0');
370:  if (*p != '.')
371:    return NULL;
372:  *out_pid = pid;
373:  return p + 1;
374:}
375:
376:static int reg_virtual_proc(const char *key, char *buf, size_t size) {
377:  int pid = 0;
378:  const char *p = reg_proc_split(key, &pid);
379:  if (!p)
380:    return 0;
381:
382:  struct ps_info pi;
383:  if (proc_get_info(pid, &pi) != 0) {
384:    buf[0] = '\0';
385:    return 1; /* live key space, dead process: EMPTY, never a stale value */
386:  }
387:
388:  if (strcmp(p, "name") == 0) {
389:    strncpy(buf, pi.name, size - 1);
390:    buf[size - 1] = '\0';
391:    return 1;
392:  }
393:  if (strcmp(p, "state") == 0) {
394:    strncpy(buf, proc_state_name(pi.state), size - 1);
395:    buf[size - 1] = '\0';
396:    return 1;
397:  }
398:  if (strcmp(p, "parent") == 0 || strcmp(p, "owner") == 0) {
399:    int par = 0, own = 0;
400:    NX_DISCARD(
401:        proc_get_lineage(pid, &par, &own),
402:        "a pid with no lineage (or already reaped) reports 0/0, which is "
403:        "the same answer this virtual key gives for init; the caller is "
404:        "reading a status field, not performing an operation");
405:    snprintf(buf, size, "%d", (strcmp(p, "owner") == 0) ? own : par);
406:    return 1;
407:  }
408:  /* `env.<NAME>` — the per-process ENVIRONMENT (Phase 17), owned by the
409:   * scheduler.  An UNSET variable answers -1 ("ours, and definitively absent")
410:   * rather than an empty string: getenv() must be able to tell "not set" from
411:   * "set to the empty string", and an empty answer would collapse the two.
412:   * -1 also stops the lookup here instead of falling through to stored nodes,
413:   * so nothing can shadow the live block. */
414:  if (strncmp(p, "env.", 4) == 0) {
415:    if (!p[4])
416:      return -1;
417:    return proc_env_get(pid, p + 4, buf, size) == 0 ? 1 : -1;
418:  }
419:  return 0; /* not a field we own: fall through to stored nodes */
420:}
421:
422:/*
423: * reg_virtual_proc_write - route a WRITE/DELETE aimed at the virtual
424: * per-process namespace.  Returns 1 (handled, *ret holds the result) or 0.
425: *
426: * Only `env.<NAME>` is writable.  The rest of the per-process view reports
427: * facts the kernel derives — a write there is not "denied for now", it is
428: * meaningless, so it is refused with -EACCES rather than quietly stored as a
429: * node that would then be shadowed by the computed value forever.
430: *
431: * NOTE the authority split: this runs BEFORE the CAP_REG_WRITE gate in
432: * sys_registry, because writing your own environment is ordinary unprivileged
433: * work.  Requiring registry-write capability for setenv() would have set the
434: * ceiling at "may reconfigure the machine" for an operation that only touches
435: * the caller's own process.  proc_env_set enforces the correct rule instead:
436: * self always, anyone else only if privileged.
437: */
438:/*
439: * registry_key_is_virtual - does this key name the computed per-process view?
440: *
441: * R2: the authority rule belongs to the KEY, not to the entry point.  All three
442: * write gates (sys_registry, the OS1_NS_REG acquisition in object.c,
443: * regfs_write) consult this so a virtual key is uniformly exempt from
444: * CAP_REG_WRITE — writing your own environment is ordinary unprivileged work,
445: * and proc_env_set enforces the real rule (self always, anyone else only if
446: * privileged).
447: *
448: * Before this, only sys_registry knew: the object and regfs paths demanded
449: * CAP_REG_WRITE for a setenv AND then stored a real node that the computed
450: * value would shadow forever — two different wrong answers for the same key
451: * depending on which door you came through.
452: */
453:int registry_key_is_virtual(const char *key) {
454:  int pid = 0;
455:  return key && reg_proc_split(key, &pid) != (const char *)0;
456:}
457:
458:static int reg_virtual_proc_write(const char *key, const char *value,
459:                                  long *ret) {
460:  int pid = 0;
461:  const char *p = reg_proc_split(key, &pid);
462:  if (!p)
463:    return 0;
464:  if (strncmp(p, "env.", 4) == 0 && p[4]) {
465:    *ret = proc_env_set(current_process, pid, p + 4, value);
466:    return 1;
467:  }
468:  *ret = -EACCES; /* computed field: not writable by anyone */
469:  return 1;
470:}
471:
472:int registry_get(const char *key, char *buffer, size_t size) {
473:  if (!key || !buffer || size == 0)
474:    return -1;
475:
476:  /* Virtual keys are answered from live kernel state BEFORE consulting stored
477:   * nodes, so a stale leftover can never shadow the truth. */
478:  int v = reg_virtual_proc(key, buffer, size);
479:  if (v)
480:    return v > 0 ? 0 : -1;
481:
482:  uint64_t flags;
483:  reg_read_lock(&flags);
484:
485:  struct reg_node *n = walk_path(key, 0);
486:  if (!n || !n->is_leaf) {
487:    reg_read_unlock(flags);
488:    return -1;
489:  }
490:  strncpy(buffer, n->value, size - 1);
491:  buffer[size - 1] = '\0';
492:  reg_read_unlock(flags);
493:  return 0;
494:}
495:
496:/* node_remove_child - unlink 'child' from parent 'p' (binary search) and free
497: * it (and its now-unused children array).  Lock held; child must have no
498: * children. */
499:static void node_remove_child(struct reg_node *p, struct reg_node *child) {
500:  int lo = 0, hi = p->n_children - 1, idx = -1;
501:  while (lo <= hi) {
502:    int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
503:    int cmp = strcmp(p->children[mid]->name, child->name);
504:    if (cmp == 0) {
505:      idx = mid;
506:      break;
507:    }
508:    if (cmp < 0)
509:      lo = mid + 1;
510:    else
511:      hi = mid - 1;
512:  }
513:  if (idx < 0)
514:    return; /* not found (should not happen) */
515:  if (child->children)
516:    kfree(child->children);
517:  kfree(child);
518:  for (int i = idx; i < p->n_children - 1; i++)
519:    p->children[i] = p->children[i + 1];
520:  p->n_children--;
521:}
522:
523:/*
524: * registry_del - remove a key.  Clears the leaf, then prunes every now-empty
525: * ancestor directory (freeing the nodes), so deleting "a.b.c" reclaims "c",
526: * then "b", then "a" if they become empty.  First-writer-wins: owner_pid != 0
527: * may delete only its own key.  Returns 0, -ENOENT if absent/not a leaf,
528: * -EACCES on ownership violation.
529: */
530:int registry_del(const char *key, int owner_pid) {
531:  if (!key)
532:    return -1;
533:
534:  /* R2: same seam-level routing as registry_set.  Deleting a virtual env key IS
535:   * unsetenv — an empty value clears the slot (see reg_virtual_proc_write). */
536:  {
537:    long vret;
538:    if (reg_virtual_proc_write(key, NULL, &vret))
539:      return (int)vret;
540:  }
541:
542:  uint64_t flags;
543:  reg_write_lock(&flags);
544:
545:  struct reg_node *n = walk_path(key, 0);
546:  if (!n || n == reg_root || !n->is_leaf) {
547:    reg_write_unlock(flags);
548:    return -ENOENT;
549:  }
550:  if (owner_pid != 0 && n->owner_pid != owner_pid) {
551:    reg_write_unlock(flags);
552:    return -EACCES;
553:  }
554:
555:  n->is_leaf = 0;
556:  n->value[0] = '\0';
557:  n->owner_pid = 0;
558:  registry_count--;
559:
560:  /* Prune empty nodes up the chain (a node with no children and no value is a
561:   * dead directory). */
562:  while (n != reg_root && n->n_children == 0 && !n->is_leaf) {
563:    struct reg_node *p = n->parent;
564:    node_remove_child(p, n);
565:    n = p;
566:  }
567:
568:  reg_write_unlock(flags);
569:  return 0;
570:}
571:
572:/* enum_dfs - depth-first walk emitting full dotted keys of LEAF nodes that
573: * match 'prefix', in sorted order.  'path' is the shared path buffer (length
574: * path_len), mutated as we descend and restored for each sibling so per-frame
575: * stack stays small (depth-bounded recursion).  Lock held. */
576:static void enum_dfs(struct reg_node *n, char *path, size_t path_len,
577:                     size_t path_cap, const char *prefix, size_t prefix_len,
578:                     char *buf, size_t size, size_t *off) {
579:  for (int ci = 0; ci < n->n_children; ci++) {
580:    struct reg_node *c = n->children[ci];
581:    size_t saved = path_len;
582:    size_t cl = path_len;
583:    if (cl && cl + 1 < path_cap)
584:      path[cl++] = '.';
585:    for (size_t k = 0; c->name[k] && cl + 1 < path_cap; k++)
586:      path[cl++] = c->name[k];
587:    path[cl] = '\0';
588:
589:    if (c->is_leaf &&
590:        (prefix_len == 0 ||
591:         (cl >= prefix_len && strncmp(path, prefix, prefix_len) == 0))) {
592:      if (*off + cl + 2 <= size) { /* key + '\n' + room for the NUL */
593:        memcpy(buf + *off, path, cl);
594:        *off += cl;
595:        buf[(*off)++] = '\n';
596:      }
597:    }
598:    enum_dfs(c, path, cl, path_cap, prefix, prefix_len, buf, size, off);
599:    path[saved] = '\0'; /* restore for the next sibling */
600:  }
601:}
602:
603:/*
604: * registry_enum - list used keys, newline-separated, into 'buf'
605: * (NUL-terminated, bounded by 'size'); returns bytes written excluding the NUL,
606: * -1 on bad args. Keys come out in sorted order (children are kept sorted).
607: * 'prefix' (NULL/"" = all) filters to keys beginning with it — the "list a
608: * namespace directory" primitive (Phase 4.1 A1a).
609: */
610:int registry_enum(const char *prefix, char *buf, size_t size) {
611:  if (!buf || size == 0)
612:    return -1;
613:
614:  /* `sys.proc.<pid>.env.` is VIRTUAL: it has no stored nodes to walk, so a
615:   * plain DFS would report a process's environment as empty.  Answer it from
616:   * the scheduler's block instead, in the same full-key form the DFS emits, so
617:   * callers cannot tell the two namespaces apart. */
618:  if (prefix) {
619:    int pid = 0;
620:    const char *f = reg_proc_split(prefix, &pid);
621:    if (f && strcmp(f, "env.") == 0) {
622:      char names[512];
623:      int n = proc_env_enum(pid, names, sizeof(names));
624:      size_t off = 0;
625:      /* Walk the newline-separated names in place (no strtok_r in the kernel
626:       * string library, and none is needed for a single scan). */
627:      for (char *k = names; n > 0 && *k;) {
628:        char *nl = k;
629:        while (*nl && *nl != '\n')
630:          nl++;
631:        char sep = *nl;
632:        *nl = '\0';
633:        size_t need = strlen(prefix) + strlen(k) + 2; /* separator + NUL */
634:        if (off + need > size)
635:          break;
636:        if (off)
637:          buf[off++] = '\n';
638:        off += (size_t)snprintf(buf + off, size - off, "%s%s", prefix, k);
639:        if (!sep)
640:          break;
641:        k = nl + 1;
642:      }
643:      buf[off] = '\0';
644:      return (int)off;
645:    }
646:  }
647:
648:  size_t prefix_len = prefix ? strlen(prefix) : 0;
649:  char path[256];
650:  path[0] = '\0';
651:
652:  uint64_t flags;
653:  reg_read_lock(&flags);
654:  size_t off = 0;
655:  enum_dfs(reg_root, path, 0, sizeof(path), prefix, prefix_len, buf, size,
656:           &off);
657:  buf[off] = '\0';
658:  reg_read_unlock(flags);
659:  return (int)off;
660:}
661:
662:/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *
663: * Single authority seam for BOTH registry entry points (S-ALIGN F5).
664: * The registry is reachable two ways — the sys_registry op-switch (syscall 250)
665: * and the /reg VFS mount below — and both mutate the same tree.  Every gate
666: * decision and caller-identity derivation lives HERE, once, so the two entry
667: * points can never drift apart on policy (they used to carry four independent
668: * copies of these checks).
669: * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
670:
671:/* registry_write_allowed - mutating the registry needs CAP_REG_WRITE.  A NULL
672: * current_process (in-kernel caller) passes: proc_has_cap(NULL) is true by
673: * definition (kernel = machine identity). */
674:bool registry_write_allowed(void) {
675:  return proc_has_cap(current_process, CAP_REG_WRITE);
676:}
677:
678:/* registry_caller_owner - first-writer-wins identity: machine AND root
679: * callers write as owner 0 (full rights), everyone else as their own PID.
680: *
681: * Root is folded in with machine here (not just "machine/kernel" as the
682: * name used to imply) because every /sys/bin system service — nxbar,
683: * nxsettings, nxntfy_srv, the launcher — runs at PLVL_ROOT via the
684: * per-path preset (level_for_path, syscall_dispatch.c), not PLVL_MACHINE.
685: * Before this, a service's OWN keys (e.g. nxntfy_srv's sys.ntfy.log.* ring)
686: * were owned by its PID; init respawning it after a crash handed the
687: * replacement a FRESH pid, which then got -EACCES writing keys the dead
688: * instance had created, silently freezing the ring until reboot.  Treating
689: * PLVL_ROOT as system authority (interim, pending real per-namespace ACLs
690: * — "system write", see the kernel/lib/registry.c file header) makes the
691: * whole ROOT-level system-service tier share one first-writer-wins owner
692: * and survive respawns; PLVL_USER (untrusted apps) still write as their own
693: * PID and cannot hijack a service's key. */
694:int registry_caller_owner(void) {
695:  return proc_is_privileged(current_process) ? 0 : (int)current_process->pid;
696:}
697:
698:/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *
699: * regfs — the registry mounted as a "/reg" file namespace (Phase 4.1 A1b).
700: * A synthetic VFS provider (no partition) over the registry tree: a key path
701: * "/reg/system/hostname" is the registry key "system.hostname".  This realises
702: * "everything is a file": registry state is read/written/listed through the
703: * uniform VFS, and "/reg" is the first non-block server in the Plan 9
704: * namespace.
705: * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
706:
707:/* regfs_path_to_key - mount-relative path ("/system/hostname") -> dotted key
708: * ("system.hostname"): drop leading slashes, collapse each '/' run to one '.'.
709: */
710:static void regfs_path_to_key(const char *relpath, char *key, size_t n) {
711:  size_t k = 0;
712:  const char *p = relpath;
713:  while (*p == '/')
714:    p++;
715:  while (*p && k + 1 < n) {
716:    if (*p == '/') {
717:      while (*p == '/')
718:        p++;
719:      if (*p && k + 1 < n)
720:        key[k++] = '.';
721:    } else {
722:      key[k++] = *p++;
723:    }
724:  }
725:  key[k] = '\0';
726:}
727:
728:static int regfs_mount(struct vfs_mount *mnt, struct partition *p) {
729:  (void)mnt;
730:  (void)p; /* synthetic server: nothing to probe */
731:  return 0;
732:}
733:
734:static int regfs_open(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path,
735:                      struct vfs_node *out) {
736:  char key[MAX_KEY_LEN];
737:  regfs_path_to_key(path, key, sizeof(key));
738:
739:  uint64_t flags;
740:  reg_read_lock(&flags);
741:  struct reg_node *n = key[0] ? walk_path(key, 0) : reg_root;
742:  if (!n) {
743:    reg_read_unlock(flags);
744:    return -1;
745:  }
746:  out->mnt = mnt;
747:  out->id = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)n; /* nodes are never freed -> stable handle */
748:  out->type = n->is_leaf ? VFS_TYPE_FILE : VFS_TYPE_DIR;
749:  out->size = n->is_leaf ? (uint64_t)strlen(n->value) : 0;
750:  reg_read_unlock(flags);
751:  return 0;
752:}
753:
754:static int regfs_read(struct vfs_node *node, uint64_t offset, void *buf,
755:                      uint32_t size) {
756:  struct reg_node *n = (struct reg_node *)(uintptr_t)node->id;
757:  if (!n)
758:    return -1;
759:  uint64_t flags;
760:  reg_read_lock(&flags);
761:  if (!n->is_leaf) {
762:    reg_read_unlock(flags);
763:    return -1;
764:  }
765:  size_t vlen = strlen(n->value);
766:  if (offset >= vlen) {
767:    reg_read_unlock(flags);
768:    return 0;
769:  }
770:  size_t avail = vlen - (size_t)offset;
771:  size_t cnt = size < avail ? size : avail;
772:  memcpy(buf, n->value + (size_t)offset, cnt);
773:  reg_read_unlock(flags);
774:  return (int)cnt;
775:}
776:
777:static int regfs_write(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path, uint64_t offset,
778:                       const void *buf, uint32_t size) {
779:  (void)mnt;
780:  /* CAP_REG_WRITE (shared seam) layers ON TOP of the CAP_FS_WRITE the
781:   * SYS_FILE_WRITE path already checked: VFS-write + registry-write authority.
782:   */
783:  char key[MAX_KEY_LEN];
784:  regfs_path_to_key(path, key, sizeof(key));
785:  if (!key[0] || offset >= MAX_VAL_LEN - 1)
786:    return -1;
787:  /* R2: the key decides the authority.  A virtual per-process key is exempt
788:   * from CAP_REG_WRITE (setenv is unprivileged; proc_env_set applies the real
789:   * self-or-privileged rule) — the gate had to move BELOW the path→key
790:   * conversion, because until the key exists there is nothing to ask about. */
791:  if (!registry_key_is_virtual(key) && !registry_write_allowed())
792:    return -EPERM;
793:
794:  size_t off = (size_t)offset;
795:  size_t cnt = size;
796:  if (off + cnt > MAX_VAL_LEN - 1)
797:    cnt = MAX_VAL_LEN - 1 - off;
798:
799:  /* Read-modify-write so a non-zero offset OVERLAYS/extends the value instead
800:   * of replacing it (offset 0 stays a plain full write).  Pad a gap past the
801:   * end. */
802:  char val[MAX_VAL_LEN];
803:  if (registry_get(key, val, sizeof(val)) != 0)
804:    val[0] = '\0';
805:  size_t curlen = strlen(val);
806:  for (size_t i = curlen; i < off; i++)
807:    val[i] = ' ';
808:  memcpy(val + off, buf, cnt);
809:  if (off + cnt >= curlen)
810:    val[off + cnt] = '\0';
811:
812:  return registry_set(key, val, registry_caller_owner()) == 0 ? (int)cnt : -1;
813:}
814:
815:/* regfs_list - space-separated immediate child names of the node at 'path'
816: * (the VFS directory-listing contract). */
817:static int regfs_list(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path, char *buf,
818:                      uint32_t size) {
819:  (void)mnt;
820:  char key[MAX_KEY_LEN];
821:  regfs_path_to_key(path, key, sizeof(key));
822:
823:  uint64_t flags;
824:  reg_read_lock(&flags);
825:  struct reg_node *n = key[0] ? walk_path(key, 0) : reg_root;
826:  if (!n) {
827:    reg_read_unlock(flags);
828:    return -1;
829:  }
830:  size_t off = 0;
831:  for (int i = 0; i < n->n_children; i++) {
832:    size_t nl = strlen(n->children[i]->name);
833:    if (off + nl + 2 > size)
834:      break;
835:    if (off)
836:      buf[off++] = ' ';
837:    memcpy(buf + off, n->children[i]->name, nl);
838:    off += nl;
839:  }
840:  buf[off] = '\0';
841:  reg_read_unlock(flags);
842:  return (int)off;
843:}
844:
845:/* regfs_create - create an empty leaf key at 'path' (fs_ops.create).  Backs
846: * handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, CREATE) on /reg so the capability route can create
847: * keys exactly like regfs_write's implicit create does.  Same authority as
848: * every registry write (registry_write_allowed + first-writer-wins ownership
849: * inside registry_set).  Interior (directory) nodes appear implicitly when a
850: * child leaf is set, so VFS_TYPE_DIR is not supported here. */
851:static int regfs_create(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path,
852:                        uint32_t type) {
853:  (void)mnt;
854:  if (type != VFS_TYPE_FILE)
855:    return -1;
856:  if (!registry_write_allowed())
857:    return -EPERM;
858:  char key[MAX_KEY_LEN];
859:  regfs_path_to_key(path, key, sizeof(key));
860:  if (!key[0])
861:    return -1;
862:  return registry_set(key, "", registry_caller_owner()) == 0 ? 0 : -1;
863:}
864:
865:/* regfs_unlink - remove the registry key at 'path' (rm /reg/...). */
866:static int regfs_unlink(struct vfs_mount *mnt, const char *path) {
867:  (void)mnt;
868:  if (!registry_write_allowed())
869:    return -EPERM;
870:  char key[MAX_KEY_LEN];
871:  regfs_path_to_key(path, key, sizeof(key));
872:  if (!key[0])
873:    return -1;
874:  return registry_del(key, registry_caller_owner());
875:}
876:
877:static const struct fs_ops regfs_ops = {
878:    .name = "regfs",
879:    .mount = regfs_mount,
880:    .open = regfs_open,
881:    .read = regfs_read,
882:    .write = regfs_write,
883:    .create = regfs_create,
884:    .list = regfs_list,
885:    .unlink = regfs_unlink,
886:};
887:
888:/* registry_mount_vfs - mount the registry as the "/reg" namespace.  Call from
889: * the composition root after vfs_init() + registry_init(). */
890:void registry_mount_vfs(void) {
891:  /* /reg is the VFS door onto the registry.  If it does not mount, that door
892:   * silently disappears while SYS_REGISTRY keeps working — the two paths stop
893:   * agreeing, which is precisely the divergence R2 exists to remove. */
894:  if (vfs_mount_at("/reg", &regfs_ops, NULL) != 0)
895:    pr_err("%s", "registry: /reg could not be mounted — the VFS door onto the "
896:                 "registry is absent while the syscall door still works\n");
897:}
898:
899:/*
900: * sys_registry - syscall handler for registry access (syscall 250).
901: *
902: * Mediates userland access via secure user-space copy helpers; all pointer
903: * arguments are validated through vmm before any data is consumed.
904: *
905: * REG_OP_ENUM: 'key' is an OPTIONAL namespace prefix (NULL = all keys).  Reads
906: *   are open to everyone.
907: * REG_OP_WRITE: needs CAP_REG_WRITE; carries the caller's identity (PID, or 0
908: *   for machine/system) into registry_set() for first-writer-wins ownership.
909: * REG_OP_READ: copies the value back (open to everyone).
910: *
911: * Returns 0 on success; negative errno on failure; -EINVAL on unknown op.
912: */
913:long sys_registry(int op, const char *key, char *value, size_t size) {
914:  char k_key[MAX_KEY_LEN];
915:  char k_val[MAX_VAL_LEN];
916:
917:  if (op == REG_OP_ENUM) {
918:    /* LIB-REG-04: enumerate keys into the user 'value' buffer.  Reads are open
919:     * to everyone (no capability required).  Phase 4.1 A1a: 'key' is an
920:     * OPTIONAL namespace prefix (NULL lists all keys — the legacy behaviour).
921:     */
922:    if (!value || size == 0)
923:      return -EINVAL;
924:    char k_prefix[MAX_KEY_LEN];
925:    const char *prefix = NULL;
926:    if (key) {
927:      if (vmm_copy_string_from_user(k_prefix, key, MAX_KEY_LEN) != 0)
928:        return -EFAULT;
929:      prefix = k_prefix;
930:    }
931:    size_t cap = size > 4096 ? 4096 : size;
932:    char *kbuf = kmalloc(cap);
933:    if (!kbuf)
934:      return -ENOMEM;
935:    int n = registry_enum(prefix, kbuf, cap);
936:    long ret;
937:    if (n < 0) {
938:      ret = -EINVAL;
939:    } else {
940:      size_t clen = (size_t)n + 1; /* include the NUL */
941:      if (clen > cap)
942:        clen = cap;
943:      ret = (vmm_copy_to_user(value, kbuf, clen) != 0) ? -EFAULT : (long)n;
944:    }
945:    kfree(kbuf);
946:    return ret;
947:  }
948:
949:  /* 1. Copy the key from user space.  STRICT: a truncated key is a DIFFERENT
950:   * key, so the write would land somewhere the matching read never looks —
951:   * a silent miss rather than a reported failure.  Refuse instead
952:   * (kernel/hal_uaccess.h explains why the tolerant form still exists). */
953:  {
954:    int r = vmm_copy_string_from_user_strict(k_key, key, MAX_KEY_LEN);
955:    if (r == -E2BIG) {
956:      pr_warn("registry: key longer than %d bytes refused (not truncated)\n",
957:              MAX_KEY_LEN - 1);
958:      return -E2BIG;
959:    }
960:    if (r != 0) {
961:      pr_err("%s", "sys_registry: Invalid key pointer\n");
962:      return -EFAULT;
963:    }
964:  }
965:
966:  if (op == REG_OP_WRITE) {
967:    /* 2. Copy the value.  STRICT for the same reason as the key, and it matters
968:     * most here: a truncated VALUE is reported as a successful write, so the
969:     * caller believes it stored something it did not.  This bit every registry
970:     * write over MAX_VAL_LEN, not just the environment — the environment is
971:     * simply the first consumer with values long enough to hit it. */
972:    {
973:      int r = vmm_copy_string_from_user_strict(k_val, value, MAX_VAL_LEN);
974:      if (r == -E2BIG) {
975:        pr_warn("registry: value for '%s' longer than %d bytes refused\n",
976:                k_key, MAX_VAL_LEN - 1);
977:        return -E2BIG;
978:      }
979:      if (r != 0) {
980:        pr_err("%s", "sys_registry: Invalid value pointer\n");
981:        return -EFAULT;
982:      }
983:    }
984:    /* USR-SEC-03 #79: writing the registry needs CAP_REG_WRITE (reads are open
985:     * to everyone) — EXCEPT for a virtual per-process key, which carries its
986:     * own authority rule (R2: the key decides, not the door).  The routing
987:     * itself now lives in registry_set, so this path no longer duplicates it.
988:     */
989:    if (!registry_key_is_virtual(k_key) && !registry_write_allowed())
990:      return -EPERM;
991:    return registry_set(k_key, k_val, registry_caller_owner());
992:  } else if (op == REG_OP_READ) {
993:    if (registry_get(k_key, k_val, sizeof(k_val)) == 0) {
994:      /* 3. Copy Result to User Space securely */
995:      size_t copy_len = strlen(k_val) + 1;
996:      if (copy_len > size)
997:        copy_len = size;
998:
999:      if (vmm_copy_to_user(value, k_val, copy_len) != 0) {
1000:        pr_err("%s", "sys_registry: Failed to copy back to user\n");
1001:        return -EFAULT;
1002:      }
1003:      return 0;
1004:    }
1005:    return -ENOENT;
1006:  } else if (op == REG_OP_DEL) {
1007:    /* Deleting needs CAP_REG_WRITE — except for a virtual key, which is
1008:     * unsetenv and unprivileged (R2).  registry_del does the routing. */
1009:    if (!registry_key_is_virtual(k_key) && !registry_write_allowed())
1010:      return -EPERM;
1011:    return registry_del(k_key, registry_caller_owner());
1012:  }
1013:
1014:  return -EINVAL; /* Invalid op */
1015:}
1016:

@@@ kernel/lib/sha256.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/lib/sha256.c
3: * SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4).  See kernel/include/kernel/sha256.h for the contract.
4: *
5: * BYTE-FOR-BYTE THE SAME ALGORITHM AS tools/mkdisk.c.  mkdisk computes the
6: * digests the kernel verifies, so a divergence here does not produce a "wrong
7: * hash" — it produces an image that fails its own integrity check on every
8: * boot, which looks like disk corruption.  Keep the two in step.
9: */
10:#include <kernel/sha256.h>
11:#include <kernel/string.h>
12:
13:static const uint32_t SHA256_K[64] = {
14:    0x428a2f98, 0x71374491, 0xb5c0fbcf, 0xe9b5dba5, 0x3956c25b, 0x59f111f1,
15:    0x923f82a4, 0xab1c5ed5, 0xd807aa98, 0x12835b01, 0x243185be, 0x550c7dc3,
16:    0x72be5d74, 0x80deb1fe, 0x9bdc06a7, 0xc19bf174, 0xe49b69c1, 0xefbe4786,
17:    0x0fc19dc6, 0x240ca1cc, 0x2de92c6f, 0x4a7484aa, 0x5cb0a9dc, 0x76f988da,
18:    0x983e5152, 0xa831c66d, 0xb00327c8, 0xbf597fc7, 0xc6e00bf3, 0xd5a79147,
19:    0x06ca6351, 0x14292967, 0x27b70a85, 0x2e1b2138, 0x4d2c6dfc, 0x53380d13,
20:    0x650a7354, 0x766a0abb, 0x81c2c92e, 0x92722c85, 0xa2bfe8a1, 0xa81a664b,
21:    0xc24b8b70, 0xc76c51a3, 0xd192e819, 0xd6990624, 0xf40e3585, 0x106aa070,
22:    0x19a4c116, 0x1e376c08, 0x2748774c, 0x34b0bcb5, 0x391c0cb3, 0x4ed8aa4a,
23:    0x5b9cca4f, 0x682e6ff3, 0x748f82ee, 0x78a5636f, 0x84c87814, 0x8cc70208,
24:    0x90befffa, 0xa4506ceb, 0xbef9a3f7, 0xc67178f2};
25:
26:#define SHA256_ROR(x, n) (((x) >> (n)) | ((x) << (32 - (n))))
27:
28:static void sha256_block(struct sha256_ctx *c, const uint8_t *p) {
29:  uint32_t w[64], a, b, cc, d, e, f, g, h;
30:  for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++)
31:    w[i] = ((uint32_t)p[i * 4] << 24) | ((uint32_t)p[i * 4 + 1] << 16) |
32:           ((uint32_t)p[i * 4 + 2] << 8) | (uint32_t)p[i * 4 + 3];
33:  for (int i = 16; i < 64; i++) {
34:    uint32_t s0 =
35:        SHA256_ROR(w[i - 15], 7) ^ SHA256_ROR(w[i - 15], 18) ^ (w[i - 15] >> 3);
36:    uint32_t s1 =
37:        SHA256_ROR(w[i - 2], 17) ^ SHA256_ROR(w[i - 2], 19) ^ (w[i - 2] >> 10);
38:    w[i] = w[i - 16] + s0 + w[i - 7] + s1;
39:  }
40:  a = c->h[0];
41:  b = c->h[1];
42:  cc = c->h[2];
43:  d = c->h[3];
44:  e = c->h[4];
45:  f = c->h[5];
46:  g = c->h[6];
47:  h = c->h[7];
48:  for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++) {
49:    uint32_t S1 = SHA256_ROR(e, 6) ^ SHA256_ROR(e, 11) ^ SHA256_ROR(e, 25);
50:    uint32_t ch = (e & f) ^ ((~e) & g);
51:    uint32_t t1 = h + S1 + ch + SHA256_K[i] + w[i];
52:    uint32_t S0 = SHA256_ROR(a, 2) ^ SHA256_ROR(a, 13) ^ SHA256_ROR(a, 22);
53:    uint32_t mj = (a & b) ^ (a & cc) ^ (b & cc);
54:    uint32_t t2 = S0 + mj;
55:    h = g;
56:    g = f;
57:    f = e;
58:    e = d + t1;
59:    d = cc;
60:    cc = b;
61:    b = a;
62:    a = t1 + t2;
63:  }
64:  c->h[0] += a;
65:  c->h[1] += b;
66:  c->h[2] += cc;
67:  c->h[3] += d;
68:  c->h[4] += e;
69:  c->h[5] += f;
70:  c->h[6] += g;
71:  c->h[7] += h;
72:}
73:
74:void sha256_init(struct sha256_ctx *c) {
75:  c->h[0] = 0x6a09e667;
76:  c->h[1] = 0xbb67ae85;
77:  c->h[2] = 0x3c6ef372;
78:  c->h[3] = 0xa54ff53a;
79:  c->h[4] = 0x510e527f;
80:  c->h[5] = 0x9b05688c;
81:  c->h[6] = 0x1f83d9ab;
82:  c->h[7] = 0x5be0cd19;
83:  c->len = 0;
84:  c->buflen = 0;
85:}
86:
87:void sha256_update(struct sha256_ctx *c, const void *data, size_t n) {
88:  const uint8_t *p = (const uint8_t *)data;
89:  c->len += n;
90:  while (n) {
91:    size_t take = 64 - c->buflen;
92:    if (take > n)
93:      take = n;
94:    memcpy(c->buf + c->buflen, p, take);
95:    c->buflen += take;
96:    p += take;
97:    n -= take;
98:    if (c->buflen == 64) {
99:      sha256_block(c, c->buf);
100:      c->buflen = 0;
101:    }
102:  }
103:}
104:
105:void sha256_final(struct sha256_ctx *c, uint8_t out[SHA256_DIGEST_SIZE]) {
106:  uint64_t bits = c->len * 8;
107:  uint8_t pad = 0x80;
108:  sha256_update(c, &pad, 1);
109:  uint8_t zero = 0;
110:  while (c->buflen != 56)
111:    sha256_update(c, &zero, 1);
112:  uint8_t lenbe[8];
113:  for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++)
114:    lenbe[i] = (uint8_t)(bits >> (56 - i * 8));
115:  sha256_update(c, lenbe, 8);
116:  for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
117:    out[i * 4] = (uint8_t)(c->h[i] >> 24);
118:    out[i * 4 + 1] = (uint8_t)(c->h[i] >> 16);
119:    out[i * 4 + 2] = (uint8_t)(c->h[i] >> 8);
120:    out[i * 4 + 3] = (uint8_t)c->h[i];
121:  }
122:}
123:
124:void sha256_buf(const void *data, size_t n, uint8_t out[SHA256_DIGEST_SIZE]) {
125:  struct sha256_ctx c;
126:  sha256_init(&c);
127:  sha256_update(&c, data, n);
128:  sha256_final(&c, out);
129:}
130:
