131:void sha256_merkle_pair(const uint8_t left[SHA256_DIGEST_SIZE],
132:                        const uint8_t right[SHA256_DIGEST_SIZE],
133:                        uint8_t out[SHA256_DIGEST_SIZE]) {
134:  struct sha256_ctx c;
135:  sha256_init(&c);
136:  sha256_update(&c, left, SHA256_DIGEST_SIZE);
137:  sha256_update(&c, right, SHA256_DIGEST_SIZE);
138:  sha256_final(&c, out);
139:}
140:

@@@ kernel/lib/stack_protector.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/lib/stack_protector.c
3: * Stack smashing protection (SSP) support
4: *
5: * Purpose:
6: *   Provides the GCC/Clang SSP ABI symbols: __stack_chk_guard (the canary
7: *   value) and __stack_chk_fail (the failure handler invoked when the compiler-
8: *   inserted canary check detects a mismatch at function return).
9: *
10: * Role:
11: *   The compiler emits a prologue/epilogue for every function compiled with
12: *   -fstack-protector or -fstack-protector-strong:
13: *     Prologue: load __stack_chk_guard; push copy onto the stack.
14: *     Epilogue: compare stack copy with __stack_chk_guard; call
15: *               __stack_chk_fail() if different.
16: *   This file supplies both symbols.
17: *
18: * Canary value:
19: *   A stack canary sits between local variables and the saved frame pointer /
20: *   return address.  If a buffer overflow overwrites the return address, it
21: *   typically also clobbers the canary.  On return, the compiler-emitted check
22: *   detects the mismatch and calls __stack_chk_fail instead of returning to
23: *   the corrupted address.
24: *
25: * Known issues:
26: *   LIB-SSP-01  (W3 SECURITY)  __stack_chk_guard is a compile-time constant
27: *               (0x595e9fbd94fda766).  It is never read from a hardware entropy
28: *               source and never randomised at boot.  Any attacker who knows the
29: *               binary (or can guess the constant) can craft an overflow that
30: *               preserves the canary value, bypassing SSP entirely.  Fix: read
31: *               RNDR (AArch64) or RDRAND (AMD64) during early init and XOR the
32: *               result into __stack_chk_guard before any guarded function runs.
33: */
34:#include <kernel/entropy.h>
35:#include <kernel/printk.h>
36:#include <kernel/ssp.h>
37:#include <stdint.h>
38:
39:/* __stack_chk_guard - the canary value inserted by the compiler into protected
40: * stack frames.  GCC/Clang load this symbol by name; it must be a global.
41: * The compile-time value is a placeholder; stack_guard_init() reseeds it from a
42: * hardware/jitter entropy source before deep boot (LIB-SSP-01 / #71). */
43:uintptr_t __stack_chk_guard = 0x595e9fbd94fda766;
44:
45:/*
46: * stack_guard_init - reseed the SSP canary from per-arch entropy.
47: *
48: * Replaces the compile-time constant with arch_entropy_u64() so an attacker who
49: * knows the binary image cannot predict the canary.  The low byte is forced to
50: * 0x00 (the classic terminator-canary trick: a string-based overflow cannot
51: * write past the NUL without supplying a terminator), and an all-zero result is
52: * rejected so the guard is never trivially defeatable.
53: *
54: * Safety: this routine takes no address of a local and declares no array, so
55: * -fstack-protector-strong inserts no canary in its own frame; it can therefore
56: * mutate the global guard and return without tripping a stale-canary check.  It
57: * must run before any still-executing caller that captured the OLD canary in
58: * its prologue would reach its epilogue — see kernel/include/kernel/ssp.h.
59: */
60:void stack_guard_init(void) {
61:  uintptr_t g = (uintptr_t)entropy_u64();
62:  g &= ~(uintptr_t)0xff; /* terminator canary: NUL low byte */
63:  if (g == 0)
64:    g = 0x595e9fbd94fda700; /* never leave the guard all-zero */
65:  __stack_chk_guard = g;
66:  pr_info("%s", "SSP: stack canary reseeded from arch entropy\n");
67:}
68:
69:/* Forward declaration required before the definition because the compiler may
70: * insert a call to __stack_chk_fail inside its own prolog/epilog for this
71: * translation unit if it is also compiled with -fstack-protector. */
72:void __stack_chk_fail(void);
73:
74:/*
75: * __stack_chk_fail - called when the SSP canary check fails at function return.
76: *
77: * Captures the return address of the corrupted frame via __builtin_return_address(0)
78: * (which is the return address from __stack_chk_fail's caller, i.e., the address
79: * of the corrupted function's epilog), then calls panic() to print the site and
80: * halt all CPUs.
81: *
82: * This function does not return.  The panic message includes the return address
83: * to help identify which function was smashed.
84: *
85: * Locking: none; inherits panic()'s uart_lock acquisition.
86: * Side effects: halts the entire system.
87: */
88:void __stack_chk_fail(void) {
89:  uint64_t ret_addr = (uint64_t)__builtin_return_address(0);
90:  panic("SSP: Stack Smash at 0x%lx\n", ret_addr);
91:}
92:

@@@ kernel/lib/string.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/lib/string.c
3: * String manipulation functions
4: *
5: * Purpose:
6: *   Provides the complete set of in-kernel string and memory primitives used
7: *   by virtually every other kernel subsystem.  This file is a self-contained
8: *   replacement for the C standard library string functions; no libc is linked
9: *   into the kernel.
10: *
11: * Role:
12: *   - Consumed by kmalloc, printk, registry, vfs, fs, sched, and driver layers.
13: *   - Shared between amd64 and aarch64 builds; no arch-specific code is present.
14: *   - String functions that mirror POSIX semantics (strlen, strcpy, strcmp …)
15: *     are also re-exported to userland programs through include/api/string.h.
16: *
17: * Invariants:
18: *   - Every function that accepts a pointer checks it for NULL before
19: *     dereferencing.  Callers can safely pass NULL and receive a defined result
20: *     (0, NULL, or dest as appropriate) rather than a fault.
21: *   - No dynamic allocation is performed; no global state is modified.
22: *   - Operations are purely sequential byte-by-byte; no SIMD or hardware assist.
23: *
24: * Known issues:
25: *   None tracked for this file (see docs/review/analysis/07-lib-headers.md).
26: *   The implementations are correct, safe, and complete for the kernel's needs.
27: */
28:#include <kernel/string.h>
29:#include <kernel/types.h>
30:
31:/*
32: * strlen - return the number of bytes in a NUL-terminated string.
33: *
34: * Params: s - string pointer; may be NULL.
35: * Returns: byte count excluding the NUL terminator, or 0 if s is NULL.
36: * Locking: none; reads only the caller's memory.
37: */
38:size_t strlen(const char *s) {
39:  if (!s)
40:    return 0;
41:  const char *p = s;
42:  while (*p)
43:    p++;
44:  return p - s;
45:}
46:
47:/*
48: * strnlen - return the number of bytes in a string, up to maxlen.
49: *
50: * Params:
51: *   s      - string pointer; may be NULL.
52: *   maxlen - maximum number of bytes to examine.
53: * Returns: byte count (< maxlen) if a NUL is found, otherwise maxlen.
54: *          Returns 0 if s is NULL.
55: * Locking: none.
56: */
57:size_t strnlen(const char *s, size_t maxlen) {
58:  if (!s)
59:    return 0;
60:  const char *p = s;
61:  while (maxlen-- && *p)
62:    p++;
63:  return p - s;
64:}
65:
66:/*
67: * strcmp - lexicographically compare two NUL-terminated strings.
68: *
69: * Params:
70: *   s1, s2 - string pointers; either may be NULL.
71: * Returns:
72: *   0 if equal (or both NULL).
73: *   Positive if s1 > s2 (unsigned byte comparison).
74: *   Negative if s1 < s2.
75: *   If exactly one is NULL, non-NULL is treated as greater.
76: * Locking: none.
77: */
78:int strcmp(const char *s1, const char *s2) {
79:  if (!s1 || !s2)
80:    return (s1 == s2) ? 0 : (s1 ? 1 : -1);
81:  while (*s1 && *s1 == *s2) {
82:    s1++;
83:    s2++;
84:  }
85:  return (unsigned char)*s1 - (unsigned char)*s2;
86:}
87:
88:/*
89: * strncmp - lexicographically compare at most n bytes of two strings.
90: *
91: * Params:
92: *   s1, s2 - string pointers; either may be NULL.
93: *   n      - maximum number of bytes to compare.
94: * Returns: same sign semantics as strcmp; 0 if n is 0.
95: *          NULL handling matches strcmp.
96: * Locking: none.
97: */
98:int strncmp(const char *s1, const char *s2, size_t n) {
99:  if (n == 0)
100:    return 0;
101:  if (!s1 || !s2)
102:    return (s1 == s2) ? 0 : (s1 ? 1 : -1);
103:  while (n-- > 1 && *s1 && *s1 == *s2) {
104:    s1++;
105:    s2++;
106:  }
107:  return (unsigned char)*s1 - (unsigned char)*s2;
108:}
109:
110:/*
111: * strcpy - copy a NUL-terminated string, including the NUL terminator.
112: *
113: * Params:
114: *   dest - destination buffer; caller is responsible for sufficient size.
115: *   src  - source string; may be NULL (returns dest unchanged).
116: * Returns: dest.
117: * Locking: none.
118: * Side effects: writes to dest.
119: */
120:char *strcpy(char *dest, const char *src) {
121:  if (!dest || !src)
122:    return dest;
123:  char *d = dest;
124:  while ((*d++ = *src++) != '\0')
125:    ;
126:  return dest;
127:}
128:
129:/*
130: * strncpy - copy at most n bytes from src to dest, zero-padding to n.
131: *
132: * Params:
133: *   dest - destination buffer of at least n bytes.
134: *   src  - source string; may be NULL (returns dest unchanged).
135: *   n    - bytes to write; if src is shorter, remaining bytes are zeroed.
136: * Returns: dest.
137: * Locking: none.
138: * Note: result is NOT guaranteed NUL-terminated if strlen(src) >= n.
139: *       Prefer strlcpy for safe, always-NUL-terminated copies.
140: */
141:char *strncpy(char *dest, const char *src, size_t n) {
142:  if (!dest || !src || n == 0)
143:    return dest;
144:  char *d = dest;
145:  while (n > 0) {
146:    n--;
147:    if ((*d++ = *src++) == '\0')
148:      break;
149:  }
150:  while (n > 0) {
151:    n--;
152:    *d++ = '\0';
153:  }
154:  return dest;
155:}
156:
157:/*
158: * strlcpy - copy string into a fixed-size buffer with guaranteed NUL termination.
159: *
160: * Copies at most (size - 1) characters from src to dest and always appends
161: * a NUL terminator (if size > 0).
162: *
163: * Params:
164: *   dest - destination buffer of exactly 'size' bytes.
165: *   src  - source string (NUL-terminated); length is measured via strlen.
166: *   size - total capacity of dest (including the NUL slot).
167: * Returns: strlen(src) — callers can detect truncation by comparing the return
168: *          value against size - 1.
169: * Locking: none.
170: */
171:size_t strlcpy(char *dest, const char *src, size_t size) {
172:  size_t len = strlen(src);
173:  if (size > 0) {
174:    size_t n = (len >= size) ? size - 1 : len;
175:    memcpy(dest, src, n);
176:    dest[n] = '\0';
177:  }
178:  return len;
179:}
180:
181:/*
182: * strcat - append src to dest (dest must be NUL-terminated on entry).
183: *
184: * Params:
185: *   dest - destination NUL-terminated string; must have space for strlen(src)+1.
186: *   src  - source string; may be NULL (returns dest unchanged).
187: * Returns: dest.
188: * Locking: none.
189: * Note: no bounds check; prefer strlcat.
190: */
191:char *strcat(char *dest, const char *src) {
192:  if (!dest || !src)
193:    return dest;
194:  char *d = dest;
195:  while (*d)
196:    d++;
197:  while ((*d++ = *src++) != '\0')
198:    ;
199:  return dest;
200:}
201:
202:/*
203: * strncat - append at most n bytes of src to dest.
204: *
205: * Params:
206: *   dest - NUL-terminated destination string; must have at least n+1 spare bytes.
207: *   src  - source string; may be NULL (returns dest unchanged).
208: *   n    - maximum bytes to append from src (not counting added NUL).
209: * Returns: dest.
210: * Locking: none.
211: * Note: the post-loop `if (n == (size_t)-1) *d = '\0'` handles the case where
212: *       src ended inside the n-byte window (the inner loop consumed the NUL but
213: *       n reached SIZE_MAX after underflow); ensures dest is always NUL-terminated.
214: */
215:char *strncat(char *dest, const char *src, size_t n) {
216:  if (!dest || !src)
217:    return dest;
218:  char *d = dest;
219:  while (*d)
220:    d++;
221:  while (n-- && (*d++ = *src++) != '\0')
222:    ;
223:  if (n == (size_t)-1)
224:    *d = '\0';
225:  return dest;
226:}
227:
228:/*
229: * strlcat - append src to dest with a bound on dest's total size.
230: *
231: * Appends as much of src as fits within size bytes total (including the
232: * existing content and the NUL terminator).
233: *
234: * Params:
235: *   dest - NUL-terminated destination buffer of capacity 'size'.
236: *   src  - source string (NUL-terminated).
237: *   size - total capacity of dest (including NUL).
238: * Returns: dlen + strlen(src) — callers can detect truncation by comparing
239: *          against size - 1.
240: * Locking: none.
241: */
242:size_t strlcat(char *dest, const char *src, size_t size) {
243:  size_t dlen = strnlen(dest, size);
244:  size_t slen = strlen(src);
245:  if (dlen < size) {
246:    strlcpy(dest + dlen, src, size - dlen);
247:  }
248:  return dlen + slen;
249:}
250:
251:/*
252: * strchr - find the first occurrence of character c in string s.
253: *
254: * Params:
255: *   s - NUL-terminated string; may be NULL (returns NULL).
256: *   c - character to locate (compared as unsigned char); '\0' is valid.
257: * Returns: pointer to first matching byte, or NULL if not found.
258: *          If c == '\0', returns a pointer to the NUL terminator.
259: * Locking: none.
260: */
261:char *strchr(const char *s, int c) {
262:  if (!s)
263:    return NULL;
264:  while (*s) {
265:    if (*s == (char)c)
266:      return (char *)s;
267:    s++;
268:  }
269:  return (c == '\0') ? (char *)s : NULL;
270:}
271:
272:/*
273: * strrchr - find the last occurrence of character c in string s.
274: *
275: * Params:
276: *   s - NUL-terminated string; may be NULL (returns NULL).
277: *   c - character to locate (compared as unsigned char); '\0' is valid.
278: * Returns: pointer to last matching byte, or NULL if not found.
279: *          If c == '\0', returns a pointer to the NUL terminator.
280: * Locking: none.
281: */
282:char *strrchr(const char *s, int c) {
283:  if (!s)
284:    return NULL;
285:  const char *last = NULL;
286:  while (*s) {
287:    if (*s == (char)c)
288:      last = s;
289:    s++;
290:  }
291:  return (c == '\0') ? (char *)s : (char *)last;
292:}
293:
294:/*
295: * strstr - locate the first occurrence of needle within haystack.
296: *
297: * Uses a naive O(m*n) sliding-window scan; adequate for kernel use where
298: * both strings are short.
299: *
300: * Params:
301: *   haystack - string to search; may be NULL (returns NULL).
302: *   needle   - pattern to locate; may be NULL (returns NULL).
303: * Returns: pointer to first occurrence, or NULL if not found.
304: *          If needle is empty, returns haystack.
305: * Locking: none.
306: */
307:char *strstr(const char *haystack, const char *needle) {
308:  if (!haystack || !needle)
309:    return NULL;
310:  size_t n = strlen(needle);
311:  if (n == 0)
312:    return (char *)haystack;
313:  while (*haystack) {
314:    if (memcmp(haystack, needle, n) == 0)
315:      return (char *)haystack;
316:    haystack++;
317:  }
318:  return NULL;
319:}
320:
321:/*
322: * memset - fill n bytes of memory starting at s with byte value c.
323: *
324: * Params:
325: *   s - pointer to memory region; may be NULL (returns s immediately).
326: *   c - byte value to fill (low 8 bits used).
327: *   n - number of bytes to fill.
328: * Returns: s.
329: * Locking: none.
330: * Side effects: writes n bytes at s.
331: */
332:void *memset(void *s, int c, size_t n) {
333:  if (!s)
334:    return s;
335:  unsigned char *p = s;
336:  while (n--)
337:    *p++ = (unsigned char)c;
338:  return s;
339:}
340:
341:/*
342: * memcpy - copy n bytes from src to dest (regions must NOT overlap).
343: *
344: * Params:
345: *   dest - destination pointer; may be NULL (returns dest immediately).
346: *   src  - source pointer; may be NULL (returns dest immediately).
347: *   n    - number of bytes to copy.
348: * Returns: dest.
349: * Locking: none.
350: * Side effects: writes n bytes at dest.
351: * Note: for overlapping regions use memmove.
352: */
353:void *memcpy(void *dest, const void *src, size_t n) {
354:  if (!dest || !src)
355:    return dest;
356:  unsigned char *d = dest;
357:  const unsigned char *s = src;
358:  while (n--)
359:    *d++ = *s++;
360:  return dest;
361:}
362:
363:/*
364: * memmove - copy n bytes from src to dest, handling overlapping regions.
365: *
366: * If dest < src, copies forward (same as memcpy).
367: * If dest > src, copies backward to avoid clobbering src bytes before they
368: * are read (handles the d > s overlap direction correctly).
369: *
370: * Params:
371: *   dest - destination pointer; may be NULL (returns dest immediately).
372: *   src  - source pointer; may be NULL (returns dest immediately).
373: *   n    - number of bytes to copy.
374: * Returns: dest.
375: * Locking: none.
376: * Side effects: writes n bytes at dest.
377: */
378:void *memmove(void *dest, const void *src, size_t n) {
379:  if (!dest || !src)
380:    return dest;
381:  unsigned char *d = dest;
382:  const unsigned char *s = src;
383:
384:  if (d < s) {
385:    /* Forward copy: safe when dest is before src or ranges do not overlap */
386:    while (n--)
387:      *d++ = *s++;
388:  } else {
389:    /* Backward copy: safe when dest is after src (prevents overwriting src) */
390:    d += n;
391:    s += n;
392:    while (n--)
393:      *--d = *--s;
394:  }
395:  return dest;
396:}
397:
398:/*
399: * memcmp - compare n bytes of two memory regions.
400: *
401: * Params:
402: *   s1, s2 - memory pointers; either may be NULL.
403: *   n      - number of bytes to compare.
404: * Returns:
405: *   0 if equal (or n is 0, or both NULL).
406: *   Positive if *s1 > *s2 at the first differing byte.
407: *   Negative if *s1 < *s2.
408: *   If exactly one is NULL, non-NULL is treated as greater.
409: * Locking: none.
410: */
411:int memcmp(const void *s1, const void *s2, size_t n) {
412:  if (n == 0)
413:    return 0;
414:  if (!s1 || !s2)
415:    return (s1 == s2) ? 0 : (s1 ? 1 : -1);
416:  const unsigned char *p1 = s1;
417:  const unsigned char *p2 = s2;
418:
419:  while (n--) {
420:    if (*p1 != *p2)
421:      return (int)*p1 - (int)*p2;
422:    p1++;
423:    p2++;
424:  }
425:  return 0;
426:}
427:
428:/*
429: * memchr - locate the first byte equal to c within the first n bytes of s.
430: *
431: * Params:
432: *   s - memory region; may be NULL (returns NULL).
433: *   c - byte value to search for (low 8 bits used).
434: *   n - number of bytes to scan.
435: * Returns: pointer to first matching byte, or NULL if not found.
436: * Locking: none.
437: */
438:void *memchr(const void *s, int c, size_t n) {
439:  if (!s)
440:    return NULL;
441:  const unsigned char *p = s;
442:  while (n--) {
443:    if (*p == (unsigned char)c)
444:      return (void *)p;
445:    p++;
446:  }
447:  return NULL;
448:}
449:
450:/*
451: * bzero - zero n bytes of memory at s (BSD compatibility wrapper for memset).
452: *
453: * Params:
454: *   s - pointer to memory region; if NULL, does nothing.
455: *   n - number of bytes to zero.
456: * Locking: none.
457: */
458:void bzero(void *s, size_t n) {
459:  if (s)
460:    memset(s, 0, n);
461:}
462:
463:/* to_lower - convert ASCII uppercase letter to lowercase; leaves others unchanged.
464: * Internal helper for strcasecmp / strncasecmp only. */
465:static int to_lower(int c) {
466:  if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z')
467:    return c + ('a' - 'A');
468:  return c;
469:}
470:
471:/*
472: * strcasecmp - case-insensitive string comparison (ASCII only).
473: *
474: * Params:
475: *   s1, s2 - strings to compare; either may be NULL.
476: * Returns: 0 if equal (ignoring case), positive/negative per strcmp semantics.
477: *          NULL handling matches strcmp.
478: * Locking: none.
479: */
480:int strcasecmp(const char *s1, const char *s2) {
481:  if (!s1 || !s2)
482:    return (s1 == s2) ? 0 : (s1 ? 1 : -1);
483:  while (*s1 && *s2) {
484:    if (to_lower((unsigned char)*s1) != to_lower((unsigned char)*s2))
485:      break;
486:    s1++;
487:    s2++;
488:  }
489:  return to_lower((unsigned char)*s1) - to_lower((unsigned char)*s2);
490:}
491:
492:/*
493: * strncasecmp - case-insensitive comparison of at most n bytes (ASCII only).
494: *
495: * Params:
496: *   s1, s2 - strings to compare; either may be NULL.
497: *   n      - maximum number of bytes to compare.
498: * Returns: 0 if equal, positive/negative per strcmp semantics; 0 if n is 0.
499: * Locking: none.
500: */
501:int strncasecmp(const char *s1, const char *s2, size_t n) {
502:  if (n == 0)
503:    return 0;
504:  if (!s1 || !s2)
505:    return (s1 == s2) ? 0 : (s1 ? 1 : -1);
506:  while (n-- > 1 && *s1 && *s2) {
507:    if (to_lower((unsigned char)*s1) != to_lower((unsigned char)*s2))
508:      break;
509:    s1++;
510:    s2++;
511:  }
512:  return to_lower((unsigned char)*s1) - to_lower((unsigned char)*s2);
513:}
514:
515:/*
516: * atoi - convert the leading decimal digits of s to an int.
517: *
518: * Skips leading whitespace, handles an optional leading '+' or '-'.
519: * Stops at the first non-digit character.  No overflow detection.
520: *
521: * Params:
522: *   s - input string; may be NULL (returns 0).
523: * Returns: integer value, or 0 on empty/NULL input.
524: * Locking: none.
525: */
526:int atoi(const char *s) {
527:  if (!s)
528:    return 0;
529:  int res = 0;
530:  int sign = 1;
531:  while (*s == ' ')
532:    s++;
533:  if (*s == '-') {
534:    sign = -1;
535:    s++;
536:  } else if (*s == '+') {
537:    s++;
538:  }
539:  int int_max = 2147483647;
540:  int int_min = -2147483648;
541:  while (*s >= '0' && *s <= '9') {
542:    int digit = *s - '0';
543:    if (res > (int_max - digit) / 10) return (sign > 0) ? int_max : int_min;
544:    res = res * 10 + digit;
545:    s++;
546:  }
547:  return res * sign;
548:}

@@@ kernel/lib/utf8.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/lib/utf8.c
3: * UTF-8 Decoder
4: *
5: * Purpose:
6: *   Decodes a single UTF-8 character sequence into its Unicode code point.
7: *   Used by the graphics / font rendering layer to iterate over multi-byte
8: *   text strings.
9: *
10: * Role:
11: *   Called from the font renderer (kernel/graphics/font.c) to step through
12: *   UTF-8 encoded strings one code point at a time.
13: *
14: * Supported encodings:
15: *   1-byte  U+0000 .. U+007F     (c < 0x80)
16: *   2-byte  U+0080 .. U+07FF     ((c & 0xE0) == 0xC0)
17: *   3-byte  U+0800 .. U+FFFF     ((c & 0xF0) == 0xE0)
18: *   4-byte  U+10000 .. U+10FFFF  ((c & 0xF8) == 0xF0)
19: *
20: * Invariants:
21: *   - Continuation bytes in multi-byte sequences are validated against the
22: *     0x80 pattern (high bit set, bit 6 clear) on all paths.
23: *   - Returns 0 (error) for invalid lead bytes or bad continuation bytes.
24: *
25: * Known issues:
26: *   LIB-UTF8-01  (W2 SECURITY)  Continuation bytes s[1], s[2], s[3] are read
27: *                without knowing the string length.  If 's' points to a buffer
28: *                whose remaining content is shorter than the sequence claims
29: *                (e.g. a partial 3-byte sequence at end of a non-NUL-terminated
30: *                buffer), up to 3 bytes beyond the valid data are read.
31: *   LIB-UTF8-02  (W1 MISSING)   Overlong encodings (e.g. U+0000 as 0xC0 0x80),
32: *                surrogate pairs (U+D800..U+DFFF), and values > U+10FFFF are
33: *                accepted and decoded rather than rejected.
34: */
35:#include <kernel/types.h>
36:#include <kernel/graphics.h>
37:
38:/*
39: * utf8_decode - decode one UTF-8 code point from the string starting at 's'.
40: *
41: * Examines the lead byte s[0] to determine the sequence length, validates
42: * continuation bytes, assembles the code point, and returns the number of
43: * bytes consumed.
44: *
45: * NOTE(LIB-UTF8-01): reads s[1..3] without a length bound; the caller must
46: *   ensure that 's' points to a NUL-terminated string with at least 4 readable
47: *   bytes beyond s[0] if the text may contain multi-byte sequences.
48: * NOTE(LIB-UTF8-02): does not reject overlong encodings, surrogates, or
49: *   code points above U+10FFFF.
50: *
51: * Params:
52: *   s    - pointer to the start of a UTF-8 sequence; must not be NULL.
53: *   code - output pointer; receives the decoded Unicode code point on success.
54: *          Must not be NULL.
55: * Returns: number of bytes consumed (1–4) on success; 0 on error (NULL args,
56: *          invalid lead byte, or bad continuation byte).
57: * Locking: none (stateless).
58: */
59:int utf8_decode(const char *s, size_t len, uint32_t *code) {
60:  if (!s || !code || len == 0) return 0;
61:  unsigned char c = (unsigned char)s[0];
62:
63:  if (c < 0x80) {
64:    /* 1-byte ASCII sequence: U+0000..U+007F */
65:    *code = c;
66:    return 1;
67:  } else if ((c & 0xE0) == 0xC0) {
68:    /* 2-byte sequence: U+0080..U+07FF */
69:    if (len < 2 || (s[1] & 0xC0) != 0x80) return 0;
70:    *code = ((uint32_t)(c & 0x1F) << 6) | (uint32_t)(s[1] & 0x3F);
71:    if (*code < 0x80) return 0;
72:    return 2;
73:  } else if ((c & 0xF0) == 0xE0) {
74:    /* 3-byte sequence: U+0800..U+FFFF */
75:    if (len < 3 || (s[1] & 0xC0) != 0x80 || (s[2] & 0xC0) != 0x80) return 0;
76:    *code = ((uint32_t)(c & 0x0F) << 12) | ((uint32_t)(s[1] & 0x3F) << 6) | (uint32_t)(s[2] & 0x3F);
77:    if (*code < 0x800) return 0;
78:    if (*code >= 0xD800 && *code <= 0xDFFF) return 0;
79:    return 3;
80:  } else if ((c & 0xF8) == 0xF0) {
81:    /* 4-byte sequence: U+10000..U+10FFFF */
82:    if (len < 4 || (s[1] & 0xC0) != 0x80 || (s[2] & 0xC0) != 0x80 || (s[3] & 0xC0) != 0x80) return 0;
83:    *code = ((uint32_t)(c & 0x07) << 18) | ((uint32_t)(s[1] & 0x3F) << 12) |
84:            ((uint32_t)(s[2] & 0x3F) << 6) | (uint32_t)(s[3] & 0x3F);
85:    if (*code < 0x10000) return 0;
86:    if (*code > 0x10FFFF) return 0;
87:    return 4;
88:  }
89:  /* Invalid lead byte (e.g. continuation byte used as lead, or 0xFF/0xFE) */
90:  return 0;
91:}
92:

@@@ kernel/lib/vsnprintf.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/lib/vsnprintf.c
3: * Bounded formatted string output (vsnprintf)
4: *
5: * Purpose:
6: *   Implements vsnprintf() — the single formatted-output primitive used by
7: *   printk(), snprintf(), and (via the userland build path) the os1 user library.
8: *   All other formatted-output functions in the kernel are thin wrappers over
9: *   this one.
10: *
11: * Role:
12: *   This file is compiled in both kernel and userland modes:
13: *     - KERNEL defined: pulls in kernel/printk.h and kernel/types.h.
14: *     - KERNEL not defined: pulls in os1.h (userland).
15: *   The same translation unit therefore serves both contexts.
16: *
17: * Supported specifiers:
18: *   %c  %s  %d/%i  %u  %x/%X  %p  %%
19: *   Length modifiers: l, ll, z.
20: *   Flags: - (left-align), + (force sign), ' ' (space sign), # (alternate),
21: *          0 (zero-pad).
22: *   Width: decimal field width, or '*' to take it from an int argument (C99);
23: *          a negative '*' width means left-justify with its magnitude.
24: *   Precision: decimal precision, or '.*' to take it from an int argument (C99);
25: *          a negative '*' precision means "no precision".  For %s this bounds
26: *          the copy, so '%.*s' is safe and does not read past the argument.
27: *
28: * Invariants:
29: *   - Every write path guards `written < (int)size - 1` before writing.
30: *   - buf[written] = '\0' is always written at exit (NUL termination).
31: *   - No %n specifier is implemented (security: no arbitrary memory write).
32: *
33: * Known issues:
34: *   LIB-VSNPRINTF-01  (W1 BUG)     Sign char emitted without decrementing width;
35: *                                   %05d of -42 produces "-00042" (6 chars) not
36: *                                   "-0042".  See print_num().
37: *   LIB-VSNPRINTF-02  (W1 REFINE)  Returns chars written, not would-be length;
38: *                                   callers cannot detect truncation. See vsnprintf.
39: *   LIB-VSNPRINTF-03  (W0 MISSING) %o (octal) and %e/%f (float) are absent.
40: *   LIB-VSNPRINTF-04  (W1 BAD-IMPL) %p hardcodes 16-digit width regardless of
41: *                                   remaining buffer space.  See case 'p'.
42: */
43:#ifdef KERNEL
44:#include <kernel/printk.h>
45:#include <kernel/types.h>
46:#else
47:#include <os1.h>
48:#endif
49:#include <stdarg.h>
50:
51:/* Number conversion flags — bit-mask used by print_num() and the vsnprintf loop.
52: * FLAG_ZEROPAD:   '0' flag: pad with '0' instead of ' ' when right-aligned.
53: * FLAG_LEFT:      '-' flag: left-justify (overrides FLAG_ZEROPAD).
54: * FLAG_PLUS:      '+' flag: always emit sign character even for non-negative.
55: * FLAG_SPACE:     ' ' flag: prefix with a space for non-negative numbers.
56: * FLAG_SPECIAL:   '#' flag: parsed but has no effect in the current implementation.
57: * FLAG_UPPERCASE: uppercase hex digits (A-F); set for %X specifier.
58: * FLAG_SIGN:      internal flag: set when the value is negative; causes '-' output.
59: */
60:#define FLAG_ZEROPAD   0x01
61:#define FLAG_LEFT      0x02
62:#define FLAG_PLUS      0x04
63:#define FLAG_SPACE     0x08
64:#define FLAG_SPECIAL   0x10
65:#define FLAG_UPPERCASE 0x20
66:#define FLAG_SIGN      0x40
67:
68:/*
69: * print_num - format an unsigned integer into buf in the given base.
70: *
71: * Digits are accumulated in reverse into tmp[], then written forward.
72: * Padding and sign/prefix characters are inserted between the width padding
73: * and the digit string in the following order:
74: *   [space padding] [sign or space] [zero padding] [digits] [left padding]
75: *
76: * Params:
77: *   buf       - output buffer; write starts at buf[0].
78: *   size      - remaining capacity of buf including NUL slot.
79: *   num       - value to format (always unsigned at this point; sign already
80: *               extracted by the caller and encoded in flags).
81: *   base      - numeric base: 10 or 16.
82: *   width     - minimum field width; 0 means no minimum.
83: *   precision - minimum digit count (zero-pad with '0'); -1 means no minimum.
84: *   flags     - bitwise OR of FLAG_* constants above.
85: * Returns: number of characters written to buf (never writes NUL).
86: * Locking: none (stateless aside from static digit tables).
87: *
88: * NOTE(LIB-VSNPRINTF-01): width is decremented by the digit count (i) before
89: *   the sign character is emitted.  When FLAG_ZEROPAD is set, the sign is
90: *   written first and then zero-padding fills width characters.  But width was
91: *   already reduced by the digit count only — not by 1 for the sign char — so
92: *   total output is (sign + width zeros + digits), which is one character more
93: *   than the requested field width.  Example: print_num(..., -42, 10, 5, -1,
94: *   FLAG_ZEROPAD|FLAG_SIGN) emits "-00042" (6 chars) instead of "-0042".
95: */
96:static int print_num(char *buf, size_t size, uint64_t num, int base, int width, int precision, int flags) {
97:    static const char digits_lower[] = "0123456789abcdef";
98:    static const char digits_upper[] = "0123456789ABCDEF";
99:    const char *digits = (flags & FLAG_UPPERCASE) ? digits_upper : digits_lower;
100:
101:    char tmp[66];
102:    int i = 0;
103:    int written = 0;
104:    int needed = 0;
105:
106:    if (num == 0) {
107:        tmp[i++] = '0';
108:    } else {
109:        while (num != 0) {
110:            tmp[i++] = digits[num % base];
111:            num /= base;
112:        }
113:    }
114:
115:    while (i < precision && i < 64) {
116:        tmp[i++] = '0';
117:    }
118:
119:    width -= i;
120:    if (flags & (FLAG_SIGN | FLAG_PLUS | FLAG_SPACE)) {
121:        width--;
122:    }
123:
124:    if (!(flags & (FLAG_ZEROPAD | FLAG_LEFT))) {
125:        while (width > 0) {
126:            if (written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = ' ';
127:            needed++;
128:            width--;
129:        }
130:    }
131:
132:    if (flags & FLAG_SIGN) {
133:        if (written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = '-';
134:        needed++;
135:    } else if (flags & FLAG_PLUS) {
136:        if (written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = '+';
137:        needed++;
138:    } else if (flags & FLAG_SPACE) {
139:        if (written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = ' ';
140:        needed++;
141:    }
142:
143:    if (flags & FLAG_ZEROPAD) {
144:        while (width > 0) {
145:            if (written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = '0';
146:            needed++;
147:            width--;
148:        }
149:    }
150:
151:    while (i > 0) {
152:        if (written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = tmp[--i];
153:        else i--;
154:        needed++;
155:    }
156:
157:    if (flags & FLAG_LEFT) {
158:        while (width > 0) {
159:            if (written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = ' ';
160:            needed++;
161:            width--;
162:        }
163:    }
164:
165:    return needed;
166:}
167:
168:#ifndef KERNEL
169:/*
170: * Floating-point conversion (%f/%F, %e/%E, %g/%G) — USERLAND ONLY.
171: *
172: * The kernel build (KERNEL defined) is compiled FPU-free and never formats
173: * a double (LIB-VSNPRINTF-03), so this whole block is excluded there: no
174: * floating-point code lands in the kernel image, no FPU save/restore is
175: * implied.  The userland os1 library, by contrast, backs Lua's number->string
176: * path (LUAI_NUMFFORMAT "%.14g", string.format("%g"/"%f"/"%e", ...)): without
177: * this, every such conversion fell through to the default case and emitted the
178: * literal spec ("%g"), corrupting all Lua numeric output.
179: *
180: * Digits come from double arithmetic only (no libm dependency): ~15-16
181: * significant decimal digits are reliable, which covers Lua's 14-digit %g.
182: */
183:
184:/*
185: * fp_gen - generate `ndigits` rounded significant decimal digits of value>0.
186: *   digs[]    receives ndigits chars '0'..'9' (digs[0] most significant);
187: *   *decexp   receives the base-10 exponent of the first digit, i.e.
188: *             value ~= digs[0].digs[1..] x 10^(*decexp).
189: * ndigits is clamped to [1,17].  Rounding is half-up on the guard digit and
190: * carries all the way (all-nines rollover bumps *decexp).
191: */
192:static void fp_gen(double value, int ndigits, char *digs, int *decexp) {
193:    if (ndigits < 1) ndigits = 1;
194:    if (ndigits > 17) ndigits = 17;
195:
196:    int e = 0;
197:    double v = value;
198:    while (v >= 10.0) { v /= 10.0; e++; }
199:    while (v < 1.0)   { v *= 10.0; e--; }
200:
201:    int d[19]; /* ndigits (<=17) + one guard digit */
202:    for (int i = 0; i <= ndigits; i++) {
203:        int digit = (int)v;
204:        if (digit < 0) digit = 0; else if (digit > 9) digit = 9;
205:        d[i] = digit;
206:        v = (v - (double)digit) * 10.0;
207:    }
208:
209:    int carry = (d[ndigits] >= 5) ? 1 : 0;
210:    for (int i = ndigits - 1; i >= 0 && carry; i--) {
211:        d[i] += 1;
212:        if (d[i] == 10) { d[i] = 0; carry = 1; } else carry = 0;
213:    }
214:    if (carry) { /* 9.999.. rounded to 10.000..: shift and bump the exponent */
215:        for (int i = ndigits - 1; i > 0; i--) d[i] = d[i - 1];
216:        d[0] = 1;
217:        e++;
218:    }
219:    for (int i = 0; i < ndigits; i++) digs[i] = (char)('0' + d[i]);
220:    *decexp = e;
221:}
222:
223:/* Append the exponent suffix (e/E +/- NN, at least two digits) to out[n..]. */
224:static int fp_exp(char *out, int n, int decexp, int upper) {
225:    out[n++] = upper ? 'E' : 'e';
226:    int ex = decexp;
227:    if (ex < 0) { out[n++] = '-'; ex = -ex; } else out[n++] = '+';
228:    char eb[8];
229:    int en = 0;
230:    if (ex == 0) eb[en++] = '0';
231:    while (ex > 0) { eb[en++] = (char)('0' + ex % 10); ex /= 10; }
232:    while (en < 2) eb[en++] = '0';
233:    while (en > 0) out[n++] = eb[--en];
234:    return n;
235:}
236:
237:/*
238: * fp_format - render `value` into out[] (NUL-terminated); returns length.
239: *   spec  : 'f', 'e' or 'g' (lowercase); `upper` selects the E/G letter case.
240: *   prec  : precision (<0 -> default 6); flags: FLAG_PLUS/SPACE/SPECIAL honored.
241: * Sign and inf/nan are handled here; field WIDTH is applied by the caller.
242: */
243:static int fp_format(char *out, double value, char spec, int prec, int flags,
244:                     int upper) {
245:    int n = 0;
246:    union { double d; uint64_t u; } bp;
247:    bp.d = value;
248:    int neg = (int)(bp.u >> 63);
249:    uint64_t expo = (bp.u >> 52) & 0x7ff;
250:    uint64_t mant = bp.u & 0xfffffffffffffULL;
251:
252:    char sgn = neg ? '-' : (flags & FLAG_PLUS) ? '+'
253:                          : (flags & FLAG_SPACE) ? ' ' : 0;
254:
255:    if (expo == 0x7ff) { /* inf / nan */
256:        if (mant) {
257:            const char *w = upper ? "NAN" : "nan";
258:            while (*w) out[n++] = *w++;
259:        } else {
260:            if (sgn) out[n++] = sgn;
261:            const char *w = upper ? "INF" : "inf";
262:            while (*w) out[n++] = *w++;
263:        }
264:        out[n] = '\0';
265:        return n;
266:    }
267:
268:    if (neg) value = -value;
269:    if (prec < 0) prec = 6;
270:    if (sgn) out[n++] = sgn;
271:
272:    char digs[20];
273:    int decexp;
274:
275:    if (spec == 'e') {
276:        int ndig = prec + 1;
277:        if (value == 0.0) { for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++) digs[i] = '0'; decexp = 0; }
278:        else fp_gen(value, ndig, digs, &decexp);
279:        out[n++] = digs[0];
280:        if (prec > 0 || (flags & FLAG_SPECIAL)) out[n++] = '.';
281:        for (int i = 1; i <= prec; i++) out[n++] = (i < 20) ? digs[i] : '0';
282:        n = fp_exp(out, n, decexp, upper);
283:    } else if (spec == 'g') {
284:        int P = prec ? prec : 1;
285:        if (value == 0.0) { for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++) digs[i] = '0'; decexp = 0; }
286:        else fp_gen(value, P, digs, &decexp);
287:        int siglen = P;
288:        if (!(flags & FLAG_SPECIAL))
289:            while (siglen > 1 && digs[siglen - 1] == '0') siglen--;
290:
291:        if (decexp < -4 || decexp >= P) { /* scientific */
292:            out[n++] = digs[0];
293:            if (siglen > 1 || (flags & FLAG_SPECIAL)) out[n++] = '.';
294:            for (int i = 1; i < siglen; i++) out[n++] = digs[i];
295:            n = fp_exp(out, n, decexp, upper);
296:        } else { /* fixed */
297:            int di = 0;
298:            if (decexp < 0) out[n++] = '0';
299:            else for (int p = decexp; p >= 0; p--)
300:                     out[n++] = (di < siglen) ? digs[di++] : '0';
301:            char frac[48];
302:            int fn = 0;
303:            if (decexp < 0) {
304:                for (int p = -1; p > decexp; p--) frac[fn++] = '0';
305:                for (int i = 0; i < siglen; i++) frac[fn++] = digs[i];
306:            } else {
307:                for (int i = decexp + 1; i < siglen; i++) frac[fn++] = digs[i];
308:            }
309:            if (fn > 0 || (flags & FLAG_SPECIAL)) {
310:                out[n++] = '.';
311:                for (int i = 0; i < fn; i++) out[n++] = frac[i];
312:            }
313:        }
314:    } else { /* 'f' */
315:        if (value == 0.0) { digs[0] = '0'; decexp = 0;
316:            for (int i = 1; i < 20; i++) digs[i] = '0'; }
317:        else {
318:            fp_gen(value, 1, digs, &decexp); /* locate the point first */
319:            int ndig = decexp + 1 + prec;
320:            if (ndig < 1) ndig = 1;
321:            if (ndig > 17) ndig = 17;
322:            fp_gen(value, ndig, digs, &decexp);
323:        }
324:        int ndig = decexp + 1 + prec;
325:        if (ndig < 1) ndig = 1;
326:        if (ndig > 17) ndig = 17;
327:        int di = 0;
328:        if (decexp < 0) out[n++] = '0';
329:        else for (int p = decexp; p >= 0; p--)
330:                 out[n++] = (di < ndig) ? digs[di++] : '0';
331:        if (prec > 0 || (flags & FLAG_SPECIAL)) out[n++] = '.';
332:        for (int p = -1; p >= -prec; p--) {
333:            int idx = decexp - p;
334:            out[n++] = (idx >= 0 && idx < ndig) ? digs[idx] : '0';
335:        }
336:    }
337:    out[n] = '\0';
338:    return n;
339:}
340:#endif /* !KERNEL */
341:
342:/*
343: * vsnprintf - format a string into buf using at most size bytes (including NUL).
344: *
345: * This is the kernel's bounded printf engine; all formatted output passes through
346: * here.  The function is compiled for both kernel and userland (see file header).
347: *
348: * Params:
349: *   buf  - destination buffer; must be at least 'size' bytes.
350: *   size - total capacity of buf; if 0, returns 0 and writes nothing.
351: *   fmt  - printf-style format string.
352: *   args - va_list of format arguments; caller owns va_start/va_end.
353: * Returns: number of characters written, NOT including the NUL terminator.
354: *   NOTE(LIB-VSNPRINTF-02): returns chars written (< size), NOT the total chars
355: *   needed if the buffer were unbounded.  Truncation is not detectable from the
356: *   return value alone; this is not POSIX-conformant vsnprintf behaviour.
357: * Locking: none (no global state modified).
358: * Side effects: writes to buf; always NUL-terminates if size > 0.
359: *
360: * Format string parsing loop:
361: *   For each '%' the loop parses:
362: *     1. Zero or more flag characters (-, +, space, #, 0).
363: *     2. Optional decimal field width.
364: *     3. Optional '.' followed by decimal precision.
365: *     4. Optional length modifier (l, ll, z).
366: *     5. Conversion specifier character.
367: *
368: * NOTE(LIB-VSNPRINTF-03): %o (octal) is not implemented; %e/%f are absent
369: *   (acceptable since the kernel does not use the FPU).
370: */
371:int vsnprintf(char *buf, size_t size, const char *fmt, va_list args) {
372:    int written = 0;
373:    int needed = 0;
374:    int width, precision;
375:    int flags;
376:    uint64_t num;
377:    const char *s;
378:
379:    if (size == 0 && buf != NULL) return 0; /* POSIX allows buf=NULL, size=0 */
380:
381:    while (*fmt) {
382:        if (*fmt != '%') {
383:            if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = *fmt;
384:            needed++;
385:            fmt++;
386:            continue;
387:        }
388:
389:        fmt++; /* Skip '%' */
390:
391:        /* Parse flags: accumulate all flag characters before width/precision */
392:        flags = 0;
393:        while (1) {
394:            if (*fmt == '-')      flags |= FLAG_LEFT;
395:            else if (*fmt == '+') flags |= FLAG_PLUS;
396:            else if (*fmt == ' ') flags |= FLAG_SPACE;
397:            else if (*fmt == '#') flags |= FLAG_SPECIAL;
398:            else if (*fmt == '0') flags |= FLAG_ZEROPAD;
399:            else break;
400:            fmt++;
401:        }
402:
403:        /* Field width: a '*' takes the width from an int argument (C99); a
404:         * negative value means left-justify with its magnitude.  Otherwise a run
405:         * of decimal digits after flags, before '.' or the specifier.
406:         * NOTE: '*' MUST consume its int arg here — omitting it desynchronises
407:         * every following va_arg (a bogus pointer lands in the next %s and
408:         * faults on deref), which is exactly the '%.*s' crash class. */
409:        width = 0;
410:        if (*fmt == '*') {
411:            fmt++;
412:            width = va_arg(args, int);
413:            if (width < 0) {
414:                flags |= FLAG_LEFT;
415:                width = -width;
416:            }
417:        } else {
418:            while (*fmt >= '0' && *fmt <= '9') {
419:                width = width * 10 + (*fmt - '0');
420:                fmt++;
421:            }
422:        }
423:
424:        /* Precision: optional '.' followed by a '*' (take from an int argument,
425:         * C99; a negative value means "no precision") or a run of decimal
426:         * digits.  -1 means no precision was specified. */
427:        precision = -1;
428:        if (*fmt == '.') {
429:            fmt++;
430:            if (*fmt == '*') {
431:                fmt++;
432:                precision = va_arg(args, int);
433:                if (precision < 0)
434:                    precision = -1;
435:            } else {
436:                precision = 0;
437:                while (*fmt >= '0' && *fmt <= '9') {
438:                    precision = precision * 10 + (*fmt - '0');
439:                    fmt++;
440:                }
441:            }
442:        }
443:
444:        /* Length modifiers:
445:         *   l  → long (is_long=1)
446:         *   ll → long long / int64_t (is_long=2)
447:         *   z  → size_t (treated as 32- or 64-bit per sizeof) */
448:        int is_long = 0;
449:        if (*fmt == 'l') {
450:            is_long = 1;
451:            fmt++;
452:            if (*fmt == 'l') {
453:                is_long = 2;
454:                fmt++;
455:            }
456:        } else if (*fmt == 'z') {
457:            is_long = (sizeof(size_t) == 8) ? 2 : 1;
458:            fmt++;
459:        }
460:
461:        /* Conversion specifier */
462:        switch (*fmt) {
463:            case 'c':
464:                if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = (char)va_arg(args, int);
465:                needed++;
466:                break;
467:
468:            case 's':
469:                s = va_arg(args, const char *);
470:                if (!s) s = "(null)";
471:                int len = 0;
472:                while (s[len]) {
473:                    if (precision >= 0 && len >= precision) break;
474:                    len++;
475:                }
476:                if (!(flags & FLAG_LEFT)) {
477:                    while (len < width) {
478:                        if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = ' ';
479:                        needed++;
480:                        width--;
481:                    }
482:                }
483:                for (int j = 0; j < len; j++) {
484:                    if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = s[j];
485:                    needed++;
486:                }
487:                while (len < width) {
488:                    if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = ' ';
489:                    needed++;
490:                    width--;
491:                }
492:                break;
493:
494:            case 'd':
495:            case 'i':
496:                if (is_long == 2)      num = va_arg(args, int64_t);
497:                else if (is_long == 1) num = va_arg(args, long);
498:                else                  num = va_arg(args, int);
499:
500:                if ((int64_t)num < 0) {
501:                    flags |= FLAG_SIGN;
502:                    num = -(int64_t)num;
503:                }
504:                needed += print_num(size > 0 ? buf + written : NULL, size > (size_t)written ? size - written : 0, num, 10, width, precision, flags);
505:                if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) {
506:                    int add = size - 1 - written;
507:                    int added = print_num(buf + written, size - written, num, 10, width, precision, flags);
508:                    written += added < add ? added : add;
509:                } else {
510:                    written += 0;
511:                }
512:                break;
513:
514:            case 'u':
515:            case 'x':
516:            case 'X':
517:                if (is_long == 2)      num = va_arg(args, uint64_t);
518:                else if (is_long == 1) num = va_arg(args, unsigned long);
519:                else                  num = va_arg(args, unsigned int);
520:
521:                if (*fmt == 'X') flags |= FLAG_UPPERCASE;
522:                
523:                int n_added = print_num(size > 0 ? buf + written : NULL, size > (size_t)written ? size - written : 0, num, (*fmt == 'u' ? 10 : 16), width, precision, flags);
524:                needed += n_added;
525:                if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) {
526:                    int add = size - 1 - written;
527:                    written += n_added < add ? n_added : add;
528:                }
529:                break;
530:
531:            case 'p': {
532:                /* Build the pointer token "0x" + 16 zero-padded hex digits in
533:                 * a scratch buffer (unchanged look for kernel logs), THEN apply
534:                 * the FIELD WIDTH to the whole token with space padding /
535:                 * left-justify.  The old code fed `width` straight into the
536:                 * hex digit count, so "%90p" produced 92 chars of zero-padded
537:                 * hex instead of a 90-wide field (LIB-VSNPRINTF-04) — which
538:                 * broke Lua's `#string.format("%90p", {}) == 90`. */
539:                num = (uint64_t)va_arg(args, void *);
540:                char pb[32];
541:                int pl = 0;
542:                pb[pl++] = '0';
543:                pb[pl++] = 'x';
544:                pl += print_num(pb + pl, sizeof(pb) - pl, num, 16, 16, -1, FLAG_ZEROPAD);
545:                int pad = width - pl;
546:                if (!(flags & FLAG_LEFT)) {
547:                    for (int k = 0; k < pad; k++) {
548:                        if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = ' ';
549:                        needed++;
550:                    }
551:                    for (int k = 0; k < pl; k++) {
552:                        if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = pb[k];
553:                        needed++;
554:                    }
555:                } else {
556:                    for (int k = 0; k < pl; k++) {
557:                        if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = pb[k];
558:                        needed++;
559:                    }
560:                    for (int k = 0; k < pad; k++) {
561:                        if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = ' ';
562:                        needed++;
563:                    }
564:                }
565:                break;
566:            }
567:
568:            case '%':
569:                if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = '%';
570:                needed++;
571:                break;
572:
573:#ifndef KERNEL
574:            case 'f': case 'F':
575:            case 'e': case 'E':
576:            case 'g': case 'G': {
577:                /* Floats are userland-only (see fp_format's header). */
578:                double dv = va_arg(args, double);
579:                char nb[512];
580:                int up = (*fmt >= 'A' && *fmt <= 'Z');
581:                char lspec = up ? (char)(*fmt + 32) : *fmt;
582:                int ln = fp_format(nb, dv, lspec, precision, flags, up);
583:                int pad = width - ln;
584:                if (!(flags & FLAG_LEFT)) {
585:                    if (flags & FLAG_ZEROPAD) {
586:                        /* zero-fill goes AFTER any sign/space prefix */
587:                        int sk = (nb[0] == '-' || nb[0] == '+' || nb[0] == ' ') ? 1 : 0;
588:                        for (int k = 0; k < sk; k++) {
589:                            if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = nb[k];
590:                            needed++;
591:                        }
592:                        for (int k = 0; k < pad; k++) {
593:                            if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = '0';
594:                            needed++;
595:                        }
596:                        for (int k = sk; k < ln; k++) {
597:                            if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = nb[k];
598:                            needed++;
599:                        }
600:                    } else {
601:                        for (int k = 0; k < pad; k++) {
602:                            if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = ' ';
603:                            needed++;
604:                        }
605:                        for (int k = 0; k < ln; k++) {
606:                            if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = nb[k];
607:                            needed++;
608:                        }
609:                    }
610:                } else {
611:                    for (int k = 0; k < ln; k++) {
612:                        if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = nb[k];
613:                        needed++;
614:                    }
615:                    for (int k = 0; k < pad; k++) {
616:                        if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = ' ';
617:                        needed++;
618:                    }
619:                }
620:                break;
621:            }
622:#endif /* !KERNEL */
623:
624:            default:
625:                if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = '%';
626:                needed++;
627:                if (size > 0 && written < (int)size - 1) buf[written++] = *fmt;
628:                needed++;
629:                break;
630:        }
631:        fmt++;
632:    }
633:
634:    if (size > 0) buf[written] = '\0';
635:    return needed;
636:}
637:

@@@ kernel/mm/buffer.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/mm/buffer.c
3: * Zero-Copy Buffer Cache Implementation
4: *
5: * Provides a block-level cache between the filesystem (ext4) and the VirtIO
6: * block device driver.  Each cached block occupies exactly one 4KB PMM page
7: * (matching the filesystem block size).  The "zero-copy" label refers to the
8: * fact that struct block_buffer.data points directly into a PMM page rather
9: * than copying into a separate heap buffer.
10: *
11: * Structure:
12: *   - hash_table[HASH_BUCKETS]: an array of singly-linked collision lists,
13: *     indexed by hash_block(block_number).  Used for O(1) average lookup.
14: *   - lru_list: doubly-linked LRU list for eviction ordering; most recently
15: *     used buffers are at the head.
16: *   - buffer_lock: a single global spinlock protecting both data structures
17: *     and the ref_count and flags fields of every struct block_buffer.
18: *
19: * Known issues:
20: *   MM-BUF-01  RESOLVED (Phase B2): MAX_BUFFERS is now a hard cap.  buffer_get()
21: *                                reserves its slot in total_buffers under
22: *                                buffer_lock before allocating; if eviction
23: *                                frees nothing because every buffer is dirty,
24: *                                it flushes via buffer_sync() and retries; if
25: *                                everything is still referenced the request
26: *                                fails loudly with NULL instead of growing
27: *                                without bound.
28: *   MM-BUF-02  (W2 PERF)        Two CPUs missing the same block both allocate
29: *                                a buffer and both issue a disk read; the loser
30: *                                is discarded after the lock is re-acquired.
31: *   MM-BUF-03  (W2 BUG/SECURITY) No per-buffer content lock: buffer_sync()
32: *                                writes buf->data while readers may be reading
33: *                                it concurrently -- data race.
34: *   MM-BUF-04  (W2 REFINE)      buffer_sync() flushes at most 64 dirty
35: *                                buffers per call; excess remain dirty.
36: *   MM-BUF-05  (W1 REFINE)      Weak hash (block % 64) and fixed bucket count.
37: */
38:#include <kernel/block.h>
39:#include <kernel/buffer.h>
40:#include <kernel/pmm.h>
41:#include <kernel/printk.h>
42:#include <kernel/string.h>
43:
44:#include <kernel/kmalloc.h>
45:#include <kernel/spinlock.h>
46:
47:#define HASH_BUCKETS 64
48:/* Number of hash buckets; NOTE(MM-BUF-05): fixed, no dynamic resize. */
49:
50:static struct list_head lru_list;
51:static struct list_head hash_table[HASH_BUCKETS];
52:/* buffer_lock: single global lock protecting hash_table, lru_list, total_buffers,
53: * and the ref_count/flags fields of every struct block_buffer.
54: * NOTE(MM-BUF-03): buf->data content is NOT protected by any lock; readers and
55: * buffer_sync() can race on the same data page. */
56:static DEFINE_SPINLOCK(buffer_lock);
57:
58:/* Simple hash function */
59:/*
60: * hash_block - map a block number to a hash_table bucket index.
61: *
62: * NOTE(MM-BUF-05): Uses a trivial modulo hash; sequential block numbers map
63: * to sequential buckets, which is poor distribution for sequential workloads.
64: */
65:static uint32_t hash_block(uint64_t block) { return block % HASH_BUCKETS; }
66:
67:/*
68: * buffer_init - initialise the buffer cache data structures.
69: *
70: * Initialises the LRU list and all HASH_BUCKETS collision lists.
71: * Must be called once at boot before buffer_get() or buffer_sync().
72: * Not re-entrant; must be called single-threaded.
73: */
74:void buffer_init(void) {
75:  pr_info("%s", "BufferCache: Initializing...\n");
76:  INIT_LIST_HEAD(&lru_list);
77:  for (int i = 0; i < HASH_BUCKETS; i++) {
78:    INIT_LIST_HEAD(&hash_table[i]);
79:  }
80:}
81:
82:/*
83: * __lookup - search the hash table for a cached buffer for 'block'.
84: *
85: * Must be called with buffer_lock held.
86: * Returns a pointer to the matching block_buffer, or NULL if not cached.
87: */
88:static struct block_buffer *__lookup(uint64_t block) {
89:  uint32_t bucket = hash_block(block);
90:  struct block_buffer *pos;
91:
92:  list_for_each_entry(pos, &hash_table[bucket], hash) {
93:    if (pos->block == block) {
94:      return pos;
95:    }
96:  }
97:  return NULL;
98:}
99:
100:/* MAX_BUFFERS: hard cap on cached blocks (FIX MM-BUF-01).  buffer_get()
101: * reserves its slot in total_buffers under buffer_lock BEFORE allocating, so
102: * the cache can never exceed MAX_BUFFERS entries (4 MB of data pages). */
103:#define MAX_BUFFERS 1024
104:static int total_buffers = 0;
105:
106:/*
107: * __evict_buffers - attempt to free buffers until total_buffers <= MAX_BUFFERS/2.
108: *
109: * Walks the LRU list tail-to-head (oldest first) and frees any buffer whose
110: * ref_count is 0 and BUFFER_DIRTY flag is clear.
111: *
112: * Must be called with buffer_lock held.
113: *
114: * May free nothing if every evictable candidate is referenced or dirty;
115: * buffer_get() handles that by flushing dirty buffers (buffer_sync) and
116: * retrying, and finally failing the request rather than exceeding the cap
117: * (FIX MM-BUF-01).
118: */
119:static void __evict_buffers(void) {
120:  struct block_buffer *pos, *n;
121:  /* Evict oldest buffers first (LRU) */
122:  list_for_each_entry_safe_reverse(pos, n, &lru_list, list) {
123:    if (total_buffers <= MAX_BUFFERS / 2) break;
124:    if (pos->ref_count == 0 && !(pos->flags & BUFFER_DIRTY)) {
125:      list_del(&pos->hash);
126:      list_del(&pos->list);
127:      pmm_free_page(pos->data);
128:      kfree(pos);
129:      total_buffers--;
130:    }
131:  }
132:}
133:
134:/*
135: * buffer_get - retrieve (or load) the cache entry for disk block 'block'.
136: *
137: * Protocol:
138: *   1. Acquire buffer_lock; look up block in hash table.
139: *      Hit: move to LRU head, bump ref_count, release lock, return.
140: *   2. Enforce the hard cap (FIX MM-BUF-01): if total_buffers >= MAX_BUFFERS,
141: *      run __evict_buffers(); if that freed nothing (all dirty/referenced),
142: *      drop the lock, flush dirty buffers with buffer_sync(), re-acquire and
143: *      evict again.  If the cache is STILL full, fail with NULL — the cap is
144: *      never exceeded.  Otherwise reserve this allocation's slot by
145: *      incrementing total_buffers before dropping the lock.
146: *   3. Release lock; allocate struct block_buffer (kmalloc) and data page (PMM).
147: *      Failure paths release the reserved slot under the lock.
148: *   4. Issue block_read() WITHOUT the lock to avoid holding the spinlock
149: *      across potentially-blocking disk I/O.
150: *   5. Re-acquire lock; re-check hash table for a race winner (MM-BUF-02).
151: *      If another CPU loaded the same block while we were reading, discard our
152: *      buffer (and its slot reservation) and return the winner's.
153: *   6. Insert into hash table and LRU (slot already counted), release lock.
154: *
155: * NOTE(MM-BUF-02): If two CPUs concurrently miss on the same block, both
156: * allocate a page and both issue a disk read.  The loser's page is freed after
157: * re-acquiring the lock, but two DMA reads were still issued unnecessarily.
158: * An in-flight table (mapping block -> pending read) would prevent this.
159: *
160: * Increments ref_count on the returned buffer.  Caller must call buffer_put()
161: * when finished.
162: *
163: * Returns: pointer to the block_buffer, or NULL on allocation or I/O failure.
164: * Locking: acquires/releases buffer_lock internally; must NOT be called with
165: *          buffer_lock already held.
166: */
167:struct block_buffer *buffer_get(uint64_t block) {
168:  uint64_t flags;
169:  struct block_buffer *buf = NULL;
170:  struct block_buffer *exists = NULL;
171:
172:  spin_lock_irqsave(&buffer_lock, &flags);
173:
174:  /* 1. Check Cache */
175:  buf = __lookup(block);
176:  if (buf) {
177:    if (!list_empty(&buf->list)) {
178:      list_move(&buf->list, &lru_list);
179:    }
180:    buf->ref_count++;
181:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&buffer_lock, flags);
182:    return buf;
183:  }
184:
185:  /* Hard cap enforcement (FIX MM-BUF-01).  Eviction first; if everything is
186:   * dirty, flush and retry once; if everything is referenced, refuse. */
187:  if (total_buffers >= MAX_BUFFERS) {
188:    __evict_buffers();
189:    if (total_buffers >= MAX_BUFFERS) {
190:      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&buffer_lock, flags);
191:      buffer_sync(); /* makes dirty buffers evictable (no locks held here) */
192:      spin_lock_irqsave(&buffer_lock, &flags);
193:      __evict_buffers();
194:    }
195:    if (total_buffers >= MAX_BUFFERS) {
196:      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&buffer_lock, flags);
197:      pr_err("BufferCache: cap reached (%d buffers all busy), refusing block %ld\n",
198:             MAX_BUFFERS, block);
199:      return NULL;
200:    }
201:  }
202:  /* Reserve this allocation's slot while still holding the lock, so
203:   * concurrent misses cannot collectively overshoot the cap. */
204:  total_buffers++;
205:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&buffer_lock, flags);
206:
207:  /* 2. Allocate New Buffer (Metadata) */
208:  buf = (struct block_buffer *)kmalloc(sizeof(struct block_buffer));
209:  if (!buf) goto fail_release_slot;
210:  memset(buf, 0, sizeof(*buf));
211:
212:  /* 3. Allocate Data Page */
213:  buf->data = (uint8_t *)pmm_alloc_page();
214:  if (!buf->data) {
215:    kfree(buf);
216:    goto fail_release_slot;
217:  }
218:
219:  /* 4. Read from Disk (OUTSIDE lock) */
220:  if (block_read(buf->data, block * SECTORS_PER_BLOCK,
221:                      SECTORS_PER_BLOCK) != 0) {
222:    pr_err("BufferCache: Disk read error block %ld\n", block);
223:    pmm_free_page(buf->data);
224:    kfree(buf);
225:    goto fail_release_slot;
226:  }
227:
228:  buf->block = block;
229:  buf->flags = BUFFER_UPTODATE;
230:  buf->ref_count = 1;
231:
232:  /* 5. Insert into Hash and LRU */
233:  spin_lock_irqsave(&buffer_lock, &flags);
234:  exists = __lookup(block);
235:  if (exists) {
236:    /* Someone else loaded it while we were reading */
237:    pmm_free_page(buf->data);
238:    kfree(buf);
239:    total_buffers--; /* release our reserved slot; the winner owns its own */
240:    exists->ref_count++;
241:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&buffer_lock, flags);
242:    return exists;
243:  }
244:
245:  uint32_t bucket = hash_block(block);
246:  list_add(&buf->hash, &hash_table[bucket]);
247:  list_add(&buf->list, &lru_list);
248:  /* total_buffers already counts this buffer (slot reserved above) */
249:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&buffer_lock, flags);
250:
251:  return buf;
252:
253:fail_release_slot:
254:  spin_lock_irqsave(&buffer_lock, &flags);
255:  total_buffers--;
256:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&buffer_lock, flags);
257:  return NULL;
258:}
259:
260:/*
261: * buffer_put - release a caller's reference on a buffer.
262: *
263: * Decrements buf->ref_count under buffer_lock.  When ref_count reaches zero
264: * the buffer becomes eligible for eviction by __evict_buffers() but is not
265: * immediately freed.
266: *
267: * Locking: acquires/releases buffer_lock.
268: */
269:void buffer_put(struct block_buffer *buf) {
270:  if (!buf)
271:    return;
272:  uint64_t flags;
273:  spin_lock_irqsave(&buffer_lock, &flags);
274:  if (buf->ref_count > 0)
275:    buf->ref_count--;
276:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&buffer_lock, flags);
277:}
278:
279:/*
280: * buffer_sync - write dirty buffers to disk.
281: *
282: * Collects up to MAX_DIRTY (64) dirty buffers under buffer_lock, temporarily
283: * incrementing their ref_count to pin them.  Then, for each dirty buffer,
284: * issues a block_write() WITHOUT buffer_lock to avoid holding the spinlock
285: * during I/O.  Clears BUFFER_DIRTY and decrements ref_count under the lock
286: * after each write.
287: *
288: * NOTE(MM-BUF-04): At most 64 buffers are flushed per call.  If more than 64
289: * buffers are dirty, the remainder are silently left dirty until the next
290: * buffer_sync() call.
291: *
292: * NOTE(MM-BUF-03): Writing buf->data (block_write) while another CPU
293: * reads it (e.g. an ext4 path that already holds a reference) constitutes an
294: * unsynchronised data race.  There is no per-buffer content lock.
295: *
296: * Locking: acquires/releases buffer_lock around the collection phase and
297: *          around each per-buffer flag update; NOT held during disk I/O.
298: */
299:void buffer_sync(void) {
300:#define MAX_DIRTY 64
301:  struct block_buffer *dirty[MAX_DIRTY];
302:  int ndirty = 0;
303:
304:  uint64_t flags;
305:  spin_lock_irqsave(&buffer_lock, &flags);
306:  struct block_buffer *buf;
307:  list_for_each_entry(buf, &lru_list, list) {
308:    if ((buf->flags & BUFFER_DIRTY) && ndirty < MAX_DIRTY) {
309:      buf->ref_count++;
310:      dirty[ndirty++] = buf;
311:    }
312:  }
313:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&buffer_lock, flags);
314:
315:  for (int i = 0; i < ndirty; i++) {
316:    /* Writeback: the DIRTY bit is cleared below to say "this buffer matches
317:     * the disk".  Clearing it after a FAILED write asserts exactly the thing
318:     * that did not happen, and the block is then never retried -- silent data
319:     * loss.  The bit is only cleared when the write actually succeeded. */
320:    int wb = block_write(dirty[i]->data, dirty[i]->block * SECTORS_PER_BLOCK,
321:                         SECTORS_PER_BLOCK);
322:    if (wb < 0)
323:      pr_err("buffer: writeback of block %lu FAILED — left dirty for retry\n",
324:             (unsigned long)dirty[i]->block);
325:    spin_lock_irqsave(&buffer_lock, &flags);
326:    if (wb >= 0)
327:      dirty[i]->flags &= ~BUFFER_DIRTY;
328:    if (dirty[i]->ref_count > 0)
329:      dirty[i]->ref_count--;
330:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&buffer_lock, flags);
331:  }
332:}
