@@@ kernel/mm/pmm.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/mm/pmm.c
3: * Physical Memory Manager (PMM)
4: *
5: * Implements the lowest layer of the OS1/NEXS memory subsystem: page-frame
6: * allocation over two zones (DMA and Normal).  The allocator is split into two
7: * phases:
8: *
9: *   pmm_early_init()  - probes the mem_region table supplied by the boot layer,
10: *                        calculates the size of per-frame metadata, and places
11: *                        the metadata (page_array + bitmaps) in the first
12: *                        usable physical region above the kernel image.  The
13: *                        MMU is NOT yet active at this point.
14: *
15: *   pmm_init()        - initialises the two zone descriptors, marks the kernel
16: *                        image and PMM metadata as reserved, and reserves any
17: *                        non-USABLE regions reported by the bootloader.
18: *
19: * Allocation primitives:
20: *   pmm_alloc_page()    - next-fit single page (Normal first, DMA fallback).
21: *   pmm_alloc_pages()   - contiguous multi-page block from ZONE_NORMAL only.
22: *   pmm_alloc_aligned() - aligned contiguous block from ZONE_NORMAL only.
23: *   pmm_free_page()     - returns a page; poisons it 0xCC; panics on double-free.
24: *
25: * PA/VA contract (MM-PMM-07 RESOLVED, Phase B2 sweep):
26: *   pmm_alloc_*() return KERNEL VIRTUAL pointers obtained through
27: *   phys_to_virt(MEMORY_BASE + pfn_to_phys(pfn)); pmm_free_*() accept the
28: *   same pointers and translate back with virt_to_phys().  Callers that
29: *   need the physical address (PTE output addresses, DMA descriptors)
30: *   must use virt_to_phys() explicitly.  All PMM metadata (page_array,
31: *   zone bitmaps) is addressed through phys_to_virt() as well.  With
32: *   KERNEL_VIRT_BASE == 0 (memlayout.h) this is bit-identical to the old
33: *   identity behaviour.
34: *
35: * Known issues:
36: *   MM-PMM-01  (W3 STUB)         pmm_init_region() is a no-op stub.
37: *   MM-PMM-02  RESOLVED (Phase B2): pmm_alloc_pages (and therefore
38: *                                pmm_alloc_aligned) now clean+fence like the
39: *                                single-page path; safe for DMA buffers.
40: *   MM-PMM-03  (W2 PERF)         Contiguous alloc is an O(n) scan from PFN 0.
41: *   MM-PMM-04  (W2 WRONG-DESIGN) pmm_alloc_pages/aligned search ZONE_NORMAL only.
42: *   MM-PMM-05  (W2 BAD-IMPL)     global free_pages (atomic) vs per-zone free_pages
43: *                                (plain under lock) can desync.
44: *   MM-PMM-06  (W1 REFINE)       next_free_pfn is ignored by the contiguous path.
45: *   MM-PMM-07  RESOLVED (Phase B2): VA/PA separation via memlayout.h (see above).
46: *   MM-PMM-08  RESOLVED (#117):  total_pages spans up to the HIGHEST usable end
47: *                                address, so address-space holes inside the span
48: *                                (amd64 PCI hole 3..4GB, VGA/BIOS 640KB..1MB)
49: *                                used to be free allocatable "RAM".  pmm_init()
50: *                                now reserves every PFN not covered by a USABLE
51: *                                region; the boot log reports the real usable
52: *                                sum next to the span.
53: */
54:#include <arch/arch.h>
55:#include <kernel/memlayout.h>
56:#include <kernel/pmm.h>
57:#include <kernel/printk.h>
58:#include <kernel/spinlock.h>
59:#include <kernel/string.h>
60:
61:/* Memory configuration from architecture */
62:#define MEMORY_BASE ARCH_RAM_START
63:#define DMA_ZONE_END (MEMORY_BASE + 0x1000000UL) /* 16MB for DMA zone */
64:
65:/* Forward declaration */
66:void pmm_init_region(uint64_t base, uint64_t size);
67:
68:/*
69: * pmm_init_region - register an additional usable RAM region with the PMM.
70: *
71: * NOTE(MM-PMM-01): This function is a stub.  It prints the region address and
72: * returns without updating any zone bitmap or metadata.  Multi-region
73: * management beyond the single early-init scan is not implemented.
74: *
75: * Parameters:
76: *   base  - physical start address of the region.
77: *   size  - length in bytes.
78: */
79:void pmm_init_region(uint64_t base, uint64_t size) {
80:  /* Mark pages in this region as usable (they are already 0 in bitmap if zone_init was called) */
81:  /* This is a placeholder; real implementation would manage multiple regions. */
82:  pr_info("PMM: Region added 0x%lx - 0x%lx\n", base, base + size);
83:}
84:
85:/* Pointers to dynamic metadata */
86:/* page_array: flat array of struct page, one entry per page frame (PFN 0..total_pages-1).
87: * Placed immediately after the kernel image by pmm_early_init().
88: * Accessed under the appropriate zone lock (or atomically for free_pages).
89: *
90: * NOTE(MM-PMM-07): page_array is addressed using the identity-map assumption
91: * (the physical address returned by the boot stage IS the usable pointer). */
92:static struct page *page_array = NULL;
93:static struct zone zones[ZONE_COUNT];
94:/* dma_bitmap / normal_bitmap: one bit per PFN in each zone; 1 = allocated/reserved, 0 = free.
95: * Stored contiguously in memory immediately after page_array. */
96:static uint64_t *dma_bitmap = NULL;
97:static uint64_t *normal_bitmap = NULL;
98:
99:/* Global statistics */
100:/* total_pages: immutable after pmm_init(); no lock needed for reads after init. */
101:static uint64_t total_pages;
102:/* free_pages: updated with atomic GCC built-ins (__sync_fetch_and_{add,sub}).
103: * NOTE(MM-PMM-05): Per-zone zone->free_pages is updated under the zone spinlock
104: * (non-atomic), while this global is atomic.  The two counters can disagree
105: * transiently if a CPU is preempted between the two updates. */
106:static uint64_t free_pages;
107:/* usable_pages: sum of the USABLE boot regions in pages (MM-PMM-08 #117).
108: * total_pages is the metadata SPAN (up to the highest usable end address) and
109: * may exceed this when the map has holes; immutable after pmm_early_init(). */
110:static uint64_t usable_pages;
111:/* pmm_metadata_end_phys: physical end of the page_array + bitmaps, set in
112: * pmm_early_init().  vmm_init() maps the bootstrap window up to here so the
113: * metadata is reachable after the CR3/TTBR switch even when a boot module
114: * pushed it far past the kernel image. */
115:static uint64_t pmm_metadata_end_phys;
116:
117:/* --- Instrumentation counters (perf brief §1; surfaced via OS1_sys_stats).
118: * Updated with relaxed atomics off the lock so the hot path pays only a single
119: * fetch-and-add; *_max uses a racy compare (a lost update on a stat is benign).
120: * search_ticks_* are raw arch_timer_get_count() ticks; the collector converts
121: * to ns via timer_counts_to_ns().  These measure the bitmap-SEARCH cost only —
122: * the fragmentation-sensitive part — not the memset/cache-clean tail. */
123:static uint64_t stat_alloc_calls;
124:static uint64_t stat_free_calls;
125:static uint64_t stat_alloc_search_ticks_total;
126:static uint64_t stat_alloc_search_ticks_max;
127:
128:uint64_t pmm_metadata_top(void) { return pmm_metadata_end_phys; }
129:
130:/*
131: * Mark a page as used in the bitmap
132: *
133: * bitmap_set - mark PFN 'bit' as allocated (1) in 'bitmap'.
134: *
135: * Must be called with the owning zone->lock held.
136: * Uses 64-bit words; 'bit' is a zone-relative PFN.
137: */
138:static void bitmap_set(uint64_t *bitmap, uint64_t bit) {
139:  bitmap[bit / 64] |= (1UL << (bit % 64));
140:}
141:
142:/*
143: * Mark a page as free in the bitmap
144: *
145: * bitmap_clear - mark PFN 'bit' as free (0) in 'bitmap'.
146: *
147: * Must be called with the owning zone->lock held.
148: */
149:static void bitmap_clear(uint64_t *bitmap, uint64_t bit) {
150:  bitmap[bit / 64] &= ~(1UL << (bit % 64));
151:}
152:
153:/*
154: * Check if a page is free
155: *
156: * bitmap_test - return non-zero if PFN 'bit' is allocated (1), zero if free.
157: *
158: * Must be called with the owning zone->lock held.
159: */
160:static int bitmap_test(uint64_t *bitmap, uint64_t bit) {
161:  return (bitmap[bit / 64] & (1UL << (bit % 64))) != 0;
162:}
163:
164:/*
165: * Find first free bit in bitmap
166: *
167: * bitmap_find_free - find the first free (0) bit in [start, end).
168: *
169: * Must be called with the owning zone->lock held.
170: * Returns the zone-relative PFN of the first free frame, or -1 if none.
171: *
172: * MM-PMM-03 RESOLVED (perf §3.1): word-level fast path.  A fully-allocated
173: * 64-bit word (== ~0) is skipped in one compare instead of 64 bit tests, so the
174: * scan cost tracks the number of *occupied words* before the first hole, not the
175: * absolute PFN.  The first non-full word's free bit is located with a single
176: * __builtin_ctzll(~w).  Sub-word head/tail are handled bit-by-bit.
177: */
178:static int64_t bitmap_find_free(uint64_t *bitmap, uint64_t start,
179:                                uint64_t end) {
180:  uint64_t i = start;
181:
182:  /* Head: advance to a word boundary one bit at a time (< 64 iterations). */
183:  while (i < end && (i & 63)) {
184:    if (!bitmap_test(bitmap, i))
185:      return (int64_t)i;
186:    i++;
187:  }
188:  /* Body: whole 64-bit words.  Skip fully-allocated words in one compare. */
189:  for (; i + 64 <= end; i += 64) {
190:    uint64_t w = bitmap[i / 64];
191:    if (w != ~0ULL)
192:      return (int64_t)(i + (uint64_t)__builtin_ctzll(~w));
193:  }
194:  /* Tail: remaining < 64 bits. */
195:  for (; i < end; i++) {
196:    if (!bitmap_test(bitmap, i))
197:      return (int64_t)i;
198:  }
199:  return -1;
200:}
201:
202:/*
203: * Find contiguous free pages
204: *
205: * bitmap_find_contiguous - find a run of 'count' consecutive free bits
206: * in [start, end).
207: *
208: * Must be called with the owning zone->lock held.
209: * Returns the zone-relative PFN of the first frame in the run, or -1.
210: *
211: * MM-PMM-03 (partial, perf §3.1): a fully-allocated 64-bit word (== ~0) that is
212: * word-aligned and breaks the current run is skipped in one compare instead of
213: * 64 bit tests — the dominant cost when scanning past occupied memory.  The
214: * run accounting stays bit-exact across word boundaries (a partial or non-full
215: * word is still walked bit-by-bit), so correctness is unchanged.
216: * NOTE(MM-PMM-06): still scans from 'start' (callers pass 0); a next_free_pfn
217: * hint for the contiguous path is a further refinement, not done here.
218: */
219:static int64_t bitmap_find_contiguous(uint64_t *bitmap, uint64_t start,
220:                                      uint64_t end, uint64_t count) {
221:  uint64_t found = 0;
222:  uint64_t first = 0;
223:  uint64_t i = start;
224:
225:  while (i < end) {
226:    /* Run is broken and we're at a word boundary: skip a fully-allocated word
227:     * in one compare. */
228:    if (found == 0 && (i & 63) == 0 && i + 64 <= end &&
229:        bitmap[i / 64] == ~0ULL) {
230:      i += 64;
231:      continue;
232:    }
233:    if (!bitmap_test(bitmap, i)) {
234:      if (found == 0)
235:        first = i;
236:      found++;
237:      if (found == count)
238:        return (int64_t)first;
239:    } else {
240:      found = 0;
241:    }
242:    i++;
243:  }
244:  return -1;
245:}
246:
247:/*
248: * Initialize a zone
249: *
250: * zone_init - initialise a struct zone descriptor for a contiguous PFN range.
251: *
252: * Parameters:
253: *   z         - zone descriptor to initialise.
254: *   name      - human-readable name (e.g. "DMA", "Normal").
255: *   start_pfn - first absolute PFN in this zone.
256: *   end_pfn   - one past the last absolute PFN in this zone.
257: *   bitmap    - pre-allocated bitmap storage (caller must size it as
258: *               ceil((end_pfn - start_pfn) / 64) * 8 bytes).
259: *
260: * Clears the bitmap (all pages initially free) and initialises the zone lock.
261: * Called from pmm_init() before any allocations are made.
262: */
263:static void zone_init(struct zone *z, const char *name, uint64_t start_pfn,
264:                      uint64_t end_pfn, uint64_t *bitmap) {
265:  z->name = name;
266:  z->start_pfn = start_pfn;
267:  z->end_pfn = end_pfn;
268:  z->free_pages = 0;
269:  z->bitmap = bitmap;
270:  z->next_free_pfn = 0;
271:  spin_lock_init(&z->lock);
272:
273:  /* Clear bitmap - all pages initially free */
274:  uint64_t npages = end_pfn - start_pfn;
275:  memset(bitmap, 0, (npages + 63) / 64 * 8);
276:  z->free_pages = npages;
277:}
278:
279:/*
280: * Early PMM initialization - allocate metadata
281: *
282: * pmm_early_init - phase-1 PMM setup: discover RAM extent and place metadata.
283: *
284: * Called very early in boot, before the MMU is active and before any dynamic
285: * allocation is possible.  Scans the mem_region table to determine the highest
286: * usable physical address (clamped at 256 GB for metadata sanity), computes
287: * the sizes of page_array, dma_bitmap, and normal_bitmap, and places them
288: * contiguously in the first sufficiently large usable region at or above the
289: * kernel image end (__kernel_end).
290: *
291: * After this function returns:
292: *   - page_array, dma_bitmap, normal_bitmap global pointers are valid.
293: *   - total_pages is set.
294: *   - No zone is initialised; no allocations are possible yet.
295: *
296: * Locking: must be called single-threaded (before SMP init).
297: * IRQ context: IRQs are not enabled at call time.
298: *
299: * Parameters:
300: *   regions - array of mem_region entries from the boot platform.
301: *   count   - number of entries in 'regions'.
302: *
303: * NOTE(MM-PMM-07): All metadata pointers are derived from physical addresses
304: * and used as C pointers directly, relying on the identity-map invariant.
305: */
306:void pmm_early_init(struct mem_region *regions, size_t count) {
307:  uint64_t mem_end = MEMORY_BASE;
308:  uint64_t max_detected = 0;
309:
310:  /* 1. Discover total RAM.  max_detected = highest usable END address (the
311:   * metadata span); usable_bytes = real RAM sum (MM-PMM-08 #117: with -m 5G
312:   * QEMU amd64 splits RAM around the 3..4GB PCI hole, so span 6GB != RAM 5GB). */
313:  uint64_t usable_bytes = 0;
314:  if (regions && count > 0) {
315:    for (size_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
316:      if (regions[i].type == MEM_REGION_USABLE) {
317:        uint64_t end = regions[i].base + regions[i].size;
318:        if (end > max_detected) max_detected = end;
319:        if (end > MEMORY_BASE)
320:          usable_bytes += end - (regions[i].base > MEMORY_BASE
321:                                     ? regions[i].base
322:                                     : MEMORY_BASE);
323:      }
324:    }
325:  } else {
326:    /* Fallback to 1GB if no regions provided */
327:    max_detected = MEMORY_BASE + (1UL << 30);
328:    usable_bytes = (1UL << 30);
329:    pr_warn("%s", "PMM: No memory regions detected, falling back to 1GB\n");
330:  }
331:
332:  /* Safety: clamp to 256GB for metadata sanity, but allow much more than 1GB */
333:  if (max_detected > MEMORY_BASE + (256UL << 30)) {
334:    max_detected = MEMORY_BASE + (256UL << 30);
335:  }
336:  
337:  mem_end = max_detected;
338:  total_pages = (mem_end - MEMORY_BASE) / PAGE_SIZE;
339:  usable_pages = usable_bytes / PAGE_SIZE;
340:  if (usable_pages > total_pages) usable_pages = total_pages;
341:
342:  /* 2. Calculate metadata sizes */
343:  size_t page_array_size = total_pages * sizeof(struct page);
344:  uint64_t dma_end_pfn = phys_to_pfn(DMA_ZONE_END - MEMORY_BASE);
345:  size_t dma_bitmap_size = (dma_end_pfn + 63) / 64 * 8;
346:  size_t normal_bitmap_size = (total_pages - dma_end_pfn + 63) / 64 * 8;
347:  size_t total_metadata_size = PAGE_ALIGN(page_array_size + dma_bitmap_size + normal_bitmap_size);
348:
349:  /* 3. Find a place for metadata (must be in the first usable region) */
350:  uintptr_t metadata_phys = 0;
351:  for (size_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
352:    if (regions[i].type == MEM_REGION_USABLE && regions[i].size >= total_metadata_size) {
353:      extern char __kernel_end[];
354:      /* __kernel_end is a link-address (virtual) symbol; compare in the
355:       * physical domain. */
356:      uint64_t kernel_limit = PAGE_ALIGN(virt_to_phys(__kernel_end));
357:      uint64_t target = regions[i].base;
358:      if (target < kernel_limit) target = kernel_limit;
359:
360:      /* Must not land on any RESERVED region.  A GRUB boot module (the
361:       * release rootfs) is loaded right after the kernel — exactly where
362:       * the metadata wants to go — so bump 'target' past every reserved
363:       * region it would overlap.  The table is unsorted, so iterate to a
364:       * fixpoint. */
365:      int bumped = 1;
366:      while (bumped) {
367:        bumped = 0;
368:        for (size_t j = 0; j < count; j++) {
369:          if (regions[j].type == MEM_REGION_USABLE)
370:            continue;
371:          uint64_t r_start = regions[j].base;
372:          uint64_t r_end = PAGE_ALIGN(regions[j].base + regions[j].size);
373:          if (target < r_end && target + total_metadata_size > r_start) {
374:            target = r_end;
375:            bumped = 1;
376:          }
377:        }
378:      }
379:
380:      if (target + total_metadata_size <= regions[i].base + regions[i].size) {
381:        metadata_phys = target;
382:        break;
383:      }
384:    }
385:  }
386:
387:  if (!metadata_phys) {
388:    panic("PMM: Failed to allocate metadata area (%lu KB needed)", total_metadata_size / 1024);
389:  }
390:
391:  /* Physical end of the metadata, so vmm_init can ensure the bootstrap map
392:   * covers it wherever it landed (a boot module can push it well past the
393:   * kernel image). */
394:  pmm_metadata_end_phys = metadata_phys + total_metadata_size;
395:
396:  /* 4. Map pointers (kernel VAs via the direct map; identity while
397:   * KERNEL_VIRT_BASE == 0) */
398:  page_array = (struct page *)phys_to_virt(metadata_phys);
399:  dma_bitmap = (uint64_t *)((uintptr_t)page_array + page_array_size);
400:  normal_bitmap = (uint64_t *)((uintptr_t)dma_bitmap + dma_bitmap_size);
401:
402:  /* 5. Zero out metadata */
403:  memset(phys_to_virt(metadata_phys), 0, total_metadata_size);
404:  
405:  pr_info("PMM: Metadata initialized at 0x%lx (%lu KB)\n", metadata_phys, total_metadata_size / 1024);
406:  pr_info("PMM: Usable RAM: %lu MB (address span %lu MB)\n",
407:          usable_pages * PAGE_SIZE / (1024 * 1024),
408:          (mem_end - MEMORY_BASE) / (1024 * 1024));
409:}
410:
411:/* Helper to reserve a range */
412:/*
413: * pmm_reserve_range - mark [start_pfn, end_pfn) as PG_RESERVED | PG_KERNEL.
414: *
415: * Updates both the zone bitmap (under zone lock via bitmap_set) and the
416: * global atomic free_pages counter.  Silently skips PFNs already reserved
417: * or beyond total_pages.
418: *
419: * Called from pmm_init() to reserve the kernel image and PMM metadata pages.
420: * Must not be called after the system is fully booted (not SMP-safe if
421: * called concurrently with allocations outside the zone lock).
422: */
423:static void pmm_reserve_range(uint64_t start_pfn, uint64_t end_pfn) {
424:  for (uint64_t pfn = start_pfn; pfn < end_pfn; pfn++) {
425:    if (pfn >= total_pages) break;
426:    struct page *pg = &page_array[pfn];
427:    if (pg->flags & PG_RESERVED) continue;
428:
429:    pg->flags = PG_RESERVED | PG_KERNEL;
430:    pg->refcount = 1;
431:
432:    /* Mark in bitmap */
433:    if (pfn < zones[ZONE_DMA].end_pfn) {
434:      bitmap_set(zones[ZONE_DMA].bitmap, pfn);
435:      zones[ZONE_DMA].free_pages--;
436:    } else {
437:      bitmap_set(zones[ZONE_NORMAL].bitmap, pfn - zones[ZONE_DMA].end_pfn);
438:      zones[ZONE_NORMAL].free_pages--;
439:    }
440:    __sync_fetch_and_sub(&free_pages, 1);
441:  }
442:}
443:
444:/*
445: * Initialize PMM with memory regions
446: *
447: * pmm_init - phase-2 PMM setup: zone construction and page reservation.
448: *
449: * Initialises ZONE_DMA (PFN 0..dma_end_pfn-1) and ZONE_NORMAL
450: * (dma_end_pfn..total_pages-1), then calls pmm_reserve_range() to mark the
451: * kernel image, PMM metadata, and any non-usable bootloader regions.
452: *
453: * If pmm_early_init() was not previously called (e.g. direct entry for
454: * testing), pmm_init() calls it here, but this path is not the normal flow.
455: *
456: * After this function returns all allocation primitives are usable.
457: *
458: * Locking: must be called single-threaded (before SMP init).
459: */
460:void pmm_init(struct mem_region *regions, size_t count) {
461:  /* If early_init wasn't called, we are in trouble, but let's try to handle it */
462:  if (!page_array) {
463:    pmm_early_init(regions, count);
464:  }
465:
466:  uint64_t dma_end_pfn = phys_to_pfn(DMA_ZONE_END - MEMORY_BASE);
467:  uint64_t normal_end_pfn = total_pages;
468:
469:  /* Initialize zones with our dynamic bitmaps */
470:  zone_init(&zones[ZONE_DMA], "DMA", 0, dma_end_pfn, dma_bitmap);
471:  zone_init(&zones[ZONE_NORMAL], "Normal", dma_end_pfn, normal_end_pfn, normal_bitmap);
472:
473:  free_pages = zones[ZONE_DMA].free_pages + zones[ZONE_NORMAL].free_pages;
474:
475:  /* Mark kernel pages as reserved (image symbols are virtual; PFNs are
476:   * physical — translate first). */
477:  extern char __kernel_start[], __kernel_end[];
478:  uint64_t kernel_start_pfn = phys_to_pfn(virt_to_phys(__kernel_start) - MEMORY_BASE);
479:  uint64_t kernel_end_pfn = phys_to_pfn(PAGE_ALIGN(virt_to_phys(__kernel_end)) - MEMORY_BASE);
480:
481:  /* Also reserve the metadata itself! */
482:  uint64_t metadata_start_pfn = phys_to_pfn(virt_to_phys(page_array) - MEMORY_BASE);
483:  size_t page_array_size = total_pages * sizeof(struct page);
484:  size_t dma_bitmap_size = (dma_end_pfn + 63) / 64 * 8;
485:  size_t normal_bitmap_size = (total_pages - dma_end_pfn + 63) / 64 * 8;
486:  uint64_t metadata_end_pfn = phys_to_pfn(PAGE_ALIGN(virt_to_phys(page_array) + page_array_size + dma_bitmap_size + normal_bitmap_size) - MEMORY_BASE);
487:
488:  pmm_reserve_range(kernel_start_pfn, kernel_end_pfn);
489:  pmm_reserve_range(metadata_start_pfn, metadata_end_pfn);
490:
491:  /* Mark other reserved regions from bootloader */
492:  for (size_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
493:    if (regions[i].type != MEM_REGION_USABLE) {
494:        uint64_t start = phys_to_pfn(regions[i].base - MEMORY_BASE);
495:        uint64_t end = phys_to_pfn(PAGE_ALIGN(regions[i].base + regions[i].size) - MEMORY_BASE);
496:        pmm_reserve_range(start, end);
497:    }
498:  }
499:
500:  /* MM-PMM-08 (#117): total_pages spans up to the HIGHEST usable end address.
501:   * Holes inside that span (amd64 PCI hole 3..4GB, VGA/BIOS 640KB..1MB) are
502:   * usually ABSENT from the boot memmap — neither usable nor reserved — so
503:   * the loop above never touches them and they would be handed out as RAM.
504:   * Walk the usable regions in address order (pick-min, the table may be
505:   * unsorted) and reserve every PFN they do not cover.  Rounding is
506:   * conservative: partial pages at region edges are reserved. */
507:  if (regions && count > 0) {
508:    uint64_t cursor = MEMORY_BASE;
509:    int done = 0;
510:    while (!done) {
511:      uint64_t next_base = (uint64_t)-1;
512:      uint64_t next_end = 0;
513:      for (size_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
514:        if (regions[i].type != MEM_REGION_USABLE) continue;
515:        uint64_t base = regions[i].base;
516:        uint64_t end = regions[i].base + regions[i].size;
517:        if (end <= cursor) continue; /* already behind the cursor */
518:        if (base < cursor) base = cursor;
519:        if (base < next_base) {
520:          next_base = base;
521:          next_end = end;
522:        }
523:      }
524:      if (next_base == (uint64_t)-1) { /* no usable RAM past cursor */
525:        next_base = MEMORY_BASE + total_pages * PAGE_SIZE;
526:        done = 1;
527:      }
528:      if (next_base > cursor) {
529:        pmm_reserve_range(phys_to_pfn(cursor - MEMORY_BASE),
530:                          phys_to_pfn(PAGE_ALIGN(next_base) - MEMORY_BASE));
531:      }
532:      if (!done) cursor = next_end;
533:    }
534:  }
535:
536:  pr_info("PMM: %lu MB usable, %lu MB free (span %lu MB; gaps reserved)\n",
537:          usable_pages * PAGE_SIZE / (1024 * 1024),
538:          free_pages * PAGE_SIZE / (1024 * 1024),
539:          total_pages * PAGE_SIZE / (1024 * 1024));
540:  pr_info("PMM: DMA zone: %lu pages, Normal zone: %lu pages\n",
541:          zones[ZONE_DMA].free_pages, zones[ZONE_NORMAL].free_pages);
542:}
543:
544:/*
545: * Allocate a single page from specified zone
546: *
547: * zone_alloc_page - allocate one page frame from zone 'z'.
548: *
549: * Uses next-fit: starts the bitmap scan at z->next_free_pfn, then wraps
550: * around to 0 if needed.  Updates z->next_free_pfn to hint the next call.
551: *
552: * After finding a free PFN:
553: *   - marks it allocated in the zone bitmap (under zone lock).
554: *   - decrements z->free_pages (under lock) and global free_pages (atomic).
555: *   - initialises struct page (flags=0, refcount=1).
556: *   - zeroes the page data (memset), cleans the D-cache line, issues a full
557: *     memory barrier (arch_mb).  This ensures DMA coherency for the caller.
558: *
559: * Returns phys_to_virt(MEMORY_BASE + pfn_to_phys(abs_pfn)): the page's
560: * kernel virtual address in the direct map (MM-PMM-07 resolved).
561: *
562: * Returns: pointer to the zeroed page, or NULL if the zone is exhausted.
563: * Locking: takes and releases z->lock with IRQ save/restore.
564: * IRQ context: safe to call from IRQ-disabled context.
565: */
566:static void *zone_alloc_page(struct zone *z, int dma) {
567:  uint64_t flags;
568:  spin_lock_irqsave(&z->lock, &flags);
569:
570:  uint64_t npages = z->end_pfn - z->start_pfn;
571:  uint64_t search_t0 = arch_timer_get_count();
572:  int64_t pfn = bitmap_find_free(z->bitmap, z->next_free_pfn, npages);
573:  if (pfn < 0) {
574:    /* Wrap around and search from the beginning */
575:    pfn = bitmap_find_free(z->bitmap, 0, z->next_free_pfn);
576:  }
577:  uint64_t search_ticks = arch_timer_get_count() - search_t0;
578:
579:  if (pfn < 0) {
580:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&z->lock, flags);
581:    return NULL;
582:  }
583:
584:  /* Update next_free_pfn for next caller */
585:  z->next_free_pfn = (pfn + 1) % npages;
586:
587:  bitmap_set(z->bitmap, pfn);
588:  z->free_pages--;
589:
590:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&z->lock, flags);
591:
592:  /* Convert to absolute PFN, then to the page's kernel virtual address
593:   * (direct map; identity while KERNEL_VIRT_BASE == 0). */
594:  uint64_t abs_pfn = z->start_pfn + pfn;
595:  struct page *pg = &page_array[abs_pfn];
596:  pg->flags = 0;
597:  pg->refcount = 1;
598:
599:  void *addr = phys_to_virt(MEMORY_BASE + pfn_to_phys(abs_pfn));
600:  memset(addr, 0, PAGE_SIZE);
601:  if (dma) {
602:    /* DMA-coherency prep (perf §3.1): make the zeroed page visible to a device
603:     * that may not snoop the CPU caches.  ONLY DMA allocations pay this — the
604:     * vast majority (page tables, kernel stacks, struct process, user/sbrk
605:     * pages, kmalloc chunks) are CPU-only and skip the per-page DC CVAC loop +
606:     * full barrier, the dominant fixed cost on the spawn hot path. */
607:    arch_cache_clean_range(addr, PAGE_SIZE);
608:    arch_mb();
609:  }
610:
611:  __sync_fetch_and_sub(&free_pages, 1);
612:
613:  /* Instrumentation (perf brief §1): count this allocation and fold in its
614:   * bitmap-search cost.  Relaxed atomics; the max is a benign racy compare. */
615:  __sync_fetch_and_add(&stat_alloc_calls, 1);
616:  __sync_fetch_and_add(&stat_alloc_search_ticks_total, search_ticks);
617:  if (search_ticks > stat_alloc_search_ticks_max)
618:    stat_alloc_search_ticks_max = search_ticks;
619:
620:  return addr;
621:}
622:
623:/*
624: * Allocate a single page
625: *
626: * pmm_alloc_page - allocate one 4KB page from the best available zone.
627: *
628: * Tries ZONE_NORMAL first (preferred to preserve DMA pages for constrained
629: * devices), falls back to ZONE_DMA if Normal is exhausted.
630: *
631: * The returned page is zeroed, cache-cleaned, and memory-barrier-fenced (done
632: * inside zone_alloc_page).
633: *
634: * Returns: pointer to a 4KB page, or NULL on global exhaustion.
635: * Locking: no caller lock required; zone locks are taken internally.
636: */
637:void *pmm_alloc_page(void) {
638:  /* Try normal zone first, then DMA.  CPU-only page (no cache-clean) — see
639:   * pmm_alloc_page_dma() for device-DMA buffers. */
640:  void *page = zone_alloc_page(&zones[ZONE_NORMAL], 0);
641:  if (!page) {
642:    page = zone_alloc_page(&zones[ZONE_DMA], 0);
643:  }
644:  return page;
645:}
646:
647:/*
648: * pmm_alloc_page_dma - like pmm_alloc_page() but cache-cleaned + fenced so the
649: * page is coherent for a device that may not snoop the CPU caches (perf §3.1).
650: * Use ONLY for buffers a device DMAs to/from (virtqueues, ring/cmd buffers,
651: * GPU backing).  Ordinary kernel allocations must use pmm_alloc_page().
652: */
653:void *pmm_alloc_page_dma(void) {
654:  void *page = zone_alloc_page(&zones[ZONE_NORMAL], 1);
655:  if (!page) {
656:    page = zone_alloc_page(&zones[ZONE_DMA], 1);
657:  }
658:  return page;
659:}
660:
661:/*
662: * Allocate multiple contiguous pages
663: *
664: * pmm_alloc_pages - allocate 'count' physically contiguous 4KB pages.
665: *
666: * Delegates to pmm_alloc_page() for count==1 (which includes cache-clean
667: * and barrier).  For count>1, searches ZONE_NORMAL only via a linear bitmap
668: * scan from PFN 0.
669: *
670: * NOTE(MM-PMM-04): Only ZONE_NORMAL is searched; there is no mechanism to
671: * allocate a contiguous DMA-zone block.  DMA device drivers that need
672: * physically contiguous memory below 16 MB cannot satisfy that requirement
673: * through this path.
674: *
675: * Like the single-page path, the returned memory is zeroed, cache-cleaned
676: * (arch_cache_clean_range) and barrier-fenced (arch_mb) so a device can DMA
677: * to/from it immediately (MM-PMM-02 resolved; pmm_alloc_aligned inherits the
678: * guarantee since it carves from this function).
679: *
680: * NOTE(MM-PMM-03): The contiguous scan is O(n) from PFN 0 on every call;
681: * there is no buddy structure or run-length metadata to accelerate it.
682: *
683: * Returns: pointer to the first page of the contiguous run, or NULL.
684: * Locking: takes and releases ZONE_NORMAL's lock with IRQ save/restore.
685: */
686:static void *alloc_pages_impl(size_t count, int dma) {
687:  if (count == 0)
688:    return NULL;
689:  if (count == 1)
690:    return dma ? pmm_alloc_page_dma() : pmm_alloc_page();
691:
692:  struct zone *z = &zones[ZONE_NORMAL];
693:  uint64_t flags;
694:
695:  spin_lock_irqsave(&z->lock, &flags);
696:
697:  uint64_t search_t0 = arch_timer_get_count();
698:  int64_t pfn =
699:      bitmap_find_contiguous(z->bitmap, 0, z->end_pfn - z->start_pfn, count);
700:  uint64_t search_ticks = arch_timer_get_count() - search_t0;
701:  if (pfn < 0) {
702:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&z->lock, flags);
703:    return NULL;
704:  }
705:
706:  /* Mark all pages as used */
707:  for (size_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
708:    bitmap_set(z->bitmap, pfn + i);
709:  }
710:  z->free_pages -= count;
711:
712:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&z->lock, flags);
713:
714:  /* Initialize pages */
715:  uint64_t abs_pfn = z->start_pfn + pfn;
716:  for (size_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
717:    struct page *pg = &page_array[abs_pfn + i];
718:    pg->flags = 0;
719:    pg->refcount = 1;
720:  }
721:
722:  void *addr = phys_to_virt(MEMORY_BASE + pfn_to_phys(abs_pfn));
723:  memset(addr, 0, PAGE_SIZE * count);
724:  if (dma) {
725:    /* DMA-coherency prep — only for device buffers (perf §3.1). */
726:    arch_cache_clean_range(addr, PAGE_SIZE * count);
727:    arch_mb();
728:  }
729:
730:  __sync_fetch_and_sub(&free_pages, count);
731:
732:  /* Instrumentation (perf brief §1): the contiguous multi-page path is the
733:   * O(n)-from-0 scan (MM-PMM-03/06) — fold its search cost in too. */
734:  __sync_fetch_and_add(&stat_alloc_calls, 1);
735:  __sync_fetch_and_add(&stat_alloc_search_ticks_total, search_ticks);
736:  if (search_ticks > stat_alloc_search_ticks_max)
737:    stat_alloc_search_ticks_max = search_ticks;
738:
739:  return addr;
740:}
741:
742:/* pmm_alloc_pages - 'count' contiguous CPU-only pages (no cache-clean). */
743:void *pmm_alloc_pages(size_t count) { return alloc_pages_impl(count, 0); }
744:
745:/* pmm_alloc_pages_dma - 'count' contiguous pages, cache-cleaned + fenced for
746: * device DMA (perf §3.1).  Use ONLY for buffers a device DMAs to/from. */
747:void *pmm_alloc_pages_dma(size_t count) { return alloc_pages_impl(count, 1); }
748:
749:/*
750: * Free a single page
751: *
752: * pmm_free_page - release a single 4KB page back to its zone.
753: *
754: * Steps:
755: *   1. Validates the pointer is within [MEMORY_BASE, MEMORY_BASE+total_pages*PAGE_SIZE).
756: *   2. Checks PG_RESERVED; logs a warning and returns without freeing if set.
757: *   3. Atomically decrements struct page refcount; if still >0 after decrement,
758: *      another reference exists (shared page) -- no free is performed.
759: *   4. Acquires the zone lock; checks bitmap to detect double-free (panics).
760: *   5. Clears the bitmap bit and increments zone->free_pages (under lock).
761: *   6. Poisons the page with 0xCC to catch use-after-free dereferences.
762: *   7. Increments global free_pages atomically.
763: *
764: * The double-free check (step 4) is done under the lock, which prevents the
765: * race where two CPUs both see refcount==1 and both attempt to free.
766: *
767: * Locking: takes and releases the zone spinlock with IRQ save/restore.
768: */
769:void pmm_free_page(void *page) {
770:  if (!page)
771:    return;
772:
773:  uint64_t phys = virt_to_phys(page);
774:#if ARCH_MEMORY_BASE > 0
775:  if (phys < MEMORY_BASE) {
776:    pr_err("PMM: Attempt to free invalid address %p (below MEMORY_BASE)\n",
777:           page);
778:    return;
779:  }
780:#endif
781:
782:  uint64_t pfn = phys_to_pfn(phys - MEMORY_BASE);
783:  if (pfn >= total_pages) {
784:    pr_err("PMM: Attempt to free invalid address %p (out of bounds)\n", page);
785:    return;
786:  }
787:
788:  struct page *pg = &page_array[pfn];
789:  if (pg->flags & PG_RESERVED) {
790:    pr_warn("PMM: Attempt to free reserved page %016lx\n", phys);
791:    return;
792:  }
793:
794:  /* Atomic decrement and check if it was the last reference */
795:  if (__sync_fetch_and_sub(&pg->refcount, 1) > 1)
796:    return;
797:
798:  /* Find which zone this belongs to */
799:  struct zone *z;
800:  uint64_t zone_pfn;
801:
802:  if (pfn < zones[ZONE_DMA].end_pfn) {
803:    z = &zones[ZONE_DMA];
804:    zone_pfn = pfn;
805:  } else {
806:    z = &zones[ZONE_NORMAL];
807:    zone_pfn = pfn - zones[ZONE_DMA].end_pfn;
808:  }
809:
810:  uint64_t flags;
811:  spin_lock_irqsave(&z->lock, &flags);
812:
813:  if (!bitmap_test(z->bitmap, zone_pfn)) {
814:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&z->lock, flags);
815:    panic("PMM: Double free detected at %p (PFN %lu)", page, pfn);
816:  }
817:
818:  bitmap_clear(z->bitmap, zone_pfn);
819:  z->free_pages++;
820:
821:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&z->lock, flags);
822:
823:  /* Poison memory to catch use-after-free bugs */
824:  memset(page, 0xCC, PAGE_SIZE);
825:
826:  __sync_fetch_and_add(&free_pages, 1);
827:  __sync_fetch_and_add(&stat_free_calls, 1); /* perf brief §1 */
828:}
829:
830:/*
831: * Free multiple contiguous pages
832: *
833: * pmm_free_pages - release 'count' contiguous pages starting at 'page'.
834: *
835: * Calls pmm_free_page() for each page sequentially.  Each call acquires and
836: * releases the zone lock independently, so this is not an atomic bulk free.
837: */
838:void pmm_free_pages(void *page, size_t count) {
839:  uint8_t *va = (uint8_t *)page;
840:  for (size_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
841:    pmm_free_page(va + i * PAGE_SIZE);
842:  }
843:}
844:
845:/*
846: * Allocate with specific alignment (for block I/O)
847: *
848: * pmm_alloc_aligned - allocate 'size' bytes with at least 'align'-byte alignment.
849: *
850: * Allocates (pages + align_pages - 1) contiguous pages via pmm_alloc_pages()
851: * to guarantee an aligned sub-range exists within the block, then frees the
852: * unused leading and trailing pages.
853: *
854: * 'align' must be a power of two and a multiple of PAGE_SIZE for the bit-mask
855: * arithmetic to be correct (no validation is performed on 'align').
856: *
857: * NOTE(MM-PMM-04): Like pmm_alloc_pages(), this function searches ZONE_NORMAL
858: * only.  Aligned contiguous allocations in the DMA zone are not possible.
859: *
860: * Cache coherency: inherited from pmm_alloc_pages(), which cleans and fences
861: * the whole run before returning (MM-PMM-02 resolved) — the aligned sub-range
862: * is therefore DMA-safe as returned.
863: *
864: * Returns: aligned pointer, or NULL on failure.
865: * Locking: delegates to pmm_alloc_pages() and pmm_free_pages(); no additional
866: *          lock is held across the gap between those calls.
867: */
868:void *pmm_alloc_aligned(size_t size, size_t align) {
869:  size_t pages = (size + PAGE_SIZE - 1) / PAGE_SIZE;
870:  size_t align_pages = (align + PAGE_SIZE - 1) / PAGE_SIZE;
871:
872:  if (align_pages <= 1) {
873:    return pmm_alloc_pages_dma(pages); /* aligned allocs are DMA-safe by contract */
874:  }
875:
876:  /* Allocate extra pages to ensure alignment.  DMA path: this API is documented
877:   * DMA-safe (block I/O), so it cleans+fences even though pmm_alloc_pages no
878:   * longer does (perf §3.1).  No current callers, but keep the contract. */
879:  size_t total = pages + align_pages - 1;
880:  void *mem = pmm_alloc_pages_dma(total);
881:  if (!mem)
882:    return NULL;
883:
884:  /* Calculate aligned address */
885:  uint64_t addr = (uint64_t)mem;
886:  uint64_t aligned = (addr + align - 1) & ~(align - 1);
887:
888:  /* Free unused pages at start */
889:  size_t skip = (aligned - addr) / PAGE_SIZE;
890:  if (skip > 0) {
891:    pmm_free_pages(mem, skip);
892:  }
893:
894:  /* Free unused pages at end */
895:  size_t unused = total - skip - pages;
896:  if (unused > 0) {
897:    pmm_free_pages((void *)(aligned + pages * PAGE_SIZE), unused);
898:  }
899:
900:  return (void *)aligned;
901:}
902:
903:/*
904: * Get page descriptor for physical address
905: *
906: * pmm_phys_to_page - return the struct page descriptor for a physical address.
907: *
908: * Returns NULL if 'phys' is below MEMORY_BASE (guarded by ARCH_MEMORY_BASE
909: * compile-time check) or beyond total_pages.
910: *
911: * 'phys' is a PHYSICAL address; pointer callers must virt_to_phys() first.
912: */
913:struct page *pmm_phys_to_page(uint64_t phys) {
914:#if ARCH_MEMORY_BASE > 0
915:  if (phys < MEMORY_BASE)
916:    return NULL;
917:#endif
918:  uint64_t pfn = phys_to_pfn(phys - MEMORY_BASE);
919:  if (pfn >= total_pages)
920:    return NULL;
921:  return &page_array[pfn];
922:}
923:
924:/*
925: * Get physical address for page descriptor
926: *
927: * pmm_page_to_phys - return the physical address corresponding to a struct page.
928: *
929: * Computes pfn = page - page_array, then returns MEMORY_BASE + pfn_to_phys(pfn).
930: * The caller is responsible for ensuring 'page' is a valid entry in page_array.
931: *
932: * The returned value is a PHYSICAL address; use phys_to_virt() to get a
933: * dereferenceable pointer.
934: */
935:uint64_t pmm_page_to_phys(struct page *page) {
936:  uint64_t pfn = page - page_array;
937:  return MEMORY_BASE + pfn_to_phys(pfn);
938:}
939:
940:/*
941: * Statistics
942: *
943: * pmm_get_free_pages - return the approximate global count of free pages.
944: *
945: * NOTE(MM-PMM-05): The global free_pages counter is updated atomically, but
946: * per-zone free_pages counters are updated under individual zone locks.  The
947: * two can transiently disagree.  This function returns only the global counter.
948: */
949:uint64_t pmm_get_free_pages(void) { return free_pages; }
950:
951:/* pmm_get_total_pages - return total_pages (immutable after pmm_init).
952: *
953: * This is the metadata SPAN, not the amount of memory that exists.  It is the
954: * bound of page_array[]/the zone bitmaps, so it is what PFN indexing must be
955: * validated against — and nothing else.  Anything reporting "how much RAM does
956: * this machine have" wants pmm_get_usable_pages(). */
957:uint64_t pmm_get_total_pages(void) { return total_pages; }
958:
959:/*
960: * pmm_get_usable_pages - RAM that actually exists, in pages.
961: *
962: * MM-PMM-09 (#94, fixed 2026-07-23): the span and the usable total are not the
963: * same number on amd64, and userland was being shown the span.  The firmware
964: * memory map has a hole below 4 GB for PCI/MMIO, so with 6 GB installed the
965: * usable regions sum to ~5119 MB while the address span from MEMORY_BASE to the
966: * highest usable end is 6144 MB.  Reporting the span made the monitor print
967: * "free 5026 / 6144 MB, used 1118 MB" — attributing the ~1 GB hardware hole to
968: * consumed memory, so used was wrong by more than an order of magnitude (the
969: * real figure is ~93 MB).
970: *
971: * The gap is already handled correctly INSIDE the PMM (the regions are reserved
972: * and never allocated); it simply must not be counted as memory.  Per the HAL
973: * abstraction rule: amd64 does not use the gap and must not present it as
974: * something that exists.  aarch64 has no such hole, so span == usable there and
975: * this changes nothing — which is the point: one number, correct on both.
976: */
977:uint64_t pmm_get_usable_pages(void) { return usable_pages; }
978:
979:/*
980: * pmm_dump_stats - print total/free/used page counts to the kernel log.
981: *
982: * Uses the global free_pages counter; see NOTE(MM-PMM-05) for caveats.
983: * Suitable for boot-time diagnostics only; takes no locks.
984: */
985:void pmm_dump_stats(void) {
986:  pr_info("%s", "PMM Statistics:\n");
987:  pr_info("  Total: %lu pages (%lu MB)\n", total_pages,
988:          total_pages * PAGE_SIZE / (1024 * 1024));
989:  pr_info("  Free:  %lu pages (%lu MB)\n", free_pages,
990:          free_pages * PAGE_SIZE / (1024 * 1024));
991:  pr_info("  Used:  %lu pages (%lu MB)\n", total_pages - free_pages,
992:          (total_pages - free_pages) * PAGE_SIZE / (1024 * 1024));
993:}
994:
995:/*
996: * pmm_get_counters - read the cumulative allocator counters (perf brief §1).
997: *
998: * search_ticks_* are raw arch_timer_get_count() ticks; the caller converts to
999: * ns via timer_counts_to_ns().  All four out-params are optional (NULL-skip).
1000: * Lock-free reads of relaxed atomics — values are a coherent-enough snapshot.
1001: */
1002:void pmm_get_counters(uint64_t *alloc_calls, uint64_t *free_calls,
1003:                      uint64_t *search_ticks_total, uint64_t *search_ticks_max) {
1004:  if (alloc_calls)       *alloc_calls = stat_alloc_calls;
1005:  if (free_calls)        *free_calls = stat_free_calls;
1006:  if (search_ticks_total) *search_ticks_total = stat_alloc_search_ticks_total;
1007:  if (search_ticks_max)  *search_ticks_max = stat_alloc_search_ticks_max;
1008:}
1009:
1010:/*
1011: * pmm_get_fragmentation - instantaneous ZONE_NORMAL fragmentation snapshot
1012: * (perf brief §1/§2.1): the largest contiguous free run (pages) and the number
1013: * of distinct free runs.  A shrinking largest_run while free_pages stays flat
1014: * is the fragmentation signature.  Word-level scan with all-free / all-allocated
1015: * fast paths; taken under the zone lock (on-demand at ~1 Hz poll, off the hot
1016: * path).  Either out-param may be NULL.
1017: */
1018:void pmm_get_fragmentation(uint64_t *largest_run, uint64_t *run_count) {
1019:  struct zone *z = &zones[ZONE_NORMAL];
1020:  uint64_t flags;
1021:  uint64_t cur = 0, max = 0, runs = 0;
1022:  int in_run = 0;
1023:
1024:  spin_lock_irqsave(&z->lock, &flags);
1025:  uint64_t npages = z->end_pfn - z->start_pfn;
1026:  uint64_t nwords = (npages + 63) / 64;
1027:  for (uint64_t wi = 0; wi < nwords; wi++) {
1028:    uint64_t w = z->bitmap[wi];
1029:    uint64_t bits = 64;
1030:    if (wi == nwords - 1 && (npages % 64))
1031:      bits = npages % 64;
1032:
1033:    if (w == 0 && bits == 64) {
1034:      /* whole word free — extend (or start) the current run */
1035:      if (!in_run) { in_run = 1; runs++; cur = 0; }
1036:      cur += 64;
1037:      if (cur > max) max = cur;
1038:    } else if (w == ~0ULL) {
1039:      /* whole word allocated — close any run */
1040:      in_run = 0; cur = 0;
1041:    } else {
1042:      for (uint64_t b = 0; b < bits; b++) {
1043:        if (!(w & (1ULL << b))) {
1044:          if (!in_run) { in_run = 1; runs++; cur = 0; }
1045:          cur++;
1046:          if (cur > max) max = cur;
1047:        } else {
1048:          in_run = 0; cur = 0;
1049:        }
1050:      }
1051:    }
1052:  }
1053:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&z->lock, flags);
1054:
1055:  if (largest_run) *largest_run = max;
1056:  if (run_count)   *run_count = runs;
1057:}

@@@ kernel/mm/vmm.c @@@
1:/*
2: * kernel/mm/vmm.c
3: * Virtual Memory Manager
4: *
5: * AArch64 4-level page table management
6: *
7: * NOTE(MM-VMM-07): The file header says "AArch64" but this file is compiled
8: * for both AArch64 and AMD64.  The page-table index arithmetic (PGD/PUD/PMD/PT
9: * at 39/30/21/12 bit) matches 4-level tables on both architectures; the heavy
10: * lifting is delegated to arch_vmm_* hooks which differ per arch.
11: *
12: * Role:
13: *   This file provides two distinct services:
14: *   1. Page-table construction helpers (vmm_map_page, vmm_map, vmm_unmap_page,
15: *      vmm_check_range) that call arch_vmm_map/unmap under per-process mm_lock.
16: *   2. MMU lifecycle (vmm_init -> vmm_dynamic_remap) and per-process PGD
17: *      management (vmm_create_pgd / vmm_destroy_pgd).
18: *
19: * PA/VA contract (kernel/memlayout.h):
20: *   In this file `uint64_t *pgd` parameters and pmm_alloc_page() results
21: *   are kernel VIRTUAL pointers; the arch_vmm_* layer takes the PGD as a
22: *   PHYSICAL address, so every delegation below converts with
23: *   virt_to_phys().  PTE output addresses are physical and are converted
24: *   with phys_to_virt() before being dereferenced (get_next_table) or
25: *   freed (vmm_destroy_pgd).  Identity while KERNEL_VIRT_BASE == 0.
26: *
27: * Known issues:
28: *   MM-VMM-01  (FIXED)           W^X enforced via vmm_map_ram_wx(): kernel
29: *                                 text RX, rodata RO+NX, all other RAM RW+NX.
30: *   MM-VMM-02  RESOLVED (Phase B2): all walkers translate PTE physical
31: *                                 addresses through phys_to_virt() and
32: *                                 store via virt_to_phys(); the kernel now
33: *                                 RUNS in the higher half on both arches
34: *                                 (KERNEL_VIRT_BASE in memlayout.h).
35: *   MM-VMM-03  (W2 REFINE/TODO)  vmm_dynamic_remap leaks the old PGD.
36: *   MM-VMM-04  (W3 BUG)          vmm_destroy_pgd leaks user RAM frames and
37: *                                 contains a dead empty loop.
38: *   MM-VMM-05  RESOLVED (Phase B2): unmap paths now satisfy the cross-CPU
39: *                                 shootdown contract — AArch64 in hardware
40: *                                 (broadcast IS TLBI), amd64 via LAPIC IPI
41: *                                 (kernel/arch/amd64/mm/tlb.c); teardown
42: *                                 broadcasts one full shootdown before
43: *                                 frames are recycled.
44: *   MM-VMM-06  (W2 REFINE)       Generic map path is 4KB-only; 2MB blocks
45: *                                 only via arch_vmm_map_range.
46: *   MM-VMM-07  (W1 DOC)          File header mentions only AArch64.
47: */
48:#include <kernel/arch.h>
49:#include <kernel/cpu.h>
50:#include <kernel/pmm.h>
51:#include <kernel/printk.h>
52:#include <kernel/sched.h>
53:#include <kernel/string.h>
54:#include <kernel/types.h>
55:#include <kernel/vmm.h>
56:#include <kernel/platform.h>
57:#include <stdint.h>
58:
59:/* Page Table Levels */
60:/* 4-level walk (48-bit VA, 4KB granule on both arches). */
61:#define PGD_SHIFT 39
62:#define PUD_SHIFT 30
63:#define PMD_SHIFT 21
64:#define PT_SHIFT 12
65:
66:#define PGD_INDEX(x) (((x) >> PGD_SHIFT) & 0x1FF)
67:#define PUD_INDEX(x) (((x) >> PUD_SHIFT) & 0x1FF)
68:#define PMD_INDEX(x) (((x) >> PMD_SHIFT) & 0x1FF)
69:#define PT_INDEX(x) (((x) >> PT_SHIFT) & 0x1FF)
70:
71:/* Global Kernel PGD */
72:/* kernel_pgd - kernel VIRTUAL pointer to the current kernel page-global
73: * directory (the hardware register gets virt_to_phys(kernel_pgd): TTBR1 on
74: * aarch64, CR3 on amd64).  Updated atomically (pointer assignment) in
75: * vmm_dynamic_remap() after the hardware root has been switched; secondary
76: * CPUs read it after arch_mb(). */
77:uint64_t *kernel_pgd;
78:
79:#define PTE_ADDR_MASK 0x0000FFFFFFFFF000UL
80:
81:/*
82: * Get or create next level table
83: *
84: * get_next_table - walk one level of the page table, optionally allocating.
85: *
86: * Parameters:
87: *   table - pointer to the current-level page-table page (512 uint64_t entries).
88: *   index - 9-bit index into 'table' for the next level.
89: *   alloc - if non-zero and the entry is not present, allocate a new table page.
90: *
91: * Returns: pointer to the next-level table, or NULL if not present and
92: *          alloc==0, or NULL if pmm_alloc_page() fails.
93: *
94: * PA/VA: entries hold PHYSICAL addresses; dereferences go through
95: * phys_to_virt() and new tables are installed via virt_to_phys()
96: * (MM-VMM-02 resolved — see kernel/memlayout.h).
97: *
98: * Locking: caller must hold the relevant PGD/process mm_lock; this helper
99: * does not take any lock itself.
100: */
101:static uint64_t *get_next_table(uint64_t *table, uint64_t index, int alloc) {
102:  if (table[index] & PTE_VALID) {
103:    /* Table entries store PHYSICAL addresses (48 bits supported); translate
104:     * through phys_to_virt() (direct map, MM-VMM-02). */
105:    uint64_t phys = table[index] & 0x0000FFFFFFFFF000UL;
106:    return (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(phys);
107:  }
108:
109:  if (!alloc)
110:    return NULL;
111:
112:  /* Allocate a new page for the table.  pmm_alloc_page() returns a pointer
113:   * usable by the kernel; what gets STORED in the entry is its physical
114:   * address (virt_to_phys below). */
115:  void *page = pmm_alloc_page();
116:  if (!page)
117:    return NULL;
118:
119:  /* Zero and Flush the new table page */
120:  memset(page, 0, 4096);
121:  arch_cache_clean_range(page, 4096);
122:  arch_mb();
123:
124:  /* Table entry flags:
125:   * AArch64: Valid (bit 0), Table (bit 1), AF (bit 10), Inner Share (bits 8-9),
126:   *          AP EL0 RW (bit 6-7, usually ignored for tables but safe).
127:   * AMD64:   Present (bit 0), RW (bit 1), User (bit 2).
128:   */
129:  table[index] = virt_to_phys(page) | PTE_TABLE | PTE_VALID;
130:
131:  /* Flush the directory entry itself */
132:  arch_cache_clean_range(&table[index], 8);
133:  arch_mb();
134:
135:  return page;
136:}
137:
138:/*
139: * Map a page
140: *
141: * vmm_map_page - map a single 4KB page in the given page table.
142: *
143: * Validates page-size alignment of both 'virt' and 'phys', then delegates to
144: * arch_vmm_map() which performs the actual PTE write.
145: *
146: * NOTE(MM-VMM-06): This function always maps 4KB pages.  2MB huge-page
147: * mappings are only used through arch_vmm_map_range() called from
148: * vmm_dynamic_remap(); the generic path is inconsistent and slower for
149: * large contiguous ranges.
150: *
151: * Parameters:
152: *   pgd   - kernel virtual pointer to the PGD (converted to its PA for the
153: *           arch layer via virt_to_phys).
154: *   virt  - virtual address to map; must be 4KB-aligned.
155: *   phys  - physical address to map to; must be 4KB-aligned.
156: *   flags - PTE attribute flags (PAGE_KERNEL_EXEC, PAGE_USER, etc.).
157: *
158: * Returns: 0 on success, -1 on alignment error.
159: * Locking: caller must hold any required mm_lock.
160: */
161:int vmm_map_page(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t virt, uint64_t phys, uint64_t flags) {
162:  if ((virt & 0xFFF) || (phys & 0xFFF)) {
163:    pr_err("VMM: Invalid alignment virt=%lx phys=%lx\n", virt, phys);
164:    return -1;
165:  }
166:
167:  /* arch_vmm_map takes the PGD as a physical address. */
168:  return arch_vmm_map(virt_to_phys(pgd), virt, phys, flags);
169:}
170:
171:/* Internal helper with locking */
172:/*
173: * vmm_map_page_locked - vmm_map_page() wrapped with proc->mm_lock.
174: *
175: * Acquires proc->mm_lock with IRQ save before calling vmm_map_page(), then
176: * releases it.  Use this variant when the caller does not already hold mm_lock.
177: *
178: * NOTE(MM-VMM-05): Even with mm_lock held, there is no TLB shootdown IPI sent
179: * to other CPUs after mapping.  On SMP, other CPUs may continue to use a
180: * stale TLB entry for this virtual address until their next context switch.
181: */
182:int vmm_map_page_locked(struct process *proc, uint64_t virt, uint64_t phys,
183:                        uint64_t flags) {
184:  uint64_t lock_flags;
185:  spin_lock_irqsave(&proc->mm_lock, &lock_flags);
186:  int ret = vmm_map_page(proc->page_table, virt, phys, flags);
187:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&proc->mm_lock, lock_flags);
188:  return ret;
189:}
190:
191:/*
192: * Check if a range is fully mapped and has required flags
193: * Returns 0 if OK, -1 if any page is missing
194: *
195: * vmm_check_range - verify every page in [virt, virt+size) is mapped with
196: *                   all bits of 'flags_mask' set.
197: *
198: * Walks the four-level page table using get_next_table() with alloc=0.
199: * Returns 0 if every PTE is present and satisfies the flags_mask, or -1 as
200: * soon as any level is missing or a PTE fails the mask check.
201: *
202: * Parameters:
203: *   pgd        - PGD to walk (kernel virtual pointer).
204: *   virt       - start virtual address (rounded down to 4KB boundary).
205: *   size       - length in bytes (rounded up to 4KB boundary).
206: *   flags_mask - set of PTE bits that must all be present; 0 skips flag check.
207: *
208: * Returns: 0 if fully mapped, -1 on first missing or non-conforming page.
209: * Locking: caller must ensure the page table is not concurrently modified.
210: */
211:int vmm_check_range(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t virt, uint64_t size,
212:                    uint64_t flags_mask) {
213:  uint64_t v = virt & ~0xFFFUL;
214:  uint64_t e = (virt + size + 4095) & ~0xFFFUL;
215:
216:  while (v < e) {
217:    uint64_t *pud, *pmd, *pt;
218:
219:    pud = get_next_table(pgd, PGD_INDEX(v), 0);
220:    if (!pud)
221:      return -1;
222:
223:    pmd = get_next_table(pud, PUD_INDEX(v), 0);
224:    if (!pmd)
225:      return -1;
226:
227:    pt = get_next_table(pmd, PMD_INDEX(v), 0);
228:    if (!pt)
229:      return -1;
230:
231:    uint64_t entry = pt[PT_INDEX(v)];
232:    if (!(entry & PTE_VALID))
233:      return -1;
234:
235:    if (flags_mask && (entry & flags_mask) != flags_mask)
236:      return -1;
237:
238:    v += 4096;
239:  }
240:  return 0;
241:}
242:
243:/*
244: * vmm_get_phys - translate a virtual address to its mapped physical address.
245: *
246: * Delegates entirely to arch_vmm_get_physical(); refer to the arch
247: * implementation for details on the walk (blocks/large pages included).
248: *
249: * Returns the physical address, or 0 / arch-defined sentinel on unmapped VA.
250: */
251:uint64_t vmm_get_phys(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t virt) {
252:  return arch_vmm_get_physical(virt_to_phys(pgd), virt);
253:}
254:
255:/*
256: * Unmap a page
257: *
258: * vmm_unmap_page - remove a single page mapping from the given PGD.
259: *
260: * Delegates to arch_vmm_unmap(), which clears the PTE and performs an SMP
261: * TLB shootdown (MM-VMM-05 resolved): on return, no online CPU still
262: * translates 'virt' through the old entry — the caller may safely recycle
263: * the backing frame.  AArch64 satisfies this with broadcast IS TLBI in
264: * hardware; amd64 with a LAPIC IPI round (see arch/amd64/mm/tlb.c).
265: */
266:void vmm_unmap_page(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t virt) {
267:  /* The contract stated directly above is that after this returns "the caller
268:   * may safely recycle the backing frame".  If the unmap FAILED, that promise
269:   * is false: the caller hands a still-mapped page back to the PMM, an idle
270:   * core hands it straight to the next allocation, and two owners write to one
271:   * frame.  Continuing past a broken invariant is worse than stopping on it,
272:   * because the corruption surfaces somewhere with no path back to here. */
273:  if (arch_vmm_unmap(virt_to_phys(pgd), virt) != 0)
274:    panic("vmm_unmap_page: unmap of VA 0x%lx failed — the frame cannot be "
275:          "recycled safely",
276:          virt);
277:}
278:
279:/*
280: * vmm_protect - rewrite the attributes of existing mappings (AMMU-02).
281: *
282: * Thin contract wrapper over arch_vmm_protect(): 'flags' is the arch's
283: * PAGE/PTE profile, frame addresses are preserved, large pages split for
284: * 4KB precision, and a cross-CPU TLB shootdown runs before returning.
285: * Returns 0, or -1 if the range contains an unmapped page (pages before
286: * the hole keep the new attributes).
287: */
288:int vmm_protect(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t virt, uint64_t size, uint64_t flags) {
289:  return arch_vmm_protect(virt_to_phys(pgd), virt, size, flags);
290:}
291:
292:/* Internal helper with locking */
293:/*
294: * vmm_unmap_page_locked - vmm_unmap_page() wrapped with proc->mm_lock.
295: *
296: * Acquires proc->mm_lock with IRQ save/restore around the unmap call.
297: * The shootdown inside runs with IRQs masked; on amd64 a peer spinning on
298: * this same mm_lock cannot ack until it unmasks — the bounded ack wait in
299: * tlb.c turns that worst case into a stall, never a deadlock.
300: */
301:void vmm_unmap_page_locked(struct process *proc, uint64_t virt) {
302:  uint64_t lock_flags;
303:  spin_lock_irqsave(&proc->mm_lock, &lock_flags);
304:  vmm_unmap_page(proc->page_table, virt);
305:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&proc->mm_lock, lock_flags);
306:}
307:
308:/*
309: * Map a range of memory
310: *
311: * vmm_map - map a contiguous virtual range [virt, virt+size) to [phys, phys+size).
312: *
313: * Both 'virt' and 'phys' are rounded down to 4KB; 'size' is rounded up.
314: * Calls vmm_map_page() once per 4KB page, stopping and returning -1 on the
315: * first failure.  Partial mappings are not cleaned up on error.
316: *
317: * NOTE(MM-VMM-06): Always maps 4KB pages regardless of alignment or size.
318: *
319: * Returns: 0 on success, -1 if any page mapping fails.
320: * Locking: caller must hold any required mm_lock.
321: */
322:int vmm_map(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t virt, uint64_t phys, uint64_t size,
323:            uint64_t flags) {
324:  uint64_t v = virt & ~0xFFFUL;
325:  uint64_t p = phys & ~0xFFFUL;
326:  uint64_t e = (virt + size + 4095) & ~0xFFFUL;
327:
328:  while (v < e) {
329:    if (vmm_map_page(pgd, v, p, flags) != 0) {
330:      return -1;
331:    }
332:    v += 4096;
333:    p += 4096;
334:  }
335:  return 0;
336:}
337:
338:/*
339: * vmm_map_ram_wx - map RAM at its direct-map VA with the W^X section split
340: * (MM-VMM-01 / AMMU-01 resolved).
341: *
342: * The kernel image layout (kernel.ld, both arches) is:
343: *   [__text_start, _etext)      text                                  → RX
344: *   [_etext≈, __erodata)        rodata, .ktests, .ksyms               → RO+NX
345: *   everything else              data/bss/heap/stacks/DTB/boot region  → RW+NX
346: * Boundaries are page-rounded; the linker aligns sections to 4 KB so the
347: * windows never overlap.  arch_vmm_map_range still uses 2MB blocks inside
348: * each window where alignment permits.
349: *
350: * Enforcement: aarch64 PXN/UXN bits (always honoured at EL1);
351: * amd64 PTE_NX (EFER.NXE set at boot) + CR0.WP for the read-only text.
352: */
353:void vmm_map_ram_wx(uint64_t *pgd, uint64_t base, uint64_t size) {
354:  extern char __text_start[], _etext[], __erodata[];
355:  /* Section symbols are link (virtual) addresses; 'base'/'cur' iterate
356:   * PHYSICAL addresses — compare in the physical domain and map each
357:   * chunk at its direct-map VA (phys_to_virt).  The RX window starts at
358:   * __text_start, NOT __kernel_start: on amd64 the latter also covers the
359:   * low boot region (1..2MB), which is data once the kernel runs. */
360:  uint64_t tx_s = virt_to_phys(__text_start) & ~0xFFFUL;
361:  uint64_t tx_e = (virt_to_phys(_etext) + 4095) & ~0xFFFUL;
362:  uint64_t ro_e = (virt_to_phys(__erodata) + 4095) & ~0xFFFUL;
363:  uint64_t end = base + size;
364:  uint64_t cur = base;
365:
366:  while (cur < end) {
367:    uint64_t flags;
368:    if (cur >= tx_s && cur < tx_e)
369:      flags = PAGE_KERNEL_RX;
370:    else if (cur >= tx_e && cur < ro_e)
371:      flags = PAGE_KERNEL_RO;
372:    else
373:      flags = PAGE_KERNEL;
374:
375:    /* Map up to the next window boundary (or the range end). */
376:    uint64_t next = end;
377:    if (tx_s > cur && tx_s < next)
378:      next = tx_s;
379:    if (tx_e > cur && tx_e < next)
380:      next = tx_e;
381:    if (ro_e > cur && ro_e < next)
382:      next = ro_e;
383:
384:    /* Boot-time direct map: a failure leaves a hole in the kernel's own view
385:     * of RAM, and the first access through it faults with nothing pointing
386:     * back to the mapping that was never made. */
387:    if (arch_vmm_map_range(virt_to_phys(pgd), (uint64_t)phys_to_virt(cur), cur,
388:                           next - cur, flags) != 0)
389:      panic("vmm: direct map failed for PA 0x%lx..0x%lx", cur, next);
390:    cur = next;
391:  }
392:}
393:
394:/*
395: * Initialize VMM and Enable MMU
396: *
397: * vmm_init - phase-1 VMM bring-up: build the first real kernel PGD (128 MB
398: *            bootstrap window) and install it as the kernel root.
399: *
400: * The MMU itself is already ON when this runs: the boot assembly (both
401: * arches) enables it with boot tables so C executes at its higher-half
402: * link address from the first instruction.
403: *
404: * Steps:
405: *   1. Allocate and zero the kernel PGD from the PMM (sets global kernel_pgd).
406: *   2. Map [ARCH_RAM_START, ARCH_RAM_START+128MB) at the direct-map VAs via
407: *      vmm_map_ram_wx() (W^X section split).
408: *   3. Map MMIO regions via arch_vmm_map_mmio().
409: *   4. Install virt_to_phys(kernel_pgd) as the kernel root via
410: *      arch_vmm_init_hw() (TTBR1 on aarch64, CR3 on amd64).
411: *
412: * After vmm_init() only the first 128 MB of RAM are mapped;
413: * vmm_dynamic_remap() extends coverage to all detected RAM.
414: *
415: * Locking: must be called single-threaded before SMP bring-up.
416: */
417:void vmm_init(void) {
418:  pr_info("%s", "VMM: Initializing MMU (Phase 1: Bootstrap)...\n");
419:
420:  /* Allocate Kernel PGD */
421:  kernel_pgd = pmm_alloc_page();
422:  if (!kernel_pgd) {
423:    panic("VMM: Failed to allocate kernel PGD\n");
424:  }
425:  memset(kernel_pgd, 0, 4096);
426:  arch_cache_clean_range(kernel_pgd, 4096);
427:
428:  /* 1. Map RAM (bootstrap) with the W^X section split: text RX, rodata RO+NX,
429:   * the rest RW+NX (MM-VMM-01).  Map at least 128MB, but always far enough to
430:   * cover the PMM metadata: arch_vmm_init_hw() switches the page table and then
431:   * touches page_array via pmm_alloc_page(), so the metadata must be mapped in
432:   * THIS pgd.  A boot module (release rootfs) can push the metadata well past
433:   * the kernel image, so a fixed 128MB window is not enough — extend to the
434:   * metadata top. */
435:  uint64_t ram_start = ARCH_RAM_START;
436:  uint64_t ram_size = 128UL * 1024 * 1024; /* Enough to boot */
437:  uint64_t meta_top = pmm_metadata_top();
438:  if (meta_top > ram_start) {
439:    uint64_t need = PAGE_ALIGN(meta_top - ram_start + 2UL * 1024 * 1024);
440:    if (need > ram_size)
441:      ram_size = need;
442:  }
443:
444:  vmm_map_ram_wx(kernel_pgd, ram_start, ram_size);
445:
446:  /* 2. Map MMIO */
447:  arch_vmm_map_mmio(kernel_pgd);
448:
449:  /* 3. Enable MMU */
450:  arch_vmm_init_hw(virt_to_phys(kernel_pgd));
451:
452:  pr_info("%s", "VMM: Bootstrap complete.\n");
453:}
454:
455:/*
456: * Dynamic remapping of all discovered RAM
457: *
458: * vmm_dynamic_remap - phase-2 mapping: remap all discovered RAM into a new PGD.
459: *
460: * Builds a new PGD from scratch, using arch_vmm_map_range() (which uses 2MB
461: * block entries where possible) to map every MEM_REGION_USABLE region returned
462: * by arch_platform_get_mem_regions().  Re-maps MMIO.  Then atomically switches
463: * the hardware to the new PGD with arch_vmm_set_pgd() and updates kernel_pgd.
464: *
465: * NOTE(MM-VMM-03): The old PGD (bootstrap) is stored in 'old_pgd' and then
466: * abandoned -- it is never freed.  A correct implementation would broadcast an
467: * IPI to all secondary CPUs, wait for them to switch, and only then return the
468: * old PGD pages to the PMM.  The (void)old_pgd suppresses the unused-variable
469: * warning.
470: *
471: * NOTE(MM-VMM-05): arch_vmm_set_pgd() flushes the local TLB; no IPI is sent
472: * to secondary CPUs.  If any secondary is running at this point it may access
473: * the old (now leaked) PGD's tables.
474: *
475: * Locking: must be called before SMP bring-up completes on secondary CPUs.
476: */
477:void vmm_dynamic_remap(void) {
478:  pr_info("%s", "VMM: Performing RAM-aware dynamic remapping...\n");
479:
480:  /* Allocate a temporary PGD to build the new map */
481:  uint64_t *new_pgd = pmm_alloc_page();
482:  if (!new_pgd) panic("VMM: Failed to allocate new dynamic PGD");
483:  memset(new_pgd, 0, 4096);
484:
485:  /* 1. Map all discovered memory regions with the W^X section split
486:   * (text RX, rodata RO+NX, all other RAM RW+NX — MM-VMM-01 resolved).
487:   * arch_vmm_map_range still uses 2MB blocks inside each window. */
488:  size_t count = 0;
489:  struct mem_region *regions = arch_platform_get_mem_regions(&count);
490:  for (size_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
491:    if (regions[i].type == MEM_REGION_USABLE) {
492:      pr_info("VMM: Mapping region 0x%lx - 0x%lx\n",
493:              regions[i].base, regions[i].base + regions[i].size);
494:      vmm_map_ram_wx(new_pgd, regions[i].base, regions[i].size);
495:    }
496:  }
497:
498:  /* 2. Re-map MMIO */
499:  arch_vmm_map_mmio(new_pgd);
500:
501:  /* 3. Atomically switch to the new PGD (kernel root: TTBR1 on aarch64,
502:   * CR3 on amd64) */
503:  uint64_t new_phys = virt_to_phys(new_pgd);
504:
505:  /* Swap the global kernel_pgd */
506:  uint64_t *old_pgd = kernel_pgd;
507:  kernel_pgd = new_pgd;
508:
509:  arch_vmm_set_kernel_pgd(new_phys);
510:  arch_tlb_flush_local();
511:  arch_mb();
512:  arch_isb();
513:
514:  /* 4. Cleanup old table - currently deferred until all CPUs have switched to new PGD */
515:  /* TODO: Implement proper synchronization (IPI broadcast) to safely free old_pgd
516:   *       after all secondary CPUs have transitioned to the new kernel_pgd.
517:   *       This requires arch_send_ipi and a TLB flush callback on all CPUs. */
518:  (void)old_pgd;
519:
520:  pr_info("%s", "VMM: Dynamic remapping successful. All discovered RAM is now accessible.\n");
521:}
522:
523:/*
524: * Create a new PGD
525: *
526: * vmm_create_pgd - allocate a new process PGD with the kernel half pre-filled.
527: *
528: * Delegates to arch_vmm_create_process_pgd() which allocates a page, copies
529: * the upper-half (kernel) PGD entries from kernel_pgd by reference (not
530: * deep-copied), and leaves the lower-half zero for user-space mappings.
531: *
532: * Returns: kernel virtual pointer to the new PGD (the arch layer returns
533: * its physical address; converted here via phys_to_virt).
534: */
535:uint64_t *vmm_create_pgd(void) {
536:  uint64_t pgd_phys = arch_vmm_create_process_pgd();
537:  if (!pgd_phys)
538:    return NULL;
539:  return (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pgd_phys);
540:}
541:
542:/*
543: * Destroy a PGD: free private page-table pages AND user RAM frames
544: *
545: * vmm_destroy_pgd - tear down the process-private half of a PGD
546: * (MM-VMM-04 + AMMU-03 resolved).
547: *
548: * Ownership rules (what may be freed):
549: *   - Only the subtree under PGD/PML4 index 0 is walked: that is the only
550: *     entry arch_vmm_create_process_pgd() builds privately; every other
551: *     populated index (aarch64 256-511, amd64 1-255 MMIO + 256-511) is a
552: *     by-value copy of a kernel_pgd entry and must not be touched.
553: *   - Inside the walk, any directory entry whose VALUE equals the kernel's
554: *     entry at the same position is shared (the create path copies kernel
555: *     entries by value: aarch64 MMIO/RAM PUD slots and 2MB RAM blocks in
556: *     the deep-copied PMD; amd64 PDPT[0]).  Shared entries are skipped.
557: *   - Block entries (PTE_IS_TABLE false) are never descended: user mappings
558: *     are always 4KB pages, so a differing block is still kernel memory
559: *     (e.g. the kernel remapped after the by-value copy).
560: *   - Leaf frames are freed only when the PTE carries PTE_USER: a private
561: *     PT may also hold kernel PTEs (a kernel 2MB block split around the ELF
562: *     header page at 0x7ffff000) whose frames belong to the kernel.
563: *   - Differing table pages (PMD/PT/PUD) were allocated for this process by
564: *     get_next_table()/the arch splitter and are freed unconditionally.
565: *
566: * There is no frame refcounting: user frames are never shared between
567: * processes today (ELF loader and sbrk map freshly allocated frames; IPC,
568: * blits and font loads copy by value).  Revisit when shared mappings arrive.
569: *
570: * Table physical addresses are dereferenced through phys_to_virt()
571: * (MM-VMM-02 resolved).
572: *
573: * Locking: caller must ensure no other CPU holds or will use this PGD
574: * (process fully stopped and de-scheduled; see the scheduler reaper).
575: */
576:void vmm_destroy_pgd(uint64_t *pgd) {
577:  if (!pgd)
578:    return;
579:
580:  /* Cross-CPU shootdown BEFORE freeing (MM-VMM-05): a peer that ran this
581:   * process earlier may still hold user translations into frames we are
582:   * about to recycle.  One full round here covers the whole address space;
583:   * the per-PTE walk below then frees without further TLB traffic. */
584:  arch_tlb_shootdown_all();
585:
586:  uint64_t freed_frames = 0;
587:  uint64_t freed_tables = 0;
588:
589:  uint64_t *pud0 =
590:      (pgd[0] & PTE_VALID) ? (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pgd[0] & PTE_ADDR_MASK) : NULL;
591:  uint64_t *k_pud0 = (kernel_pgd[0] & PTE_VALID)
592:                         ? (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(kernel_pgd[0] & PTE_ADDR_MASK)
593:                         : NULL;
594:
595:  if (pud0 && pud0 != k_pud0) {
596:    for (int i = 0; i < 512; i++) {
597:      uint64_t pud_e = pud0[i];
598:      if (!(pud_e & PTE_VALID))
599:        continue;
600:      if (k_pud0 && pud_e == k_pud0[i])
601:        continue; /* shared kernel entry (MMIO block, kernel RAM table) */
602:      if (!PTE_IS_TABLE(pud_e))
603:        continue; /* 1GB block: never a user mapping */
604:
605:      uint64_t *pmd = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pud_e & PTE_ADDR_MASK);
606:      uint64_t *k_pmd = NULL;
607:      if (k_pud0 && (k_pud0[i] & PTE_VALID) && PTE_IS_TABLE(k_pud0[i]))
608:        k_pmd = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(k_pud0[i] & PTE_ADDR_MASK);
609:
610:      for (int j = 0; j < 512; j++) {
611:        uint64_t pmd_e = pmd[j];
612:        if (!(pmd_e & PTE_VALID))
613:          continue;
614:        if (k_pmd && pmd_e == k_pmd[j])
615:          continue; /* by-value copy of a kernel entry (2MB RAM block) */
616:        if (!PTE_IS_TABLE(pmd_e))
617:          continue; /* private 2MB block: not user (user maps 4KB only) */
618:
619:        uint64_t *pt = (uint64_t *)phys_to_virt(pmd_e & PTE_ADDR_MASK);
620:        for (int k = 0; k < 512; k++) {
621:          uint64_t pte = pt[k];
622:          if ((pte & PTE_VALID) && (pte & PTE_USER)) {
623:            /* PTE carries the frame's PHYSICAL address; the PMM takes
624:             * direct-map pointers. */
625:            pmm_free_page(phys_to_virt(pte & PTE_ADDR_MASK));
626:            freed_frames++;
627:          }
628:        }
629:        pmm_free_page(pt);
630:        freed_tables++;
631:      }
632:      pmm_free_page(pmd);
633:      freed_tables++;
634:    }
635:    pmm_free_page(pud0);
636:    freed_tables++;
637:  }
638:
639:  pmm_free_page((void *)pgd);
640:  freed_tables++;
641:
642:  pr_debug("VMM: PGD %p destroyed: freed %lu user frames, %lu table pages "
643:          "(free now %lu)\n",
644:          (void *)pgd, freed_frames, freed_tables, pmm_get_free_pages()); /* hot path: demoted (perf §1) */
645:}
646:
