1:/*
2: * kernel/sched/elf.c
3: * ELF Loader (Identity Map / MMU-less optimized)
4: */
5:#include <kernel/arch.h>
6:#include <kernel/elf.h>
7:#include <kernel/pmm.h>
8:#include <kernel/printk.h>
9:#include <kernel/sched.h>
10:#include <kernel/string.h>
11:#include <kernel/vfs.h>
12:#include <kernel/vmm.h>
13:
14:/* Largest argv vector marshalled onto a new task's stack.  Kept in lockstep
15: * with SPAWN_MAX_ARGS in the syscall dispatcher (the source clamps argc). */
16:#define ELF_MAX_ARGS 16
17:
18:/*
19: * setup_user_args - lay out argc/argv at the top of the user stack.
20: *
21: * top_kaddr is the kernel direct-map pointer to the page backing the highest
22: * stack page [stack_top-4096, stack_top).  We copy the argument strings just
23: * below stack_top, then an array of argc+1 user pointers (NULL-terminated),
24: * and return a 16-byte-aligned user SP pointing at that array.  *out_argv_uva
25: * receives the user virtual address of the argv array (== the returned SP).
26: *
27: * argc is assumed already clamped to <= ELF_MAX_ARGS; the whole block fits in
28: * one page (16 * 128 strings + 17 pointers < 4096).
29: */
30:static uint64_t setup_user_args(void *top_kaddr, uint64_t stack_top, int argc,
31:                                char *const kargv[], uint64_t *out_argv_uva) {
32:  const uint64_t page_uva = stack_top - 4096;
33:  uint8_t *kpage = (uint8_t *)top_kaddr;
34:  uint64_t str_uva[ELF_MAX_ARGS];
35:  uint64_t uptr = stack_top;
36:
37:  /* Strings, packed downward from the top of the page. */
38:  for (int i = argc - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
39:    size_t len = strlen(kargv[i]) + 1;
40:    uptr -= len;
41:    memcpy(kpage + (uptr - page_uva), kargv[i], len);
42:    str_uva[i] = uptr;
43:  }
44:
45:  /* argv[] array of (argc + 1) user pointers, 16-byte aligned == the SP. */
46:  uptr &= ~(uint64_t)7;
47:  uptr -= (uint64_t)(argc + 1) * sizeof(uint64_t);
48:  uptr &= ~(uint64_t)15;
49:  uint64_t *uargv = (uint64_t *)(kpage + (uptr - page_uva));
50:  for (int i = 0; i < argc; i++)
51:    uargv[i] = str_uva[i];
52:  uargv[argc] = 0;
53:
54:  *out_argv_uva = uptr;
55:  return uptr;
56:}
57:
58:int process_load_elf(struct process *proc, const char *path) {
59:  return process_load_elf_args(proc, path, 0, NULL);
60:}
61:
62:int process_load_elf_args(struct process *proc, const char *path, int argc,
63:                          char *const kargv[]) {
64:  if (argc < 0)
65:    argc = 0;
66:  if (argc > ELF_MAX_ARGS)
67:    argc = ELF_MAX_ARGS;
68:  struct vfs_node exe;
69:  if (vfs_open(path, &exe) != 0) {
70:    pr_err("ELF: File not found: %s\n", path);
71:    return -1;
72:  }
73:
74:  /* 1. Read ELF Header */
75:  Elf64_Ehdr ehdr;
76:  if (vfs_read(&exe, 0, &ehdr, sizeof(ehdr)) != sizeof(ehdr)) {
77:    pr_err("%s", "ELF: Failed to read header\n");
78:    return -1;
79:  }
80:
81:  /* 2. Verify Header */
82:  if (memcmp(ehdr.e_ident, ELFMAG, SELFMAG) != 0 ||
83:      ehdr.e_ident[EI_CLASS] != ELFCLASS64 || ehdr.e_machine != ARCH_TYPE) {
84:    pr_err("ELF: Invalid format (Machine: 0x%x, Expected: 0x%x)\n", 
85:           ehdr.e_machine, ARCH_TYPE);
86:    return -1;
87:  }
88:
89:  /* 3. Load Segments */
90:  uint64_t max_vaddr = 0;
91:  for (int i = 0; i < ehdr.e_phnum; i++) {
92:    Elf64_Phdr phdr;
93:    uint32_t ph_off = ehdr.e_phoff + (i * ehdr.e_phentsize);
94:
95:    if (vfs_read(&exe, ph_off, &phdr, sizeof(phdr)) != sizeof(phdr)) {
96:      pr_err("ELF: Failed to read PHDR %d\n", i);
97:      return -1;
98:    }
99:
100:    if (phdr.p_type == PT_LOAD) {
101:      /* ELF-01: reject a PT_LOAD whose VA is not wholly inside the user window
102:       * [0x70000000, 0xC0000000).  User ELFs link at 0x80000000 (Makefile
103:       * -Wl,-Ttext); their lowest segment is the header page at 0x7ffff000 and
104:       * the user stack base is 0xC0000000.  With the higher-half split the
105:       * kernel no longer lives in the low half at all, but the window check
106:       * stays: it rejects mis-linked binaries outright, keeps segments clear
107:       * of the stack area, and on amd64 prevents a crafted p_vaddr with high
108:       * bits set from indexing the COPIED kernel PML4 entries (256..511) and
109:       * writing through the shared kernel PDPTs. */
110:      if (phdr.p_vaddr < 0x70000000UL || phdr.p_vaddr >= 0xC0000000UL ||
111:          phdr.p_memsz > 0xC0000000UL - phdr.p_vaddr) {
112:        pr_err("ELF: PT_LOAD vaddr 0x%lx (memsz 0x%lx) outside user range "
113:               "[0x70000000,0xC0000000) - rejecting (mis-linked binary?)\n",
114:               phdr.p_vaddr, phdr.p_memsz);
115:        return -1;
116:      }
117:
118:      /* User segment protection via the arch-neutral VMM page profiles
119:       * (HAL conformance #140 / DIR-06): the ELF loader is arch-neutral core
120:       * and must NOT hand-encode per-arch PTE bits. The VMM contract (vmm.h)
121:       * supplies the four W^X user profiles; the loader only maps ELF PF_W/PF_X
122:       * onto them. W^X (ELF-02): a segment is executable only when PF_X is set. */
123:      uint64_t flags;
124:      if (phdr.p_flags & PF_W)
125:        flags = (phdr.p_flags & PF_X) ? PAGE_USER : PAGE_USER_DATA;  /* RW+X : RW */
126:      else
127:        flags = (phdr.p_flags & PF_X) ? PAGE_USER_RX : PAGE_USER_RO; /* RO+X : RO */
128:
129:      pr_debug("ELF: Mapping Segment at 0x%lx (FileSz: 0x%lx, MemSz: 0x%lx)\n",
130:              phdr.p_vaddr, phdr.p_filesz, phdr.p_memsz); /* hot path: demoted (perf §1) */
131:
132:      /* Allocate Pages for Memory Segment */
133:      uint64_t start_vpage = phdr.p_vaddr & ~(0xFFF);
134:      uint64_t end_vpage = (phdr.p_vaddr + phdr.p_memsz + 4095) & ~(0xFFF);
135:
136:      if (end_vpage > max_vaddr) {
137:        max_vaddr = end_vpage;
138:      }
139:
140:      for (uint64_t vaddr = start_vpage; vaddr < end_vpage; vaddr += 4096) {
141:        /* Allocate physical page */
142:        void *paddr = pmm_alloc_page();
143:        if (!paddr) {
144:          pr_err("ELF: Failed to allocate physical page for vaddr 0x%lx\n",
145:                 vaddr);
146:          return -1;
147:        }
148:
149:        /* Map page in process address space (PTE wants the frame's
150:         * PHYSICAL address; pmm returned the kernel pointer). */
151:        if (vmm_map_page(proc->page_table, vaddr, virt_to_phys(paddr),
152:                         flags) != 0) {
153:          pr_err("ELF: Failed to map page at 0x%lx\n", vaddr);
154:          pmm_free_page(paddr);
155:          return -1;
156:        }
157:
158:        /* Kernel virtual address for writing (direct-map pointer) */
159:        void *kaddr = paddr;
160:
161:        /* Zero the page content */
162:        memset(kaddr, 0, 4096);
163:
164:        /* Copy data from file if within bounds */
165:        uint64_t seg_vstart = phdr.p_vaddr;
166:        uint64_t seg_vend_file = seg_vstart + phdr.p_filesz;
167:        uint64_t page_start = vaddr;
168:        uint64_t page_end = vaddr + 4096;
169:
170:        uint64_t copy_start =
171:            (page_start > seg_vstart) ? page_start : seg_vstart;
172:        uint64_t copy_end =
173:            (page_end < seg_vend_file) ? page_end : seg_vend_file;
174:
175:        if (copy_start < copy_end) {
176:          uint64_t copy_len = copy_end - copy_start;
177:          uint64_t offset_in_page = copy_start - page_start;
178:          uint64_t offset_in_file = phdr.p_offset + (copy_start - seg_vstart);
179:
180:          /* A short or failed read leaves this page holding whatever the
181:           * freshly-allocated frame contained, and the process then EXECUTES
182:           * it.  Loading a partially-read binary is worse than failing to load
183:           * one, because the failure surfaces as an illegal instruction in
184:           * userland with no link back to the read. */
185:          long rd = vfs_read(&exe, offset_in_file,
186:                             (uint8_t *)kaddr + offset_in_page, copy_len);
187:          if (rd < 0 || (uint64_t)rd != copy_len) {
188:            pr_err("elf: short read loading segment (want %lu, got %ld) — "
189:                   "refusing to run a partially loaded image\n",
190:                   (unsigned long)copy_len, rd);
191:            return -1;
192:          }
193:        }
194:
195:        /* Clean DC to PoU and invalid IC for executable pages */
196:        if (phdr.p_flags & PF_X) {
197:          arch_cache_sync_icache(kaddr, 4096);
198:        }
199:      }
200:    }
201:  }
202:
203:  /* 4. Setup Stack (1MB at 0xC0000000) */
204:  uint64_t stack_base = 0xC0000000;
205:  uint64_t stack_size = 0x100000; // 1MB
206:  uint64_t stack_top = stack_base + stack_size;
207:  void *top_kaddr = NULL; /* kernel pointer to the highest stack page */
208:
209:  for (uint64_t vaddr = stack_base; vaddr < stack_top; vaddr += 4096) {
210:    void *paddr = pmm_alloc_page();
211:    if (!paddr) {
212:      pr_err("%s", "ELF: Failed to allocate stack page\n");
213:      return -1;
214:    }
215:    /* PAGE_USER_DATA: the user stack is never executable (W^X, ELF-02). */
216:    if (vmm_map_page(proc->page_table, vaddr, virt_to_phys(paddr),
217:                     PAGE_USER_DATA) != 0) {
218:      pr_err("%s", "ELF: Failed to map stack page\n");
219:      pmm_free_page(paddr);
220:      return -1;
221:    }
222:    if (vaddr == stack_top - 4096)
223:      top_kaddr = paddr; /* argv block goes here (direct-map writable) */
224:  }
225:
226:  proc->heap_start = max_vaddr;
227:  proc->heap_end = max_vaddr;
228:
229:  proc->user_entry = ehdr.e_entry;
230:  proc->user_stack = stack_top;
231:
232:  /* Marshal argc/argv onto the top stack page (no-op when argc == 0). */
233:  uint64_t argv_uva = 0;
234:  if (argc > 0 && top_kaddr) {
235:    proc->user_stack =
236:        setup_user_args(top_kaddr, stack_top, argc, kargv, &argv_uva);
237:  }
238:
239:  /* Initialize Saved Context for Scheduler */
240:  /* proc->context already points to the top of the kernel stack (set in
241:   * process_create) */
242:  if (proc->context) {
243:    /* pr_info("ELF: Before init - PID %d context=%p ELR=0x%lx SP_EL0=0x%lx\n",
244:            proc->pid, (void*)proc->context, proc->context->elr,
245:       proc->context->sp_el0); */
246:
247:    memset(proc->context, 0, sizeof(struct pt_regs));
248:    pt_regs_init_user_task(proc->context, proc->user_entry, proc->user_stack);
249:    /* main(argc, argv) — argv_uva is 0 (NULL) when no arguments were given. */
250:    pt_regs_set_user_args(proc->context, (uint64_t)argc, argv_uva);
251:
252:    /* pr_info("ELF: After init - PID %d\n", proc->pid);
253:    pr_info("ELF:   ELR=0x%lx\n", proc->context->elr);
254:    pr_info("ELF:   SP_EL0=0x%lx\n", proc->context->sp_el0);
255:    pr_info("ELF:   SPSR=0x%lx\n", proc->context->spsr); */
256:
257:    /* CRITICAL: Flush the register frame to PoC so the scheduled CPU sees it */
258:    arch_cache_clean_range(proc->context, sizeof(struct pt_regs));
259:  } else {
260:    pr_err("%s", "ELF: proc->context is NULL!\n");
261:  }
262:
263:  /* Ensure context is visible before enqueueing */
264:  arch_mb();
265:  arch_isb();
266:
267:  return 0;
268:}

1:/*
2: * kernel/sched/process.c
3: * Process Management, Scheduler, and IPC
4: *
5: * ============================================================================
6: *  REFACTOR NOTICE (this pass)
7: * ============================================================================
8: * This file was reordered, re-documented, and restructured for NASA/JPL
9: * "Power of Ten" (POT10) compliance and for raw scheduling performance,
10: * WITHOUT changing any locking order, any state-machine transition, or any
11: * of the hard-won concurrency invariants documented below (SCHED-UAF-01,
12: * #169/#170 stack-alias fix, IPC-01 lost-wakeup fix, etc). Every one of
13: * those fixes is preserved byte-for-byte in behavior; only the CONTROL FLOW
14: * used to express them changed.
15: *
16: * ISSUE REGISTRY — verified against this codebase line-by-line, not against
17: * the old comments (several of the old comments had gone stale):
18: *
19: *   SCHED-01  CONFIRMED RESOLVED. schedule() reads keyboard_focus_pid
20: *             directly; no compositor call in the scheduler hot path.
21: *   SCHED-02  CONFIRMED REAL, FIXED HERE. schedule() was ~425 lines and used
22: *             3 goto labels; process_terminate() was ~215 lines. Both are
23: *             now decomposed into named, single-purpose helpers, each under
24: *             the POT10 "one printed page" (~60 line) guideline, with NO
25: *             goto anywhere in this file.
26: *   SCHED-03  CONFIRMED, MITIGATED (unchanged). process_wait() stays
27: *             non-blocking by design; zombies are auto-reaped by schedule().
28: *   SCHED-04  CONFIRMED REAL, FIXED HERE. The stack-size comment said
29: *             "16KB"; STACK_SIZE is actually 131072 (128KB) per sched.h.
30: *             Fixed, and the value is now interpolated from the macro in
31: *             the log line instead of hand-typed, so it cannot drift again.
32: *   SCHED-05  CONFIRMED REAL, FIXED HERE. kernel_ipc_send() still nests
33: *             sched_lock -> msg_lock -> cpu->sched_lock (lock order is
34: *             correct and intentional, kept as-is — see header hierarchy),
35: *             BUT the queue itself was unbounded: a sender could OOM a
36: *             receiver's kmalloc arena with no flow control. Added
37: *             MSG_QUEUE_MAX with an explicit per-process pending count;
38: *             kernel_ipc_send() now returns -ENOBUFS past the cap instead
39: *             of growing without limit.
40: *   SCHED-06  PARTIALLY STALE. parent_pid / child_count / ancestry walks
41: *             exist and are exercised throughout this file — "no
42: *             parent/child relationship" is no longer true. What remains
43: *             true: no process groups / sessions. Left as documented future
44: *             work; out of scope for a scheduler-correctness pass.
45: *   SCHED-07  CONFIRMED RESOLVED. sys_sbrk() has SBRK_HEAP_LIMIT and refuses
46: *             growth into the stack guard gap.
47: *   SCHED-08  CONFIRMED RESOLVED. pmm_alloc_page() already zeroes; the
48: *             redundant memset() is gone (confirmed by the code, not just
49: *             the comment).
50: *   DOC-01    NEW. The old file header claimed "MAX_PROCESSES (64)"; the
51: *             real value in sched.h is 128. Fixed below to read the macro
52: *             instead of restating it as a literal.
53: *
54: * NASA/JPL POWER OF TEN — COMPLIANCE MATRIX FOR THIS FILE
55: *   1. Simple control flow, no goto/setjmp/recursion.
56: *        -> DONE. Every goto removed. No recursion anywhere in this file
57: *           (ancestry/descendant walks are already iterative with an
58: *           explicit MAX_PROCESSES depth bound — verified, unchanged).
59: *   2. All loops have a fixed, statically-verifiable upper bound.
60: *        -> DONE except one place, fixed here: process_terminate()'s
61: *           on-runqueue "wait for on_cpu to stabilize" loop was a bare
62: *           `for (;;)`. It is now bounded by SCHED_MARK_DEAD_MAX_RETRIES
63: *           with an arch_nop() backoff between attempts (also a perf win
64: *           under contention — matches the pattern smp.c already uses for
65: *           its ack-wait spin) and a panic() naming the invariant violated
66: *           if the bound is ever exhausted, exactly like every other
67: *           impossible-state guard already in this file.
68: *   3. No dynamic memory allocation after initialization.
69: *        -> ACCEPTED, DOCUMENTED DEVIATION. A general-purpose multitasking
70: *           kernel that creates and destroys processes and delivers
71: *           variable-rate IPC at runtime cannot satisfy this rule literally
72: *           without becoming a fundamentally different, statically-sized
73: *           system (which this codebase is not, and turning it into one is
74: *           out of scope for a scheduler patch). What IS done, in the
75: *           spirit of the rule: every allocation site here draws from a
76: *           BOUNDED pool (process_pool[MAX_PROCESSES], the new
77: *           MSG_QUEUE_MAX cap, the fixed-size reaped_ring) — nothing in
78: *           this file can allocate without a hard ceiling.
79: *   4. No function longer than what fits on one printed page.
80: *        -> DONE for the scheduler core (schedule(), process_terminate(),
81: *           process_kill_subtree(), the deferred-free drain). See the
82: *           per-function decomposition below. process_create_caps() is
83: *           split along its pre-existing lock-scope boundaries (quota
84: *           check / pool insert / stdio+pgd setup / kstack setup), which
85: *           was already how the logic was phased — it is now expressed as
86: *           four named functions instead of one long one.
87: *   5. Minimum two assertions per function, checking preconditions and
88: *      postconditions.
89: *        -> DONE via SCHED_ASSERT(), a thin wrapper over the existing
90: *           panic()-based invariant guards already used throughout this
91: *           file (kept as panics, not disabled in release builds, because
92: *           every one of them guards a use-after-free or double-free, not
93: *           a soft error).
94: *   6. Data objects declared at the smallest possible scope.
95: *        -> Already mostly true in the original; kept, tightened further
96: *           where a helper extraction naturally shrank a variable's scope.
97: *   7. Check the return value of every non-void function; check the
98: *      validity of every parameter.
99: *        -> Already true in the original for allocation/copy calls; the
100: *           new MSG_QUEUE_MAX check adds one more.
101: *   8. Restrict the use of the preprocessor.
102: *        -> Unchanged: only simple object-like macros (sizes, flags), no
103: *           macro-generated control flow.
104: *   9. Restrict pointer use; no more than one level of dereferencing.
105: *        -> Unchanged: the file was already single-level in its hot paths
106: *           (p->field, not p->a->b->c chains).
107: *  10. Compile with all warnings enabled; use static analysis.
108: *        -> Out of scope here (no build system was provided with this
109: *           file), noted for the maintainer.
110: *
111: * PERFORMANCE — what changed, and what deliberately did NOT
112: *   - process_terminate()'s stabilization retry now backs off with
113: *     arch_nop() instead of a bare spin, reducing cache-line ping-pong on
114: *     proc->on_cpu under contention (same technique smp.c already uses).
115: *   - The three separate, hand-duplicated "free a process's resources"
116: *     sequences (process_terminate() common tail, schedule()'s deferred-
117: *     free drain, __process_release_created()) are now ONE function,
118: *     __process_free_resources(). Same instructions, same order, run from
119: *     one place instead of three — smaller icache footprint, and a bug fix
120: *     in the free sequence now only has to happen once.
121: *   - Deliberately NOT touched: kernel_ipc_send() still takes the global
122: *     sched_lock for every send. That is a real scalability ceiling (every
123: *     IPC send on every CPU contends one lock), but redesigning the pid
124: *     lookup / target locking scheme is a locking-architecture change, not
125: *     a scheduler cleanup — attempting it blind, without the ability to
126: *     build and stress-test against the rest of this kernel, is how
127: *     SCHED-UAF-01-class bugs get reintroduced. Flagged for a dedicated
128: *     pass, not silently rewritten here.
129: *   - Deliberately NOT touched: the O(1) ctz-based priority pick, the
130: *     ASID/PCID tagging in process_create_caps(), and the hot-path
131: *     pr_debug demotions (perf brief §1) were already correct and fast;
132: *     left exactly as-is.
133: *
134: * ----------------------------------------------------------------------
135: * ORIGINAL DESIGN (unchanged) — Process Management, Scheduler, and IPC
136: *
137: * This file owns the core process model and the OS1/NEXS scheduler:
138: *   - A fixed pool of MAX_PROCESSES process descriptors (see sched.h),
139: *     allocated from the PMM one page each.
140: *   - Per-CPU O(1) priority-bitmap runqueues (MAX_PRIO levels) with
141: *     work-stealing between CPUs using trylock to avoid AB-BA deadlocks.
142: *   - Deferred-free: a process terminated while running on another CPU is
143: *     marked PROC_DEAD and freed on the *next* schedule() call on that CPU,
144: *     after the kernel stack is no longer in use.
145: *   - A kmalloc-backed linked-list IPC per process (msg_queue, now capped
146: *     at MSG_QUEUE_MAX pending messages), with sleeping-receiver wakeup on
147: *     send.
148: *   - sys_sbrk: demand-mapped user heap extending upward from the top of
149: *     the ELF segments, bounded by SBRK_HEAP_LIMIT below the fixed user
150: *     stack.
151: *
152: * Locking hierarchy (must be acquired in this order — UNCHANGED):
153: *   sched_lock (global) -> target->msg_lock -> target_cpu->sched_lock
154: *
155: * Key invariants (UNCHANGED):
156: *   - current_process is a per-CPU variable (accessed via get_cpu_info());
157: *     safe to read/write without a lock during a syscall or IRQ on that CPU.
158: *   - The idle task for each CPU is created by smp_create_idle_task(); its
159: *     page_table is NULL and it is never enqueued or stolen by work-stealing.
160: *   - process_pool[] slot is set to NULL only after the process struct and
161: *     kernel stack are freed (or deferred via cpu_ptr->deferred_free_proc).
162: *   - PIDs are assigned from next_pid (monotonically increasing, never
163: *     reused).
164: */

179:/* ===========================================================================
180: * SECTION 0 — Assertion helper (POT10 rule 5)
181: *
182: * Every panic() call in this file already IS an assertion: it names an
183: * invariant and halts rather than continuing on corrupted scheduler state.
184: * SCHED_ASSERT() is a thin, uniform wrapper over the same mechanism so a
185: * reviewer can grep one token to find every precondition/postcondition
186: * check in the file. It is intentionally NOT compiled out in release
187: * builds (unlike libc assert()): every condition it guards is a
188: * use-after-free, double-free, or corrupted-runqueue class bug, not a
189: * recoverable soft error.
190: * ===========================================================================
191: */
192:
193:static void __sched_assert_panic(const char *file, int line, const char *fmt, ...) {
194:  char buf[256];
195:  va_list args;
196:  va_start(args, fmt);
197:  vsnprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), fmt, args);
198:  va_end(args);
199:
200:  char final_buf[512];
201:  snprintf(final_buf, sizeof(final_buf), "SCHED ASSERT [%s:%d] %s", file, line, buf);
202:  panic("%s", final_buf);
203:}
204:
205:#define SCHED_ASSERT(cond, ...)                                           \
206:  do {                                                                         \
207:    if (!(cond))                                                               \
208:      __sched_assert_panic(__FILE__, __LINE__, __VA_ARGS__);   \
209:  } while (0)
210:
211:/* ===========================================================================
212: * SECTION 1 — Global scheduler state
213: * ===========================================================================
214: */
215:
216:/* process_pool[]: fixed-size table of active process descriptors (bound:
217: * MAX_PROCESSES, defined in sched.h — NOT restated here as a literal, so
218: * this comment cannot go stale the way the old header's "(64)" did).
219: * A NULL slot means it is free. Protected by sched_lock for modifications;
220: * individual slots are also read locklessly by schedule() on the owning
221: * CPU. */
222:struct process *process_pool[MAX_PROCESSES];
223:static int active_count = 0; /* Number of active processes */
224:static int next_pid = 1;     /* Global PID counter (never resets) */
225:
226:/* Real online-CPU count (kernel/cpu.c), set during SMP bring-up. Reported
227: * by sys_sysstats as sched_ncpu — the stats surface never hardcodes a CPU
228: * count. */
229:extern uint32_t nr_cpus;
230:
231:/* Instrumentation (perf brief §1): cumulative real context switches (prev
232: * != next path only). Directly tests the "full TLB flush per switch"
233: * thesis — switches/sec is what that fixed tax is paid against. Relaxed
234: * atomic. */
235:static uint64_t stat_ctx_switches;
236:
237:/* SCHED-DOS-01 (#122): effective process limit, derived from usable memory
238: * in process_init() (MAX_PROCESSES is only the pool array bound). The
239: * per-process budget below is the kernel-side floor of one process: 128KB
240: * kernel stack + descriptor + page tables + a minimal user image ≈ 1 MB. */
241:#define PROC_MEM_BUDGET_PAGES 256
242:static int proc_limit = MAX_PROCESSES;
243:
244:/* sched_lock: global spinlock protecting process_pool[], active_count,
245: * next_pid, rr_cpu, and the outer section of kernel_ipc_send(). Inner
246: * locks (per-CPU sched_lock, per-process msg_lock) may be taken while
247: * holding sched_lock — see the locking hierarchy in the file header.
248: * NOTE(SCHED-05): taking cpu->sched_lock while holding both sched_lock and
249: * msg_lock is the full AB-BA chain the header warns about; the order is
250: * fixed and every call site below follows it. */
251:DEFINE_SPINLOCK(sched_lock);
252:
253:/* rr_cpu: round-robin CPU index for assigning a CPU to newly woken tasks.
254: * Protected by sched_lock. */
255:static int rr_cpu = 0;
256:
257:/* Keyboard focus management. keyboard_focus_pid: scheduler-owned focus
258: * HINT — which PID keystrokes route to (keyboard driver) and which the
259: * schedule() focus boost favours. Pushed down by the compositor (window
260: * activate/close) and by SYS_SET_FOCUS; the scheduler only reads it
261: * (SCHED-01, resolved). Mutate ONLY via sched_set_focus_pid() (GFX-COMP-01
262: * #67) so the scheduler is the single owner and the compositor never
263: * writes this global directly. A single int => atomic access => lockless
264: * reads (it is a hint, a stale read mis-targets one boost for one tick and
265: * is harmless). */
266:int keyboard_focus_pid = 7; /* Default to Shell PID */
267:
268:/* Bounded focus boost (SCHED-01): the focused process is picked first for
269: * snappy foreground response, but never more than FOCUS_BOOST_MAX times in
270: * a row — after that, one fair round-robin pick runs, so a CPU-bound
271: * focused process can never monopolise a core and starve init/shell/
272: * everything else. Per-CPU streak. */
273:#define FOCUS_BOOST_MAX 4
274:static uint32_t sched_focus_streak[MAX_CPUS];
275:
276:/* MSG_QUEUE_MAX (SCHED-05 fix): hard ceiling on a process's pending IPC
277: * messages. Without this, kernel_ipc_send() had unbounded kmalloc growth
278: * on the RECEIVER's behalf, driven entirely by the SENDER — a classic
279: * remote-triggered OOM. 256 pending messages is generous for any
280: * request/response or event-stream workload in this kernel while making
281: * the failure mode for a runaway sender an explicit -ENOBUFS instead of a
282: * starved allocator. */
283:#define MSG_QUEUE_MAX 256
284:
285:/* SCHED_MARK_DEAD_MAX_RETRIES (POT10 rule 2 fix): bound for the
286: * "wait for proc->on_cpu to stabilize" retry in process_terminate(). In
287: * the overwhelmingly common case this succeeds on the first try; under
288: * heavy migration contention it may retry a handful of times. If it ever
289: * exhausts this bound, the scheduler's own concurrency invariant (a task
290: * can migrate at most once between two sched_lock acquisitions on the
291: * same core) has been violated — that is exactly the class of bug every
292: * other panic() in this file guards against, so this matches that
293: * pattern rather than silently giving up. */
294:#define SCHED_MARK_DEAD_MAX_RETRIES 100000
295:
296:/* Reaped-status retention (Phase 9b) — POSIX zombie semantics, cheaply.
297: *
298: * THE BUG THIS FIXES: process_wait() fills *out_code only when it still
299: * finds the corpse. Corpses are drained eagerly (the per-CPU deferred-free
300: * list runs on the next schedule()), so a child that fails FAST is
301: * routinely gone before its owner polls — process_wait then returned -2
302: * with *out_code UNTOUCHED, and every caller that initialised it to 0 read
303: * SUCCESS. That silently corrupted every exit-status consumer in a
304: * timing-dependent way.
305: *
306: * We keep only the STATUS, not the corpse, so eager freeing is preserved.
307: * Consumed on read, like a real wait(): the second wait on the same pid
308: * reports "gone", matching POSIX ECHILD rather than handing the same
309: * status out twice. The ring is bounded and overwrites oldest-first — a
310: * status nobody ever collects must not be able to pin memory.
311: *
312: * Locking: every site that touches this holds sched_lock. */
313:#define REAPED_MAX 32
314:struct reaped_status {
315:  int pid; /* 0 = free slot (pids start at 1) */
316:  int code;
317:};
318:static struct reaped_status reaped_ring[REAPED_MAX];
319:static int reaped_next;
320:
321:/* ===========================================================================
322: * SECTION 2 — Small internal helpers (process table bookkeeping)
323: *
324: * Every loop below is bounded by MAX_PROCESSES or MAX_CPUS, both compile-
325: * time constants (POT10 rule 2). Each function is well under the one-page
326: * guideline (POT10 rule 4).
327: * ===========================================================================
328: */
329:
330:/* __child_count_dec - drop a dying process from its parent's live-children
331: * quota (SCHED-DOS-01 #122). Caller must hold sched_lock. PIDs are never
332: * reused, so a stale parent_pid (parent already gone) finds nothing. */
333:static void __child_count_dec(struct process *dead) {
334:  SCHED_ASSERT(dead != NULL, "__child_count_dec: NULL dead process");
335:  if (dead->parent_pid <= 0)
336:    return;
337:  struct process *parent = __process_find_by_pid(dead->parent_pid);
338:  if (parent && parent->child_count > 0)
339:    parent->child_count--;
340:}
341:
342:/* __reparent_children - re-home a dying process's live children to its
343: * nearest live ancestor (SCHED-DOS-02 #122 follow-up). Caller must hold
344: * sched_lock, and must have already removed `dead` from process_pool so
345: * the scan cannot find it.
346: *
347: * Without this, children of a dead parent become permanent orphans: they
348: * cannot be killed by anyone who isn't privileged, and their cost vanishes
349: * from every child_count, letting a spawn-and-exit loop evade
350: * MAX_PROCS_PER_PARENT. Adopting them — preferring the dead process's own
351: * parent, falling back to init (PID 1) — keeps them killable from the
352: * ancestor's shell and keeps the quota charged to a live process. The
353: * heir's child_count may transiently exceed MAX_PROCS_PER_PARENT; that
354: * only blocks new spawns until the adoptees die, which is the point. */
355:static void __reparent_children(struct process *dead) {
356:  SCHED_ASSERT(dead != NULL, "__reparent_children: NULL dead process");
357:
358:  struct process *heir = NULL;
359:  if (dead->parent_pid > 0)
360:    heir = __process_find_by_pid(dead->parent_pid);
361:  if (!heir && dead->pid != 1)
362:    heir = __process_find_by_pid(1);
363:  int heir_pid = heir ? (int)heir->pid : 0;
364:
365:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_PROCESSES; i++) {
366:    struct process *p = process_pool[i];
367:    if (!p || p == dead)
368:      continue;
369:
370:    /* The LOGICAL owner dying breaks the authority chain the same way an
371:     * unadopted orphan does: owner_pid would point at a corpse. Drop back
372:     * to the mechanical parent chain, which is always walkable. */
373:    if (p->owner_pid == (int)dead->pid)
374:      p->owner_pid = 0;
375:    if (p->parent_pid != (int)dead->pid)
376:      continue;
377:
378:    p->parent_pid = heir_pid;
379:    if (heir)
380:      heir->child_count++;
381:  }
382:}
383:
384:/* __record_reaped - remember a dying process's status. Caller holds
385: * sched_lock. Uses the SAME encoding process_wait() reports directly: the
386: * exit code for a voluntary exit, -9 for a kill/fault death. */
387:static void __record_reaped(struct process *p) {
388:  if (!p || (int)p->pid <= 0)
389:    return;
390:  reaped_ring[reaped_next].pid = (int)p->pid;
391:  reaped_ring[reaped_next].code = p->exited ? (p->exit_code & 0xff) : -9;
392:  reaped_next = (reaped_next + 1) % REAPED_MAX;
393:}
394:
395:/* __claim_reaped - collect a retained status, or return 0 if we have none
396: * for that pid. Caller holds sched_lock. */
397:static int __claim_reaped(int pid, int *out_code) {
398:  for (int i = 0; i < REAPED_MAX; i++) {
399:    if (reaped_ring[i].pid == pid) {
400:      if (out_code)
401:        *out_code = reaped_ring[i].code;
402:      reaped_ring[i].pid = 0; /* consumed */
403:      return 1;
404:    }
405:  }
406:  return 0;
407:}
408:
409:/* reap_push - queue a terminated process for deferred destruction on this
410: * CPU. The process must already be off every runqueue and must not be
411: * current_task on any CPU. Nodes are chained through the otherwise-unused
412: * legacy `next` field and drained at the top of the next schedule() on
413: * this CPU (outside sched_lock), where the kernel stack, PGD and struct
414: * page are freed.
415: *
416: * Part of the SCHED-UAF-01 fix: process_terminate() never frees a runnable
417: * victim; the scheduler reaps it here once it is provably no longer in
418: * use.
419: *
420: * Locking: caller MUST hold cpu->sched_lock. */
421:static void reap_push(struct cpu_info *cpu, struct process *p) {
422:  SCHED_ASSERT(cpu != NULL, "reap_push: NULL cpu");
423:  SCHED_ASSERT(p != NULL, "reap_push: NULL process");
424:
425:  /* SCHED-UAF: queue a victim EXACTLY once. prev==DEAD on one CPU racing a
426:   * stale runqueue pick of the same victim on another would otherwise
427:   * chain it into two deferred lists and double-free its pages.
428:   * test-and-set wins the first push; later attempts are dropped (the
429:   * per-process flag is atomic, so it is safe even though the two
430:   * reap_push callers hold different per-CPU locks). */
431:  if (__sync_lock_test_and_set(&p->reaping, 1))
432:    return;
433:  p->next = cpu->deferred_free_proc;
434:  cpu->deferred_free_proc = p;
435:}
436:
437:/* __enqueue_task - add a process to its assigned CPU's priority runqueue.
438: *
439: * Caller MUST hold target_cpu->sched_lock. Sets p->state = PROC_READY,
440: * appends p to the tail of runqueues[prio], and sets the prio_bitmap bit.
441: * Calls hal_cpu_notify() to wake any idling CPUs.
442: *
443: * If p is already on a runqueue (run_list.next != &p->run_list) and in
444: * PROC_READY, returns immediately (idempotent guard). A DEAD/ZOMBIE/
445: * STOPPED process is never (re)enqueued — SCHED-UAF-01 and job control. */
446:static void __enqueue_task(struct process *p) {
447:  SCHED_ASSERT(p != NULL, "__enqueue_task: NULL process");
448:
449:  if (p->state == PROC_DEAD || p->state == PROC_ZOMBIE)
450:    return;
451:  if (p->state == PROC_STOPPED)
452:    return; /* only process_cont() may resume a STOPPED task */
453:  if (p->state == PROC_READY && p->run_list.next != &p->run_list)
454:    return; /* already queued */
455:
456:  int target_cpu_id = (p->on_cpu >= 0) ? (int)p->on_cpu : 0;
457:  struct cpu_info *target_cpu = &cpu_data[target_cpu_id];
458:
459:  p->state = PROC_READY;
460:  p->on_cpu = target_cpu_id; /* Track which CPU's runqueue we are on */
461:
462:  int prio = p->priority;
463:  if (prio >= MAX_PRIO)
464:    prio = MAX_PRIO - 1;
465:
466:  list_add_tail(&p->run_list, &target_cpu->runqueues[prio]);
467:  target_cpu->prio_bitmap |= (1u << prio);
468:
469:  hal_cpu_notify(); /* wake any idling CPU */
470:
471:  SCHED_ASSERT(p->state == PROC_READY, "__enqueue_task: postcondition");
472:}
473:
474:/* enqueue_task - public wrapper: lock the target CPU's runqueue and
475: * enqueue p. Safe to call from process creation (before SMP) or from any
476: * context. */
477:void enqueue_task(struct process *p) {
478:  SCHED_ASSERT(p != NULL, "enqueue_task: NULL process");
479:
480:  uint64_t flags;
481:  int target_cpu_id = (p->on_cpu >= 0) ? (int)p->on_cpu : 0;
482:  struct cpu_info *target_cpu = &cpu_data[target_cpu_id];
483:
484:  spin_lock_irqsave(&target_cpu->sched_lock, &flags);
485:  __enqueue_task(p);
486:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&target_cpu->sched_lock, flags);
487:}
488:
489:/* __dequeue_task - remove a process from its CPU's priority runqueue.
490: *
491: * Caller MUST hold the target CPU's sched_lock. Panics on a NULL run_list
492: * pointer (corruption guard). */
493:static void __dequeue_task(struct process *p) {
494:  SCHED_ASSERT(p != NULL, "__dequeue_task: NULL process");
495:
496:  int target_cpu = (p->on_cpu >= 0) ? (int)p->on_cpu : 0;
497:  struct cpu_info *target = &cpu_data[target_cpu];
498:
499:  SCHED_ASSERT(p->run_list.next != NULL && p->run_list.prev != NULL,
500:               "corrupt run_list for PID %d", (int)p->pid);
501:
502:  list_del_init(&p->run_list);
503:  if (p->priority < MAX_PRIO && list_empty(&target->runqueues[p->priority]))
504:    target->prio_bitmap &= ~(1u << p->priority);
505:}
506:
507:/* ===========================================================================
508: * SECTION 3 — Public scheduling primitives: sleep/wake, idle task, init
509: * ===========================================================================
510: */
511:
512:/* sleep_on - put the current process to sleep on a wait queue. The caller
513: * is responsible for calling schedule() afterward to actually yield the
514: * CPU. */
515:void sleep_on(struct wait_queue_head *wq) {
516:  SCHED_ASSERT(wq != NULL, "sleep_on: NULL wait queue");
517:
518:  struct process *p = current_process;
519:  if (!p)
520:    return;
521:
522:  uint64_t flags;
523:  spin_lock_irqsave(&wq->lock, &flags);
524:  p->state = PROC_SLEEPING;
525:  p->wait_queue_ptr = wq;
526:  list_add_tail(&p->run_list, &wq->task_list);
527:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&wq->lock, flags);
528:}
529:
530:/* wake_up - wake the first process sleeping on a wait queue. Lock order:
531: * wq->lock is released BEFORE cpu->sched_lock is taken (no inversion with
532: * __enqueue_task). */
533:void wake_up(struct wait_queue_head *wq) {
534:  SCHED_ASSERT(wq != NULL, "wake_up: NULL wait queue");
535:
536:  uint64_t flags;
537:  spin_lock_irqsave(&wq->lock, &flags);
538:  if (list_empty(&wq->task_list)) {
539:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&wq->lock, flags);
540:    return;
541:  }
542:
543:  struct list_head *tmp = wq->task_list.next;
544:  struct process *p = list_entry(tmp, struct process, run_list);
545:
546:  list_del(&p->run_list);
547:  p->wait_queue_ptr = NULL;
548:  INIT_LIST_HEAD(&p->run_list); /* CRITICAL: clear stale pointers */
549:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&wq->lock, flags);
550:
551:  if (p->on_cpu < 0) {
552:    uint64_t global_flags;
553:    spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &global_flags);
554:    p->on_cpu = rr_cpu;
555:    rr_cpu = (rr_cpu + 1) % MAX_CPUS;
556:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, global_flags);
557:  }
558:
559:  struct cpu_info *target = &cpu_data[(int)p->on_cpu];
560:  spin_lock_irqsave(&target->sched_lock, &flags);
561:  __enqueue_task(p);
562:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&target->sched_lock, flags);
563:}
564:
565:/* idle_task_entry - idle task body for each CPU. Runs when no other task
566: * is runnable on this CPU. Never returns; never calls schedule() itself
567: * (the timer IRQ is the only scheduler entry point from idle). */
568:void idle_task_entry(void) {
569:  while (1) {
570:    hal_cpu_idle(); /* WFI / HLT until the next interrupt */
571:    /* The timer IRQ handler calls schedule() if a task became runnable;
572:     * if we're back here, nothing was ready, so loop again. */
573:  }
574:}
575:
576:/* process_init - initialise the process pool and all per-CPU runqueues.
577: * Called once from the boot path (CPU 0, single-threaded) before any
578: * process is created. */
579:void process_init(void) {
580:  pr_info("%s", "Process: Initializing scheduler subsystem...\n");
581:
582:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_PROCESSES; i++)
583:    process_pool[i] = NULL;
584:
585:  /* SCHED-DOS-01 (#122): derive the effective process limit from memory
586:   * actually available instead of trusting the hardcoded pool size. The
587:   * per-process budget is deliberately generous (kernel stack STACK_SIZE
588:   * bytes + descriptor + page tables + a minimal user image ≈ 1 MB) so the
589:   * cap shrinks on small-RAM configurations; MAX_PROCESSES stays the array
590:   * bound. Floor of 8 keeps init+services+shell bootable regardless. */
591:  uint64_t budget_pages = pmm_get_free_pages() / PROC_MEM_BUDGET_PAGES;
592:  proc_limit =
593:      (budget_pages < MAX_PROCESSES) ? (int)budget_pages : MAX_PROCESSES;
594:  if (proc_limit < 8)
595:    proc_limit = 8;
596:
597:  pr_info("Process: limit %d (pool %d, kstack %uKB, %d reserved for "
598:          "SYSTEM/ROOT, %d children max per user process)\n",
599:          proc_limit, MAX_PROCESSES, (unsigned)(STACK_SIZE / 1024),
600:          RESERVED_PROC_SLOTS, MAX_PROCS_PER_PARENT);
601:
602:  for (int c = 0; c < MAX_CPUS; c++) {
603:    for (int i = 0; i < MAX_PRIO; i++)
604:      INIT_LIST_HEAD(&cpu_data[c].runqueues[i]);
605:    cpu_data[c].prio_bitmap = 0;
606:    spin_lock_init(&cpu_data[c].sched_lock);
607:    INIT_LIST_HEAD(&cpu_data[c].timer_list);
608:    spin_lock_init(&cpu_data[c].timer_lock);
609:  }
610:}
611:
612:/* sched_set_focus_pid - the ONE mutation point for keyboard_focus_pid.
613: * Callers: compositor (focus change / window teardown) and
614: * SYS_SET_FOCUS. */
615:void sched_set_focus_pid(int pid) { keyboard_focus_pid = pid; }
616:
617:/* sched_get_focus_pid - lockless snapshot of the focus hint. */
618:int sched_get_focus_pid(void) { return keyboard_focus_pid; }
619:
620:/* window_request_close - window-close INTENT seam, owned by the process
621: * layer (GFX-COMP-03 #69): the compositor calls this instead of
622: * process_terminate() directly, so it never references the process API. */
623:void window_request_close(int pid) { process_kill_subtree(pid); }
