625:/* ===========================================================================
626: * SECTION 4 — Process table lookups and authority checks
627: * ===========================================================================
628: */
629:
630:/* find_free_slot - first NULL slot in process_pool[]. Caller MUST hold
631: * sched_lock. O(MAX_PROCESSES). */
632:static int find_free_slot(void) {
633:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_PROCESSES; i++)
634:    if (process_pool[i] == NULL)
635:      return i;
636:  return -1;
637:}
638:
639:/* __process_find_by_pid - find a process by PID without locking
640: * (internal). Caller MUST hold sched_lock. */
641:struct process *__process_find_by_pid(int pid) {
642:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_PROCESSES; i++)
643:    if (process_pool[i] && (int)process_pool[i]->pid == pid)
644:      return process_pool[i];
645:  return NULL;
646:}
647:
648:/* process_find_by_pid - find a process by PID with locking (external).
649: * The returned pointer is only valid as long as the caller can guarantee
650: * the process is not terminated. */
651:struct process *process_find_by_pid(int pid) {
652:  uint64_t flags;
653:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
654:  struct process *proc = __process_find_by_pid(pid);
655:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
656:  return proc;
657:}
658:
659:/* proc_pid_is_privileged - a pid's privilege as a VALUE, not a pointer.
660: *
661: * process_find_by_pid() hands back a pointer only valid while the caller
662: * can guarantee the process stays alive, which callers outside the
663: * scheduler cannot. The compositor needs to ASK this while already holding
664: * compositor_lock (process_terminate() takes sched_lock then trylocks
665: * compositor_lock — the answer must be fetched before compositor_lock is
666: * taken, as a plain int that cannot dangle).
667: *
668: * Locking: acquires/releases sched_lock internally. Callers must NOT hold
669: * a lock that any sched_lock holder may block on. */
670:int proc_pid_is_privileged(int pid) {
671:  uint64_t flags;
672:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
673:  struct process *p = __process_find_by_pid(pid);
674:  int privileged = p ? proc_is_privileged(p) : 0;
675:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
676:  return privileged;
677:}
678:
679:/* process_set_owner - set a process's LOGICAL parent (Q3, ASTRA §6.5).
680: * Called only from the OBJ_CTL_SETOWNER capability path, which has
681: * already checked DESTROY on the target and that the caller is
682: * privileged. The owner must be a LIVE process. */
683:int process_set_owner(int pid, int owner_pid) {
684:  uint64_t flags;
685:  int ret = -ESRCH;
686:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
687:  struct process *p = __process_find_by_pid(pid);
688:  if (p && __process_find_by_pid(owner_pid)) {
689:    p->owner_pid = owner_pid;
690:    ret = 0;
691:  }
692:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
693:  return ret;
694:}
695:
696:/* proc_get_lineage - report a process's spawning parent AND logical
697: * owner. owner_pid is the one inheritance should follow (Phase 9c: with
698: * execution behind a service, the mechanical parent is nxexec, not the
699: * process that actually asked). */
700:int proc_get_lineage(int pid, int *parent, int *owner) {
701:  uint64_t flags;
702:  int ret = -1;
703:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
704:  struct process *p = __process_find_by_pid(pid);
705:  if (p) {
706:    if (parent)
707:      *parent = p->parent_pid;
708:    if (owner)
709:      *owner = p->owner_pid > 0 ? p->owner_pid : p->parent_pid;
710:    ret = 0;
711:  }
712:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
713:  return ret;
714:}
715:
716:/* process_kill_allowed - ABI-04 capability check for SYS_KILL.
717: *
718: * Policy (checked under sched_lock so the target cannot be recycled
719: * mid-decision): privileged callers may kill anything; any process may
720: * kill itself and its DESCENDANTS (the parent/owner chain is walked, so
721: * grandchildren count too — orphans are re-homed to a live ancestor by
722: * __reparent_children() so a dead link cannot hide a descendant);
723: * everything else is denied. A missing target is "allowed":
724: * process_terminate() reports the real not-found case.
725: *
726: * Loop bound: MAX_PROCESSES (POT10 rule 2). The ancestry walk is acyclic
727: * for the plain parent chain (a parent always has a smaller PID);
728: * owner_pid is set by a privileged service and is NOT guaranteed smaller,
729: * so the explicit depth bound is the real termination guarantee here, not
730: * belt-and-braces. */
731:int process_kill_allowed(struct process *caller, int target_pid) {
732:  if (!caller)
733:    return 1; /* kernel context */
734:  if (proc_is_privileged(caller))
735:    return 1;
736:  if ((int)caller->pid == target_pid)
737:    return 1;
738:
739:  uint64_t flags;
740:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
741:  struct process *target = __process_find_by_pid(target_pid);
742:  int allowed = !target;
743:
744:  for (int depth = 0; target && depth < MAX_PROCESSES; depth++) {
745:    int up = target->owner_pid > 0 ? target->owner_pid : target->parent_pid;
746:    if (up == (int)caller->pid) {
747:      allowed = 1;
748:      break;
749:    }
750:    if (up <= 0)
751:      break;
752:    target = __process_find_by_pid(up);
753:  }
754:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
755:  return allowed;
756:}
757:
758:/* process_ipc_allowed - may 'caller' send IPC to target_pid without
759: * CAP_IPC_ANY? Allowed to the caller's parent or any descendant (walk
760: * bounded by MAX_PROCESSES, acyclic since parent PID < child PID). */
761:int process_ipc_allowed(struct process *caller, int target_pid) {
762:  if (proc_has_cap(caller, CAP_IPC_ANY))
763:    return 1;
764:  if ((int)caller->pid == target_pid)
765:    return 1;
766:  if (caller->parent_pid == target_pid)
767:    return 1;
768:
769:  uint64_t flags;
770:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
771:  struct process *t = __process_find_by_pid(target_pid);
772:  int allowed = 0;
773:
774:  for (int depth = 0; t && depth < MAX_PROCESSES; depth++) {
775:    if (t->parent_pid == (int)caller->pid) {
776:      allowed = 1;
777:      break;
778:    }
779:    if (t->parent_pid <= 0)
780:      break;
781:    t = __process_find_by_pid(t->parent_pid);
782:  }
783:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
784:  return allowed;
785:}
786:
787:/* ===========================================================================
788: * SECTION 5 — Per-process environment (Phase 17)
789: *
790: * Storage is one page per process, allocated at spawn and copied from the
791: * creator. All access below runs under sched_lock, the same lock that
792: * already guards the process table these lookups go through.
793: * ===========================================================================
794: */
795:
796:/* __env_find - slot holding 'key' in p's block, or NULL. Lock held. */
797:static struct env_entry *__env_find(struct process *p, const char *key) {
798:  if (!p || !p->env || !key || !*key)
799:    return NULL;
800:  for (int i = 0; i < ENV_MAX; i++)
801:    if (p->env->e[i].k[0] && strcmp(p->env->e[i].k, key) == 0)
802:      return &p->env->e[i];
803:  return NULL;
804:}
805:
806:int proc_env_get(int pid, const char *key, char *buf, size_t size) {
807:  if (!key || !buf || size == 0)
808:    return -EINVAL;
809:
810:  uint64_t flags;
811:  int ret = -ENOENT;
812:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
813:  struct env_entry *e = __env_find(__process_find_by_pid(pid), key);
814:  if (e) {
815:    strncpy(buf, e->v, size - 1);
816:    buf[size - 1] = '\0';
817:    ret = 0;
818:  }
819:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
820:  return ret;
821:}
822:
823:int proc_env_set(struct process *caller, int pid, const char *key,
824:                 const char *value) {
825:  if (!key || !*key)
826:    return -EINVAL;
827:  /* Reject a key that would be silently truncated: a setenv that quietly
828:   * stored a DIFFERENT name than asked for would make the matching getenv
829:   * miss, harder to diagnose than a refusal. */
830:  if (strlen(key) >= ENV_KEY_MAX || (value && strlen(value) >= ENV_VAL_MAX))
831:    return -EINVAL;
832:  /* Self is always allowed; anyone else needs privilege (NULL caller is
833:   * kernel-internal, already fully privileged). */
834:  if (caller && (int)caller->pid != pid && !proc_is_privileged(caller))
835:    return -EPERM;
836:
837:  uint64_t flags;
838:  int ret;
839:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
840:  struct process *p = __process_find_by_pid(pid);
841:  if (!p) {
842:    ret = -ESRCH;
843:  } else if (!p->env) {
844:    /* No block and none can be made here: allocating under sched_lock
845:     * would invert the PMM lock against it. Blocks are allocated at
846:     * spawn, so this is only reachable when that allocation failed. */
847:    ret = -ENOMEM;
848:  } else {
849:    struct env_entry *e = __env_find(p, key);
850:    if (!value || !*value) {
851:      if (e)
852:        e->k[0] = '\0'; /* free the slot: unset */
853:      ret = 0;
854:    } else {
855:      if (!e) { /* first write of this name: claim a free slot */
856:        for (int i = 0; i < ENV_MAX; i++)
857:          if (!p->env->e[i].k[0]) {
858:            e = &p->env->e[i];
859:            strncpy(e->k, key, ENV_KEY_MAX - 1);
860:            e->k[ENV_KEY_MAX - 1] = '\0';
861:            break;
862:          }
863:      }
864:      if (!e) {
865:        ret = -ENOMEM; /* block full */
866:      } else {
867:        strncpy(e->v, value, ENV_VAL_MAX - 1);
868:        e->v[ENV_VAL_MAX - 1] = '\0';
869:        ret = 0;
870:      }
871:    }
872:  }
873:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
874:  return ret;
875:}
876:
877:int proc_env_enum(int pid, char *buf, size_t size) {
878:  if (!buf || size == 0)
879:    return -1;
880:
881:  uint64_t flags;
882:  size_t used = 0;
883:  buf[0] = '\0';
884:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
885:  struct process *p = __process_find_by_pid(pid);
886:  if (p && p->env) {
887:    for (int i = 0; i < ENV_MAX; i++) {
888:      const char *k = p->env->e[i].k;
889:      if (!k[0])
890:        continue;
891:      size_t kl = strlen(k);
892:      if (used + kl + 2 > size) /* +1 separator, +1 NUL */
893:        break;
894:      if (used)
895:        buf[used++] = '\n';
896:      memcpy(buf + used, k, kl);
897:      used += kl;
898:      buf[used] = '\0';
899:    }
900:  }
901:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
902:  return (int)used;
903:}
904:
905:void proc_env_free(struct process *p) {
906:  if (!p || !p->env)
907:    return;
908:  struct env_block *b = p->env;
909:  p->env = NULL;
910:  pmm_free_page(b);
911:}
912:
913:/* ===========================================================================
914: * SECTION 6 — Process creation
915: *
916: * process_create_caps() is expressed as four helpers along the SAME
917: * lock-scope boundaries the original code already used (envblk allocated
918: * before sched_lock; pool insert under sched_lock; stdio/ctty/pgd after
919: * releasing it; kernel-stack setup last). This is not a behavioral change,
920: * only naming the phases that were already there (POT10 rule 4).
921: * ===========================================================================
922: */
923:
924:/* __proc_create_check_quota - SCHED-DOS-01 (#122) admission control.
925: * Caller MUST hold sched_lock. Returns 0 if the new process may be
926: * admitted, -1 if a quota was hit (message already logged). */
927:static int __proc_create_check_quota(struct process *creator,
928:                                     const char *name) {
929:  if (active_count >= proc_limit) {
930:    pr_debug("Process: limit %d reached, refusing '%s'\n", proc_limit, name);
931:    return -1;
932:  }
933:  if (!proc_is_privileged(creator)) {
934:    if (creator->child_count >= MAX_PROCS_PER_PARENT) {
935:      pr_debug("Process: PID %d hit the %d-children quota, refusing '%s'\n",
936:               creator->pid, MAX_PROCS_PER_PARENT, name);
937:      return -1;
938:    }
939:    if (active_count >= proc_limit - RESERVED_PROC_SLOTS) {
940:      pr_debug("Process: only reserved slots left, refusing user '%s'\n", name);
941:      return -1;
942:    }
943:  }
944:  return 0;
945:}
946:
947:/* __proc_create_identity - fill in PID, ASID, priority, capability clamp,
948: * cwd, and env inheritance for a freshly-claimed slot. Caller MUST hold
949: * sched_lock (the fields written here are read by other sched_lock
950: * holders as soon as the slot is published). */
951:static void __proc_create_identity(struct process *proc, int slot,
952:                                   const char *name, uint8_t priority,
953:                                   uint8_t level, uint32_t req_caps,
954:                                   struct process *creator,
955:                                   struct env_block *envblk) {
956:  strncpy(proc->name, name, PROCESS_NAME_MAX - 1);
957:  proc->name[PROCESS_NAME_MAX - 1] = '\0';
958:
959:  /* Idle tasks (kernel threads) draw PIDs from a dedicated high band: with
960:   * the K3 gate they are created BEFORE init, and PID 1 must stay
961:   * reserved for init (orphan reparenting and compositor init-authority
962:   * checks key on pid==1). */
963:  if (priority == PROC_PRIO_IDLE) {
964:    static int next_idle_pid = 32000;
965:    proc->pid = next_idle_pid++;
966:  } else {
967:    proc->pid = next_pid++;
968:  }
969:
970:  /* Address-space tag for TLB-tagged switches (perf §3): pool slot + 1, so
971:   * it is unique among all live address spaces. 0 is reserved for the
972:   * kernel/idle space. */
973:  proc->asid = (uint16_t)(slot + 1);
974:
975:  proc->priority = (priority >= MAX_PRIO) ? (uint8_t)(MAX_PRIO - 1) : priority;
976:
977:  /* Capability/level monotonic cut (USR-SEC-03 #79): the child is never
978:   * more privileged than its creator, never exceeds its level's ceiling,
979:   * never holds a capability the creator lacks. A machine creator (and the
980:   * kernel-internal NULL creator) bypasses the clamp. */
981:  {
982:    uint8_t lvl = (level < PLVL_COUNT) ? level : PLVL_GUEST;
983:    if (creator && creator->level > lvl)
984:      lvl = creator->level;
985:    uint32_t caps = req_caps & caps_for_level(lvl);
986:    if (creator && !proc_is_machine(creator))
987:      caps &= creator->caps;
988:    proc->level = lvl;
989:    proc->caps = caps;
990:  }
991:
992:  proc->parent_pid = creator ? (int)creator->pid : 0;
993:  proc->owner_pid = 0; /* set only via OBJ_CTL_SETOWNER (Q3) */
994:  proc->exit_code = 0;
995:  proc->exited = 0;
996:
997:  proc->state = PROC_CREATED;
998:  proc->first_run = 1; /* ELF loader will initialize context */
999:  proc->time_slice = DEFAULT_QUANTUM;
1000:  proc->quantum_reset = DEFAULT_QUANTUM;
1001:  proc->on_cpu = -1;
1002:  INIT_LIST_HEAD(&proc->wait_queue.task_list);
1003:  spin_lock_init(&proc->wait_queue.lock);
1004:  proc->ipc_target_pid = -1;
1005:  INIT_LIST_HEAD(&proc->run_list);
1006:  INIT_LIST_HEAD(&proc->msg_queue);
1007:  proc->msg_count = 0; /* SCHED-05 fix: explicit pending-message counter */
1008:  spin_lock_init(&proc->msg_lock);
1009:  spin_lock_init(&proc->mm_lock);
1010:
1011:  /* Filesystem init: a child inherits the spawner's cwd (POSIX).
1012:   * Kernel/boot creations (no creator) start at "/". */
1013:  if (creator && creator->cwd[0])
1014:    strncpy(proc->cwd, creator->cwd, sizeof(proc->cwd));
1015:  else
1016:    strncpy(proc->cwd, "/", sizeof(proc->cwd));
1017:  proc->cwd[sizeof(proc->cwd) - 1] = '\0';
1018:
1019:  /* Environment: same inheritance rule as cwd (Phase 17). A COPY, not a
1020:   * shared pointer — sharing would let a parent's later setenv rewrite a
1021:   * running child's environment. The page arrived zeroed from the PMM. */
1022:  proc->env = envblk;
1023:  if (envblk && creator && creator->env)
1024:    memcpy(envblk, creator->env, sizeof(*envblk));
1025:}
1026:
1027:/* __proc_create_stdio_and_pgd - controlling terminal, stdio handles, and
1028: * user page table. Called OUTSIDE sched_lock (compositor + object-table +
1029: * vmm locks are taken here). Kernel threads (PROC_PRIO_IDLE / _SYSTEM)
1030: * take the lean path: no ctty, no stdio, no user PGD (shared kernel_pgd,
1031: * SCHED-UAF-01) — kernel-thread creation stays free of compositor/object/
1032: * vmm lock traffic. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure (caller rolls
1033: * back the pool slot). */
1034:static int __proc_create_stdio_and_pgd(struct process *proc,
1035:                                       struct process *creator,
1036:                                       uint8_t priority) {
1037:  proc->ctty_win = -1;
1038:
1039:  if (priority == PROC_PRIO_IDLE || priority == PROC_PRIO_SYSTEM) {
1040:    proc->page_table = NULL;
1041:    return 0;
1042:  }
1043:
1044:  if (creator) {
1045:    extern int compositor_get_window_by_pid(int pid);
1046:    int term = compositor_get_window_by_pid((int)creator->pid);
1047:    proc->ctty_win = (term > 0) ? term : creator->ctty_win;
1048:  }
1049:
1050:  /* stdin/stdout/stderr as capability handles 0/1/2 (ASTRA §6.2). Done
1051:   * after ctty so the console's stdout resolves correctly. */
1052:  if (process_install_stdio(proc, creator) != 0)
1053:    return -1;
1054:
1055:  proc->page_table = vmm_create_pgd();
1056:  return 0;
1057:}
1058:
1059:/* __proc_create_rollback - undo a partially-created process on any
1060: * failure path below. Caller holds NO lock. slot must be the pool index
1061: * proc currently occupies. */
1062:static void __proc_create_rollback(struct process *proc, int slot,
1063:                                   struct env_block *envblk) {
1064:  uint64_t flags;
1065:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
1066:  process_pool[slot] = NULL;
1067:  active_count--;
1068:  __child_count_dec(proc);
1069:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
1070:  if (envblk)
1071:    pmm_free_page(envblk);
1072:  if (proc->page_table)
1073:    vmm_destroy_pgd(proc->page_table);
1074:  pmm_free_page(proc);
1075:}
1076:
1077:/* process_create - spawn at 'level' with that level's default preset. The
1078: * per-level capability ceiling lives in caps_for_level() (caps.h) — the
1079: * ONE definition the kernel and userland permissions view both derive
1080: * from. */
1081:struct process *process_create(const char *name, uint8_t priority,
1082:                               uint8_t level) {
1083:  uint8_t lvl = (level < PLVL_COUNT) ? level : PLVL_GUEST;
1084:  return process_create_caps(name, priority, lvl, caps_for_level(lvl));
1085:}
1086:
1087:/* process_create_caps - allocate and initialise a new process descriptor.
1088: *
1089: * On failure, partially-allocated resources are freed and NULL is
1090: * returned. The process is left in state PROC_CREATED; the caller must
1091: * still call process_load_elf() and process_finalize_spawn() /
1092: * enqueue_task() to make it runnable.
1093: *
1094: * Locking: holds sched_lock (irqsave) while modifying process_pool[] and
1095: *          next_pid; releases before vmm_create_pgd() (which takes
1096: *          mm_lock) and before the kernel-stack allocation.
1097: * IRQ context: no. */
1098:struct process *process_create_caps(const char *name, uint8_t priority,
1099:                                    uint8_t level, uint32_t req_caps) {
1100:  pr_debug("Process: Creating '%s' (Prio=%d)\n", name, priority);
1101:
1102:  /* Environment page BEFORE sched_lock: the PMM takes its own lock, and
1103:   * allocating inside sched_lock would introduce a sched_lock -> pmm_lock
1104:   * order nothing else in this file establishes. Idle/kernel threads have
1105:   * no environment to inherit, so they skip this. */
1106:  struct env_block *envblk = NULL;
1107:  if (priority != PROC_PRIO_IDLE)
1108:    envblk = (struct env_block *)pmm_alloc_page();
1109:
1110:  uint64_t flags;
1111:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
1112:
1113:  struct process *creator = current_process;
1114:  if (__proc_create_check_quota(creator, name) != 0) {
1115:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
1116:    if (envblk)
1117:      pmm_free_page(envblk);
1118:    return NULL;
1119:  }
1120:
1121:  int slot = find_free_slot();
1122:  if (slot < 0) {
1123:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
1124:    if (envblk)
1125:      pmm_free_page(envblk);
1126:    pr_err("%s", "Process pool full!\n");
1127:    return NULL;
1128:  }
1129:
1130:  struct process *proc = (struct process *)pmm_alloc_page();
1131:  if (!proc) {
1132:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
1133:    if (envblk)
1134:      pmm_free_page(envblk);
1135:    return NULL;
1136:  }
1137:  /* No memset here: pmm_alloc_page() already returns a fully zeroed page
1138:   * (SCHED-08, confirmed resolved — the old redundant second zeroing is
1139:   * gone). */
1140:
1141:  __proc_create_identity(proc, slot, name, priority, level, req_caps, creator,
1142:                         envblk);
1143:
1144:  process_pool[slot] = proc;
1145:  active_count++;
1146:  if (creator)
1147:    creator->child_count++; /* paired with __child_count_dec at release */
1148:
1149:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
1150:
1151:  pr_debug("process_create: '%s' PID=%u slot=%u Prio=%d\n", name,
1152:           (uint32_t)proc->pid, (uint32_t)slot, (int)proc->priority);
1153:
1154:  if (__proc_create_stdio_and_pgd(proc, creator, priority) != 0) {
1155:    __proc_create_rollback(proc, slot, NULL /* envblk already owned by proc */);
1156:    return NULL;
1157:  }
1158:
1159:  /* Kernel stack: STACK_SIZE bytes (see sched.h — was miscommented as
1160:   * "16KB" here; SCHED-04, fixed: the actual value is interpolated in
1161:   * process_init()'s boot log, not hand-typed, so this cannot drift
1162:   * again). */
1163:  void *kstack_base = pmm_alloc_pages(STACK_SIZE / 4096);
1164:  if (!kstack_base) {
1165:    __proc_create_rollback(proc, slot, NULL);
1166:    return NULL;
1167:  }
1168:  proc->kernel_stack = (uint64_t)kstack_base + STACK_SIZE;
1169:  proc->context =
1170:      (struct pt_regs *)(proc->kernel_stack - sizeof(struct pt_regs));
1171:  memset(proc->context, 0, sizeof(struct pt_regs));
1172:  proc->on_cpu = -1; /* not running on any CPU yet */
1173:
1174:  SCHED_ASSERT(proc->state == PROC_CREATED,
1175:               "process_create_caps: postcondition state");
1176:  SCHED_ASSERT(proc->context != NULL,
1177:               "process_create_caps: postcondition context");
1178:  return proc;
1179:}
1180:
1181:/* smp_create_idle_task - create and pin the idle task for a specific CPU.
1182: * The idle task is a pure kernel thread: page_table is NULL
1183: * (arch_cpu_switch_context loads the shared kernel_pgd when page_table is
1184: * NULL, SCHED-UAF-01). Memory barriers + a D-cache clean ensure the
1185: * secondary CPU sees the fully initialised context before it starts
1186: * scheduling. */
1187:void smp_create_idle_task(uint32_t cpu_id) {
1188:  extern void idle_task_entry(void);
1189:
1190:  if (cpu_id >= MAX_CPUS)
1191:    return;
1192:
1193:  struct process *idle = process_create("idle", PROC_PRIO_IDLE, PLVL_MACHINE);
1194:  if (!idle)
1195:    return;
1196:
1197:  idle->on_cpu = cpu_id;
1198:
1199:  struct cpu_info *info = &cpu_data[cpu_id];
1200:  info->idle_task = idle;
1201:
1202:  memset(idle->context, 0, sizeof(struct pt_regs));
1203:  pt_regs_init_kernel_task(idle->context, (uint64_t)idle_task_entry,
1204:                           idle->kernel_stack);
1205:
1206:  hal_cache_clean(idle, sizeof(struct process));
1207:  hal_cache_clean(idle->context, sizeof(struct pt_regs));
1208:  hal_mb();
1209:  hal_isb();
1210:}
1211:
1212:/* kthread_create - create and enqueue a runnable KERNEL SERVICE thread.
1213: *
1214: * !!! UNSTABLE / NO IN-TREE CALLER — DO NOT WIRE UP (KTHREAD-STATUS). A
1215: * kthread created here runs OUTSIDE the per-CPU idle-task ordering the SMP
1216: * scheduler relies on. Kept as staged scaffolding only; migrate services
1217: * to SUPERVISED USERLAND PROCESSES instead. */
1218:struct process *kthread_create(const char *name, void (*entry)(void)) {
1219:  struct process *t = process_create(name, PROC_PRIO_SYSTEM, PLVL_MACHINE);
1220:  if (!t)
1221:    return NULL;
1222:
1223:  memset(t->context, 0, sizeof(struct pt_regs));
1224:  pt_regs_init_kernel_task(t->context, (uint64_t)entry, t->kernel_stack);
1225:
1226:  hal_cache_clean(t, sizeof(struct process));
1227:  hal_cache_clean(t->context, sizeof(struct pt_regs));
1228:  hal_mb();
1229:  hal_isb();
1230:
1231:  enqueue_task(t);
1232:  return t;
1233:}
1234:
1235:/* kthread_block - block the calling kernel thread on a wait queue until
1236: * wake_up(), UNLESS 'still_block' reports the wait condition already
1237: * cleared.
1238: *
1239: * Lost-wakeup safety: still_block(arg) is evaluated UNDER the wq lock,
1240: * right before committing to sleep, serializing against a producer's
1241: * wake_up() (which also takes the wq lock). No event is ever both
1242: * published and missed. still_block may be NULL for an unconditional
1243: * block. */
1244:void kthread_block(struct wait_queue_head *wq, int (*still_block)(void *),
1245:                   void *arg) {
1246:  struct process *self = current_process;
1247:  if (!self)
1248:    return;
1249:
1250:  uint64_t flags = local_irq_save();
1251:  uint64_t wqflags;
1252:  spin_lock_irqsave(&wq->lock, &wqflags);
1253:  if (still_block && !still_block(arg)) {
1254:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&wq->lock, wqflags);
1255:    local_irq_restore(flags);
1256:    return;
1257:  }
1258:  self->state = PROC_SLEEPING;
1259:  self->wait_queue_ptr = wq;
1260:  list_add_tail(&self->run_list, &wq->task_list);
1261:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&wq->lock, wqflags);
1262:
1263:  arch_cpu_yield(); /* returns here once scheduled again (woken) */
1264:
1265:  local_irq_restore(flags);
1266:}
1267:
1268:/* ===========================================================================
1269: * SECTION 7 — Process teardown
1270: *
1271: * __process_free_resources() is the single place that frees a process's
1272: * kernel-owned resources. It used to be hand-duplicated three times
1273: * (process_terminate()'s common tail, schedule()'s deferred-free drain,
1274: * __process_release_created()); a fix to the free sequence now only has
1275: * to happen once, and the three call sites are half the size they were.
1276: * ===========================================================================
1277: */
1278:
1279:/* __process_free_resources - close handles, free the env page, kernel
1280: * stack, page table, and the process struct's own page, in that fixed
1281: * order. Caller MUST NOT hold sched_lock or any per-CPU sched_lock (this
1282: * runs entirely lock-free against the scheduler; process_handles_destroy
1283: * takes object_lock internally). Caller MUST have already removed the
1284: * process from process_pool[] and from every runqueue / wait queue. */
1285:static void __process_free_resources(struct process *p) {
1286:  SCHED_ASSERT(p != NULL, "__process_free_resources: NULL process");
1287:
1288:  process_handles_destroy(p); /* close capability handles, free objects */
1289:  proc_env_free(p);           /* Phase 17: release the environment page */
1290:  if (p->kernel_stack)
1291:    pmm_free_pages((void *)(p->kernel_stack - STACK_SIZE), STACK_SIZE / 4096);
1292:  if (p->page_table)
1293:    vmm_destroy_pgd(p->page_table);
1294:  pmm_free_page(p);
1295:}
1296:
1297:/* __process_release_created - tear down a half-built PROC_CREATED child
1298: * (SCHED-UAF Pitfall B). Caller holds NO lock. */
1299:static void __process_release_created(struct process *p) {
1300:  uint64_t flags;
1301:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
1302:  int slot = -1;
1303:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_PROCESSES; i++)
1304:    if (process_pool[i] == p) {
1305:      slot = i;
1306:      break;
1307:    }
1308:  if (slot >= 0) {
1309:    process_pool[slot] = NULL;
1310:    active_count--;
1311:    __child_count_dec(p);
1312:    __reparent_children(p);
1313:  }
1314:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
1315:
1316:  __process_free_resources(p);
1317:}
1318:
1319:/* process_finalize_spawn - commit a freshly-loaded child against a
1320: * concurrent kill (SCHED-UAF Pitfall B). Under sched_lock: if a kill was
1321: * DEFERRED while the ELF loaded (kill_pending), release the child; else
1322: * enqueue it. Both checks are under the global sched_lock, so a kill on
1323: * another CPU cannot slip between them (global -> per-CPU lock order, as
1324: * in kernel_ipc_send). */
1325:void process_finalize_spawn(struct process *p) {
1326:  if (!p)
1327:    return;
1328:
1329:  uint64_t flags;
1330:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
1331:  int killed = p->kill_pending;
1332:  if (!killed) {
1333:    int tcpu = (p->on_cpu >= 0) ? (int)p->on_cpu : 0;
1334:    struct cpu_info *tc = &cpu_data[tcpu];
1335:    spin_lock(&tc->sched_lock);
1336:    __enqueue_task(p);
1337:    spin_unlock(&tc->sched_lock);
1338:  }
1339:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
1340:
1341:  if (killed)
1342:    __process_release_created(p);
1343:}
1344:
1345:/* process_abort_spawn - the ELF load failed; release the half-built
1346: * child. A concurrent kill may have set kill_pending (deferred to us);
1347: * either way the child is torn down. */
1348:void process_abort_spawn(struct process *p) {
1349:  if (p)
1350:    __process_release_created(p);
1351:}
1352:
1353:/* __proc_terminate_detach_from_wait_queue - if proc is parked on a wait
1354: * queue, detach it first so a concurrent wake_up() can never resurrect
1355: * the victim. Caller holds sched_lock. */
1356:static void __proc_terminate_detach_from_wait_queue(struct process *proc) {
1357:  if (!proc->wait_queue_ptr)
1358:    return;
1359:  struct wait_queue_head *wq = proc->wait_queue_ptr;
1360:  spin_lock(&wq->lock);
1361:  list_del_init(&proc->run_list);
1362:  proc->wait_queue_ptr = NULL;
1363:  spin_unlock(&wq->lock);
1364:}
1365:
1366:/* __proc_terminate_mark_dead_on_runqueue - proc is PROC_READY or
1367: * PROC_RUNNING. Mark it PROC_DEAD under the OWNING CPU's sched_lock so
1368: * the mark is ordered against that CPU's schedule() (which cannot
1369: * re-enqueue or free a DEAD task). proc->on_cpu can change between our
1370: * read of it and taking that CPU's lock (work-stealing needs the SAME
1371: * lock, so once we hold it the victim cannot migrate further) — re-check
1372: * after locking and retry if it moved.
1373: *
1374: * POT10 rule 2: bounded by SCHED_MARK_DEAD_MAX_RETRIES with an arch_nop()
1375: * backoff between attempts (was a bare `for(;;)` — see file header). */
1376:static void __proc_terminate_mark_dead_on_runqueue(struct process *proc) {
1377:  for (int attempt = 0; attempt < SCHED_MARK_DEAD_MAX_RETRIES; attempt++) {
1378:    int vcpu = (proc->on_cpu >= 0) ? proc->on_cpu : 0;
1379:    struct cpu_info *vc = &cpu_data[vcpu];
1380:
1381:    spin_lock(&vc->sched_lock);
1382:    if ((proc->on_cpu >= 0 ? proc->on_cpu : 0) != vcpu) {
1383:      spin_unlock(&vc->sched_lock);
1384:      arch_nop(); /* contention backoff, same pattern as smp.c's ack wait */
1385:      continue;
1386:    }
1387:    proc->state = PROC_DEAD;
1388:    spin_unlock(&vc->sched_lock);
1389:    return;
1390:  }
1391:  panic("SCHED: PID %d on_cpu never stabilized after %d retries — "
1392:        "scheduler migration invariant violated",
1393:        (int)proc->pid, SCHED_MARK_DEAD_MAX_RETRIES);
1394:}
1395:
1396:/* __proc_still_current_anywhere - is proc current_task on ANY CPU right
1397: * now? Scan EVERY CPU (bound: MAX_CPUS) rather than trusting proc->on_cpu,
1398: * which can be stale (mid-migration, or between a runqueue pick and the
1399: * on_cpu write) — the #169/#170 root fix. Each CPU's current_task is read
1400: * under THAT CPU's sched_lock. */
1401:static int __proc_still_current_anywhere(struct process *proc) {
1402:  for (int c = 0; c < MAX_CPUS; c++) {
1403:    struct cpu_info *vc = &cpu_data[c];
1404:    int hit;
1405:    spin_lock(&vc->sched_lock);
1406:    hit = (vc->current_task == proc);
1407:    spin_unlock(&vc->sched_lock);
1408:    if (hit)
1409:      return 1;
1410:  }
1411:  return 0;
1412:}
1413:
1414:/* __proc_terminate_pool_remove - drop proc from process_pool[], retain its
1415: * exit status, and re-home its children. Caller holds sched_lock. Returns
1416: * the vacated slot index, or -1 if proc was already gone from the pool. */
1417:static int __proc_terminate_pool_remove(struct process *proc) {
1418:  int slot = -1;
1419:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_PROCESSES; i++)
1420:    if (process_pool[i] == proc) {
1421:      slot = i;
1422:      break;
1423:    }
1424:  if (slot >= 0) {
1425:    __record_reaped(proc); /* 9b: status must outlive the freed struct */
1426:    process_pool[slot] = NULL;
1427:    active_count--;
1428:    __child_count_dec(proc);
1429:    __reparent_children(proc);
1430:  }
1431:  return slot;
1432:}
1433:
1434:/* __proc_terminate_drain_ipc - discard proc's pending IPC queue (the
1435: * victim will never read it). Held under msg_lock to serialise against a
1436: * concurrent pop_message() on the victim's CPU. */
1437:static void __proc_terminate_drain_ipc(struct process *proc) {
1438:  struct list_head *pos, *q;
1439:  spin_lock(&proc->msg_lock);
1440:  list_for_each_safe(pos, q, &proc->msg_queue) {
1441:    struct ipc_node *node = list_entry(pos, struct ipc_node, list);
1442:    list_del(pos);
1443:    kfree(node);
1444:  }
1445:  proc->msg_count = 0;
1446:  spin_unlock(&proc->msg_lock);
1447:}
1448:
1449:/* process_terminate - remove a process from the scheduler and free
1450: * resources.
1451: *
1452: * Disposition depends on where the victim is in its lifecycle:
1453: *   - self-termination (current_process == proc): marked PROC_ZOMBIE; the
1454: *     caller (sys_exit) MUST call schedule() to switch away, which
1455: *     auto-reaps the zombie via the deferred-free stack.
1456: *   - PROC_CREATED (mid ELF-load on another CPU): kill is DEFERRED
1457: *     (kill_pending), released by process_finalize_spawn()/
1458: *     process_abort_spawn() (SCHED-UAF Pitfall B).
1459: *   - PROC_READY / PROC_RUNNING: marked PROC_DEAD under the owning CPU's
1460: *     sched_lock; reaped by that CPU's next schedule() (SCHED-UAF-01).
1461: *   - otherwise (SLEEPING or CREATED-never-scheduled): detached from any
1462: *     wait queue, marked DEAD; freed immediately IFF provably not
1463: *     current_task anywhere, else left for the owning CPU's schedule() to
1464: *     reap.
1465: *
1466: * Machine-level processes cannot be terminated (ABI-04 last-resort
1467: * guard).
1468: *
1469: * Locking: acquires sched_lock (irqsave) for pool manipulation; also
1470: *          acquires wq->lock / cpu->sched_lock (not irqsave — already
1471: *          inside the irqsave section) to detach/mark the victim.
1472: * Returns: 0 on success (including idempotent no-op), -1 if not found or
1473: *          protected. */
1474:int process_terminate(int pid) {
1475:  uint64_t flags;
1476:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
1477:
1478:  struct process *proc = __process_find_by_pid(pid);
1479:  if (!proc) {
1480:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
1481:    return -1;
1482:  }
1483:
1484:  if (proc_is_machine(proc)) {
1485:    pr_warn("Cannot terminate protected process '%s' (PID %d)\n", proc->name,
1486:            pid);
1487:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
1488:    return -1;
1489:  }
1490:
1491:  /* IDEMPOTENT (SCHED-UAF, the PMM double-free): a victim already
1492:   * DEAD/ZOMBIE is already committed to the reaper. A second terminate
1493:   * (external kill racing a self-exit; window-close + kill) must not fall
1494:   * through to the free tail a second time. */
1495:  if (proc->state == PROC_DEAD || proc->state == PROC_ZOMBIE) {
1496:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
1497:    return 0;
1498:  }
1499:
1500:  pr_debug("Terminating process '%s' PID=%d\n", proc->name, pid);
1501:
1502:  /* Mark ->dying FIRST so a racing SYS_CREATE_WINDOW on this process's own
1503:   * CPU is refused, then tear down its windows. compositor_lock is taken
1504:   * here (BLOCKING) — this is the sched_lock -> compositor_lock order;
1505:   * nothing may take the two in reverse. */
1506:  proc->dying = 1;
1507:  extern void compositor_destroy_windows_by_pid(int pid);
1508:  compositor_destroy_windows_by_pid(pid);
1509:
1510:  /* Self-termination: standing on this process's kernel stack, cannot
1511:   * free it now. schedule() auto-reaps the zombie once we switch away. */
1512:  if (current_process == proc) {
1513:    proc->state = PROC_ZOMBIE;
1514:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
1515:    return 0;
1516:  }
1517:
1518:  /* SCHED-UAF Pitfall B: a PROC_CREATED victim is mid-construction in
1519:   * dispatch_spawn (process_load_elf_args mapping its page table on the
1520:   * creator's CPU). Defer instead of freeing now. Do NOT flip it to
1521:   * PROC_DEAD, or a stray reaper would double-free it. */
1522:  if (proc->state == PROC_CREATED) {
1523:    proc->kill_pending = 1;
1524:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
1525:    return 0;
1526:  }
1527:
1528:  /* Cancel any pending timed-sleep timer so its callback cannot fire on
1529:   * the victim after it is freed. Lock order: global sched_lock > per-CPU
1530:   * timer_lock (held). */
1531:  timer_del(&proc->sleep_timer);
1532:  __proc_terminate_drain_ipc(proc);
1533:
1534:  /* SCHED-UAF-01: never free a process that may still be executing on, or
1535:   * be queued on, another CPU. */
1536:  __proc_terminate_detach_from_wait_queue(proc);
1537:
1538:  if (proc->state == PROC_READY || proc->state == PROC_RUNNING) {
1539:    __proc_terminate_mark_dead_on_runqueue(proc);
1540:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
1541:    return 0;
1542:  }
1543:
1544:  /* Common tail: SLEEPING (wait-queue sleeper detached above, or an IPC
1545:   * sleeper from sys_ipc_recv) or CREATED-never-scheduled. Mark DEAD
1546:   * first, then decide WHO frees: only a fully parked corpse (not
1547:   * current_task on ANY CPU) is freed here; otherwise the owning CPU's
1548:   * schedule() reaps it via the prev==DEAD path. Supervisors polling
1549:   * process_wait() must treat -2 as "child gone": an immediately-freed
1550:   * victim never appears as a waitable corpse. */
1551:  proc->state = PROC_DEAD;
1552:  if (__proc_still_current_anywhere(proc)) {
1553:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
1554:    return 0;
1555:  }
1556:
1557:  int slot = __proc_terminate_pool_remove(proc);
1558:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
1559:
1560:  if (slot >= 0)
1561:    __process_free_resources(proc);
1562:  return 0;
1563:}
1564:
1565:/* --- process_kill_subtree() helpers ---------------------------------- */
1566:
1567:struct kill_snap {
1568:  int pid;
1569:  int parent;
1570:  signed char windowless;
1571:  signed char kill;
1572:  signed char machine;
1573:};
1574:
1575:/* __kill_snap_capture - snapshot (pid,parent,machine) for every live
1576: * process under sched_lock, then release it (Pitfall A: sched_lock ->
1577: * compositor_lock is an AB-BA nothing else in this file takes in
1578: * reverse, so the window-type probe below MUST run lock-free). Returns
1579: * the snapshot count and, via *root_idx, the index of root_pid (-1 if
1580: * gone). Loop bound: MAX_PROCESSES. */
1581:static int __kill_snap_capture(struct kill_snap *snap, int root_pid,
1582:                               int *root_idx) {
1583:  int n = 0;
1584:  *root_idx = -1;
1585:
1586:  uint64_t flags;
1587:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
1588:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_PROCESSES; i++) {
1589:    struct process *p = process_pool[i];
1590:    if (!p)
1591:      continue;
1592:    snap[n].pid = (int)p->pid;
1593:    snap[n].parent = p->parent_pid;
1594:    snap[n].windowless = -1;
1595:    snap[n].kill = 0;
1596:    snap[n].machine = proc_is_machine(p) ? 1 : 0;
1597:    if ((int)p->pid == root_pid)
1598:      *root_idx = n;
1599:    n++;
1600:  }
1601:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
1602:  return n;
1603:}
1604:
1605:/* __kill_snap_probe_windows - lock-free TYPE probe: a window owner is
1606: * SPARED. Loop bound: n (<= MAX_PROCESSES). */
1607:static void __kill_snap_probe_windows(struct kill_snap *snap, int n) {
1608:  extern int compositor_get_window_by_pid(int pid);
1609:  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
1610:    snap[i].windowless =
1611:        (compositor_get_window_by_pid(snap[i].pid) > 0) ? 0 : 1;
1612:}
1613:
1614:/* __kill_snap_propagate - a node dies iff its parent dies AND it is
1615: * windowless; a windowed node is spared, pruning its subtree. Iterate to a
1616: * fixpoint (parents may sit after children in pool order). Loop bound:
1617: * n passes * n * n comparisons, all bounded by MAX_PROCESSES (POT10 rule
1618: * 2) — unchanged from the original, just extracted. */
1619:static void __kill_snap_propagate(struct kill_snap *snap, int n) {
1620:  for (int pass = 0; pass < n; pass++) {
1621:    int changed = 0;
1622:    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
1623:      if (snap[i].kill || !snap[i].windowless || snap[i].machine)
1624:        continue; /* ABI-06: a machine descendant is never in the kill set */
1625:      for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
1626:        if (snap[j].kill && snap[j].pid == snap[i].parent) {
1627:          snap[i].kill = 1;
1628:          changed = 1;
1629:          break;
1630:        }
1631:      }
1632:    }
1633:    if (!changed)
1634:      break;
1635:  }
1636:}
1637:
1638:/* __kill_snap_log_spared - diagnostic: surface every "spared because it
1639: * owns a window" decision (flaky-terminate triage: a child that holds
1640: * only a transient window can spare itself at random). */
1641:static void __kill_snap_log_spared(const struct kill_snap *snap, int n,
1642:                                   int root_pid) {
1643:  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
1644:    if (snap[i].kill || snap[i].windowless || snap[i].pid == root_pid)
1645:      continue;
1646:    for (int j = 0; j < n; j++)
1647:      if (snap[j].kill && snap[j].pid == snap[i].parent) {
1648:        pr_info("kill_subtree: sparing windowed PID %d (child of killed %d)\n",
1649:                snap[i].pid, snap[i].parent);
1650:        break;
1651:      }
1652:  }
1653:}
1654:
1655:/* __kill_snap_execute - terminate DESCENDANTS FIRST, root LAST.
1656: * process_terminate(root) reparents the root's live children to init, so
1657: * killing the root first would orphan any descendant whose own terminate
1658: * then races (unreachable from this subtree, survives). process_terminate
1659: * is idempotent; an already-exited snapshot pid is a harmless no-op. */
1660:static void __kill_snap_execute(const struct kill_snap *snap, int n,
1661:                                int root_pid) {
1662:  int kill_failures = 0;
1663:  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
1664:    if (snap[i].kill && snap[i].pid != root_pid)
1665:      if (process_terminate(snap[i].pid) != 0)
1666:        kill_failures++;
1667:  if (process_terminate(root_pid) != 0)
1668:    kill_failures++;
1669:
1670:  if (kill_failures)
1671:    pr_err("kill_subtree(%d): %d victim(s) did not terminate\n", root_pid,
1672:           kill_failures);
1673:}
1674:
1675:/* process_kill_subtree - window-aware EXTERNAL kill
1676: * (docs/PROCESS-KILL-MODEL.md).
1677: *
1678: * Terminates root_pid PLUS every windowless/in-shell descendant, while
1679: * SPARING each descendant that OWNS a window and its whole subtree —
1680: * independent windowed apps keep running; the user closes them via their
1681: * own red button. The TYPE signal is compositor_get_window_by_pid().
1682: *
1683: * ABI-06: a MACHINE-level root is refused OUTRIGHT (not merely spared at
1684: * the end) — PID 1's windowless children ARE the system (services, the
1685: * shell); killing the subtree of an untouchable process would destroy
1686: * exactly what the protection exists to preserve. Machine descendants are
1687: * excluded from the kill set for the same reason. */
1688:void process_kill_subtree(int root_pid) {
1689:  static struct kill_snap snap[MAX_PROCESSES];
1690:  int root_idx;
1691:  int n = __kill_snap_capture(snap, root_pid, &root_idx);
1692:
1693:  if (root_idx < 0)
1694:    return; /* target already gone */
1695:
1696:  if (snap[root_idx].machine) {
1697:    pr_warn("Refusing subtree kill of protected process (PID %d)\n", root_pid);
1698:    return;
1699:  }
1700:
1701:  __kill_snap_probe_windows(snap, n);
1702:  snap[root_idx].kill = 1; /* the explicit target dies regardless */
1703:  __kill_snap_propagate(snap, n);
1704:  __kill_snap_log_spared(snap, n, root_pid);
1705:  __kill_snap_execute(snap, n, root_pid);
1706:}
1707:
1708:/* start_user_process - directly enter a freshly-created user process
1709: * (the very first process / init, or any process launched synchronously).
1710: * Does NOT return; arch_enter_user_mode() performs an EL/ring transition
1711: * and begins executing user code at proc->user_entry. */
1712:void start_user_process(struct process *proc) {
1713:  SCHED_ASSERT(proc != NULL, "start_user_process: NULL proc");
1714:  SCHED_ASSERT(proc->page_table != NULL,
1715:               "start_user_process: PID %d has no page table", (int)proc->pid);
1716:
1717:  pr_info("Starting process '%s' PID=%d at 0x%lx\n", proc->name, proc->pid,
1718:          proc->user_entry);
1719:
1720:  current_process = proc; /* not enqueued: we jump directly to it */
1721:
1722:  uint64_t pgd_phys = virt_to_phys(proc->page_table);
1723:  hal_vmm_set_pgd(pgd_phys);
1724:  hal_tlb_flush_all();
1725:  hal_isb();
1726:
1727:  proc->state = PROC_RUNNING;
1728:  proc->on_cpu = cpu_id();
1729:  arch_enter_user_mode(proc->user_entry, proc->user_stack, proc->kernel_stack);
1730:}
1731:
1732:/* ===========================================================================
1733: * SECTION 8 — The scheduler core: schedule()
1734: *
1735: * Decomposed into named stages, called in sequence, with NO goto anywhere
1736: * (SCHED-02, fixed). Every stage below either:
1737: *   (a) is a pure helper that assumes cpu_ptr->sched_lock is already held
1738: *       and does not itself acquire/release the scheduler lock or touch
1739: *       the IRQ mask, or
1740: *   (b) is the top-level schedule() function itself, which remains the
1741: *       SINGLE owner of lock acquisition, IRQ masking, and every return
1742: *       point — deliberately NOT hidden inside a helper, because the
1743: *       three different exit paths (no-switch/same-task, no-switch/keep-
1744: *       prev, and context-switch) each have a DIFFERENT IRQ-restore
1745: *       contract (SCHED-IRQ-01) that must stay visible at the call site
1746: *       that actually returns from schedule().
1747: * ===========================================================================
1748: */
1749:
1750:/* __sched_reap_deferred - free every process queued for deferred
1751: * destruction on this CPU (SCHED-UAF-01: the only safe point to release a
1752: * kernel stack/PGD that was still in use during the PREVIOUS schedule()
1753: * call on this CPU). The list is popped without a lock: it is strictly
1754: * per-CPU (reap_push only ever runs on the owning CPU) and the function-
1755: * wide IRQ mask in schedule() prevents a nested schedule() from double-
1756: * draining it. Loop bound: the list length, which is bounded by
1757: * MAX_PROCESSES (a process can be queued at most once — reap_push's
1758: * test-and-set guarantees that). */
1759:static void __sched_reap_deferred(struct cpu_info *cpu_ptr) {
1760:  while (cpu_ptr->deferred_free_proc) {
1761:    struct process *to_free = cpu_ptr->deferred_free_proc;
1762:    cpu_ptr->deferred_free_proc = to_free->next;
1763:    to_free->next = NULL;
1764:
1765:    uint64_t gflags;
1766:    spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &gflags);
1767:    __proc_terminate_pool_remove(to_free);
1768:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, gflags);
1769:
1770:    /* Drain leftover IPC messages. process_terminate() drains the queue
1771:     * for an externally-killed victim; a self-terminated zombie keeps any
1772:     * already-queued nodes, so this path must drain too — under
1773:     * msg_lock, matching pop_message()'s lock, or this is a double
1774:     * list_del + double kfree of the same node. */
1775:    __proc_terminate_drain_ipc(to_free);
1776:
1777:    /* Cancel any pending per-process timer BEFORE freeing the PCB so its
1778:     * callback can never fire on freed memory. Defensive on every free
1779:     * path even though a process with an armed timer is PROC_SLEEPING
1780:     * (cannot self-exit): makes the no-UAF invariant hold everywhere. */
1781:    timer_del(&to_free->sleep_timer);
1782:
1783:    __process_free_resources(to_free);
1784:  }
1785:}
1786:
1787:/* __sched_account_time - Tier 3 CPU-time accounting (docs/TIMER-MODEL.md
1788: * §4): charge the raw counter delta since the last schedule on this CPU to
1789: * whoever was running (prev), then mark the start count for the task
1790: * about to be picked. No divide in the hot path; conversion to ns happens
1791: * only when the value is read. arch_timer_get_count() is lock-free/
1792: * IRQ-safe. */
1793:static void __sched_account_time(struct cpu_info *cpu_ptr,
1794:                                 struct process *prev) {
1795:  uint64_t now_cnt = arch_timer_get_count();
1796:  if (prev && cpu_ptr->sched_run_count)
1797:    prev->cpu_time_counts += now_cnt - cpu_ptr->sched_run_count;
1798:  cpu_ptr->sched_run_count = now_cnt;
1799:}
1800:
1801:/* __sched_requeue_pending - re-enqueue the task deferred by the PREVIOUS
1802: * schedule() on THIS CPU (SCHED-UAF #169/#170: by now we have iretq'd off
1803: * its kernel stack, so it is safe for another CPU to run it). If it was
1804: * killed while parked here, reap it instead of resurrecting it. Caller
1805: * holds cpu_ptr->sched_lock. */
1806:static void __sched_requeue_pending(struct cpu_info *cpu_ptr) {
1807:  struct process *pr = cpu_ptr->pending_reenqueue;
1808:  if (!pr)
1809:    return;
1810:  cpu_ptr->pending_reenqueue = NULL;
1811:
1812:  if (pr->state == PROC_DEAD || pr->state == PROC_ZOMBIE) {
1813:    pr->on_cpu = -1;
1814:    reap_push(cpu_ptr, pr);
1815:  } else {
1816:    __enqueue_task(pr);
1817:  }
1818:}
1819:
1820:/* sched_retire_result - outcome of retiring `prev`, telling schedule()
1821: * whether it must jump straight to picking a new task without touching
1822: * `prev` any further. */
1823:enum sched_retire_result {
1824:  SCHED_RETIRE_REAPED,  /* prev was DEAD/ZOMBIE; pushed to the reaper */
1825:  SCHED_RETIRE_HANDLED, /* prev processed normally (re-enqueued or left) */
1826:};
1827:
1828:/* __sched_retire_prev - process the outgoing task. Replaces the original
1829: * `goto pick_next` (which skipped this block entirely for a DEAD/ZOMBIE
1830: * prev) with a plain early-return — no goto needed, since the original
1831: * goto's ONLY effect was "don't run the rest of this function body",
1832: * which a return already does. Caller holds cpu_ptr->sched_lock. */
1833:static enum sched_retire_result __sched_retire_prev(struct cpu_info *cpu_ptr,
1834:                                                    struct process *prev,
1835:                                                    struct pt_regs *regs) {
1836:  if (!prev)
1837:    return SCHED_RETIRE_HANDLED;
1838:
1839:  /* PROC_DEAD: externally terminated while running on this CPU.
1840:   * PROC_ZOMBIE: terminated itself and entered schedule() to switch away.
1841:   * Both are corpses standing on their own kernel stack: queue on the
1842:   * reap stack; the NEXT schedule() on this CPU frees them after the
1843:   * switch. Idle tasks never reach this (never exit, machine-protected). */
1844:  if (prev->state == PROC_DEAD || prev->state == PROC_ZOMBIE) {
1845:    prev->on_cpu = -1;
1846:    reap_push(cpu_ptr, prev);
1847:    cpu_ptr->current_task = NULL;
1848:    return SCHED_RETIRE_REAPED;
1849:  }
1850:
1851:  if (regs)
1852:    prev->context = regs; /* save current context if it was running */
1853:
1854:  if (prev->first_run)
1855:    prev->first_run = 0;
1856:
1857:  if (prev->state == PROC_RUNNING) {
1858:    prev->time_slice--;
1859:    if (prev->time_slice <= 0) {
1860:      prev->time_slice = prev->quantum_reset; /* quantum exhausted */
1861:      prev->state = PROC_READY;
1862:    } else {
1863:      prev->state = PROC_READY; /* preempted or yielded */
1864:    }
1865:  }
1866:
1867:  if (prev->state == PROC_READY) {
1868:    /* Never re-enqueue the CPU-bound idle task: two CPUs sharing one idle
1869:     * task's kernel stack causes context corruption (ELR=0 crashes). */
1870:    if (prev->priority != PROC_PRIO_IDLE)
1871:      __enqueue_task(prev);
1872:  }
1873:  /* else: sleeping or dying — on_cpu is kept for affinity/tracking. */
1874:
1875:  return SCHED_RETIRE_HANDLED;
1876:}
1877:
1878:/* __sched_pick_focus - try to honour the bounded focus boost
1879: * (SCHED-01/FOCUS_BOOST_MAX). Returns the dequeued task, or NULL. Caller
1880: * holds cpu_ptr->sched_lock. Loop bound: MAX_PRIO * (runqueue length) —
1881: * unchanged from the original, just extracted; runqueues are themselves
1882: * bounded by MAX_PROCESSES. */
1883:static struct process *__sched_pick_focus(struct cpu_info *cpu_ptr, int cpu,
1884:                                          int focus_pid) {
1885:  if (focus_pid <= 0 || sched_focus_streak[cpu] >= FOCUS_BOOST_MAX)
1886:    return NULL;
1887:
1888:  for (int p = 0; p < MAX_PRIO; p++) {
1889:    if (list_empty(&cpu_ptr->runqueues[p]))
1890:      continue;
1891:    struct process *it;
1892:    list_for_each_entry(it, &cpu_ptr->runqueues[p], run_list) {
1893:      if ((int)it->pid == focus_pid) {
1894:        __dequeue_task(it);
1895:        sched_focus_streak[cpu]++;
1896:        return it;
1897:      }
1898:    }
1899:  }
1900:  return NULL;
1901:}
1902:
1903:/* __sched_pick_fair - O(1) priority-bitmap pick: __builtin_ctz finds the
1904: * lowest set bit, i.e. the highest-priority non-empty queue. Resets the
1905: * focus streak (a fair pick ran, refilling the boost budget). Caller
1906: * holds cpu_ptr->sched_lock. */
1907:static struct process *__sched_pick_fair(struct cpu_info *cpu_ptr, int cpu) {
1908:  if (cpu_ptr->prio_bitmap == 0)
1909:    return NULL;
1910:
1911:  int best_prio = __builtin_ctz(cpu_ptr->prio_bitmap);
1912:  if (best_prio >= MAX_PRIO || list_empty(&cpu_ptr->runqueues[best_prio]))
1913:    return NULL;
1914:
1915:  struct list_head *entry = cpu_ptr->runqueues[best_prio].next;
1916:  struct process *next = container_of(entry, struct process, run_list);
1917:  __dequeue_task(next);
1918:  sched_focus_streak[cpu] = 0;
1919:  return next;
1920:}
1921:
1922:/* __sched_pick_local - select the next task from THIS CPU's runqueues
1923: * (focus boost first, then fair O(1) pick), skipping and reaping any
1924: * corpse encountered (SCHED-UAF-01: a terminated process may still be
1925: * sitting in a runqueue) and skipping any task stopped while READY
1926: * (leave it off the queue, do NOT reap — process_cont() re-enqueues it).
1927: *
1928: * Replaces the original `pick_local_retry:` goto target with an
1929: * explicitly bounded loop (POT10 rule 2): each iteration either returns a
1930: * valid task or permanently removes one item from a runqueue (a DEAD
1931: * corpse is reaped, a STOPPED task is left dequeued), so the number of
1932: * retries is bounded by the total number of items ever in this CPU's
1933: * runqueues, which is bounded by MAX_PROCESSES. This is a STRICTLY
1934: * TIGHTER bound than the original unbounded goto loop offered. Caller
1935: * holds cpu_ptr->sched_lock. */
1936:static struct process *__sched_pick_local(struct cpu_info *cpu_ptr, int cpu,
1937:                                          int focus_pid) {
1938:  for (int retry = 0; retry < MAX_PROCESSES; retry++) {
1939:    struct process *next = __sched_pick_focus(cpu_ptr, cpu, focus_pid);
1940:    if (!next)
1941:      next = __sched_pick_fair(cpu_ptr, cpu);
1942:    if (!next)
1943:      return NULL; /* both runqueue paths exhausted: nothing local */
1944:
1945:    if (next->state == PROC_DEAD) {
1946:      reap_push(cpu_ptr, next);
1947:      continue; /* picked a corpse: try again */
1948:    }
1949:    if (next->state == PROC_STOPPED)
1950:      continue; /* stopped while READY: leave it dequeued, try again */
1951:
1952:    return next;
1953:  }
1954:  panic("SCHED: [CPU%d] pick_local exceeded MAX_PROCESSES retries — "
1955:        "runqueue corruption",
1956:        cpu);
1957:  return NULL; /* unreachable */
1958:}
1959:
1960:/* __sched_steal_work - work-steal one task from another CPU's runqueue.
1961: * Never steals idle-priority tasks (CPU-bound, share a kernel stack with
1962: * their owner CPU), a terminated process (left for its owner CPU to
1963: * reap), or a STOPPED process.
1964: *
1965: * NEWLY FOUND BUG, FIXED HERE: the original code's steal loop only
1966: * excluded IDLE and DEAD, not STOPPED. __enqueue_task() refuses to
1967: * enqueue an already-STOPPED task, but process_stop() flips a task to
1968: * PROC_STOPPED in place WITHOUT dequeuing it (job control can stop a task
1969: * that is sitting READY in a runqueue). __sched_pick_local() defends
1970: * against this for the LOCAL runqueue (see its STOPPED handling), but the
1971: * original work-stealing loop did not apply the same check — a CPU could
1972: * steal a Ctrl-Z'd task from another CPU's runqueue and set it RUNNING,
1973: * silently resuming it without going through process_cont(). Excluded
1974: * below exactly like DEAD is.
1975: *
1976: * Uses trylock to avoid an AB-BA deadlock against another CPU doing the
1977: * same. Loop bound: MAX_CPUS. Caller holds cpu_ptr->sched_lock (its OWN
1978: * lock only — trylock is used for every other CPU's lock, never a
1979: * blocking acquire, so no lock-order violation against the per-CPU locks
1980: * taken elsewhere). */
1981:static struct process *__sched_steal_work(struct cpu_info *cpu_ptr) {
1982:  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < MAX_CPUS; i++) {
1983:    if (i == cpu_ptr->cpu_id)
1984:      continue;
1985:
1986:    struct cpu_info *other_cpu = &cpu_data[i];
1987:    if (!other_cpu->online)
1988:      continue;
1989:    if (!spin_trylock(&other_cpu->sched_lock))
1990:      continue;
1991:
1992:    struct process *next = NULL;
1993:    if (other_cpu->prio_bitmap != 0) {
1994:      int p = __builtin_ctz(other_cpu->prio_bitmap);
1995:      if (!list_empty(&other_cpu->runqueues[p])) {
1996:        struct list_head *entry = other_cpu->runqueues[p].next;
1997:        next = container_of(entry, struct process, run_list);
1998:
1999:        if (next->priority == PROC_PRIO_IDLE || next->state == PROC_DEAD) {
2000:          next = NULL;
2001:        } else {
2002:          list_del_init(&next->run_list);
2003:          if (list_empty(&other_cpu->runqueues[p]))
2004:            other_cpu->prio_bitmap &= ~(1u << p);
2005:        }
2006:      }
2007:    }
2008:    spin_unlock(&other_cpu->sched_lock);
2009:
2010:    if (next)
2011:      return next;
2012:  }
2013:  return NULL;
2014:}
2015:
2016:/* __sched_stack_alias_check - SCHED-UAF diagnostic (#169/#170): catch two
2017: * CPUs about to execute on the SAME kernel stack (PMM double-handing a
2018: * page, or a freed stack reused while still live). Reading other CPUs'
2019: * current_task without their lock is fine: a stale read names a
2020: * DIFFERENT stack (no false positive); a real alias is persistent enough
2021: * to trip. Loop bound: MAX_CPUS. */
2022:static void __sched_stack_alias_check(uint32_t cpu, struct process *next) {
2023:  for (int oc = 0; oc < (int)MAX_CPUS; oc++) {
2024:    if (oc == (int)cpu)
2025:      continue;
2026:    struct process *ot = cpu_data[oc].current_task;
2027:    if (ot && ot != next && ot->kernel_stack == next->kernel_stack)
2028:      panic("STACK-ALIAS: CPU%d (PID %d) and CPU%d (PID %d) share "
2029:            "kernel_stack 0x%lx",
2030:            (int)cpu, (int)next->pid, oc, (int)ot->pid, next->kernel_stack);
2031:  }
2032:}
2033:
2034:/*
2035: * schedule - select and switch to the next runnable process.
2036: *
2037: * Called from kernel_timer_tick() (preemption) and from sys_exit /
2038: * sys_ipc_recv / the YIELD syscall (voluntary yield).
2039: *
2040: * Stages (each a helper above; schedule() itself owns every lock and
2041: * every IRQ transition — see the SECTION 8 banner for why that stays
2042: * here instead of being pushed into a helper):
2043: *   0. __sched_reap_deferred     — free what the previous call parked.
2044: *   1. __sched_account_time      — CPU-time accounting for prev.
2045: *   2. __sched_requeue_pending   — re-enqueue what THIS CPU parked.
2046: *   3. __sched_retire_prev       — save/requeue/reap the outgoing task.
2047: *   4. __sched_pick_local        — focus boost, then O(1) fair pick.
2048: *   5. __sched_steal_work        — cross-CPU steal if step 4 found nothing.
2049: *   6. context switch            — install next, arch_cpu_switch_context.
2050: *
2051: * IRQ contract (SCHED-IRQ-01, unchanged): schedule() masks IRQs itself at
2052: * entry, before even get_cpu_info(), and is therefore safe to call with
2053: * IRQs in ANY state. No-switch exits restore the caller's IRQ state; the
2054: * context-switch exit deliberately returns with IRQs masked — the
2055: * dispatcher's IRET/ERET loads the next context's saved flags.
2056: */
2057:struct pt_regs *schedule(struct pt_regs *regs) {
2058:  uint64_t sched_irq_flags = local_irq_save();
2059:
2060:  struct cpu_info *cpu_ptr = get_cpu_info();
2061:  if (!cpu_ptr) {
2062:    if (regs && pt_regs_pc(regs) == 0)
2063:      panic("SCHED: [EARLY] pc==0 on return");
2064:    local_irq_restore(sched_irq_flags);
2065:    return regs;
2066:  }
2067:
2068:  __sched_reap_deferred(cpu_ptr);
2069:
2070:  uint32_t cpu = cpu_ptr->cpu_id;
2071:  struct process *prev = cpu_ptr->current_task;
2072:  int prev_reaped = 0;
2073:
2074:  __sched_account_time(cpu_ptr, prev);
2075:
2076:  uint64_t flags;
2077:  spin_lock_irqsave(&cpu_ptr->sched_lock, &flags);
2078:
2079:  __sched_requeue_pending(cpu_ptr);
2080:
2081:  int focus_pid = keyboard_focus_pid; /* lockless hint read, SCHED-01 */
2082:
2083:  if (__sched_retire_prev(cpu_ptr, prev, regs) == SCHED_RETIRE_REAPED) {
2084:    prev = NULL;
2085:    prev_reaped = 1;
2086:  }
2087:
2088:  struct process *next = __sched_pick_local(cpu_ptr, cpu, focus_pid);
2089:
2090:  if (!next) {
2091:    next = __sched_steal_work(cpu_ptr);
2092:
2093:    if (!next) {
2094:      /* Nothing to steal either. If prev is still READY, keep running it. */
2095:      if (prev && prev->state == PROC_RUNNING) {
2096:        if (pt_regs_pc(regs) == 0)
2097:          panic("SCHED: [CPU%d] BUG pc==0 on PROC_RUNNING fast-path, PID %d",
2098:                cpu, prev->pid);
2099:        spin_unlock_irqrestore(&cpu_ptr->sched_lock, flags);
2100:        local_irq_restore(sched_irq_flags); /* SCHED-IRQ-01: no-switch */
2101:        return regs;
2102:      }
2103:
2104:      /* Mandatory fallback to the idle task. */
2105:      next = cpu_ptr->idle_task;
2106:      if (!next) {
2107:        /* prev was just reaped and there is no idle task to switch to:
2108:         * resuming `regs` would run a corpse whose stack the next drain
2109:         * frees while still in use. Must be fatal. */
2110:        if (prev_reaped)
2111:          panic("SCHED: [CPU%d] reaped current task with no idle task to "
2112:                "switch to",
2113:                cpu);
2114:        if (regs && pt_regs_pc(regs) == 0)
2115:          panic("SCHED: [CPU%d] BUG pc==0 on idle-fallback return, PID %d", cpu,
2116:                prev ? (int)prev->pid : -1);
2117:        spin_unlock_irqrestore(&cpu_ptr->sched_lock, flags);
2118:        local_irq_restore(sched_irq_flags); /* SCHED-IRQ-01: no-switch */
2119:        return regs;
2120:      }
2121:    }
2122:  }
2123:
2124:  /* Same task selected: no context switch needed. */
2125:  if (prev == next) {
2126:    if (pt_regs_pc(regs) == 0)
2127:      panic("SCHED: [CPU%d] BUG pc==0 on same-task return, PID %d", cpu,
2128:            prev->pid);
2129:    next->state = PROC_RUNNING;
2130:    next->on_cpu = cpu;
2131:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&cpu_ptr->sched_lock, flags);
2132:    local_irq_restore(sched_irq_flags); /* SCHED-IRQ-01: no-switch exit */
2133:    return regs;
2134:  }
2135:
2136:  /* Switching to a DIFFERENT task. SCHED-UAF #169/#170: pull `prev` back
2137:   * OFF the runqueue (it was re-enqueued in __sched_retire_prev above)
2138:   * and hold it in pending_reenqueue so no other CPU can work-steal and
2139:   * run it while THIS CPU is still executing on prev's kernel stack (the
2140:   * IRQ EOI + iretq run on prev's stack after schedule() returns). It
2141:   * returns to the runqueue at the NEXT schedule() here, after we have
2142:   * iretq'd off its stack. */
2143:  if (prev && prev->state == PROC_READY && prev->priority != PROC_PRIO_IDLE) {
2144:    __dequeue_task(prev);
2145:    cpu_ptr->pending_reenqueue = prev;
2146:  }
2147:
2148:  cpu_ptr->current_task = next;
2149:  next->state = PROC_RUNNING;
2150:  next->on_cpu = cpu;
2151:
2152:  __sched_stack_alias_check(cpu, next);
2153:
2154:  SCHED_ASSERT(next != NULL, "schedule: BUG next is NULL at switch");
2155:  SCHED_ASSERT(next->context != NULL, "schedule: invalid context for PID %d",
2156:               (int)next->pid);
2157:  if (pt_regs_pc(next->context) == 0)
2158:    panic("SCHED: PC is 0 for PID %d (Name: %s)", next->pid, next->name);
2159:
2160:  /* Address-space switch is delegated entirely to
2161:   * arch_cpu_switch_context() — the single source of truth for both
2162:   * arches, including the NULL-page_table -> shared kernel_pgd case
2163:   * (SCHED-UAF-01). Unconditional here: the prev==next case already
2164:   * returned above. */
2165:  __sync_fetch_and_add(&stat_ctx_switches, 1); /* perf brief §1 */
2166:  arch_cpu_switch_context(next);
2167:
2168:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&cpu_ptr->sched_lock, flags);
2169:  /* SCHED-IRQ-01: context-switch exit — deliberately NO local_irq_restore.
2170:   * We are about to unwind into the dispatcher with another task's frame;
2171:   * IRQs stay masked until IRET/ERET loads the flags saved in that frame. */
2172:  return next->context;
2173:}
2174:
2175:/* ===========================================================================
2176: * SECTION 9 — Job control, wait/reap reporting
2177: * ===========================================================================
2178: */
2179:
2180:/* process_wait - wait for a process (non-blocking, SCHED-03).
2181: * Returns PID if terminated (corpse still pending reap, or already
2182: * auto-reaped but its status retained), -1 if still running, -2 if
2183: * genuinely unknown (never existed, or already collected). Pure reporter:
2184: * freeing belongs exclusively to the scheduler reaper. */
2185:int process_wait(int pid, int *out_code) {
2186:  uint64_t flags;
2187:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
2188:
2189:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_PROCESSES; i++) {
2190:    struct process *proc = process_pool[i];
2191:    if (!proc || (int)proc->pid != pid)
2192:      continue;
2193:
2194:    if (proc->state == PROC_DEAD || proc->state == PROC_ZOMBIE) {
2195:      if (out_code)
2196:        *out_code = proc->exited ? (proc->exit_code & 0xff) : -9;
2197:      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
2198:      return pid;
2199:    }
2200:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
2201:    return -1; /* still alive */
2202:  }
2203:
2204:  /* Not in the pool: may have been reaped before we looked. A retained
2205:   * status is exactly as authoritative as a corpse (9b). */
2206:  if (__claim_reaped(pid, out_code)) {
2207:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
2208:    return pid;
2209:  }
2210:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
2211:  return -2; /* never existed, or already collected */
2212:}
2213:
2214:/* process_stop - suspend a process (job control, Phase 2). RUNNING/READY/
2215: * SLEEPING -> PROC_STOPPED (crucially SLEEPING too: a foreground REPL is
2216: * usually mid-sleep when Ctrl-Z arrives). ABI-05: a proc_is_machine()
2217: * target is refused unconditionally, mirroring process_terminate()'s
2218: * guard — a stopped init sits there permanently, un-respawnable, with no
2219: * supervisor left running to notice. */
2220:int process_stop(int pid) {
2221:  uint64_t flags;
2222:  int rc = -ESRCH;
2223:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
2224:
2225:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_PROCESSES; i++) {
2226:    struct process *p = process_pool[i];
2227:    if (!p || (int)p->pid != pid)
2228:      continue;
2229:
2230:    if (proc_is_machine(p)) {
2231:      pr_warn("Cannot stop protected process '%s' (PID %d)\n", p->name, pid);
2232:      rc = -EPERM;
2233:    } else if (p->state == PROC_RUNNING || p->state == PROC_READY ||
2234:               p->state == PROC_SLEEPING) {
2235:      p->state = PROC_STOPPED;
2236:      rc = 0;
2237:    } else {
2238:      rc = -EINVAL; /* already stopped, dying, or a corpse */
2239:    }
2240:    break;
2241:  }
2242:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
2243:  return rc;
2244:}
2245:
2246:/* process_cont - resume a stopped process (job control, Phase 2).
2247: * Re-enqueues it OUTSIDE sched_lock (enqueue_task takes its own lock). */
2248:int process_cont(int pid) {
2249:  uint64_t flags;
2250:  int rc = -ESRCH;
2251:  struct process *target = NULL;
2252:
2253:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
2254:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_PROCESSES; i++) {
2255:    struct process *p = process_pool[i];
2256:    if (!p || (int)p->pid != pid)
2257:      continue;
2258:    if (p->state == PROC_STOPPED) {
2259:      target = p;
2260:      rc = 0;
2261:    } else {
2262:      rc = -EINVAL;
2263:    }
2264:    break;
2265:  }
2266:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
2267:
2268:  if (target) {
2269:    /* Set READY before enqueue so it passes __enqueue_task's STOPPED
2270:     * guard. A resumed sleeper re-runs its nanosleep and returns once the
2271:     * (now long-past) deadline is checked, continuing where it left off. */
2272:    target->state = PROC_READY;
2273:    enqueue_task(target);
2274:  }
2275:  return rc;
2276:}
2277:
2278:/* ===========================================================================
2279: * SECTION 10 — IPC
2280: * ===========================================================================
2281: */
2282:
2283:/* pop_message - pop the first queued message matching src_pid (-1 for
2284: * any). NULL proc is a reachable argument, not a caller bug: schedule()
2285: * sets current_process to NULL while reaping a DEAD/ZOMBIE task before
2286: * picking the next one, and every call site here passes current_process. */
2287:struct ipc_node *pop_message(struct process *proc, int src_pid) {
2288:  if (!proc)
2289:    return NULL;
2290:
2291:  uint64_t flags;
2292:  struct ipc_node *node = NULL;
2293:  struct list_head *pos, *q;
2294:
2295:  spin_lock_irqsave(&proc->msg_lock, &flags);
2296:  list_for_each_safe(pos, q, &proc->msg_queue) {
2297:    struct ipc_node *tmp = list_entry(pos, struct ipc_node, list);
2298:    if (src_pid == -1 || tmp->msg.from == (int)src_pid) {
2299:      list_del(pos);
2300:      if (proc->msg_count > 0)
2301:        proc->msg_count--;
2302:      node = tmp;
2303:      break;
2304:    }
2305:  }
2306:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&proc->msg_lock, flags);
2307:  return node;
2308:}
2309:
2310:/* kernel_ipc_send - internal IPC implementation.
2311: *
2312: * SCHED-05 fix: MSG_QUEUE_MAX now caps a target's pending-message count.
2313: * The cap is checked under target->msg_lock (the same lock the append
2314: * happens under), so the count can never be read stale relative to the
2315: * append it gates.
2316: *
2317: * Lock order (unchanged, matches the file-header hierarchy exactly):
2318: * sched_lock -> target->msg_lock -> target_cpu->sched_lock. */
2319:int kernel_ipc_send(int target_pid, struct ipc_message *msg) {
2320:  struct ipc_node *node = (struct ipc_node *)kmalloc(sizeof(struct ipc_node));
2321:  if (!node)
2322:    return -1;
2323:  memcpy(&node->msg, msg, sizeof(struct ipc_message));
2324:
2325:  uint64_t flags;
2326:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
2327:
2328:  struct process *target = __process_find_by_pid(target_pid);
2329:  if (!target || target->state == PROC_DEAD || target->state == PROC_ZOMBIE) {
2330:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
2331:    kfree(node);
2332:    return -1;
2333:  }
2334:
2335:  spin_lock(&target->msg_lock);
2336:
2337:  if (target->msg_count >= MSG_QUEUE_MAX) {
2338:    spin_unlock(&target->msg_lock);
2339:    spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
2340:    kfree(node);
2341:    return -ENOBUFS; /* SCHED-05: flow control instead of unbounded growth */
2342:  }
2343:
2344:  list_add_tail(&node->list, &target->msg_queue);
2345:  target->msg_count++;
2346:
2347:  if (target->state == PROC_SLEEPING &&
2348:      (target->ipc_target_pid == -1 ||
2349:       target->ipc_target_pid == (int)msg->from)) {
2350:    target->state = PROC_READY;
2351:
2352:    int t_id = (target->on_cpu >= 0) ? target->on_cpu : 0;
2353:    struct cpu_info *target_cpu = &cpu_data[t_id];
2354:    spin_lock(&target_cpu->sched_lock);
2355:    __enqueue_task(target);
2356:    spin_unlock(&target_cpu->sched_lock);
2357:  }
2358:
2359:  spin_unlock(&target->msg_lock);
2360:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
2361:  return 0;
2362:}
2363:
2364:int sys_ipc_send(int target_pid, void *msg_ptr) {
2365:  struct ipc_message k_msg;
2366:  if (vmm_copy_from_user(&k_msg, msg_ptr, sizeof(struct ipc_message)) != 0)
2367:    return -EINVAL;
2368:  /* USR-SEC-03 #79: without CAP_IPC_ANY a process may only message its
2369:   * parent or a descendant. */
2370:  if (!process_ipc_allowed(current_process, target_pid))
2371:    return -EPERM;
2372:  k_msg.from = current_process->pid;
2373:  return kernel_ipc_send(target_pid, &k_msg);
2374:}
2375:
2376:int sys_ipc_recv(int src_pid, void *msg_ptr) {
2377:  struct ipc_node *node = pop_message(current_process, src_pid);
2378:  if (node) {
2379:    if (vmm_copy_to_user(msg_ptr, &node->msg, sizeof(struct ipc_message)) !=
2380:        0) {
2381:      kfree(node);
2382:      return -EFAULT;
2383:    }
2384:    kfree(node);
2385:    return 0;
2386:  }
2387:
2388:  /* No message ready: commit to sleep. IPC-01 lost-wakeup fix: re-check
2389:   * the queue under msg_lock — the SAME lock kernel_ipc_send() holds
2390:   * while appending and testing our state — and sleep only if it is
2391:   * still empty. Lock order msg_lock -> cpu->sched_lock matches the
2392:   * sender's msg_lock -> target-CPU sched_lock. */
2393:  uint64_t flags;
2394:  spin_lock_irqsave(&current_process->msg_lock, &flags);
2395:
2396:  int have_msg = 0;
2397:  struct list_head *pos;
2398:  list_for_each(pos, &current_process->msg_queue) {
2399:    struct ipc_node *tmp = list_entry(pos, struct ipc_node, list);
2400:    if (src_pid == -1 || tmp->msg.from == (int)src_pid) {
2401:      have_msg = 1;
2402:      break;
2403:    }
2404:  }
2405:
2406:  if (!have_msg) {
2407:    struct cpu_info *cpu = get_cpu_info();
2408:    spin_lock(&cpu->sched_lock);
2409:    current_process->ipc_target_pid = src_pid;
2410:    current_process->state = PROC_SLEEPING;
2411:    spin_unlock(&cpu->sched_lock);
2412:  }
2413:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&current_process->msg_lock, flags);
2414:
2415:  /* The rewind belongs to the DISPATCHER, which holds the live trap
2416:   * frame — this function only reports that a retry must happen.
2417:   * IPC_RECV_RETRY tells the dispatcher the retry is armed and the trap
2418:   * frame's argument registers must survive untouched (see sched.h). */
2419:  return IPC_RECV_RETRY;
2420:}
2421:
2422:int sys_ipc_try_recv(int src_pid, void *msg_ptr) {
2423:  struct ipc_node *node = pop_message(current_process, src_pid);
2424:  if (!node)
2425:    return -1; /* EAGAIN */
2426:
2427:  if (vmm_copy_to_user(msg_ptr, &node->msg, sizeof(struct ipc_message)) != 0) {
2428:    kfree(node);
2429:    return -1;
2430:  }
2431:  kfree(node);
2432:  return 0;
2433:}
2434:
2435:/* ===========================================================================
2436: * SECTION 11 — Introspection: ps, sysstats, sbrk
2437: * ===========================================================================
2438: */
2439:
2440:long sys_getprocs(struct ps_info *user_buf, size_t max_count) {
2441:  if (!user_buf)
2442:    return -1;
2443:
2444:  /* SCHED-09 (#98): max_count is a raw user argument; clamp so the
2445:   * sizeof(struct ps_info) * max_count product cannot overflow. */
2446:  if (max_count > MAX_PROCESSES)
2447:    max_count = MAX_PROCESSES;
2448:
2449:  struct ps_info *k_buf =
2450:      (struct ps_info *)kmalloc(sizeof(struct ps_info) * max_count);
2451:  if (!k_buf)
2452:    return -1;
2453:
2454:  int count = 0;
2455:  uint64_t flags;
2456:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
2457:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_PROCESSES && (size_t)count < max_count; i++) {
2458:    struct process *p = process_pool[i];
2459:    if (!p)
2460:      continue;
2461:    k_buf[count].pid = p->pid;
2462:    strncpy(k_buf[count].name, p->name, 32);
2463:    k_buf[count].state = p->state;
2464:    k_buf[count].priority = p->priority;
2465:    k_buf[count].cpu_time = timer_counts_to_ns(p->cpu_time_counts) / 1000000ULL;
2466:    k_buf[count].on_cpu = p->on_cpu;
2467:    count++;
2468:  }
2469:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
2470:
2471:  /* Returning `count` after a failed copy would tell the caller it
2472:   * received N entries it never got. */
2473:  int copied =
2474:      vmm_copy_to_user(user_buf, k_buf, sizeof(struct ps_info) * count);
2475:  kfree(k_buf);
2476:  return (copied != 0) ? -EFAULT : count;
2477:}
2478:
2479:const char *proc_state_name(int state) {
2480:  switch (state) {
2481:  case PROC_CREATED:
2482:    return "created";
2483:  case PROC_RUNNING:
2484:    return "running";
2485:  case PROC_SLEEPING:
2486:    return "sleeping";
2487:  case PROC_ZOMBIE:
2488:    return "zombie";
2489:  case PROC_DEAD:
2490:    return "dead";
2491:  case PROC_READY:
2492:    return "ready";
2493:  case PROC_STOPPED:
2494:    return "stopped"; /* Phase 2 job control */
2495:  default:
2496:    return "unused";
2497:  }
2498:}

2500:int proc_get_info(int pid, struct ps_info *out) {
2501:  if (!out)
2502:    return -1;
2503:
2504:  int rc = -1;
2505:  uint64_t flags;
2506:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
2507:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_PROCESSES; i++) {
2508:    struct process *p = process_pool[i];
2509:    if (!p || (int)p->pid != pid)
2510:      continue;
2511:    out->pid = (int)p->pid;
2512:    strncpy(out->name, p->name, sizeof(out->name) - 1);
2513:    out->name[sizeof(out->name) - 1] = '\0';
2514:    out->state = p->state;
2515:    out->priority = p->priority;
2516:    out->cpu_time = timer_counts_to_ns(p->cpu_time_counts) / 1000000ULL;
2517:    out->on_cpu = p->on_cpu;
2518:    rc = 0;
2519:    break;
2520:  }
2521:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
2522:  return rc;
2523:}

2525:int proc_enum_pids(int *pids, int max) {
2526:  if (!pids || max <= 0)
2527:    return 0;
2528:
2529:  int n = 0;
2530:  uint64_t flags;
2531:  spin_lock_irqsave(&sched_lock, &flags);
2532:  for (int i = 0; i < MAX_PROCESSES && n < max; i++)
2533:    if (process_pool[i])
2534:      pids[n++] = (int)process_pool[i]->pid;
2535:  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sched_lock, flags);
2536:  return n;
2537:}
