158:/* One cache slot per (theme, app id).  `tried` distinguishes "never asked"
159: * from "asked and it's missing/bad" so a permanently-absent icon costs one
160: * failed load for the whole process lifetime, not one per redraw. */
161:typedef struct {
162:  os1_image_t *img;
163:  int tried;
164:} nxicon_slot_t;
165:
166:static nxicon_slot_t nxicon_cache[2][NXICON_COUNT];
167:static int nxicon_tile_size; /* size the cache was last built for */
168:
169:/* nxicon_ci_prefix - case-insensitive prefix test: 1 if 's' starts with
170: * 'prefix' ignoring ASCII case, 0 otherwise. This environment's os1.h only
171: * declares strcasecmp() (whole-string), not a bounded/prefix strncasecmp(),
172: * so this is a tiny self-contained helper in the same header-only style as
173: * the rest of nxicon.h — no new libc dependency. */
174:static inline int nxicon_ci_prefix(const char *s, const char *prefix) {
175:  while (*prefix) {
176:    if (!*s)
177:      return 0;
178:    char a = *s, b = *prefix;
179:    if (a >= 'A' && a <= 'Z')
180:      a = (char)(a + 32);
181:    if (b >= 'A' && b <= 'Z')
182:      b = (char)(b + 32);
183:    if (a != b)
184:      return 0;
185:    s++;
186:    prefix++;
187:  }
188:  return 1;
189:}
190:
191:/*
192: * nxicon_classify - map a window title to an NXICON_* id, for a RUNNING
193: * window (nxui's dock). Use nxicon_classify_path() below for an app-table
194: * entry's executable path (nxlauncher's grid) instead — a window title can
195: * carry extra text a bare exe path never would (e.g. nxshell titles its
196: * window "NXShell PID 6": different case than the binary name "nxshell",
197: * plus a trailing " PID <n>"), so this is deliberately looser:
198: *
199: *   - strips any directory prefix first (some windows carry the full exe
200: *     path as their title instead of a bare name);
201: *   - matches case-INSENSITIVELY, since an app is free to title-case its
202: *     own window ("NXShell") while its binary on disk is lowercase
203: *     ("nxshell");
204: *   - matches by PREFIX, not exact, so a trailing suffix ("NXShell PID 6",
205: *     "nxfilem — folder view") doesn't defeat the match.
206: *
207: * Checked longest/most-specific prefix first where one binary name could
208: * otherwise shadow another (none currently collide, but nxmemstat/nxsettings
209: * etc. are kept in a stable, deliberate order rather than alphabetical).
210: *
211: * Anything unrecognised is NXICON_UNKNOWN — a valid icon choice, not a
212: * failure.
213: */
214:static inline int nxicon_classify(const char *title) {
215:  if (!title)
216:    return NXICON_UNKNOWN;
217:  const char *base = strrchr(title, '/');
218:  base = base ? base + 1 : title;
219:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nxlauncher"))
220:    return NXICON_LAUNCHER;
221:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nxshell"))
222:    return NXICON_SHELL;
223:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nxfilem"))
224:    return NXICON_FILEM;
225:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nximage"))
226:    return NXICON_IMAGE;
227:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nxinfo"))
228:    return NXICON_INFO;
229:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nxmemstat"))
230:    return NXICON_MEMSTAT;
231:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nxperm"))
232:    return NXICON_PERM;
233:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nxpower"))
234:    return NXICON_POWER;
235:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nxreg"))
236:    return NXICON_REG;
237:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nxsettings"))
238:    return NXICON_SETTINGS;
239:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "nxtop"))
240:    return NXICON_TOP;
241:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "doom"))
242:    return NXICON_DOOM;
243:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "raptor"))
244:    return NXICON_RAPTOR;
245:  if (nxicon_ci_prefix(base, "kilo"))
246:    return NXICON_TEXTEDIT;
247:  return NXICON_UNKNOWN;
248:}
249:
250:/*
251: * nxicon_classify_path - map an app-table executable path (e.g.
252: * "/sys/bin/nxshell") to an NXICON_* id by an EXACT basename match.
253: * Anything unrecognised is NXICON_UNKNOWN (the generic app icon).
254: */
255:static inline int nxicon_classify_path(const char *path) {
256:  if (!path)
257:    return NXICON_UNKNOWN;
258:  const char *base = strrchr(path, '/');
259:  base = base ? base + 1 : path;
260:  if (strcmp(base, "nxlauncher") == 0)
261:    return NXICON_LAUNCHER;
262:  if (strcmp(base, "nxshell") == 0)
263:    return NXICON_SHELL;
264:  if (strcmp(base, "nxfilem") == 0)
265:    return NXICON_FILEM;
266:  if (strcmp(base, "nximage") == 0)
267:    return NXICON_IMAGE;
268:  if (strcmp(base, "nxinfo") == 0)
269:    return NXICON_INFO;
270:  if (strcmp(base, "nxmemstat") == 0)
271:    return NXICON_MEMSTAT;
272:  if (strcmp(base, "nxperm") == 0)
273:    return NXICON_PERM;
274:  if (strcmp(base, "nxpower") == 0)
275:    return NXICON_POWER;
276:  if (strcmp(base, "nxreg") == 0)
277:    return NXICON_REG;
278:  if (strcmp(base, "nxsettings") == 0)
279:    return NXICON_SETTINGS;
280:  if (strcmp(base, "nxtop") == 0)
281:    return NXICON_TOP;
282:  if (strcmp(base, "doom") == 0)
283:    return NXICON_DOOM;
284:  if (strcmp(base, "raptor") == 0)
285:    return NXICON_RAPTOR;
286:  if (strcmp(base, "kilo") == 0)
287:    return NXICON_TEXTEDIT;
288:  return NXICON_UNKNOWN;
289:}
290:
291:/*
292: * nxicon_classify_file - map a filesystem entry (name + is_dir) to an
293: * NXICON_* id for nxfilem's content list.  Directories always get
294: * NXICON_FOLDER regardless of name.  Files are classified by extension
295: * (case-insensitive, via os1_image_ext_eq from image.h — same helper
296: * os1_image_path_has_known_ext already uses), falling back to
297: * NXICON_FILE_GENERIC for anything unrecognised.  Kept in the same
298: * header-only, static-inline style as nxicon_classify()/nxicon_classify_path()
299: * above; deliberately independent of nxassoc.h (icon choice and launch
300: * association are separate concerns that happen to share extension lists).
301: */
302:static inline int nxicon_classify_file(const char *name, int is_dir) {
303:  if (is_dir)
304:    return NXICON_FOLDER;
305:  if (!name)
306:    return NXICON_FILE_GENERIC;
307:  const char *ext = strrchr(name, '.');
308:  if (!ext || ext == name)
309:    return NXICON_FILE_GENERIC;
310:
311:  static const char *const c_exts[] = {".c",   ".h", ".cpp", ".cc",
312:                                       ".hpp", ".s", NULL};
313:  static const char *const text_exts[] = {".txt", ".md",  ".log",
314:                                          ".rst", ".csv", NULL};
315:  static const char *const cfg_exts[] = {".cfg",  ".json", ".ini", ".toml",
316:                                         ".yaml", ".yml",  NULL};
317:  static const char *const html_exts[] = {".html", ".htm", ".css", NULL};
318:  static const char *const script_exts[] = {".lua", ".sh", ".py", NULL};
319:  static const char *const video_exts[] = {".mp4", ".mkv",  ".avi", ".webm",
320:                                           ".mpg", ".mpeg", NULL};
321:  static const char *const bin_exts[] = {".bin", ".dat", ".o", ".elf", NULL};
322:
323:  if (os1_image_path_has_known_ext(name))
324:    return NXICON_FILE_IMAGE;
325:  for (int i = 0; c_exts[i]; i++)
326:    if (os1_image_ext_eq(ext, c_exts[i]))
327:      return NXICON_FILE_C;
328:  for (int i = 0; script_exts[i]; i++)
329:    if (os1_image_ext_eq(ext, script_exts[i]))
330:      return NXICON_FILE_SCRIPT;
331:  for (int i = 0; html_exts[i]; i++)
332:    if (os1_image_ext_eq(ext, html_exts[i]))
333:      return NXICON_FILE_HTML;
334:  for (int i = 0; cfg_exts[i]; i++)
335:    if (os1_image_ext_eq(ext, cfg_exts[i]))
336:      return NXICON_FILE_CONFIG;
337:  for (int i = 0; text_exts[i]; i++)
338:    if (os1_image_ext_eq(ext, text_exts[i]))
339:      return NXICON_FILE_TEXT;
340:  for (int i = 0; video_exts[i]; i++)
341:    if (os1_image_ext_eq(ext, video_exts[i]))
342:      return NXICON_FILE_VIDEO;
343:  if (os1_image_ext_eq(ext, ".elf"))
344:    return NXICON_FILE_EXECUTABLE;
345:  for (int i = 0; bin_exts[i]; i++)
346:    if (os1_image_ext_eq(ext, bin_exts[i]))
347:      return NXICON_FILE_BINARY;
348:  return NXICON_FILE_GENERIC;
349:}
350:
351:/* nxicon_reset_cache - drop every cached scaled icon and retry flag (both
352: * themes).  Only needed if the tile size itself changes (a future DPI/zoom
353: * feature); a plain theme flip does NOT need this, since both themes are
354: * cached side by side already. */
355:static inline void nxicon_reset_cache(void) {
356:  for (int t = 0; t < 2; t++)
357:    for (int i = 0; i < NXICON_COUNT; i++) {
358:      if (nxicon_cache[t][i].img)
359:        os1_image_free(nxicon_cache[t][i].img);
360:      nxicon_cache[t][i].img = NULL;
361:      nxicon_cache[t][i].tried = 0;
362:    }
363:  nxicon_tile_size = 0;
364:}
365:
366:/*
367: * nxicon_get - cached tile_size x tile_size ARGB icon for (app_id, light), or
368: * NULL if icons are disabled or this asset is missing/undecodable.  Callers
369: * always treat NULL as "fall back to the classic flat-color rounded tile" —
370: * see the header comment above.
371: */
372:static inline os1_image_t *nxicon_get(int app_id, int light, int tile_size) {
373:#if !NXICON_ENABLE
374:  (void)app_id;
375:  (void)light;
376:  (void)tile_size;
377:  return NULL;
378:#else
379:  if (app_id < 0 || app_id >= NXICON_COUNT || tile_size <= 0)
380:    return NULL;
381:
382:  if (nxicon_tile_size != tile_size)
383:    nxicon_reset_cache(); /* size changed since the cache was built: rebuild
384:                           * lazily, one icon at a time, as each is next
385:                           * requested — not an eager reload of all fifteen. */
386:  nxicon_tile_size = tile_size;
387:
388:  int theme = light ? NXICON_THEME_LIGHT : NXICON_THEME_DARK;
389:  nxicon_slot_t *slot = &nxicon_cache[theme][app_id];
390:  if (slot->img)
391:    return slot->img;
392:  if (slot->tried)
393:    return NULL;
394:  slot->tried = 1;
395:
396:  os1_image_t *src = os1_image_load(nxicon_paths[theme][app_id]);
397:  if (!src)
398:    return NULL;
399:
400:  /* Trusted-asset fast path: known-square OS icon, so resample straight to
401:   * the tile size instead of nximage.c's aspect-fit dance for arbitrary user
402:   * photos.  Skip the resample entirely if the asset already matches. */
403:  os1_image_t *scaled = (src->w == tile_size && src->h == tile_size)
404:                            ? src
405:                            : os1_image_resample(src, tile_size, tile_size);
406:  if (scaled != src)
407:    os1_image_free(src);
408:  if (!scaled)
409:    return NULL;
410:
411:  slot->img = scaled;
412:  return slot->img;
413:#endif
414:}
415:
416:#endif /* _USER_NXICON_H */

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxinfo.h @@@
1:#ifndef _USER_NXINFO_H
2:#define _USER_NXINFO_H
3:
4:/*
5: * user/sys/bin/nxinfo.h
6: * NEXS stratified system-information helper (ASTRA service layer).
7: *
8: * Helper layer on the nxproc.h stratified pattern, reading coarse system
9: * state: uptime, live process count, desktop resolution, the caller's own
10: * pid/cwd, and the OS version banner.  Header-only (all routines `static
11: * inline`) so consumers pull it in without Makefile churn.  Today its only
12: * consumer is nxinfo.c — kept as a header for pattern consistency, not
13: * because reuse is already demonstrated (contrast nxproc.h's 3 consumers).
14: *
15: * SECURITY MODEL: this layer adds NO ambient permission checks of its own.
16: * Every routine is a thin wrapper over an existing READ-ONLY OS1 syscall
17: * (get_time/os1_mono_ns, _sys_get_procs, _sys_display_info, get_pid, getcwd),
18: * and the kernel already gates those syscalls per caller.  Security is
19: * therefore "by caller" automatically: a privileged system app and an
20: * unprivileged user app calling the same helper each see exactly what the
21: * kernel grants them — the helper neither widens nor narrows that.  Nothing
22: * here mutates system state.
23: *
24: * Process counting reuses nxproc_snapshot() from nxproc.h rather than
25: * duplicating the SYS_GET_PS marshalling, keeping a single source of truth for
26: * the table.
27: *
28: * Consumers: user/sys/bin/nxinfo.c.
29: */
30:
31:#include "nxproc.h" /* nxproc_snapshot(), NXPROC_MAX, struct ps_info */
32:#include <os1.h>
33:
34:/* OS version banner.  Mirrors the build's VERSION (Makefile: VERSION ?=
35: * V0.0.5.4); kept as a userland constant since there is no syscall that reports
36: * it.
37: * TODO: surface the kernel build string via a syscall and read it here instead
38: * of hardcoding, so the banner can never drift from the running kernel. */
39:
40:#ifdef ARCH_AMD64
41:#define KERNEL_NAME "AMD64 NexsOS1"
42:#else
43:#define KERNEL_NAME "AArch64 NexsOS1"
44:#endif
45:
46:#define NXINFO_OS_NAME KERNEL_NAME
47:#define NXINFO_OS_VERSION "V0.0.5.4"
48:
49:/*
50: * nxinfo_uptime_ms - milliseconds elapsed since boot.
51: *
52: * Thin wrapper over get_time() (SYS_GET_TIME), which is the millisecond
53: * monotonic clock the rest of userland already uses.  Never negative in normal
54: * operation; the raw syscall value is returned unmodified.
55: */
56:static inline long nxinfo_uptime_ms(void) { return get_time(); }
57:
58:/*
59: * nxinfo_proc_count - number of entries currently in the process table.
60: *
61: * Takes a point-in-time snapshot via nxproc_snapshot() (capped at NXPROC_MAX)
62: * and returns the count it reported (0..NXPROC_MAX), or a negative value if the
63: * underlying syscall failed.  No heap allocation: the snapshot lives on the
64: * caller's stack for the duration of the call only.
65: */
66:static inline int nxinfo_proc_count(void) {
67:  struct ps_info procs[NXPROC_MAX];
68:  return nxproc_snapshot(procs, NXPROC_MAX);
69:}
70:
71:/*
72: * nxinfo_display - current desktop resolution.
73: *
74: * w/out, h/out: optional out-params; either may be NULL if the caller only
75: *               wants the other dimension (or just the side effect of probing).
76: *
77: * Thin wrapper over OS1_display_info(), which returns the packed value
78: * ((w << 16) | h).  Unpacks the two 16-bit fields into *w and *h.
79: */
80:static inline void nxinfo_display(int *w, int *h) {
81:  long info = OS1_display_info();
82:  if (w)
83:    *w = (int)((info >> 16) & 0xFFFF);
84:  if (h)
85:    *h = (int)(info & 0xFFFF);
86:}
87:
88:/*
89: * nxinfo_emit - internal: route one preformatted line to stdout or a window.
90: *
91: * win_id_or_neg: a compositor window id to write into, or any negative value to
92: *                emit to the caller's stdout/own window via printf().
93: *
94: * This is the single place that branches on the output sink so the summary
95: * formatter below can stay sink-agnostic.  `s` is expected to be
96: * NUL-terminated.
97: */
98:static inline void nxinfo_emit(int win_id_or_neg, const char *s) {
99:  if (win_id_or_neg < 0)
100:    printf("%s", s);
101:  else
102:    printf_win(win_id_or_neg, "%s", s);
103:}
104:
105:/*
106: * nxinfo_print_summary - format and emit a readable multi-line system summary.
107: *
108: * win_id_or_neg: negative -> write to the caller's stdout (printf); otherwise
109: *                write into the given compositor window (printf_win).
110: *
111: * Lines: OS banner, uptime (ms and seconds), process count, desktop resolution,
112: * own pid, and current working directory.  All values come from the read-only
113: * wrappers above, so the summary is "secure by caller" — it reveals only what
114: * the kernel already lets this caller read.  Each line is rendered into a small
115: * stack buffer with snprintf() (bounded, no heap) and then routed to the chosen
116: * sink, so the formatting is shared between the stdout and windowed paths.
117: */
118:static inline void nxinfo_print_summary(int win_id_or_neg) {
119:  char line[160];
120:  char cwd[128];
121:
122:  long up_ms = nxinfo_uptime_ms();
123:  int procs = nxinfo_proc_count();
124:  int w = 0, h = 0;
125:  nxinfo_display(&w, &h);
126:  int pid = get_pid();
127:
128:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%s %s\n", NXINFO_OS_NAME, NXINFO_OS_VERSION);
129:  nxinfo_emit(win_id_or_neg, line);
130:
131:  /* Uptime shown both raw (ms) and in whole seconds for quick reading. */
132:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "uptime:     %ld ms (%ld s)\n", up_ms,
133:           up_ms / 1000);
134:  nxinfo_emit(win_id_or_neg, line);
135:
136:  if (procs < 0)
137:    snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "processes:  <unavailable> (err %d)\n", procs);
138:  else
139:    snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "processes:  %d\n", procs);
140:  nxinfo_emit(win_id_or_neg, line);
141:
142:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "resolution: %dx%d\n", w, h);
143:  nxinfo_emit(win_id_or_neg, line);
144:
145:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "pid:        %d\n", pid);
146:  nxinfo_emit(win_id_or_neg, line);
147:
148:  /* getcwd writes a NUL-terminated path; fall back to "?" on failure so the
149:   * line is always printable. */
150:  if (getcwd(cwd, sizeof(cwd)) != 0)
151:    cwd[0] = '\0';
152:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "cwd:        %s\n", cwd[0] ? cwd : "?");
153:  nxinfo_emit(win_id_or_neg, line);
154:}
155:
156:#endif /* _USER_NXINFO_H */
157:

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxjobs.h @@@
1:#ifndef _USER_NXJOBS_H
2:#define _USER_NXJOBS_H
3:
4:/*
5: * user/sys/bin/nxjobs.h
6: * NEXS shell job table (ASTRA service layer) — "job control, light".
7: *
8: * Tracks pids launched in the BACKGROUND (`cmd &`) and jobs suspended with
9: * Ctrl-Z, so `jobs`/`fg`/`bg` have something to operate on.
10: *
11: *   - background (&), jobs, fg   A background job is a spawned pid the shell
12: *     chose not to wait() on immediately; nxjobs_poll() drains SYS_WAIT
13: *     non-blockingly each loop tick to notice when one finishes.
14: *
15: *   - suspend (Ctrl-Z), bg, fg   REAL since Phase 2: the scheduler has a
16: *     PROC_STOPPED state with process_stop/process_cont behind the
17: *     DESTROY-gated OBJ_CTL_STOP/CONT verbs, so a stopped job genuinely
18: *     stops and genuinely resumes.
19: *
20: *   - exit status                REAL since Phase 2/9b: waitpid() carries a
21: *     POSIX status that survives reaping, so a job reports "Done (N)" or
22: *     "Killed (N)", not a bare "Done".
23: *
24: * (This header used to state the opposite for the last two — written before
25: * the kernel work landed and never updated.  The stale text was quoted back
26: * as fact by a later review, so it is corrected here rather than deleted:
27: * PLAN-2026-07-17 §"Known live bugs" records that failure mode.)
28: *
29: * Job SELECTION follows POSIX XCU §2.9.3.1 — see nxjobs_resolve().
30: */
31:
32:#include "nxexec.h" /* nxexec_window_stable() — the single shared debounce
33:                      * also used by nxexec_run_foreground() and nxexec.c's
34:                      * grace probe, see nxjobs_poll() below. */
35:#include <os1.h>
36:#include <string.h>
37:#include <sys/wait.h> /* WIFEXITED/WEXITSTATUS/WIFSIGNALED — Phase 2 real status */
38:
39:#define NXJOBS_MAX 16
40:#define NXJOBS_CMD_MAX 64
41:
42:enum { NXJOB_RUNNING = 0, NXJOB_DONE = 1, NXJOB_STOPPED = 2 };
43:
44:struct nxjob {
45:  int in_use;
46:  int id; /* 1-based, stable for the job's lifetime (the "%1" in fg %1) */
47:  int pid;
48:  int state;
49:  int status; /* POSIX wait status once NXJOB_DONE (Phase 2): WEXITSTATUS /
50:               * WIFSIGNALED decode it — "Done (N)" vs "Killed". */
51:  char cmd[NXJOBS_CMD_MAX];
52:  /* Debounce state for the "did this background job turn out to be a GUI
53:   * app?" test in nxjobs_poll() — same shape as nxexec_run_foreground()'s
54:   * local last_win/stable, just kept per-slot since nxjobs_poll() checks
55:   * every tracked job on a single shared tick instead of blocking on one. */
56:  int win_last;
57:  int win_stable;
58:};
59:
60:struct nxjobs {
61:  struct nxjob slot[NXJOBS_MAX];
62:  int next_id;
63:  /* POSIX current/previous job (`%%`/`%+` and `%-`, and what a bare `fg`/`bg`
64:   * operates on).  Stored as IDS and updated on the EVENTS that define them,
65:   * because "most recently stopped" is not recoverable from the table's state:
66:   * with two stopped jobs, nothing in the slots says which stopped last. */
67:  int current_id;
68:  int previous_id;
69:};
70:
71:static inline void nxjobs_init(struct nxjobs *j) {
72:  memset(j, 0, sizeof(*j));
73:  j->next_id = 1;
74:}
75:
76:/* __nxjobs_slot_of_id - slot for `id`, but only if it still names a job that
77: * can be foregrounded.  A finished job is deliberately NOT eligible: it is
78: * about to leave the table, and selecting a corpse is not a selection. */
79:static inline int __nxjobs_slot_of_id(struct nxjobs *j, int id) {
80:  if (id <= 0)
81:    return -1;
82:  for (int i = 0; i < NXJOBS_MAX; i++)
83:    if (j->slot[i].in_use && j->slot[i].id == id &&
84:        j->slot[i].state != NXJOB_DONE)
85:      return i;
86:  return -1;
87:}
88:
89:/* __nxjobs_pick - the POSIX current-job RULE, applied from scratch.
90: *
91: * "the most recently stopped job, or, if there are no stopped jobs, the most
92: * recently started background job".  `skip_id` asks for the next one down,
93: * which is how the previous job is chosen.  Used only to REBUILD the ids after
94: * the job they named went away — the event-driven path above is what makes
95: * "most recently stopped" mean the right thing while both jobs are stopped. */
96:static inline int __nxjobs_pick(struct nxjobs *j, int skip_id) {
97:  for (int pass = 0; pass < 2; pass++) {
98:    int want = (pass == 0) ? NXJOB_STOPPED : NXJOB_RUNNING;
99:    int best = -1;
100:    for (int i = 0; i < NXJOBS_MAX; i++) {
101:      if (!j->slot[i].in_use || j->slot[i].state != want)
102:        continue;
103:      if (j->slot[i].id == skip_id)
104:        continue;
105:      if (best < 0 || j->slot[i].id > j->slot[best].id)
106:        best = i;
107:    }
108:    if (best >= 0)
109:      return best;
110:  }
111:  return -1;
112:}
113:
114:/* __nxjobs_resync - drop current/previous ids that no longer name an eligible
115: * job and refill them from the rule.  Called before every resolution, so a job
116: * finishing or being disowned cannot leave `fg` pointing at nothing. */
117:static inline void __nxjobs_resync(struct nxjobs *j) {
118:  if (__nxjobs_slot_of_id(j, j->current_id) < 0)
119:    j->current_id = 0;
120:  if (__nxjobs_slot_of_id(j, j->previous_id) < 0)
121:    j->previous_id = 0;
122:  if (j->current_id == 0) {
123:    int s = __nxjobs_pick(j, j->previous_id);
124:    j->current_id = (s >= 0) ? j->slot[s].id : 0;
125:  }
126:  if (j->previous_id == 0) {
127:    int s = __nxjobs_pick(j, j->current_id);
128:    j->previous_id = (s >= 0) ? j->slot[s].id : 0;
129:  }
130:}
131:
132:/* __nxjobs_promote - `id` becomes the current job, the old current becomes the
133: * previous one.  This is the only way current_id is set on the happy path: it
134: * is called when a job is started in the background and when one is stopped,
135: * which are exactly the two events POSIX defines the current job by. */
136:static inline void __nxjobs_promote(struct nxjobs *j, int id) {
137:  if (id <= 0 || id == j->current_id)
138:    return;
139:  j->previous_id = j->current_id;
140:  j->current_id = id;
141:}
142:
143:/* nxjobs_add - register a newly-spawned BACKGROUND pid. Returns the job id
144: * (>=1), or 0 if the table is full (the process still runs, it's just
145: * untracked by `jobs`/`fg` — never a reason to refuse the spawn itself). */
146:static inline int nxjobs_add(struct nxjobs *j, int pid, const char *cmd) {
147:  for (int i = 0; i < NXJOBS_MAX; i++) {
148:    if (!j->slot[i].in_use) {
149:      j->slot[i].in_use = 1;
150:      j->slot[i].id = j->next_id++;
151:      j->slot[i].pid = pid;
152:      j->slot[i].state = NXJOB_RUNNING;
153:      j->slot[i].status = 0;
154:      j->slot[i].win_last = -1;
155:      j->slot[i].win_stable = 0;
156:      snprintf(j->slot[i].cmd, NXJOBS_CMD_MAX, "%s", cmd);
157:      __nxjobs_promote(j, j->slot[i].id); /* POSIX: a new background job is
158:                                           * the current job */
159:      return j->slot[i].id;
160:    }
161:  }
162:  return 0;
163:}
164:
165:/* nxjobs_mark_stopped - record that a job has been suspended.
166: *
167: * Separate from nxjobs_stop() because Ctrl-Z is detected by the foreground
168: * watcher, which has already suspended the process — only the bookkeeping is
169: * left.  Both paths must come through here, though, because a stopped job
170: * becomes the CURRENT job, and a shell where Ctrl-Z did not change what a bare
171: * `fg` resumes is the one thing job control has to get right. */
172:static inline void nxjobs_mark_stopped(struct nxjobs *j, int slot) {
173:  if (slot < 0 || slot >= NXJOBS_MAX || !j->slot[slot].in_use)
174:    return;
175:  j->slot[slot].state = NXJOB_STOPPED;
176:  __nxjobs_promote(j, j->slot[slot].id);
177:}
178:
179:/* nxjobs_reap - drop a job from the table (finished, or just promoted to
180: * the foreground and waited on directly). Defined ahead of nxjobs_poll()
181: * since that now calls it directly (windowed-handoff case) rather than only
182: * being called from nxshell.c's `fg` path. */
183:static inline void nxjobs_reap(struct nxjobs *j, int slot) {
184:  if (slot >= 0 && slot < NXJOBS_MAX)
185:    j->slot[slot].in_use = 0;
186:}
187:
188:/* nxjobs_poll - non-blocking refresh of every tracked job's state. wait()
189: * (OS1low_process_wait / SYS_WAIT) is itself non-blocking (-1 = still
190: * running), so this is cheap to call once per shell loop tick.
191: *
192: * A background job ('cmd &') is spawned through the same non-detached path
193: * as a foreground one (nxexec_spawn_search(..., detached=0) in nxshell.c),
194: * so it never goes through nxexec_run_foreground()'s own window-ownership
195: * debounce — nothing ever told nxjobs a backgrounded child turned out to be
196: * a GUI app.  Left unchecked, such a job sits in the table as "Running"
197: * forever (wait() never returns non-(-1) for it — it only ever exits when
198: * the user closes its window, which nxjobs has no way to notice either),
199: * a phantom entry that both `jobs` misreports and `fg`/reap can never
200: * clean up.  Uses the same nxexec_window_stable() debounce nxexec.h's own
201: * watchers use (single source of truth for the threshold/reset rule) on a
202: * per-slot basis instead of blocking: once a job's window id is stable
203: * across NXEXEC_STABLE_POLLS ticks, it is handed off — reaped from this
204: * table without ever appearing as "Done" (it isn't dead, it just left the
205: * shell's job-control domain for nxwins/dock's, per nxexec.h's ownership
206: * model). */
207:static inline void nxjobs_poll(struct nxjobs *j) {
208:  for (int i = 0; i < NXJOBS_MAX; i++) {
209:    if (!j->slot[i].in_use || j->slot[i].state != NXJOB_RUNNING)
210:      continue;
211:
212:    if (nxexec_window_stable(j->slot[i].pid, &j->slot[i].win_last,
213:                             &j->slot[i].win_stable)) {
214:      nxjobs_reap(j, i); /* handed off to nxwins/dock; not "Done" */
215:      continue;
216:    }
217:
218:    /* Standard waitpid (Phase 2): WNOHANG poll, real POSIX status. r>0 reaped
219:     * (status valid), r==-1 gone (reaped elsewhere), r==0 still running. */
220:    int status = 0;
221:    int r = waitpid(j->slot[i].pid, &status, WNOHANG);
222:    if (r != 0) {
223:      j->slot[i].status = (r > 0) ? status : 0;
224:      j->slot[i].state = NXJOB_DONE;
225:    }
226:  }
227:}
228:
229:/* nxjobs_find - look up a job by its %N (or bare N) id. Returns the slot
230: * index, or -1 if not found. */
231:static inline int nxjobs_find(struct nxjobs *j, int id) {
232:  for (int i = 0; i < NXJOBS_MAX; i++)
233:    if (j->slot[i].in_use && j->slot[i].id == id)
234:      return i;
235:  return -1;
236:}
237:
238:/* nxjobs_print - `jobs` builtin body.
239: *
240: * The current job is marked '+' and the previous one '-', as POSIX specifies:
241: * without them the output does not say what a bare `fg` would act on, which is
242: * the only reason a user needs to read it before typing one. */
243:static inline void nxjobs_print(struct nxjobs *j) {
244:  int any = 0;
245:  __nxjobs_resync(j);
246:  for (int i = 0; i < NXJOBS_MAX; i++) {
247:    if (!j->slot[i].in_use)
248:      continue;
249:    any = 1;
250:    char mark = (j->slot[i].id == j->current_id)    ? '+'
251:                : (j->slot[i].id == j->previous_id) ? '-'
252:                                                    : ' ';
253:    const char *st;
254:    char stbuf[24];
255:    if (j->slot[i].state == NXJOB_RUNNING) {
256:      st = "Running";
257:    } else if (j->slot[i].state == NXJOB_STOPPED) {
258:      st = "Stopped";
259:    } else { /* NXJOB_DONE: decode the real POSIX status (Phase 2) */
260:      int s = j->slot[i].status;
261:      if (WIFSIGNALED(s))
262:        snprintf(stbuf, sizeof(stbuf), "Killed (%d)", WTERMSIG(s));
263:      else
264:        snprintf(stbuf, sizeof(stbuf), "Done (%d)", WEXITSTATUS(s));
265:      st = stbuf;
266:    }
267:    printf("[%d]%c %-12s pid=%-6d %s\n", j->slot[i].id, mark, st,
268:           j->slot[i].pid, j->slot[i].cmd);
269:  }
270:  if (!any)
271:    print("No background jobs.\n");
272:}
273:
274:/* nxjobs_parse_id - parse a `fg`/`bg` argument in either "%3" or "3" form.
275: * Returns the id, or -1 if arg isn't a valid job reference. */
276:static inline int nxjobs_parse_id(const char *arg) {
277:  if (!arg || !*arg)
278:    return -1;
279:  if (arg[0] == '%')
280:    arg++;
281:  if (!*arg)
282:    return -1;
283:  int id = atoi(arg);
284:  return id > 0 ? id : -1;
285:}
286:
287:/* __nxjobs_match - most recent job whose command matches `s`, by prefix or
288: * (with `anywhere`) by substring.  POSIX `%string` and `%?string`. */
289:static inline int __nxjobs_match(struct nxjobs *j, const char *s, int anywhere) {
290:  if (!s || !*s)
291:    return -1;
292:  size_t len = strlen(s);
293:  int best = -1;
294:  for (int i = 0; i < NXJOBS_MAX; i++) {
295:    if (!j->slot[i].in_use)
296:      continue;
297:    int hit = anywhere ? (strstr(j->slot[i].cmd, s) != (char *)0)
298:                       : (strncmp(j->slot[i].cmd, s, len) == 0);
299:    if (hit && (best < 0 || j->slot[i].id > j->slot[best].id))
300:      best = i;
301:  }
302:  return best;
303:}
304:
305:/*
306: * nxjobs_resolve - turn a `fg`/`bg`/`disown` operand into a slot index.
307: *
308: * POSIX job_id syntax (XCU §2.9.3.1), which this now actually implements:
309: *
310: *   (omitted)  the CURRENT job
311: *   %% or %+   the current job          %-        the previous job
312: *   %N         job number N             %string   job whose command starts
313: *   %?string   ...whose command contains string     with string
314: *
315: * TWO CORRECTIONS, 2026-07-23:
316: *
317: * 1. A bare `fg` used to take "the highest job id still in the table"
318: *    (nxjobs_last).  That is not the current job and, worse, the table
319: *    includes FINISHED jobs — so `fg` could resume nothing, and Ctrl-Z'ing a
320: *    job did not change what a bare `fg` would bring back.  It now follows the
321: *    real rule: most recently stopped, else most recently backgrounded, never
322: *    a finished one.  Omitting the operand IS standard; picking the wrong job
323: *    for it was not.
324: *
325: * 2. A BARE NAME (`fg lua`, no `%`) used to resolve by command prefix.  That
326: *    is not a job id in any shell — `lua` there is a command name, and
327: *    accepting it means `fg` silently guesses when the user meant something
328: *    else.  Removed; `fg %lua` is the spelling.  A bare NUMBER stays: `fg 1`
329: *    for `%1` is the one extension every shell accepts.
330: *
331: * Returns the slot, or -1 if the operand names no job.
332: */
333:static inline int nxjobs_resolve(struct nxjobs *j, const char *arg) {
334:  __nxjobs_resync(j);
335:
336:  if (!arg || !*arg)
337:    return __nxjobs_slot_of_id(j, j->current_id);
338:
339:  if (arg[0] != '%') {
340:    for (const char *p = arg; *p; p++)
341:      if (*p < '0' || *p > '9')
342:        return -1; /* a bare name is a command, not a job id */
343:    return nxjobs_find(j, atoi(arg));
344:  }
345:
346:  arg++;
347:  if (!*arg)
348:    return -1; /* a lone "%" names nothing */
349:  if (arg[0] == '%' || arg[0] == '+')
350:    return __nxjobs_slot_of_id(j, j->current_id);
351:  if (arg[0] == '-')
352:    return __nxjobs_slot_of_id(j, j->previous_id);
353:  if (arg[0] == '?')
354:    return __nxjobs_match(j, arg + 1, 1);
355:
356:  int numeric = 1;
357:  for (const char *p = arg; *p; p++)
358:    if (*p < '0' || *p > '9') {
359:      numeric = 0;
360:      break;
361:    }
362:  if (numeric)
363:    return nxjobs_find(j, atoi(arg));
364:  return __nxjobs_match(j, arg, 0);
365:}
366:
367:/* nxjobs_stop - suspend a job (Ctrl-Z / `stop %N`): kernel PROC_STOPPED via
368: * OS1_process_stop, then mark it Stopped so `jobs` reflects it and `bg`/`fg`
369: * can resume it (Phase 2 — a real stopped state exists now). */
370:static inline int nxjobs_stop(struct nxjobs *j, int slot) {
371:  if (slot < 0 || slot >= NXJOBS_MAX || !j->slot[slot].in_use)
372:    return -1;
373:  int r = OS1_process_stop(j->slot[slot].pid);
374:  if (r == 0)
375:    nxjobs_mark_stopped(j, slot); /* also makes it the current job */
376:  return r;
377:}
378:
379:/* nxjobs_cont - resume a stopped job in the BACKGROUND (`bg`): OS1_process_cont
380: * + mark Running.  For `fg`, the caller conts and then waits in the foreground.
381: * Returns 0, or a negative errno (e.g. the job was not stopped). */
382:static inline int nxjobs_cont(struct nxjobs *j, int slot) {
383:  if (slot < 0 || slot >= NXJOBS_MAX || !j->slot[slot].in_use)
384:    return -1;
385:  int r = OS1_process_cont(j->slot[slot].pid);
386:  if (r == 0 && j->slot[slot].state == NXJOB_STOPPED)
387:    j->slot[slot].state = NXJOB_RUNNING;
388:  return r;
389:}
390:
391:#endif /* _USER_NXJOBS_H */

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxline.h @@@
1:#ifndef _USER_NXLINE_H
2:#define _USER_NXLINE_H
3:
4:/*
5: * user/sys/bin/nxline.h
6: * NEXS interactive line editor (ASTRA service layer) — cursor movement,
7: * persistent history, incremental search, and command/path completion for
8: * a single input line hosted in a compositor terminal window.
9: *
10: * Header-only, static-inline, same pattern as nxexec.h/nxassoc.h/nxinfo.h.
11: * Extracted out of nxshell.c's original "cmd_buf + cmd_len, backspace-only"
12: * editor so any future interactive prompt (a REPL, a debugger console) can
13: * reuse the same editing model instead of re-deriving it.
14: *
15: * RENDERING MODEL: nxline never touches window pixels or the cell grid
16: * directly. It drives the SAME VT100/ANSI terminal emulator every other
17: * program already writes through (kernel/graphics/term.c: term_write /
18: * handle_csi), via plain printf()/print() escape sequences:
19: *
20: *   \b              backspace (cursor left one cell — term.c handles it)
21: *   \033[C  \033[D   cursor right/left by N cells (final 'C'/'D', handle_csi)
22: *   \033[K           erase from cursor to end of line (final 'K', mode 0)
23: *
24: * Every edit below is expressed as a RELATIVE cursor movement from wherever
25: * the cursor already is, never an absolute column. That means nxline needs
26: * no knowledge of the visible width of a colored, theme-dependent prompt
27: * string (nxshell's prompt embeds \033[32m/\033[34m SGR codes whose glyphs
28: * take zero columns) — it only ever moves relative to its own last output.
29: *
30: * INPUT MODEL: nxshell already receives ASCII + scancode pairs via
31: * input_poll_event() (INPUT_TYPE_KEYBOARD). Control-letter combinations
32: * arrive as ASCII control codes (nxexec.h already treats 0x03 as Ctrl-C on
33: * this same path) — nxline follows that precedent: Ctrl-A/E/L/R/D are
34: * 0x01/0x05/0x0C/0x12/0x04 (the letter's position in the alphabet, exactly
35: * like the existing Ctrl-C=0x03). Arrow keys / Home / End / Delete have no
36: * ASCII representation and are read from ev.keyboard.scancode instead, via
37: * INPUT_KEY_LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN/HOME/END/DELETE — ASSUMED to sit in input.h
38: * alongside the already-used INPUT_KEY_ENTER/INPUT_KEY_BACKSPACE. If they
39: * are not yet defined there, add them to the keyboard driver's scancode
40: * table before arrow-key/Home/End/Delete input will do anything here;
41: * everything else (Ctrl combos, history, completion, plain typing) works
42: * without them.
43: *
44: * HISTORY PERSISTENCE: the whole in-memory ring is serialized newline-
45: * separated and written with OS1_fs_write(path, buf, n, 0) on every new
46: * entry. offset 0 + ext4_write's truncate-to-length behaviour (see lib.c
47: * rename()'s comment) means this is always a clean overwrite, never stale
48: * trailing garbage from a longer previous file. Bounded to
49: * NXLINE_HIST_MAX * NXLINE_MAX bytes (16 KB at the defaults below), so a
50: * full rewrite per command is cheap enough not to need incremental append.
51: */
52:
53:#include <os1.h>
54:#include <input.h>
55:#include <string.h>
56:
57:/* nxline_contains - tiny local substring search, used only by Ctrl-R
58: * incremental search below. memmove/strlen/strncmp/strchr are confirmed
59: * present in this libc (memmove is already used in term.c; the others are
60: * used throughout nxexec.h/nxassoc.h), but strstr() appears nowhere in the
61: * existing codebase — so this avoids assuming it exists rather than risk a
62: * link failure over one call site. */
63:static inline int nxline_contains(const char *hay, const char *needle) {
64:  if (!*needle)
65:    return 1;
66:  size_t nl = strlen(needle);
67:  for (const char *p = hay; *p; p++)
68:    if (strncmp(p, needle, nl) == 0)
69:      return 1;
70:  return 0;
71:}
72:
73:#define NXLINE_MAX 256
74:#define NXLINE_HIST_MAX 64
75:
76:enum {
77:  NXLINE_NONE = 0,        /* keep editing */
78:  NXLINE_SUBMIT,          /* Enter: nl->buf/nl->len hold the finished line */
79:  NXLINE_EOF,             /* Ctrl-D on an empty line */
80:  NXLINE_CLEAR_SCREEN,    /* Ctrl-L: caller should clear the screen and repaint */
81:};
82:
83:struct nxline {
84:  char buf[NXLINE_MAX];
85:  int len;    /* bytes currently in buf (not counting the NUL) */
86:  int cursor; /* 0..len, insertion point */
87:
88:  char history[NXLINE_HIST_MAX][NXLINE_MAX];
89:  int hist_count; /* entries currently stored (<= NXLINE_HIST_MAX) */
90:  int hist_pos;   /* -1 = editing the live line; else index into history[] */
91:  char live_stash[NXLINE_MAX]; /* live buffer, saved when history browsing starts */
92:
93:  int searching; /* 1 while a Ctrl-R incremental search is active */
94:  char search_buf[NXLINE_MAX];
95:  int search_len;
96:  char search_stash[NXLINE_MAX]; /* buf contents when Ctrl-R was pressed */
97:
98:  char hist_path[64]; /* e.g. "/home/.nxshell_history"; empty = no persistence */
99:
100:  /* Caller hook: print JUST the prompt string (no leading newline, no line
101:   * content) — invoked by nxline when it needs to repaint a whole line from
102:   * column 0 (Ctrl-L, multi-match tab listing). ctx is passed through
103:   * unchanged (nxshell has no per-instance state today, but this keeps the
104:   * header reusable for a future multi-window consumer). */
105:  void (*print_prompt)(void *ctx);
106:  void *ctx;
107:};
108:
109:/* ---------------- init / history load-save ---------------- */
110:
111:static inline void nxline_init(struct nxline *nl, const char *hist_path,
112:                               void (*print_prompt)(void *), void *ctx) {
113:  memset(nl, 0, sizeof(*nl));
114:  nl->hist_pos = -1;
115:  nl->print_prompt = print_prompt;
116:  nl->ctx = ctx;
117:  if (hist_path)
118:    snprintf(nl->hist_path, sizeof(nl->hist_path), "%s", hist_path);
119:}
120:
121:/* nxline_load_history - populate history[] from hist_path, if set. Silent
122: * no-op if the file doesn't exist yet (first run) or persistence is off. */
123:static inline void nxline_load_history(struct nxline *nl) {
124:  if (!nl->hist_path[0])
125:    return;
126:  char buf[NXLINE_HIST_MAX * NXLINE_MAX];
127:  int n = file_read(nl->hist_path, buf, sizeof(buf) - 1, 0);
128:  if (n <= 0)
129:    return;
130:  buf[n] = '\0';
131:
132:  nl->hist_count = 0;
133:  char *save = NULL;
134:  for (char *line = strtok_r(buf, "\n", &save); line && nl->hist_count < NXLINE_HIST_MAX;
135:       line = strtok_r(NULL, "\n", &save)) {
136:    if (!*line)
137:      continue;
138:    snprintf(nl->history[nl->hist_count], NXLINE_MAX, "%s", line);
139:    nl->hist_count++;
140:  }
141:}
142:
143:/* nxline_save_history - flush the in-memory ring back to hist_path (a full
144: * overwrite; see the header comment on why that's safe and cheap here). */
145:static inline void nxline_save_history(struct nxline *nl) {
146:  if (!nl->hist_path[0])
147:    return;
148:  char buf[NXLINE_HIST_MAX * NXLINE_MAX];
149:  int n = 0;
150:  for (int i = 0; i < nl->hist_count; i++) {
151:    int l = (int)strlen(nl->history[i]);
152:    if (n + l + 1 >= (int)sizeof(buf))
153:      break;
154:    memcpy(buf + n, nl->history[i], l);
155:    n += l;
156:    buf[n++] = '\n';
157:  }
158:  OS1_fs_write(nl->hist_path, buf, n, 0);
159:}
160:
161:/* nxline_history_add - push a finished command onto the ring (dropping the
162: * oldest entry once full) and persist it. Skips blank lines and an exact
163: * repeat of the immediately-previous entry (the common readline behaviour:
164: * mashing Enter or repeating the same command doesn't spam history). */
165:static inline void nxline_history_add(struct nxline *nl, const char *cmd) {
166:  if (!cmd || !*cmd)
167:    return;
168:  if (nl->hist_count > 0 &&
169:      strncmp(nl->history[nl->hist_count - 1], cmd, NXLINE_MAX) == 0)
170:    return;
171:
172:  if (nl->hist_count < NXLINE_HIST_MAX) {
173:    snprintf(nl->history[nl->hist_count], NXLINE_MAX, "%s", cmd);
174:    nl->hist_count++;
175:  } else {
176:    /* ring: drop oldest, shift everyone down one */
177:    for (int i = 1; i < NXLINE_HIST_MAX; i++)
178:      memcpy(nl->history[i - 1], nl->history[i], NXLINE_MAX);
179:    snprintf(nl->history[NXLINE_HIST_MAX - 1], NXLINE_MAX, "%s", cmd);
180:  }
181:  nxline_save_history(nl);
182:}
183:
184:/* ---------------- low-level relative-cursor primitives ---------------- */
185:
186:static inline void nxline_move_left_n(int n) {
187:  if (n > 0)
188:    printf("\033[%dD", n);
189:}
190:static inline void nxline_move_right_n(int n) {
191:  if (n > 0)
192:    printf("\033[%dC", n);
193:}
194:
195:/* nxline_replace_line - wipe the currently-displayed line content (NOT the
196: * prompt) and print newtext in its place. Used by history browsing and
197: * Ctrl-R acceptance. Purely relative: moves left by the CURRENT cursor
198: * position to reach column 0 of the input, erases to end of line, prints
199: * newtext, cursor lands at the end. */
200:static inline void nxline_replace_line(struct nxline *nl, const char *newtext) {
201:  nxline_move_left_n(nl->cursor);
202:  print("\033[K");
203:  size_t tl = strlen(newtext);
204:  if (tl >= NXLINE_MAX)
205:    tl = NXLINE_MAX - 1;
206:  memcpy(nl->buf, newtext, tl);
207:  nl->buf[tl] = '\0';
208:  nl->len = (int)tl;
209:  nl->cursor = (int)tl;
210:  print(nl->buf);
211:}
212:
213:/* nxline_repaint_inline - reprint the CURRENT buffer starting at column 0,
214: * assuming the caller already positioned the cursor there (e.g. right after
215: * printing a fresh prompt on a new line). Leaves the terminal cursor at
216: * nl->cursor, not necessarily at the end. */
217:static inline void nxline_repaint_inline(struct nxline *nl) {
218:  print(nl->buf);
219:  if (nl->cursor < nl->len)
220:    nxline_move_left_n(nl->len - nl->cursor);
221:}
222:
223:/* ---------------- editing operations ---------------- */
224:
225:static inline void nxline_insert_char(struct nxline *nl, char c) {
226:  if (nl->len >= NXLINE_MAX - 1)
227:    return;
228:  memmove(&nl->buf[nl->cursor + 1], &nl->buf[nl->cursor], nl->len - nl->cursor);
229:  nl->buf[nl->cursor] = c;
230:  nl->len++;
231:  nl->buf[nl->len] = '\0';
232:  print(&nl->buf[nl->cursor]); /* prints the new char + the shifted tail */
233:  nl->cursor++;
234:  nxline_move_left_n(nl->len - nl->cursor); /* put the caret back after c */
235:}
236:
237:static inline void nxline_delete_before(struct nxline *nl) { /* Backspace */
238:  if (nl->cursor == 0)
239:    return;
240:  memmove(&nl->buf[nl->cursor - 1], &nl->buf[nl->cursor], nl->len - nl->cursor);
241:  nl->cursor--;
242:  nl->len--;
243:  nl->buf[nl->len] = '\0';
244:  print("\b");
245:  print(&nl->buf[nl->cursor]);
246:  print(" "); /* erase the leftover glyph from the old, longer line */
247:  nxline_move_left_n(nl->len - nl->cursor + 1);
248:}
249:
250:static inline void nxline_delete_at(struct nxline *nl) { /* Delete (forward) */
251:  if (nl->cursor >= nl->len)
252:    return;
253:  memmove(&nl->buf[nl->cursor], &nl->buf[nl->cursor + 1],
254:          nl->len - nl->cursor - 1);
255:  nl->len--;
256:  nl->buf[nl->len] = '\0';
257:  print(&nl->buf[nl->cursor]);
258:  print(" ");
259:  nxline_move_left_n(nl->len - nl->cursor + 1);
260:}
261:
262:static inline void nxline_move_left(struct nxline *nl) {
263:  if (nl->cursor > 0) {
264:    print("\033[D");
265:    nl->cursor--;
266:  }
267:}
268:static inline void nxline_move_right(struct nxline *nl) {
269:  if (nl->cursor < nl->len) {
270:    print("\033[C");
271:    nl->cursor++;
272:  }
273:}
274:static inline void nxline_move_home(struct nxline *nl) {
275:  nxline_move_left_n(nl->cursor);
276:  nl->cursor = 0;
277:}
278:static inline void nxline_move_end(struct nxline *nl) {
279:  nxline_move_right_n(nl->len - nl->cursor);
280:  nl->cursor = nl->len;
281:}
282:
283:/* ---------------- history browsing ---------------- */
284:
285:static inline void nxline_history_prev(struct nxline *nl) {
286:  if (nl->hist_count == 0)
287:    return;
288:  if (nl->hist_pos == -1) {
289:    snprintf(nl->live_stash, NXLINE_MAX, "%s", nl->buf);
290:    nl->hist_pos = nl->hist_count - 1;
291:  } else if (nl->hist_pos > 0) {
292:    nl->hist_pos--;
293:  } else {
294:    return; /* already at the oldest entry */
295:  }
296:  nxline_replace_line(nl, nl->history[nl->hist_pos]);
297:}
298:
299:static inline void nxline_history_next(struct nxline *nl) {
300:  if (nl->hist_pos == -1)
301:    return;
302:  nl->hist_pos++;
303:  if (nl->hist_pos >= nl->hist_count) {
304:    nl->hist_pos = -1;
305:    nxline_replace_line(nl, nl->live_stash);
306:  } else {
307:    nxline_replace_line(nl, nl->history[nl->hist_pos]);
308:  }
309:}
310:
311:/* ---------------- Ctrl-R incremental search ---------------- */
312:
313:/* nxline_search_render - redraw as "(reverse-i-search)`query': match". This
314: * temporarily overwrites the visible line the same way history browsing
315: * does (relative erase + reprint); the ACTUAL nl->buf is untouched until
316: * the search is accepted (Enter) or cancelled (Esc/Ctrl-G). */
317:static inline void nxline_search_render(struct nxline *nl) {
318:  nxline_move_left_n(nl->cursor);
319:  print("\033[K");
320:  char line[NXLINE_MAX];
321:  const char *match = "";
322:  for (int i = nl->hist_count - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
323:    if (nl->search_len == 0 || nxline_contains(nl->history[i], nl->search_buf)) {
324:      match = nl->history[i];
325:      break;
326:    }
327:  }
328:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "(reverse-i-search)`%s': %s", nl->search_buf,
329:           match);
330:  print(line);
331:  /* cursor tracking during search is a display-only concept: park it at the
332:   * end of the rendered line (cursor math resumes once the search ends). */
333:  nl->cursor = (int)strlen(line);
334:  nl->len = nl->cursor;
335:  /* stash the actual match so Enter can accept it without re-searching */
336:  snprintf(nl->buf, NXLINE_MAX, "%s", match);
337:}
338:
339:static inline void nxline_search_start(struct nxline *nl) {
340:  nl->searching = 1;
341:  nl->search_len = 0;
342:  nl->search_buf[0] = '\0';
343:  snprintf(nl->search_stash, NXLINE_MAX, "%s", nl->buf);
344:  nxline_search_render(nl);
345:}
346:
347:static inline void nxline_search_cancel(struct nxline *nl) {
348:  nl->searching = 0;
349:  nxline_replace_line(nl, nl->search_stash);
350:}
351:
352:static inline void nxline_search_accept(struct nxline *nl) {
353:  /* nl->buf already holds the matched command (set by nxline_search_render);
354:   * just stop searching and leave it as the live line, cursor at end. */
355:  nl->searching = 0;
356:  nl->len = (int)strlen(nl->buf);
357:  nl->cursor = nl->len;
358:  nxline_replace_line(nl, nl->buf); /* re-render cleanly without the search prefix */
359:}
360:
361:/* ---------------- tab completion ---------------- */
362:
363:/* nxline_word_start - index of the start of the word ending at nl->cursor
364: * (whitespace-delimited), for completion. */
365:static inline int nxline_word_start(struct nxline *nl) {
366:  int i = nl->cursor;
367:  while (i > 0 && nl->buf[i - 1] != ' ' && nl->buf[i - 1] != '\t')
368:    i--;
369:  return i;
370:}
371:
372:/* nxline_complete - Tab handling. Completes either a bare command name
373: * (scanning /bin then /sys/bin, mirroring nxshell's own help_list_programs)
374: * or, if the current word contains '/', a path (scanning that directory).
375: * A single match is inserted inline; multiple matches are listed on a new
376: * line and the prompt+buffer are repainted below them via print_prompt(). */
377:static inline void nxline_complete(struct nxline *nl) {
378:  int ws = nxline_word_start(nl);
379:  char word[NXLINE_MAX];
380:  int wl = nl->cursor - ws;
381:  if (wl <= 0 || wl >= NXLINE_MAX)
382:    return;
383:  memcpy(word, &nl->buf[ws], wl);
384:  word[wl] = '\0';
385:
386:  const char *slash = strrchr(word, '/');
387:  char dir[128];
388:  const char *prefix;
389:  if (slash) {
390:    int dl = (int)(slash - word);
391:    if (dl == 0)
392:      snprintf(dir, sizeof(dir), "/");
393:    else
394:      snprintf(dir, sizeof(dir), "%.*s", dl, word);
395:    prefix = slash + 1;
396:  } else {
397:    dir[0] = '\0'; /* sentinel: search /bin then /sys/bin below */
398:    prefix = word;
399:  }
400:  size_t plen = strlen(prefix);
401:
402:  char matches[16][NXLINE_MAX];
403:  int nmatch = 0;
404:  char listing[2][1024];
405:  int nlisting = dir[0] ? 1 : 2;
406:  if (dir[0]) {
407:    int n = list_dir(dir, listing[0], sizeof(listing[0]) - 1);
408:    listing[0][n > 0 ? n : 0] = '\0';
409:  } else {
410:    int n0 = list_dir("/bin", listing[0], sizeof(listing[0]) - 1);
411:    listing[0][n0 > 0 ? n0 : 0] = '\0';
412:    int n1 = list_dir("/sys/bin", listing[1], sizeof(listing[1]) - 1);
413:    listing[1][n1 > 0 ? n1 : 0] = '\0';
414:  }
415:
416:  for (int li = 0; li < nlisting && nmatch < 16; li++) {
417:    char *save = NULL;
418:    for (char *tok = strtok_r(listing[li], " \t", &save); tok && nmatch < 16;
419:         tok = strtok_r(NULL, " \t", &save)) {
420:      if (plen == 0 || strncmp(tok, prefix, plen) == 0) {
421:        int already = 0;
422:        for (int i = 0; i < nmatch; i++)
423:          if (strcmp(matches[i], tok) == 0)
424:            already = 1;
425:        if (!already)
426:          snprintf(matches[nmatch++], NXLINE_MAX, "%s", tok);
427:      }
428:    }
429:  }
430:
431:  if (nmatch == 0)
432:    return;
433:
434:  if (nmatch == 1) {
435:    const char *suffix = matches[0] + plen;
436:    while (*suffix)
437:      nxline_insert_char(nl, *suffix++);
438:    return;
439:  }
440:
441:  /* Multiple matches: list them, then repaint prompt + current buffer. */
442:  print("\r\n");
443:  for (int i = 0; i < nmatch; i++)
444:    printf("%-16s", matches[i]);
445:  print("\r\n");
446:  if (nl->print_prompt)
447:    nl->print_prompt(nl->ctx);
448:  nxline_repaint_inline(nl);
449:}
450:
451:/* ---------------- main key-feed entry point ---------------- */
452:
453:/* nxline_feed_key - handle one keyboard event. Returns an NXLINE_* code;
454: * NXLINE_SUBMIT means nl->buf (NUL-terminated, nl->len bytes) is the
455: * completed line — the caller should process it, then call
456: * nxline_history_add() and reset nl->len/cursor to 0 for the next line. */
457:static inline int nxline_feed_key(struct nxline *nl, unsigned char key,
458:                                  uint16_t scancode) {
459:  if (nl->searching) {
460:    if (key == '\n' || key == '\r' || scancode == INPUT_KEY_ENTER) {
461:      nxline_search_accept(nl);
462:      return NXLINE_NONE;
463:    }
464:    if (key == 0x07 || key == 0x1B) { /* Ctrl-G / Esc: cancel */
465:      nxline_search_cancel(nl);
466:      return NXLINE_NONE;
467:    }
468:    if (key == 0x12) { /* Ctrl-R again: skip to the next older match */
469:      return NXLINE_NONE; /* simplest correct behaviour: no-op, avoids
470:                            * accidentally cycling past the only match */
471:    }
472:    if ((key == '\b' || key == 127) && nl->search_len > 0) {
473:      nl->search_buf[--nl->search_len] = '\0';
474:      nxline_search_render(nl);
475:      return NXLINE_NONE;
476:    }
477:    if (key >= 32 && key < 127 && nl->search_len < NXLINE_MAX - 1) {
478:      nl->search_buf[nl->search_len++] = (char)key;
479:      nl->search_buf[nl->search_len] = '\0';
480:      nxline_search_render(nl);
481:    }
482:    return NXLINE_NONE;
483:  }
484:
485:  if (key == '\n' || key == '\r' || scancode == INPUT_KEY_ENTER)
486:    return NXLINE_SUBMIT;
487:
488:  if (key == '\b' || key == 127 || scancode == INPUT_KEY_BACKSPACE) {
489:    nxline_delete_before(nl);
490:    return NXLINE_NONE;
491:  }
492:
493:  if (key == 0x01) { /* Ctrl-A */
494:    nxline_move_home(nl);
495:    return NXLINE_NONE;
496:  }
497:  if (key == 0x05) { /* Ctrl-E */
498:    nxline_move_end(nl);
499:    return NXLINE_NONE;
500:  }
501:  if (key == 0x0C) /* Ctrl-L */
502:    return NXLINE_CLEAR_SCREEN;
503:  if (key == 0x12) { /* Ctrl-R */
504:    nxline_search_start(nl);
505:    return NXLINE_NONE;
506:  }
507:  if (key == 0x04) { /* Ctrl-D */
508:    if (nl->len == 0)
509:      return NXLINE_EOF;
510:    nxline_delete_at(nl); /* non-empty line: acts as forward-delete */
511:    return NXLINE_NONE;
512:  }
513:  if (key == '\t') {
514:    nxline_complete(nl);
515:    return NXLINE_NONE;
516:  }
517:
518:  if (scancode == INPUT_KEY_LEFT) {
519:    nxline_move_left(nl);
520:    return NXLINE_NONE;
521:  }
522:  if (scancode == INPUT_KEY_RIGHT) {
523:    nxline_move_right(nl);
524:    return NXLINE_NONE;
525:  }
526:  if (scancode == INPUT_KEY_UP) {
527:    nxline_history_prev(nl);
528:    return NXLINE_NONE;
529:  }
530:  if (scancode == INPUT_KEY_DOWN) {
531:    nxline_history_next(nl);
532:    return NXLINE_NONE;
533:  }
534:  if (scancode == INPUT_KEY_HOME) {
535:    nxline_move_home(nl);
536:    return NXLINE_NONE;
537:  }
538:  if (scancode == INPUT_KEY_END) {
539:    nxline_move_end(nl);
540:    return NXLINE_NONE;
541:  }
542:  if (scancode == INPUT_KEY_DELETE) {
543:    nxline_delete_at(nl);
544:    return NXLINE_NONE;
545:  }
546:
547:  if (key >= 32 && key < 127)
548:    nxline_insert_char(nl, (char)key);
549:
550:  return NXLINE_NONE;
551:}
552:
553:/* nxline_reset - clear the buffer for the next line (call after SUBMIT is
554: * handled and, typically, nxline_history_add() has been called). */
555:static inline void nxline_reset(struct nxline *nl) {
556:  nl->len = 0;
557:  nl->cursor = 0;
558:  nl->buf[0] = '\0';
559:  nl->hist_pos = -1;
560:}
561:
562:#endif /* _USER_NXLINE_H */
563:

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxmemstat.h @@@
1:#ifndef _USER_NXMEMSTAT_H
2:#define _USER_NXMEMSTAT_H
3:
4:/*
5: * user/sys/bin/nxmemstat.h
6: * NEXS stratified system-statistics helper (ASTRA service layer).
7: *
8: * Reusable header-only helper (all routines `static inline`) over the
9: * privileged OS1_sys_stats() syscall, mirroring nxproc.h.  SECURITY MODEL: no
10: * ambient checks of its own — OS1_sys_stats() is gated to ROOT/machine in the
11: * kernel, so only an NX service (this runs as /sys/bin/nxmemstat at ROOT) can
12: * read the raw stats; USER apps consume the service's GUI, never the syscall.
13: *
14: * Two surfaces:
15: *   - GUI: nxmemstat_render_if_changed() draws a compositor WINDOW (virtio UI),
16: *     redrawing only when a MEANINGFUL value changed (the signature
17: * deliberately EXCLUDES the always-incrementing cumulative counters — ctx
18: * switches, alloc /free calls, search-ns total, uptime — so the window does not
19: * "repeat" every tick; those are shown as derived rates but do not force a
20: * redraw).
21: *   - Log: nxmemstat_csv_line() formats one MEMSTAT CSV record for a headless
22: *     serial capture consumed by tools/analyze_drift.py.
23: */
24:
25:#include <os1.h>
26:
27:/* nxmemstat_snapshot - fill *out with one stats snapshot.  Returns >0 (bytes)
28: * on success, or a negative errno (-EPERM if the caller is not ROOT/machine).
29: */
30:static inline long nxmemstat_snapshot(struct os1_sysstats *out) {
31:  return OS1_sys_stats(out);
32:}
33:
34:/* Signature over the SLOWLY-changing, user-meaningful fields only.  Page counts
35: * are bucketed to MB so ordinary churn of a few pages does not force a redraw;
36: * the cumulative rate counters are intentionally absent. */
37:static inline unsigned long nxmemstat_signature(const struct os1_sysstats *s) {
38:  unsigned long h = 1469598103934665603UL; /* FNV-1a basis */
39:#define MIX(v) (h = (h ^ (unsigned long)(v)) * 1099511628211UL)
40:  MIX(s->pmm_free_pages >> 8);         /* ~MB buckets */
41:  MIX(s->pmm_largest_contig_run >> 8); /* ~MB buckets */
42:  MIX(s->pmm_free_run_count);
43:  MIX(s->km_bytes_in_use >> 10); /* KB buckets */
44:  MIX(s->km_live_allocs);
45:  MIX(s->sched_nproc);
46:  MIX(s->sched_zombie_count);
47:  MIX(s->sched_runnable);
48:  for (int i = 0; i < OBJ_TYPE_COUNT; i++)
49:    MIX(s->obj_live_by_type[i]);
50:#undef MIX
51:  return h;
52:}
53:
54:/* nxmemstat_render - draw the stats into window win_id.  prev/dt_ms give the
55: * previous sample and elapsed ms so per-interval rates can be shown; pass
56: * prev==NULL (or dt_ms==0) on the first frame to omit rates. */
57:static inline void nxmemstat_render(int win_id, const struct os1_sysstats *s,
58:                                    const struct os1_sysstats *prev,
59:                                    unsigned long dt_ms) {
60:  unsigned long free_mb = (unsigned long)((s->pmm_free_pages * 4UL) / 1024UL);
61:  unsigned long tot_mb = (unsigned long)((s->pmm_total_pages * 4UL) / 1024UL);
62:  unsigned long lcr_mb =
63:      (unsigned long)((s->pmm_largest_contig_run * 4UL) / 1024UL);
64:
65:  unsigned long csw_rate = 0, a_rate = 0, mean_srch = 0;
66:  if (prev && dt_ms > 0) {
67:    csw_rate =
68:        (unsigned long)((s->sched_ctx_switches - prev->sched_ctx_switches) *
69:                        1000UL / dt_ms);
70:    unsigned long da =
71:        (unsigned long)(s->pmm_alloc_calls - prev->pmm_alloc_calls);
72:    a_rate = da * 1000UL / dt_ms;
73:    if (da)
74:      mean_srch = (unsigned long)((s->pmm_alloc_search_ns_total -
75:                                   prev->pmm_alloc_search_ns_total) /
76:                                  da);
77:  }
78:
79:  _sys_window_write(win_id, "\033[H\033[J", 6); /* clear */
80:  _sys_window_write(win_id, "\033[1;34m", 7);   /* bold Blue */
81:  printf_win(win_id, "NEXS System Monitor            uptime %lus\n",
82:             (unsigned long)(s->uptime_ns / 1000000000ULL));
83:  _sys_window_write(win_id, "\033[0m", 4);
84:  _sys_window_write(win_id, "--------------------------------------------\n",
85:                    45);
86:  printf_win(win_id, "CPU    : %lu online   runnable %lu   zombies %lu\n",
87:             (unsigned long)s->sched_ncpu, (unsigned long)s->sched_runnable,
88:             (unsigned long)s->sched_zombie_count);
89:  printf_win(win_id, "ctxsw  : %lu total   (~%lu/s)\n",
90:             (unsigned long)s->sched_ctx_switches, csw_rate);
91:  printf_win(win_id, "PMM    : free %lu / %lu MB   used %lu MB\n", free_mb,
92:             tot_mb, tot_mb - free_mb);
93:  printf_win(win_id, "frag   : largest %lu MB (%lu pg)   runs %lu\n", lcr_mb,
94:             (unsigned long)s->pmm_largest_contig_run,
95:             (unsigned long)s->pmm_free_run_count);
96:  printf_win(win_id, "alloc  : %lu calls (~%lu/s)   search ~%lu ns (max %lu)\n",
97:             (unsigned long)s->pmm_alloc_calls, a_rate, mean_srch,
98:             (unsigned long)s->pmm_alloc_search_ns_max);
99:  printf_win(win_id,
100:             "kheap  : in-use %lu KB  hi %lu KB  live %lu  pool %lu KB\n",
101:             (unsigned long)(s->km_bytes_in_use / 1024UL),
102:             (unsigned long)(s->km_high_water_bytes / 1024UL),
103:             (unsigned long)s->km_live_allocs,
104:             (unsigned long)(s->km_heap_total_bytes / 1024UL));
105:  /* NOTE(OBJ-COUNT-01): these are live CAPABILITY-HANDLE objects (created only
106:   * via SYS_HANDLE_CREATE/OS1low_handle_create — see include/api/object.h),
107:   * NOT a live inventory of "windows on screen" or "running processes".  Most
108:   * everyday operations still go through legacy direct syscalls that never
109:   * touch this layer: SYS_CREATE_WINDOW (the compositor's own window array),
110:   * SYS_SPAWN/SYS_KILL (process_pool), SYS_REGISTRY_GET/SET (the registry
111:   * tree) — none of them call kobj_alloc(), so FILE/PROC/REGKEY/WINDOW read 0
112:   * whenever nothing has an OPEN capability handle of that type at the exact
113:   * snapshot instant (e.g. a file handle from a startup WAD/font read is
114:   * already closed by the time this polls).  This is the documented state of
115:   * the call-surface refactor (DIR-01/#164, ASTRA.md §7.10): the object layer
116:   * is not yet the path every subsystem uses.  CONSOLE is the one type every
117:   * live process actually holds (process_install_stdio gives it 3 handles to
118:   * one shared object) and is shown here so the line always has a
119:   * nonzero, meaningful number when processes are running. */
120:  printf_win(win_id,
121:             "objs   : FILE %lu  PROC %lu  REGKEY %lu  WINDOW %lu  CONSOLE %lu\n",
122:             (unsigned long)s->obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_FILE],
123:             (unsigned long)s->obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS],
124:             (unsigned long)s->obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_REGKEY],
125:             (unsigned long)s->obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW],
126:             (unsigned long)s->obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_CONSOLE]);
127:}
128:
129:/* nxmemstat_render_if_changed - snapshot, redraw the window only when the
130: * meaningful signature changed.  *prev holds the last snapshot (for rates);
131: * *last_sig the last signature; dt_ms the loop cadence.  Returns 1 if redrawn,
132: * 0 if skipped, negative on syscall error. */
133:static inline int nxmemstat_render_if_changed(int win_id,
134:                                              struct os1_sysstats *prev,
135:                                              unsigned long *last_sig,
136:                                              unsigned long dt_ms) {
137:  struct os1_sysstats cur;
138:  long r = nxmemstat_snapshot(&cur);
139:  if (r < 0) {
140:    unsigned long err_sig = ~0UL;
141:    if (last_sig && *last_sig != err_sig) {
142:      _sys_window_write(win_id, "OS1_sys_stats denied (need ROOT) or failed\n",
143:                        43);
144:      *last_sig = err_sig;
145:    }
146:    return (int)r;
147:  }
148:  unsigned long sig = nxmemstat_signature(&cur);
149:  int had_prev = (last_sig && *last_sig != 0 && *last_sig != ~0UL);
150:  if (last_sig && *last_sig == sig) {
151:    *prev = cur; /* keep rates fresh even when we skip the redraw */
152:    return 0;
153:  }
154:  nxmemstat_render(win_id, &cur, had_prev ? prev : (struct os1_sysstats *)0,
155:                   dt_ms);
156:  if (prev)
157:    *prev = cur;
158:  if (last_sig)
159:    *last_sig = sig;
160:  return 1;
161:}
162:
163:/* nxmemstat_csv_line - format one MEMSTAT CSV record (headless --log mode),
164: * matching tools/analyze_drift.py's column order.  't_s' is seconds since the
165: * logger started; 'cycles' is not known to the service, emitted as 0. */
166:static inline int nxmemstat_csv_line(char *buf, int size,
167:                                     const struct os1_sysstats *s,
168:                                     unsigned long t_s) {
169:  return snprintf(
170:      buf, size,
171:      "MEMSTAT,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,%lu,"
172:      "%lu,%lu,%lu,0\n",
173:      t_s, (unsigned long)s->pmm_free_pages,
174:      (unsigned long)s->pmm_largest_contig_run,
175:      (unsigned long)s->pmm_free_run_count, (unsigned long)s->pmm_alloc_calls,
176:      (unsigned long)s->pmm_free_calls,
177:      (unsigned long)s->pmm_alloc_search_ns_total,
178:      (unsigned long)s->pmm_alloc_search_ns_max,
179:      (unsigned long)s->km_bytes_in_use, (unsigned long)s->km_high_water_bytes,
180:      (unsigned long)s->km_live_allocs, (unsigned long)s->sched_ctx_switches,
181:      (unsigned long)s->sched_runnable, (unsigned long)s->sched_zombie_count,
182:      (unsigned long)s->obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_FILE],
183:      (unsigned long)s->obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS],
184:      (unsigned long)s->obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_REGKEY],
185:      (unsigned long)s->obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW],
186:      (unsigned long)s->obj_live_by_type[OBJ_TYPE_CONSOLE]);
187:}
188:
189:#endif /* _USER_NXMEMSTAT_H */
