@@@ user/sys/bin/nxperm.h @@@
1:#ifndef _USER_NXPERM_H
2:#define _USER_NXPERM_H
3:
4:/*
5: * user/sys/bin/nxperm.h
6: * NEXS users/permissions helper (ASTRA service layer) — FOUNDATION.
7: *
8: * The privilege model (include/api/caps.h): every process has one LEVEL —
9: * machine (the computer itself, NOT a login user), root, user, guest — which is
10: * the resolver for the (future) multi-user model, plus a capability MASK
11: * enforced at the syscall boundary.  nxperm presents this as a LEVEL-based view
12: * so applications reason in terms of machine/root/user/guest and never touch the
13: * raw capability bits (ASTRA goal: hide the capability layer behind a
14: * kernel-managed standard).
15: *
16: * This header is the INTROSPECTION foundation only.  The full vision — login,
17: * named users + passwords, su elevation, UAC approval popups rendered as
18: * kernel-trusted windows, and a capability-partitioned VFS — is the dedicated
19: * users phase.
20: *
21: * SECURITY: read-only, adds no checks.  Identity comes from OS1_identity(),
22: * which only ever reveals the caller's OWN level/mask — secure by caller.
23: */
24:#include <os1.h> /* pulls caps.h (PLVL_ and CAP_ macros) + OS1_identity + printf */
25:#include <string.h>
26:
27:/* Level name (machine/root/user/guest), or "?" out of range. */
28:static inline const char *nxperm_level_name(int level) {
29:  switch (level) {
30:  case PLVL_MACHINE: return "machine";
31:  case PLVL_ROOT:    return "root";
32:  case PLVL_USER:    return "user";
33:  case PLVL_GUEST:   return "guest";
34:  default:           return "?";
35:  }
36:}
37:
38:/* The capability mask a level grants.  Derives from caps_for_level() in the
39: * shared caps header — the ONE definition of the level->mask policy (B2.1).
40: * This used to be a hand-maintained copy of the kernel's level_ceiling[]; a
41: * copy is a drift bug waiting to happen, so it is now a thin alias. */
42:static inline unsigned int nxperm_level_mask(int level) {
43:  return caps_for_level(level);
44:}
45:
46:/* One capability bit -> a human service label. */
47:struct nxperm_cap {
48:  unsigned int bit;
49:  const char *label;
50:};
51:static const struct nxperm_cap NXPERM_CAPS[] = {
52:    {CAP_SPAWN, "spawn"},     {CAP_FS_WRITE, "files"},
53:    {CAP_IPC_ANY, "ipc"},     {CAP_WINDOW, "windows"},
54:    {CAP_REG_WRITE, "registry"},
55:};
56:#define NXPERM_NCAPS (int)(sizeof(NXPERM_CAPS) / sizeof(NXPERM_CAPS[0]))
57:
58:/* Render a cap mask as a space-separated label list into buf ("-" if none). */
59:static inline void nxperm_mask_str(unsigned int mask, char *buf, int n) {
60:  int p = 0;
61:  if (n > 0)
62:    buf[0] = '\0';
63:  for (int i = 0; i < NXPERM_NCAPS; i++) {
64:    if (!(mask & NXPERM_CAPS[i].bit))
65:      continue;
66:    const char *l = NXPERM_CAPS[i].label;
67:    if (p && p + 1 < n)
68:      buf[p++] = ' ';
69:    for (int k = 0; l[k] && p + 1 < n; k++)
70:      buf[p++] = l[k];
71:    buf[p] = '\0';
72:  }
73:  if (p == 0 && n > 1) {
74:    buf[0] = '-';
75:    buf[1] = '\0';
76:  }
77:}
78:
79:/* A declared system service + the capability needed to use it (ASTRA: every
80: * service is gated by a capability — only programs granted that capability may
81: * activate it).  Foundation list; extended as services land. */
82:struct nxperm_service {
83:  const char *name;
84:  const char *desc;
85:  unsigned int cap;
86:};
87:static const struct nxperm_service NXPERM_SERVICES[] = {
88:    {"windows", "create/draw windows", CAP_WINDOW},
89:    {"spawn", "launch programs", CAP_SPAWN},
90:    {"files", "write files", CAP_FS_WRITE},
91:    {"registry", "write registry", CAP_REG_WRITE},
92:    {"ipc", "message non-kin", CAP_IPC_ANY},
93:};
94:#define NXPERM_NSERVICES                                                        \
95:  (int)(sizeof(NXPERM_SERVICES) / sizeof(NXPERM_SERVICES[0]))
96:
97:static inline void nxperm_emit(int win, const char *s) {
98:  if (win < 0)
99:    printf("%s", s);
100:  else
101:    printf_win(win, "%s", s);
102:}
103:
104:/* "whoami": current level + the services it may use. */
105:static inline void nxperm_print_identity(int win) {
106:  int level = 0;
107:  unsigned int mask = 0;
108:  OS1_identity(&level, &mask);
109:  char m[96];
110:  nxperm_mask_str(mask, m, (int)sizeof(m));
111:  char line[160];
112:  snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "level: %s\ncan:   %s\n",
113:           nxperm_level_name(level), m);
114:  nxperm_emit(win, line);
115:}
116:
117:/* List the levels and the mask each grants. */
118:static inline void nxperm_print_levels(int win) {
119:  nxperm_emit(win, "LEVEL    SERVICES\n");
120:  for (int lv = 0; lv < PLVL_COUNT; lv++) {
121:    char m[96];
122:    nxperm_mask_str(nxperm_level_mask(lv), m, (int)sizeof(m));
123:    char line[160];
124:    snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%-8s %s\n", nxperm_level_name(lv), m);
125:    nxperm_emit(win, line);
126:  }
127:}
128:
129:/* List the declared services + the capability each requires, and whether the
130: * current caller holds it. */
131:static inline void nxperm_print_services(int win) {
132:  int level = 0;
133:  unsigned int mask = 0;
134:  OS1_identity(&level, &mask);
135:  nxperm_emit(win, "SERVICE   ALLOWED  DESCRIPTION\n");
136:  for (int i = 0; i < NXPERM_NSERVICES; i++) {
137:    const struct nxperm_service *s = &NXPERM_SERVICES[i];
138:    char line[160];
139:    snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%-9s %-8s %s\n", s->name,
140:             (mask & s->cap) ? "yes" : "no", s->desc);
141:    nxperm_emit(win, line);
142:  }
143:}
144:
145:#endif /* _USER_NXPERM_H */
146:

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxproc.h @@@
1:#ifndef _USER_NXPROC_H
2:#define _USER_NXPROC_H
3:
4:/*
5: * user/sys/bin/nxproc.h
6: * NEXS stratified process-management helper (ASTRA service layer).
7: *
8: * A REUSABLE helper layer that both user and system apps may link against to
9: * inspect and act on the process table.  It is intentionally header-only
10: * (all routines `static inline`) so consumers pull it in without any extra
11: * object or link-rule churn in the Makefile.
12: *
13: * SECURITY MODEL: this layer adds NO ambient permission checks of its own.
14: * Every routine is a thin wrapper over an existing OS1 syscall, and the kernel
15: * already gates those syscalls per caller (e.g. kill is checked against the
16: * caller's capability/level).  Security is therefore "by caller" automatically:
17: * a privileged system app and an unprivileged user app calling the same helper
18: * get exactly the rights the kernel grants each of them — the helper neither
19: * widens nor narrows that.
20: *
21: * State integer to string mapping uses the values defined in the kernel's
22: * sched/process.h (PROC_CREATED=1, RUNNING=2, SLEEPING=3, ZOMBIE=4, DEAD=5,
23: * READY=6).  Any other value maps to "UNUSED".
24: *
25: * Consumers:
26: *   user/sys/bin/nxproc.c  — INLINE ELF: shell `ps`, one-shot stdout dump
27: *                            via nxproc_render_inline().  No compositor
28: *                            window is opened; every row goes through printf
29: *                            (write(1, ...)), so the shell's terminal shows
30: *                            the table.
31: *   user/sys/bin/nxtop.c   — WINDOWED realtime: opens its own compositor
32: *                            window and refreshes at ~1Hz via
33: *                            nxproc_render_if_changed(), redrawing only when
34: *                            the table actually changes.
35: */
36:
37:#include <os1.h>
38:
39:/* Hard cap on processes we ever snapshot/render in one pass (matches the
40: * kernel's MAX_PROCESSES ceiling used elsewhere in userland). */
41:#define NXPROC_MAX 32
42:
43:/*
44: * nxproc_snapshot - fill a caller-provided array with the live process table.
45: *
46: * out:       caller-owned array of at least `max` struct ps_info entries.
47: * max:       capacity of `out`; clamped to NXPROC_MAX internally.
48: *
49: * Thin wrapper over _sys_get_procs() (SYS_GET_PS).  Returns the number of
50: * entries written (0..max), or a negative value on syscall error.  No heap
51: * allocation; the snapshot is a point-in-time copy.
52: */
53:static inline int nxproc_snapshot(struct ps_info *out, int max) {
54:  if (!out || max <= 0)
55:    return 0;
56:  if (max > NXPROC_MAX)
57:    max = NXPROC_MAX;
58:  return _sys_get_procs(out, (size_t)max);
59:}
60:
61:/*
62: * nxproc_kill - request termination of a process by pid.
63: *
64: * pid: target process id.
65: *
66: * Thin wrapper over kill_process() (which routes to SYS_KILL).  Returns the
67: * syscall result (0 on success, negative on failure/denial).  The kernel
68: * enforces whether the *caller* is allowed to kill `pid`; this wrapper performs
69: * no check of its own.
70: */
71:static inline int nxproc_kill(int pid) { return kill_process(pid); }
72:
73:/*
74: * nxproc_state_str - map a numeric proc_state to a human-readable string.
75: *
76: * Values match kernel enum proc_state (kernel/sched/process.h).  Unknown values
77: * map to "UNUSED" so callers always get a printable, fixed token.
78: */
79:static inline const char *nxproc_state_str(int state) {
80:  switch (state) {
81:  case 1:
82:    return "CREATED";
83:  case 2:
84:    return "RUNNING";
85:  case 3:
86:    return "SLEEPING";
87:  case 4:
88:    return "ZOMBIE";
89:  case 5:
90:    return "DEAD";
91:  case 6:
92:    return "READY";
93:  case 7:
94:    return "STOPPED"; /* PROC_STOPPED (Phase 2 job control) */
95:  default:
96:    return "UNUSED";
97:  }
98:}
99:
100:/*
101: * nxproc_signature - fold the render-relevant fields of a snapshot into a
102: * single 64-bit value.
103: *
104: * procs: snapshot array.
105: * count: number of valid entries.
106: *
107: * Only the fields the rendered list actually shows (count, pid, state,
108: * priority, on_cpu) are mixed in, using a cheap FNV-1a-style rolling hash.
109: * Two snapshots that would render identically produce the same signature, so a
110: * renderer can compare against the previous signature and skip the redraw when
111: * nothing visible changed.  cpu_time is deliberately excluded: it ticks every
112: * sample and would defeat change-detection without altering the displayed
113: * columns.
114: */
115:static inline unsigned long nxproc_signature(const struct ps_info *procs,
116:                                             int count) {
117:  unsigned long h = 1469598103934665603UL; /* FNV-1a 64-bit offset basis */
118:  /* Mix the count itself so a process appearing/disappearing always shifts. */
119:  h = (h ^ (unsigned long)(unsigned int)count) * 1099511628211UL;
120:  for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
121:    h = (h ^ (unsigned long)(unsigned int)procs[i].pid) * 1099511628211UL;
122:    h = (h ^ (unsigned long)(unsigned int)procs[i].state) * 1099511628211UL;
123:    h = (h ^ (unsigned long)(unsigned int)procs[i].priority) * 1099511628211UL;
124:    h = (h ^ (unsigned long)(unsigned int)procs[i].on_cpu) * 1099511628211UL;
125:  }
126:  return h;
127:}
128:
129:/*
130: * nxproc_render_rows - write the formatted, ANSI-coloured process list to a
131: * window.
132: *
133: * win_id: compositor window id to write into.
134: * procs:  snapshot array.
135: * count:  number of valid entries.
136: *
137: * This is the rendering logic: a header row, a separator, then one colourised
138: * row per process (bright green
139: * for RUNNING, grey for SLEEPING, terminal default otherwise).  The screen is
140: * cleared first via ANSI so the window always reflects the current table.
141: *
142: * Unconditional: callers that want change-detection should gate this behind
143: * nxproc_render_if_changed() rather than calling it every tick.
144: */
145:/*
146: * nxproc_cpu_color - pick an ANSI 256-colour escape for the per-process CPU
147: * id column.
148: *
149: * cpu is clamped to [0, 255]; the cpu id IS the xterm-256 palette index, so
150: * every one of the 256 possible cpu ids gets its own swatch.  cpu == -1
151: * (process not currently on a cpu, sleeping/created/zombie/dead) returns a
152: * plain grey; the caller's STATE colour already telegraphs the situation, so
153: * the cpu cell should not steal the show.
154: */
155:static inline const char *nxproc_cpu_color(int cpu) {
156:  if (cpu < 0 || cpu > 255)
157:    return "\033[90m";
158:  /* Direct 1-to-1 mapping: cpu id is the xterm-256 palette index.  The
159:   * compositor's ANSI parser (\033[38;5;N in term.c:105) supports all 256
160:   * entries, so each of the 256 possible cpu ids gets its own swatch and
161:   * adjacent cpu ids are always distinguishable.  The palette is identity
162:   * (cpu → idx) by design: no remapping math, no saturation loss, the
163:   * digit carries the colour chosen by the system palette author. */
164:  static char buf[2][16];
165:  static int slot;
166:  slot ^= 1;
167:  char *p = buf[slot];
168:  int n = 0;
169:  p[n++] = '\033';
170:  p[n++] = '[';
171:  p[n++] = '3';
172:  p[n++] = '8';
173:  p[n++] = ';';
174:  p[n++] = '5';
175:  p[n++] = ';';
176:  int v = cpu;
177:  char tmp[3];
178:  int t = 0;
179:  if (v >= 100)
180:    tmp[t++] = '0' + (v / 100);
181:  v %= 100;
182:  if (v >= 10 || t > 0)
183:    tmp[t++] = '0' + (v / 10);
184:  v %= 10;
185:  tmp[t++] = '0' + v;
186:  for (int i = 0; i < t; i++)
187:    p[n++] = tmp[i];
188:  p[n++] = 'm';
189:  p[n] = '\0';
190:  return buf[slot];
191:}
192:
193:static inline void nxproc_render_rows(int win_id, const struct ps_info *procs,
194:                                      int count) {
195:  /* Clear screen using ANSI (handled by our compositor Terminal Emulator). */
196:  _sys_window_write(win_id, "\033[H\033[J", 6);
197:  _sys_window_write(win_id, "\033[1;34m", 7); /* bold blue header */
198:  printf_win(win_id, "%-4s %-16s %-10s %-4s %-3s\n", "PID", "NAME", "STATE",
199:             "PRIO", "CPU");
200:  _sys_window_write(win_id, "\033[0m", 4);
201:  _sys_window_write(win_id, "--------------------------------------------\n",
202:                    45);
203:
204:  for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
205:    const char *state_str = nxproc_state_str(procs[i].state);
206:    int cpu = procs[i].on_cpu;
207:
208:    /* Per-process STATE colour reflects the lifecycle.  READY (6) gets aqua so
209:     * a runnable-but-not-currently-running process stays distinct from
210:     * RUNNING (2, bold green).  ZOMBIE is muted brown; DEAD dim red. */
211:    const char *state_color;
212:    int state_len;
213:    if (procs[i].state == 2) {              /* RUNNING */
214:      state_color = "\033[1;32m"; state_len = 7;
215:    } else if (procs[i].state == 6) {       /* READY */
216:      state_color = "\033[38;5;51m"; state_len = 10;
217:    } else if (procs[i].state == 3) {       /* SLEEPING */
218:      state_color = "\033[90m"; state_len = 5;
219:    } else if (procs[i].state == 4) {       /* ZOMBIE */
220:      state_color = "\033[38;5;130m"; state_len = 11;
221:    } else if (procs[i].state == 5) {       /* DEAD */
222:      state_color = "\033[31m"; state_len = 5;
223:    } else {                                 /* CREATED=1 or anything else */
224:      state_color = "\033[37m"; state_len = 5;
225:    }
226:
227:    /* Identity columns in the STATE colour. */
228:    _sys_window_write(win_id, state_color, state_len);
229:    printf_win(win_id, "%-4d %-16s %-10s %-4d ", procs[i].pid, procs[i].name,
230:               state_str, procs[i].priority);
231:
232:    /* CPU column: pad left, then emit the digits in the per-cpu gradient.
233:     * The left-pad spaces stay in the STATE colour so only the digits carry
234:     * the cpu hue (the OPSERV-PROCS-02 #141 rule: "only the number is
235:     * coloured").  cpu == -1 (not on a cpu) gets grey for the whole cell.
236:     * The column is 3 chars wide (header "%-3s"), so any cpu ≥ 3 digits
237:     * overflows the cell visually — acceptable since 1000+ cores is
238:     * unrealistic for the current scheduler and the per-cpu palette still
239:     * distinguishes it. */
240:    if (cpu >= 0 && cpu <= 255) {
241:      const char *ccol = nxproc_cpu_color(cpu);
242:      int digits;
243:      if (cpu < 10)
244:        digits = 1;
245:      else if (cpu < 100)
246:        digits = 2;
247:      else
248:        digits = 3;
249:      /* pad = 3 - digits spaces in state colour */
250:      for (int s = 0; s < 3 - digits; s++)
251:        _sys_window_write(win_id, " ", 1);
252:      /* IMPORTANT: _sys_window_write takes an explicit byte count — passing 0
253:       * here would silently drop the cpu-colour escape and leave the digits
254:       * in the previous (state) colour.  Use strlen() on the NUL-terminated
255:       * escape so we always emit the whole "\033[38;5;Nm" sequence. */
256:      _sys_window_write(win_id, ccol, (unsigned long)strlen(ccol));
257:      printf_win(win_id, "%d", cpu);
258:      _sys_window_write(win_id, "\033[0m", 4);
259:      _sys_window_write(win_id, state_color, state_len);
260:    } else {
261:      printf_win(win_id, "%-3d", cpu);
262:    }
263:
264:    _sys_window_write(win_id, "\n", 1);
265:    _sys_window_write(win_id, "\033[0m", 4); /* Reset color */
266:  }
267:}
268:
269:/*
270: * nxproc_render_inline - emit the formatted, ANSI-coloured process list to the
271: * caller's stdout (fd 1, the TTY/window the program is running in).
272: *
273: * procs: snapshot array.
274: * count: number of valid entries.
275: *
276: * INLINE-STDOUT variant of nxproc_render_rows().  No compositor window is
277: * created: every row goes through printf(), which lib.c:429 routes to
278: * write(1, ...) — the same fd the kernel gives every spawned process as its
279: * TTY.  Used by `nxproc --inline` so the shell's `ps` command can dump the
280: * table onto its own terminal without spawning a window.  The ANSI escapes
281: * (clear-screen + colour SGRs) are identical to the windowed version so the
282: * caller's terminal emulator handles them the same way.
283: *
284: * Unconditional: one-shot callers (nxproc's `cmd_print`) render exactly once,
285: * so no change-detection wrapper exists for the inline variant — the windowed
286: * loop uses nxproc_render_if_changed() below.
287: */
288:static inline void nxproc_render_inline(const struct ps_info *procs,
289:                                       int count) {
290:  /* Inline render into the caller's controlling terminal.  Intentionally NO
291:   * "\033[H\033[J" clear-screen here: when `nxproc` runs as a child of the
292:   * shell (USR-TTY-01, inherited ctty) the clearing would wipe the shell's
293:   * prompt too, forcing the user to press Enter to repaint it.  The ANSI SGR
294:   * colour sequences below are otherwise identical to the windowed variant
295:   * so the terminal emulator in the compositor renders them the same way. */
296:  printf("\033[1;34m"); /* bold blue header */
297:  printf("%-4s %-16s %-10s %-4s %-3s\n", "PID", "NAME", "STATE", "PRIO", "CPU");
298:  printf("\033[0m");
299:  printf("--------------------------------------------\n");
300:
301:  for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
302:    const char *state_str = nxproc_state_str(procs[i].state);
303:    int cpu = procs[i].on_cpu;
304:
305:    const char *state_color;
306:    if (procs[i].state == 2) {              /* RUNNING */
307:      state_color = "\033[1;32m";
308:    } else if (procs[i].state == 6) {       /* READY */
309:      state_color = "\033[38;5;51m";
310:    } else if (procs[i].state == 3) {       /* SLEEPING */
311:      state_color = "\033[90m";
312:    } else if (procs[i].state == 4) {       /* ZOMBIE */
313:      state_color = "\033[38;5;130m";
314:    } else if (procs[i].state == 5) {       /* DEAD */
315:      state_color = "\033[31m";
316:    } else {                                 /* CREATED=1 or anything else */
317:      state_color = "\033[37m";
318:    }
319:
320:    printf("%s", state_color);
321:    printf("%-4d %-16s %-10s %-4d ", procs[i].pid, procs[i].name, state_str,
322:           procs[i].priority);
323:
324:    if (cpu >= 0 && cpu <= 255) {
325:      const char *ccol = nxproc_cpu_color(cpu);
326:      int digits;
327:      if (cpu < 10)
328:        digits = 1;
329:      else if (cpu < 100)
330:        digits = 2;
331:      else
332:        digits = 3;
333:      for (int s = 0; s < 3 - digits; s++)
334:        printf(" ");
335:      /* The colour escape is a NUL-terminated string built by
336:       * nxproc_cpu_color(); printf("%s", ...) emits the whole sequence
337:       * (lib.c printf goes through vsnprintf -> strlen(buf) -> write(1, ...),
338:       * so there is no count=0 silent-drop hazard like _sys_window_write). */
339:      printf("%s%d", ccol, cpu);
340:      printf("\033[0m");
341:      printf("%s", state_color);
342:    } else {
343:      printf("%-3d", cpu);
344:    }
345:
346:    printf("\n");
347:    printf("\033[0m");
348:  }
349:}
350:
351:/*
352: * nxproc_render_if_changed - OPTIMIZED render: snapshot the table and only
353: * rebuild+write the window when the visible content actually changed.
354: *
355: * win_id:   compositor window id to write into.
356: * last_sig: in/out pointer to the caller's "previous signature" state.  Seed it
357: *           with a sentinel (e.g. 0) on the first call; the helper updates it.
358: *
359: * Computes the snapshot's signature (see nxproc_signature) and compares it to
360: * *last_sig.  If unchanged, returns immediately WITHOUT touching the window, so
361: * an N-Hz refresh loop never busy-redraws an unchanged list.  If changed, it
362: * re-renders via nxproc_render_rows() and stores the new signature.
363: *
364: * Returns 1 if it (re)rendered, 0 if it skipped because nothing changed, or a
365: * negative value if the snapshot syscall failed.
366: */
367:static inline int nxproc_render_if_changed(int win_id,
368:                                           unsigned long *last_sig) {
369:  struct ps_info procs[NXPROC_MAX];
370:
371:  int count = nxproc_snapshot(procs, NXPROC_MAX);
372:  if (count < 0) {
373:    /* Surface the error once, but don't keep
374:     * rewriting it: fold the error into the signature so a persistent failure
375:     * is reported a single time. */
376:    unsigned long err_sig = ~0UL;
377:    if (last_sig && *last_sig != err_sig) {
378:      _sys_window_write(win_id, "Error fetching process list\n", 28);
379:      *last_sig = err_sig;
380:    }
381:    return count;
382:  }
383:
384:  unsigned long sig = nxproc_signature(procs, count);
385:  if (last_sig && *last_sig == sig)
386:    return 0; /* Unchanged since last render: skip the write entirely. */
387:
388:  nxproc_render_rows(win_id, procs, count);
389:  if (last_sig)
390:    *last_sig = sig;
391:  return 1;
392:}
393:
394:#endif /* _USER_NXPROC_H */

@@@ user/sys/bin/nxres.h @@@
1:#ifndef _USER_NXRES_H
2:#define _USER_NXRES_H
3:
4:/*
5: * user/sys/bin/nxres.h
6: * Compositor look (style/theme/background) — single canonical getter/setter
7: * pair, shared by every consumer instead of each one re-reading raw registry
8: * keys and re-deriving id<->name mappings on its own (nxsettings, nxbar,
9: * nxntfy_srv, nxui and nxlauncher used to do this independently, and only
10: * nxres.c's own copy was ever kept in sync with the kernel enum order).
11: *
12: * Same pattern as nxinfo.h/nxperm.h/nxproc.h: a header-only, static-inline
13: * helper layer over the plain OS1_ syscalls, dropped into any translation
14: * unit that needs it.
15: *
16: * Ground truth: kernel/core/syscall_dispatch.c's SYS_SET_STYLE handler
17: * writes style.name/theme.color/background.name into the registry itself on
18: * every successful change (any caller, not just nxres) — see
19: * kernel/lib/registry.c registry_caller_owner() for why a ROOT-level service
20: * changing the look does not get its write rejected as "not the owner".
21: * The registry mirror here is kept as a second write for callers running
22: * against a kernel build that predates that mirror; it is idempotent
23: * (same value) against a kernel that already wrote it.
24: *
25: * Change propagation: a successful nxres_set_*() posts through the EXISTING
26: * async notification transport — send()/IPC_TYPE_NOTIFY, the exact
27: * mechanism nxntfy_srv.c already uses for popups — instead of a new bespoke
28: * broadcast mechanism or per-frame registry polling:
29: *   - the user-facing popup goes to srv.notify_pid via notify(), same as
30: *     any other system notification;
31: *   - a SILENT ping (same IPC_TYPE_NOTIFY, tagged with IPC_LOOK_PING_MAGIC
32: *     in data2, posix_types.h, so it is never confused with a real user
33: *     notification) goes to every singleton system service's registered
34: *     pid — srv.dock_pid (nxui), srv.bar_pid (nxbar), srv.launcher_pid
35: *     (nxlauncher) — published by init the same way it already publishes
36: *     srv.notify_pid (register_service_pid, user/sys/bin/nxinit.c) and
37: *     refreshed on every respawn so the ping can never land on a corpse's
38: *     stale pid.  A windowed app sees this ping as INPUT_TYPE_LOOK_CHANGED
39: *     from its EXISTING input_poll_event() loop (input.h/lib.c) — NOT a
40: *     second try_recv() loop: input_poll_event() is the single consumer of
41: *     an app's IPC mailbox, and a competing try_recv() elsewhere in the
42: *     same app would silently steal keyboard/mouse messages before
43: *     input_poll_event ever saw them (the bug in this feature's first cut).
44: *     nxntfy_srv is the one exception — it has no input_poll_event loop of
45: *     its own (its window is passive/click-through), so it checks
46: *     msg.data2 directly in its own recv()/try_recv() loop, which already
47: *     is that app's single mailbox consumer.
48: * nxsettings is on the same ping list even though it is not an init-
49: * supervised singleton: it self-registers "srv.settings_pid" when its
50: * window opens (main_gui() in nxsettings.c) so an EXTERNAL change (made via
51: * `nxres` from a shell, or by another app) still repaints its already-open
52: * window instead of only taking effect the next time it is opened. */
53:#include <os1.h>
54:#include <string.h>
55:#include <style_names.h>
56:
57:/* The well-known registry keys init.c publishes each singleton system
58: * service's live pid under (register_service_pid).  srv.notify_pid is
59: * deliberately NOT here: it already gets the user-facing notify() popup
60: * above, and a second silent ping would just be a wasted send(). */
61:static const char *const nxres_look_ping_targets[] = {
62:    "srv.dock_pid",
63:    "srv.bar_pid",
64:    "srv.launcher_pid",
65:    /* nxsettings is not init-supervised (user-launched, not a singleton
66:     * service), so it self-registers this key on window creation instead of
67:     * init publishing it — see main_gui() in nxsettings.c.  Last-opened
68:     * instance wins if more than one is ever open at once. */
69:    "srv.settings_pid",
70:    /* Same self-registration pattern as nxsettings: nxfilem is user-launched
71:     * (not a singleton), so it publishes its own pid here on window
72:     * creation (see fm_ui_init in ui.c) so an external style/theme/bg change
73:     * repaints its already-open window instead of only the next launch. */
74:    "srv.filem_pid",
75:    /* nxshell self-registers srv.shell_pid on window creation (nxshell.c);
76:     * last-opened shell wins if several are open — others still track theme
77:     * via the per-loop nxres_theme_is_light() poll in the shell event loop. */
78:    "srv.shell_pid",
79:};
80:#define NXRES_LOOK_PING_NTARGETS                                               \
81:  (int)(sizeof(nxres_look_ping_targets) / sizeof(nxres_look_ping_targets[0]))
82:
83:/* nxres_broadcast_look - silent IPC_TYPE_NOTIFY ping to every registered
84: * system service so its already-running event loop can re-derive its
85: * palette.  Best-effort: a service that is not up yet (registry key absent)
86: * or whose pid is momentarily stale (mid-respawn) is simply skipped — the
87: * next nxres_set_*() call (or the service's own startup read) catches it. */
88:static inline void nxres_broadcast_look(void) {
89:  for (int i = 0; i < NXRES_LOOK_PING_NTARGETS; i++) {
90:    char pidbuf[16];
91:    if (OS1_registry_get(nxres_look_ping_targets[i], pidbuf, sizeof(pidbuf)) !=
92:        0)
93:      continue;
94:    int pid = atoi(pidbuf);
95:    if (pid <= 0)
96:      continue;
97:    struct ipc_message msg = {0};
98:    msg.type = IPC_TYPE_NOTIFY;
99:    msg.data2 = IPC_LOOK_PING_MAGIC;
100:    send(pid, &msg);
101:  }
102:}

104:/* nxres_get_style/theme/background - the current APPLIED look, as last
105: * mirrored into the registry by SYS_SET_STYLE (kernel-side) or a prior
106: * nxres_set_*() call.  Returns 0 and fills 'buf', or -1 if the key is
107: * absent (never set since boot — should not happen post registry_init). */
108:static inline int nxres_get_style(char *buf, size_t sz) {
109:  return OS1_registry_get("style.name", buf, sz);
110:}
111:static inline int nxres_get_theme(char *buf, size_t sz) {
112:  return OS1_registry_get("theme.color", buf, sz);
113:}
114:static inline int nxres_get_background(char *buf, size_t sz) {
115:  return OS1_registry_get("background.name", buf, sz);
116:}
117:
118:/* nxres_theme_is_light - the one boolean every app's palette switch actually
119: * needs.  Defaults to dark (0) on any read failure or unrecognised value,
120: * matching registry_init's "dark" default. */
121:static inline int nxres_theme_is_light(void) {
122:  char val[8] = {0};
123:  return nxres_get_theme(val, sizeof(val)) == 0 &&
124:         strncmp(val, "light", 6) == 0;
125:}
126:
127:/* os1_bg_colors - the 16 background anchor colours (compositor's
128: * backgrounds[].bg_color field, not the gradient stops) as parallel ARGB
129: * literals, indexed by the same id that BG_* enums use in kernel/graphics/
130: * compositor_style.h.  Same role as os1_bg_names above: the userland-
131: * facing name table that the kernel's style/theme/background mirror in the
132: * registry is keyed by.  The pattern — kernel enum + kernel struct +
133: * style_names.h os1_bg_names + this os1_bg_colors — is the SAME pattern
134: * the codebase already established for the *names*, just extended one step
135: * further so a userland app that wants to paint against the current
136: * background does not have to invent its own colour-resolution code
137: * (nxbar's "X" glyph, nxui's dock-tile bevel, any future cutout button
138: * that should read as a hole through to the desktop).  Order MUST match
139: * os1_bg_names above.  If a background is added, the chain to update is
140: * identical to the names' chain: kernel enum -> kernel backgrounds[] ->
141: * style_names.h (here) -> os1_bg_names -> os1_bg_colors. */
142:static const unsigned int os1_bg_colors[] = {
143:    0xFF121212u, /* BG_BLACK         */
144:    0xFFB33A3Au, /* BG_RED           */
145:    0xFF3E8E5Bu, /* BG_GREEN         */
146:    0xFFC9A227u, /* BG_YELLOW        */
147:    0xFF143060u, /* BG_BLUE          */
148:    0xFF8E44ADu, /* BG_MAGENTA       */
149:    0xFF2A9D8Fu, /* BG_CYAN          */
150:    0xFFD8D8DCu, /* BG_WHITE         */
151:    0xFF4A4A52u, /* BG_GRAY          */
152:    0xFFE8604Fu, /* BG_BRIGHT_RED    */
153:    0xFF52B788u, /* BG_BRIGHT_GREEN  */
154:    0xFFF2C94Cu, /* BG_BRIGHT_YELLOW */
155:    0xFF4A78C0u, /* BG_BRIGHT_BLUE   */
156:    0xFFB07CD1u, /* BG_BRIGHT_MAGENTA*/
157:    0xFF56C9C9u, /* BG_BRIGHT_CYAN   */
158:    0xFFF5F5F7u, /* BG_BRIGHT_WHITE  */
159:};
160:#define OS1_BG_COLORS_COUNT                                                    \
161:  (int)(sizeof(os1_bg_colors) / sizeof(os1_bg_colors[0]))
162:
163:/* nxres_bg_color - the ARGB colour of the currently applied background,
164: * as the userland-side lookup against the registry's "background.name"
165: * key (the same name every other app — nxsettings, nxlauncher, etc. —
166: * already reads).  Resolves the name to an id via the shared
167: * os1_bg_names table, then reads the colour out of the parallel
168: * os1_bg_colors table — the same two-step name-to-X pattern nxsettings
169: * already uses for background NAMES (NXS_BG = os1_bg_names), just
170: * extended one step further so callers can pick the actual anchor
171: * colour without re-implementing the table themselves.  Returns the dark
172: * default (0xFF1C1C24u) on any read failure, unknown name, or
173: * out-of-range id, matching the dark default every other "look" getter
174: * in this header falls back to.  Inherits the change-propagation path of
175: * the rest of the look: a successful nxres_set_background() pings every
176: * registered service via INPUT_TYPE_LOOK_CHANGED, and the app re-derives
177: * its palette on that ping. */
178:static inline unsigned int nxres_bg_color(void) {
179:  char val[32] = {0};
180:  if (nxres_get_background(val, sizeof(val)) != 0)
181:    return 0xFF1C1C24u; /* read failed */
182:  for (int i = 0; i < OS1_BG_COUNT && i < OS1_BG_COLORS_COUNT; i++) {
183:    if (strncmp(val, os1_bg_names[i], 32) == 0)
184:      return os1_bg_colors[i];
185:  }
186:  return 0xFF1C1C24u; /* unknown name */
187:}
188:
189:/* nxres_name_to_id - linear lookup in one of the os1_*_names[] tables
190: * (style_names.h).  Exact match up to and including the NUL; -1 if absent. */
191:static inline int nxres_name_to_id(const char *name, const char *const *list,
192:                                   int n) {
193:  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
194:    if (strncmp(name, list[i], 32) == 0)
195:      return i;
196:  return -1;
197:}
198:
199:/* nxres_set_style/theme/background - resolve 'name' against the shared
200: * tables, apply it via SYS_SET_STYLE (OS1_display_set_style/background),
201: * and mirror the name into the registry on success.  Returns 0 on success,
202: * -1 for an unknown name, -2 if the syscall itself failed. */
203:static inline int nxres_set_style(const char *name) {
204:  int id = nxres_name_to_id(name, os1_style_names, OS1_STYLE_COUNT);
205:  if (id < 0)
206:    return -1;
207:  if (OS1_display_set_style(id, -1) != 0)
208:    return -2;
209:  OS1_registry_set("style.name", os1_style_names[id]);
210:  notify("Style", os1_style_names[id]);
211:  nxres_broadcast_look();
212:  return 0;
213:}
214:static inline int nxres_set_theme(const char *name) {
215:  int id = nxres_name_to_id(name, os1_theme_names, OS1_THEME_COUNT);
216:  if (id < 0)
217:    return -1;
218:  if (OS1_display_set_style(-1, id) != 0)
219:    return -2;
220:  OS1_registry_set("theme.color", os1_theme_names[id]);
221:  notify("Theme", os1_theme_names[id]);
222:  nxres_broadcast_look();
223:  return 0;
224:}
225:static inline int nxres_set_background(const char *name) {
226:  int id = nxres_name_to_id(name, os1_bg_names, OS1_BG_COUNT);
227:  if (id < 0)
228:    return -1;
229:  if (OS1_display_set_background(id) != 0)
230:    return -2;
231:  OS1_registry_set("background.name", os1_bg_names[id]);
232:  notify("Background", os1_bg_names[id]);
233:  nxres_broadcast_look();
234:  return 0;
235:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/coreutils/patches/system.h.patch @@@
1:--- a/user/bin/coreutils/src/system.h
2:+++ b/user/bin/coreutils/src/system.h

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/coreutils/coreutils_os1_glue.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/lib/portability/coreutils/coreutils_os1_glue.c
3: * Implementation of Coreutils glue for NexsOS1.
4: */
5:
6:#include "coreutils_os1_glue.h"
7:#include <string.h>
8:#include <stdio.h>
9:#include <errno.h>
10:#include <sys/stat.h>
11:#include <poll.h>
12:#include <unistd.h>
13:
14:int coreutils_os1_uname(struct os1_utsname *buf) {
15:    if (!buf) {
16:        errno = EFAULT;
17:        return -1;
18:    }
19:    strncpy(buf->sysname, "NexsOS1", sizeof(buf->sysname) - 1);
20:    buf->sysname[sizeof(buf->sysname) - 1] = '\0';
21:
22:    strncpy(buf->nodename, "nexsos", sizeof(buf->nodename) - 1);
23:    buf->nodename[sizeof(buf->nodename) - 1] = '\0';
24:
25:    strncpy(buf->release, "0.0.5.4", sizeof(buf->release) - 1);
26:    buf->release[sizeof(buf->release) - 1] = '\0';
27:
28:    strncpy(buf->version, "ASTRA-V0.0.5.4", sizeof(buf->version) - 1);
29:    buf->version[sizeof(buf->version) - 1] = '\0';
30:
31:#if defined(ARCH_AMD64) || defined(__x86_64__)
32:    strncpy(buf->machine, "x86_64", sizeof(buf->machine) - 1);
33:#else
34:    strncpy(buf->machine, "aarch64", sizeof(buf->machine) - 1);
35:#endif
36:    buf->machine[sizeof(buf->machine) - 1] = '\0';
37:
38:    return 0;
39:}
40:
41:int posix2_version(void) {
42:    return 200809;
43:}
44:
45:int isapipe(int fd) {
46:    struct stat st;
47:    if (fstat(fd, &st) < 0)
48:        return 0;
49:    return S_ISFIFO(st.st_mode) ? 1 : 0;
50:}
51:
52:int iopoll(int fdin, int fdout, bool block) {
53:    (void)fdin;
54:    (void)block;
55:    if (fdout < 0)
56:        return 0;
57:
58:    struct pollfd pfd;
59:    pfd.fd = fdout;
60:    pfd.events = POLLOUT;
61:    pfd.revents = 0;
62:
63:    int r = poll(&pfd, 1, block ? -1 : 0);
64:    if (r < 0)
65:        return -3; /* IOPOLL_ERROR */
66:    if (r == 0 && !block)
67:        return 0;
68:    if (pfd.revents & (POLLHUP | POLLERR | POLLNVAL))
69:        return -2; /* IOPOLL_BROKEN_OUTPUT */
70:
71:    return 0;
72:}
73:
74:bool iopoll_input_ok(int fdin) {
75:    struct stat st;
76:    bool always_ready = fstat(fdin, &st) == 0
77:                        && (S_ISREG(st.st_mode) || S_ISBLK(st.st_mode));
78:    return !always_ready;
79:}
80:
81:bool iopoll_output_ok(int fdout) {
82:    return isapipe(fdout) > 0;
83:}
84:
85:bool write_wait(int fd, void const *buffer, size_t size) {
86:    char const *buf = buffer;
87:
88:#ifndef EWOULDBLOCK
89:#define EWOULDBLOCK EAGAIN
90:#endif
91:
92:    while (size > 0) {
93:        ssize_t written = write(fd, buf, size);
94:        if (written < 0) {
95:            if (errno == EAGAIN || errno == EWOULDBLOCK) {
96:                struct pollfd pfd;
97:                pfd.fd = fd;
98:                pfd.events = POLLOUT;
99:                pfd.revents = 0;
100:
101:                int rc = poll(&pfd, 1, -1);
102:                if (rc < 0 && errno == EINTR)
103:                    continue;
104:                if (rc < 0)
105:                    return false;
106:                continue;
107:            }
108:            return false;
109:        }
110:        if (written == 0)
111:            return false;
112:        buf += written;
113:        size -= (size_t)written;
114:    }
115:
116:    return true;
117:}
118:
119:/* mbschr and mbslen: multibyte string functions for coreutils.
120: * In NexsOS1, we treat strings as UTF-8 but operate on bytes.
121: * These stubs provide basic ASCII-compatible implementations. */
122:
123:/* mbschr: find character in multibyte string.
124: * In NexsOS1, since we're ASCII-compatible, just use strchr. */
125:char *mbschr(const char *s, int c) {
126:  if (!s)
127:    return NULL;
128:  return (char *)strchr(s, c);
129:}
130:
131:/* mbslen: length of multibyte string.
132: * In NexsOS1, treat as byte length (like strlen for ASCII). */
133:size_t mbslen(const char *s) {
134:  if (!s)
135:    return 0;
136:  return strlen(s);
137:}
138:
139:/* mbrlen: minimal byte-wise multibyte-length helper used by pathchk.c.
140: * NexsOS1 treats all bytes as single-byte characters in the bootstrap layer. */
141:size_t mbrlen(const char *s, size_t n, mbstate_t *ps) {
142:    (void)n;
143:    if (ps)
144:        memset(ps, 0, sizeof(*ps));
145:    if (!s)
146:        return 0;
147:    if (*s == '\0')
148:        return 0;
149:    return 1;
150:}
151:

27:
28:/* Type representing a Unicode character.  */
29:typedef uint32_t ucs4_t;
30:
31:/* Attribute of a function whose result depends only on the arguments
32:   (not pointers!) and which has no side effects.  */
33:#ifndef _UC_ATTRIBUTE_CONST
34:# if __GNUC__ > 2 || (__GNUC__ == 2 && __GNUC_MINOR__ >= 95) || defined __clang__
35:#  define _UC_ATTRIBUTE_CONST __attribute__ ((__const__))
36:# else
37:#  define _UC_ATTRIBUTE_CONST
38:# endif
39:#endif

41:/* Attribute of a function whose result depends only on the arguments
42:   (possibly pointers) and global memory, and which has no side effects.  */
43:#ifndef _UC_ATTRIBUTE_PURE
44:# if __GNUC__ > 2 || (__GNUC__ == 2 && __GNUC_MINOR__ >= 96) || defined __clang__
45:#  define _UC_ATTRIBUTE_PURE __attribute__ ((__pure__))
46:# else
47:#  define _UC_ATTRIBUTE_PURE
48:# endif
49:#endif
50:
51:/* Qualifier in a function declaration, that asserts that the caller must
52:   pass a pointer to a different object in the specified pointer argument
53:   than in the other pointer arguments.  */
54:#ifndef _UC_RESTRICT
55:# if defined __restrict \
56:     || 2 < __GNUC__ + (95 <= __GNUC_MINOR__) \
57:     || __clang_major__ >= 3
58:#  define _UC_RESTRICT __restrict
59:# elif 199901L <= __STDC_VERSION__ || defined restrict
60:#  define _UC_RESTRICT restrict
61:# else
62:#  define _UC_RESTRICT
63:# endif
64:#endif
65:
66:
67:#ifdef __cplusplus
68:}
69:#endif

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/d3d9/os1_d3d9_present.c @@@
1:/* OS1 D3D9-style presentation chain over the portability adapter. */
2:#include "os1_d3d9_present.h"
3:
4:#include <errno.h>
5:#include <stdlib.h>
6:#include <string.h>
7:
8:#include "../os1_video_platform.h"
9:
10:/* Backend dispatch table: device/context-facing entry points never branch on
11: * the backend themselves, they forward here.  A future ASTRA GPU-context
12: * backend adds one more table, not new personality code. */
13:struct os1_d3d9_present_ops {
14:  uint32_t backend;
15:  int (*create)(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain,
16:                const struct os1_d3d9_present_params *params);
17:  void (*destroy)(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain);
18:  int (*lock)(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain,
19:              struct os1_d3d9_locked_rect *out);
20:  int (*unlock)(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain);
21:  int (*present)(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain,
22:                 const struct os1_d3d9_dirty_rect *dirty);
23:  int (*reset)(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain, int width, int height);
24:};
25:
26:struct os1_d3d9_swapchain {
27:  const struct os1_d3d9_present_ops *ops;
28:  int window;
29:  int width;
30:  int height;
31:  int locked;
32:  uint32_t *backbuffer;
33:};
34:
35:/* ── Software backend: CPU backbuffer presented over os1_video_platform ── */
36:
37:static int sw_create(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *sc,
38:                     const struct os1_d3d9_present_params *params) {
39:  size_t count = (size_t)params->width * (size_t)params->height;
40:  sc->backbuffer = (uint32_t *)malloc(count * sizeof(uint32_t));
41:  if (!sc->backbuffer)
42:    return -ENOMEM;
43:  memset(sc->backbuffer, 0, count * sizeof(uint32_t));
44:
45:  sc->window = os1_video_window_create(params->x, params->y, params->width,
46:                                       params->height, params->title);
47:  if (sc->window < 0) {
48:    free(sc->backbuffer);
49:    sc->backbuffer = NULL;
50:    return sc->window;
51:  }
52:  sc->width = params->width;
53:  sc->height = params->height;
54:  return 0;
55:}
56:
57:static void sw_destroy(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *sc) {
58:  if (sc->window >= 0)
59:    os1_video_window_destroy(sc->window);
60:  free(sc->backbuffer);
61:  sc->backbuffer = NULL;
62:}
63:
64:static int sw_lock(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *sc,
65:                   struct os1_d3d9_locked_rect *out) {
66:  out->bits = sc->backbuffer;
67:  out->pitch = (size_t)sc->width * sizeof(uint32_t);
68:  return 0;
69:}
70:
71:static int sw_unlock(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *sc) {
72:  (void)sc;
73:  return 0;
74:}
75:
76:static int sw_present(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *sc,
77:                      const struct os1_d3d9_dirty_rect *dirty) {
78:  int x = 0, y = 0, w = sc->width, h = sc->height;
79:  if (dirty) {
80:    x = dirty->x;
81:    y = dirty->y;
82:    w = dirty->width;
83:    h = dirty->height;
84:    /* Clamp to the backbuffer (D3D9 rejects out-of-range source rects). */
85:    if (x < 0 || y < 0 || w <= 0 || h <= 0 || x + w > sc->width ||
86:        y + h > sc->height)
87:      return -EINVAL;
88:  }
89:  const uint32_t *first_row = sc->backbuffer + (size_t)y * sc->width + x;
90:  size_t remaining =
91:      (size_t)sc->width * sc->height - ((size_t)y * sc->width + x);
92:  int rc = os1_video_present_argb8888_strided(sc->window, x, y, w, h,
93:                                              first_row, (size_t)sc->width,
94:                                              remaining);
95:  if (rc < 0)
96:    return rc;
97:  os1_video_render();
98:  return 0;
99:}
100:
101:static int sw_reset(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *sc, int width, int height) {
102:  size_t count = (size_t)width * (size_t)height;
103:  uint32_t *fresh = (uint32_t *)malloc(count * sizeof(uint32_t));
104:  if (!fresh)
105:    return -ENOMEM;
106:  memset(fresh, 0, count * sizeof(uint32_t));
107:
108:  int rc = os1_video_window_resize(sc->window, width, height);
109:  if (rc < 0) {
110:    free(fresh);
111:    return rc;
112:  }
113:  free(sc->backbuffer);
114:  sc->backbuffer = fresh;
115:  sc->width = width;
116:  sc->height = height;
117:  return 0;
118:}
119:
120:static const struct os1_d3d9_present_ops software_present_ops = {
121:    .backend = OS1_VIDEO_BACKEND_SOFTWARE,
122:    .create = sw_create,
123:    .destroy = sw_destroy,
124:    .lock = sw_lock,
125:    .unlock = sw_unlock,
126:    .present = sw_present,
127:    .reset = sw_reset,
128:};
129:
130:/* ── Backend-independent dispatch ──────────────────────────────────────── */
131:
132:static const struct os1_d3d9_present_ops *select_present_ops(void) {
133:  struct os1_video_info info;
134:  if (os1_video_query(&info) != 0)
135:    return NULL;
136:  if (info.backend == OS1_VIDEO_BACKEND_SOFTWARE &&
137:      (info.capabilities & OS1_VIDEO_CAP_ARGB8888))
138:    return &software_present_ops;
139:  /* OS1_VIDEO_BACKEND_GPU_CONTEXT is reserved for the ASTRA GPU object. */
140:  return NULL;
141:}
142:
143:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_create(const struct os1_d3d9_present_params *params,
144:                              struct os1_d3d9_swapchain **out) {
145:  if (!params || !out || params->width <= 0 || params->height <= 0 ||
146:      !params->title)
147:    return -EINVAL;
148:
149:  const struct os1_d3d9_present_ops *ops = select_present_ops();
150:  if (!ops)
151:    return -ENOSYS;
152:
153:  struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *sc =
154:      (struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *)malloc(sizeof(*sc));
155:  if (!sc)
156:    return -ENOMEM;
157:  memset(sc, 0, sizeof(*sc));
158:  sc->ops = ops;
159:  sc->window = -1;
160:
161:  int rc = ops->create(sc, params);
162:  if (rc < 0) {
163:    free(sc);
164:    return rc;
165:  }
166:  *out = sc;
167:  return 0;
168:}
169:
170:void os1_d3d9_swapchain_destroy(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain) {
171:  if (!swapchain)
172:    return;
173:  swapchain->ops->destroy(swapchain);
174:  free(swapchain);
175:}
176:
177:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_lock(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain,
178:                            struct os1_d3d9_locked_rect *out) {
179:  if (!swapchain || !out)
180:    return -EINVAL;
181:  if (swapchain->locked)
182:    return -EBUSY;
183:  int rc = swapchain->ops->lock(swapchain, out);
184:  if (rc == 0)
185:    swapchain->locked = 1;
186:  return rc;
187:}
188:
189:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_unlock(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain) {
190:  if (!swapchain)
191:    return -EINVAL;
192:  if (!swapchain->locked)
193:    return -EINVAL;
194:  int rc = swapchain->ops->unlock(swapchain);
195:  if (rc == 0)
196:    swapchain->locked = 0;
197:  return rc;
198:}
199:
200:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_present(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain,
201:                               const struct os1_d3d9_dirty_rect *dirty) {
202:  if (!swapchain)
203:    return -EINVAL;
204:  if (swapchain->locked)
205:    return -EINVAL; /* D3D9: presenting a locked surface is illegal */
206:  return swapchain->ops->present(swapchain, dirty);
207:}
208:
209:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_reset(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain, int width,
210:                             int height) {
211:  if (!swapchain || width <= 0 || height <= 0)
212:    return -EINVAL;
213:  if (swapchain->locked)
214:    return -EBUSY;
215:  return swapchain->ops->reset(swapchain, width, height);
216:}
217:
218:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_backend(const struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain) {
219:  if (!swapchain)
220:    return -EINVAL;
221:  return (int)swapchain->ops->backend;
222:}
223:

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/d3d9/os1_d3d9_present.h @@@
1:/*
2: * OS1 D3D9-style presentation chain.
3: *
4: * The presentation seam for the Direct3D 9 personality: a swapchain with a
5: * CPU backbuffer, D3D9 Lock/Unlock/Present/Reset semantics, mapped onto the
6: * os1_video_platform portability header.  Device/context dispatch is
7: * backend-independent: every entry point forwards through an ops table chosen
8: * at creation from the platform's advertised backend, so the software
9: * presenter can later be swapped for the ASTRA GPU-context object without
10: * touching D3D9-personality callers.
11: */
12:#ifndef OS1_D3D9_PRESENT_H
13:#define OS1_D3D9_PRESENT_H
14:
15:#include <stddef.h>
16:#include <stdint.h>
17:
18:struct os1_d3d9_present_params {
19:  int x;
20:  int y;
21:  int width;  /* backbuffer width in pixels  */
22:  int height; /* backbuffer height in pixels */
23:  const char *title;
24:};
25:
26:/* D3DLOCKED_RECT analogue: pitch is in BYTES, pixels are ARGB8888. */
27:struct os1_d3d9_locked_rect {
28:  uint32_t *bits;
29:  size_t pitch;
30:};
31:
32:/* Optional Present() dirty rect (D3D9 pSourceRect analogue). */
33:struct os1_d3d9_dirty_rect {
34:  int x;
35:  int y;
36:  int width;
37:  int height;
38:};
39:
40:struct os1_d3d9_swapchain; /* opaque; owns window + backbuffer */
41:
42:/* Create a swapchain on the platform's active backend.  Returns 0 and a
43: * swapchain, -ENOSYS when only an unsupported backend is advertised, or a
44: * negative OS1 error. */
45:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_create(const struct os1_d3d9_present_params *params,
46:                              struct os1_d3d9_swapchain **out);
47:void os1_d3d9_swapchain_destroy(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain);
48:
49:/* Lock grants CPU access to the backbuffer; Present while locked fails with
50: * -EINVAL (D3D9 forbids presenting a locked surface). */
51:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_lock(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain,
52:                            struct os1_d3d9_locked_rect *out);
53:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_unlock(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain);
54:
55:/* Present the backbuffer (or just `dirty` when non-NULL) and notify the
56: * compositor. */
57:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_present(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain,
58:                               const struct os1_d3d9_dirty_rect *dirty);
59:
60:/* D3D9 Reset analogue: resize window + backbuffer.  Fails while locked. */
61:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_reset(struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain, int width,
62:                             int height);
63:
64:/* The enum os1_video_backend this swapchain runs on. */
65:int os1_d3d9_swapchain_backend(const struct os1_d3d9_swapchain *swapchain);
66:
67:#endif /* OS1_D3D9_PRESENT_H */
68:

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/d3d9/README.md @@@
1:# D3D9 presentation backend
2:
3:`os1_d3d9_present.{h,c}` is the presentation seam for the Direct3D 9
4:personality: a swapchain with a CPU ARGB8888 backbuffer and D3D9
5:Lock/Unlock/Present/Reset semantics over `os1_video_platform.h`. Dispatch is
6:backend-independent (an ops table selected from the platform's advertised
7:backend), so the software presenter can later be swapped for the ASTRA
8:GPU-context object without touching personality callers.
9:
10:This is deliberately NOT a Direct3D API implementation: device/context/shader
11:dispatch belongs to the D3D9 compatibility layer sourced from the Wine
12:submodule on its `nexsos-port-d3d9` branch. Only the OS-facing presentation
13:glue lives here, per the non-negotiable constraint that upstream trees are
14:never patched for NexsOS integration.
15:
16:`demo3d` is the reference client: it renders its cube into the locked
17:backbuffer and presents through the swapchain, exercising the chain end to
18:end on both architectures.
19:

1:/* Compatibility generation for GNU libc scratch buffer internals.
2:   NexsOS1 uses the upstream Gnulib sources directly and expects the generated
3:   header that glibc-internal/scratch_buffer would normally create.  This file
4:   provides the minimal API surface required by canonicalize.c and similar
5:   helpers. */
6:
7:#ifndef _GL_SCRATCH_BUFFER_GL_H
8:#define _GL_SCRATCH_BUFFER_GL_H
9:
10:#include <stdbool.h>
11:#include <stddef.h>
12:#include <stdlib.h>
13:
14:#ifndef _GL_LIKELY
15:# define _GL_LIKELY(cond) __builtin_expect ((cond), 1)
16:# define _GL_UNLIKELY(cond) __builtin_expect ((cond), 0)
17:#endif
18:
19:#ifndef __GLIBC_LIKELY
20:# define __GLIBC_LIKELY(cond) _GL_LIKELY (cond)
21:# define __GLIBC_UNLIKELY(cond) _GL_UNLIKELY (cond)
22:#endif
23:
24:#define __libc_scratch_buffer_grow _gl_scratch_buffer_grow
25:#define __libc_scratch_buffer_grow_preserve _gl_scratch_buffer_grow_preserve
26:#define __libc_scratch_buffer_set_array_size _gl_scratch_buffer_set_array_size
27:
28:struct scratch_buffer {
29:  void *data;
30:  size_t length;
31:  union { long double __align; char __c[1024]; } __space;
32:};
33:
34:static inline void
35:scratch_buffer_init (struct scratch_buffer *buffer)
36:{
37:  buffer->data = buffer->__space.__c;
38:  buffer->length = sizeof (buffer->__space);
39:}
40:
41:static inline void
42:scratch_buffer_free (struct scratch_buffer *buffer)
43:{
44:  if (buffer->data != buffer->__space.__c)
45:    free (buffer->data);
46:}
47:
48:bool __libc_scratch_buffer_grow (struct scratch_buffer *buffer);
49:static __inline__ bool
50:scratch_buffer_grow (struct scratch_buffer *buffer)
51:{
52:  return __GLIBC_LIKELY (__libc_scratch_buffer_grow (buffer));
53:}
54:
55:bool __libc_scratch_buffer_grow_preserve (struct scratch_buffer *buffer);
56:static __inline__ bool
57:scratch_buffer_grow_preserve (struct scratch_buffer *buffer)
58:{
59:  return __GLIBC_LIKELY (__libc_scratch_buffer_grow_preserve (buffer));
60:}
61:
62:bool __libc_scratch_buffer_set_array_size (struct scratch_buffer *buffer,
63:                                           size_t nelem, size_t size);
64:static __inline__ bool
65:scratch_buffer_set_array_size (struct scratch_buffer *buffer,
66:                              size_t nelem, size_t size)
67:{
68:  return __GLIBC_LIKELY (__libc_scratch_buffer_set_array_size (buffer, nelem, size));
69:}

71:#endif

1:/*
2: * user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/fts_.h
3: * Shim for Gnulib's fts_.h, generated from fts.in.h
4: * NexsOS1 doesn't have a real fts implementation, so this provides minimal stubs.
5: */
6:
7:#ifndef FTS_H
8:#define FTS_H
9:
10:#include <sys/types.h>
11:#include <dirent.h>
12:
13:/* FTS entry types */
14:#define FTS_D     1    /* preorder directory */
15:#define FTS_DC    2    /* directory that causes cycles */
16:#define FTS_DEFAULT 3  /* none of the above */
17:#define FTS_DNR   4    /* unreadable directory */
18:#define FTS_DOT   5    /* dot or dot-dot */
19:#define FTS_DP    6    /* postorder directory */
20:#define FTS_ERR   7    /* error; errno is set */
21:#define FTS_F     8    /* regular file */
22:#define FTS_INIT  9    /* initialized only */
23:#define FTS_NS   10    /* stat(2) failed */
24:#define FTS_NSOK 11    /* no stat(2) requested */
25:#define FTS_SL   12    /* symbolic link */
26:#define FTS_SLNONE 13  /* symbolic link with no file */
27:#define FTS_W    14    /* whiteout object */
28:
29:/* FTS options */
30:#define FTS_COMFOLLOW  0x0001
31:#define FTS_LOGICAL    0x0002
32:#define FTS_NOCHDIR    0x0004
33:#define FTS_NOSTAT     0x0008
34:#define FTS_PHYSICAL   0x0010
35:#define FTS_SEEDOT     0x0020

72:/*
73: * NexsOS1 getcwd() returns int; POSIX/gnulib expects char *.
74: * Use the underlying _sys_getcwd and provide a POSIX shim.
75: */
76:extern int _sys_getcwd(char *buf, size_t size);
77:
78:static inline char *getcwd(char *buf, size_t size) {
79:  char *ret = buf;
80:  if (!buf) {
81:    size = size ? size : 4096;
82:    ret = (char *)malloc(size);
83:    if (!ret) return (char *)0;
84:  }
85:  if (_sys_getcwd(ret, size) != 0) {
86:    if (!buf) free(ret);
87:    return (char *)0;
88:  }
89:  return ret;
90:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/gnulib_os1_glue.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/gnulib_os1_glue.c
3: * Real implementation connecting Gnulib abstractions to NexsOS1 syscalls and VFS.
4: */
5:
6:#define _GNULIB_OS1_GLUE_IMPL
7:#include "gnulib_os1_glue.h"
8:#include <stdio.h>
9:#include <stdlib.h>
10:#include <string.h>
11:#include <unistd.h>
12:#include <fcntl.h>
13:#include <sys/stat.h>
14:
15:/* La variabile program_name viene impostata da gnulib (progname.c)
16:   tramite set_program_name() all'avvio di ogni programma GNU. */
17:extern char *program_name;
18:
19:static char g_progname_buf[64] = "nexsos_app";
20:
21:int gnulib_os1_getpagesize(void) {
22:    return NEXSOS_PAGE_SIZE;
23:}
24:
25:int gnulib_os1_getdtablesize(void) {
26:    return NEXSOS_MAX_FD;
27:}
28:
29:const char *gnulib_os1_getprogname(void) {
30:    /* Se il buffer contiene ancora il default, prova a usare program_name
31:       che gnulib ha impostato (es. "mkdir", "cat", "ls"). */
32:    if (strcmp(g_progname_buf, "nexsos_app") == 0) {
33:        if (program_name && program_name[0] != '\0')
34:            return program_name;
35:    }
36:    return g_progname_buf;
37:}
38:
39:void gnulib_os1_setprogname(const char *name) {
40:    if (!name || !*name)
41:        return;
42:    const char *p = strrchr(name, '/');
43:    if (p)
44:        name = p + 1;
45:    strncpy(g_progname_buf, name, sizeof(g_progname_buf) - 1);
46:    g_progname_buf[sizeof(g_progname_buf) - 1] = '\0';
47:}

49:ssize_t gnulib_os1_safe_read(int fd, void *buf, size_t count) {
50:    if (fd < 0 || !buf) {
51:        errno = EBADF;
52:        return -1;
53:    }
54:    long ret = read(fd, (char *)buf, (unsigned long)count);
55:    if (ret < 0) {
56:        errno = (int)(-ret);
57:        return -1;
58:    }
59:    return (ssize_t)ret;
60:}
61:
62:ssize_t gnulib_os1_safe_write(int fd, const void *buf, size_t count) {
63:    if (fd < 0 || !buf) {
64:        errno = EBADF;
65:        return -1;
66:    }
67:    long ret = write(fd, (const char *)buf, count);
68:    if (ret < 0) {
69:        errno = (int)(-ret);
70:        return -1;
71:    }
72:    return (ssize_t)ret;
73:}

75:void *gnulib_os1_rawmemchr(const void *s, int c) {
76:    const unsigned char *p = (const unsigned char *)s;
77:    unsigned char uc = (unsigned char)c;
78:    while (*p != uc) {
79:        p++;
80:    }
81:    return (void *)p;
82:}
83:
84:void *gnulib_os1_memrchr(const void *s, int c, size_t n) {
85:    if (n == 0 || !s)
86:        return NULL;
87:    const unsigned char *p = (const unsigned char *)s + n;
88:    unsigned char uc = (unsigned char)c;
89:    while (n > 0) {
90:        p--;
91:        if (*p == uc)
92:            return (void *)p;
93:        n--;
94:    }
95:    return NULL;
96:}

105:void verror(int status, int errnum, const char *format, va_list args) {
106:    fflush(stdout);
107:    if (error_print_progname) {
108:        error_print_progname();
109:    } else {
110:        const char *pname = getprogname();
111:        if (pname && *pname) {
112:            fprintf(stderr, "%s: ", pname);
113:        }
114:    }
115:    vfprintf(stderr, format, args);
116:    if (errnum) {
117:        fprintf(stderr, ": %s", strerror(errnum));
118:    }
119:    fprintf(stderr, "\n");
120:    fflush(stderr);
121:    error_message_count++;
122:    if (status) {
123:        exit(status);
124:    }
125:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/hard_locale_compat.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/hard_locale_compat.c
3: * NexsOS1 locale compatibility layer for Gnulib hard_locale() function.
4: *
5: * Coreutils (via gnulib) calls hard_locale(category) to check if the
6: * current locale for that category (LC_TIME, LC_COLLATE, etc.) is non-C.
7: * NexsOS1 runs ONLY in the C/POSIX locale with no locale switching,
8: * so we provide minimal stubs here that declare NexsOS1 is always in C locale.
9: *
10: * This avoids compiling gnulib's complex setlocale_null.c, which has
11: * threading infrastructure and platform-specific logic we don't need.
12: */
13:
14:#include <stdbool.h>
15:#include <stddef.h>
16:#include <string.h>
17:
18:/* SETLOCALE_NULL_MAX: max size for locale category name buffer.
19: * Standard gnulib definition. */
20:#define SETLOCALE_NULL_MAX (256+1)
21:
22:/* setlocale_null_r_unlocked: get the current locale category name without locking.
23: * In NexsOS1, always returns "C" for any category.
24: * Returns 0 on success, EINVAL if category is invalid. */
25:int setlocale_null_r_unlocked(int category, char *buf, size_t bufsize) {
26:  /* Validate category */
27:  if (category < 0) {
28:    return 22; /* EINVAL */
29:  }
30:
31:  /* NexsOS1 is always in C locale */
32:  const char *locale_name = "C";
33:  size_t needed = strlen(locale_name) + 1;
34:
35:  if (bufsize < needed) {
36:    return 34; /* ERANGE */
37:  }
38:
39:  if (buf) {
40:    strncpy(buf, locale_name, bufsize - 1);
41:    buf[bufsize - 1] = '\0';
42:  }
43:  return 0; /* Success */
44:}
45:
46:/* setlocale_null_r: thread-safe version (in NexsOS1, no threading needed).
47: * Returns error code like setlocale_null_r_unlocked. */
48:int setlocale_null_r(int category, char *buf, size_t bufsize) {
49:  /* No threading in freestanding NexsOS1, so just call the unlocked version */
50:  return setlocale_null_r_unlocked(category, buf, bufsize);
51:}
52:
53:/* hard_locale: determine if the current locale category is "hard" (non-C).
54: * A "hard" locale has special behavior (collation, formatting, etc.).
55: * NexsOS1 always runs in C/POSIX locale, so this always returns false. */
56:bool hard_locale(int category) {
57:  (void)category; /* Unused in NexsOS1 */
58:  return false;
59:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/mbs_compat.c @@@
1:#include <stddef.h>
2:#include <string.h>
3:
4:/* Minimal multibyte-string compatibility shims needed by Coreutils on NexsOS1.
5: * These are intentionally small and conservative; they satisfy the GNU-like
6: * symbols referenced by expr without modifying the upstream second-repository
7: * sources.
8: */
9:
10:size_t mbslen(const char *string)
11:{
12:  size_t count = 0;
13:  if (!string)
14:    return 0;
15:
16:  while (*string) {
17:    unsigned char ch = (unsigned char)*string;
18:    if ((ch & 0x80) == 0) {
19:      string++;
20:      count++;
21:      continue;
22:    }
23:
24:    /* Count UTF-8 codepoints conservatively: skip one full codepoint. */
25:    if ((ch & 0xE0) == 0xC0) {
26:      string += 2;
27:    } else if ((ch & 0xF0) == 0xE0) {
28:      string += 3;
29:    } else if ((ch & 0xF8) == 0xF0) {
30:      string += 4;
31:    } else {
32:      string++;
33:    }
34:    count++;
35:  }
36:
37:  return count;
38:}
39:
40:char *mbschr(const char *string, int c)
41:{
42:  if (!string)
43:    return NULL;
44:
45:  while (*string) {
46:    unsigned char ch = (unsigned char)*string;
47:    if ((ch & 0x80) == 0) {
48:      if ((unsigned char)c == ch)
49:        return (char *)string;
50:      string++;
51:      continue;
52:    }
53:
54:    /* ASCII-compatible single-byte search only; UTF-8 codepoints are treated
55:     * as opaque for the current NexsOS1 bootstrap layer. */
56:    if ((ch & 0xE0) == 0xC0) {
57:      string += 2;
58:    } else if ((ch & 0xF0) == 0xE0) {
59:      string += 3;
60:    } else if ((ch & 0xF8) == 0xF0) {
61:      string += 4;
62:    } else {
63:      string++;
64:    }
65:  }
66:
67:  return NULL;
68:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/obstack.h @@@
1:/* obstack.h - object stack macros
2:   Copyright (C) 1988-2026 Free Software Foundation, Inc.
3:   This file is part of the GNU C Library.
4:
5:   The GNU C Library is free software; you can redistribute it and/or
6:   modify it under the terms of the GNU Lesser General Public
7:   License as published by the Free Software Foundation; either
8:   version 2.1 of the License, or (at your option) any later version.
9:
10:   The GNU C Library is distributed in the hope that it will be useful,
11:   but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
12:   MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.  See the GNU
13:   Lesser General Public License for more details.
14:
15:   You should have received a copy of the GNU Lesser General Public
16:   License along with the GNU C Library; if not, see
17:   <https://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.  */
18:
19:/* Summary:
20:
21:   All the apparent functions defined here are macros. The idea
22:   is that you would use these pre-tested macros to solve a
23:   very specific set of problems, and they would run fast.
24:   Caution: no side-effects in arguments please!! They may be
25:   evaluated MANY times!!
26:
27:   These macros operate a stack of objects.  Each object starts life
28:   small, and may grow to maturity.  (Consider building a word syllable
29:   by syllable.)  An object can move while it is growing.  Once it has
30:   been "finished" it never changes address again.  So the "top of the
31:   stack" is typically an immature growing object, while the rest of the
32:   stack is of mature, fixed size and fixed address objects.
33:
34:   These routines grab large chunks of memory, using a function you
35:   supply, called 'obstack_chunk_alloc'.  On occasion, they free chunks,
36:   by calling 'obstack_chunk_free'.  You must define them and declare
37:   them before using any obstack macros.
38:
39:   Each independent stack is represented by a 'struct obstack'.
40:   Each of the obstack macros expects a pointer to such a structure
41:   as the first argument.
42:
43:   One motivation for this package is the problem of growing char strings
44:   in symbol tables.  Unless you are "fascist pig with a read-only mind"
45:   --Gosper's immortal quote from HAKMEM item 154, out of context--you
46:   would not like to put any arbitrary upper limit on the length of your
47:   symbols.
48:
49:   In practice this often means you will build many short symbols and a
50:   few long symbols.  At the time you are reading a symbol you don't know
51:   how long it is.  One traditional method is to read a symbol into a
52:   buffer, realloc()ating the buffer every time you try to read a symbol
53:   that is longer than the buffer.  This is beaut, but you still will
54:   want to copy the symbol from the buffer to a more permanent
55:   symbol-table entry say about half the time.
56:
57:   With obstacks, you can work differently.  Use one obstack for all symbol
58:   names.  As you read a symbol, grow the name in the obstack gradually.
59:   When the name is complete, finalize it.  Then, if the symbol exists already,
60:   free the newly read name.
61:
62:   The way we do this is to take a large chunk, allocating memory from
63:   low addresses.  When you want to build a symbol in the chunk you just
64:   add chars above the current "high water mark" in the chunk.  When you
65:   have finished adding chars, because you got to the end of the symbol,
66:   you know how long the chars are, and you can create a new object.
67:   Mostly the chars will not burst over the highest address of the chunk,
68:   because you would typically expect a chunk to be (say) 100 times as
69:   long as an average object.
70:
71:   In case that isn't clear, when we have enough chars to make up
72:   the object, THEY ARE ALREADY CONTIGUOUS IN THE CHUNK (guaranteed)
73:   so we just point to it where it lies.  No moving of chars is
74:   needed and this is the second win: potentially long strings need
75:   never be explicitly shuffled. Once an object is formed, it does not
76:   change its address during its lifetime.
77:
78:   When the chars burst over a chunk boundary, we allocate a larger
79:   chunk, and then copy the partly formed object from the end of the old
80:   chunk to the beginning of the new larger chunk.  We then carry on
81:   accreting characters to the end of the object as we normally would.
82:
83:   A special macro is provided to add a single char at a time to a
84:   growing object.  This allows the use of register variables, which
85:   break the ordinary 'growth' macro.
86:
87:   Summary:
88:        We allocate large chunks.
89:        We carve out one object at a time from the current chunk.
90:        Once carved, an object never moves.
91:        We are free to append data of any size to the currently
92:          growing object.
93:        Exactly one object is growing in an obstack at any one time.
94:        You can run one obstack per control block.
95:        You may have as many control blocks as you dare.
96:        Because of the way we do it, you can "unwind" an obstack
97:          back to a previous state. (You may remove objects much
98:          as you would with a stack.)
99: */
100:
101:/* Documentation (part of the GNU libc manual):
102:   <https://www.gnu.org/software/libc/manual/html_node/Obstacks.html>  */
103:
104:
105:/* Don't do the contents of this file more than once.  */
106:#ifndef _OBSTACK_H
107:#define _OBSTACK_H 1
108:
109:#if defined __GL_GNULIB_HEADER
110:/* This file uses _GL_ATTRIBUTE_PURE, FLEXIBLE_ARRAY_MEMBER.  */
111:# if !_GL_CONFIG_H_INCLUDED
112:  #error "Please include config.h first."
113:# endif
114:#endif
115:
116:/* For backward compatibility with older glibc,
117:   define the otherwise-unused macro PTR_INT_TYPE.  If __PTRDIFF_TYPE__ is
118:   defined, as with GNU C, use that; that way we don't pollute the
119:   namespace with <stddef.h>'s symbols.  Otherwise, include <stddef.h>
120:   and use ptrdiff_t.  */
121:#ifdef __PTRDIFF_TYPE__
122:# define PTR_INT_TYPE __PTRDIFF_TYPE__
123:#else
124:# include <stddef.h>
125:# define PTR_INT_TYPE ptrdiff_t
126:#endif
127:
128:/* An integer type wide enough to hold a pointer value,
129:   if such a type is available.  */
130:#ifdef __UINTPTR_TYPE__
131:# define _OBSTACK_UINTPTR_TYPE __UINTPTR_TYPE__
132:#elif defined __STDC_VERSION__ && 199901L <= __STDC_VERSION__
133:# include <stdint.h>
134:# ifdef UINTPTR_MAX
135:#  define _OBSTACK_UINTPTR_TYPE uintptr_t
136:# endif
137:#endif
138:
139:/* A type suitable for comparing pointers regardless of whether they
140:   point into the same object, e.g., (_OBSTACK_CPTR) p < (_OBSTACK_CPTR) q.
141:   If possible, use uintptr_t to avoid undefined behavior and pacify
142:   sanitizers.  Otherwise, use a pointer directly and hope for the best.  */
143:#ifdef _OBSTACK_UINTPTR_TYPE
144:typedef _OBSTACK_UINTPTR_TYPE _OBSTACK_CPTR;
145:#else
146:typedef char *_OBSTACK_CPTR;
147:#endif
148:
149:/* These macros highlight the places where this implementation
150:   is different from the one in GNU libc.  */
151:#if defined __GL_GNULIB_HEADER
152:/* In Gnulib, we use sane types, especially for 64-bit hosts.  */
153:# define _OBSTACK_INDEX_T size_t
154:# define _OBSTACK_SIZE_T size_t
155:# define _OBSTACK_CHUNK_SIZE_T size_t
156:# define _OBSTACK_CAST(type, expr) (expr)
157:# define _OBSTACK_CHUNK_CONTENTS_SIZE FLEXIBLE_ARRAY_MEMBER
158:#else
159:/* For backward compatibility, glibc limits object sizes to int range.  */
160:# define _OBSTACK_INDEX_T int
161:# define _OBSTACK_SIZE_T unsigned int
162:# define _OBSTACK_CHUNK_SIZE_T long int
163:# define _OBSTACK_CAST(type, expr) ((type) (expr))
164:# define _OBSTACK_CHUNK_CONTENTS_SIZE 4
165:#endif
166:
167:/* If B is the base of an object addressed by P, return the result of
168:   aligning P to the next multiple of A + 1.  B and P must be of type
169:   char *.  A + 1 must be a power of 2.  With no uintptr_t, play it
170:   safe and compute the alignment relative to B.  Otherwise, use the
171:   faster strategy of computing the alignment through uintptr_t.  */
172:#ifndef _OBSTACK_UINTPTR_TYPE
173:# define __PTR_ALIGN(B, P, A) \
174:   ((B) + (((P) - (B) + (A)) & ~(A)))
175:#else
176:# define __PTR_ALIGN(B, P, A) \
177:   ((P) + ((- (_OBSTACK_UINTPTR_TYPE) (P)) & (A)))
178:#endif
179:
180:/* For memcpy, size_t.  */
181:#include <string.h>
182:
183:#ifndef __attribute_pure__
184:# define __attribute_pure__ _GL_ATTRIBUTE_PURE
185:#endif
186:
187:/* Not the same as _Noreturn, since it also works with function pointers.  */
188:#ifndef __attribute_noreturn__
189:# if ((defined __GNUC__ && 2 < __GNUC__ + (8 <= __GNUC_MINOR__)) \
190:      || defined __clang__ \
191:      || (defined __SUNPRO_C && 0x5110 <= __SUNPRO_C))
192:#  define __attribute_noreturn__ __attribute__ ((__noreturn__))
193:# else
194:#  define __attribute_noreturn__
195:# endif
196:#endif

198:#ifdef __cplusplus
199:extern "C" {
200:#endif
201:
202:struct _obstack_chunk           /* Lives at front of each chunk. */
203:{
204:  char *limit;                  /* 1 past end of this chunk */
205:  struct _obstack_chunk *prev;  /* address of prior chunk or NULL */
206:  char contents[_OBSTACK_CHUNK_CONTENTS_SIZE]; /* objects begin here */
207:};
208:
209:struct obstack          /* control current object in current chunk */
210:{
211:  _OBSTACK_CHUNK_SIZE_T chunk_size;  /* preferred size to allocate chunks in */
212:  struct _obstack_chunk *chunk; /* address of current struct obstack_chunk */
213:  char *object_base;            /* address of object we are building */
214:  char *next_free;              /* where to add next char to current object */
215:  char *chunk_limit;            /* address of char after current chunk */
216:  union
217:  {
218:    _OBSTACK_SIZE_T tempint;
219:    void *tempptr;
220:  } temp;                       /* Temporary for some macros.  */
221:  _OBSTACK_INDEX_T alignment_mask;  /* Mask of alignment for each object. */
222:
223:  /* These prototypes vary based on 'use_extra_arg'.  */
224:  union
225:  {
226:    void *(*plain) (_OBSTACK_CHUNK_SIZE_T);
227:    void *(*extra) (void *, _OBSTACK_CHUNK_SIZE_T);
228:  } chunkfun;
229:  union
230:  {
231:    void (*plain) (void *);
232:    void (*extra) (void *, void *);
233:  } freefun;
234:
235:  void *extra_arg;              /* first arg for chunk alloc/dealloc funcs */
236:  unsigned use_extra_arg : 1;     /* chunk alloc/dealloc funcs take extra arg */
237:  unsigned maybe_empty_object : 1; /* There is a possibility that the current
238:                                      chunk contains a zero-length object.  This
239:                                      prevents freeing the chunk if we allocate
240:                                      a bigger chunk to replace it. */
241:  unsigned alloc_failed : 1;      /* No longer used, as we now call the failed
242:                                     handler on error, but retained for binary
243:                                     compatibility.  */
244:};

246:/* Declare the external functions we use; they are in obstack.c.  */
247:
248:/* Symbol mapping for gnulib.  */
249:#if defined __GL_GNULIB_HEADER && defined __GL_REPLACE_OBSTACK__

259:   but gnulib overrides this by defining '__obstack_free' above.  */
260:#ifndef __obstack_free

272:                             void (*) (void *, void *), void *);

274:  __attribute_pure__;

278:/* Error handler called when 'obstack_chunk_alloc' failed to allocate
279:   more memory.  This can be set to a user defined function which
280:   should either abort gracefully or use longjump - but shouldn't
281:   return.  The default action is to print a message and abort.  */
282:extern __attribute_noreturn__ void (*obstack_alloc_failed_handler) (void);
283:

285:extern int obstack_exit_failure;

287:/* Pointer to beginning of object being allocated or to be allocated next.
288:   Note that this might not be the final address of the object
289:   because a new chunk might be needed to hold the final size.  */

344:#if (defined __GNUC__ || defined __clang__ \

350:/* For GNU C, if not -traditional,
351:   we can define these macros to compute all args only once
352:   without using a global variable.
353:   Also, we can avoid using the 'temp' slot, to make faster code.  */
