355:# define obstack_object_size(OBSTACK) \
356:  __extension__ \
357:    ({ struct obstack const *__o = (OBSTACK); \
358:       (_OBSTACK_SIZE_T) (__o->next_free - __o->object_base); })
359:
360:/* The local variable is named __o1 to avoid a shadowed variable
361:   warning when invoked from other obstack macros.  */
362:# define obstack_room(OBSTACK) \
363:  __extension__ \
364:    ({ struct obstack const *__o1 = (OBSTACK); \
365:       (_OBSTACK_SIZE_T) (__o1->chunk_limit - __o1->next_free); })
366:
367:# define obstack_make_room(OBSTACK, length) \
368:  __extension__ \
369:    ({ struct obstack *__o = (OBSTACK); \
370:       _OBSTACK_INDEX_T __len = length; \
371:       if (obstack_room (__o) < __len) \
372:         _obstack_newchunk (__o, __len); \
373:       (void) 0; })
374:
375:# define obstack_empty_p(OBSTACK) \
376:  __extension__ \
377:    ({ struct obstack const *__o = (OBSTACK); \
378:       (__o->chunk->prev == 0 \
379:        && __o->next_free == __PTR_ALIGN ((char *) __o->chunk, \
380:                                          __o->chunk->contents, \
381:                                          __o->alignment_mask)); })
382:
383:# define obstack_grow(OBSTACK, where, length) \
384:  __extension__ \
385:    ({ struct obstack *__o = (OBSTACK); \
386:       _OBSTACK_INDEX_T __len = length; \
387:       if (obstack_room (__o) < __len) \
388:         _obstack_newchunk (__o, __len); \
389:       memcpy (__o->next_free, where, __len); \
390:       __o->next_free += __len; \
391:       (void) 0; })
392:
393:# define obstack_grow0(OBSTACK, where, length) \
394:  __extension__ \
395:    ({ struct obstack *__o = (OBSTACK); \
396:       _OBSTACK_INDEX_T __len = length; \
397:       if (obstack_room (__o) <= __len) \
398:         _obstack_newchunk (__o, __len + 1); \
399:       memcpy (__o->next_free, where, __len); \
400:       __o->next_free += __len; \
401:       *(__o->next_free)++ = 0; \
402:       (void) 0; })
403:
404:# define obstack_1grow(OBSTACK, datum) \
405:  __extension__ \
406:    ({ struct obstack *__o = (OBSTACK); \
407:       if (obstack_room (__o) < 1) \
408:         _obstack_newchunk (__o, 1); \
409:       obstack_1grow_fast (__o, datum); \
410:       (void) 0; })
411:
412:/* These assume that the obstack alignment is good enough for pointers
413:   or ints, and that the data added so far to the current object
414:   shares that much alignment.  */
415:
416:# define obstack_ptr_grow(OBSTACK, datum) \
417:  __extension__ \
418:    ({ struct obstack *__o = (OBSTACK); \
419:       if (obstack_room (__o) < sizeof (void *)) \
420:         _obstack_newchunk (__o, sizeof (void *)); \
421:       obstack_ptr_grow_fast (__o, datum); })
422:
423:# define obstack_int_grow(OBSTACK, datum) \
424:  __extension__ \
425:    ({ struct obstack *__o = (OBSTACK); \
426:       if (obstack_room (__o) < sizeof (int)) \
427:         _obstack_newchunk (__o, sizeof (int)); \
428:       obstack_int_grow_fast (__o, datum); })
429:
430:# define obstack_ptr_grow_fast(OBSTACK, aptr) \
431:  __extension__ \
432:    ({ struct obstack *__o1 = (OBSTACK); \
433:       void *__p1 = __o1->next_free; \
434:       *(const void **) __p1 = (aptr); \
435:       __o1->next_free += sizeof (const void *); \
436:       (void) 0; })
437:
438:# define obstack_int_grow_fast(OBSTACK, aint) \
439:  __extension__ \
440:    ({ struct obstack *__o1 = (OBSTACK); \
441:       void *__p1 = __o1->next_free; \
442:       *(int *) __p1 = (aint); \
443:       __o1->next_free += sizeof (int); \
444:       (void) 0; })
445:
446:# define obstack_blank(OBSTACK, length) \
447:  __extension__ \
448:    ({ struct obstack *__o = (OBSTACK); \
449:       _OBSTACK_INDEX_T __len = length; \
450:       if (obstack_room (__o) < __len) \
451:         _obstack_newchunk (__o, __len); \
452:       obstack_blank_fast (__o, __len); \
453:       (void) 0; })
454:
455:# define obstack_alloc(OBSTACK, length) \
456:  __extension__ \
457:    ({ struct obstack *__h = (OBSTACK); \
458:       obstack_blank (__h, (length)); \
459:       obstack_finish (__h); })
460:
461:# define obstack_copy(OBSTACK, where, length) \
462:  __extension__ \
463:    ({ struct obstack *__h = (OBSTACK); \
464:       obstack_grow (__h, (where), (length)); \
465:       obstack_finish (__h); })
466:
467:# define obstack_copy0(OBSTACK, where, length) \
468:  __extension__ \
469:    ({ struct obstack *__h = (OBSTACK); \
470:       obstack_grow0 (__h, (where), (length)); \
471:       obstack_finish (__h); })
472:
473:/* The local variable is named __o1 to avoid a shadowed variable
474:   warning when invoked from other obstack macros, typically obstack_free.  */
475:# define obstack_finish(OBSTACK) \
476:  __extension__ \
477:    ({ struct obstack *__o1 = (OBSTACK); \
478:       void *__value = (void *) __o1->object_base; \
479:       if (__o1->next_free == __value) \
480:         __o1->maybe_empty_object = 1; \
481:       __o1->next_free \
482:         = __PTR_ALIGN (__o1->object_base, __o1->next_free, \
483:                        __o1->alignment_mask); \
484:       __o1->object_base = __o1->next_free; \
485:       __value; })
486:
487:# define obstack_free(OBSTACK, OBJ) \
488:  __extension__ \
489:    ({ struct obstack *__o = (OBSTACK); \
490:       void *__obj = (OBJ); \
491:       if ((_OBSTACK_CPTR) __o->chunk < (_OBSTACK_CPTR) __obj \
492:           && (_OBSTACK_CPTR) __obj < (_OBSTACK_CPTR) __o->chunk_limit) \
493:         __o->next_free = __o->object_base = (char *) __obj; \
494:       else \
495:         __obstack_free (__o, __obj); })
496:
497:#else /* not __GNUC__-like */
498:
499:# define obstack_object_size(h) \
500:  ((_OBSTACK_SIZE_T) ((h)->next_free - (h)->object_base))
501:
502:# define obstack_room(h) \
503:  ((_OBSTACK_SIZE_T) ((h)->chunk_limit - (h)->next_free))
504:
505:# define obstack_empty_p(h) \
506:  ((h)->chunk->prev == 0 \
507:   && (h)->next_free == __PTR_ALIGN ((char *) (h)->chunk, \
508:                                     (h)->chunk->contents, \
509:                                     (h)->alignment_mask))
510:
511:/* Note that the call to _obstack_newchunk is enclosed in (..., 0)
512:   so that we can avoid having void expressions
513:   in the arms of the conditional expression.
514:   Casting the third operand to void was tried before,
515:   but some compilers won't accept it.  */
516:
517:# define obstack_make_room(h, length) \
518:  ((h)->temp.tempint = (length), \
519:   ((obstack_room (h) < (h)->temp.tempint) \
520:    ? (_obstack_newchunk (h, (h)->temp.tempint), 0) : 0), \
521:   (void) 0)
522:
523:# define obstack_grow(h, where, length) \
524:  ((h)->temp.tempint = (length), \
525:   ((obstack_room (h) < (h)->temp.tempint) \
526:   ? (_obstack_newchunk ((h), (h)->temp.tempint), 0) : 0), \
527:   memcpy ((h)->next_free, where, (h)->temp.tempint), \
528:   (h)->next_free += (h)->temp.tempint, \
529:   (void) 0)
530:
531:# define obstack_grow0(h, where, length) \
532:  ((h)->temp.tempint = (length), \
533:   ((obstack_room (h) <= (h)->temp.tempint) \
534:   ? (_obstack_newchunk ((h), (h)->temp.tempint + 1), 0) : 0), \
535:   memcpy ((h)->next_free, where, (h)->temp.tempint), \
536:   (h)->next_free += (h)->temp.tempint, \
537:   *((h)->next_free)++ = 0, \
538:   (void) 0)
539:
540:# define obstack_1grow(h, datum) \
541:  (((obstack_room (h) < 1) \
542:    ? (_obstack_newchunk ((h), 1), 0) : 0), \
543:   obstack_1grow_fast (h, datum), \
544:   (void) 0)
545:
546:# define obstack_ptr_grow(h, datum) \
547:  (((obstack_room (h) < sizeof (char *)) \
548:    ? (_obstack_newchunk ((h), sizeof (char *)), 0) : 0), \
549:   obstack_ptr_grow_fast (h, datum))
550:
551:# define obstack_int_grow(h, datum) \
552:  (((obstack_room (h) < sizeof (int)) \
553:    ? (_obstack_newchunk ((h), sizeof (int)), 0) : 0), \
554:   obstack_int_grow_fast (h, datum))
555:
556:# define obstack_ptr_grow_fast(h, aptr) \
557:  (((const void **) ((h)->next_free += sizeof (void *)))[-1] = (aptr), \
558:   (void) 0)
559:
560:# define obstack_int_grow_fast(h, aint) \
561:  (((int *) ((h)->next_free += sizeof (int)))[-1] = (aint), \
562:   (void) 0)
563:
564:# define obstack_blank(h, length) \
565:  ((h)->temp.tempint = (length), \
566:   ((obstack_room (h) < (h)->temp.tempint) \
567:   ? (_obstack_newchunk ((h), (h)->temp.tempint), 0) : 0), \
568:   obstack_blank_fast (h, (h)->temp.tempint), \
569:   (void) 0)
570:
571:# define obstack_alloc(h, length) \
572:  (obstack_blank ((h), (length)), obstack_finish ((h)))
573:
574:# define obstack_copy(h, where, length) \
575:  (obstack_grow ((h), (where), (length)), obstack_finish ((h)))
576:
577:# define obstack_copy0(h, where, length) \
578:  (obstack_grow0 ((h), (where), (length)), obstack_finish ((h)))
579:
580:# define obstack_finish(h) \
581:  (((h)->next_free == (h)->object_base \
582:    ? (((h)->maybe_empty_object = 1), 0) \
583:    : 0), \
584:   (h)->temp.tempptr = (h)->object_base, \
585:   (h)->next_free \
586:     = __PTR_ALIGN ((h)->object_base, (h)->next_free, \
587:                    (h)->alignment_mask), \
588:   (h)->object_base = (h)->next_free, \
589:   (h)->temp.tempptr)
590:
591:# define obstack_free(h, obj) \
592:  ((h)->temp.tempptr = (void *) (obj), \
593:   (((_OBSTACK_CPTR) (h)->chunk < (_OBSTACK_CPTR) (h)->temp.tempptr \
594:     && (_OBSTACK_CPTR) (h)->temp.tempptr < (_OBSTACK_CPTR) (h)->chunk_limit) \
595:    ? (void) ((h)->next_free = (h)->object_base = (char *) (h)->temp.tempptr) \
596:    : __obstack_free (h, (h)->temp.tempptr)))
597:
598:#endif /* not __GNUC__-like */
599:
600:#ifdef __cplusplus
601:}       /* C++ */
602:#endif

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/os1_time.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/os1_time.c
3: * NexsOS1 time function implementations for Gnulib portability layer.
4: * These are the canonical implementations for localtime(), gmtime(), and mktime()
5: * backed directly by OS1 syscalls, and Gnulib's time module replacements are not used.
6: */
7:
8:#include <time.h>
9:#include <os1.h>
10:#include <string.h>
11:
12:time_t time(time_t *t) {
13:  time_t sec = (time_t)OS1_time_now();
14:  if (t) {
15:    *t = sec;
16:  }
17:  return sec;
18:}
19:
20:struct tm *localtime(const time_t *timep) {
21:  static struct tm result;
22:  if (!timep)
23:    return NULL;
24:
25:  time_t t = *timep;
26:  result.tm_sec = t % 60;
27:  t /= 60;
28:  result.tm_min = t % 60;
29:  t /= 60;
30:  result.tm_hour = t % 24;
31:  t /= 24;
32:
33:  /* Epoch started Jan 1 1970, which was Thursday (wday = 4) */
34:  result.tm_wday = (t + 4) % 7;
35:
36:  int year = 1970;
37:  while (1) {
38:    int days_in_year = 365;
39:    if ((year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || (year % 400 == 0)) {
40:      days_in_year = 366;
41:    }
42:    if (t < days_in_year)
43:      break;
44:    t -= days_in_year;
45:    year++;
46:  }
47:  result.tm_year = year - 1900;
48:  result.tm_yday = t;
49:
50:  int month_days[] = {31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31};
51:  if ((year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || (year % 400 == 0)) {
52:    month_days[1] = 29;
53:  }
54:
55:  int mon = 0;
56:  while (t >= month_days[mon]) {
57:    t -= month_days[mon];
58:    mon++;
59:  }
60:  result.tm_mon = mon;
61:  result.tm_mday = t + 1;
62:  result.tm_isdst = 0;
63:  return &result;
64:}
65:
66:struct tm *gmtime(const time_t *timep) {
67:  return localtime(timep);
68:}
69:
70:time_t mktime(struct tm *tm) {
71:  int year = tm->tm_year + 1900;
72:  int mon = tm->tm_mon;
73:  int mday = tm->tm_mday;
74:
75:  long days = 0;
76:  for (int y = 1970; y < year; y++) {
77:    days += ((y % 4 == 0 && y % 100 != 0) || (y % 400 == 0)) ? 366 : 365;
78:  }
79:  int month_days[] = {31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31};
80:  if ((year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || (year % 400 == 0)) {
81:    month_days[1] = 29;
82:  }
83:  for (int m = 0; m < mon; m++) {
84:    days += month_days[m];
85:  }
86:  days += mday - 1;
87:
88:  return days * 86400 + tm->tm_hour * 3600 + tm->tm_min * 60 + tm->tm_sec;
89:}
90:
91:static const char *const os1_weekday_names[] = {
92:  "Sun", "Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat"
93:};
94:
95:static const char *const os1_month_names[] = {
96:  "Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun",
97:  "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"
98:};
99:
100:size_t strftime(char *s, size_t max, const char *format, const struct tm *tm) {
101:  if (!s || !format || !tm || max == 0) {
102:    return 0;
103:  }
104:
105:  size_t out = 0;
106:  const char *p = format;
107:
108:  while (*p && out + 1 < max) {
109:    if (*p != '%') {
110:      s[out++] = *p++;
111:      continue;
112:    }
113:
114:    p++;
115:    if (!*p) {
116:      break;
117:    }
118:
119:    char temp[64];
120:    int n = 0;
121:
122:    switch (*p) {
123:      case '%':
124:        s[out++] = '%';
125:        break;
126:      case 'a':
127:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%s", os1_weekday_names[(tm->tm_wday + 7) % 7]);
128:        break;
129:      case 'A':
130:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%s", os1_weekday_names[(tm->tm_wday + 7) % 7]);
131:        break;
132:      case 'b':
133:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%s", os1_month_names[(tm->tm_mon + 12) % 12]);
134:        break;
135:      case 'B':
136:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%s", os1_month_names[(tm->tm_mon + 12) % 12]);
137:        break;
138:      case 'd':
139:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%02d", tm->tm_mday);
140:        break;
141:      case 'e':
142:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%2d", tm->tm_mday);
143:        break;
144:      case 'H':
145:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%02d", tm->tm_hour);
146:        break;
147:      case 'I':
148:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%02d", (tm->tm_hour % 12) ? (tm->tm_hour % 12) : 12);
149:        break;
150:      case 'j':
151:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%03d", tm->tm_yday + 1);
152:        break;
153:      case 'm':
154:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%02d", tm->tm_mon + 1);
155:        break;
156:      case 'M':
157:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%02d", tm->tm_min);
158:        break;
159:      case 'n':
160:        s[out++] = '\n';
161:        break;
162:      case 'p':
163:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%s", (tm->tm_hour >= 12) ? "PM" : "AM");
164:        break;
165:      case 'r':
166:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%02d:%02d:%02d %s",
167:                     (tm->tm_hour % 12) ? (tm->tm_hour % 12) : 12,
168:                     tm->tm_min, tm->tm_sec,
169:                     (tm->tm_hour >= 12) ? "PM" : "AM");
170:        break;
171:      case 'R':
172:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%02d:%02d",
173:                     tm->tm_hour, tm->tm_min);
174:        break;
175:      case 'S':
176:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%02d", tm->tm_sec);
177:        break;
178:      case 'T':
179:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%02d:%02d:%02d",
180:                     tm->tm_hour, tm->tm_min, tm->tm_sec);
181:        break;
182:      case 'Y':
183:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%d", tm->tm_year + 1900);
184:        break;
185:      case 'y':
186:        n = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp), "%02d", (tm->tm_year + 1900) % 100);
187:        break;
188:      case 'z':
189:      case 'Z':
190:        temp[0] = '\0';
191:        n = 0;
192:        break;
193:      case 't':
194:        s[out++] = '\t';
195:        break;
196:      default:
197:        s[out++] = *p;
198:        break;
199:    }
200:
201:    if (n > 0) {
202:      size_t copy = (size_t)n;
203:      if (copy >= max - out) {
204:        copy = max - out - 1;
205:      }
206:      memcpy(s + out, temp, copy);
207:      out += copy;
208:    }
209:
210:    p++;
211:    if (*p == '\0' && out + 1 < max) {
212:      break;
213:    }
214:  }
215:
216:  s[out] = '\0';
217:  return out;
218:}
219:
220:bool hard_locale(int category) {
221:  (void)category;
222:  return false;
223:}
224:

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/parse-datetime.c @@@
1:/* NexsOS1 compatibility shim for GNU parse_datetime() support.
2:   This lives in the portability layer, not in the upstream gnulib source tree. */
3:
4:#include <config.h>
5:
6:#include <ctype.h>
7:#include <errno.h>
8:#include <stdlib.h>
9:#include <string.h>
10:#include <time.h>
11:
12:#include "parse-datetime.h"
13:#include "posixtm.h"
14:#include "timespec.h"
15:
16:static bool
17:parse_relative_timespec(struct timespec *result, const char *p,
18:                        struct timespec const *now)
19:{
20:  if (!result || !p)
21:    return false;
22:
23:  while (*p && isspace((unsigned char) *p))
24:    p++;
25:
26:  if (!*p)
27:    return false;
28:
29:  if (strcmp(p, "now") == 0 || strcmp(p, "today") == 0 || strcmp(p, "this") == 0)
30:    {
31:      *result = now ? *now : current_timespec();
32:      return true;
33:    }
34:
35:  char *end = NULL;
36:  errno = 0;
37:  long value = strtol(p, &end, 10);
38:  if (end == p || errno != 0)
39:    return false;
40:
41:  while (*end && isspace((unsigned char) *end))
42:    end++;
43:
44:  if (!*end)
45:    {
46:      if (now)
47:        {
48:          result->tv_sec = now->tv_sec + value;
49:          result->tv_nsec = now->tv_nsec;
50:          return true;
51:        }
52:      return false;
53:    }
54:
55:  long seconds = 0;
56:  if (strncmp(end, "second", 6) == 0 || strncmp(end, "seconds", 7) == 0 ||
57:      strncmp(end, "sec", 3) == 0 || strncmp(end, "s", 1) == 0)
58:    seconds = value;
59:  else if (strncmp(end, "minute", 6) == 0 || strncmp(end, "minutes", 7) == 0 ||
60:           strncmp(end, "min", 3) == 0 || strncmp(end, "m", 1) == 0)
61:    seconds = value * 60;
62:  else if (strncmp(end, "hour", 4) == 0 || strncmp(end, "hours", 5) == 0 ||
63:           strncmp(end, "hr", 2) == 0 || strncmp(end, "h", 1) == 0)
64:    seconds = value * 3600;
65:  else if (strncmp(end, "day", 3) == 0 || strncmp(end, "days", 4) == 0 ||
66:           strncmp(end, "d", 1) == 0)
67:    seconds = value * 86400;
68:  else if (strncmp(end, "week", 4) == 0 || strncmp(end, "weeks", 5) == 0 ||
69:           strncmp(end, "w", 1) == 0)
70:    seconds = value * 604800;
71:  else if (strncmp(end, "month", 5) == 0 || strncmp(end, "months", 6) == 0)
72:    seconds = value * 30 * 86400;
73:  else if (strncmp(end, "year", 4) == 0 || strncmp(end, "years", 5) == 0 ||
74:           strncmp(end, "y", 1) == 0)
75:    seconds = value * 365 * 86400;
76:  else
77:    return false;
78:
79:  if (now)
80:    {
81:      result->tv_sec = now->tv_sec + seconds;
82:      result->tv_nsec = now->tv_nsec;
83:      return true;
84:    }
85:
86:  return false;
87:}
88:
89:bool parse_datetime(struct timespec *restrict result,
90:                    char const *p,
91:                    struct timespec const *now)
92:{
93:  if (!result || !p)
94:    return false;
95:
96:  while (*p && isspace((unsigned char) *p))
97:    p++;
98:
99:  if (!*p)
100:    return false;
101:
102:  if (parse_relative_timespec(result, p, now))
103:    return true;
104:
105:  time_t secs = 0;
106:  if (posixtime(&secs, p, PDS_TRAILING_YEAR | PDS_CENTURY | PDS_SECONDS))
107:    {
108:      result->tv_sec = secs;
109:      result->tv_nsec = 0;
110:      return true;
111:    }
112:
113:  return false;
114:}
115:
116:bool parse_datetime2(struct timespec *restrict result,
117:                    char const *p,
118:                    struct timespec const *now,
119:                    unsigned int flags,
120:                    timezone_t tz,
121:                    char const *tzstring)
122:{
123:  (void)flags;
124:  (void)tz;
125:  (void)tzstring;
126:  return parse_datetime(result, p, now);
127:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/README.md @@@
1:# Gnulib Capability & Portability Overlay per NexsOS1
2:
3:Questo capability/portability layer consente la compilazione e l'integrazione di GNU Gnulib su **NexsOS1** senza modificare il submodule upstream `user/sys/lib/gnulib`.
4:
5:## Architettura e Layering
6:
7:1. **Configurazione forzata (`gnulib_config_nexsos.h`)**:
8:   - Fornita via `-include user/sys/lib/portability/gnulib/gnulib_config_nexsos.h`.
9:   - Neutralizza le assunzioni host di autoconf/gnulib e dichiara la conformità al modello standard C99/C11 e POSIX di NexsOS1.
10:
11:2. **OS1 Real Glue Layer (`gnulib_os1_glue.c` / `gnulib_os1_glue.h`)**:
12:   - Collega le API di Gnulib al runtime `os1.h`, alle reali syscall di NexsOS1 (`_sys_*`), al VFS (ext4, procfs, regfs) e al capability/process engine (`OS1low_process_*`).
13:   - Nessun mock o fake stub: tutte le operazioni sono connesse direttamente ai descrittori e servizi del sistema operativo.
14:
15:3. **Integrazione Build (`overlay.mk`)**:
16:   - Compila la suite di moduli fondamentali Gnulib in un archivio statico `libgnulib.a`.
17:   - Linkato con `user/sys/lib/lib.c`, `user/sys/lib/malloc.c`, `user/sys/lib/math.c` e `syscall.o`.
18:

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/lua/lua_portability.c @@@
1:#include "lua_portability.h"
2:#include <os1.h>
3:#include <stdio.h>
4:#include <stdlib.h>
5:#include <string.h>
6:
7:#include <locale.h>
8:
9:/* Time implementation lives in the canonical NexsOS1 libc layer.
10: * Lua must use that single ABI surface instead of redefining time(). */
11:
12:char *tmpnam(char *s) {
13:  static char static_buf[128];
14:  static int temp_counter = 0;
15:  char *buf = s ? s : static_buf;
16:  /* /home is the ONLY user-writable tree (kernel/fs/vfs.c vfs_write_allowed);
17:   * the old "/tmpfile_%d" sat at the non-writable root, so os.tmpname()'s path
18:   * could never be created even once file creation via SYS_FILE_WRITE landed.
19:   * (fopen("w") still needs open(2) to honour O_CREAT for these to fully work
20:   * — tracked separately; this at least puts the name in the right tree.) */
21:  sprintf(buf, "/home/.luatmp_%d", temp_counter++);
22:  return buf;
23:}
24:
25:clock_t clock(void) { return (clock_t)os1_cpu_ns(); }
26:
27:double difftime(time_t time1, time_t time0) { return (double)(time1 - time0); }
28:
29:/* strcoll is provided by the central NexsOS libc compatibility layer so that
30: * both Coreutils and Lua share the same ABI surface without duplicate symbol
31: * definitions at link time. */
32:
33:/*
34: * os1_lua_readline - REPL line reader for nxlua (lua_portability.h's
35: * lua_readline override; see that header for why fgets(stdin) is replaced).
36: *
37: * NOTE(LUA-TTY-01): fgets()/OS1 console read() hand back keyboard.c's BASE
38: * ascii_map byte (data1's low byte), not the character after the active
39: * keyboard layout's overrides (payload) - the same .key vs .utf8 split
40: * input_event_t already exposes for windowed apps. nxlua has no window, so
41: * it decodes its own mailbox here instead. Echo is NOT done here: nxexec.h's
42: * host-side relay (USR-TTY-01 #123) already echoes every byte it forwards,
43: * in the same style as nxshell.c's read(0,...) loop; echoing again here
44: * would double every character on screen.
45: *
46: * Returns 1 with buf NUL-terminated and ending in '\n' (matches fgets(),
47: * which pushline() in lua.c strips itself), or 0 on Ctrl-C (EOF-like).
48: */
49:int os1_lua_readline(char *buf, int bufsize) {
50:  /*
51:   * NOTE(LUA-TTY-03): the keyboard-mailbox path below is ONLY correct for a
52:   * real console.  `-i` FORCES interactive mode regardless of
53:   * lua_stdin_is_tty(), so `lua -i < script` and `echo ... | lua -i` reach the
54:   * REPL with stdin redirected to a FILE or a PIPE — there the line must come
55:   * from fd 0, not from the keyboard (otherwise the REPL ignores the supplied
56:   * program and blocks on a keypress that never comes).  isatty() is the same
57:   * capability-type test the tty check uses, so the two agree by construction.
58:   */
59:  if (!isatty(0))
60:    return fgets(buf, bufsize, stdin) ? 1 : 0; /* NULL => EOF, like Ctrl-C */
61:
62:  int len = 0;
63:  while (1) {
64:    struct ipc_message m;
65:    if (try_recv(-1, &m) != 0 || m.type != IPC_TYPE_INPUT || m.data2 == 0) {
66:      OS1_sleep(15);
67:      continue;
68:    }
69:    char c = m.payload[0];
70:    if (c == 0x03) /* Ctrl-C: EOF-like */
71:      return 0;
72:    if (c == '\r' || c == '\n') {
73:      if (len + 1 >= bufsize)
74:        len = bufsize - 2;
75:      buf[len++] = '\n';
76:      buf[len] = '\0';
77:      return 1;
78:    }
79:    if (c == '\b' || c == 127) {
80:      if (len > 0)
81:        len--;
82:      continue;
83:    }
84:    if (c != 0 && len + 1 < bufsize) {
85:      buf[len++] = c;
86:      buf[len] = '\0';
87:    }
88:  }
89:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/opengl/os1_gl_platform.c @@@
1:/* OS1 software implementation of the OpenGL presentation seam. */
2:#include "os1_gl_platform.h"
3:
4:#include <errno.h>
5:#include <stdlib.h>
6:#include <string.h>
7:
8:#include "../os1_video_platform.h"
9:
10:struct os1_gl_surface {
11:  uint32_t backend;
12:  int window;
13:  int width;
14:  int height;
15:  uint32_t *color_buffer;
16:};
17:
18:int os1_gl_surface_create(const struct os1_gl_surface_params *params,
19:                          struct os1_gl_surface **out) {
20:  if (!params || !out || params->width <= 0 || params->height <= 0 ||
21:      !params->title)
22:    return -EINVAL;
23:
24:  struct os1_video_info info;
25:  if (os1_video_query(&info) != 0)
26:    return -ENOSYS;
27:  if (info.backend != OS1_VIDEO_BACKEND_SOFTWARE ||
28:      !(info.capabilities & OS1_VIDEO_CAP_ARGB8888))
29:    return -ENOSYS; /* GPU-context backend reserved for the ASTRA object */
30:
31:  struct os1_gl_surface *surface =
32:      (struct os1_gl_surface *)malloc(sizeof(*surface));
33:  if (!surface)
34:    return -ENOMEM;
35:  memset(surface, 0, sizeof(*surface));
36:  surface->backend = info.backend;
37:  surface->window = -1;
38:
39:  size_t count = (size_t)params->width * (size_t)params->height;
40:  surface->color_buffer = (uint32_t *)malloc(count * sizeof(uint32_t));
41:  if (!surface->color_buffer) {
42:    free(surface);
43:    return -ENOMEM;
44:  }
45:  memset(surface->color_buffer, 0, count * sizeof(uint32_t));
46:
47:  surface->window = os1_video_window_create(params->x, params->y,
48:                                            params->width, params->height,
49:                                            params->title);
50:  if (surface->window < 0) {
51:    int rc = surface->window;
52:    free(surface->color_buffer);
53:    free(surface);
54:    return rc;
55:  }
56:  surface->width = params->width;
57:  surface->height = params->height;
58:  *out = surface;
59:  return 0;
60:}
61:
62:void os1_gl_surface_destroy(struct os1_gl_surface *surface) {
63:  if (!surface)
64:    return;
65:  if (surface->window >= 0)
66:    os1_video_window_destroy(surface->window);
67:  free(surface->color_buffer);
68:  free(surface);
69:}
70:
71:uint32_t *os1_gl_surface_buffer(struct os1_gl_surface *surface, int *width,
72:                                int *height, size_t *pitch_bytes) {
73:  if (!surface)
74:    return NULL;
75:  if (width)
76:    *width = surface->width;
77:  if (height)
78:    *height = surface->height;
79:  if (pitch_bytes)
80:    *pitch_bytes = (size_t)surface->width * sizeof(uint32_t);
81:  return surface->color_buffer;
82:}
83:
84:int os1_gl_surface_swap(struct os1_gl_surface *surface) {
85:  if (!surface)
86:    return -EINVAL;
87:  int rc = os1_video_present_argb8888(
88:      surface->window, 0, 0, surface->width, surface->height,
89:      surface->color_buffer, (size_t)surface->width * surface->height);
90:  if (rc < 0)
91:    return rc;
92:  os1_video_render();
93:  return 0;
94:}
95:
96:int os1_gl_surface_resize(struct os1_gl_surface *surface, int width,
97:                          int height) {
98:  if (!surface || width <= 0 || height <= 0)
99:    return -EINVAL;
100:
101:  size_t count = (size_t)width * (size_t)height;
102:  uint32_t *fresh = (uint32_t *)malloc(count * sizeof(uint32_t));
103:  if (!fresh)
104:    return -ENOMEM;
105:  memset(fresh, 0, count * sizeof(uint32_t));
106:
107:  int rc = os1_video_window_resize(surface->window, width, height);
108:  if (rc < 0) {
109:    free(fresh);
110:    return rc;
111:  }
112:  free(surface->color_buffer);
113:  surface->color_buffer = fresh;
114:  surface->width = width;
115:  surface->height = height;
116:  return 0;
117:}
118:
119:int os1_gl_surface_backend(const struct os1_gl_surface *surface) {
120:  if (!surface)
121:    return -EINVAL;
122:  return (int)surface->backend;
123:}

1:/*
2: * OS1 OpenGL presentation seam.
3: *
4: * The surface an OSMesa-style software GL renders into: a CPU ARGB8888
5: * top-down colour buffer bound to an OS1 window, swapped through the
6: * os1_video_platform portability header.  The GL personality (Mesa's OSMesa
7: * frontend on the nexsos-port-opengl branch, pinned at the last release
8: * that ships it) binds this buffer with OSMesaMakeCurrent + OSMESA_Y_UP=0;
9: * nothing here depends on Mesa headers, so the seam builds and ships ahead
10: * of the library.  The backend field mirrors os1_video_backend: the CPU
11: * buffer is the intentional swap-in point for the future ASTRA GPU-context
12: * object, exactly like the D3D9 presentation chain.
13: */
14:#ifndef OS1_GL_PLATFORM_H
15:#define OS1_GL_PLATFORM_H
16:
17:#include <stddef.h>
18:#include <stdint.h>
19:
20:struct os1_gl_surface_params {
21:  int x;
22:  int y;
23:  int width;
24:  int height;
25:  const char *title;
26:};
27:
28:struct os1_gl_surface; /* opaque: OS1 window + CPU colour buffer */
29:
30:/* Create/destroy a presentable GL surface on the platform's active backend.
31: * Returns 0, -ENOSYS when only an unsupported backend is advertised, or a
32: * negative OS1 error. */
33:int os1_gl_surface_create(const struct os1_gl_surface_params *params,
34:                          struct os1_gl_surface **out);
35:void os1_gl_surface_destroy(struct os1_gl_surface *surface);
36:
37:/* The colour buffer a software GL binds (ARGB8888, top-down rows, tight
38: * pitch).  Geometry is reported through the out parameters; the pointer
39: * stays valid until destroy or resize. */
40:uint32_t *os1_gl_surface_buffer(struct os1_gl_surface *surface, int *width,
41:                                int *height, size_t *pitch_bytes);
42:
43:/* SwapBuffers analogue: present the whole colour buffer and notify the
44: * compositor. */
45:int os1_gl_surface_swap(struct os1_gl_surface *surface);
46:
47:/* Adopt a new size (nxlauncher resize contract): kernel logical resize +
48: * buffer reallocation.  The previously returned buffer pointer is invalid
49: * after a successful resize; re-fetch it with os1_gl_surface_buffer. */
50:int os1_gl_surface_resize(struct os1_gl_surface *surface, int width,
51:                          int height);
52:
53:/* The enum os1_video_backend this surface presents on. */

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/sdl2/README.md @@@
1:# SDL2 NexsOS overlay
2:
3:This overlay supplies the SDL2 `nexsos` video driver without editing the SDL
4:submodule. Its build manifest is `overlay.mk`; the eventual SDL cross-build
5:must compile those three sources with `SDL_VIDEO_DRIVER_NEXSOS` and link them
6:with `lib.c`/`os1_video_platform.c`.
7:
8:Implemented scope: software ARGB8888 windows, pitch-safe partial framebuffer
9:presentation, focused keyboard/mouse/resize event pumping and resize requests.
10:OpenGL contexts, relative pointer mode, clipboard, title mutation and hardware
11:acceleration are deliberately not advertised yet.

41:static SDL_Scancode nexsos_scancode(uint32_t code) {
42:  if (code < SDL_arraysize(nexsos_scancode_table))
43:    return nexsos_scancode_table[code];
44:  switch (code) {
45:  case 87: return SDL_SCANCODE_F11;
46:  case 88: return SDL_SCANCODE_F12;
47:  case 97: return SDL_SCANCODE_RCTRL;
48:  case 100: return SDL_SCANCODE_RALT;
49:  case 102: return SDL_SCANCODE_HOME;
50:  case 103: return SDL_SCANCODE_UP;
51:  case 104: return SDL_SCANCODE_PAGEUP;
52:  case 105: return SDL_SCANCODE_LEFT;
53:  case 106: return SDL_SCANCODE_RIGHT;
54:  case 107: return SDL_SCANCODE_END;
55:  case 108: return SDL_SCANCODE_DOWN;
56:  case 109: return SDL_SCANCODE_PAGEDOWN;
57:  case 110: return SDL_SCANCODE_INSERT;
58:  case 111: return SDL_SCANCODE_DELETE;
59:  default: return SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN;
60:  }
61:}
62:
63:static Uint8 nexsos_mouse_button(int button) {
64:  if (button == 0x110) return SDL_BUTTON_LEFT;
65:  if (button == 0x111) return SDL_BUTTON_RIGHT;
66:  if (button == 0x112) return SDL_BUTTON_MIDDLE;
67:  return 0;
68:}
69:
70:void NEXSOS_PumpEvents(_THIS) {
71:  NEXSOS_VideoData *data = (NEXSOS_VideoData *)_this->driverdata;
72:  struct os1_video_event event;
73:  while (os1_video_poll_event(&event) > 0) {
74:    SDL_Window *window = data->focused_window;
75:    if (!window)
76:      continue;
77:    if (event.type == OS1_VIDEO_EVENT_KEY) {
78:      SDL_Scancode code = nexsos_scancode(event.data.key.scancode);
79:      SDL_SendKeyboardKey(event.data.key.state ? SDL_PRESSED : SDL_RELEASED,
80:                          code);
81:      if (event.data.key.state && event.data.key.utf8[0]) {
82:        char text[9];
83:        SDL_memcpy(text, event.data.key.utf8, 8);
84:        text[8] = '\0';
85:        SDL_SendKeyboardText(text);
86:      }
87:    } else if (event.type == OS1_VIDEO_EVENT_MOUSE_BUTTON) {
88:      Uint8 button = nexsos_mouse_button(event.data.mouse.button);
89:      SDL_SendMouseMotion(window, 0, 0, event.data.mouse.x, event.data.mouse.y);
90:      if (button)
91:        SDL_SendMouseButton(window, 0,
92:                            event.data.mouse.state ? SDL_PRESSED : SDL_RELEASED,
93:                            button);
94:    } else if (event.type == OS1_VIDEO_EVENT_RESIZE) {
95:      SDL_SendWindowEvent(window, SDL_WINDOWEVENT_RESIZED,
96:                          event.data.resize.width, event.data.resize.height);
97:    }
98:  }
99:}
100:
101:#endif /* SDL_VIDEO_DRIVER_NEXSOS */
102:

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/sdl2/SDL_nexsosframebuffer.c @@@
1:/* SDL2 software framebuffer presentation over the NexsOS portability ABI. */
2:#include "../../sdl/src/SDL_internal.h"
3:
4:#ifdef SDL_VIDEO_DRIVER_NEXSOS
5:
6:#include "SDL_nexsosvideo.h"
7:#include "../os1_video_platform.h"
8:
9:int NEXSOS_CreateWindowFramebuffer(_THIS, SDL_Window *window, Uint32 *format,
10:                                   void **pixels, int *pitch) {
11:  (void)_this;
12:  NEXSOS_WindowData *data = (NEXSOS_WindowData *)window->driverdata;
13:  NEXSOS_DestroyWindowFramebuffer(_this, window);
14:  /* Adopt the (possibly compositor-driven) size as the OS1 LOGICAL surface
15:   * before allocating the matching SDL framebuffer — the nxlauncher resize
16:   * pattern (GFX-DYN-01): the kernel no-ops when the size is unchanged, so
17:   * the first acquisition and grip-resize echoes cannot loop. */
18:  (void)os1_video_window_resize(data->os1_window, window->w, window->h);
19:  data->framebuffer = SDL_CreateRGBSurfaceWithFormat(
20:      0, window->w, window->h, 32, SDL_PIXELFORMAT_ARGB8888);
21:  if (!data->framebuffer)
22:    return -1;
23:  *format = SDL_PIXELFORMAT_ARGB8888;
24:  *pixels = data->framebuffer->pixels;
25:  *pitch = data->framebuffer->pitch;
26:  return 0;
27:}
28:
29:int NEXSOS_UpdateWindowFramebuffer(_THIS, SDL_Window *window,
30:                                   const SDL_Rect *rects, int numrects) {
31:  (void)_this;
32:  NEXSOS_WindowData *data = (NEXSOS_WindowData *)window->driverdata;
33:  if (!data || !data->framebuffer)
34:    return SDL_SetError("NexsOS framebuffer unavailable");
35:
36:  SDL_Surface *surface = data->framebuffer;
37:  int first = (numrects > 0) ? 0 : -1;
38:  int last = (numrects > 0) ? numrects : 1;
39:  SDL_Rect full = {0, 0, surface->w, surface->h};
40:  for (int i = first; i < last; i++) {
41:    SDL_Rect area = (i < 0) ? full : rects[i];
42:    if (!SDL_IntersectRect(&area, &full, &area))
43:      continue;
44:    const uint32_t *pixels = (const uint32_t *)surface->pixels +
45:                             (size_t)area.y * (surface->pitch / 4) + area.x;
46:    size_t stride = (size_t)(surface->pitch / 4);
47:    size_t source_count = (size_t)surface->h * stride;
48:    if (os1_video_present_argb8888_strided(data->os1_window, area.x, area.y,
49:                                           area.w, area.h, pixels, stride,
50:                                           source_count - (size_t)area.y * stride - area.x) < 0)
51:      return SDL_SetError("NexsOS framebuffer presentation failed");
52:  }
53:  os1_video_render();
54:  return 0;
55:}
56:
57:void NEXSOS_DestroyWindowFramebuffer(_THIS, SDL_Window *window) {
58:  (void)_this;
59:  NEXSOS_WindowData *data = (NEXSOS_WindowData *)window->driverdata;
60:  if (data) {
61:    SDL_FreeSurface(data->framebuffer);
62:    data->framebuffer = NULL;
63:  }
64:}
65:
66:#endif /* SDL_VIDEO_DRIVER_NEXSOS */

1:/* SDL2 NexsOS timer backend over the OS1 Tier-3 time primitives.

10:/* Mirrors <os1.h> (docs/TIMER-MODEL.md §4); declared directly so OS1's
11: * macro surface (STACK_SIZE, FP_ONE, ...) does not leak into SDL units. */
12:extern unsigned long long os1_mono_ns(void);

14:
15:static SDL_bool ticks_started = SDL_FALSE;
16:static Uint64 start_ns;
17:
18:void SDL_TicksInit(void)
19:{
20:    if (ticks_started) {
21:        return;
22:    }
23:    ticks_started = SDL_TRUE;
24:    start_ns = os1_mono_ns();
25:}
26:

28:{
29:    ticks_started = SDL_FALSE;
30:}
31:
32:Uint64 SDL_GetTicks64(void)
33:{
34:    if (!ticks_started) {
35:        SDL_TicksInit();
36:    }
37:    return (Uint64)(os1_mono_ns() - start_ns) / 1000000ull;
38:}
39:

41:{
42:    return (Uint64)os1_mono_ns();
43:}
44:
45:Uint64 SDL_GetPerformanceFrequency(void)
46:{
47:    return 1000000000ull; /* os1_mono_ns counts nanoseconds */
48:}
49:
50:void SDL_Delay(Uint32 ms)
51:{
52:    _sys_nanosleep((unsigned long long)ms * 1000000ull);

76:int NEXSOS_CreateWindow(_THIS, SDL_Window *window) {
77:  NEXSOS_WindowData *data = SDL_calloc(1, sizeof(*data));
78:  if (!data)
79:    return SDL_OutOfMemory();
80:
81:  /* SDL core applies the title AFTER CreateSDLWindow (via SetWindowTitle),
82:   * so window->title is still NULL here; OS1 requires a title at creation.
83:   * Positions may still carry the UNDEFINED/CENTERED magic values. */
84:  const char *title = window->title ? window->title : "SDL2";
85:  int x = window->x;
86:  int y = window->y;
87:  if (SDL_WINDOWPOS_ISUNDEFINED(x) || SDL_WINDOWPOS_ISCENTERED(x))
88:    x = 60;
89:  if (SDL_WINDOWPOS_ISUNDEFINED(y) || SDL_WINDOWPOS_ISCENTERED(y))
90:    y = 60;
91:
92:  data->os1_window =
93:      os1_video_window_create(x, y, window->w, window->h, title);
94:  if (data->os1_window < 0) {
95:    SDL_free(data);
96:    return SDL_SetError("NexsOS window creation failed");
97:  }
98:  window->driverdata = data;
99:  window->flags &= ~SDL_WINDOW_HIDDEN;
100:  window->flags |= SDL_WINDOW_SHOWN | SDL_WINDOW_INPUT_FOCUS;
101:  ((NEXSOS_VideoData *)_this->driverdata)->focused_window = window;
102:  SDL_SetMouseFocus(window);
103:  SDL_SetKeyboardFocus(window);
104:  return 0;
105:}

111:  NEXSOS_DestroyWindowFramebuffer(_this, window);
112:  os1_video_window_destroy(data->os1_window);
113:  if (((NEXSOS_VideoData *)_this->driverdata)->focused_window == window)
114:    ((NEXSOS_VideoData *)_this->driverdata)->focused_window = NULL;
115:  SDL_free(data);
116:  window->driverdata = NULL;
117:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/portability/os1_video_platform.c @@@
1:/* OS1 software-video implementation of the portability adapter. */
2:#include "os1_video_platform.h"
3:
4:#include <errno.h>
5:#include <input.h>
6:#include <os1.h>
7:#include <stdlib.h>
8:#include <string.h>
9:
10:#define OS1_VIDEO_ABI_VERSION 1u
11:
12:int os1_video_query(struct os1_video_info *out) {
13:  if (!out)
14:    return -EINVAL;
15:
16:  long packed = _sys_display_info();
17:  if (packed < 0)
18:    return (int)packed;
19:
20:  out->abi_version = OS1_VIDEO_ABI_VERSION;
21:  out->backend = OS1_VIDEO_BACKEND_SOFTWARE;
22:  out->capabilities = OS1_VIDEO_CAP_ARGB8888 | OS1_VIDEO_CAP_WINDOW_RESIZE |
23:                      OS1_VIDEO_CAP_DAMAGE_PRESENT |
24:                      OS1_VIDEO_CAP_SOFTWARE_3D;
25:  out->width = (int)((packed >> 16) & 0xffff);
26:  out->height = (int)(packed & 0xffff);
27:  return 0;
28:}
29:
30:int os1_video_window_create(int x, int y, int width, int height,
31:                            const char *title) {
32:  if (width <= 0 || height <= 0 || !title)
33:    return -EINVAL;
34:  return _sys_create_window(x, y, width, height, title);
35:}
36:
37:void os1_video_window_destroy(int window) { _sys_destroy_window(window); }
38:
39:int os1_video_window_resize(int window, int width, int height) {
40:  if (width <= 0 || height <= 0)
41:    return -EINVAL;
42:  return _sys_window_resize(window, width, height);
43:}
44:
45:int os1_video_present_argb8888(int window, int x, int y, int width,
46:                               int height, const uint32_t *pixels,
47:                               size_t pixel_count) {
48:  return os1_video_present_argb8888_strided(window, x, y, width, height,
49:                                            pixels, (size_t)width,
50:                                            pixel_count);
51:}
52:
53:int os1_video_present_argb8888_strided(int window, int x, int y, int width,
54:                                       int height, const uint32_t *pixels,
55:                                       size_t source_stride,
56:                                       size_t source_pixel_count) {
57:  if (window < 0 || width <= 0 || height <= 0 || !pixels)
58:    return -EINVAL;
59:
60:  size_t row_width = (size_t)width;
61:  size_t rows = (size_t)height;
62:  if (source_stride < row_width)
63:    return -EINVAL;
64:
65:  size_t packed_count = row_width * rows;
66:  if (packed_count / row_width != rows)
67:    return -EINVAL;
68:  size_t source_count = (rows - 1) * source_stride + row_width;
69:  if ((rows - 1) != 0 && (source_count - row_width) / (rows - 1) != source_stride)
70:    return -EINVAL;
71:  if (source_pixel_count < source_count)
72:    return -EINVAL;
73:
74:  if (source_stride == row_width) {
75:    _sys_window_blit(window, x, y, width, height, pixels);
76:    return 0;
77:  }
78:
79:  if (packed_count > ((size_t)-1) / sizeof(uint32_t))
80:    return -EINVAL;
81:  uint32_t *packed = (uint32_t *)malloc(packed_count * sizeof(uint32_t));
82:  if (!packed)
83:    return -ENOMEM;
84:  for (size_t row = 0; row < rows; row++)
85:    memcpy(packed + row * row_width, pixels + row * source_stride,
86:           row_width * sizeof(uint32_t));
87:
88:  _sys_window_blit(window, x, y, width, height, packed);
89:  free(packed);
90:  return 0;
91:}
92:
93:int os1_video_poll_event(struct os1_video_event *out) {
94:  if (!out)
95:    return -EINVAL;
96:
97:  input_event_t input;
98:  int result = input_poll_event(&input);
99:  if (result <= 0)
100:    return result;
101:
102:  if (input.type == INPUT_TYPE_KEYBOARD) {
103:    out->type = OS1_VIDEO_EVENT_KEY;
104:    out->data.key.scancode = input.keyboard.scancode;
105:    out->data.key.key = input.keyboard.key;
106:    out->data.key.state = (uint8_t)input.keyboard.state;
107:    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++)
108:      out->data.key.utf8[i] = input.keyboard.utf8[i];
109:    return 1;
110:  }
111:  if (input.type == INPUT_TYPE_MOUSE) {
112:    out->type = OS1_VIDEO_EVENT_MOUSE_BUTTON;
113:    out->data.mouse.button = input.mouse.button;
114:    out->data.mouse.state = input.mouse.state;
115:    out->data.mouse.x = input.mouse.x;
116:    out->data.mouse.y = input.mouse.y;
117:    return 1;
118:  }
119:  if (input.type == INPUT_TYPE_RESIZE) {
120:    out->type = OS1_VIDEO_EVENT_RESIZE;
121:    out->data.resize.width = input.resize.w;
122:    out->data.resize.height = input.resize.h;
123:    return 1;
124:  }
125:  return 0;
126:}
127:
128:void os1_video_render(void) { _sys_compositor_render(); }

76:                                       int height, const uint32_t *pixels,

@@@ user/sys/lib/execsvc_client.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/lib/execsvc_client.c
3: * Client stub for the execution service (Phase 9c).
4: *
5: * Deliberately its OWN translation unit rather than more code inside lib.c:
6: * Phase 10a/12 will split service clients out of the libc entirely, and lib.c is
7: * already the file whose entanglement those phases exist to undo.  Starting it
8: * separate means that split is a Makefile move, not another extraction.
9: *
10: * WHAT THIS IS FOR: nxexec is meant to be THE standard executor and the POSIX
11: * compatibility point for execution.  system() historically bypassed it
12: * completely (it spawned the shell itself), so the POSIX surface had its own
13: * private execution path — exactly the divergence the daemon exists to remove.
14: *
15: * WHAT IT IS NOT FOR: interactive foreground jobs.  The service becomes the
16: * spawning parent, and while OBJ_CTL_SETOWNER restores AUTHORITY it does NOT
17: * move the controlling terminal, so Ctrl-Z/Ctrl-C would break.  That is Phase 9d
18: * (ctty handback), and until then interactive jobs keep the in-process path.
19: */
20:#include <execsvc.h>
21:#include <os1.h>
22:#include <string.h>
23:#include <unistd.h>
24:
25:/* write_full - a pipe write may be short; a partial request would be read as a
26: * malformed one by the service, so finish it or fail. */
27:static int write_full(int fd, const char *buf, int len) {
28:  int done = 0;
29:  while (done < len) {
30:    long w = write(fd, buf + done, (unsigned long)(len - done));
31:    if (w <= 0)
32:      return done;
33:    done += (int)w;
34:  }
35:  return done;
36:}
37:
38:/* read_full - same reasoning on the reply. */
39:static int read_full_c(int fd, char *buf, int want) {
40:  int got = 0;
41:  while (got < want) {
42:    long r = read(fd, buf + got, (unsigned long)(want - got));
43:    if (r <= 0)
44:      return got;
45:    got += (int)r;
46:  }
47:  return got;
48:}
49:
50:/*
51: * execsvc_spawn - ask the execution service to run argv, returning its pid.
52: *
53: * Returns > 0 (pid) on success, or < 0 if the service is unreachable or refuses
54: * — the caller is expected to FALL BACK to spawning directly.  That fallback is
55: * not defensive padding: the service is supervised by init and can be briefly
56: * absent across a respawn, and a POSIX system() that failed in that window
57: * would be a worse regression than the divergence being removed.
58: */
59:int execsvc_spawn(int argc, char *const argv[], unsigned int flags) {
60:  if (argc <= 0 || argc > EXECSVC_ARG_MAX || !argv)
61:    return -1;
62:
63:  int svc = OS1_port_open(OS1NX_PORT_EXEC);
64:  if (svc < 0)
65:    return -1; /* no service published: caller falls back */
66:
67:  int reqp[2] = {-1, -1}, repp[2] = {-1, -1};
68:  int pid = -1;
69:  if (pipe(reqp) != 0) {
70:    OS1low_handle_close(svc);
71:    return -1;
72:  }
73:  if (pipe(repp) != 0) {
74:    close(reqp[0]);
75:    close(reqp[1]);
76:    OS1low_handle_close(svc);
77:    return -1;
78:  }
79:
80:  /* Header + packed body: [redir][cwd\0][argv[i]\0...].  No redirections here:
81:   * system() inherits the caller's stdio, which the child gets by default. */
82:  struct execsvc_spawn_hdr hdr;
83:  char body[EXECSVC_BODY_MAX];
84:  unsigned int off = 0;
85:  int ok = 1;
86:
87:  memset(&hdr, 0, sizeof(hdr));
88:  hdr.version = EXECSVC_VERSION;
89:  hdr.flags = flags;
90:  hdr.argc = argc;
91:  hdr.nredir = 0;
92:
93:  /* cwd: the REQUESTER's, always sent.
94:   *
95:   * This used to send an empty string commented "service default", which is
96:   * not a default at all — the child is created by the service, so it inherits
97:   * the SERVICE's cwd ("/"), and every relative path in a command silently
98:   * resolved against the wrong directory.  `os.execute("lua main.lua")` from
99:   * /home/LUA/luatest looked like a missing file.  cwd is a per-process
100:   * attribute that is inherited at creation, so it is wrong for exactly the
101:   * same reason the environment is (plan S1) — the difference is that it costs
102:   * nothing to carry, because the protocol body already has a slot for it. */
103:  {
104:    char cwd[EXECSVC_PATH_MAX];
105:    if (getcwd(cwd, sizeof(cwd)) != 0 || !cwd[0])
106:      cwd[0] = '\0'; /* unknown: the service leaves its own cwd alone */
107:    unsigned int n = (unsigned int)strlen(cwd) + 1;
108:    if (n > sizeof(body)) {
109:      close(reqp[0]);
110:      close(reqp[1]);
111:      close(repp[0]);
112:      close(repp[1]);
113:      OS1low_handle_close(svc);
114:      return -1;
115:    }
116:    memcpy(body + off, cwd, n);
117:    off += n;
118:  }
119:  for (int i = 0; i < argc && ok; i++) {
120:    unsigned int n = (unsigned int)strlen(argv[i]) + 1;
121:    if (off + n > sizeof(body)) {
122:      ok = 0; /* refuse rather than silently truncate a command */
123:      break;
124:    }
125:    memcpy(body + off, argv[i], n);
126:    off += n;
127:  }
128:  hdr.body_len = off;
129:
130:  if (ok) {
131:    /* Transfer the channels THROUGH the port: a handle index is meaningful only
132:     * inside one process's table, and cap_grant would need the service's PID —
133:     * which the port model deliberately does not expose. */
134:    struct ipc_message m;
135:    memset(&m, 0, sizeof(m));
136:    m.type = EXECSVC_REQ_SPAWN;
137:    int give[2];
138:    give[0] = reqp[0];
139:    give[1] = repp[1];
140:    if (OS1_port_send_caps(svc, &m, give, 2) == (long)sizeof(m)) {
141:      write_full(reqp[1], (const char *)&hdr, (int)sizeof(hdr));
142:      write_full(reqp[1], body, (int)off);
143:      close(reqp[1]); /* EOF: a short body must not hang the service */
144:      reqp[1] = -1;
145:
146:      struct execsvc_spawn_rep rep;
147:      memset(&rep, 0, sizeof(rep));
148:      if (read_full_c(repp[0], (char *)&rep, (int)sizeof(rep)) ==
149:              (int)sizeof(rep) &&
150:          rep.version == EXECSVC_VERSION)
151:        pid = rep.pid;
152:    }
153:  }
154:
155:  if (reqp[0] >= 0)
156:    close(reqp[0]);
157:  if (reqp[1] >= 0)
158:    close(reqp[1]);
159:  close(repp[0]);
160:  close(repp[1]);
161:  OS1low_handle_close(svc);
162:  return pid;
163:}
164:

@@@ user/sys/lib/font_lib.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/lib/font_lib.c
3: * Userland font rendering library
4: *
5: * Provides loading, measurement, and rendering of pre-rasterised bitmap fonts
6: * produced by nxfont.  The on-disk format is:
7: *
8: *   [ struct font_header ]
9: *   [ struct font_glyph_info * header.num_chars ]
10: *   [ raw alpha bitmap bytes ]
11: *
12: * The font_ctx structure holds pointers into a single contiguous heap buffer
13: * (raw_data) allocated by font_load().
14: *
15: * Rendering path (draw_glyph):
16: *   Each glyph row is converted into horizontal opaque spans and each span is
17: *   drawn with one window_draw() call. This preserves transparent backgrounds
18: *   while avoiding the old one-syscall-per-lit-pixel path.
19: *
20: * UTF-8 iteration (font_draw_string, font_string_width):
21: *   Calls utf8_decode() (lib.c) per character; advances by the byte count
22: *   returned.  Invalid sequences (utf8_decode returns 0) skip one byte to
23: *   prevent an infinite loop.
24: *
25: * NOTE: font_lib.c is compiled as part of lib.o (included by lib.c:57) rather
26: * than compiled separately.  Its symbols are therefore available to all ELFs
27: * that link lib.o.
28: */
29:#include <font_lib.h>
30:#include <stdio.h>
31:#include <stdlib.h>
32:#include <string.h>
33:
34:static int add_overflows_size(size_t a, size_t b) {
35:  return a > ((size_t)-1) - b;
36:}
37:
38:static int mul_overflows_size(size_t a, size_t b) {
39:  return b != 0 && a > ((size_t)-1) / b;
40:}
41:
42:static int font_validate_buffer(const void *data, size_t size) {
43:  if (!data || size < sizeof(struct font_header))
44:    return 0;
45:
46:  const struct font_header *h = (const struct font_header *)data;
47:  if (h->magic != FONT_MAGIC)
48:    return 0;
49:  if (h->num_chars == 0)
50:    return 0;
51:  if ((uint32_t)h->ascent + (uint32_t)h->descent == 0)
52:    return 0;
53:
54:  if (mul_overflows_size(h->num_chars, sizeof(struct font_glyph_info)))
55:    return 0;
56:  size_t glyph_bytes = (size_t)h->num_chars * sizeof(struct font_glyph_info);
57:  if (add_overflows_size(sizeof(struct font_header), glyph_bytes))
58:    return 0;
59:  size_t bitmap_offset = sizeof(struct font_header) + glyph_bytes;
60:  if (add_overflows_size(bitmap_offset, h->bitmap_size))
61:    return 0;
62:  if (bitmap_offset + h->bitmap_size > size)
63:    return 0;
64:
65:  const struct font_glyph_info *glyphs =
66:      (const struct font_glyph_info *)((const uint8_t *)data +
67:                                       sizeof(struct font_header));
68:  for (uint16_t i = 0; i < h->num_chars; i++) {
69:    const struct font_glyph_info *gi = &glyphs[i];
70:    if (mul_overflows_size(gi->width, gi->height))
71:      return 0;
72:    size_t glyph_size = (size_t)gi->width * (size_t)gi->height;
73:    if (add_overflows_size(gi->data_offset, glyph_size))
74:      return 0;
75:    if (gi->data_offset + glyph_size > h->bitmap_size)
76:      return 0;
77:  }
78:
79:  return 1;
80:}
81:
82:/*
83: * font_load - read a packed font file and set up a font_ctx.
84: *
85: * path: filesystem path to a packed font produced by nxfont.
86: *
87: * Reads the file in two calls (size probe then full read), validates the
88: * FONT_MAGIC header field, and sets up interior pointers into the single
89: * raw_data allocation:
90: *   ctx->glyphs  = raw_data + sizeof(font_header)
91: *   ctx->bitmap  = raw_data + sizeof(font_header) + num_chars *
92: * sizeof(glyph_info)
93: *
94: * Returns a heap-allocated font_ctx on success, or NULL on file-not-found,
95: * malloc failure, or magic mismatch.
96: *
97: * Ownership: caller must pass the returned ctx to font_free() when done.
98: */
99:struct font_ctx *font_load(const char *path) {
100:  /* Probe file size: file_read with buf=NULL, size=0 returns byte count. */
101:  int size = file_read(path, NULL, 0, 0);
102:  if (size <= 0)
103:    return NULL;
104:
105:  void *data = malloc(size);
106:  if (!data)
107:    return NULL;
108:
109:  if (file_read(path, data, size, 0) != size) {
110:    free(data);
111:    return NULL;
112:  }
113:
114:  if (!font_validate_buffer(data, (size_t)size)) {
115:    free(data);
116:    return NULL;
117:  }
118:
119:  struct font_header *h = (struct font_header *)data;
120:  struct font_ctx *ctx = malloc(sizeof(struct font_ctx));
121:  if (!ctx) {
122:    free(data);
123:    return NULL;
124:  }
125:
126:  ctx->header = *h; /* Copy header fields by value */
127:  /* glyphs array immediately follows the font_header in the packed buffer. */
128:  ctx->glyphs =
129:      (struct font_glyph_info *)((uint8_t *)data + sizeof(struct font_header));
130:  /* Bitmap bytes follow the glyph array. */
131:  ctx->bitmap =
132:      (uint8_t *)ctx->glyphs + h->num_chars * sizeof(struct font_glyph_info);
133:  ctx->raw_data = data; /* Retains ownership for font_free() */
134:
135:  return ctx;
136:}
137:
138:/*
139: * font_free - release a font_ctx and its underlying heap buffer.
140: *
141: * Frees ctx->raw_data (which also invalidates ctx->glyphs and ctx->bitmap
142: * since they point into it), then frees ctx itself.
143: *
144: * Safe to call with NULL ctx.
145: */
146:void font_free(struct font_ctx *ctx) {
147:  if (ctx) {
148:    if (ctx->raw_data)
149:      free(ctx->raw_data);
150:    free(ctx);
151:  }
152:}
153:
154:/*
155: * draw_glyph - render a single Unicode codepoint into a compositor window.
156: *
157: * win_id:    compositor window ID.
158: * ctx:       loaded font context.
159: * x, y:      pen position (baseline left corner).
160: * codepoint: Unicode codepoint to render.
161: * color:     ARGB foreground colour (0xAARRGGBB).
162: *
163: * The glyph bitmap is a row-major alpha (grayscale) image; each byte is an
164: * opacity value 0..255. Pixels with alpha > 128 are drawn as filled spans.
165: *
166: * start_y accounts for the font ascent so that the baseline is at y + ascent
167: * and gi->y0 is a signed offset from that baseline.
168: *
169: * Codepoints outside the font's first_char..first_char+num_chars range are
170: * silently skipped (no replacement glyph).
171: *
172: * Performance note: contiguous pixels on the same row are coalesced into a
173: * single rectangle, which keeps text transparent while sharply reducing
174: * compositor syscalls for normal glyphs.
175: */
176:static void draw_glyph(int win_id, struct font_ctx *ctx, int x, int y,
177:                       uint32_t codepoint, uint32_t color) {
178:  int idx = (int)codepoint - ctx->header.first_char;
179:  if (idx < 0 || idx >= ctx->header.num_chars)
180:    return;
181:
182:  struct font_glyph_info *gi = &ctx->glyphs[idx];
183:  uint8_t *bitmap = ctx->bitmap + gi->data_offset;
184:
185:  /* start_y: baseline = y + ascent; gi->y0 is a signed descent offset. */
186:  int start_x = x + gi->x0;
187:  int start_y = y + ctx->header.ascent + gi->y0;
188:
189:  for (int gy = 0; gy < gi->height; gy++) {
190:    int gx = 0;
191:    while (gx < gi->width) {
192:      while (gx < gi->width && bitmap[gy * gi->width + gx] <= 128) {
193:        gx++;
194:      }
195:
196:      int span_start = gx;
197:      while (gx < gi->width && bitmap[gy * gi->width + gx] > 128) {
198:        gx++;
199:      }
200:
201:      if (gx > span_start) {
202:        window_draw(win_id, start_x + span_start, start_y + gy, gx - span_start,
203:                    1, color);
204:      }
205:    }
206:  }
207:}
208:
209:/*
210: * font_draw_string - render a UTF-8 string into a compositor window.
211: *
212: * Iterates the string using utf8_decode() to handle multi-byte sequences,
213: * calls draw_glyph() for each codepoint, and advances cursor_x by the
214: * glyph's advance width.
215: *
216: * Invalid UTF-8 bytes (utf8_decode returns 0) advance the pointer by one
217: * byte to prevent an infinite loop; no replacement glyph is drawn.
218: *
219: * Codepoints outside the font range are skipped (no advance applied either,
220: * so they consume no horizontal space).
221: */
222:void font_draw_string(int win_id, struct font_ctx *ctx, int x, int y,
223:                      const char *str, uint32_t color) {
224:  if (!ctx || !str)
225:    return;
226:
227:  int cursor_x = x;
228:  uint32_t codepoint;
229:  int consumed;
230:  size_t rem = 0;
231:  const char *p = str;
232:  while (*p) {
233:    p++;
234:    rem++;
235:  }
236:
237:  while (*str) {
238:    consumed = utf8_decode(str, rem, &codepoint);
239:    if (consumed <= 0) {
240:      str++; /* Skip invalid byte to avoid infinite loop */
241:      rem--;
242:      continue;
243:    }
244:    draw_glyph(win_id, ctx, cursor_x, y, codepoint, color);
245:    int idx = (int)codepoint - ctx->header.first_char;
246:    if (idx >= 0 && idx < ctx->header.num_chars) {
247:      cursor_x += ctx->glyphs[idx].advance;
248:    }
249:    str += consumed;
250:    rem -= consumed;
251:  }
252:}
253:
254:/*
255: * font_string_width - compute the rendered pixel width of a UTF-8 string.
256: *
257: * Walks the string identically to font_draw_string but accumulates advance
258: * widths without drawing.  Used by callers to centre or right-align text.
259: *
260: * Returns the total advance in pixels, or 0 for NULL/empty input.
261: *
262: * Note: does not account for kerning (stb_truetype provides per-pair
263: * kerning but the packed font format does not store a kerning table).
264: */
265:int font_string_width(struct font_ctx *ctx, const char *str) {
266:  if (!ctx || !str)
267:    return 0;
268:
269:  int width = 0;
270:  uint32_t codepoint;
271:  int consumed;
272:  size_t rem = 0;
273:  const char *p = str;
274:  while (*p) {
275:    p++;
276:    rem++;
277:  }
278:
279:  while (*str) {
280:    consumed = utf8_decode(str, rem, &codepoint);
281:    if (consumed <= 0) {
282:      str++; /* Skip invalid byte */
283:      rem--;
284:      continue;
285:    }
286:    int idx = (int)codepoint - ctx->header.first_char;
287:    if (idx >= 0 && idx < ctx->header.num_chars) {
288:      width += ctx->glyphs[idx].advance;
289:    }
290:    str += consumed;
291:    rem -= consumed;
292:  }
293:  return width;
294:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/lib.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/lib/lib.c
3: * Userland C runtime and system call wrapper library
4: *
5: * This file is the sole C runtime for all userland processes.  It is
6: * compiled into lib.o and linked WHOLE (no archive, no --gc-sections) into
7: * every ELF (there is no shared library mechanism) — see USR-BLOAT-01/02
8: * below for why that specific fact matters. It provides:
9: *
10: *   - Thin C wrappers around every _sys_*() assembly stub from syscall.S.
11: *   - Standard I/O emulation (fopen/fclose/fread/fwrite/fseek/ftell) backed
12: *     by file_read/file_write syscalls, write-buffered per FILE.
13: *   - Formatting (printf, snprintf, sprintf, vsnprintf, vsscanf, sscanf).
14: *   - Input event decoding (input_poll_event: keyboard and mouse IPC msgs).
15: *   - Graphics helpers (graphics_draw_rect, graphics_blit, graphics_draw_text,
16: *     graphics_text_width, graphics_load_image).
17: *   - A real (registry-backed) POSIX personality: strdup, strtol, abs, fabs,
18: *     atof/strtod, getenv/setenv/unsetenv, mkdir, system, stat, puts, fflush,
19: *     remove, rename, vfprintf, waitpid, pipe, and ~100 further shims.
20: *   - UTF-8 decoder (utf8_decode).
21: *   - Stack smash protector stub (__stack_chk_guard, __stack_chk_fail).
22: *
23: * NASA/JPL "Power of Ten" compliance policy (added by this pass, applied
24: * incrementally module-by-module — see MODULE banners below for what has
25: * been brought into line so far):
26: *   R1  Simple control flow only: no goto, no direct or indirect recursion.
27: *   R2  Every loop has a statically visible upper bound.
28: *   R3  No heap allocation after process start-up on any syscall-veneer or
29: *       formatting hot path (malloc.c's arena is for application code).
30: *   R4  A function body fits on one printed "page" (~60 lines); split
31: *       larger ones into named helpers.
32: *   R5  >= 2 runtime assertions per non-trivial function, guarding
33: *       preconditions/postconditions; gated behind NX_STRICT (opt-in via
34: *       `make NX_STRICT=1`, the same knob kernel/nx_contract.h's
35: *       NX_MUST_USE checks were originally gated behind — see nx_assert()
36: *       below for why this file keeps it opt-in) so release builds keep
37: *       today's perf and debug builds get the checks.
38: *   R6  Declare every object at the smallest possible scope.
39: *   R7  Check the return value of every non-void call, or cast to
40: *       (void) with a comment saying why the result is intentionally
41: *       unused.
42: *   R8  Preprocessor limited to inclusion guards and simple constant/
43: *       function-like macros; no conditional compilation that hides a
44: *       function's control flow from the reader.
45: *   R9  At most one level of pointer dereference per expression; no more
46: *       than one function-pointer indirection (s_atexit_handlers[] is the
47: *       one deliberate exception — a fixed-size callback table, not a
48: *       dispatch chain).
49: *   R10 Compile clean under -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wshadow
50: *       -Wwrite-strings (already COMMON_FLAGS) with zero suppressions
51: *       introduced by this pass.
52: * Deviations from R1-R10 that cannot be closed inside this file alone are
53: * recorded at the point of deviation with a "DEVIATION(Rn): ..." comment
54: * instead of being silently left out — see USR-BLOAT-01/02 and
55: * USR-LIB-01 immediately below for the two structural ones.
56: *
57: * STB libraries (NOTE USR-BLOAT-01/02 — VERIFIED STILL OPEN, 2026-09,
58: * cross-checked against the top-level Makefile in the provided source
59: * bundle):
60: *   STB_IMAGE_IMPLEMENTATION is compiled unconditionally into lib.o, and
61: *   lib.o is linked as a single whole object (USER_LIB_O in the top-level
62: *   Makefile) into every user-space ELF (all "*.elf" targets built from
63: *   user/) with no -ffunction-sections/
64: *   -fdata-sections, no -Wl,--gc-sections, and no strip step — confirmed by
65: *   counter.c's own header, which measures counter.elf at ~503KB with ~52KB
66: *   of unused stb_image/stb_easy_font code and ~70% DWARF debug data.
67: *   DEVIATION(R3/perf): this is NOT fixable from inside lib.c — GCC already
68: *   places each function in its own section under -ffunction-sections, so no
69: *   source change here helps until the link step actually asks for
70: *   --gc-sections and a strip pass. The concrete fix is a build-system
71: *   change (documented separately for review, since it touches the shared
72: *   top-level Makefile, not lib.c): add -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections
73: *   to USER_CFLAGS, add -Wl,--gc-sections (and a BUILD=release
74: *   `strip -s`/`-Wl,-s` step, keeping unstripped for BUILD=debug) to the ELF
75: *   link rules. Text rendering itself no longer needs stb_easy_font — it now
76: *   uses the OS1 packed bitmap font path — so once gc-sections works,
77: *   non-image-loading binaries drop both libraries automatically with no
78: *   further lib.c change.
79: *
80: * Kernel source inclusion (NOTE USR-LIB-01 — VERIFIED STILL OPEN):
81: *   vsnprintf.c, math.c, string.c are sourced directly from kernel/lib/ via
82: *   relative #include paths (see the MODULE 2 banner below, where the
83: *   #includes live). Any internal change to those kernel files silently
84: *   changes userland behaviour with no compiler diagnostic.
85: *   DEVIATION(R8): this is a real boundary violation, not just a style
86: *   nit, and the correct fix is architectural, not a #include swap: extract
87: *   the freestanding-safe subset of those three kernel files into a THIRD
88: *   location (e.g. lib/common/{string,vsnprintf,math}.c) that both
89: *   kernel/lib/ and user/sys/lib/ symlink or copy from at build time, so
90: *   there is exactly one source of truth instead of an include-path
91: *   coupling. That move touches kernel/lib/ and the Makefile, which are
92: *   outside this file's blast radius for this pass — left as a documented,
93: *   correctly-scoped TODO rather than papered over.
94: *
95: * Known issues — RE-AUDITED against the actual code below and the kernel
96: * source (not just re-asserted from the previous pass):
97: *   USR-LIB-01   OPEN (see above; unchanged).
98: *   USR-LIB-02   FIXED. Stdio wrappers do proper NULL checks (no more
99: *                `(size_t)fp > 10` magic-value guard). fopen() streams are
100: *                write-buffered (FILE.wbuf, FILE_WBUF_SIZE) so incremental
101: *                writers issue one syscall per bufferful instead of one per
102: *                fwrite(); fflush/fclose/fseek and every fread() flush first.
103: *   USR-LIB-03   FIXED. graphics_draw_text no longer declares a 100KB static
104: *                buffer or falls back to terminal rendering.
105: *   USR-LIB-04   FIXED, contrary to what this note previously claimed:
106: *                system() runs NXShell for real and returns its exit status
107: *                (not a hardcoded 0); getenv/setenv/unsetenv/environ are a
108: *                real POSIX personality over a registry-backed OS1_env_*
109: *                layer (see the ENVIRONMENT module); atof() is strtod(), a
110: *                real IEEE-754 parse, not `(double)atoi()`; mkdir() composes
111: *                over a real parent-directory capability (OS1_fs_mkdir).
112: *                The previous note describing these as no-ops/truncating was
113: *                itself stale documentation, not a bug in the code — kept
114: *                here, corrected, so the history is not lost.
115: *   USR-LIB-05   FIXED, likewise stale as previously written: vfprintf()
116: *                honours `stream` via fwrite() — a real fopen()ed FILE*
117: *                writes to its own path/position, it does not land on fd 1.
118: *                One real, narrower gap remains and is worth keeping on
119: *                record: stdin/stdout/stderr are three fds over ONE kernel
120: *                CONSOLE object (kernel/core/object.c), so stdout and
121: *                stderr are visually indistinguishable on this console —
122: *                that is a kernel/console-object property, not something
123: *                vfprintf can fix by itself.
124: *   USR-SEC-01   FIXED AT THE KERNEL BOUNDARY, which is the architecturally
125: *                correct place for it: SYS_REGISTRY's write path is gated by
126: *                CAP_REG_WRITE and a first-writer-wins owner_pid check
127: *                (kernel/lib/registry.c), enforced before userland ever gets
128: *                a say — so a userland-side re-check here would be
129: *                redundant, not defense in depth (the untrusted side cannot
130: *                be the enforcement point). Kept as a comment at the
131: *                OS1_registry_* wrappers pointing at the kernel enforcement,
132: *                so the next reader does not "fix" it a second time.
133: *   USR-SEC-02   FIXED AT THE KERNEL BOUNDARY, same shape as USR-SEC-01:
134: *                SYS_KILL is gated by process_kill_allowed()
135: *                (kernel/core/syscall_dispatch.c — CAP_IPC_ANY, or
136: *                target is caller's parent/ancestor) and SYS_SEND is gated
137: *                by CAP_IPC_ANY for non-relatives. send()/kill_process()
138: *                stay thin veneers on purpose; duplicating the check in
139: *                userland cannot add real security since userland is not
140: *                the trust boundary.
141: *   USR-BLOAT-01 OPEN (see above).
142: *   USR-BLOAT-02 OPEN (see above).
143: */

220:/* nx_assert - Power-of-Ten R5 runtime assertion, compiled in only when
221: * NX_STRICT is defined. VERIFIED against the actual Makefile (not assumed):
222: * NX_STRICT is opt-in (`make NX_STRICT=1`), gating warn_unused_result via
223: * NX_MUST_USE in kernel/nx_contract.h for the SAME stated reason this file
224: * documents below — nx_contract.h's own history is that a gate you have to
225: * remember to switch on caught nothing, so NX_MUST_USE was made unconditional
226: * there. nx_assert() stays opt-in rather than copying that fix, because unlike
227: * a compiler attribute it has a real runtime cost and an abort side effect;
228: * `make NX_STRICT=1` is this project's existing "how much does the strict
229: * profile catch" report (see the Makefile's own NX_STRICT comment) and this
230: * hooks into that same report instead of adding a second strictness knob.
231: * When active, on failure it reports through the ONE error seam
232: * (OS1_report_error, prototyped in <os1.h> and already included above) with
233: * EFAULT, so a violated invariant is visible the same way a hard I/O fault
234: * is, then aborts via OS1low_process_exit (likewise from <os1.h>) — a
235: * violated precondition here means a bug in the caller, not a recoverable
236: * I/O condition, so returning an error code is not an option: continuing
237: * would touch dangling handles or a NULL stream with a "confirmed working"
238: * codepath around it. */
239:#ifdef NX_STRICT
240:#define nx_assert(cond)                                                      \
241:  do {                                                                       \
242:    if (!(cond)) {                                                           \
243:      OS1_report_error("nx_assert:" __FILE__ ":" #cond, EFAULT);             \
244:      OS1low_process_exit(134); /* 128+SIGABRT, matching POSIX abort() */    \
245:    }                                                                        \
246:  } while (0)
247:#else
248:/* R5/off-path: NX_STRICT off must not just vanish to ((void)0) — that leaves
249: * every variable that existed only to feed a condition (e.g. `idlen` in
250: * OS1low_process_wait_status) looking "assigned but never read" to
251: * -Wunused-variable, and this tree builds with -Werror. `(void)(cond)`
252: * still counts as a use for the compiler, still costs nothing observable
253: * (the comparison's result is discarded, and `cond` must stay
254: * side-effect-free by the same rule any assert() condition follows), and
255: * keeps release builds warning-clean without adding an abort path. */
256:#define nx_assert(cond) ((void)(cond))
257:#endif
