265:/*
266: * errno_ret - THE POSIX errno seam for the syscall veneers below.
267: *
268: * Kernel syscalls return a NEGATIVE errno on failure (e.g. -ENOENT, -EACCES);
269: * the POSIX contract every libc caller relies on is "set errno to the positive
270: * code and return -1".  Routing the file/fd wrappers through here is what stops
271: * failures surfacing as strerror(0) == "Success" (the "(Success)" Lua's
272: * io.open printed on a missing file) — and it is deliberately generic: ANY
273: * POSIX-style consumer, not just Lua, gets correct errno/strerror from now on.
274: */
275:/* ==========================================================================
276: * MODULE 1 — errno seam and the single error-reporting policy
277: * (R1-R10 applied; see the file header's compliance policy)
278: * ========================================================================== */
279:static long errno_ret_ctx(long r, const char *ctx) {
280:  if (r < 0) {
281:    /* R5: `errno = (int)-r` truncates a long to an int; every kernel errno
282:     * is a small positive constant (<posix_types.h>), so -r must already
283:     * fit in an int before the cast — assert it instead of silently
284:     * truncating a would-be-huge "errno" into an unrelated small one. */
285:    nx_assert(-r > 0 && -r <= INT_MAX);
286:    errno = (int)-r;
287:    /*
288:     * The classifier runs HERE, so the diagnostic declaration is universal.
289:     *
290:     * OS1_report_error's own comment promises that a hard failure in ANY libc
291:     * or portability path becomes visible, but it was reached from three call
292:     * sites only — so every OTHER POSIX veneer set errno correctly and was
293:     * never classified.  A promise kept at three sites is not a policy, it is
294:     * a convention each new compatibility layer (SDL, lua, doom, tomorrow
295:     * musl) has to remember to call — and "remember to call it" is the shape
296:     * of a duplication waiting to diverge.
297:     *
298:     * Safe to route everything through it because the POLICY is already
299:     * selective: ENOENT/EAGAIN and the rest of normal control flow stay
300:     * silent, EACCES/EPERM warn, and only EIO/EFAULT/ENOMEM/ENOSPC/EROFS
301:     * raise the red one.  Probes cannot spam it.
302:     */
303:    OS1_report_error(ctx, (int)r);
304:    return -1;
305:  }
306:  return r;
307:}
308:
309:/* errno_ret - the POSIX seam without a context tag (ctx defaults to "libc").
310: * Callers that know the object they failed on should use errno_ret_ctx so the
311: * notification names it. */
312:static long errno_ret(long r) { return errno_ret_ctx(r, NULL); }
313:
314:/*
315: * OS1_report_error - THE single userland error-surfacing seam
316: * (PLAN-2026-07-17-STRATIFICATION.md, Phase 0).
317: *
318: * Maps an errno to the notification system BY SEVERITY CLASS, so a hard
319: * failure in ANY libc / portability path (SDL, lua, doom, ...) becomes visible
320: * — a red/amber notification with context — instead of a silent -1 an app can
321: * ignore and loop on.  Every layer calls THIS one policy; none hand-rolls its
322: * own notify (no duplication, uniform behaviour).  Normal control-flow errors
323: * stay silent so probes (ENOENT, EAGAIN) never spam:
324: *
325: *   EIO/EFAULT/ENOMEM/ENOSPC/EROFS -> error (red)   — unexpected / hard fault
326: *   EACCES/EPERM                   -> warn  (amber) — policy denial
327: *   everything else                -> silent        — normal control flow
328: *
329: * `err` may be given as errno (positive) or as a raw -errno syscall return.
330: * `ctx` is a short tag: a subsystem ("vfs", "mmap") or "op path".
331: */
332:void OS1_report_error(const char *ctx, int err) {
333:  if (err < 0)
334:    err = -err;
335:  if (!ctx)
336:    ctx = "libc";
337:  switch (err) {
338:  case EIO:
339:  case EFAULT:
340:  case ENOMEM:
341:  case ENOSPC:
342:  case EROFS:
343:    OS1_notify_error(ctx, strerror(err));
344:    break;
345:  case EACCES:
346:  case EPERM:
347:    OS1_notify_warn(ctx, strerror(err));
348:    break;
349:  default:
350:    break; /* normal control-flow error: no notification */
351:  }
352:}
353:
354:/* ==========================================================================
355: * MODULE 2 — Syscall wrappers, time, and process control
356: * (R1-R10 applied to this module; see the file header's compliance policy)
357: *
358: * Each function below is a thin C-callable veneer over an assembly stub in
359: * user/arch/<arch>/syscall.S.  Arguments are passed in the arch ABI registers
360: * (x0-x5 on AArch64, rdi/rsi/rdx/r10/r8/r9 on x86-64) by the C compiler;
361: * the stub moves the syscall number into x8/rax and issues svc/syscall.
362: *
363: * send(), kill_process(), and spawn() deliberately accept any pid/path with
364: * NO check in this file — see USR-SEC-02 in the file header: SYS_KILL and
365: * SYS_SEND are capability-gated in the kernel (process_kill_allowed(),
366: * CAP_IPC_ANY), which is the real trust boundary; a second check here would
367: * be theatre, not defense in depth.
368: * ========================================================================== */
369:long read(int fd, char *buf, unsigned long count) {
370:  return errno_ret(_sys_read(fd, buf, count));
371:}
372:long write(int fd, const char *buf, size_t count) {
373:  return errno_ret(_sys_write(fd, buf, count));
374:}
375:long OS1_time_now(void) { return _sys_get_time(); }
376:long get_time(void) { return OS1_time_now(); } /* compat shim (DIR-01 F4) */
377:
378:time_t time(time_t *t) {
379:  time_t sec = (time_t)OS1_time_now();
380:  if (t)
381:    *t = sec;
382:  return sec;
383:}
384:
385:/* Tier 3 os1 time primitives (docs/TIMER-MODEL.md §4); SYS_CLOCK_GETTIME
386: * clk 0 = monotonic ns since boot, clk 1 = this process's CPU time in ns. */
387:unsigned long long os1_mono_ns(void) {
388:  return (unsigned long long)_sys_clock_gettime(0);
389:}
390:unsigned long long os1_cpu_ns(void) {
391:  return (unsigned long long)_sys_clock_gettime(1);
392:}
393:/* clock_gettime: POSIX layer over the os1 primitives (<time.h>). */
394:int clock_gettime(int clk, struct timespec *ts) {
395:  if (!ts)
396:    return -1;
397:  unsigned long long ns =
398:      (clk == CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID) ? os1_cpu_ns() : os1_mono_ns();
399:  ts->tv_sec = (time_t)(ns / 1000000000ULL);
400:  ts->tv_nsec = (long)(ns % 1000000000ULL);
401:  return 0;
402:}
403:
404:/* nanosleep: POSIX blocking sleep over the SYS_NANOSLEEP primitive (<time.h>).
405: * Not interruptible here, so it always completes: *rem is zeroed, returns 0. */
406:int nanosleep(const struct timespec *req, struct timespec *rem) {
407:  if (!req || req->tv_nsec < 0 || req->tv_nsec >= 1000000000L)
408:    return -1;
409:  unsigned long long ns = (unsigned long long)req->tv_sec * 1000000000ULL +
410:                          (unsigned long long)req->tv_nsec;
411:  _sys_nanosleep(ns);
412:  if (rem) {
413:    rem->tv_sec = 0;
414:    rem->tv_nsec = 0;
415:  }
416:  return 0;
417:}
418:/* --- Process control: OS1low_ canonical primitives (ASTRA §6.1, DIR-01 F4) ---
419: * The stable low-level process surface; each just wraps a _sys_ stub, so there
420: * is no new syscall and no behaviour change.  The bare verbs below are
421: * zero-breakage compat shims forwarding here (kill_process/wait/yield are shims
422: * defined further down, next to their original neighbours).  exit keeps the
423: * while(1): unreachable dead code that silences the "noreturn" warning in
424: * compilers that do not see svc #0 as a terminator. */
425:/* Forward declaration: every spawn primitive below propagates
426: * the caller's environment into the child's per-process registry
427: * namespace before returning the pid — see __env_propagate_to_child,
428: * defined further down with the rest of the OS1_env_* surface. */
429:static void __env_propagate_to_child(long child_pid);
430:
431:long OS1low_process_spawn(const char *path, int argc, char *const argv[]) {
432:  long pid = _sys_spawn(path, argc, argv, 0);
433:  __env_propagate_to_child(pid);
434:  return pid;
435:}
436:/* Detached (SPAWN_FLAG_DETACHED, #193): the child does NOT inherit the spawner
437: * as ctty — the nxexec launcher-mode.  See caps.h for the flag semantics. */
438:long OS1low_process_spawn_detached(const char *path, int argc,
439:                                   char *const argv[]) {
440:  long pid = _sys_spawn(path, argc, argv, SPAWN_FLAG_DETACHED);
441:  __env_propagate_to_child(pid);
442:  return pid;
443:}
444:/* Phase 4: spawn with fd redirection (shell `<`/`>`/`>>`/`2>`).  The redirect
445: * targets must already be open in THIS process; the kernel dups them into the
446: * child, so the caller closes its copies after we return. */
447:long OS1low_process_spawn_redir(const char *path, int argc, char *const argv[],
448:                                unsigned int flags,
449:                                const struct spawn_redir *redir, int nredir) {
450:  long pid = (nredir <= 0)
451:                 ? _sys_spawn(path, argc, argv, flags)
452:                 : _sys_spawn_redir(path, argc, argv, flags, redir, nredir);
453:  __env_propagate_to_child(pid);
454:  return pid;
455:}
456:long OS1low_process_spawn_caps(const char *path, int level,
457:                               unsigned long caps) {
458:  long pid = _sys_spawn_caps(path, level, caps, 0);
459:  __env_propagate_to_child(pid);
460:  return pid;
461:}
462:/* OS1low_pipe (Phase 4): anonymous byte pipe (OBJ_TYPE_PIPE).  fds[0]=read end,
463: * fds[1]=write end.  The kernel installs both handles; read/write/close operate
464: * on them like any other fd. */
465:int OS1low_pipe(int fds[2]) { return (int)errno_ret(_sys_pipe(fds)); }
466:/* POSIX pipe(): thin personality over OS1low_pipe (unistd.h). */
467:int pipe(int pipefd[2]) { return OS1low_pipe(pipefd); }
468:int OS1low_process_kill(int pid) { return _sys_kill(pid); }
469:/* OS1low_process_wait (F4 M4.5): wait via a PROCESS capability +
470: * OS1_object_wait. A WAIT-only handle is acquirable for any live process
471: * (wait-right is separable from kill-right); if the process is already gone,
472: * acquisition fails and we fall back to the ambient SYS_WAIT so the legacy "not
473: * found" (-2) result is preserved. */
474:/* __wait_encode - map the kernel's NEXS-neutral wait code to the POSIX status
475: * word (Phase 2). code >= 0: voluntary exit -> exit code in bits 8..15
476: * (WIFEXITED). code < 0: killed -> low byte = -code (WIFSIGNALED). */
477:static int __wait_encode(int code) {
478:  if (code < 0)
479:    return (-code) & 0x7f;
480:  return (code & 0xff) << 8;
481:}
482:
483:int OS1low_process_wait(int pid) { return OS1low_process_wait_status(pid, 0); }
484:
485:/* OS1low_process_wait_status - like OS1low_process_wait, but on reap writes the
486: * process's raw exit_code to *code (Phase 2). Carried through the PROCESS
487: * capability's OS1_object_wait(handle, &code); the ambient fallback has no
488: * status channel, so *code stays 0 there. */
489:int OS1low_process_wait_status(int pid, int *code) {
490:  char idbuf[16];
491:  /* R5/R7: a 32-bit pid renders as at most 11 chars ("-2147483648") + NUL =
492:   * 12, well inside idbuf[16]; assert the fit instead of trusting it
493:   * silently, and check sprintf's own return (chars written, excluding
494:   * NUL) rather than discarding it. */
495:  int idlen = sprintf(idbuf, "%d", pid);
496:  nx_assert(idlen > 0 && (size_t)idlen < sizeof(idbuf));
497:  long h = OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_PROC, idbuf, OS1_RIGHT_WAIT,
498:                                OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS);
499:  if (h < 0) {
500:    /* No capability: the process is already GONE — which since Phase 9b is the
501:     * case where a retained status is precisely what we are after, so the
502:     * ambient path must carry it back rather than drop it. */
503:    return _sys_wait_status(pid, code);
504:  }
505:  long r = OS1_object_wait((int)h, (long)code);
506:  /* R7: close() failing here (an already-invalid handle) cannot change what
507:   * we return — the wait result in `r` is already committed — so the value
508:   * is intentionally discarded, not merely forgotten. */
509:  (void)OS1low_handle_close((int)h);
510:  return (int)r;
511:}
512:/* OS1_process_stop / _cont - job control (Phase 2). Acquire a PROCESS
513: * capability with the control (DESTROY) right — the same authority as kill —
514: * and issue OBJ_CTL_STOP/CONT. Returns 0 or a negative errno. */
515:static int os1_process_ctl(int pid, int cmd) {
516:  char idbuf[16];
517:  int idlen = sprintf(idbuf, "%d", pid);
518:  nx_assert(idlen > 0 && (size_t)idlen < sizeof(idbuf));
519:  long h = OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_PROC, idbuf, OS1_RIGHT_DESTROY,
520:                                OBJ_TYPE_PROCESS);
521:  if (h < 0)
522:    return (int)h;
523:  long r = OS1_object_ctl((int)h, cmd, 0);
524:  (void)OS1low_handle_close((int)h); /* R7: see rationale above */
525:  return (int)r;
526:}
527:int OS1_process_stop(int pid) { return os1_process_ctl(pid, OBJ_CTL_STOP); }
528:int OS1_process_cont(int pid) { return os1_process_ctl(pid, OBJ_CTL_CONT); }
529:
530:void OS1low_process_yield(void) { _sys_yield(); }
531:int OS1low_process_self(void) { return _sys_get_pid(); }
532:void OS1low_process_exit(int status) {
533:  _sys_exit(status);
534:  while (1)
535:    ;
536:}

538:/* Bare-name compat shims (DIR-01). */
539:int get_pid(void) { return OS1low_process_self(); }
540:/* --- POSIX <unistd.h> personality (thin mapping onto the OS1 verbs above) ---
541: */
542:/* getpid: the POSIX spelling of get_pid(). */
543:int getpid(void) { return get_pid(); }

545:/* Minimal Linux-compatible random API for GNU Coreutils and other ports.
546: * The kernel does not expose a SYS_getrandom syscall in this tree yet, so the
547: * libc layer synthesizes a non-blocking pseudo-random source from a tiny xorshift
548: * state seeded from the OS1 clock and PID.  This is intentionally sufficient to
549: * satisfy compile-time/test-time expectations and keep the userland port moving
550: * without special-casing any applet. */
551:static unsigned long long os1_rand_state = 0;
552:static unsigned long long os1_rand_next(void) {
553:  unsigned long long x = os1_rand_state;
554:  if (x == 0) {
555:    x = (unsigned long long)OS1_time_now() ^ 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL;
556:    x ^= (unsigned long long)getpid() << 13;
557:    x ^= (unsigned long long)os1_mono_ns();
558:  }
559:  x ^= x >> 12;
560:  x ^= x << 25;
561:  x ^= x >> 27;
562:  os1_rand_state = x;
563:  return x;
564:}
565:
566:ssize_t getrandom(void *buf, size_t buflen, unsigned int flags) {
567:  (void)flags;
568:  if (!buf && buflen != 0) {
569:    errno = EFAULT;
570:    return -1;
571:  }
572:  unsigned char *p = (unsigned char *)buf;
573:  for (size_t i = 0; i < buflen; ++i) {
574:    if ((i & 7) == 0) {
575:      unsigned long long v = os1_rand_next();
576:      for (int j = 0; j < 8 && i + j < buflen; ++j)
577:        p[i + j] = (unsigned char)(v >> (8 * j));
578:      i += 7;
579:    }
580:  }
581:  return (ssize_t)buflen;
582:}
583:
584:int getentropy(void *buffer, size_t length) {
585:  if (!buffer && length != 0) {
586:    errno = EFAULT;
587:    return -1;
588:  }
589:  if (length > 256) {
590:    errno = EINVAL;
591:    return -1;
592:  }
593:  ssize_t r = getrandom(buffer, length, 0);
594:  if (r < 0)
595:    return -1;
596:  return 0;
597:}

599:/* isatty: a descriptor is a terminal iff the object behind its handle is a
600: * CONSOLE.  This is the REAL test via the capability type (OS1low_cap_query),
601: * not the old "fd < 3" assumption: with shell redirection fd 1 may be a FILE
602: * (`cmd > out`) or a PIPE (`cmd | cmd`), and interactive programs (the lua
603: * REPL) must see isatty() == 0 in exactly those cases. */
604:int isatty(int fd) {
605:  long q = OS1low_cap_query(fd);
606:  if (q < 0) {
607:    errno = EBADF;
608:    return 0;
609:  }
610:  return OS1_CAPQ_TYPE(q) == OBJ_TYPE_CONSOLE ? 1 : 0;
611:}
612:#define MAX_ATEXIT 32
613:static void (*s_atexit_handlers[MAX_ATEXIT])(void);
614:static int s_atexit_count = 0;
615:
616:int atexit(void (*function)(void)) {
617:  if (!function || s_atexit_count >= MAX_ATEXIT)
618:    return -1;
619:  s_atexit_handlers[s_atexit_count++] = function;
620:  return 0;
621:}
622:
623:void exit(int status) {
624:  while (s_atexit_count > 0) {
625:    void (*fn)(void) = s_atexit_handlers[--s_atexit_count];
626:    if (fn)
627:      fn();
628:  }
629:  fflush(stdout);
630:  fflush(stderr);
631:  OS1low_process_exit(status);
632:}

674:/* --- Service ports (ASTRA §6.5) -------------------------------------------
675: * Thin personality over handle_create + object I/O: the port is the capability,
676: * so there is no separate "port syscall" to add — acquiring the handle IS the
677: * authority decision, and send/receive are ordinary object writes/reads.
678: */
679:int OS1_port_create(const char *name) {
680:  /* RECEIVE right publishes the port and claims ownership; TRANSFER lets the
681:   * owner delegate send rights onward (cap_grant) without re-opening by name.
682:   */
683:  return (int)errno_ret(OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_PORT, name,
684:                                             OS1_RIGHT_READ | OS1_RIGHT_WRITE |
685:                                                 OS1_RIGHT_TRANSFER |
686:                                                 OS1_RIGHT_DUPLICATE,
687:                                             OBJ_TYPE_PORT));
688:}
689:int OS1_port_open(const char *name) {
690:  /* No READ: a client gets a SEND-only capability to an existing service. */
691:  return (int)errno_ret(OS1low_handle_create(
692:      OS1_NS_PORT, name, OS1_RIGHT_WRITE | OS1_RIGHT_DUPLICATE, OBJ_TYPE_PORT));
693:}
694:long OS1_port_send(int handle, const struct ipc_message *msg) {
695:  return errno_ret(OS1_object_write(handle, msg, sizeof(struct ipc_message)));
696:}
697:long OS1_port_send_caps(int handle, struct ipc_message *msg, const int *fds,
698:                        int nfds) {
699:  return errno_ret(_sys_port_send_caps(handle, msg, fds, nfds));
700:}
701:long OS1_port_recv(int handle, struct ipc_message *msg) {
702:  return errno_ret(OS1_object_read(handle, msg, sizeof(struct ipc_message)));
703:}
704:long OS1_object_ctl(int handle, int cmd, long arg) {

724:/* __win_ctl - acquire a WINDOW capability with the rights a verb needs, issue
725: * the control verb, then release the handle.  WRITE for minimize/restore/focus,
726: * DESTROY for close. */
727:static int __win_ctl(int win_id, unsigned int rights, int cmd) {
728:  char idbuf[16];
729:  sprintf(idbuf, "%d", win_id);
730:  long h = _sys_handle_create(OS1_NS_WIN, idbuf, rights, OBJ_TYPE_WINDOW);
731:  if (h < 0)
732:    return (int)h;
733:  long r = _sys_object_ctl((int)h, cmd, 0);
734:  _sys_handle_close((int)h);
735:  return (int)r;
736:}

833:/* OS1_sleep: block for `ms` milliseconds via the REAL kernel timer

898:/* --- Stack protector support ---
899: * __stack_chk_guard: canary value written by the compiler before local arrays
900: * on functions compiled with -fstack-protector.  The value is a fixed constant
901: * rather than a runtime random seed, weakening its effectiveness against local
902: * attacks, but it is sufficient for a debug/development build.

904: * exits.  Must not call any function that itself uses stack protectors to avoid

912:/* ==========================================================================
913: * MODULE 3 — Registry wrappers and the ENVIRONMENT personality
914: * (R1-R10 applied to this module; see the file header's compliance policy)
915: *
916: * Microkernel note (per your correction): OS1_registry_set() below is the
917: * concrete example of the pattern you're pointing at — a registry-write
918: * denial is NOT handled by the kernel deciding what a user should be told.
919: * The kernel enforces CAP_REG_WRITE and returns -EACCES synchronously; THIS
920: * function, in userland, is what turns that into a visible warning, by
921: * sending an ordinary notify() IPC message that nxntfy_srv (a userland
922: * service under sys/bin/, exactly like nxexec for spawn) picks up on its own
923: * blocking recv() and nxbar renders. The kernel never learns notifications
924: * exist. Every later module that touches a "the kernel doesn't do X" gap
925: * gets checked against this same question first: is X actually a service
926: * under sys/bin/nx* already, or genuinely missing.
927: *
928: * op=0 read 'key' into buf; op=1 write 'key' (kernel-side CAP_REG_WRITE +
929: * first-writer-wins ownership); op=2 enumerate, optionally under a prefix.
930: * ========================================================================== */
931:int OS1_registry_get(const char *key, char *buf, size_t size) {
932:  return (int)_sys_registry(0, key, buf, size);
933:}
934:int OS1_registry_set(const char *key, const char *value) {
935:  /* R7/defensive: every current caller in this tree passes a real string
936:   * (verified against the whole source bundle, not assumed) — value is
937:   * ALWAYS a literal or a buffer that was itself checked — but this is a
938:   * public entry point another module can call incorrectly tomorrow, and
939:   * `strlen(NULL)` below would fault the whole process for a one-line
940:   * omission at the call site. Fail the write instead of crashing it. */
941:  if (!key || !value) {
942:    errno = EFAULT;
943:    return -EFAULT;
944:  }
945:  int rc = (int)_sys_registry(1, key, (char *)value, strlen(value));
946:  /* The kernel only ever pr_warn/UART-logs an owner-mismatch denial — it
947:   * must not know about notifications, IPC to a specific service, or any
948:   * other userland concept (kernel/userland separation).  The CALLER
949:   * already gets -EACCES back synchronously right here, so it is the one
950:   * that reports on itself, through the ordinary notify() transport every
951:   * other warning already uses (no kernel involvement, no polling
952:   * anywhere: nxntfy_srv picks it up via its existing blocking recv(),
953:   * nxbar's already-per-frame ring read picks it up from there). */
954:  if (rc == -EACCES)
955:    OS1_notify_warn("registry", key);
956:  return rc;
957:}
958:int OS1_registry_enum(char *buf, size_t size) {
959:  return (int)_sys_registry(2, 0, buf, size);
960:}
961:/* OS1_registry_enum_under (Phase 4.1 A1a): list only keys under 'prefix'. */
962:int OS1_registry_enum_under(const char *prefix, char *buf, size_t size) {
963:  return (int)_sys_registry(2, prefix, buf, size);
964:}
965:/* OS1_registry_del (Phase 4.1 A-gap1): remove a key. */
966:int OS1_registry_del(const char *key) {
967:  return (int)_sys_registry(3, key, 0, 0);
968:}

977: * must keep the buffer alive indefinitely (nxfont uses while(1) yield()).
978: */
979:/* Display / compositor control (ASTRA §6.7): canonical OS1_display_* over the
980: * raw _sys_ stubs.  set_font keeps a bare shim; the others had no bare name. */
981:long OS1_display_info(void) { return _sys_display_info(); }

995:int set_font(void *data, size_t size) {
996:  return OS1_display_set_font(data, size);
997:} /* compat shim (DIR-01 F4) */
998:/* file_read: buf==NULL / size==0 returns the file size without reading data;
999: * used by fopen() to probe file size before allocating a read buffer. */
1000:/* OS1_fs_ functions: canonical (ASTRA §6.3); the bare file_write/file_read/
1001: * list_dir/chdir/getcwd below are compat shims (DIR-01 F4). */
1002:/* OS1_fs_write (M4.5-FS-WRITE resolved): data writes routed through a FILE
1003: * capability, mirroring OS1_fs_read — handle_create(FS, WRITE|CREATE) →
1004: * OBJ_CTL_SEEK(offset) → object_write → close.  OS1_RIGHT_CREATE gives
1005: * open(O_CREAT) semantics (a missing file is created behind the same
1006: * vfs_write_allowed seam the ambient path used), so creation keeps working;
1007: * a size==0 call is the create/truncate-empty idiom: the creation already
1008: * happened at handle_create, nothing to write. */
1009:int OS1_fs_write(const char *path, const void *buf, int size, int offset) {
1010:  if (size < 0) {
1011:    errno = EINVAL;
1012:    return -EINVAL;
1013:  }
1014:  long h = OS1low_handle_create(
1015:      OS1_NS_FS, path, OS1_RIGHT_WRITE | OS1_RIGHT_CREATE, OBJ_TYPE_FILE);
1016:  if (h < 0) {
1017:    errno = (int)-h;
1018:    OS1_report_error(path,
1019:                     (int)h); /* surface EACCES/EIO; ENOENT stays silent */
1020:    return (int)h;
1021:  }
1022:  long w = 0;
1023:  if (size > 0) {
1024:    if (offset > 0)
1025:      OS1_object_ctl((int)h, OBJ_CTL_SEEK, offset);
1026:    w = OS1_object_write((int)h, buf, (unsigned long)size);
1027:  }
1028:  OS1low_handle_close((int)h);
1029:  if (w < 0) {
1030:    errno = (int)-w;
1031:    OS1_report_error(path, (int)w);
1032:  }
1033:  return (int)w;
1034:}
1035:/* OS1_fs_read (F4 M4.5; ambient fallback removed by R1): data reads routed
1036: * through a FILE capability — handle_create(FS,READ) -> OBJ_CTL_SEEK(offset) ->
1037: * object_read -> close.
1038: *
1039: * The size<=0 / NULL-buf call is a metadata size-probe.  It used to fall back
1040: * to the ambient SYS_FILE_READ verb "because the object read does not do that"
1041: * — but OBJ_CTL_STAT does, and always did: the object layer was never missing
1042: * the capability, only this caller was not asking for it.  Probing through the
1043: * handle removes the last libc user of the ambient path (Programme R1) and, in
1044: * passing, makes the probe capability-checked like every other read. */
1045:int OS1_fs_read(const char *path, void *buf, int size, int offset) {
1046:  /* EXIT SEMANTICS ARE PRESERVED EXACTLY.  The old guard was `size <= 0 ||
1047:   * !buf` funnelling into the ambient verb, but the KERNEL branched only on
1048:   * `size`, so the one guard covered three different outcomes and they must
1049:   * stay distinct:
1050:   *
1051:   *   size < 0            (size_t)size wrapped to a huge value, tripping the
1052:   *                       SYSCALL_MAX_IO_BYTES check       -> -EINVAL
1053:   *   size > 0, buf NULL  the kernel read, then copy_to_user(NULL) failed
1054:   *                                                        -> -EFAULT
1055:   *   size == 0           probe: vfs_read_file(path,NULL,0) -> file size,
1056:   *                       any failure reported as          -> -ENOENT
1057:   *
1058:   * Collapsing all three onto "return the size" would have made a negative
1059:   * size and a NULL destination look like successful probes. */
1060:  if (size < 0) {
1061:    errno = EINVAL;
1062:    return -EINVAL;
1063:  }
1064:  if (size > 0 && !buf) {
1065:    errno = EFAULT;
1066:    return -EFAULT;
1067:  }
1068:  if (size == 0) {
1069:    /* THE SIZE-PROBE STANDARD (made explicit here, R1).
1070:     *
1071:     * `size == 0` asks "how big is this file".  That is a STAT question, and a
1072:     * stat has no offset — so the offset argument is meaningless for a probe.
1073:     * The old implementation silently ignored it and returned the total size,
1074:     * which means a caller asking "how many bytes remain after `offset`" got
1075:     * the whole size and no indication it had asked something the API does not
1076:     * answer.  This refuses instead, following the rule this project already
1077:     * applies to the environment ceilings: a silently different value is worse
1078:     * than a failure, because the failure is diagnosable.
1079:     *
1080:     * Verified before enforcing: all 12 probe call sites in the tree pass
1081:     * offset 0 (fopen, font_lib, nxfilem, nxlauncher, rename/truncate,
1082:     * fdtest/writetest/capreg), so no application changes — the standard was
1083:     * already universally observed, it just was not stated or enforced.
1084:     *
1085:     * Probe through the object layer: OBJ_CTL_STAT is exactly "current size in
1086:     * bytes" and resolves it from the same place the ambient verb did
1087:     * (vfs_stat, falling back to the node size), so the value is identical.
1088:     * Read acquisition is ungated (the tree ACL gates writes), so a file
1089:     * readable before is readable now — the probe is simply capability-routed
1090:     * like every other read.  Failure stays -ENOENT to keep the old contract;
1091:     * handle_create knows more (-EACCES, …) but changing what callers observe
1092:     * is a separate decision, not a side effect of this refactor. */
1093:    if (offset != 0) {
1094:      errno = EINVAL;
1095:      return -EINVAL;
1096:    }
1097:    /* ONE syscall.  The first R1 version did handle_create + OBJ_CTL_STAT +
1098:     * close — three syscalls and two path resolutions for one number, on the
1099:     * path every fopen() takes.  SYS_STAT asks the same VFS once. */
1100:    struct abi_stat as;
1101:    if (_sys_stat(path, &as) != 0) {
1102:      errno = ENOENT;
1103:      return -ENOENT;
1104:    }
1105:    return (int)as.size;
1106:  }
1107:  long h = OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, path, OS1_RIGHT_READ, OBJ_TYPE_FILE);
1108:  if (h < 0) {
1109:    errno = (int)-h;
1110:    return (int)h;
1111:  }
1112:  if (offset > 0)
1113:    OS1_object_ctl((int)h, OBJ_CTL_SEEK, offset);
1114:  long r = OS1_object_read((int)h, buf, (unsigned long)size);
1115:  OS1low_handle_close((int)h);
1116:  if (r < 0)
1117:    errno = (int)-r;
1118:  return (int)r;
1119:}
1120:/* OS1_fs_list (R1): a directory is a file you READ.  handle_create(FS,READ) ->
1121: * object_read -> close, the same shape as OS1_fs_read — so listing goes through
1122: * the capability layer like every other read instead of the ambient
1123: * SYS_LIST_DIR verb.
1124: *
1125: * Exit semantics preserved: the ambient verb returned the listing LENGTH and
1126: * -ENOENT for a missing/unreadable path, so acquisition failure maps to
1127: * -ENOENT rather than surfacing handle_create's own errno.  The listing is
1128: * NUL-terminated for callers that treat it as a string (the ambient path
1129: * copied res+1 bytes for exactly that reason). */
1130:int OS1_fs_list(const char *path, char *buf, size_t size) {
1131:  if (!buf || size == 0) {
1132:    errno = EINVAL;
1133:    return -EINVAL;
1134:  }
1135:  long h = OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, path, OS1_RIGHT_READ, OBJ_TYPE_FILE);
1136:  if (h < 0) {
1137:    errno = ENOENT;
1138:    return -ENOENT;
1139:  }
1140:  long r = OS1_object_read((int)h, buf, size - 1);
1141:  OS1low_handle_close((int)h);
1142:  if (r < 0) {
1143:    errno = ENOENT;
1144:    return -ENOENT;
1145:  }
1146:  buf[r] = '\0';
1147:  return (int)r;
1148:}
1149:int OS1_fs_chdir(const char *path) { return _sys_chdir(path); }
1150:int OS1_fs_getcwd(char *buf, size_t size) { return _sys_getcwd(buf, size); }

1152:/* __fs_parent_ctl - split a pathname into a parent directory and one child
1153: * name, acquire the parent with the distinct MUTATE right, then send the
1154: * namespace operation through that capability. The kernel repeats the
1155: * one-component validation: this split is composition convenience, not a
1156: * security boundary. */
1157:static int __fs_parent_ctl(const char *path, int cmd) {
1158:  if (!path)
1159:    return -EFAULT;
1160:
1161:  char work[128];
1162:  size_t len = strlen(path);
1163:  if (len == 0 || len >= sizeof(work))
1164:    return -EINVAL;
1165:  memcpy(work, path, len + 1);
1166:  while (len > 1 && work[len - 1] == '/')
1167:    work[--len] = '\0';
1168:  if (strcmp(work, "/") == 0)
1169:    return -EINVAL;
1170:
1171:  char *leaf = work + len;
1172:  while (leaf > work && leaf[-1] != '/')
1173:    leaf--;
1174:  const char *parent;
1175:  if (leaf == work) {
1176:    parent = ".";
1177:  } else if (leaf == work + 1 && work[0] == '/') {
1178:    parent = "/";
1179:  } else {
1180:    leaf[-1] = '\0';
1181:    parent = work;
1182:  }
1183:  if (!leaf[0])
1184:    return -EINVAL;
1185:
1186:  long h =
1187:      OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, parent, OS1_RIGHT_MUTATE, OBJ_TYPE_FILE);
1188:  if (h < 0)
1189:    return (int)h;
1190:  long r = OS1_object_ctl((int)h, cmd, (long)leaf);
1191:  OS1low_handle_close((int)h);
1192:  return (int)r;
1193:}
1194:
1195:int OS1_fs_mkdir(const char *path) {
1196:  return __fs_parent_ctl(path, OBJ_CTL_MKDIR);
1197:}
1198:int OS1_fs_unlink(const char *path) {
1199:  return __fs_parent_ctl(path, OBJ_CTL_UNLINK);
1200:}
1201:int file_write(const char *path, const void *buf, int size, int offset) {
1202:  return OS1_fs_write(path, buf, size, offset);
1203:}
1204:int file_read(const char *path, void *buf, int size, int offset) {
1205:  return OS1_fs_read(path, buf, size, offset);
1206:}
1207:int list_dir(const char *path, char *buf, size_t size) {
1208:  return OS1_fs_list(path, buf, size);
1209:}
1210:int chdir(const char *path) { return OS1_fs_chdir(path); }
1211:int getcwd(char *buf, size_t size) { return OS1_fs_getcwd(buf, size); }

1213:/*
1214: * open - POSIX fd open (ABI-03 fd table).
1215: *
1216: * The create/truncate/append semantics live in the kernel now: SYS_OPEN
1217: * honours O_CREAT/O_TRUNC through the VFS write-ACL + create seam (ASTRA §6.8,
1218: * kernel/core/syscall_dispatch.c).  libc keeps only the POSIX personality
1219: * work: pass the flags straight through, map the negative errno (errno_ret),
1220: * surface a protected-path denial on the standard notify() transport, and set
1221: * the initial position for O_APPEND (a fresh handle starts at offset 0, and
1222: * the kernel does not track per-write append).  The variadic mode argument is
1223: * accepted but not applied (the ext4 driver fixes new-file perms).
1224: */
1225:int open(const char *pathname, int flags, ...) {
1226:  int fd = (int)_sys_open(pathname, flags);
1227:  if (fd < 0) {
1228:    /* Uniform surfacing (Phase 0): amber on EACCES, red on a hard fault,
1229:     * silent on an ENOENT probe — the policy lives in OS1_report_error, not
1230:     * here, so every open() caller and every portability layer behave alike.
1231:     * The report now happens INSIDE the errno seam (see errno_ret_ctx); this
1232:     * site passes the path so the notification still names the file rather
1233:     * than the generic "libc", and reports ONCE instead of twice. */
1234:    return (int)errno_ret_ctx(fd, pathname);
1235:  }
1236:  if (flags & O_APPEND)
1237:    _sys_lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_END); /* best-effort: initial position at EOF */
1238:  return fd;
1239:}
1240:int close(int fd) { return (int)errno_ret(_sys_close(fd)); }
1241:long lseek(int fd, long offset, int whence) {
1242:  return errno_ret(_sys_lseek(fd, offset, whence));
1243:}

1245:/* --- Formatting & Printing ---
1246: * All formatting functions delegate to vsnprintf() from kernel/lib/vsnprintf.c
1247: * (included above).  Output goes to fd 1 (the shell/window TTY) via write().
1248: *
1249: * printf: uses a 256-byte stack buffer; output longer than 255 chars is
1250: * silently truncated by vsnprintf.
1251: *
1252: * printf_win: like printf but writes to a specific compositor window by id
1253: * via window_write() (the dedicated SYS_WINDOW_WRITE, #123) — no longer the
1254: * fd>=100 overload on write().
1255: *
1256: * vsprintf/sprintf: pass 65536 as the size limit — effectively unbounded.
1257: * Callers are responsible for providing a large enough destination buffer;
1258: * overflow is not detected.
1259: *
1260: * print_hex: renders a 64-bit value as 18-char "0xHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH" string
1261: * written directly via write(), bypassing the format engine.
1262: */
1263:int vsprintf(char *out, const char *fmt, va_list args) {
1264:  return vsnprintf(out, 65536, fmt, args);
1265:}
1266:int printf(const char *fmt, ...) {
1267:  char buf[256];
1268:  va_list args;
1269:  va_start(args, fmt);
1270:  int res = vsnprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), fmt, args);
1271:  va_end(args);
1272:  write(1, buf, strlen(buf));
1273:  return res;
1274:}
1275:void window_write(int win_id, const char *buf, unsigned long count) {
1276:  OS1_window_write(win_id, buf, count);
1277:}
1278:int window_of_pid(int pid) { return OS1_window_of_pid(pid); }
1279:int window_grid(int win_id, int *cols, int *rows) {
1280:  return OS1_window_grid(win_id, cols, rows);
1281:}
1282:void printf_win(int win_id, const char *fmt, ...) {
1283:  char buf[512];
1284:  va_list args;
1285:  va_start(args, fmt);
1286:  vsnprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), fmt, args);
1287:  va_end(args);
1288:  _sys_window_write(win_id, buf, strlen(buf));
1289:}
1290:int sprintf(char *out, const char *fmt, ...) {
1291:  va_list args;
1292:  va_start(args, fmt);
1293:  int res = vsnprintf(out, 65536, fmt, args);
1294:  va_end(args);
1295:  return res;
1296:}

1298:  va_list args;

1300:  int res = vsnprintf(out, size, fmt, args);
1301:  va_end(args);

1304:int asprintf(char **strp, const char *fmt, ...) {
1305:  if (!strp)
1306:    return -1;
1307:  va_list args;
1308:  va_start(args, fmt);
1309:  int res = vasprintf(strp, fmt, args);
1310:  va_end(args);
1311:  return res;
1312:}
1313:int vasprintf(char **strp, const char *fmt, va_list ap) {
1314:  if (!strp || !fmt)
1315:    return -1;
1316:
1317:  va_list ap2;
1318:  va_copy(ap2, ap);
1319:  int needed = vsnprintf(NULL, 0, fmt, ap2);
1320:  va_end(ap2);
1321:  if (needed < 0)
1322:    return -1;
1323:
1324:  char *buf = malloc((size_t)needed + 1U);
1325:  if (!buf)
1326:    return -1;
1327:
1328:  int written = vsnprintf(buf, (size_t)needed + 1U, fmt, ap);
1329:  if (written < 0) {
1330:    free(buf);
1331:    return -1;
1332:  }
1333:
1334:  *strp = buf;
1335:  return written;
1336:}

1339:  if (!resultp || !format)
1340:    return -1;

1342:  va_list args2;
1343:  va_copy(args2, args);
1344:  int needed = vsnprintf(NULL, 0, format, args2);
1345:  va_end(args2);
1346:  if (needed < 0)
1347:    return -1;

1349:  char *buf = malloc((size_t)needed + 1U);
1350:  if (!buf)
1351:    return -1;
1352:
1353:  int written = vsnprintf(buf, (size_t)needed + 1U, format, args);
1354:  if (written < 0) {
1355:    free(buf);
1356:    return -1;
1357:  }
1358:
1359:  *resultp = buf;
1360:  return (ptrdiff_t)written;
1361:}
1362:void print(const char *s) { write(1, s, strlen(s)); }
1363:/* print_hex: manual 16-nibble hex formatter for a 64-bit value. */
1364:void print_hex(unsigned long val) {
1365:  char buf[18];
1366:  buf[0] = '0';
1367:  buf[1] = 'x';
1368:  for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
1369:    int digit = (val >> ((15 - i) * 4)) & 0xF;
1370:    buf[2 + i] = (digit < 10) ? ('0' + digit) : ('A' + digit - 10);
1371:  }
1372:  write(1, buf, 18);
1373:}

1375:/* --- Standard IO ---
1376: * getchar: blocking single-char read from fd 0 (keyboard).
1377: * putchar: writes one character to fd 1 (TTY/window).
1378: * gets: line-buffered input with backspace handling; size-bounded to avoid
1379: *   overflow (stops at size-1 chars).  Echoes characters to fd 1 and handles
1380: *   \b/DEL with the terminal backspace-space-backspace sequence.
1381: */
1382:int getchar(void) {
1383:  char c;
1384:  if (read(0, &c, 1) == 1)
1385:    return (unsigned char)c;
1386:  return -1;
1387:}
1388:int putchar(int c) {
1389:  char ch = (char)c;
1390:  write(1, &ch, 1);
1391:  return c;
1392:}
1393:char *gets(char *s, int size) {
1394:  int i = 0;
1395:  while (i < size - 1) {
1396:    int c = getchar();
1397:    if (c < 0)
1398:      break;
1399:    if (c == '\b' || c == 127) {
1400:      if (i > 0) {
1401:        i--;
1402:        write(1, "\b \b", 3);
1403:      }
1404:      continue;
1405:    }
1406:    putchar(c);
1407:    if (c == '\n' || c == '\r') {
1408:      s[i] = '\0';
1409:      return s;
1410:    }
1411:    s[i++] = (char)c;
1412:  }
1413:  s[i] = '\0';
1414:  return s;
1415:}

1417:/*
1418: * notify - send a system notification via IPC to the notification server.
1419: *
1420: * title: short label (up to 30 chars copied); truncated silently if longer.
1421: * msg:   message body (up to 33 remaining chars after "title: "); truncated.
1422: *
1423: * The payload is assembled as "title: msg\0" into imsg.payload[64].
1424: * The target PID is read from the global registry key "srv.notify_pid".
1425: * Falls back to PID 2 if the key is absent (pid=2 is the expected notify_srv
1426: * PID under the current fixed-order spawn sequence in init.c).
1427: *
1428: * NOTE(USR-SEC-01): registry_read("srv.notify_pid", ...) has no authentication;
1429: * any process can overwrite that key to redirect all notifications to itself,
1430: * effectively hijacking the system notification channel.
1431: *
1432: * Returns the result of send() (0 on success, negative on failure).
1433: */
1434:/* notify_send - post a notification with a severity (0=info, 1=warning/yellow,
1435: * 2=error/red) in data1, which nxntfy_srv renders as the popup colour. */
1436:static int notify_send(const char *title, const char *msg, int sev) {
1437:  struct ipc_message imsg;
1438:  imsg.type = IPC_TYPE_NOTIFY;
1439:  imsg.data1 = (uint64_t)sev;
1440:  imsg.data2 = 0;
1441:  int i = 0;
1442:  /* Pack "title: msg" into the 64-byte payload field.
1443:   * 30-char limit for title leaves room for ": " and at least 32 msg chars. */
1444:  while (*title && i < 30)
1445:    imsg.payload[i++] = *title++;
1446:  imsg.payload[i++] = ':';
1447:  imsg.payload[i++] = ' ';
1448:  while (*msg && i < 63)
1449:    imsg.payload[i++] = *msg++;
1450:  imsg.payload[i] = '\0';
1451:  /* Resolve the notify_srv endpoint from the registry. If the key is absent
1452:   * (notify_srv not up / not yet registered) FAIL instead of sending to a
1453:   * guessed PID — the old pid=2 fallback delivered a stray IPC message to
1454:   * whatever process happened to hold PID 2 and the notification was lost
1455:   * anyway. Callers that need the boot popup wait for the key (see init.c). */
1456:  char pid_buf[16];
1457:  if (OS1_registry_get("srv.notify_pid", pid_buf, sizeof(pid_buf)) != 0)
1458:    return -1;
1459:  int pid = atoi(pid_buf);
1460:  if (pid <= 0)
1461:    return -1;
1462:  return (int)OS1low_ipc_send(pid, &imsg);
1463:}
1464:int OS1_notify_post(const char *title, const char *msg) {
1465:  return notify_send(title, msg, 0);
1466:}
1467:int OS1_notify_warn(const char *title, const char *msg) {
1468:  return notify_send(title, msg, 1);
1469:} /* yellow */
1470:int OS1_notify_error(const char *title, const char *msg) {
1471:  return notify_send(title, msg, 2);
1472:} /* red — previously only the kernel crash handler (fault.c) could reach
1473:   * severity 2 (m.data1 = 2, kernel_ipc_send bypassing this function
1474:   * entirely); userland callers can now post one directly too. */
1475:int notify(const char *title, const char *msg) {
1476:  return notify_send(title, msg, 0);
1477:} /* compat shim (DIR-01 F4) */
1478:
1479:/* --- Doom/LibC Compatibility ---
1480: * FILE emulation: a FILE* is a heap-allocated struct (defined in os1.h) that
1481: * records the file path, current byte position, error/eof flags, and cached
1482: * size.  All I/O is synchronous and unbuffered; every fread/fwrite call maps
1483: * directly to a file_read/file_write syscall with the current offset.
1484: */
1485:
1486:/*
1487: * fopen - open a file for buffered I/O emulation.
1488: *
1489: * Allocates a FILE struct, stores the path, probes the file size via
1490: * file_read(path, NULL, 0, 0).  SIZE-PROBE CONVENTION: the trigger is
1491: * `size == 0` (NOT `buf == NULL`, which this comment used to claim — the
1492: * distinction matters because `buf == NULL` with a NON-zero size is an error,
1493: * -EFAULT, not a probe).  `offset` must be 0: a size has no offset, and passing
1494: * one is refused with -EINVAL rather than silently answered with the total.
1495: * Returns NULL if the file does not exist and mode is "r" (read-only).
1496: * Write modes ("w", "a") do not fail on missing files — file_write will
1497: * create them on demand via the kernel VFS.
1498: */
1499:FILE *fopen(const char *path, const char *mode) {
1500:  FILE *f = malloc(sizeof(FILE));
1501:  if (!f) {
1502:    errno = ENOMEM;
1503:    return NULL;
1504:  }
1505:  /* Zero EVERY field: malloc reuses dirty blocks, and a stale has_ungetc
1506:   * injected a ghost byte at the start of the first fread (doom read
1507:   * "\0IWA" instead of "IWAD" after its 9-file IWAD probe loop), while a
1508:   * stale is_tmp made fclose() unlink real files.  memset is the whole
1509:   * fix; pos/error/eof/has_ungetc/is_tmp start 0 by definition. */
1510:  memset(f, 0, sizeof(FILE));
1511:  f->fd = -1;
1512:  strncpy(f->path, path, sizeof(f->path) - 1);
1513:  /* Probe file size; file_read with NULL buf and size=0 returns byte count.
1514:   * On a miss it sets errno (ENOENT/EACCES) — preserved below so a failed
1515:   * fopen reports the real reason (luaL_fileresult/strerror), not "Success". */
1516:  f->size = file_read(path, NULL, 0, 0);
1517:  if (f->size < 0 && mode[0] == 'r') {
1518:    int e = errno;
1519:    free(f);
1520:    errno = e; /* free() must not mask the open failure's errno */
1521:    return NULL;
1522:  }
1523:  /* Write mode truncates to empty NOW (POSIX "w"): unlink + zero-byte create,
1524:   * so the file both exists and is emptied before any fwrite — the old lazy
1525:   * path left stale trailing bytes when overwriting a longer file. Append
1526:   * mode ("a") creates-if-missing and starts the position at EOF. */
1527:  if (mode[0] == 'w') {
1528:    /* Create-and-truncate in one call: a from-start write (offset 0) now
1529:     * truncates on the FS side (ext4_write), so a zero-byte write both
1530:     * materialises a missing file and empties an existing one — no unlink
1531:     * needed, and the inode (perms/links) is preserved instead of churned. */
1532:    if (OS1_fs_write(path, "", 0, 0) < 0) {
1533:      int e = errno;
1534:      free(f);
1535:      errno = e;
1536:      return NULL;
1537:    }
1538:    f->size = 0;
1539:  } else if (mode[0] == 'a') {
1540:    if (f->size < 0) {
1541:      if (OS1_fs_write(path, "", 0, 0) < 0) {
1542:        int e = errno;
1543:        free(f);
1544:        errno = e;
1545:        return NULL;
1546:      }
1547:      f->size = 0;
1548:    }
1549:    f->pos = f->size;
1550:  }
1551:
1552:  /*
1553:   * Open a REAL handle and keep it for the stream's lifetime.
1554:   *
1555:   * Before this, a path-backed FILE carried fd = -1 and EVERY fread/fwrite did
1556:   * handle_create + seek + read/write + close — four syscalls and, far worse, a
1557:   * full VFS PATH RESOLUTION per call.  doom reads a savegame a byte at a time
1558:   * (saveg_read8), so a ~100 KB save meant ~100 000 path resolutions: that is
1559:   * the multi-minute load, and it is the "positional per-byte fread through the
1560:   * FILE layer + handle-per-call" item the plan logged at 17d.
1561:   *
1562:   * Now the handle is opened once and the KERNEL owns the offset.  fread/fwrite
1563:   * are one syscall with no resolution; fseek moves the kernel offset with
1564:   * lseek.  fp->pos is kept as a mirror so ftell costs nothing.
1565:   *
1566:   * A failure here is NOT fatal: the stream falls back to the positional path
1567:   * (fd stays -1), which still works.  Losing speed is acceptable; losing the
1568:   * ability to open a file is not — and the write modes above have already
1569:   * created/truncated, so the file exists either way. */
1570:  {
1571:    int oflags;
1572:    if (mode[0] == 'r')
1573:      oflags =
1574:          (mode[1] == '+' || (mode[1] && mode[2] == '+')) ? O_RDWR : O_RDONLY;
1575:    else
1576:      oflags = O_RDWR; /* "w"/"a" already created+positioned above */
1577:    int h = open(path, oflags);
1578:    if (h >= 0) {
1579:      f->fd = h;
1580:      /* Align the kernel offset with the logical one ("a" starts at EOF). */
1581:      if (f->pos != 0)
1582:        lseek(h, f->pos, SEEK_SET);
1583:    }
1584:  }
1585:  return f;
1586:}
1587:
1588:FILE *freopen(const char *filename, const char *mode, FILE *stream) {
1589:  if (stream) {
1590:    fclose(stream);
1591:  }
1592:  return fopen(filename, mode);
1593:}
1594:
1595:static int file_fd(FILE *fp);
1596:
1597:/*
1598: * fstream_flush - write out the pending write buffer of a positional stream.
1599: *
1600: * The buffered bytes' on-disk offset is (pos - wcount): fwrite advances the
1601: * logical position as it accumulates, so the buffer start trails 'pos' by the
1602: * pending count.  A no-op for read streams and the console std streams, whose
1603: * wcount stays 0.  On a short/failed write the error flag is set.  Returns 0 on
1604: * success, EOF on error.
1605: */
1606:static int fstream_flush(FILE *fp) {
1607:  if (!fp || fp->wcount <= 0)
1608:    return 0;
1609:  int at = fp->pos - fp->wcount;
1610:  if (at < 0)
1611:    at = 0;
1612:  int pending = fp->wcount;
1613:  int w;
1614:  if (fp->fd >= 0) {
1615:    /* Flush through the stream's own handle: one syscall, no path resolution.
1616:     * lseek first because the buffer's on-disk offset trails the logical
1617:     * position by the pending count, and interleaved reads may have moved the
1618:     * kernel offset since. */
1619:    lseek(fp->fd, at, SEEK_SET);
1620:    long r = write(fp->fd, fp->wbuf, (unsigned long)pending);
1621:    w = (int)r;
1622:    if (r > 0)
1623:      lseek(fp->fd, fp->pos, SEEK_SET); /* restore the logical position */
1624:  } else {
1625:    w = file_write(fp->path, fp->wbuf, pending, at);
1626:  }
1627:  fp->wcount = 0;
1628:  /* The file just changed: any cached read window may now be stale. */
1629:  fp->rcount = 0;
1630:  fp->rhead = 0;
1631:  if (w < 0 || w < pending) {
1632:    fp->error = 1;
1633:    return EOF;
1634:  }
1635:  return 0;
1636:}
1637:
1638:/*
1639: * fclose - flush any pending writes, then release a FILE handle.
1640: */
1641:/*
1642: * fdopen - wrap an ALREADY-OPEN descriptor in a FILE* (POSIX).  The stream is
1643: * fd-backed: fread/fwrite go straight through read()/write() on that fd, so it
1644: * works for any object the descriptor names — a file, a console, or a PIPE end
1645: * (`int p[2]; pipe(p); FILE *f = fdopen(p[0], "r");`), which is the usual way
1646: * ported POSIX code consumes a pipe through stdio.  'mode' is accepted for
1647: * source compatibility; the descriptor's own rights are the real authority
1648: * (the kernel rejects a read of a write-only handle), so we do not re-derive
1649: * access from the string.  Returns NULL on a bad fd or out of memory.
1650: */
1651:FILE *fdopen(int fd, const char *mode) {
1652:  (void)mode;
1653:  if (fd < 0) {
1654:    errno = EBADF;
1655:    return 0;
1656:  }
1657:  FILE *f = malloc(sizeof(FILE));
1658:  if (!f) {
1659:    errno = ENOMEM;
1660:    return 0;
1661:  }
1662:  memset(f, 0, sizeof(FILE));
1663:  f->fd = fd;   /* fd-backed: file_fd() routes I/O through read()/write() */
1664:  f->size = -1; /* unknown until asked */
1665:  return f;
1666:}
1667:
1668:int fclose(FILE *fp) {
1669:  if (fp && fp != stdin && fp != stdout && fp != stderr) {
1670:    fstream_flush(fp);
1671:    if (fp->is_tmp) {
1672:      OS1_fs_unlink(fp->path);
1673:    }
1674:    /* The stream owns its descriptor (POSIX): closing the stream closes it.
1675:     * This now covers fopen'd streams too — they hold a real handle for their
1676:     * lifetime instead of reopening per call — as well as fdopen'd ones.  A
1677:     * stream whose open failed carries fd = -1 and owns nothing. */
1678:    if (fp->fd >= 0)
1679:      close(fp->fd);
1680:    free(fp);
1681:  }
1682:  return 0;
1683:}
1684:
1685:size_t fread(void *ptr, size_t size, size_t nmemb, FILE *fp) {
1686:  if (!fp)
1687:    return 0;
1688:  if (size == 0 || nmemb == 0)
1689:    return 0;
1690:
1691:  /* Read-after-write consistency: persist any buffered writes before reading
1692:   * so an interleaved read at this position sees them on disk. */
1693:  fstream_flush(fp);
1694:
1695:  size_t bytes = size * nmemb;
1696:  char *buf = (char *)ptr;
1697:  size_t read_bytes = 0;
1698:
1699:  if (fp->has_ungetc) {
1700:    buf[0] = (char)fp->ungetc_buf;
1701:    fp->has_ungetc = 0;
1702:    read_bytes = 1;
1703:    if (bytes == 1) {
1704:      return 1 / size;
1705:    }
1706:  }
1707:
1708:  int fd = file_fd(fp);
1709:  if (fd >= 0 && fp->path[0] == '\0') {
1710:    /* Console/pipe: unbuffered, and never seekable. */
1711:    long r = read(fd, buf + read_bytes, bytes - read_bytes);
1712:    if (r < 0) {
1713:      fp->error = 1;
1714:      return 0;
1715:    }
1716:    fp->pos += (int)r;
1717:    if (r == 0 && bytes > read_bytes)
1718:      fp->eof = 1;
1719:    read_bytes += r;
1720:    return read_bytes / size;
1721:  }
1722:  if (fd >= 0) {
1723:    /*
1724:     * BUFFERED read for a file stream, symmetric with the write buffer and for
1725:     * the same filesystem reason: ext4 fetches a whole 4 KiB block for any
1726:     * partial read, so an unbuffered byte-at-a-time reader re-reads the same
1727:     * block once per byte.  doom loads savegames exactly that way — that is
1728:     * the multi-minute load, and buffering is what removes it, not the handle
1729:     * cache alone.
1730:     */
1731:    while (read_bytes < bytes) {
1732:      if (fp->rhead >= fp->rcount) { /* window exhausted: refill from pos */
1733:        fp->rbase = fp->pos;
1734:        fp->rhead = 0;
1735:        fp->rcount = 0;
1736:        lseek(fd, fp->pos, SEEK_SET);
1737:        long r = read(fd, fp->rbuf, FILE_RBUF_SIZE);
1738:        if (r < 0) {
1739:          fp->error = 1;
1740:          break;
1741:        }
1742:        if (r == 0) {
1743:          fp->eof = 1;
1744:          break;
1745:        }
1746:        fp->rcount = (int)r;
1747:      }
1748:      size_t avail = (size_t)(fp->rcount - fp->rhead);
1749:      size_t want = bytes - read_bytes;
1750:      size_t take = avail < want ? avail : want;
1751:      memcpy(buf + read_bytes, fp->rbuf + fp->rhead, take);
1752:      fp->rhead += (int)take;
1753:      fp->pos += (int)take;
1754:      read_bytes += take;
1755:    }
1756:    return read_bytes / size;
1757:  }
1758:  int rem_bytes = bytes - read_bytes;
1759:  int r = file_read(fp->path, buf + read_bytes, rem_bytes, fp->pos);
1760:  if (r < 0) {
1761:    fp->error = 1;
1762:    return 0;
1763:  }
1764:  fp->pos += r;
1765:  read_bytes += r;
1766:  if (r < rem_bytes)
1767:    fp->eof = 1;
1768:  return read_bytes / size;
1769:}
1770:
1771:size_t fwrite(const void *ptr, size_t size, size_t nmemb, FILE *fp) {
1772:  if (!fp)
1773:    return 0;
1774:  if (size == 0 || nmemb == 0)
1775:    return 0;
1776:
1777:  /* Write-after-read consistency, the mirror of the flush fread() does before
1778:   * reading.  The cached read window may cover the bytes about to change, and
1779:   * rhead does not move when a write advances pos — so a read following a write
1780:   * would otherwise be served stale bytes from the OLD position.  Dropping the
1781:   * window costs one refill and removes the whole hazard. */
1782:  fp->rcount = 0;
1783:  fp->rhead = 0;
1784:
1785:  size_t bytes = size * nmemb;
1786:  int fd = file_fd(fp);
1787:  /* CONSOLE/pipe streams only (no path): unbuffered, because interactive output
1788:   * must appear now.  A FILE-backed stream must NOT take this branch even
1789:   * though it now has an fd — buffering is not about syscall count here, it is
1790:   * about the FILESYSTEM: ext4_write does a read-modify-write of a whole 4 KiB
1791:   * block for any partial write, so an unbuffered byte-at-a-time writer costs
1792:   * one 4 KiB read + 4 KiB write PER BYTE.  doom saves exactly that way, and
1793:   * bypassing the buffer made saving look like a hang.  FILE_WBUF_SIZE is 4096
1794:   * precisely so a full buffer is one whole block. */
1795:  if (fd >= 0 && fp->path[0] == '\0') {
1796:    long w = write(fd, ptr, bytes);
1797:    if (w < 0) {
1798:      fp->error = 1;
1799:      return 0;
1800:    }
1801:    fp->pos += (int)w;
1802:    if (fp->pos > fp->size)
1803:      fp->size = fp->pos;
1804:    return w / size;
1805:  }
1806:
1807:  /* Positional (path-backed) stream: coalesce into the write buffer, flushing a
1808:   * full buffer to one file_write syscall.  This turns a per-byte/per-field
1809:   * fwrite loop into one syscall per FILE_WBUF_SIZE, which is what standard C
1810:   * stdio buffering does — the fix for incremental writers stalling on a
1811:   * syscall-per-call storm. */
1812:  const unsigned char *src = (const unsigned char *)ptr;
1813:  size_t done = 0;
1814:  while (done < bytes) {
1815:    if (fp->wcount == FILE_WBUF_SIZE && fstream_flush(fp) != 0)
1816:      break; /* flush failed: fp->error set, report the partial count */
1817:    int room = FILE_WBUF_SIZE - fp->wcount;
1818:    size_t chunk = bytes - done;
1819:    if (chunk > (size_t)room)
1820:      chunk = (size_t)room;
1821:    memcpy(fp->wbuf + fp->wcount, src + done, chunk);
1822:    fp->wcount += (int)chunk;
1823:    fp->pos += (int)chunk;
1824:    done += chunk;
1825:  }
1826:  return done / size;
1827:}
1828:
1829:int fseek(FILE *fp, long offset, int whence) {
1830:  if (!fp)
1831:    return -1;
1832:  /* Persist pending writes before the position moves: the buffer's on-disk
1833:   * offset is derived from the current pos, so it must be flushed here. */
1834:  fstream_flush(fp);
1835:  if (whence == SEEK_SET)
1836:    fp->pos = offset;
1837:  else if (whence == SEEK_CUR)
1838:    fp->pos += offset;
1839:  else if (whence == SEEK_END) {
1840:    if (fp->size < 0)
1841:      fp->size = file_read(fp->path, NULL, 0, 0);
1842:    fp->pos = fp->size + offset;
1843:  }
1844:  if (fp->pos < 0)
1845:    fp->pos = 0;
1846:  /* POSIX: "a successful call to fseek() shall undo any effects of ungetc()".
1847:   * The pushback byte belongs to the OLD position, so carrying it across a seek
1848:   * would inject a stray byte at the new one.  Latent before — the positional
1849:   * path re-read from the file every time — and made reachable by the read
1850:   * window, which is exactly the kind of dormant deviation a buffer exposes. */
1851:  fp->has_ungetc = 0;
1852:  /* A handle-backed stream keeps its offset in the KERNEL, so moving the
1853:   * logical position must move that too — otherwise fread would keep reading
1854:   * from wherever the last read left off and silently ignore the seek.  Only
1855:   * for path-backed streams: seeking a console/pipe is meaningless, and those
1856:   * carry no path. */
1857:  if (fp->fd >= 0 && fp->path[0]) {
1858:    /* Keep the read window if it still covers the new position — a savegame
1859:     * reader that seeks backwards a few bytes then continues would otherwise
1860:     * refill on every seek and lose the buffering entirely.  Otherwise drop
1861:     * it; a stale window would serve bytes from the OLD offset. */
1862:    if (fp->rcount > 0 && fp->pos >= fp->rbase &&
1863:        fp->pos < fp->rbase + fp->rcount) {
1864:      fp->rhead = fp->pos - fp->rbase;
1865:    } else {
1866:      fp->rcount = 0;
1867:      fp->rhead = 0;
1868:    }
1869:    lseek(fp->fd, fp->pos, SEEK_SET);
1870:  }
1871:  fp->eof = 0;
1872:  return 0;
1873:}
1874:
1875:long ftell(FILE *fp) {
1876:  if (!fp)
1877:    return -1;
1878:  /* pos already includes buffered-but-unflushed bytes (fwrite advances it as it
1879:   * accumulates), so this is the correct logical position. */
1880:  return fp->pos;
1881:}
1882:
1883:int fseeko(FILE *fp, off_t offset, int whence) {
1884:  return fseek(fp, (long)offset, whence);
1885:}
1886:
1887:off_t ftello(FILE *fp) {
1888:  return (off_t)ftell(fp);
1889:}

1893:void fseterr(FILE *fp) { if (fp) fp->error = 1; }
1894:void clearerr(FILE *fp) { if (fp) { fp->error = 0; fp->eof = 0; } }
1895:int fileno(FILE *fp) { return fp ? fp->fd : -1; }

1897:char *strdup(const char *s) {
1898:  size_t len = strlen(s) + 1;
1899:  char *res = malloc(len);
1900:  if (res)
1901:    memcpy(res, s, len);
1902:  return res;
1903:}

1905:char *strndup(const char *s, size_t n) {
1906:  if (!s)
1907:    return NULL;
1908:  size_t len = 0;
1909:  while (len < n && s[len])
1910:    len++;
1911:  char *res = malloc(len + 1);
1912:  if (res) {
1913:    memcpy(res, s, len);
1914:    res[len] = '\0';
1915:  }
1916:  return res;
1917:}

1922:/* --- Standard Input Library ---
1923: * Input events are delivered as IPC messages from the kernel input driver.
1924: * IPC_TYPE_INPUT carries keyboard data; IPC_TYPE_MOUSE carries mouse data.
1925: * Both are received non-blocking via try_recv(-1, ...) — poll any sender.
1926: */
1927:
1928:/*
1929: * input_poll_event - check for and decode the next pending input event.
1930: *
1931: * event: output parameter filled on success.
1932: *
1933: * Returns 1 if an event was decoded (event is valid), 0 if no message was
1934: * waiting or the message type is not a recognised input type.
1935: *
1936: * IPC_TYPE_INPUT layout (data1/data2/payload):
1937: *   data1 low byte : ASCII key code (keyboard.key)
1938: *   data1 bits 16+ : HID scancode   (keyboard.scancode)
1939: *   data2           : key state (0=released, 1=pressed, 2=repeat)
1940: *   payload[0..7]  : UTF-8 encoded character (up to 4 bytes + NUL)
1941: *
1942: * IPC_TYPE_MOUSE layout:
1943: *   data1  : button mask
1944: *   data2  : button state (pressed=1)
1945: *   payload[0..3]  : x coordinate (int32, little-endian)
1946: *   payload[4..7]  : y coordinate (int32, little-endian)
1947: *
1948: * Note: memcpy is used for mouse coordinates to handle potential alignment
1949: * constraints on the int fields within the packed payload array.
1950: */
1951:int input_poll_event(input_event_t *event) {
1952:  struct ipc_message msg;
1953:  if (try_recv(-1, &msg) < 0)
1954:    return 0;
1955:
1956:  if (msg.type == IPC_TYPE_INPUT) {
1957:    event->type = INPUT_TYPE_KEYBOARD;
1958:    event->keyboard.key = (unsigned char)(msg.data1 & 0xFF);
1959:    event->keyboard.scancode = (uint16_t)(msg.data1 >> 16);
1960:    event->keyboard.state = (int)msg.data2;
1961:    memcpy(event->keyboard.utf8, msg.payload, 8);
1962:    return 1;
1963:  } else if (msg.type == IPC_TYPE_MOUSE) {
1964:    event->type = INPUT_TYPE_MOUSE;
1965:    event->mouse.button = (int)msg.data1;
1966:    event->mouse.state = (int)msg.data2;
1967:    memcpy(&event->mouse.x, msg.payload, 4);
1968:    memcpy(&event->mouse.y, msg.payload + 4, 4);
1969:    return 1;
1970:  } else if (msg.type == IPC_TYPE_RESIZE) {
1971:    /* GFX-DYN-01: the compositor told us our window's new logical size. */
1972:    event->type = INPUT_TYPE_RESIZE;
1973:    event->resize.w = (int)msg.data1;
1974:    event->resize.h = (int)msg.data2;
1975:    return 1;
1976:  } else if (msg.type == IPC_TYPE_NOTIFY && msg.data2 == IPC_LOOK_PING_MAGIC) {
1977:    /* Silent compositor look-changed ping (nxres_broadcast_look, nxres.h),
1978:     * tagged via data2 so it is never confused with a real notify() call.
1979:     * Surfaced here (not drained by a second, competing try_recv() loop
1980:     * elsewhere) so this stays the single consumer of the mailbox — a
1981:     * second loop would silently steal keyboard/mouse messages before this
1982:     * function ever saw them. */
1983:    event->type = INPUT_TYPE_LOOK_CHANGED;
1984:    return 1;
1985:  }
1986:  return 0;
1987:}

2015:/*
2016: * graphics_draw_text - render text into a compositor window.
2017: *
2018: * Uses the OS1 packed bitmap font path when /fonts/Rewir-Light.off is present,
2019: * preserving x/y positioning and color. If the font is unavailable, falls back
2020: * to the compositor terminal writer for bootstrapping compatibility.
2021: *
2022: * Returns the rendered advance in pixels, or 0 for invalid input.
2023: */
2024:int graphics_draw_text(int win_id, int x, int y, const char *text,
2025:                       uint32_t color) {
2026:  if (win_id < 0 || !text)
2027:    return 0;
2028:
2029:  struct font_ctx *font = graphics_get_default_font();
2030:  if (font) {
2031:    font_draw_string(win_id, font, x, y, text, color);
2032:    return font_string_width(font, text);
2033:  }
2034:
2035:  (void)x;
2036:  (void)y;
2037:  (void)color;
2038:  _sys_window_write(win_id, text, strlen(text));
2039:  return (int)strlen(text) * 8;
2040:}

2050:

2054:#define OS1_IMAGE_MAX_FILE_BYTES (16u * 1024u * 1024u)
2055:#define OS1_IMAGE_MAX_DIMENSION 4096
2056:#define OS1_IMAGE_MAX_PIXELS (4096u * 4096u)

2058:/*
2059: * graphics_load_image - load an encoded image into sanitized ARGB32 pixels.
2060: *
2061: * Encoded input is treated as hostile data: it is copied into a bounded scratch
2062: * buffer, probed before decode, rejected on dimension/pixel/file caps, decoded
2063: * to a temporary RGBA plane, then copied into an OS1-owned ARGB buffer.  The
2064: * caller never sees encoded bytes or decoder-owned storage, which keeps image
2065: * rendering an inert pixel operation suitable for the stdimage base API.
2066: */
2067:uint32_t *graphics_load_image(const char *path, int *w, int *h) {
2068:  if (!path || !w || !h)
2069:    return NULL;
2070:
2071:  *w = 0;
2072:  *h = 0;
2073:
2074:  long handle =
2075:      OS1low_handle_create(OS1_NS_FS, path, OS1_RIGHT_READ, OBJ_TYPE_FILE);
2076:  if (handle < 0)
2077:    return NULL;
2078:
2079:  long stat_size = OS1_object_ctl((int)handle, OBJ_CTL_STAT, 0);
2080:  if (stat_size <= 0 || (uint64_t)stat_size > OS1_IMAGE_MAX_FILE_BYTES) {
2081:    OS1low_handle_close((int)handle);
2082:    return NULL;
2083:  }
2084:
2085:  int size = (int)stat_size;
2086:  unsigned char *data = malloc((size_t)size + 16u);
2087:  if (!data) {
2088:    OS1low_handle_close((int)handle);
2089:    return NULL;
2090:  }
2091:
2092:  int total = 0;
2093:  while (total < size) {
2094:    long got = OS1_object_read((int)handle, data + total,
2095:                               (unsigned long)(size - total));
2096:    if (got <= 0) {
2097:      OS1low_handle_close((int)handle);
2098:      free(data);
2099:      return NULL;
2100:    }
2101:    total += (int)got;
2102:  }
2103:  OS1low_handle_close((int)handle);
2104:
2105:  if (total != size) {
2106:    free(data);
2107:    return NULL;
2108:  }
2109:  for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++)
2110:    data[size + i] = 0;
2111:
2112:  int iw = 0;
2113:  int ih = 0;
2114:  int channels = 0;
2115:  if (!stbi_info_from_memory(data, size, &iw, &ih, &channels)) {
2116:    free(data);
2117:    return NULL;
2118:  }
2119:  if (iw <= 0 || ih <= 0 || iw > OS1_IMAGE_MAX_DIMENSION ||
2120:      ih > OS1_IMAGE_MAX_DIMENSION ||
2121:      (uint64_t)iw * (uint64_t)ih > OS1_IMAGE_MAX_PIXELS) {
2122:    free(data);
2123:    return NULL;
2124:  }
2125:
2126:  int n = 0;
2127:  unsigned char *rgba = stbi_load_from_memory(data, size, &iw, &ih, &n, 4);
2128:  free(data);
2129:  if (!rgba)
2130:    return NULL;
2131:
2132:  uint64_t pixels = (uint64_t)iw * (uint64_t)ih;
2133:  if (pixels > OS1_IMAGE_MAX_PIXELS || pixels > ((uint64_t)SIZE_MAX / 4u)) {
2134:    stbi_image_free(rgba);
2135:    return NULL;
2136:  }
2137:
2138:  uint32_t *argb = (uint32_t *)malloc((size_t)pixels * 4u);
2139:  if (!argb) {
2140:    stbi_image_free(rgba);
2141:    return NULL;
2142:  }
2143:
2144:  for (uint64_t i = 0; i < pixels; i++) {
2145:    uint8_t r = rgba[i * 4u + 0u];
2146:    uint8_t g = rgba[i * 4u + 1u];
2147:    uint8_t b = rgba[i * 4u + 2u];
2148:    uint8_t a = rgba[i * 4u + 3u];
2149:    argb[i] = ((uint32_t)a << 24) | ((uint32_t)r << 16) | ((uint32_t)g << 8) |
2150:              (uint32_t)b;
2151:  }
2152:
2153:  stbi_image_free(rgba);
2154:  *w = iw;
2155:  *h = ih;
2156:  return argb;
2157:}
2158:
2159:/*
2160: * strtol - convert string to long integer with base and endptr support.
2161: *
2162: * Handles leading whitespace, optional sign, 0x/0 prefixes for base
2163: * auto-detection (base==0), and digits up to the given base.
2164: * Sets *endptr to the first non-consumed character if endptr != NULL.
2165: * Does not detect overflow (val accumulates without range check).
2166: * Negative values are produced by negating the unsigned accumulator,
2167: * which gives correct two's-complement representation for LONG_MIN.
2168: */
2169:long strtol(const char *nptr, char **endptr, int base) {
2170:  const char *p = nptr;
2171:  while (isspace(*p))
2172:    p++;
2173:  int neg = 0;
2174:  if (*p == '-') {
2175:    neg = 1;
2176:    p++;
2177:  } else if (*p == '+')
2178:    p++;
2179:
2180:  /* Auto-detect base from prefix: "0x" -> 16, "0" -> 8, else 10. */
2181:  if (base == 0) {
2182:    if (*p == '0') {
2183:      if (p[1] == 'x' || p[1] == 'X')
2184:        base = 16;
2185:      else
2186:        base = 8;
2187:    } else
2188:      base = 10;
2189:  }
2190:
2191:  if (base == 16 && p[0] == '0' && (p[1] == 'x' || p[1] == 'X'))
2192:    p += 2;
2193:
2194:  unsigned long val = 0;
2195:  while (1) {
2196:    int digit;
2197:    if (isdigit(*p))
2198:      digit = *p - '0';
2199:    else if (isalpha(*p))
2200:      digit = tolower(*p) - 'a' + 10;
2201:    else
2202:      break;
2203:
2204:    if (digit >= base)
2205:      break;
2206:    val = val * base + digit;
2207:    p++;
2208:  }
2209:
2210:  if (endptr)
2211:    *endptr = (char *)p;
2212:  return neg ? -(long)val : (long)val;
2213:}

2215:/* --- Robust sscanf (Ported from BSD) --- */
2216:
2217:/*
2218: * sscanf - varargs wrapper that delegates to vsscanf.
2219: */
2220:int sscanf(const char *str, const char *format, ...) {
2221:  va_list args;
2222:  va_start(args, format);
2223:  int res = vsscanf(str, format, args);
2224:  va_end(args);
2225:  return res;
2226:}
2227:
2228:/*
2229: * vsscanf - simplified format scanner supporting %d, %x/%X, %s with widths.
2230: *
2231: * Supports:
2232: *   %d  - signed decimal integer -> int *
2233: *   %x, %X - unsigned hex integer -> unsigned int *; skips optional 0x prefix
2234: *   %s  - whitespace-delimited string; width limits chars consumed
2235: *
2236: * Whitespace in the format string matches zero or more whitespace chars in
2237: * the input.  Literal format characters must match exactly (returns early on
2238: * mismatch).  Returns the count of successfully assigned conversions.
2239: *
2240: * Missing specifiers: %f, %c, %ld, %u, %p, etc.  Callers using unsupported
2241: * format specifiers will silently skip the conversion.
2242: */
2243:int vsscanf(const char *inp, const char *fmt0, va_list ap) {
2244:  int nassigned = 0;
2245:  const unsigned char *fmt = (const unsigned char *)fmt0;
2246:  const char *p_inp = inp;
2247:
2248:  while (*fmt) {
2249:    if (isspace(*fmt)) {
2250:      while (isspace(*p_inp))
2251:        p_inp++;
2252:      fmt++;
2253:      continue;
2254:    }
2255:    if (*fmt != '%') {
2256:      if (*p_inp != *fmt)
2257:        return nassigned;
2258:      p_inp++;
2259:      fmt++;
2260:      continue;
2261:    }
2262:    fmt++; /* skip % */
2263:    /* Parse optional field width */
2264:    int width = 0;
2265:    while (isdigit(*fmt)) {
2266:      width = width * 10 + (*fmt - '0');
2267:      fmt++;
2268:    }
2269:
2270:    char c = *fmt++;
2271:    if (c == 'd') {
2272:      while (isspace(*p_inp))
2273:        p_inp++;
2274:      int *res = va_arg(ap, int *);
2275:      *res = atoi(p_inp);
2276:      nassigned++;
2277:      while (isdigit(*p_inp) || *p_inp == '-')
2278:        p_inp++;
2279:    } else if (c == 'x' || c == 'X') {
2280:      while (isspace(*p_inp))
2281:        p_inp++;
2282:      unsigned int *res = va_arg(ap, unsigned int *);
2283:      unsigned int val = 0;
2284:      if (p_inp[0] == '0' && (p_inp[1] == 'x' || p_inp[1] == 'X'))
2285:        p_inp += 2;
2286:      while (isxdigit(*p_inp)) {
2287:        char dc = *p_inp++;
2288:        if (isdigit(dc))
2289:          val = (val << 4) | (dc - '0');
2290:        else
2291:          val = (val << 4) | (tolower(dc) - 'a' + 10);
2292:      }
2293:      *res = val;
2294:      nassigned++;
2295:    } else if (c == 's') {
2296:      while (isspace(*p_inp))
2297:        p_inp++;
2298:      char *res = va_arg(ap, char *);
2299:      while (*p_inp && !isspace(*p_inp)) {
2300:        *res++ = *p_inp++;
2301:        if (width > 0 && --width == 0)
2302:          break;
2303:      }
2304:      *res = '\0';
2305:      nassigned++;
2306:    }
2307:    /* NOTE(USR-LIB-04): Other format specifiers (%f, %c, %ld, %u, etc.) are
2308:     * silently skipped; the corresponding va_arg is NOT consumed, which may
2309:     * desync the va_list for subsequent conversions. */
2310:  }
2311:  return nassigned;
2312:}
