2314:/* NOTE(USR-LIB-04): system/getenv are still no-op stubs; atof truncates
2315: * decimal fractions by delegating to atoi() and casting, so "3.14" -> 3.0.
2316: * mkdir is no longer a stub — it composes over a parent directory capability.
2317: */
2318:/* mkdir - create a directory through its parent directory capability. The
2319: * POSIX mode argument is accepted but not yet applied (the ext4 driver fixes
2320: * new directories at 0755); returns 0 on success, -1 on error (path exists,
2321: * not permitted, or provider failure), matching the POSIX contract. */
2322:int mkdir(const char *path, mode_t mode) {
2323:  (void)mode;
2324:  if (!path) {
2325:    errno = EFAULT;
2326:    return -1;
2327:  }
2328:  /* EXT4-ERRNO-01 (userland half): this returned a bare -1 without touching
2329:   * errno, so a caller doing the POSIX thing — check -1, then read errno —
2330:   * read whatever a PREVIOUS call had left there.  A stale errno is worse than
2331:   * none: it is indistinguishable from a fresh one.  Routed through
2332:   * errno_ret() like every other syscall veneer. */
2333:  return (int)errno_ret_ctx(OS1_fs_mkdir(path), path);
2334:}
2335:/*
2336: * system - run a shell command and wait for it (<stdlib.h>).
2337: *
2338: * FIX(USR-LIB-04): this used to unconditionally return 0. That silently
2339: * broke two separate contracts real POSIX-shaped code relies on:
2340: *
2341: *   1. system(NULL) must return non-zero IFF a command processor exists.
2342: *      Lua's os.execute() with no argument is exactly this check (e.g.
2343: *      `assert(os.execute())` in the Lua test suite reads "0" as "no
2344: *      shell available" and fails, even though NXShell is right there).
2345: *   2. system(cmd) must actually run cmd and hand back its real exit
2346: *      status, so os.execute(cmd)/os.execute(cmd) callers get true
2347: *      success/failure instead of a hardcoded fake "it worked".
2348: *
2349: * NOTE: NXSHELL_PATH and the "-c" argv convention below are the standard
2350: * Unix shell invocation shape (`sh -c "cmd"`). Adjust NXSHELL_PATH (and the
2351: * argv construction, if NXShell parses its command-line differently) to
2352: * match the actual shell binary shipped on this system.
2353: */
2354:#define NXSHELL_PATH "/sys/bin/nxshell"
2355:
2356:int system(const char *command) {
2357:  if (command == NULL) {
2358:    return 1; /* POSIX: non-zero only if a command processor exists.
2359:               * NXShell is available. */
2360:  }
2361:
2362:  char *argv[4];
2363:  argv[0] = (char *)NXSHELL_PATH;
2364:  argv[1] = (char *)"-c";
2365:  argv[2] = (char *)command;
2366:  argv[3] = NULL;
2367:
2368:  /* Phase 9c HELD AT THE GATE (2026-07-23) — the in-process path is the one
2369:   * that runs, and the reason is the migration rule this phase set for itself.
2370:   *
2371:   * DESIGN-2026-07-18-NXEXEC-DAEMON §6 step 3: route a caller through the
2372:   * service "keeping the in-process path behind a fallback UNTIL the suite is
2373:   * at least as green as before".  It was not.  A child created by the service
2374:   * inherits its per-process attributes from the SERVICE, and two of the three
2375:   * were simply wrong:
2376:   *
2377:   *   cwd  — FIXED: the request now carries the requester's cwd and the
2378:   *          service adopts it around the spawn (execsvc_client.c, nxexec.c).
2379:   *          It was being parsed and discarded.
2380:   *   ctty — NOT FIXED, and NOT fixable here.  sys_write resolves stdout to
2381:   *          the writer's own window, else its ctty_win (kernel/core/object.c).
2382:   *          The service has no window and no ctty, so every child it creates
2383:   *          gets ctty_win = -1 and its output goes NOWHERE.  fd redirection
2384:   *          cannot patch this: the destination comes from the process, not
2385:   *          from the handle.
2386:   *   env  — plan stall S1, same shape, already owned.
2387:   *
2388:   * Carrying ctty needs the spawn itself to carry it, which is Phase 9d — and
2389:   * 9d is gated by Phase 16.  Inventing a second mechanism for it now (a
2390:   * post-spawn ctty verb, or hanging it off OBJ_CTL_SETOWNER) is exactly the
2391:   * duplicate-mechanism mistake the plan already recorded and withdrew when it
2392:   * deleted 17b.  So the routing waits for the ONE mechanism instead.
2393:   *
2394:   * execsvc_spawn() is NOT dead: captest exercises the protocol directly
2395:   * ("exec service" section), so the daemon stays verified while it is off the
2396:   * POSIX critical path.  Re-enable here — and nowhere else — once 9d lands. */
2397:  int pid = spawn_args(NXSHELL_PATH, 3, argv);
2398:  if (pid < 0) {
2399:    errno = ENOENT;
2400:    return -1;
2401:  }
2402:
2403:  /* Blocking join through polling, using the same pattern as
2404:   * nxexec_run_foreground():
2405:   * wait() is non-blocking (-1 = still running / pid reaped / -2 = not
2406:   * found), so it must be queried in a loop until it no longer reports
2407:   * "running" — not called only once like before (that single -1 result
2408:   * was interpreted as ECHILD, causing system() to fail almost every time). */
2409:  int w, code = 0;
2410:  while ((w = OS1low_process_wait_status(pid, &code)) == -1)
2411:    OS1_sleep(15);
2412:
2413:  /* POSIX system() status word: WEXITSTATUS reads (status>>8)&0xff (Phase 2).
2414:   * A -2 "reaped elsewhere" leaves code 0 — the command still ran. */
2415:  (void)w;
2416:  return __wait_encode(code);
2417:}
2418:
2419:/*
2420: * waitpid - POSIX <sys/wait.h> wait (Phase 2).  Was declared but never
2421: * defined (an undefined-symbol trap for ported code).  Backed by the PROCESS
2422: * capability wait; fills *status with the POSIX-encoded exit code.  WNOHANG is
2423: * a single non-blocking poll; other options (WUNTRACED) are ignored (no
2424: * stopped-process state yet — a Phase 2 follow-up).
2425: */
2426:int waitpid(int pid, int *status, int options) {
2427:  int code = 0, w;
2428:  if (options & WNOHANG) {
2429:    w = OS1low_process_wait_status(pid, &code);
2430:    if (w == -1)
2431:      return 0; /* still running */
2432:    if (w == -2) {
2433:      errno = ECHILD;
2434:      return -1;
2435:    }
2436:    if (status)
2437:      *status = __wait_encode(code);
2438:    return pid;
2439:  }
2440:  while ((w = OS1low_process_wait_status(pid, &code)) == -1)
2441:    OS1_sleep(15);
2442:  if (w == -2) {
2443:    errno = ECHILD;
2444:    return -1;
2445:  }
2446:  if (status)
2447:    *status = __wait_encode(code);
2448:  return pid;
2449:}
2450:
2451:/*
2452: * cmdline_split - split a command line into argv[], honoring quotes.
2453: *
2454: * THE shared command tokenizer (used by nxshell for both interactive input
2455: * and `nxshell -c "<cmd>"`, which is how system()/Lua os.execute() reach a
2456: * program).  Whitespace separates words EXCEPT inside a '...' or "..." span,
2457: * which is kept as one token with its surrounding quotes REMOVED — so a
2458: * shell-style quoted program name like "lua" resolves to lua (not the
2459: * literal /bin/"lua" that broke os.execute), and a quoted argument that
2460: * contains spaces (Lua's `lua -e "a = 1"`) survives as a single argv entry.
2461: * A backslash inside a double-quoted span escapes a following '"' or '\'.
2462: *
2463: * Tokens are compacted IN PLACE inside s (out <= s always, so writing the
2464: * NUL terminators never clobbers a not-yet-scanned token).  Returns argc;
2465: * each argv[i] points into s.  Matches the previous whitespace-only splitter
2466: * when no quotes are present.
2467: */
2468:int cmdline_split(char *s, char **argv, int max) {
2469:  int argc = 0;
2470:  if (!s || !argv || max <= 0)
2471:    return 0;
2472:  while (*s && argc < max) {
2473:    while (*s == ' ' || *s == '\t')
2474:      s++;
2475:    if (!*s)
2476:      break;
2477:    char *out = s;
2478:    argv[argc++] = out;
2479:    while (*s && *s != ' ' && *s != '\t') {
2480:      char c = *s;
2481:      if (c == '"' || c == '\'') {
2482:        char q = c;
2483:        s++;
2484:        while (*s && *s != q) {
2485:          if (q == '"' && *s == '\\' && (s[1] == '"' || s[1] == '\\'))
2486:            s++; /* consume the backslash, copy the escaped char verbatim */
2487:          *out++ = *s++;
2488:        }
2489:        if (*s == q)
2490:          s++; /* consume the closing quote */
2491:      } else {
2492:        *out++ = *s++;
2493:      }
2494:    }
2495:    if (*s)
2496:      s++;       /* step past the delimiter for the next scan */
2497:    *out = '\0'; /* terminate the compacted token (out <= s) */
2498:  }
2499:  return argc;
2500:}
2501:/* atof: real IEEE-754 float parse via strtod (math.c). See the file header's
2502: * USR-LIB-04 entry — the previous inline note here ("only integer part is
2503: * parsed") was stale documentation describing code that had already been
2504: * fixed; removed rather than repeated a second time in this file. */
2505:double atof(const char *nptr) { return strtod(nptr, NULL); }
2506:/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
2507: * ENVIRONMENT — Phase 17
2508: *
2509: * TWO LAYERS, because ASTRA §6.8 and this plan's opening rule both require it:
2510: * the kernel is NOT POSIX; POSIX is a personality built ON TOP of OS1.
2511: *
2512: *   OS1_env_*   the NATIVE surface.  Owns the one fact that the kernel exposes
2513: *               the environment through the `sys.proc.<pid>.env.*` registry
2514: *               namespace, with `sys.env.*` beneath it as machine defaults.
2515: *   getenv/...  the POSIX personality: a THIN mapping over OS1_env_*, with no
2516: *               knowledge of the registry whatsoever.
2517: *
2518: * The first cut of this phase collapsed the two — POSIX built registry key
2519: * strings itself — which put the registry's path syntax into the POSIX API and
2520: * led to setenv() rejecting any name containing a '.'.  That restriction was
2521: * never real: the kernel's virtual-key router hands everything after "env." to
2522: * the scheduler as one opaque name, so dots always worked.  It was a limit
2523: * invented to serve a layering mistake.
2524: * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
2525:
2526:#define OS1_ENV_KEYMAX 96
2527:
2528:/* env_self - our own pid, resolved once.
2529: *
2530: * getpid() is a syscall, and every env operation needs the pid to name its own
2531: * branch of the namespace — so the naive form costs TWO syscalls per getenv(),
2532: * on a function that path resolution calls per spawn.  A process's pid never
2533: * changes (pids come from a monotonic counter and there is no fork), so the
2534: * value is cacheable without an invalidation story. */
2535:static int env_self(void) {
2536:  static int self_pid;
2537:  if (self_pid <= 0)
2538:    self_pid = getpid();
2539:  return self_pid;
2540:}
2541:
2542:/* env_key - build the per-process namespace path.  The ONLY place in userland
2543: * that knows this syntax. */
2544:static int env_key(char *out, size_t size, const char *name) {
2545:  if (!name || !*name || strchr(name, '='))
2546:    return -1; /* POSIX: '=' separates name from value, so it cannot be in one
2547:                */
2548:  int n = snprintf(out, size, "sys.proc.%d.env.%s", env_self(), name);
2549:  /* R7: snprintf() returning > 0 alone does NOT mean the key fit — a long
2550:   * `name` truncates silently and a truncated key can alias a DIFFERENT,
2551:   * unrelated variable instead of failing loudly. Check the full contract:
2552:   * the return is the length it WOULD have written; only n < size means it
2553:   * actually did. */
2554:  return (n > 0 && (size_t)n < size) ? 0 : -1;
2555:}
2556:
2557:int OS1_env_get(const char *name, char *buf, size_t size) {
2558:  char key[OS1_ENV_KEYMAX];
2559:  if (!buf || size == 0 || env_key(key, sizeof(key), name) != 0)
2560:    return -1;
2561:  /* Process value first: it SHADOWS the machine default, which is the whole
2562:   * point of having both layers. */
2563:  if (OS1_registry_get(key, buf, size) == 0)
2564:    return 0;
2565:  int n = snprintf(key, sizeof(key), "sys.env.%s", name);
2566:  if (n <= 0 || (size_t)n >= sizeof(key)) /* R7: same truncation check */
2567:    return -1;
2568:  if (OS1_registry_get(key, buf, size) == 0 && buf[0])
2569:    return 0;
2570:  return -1;
2571:}
2572:
2573:int OS1_env_set(const char *name, const char *value) {
2574:  char key[OS1_ENV_KEYMAX];
2575:  if (env_key(key, sizeof(key), name) != 0)
2576:    return -1;
2577:  /* Writes always land on the PROCESS layer, never on sys.env.*: a program
2578:   * calling setenv means "for me and my children", not "reconfigure the
2579:   * machine".  Keeping that distinction here is why setenv needs no privilege
2580:   * while editing the defaults still does. */
2581:  return OS1_registry_set(key, value ? value : "") == 0 ? 0 : -1;
2582:}
2583:
2584:int OS1_env_unset(const char *name) {
2585:  char key[OS1_ENV_KEYMAX];
2586:  if (env_key(key, sizeof(key), name) != 0)
2587:    return -1;
2588:  /* R7: DEL and set-to-empty both clear the slot, so a DEL failure here
2589:   * (e.g. the key was never set) changes nothing this function has promised
2590:   * — unsetenv() of an already-unset name is a POSIX no-op success, not an
2591:   * error — so the result is intentionally, not accidentally, discarded. */
2592:  (void)OS1_registry_del(key);
2593:  return 0;
2594:}
2595:
2596:int OS1_env_enum(char *buf, size_t size) {
2597:  char prefix[OS1_ENV_KEYMAX];
2598:  if (!buf || size == 0)
2599:    return -1;
2600:  int plen0 = snprintf(prefix, sizeof(prefix), "sys.proc.%d.env.", env_self());
2601:  if (plen0 <= 0 || (size_t)plen0 >= sizeof(prefix)) /* R7: truncation check */
2602:    return -1;
2603:  int n = OS1_registry_enum_under(prefix, buf, size - 1);
2604:  if (n <= 0) {
2605:    buf[0] = '\0';
2606:    return 0;
2607:  }
2608:  /* R5: OS1_registry_enum_under() is a syscall veneer; trust its own bound
2609:   * but not blindly — n must fit the buffer we gave it (size - 1) before we
2610:   * index buf[n] below. */
2611:  nx_assert(n > 0 && (size_t)n <= size - 1);
2612:  buf[n] = '\0';
2613:  /* Enumeration returns FULL keys; strip the namespace so callers above this
2614:   * layer never see it.  Rewrites in place, line by line. */
2615:  size_t plen = strlen(prefix);
2616:  char *w = buf;
2617:  for (char *r = buf; *r;) {
2618:    char *nl = strchr(r, '\n');
2619:    size_t len = nl ? (size_t)(nl - r) : strlen(r);
2620:    const char *nm =
2621:        (len > plen && strncmp(r, prefix, plen) == 0) ? r + plen : r;
2622:    size_t nlen = len - (size_t)(nm - r);
2623:    /* R5/R2: the write cursor `w` can only ever trail the read cursor `r`
2624:     * (stripping a prefix removes bytes, never adds them), so this loop is
2625:     * bounded by the same `n <= size - 1` proven above — assert it instead
2626:     * of trusting the arithmetic silently on every iteration. */
2627:    nx_assert((size_t)(w - buf) <= (size_t)(r - buf));
2628:    memmove(w, nm, nlen);
2629:    w += nlen;
2630:    if (!nl)
2631:      break;
2632:    *w++ = '\n';
2633:    r = nl + 1;
2634:  }
2635:  *w = '\0';
2636:  return (int)(w - buf);
2637:}
2638:
2639:/* --- POSIX personality (<stdlib.h>) — a thin mapping, nothing more --------
2640: *
2641: * Documented deviation: the string returned by getenv() lives in a small
2642: * rotating buffer pool, so it is valid until GETENV_SLOTS further getenv()
2643: * calls, not until the next setenv().  Callers keeping a value across many
2644: * lookups must copy it.  The alternative — a per-name heap cache that is never
2645: * freed — leaks by design. */
2646:#define GETENV_SLOTS 4
2647:#define GETENV_VALMAX 128
2648:
2649:static char *_default_environ[] = { NULL };
2650:char **environ = _default_environ;
2651:
2652:char *getenv(const char *name) {
2653:
2654:  static char slots[GETENV_SLOTS][GETENV_VALMAX];
2655:  static int next_slot;
2656:  char *out = slots[next_slot];
2657:  if (OS1_env_get(name, out, GETENV_VALMAX) != 0)
2658:    return NULL;
2659:  next_slot = (next_slot + 1) % GETENV_SLOTS;
2660:  return out;
2661:}
2662:
2663:int setenv(const char *name, const char *value, int overwrite) {
2664:  if (!overwrite && getenv(name))
2665:    return 0;
2666:  return OS1_env_set(name, value);
2667:}

2669:int unsetenv(const char *name) { return OS1_env_unset(name); }
2670:
2671:/*
2672: * putenv - POSIX's older "NAME=VALUE" form.
2673: *
2674: * POSIX says the caller's string BECOMES part of the environment, so later
2675: * edits to it are visible.  We cannot honour that — the storage is in the
2676: * kernel — so this parses and copies, like setenv.  Stated because a caller
2677: * relying on the aliasing would otherwise be silently wrong; in practice every
2678: * caller in this tree passes a string literal.
2679: */
2680:int putenv(char *string) {
2681:  if (!string)
2682:    return -1;
2683:  const char *eq = strchr(string, '=');
2684:  if (!eq)
2685:    return unsetenv(string); /* "NAME" with no '=' unsets, per POSIX */
2686:  char name[OS1_ENV_KEYMAX];
2687:  size_t nl = (size_t)(eq - string);
2688:  if (nl == 0 || nl >= sizeof(name))
2689:    return -1;
2690:  memcpy(name, string, nl);
2691:  name[nl] = '\0';
2692:  return setenv(name, eq + 1, 1);
2693:}

2695:int clearenv(void) {
2696:  char buf[512];
2697:  if (OS1_env_enum(buf, sizeof(buf)) <= 0)
2698:    return 0;
2699:  char *save = NULL;
2700:  for (char *k = strtok_r(buf, "\n", &save); k; k = strtok_r(NULL, "\n", &save))
2701:    OS1_env_unset(k);
2702:  return 0;
2703:}
2704:
2705:/*
2706: * env_names - NexsOS extension replacing POSIX `environ`.
2707: *
2708: * The POSIX way to enumerate assumes the environment is a userland array the
2709: * process can point at.  Here it is kernel state, so a `char **environ` would
2710: * mean publishing a snapshot and then lying about how fresh it is.  An explicit
2711: * enumerator says what it actually does: names only, values via getenv().
2712: */
2713:int env_names(char *names[], int max) {
2714:  static char buf[512];
2715:  int count = 0;
2716:  if (OS1_env_enum(buf, sizeof(buf)) <= 0)
2717:    return 0;
2718:  char *save = NULL;
2719:  for (char *k = strtok_r(buf, "\n", &save); k && count < max;
2720:       k = strtok_r(NULL, "\n", &save))
2721:    names[count++] = k;
2722:  return count;
2723:}
2724:
2725:/*
2726: * __env_propagate_to_child - copies every variable that THIS process has
2727: * set (its own branch sys.proc.<self>.env.* — the machine defaults
2728: * under sys.env.* don't need copying, the child inherits them anyway
2729: * via the fallback of OS1_env_get) into the branch of the child just spawned.
2730: *
2731: * Without this every child starts with an EMPTY environment: nothing in
2732: * this tree wrote it, so an `export PATH=...` (or any setenv())
2733: * in a shell was invisible to everything it launched, and `printenv PATH`
2734: * in a child always failed even with the parent's PATH set.
2735: * execsvc_client.c already carries the cwd of the requester through the
2736: * service protocol for exactly the same reason ("cwd is wrong for exactly
2737: * the same reason the environment is"); this is the same correction applied
2738: * to the direct spawn path, the one that nxexec_spawn_search_redir/
2739: * nxshell use for every foreground and background command.
2740: *
2741: * Best-effort: a write failure here doesn't fail the spawn (the child starts
2742: * anyway, just without that variable) — consistent with setenv() which is
2743: * also a best-effort registry write.
2744: *
2745: * NOTE: the execsvc path (Phase 9c) is NOT covered here — a spawn routed
2746: * via /sys/bin/nxexec happens IN THE SERVICE PROCESS, so "self" in the
2747: * point where __env_propagate_to_child would run is the service, not the
2748: * requester. Fixing it requires bringing the environment into the network
2749: * protocol like already happens for the cwd (bump of EXECSVC_VERSION) —
2750: * left as a follow-on, in line with the note Phase 9d of the header on
2751: * cwd/ctty/env that must arrive together "as ONE mechanism".
2752: */
2753:static void __env_propagate_to_child(long child_pid) {
2754:  if (child_pid <= 0)
2755:    return;
2756:  char buf[512];
2757:  if (OS1_env_enum(buf, sizeof(buf)) <= 0)
2758:    return;
2759:  char *save = NULL;
2760:  for (char *name = strtok_r(buf, "\n", &save); name;
2761:       name = strtok_r(NULL, "\n", &save)) {
2762:    char val[GETENV_VALMAX];
2763:    if (OS1_env_get(name, val, sizeof(val)) != 0)
2764:      continue;
2765:    char key[OS1_ENV_KEYMAX];
2766:    int klen = snprintf(key, sizeof(key), "sys.proc.%ld.env.%s", child_pid, name);
2767:    if (klen <= 0 || (size_t)klen >= sizeof(key)) /* R7: truncation check */
2768:      continue;
2769:    /* R7: best-effort by design (see the function comment above) — a single
2770:     * variable failing to propagate must not abort the spawn, so the result
2771:     * is intentionally discarded here, not merely unchecked. */
2772:    (void)OS1_registry_set(key, val);
2773:  }
2774:}
2775:
2776:/*
2777: * stat - path metadata in ONE syscall (SYS_STAT).
2778: *
2779: * It used to infer the type: "list_dir succeeds ONLY on directories, so a >= 0
2780: * probe IS a directory".  That invariant was load-bearing in TWO places (here
2781: * and opendir) and R1 broke it — once a READ handle could be acquired on any
2782: * path, listing a regular FILE returned its CONTENT instead of failing, so
2783: * every file looked like a directory and the file manager tried to chdir into
2784: * them ("Cannot open directory").
2785: *
2786: * Inference replaced by a fact: the kernel is the only place that knows a
2787: * node's type, so it reports it.  One round trip instead of a listing probe
2788: * plus a size probe.
2789: */
2790:int stat(const char *path, struct stat *buf)
2791:
2792:{
2793:    if (!path) {
2794:        errno = EFAULT;
2795:        return -1;
2796:    }
2797:
2798:    if (buf)
2799:        memset(buf, 0, sizeof(struct stat));
2800:
2801:    struct abi_stat as;
2802:    int r = _sys_stat(path, &as);
2803:    if (r != 0) {
2804:        errno = ENOENT;          /* o meglio: errno = -r; se il kernel restituisce errno negativi */
2805:        return -1;
2806:    }
2807:
2808:    if (buf) {
2809:        buf->st_size  = (off_t)as.size;
2810:        buf->st_mode  = (as.type == ABI_S_TYPE_DIR) ? (S_IFDIR | 0755) : (S_IFREG | 0644);
2811:        buf->st_nlink = 1;
2812:        buf->st_uid   = 0;
2813:        buf->st_gid   = 0;
2814:        buf->st_blksize = 4096;
2815:        buf->st_blocks  = (as.size + 511) / 512;
2816:
2817:        /* Timestamp temporanei (finché il VFS non li supporta davvero) */
2818:        time_t now = time(NULL);
2819:        buf->st_atime = now;
2820:        buf->st_mtime = now;
2821:        buf->st_ctime = now;
2822:
2823:#if defined(_STATBUF_ST_NSEC) || defined(__USE_XOPEN2K8)
2824:        buf->st_atim.tv_sec  = now;
2825:        buf->st_atim.tv_nsec = 0;
2826:        buf->st_mtim.tv_sec  = now;
2827:        buf->st_mtim.tv_nsec = 0;
2828:        buf->st_ctim.tv_sec  = now;
2829:        buf->st_ctim.tv_nsec = 0;
2830:#endif
2831:    }
2832:
2833:    return 0;
2834:}

2836:int statfs(const char *path, struct statfs *buf)
2837:{
2838:    if (!buf) {
2839:        errno = EFAULT;
2840:        return -1;
2841:    }
2842:    if (!path) {
2843:        errno = EFAULT;
2844:        return -1;
2845:    }
2846:
2847:    memset(buf, 0, sizeof(*buf));
2848:

2861:    buf->f_ffree   = 0;
2862:    buf->f_fsid.__val[0] = 0;
2863:    buf->f_fsid.__val[1] = 0;

2870:int fstatfs(int fd, struct statfs *buf)
2871:{
2872:    if (!buf) {
2873:        errno = EFAULT;
2874:        return -1;
2875:    }
2876:    if (fd < 0) {
2877:        errno = EBADF;
2878:        return -1;
2879:    }
2880:
2881:    /* NexsOS1 non ha ancora un modo per ottenere il path da un fd,
2882:       quindi per ora usiamo un placeholder basato su fstat.
2883:       Quando avremo fd → path o una vera syscall di fsinfo, si sistemerà. */
2884:    struct stat st;
2885:    if (fstat(fd, &st) != 0)
2886:        return -1;
2887:
2888:    memset(buf, 0, sizeof(*buf));
2889:    buf->f_type    = 0x01021994UL;
2890:    buf->f_bsize   = 4096;
2891:    buf->f_frsize  = 4096;
2892:    buf->f_blocks  = (st.st_size + 4095) / 4096;
2893:    buf->f_bfree   = buf->f_blocks;
2894:    buf->f_bavail  = buf->f_blocks;
2895:    buf->f_files   = 0;
2896:    buf->f_ffree   = 0;
2897:    buf->f_fsid.__val[0] = 0;
2898:    buf->f_fsid.__val[1] = 0;
2899:    buf->f_namelen = 255;
2900:    buf->f_flags   = 0;
2901:
2902:    return 0;
2903:}

2905:/*
2906: * vfprintf - format and write to a FILE stream.
2907: *
2908: * Routes through fwrite(), so it honours 'stream' exactly like any other
2909: * stream I/O: stdin/stdout/stderr go via file_fd()+write() (all three share
2910: * one CONSOLE object kernel-side, so stdout/stderr are visually
2911: * indistinguishable today, but a real fopen()ed FILE* now writes to its own
2912: * path/position instead of unconditionally landing on fd 1 (fixes
2913: * USR-LIB-05).
2914: *
2915: * Output is limited to 1023 chars by the stack buffer; longer output is
2916: * silently truncated by vsnprintf. Returns the formatted length (vsnprintf's
2917: * return value), not the byte count actually written.
2918: */
2919:int vfprintf(FILE *stream, const char *format, va_list ap) {
2920:  char buf[1024];
2921:  int n = vsnprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), format, ap);
2922:  fwrite(buf, 1, strlen(buf), stream);
2923:  return n;
2924:}
2925:
2926:int vprintf(const char *format, va_list ap) {
2927:  return vfprintf(stdout, format, ap);
2928:}
2929:
2930:int fprintf(FILE *stream, const char *format, ...) {
2931:  va_list args;
2932:  va_start(args, format);
2933:  int res = vfprintf(stream, format, args);
2934:  va_end(args);
2935:  return res;
2936:}
2937:/* fflush: write out a positional stream's pending write buffer.  fflush(NULL)
2938: * is defined to flush all open output streams; this libc keeps no open-stream
2939: * registry, so that form is a no-op (callers flush the specific stream). */
2940:int fflush(FILE *stream) {
2941:  if (!stream)
2942:    return 0;
2943:  return fstream_flush(stream);
2944:}
2945:/*
2946: * remove - delete a file (POSIX/<stdio.h>).  Was a no-op stub that returned
2947: * success while deleting nothing, so os.remove()/temp-file cleanup silently
2948: * did nothing; the unlink syscall existed all along (OS1_fs_unlink).
2949: */
2950:int remove(const char *pathname) {
2951:  return (int)errno_ret_ctx(OS1_fs_unlink(pathname), pathname);
2952:}
2953:/*
2954: * unlink - remove a file (POSIX <unistd.h>).  The unistd.h declaration existed
2955: * with no definition in this libc (only in vendored musl, which our programs
2956: * don't link), so a caller would have hit an undefined symbol.  Real now — the
2957: * same VFS unlink `remove()` uses.
2958: */
2959:int unlink(const char *pathname) {
2960:  return (int)errno_ret_ctx(OS1_fs_unlink(pathname), pathname);
2961:}
2962:/*
2963: * link - create a second name for the same file contents.
2964: *
2965: * The current NexsOS1 FS layer provides create/write/read and delete, but no
2966: * inode-level hard-link syscall; the correct compatibility point is therefore
2967: * the existing file-creation path, not a synthetic extra file or fake kernel ABI.
2968: * We copy the source bytes into the destination path, fail if the destination
2969: * already exists, and leave the original untouched.
2970: */
2971:int link(const char *oldpath, const char *newpath) {
2972:  int size = OS1_fs_read(oldpath, NULL, 0, 0);
2973:  if (size < 0)
2974:    return -1;
2975:  if (OS1_fs_read(newpath, NULL, 0, 0) >= 0) {
2976:    errno = EEXIST;
2977:    return -1;
2978:  }
2979:  if (size == 0) {
2980:    return OS1_fs_write(newpath, "", 0, 0) < 0 ? -1 : 0;
2981:  }
2982:  char *buf = malloc((size_t)size);
2983:  if (!buf) {
2984:    errno = ENOMEM;
2985:    return -1;
2986:  }
2987:  int n = OS1_fs_read(oldpath, buf, size, 0);
2988:  if (n < 0) {
2989:    free(buf);
2990:    return -1;
2991:  }
2992:  int w = OS1_fs_write(newpath, buf, n, 0);
2993:  free(buf);
2994:  if (w < 0)
2995:    return -1;
2996:  return 0;
2997:}

3076:/*
3077: * getloadavg - get system load average (real implementation via OS1_sys_stats).
3078: *
3079: * NexsOS1 provides instantaneous scheduler load via OS1_sys_stats(sched_runnable).
3080: * Since there is no historical load tracking, we report the current snapshot
3081: * (number of ready+running processes) for all three intervals (1m, 5m, 15m).
3082: * This gives userland programs an accurate instantaneous load, not a moving average.
3083: */
3084:int getloadavg(double loadavg[], int nelem) {
3085:  if (!loadavg || nelem < 1) {
3086:    errno = EINVAL;
3087:    return -1;
3088:  }
3089:  
3090:  struct os1_sysstats stats;
3091:  long ret = OS1_sys_stats(&stats);
3092:  if (ret < 0) {
3093:    errno = (int)-ret;
3094:    return -1;
3095:  }
3096:  
3097:  /* Use the current runnable count (READY+RUNNING processes) as load */
3098:  double load = (double)stats.sched_runnable;
3099:  
3100:  /* Fill the array up to nelem with the same load value */
3101:  for (int i = 0; i < nelem; i++)
3102:    loadavg[i] = load;
3103:  
3104:  return nelem;  /* Return number of elements filled */
3105:}

3126:/*
3127: * exec family - replace the process image (stub).

3132:int execv(const char *pathname, char *const argv[]) {

3162:/*
3163: * localtime - convert time_t to struct tm.
3164: * Canonical OS1 userland implementation kept in lib.c so every ELF gets a
3165: * single consistent UTC conversion path.
3166: */
3167:struct tm *localtime(const time_t *timep) {
3168:  static struct tm result;
3169:  if (!timep)
3170:    return NULL;
3171:
3172:  time_t t = *timep;
3173:  result.tm_sec = t % 60;
3174:  t /= 60;
3175:  result.tm_min = t % 60;
3176:  t /= 60;
3177:  result.tm_hour = t % 24;
3178:  t /= 24;
3179:
3180:  result.tm_wday = (t + 4) % 7;
3181:
3182:  int year = 1970;
3183:  while (1) {
3184:    int days_in_year = 365;
3185:    if ((year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || (year % 400 == 0))
3186:      days_in_year = 366;
3187:    if (t < days_in_year)
3188:      break;
3189:    t -= days_in_year;
3190:    year++;
3191:  }
3192:  result.tm_year = year - 1900;
3193:  result.tm_yday = t;
3194:
3195:  int month_days[] = {31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31};
3196:  if ((year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || (year % 400 == 0))
3197:    month_days[1] = 29;
3198:
3199:  int mon = 0;
3200:  while (t >= month_days[mon]) {
3201:    t -= month_days[mon];
3202:    mon++;
3203:  }
3204:  result.tm_mon = mon;
3205:  result.tm_mday = t + 1;
3206:  result.tm_isdst = 0;
3207:  return &result;
3208:}
3209:
3210:/*
3211: * mktime - convert struct tm to time_t.
3212: */
3213:time_t mktime(struct tm *tm) {
3214:  int year = tm->tm_year + 1900;
3215:  int mon = tm->tm_mon;
3216:  int mday = tm->tm_mday;
3217:
3218:  long days = 0;
3219:  for (int y = 1970; y < year; y++)
3220:    days += ((y % 4 == 0 && y % 100 != 0) || (y % 400 == 0)) ? 366 : 365;
3221:
3222:  int month_days[] = {31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31};
3223:  if ((year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || (year % 400 == 0))
3224:    month_days[1] = 29;
3225:
3226:  for (int m = 0; m < mon; m++)
3227:    days += month_days[m];
3228:  days += mday - 1;
3229:
3230:  return days * 86400 + tm->tm_hour * 3600 + tm->tm_min * 60 + tm->tm_sec;
3231:}

3234: * gmtime - convert time_t to UTC struct tm.
3235: */
3236:struct tm *gmtime(const time_t *timep) {
3237:  return localtime(timep);

3240:/*
3241: * strftime - format a broken-down time in UTC using a minimal subset of
3242: * conversion directives required by Lua and Gnulib.
3243: */
3244:size_t strftime(char *s, size_t max, const char *format, const struct tm *tm) {
3245:  if (!s || !format || !tm || max == 0)
3246:    return 0;
3247:
3248:  size_t out = 0;
3249:  const char *p = format;
3250:  while (*p && out + 1 < max) {
3251:    if (*p != '%') {
3252:      s[out++] = *p++;
3253:      continue;
3254:    }
3255:
3256:    p++;
3257:    if (!*p)
3258:      break;
3259:
3260:    char buf[64];
3261:    int len = 0;
3262:    switch (*p) {
3263:    case '%':
3264:      s[out++] = '%';
3265:      break;
3266:    case 'Y':
3267:      len = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%d", tm->tm_year + 1900);
3268:      break;
3269:    case 'm':
3270:      len = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%02d", tm->tm_mon + 1);
3271:      break;
3272:    case 'd':
3273:      len = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%02d", tm->tm_mday);
3274:      break;
3275:    case 'H':
3276:      len = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%02d", tm->tm_hour);
3277:      break;
3278:    case 'M':
3279:      len = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%02d", tm->tm_min);
3280:      break;
3281:    case 'S':
3282:      len = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%02d", tm->tm_sec);
3283:      break;
3284:    case 'a':
3285:      len = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%s", "Sun");
3286:      break;
3287:    case 'A':
3288:      len = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%s", "Sunday");
3289:      break;
3290:    case 'b':
3291:      len = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%s", "Jan");
3292:      break;
3293:    default:
3294:      s[out++] = *p;
3295:      break;
3296:    }
3297:
3298:    if (len > 0) {
3299:      size_t n = (size_t)len;
3300:      if (n >= max - out)
3301:        n = max - out - 1;
3302:      memcpy(s + out, buf, n);
3303:      out += n;
3304:    }
3305:    p++;
3306:  }
3307:
3308:  s[out] = '\0';
3309:  return out;
3310:}

3346:int rename(const char *oldpath, const char *newpath) {
3347:  int size = OS1_fs_read(oldpath, NULL, 0, 0); /* size probe; errno on miss */
3348:  if (size < 0)
3349:    return -1;
3350:  /* The destination write starts at offset 0, so ext4_write truncates any
3351:   * longer pre-existing dst to exactly the copied length — no separate unlink
3352:   * of newpath is needed to avoid trailing garbage. */
3353:  if (size > 0) {
3354:    char *buf = malloc((size_t)size);
3355:    if (!buf) {
3356:      errno = ENOMEM;
3357:      return -1;
3358:    }
3359:    int n = OS1_fs_read(oldpath, buf, size, 0);
3360:    if (n < 0) {
3361:      free(buf);
3362:      return -1;
3363:    }
3364:    int w = OS1_fs_write(newpath, buf, n, 0);
3365:    free(buf);
3366:    if (w < 0)
3367:      return -1;
3368:  } else if (OS1_fs_write(newpath, "", 0, 0) < 0) {
3369:    return -1;
3370:  }
3371:  OS1_fs_unlink(oldpath);
3372:  return 0;
3373:}

3375:/*
3376: * truncate - set a file's length to exactly `length` (POSIX <unistd.h>).
3377: *
3378: * The NexsOS write model (PLAN-2026-07-17-STRATIFICATION.md Phase 1): a
3379: * from-start write (offset 0) IS the whole-file-replace/truncate primitive at
3380: * the FS layer (ext4_write), so this builds on it with no new kernel call:
3381: *   - length == 0        -> a zero-byte offset-0 write empties the file;
3382: *   - length <  size     -> re-write the first `length` bytes at offset 0,
3383: *                           which truncates the tail;
3384: *   - length >  size     -> zero-extend from the old EOF.
3385: * Explicit truncation for programs that don't go through fopen("w").
3386: * ftruncate(fd) needs an fd->path or an OBJ_CTL_TRUNCATE verb (a kernel
3387: * follow-up), so it is intentionally not provided yet rather than faked.
3388: */
3389:int truncate(const char *path, long length) {
3390:  if (length < 0) {
3391:    errno = EINVAL;
3392:    return -1;
3393:  }
3394:  int size = OS1_fs_read(path, NULL, 0, 0); /* current size; errno on miss */
3395:  if (size < 0)
3396:    return -1;
3397:  if (length == (long)size)
3398:    return 0;
3399:  if (length == 0)
3400:    return OS1_fs_write(path, "", 0, 0) < 0 ? -1 : 0;
3401:  if (length < (long)size) {
3402:    char *buf = malloc((size_t)length);
3403:    if (!buf) {
3404:      errno = ENOMEM;
3405:      return -1;
3406:    }
3407:    int n = OS1_fs_read(path, buf, (int)length, 0);
3408:    int r = (n < 0 || OS1_fs_write(path, buf, n, 0) < 0) ? -1 : 0;
3409:    free(buf);
3410:    return r;
3411:  }
3412:  /* extend: zero-fill from the old EOF up to `length` */
3413:  {
3414:    long pad = length - (long)size;
3415:    char *z = calloc(1, (size_t)pad);
3416:    if (!z) {
3417:      errno = ENOMEM;
3418:      return -1;
3419:    }
3420:    int r = OS1_fs_write(path, z, (int)pad, size) < 0 ? -1 : 0;
3421:    free(z);
3422:    return r;
3423:  }
3424:}
3425:/*
3426: * ftruncate - set an OPEN descriptor's file length (POSIX).  Closes the Phase 1
3427: * leftover ("ftruncate awaits an fd->path / OBJ_CTL_TRUNCATE kernel verb").
3428: *
3429: * Composed from the primitives rather than duplicating truncate()'s path-based
3430: * logic in the kernel:
3431: *   - shrink to N>0: read the first N bytes back, then rewrite them from offset
3432: *     0 — an offset-0 write REPLACES the whole file (the Phase 1 FS standard),
3433: *     so the rewrite IS the truncation;
3434: *   - shrink to 0: needs OBJ_CTL_TRUNCATE, because POSIX defines
3435: *     write(fd, buf, 0) as a NO-OP and so it cannot express "empty this file";
3436: *   - extend: zero-fill from the old EOF up to the new length.
3437: */
3438:int ftruncate(int fd, long length) {
3439:  if (length < 0) {
3440:    errno = EINVAL;
3441:    return -1;
3442:  }
3443:  long size = lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_END);
3444:  if (size < 0)
3445:    return -1;
3446:  if (length == size)
3447:    return 0;
3448:
3449:  if (length == 0)
3450:    return OS1_object_ctl(fd, OBJ_CTL_TRUNCATE, 0) < 0 ? -1 : 0;
3451:
3452:  if (length < size) {
3453:    char *buf = malloc((size_t)length);
3454:    if (!buf) {
3455:      errno = ENOMEM;
3456:      return -1;
3457:    }
3458:    int r = -1;
3459:    if (lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_SET) >= 0) {
3460:      long n = read(fd, buf, (unsigned long)length);
3461:      if (n >= 0 && lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_SET) >= 0 &&
3462:          write(fd, buf, (size_t)n) >= 0)
3463:        r = 0; /* offset-0 write replaced the file with n bytes */
3464:    }
3465:    free(buf);
3466:    return r;
3467:  }
3468:
3469:  { /* extend: zero-fill from the old EOF up to `length` */
3470:    long pad = length - size;
3471:    char *z = calloc(1, (size_t)pad);
3472:    if (!z) {
3473:      errno = ENOMEM;
3474:      return -1;
3475:    }
3476:    int r = (lseek(fd, size, SEEK_SET) >= 0 && write(fd, z, (size_t)pad) >= 0)
3477:                ? 0
3478:                : -1;
3479:    free(z);
3480:    return r;
3481:  }
3482:}

3492:/*
3493: * utf8_decode - decode the first UTF-8 codepoint from string s.
3494: *
3495: * s:    pointer to the start of a UTF-8 byte sequence (not necessarily NUL).
3496: * code: output parameter; receives the Unicode codepoint on success.
3497: *
3498: * Returns the number of bytes consumed (1–4), or 0 on invalid/null input.
3499: *
3500: * Encoding rules applied:
3501: *   0xxxxxxx (< 0x80)      : 1-byte ASCII
3502: *   110xxxxx 10xxxxxx      : 2-byte (U+0080..U+07FF)
3503: *   1110xxxx 10xxxxxx x2   : 3-byte (U+0800..U+FFFF)
3504: *   11110xxx 10xxxxxx x3   : 4-byte (U+10000..U+10FFFF)
3505: *
3506: * No validation of continuation bytes (0x3F mask is applied without checking
3507: * the 0x80 bit); malformed sequences may produce incorrect codepoints silently.
3508: *
3509: * Used by font_lib.c:font_draw_string() to iterate a UTF-8 string glyph by
3510: * glyph.
3511: */
3512:int utf8_decode(const char *s, size_t len, uint32_t *code) {
3513:  if (!s || !code || len == 0)
3514:    return 0;
3515:  unsigned char c = (unsigned char)s[0];
3516:
3517:  if (c < 0x80) {
3518:    *code = c;
3519:    return 1;
3520:  } else if ((c & 0xE0) == 0xC0) {
3521:    if (len < 2 || (s[1] & 0xC0) != 0x80)
3522:      return 0;
3523:    *code = ((uint32_t)(c & 0x1F) << 6) | (uint32_t)(s[1] & 0x3F);
3524:    if (*code < 0x80)
3525:      return 0;
3526:    return 2;
3527:  } else if ((c & 0xF0) == 0xE0) {
3528:    if (len < 3 || (s[1] & 0xC0) != 0x80 || (s[2] & 0xC0) != 0x80)
3529:      return 0;
3530:    *code = ((uint32_t)(c & 0x0F) << 12) | ((uint32_t)(s[1] & 0x3F) << 6) |
3531:            (uint32_t)(s[2] & 0x3F);
3532:    if (*code < 0x800)
3533:      return 0;
3534:    if (*code >= 0xD800 && *code <= 0xDFFF)
3535:      return 0;
3536:    return 3;
3537:  } else if ((c & 0xF8) == 0xF0) {
3538:    if (len < 4 || (s[1] & 0xC0) != 0x80 || (s[2] & 0xC0) != 0x80 ||
3539:        (s[3] & 0xC0) != 0x80)
3540:      return 0;
3541:    *code = ((uint32_t)(c & 0x07) << 18) | ((uint32_t)(s[1] & 0x3F) << 12) |
3542:            ((uint32_t)(s[2] & 0x3F) << 6) | (uint32_t)(s[3] & 0x3F);
3543:    if (*code < 0x10000)
3544:      return 0;
3545:    if (*code > 0x10FFFF)
3546:      return 0;
3547:    return 4;
3548:  }
3549:  return 0;
3550:}

3563:char *strtok_r(char *str, const char *delim, char **saveptr) {
3564:  char *s = str ? str : *saveptr;
3565:  if (!s)
3566:    return NULL;
3567:  while (*s && strchr(delim, (int)(unsigned char)*s))
3568:    s++;
3569:  if (*s == '\0') {
3570:    *saveptr = s;
3571:    return NULL;
3572:  }
3573:  char *tok = s;
3574:  while (*s && !strchr(delim, (int)(unsigned char)*s))
3575:    s++;
3576:  if (*s) {
3577:    *s = '\0';
3578:    s++;
3579:  }
3580:  *saveptr = s;
3581:  return tok;
3582:}

3629:/* strtoul / strtoull — unsigned variants of strtol */
3630:unsigned long strtoul(const char *nptr, char **endptr, int base) {
3631:  while (*nptr == ' ' || *nptr == '\t' || *nptr == '\n' ||
3632:         *nptr == '\r' || *nptr == '\f' || *nptr == '\v')
3633:    nptr++;
3634:  int neg = 0;
3635:  if (*nptr == '-') { neg = 1; nptr++; }
3636:  else if (*nptr == '+') nptr++;
3637:  if (base == 0) {
3638:    if (nptr[0] == '0' && (nptr[1] == 'x' || nptr[1] == 'X')) {
3639:      base = 16; nptr += 2;
3640:    } else if (nptr[0] == '0') {
3641:      base = 8; nptr++;
3642:    } else {
3643:      base = 10;
3644:    }
3645:  } else if (base == 16 && nptr[0] == '0' &&
3646:             (nptr[1] == 'x' || nptr[1] == 'X')) {
3647:    nptr += 2;
3648:  }
3649:  unsigned long result = 0;
3650:  const char *start = nptr;
3651:  while (*nptr) {
3652:    int digit;
3653:    if (*nptr >= '0' && *nptr <= '9')      digit = *nptr - '0';
3654:    else if (*nptr >= 'a' && *nptr <= 'z') digit = *nptr - 'a' + 10;
3655:    else if (*nptr >= 'A' && *nptr <= 'Z') digit = *nptr - 'A' + 10;
3656:    else break;
3657:    if (digit >= base) break;
3658:    result = result * (unsigned long)base + (unsigned long)digit;
3659:    nptr++;
3660:  }
3661:  if (endptr) *endptr = (char *)(nptr == start ? start : nptr);
3662:  return neg ? -result : result;
3663:}
3664:
3665:unsigned long long strtoull(const char *nptr, char **endptr, int base) {
3666:  return (unsigned long long)strtoul(nptr, endptr, base);
3667:}

3674:/* qsort: in-place insertion sort with byte-wise swaps (no temp buffer / VLA,
3675: * no recursion).  O(n^2) but adequate for the small arrays NEXS sorts. */
3676:void qsort(void *base, size_t nmemb, size_t size,
3677:           int (*compar)(const void *, const void *)) {
3678:  char *arr = (char *)base;
3679:  for (size_t i = 1; i < nmemb; i++) {
3680:    for (size_t j = i;
3681:         j > 0 && compar(arr + (j - 1) * size, arr + j * size) > 0; j--) {
3682:      char *a = arr + (j - 1) * size;
3683:      char *b = arr + j * size;
3684:      for (size_t k = 0; k < size; k++) {
3685:        char t = a[k];
3686:        a[k] = b[k];
3687:        b[k] = t;
3688:      }
3689:    }
3690:  }
3691:}

3697:FILE _stdout_struct = {.fd = 1};
3698:FILE _stderr_struct = {.fd = 2};
3699:
3700:/* file_fd - the descriptor behind a stream, or -1 for a positional
3701: * (path-backed) one.  The three console streams carry fd 0/1/2 in their own
3702: * structs and fopen() sets fd = -1 to select path I/O, so returning the field
3703: * is EXACTLY equivalent to the old stdin/stdout/stderr pointer comparison —
3704: * and additionally makes fdopen()'d streams (e.g. a pipe end wrapped in a
3705: * FILE*) route through read()/write() like any other descriptor. */
3706:static int file_fd(FILE *fp) { return fp ? fp->fd : -1; }
3707:
3708:/*
3709: * fputc/fputs/fgetc delegate to fwrite/fread rather than calling write()/read()
3710: * on the descriptor themselves.
3711: *
3712: * They used to take an `if (fd >= 0)` shortcut straight to the syscall.  That
3713: * was correct while only the console had a descriptor and a path-backed FILE
3714: * had none — but a FILE now keeps an open handle for its lifetime, so `fd >= 0`
3715: * became true for ordinary files too and the shortcut started bypassing the
3716: * stream buffers.  The consequences were not symmetric and neither was
3717: * cosmetic:
3718: *
3719: *   - fgetc read one byte straight from the descriptor and never advanced
3720: *     fp->pos.  A reader that mixes getc() with fread() — which is exactly what
3721: *     Lua's loader does when it skips a `#!` line — desynchronised: fread then
3722: *     refilled from the stale fp->pos and re-read the file from the beginning.
3723: *   - fputc/fputs wrote straight through while buffered bytes were still
3724: *     pending in wbuf, so the two landed out of order: silent corruption, not a
3725: *     visible failure.
3726: *
3727: * fread/fwrite already own the one correct rule — the descriptor fast path is
3728: * for CONSOLE/pipe streams only (`path[0] == '\0'`), never for a file — so
3729: * these three defer to it instead of carrying a second, older copy of the same
3730: * decision.  ext4's 4 KiB read-modify-write granularity is why that rule
3731: * exists; see the comment in fwrite.
3732: */
3733:int fputc(int c, FILE *fp) {
3734:  unsigned char ch = (unsigned char)c;
3735:  if (fwrite(&ch, 1, 1, fp) != 1)
3736:    return EOF;
3737:  return (int)ch;
3738:}
3739:
3740:int fputs(const char *s, FILE *fp) {
3741:  size_t len = strlen(s);
3742:  if (len && fwrite(s, 1, len, fp) != len)
3743:    return EOF;
3744:  return 0;
3745:}
3746:
3747:int fgetc(FILE *fp) {
3748:  if (!fp)
3749:    return EOF;
3750:  if (fp->has_ungetc) {
3751:    fp->has_ungetc = 0;
3752:    return fp->ungetc_buf;
3753:  }
3754:  unsigned char ch;
3755:  if (fread(&ch, 1, 1, fp) != 1)
3756:    return EOF;
3757:  return (int)ch;
3758:}
3759:
3760:char *fgets(char *s, int size, FILE *fp) {
3761:  if (size <= 0)
3762:    return NULL;
3763:  int i = 0;
3764:  while (i < size - 1) {
3765:    int c = fgetc(fp);
3766:    if (c == EOF) {
3767:      if (i == 0)
3768:        return NULL;
3769:      break;
3770:    }
3771:    s[i++] = (char)c;
3772:    if (c == '\n')
3773:      break;
3774:  }
3775:  s[i] = '\0';
3776:  return s;
3777:}
3778:
3779:int ungetc(int c, FILE *fp) {
3780:  if (!fp || c == EOF)
3781:    return EOF;
3782:  fp->ungetc_buf = c;
3783:  fp->has_ungetc = 1;
3784:  fp->eof = 0;
3785:  return c;
3786:}
3787:
3788:/*
3789: * rewind - POSIX: equivalent to fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_SET) except that it also
3790: * clears the error indicator and returns nothing.  Added because it was the one
3791: * standard stdio entry point missing from this libc, and code ported from POSIX
3792: * reaches for it after a failed read; without it the link failed rather than
3793: * the call misbehaving, which is why it went unnoticed.
3794: */
3795:void rewind(FILE *fp) {
3796:  if (!fp)
3797:    return;
3798:  fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_SET);
3799:  fp->error = 0;
3800:}

3944:/* --- <sys/ioctl.h> --- only TIOCGWINSZ, answered from the window grid. */
3945:int ioctl(int fd, unsigned long request, ...) {
3946:  (void)fd;
3947:  if (request == TIOCGWINSZ) {
3948:    va_list ap;
3949:    va_start(ap, request);
3950:    struct winsize *ws = va_arg(ap, struct winsize *);
3951:    va_end(ap);
3952:    int cols = 0, rows = 0;
3953:    int wid = window_of_pid(get_pid());
3954:    if (ws && wid > 0 && window_grid(wid, &cols, &rows) == 0) {
3955:      ws->ws_col = (unsigned short)cols;
3956:      ws->ws_row = (unsigned short)rows;
3957:      ws->ws_xpixel = 0;
3958:      ws->ws_ypixel = 0;
3959:      return 0;
3960:    }
3961:  }
3962:  return -1;
3963:}

3965:/* --- <dirent.h> --- over list_dir() (space-separated names from ext4_list). */
3966:DIR *opendir(const char *name) {
3967:  /* Verify it IS a directory before listing.  opendir() used to rely on
3968:   * list_dir failing for a regular file; since a directory is now read through
3969:   * the same object path as a file, listing a FILE returns its content and the
3970:   * call would "succeed" on anything.  Callers use opendir() as the
3971:   * file-or-directory test (the file manager does), so this must be exact. */
3972:  struct abi_stat as;
3973:  if (_sys_stat(name, &as) != 0 || as.type != ABI_S_TYPE_DIR) {
3974:    errno = ENOTDIR;
3975:    return NULL;
3976:  }
3977:  DIR *d = malloc(sizeof(DIR));
3978:  if (!d)
3979:    return NULL;
3980:  if (list_dir(name, d->buf, sizeof(d->buf)) < 0) {
3981:    free(d);
3982:    return NULL;
3983:  }
3984:  d->pos = 0;
3985:  return d;
3986:}

3988:struct dirent *readdir(DIR *dirp) {
3989:  if (!dirp)
3990:    return NULL;
3991:  while (dirp->buf[dirp->pos] == ' ')
3992:    dirp->pos++;
3993:  if (dirp->buf[dirp->pos] == '\0')
3994:    return NULL;
3995:  int i = 0;
3996:  while (dirp->buf[dirp->pos] != ' ' && dirp->buf[dirp->pos] != '\0' &&
3997:         i < (int)sizeof(dirp->ent.d_name) - 1)
3998:    dirp->ent.d_name[i++] = dirp->buf[dirp->pos++];
3999:  dirp->ent.d_name[i] = '\0';
4000:  dirp->ent.d_ino = 0;
4001:  dirp->ent.d_type = DT_UNKNOWN;
4002:  return &dirp->ent;
4003:}

4010:size_t strspn(const char *s, const char *accept) {
4011:  const char *p = s;
4012:  while (*p) {
4013:    const char *a = accept;
4014:    while (*a && *a != *p) {
4015:      a++;
4016:    }
4017:    if (*a == '\0') {
4018:      break;
4019:    }
4020:    p++;
4021:  }
4022:  return p - s;
4023:}

4025:size_t strcspn(const char *s, const char *reject) {
4026:  const char *p = s;
4027:  while (*p) {
4028:    const char *r = reject;
4029:    while (*r) {
4030:      if (*p == *r)
4031:        return p - s;
4032:      r++;
4033:    }
4034:    p++;
4035:  }
4036:  return p - s;
4037:}

4130:static int wctype_value(wint_t wc, const char *property) {
4131:  if (!property)
4132:    return 0;
4133:  if (strcmp(property, "alnum") == 0) return iswalnum(wc);
4134:  if (strcmp(property, "alpha") == 0) return iswalpha(wc);
4135:  if (strcmp(property, "blank") == 0) return iswblank(wc);
4136:  if (strcmp(property, "cntrl") == 0) return iswcntrl(wc);
4137:  if (strcmp(property, "digit") == 0) return iswdigit(wc);
4138:  if (strcmp(property, "graph") == 0) return iswgraph(wc);
4139:  if (strcmp(property, "lower") == 0) return iswlower(wc);
4140:  if (strcmp(property, "print") == 0) return iswprint(wc);
4141:  if (strcmp(property, "punct") == 0) return iswpunct(wc);
4142:  if (strcmp(property, "space") == 0) return iswspace(wc);
4143:  if (strcmp(property, "upper") == 0) return iswupper(wc);
4144:  if (strcmp(property, "xdigit") == 0) return iswxdigit(wc);
4145:  if (strcmp(property, "any") == 0) return 1;
4146:  return 0;
4147:}

4394:ssize_t writev(int fd, const struct iovec *iov, int iovcnt) {
4395:  if (iovcnt < 0 || !iov) {
4396:    errno = EINVAL;
4397:    return -1;
4398:  }
4399:  ssize_t total = 0;
4400:  for (int i = 0; i < iovcnt; i++) {
4401:    if (iov[i].iov_len == 0)
4402:      continue;
4403:    if (!iov[i].iov_base) {
4404:      errno = EFAULT;
4405:      return -1;
4406:    }
4407:    long w = write(fd, iov[i].iov_base, iov[i].iov_len);
4408:    if (w < 0) {
4409:      return total > 0 ? total : -1;
4410:    }
4411:    total += w;
4412:    if ((size_t)w < iov[i].iov_len)
4413:      break;
4414:  }
4415:  return total;
4416:}
4417:

4419:  if (iovcnt < 0 || !iov) {
4420:    errno = EINVAL;
4421:    return -1;
4422:  }
4423:  ssize_t total = 0;
4424:  for (int i = 0; i < iovcnt; i++) {
4425:    if (iov[i].iov_len == 0)
4426:      continue;
4427:    if (!iov[i].iov_base) {
4428:      errno = EFAULT;
4429:      return -1;
4430:    }
4431:    long r = read(fd, iov[i].iov_base, iov[i].iov_len);
4432:    if (r <= 0) {
4433:      return total > 0 ? total : r;
4434:    }
4435:    total += r;
4436:    if ((size_t)r < iov[i].iov_len)
4437:      break;
4438:  }
4439:  return total;

4772:/*
4773: * utime - set access and modification times of a file.
4774: * times == NULL → set both to current time.
4775: */
4776:__attribute__((weak))
4777:int utime(const char *path, const struct utimbuf *times)
4778:{
4779:    if (!path) {
4780:        errno = EFAULT;
4781:        return -1;
4782:    }
4783:
4784:    /* Assicuriamoci che il file esista (comportamento di touch) */
4785:    struct stat st;
4786:    if (stat(path, &st) != 0) {
4787:        int fd = open(path, O_CREAT | O_WRONLY | O_TRUNC, 0644);
4788:        if (fd < 0)
4789:            return -1;
4790:        close(fd);
4791:    }
4792:
4793:    (void)times;   /* il filesystem non salva ancora i timestamp */
4794:    return 0;
4795:}
4796:
4797:__attribute__((weak))
4798:int utimes(const char *path, const struct timeval times[2])
4799:{
4800:    if (!path) {
4801:        errno = EFAULT;
4802:        return -1;
4803:    }
4804:
4805:    struct utimbuf buf;
4806:    if (times) {
4807:        buf.actime  = times[0].tv_sec;
4808:        buf.modtime = times[1].tv_sec;
4809:    } else {
4810:        time_t now = time(NULL);
4811:        buf.actime  = now;
4812:        buf.modtime = now;
4813:    }
4814:    return utime(path, times ? &buf : NULL);
4815:}
4816:
4817:__attribute__((weak))
4818:int utimensat(int dirfd, const char *path,
4819:              const struct timespec times[2], int flags)
4820:{
4821:    (void)flags;
4822:
4823:    if (dirfd != AT_FDCWD) {
4824:        errno = ENOTSUP;
4825:        return -1;
4826:    }
4827:    if (!path) {
4828:        errno = EFAULT;
4829:        return -1;
4830:    }
4831:
4832:    struct timeval tv[2];
4833:    if (times) {
4834:        tv[0].tv_sec  = times[0].tv_sec;
4835:        tv[0].tv_usec = times[0].tv_nsec / 1000;
4836:        tv[1].tv_sec  = times[1].tv_sec;
4837:        tv[1].tv_usec = times[1].tv_nsec / 1000;
4838:    }
4839:    return utimes(path, times ? tv : NULL);
4840:}
4841:__attribute__((weak))
4842:int futimens(int fd, const struct timespec times[2])
4843:{
4844:    if (fd < 0) {
4845:        errno = EBADF;
4846:        return -1;
4847:    }
4848:    (void)times;
4849:    return 0;
4850:}

@@@ user/sys/lib/malloc.c @@@
1:/*
2: * user/sys/lib/malloc.c
3: * Userland Heap Allocator — segregated free lists + boundary-tag coalescing
4: *
5: * Built entirely on top of OS1's SYS_SBRK (#216) via _sys_sbrk(); no other
6: * kernel primitive is required. This replaces the earlier "singly linked
7: * free/alloc chain" design with the standard technique (Knuth's boundary
8: * tags, as used by dlmalloc-family allocators) so correctness no longer
9: * depends on maintaining an address-order invariant by hand.
10: *
11: * ---- Block layout ----
12: *
13: *   [ header (16B) ][ payload (>=32B, 16B-aligned) ][ footer (8B) ]
14: *
15: *   header.size / footer.size both hold the TOTAL block size (header +
16: *   payload + footer) with bit0 used as the FREE flag. Every block's total
17: *   size is a multiple of 16 by construction, so bit0 is otherwise always
18: *   0 and safe to steal for the flag.
19: *
20: *   Storing the size at BOTH ends means any block's neighbours — forward
21: *   (address + size) or backward (read the size word immediately before
22: *   this block's header) — can be located and inspected in O(1), for ANY
23: *   block, allocated or free, however it was created. This is what makes
24: *   coalescing safe without assuming a block's list-neighbour is its
25: *   memory-neighbour (the bug in the previous design, USR-MALLOC-02).
26: *
27: *   A FREE block additionally overlays two pointers (next/prev) at the
28: *   start of its payload — the intrusive doubly-linked list node for its
29: *   size bin. Safe because payload is always >= 32 bytes when free.
30: *
31: * ---- Allocation strategy ----
32: *
33: *   8 segregated bins by payload size (32/64/128/256/512/1024/2048/+inf).
34: *   malloc() does first-fit *within and above* the requested bin — an
35: *   approximate best-fit that is O(1) amortized for the common case
36: *   instead of O(n) over the whole heap.
37: *
38: * ---- What this fixes relative to the original allocator ----
39: *
40: *   USR-MALLOC-02 (coalescing corruption): gone by construction — no
41: *     "assume physical adjacency" step exists anymore; boundary tags let
42: *     us verify it directly.
43: *   USR-MALLOC-03 (no backward coalescing): implemented (see free()).
44: *   USR-MALLOC-04 (heap never shrinks): the trailing free block is
45: *     returned to the kernel via a negative sbrk() in free().
46: *   USR-MALLOC-05 (payload not 16-byte aligned): fixed for real — the
47: *     16-byte header plus the size-residue trick below guarantee every
48: *     payload starts 16-byte aligned (given a 16-aligned heap start,
49: *     which grow_heap() enforces defensively on first use).
50: *   USR-MALLOC-06 (realloc shrink check): realloc() below compares
51: *     against actual old payload capacity, same tradeoff as before
52: *     (documented, not a correctness bug) — still returns in place when
53: *     it fits, to avoid pointless copies.
54: */
55:#include <os1.h>
56:#include <stddef.h>
57:#include <stdint.h>
58:
59:typedef struct header {
60:  size_t size;   /* total block size | FREE_BIT (see above) */
61:  size_t canary; /* unused; pads header to 16B so payload is 16B-aligned */
62:} header_t;
63:
64:typedef struct free_node {
65:  struct free_node *next;
66:  struct free_node *prev;
67:} free_node_t;
68:
69:#define HEADER_SIZE (sizeof(header_t)) /* 16 */
70:#define FOOTER_SIZE (sizeof(size_t))   /* 8  */
71:#define FREE_BIT ((size_t)1)
72:#define SIZE_MASK (~FREE_BIT)
73:#define MALLOC_ALIGN 16UL
74:#define MIN_PAYLOAD 32UL /* room for a free_node_t plus slack */
75:#define MIN_BLOCK (HEADER_SIZE + MIN_PAYLOAD + FOOTER_SIZE)
76:#define NUM_BINS 8
77:
78:static free_node_t *bins[NUM_BINS];
79:static uint8_t *heap_start = NULL;
80:static uint8_t *heap_end = NULL; /* current program break */
81:
82:/* ---------------- boundary-tag helpers ---------------- */
83:
84:static inline size_t blk_size(header_t *h) { return h->size & SIZE_MASK; }
85:static inline int blk_free(header_t *h) { return (int)(h->size & FREE_BIT); }
86:
87:/* Writes both the header and the mirrored footer in one place, so the two
88: * can never drift apart. Every size/flag change goes through this. */
89:static void set_block(header_t *h, size_t total_size, int is_free) {
90:  size_t enc = (total_size & SIZE_MASK) | (is_free ? FREE_BIT : 0);
91:  h->size = enc;
92:  *(size_t *)((uint8_t *)h + total_size - FOOTER_SIZE) = enc;
93:}
94:
95:static header_t *node_to_header(free_node_t *n) {
96:  return (header_t *)((uint8_t *)n - HEADER_SIZE);
97:}
98:
99:static int bin_index(size_t payload) {
100:  static const size_t thresh[NUM_BINS - 1] = {32,  64,   128, 256,
101:                                              512, 1024, 2048};
102:  for (int i = 0; i < NUM_BINS - 1; i++)
103:    if (payload <= thresh[i])
104:      return i;
105:  return NUM_BINS - 1;
106:}
107:
108:static void bin_remove(header_t *h) {
109:  free_node_t *n = (free_node_t *)(h + 1);
110:  int idx = bin_index(blk_size(h) - HEADER_SIZE - FOOTER_SIZE);
111:  if (n->prev)
112:    n->prev->next = n->next;
113:  else
114:    bins[idx] = n->next;
115:  if (n->next)
116:    n->next->prev = n->prev;
117:}
118:
119:static void bin_insert(header_t *h) {
120:  int idx = bin_index(blk_size(h) - HEADER_SIZE - FOOTER_SIZE);
121:  free_node_t *n = (free_node_t *)(h + 1);
122:  n->prev = NULL;
123:  n->next = bins[idx];
124:  if (bins[idx])
125:    bins[idx]->prev = n;
126:  bins[idx] = n;
127:}
128:
129:/* ---------------- sbrk shims (unchanged ABI) ---------------- */
130:
131:void *OS1low_vm_sbrk(intptr_t increment) { return _sys_sbrk(increment); }
132:void *sbrk(intptr_t increment) { return OS1low_vm_sbrk(increment); }
133:
134:/*
135: * sbrk_failed - did this sbrk() return an error rather than a break address?
136: *
137: * SYS_SBRK (kernel/sched/process.c sys_sbrk) returns a NEGATIVE errno on
138: * failure — -ENOMEM when the heap hits SBRK_HEAP_LIMIT or a page can't be
139: * allocated, -EINVAL on a bad shrink — NOT the (void *)-1 that plain sbrk()
140: * uses.  Any value in the top page ([-4095, -1]) is such an error code; a
141: * real user-heap break never lands there.  Checking only ==(void *)-1 let
142: * -ENOMEM (-12 -> 0xfffffffffffffff4) slip through as a "pointer", and
143: * grow_heap()/set_block() then wrote a block header to it: the Data Abort at
144: * addr=0xfffffffffffffff4 in malloc under memory pressure (Lua GC stress).
145: */
146:static inline int sbrk_failed(void *p) {
147:  return (uintptr_t)p >= (uintptr_t)(-4095);
148:}
149:
150:/* Grows the heap by exactly min_total bytes (already a multiple of 16) and
151: * returns a fresh block header covering the extension, marked free. On the
152: * very first call it defensively aligns the initial break up to 16 bytes
153: * (via a tiny probe + pad sbrk) in case the kernel's initial break isn't
154: * already aligned — everything after that stays aligned by induction,
155: * since every block's total size is a multiple of 16. */
156:static header_t *grow_heap(size_t min_total) {
157:  if (!heap_start) {
158:    void *probe = sbrk(0);
159:    if (!sbrk_failed(probe)) {
160:      uintptr_t addr = (uintptr_t)probe;
161:      uintptr_t pad =
162:          (MALLOC_ALIGN - (addr & (MALLOC_ALIGN - 1))) & (MALLOC_ALIGN - 1);
163:      if (pad) {
164:        if (sbrk_failed(sbrk((intptr_t)pad)))
165:          return NULL;
166:      }
167:    }
168:  }
169:
170:  void *p = sbrk((intptr_t)min_total);
171:  if (sbrk_failed(p))
172:    return NULL;
173:
174:  if (!heap_start)
175:    heap_start = (uint8_t *)p;
176:  heap_end = (uint8_t *)p + min_total;
177:
178:  header_t *h = (header_t *)p;
179:  set_block(h, min_total, 1);
180:  return h;
181:}
182:
183:/* ---------------- malloc ---------------- */
184:
185:void *malloc(size_t size) {
186:  if (size == 0)
187:    return NULL;
188:
189:  /* Round up to 16, then add an 8-byte residue so that
190:   * HEADER(16) + payload + FOOTER(8) is itself always a multiple of 16
191:   * — this is what keeps every block's payload 16-byte aligned. */
192:  size_t payload = (size + (MALLOC_ALIGN - 1)) & ~(MALLOC_ALIGN - 1);
193:  if (payload < MIN_PAYLOAD)
194:    payload = MIN_PAYLOAD;
195:  payload += 8;
196:
197:  size_t need = HEADER_SIZE + payload + FOOTER_SIZE;
198:
199:  int start_bin = bin_index(payload);
200:  for (int b = start_bin; b < NUM_BINS; b++) {
201:    for (free_node_t *n = bins[b]; n; n = n->next) {
202:      header_t *h = node_to_header(n);
203:      if (blk_size(h) < need)
204:        continue;
205:
206:      bin_remove(h);
207:      size_t total = blk_size(h);
208:      size_t remainder = total - need;
209:
210:      if (remainder >= MIN_BLOCK) {
211:        set_block(h, need, 0);
212:        header_t *rem = (header_t *)((uint8_t *)h + need);
213:        set_block(rem, remainder, 1);
214:        bin_insert(rem);
215:      } else {
216:        set_block(h, total, 0); /* keep the few extra bytes */
217:      }
218:      return (void *)(h + 1);
219:    }
220:  }
221:
222:  /* Nothing fits in any bin: extend the heap for exactly this request. */
223:  header_t *h = grow_heap(need);
224:  if (!h)
225:    return NULL;
226:  set_block(h, need, 0);
227:  return (void *)(h + 1);
228:}
229:
230:/* ---------------- free ---------------- */
231:
232:void free(void *ptr) {
233:  if (!ptr)
234:    return;
235:
236:  header_t *h = (header_t *)ptr - 1;
237:  size_t total = blk_size(h);
238:  set_block(h, total, 1);
239:
240:  /* Forward coalesce: the boundary tag lets us check the ACTUAL next
241:   * block in memory directly, whatever it is — no assumption needed. */
242:  uint8_t *next_addr = (uint8_t *)h + total;
243:  if (next_addr < heap_end) {
244:    header_t *nh = (header_t *)next_addr;
245:    if (blk_free(nh)) {
246:      bin_remove(nh);
247:      total += blk_size(nh);
248:      set_block(h, total, 1);
249:    }
250:  }
251:
252:  /* Backward coalesce: read the size word immediately before this
253:   * block's header (the previous block's footer) to jump straight to
254:   * its header in O(1) and check whether IT is free. */
255:  if ((uint8_t *)h > heap_start) {
256:    size_t prev_enc = *((size_t *)h - 1);
257:    size_t prev_size = prev_enc & SIZE_MASK;
258:    header_t *ph = (header_t *)((uint8_t *)h - prev_size);
259:    if (blk_free(ph)) {
260:      bin_remove(ph);
261:      total = prev_size + total;
262:      set_block(ph, total, 1);
263:      h = ph;
264:    }
265:  }
266:
267:  /* If the coalesced free block now reaches the end of the heap, hand
268:   * it back to the kernel instead of keeping it around unused. */
269:  if ((uint8_t *)h + total == heap_end) {
270:    heap_end = (uint8_t *)h;
271:    sbrk(-(intptr_t)total);
272:    return;
273:  }
274:
275:  bin_insert(h);
276:}
277:
278:/* ---------------- realloc ---------------- */
279:
280:void *realloc(void *ptr, size_t size) {
281:  if (!ptr)
282:    return malloc(size);
283:  if (size == 0) {
284:    free(ptr);
285:    return NULL;
286:  }
287:
288:  header_t *h = (header_t *)ptr - 1;
289:  size_t old_payload = blk_size(h) - HEADER_SIZE - FOOTER_SIZE;
290:
291:  if (old_payload >= size)
292:    return ptr; /* already fits */
293:
294:  void *new_ptr = malloc(size);
295:  if (new_ptr) {
296:    memcpy(new_ptr, ptr, old_payload);
297:    free(ptr);
298:  }
299:  return new_ptr;
300:}
301:
302:/* ---------------- calloc ---------------- */
303:
304:void *calloc(size_t nmemb, size_t size) {
305:  /* Pre-multiply overflow check (USR-MALLOC-01): rejects any input whose
306:   * product would wrap, without relying on the wraparound happening. */
307:  if (nmemb != 0 && size > SIZE_MAX / nmemb)
308:    return NULL;
309:
310:  size_t total = nmemb * size;
311:  void *ptr = malloc(total);
312:  if (ptr)
313:    memset(ptr, 0, total);
314:  return ptr;
315:}

128:/* ============================================================================
129: * Square root — Newton-Raphson iteration
130: * ============================================================================

132:
133:float sqrtf(float x) {
134:  if (__f32_bits(x) == 0 || __f32_bits(x) == 0x80000000u)
135:    return x;
136:  if (__f32_abs_bits(x) > 0x7f800000u)
137:    return x;
138:  if (__f32_bits(x) >> 31)
139:    return __f32_from_bits(0x7fc00000u);
140:  if (__f32_abs_bits(x) == 0x7f800000u)
141:    return x;
142:
143:  uint32_t ix = __f32_bits(x);
144:  uint32_t est = (ix >> 1) + 0x1fbb67a8u;
145:  float y = __f32_from_bits(est);
146:
147:  y = 0.5f * (y + x / y);
148:  y = 0.5f * (y + x / y);
149:  y = 0.5f * (y + x / y);
150:  return y;
151:}
152:
153:double sqrt(double x) {
154:  if (__f64_bits(x) == 0 || __f64_bits(x) == 0x8000000000000000ULL)
155:    return x;
156:  if (__f64_abs_bits(x) > 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
157:    return x;
158:  if (__f64_bits(x) >> 63)
159:    return __f64_from_bits(0x7ff8000000000000ULL);
160:  if (__f64_abs_bits(x) == 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
161:    return x;
162:
163:  uint64_t ix = __f64_bits(x);
164:  uint64_t est = (ix >> 1) + 0x1ff7a7bea2a2a2a2ULL;
165:  double y = __f64_from_bits(est);
166:
167:  y = 0.5 * (y + x / y);
168:  y = 0.5 * (y + x / y);
169:  y = 0.5 * (y + x / y);
170:  y = 0.5 * (y + x / y);
171:  return y;
172:}

179:float floorf(float x) {
180:  uint32_t ix = __f32_bits(x);
181:  int e = (int)((ix >> 23) & 0xff) - 0x7f;
182:  uint32_t m;
183:
184:  if (e >= 23)
185:    return x;
186:  if (e < 0) {
187:    if (ix >> 31)
188:      return -1.0f;
189:    return 0.0f * x;
190:  }
191:
192:  m = 0x007fffffu >> e;
193:  if ((ix & m) == 0)
194:    return x;
195:
196:  if (ix >> 31)
197:    ix += m;
198:  ix &= ~m;
199:  return __f32_from_bits(ix);
200:}

323:  if (e >= 52)
324:    return x;
325:  if (e < -1)
326:    return 0.0 * x;
327:
328:  m = 0x000fffffffffffffULL >> e;
329:  if ((ix & m) == 0)
330:    return x;
331:
332:  ix += 0x0008000000000000ULL >> e;
333:  ix &= ~m;
334:  return __f64_from_bits(ix);
335:}

337:/* ============================================================================
338: * Fmod — floating-point remainder
339: * ============================================================================
340: */
341:
342:float fmodf(float x, float y) {
343:  uint32_t ix = __f32_bits(x), iy = __f32_bits(y);
344:  int ex, ey;
345:  uint32_t mx, my;
346:
347:  if (iy << 1 == 0 || (iy & 0x7f800000u) == 0x7f800000u ||
348:      (ix & 0x7f800000u) == 0x7f800000u)
349:    return (x * y) / (x * y);
350:
351:  ex = (int)((ix >> 23) & 0xff) - 0x7f;
352:  ey = (int)((iy >> 23) & 0xff) - 0x7f;
353:  mx = (ix & 0x007fffffu) | 0x00800000u;
354:  my = (iy & 0x007fffffu) | 0x00800000u;
355:
356:  if (ex < ey)
357:    return x;
358:
359:  while (ex > ey) {
360:    if (mx >= my)
361:      mx -= my;
362:    mx <<= 1;
363:    ex--;
364:  }
365:  if (mx >= my)
366:    mx -= my;
367:
368:  if (mx == 0)
369:    return __f32_from_bits(ix & 0x80000000u);
370:
371:  while ((mx & 0x00800000u) == 0) {
372:    mx <<= 1;
373:    ex--;
374:  }
375:
376:  ix =
377:      (ix & 0x80000000u) | (((uint32_t)(ex + 0x7f)) << 23) | (mx & 0x007fffffu);
378:  return __f32_from_bits(ix);
379:}

381:double fmod(double x, double y) {
382:  uint64_t ix = __f64_bits(x), iy = __f64_bits(y);
383:  int ex, ey;
384:  uint64_t mx, my;
385:
386:  if (iy << 1 == 0 || (iy & 0x7ff0000000000000ULL) == 0x7ff0000000000000ULL ||
387:      (ix & 0x7ff0000000000000ULL) == 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
388:    return (x * y) / (x * y);
389:
390:  ex = (int)((ix >> 52) & 0x7ff) - 0x3ff;
391:  ey = (int)((iy >> 52) & 0x7ff) - 0x3ff;
392:  mx = (ix & 0x000fffffffffffffULL) | 0x0010000000000000ULL;
393:  my = (iy & 0x000fffffffffffffULL) | 0x0010000000000000ULL;
394:
395:  if (ex < ey)
396:    return x;
397:
398:  while (ex > ey) {
399:    if (mx >= my)
400:      mx -= my;
401:    mx <<= 1;
402:    ex--;
403:  }
404:  if (mx >= my)
405:    mx -= my;
406:
407:  if (mx == 0)
408:    return __f64_from_bits(ix & 0x8000000000000000ULL);
409:
410:  while ((mx & 0x0010000000000000ULL) == 0) {
411:    mx <<= 1;
412:    ex--;
413:  }
414:
415:  ix = (ix & 0x8000000000000000ULL) | (((uint64_t)(ex + 0x3ff)) << 52) |
416:       (mx & 0x000fffffffffffffULL);
417:  return __f64_from_bits(ix);
418:}

431:    return y;

433:    return x;

454:float frexpf(float x, int *exp) {
455:  uint32_t ix = __f32_bits(x);
456:  int e = (int)((ix >> 23) & 0xff);
457:
458:  if (e == 0) {
459:    if ((ix & 0x007fffffu) == 0) {
460:      if (exp)
461:        *exp = 0;
462:      return x;
463:    }
464:    x *= 0x1.0p64f;
465:    ix = __f32_bits(x);
466:    e = (int)((ix >> 23) & 0xff) - 64;
467:  } else if (e == 0xff) {
468:    if (exp)
469:      *exp = 0;
470:    return x;
471:  }
472:
473:  if (exp)
474:    *exp = e - 0x7e;
475:  ix = (ix & 0x807fffffu) | 0x3f000000u;
476:  return __f32_from_bits(ix);
477:}

479:float ldexpf(float x, int exp) {
480:  uint32_t ix = __f32_bits(x);
481:  int e = (int)((ix >> 23) & 0xff);
482:
483:  if (e == 0 || e == 0xff)
484:    return x;
485:
486:  e += exp;
487:  if (e >= 0xff)
488:    return __f32_from_bits((ix & 0x80000000u) | 0x7f800000u);
489:  if (e <= 0) {
490:    if (e <= -24)
491:      return __f32_from_bits(ix & 0x80000000u);
492:    ix = (ix & 0x807fffffu) | ((uint32_t)(1) << 23);
493:    while (e < 0) {
494:      ix >>= 1;
495:      e++;
496:    }
497:    ix = (ix & 0x807fffffu) | ((uint32_t)(e) << 23);
498:    return __f32_from_bits(ix);
499:  }
500:  ix = (ix & 0x807fffffu) | ((uint32_t)(e) << 23);
501:  return __f32_from_bits(ix);
502:}

533:double frexp(double x, int *exp) {
534:  uint64_t ix = __f64_bits(x);
535:  int e = (int)((ix >> 52) & 0x7ff);
536:
537:  if (e == 0) {
538:    if ((ix & 0x000fffffffffffffULL) == 0) {
539:      if (exp)
540:        *exp = 0;
541:      return x;
542:    }
543:    x *= 0x1.0p64;
544:    ix = __f64_bits(x);
545:    e = (int)((ix >> 52) & 0x7ff) - 64;
546:  } else if (e == 0x7ff) {
547:    if (exp)
548:      *exp = 0;
549:    return x;
550:  }
551:
552:  if (exp)
553:    *exp = e - 0x3fe;
554:  ix = (ix & 0x800fffffffffffffULL) | 0x3fe0000000000000ULL;
555:  return __f64_from_bits(ix);
556:}

558:double ldexp(double x, int exp) {
559:  uint64_t ix = __f64_bits(x);
560:  int e = (int)((ix >> 52) & 0x7ff);
561:
562:  if (e == 0 || e == 0x7ff)
563:    return x;
564:
565:  e += exp;
566:  if (e >= 0x7ff)
567:    return __f64_from_bits((ix & 0x8000000000000000ULL) |
568:                           0x7ff0000000000000ULL);
569:  if (e <= 0) {
570:    if (e <= -53)
571:      return __f64_from_bits(ix & 0x8000000000000000ULL);
572:    ix = (ix & 0x800fffffffffffffULL) | 0x0010000000000000ULL;
573:    while (e < 0) {
574:      ix >>= 1;
575:      e++;
576:    }
577:    ix = (ix & 0x800fffffffffffffULL) | ((uint64_t)(e) << 52);
578:    return __f64_from_bits(ix);
579:  }
580:  ix = (ix & 0x800fffffffffffffULL) | ((uint64_t)(e) << 52);
581:  return __f64_from_bits(ix);
582:}

589:static const float __expf_c[6] = {1.0f,
590:                                  0.5f,
591:                                  0.16666667163372039794921875f,
592:                                  0.041666485369205474853515625f,
593:                                  0.00833336085736751556396484375f,
594:                                  0.00137857165321695804595947265625f};

596:float expf(float x) {
597:  float y, r;
598:  int n;
599:
600:  if (__f32_bits(x) >= 0x42b17218u) {
601:    if (__f32_bits(x) >= 0x7f800000u) {
602:      if (__f32_bits(x) == 0x7f800000u)
603:        return x;
604:      return x;
605:    }
606:    return 0x1.fffffep+127f * 0x1.fffffep+127f;
607:  }
608:  if (__f32_bits(x) >= 0xc2d20000u)
609:    return 0.0f;
610:
611:  n = (int)(x * 1.44269504088896340736f + (__f32_sign(x) ? -0.5f : 0.5f));
612:  r = x - (float)n * 0.69314718055994530942f;
613:
614:  y = __expf_c[0] +
615:      r * (__expf_c[1] +
616:           r * (__expf_c[2] +
617:                r * (__expf_c[3] + r * (__expf_c[4] + r * __expf_c[5]))));
618:
619:  return ldexpf(y, n);
620:}

624:float logf(float x) {
625:  uint32_t ix = __f32_bits(x);
626:  int e;
627:  float y, z;
628:
629:  if ((ix & 0x7f800000u) == 0) {
630:    if (ix << 1 == 0)
631:      return -INFINITY;
632:    return __f32_from_bits(0x7fc00000u);
633:  }
634:  if (ix >= 0x7f800000u)
635:    return x;
636:
637:  e = (int)((ix >> 23) & 0xff) - 0x7f;
638:  ix = (ix & 0x007fffffu) | 0x3f800000u;
639:  x = __f32_from_bits(ix);
640:
641:  y = (x - 1.0f) / (x + 1.0f);
642:  z = y * y;
643:  y = y * (2.0f + z * (0.666666686534881591796875f + z * 0.4f));
644:
645:  return y + (float)e * 0.69314718055994530942f;
646:}

648:float log2f(float x) { return logf(x) * 1.44269504088896340736f; }

650:float log10f(float x) { return logf(x) * 0.43429448190325182765f; }

652:static const double __exp_c[8] = {1.0,
653:                                  0.5,
654:                                  0.16666666666666665741,
655:                                  0.041666666666666664353,
656:                                  0.0083333333333333332177,
657:                                  0.0013888888888888889419,
658:                                  0.0001984126984126984127,
659:                                  0.000024801587301587301587};

661:double exp(double x) {
662:  double y, r;
663:  int n;
664:
665:  if (__f64_bits(x) >= 0x40862e42fefa39efULL) {
666:    if (__f64_bits(x) >= 0x7ff0000000000000ULL) {
667:      if (__f64_bits(x) == 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
668:        return x;
669:      return x;
670:    }
671:    return 0x1.fffffffffffffp+1023 * 0x1.fffffffffffffp+1023;
672:  }
673:  if (__f64_bits(x) >= 0xc0874910d52d3051ULL)
674:    return 0.0;
675:
676:  n = (int)(x * 1.44269504088896340736 + (__f64_sign(x) ? -0.5 : 0.5));
677:  r = x - (double)n * 0.69314718055994530942;
678:
679:  y = __exp_c[0] +
680:      r * (__exp_c[1] +
681:           r * (__exp_c[2] +
682:                r * (__exp_c[3] +
683:                     r * (__exp_c[4] +
684:                          r * (__exp_c[5] +
685:                               r * (__exp_c[6] + r * __exp_c[7]))))));
686:
687:  return ldexp(y, n);
688:}

692:double log(double x) {
693:  uint64_t ix = __f64_bits(x);
694:  int e;
695:  double y, z;
696:
697:  if ((ix & 0x7ff0000000000000ULL) == 0) {
698:    if (ix << 1 == 0)
699:      return -INFINITY;
700:    return __f64_from_bits(0x7ff8000000000000ULL);
701:  }
702:  if (ix >= 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
703:    return x;
704:
705:  e = (int)((ix >> 52) & 0x7ff) - 0x3ff;
706:  ix = (ix & 0x000fffffffffffffULL) | 0x3ff0000000000000ULL;
707:  x = __f64_from_bits(ix);
708:
709:  y = (x - 1.0) / (x + 1.0);
710:  z = y * y;
711:  y = y * (2.0 + z * (0.66666666666666662966 +
712:                      z * (0.4 + z * 0.28571428571428569843)));
713:
714:  return y + (double)e * 0.69314718055994530942;
715:}

721:/* ============================================================================
722: * Power function
723: * ============================================================================
724: */

726:float powf(float x, float y) {
727:  uint32_t ix = __f32_bits(x), iy = __f32_bits(y);
728:  float r;
729:
730:  if (iy == 0 || x == 1.0f)
731:    return 1.0f;
732:  if (__float32_isnan(x) || __float32_isnan(y))
733:    return x + y;
734:  if (x == 0.0f) {
735:    if ((iy & 0x7fffffffu) > 0x7f800000u)
736:      return x + y;
737:    if (y > 0.0f)
738:      return (iy >> 31) ? INFINITY : 0.0f;
739:    if (y < 0.0f)
740:      return (iy >> 31) ? 0.0f : INFINITY;
741:    return 1.0f;
742:  }
743:  if (__float32_isinf(y)) {
744:    if (fabsf(x) == 1.0f)
745:      return 1.0f;
746:    if ((ix >> 31) == 0) {
747:      if (y > 0.0f)
748:        return (fabsf(x) > 1.0f) ? INFINITY : 0.0f;
749:      return (fabsf(x) > 1.0f) ? 0.0f : INFINITY;
750:    }
751:  }
752:
753:  r = logf(fabsf(x));
754:  r = expf(y * r);
755:
756:  if (ix >> 31) {
757:    float fy = floorf(y);
758:    if (y == fy) {
759:      uint32_t iy_int = (uint32_t)(int)fy;
760:      if (iy_int & 1)
761:        r = -r;
762:    } else {
763:      return __f32_from_bits(0x7fc00000u);
764:    }
765:  }
766:  return r;
767:}
