769:double pow(double x, double y) {
770:  uint64_t ix = __f64_bits(x), iy = __f64_bits(y);
771:  double r;
772:
773:  if (iy == 0 || x == 1.0)
774:    return 1.0;
775:  if (__float64_isnan(x) || __float64_isnan(y))
776:    return x + y;
777:  if (x == 0.0) {
778:    if ((iy & 0x7fffffffffffffffULL) > 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
779:      return x + y;
780:    if (y > 0.0)
781:      return (iy >> 63) ? INFINITY : 0.0;
782:    if (y < 0.0)
783:      return (iy >> 63) ? 0.0 : INFINITY;
784:    return 1.0;
785:  }
786:  if (__float64_isinf(y)) {
787:    if (fabs(x) == 1.0)
788:      return 1.0;
789:    if ((ix >> 63) == 0) {
790:      if (y > 0.0)
791:        return (fabs(x) > 1.0) ? INFINITY : 0.0;
792:      return (fabs(x) > 1.0) ? 0.0 : INFINITY;
793:    }
794:  }
795:
796:  /* Fast path: integer exponent (common case in Lua) */
797:  {
798:    double fy = floor(y);
799:    if (y == fy) {
800:      long long n = (long long)fy;
801:      int neg = 0;
802:      if (n < 0) {
803:        neg = 1;
804:        n = -n;
805:      }
806:      double r_fast = 1.0;
807:      double b = x;
808:      while (n) {
809:        if (n & 1)
810:          r_fast *= b;
811:        b *= b;
812:        n >>= 1;
813:      }
814:      return neg ? 1.0 / r_fast : r_fast;
815:    }
816:  }
817:
818:  r = log(fabs(x));
819:  r = exp(y * r);
820:
821:  if (ix >> 63) {
822:    double fy = floor(y);
823:    if (y == fy) {
824:      uint64_t iy_int = (uint64_t)(long long)fy;
825:      if (iy_int & 1)
826:        r = -r;
827:    } else {
828:      return __f64_from_bits(0x7ff8000000000000ULL);
829:    }
830:  }
831:  return r;
832:}

834:/* ============================================================================
835: * Trigonometric functions — minimax polynomial with range reduction
836: * ============================================================================
837: */
838:
839:static const float __sinf_c[4] = {
840:    0.99999999999999991673f, -0.16666666666666665741f,
841:    0.0083333333333333332177f, -0.0001984126984126984127f};
842:
843:static const float __cosf_c[4] = {1.0f, -0.5f, 0.041666666666666664353f,
844:                                  -0.0013888888888888889419f};
845:
846:/* Range-reduce x into [-pi/4, pi/4], return the quadrant (0..3) */
847:static int __sinf_reduce(float *x) {
848:  const float pi = 3.14159265358979323846f;
849:  const float two_over_pi = 0.63661977236758134308f;
850:  int q;
851:  float y;
852:
853:  if (fabsf(*x) < 1.0e6f) {
854:    q = (int)(*x * two_over_pi + (__f32_sign(*x) ? -0.5f : 0.5f));
855:    y = *x - (float)q * (pi / 2.0f);
856:  } else {
857:    float t = *x * two_over_pi;
858:    q = (int)(t + (__f32_sign(*x) ? -0.5f : 0.5f));
859:    y = *x - (float)q * 1.57079632679489661923f;
860:    y = y - (float)q * 6.12323399573676588613e-17f;
861:  }
862:  *x = y;
863:  return q & 3;
864:}
865:
866:float sinf(float x) {
867:  float z, s;
868:  int q;
869:
870:  if (__f32_abs_bits(x) >= 0x7f800000u)
871:    return x - x;
872:
873:  q = __sinf_reduce(&x);
874:  z = x * x;
875:
876:  s = x *
877:      (__sinf_c[0] + z * (__sinf_c[1] + z * (__sinf_c[2] + z * __sinf_c[3])));
878:
879:  if (q & 1)
880:    s = copysignf(1.0f, s) - s;
881:  if (q & 2)
882:    s = -s;
883:
884:  return s;
885:}
886:
887:float cosf(float x) {
888:  float z, c;
889:  int q;
890:
891:  if (__f32_abs_bits(x) >= 0x7f800000u)
892:    return x - x;
893:
894:  q = __sinf_reduce(&x);
895:  q = (q + 1) & 3;
896:
897:  z = x * x;
898:  c = __cosf_c[0] + z * (__cosf_c[1] + z * (__cosf_c[2] + z * __cosf_c[3]));
899:
900:  if (q & 1)
901:    c = copysignf(1.0f, c) - c;
902:  if (q & 2)
903:    c = -c;
904:
905:  return c;
906:}
907:
908:float tanf(float x) {
909:  float s, c;
910:  if (__f32_abs_bits(x) >= 0x7f800000u)
911:    return x - x;
912:  s = sinf(x);
913:  c = cosf(x);
914:  if (c == 0.0f)
915:    return copysignf(INFINITY, s);
916:  return s / c;
917:}
918:
919:float asinf(float x) {
920:  float z, r;
921:  uint32_t ix = __f32_bits(x);
922:
923:  if (ix >= 0x7f800000u)
924:    return x - x;
925:  if (ix >= 0x3f800000u) {
926:    if (ix == 0x3f800000u)
927:      return (ix >> 31) ? -M_PI_2 : M_PI_2;
928:    if (ix > 0x3f800000u)
929:      return __f32_from_bits(0x7fc00000u);
930:  }
931:
932:  z = x * x;
933:  r = x * (1.0f + z * (0.16666667163372039794921875f +
934:                       z * (0.07500000298023223876953125f +
935:                            z * 0.0446428574621677398681640625f)));
936:  return r;
937:}
938:
939:float acosf(float x) { return M_PI_2 - asinf(x); }
940:
941:float atanf(float x) {
942:  float z, r;
943:  uint32_t ix = __f32_bits(x);
944:  int sign = ix >> 31;
945:
946:  if (ix >= 0x7f800000u) {
947:    if (ix == 0x7f800000u)
948:      return sign ? -M_PI_2 : M_PI_2;
949:    return x - x;
950:  }
951:
952:  x = fabsf(x);
953:
954:  if (x > 1.0f) {
955:    x = 1.0f / x;
956:    z = x * x;
957:    r = M_PI_2 -
958:        x * (1.0f + z * (-0.3333333432674407958984375f +
959:                         z * (0.199999988079071044921875f +
960:                              z * (-0.14285714924335479736328125f +
961:                                   z * 0.111111111938953399658203125f))));
962:    return sign ? -r : r;
963:  }
964:
965:  z = x * x;
966:  r = x * (1.0f + z * (-0.3333333432674407958984375f +
967:                       z * (0.199999988079071044921875f +
968:                            z * (-0.14285714924335479736328125f +
969:                                 z * 0.111111111938953399658203125f))));
970:  return sign ? -r : r;
971:}
972:
973:float atan2f(float y, float x) {
974:  uint32_t ix = __f32_bits(x), iy = __f32_bits(y);
975:
976:  if (__float32_isnan(x) || __float32_isnan(y))
977:    return x + y;
978:  if (iy == 0)
979:    return (ix >> 31) ? (ix == 0x80000000u ? M_PI : 0.0f) : 0.0f;
980:  if (ix == 0)
981:    return (iy >> 31) ? -M_PI_2 : M_PI_2;
982:
983:  if (__float32_isinf(x)) {
984:    if (__float32_isinf(y)) {
985:      return (ix >> 31) ? ((iy >> 31) ? -2.35619449019234492885f
986:                                      : 2.35619449019234492885f)
987:                        : ((iy >> 31) ? -0.78539816339744830962f
988:                                      : 0.78539816339744830962f);
989:    }
990:    return (ix >> 31) ? ((iy >> 31) ? -M_PI : M_PI)
991:                      : ((iy >> 31) ? -0.0f : 0.0f);
992:  }
993:  if (__float32_isinf(y))
994:    return (iy >> 31) ? -M_PI_2 : M_PI_2;
995:
996:  return atanf(y / x) + ((x < 0.0f) ? ((y < 0.0f) ? -M_PI : M_PI) : 0.0f);
997:}
998:
999:/* Double-precision trig */
1000:static const double __sin_c[5] = {
1001:    1.0, -0.16666666666666665741, 0.0083333333333333332177,
1002:    -0.0001984126984126984127, 0.0000027557319223985890653};
1003:
1004:static const double __cos_c[5] = {1.0, -0.5, 0.041666666666666664353,
1005:                                  -0.0013888888888888889419,
1006:                                  0.000024801587301587301587};
1007:
1008:static int __sin_reduce(double *x) {
1009:  const double two_over_pi = 0.63661977236758134308;
1010:  int q;
1011:  double y;
1012:
1013:  if (fabs(*x) < 1.0e14) {
1014:    q = (int)(*x * two_over_pi + (__f64_sign(*x) ? -0.5 : 0.5));
1015:    y = *x - (double)q * (M_PI / 2.0);
1016:  } else {
1017:    double t = *x * two_over_pi;
1018:    q = (int)(t + (__f64_sign(*x) ? -0.5 : 0.5));
1019:    y = *x - (double)q * 1.57079632679489661923;
1020:    y = y - (double)q * 6.12323399573676588613e-17;
1021:  }
1022:  *x = y;
1023:  return q & 3;
1024:}
1025:
1026:double sin(double x) {
1027:  double z, s;
1028:  int q;
1029:
1030:  if (__f64_abs_bits(x) >= 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
1031:    return x - x;
1032:
1033:  q = __sin_reduce(&x);
1034:  z = x * x;
1035:
1036:  s = x *
1037:      (__sin_c[0] +
1038:       z * (__sin_c[1] + z * (__sin_c[2] + z * (__sin_c[3] + z * __sin_c[4]))));
1039:
1040:  if (q & 1)
1041:    s = copysign(1.0, s) - s;
1042:  if (q & 2)
1043:    s = -s;
1044:
1045:  return s;
1046:}
1047:
1048:double cos(double x) {
1049:  double z, c;
1050:  int q;
1051:
1052:  if (__f64_abs_bits(x) >= 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
1053:    return x - x;
1054:
1055:  q = __sin_reduce(&x);
1056:  q = (q + 1) & 3;
1057:
1058:  z = x * x;
1059:  c = __cos_c[0] +
1060:      z * (__cos_c[1] + z * (__cos_c[2] + z * (__cos_c[3] + z * __cos_c[4])));
1061:
1062:  if (q & 1)
1063:    c = copysign(1.0, c) - c;
1064:  if (q & 2)
1065:    c = -c;
1066:
1067:  return c;
1068:}
1069:
1070:double tan(double x) {
1071:  double s, c;
1072:  if (__f64_abs_bits(x) >= 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
1073:    return x - x;
1074:  s = sin(x);
1075:  c = cos(x);
1076:  if (c == 0.0)
1077:    return copysign(INFINITY, s);
1078:  return s / c;
1079:}
1080:
1081:double asin(double x) {
1082:  double z, r;
1083:  uint64_t ix = __f64_bits(x);
1084:
1085:  if (ix >= 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
1086:    return x - x;
1087:  if (ix >= 0x3ff0000000000000ULL) {
1088:    if (ix == 0x3ff0000000000000ULL)
1089:      return (ix >> 63) ? -M_PI_2 : M_PI_2;
1090:    if (ix > 0x3ff0000000000000ULL)
1091:      return __f64_from_bits(0x7ff8000000000000ULL);
1092:  }
1093:
1094:  z = x * x;
1095:  r = x * (1.0 + z * (0.16666666666666665741 + z * (0.075000000000000000000 +
1096:                                                    z * 0.044642857142857143)));
1097:  return r;
1098:}
1099:
1100:double acos(double x) { return M_PI_2 - asin(x); }
1101:
1102:double atan(double x) {
1103:  double z, r;
1104:  uint64_t ix = __f64_bits(x);
1105:  int sign = (int)(ix >> 63);
1106:
1107:  if (ix >= 0x7ff0000000000000ULL) {
1108:    if (ix == 0x7ff0000000000000ULL)
1109:      return sign ? -M_PI_2 : M_PI_2;
1110:    return x - x;
1111:  }
1112:
1113:  x = fabs(x);
1114:
1115:  if (x > 1.0) {
1116:    x = 1.0 / x;
1117:    z = x * x;
1118:    r = M_PI_2 - x * (1.0 + z * (-0.33333333333333331483 +
1119:                                 z * (0.19999999999999995559 +
1120:                                      z * (-0.14285714285714287654 +
1121:                                           z * 0.11111111111111110494))));
1122:    return sign ? -r : r;
1123:  }
1124:
1125:  z = x * x;
1126:  r = x *
1127:      (1.0 +
1128:       z * (-0.33333333333333331483 +
1129:            z * (0.19999999999999995559 +
1130:                 z * (-0.14285714285714287654 + z * 0.11111111111111110494))));
1131:  return sign ? -r : r;
1132:}
1133:
1134:double atan2(double y, double x) {
1135:  uint64_t ix = __f64_bits(x), iy = __f64_bits(y);
1136:
1137:  if (__float64_isnan(x) || __float64_isnan(y))
1138:    return x + y;
1139:  if (iy == 0)
1140:    return (ix >> 63) ? (ix == 0x8000000000000000ULL ? M_PI : 0.0) : 0.0;
1141:  if (ix == 0)
1142:    return (iy >> 63) ? -M_PI_2 : M_PI_2;
1143:
1144:  if (__float64_isinf(x)) {
1145:    if (__float64_isinf(y)) {
1146:      return (ix >> 63) ? ((iy >> 63) ? -2.35619449019234492885
1147:                                      : 2.35619449019234492885)
1148:                        : ((iy >> 63) ? -0.78539816339744830962
1149:                                      : 0.78539816339744830962);
1150:    }
1151:    return (ix >> 63) ? ((iy >> 63) ? -M_PI : M_PI) : ((iy >> 63) ? -0.0 : 0.0);
1152:  }
1153:  if (__float64_isinf(y))
1154:    return (iy >> 63) ? -M_PI_2 : M_PI_2;
1155:
1156:  return atan(y / x) + ((x < 0.0) ? ((y < 0.0) ? -M_PI : M_PI) : 0.0);
1157:}

1197:
1198:double strtod(const char *nptr, char **endptr) {
1199:  const char *p = nptr;
1200:  while (*p == ' ' || *p == '\t' || *p == '\n' || *p == '\r' || *p == '\f' ||
1201:         *p == '\v') {
1202:    p++;
1203:  }
1204:
1205:  double sign = 1.0;
1206:  if (*p == '-') {
1207:    sign = -1.0;
1208:    p++;
1209:  } else if (*p == '+') {
1210:    p++;
1211:  }
1212:
1213:  /* INF/INFINITY */
1214:  if (strncasecmp(p, "infinity", 8) == 0) {
1215:    if (endptr) *endptr = (char *)(p + 8);
1216:    return sign * HUGE_VAL;
1217:  }
1218:  if (strncasecmp(p, "inf", 3) == 0) {
1219:    if (endptr) *endptr = (char *)(p + 3);
1220:    return sign * HUGE_VAL;
1221:  }
1222:
1223:  /* NAN */
1224:  if (strncasecmp(p, "nan", 3) == 0) {
1225:    p += 3;
1226:    if (*p == '(') {
1227:      const char *q = p + 1;
1228:      while ((*q >= '0' && *q <= '9') ||
1229:             (*q >= 'a' && *q <= 'z') ||
1230:             (*q >= 'A' && *q <= 'Z') ||
1231:             *q == '_') {
1232:        q++;
1233:      }
1234:      if (*q == ')') {
1235:        p = q + 1;
1236:      }
1237:    }
1238:    if (endptr) *endptr = (char *)p;
1239:    return sign < 0 ? -NAN : NAN;
1240:  }
1241:
1242:  /* Hexadecimal Float */
1243:  if (p[0] == '0' && (p[1] == 'x' || p[1] == 'X')) {
1244:    const char *hstart = p;
1245:    const char *q = p + 2;
1246:    double mant = 0.0;
1247:    int any_digits = 0;
1248:
1249:    while (1) {
1250:      char c = *q;
1251:      int d;
1252:      if (c >= '0' && c <= '9')
1253:        d = c - '0';
1254:      else if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f')
1255:        d = c - 'a' + 10;
1256:      else if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F')
1257:        d = c - 'A' + 10;
1258:      else
1259:        break;
1260:      mant = mant * 16.0 + (double)d;
1261:      q++;
1262:      any_digits = 1;
1263:    }
1264:    if (*q == '.') {
1265:      q++;
1266:      double scale = 1.0 / 16.0;
1267:      while (1) {
1268:        char c = *q;
1269:        int d;
1270:        if (c >= '0' && c <= '9')
1271:          d = c - '0';
1272:        else if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f')
1273:          d = c - 'a' + 10;
1274:        else if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F')
1275:          d = c - 'A' + 10;
1276:        else
1277:          break;
1278:        mant += (double)d * scale;
1279:        scale /= 16.0;
1280:        q++;
1281:        any_digits = 1;
1282:      }
1283:    }
1284:
1285:    if (any_digits) {
1286:      int exp = 0;
1287:      if (*q == 'p' || *q == 'P') {
1288:        q++;
1289:        int exp_sign = 1;
1290:        if (*q == '-') {
1291:          exp_sign = -1;
1292:          q++;
1293:        } else if (*q == '+') {
1294:          q++;
1295:        }
1296:        int e = 0;
1297:        while (*q >= '0' && *q <= '9') {
1298:          e = e * 10 + (*q - '0');
1299:          q++;
1300:        }
1301:        exp = exp_sign * e;
1302:      }
1303:      double result = ldexp(mant, exp);
1304:      if (endptr)
1305:        *endptr = (char *)q;
1306:      return sign * result;
1307:    }
1308:    /* '0x' with no hex digits after it: not a valid hex-float. Fall back
1309:     * to decimal parsing below, which will read the leading '0'. */
1310:    p = hstart;
1311:  }
1312:
1313:  /* Decimal Path */
1314:  unsigned long long mant = 0ULL;
1315:  int mant_digits = 0;
1316:  int frac_digits = 0;
1317:  int seen_dot = 0;
1318:  int has_digits = 0;
1319:  while (1) {
1320:    char c = *p;
1321:    if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') {
1322:      has_digits = 1;
1323:      if (mant_digits < 19) {
1324:        mant = mant * 10ULL + (unsigned long long)(c - '0');
1325:        mant_digits++;
1326:        if (seen_dot)
1327:          frac_digits++;
1328:      } else if (!seen_dot) {
1329:        frac_digits--;
1330:      }
1331:      p++;
1332:    } else if (c == '.' && !seen_dot) {
1333:      seen_dot = 1;
1334:      p++;
1335:    } else {
1336:      break;
1337:    }
1338:  }
1339:
1340:  if (!has_digits) {
1341:    if (endptr)
1342:      *endptr = (char *)nptr;
1343:    return 0.0;
1344:  }
1345:
1346:  int exp10 = 0;
1347:  if (*p == 'e' || *p == 'E') {
1348:    const char *estart = p;
1349:    p++;
1350:    int exp_sign = 1;
1351:    if (*p == '-') {
1352:      exp_sign = -1;
1353:      p++;
1354:    } else if (*p == '+') {
1355:      p++;
1356:    }
1357:    if (*p >= '0' && *p <= '9') {
1358:      int e = 0;
1359:      while (*p >= '0' && *p <= '9') {
1360:        e = e * 10 + (*p - '0');
1361:        p++;
1362:      }
1363:      exp10 = exp_sign * e;
1364:    } else {
1365:      p = estart;
1366:    }
1367:  }
1368:
1369:  double val = (double)mant;
1370:  int total_exp = exp10 - frac_digits;
1371:  {
1372:    static const double p10[] = {1e0,  1e1,  1e2,  1e3,  1e4,  1e5,  1e6,  1e7,
1373:                                 1e8,  1e9,  1e10, 1e11, 1e12, 1e13, 1e14, 1e15,
1374:                                 1e16, 1e17, 1e18, 1e19, 1e20, 1e21, 1e22};
1375:    int e = total_exp;
1376:    if (e > 0) {
1377:      while (e > 22) {
1378:        val *= 1e22;
1379:        e -= 22;
1380:      }
1381:      val *= p10[e];
1382:    } else if (e < 0) {
1383:      e = -e;
1384:      while (e > 22) {
1385:        val /= 1e22;
1386:        e -= 22;
1387:      }
1388:      val /= p10[e];
1389:    }
1390:  }
1391:
1392:  if (endptr) {
1393:    *endptr = (char *)p;
1394:  }
1395:
1396:  return sign * val;
1397:}
1398:
1399:/* ============================================================================
1400: * Fixed-point (legacy — kept for Doom compat)
1401: * ============================================================================
1402: */
1403:
1404:int32_t fixmul(int32_t a, int32_t b) {
1405:  int64_t result = (int64_t)a * b;
1406:  return (int32_t)(result >> FP_SHIFT);
1407:}
1408:
1409:int32_t sin_fp(int32_t x) {
1410:  while (x > FP_PI)
1411:    x -= FP_2PI;
1412:  while (x < -FP_PI)
1413:    x += FP_2PI;
1414:
1415:  int32_t half_pi = 102944;
1416:  if (x > half_pi)
1417:    x = FP_PI - x;
1418:  else if (x < -half_pi)
1419:    x = -FP_PI - x;
1420:
1421:  int32_t x2 = fixmul(x, x);
1422:  int32_t x3 = fixmul(x2, x);
1423:  int32_t x5 = fixmul(x3, x2);
1424:
1425:  int32_t term1 = x;
1426:  int32_t term2 = fixmul(x3, 10923);
1427:  int32_t term3 = fixmul(x5, 546);
1428:
1429:  return term1 - term2 + term3;
1430:}
1431:
1432:int32_t cos_fp(int32_t x) { return sin_fp(x + 102944); }

20:#   make BUILD=debug   → full symbols, no strip (default)
21:#   make BUILD=release → --gc-sections + strip
22:BUILD ?= debug

24:# Optional escape hatch for incomplete userland compatibility layers: when set,
25:# the user-space compile rules drop -Werror without weakening the kernel build.
26:# GNU make does not accept arbitrary --bypas-sec switches, so the supported form
27:# is a variable assignment such as: make ARCH=aarch64 BYPASS_SEC=1 run
28:BYPASS_SEC ?= 0

48:# Common Compiler Flags
49:# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
50:# CONTRACT GATE — read before you reach for a way around it.
51:#
52:# kernel/include/kernel/nx_contract.h turns the invariants C cannot check into
53:# build failures: NX_MUST_USE on every -errno return, NX_ASSERT_OFFSET on every
54:# layout assembly depends on.  It is ALWAYS ON.  There is deliberately no flag
55:# to disable it, and adding one would defeat the reason it exists -- an earlier
56:# version was gated behind NX_STRICT and the result was that nobody ever saw a
57:# single diagnostic, because a gate you have to remember to switch on is a gate
58:# that is off.
59:#
60:# When the build stops on one of these, the build is correct and the code is
61:# not.  The three legitimate responses, in order of preference:
62:#
63:#   1. Handle the failure.  This is almost always the right answer.
64:#   2. Make the failure visible where it happens -- pr_err with the CONSEQUENCE
65:#      named, not just the fact ("no key events" beats "irq_register failed").
66:#   3. NX_DISCARD(expr, "why") -- only for an error-unwind path where the
67:#      cleanup failing changes nothing, or a best-effort refresh whose fallback
68:#      is documented.  It requires a written reason precisely so it can be
69:#      reviewed rather than merely noticed.
70:#
71:# What is NOT a response: deleting the annotation, adding -Wno-unused-result,
72:# or a (void) cast (which does not suppress warn_unused_result under GCC and
73:# only makes the omission look intentional -- the tree already had one).
74:# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
75:
76:COMMON_FLAGS = -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wpedantic -Wshadow -Wwrite-strings \
77:               -Wmissing-prototypes -Wstrict-prototypes \
78:               -ffreestanding -fno-builtin -nostdlib -nostartfiles \
79:               -fno-common -fstack-protector-strong \
80:               -fno-pic -fno-pie \
81:               -fno-omit-frame-pointer \
82:               -O2 -g
83:
84:# NX_STRICT=1 turns the nx_contract.h annotations into enforced attributes
85:# (NX_MUST_USE -> warn_unused_result).  With -Werror that makes every ignored
86:# -errno a hard error, which is the point: `make NX_STRICT=1` is the report of
87:# how much of the surface still drops failures on the floor.
88:ifeq ($(NX_STRICT),1)
89:COMMON_FLAGS += -DNX_STRICT
90:endif

301:# Dependency files
302:# Every %.o: %.c rule (kernel AND user, see "Common compilation rules" below)
303:# passes -MMD -MP, so a per-TU .d file listing every header it pulled in
304:# lands next to each .o.  DEPS used to be JUST the kernel ones
305:# (KERN_C_OBJECTS:.o=.d) — userland .o files (nxres.o, nxsettings.o, ...)
306:# never got their .d included, so `make` had no idea a userland .c depended
307:# on a header like nxres.h/style_names.h: editing ONLY the header left every
308:# .o that #included it stale and un-rebuilt, silently running old code with
309:# no compile error to flag it.  Globbing every .d already on disk (kernel
310:# and user alike) closes that gap; empty on a clean tree (no .d files yet),
311:# which is fine — -include tolerates a missing/empty list.
312:DEPS = $(shell find $(BUILD_ROOT) -name '*.d' 2>/dev/null)

376:# Two-pass link for the in-kernel symbol table (Phase A, kernel/lib/backtrace.c):
377:# pass 1 links without .ksyms, gen_ksyms.sh derives the table from `nm -n` of
378:# pass 1, pass 2 relinks with it.  .ksyms sits after .text in both kernel.ld
379:# scripts, so text addresses are identical across the passes (the table stays
380:# valid).  If generation ever fails the empty-table fallback in backtrace.c
381:# keeps the kernel functional (raw addresses).
382:NM = $(CROSS_COMPILE)nm
383:KERNEL_PRE = $(BUILD_DIR)/kernel.pre.elf
384:KSYMS_S    = $(BUILD_DIR)/ksyms.S
385:KSYMS_O    = $(BUILD_DIR)/ksyms.o
386:
387:$(KERNEL_PRE): $(KERN_OBJECTS)
388:	@$(LD) $(LDFLAGS_KERN) -o $@ $^
389:
390:$(KSYMS_O): $(KERNEL_PRE) tools/gen_ksyms.sh
391:	@tools/gen_ksyms.sh "$(NM)" $(KERNEL_PRE) $(KSYMS_S)
392:	@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c -o $@ $(KSYMS_S)
393:
394:$(KERNEL_ELF): $(KERN_OBJECTS) $(KSYMS_O)
395:	@$(LD) $(LDFLAGS_KERN) -o $@ $^
396:
397:$(KERNEL_BIN): $(KERNEL_ELF)
398:	@$(OBJCOPY) -O binary $< $@

458:# SDL cannot build under the kernel's -Werror/-Wpedantic regime; codegen and

460:# into OS1 apps.  GCC>=14 permerrors are demoted for SDL's own fallback code

470:              $(SDL_NEXSOS_OVERLAY_CPPFLAGS)

534:LUA_PORT_OBJ  := $(BUILD_DIR)/$(USER_LIB_DIR)/portability/lua/lua_portability.o
535:LUA_OS1_OBJ   := $(BUILD_DIR)/$(USER_LIB_DIR)/os1LUA_lib.o
536:
537:LUA_LIB     := $(BUILD_DIR)/lua.a
538:LUA_OS1_LIB := $(BUILD_DIR)/libos1lua.a
539:
540:# The Lua module search path (LUA_ROOT/LDIR/CDIR/LUA_PATH_DEFAULT) is owned
541:# SOLELY by the force-included lua_portability.h — a C header, so the ';'
542:# path separators are inside a real string literal.  It must NOT be passed
543:# as -DLUA_PATH_DEFAULT=\"...;...\" here: Make forwards the \" verbatim, the
544:# shell reads it as a literal quote (not a delimiter), and the unquoted ';'
545:# then split the gcc line into pieces ("no input files" + bogus commands).
546:LUA_CFLAGS = $(ARCH_CFLAGS) -O2 -g -Wall \
547:             -Wno-error \
548:             -ffreestanding -fno-builtin -nostdlib -nostartfiles \
549:             -fno-common -fstack-protector-strong -fno-pic -fno-pie \
550:             -fno-omit-frame-pointer \
551:             -DLUA_USE_NEXSOS \
552:             -Iinclude/abi \
553:             -Iinclude/api \
554:             -I$(LUA_DIR) \
555:             -I$(USER_LIB_DIR)/portability/lua \
556:             -include lua_portability.h
557:
558:$(LUA_OBJ_DIR)/%.o: $(LUA_DIR)/%.c $(LUA_PORT_HDR)
559:	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
560:	@$(CC) $(LUA_CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@
561:
562:$(LUA_PORT_OBJ): $(LUA_PORT_SRCS) $(LUA_PORT_HDR)
563:	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
564:	@$(CC) $(LUA_CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@
565:
566:$(LUA_OS1_OBJ): $(LUA_OS1_SRCS) $(LUA_PORT_HDR)
567:	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
568:	@$(CC) $(LUA_CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@
569:
570:$(LUA_LIB): $(LUA_CORE_OBJS) $(LUA_PORT_OBJ)
571:	@echo "  [AR]     $@"
572:	@$(AR) rcs $@ $^
573:
574:$(LUA_OS1_LIB): $(LUA_OS1_OBJ)
575:	@echo "  [AR]     $@"
576:	@$(AR) rcs $@ $^
577:
578:liblua: $(LUA_LIB) $(LUA_OS1_LIB)
579:.PHONY: liblua
580:
581:$(LUA_OBJ_DIR)/lua.o: $(LUA_DIR)/lua.c $(LUA_PORT_HDR)
582:	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
583:	@$(CC) $(LUA_CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@
584:
585:$(BUILD_DIR)/lua.elf: $(LUA_OBJ_DIR)/lua.o $(LUA_OS1_LIB) $(LUA_LIB) $(USER_LIB_O) $(USER_SYSCALL_O) $(USER_MALLOC_O)
586:	@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(USER_LINK_FLAGS) -Wl,-Ttext=0x80000000 -e _start -o $@ \
587:		$(LUA_OBJ_DIR)/lua.o \
588:		-Wl,--start-group $(LUA_LIB) $(LUA_OS1_LIB) -Wl,--end-group \
589:		$(USER_LIB_O) $(USER_SYSCALL_O) $(USER_MALLOC_O)

771:# Userland link flags.
772:# --gc-sections drops unused functions/data from the whole-linked lib.o
773:# (the main source of the ~50-70 KB bloat measured in counter.elf).
774:# In release builds we also strip symbols; debug keeps everything.

804:# Disk Generation
805:rootfs: user libsdl2 liblua libgnulib coreutils
806:	@rm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs
807:	@mkdir -p $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/sys/bin
808:	@mkdir -p $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/bin
809:	@mkdir -p $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/etc
810:	@mkdir -p $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/tmp
811:	@mkdir -p $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/var/tmp
812:	@mkdir -p $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/sys/lib
813:	@mkdir -p $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/home/Pictures/background
814:	@mkdir -p $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/home/Pictures/icon/dark
815:	@mkdir -p $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/home/Pictures/icon/light
816:	@mkdir -p $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/lib
817:	@# Lua module search root (lua_portability.h LUA_LDIR/LUA_CDIR): system
818:	@# .lua/.so modules live here — read-for-all, root-write-only (unlike
819:	@# /home). ext4 has no runtime dir creation, so pre-create the tree.
820:	@mkdir -p $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/lib/lua/5.4/lib
821:	@mkdir -p  $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/sys/lib/include
822:	@# /home: the ONLY user-writable tree (vfs_write_allowed tree ACL —
823:	@# /sys/bin machine-only, every other tree root-only, guests confined to
824:	@# /home/shared).  Pre-created because ext4 has no directory creation yet:
825:	@# Documents/doom hosts doom's config+savegames (replaces the hardcoded
826:	@mkdir -p $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/home/Documents/doom
827:	@mkdir -p $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/home/Video
828:	@mkdir -p $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/home/shared
829:	@mkdir -p $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/home/Settings
830:	@-cp -r user/home/Settings/. $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/home/Settings/ 2>/dev/null || true
831:	@cp $(SYS_ELFS) $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/sys/bin/
832:	@cp $(BIN_ELFS) $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/bin/
833:	@cp user/sys/bin/init.cfg $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/etc/
834:	@# Pre-create a 16KB scratch file for the /bin/stress file lane: the FS has no
835:	@# runtime file creation (O_CREAT -> -EINVAL), and file_write only extends an
836:	@# EXISTING file, so ship one (perf §6 stress harness).
837:	@dd if=/dev/zero of=$(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/etc/stress.tmp bs=1024 count=16 2>/dev/null
838:	@# Copy essential WAD files to the root and /bin for engine detection
839:	@-cp user/bin/doom/freedoom1.wad $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/bin/ 2>/dev/null || true
840:	@-cp user/bin/doom/freedoom2.wad $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/bin/ 2>/dev/null || true
841:	@-cp user/home/Pictures/icon/dark/*.png $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/home/Pictures/icon/dark/ 2>/dev/null || true
842:	@-cp user/sys/bin/background/nxduck.png $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/sys/bin/background/ 2>/dev/null || true
843:	@# Dock/launcher tile icons (nxicon.h): both theme sets, so a runtime
844:	@# theme flip never needs a rebuilt image — see nxicon.h's header comment.
845:	@-cp user/home/Pictures/globe.png $(BUILD_DIR)/rootfs/home/Pictures/ 2>/dev/null || true

897:# ==============================================================================
898:# QEMU Flags
899:# ==============================================================================
900:
901:# A terminal launched from a snap-packaged GUI app (VS Code's integrated
902:# terminal is the common case on Ubuntu) exports GTK_PATH/GTK_EXE_PREFIX/
903:# GTK_MODULES/GIO_MODULE_DIR/XDG_DATA_DIRS/LOCPATH pointing into that snap's
904:# own bundle (e.g. /snap/code/<rev>/usr/lib/.../gtk-3.0). Any GTK app started
905:# from that shell — including QEMU with -display default, which is a GTK
906:# frontend — inherits them and tries to dlopen its GTK module set from the
907:# wrong snap's directory tree, which pulls in an old bundled libpthread.so.0
908:# incompatible with the host's glibc (undefined symbol __libc_pthread_init,
909:# GLIBC_PRIVATE) and QEMU dies before ever opening a window. None of these
910:# vars are needed for our own display: strip them unconditionally (no-op if
911:# unset, so this is a no-op on macOS/BSD too) rather than ask every
912:# contributor to remember to launch from a "clean" terminal.
913:QEMU_RUN = env -u GTK_PATH -u GTK_EXE_PREFIX -u GTK_MODULES -u GTK_IM_MODULE_FILE \
914:               -u GIO_MODULE_DIR -u GSETTINGS_SCHEMA_DIR -u XDG_DATA_DIRS \
915:               -u XDG_DATA_HOME -u LOCPATH $(QEMU)
916:
917:ifeq ($(ARCH), amd64)
918:QEMU_FLAGS = -m 5G -smp 4 -serial mon:stdio \
919:             -display default,show-cursor=on \
920:			 -vga none \
921:             -device virtio-gpu-pci,disable-legacy=on,disable-modern=off \
922:             -device virtio-keyboard-pci,disable-legacy=on,disable-modern=off \
923:             -device virtio-mouse-pci,disable-legacy=on,disable-modern=off \
924:             -drive if=none,file=$(DISK_IMG),id=hd0,format=raw \
925:             -device virtio-blk-pci,drive=hd0,disable-legacy=on,disable-modern=off
926:
927:QEMU_RELEASE_FLAGS = -m 5G -smp 4 -serial mon:stdio \
928:                     -display default,show-cursor=on \
929:                     -device virtio-gpu-pci,disable-legacy=on,disable-modern=off \
930:                     -device virtio-keyboard-pci,disable-legacy=on,disable-modern=off \
931:                     -device virtio-mouse-pci,disable-legacy=on,disable-modern=off
932:else
933:# AArch64: pass -dtb $(VIRT_DTB) so QEMU loads the pre-generated device tree into RAM
934:# and sets x0 = dtb_load_address in its aarch64 boot stub.  Without -dtb, QEMU does not
935:# generate/load a DTB for bare-metal ELF kernels and x0 arrives as 0 at _start.
936:QEMU_FLAGS = -M virt -cpu cortex-a57 -m 5G -smp 4 -serial mon:stdio \
937:             -display default,show-cursor=on \
938:             -device virtio-gpu-device \
939:             -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-mouse-device \
940:             -drive if=none,file=$(DISK_IMG),id=hd0,format=raw -device virtio-blk-device,drive=hd0 \
941:             -dtb $(VIRT_DTB)
942:
943:QEMU_RELEASE_FLAGS = -M virt -cpu cortex-a57 -m 5G -smp 4 -serial mon:stdio \
944:                     -display default,show-cursor=on \
945:                     -device virtio-gpu-device \
946:                     -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-mouse-device \
947:                     -drive if=none,file=$(RELEASE_DIR)/disk.img,id=hd0,format=raw -device virtio-blk-device,drive=hd0
948:endif

969:	@if [ "$(ARCH)" = "amd64" ]; then \
970:		set -e; \

972:		cp $(KERNEL_ELF) $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/kernel.elf; \
973:		cp $(DISK_IMG) $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/disk.img; \

977:		echo '    insmod part_gpt' >> $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
978:		echo '    insmod ext2' >> $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
979:		echo '    insmod loopback' >> $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
980:		echo '    multiboot2 /boot/kernel.elf' >> $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
981:		echo '    loopback loop /boot/disk.img' >> $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
982:		echo '    ls (loop,gpt3)/' >> $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
983:		echo '    module2 /boot/disk.img diskimg' >> $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
984:		echo '    boot' >> $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
985:		echo '}' >> $(RELEASE_DIR)/boot/grub/grub.cfg; \
986:		echo "AMD64 files ready: boot/kernel.elf, boot/disk.img"; \
987:		mkdir -p $(RELEASE_DIR)/iso/boot/grub; \

989:		GRUB_MKRESCUE=""; \

992:				GRUB_MKRESCUE=$$c; break; \
993:			fi; \
994:		done; \
995:		if [ -z "$$GRUB_MKRESCUE" ]; then \
996:			echo "Errore: grub-mkrescue non trovato"; \
997:			exit 1; \
998:		fi; \

1000:		$$GRUB_MKRESCUE -o $(RELEASE_DIR)/NexsOS1-amd64-$(VERSION).iso $(RELEASE_DIR)/iso; \
1001:		echo "-> Rimuovo MBR hybrid per renderla leggibile da macOS..."; \
1002:		dd if=/dev/zero of=$(RELEASE_DIR)/NexsOS1-amd64-$(VERSION).iso bs=512 count=1 conv=notrunc 2>/dev/null; \
1003:		echo "ISO creata: $(RELEASE_DIR)/NexsOS1-amd64-$(VERSION).iso"; \
1004:	else \
1005:		cp $(KERNEL_BIN) $(RELEASE_DIR)/kernel.img; \
1006:		cp $(DISK_IMG) $(RELEASE_DIR)/disk.img; \

1021:# Development Execution
1022:# ==============================================================================
1023:
1024:# AArch64: generate the QEMU virt device tree for the exact machine configuration
1025:# used in the run target.  The DTB must match the devices, memory size, and SMP
1026:# count so that fdt_get_mem_regions() and fdt_count_cpus() see accurate data.
1027:# dumpdtb exits immediately after writing the DTB; no kernel is required.
1028:# amd64 does not use a DTB (discovery via multiboot2), so this target is aarch64-only.
1029:ifeq ($(ARCH), aarch64)
1030:$(VIRT_DTB): disk | $(BUILD_DIR)
1031:	@echo "  [DTB]    Generating QEMU virt device tree -> $@"
1032:	@ERRLOG=$$(mktemp); \
1033:	if ! $(QEMU_RUN) -M virt -cpu cortex-a57 -m 5G -smp 4 \
1034:	         -device virtio-gpu-device \
1035:	         -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-mouse-device \
1036:	         -drive if=none,file=$(DISK_IMG),id=hd0,format=raw \
1037:	         -device virtio-blk-device,drive=hd0 \
1038:	         -machine dumpdtb=$@ 2>"$$ERRLOG"; then \
1039:	    cat "$$ERRLOG" >&2; rm -f "$$ERRLOG"; \
1040:	    echo "  [DTB]    $(QEMU_RUN) failed — see stderr above (broken/snap-shadowed QEMU install is a common cause)." >&2; \
1041:	    exit 1; \
1042:	fi; \
1043:	rm -f "$$ERRLOG"
1044:	@echo "  [DTB]    Done ($$($(STAT_SIZE) $@) bytes)"
1045:
1046:# AArch64 run: use kernel.bin (raw binary) so QEMU's aarch64 boot stub sets x0 = dtb_addr.
1047:# A raw binary triggers QEMU's arm_load_kernel image-loading path; combined with -dtb,
1048:# QEMU loads the DTB into RAM and passes its address in x0 before jumping to the entry.
1049:# Using kernel.elf (ELF) without a Linux image header leaves x0=0 (no DTB handover).
1050:run: all $(VIRT_DTB)
1051:	$(QEMU_RUN) $(QEMU_FLAGS) -kernel $(KERNEL_BIN)
1052:
1053:run-direct: run
1054:
1055:debug: all
1056:	$(QEMU_RUN) $(QEMU_FLAGS) -kernel $(KERNEL_BIN) -s -S
1057:else
1058:run: all
1059:	$(QEMU_RUN) $(QEMU_FLAGS) -kernel $(KERNEL_ELF)
1060:
1061:run-direct: run
1062:
1063:debug: all
1064:	$(QEMU_RUN) $(QEMU_FLAGS) -kernel $(KERNEL_ELF) -s -S
1065:endif

1071:# Run it before touching the scheduler or any teardown path.
1072:lockcheck:

@@@ README.md @@@
1:# NexsOS1 (OS1)
2:
3:### Multi-architecture open-source hybrid-kernel operating system
4:
5:[![License: GPL v2](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-GPLv2-blue.svg)](LICENSE.md)
6:[![Arch](https://img.shields.io/badge/arch-aarch64%20%7C%20amd64-green.svg)](#)
7:[![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-QEMU-orange.svg)](https://www.qemu.org/)
8:[![Language](https://img.shields.io/badge/language-C99-yellow.svg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C99)
9:
10:NexsOS1 (codename **OS1**) is an educational and research hybrid-kernel operating system built from scratch. It boots on both ARM64 (AArch64) and x86-64 (AMD64) under QEMU, brings up Symmetric Multiprocessing (SMP), drives native **VirtIO** devices (GPU, input, block), mounts an **Ext4** root filesystem, composites overlapping windows in a custom graphical user interface, and executes user-space ELF binaries with an interactive **TTY shell**.
11:
12:> **Honesty note.** This README describes the *verified* state. For the complete, evidence-based picture — including bugs, gaps, and severity — see [`docs/review/REVIEW.md`](docs/review/REVIEW.md). For where the project is *going* (a seL4-style, Plan 9-inspired Microkernel), see [`docs/PROJECT_CHARTER.md`](docs/PROJECT_CHARTER.md). This project is licensed under **GPL v2** (see [`LICENSE.md`](LICENSE.md)).
13:

29:
30:## 🚀 Key Features
31:
32:*   **Architectural Abstraction Layer (HAL):** The HAL provides complete transparency to the kernel. There are no architecture-specific `#define` statements within the common kernel codebase, ensuring easy portability to other architectures.
33:*   **Secure Memory Paging:** Physical (zone-based PMM bitmap allocator) and Virtual Memory Managers handle paging. On AMD64, the system enforces the strict **$W \oplus X$ (Write or Execute)** security protocol (executable text is RX, read-only data is RO+NX, all other regions are RW+NX) alongside Higher-Half kernel mappings (`0xFFFF000000000000` on AArch64 via TTBR1, `0xFFFF800000000000` on AMD64), with cross-CPU TLB shootdown.
34:*   **Preemptive SMP & Multiprocessing:** Preemptive O(1) SMP scheduler with per-CPU priority run-queues and work-stealing. Cores are initialized and managed by user-space idle tasks once primary boot completes. Multiple processes are cleanly distributed across cores, with full support for `child` creation, `kill` termination, and an `exec` utility managing terminal, graphical, and integrated terminal modes.
35:*   **Capability-Based Security:** Syscalls and system resources are checked and restricted through a capabilities security model mapped to abstract user levels (`Machine`, `Root`, `User`, `Guest`). The only processes allowed to run at the highly privileged `Machine` level are `nxinit` (early init) and the idle tasks.
36:*   **Graphics Stack & Window Compositor:** GPU abstraction, display drivers (`virtio-pci-device` and `virtio-gpu-device`), and the compositor are currently inside the kernel (rendering overlapping windows, drag, focus, and Z-order). The compositor processes individual application framebuffers rendered in userland. Supports custom themes and styles; all interface components are compiled as independent ELF binaries.
37:*   **Isolated Userland & Release System:** The userland environment resides in a dedicated disk image (`disk.img`), allowing independent loading of the kernel and filesystem in QEMU for rapid testing. At boot, the kernel loads `disk.img` into a temporary RAM disk, and launches the `init` supervisor. `init` manages core services, respawning them automatically if they terminate. The release tool compiles a hybrid, bootable AMD64 ISO via GRUB.
38:*   **Fault & Trace Isolation:** Recoverable fault handling with total vector coverage on both architectures. A userland application crash is isolated and never kills the kernel, leaving the shell and compositor running. Provides symbolized in-kernel backtraces (`.ksyms`) on dedicated fault stacks.
39:*   **VFS & Ext4 File System:** Virtual File System (with mount tables and `fs_ops` providers) supporting Ext4 (extent-tree reads, legacy reads, INCOMPAT enforcement, and extended write paths) and GPT partition mapping with MBR fallback, and a buffer cache.
40:*   **Coherent Syscall ABI:** Single unified syscall numbering (`include/api/syscall_nums.h`) compiled into both the kernel dispatcher and the userland stubs, returning negative `errno` values.
41:

44:## 📊 Verified Runtime Status
45:
46:### Capability Matrix
47:Successfully tested and verified by building and running:
48:
49:| Capability | AArch64 (`make run`) | AMD64 (`make run`) |
50:|---|:---:|:---:|
51:| **Clean Build** (`-Werror -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wshadow`) | ✅ | ✅ |
52:| **Boots to TTY Shell** (In a composited window) | ✅ | ✅ |
53:| **Higher-Half Kernel** (PA/VA contract, direct map, $W \oplus X$) | ✅ `0xFFFF0000...` | ✅ `0xFFFF8000...` |
54:| **Dynamic RAM Detection** (Full boot-protocol memory map) | ✅ (DTB) | ✅* (PVH/MB1/MB2) |
55:| **Symmetric Multiprocessing** (SMP Core Bring-up) | ✅ (4/4 Online) | ✅ |
56:| **VirtIO Drivers** (GPU, Input/Keyboard/Mouse, Block) | ✅ | ✅ |
57:| **Ext4 Support** (Extent-tree reads, GPT/MBR fallback) | ✅ | ✅ |
58:| **Userland Environment** (ELF Loader, IPC, Registry, Fonts) | ✅ | ✅ |
59:| **Fault Isolation** (User crash isolated, Symbolized Backtrace) | ✅ | ✅ |
60:| **Coherent Syscall ABI** (Negative `errno`, Capability Layer) | ✅ | ✅ |
61:
62:> [!NOTE]  
63:> \* The AMD64 boot pipeline parses the physical PVH memory map, resolving previous hardcoded fallback constraints. However, total RAM estimation currently treats the 3–4 GB PCI hole as RAM. AArch64 remains the reference, fully standard platform.

75:| **Linux (Debian / Arch / Alpine)** | ✅ | Toolchain verified; environment features auto-detection |
76:| **BSD Derivatives** | ⬜ | Not yet supported |
77:| **UTM (AMD64 ISO release)** | ✅ | Verified test on UTM (virtio-pci-gpu / PS/2 input) |

105:## 🛠 Prerequisites & Toolchain Setup
106:
107:To compile and execute NexsOS1, you will need the official cross-compiler toolchain. The official toolchain can be installed via `setup-toolchain-macos.sh` and `setup-toolchain-linux.sh`. The build system has been fully verified on macOS (Intel/Apple Silicon) and Linux (Ubuntu, Debian, and Arch). BSD is not yet supported.
108:
109:The setup scripts automate the builds of pinned GNU compilers directly from source (`x86_64-elf-gcc` 13.2.0, `aarch64-none-elf-gcc` 7.2.0), taking about 10-30 minutes. It also auto-downloads the required userland repositories from GitHub, including ported libraries and applications such as `kilo`, `freedoom`, `sdl`, `musl`, `busybox`, `lua`, `opengl`, and `direct3d9`.
110:
111:*(Note: On WSL2, the script automatically prints configuration guides for WSLg graphics and KVM permissions.)*
112:
113:### 1. Clone the Repository
114:```bash
115:git clone https://github.com/olmox001/NexsOS1
116:cd NexsOS1
117:```
118:
119:### 2. Configure Your Build Environment
120:Run the corresponding script for your operating system:
121:
122:*   **For Linux (Ubuntu, Debian, Arch, Alpine):**
123:    ```bash
124:    ./tools/setup-toolchain-linux.sh
125:    ```
126:
127:*   **For macOS:**
128:    ```bash
129:    ./tools/setup-toolchain-macos.sh
130:    ```
131:
132:### 3. Verify the Installation
133:Ensure the cross-compilers are correctly linked and ready:
134:```bash
135:make check ARCH=aarch64
136:make check ARCH=amd64
137:```
138:
139:---
140:
141:## 💻 Compilation & Execution
142:
143:NexsOS1 uses a streamlined `Makefile` interface. To compile the bootloader, kernel, and userland disk image, and immediately boot them in QEMU, run:
144:
145:```bash
146:# Build and run the ARM64 (AArch64) graphical system (Reference)
147:make run ARCH=aarch64
148:
149:# Build and run the x86_64 (AMD64) graphical system
150:make run ARCH=amd64
151:```
152:
153:### Additional Build Targets
154:
155:| Target Command | Description |
156:| :--- | :--- |
157:| `make all ARCH=<arch>` | Compiles the operating system without launching QEMU. |
158:| `make debug ARCH=<arch>` | Boots QEMU with GDB stub debugging enabled (`-s -S`). |
159:| `make release VERSION=x.y` | Builds release-ready packages (e.g., hybrid, bootable AMD64 ISOs via GRUB). |
160:| `make clean` | Wipes build outputs. Strongly recommended after userland changes in `user/` to make modifications effective. |
161:
162:The official kernel API for userspace can be found inside `include/api/`, focusing primarily on `os1.h` and `object.h`.
163:

166:## 📁 Project Layout
167:
168:```text
169:.
170:├── boot/                        # Stage 1 & Stage 2 bootloaders and linker scripts
171:│   ├── aarch64/
172:│   └── amd64/
173:├── docs/                        # Technical documentation, specifications, and reports
174:│   ├── LOGO/                    # Graphical assets and project logotypes
175:│   ├── direction/               # Architectural plans, design mandates, and directions
176:│   ├── graphics-port/           # Graphic system porting and validation logs
177:│   ├── man/                     # System manuals and user references
178:│   ├── report/                  # Performance, debugging, and analytical reports
179:│   ├── review/
180:│   │   └── analysis/            # Code reviews, bug taxonomy, and findings
181:│   ├── screen/                  # Architectural screenshots and system captures
182:│   └── userland-port/           # Guides and porting updates for the userspace
183:├── include/
184:│   └── api/                     # Public system API definitions for userland
185:│       └── sys/                 # Native C library definitions (os1.h, object.h)
186:├── kernel/
187:│   ├── arch/                    # Architecture-specific abstraction layers
188:│   │   ├── aarch64/             # ARM64 CPU setup, MMU page tables, GIC, PL011 drivers
189:│   │   └── amd64/               # AMD64 CPU setup, APIC, IOAPIC, PIT, serial drivers
190:│   ├── core/                    # Core kernel engine (Syscall dispatcher, device bus)
191:│   ├── drivers/                 # Unified hardware drivers
192:│   │   ├── block/               # Mass storage block drivers
193:│   │   ├── gic/                 # ARM Interrupt Controllers
194:│   │   ├── gpu/                 # GPU framebuffers and VirtIO screen devices
195:│   │   ├── keyboard/            # Key input devices
196:│   │   ├── pci/                 # Peripheral Component Interconnect bus driver
197:│   │   ├── ps2/                 # Traditional PS/2 mouse and keyboard
198:│   │   ├── timer/               # System clocks
199:│   │   ├── uart/                # Serial logging interfaces
200:│   │   ├── usb/                 # Universal Serial Bus (USB) driver stub
201:│   │   └── virtio/              # Virtual I/O drivers (GPU, Block, Input)
202:│   ├── fs/                      # Virtual File System (VFS) and Ext4 disk system
203:│   ├── graphics/                # Compositor engine, TTF fonts, and window servers
204:│   │   └── logo/
205:│   ├── include/                 # Internal, private kernel headers
206:│   ├── irq/                     # Global interrupt request dispatchers
207:│   ├── lib/                     # In-kernel shared helper libraries (printf, kmalloc)
208:│   ├── mm/                      # Memory management (Bitmap PMM, Virtual MM, Heap)
209:│   └── sched/                   # Preemptive priority scheduler and ELF loader
210:├── tools/
211:│   ├── kernel_doctor/           # Technical debugging, tracing, and analysis suite
212:│   └── mkdisk.c                 # Tool for packaging userland into an Ext4 disk image
213:└── user/
214:    ├── arch/                    # Architecture-specific runtime startup routines
215:    │   ├── aarch64/
216:    │   └── amd64/
217:    ├── bin/                     # Standalone user applications and demos
218:    │   ├── base-nexs/           # Native testing and compatibility tools
219:    │   ├── busybox/             # Unix terminal utilities
220:    │   ├── doom/                # Ported Doom engine
221:    │   └── kilo/                # Ported ultra-lightweight text editor
222:    ├── home/                    # System root home directory structure
223:    │   └── Pictures/
224:    └── sys/                     # Operating system critical subsystems
225:        ├── bin/                 # Userland base services (init, shell, panel, dock)
226:        └── lib/                 # Core shared library runtimes (libos1, libc-stubs)
227:```

231:## 🗺 The ASTRA Roadmap
232:
233:### Core Kernel Foundation
234:- [x] Clean-boot on AArch64 and AMD64
235:- [x] Architectural HAL with complete ISA insulation
236:- [x] Preemptive SMP scheduling with work-stealing queues
237:- [x] Unified Physical and Virtual Memory Managers
238:- [x] Higher Half Kernel Mapping
239:- [x] Rigid $W \oplus X$ memory protection
240:- [x] Thread/Context Isolation using ASID/PCID
241:- [x] Secure ELF64 loader
242:- [x] Zero-copy synchronous IPC primitives
243:- [x] Capability-based system security model
244:- [x] Object Manager abstraction
245:- [x] Unified VirtIO Drivers (MMIO & PCI)
246:- [x] Capability-based Virtual File System (VFS)
247:- [x] Ext4 filesystem layout support (Extent Trees)
248:- [x] System registry as a hierarchical VFS namespace
249:- [x] Native window graphics compositor
250:- [x] Intuitive Window Manager
251:- [x] Supervised initialization service (`init` supervisor)
252:
253:### ASTRA Phase B — Architectural Maturation
254:- [x] **B1:** High-fidelity VFS integration as a core ASTRA provider
255:- [x] **B2:** Complete, architecture-agnostic memory management model
256:- [x] **B3:** Coherent Capability ABI validation & unified Object Manager
257:- [ ] **B4:** Complete AMD64 platform parity (native ACPI / MADT mapping)
258:- [ ] **B5:** Complete separation of the HAL and the Service Runtime Layer (SRL)
259:- [ ] **B6:** SMP refinement and asynchronous I/O event loops
260:
261:### ASTRA Phase C — Service Demoting (Microkernel Boundary)
262:- [ ] Formalization of the low-level `OS1low` ABI
263:- [ ] Demoting system drivers to supervised userland tasks
264:- [ ] User-space GPU Service
265:- [ ] User-space Network Service Stack
266:- [ ] User-space Audio Service
267:- [ ] User-space Input Handling Daemon
268:- [ ] User-space System Registry daemon
269:- [ ] Migrating the Compositor into a dedicated user-space application
270:- [ ] Separating the Window Server completely from kernel authority
271:
272:### ASTRA Phase D — Standard Userland Porting
273:- [ ] Development of the official native `libOS1` userland library
274:- [ ] Upstream port of the `musl` C library to the native OS1 ABI
275:- [ ] Full POSIX standards personality layer
276:- [ ] Lua runtime engine integration
277:- [ ] Full integration of standard `BusyBox` utilities
278:
279:### ASTRA Phase E — Optimization & Hardening
280:- [ ] Extensive optimization of the userland runtimes
281:- [ ] Minimization of boot-time and RAM footprint
282:- [ ] High-performance low-latency scheduler and ultra-fast IPC paths
283:- [ ] Core System Auditing and sandboxing capabilities
284:- [ ] Kernel hardening, fault recovery, and DWARF backtrace debugging
285:
286:### Hardware support targets
287:- [ ] Networking
288:- [ ] Audio
289:- [ ] USB complete support
290:- [ ] Hardware graphics acceleration
291:- [ ] Advanced storage drivers
292:
293:### File System targets
294:- [ ] Journaling support
295:- [ ] Dynamic mounts
296:- [ ] Support for multiple filesystems
297:- [ ] Fully capability-based VFS
298:
299:### Security targets
300:- [ ] Full syscall auditing
301:- [ ] Hardening kernel
302:- [ ] Recovery mode
303:- [ ] Backtrace DWARF parser
304:- [ ] Advanced sandboxing capabilities

308:## 🤝 Democratic Development & Contributing
309:
310:NexsOS1 is, first and foremost, a free and open-source project. While it began as a personal research initiative, the long-term goal is to build an operating system that belongs to its community. Everyone is welcome to participate, whether by writing code, reporting bugs, reviewing the architecture, improving the documentation, testing on new hardware, or simply sharing ideas.
311:
312:Technical choices are made democratically:
313:*   **Democratic Architecture:** Major architectural decisions, API layouts, and roadmap adjustments should reflect community consensus rather than unilateral design.
314:*   **GitHub Discussions:** We use Discussions as our town square. We highly encourage developers, researchers, students, and enthusiasts to raise technical inquiries, debate architectural improvements, propose new subsystems, and host community polls! All requests will be taken into consideration.
315:
316:### How to Contribute
317:1. Fork the repository.
318:2. Create a dedicated feature branch (`feature/your-feature`, `fix/your-fix`, `refactor/your-refactor`).
319:3. Keep the coding style consistent: **K&R Style, 2-space indentation**, and a warnings-clean build with strict compiler flags (`-Werror -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wshadow`).
320:4. Avoid regressions on both supported architectures (AArch64 and AMD64) whenever possible.
321:5. Update documentation when introducing significant architectural changes.
322:6. For large changes, please open a Discussion or an Issue before starting the implementation.

332:## 🙏 Acknowledgments
333:
334:NexsOS1 stands on the shoulders of the incredible open-source community. Key portions of the userland system are maintained as custom forks specifically optimized for the native OS1 APIs.
335:
336:Special thanks to the authors and maintainers of:
337:*   **BusyBox:** The foundational utility provider for Unix-style userlands.
338:*   **Kilo:** The incredibly lightweight text editor adapted to OS1.
339:*   **Doom Generic:** Providing the core codebase for our graphics validation.
340:*   **SDL2:** Serving as our multimedia abstraction target.
341:*   **Mesa:** The baseline foundation for our future OpenGL compatibility.
342:*   **Wine:** The core source of inspiration and architectural reference for our Direct3D 9 compatibility layer.
343:*   **musl libc:** The lightweight standard C library being adapted to our system ABI.
344:*   **Lua:** The ultra-fast scripting engine scheduled for system-wide integration.
345:*   **base-nexs:** Portable script languages.
346:
347:We also draw technical inspiration from pioneers in operating system research, notably **Linux**, **Plan 9 from Bell Labs**, **seL4**, **Fuchsia**, **Windows NT**, **Darwin (XNU)**, and **TempleOS**. These projects are sources of ideas and architectural inspiration only; NexsOS1 is an independent implementation developed from scratch.
348:
349:Finally, thanks to everyone who tests the project, reports bugs, reviews the architecture, proposes improvements, or simply takes the time to explore the code. Every contribution helps make NexsOS1 a better operating system.
